articles.title: ‘Lilo & Scratch’: Disney Animation Blends 2D and 3D to Bring Back Stitch to the Big Screen in a New Short
articles.full_text: × Nov 13, 2026 9:00am PT ‘Lilo & Scratch’: Disney Animation Blends 2D and 3D to Bring Back Stitch to the Big Screen in a New Short By Carole Horst Plus Icon Carole Horst Latest AI ‘Gods,’ Big-Budget Sci Fi, Star-Studded Genre Pics and More Generate Buzz at AFM 2 days ago AFM: First Look at Highland Film Group Thriller ‘The Black Demon: Atlantis’ Starring Jack Kesy (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago The ‘Air Bud Returns’ Team Hits AFM With Reenergized International Sales and More Family-Friendly Canine Adventures (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Walt Disney Animation The new animated short “Lilo & Scratch” immediately sets up audience expectations with its opening shot featuring a clip of the Three Stooges — expect comic hijinks, anarchy and cartoon destruction. For the first “Lilo & Stitch” project from Disney Animation since the original 2002 feature, and the first short from the unit in five years, directors Malcolm Pierce and Fawn Veerasunthorn ride the anarchy of the Stooges that lives in Stitch and introduce a new character, Scratch, a cute, cuddly kitten whose destructive forces rival the Lilo’s beloved blue “dog.” The short will unspool before Disney’s “Hexed,” which will be released Nov. 25. “Stitch is awesome,” says Pierce. “I feel like what I love is that he sort of lets his intrusive thoughts win, but he’s kind of a troublemaker too, which is really fun. So that was just super exciting, just to see what we can do that could put Stitch in a situation where he can make the most mischievous and troublemaking choices.” The plot of the short sees Lilo come home with a cute cat, which she calls Scratch, then leave the new pet in the care of Stitch (who’s watching the Three Stooges with glee). The cat quickly shows its true colors, creating trouble in ever-escalating comic situations that are laugh out loud funny and absurd. Related Stories 'Nobody Wants This' Renewed for Season 4 at Netflix Hollywood's Next Big Deal: Will Netflix Make an M&A Play for NBCU? Veerasunthorn is also a big Stitch fan, noting the 2002 film’s bold comedy and “the character’s deep desire to belong. It also came out when I was still in art school, so this film had made a big impression on me as an artist.” She adds that “when Jared Bush, [Walt Disney Animation Studios] chief creative officer, had this casual conversation with us — and I say casual because it happened in the hallway” to create a comedy-forward short “that showcases the fun of animation,” it was a no-brainer to go back to Lilo and Stitch. She says that she, Pierce and producer Nathan Curtis bounced around ideas and they narrowed the theme down to one question: Wouldn’t it be fun if chaotic stitch had to take care of a mysterious cute cat? Bush also wanted to play with new techniques for their animation pipeline. “The most exciting thing was to kind of merge these two worlds from Disney Animation, this old school Disney renaissance 2D aesthetic with our more modern CG pipeline,” says VFX supervisor Jeremy Sikorski. “We got a taste of what this would be on some of our other short form projects like ‘Paper Man’ and more recently, ‘Once Upon a Studio.’ So this felt like a real opportunity to somewhat officialize and push things even further to see where we could kind of take these aesthetics that the world has loved for so many years.” He adds: “We asked ourselves how could we create a production pipeline that no matter the artist’s chosen mediums, they could work in the project and work all together — quite often in the same exact frame — in a totally revolutionary and new way of working.” For the short, they studied the original feature and created a “toolset that would allow artists to blend their talents.” For example, a background could be hand-painted watercolor, but the Lilo and Stitch characters set against the background are 3D sculptures. They did an early test to see if their concept was going to work, using a hand-drawn Scratch and a CG Stitch holding a blaster in a sequence. “And the blaster he’s holding actually transitions from CG to hand drawn as Scratch eats it. When we looked at the finished results of this test, we were convinced we could do it, and we knew this was going to work, which is super exciting,” says Sikorski. Adds Veerasunthorn, “We wanted to give our artists an ability to choose their preferred medium to create a brand-new background for the short. So we actually do both. Some of these are digitally painted in Photoshop to look like watercolor, and some are actually hand painted on paper traditionally.” The six-minute short packs a lot of action and gags. “I think because Stitch is so popular, folks have an assumption of what Stitch is. He’s in merchandise everywhere. He’s he can be so familiar nowadays, so we really wanted to remind people of how you know hardcore he can be, how he can break stuff, and gets grumpy, and he’s got an edge to him, and so we really had fun just thinking about ‘What are all like the crazy things Stitch can do?’” says Pierce. Veerasunthorns adds: “We thought, who would be the worthy opponent of Stitch? They must meet each other at the same one-upping level. You know we always think Stitch would say, ‘I got this,’ and then Scratch would be like ‘Hold my beer, I got more.’ How do they kind of keep escalating the situation? And actually, the first cut of this reel was about 10 minutes because we had so many more jokes, and we had to narrow it down and say goodbye to some of our darlings.” A cat opponent would be a natural antagonist for Stitch, who’s still called Lilo’s “ugly blue dog.” Veerasunthorn said her initial design was more mysterious-looking and sort of weird, but they realized she had to be a lot cuter for audiences to embrace her. She also needed her own sound, which is where composers Haim Mazar and Grace Fisher came in. “She definitely has, like, a heavy metal voice, which is very unique to this short,” says Fisher. The duo had a lot of fun creating the music for the comedic action sequences — inspired by Carl Stalling and Tom and Jerry cartoons. The familiar had to blend with the new in the short. Says Mazar, “One of our biggest challenges was coming up with something that would feel fresh and contemporary, and at the same time, feel familiar, so that right from the first note you feel like, ‘I know this world’ and welcome to our ohana, so to speak. I think if I had to explain it, it was it was probably a combination of the style of the melodic material that we were we were going for something that would feel like it’s melodic and maybe even lyrical at times, but it also has a little sense of — I guess dare I say — pop music, and it it feels like a little bit of a fun ear worm.” Mazar adds that they recorded an orchestra, but also “small ensembles that had a lot of close miking and very tactile sounding shakers and and and all sorts of Hawaiian guitars, and I think producing it in a way that feels very contemporary, like a like a like a record that you would hear nowadays, and fusing that with the orchestra was what kind of gave it a little bit of a fresh taste.” Veerasunthorns adds that because the characters are mostly non-verbal, it’s really like paradise for animation. … the fact that we are able to get hand-drawn artists and CG animators working together is something that we’re super proud of, because we used to be like either or, and everyone just wanted to work on it.” Arnold Schwarzenegger Explains to Jimmy Kimmel Why He’s ‘Absolutely’ Still a Republican After the Blue ‘Tsunami’ Midterms Aly Muritiba Says It Was ‘Revolutionary’ to Centre Black Joy in Brazilian Musical ‘Funk’ Led by Rising Star Duda Santos ‘Kantara: A Legend,’ ‘The Kerala Story 2,’ Volker Schlondorff’s ‘Visitation’ Among 15 Films in Goa Festival International Competition Vampire Santa Claus Is Coming to Town in Ilja Rautsi’s Charades-Sold ‘Red Snow,’ Which Debuts Clip: ‘It’s a Gruesome Christmas Present’ (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Heartland’ Review: Jessica Chastain Rocks a Stetson and a Swagger for a Soapy Nashville Noir Aspyn Ovard on Her Divorce, Being in a Throuple and Joining ‘The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives’ Universe: ‘I Hope People Can Understand Me a Little Bit Better’ Loading comments...

articles.title: Tom Hopper, Rita Ora and Mila Harris to Star in Sci-Fi Thriller ‘The Signalers,’ WME Independent Launches Sales (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 13, 2026 9:00am PT Tom Hopper, Rita Ora and Mila Harris to Star in Sci-Fi Thriller ‘The Signalers,’ WME Independent Launches Sales (EXCLUSIVE) By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Conspiracy Thriller ‘The Awakening,’ Starring Kevin Spacey, Gets U.S. Release (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Laika’s ‘Wildwood’ Passes $60 Million Worldwide (EXCLUSIVE) 15 hours ago ‘The Witcher’ Star Freya Allan to Lead Joachim Rønning’s Horror Movie ‘System’ (EXCLUSIVE) 16 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Credit: Michael Shelford, Kaj Jeffries, Cathryn Farnsworth Tom Hopper (“The Umbrella Academy,” “The Terminal List”), singer and actress Rita Ora (“Fifty Shades of Grey,” “Tin Soldier”), and rising young Hollywood star Mila Harris (“No Exit,” “Mary”) are set to star in upcoming sci-fi adventure thriller “The Signaler.” Missi Pyle (“Galaxy Quest”) and Nolan North (“Uncharted”) have also joined the cast in supporting roles alongside Paulina Alvarez, David Silverman, and Wolfgang Fiegl. Now in production, “The Signaler.” comes from Gramercy Park Media, was written by was(“The Plumber,” “Masque” and a former detective and military intelligence specialist) and is being directed by Gille Klabin (“The Wave”). WME Independent is handling domestic sales, while Peachtree Group provided the financing. Related Stories 'The Body' Creator on the Dance Team's Sexuality, What Happened to Grace and Whether God Is Real Alex de la Iglesia on His Upcoming Chilean Shoot ‘The Misunderstanding’: ‘Reality Has Become My Parallel World’ The film follows a remote air traffic controller (Hopper) and his estranged niece (Harris) after they detect an impossible signal deep in the Canadian wilderness that is causing strange and dangerous phenomena to occur. As they set off to uncover the origins of the troubling signal, they encounter research scientists (Ora and Pyle) also on the hunt for the occurrence, and inadvertently uncover a buried unearthly force that is awakening around them. “We are thrilled to be on set capturing the intense, visually stunning excitement of this film,” said Harris of Peachtree Media Partners. “Cate’s script provides an incredible launching point for our cast to bring this story to life and with all the news about alien disclosures and otherworldly cover-ups, this classic Spielberg inspired film is exactly the type of story audiences have been waiting for!” Joining Harris of Peachtree and Gramercy Park Media, the film features an experienced producing team including Mary Aloe of Aloe Entertainment and Cate Carson and Jay De La Jara of Ed Motel Entertainment. Ford Corbett and Nathan Klingher of Gramercy Park Media are executive producing alongside Danielle Bisutti and Ron Greenbaum of Pen Ultimate Films. The behind-the-scenes creative team includes director of photography Aaron Grasso, production designer Mollie Wartelle, and costume designer Erika Benton. Filming is currently underway in and around Atlanta Georgia, with post-production scheduled ahead of an anticipated 2027 release. articles.title: Evil Moms: From ‘East of Eden’ to ‘Carrie,’ TV’s Latest Trope Is Honoring Women Who Choose Themselves
articles.full_text: × Nov 13, 2026 9:00am PT Evil Moms: From ‘East of Eden’ to ‘Carrie,’ TV’s Latest Trope Is Honoring Women Who Choose Themselves By Aramide Tinubu Plus Icon Aramide Tinubu Latest Anthony Mackie and Jamie Dornan’s Heist Drama ’12 12 12′ Feels Like a Bad Video Game: TV Review 3 hours ago Netflix’s Genre-Bending YA Drama ‘The Body’ Is a Queer Y2K Extravaganza: TV Review 2 days ago ‘Wanted’ Broadway Review: Dazzling Cast Can’t Elevate the Musical’s Muted Narrative 5 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source COURTESY OF NETFLIX / SUZANNE TENNER/NETFLIX / Peacock / Courtesy of Prime / David Astorga Television has recently been preoccupied with evil moms, or at least that’s who they appear to be at first glance. In Zoe Kazan’s sweeping adaptation of John Steinbeck’s “ East of Eden ,” Lee (Hoon Lee), the Trask family’s domestic servant and surrogate father to the twin boys Aron (Joe Anders) and Cal (Joseph Zada), offers a poignant reflection. “There’s a beauty in the truth, even if it’s a dreadful beauty,” he says. Often, we evade or step around the facts. But dishonesty, no matter how innocent, is extremely harmful. The truth is that the world has rarely, if ever, been a safe space for women. To come of age in a patriarchal and violent society is a horrific thing. It corrodes the mind. It also forces girls and women to choose between two distinct paths. You either lean into male-centeredness or shun it entirely. Unfortunately, because patriarchy is a system that cannot be usurped, whether you lean toward it or try to burn it down, you will always be seen as monstrous by someone. Related Stories Netflix Hires Apple Alum Steve Wilson to Lead Podcast Content Acquisition Alex de la Iglesia on His Upcoming Chilean Shoot ‘The Misunderstanding’: ‘Reality Has Become My Parallel World’ Television programming typically works in conversation with popular culture. Currently, there is a lot to be said about motherhood, women’s experiences across time and what it truly means to be evil. Netflix’s “ Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story ” and “East of Eden,” Peacock’s “Friday the 13th” prequel “ Crystal Lake ,” Prime Video’s “ Carrie ” and Hulu’s comedic thriller “ Phony ” are distinct entities that all speak to one another. These are narratives centered on women reclaiming their stories from men who have only been able to view them in limited ways. These shows are all about women who have done horrendous things. However, their actions, despite how they’re presented on the surface, have not been without reason. In popular culture, men are depicted as barbarous, causing harm with impunity. Their behaviors are justified because, under patriarchy, men are poorly socialized and rely on women for empathy, care and comfort. As a result, when villainous men appear on screen in series like Ryan Murphy’s “Monster” franchise, Starz’s “Power” universe or HBO’s “Half Man,” they are senselessly volatile, nasty and murderous. This is not to suggest that women are immune to psychopathy. Yet their rates are far lower than men’s. Moreover, by living in a world not built for them, many women have learned to mask their most callous traits, making them unassuming and often, more lethal. When a woman is outwardly sinister, it typically shocks those around her. As Cathy Ames (Florence Pugh) reflects in “East of Eden,” “Evil is not always apparent at first glance; it can come cloaked in beauty or goodness or love.” Furthermore, when people learn these depraved women are mothers, it completely upends how the matriarchal role is viewed, making them all the more compelling. Florence Pugh in “East of Eden” COURTESY OF NETFLIX Perhaps it’s the nature of where we are in society, as female healthcare becomes increasingly sparse in certain parts of the country, as a rapist sits in the White House and as a generation of men seems intent on dragging women back in time to the 1950s. No matter the fixation, streamers, in particular, are turning their lens on several women determined to gain their agency by any means necessary. In “Monster: Lizzie Borden,” set in the late 19th century, Lizzie (Ella Beatty) is terrorized by her conniving stepmother, Abby (Rebecca Hall), whom she calls Mrs. Borden. Because of the confining nature of her role as a bored, bitter housewife (despite her privilege), Mrs. Borden revels in wickedness. With no recourse against her aloof, philandering husband, Andrew (Charlie Hunnam), she lashes out at the only people she can control: her staff and her naive, flighty stepdaughter. Wielding her cruelty for sport, the first two episodes of “Lizzie Borden” show Mrs. Borden throwing hot soup in her maid’s face, beating Lizzie and speaking to her harshly. However, the final straw before Lizzie swings the ax, ending Mrs. Borden’s life, comes when the older woman shoots up the girl’s beloved dovecote in a flurry of bloody feathers. Mrs. Borden likely always had a tinge of nastiness to her spirit, but being trapped in a marriage with no recourse to freedom exacerbated it. It’s no surprise, then, that when a monster raises you, you often become larger and more vicious than ever dreamed. Rebecca Hall and Ella Beatty in “Monster: The Lizzie Borden Story” SUZANNE TENNER/NETFLIX Mrs. Borden’s villainy likely stems from boredom and resentment. But some women are forced to emerge from something much more depraved. When “East of Eden” opens, audiences meet a bloodied and battered Cathy. She is on the brink of death as she drags herself onto the porch of brothers Adam (Christopher Abbott) and Charlie’s (Mike Faist) modest Connecticut home. Though Adam is immediately mesmerized by Cathy, Charlie, barely able to contain his fury, senses the darkness within her. Like Mrs. Borden, Cathy’s wickedness does not sprout from thin air. In Kazan’s narrative, she is sexually abused at age 5. This horrific incident forces Cathy to see the world in all of its depravity and the maddening horror of the people who let it fester in an effort to keep the peace. With absolute disdain for social norms and an understanding of the power and burden of her beauty, Cathy decides to carve her own path. She uses the men around her, including Adam, to obtain the one thing she’s striving for — financial independence. She does terrible things, but she is always honest about her intentions. She abandons her twin sons, telling Adam, “I don’t want them, I won’t change.” Later, when she sets her sights on Madame Faye (Martha Plimpton) to steal her brothel, she warns the older woman of her intentions before doing just that. Cathy is cold and calculated, but she is not overtly evil; she is unpunishable in a world intent on punishing women for much less. Linda Cardellini in “Crystal Lake” Peacock A half-century later in Peacock’s “Crystal Lake,” Pam Voorhees (Linda Cardellini) is grieving her dead son. Previously immersed in the joys and trials of motherhood, she is adrift without Jason (Callum Vinson). Yet, the world wounded her long before her son drowned. Her humiliation begins a decade earlier when her husband moves her from New York City to Texas for what she believes is advanced prenatal treatment. Following Jason’s birth, she learns they’ve both been experimented on for the sake of her husband’s career. Though she escapes and tries to put the horrible endeavor behind her, after Jason dies and her husband hunts her down, Pam lashes out in gruesome ways. Her wrath, like Lizzie’s, is not self–made — it is born out of the lie of female hysteria which festers under the stifling cloak of misogyny. Presently, America seems stuck in a state of appalling religious psychosis, a space Margaret White in “Carrie” knows all too well. Though she loves Carrie (Summer H. Howell), Margaret lets herself become a puppet of the patriarchy. Loyal to a male-centric theology, she terrorizes her only child, not even offering her the compassion of understanding her own body and menstrual cycle. What’s intriguing is that it’s clear Margaret feels trapped by her own religious beliefs, which is why, out of a desire to steer her own ship, she fashions herself an anti-bullying crusader while actively bullying and abusing Carrie. Instead of breaking the mold she’s been given, especially in the wake of her conspiracy theorist husband’s death, she chooses to work within it while manipulating and acting cruelly for her own gain. Summer H. Howell and Samantha Sloyan in “Carrie” Liane Hentscher/ Prime Finally, there is Ellen Cooke from “Phony” (Connie Britton). Though the show is told mostly from the perspective of Ellen’s teenage son, Sonny (Sam Nivola), the series showcases how deeply present and active maternal figures affect their children’s well-being and what happens when those children sense something is amiss. Though Ellen isn’t as openly chaotic and sinister as Mrs. Borden, Cathy, Pam or Margaret, she acts in unnerving ways, shattering the connection Sonny has spent a lifetime building with her. The horror then becomes when women aren’t behaving as society or even their children expect them to. Television is most interesting when characters are allowed to do outrageous things. When women operate outside of social norms, particularly mothers, it can be seen as horrific. The ladies depicted in these shows certainly have heinous moments. Yet, much of the terror we feel as viewers is because they choose themselves, even if it’s at the expense of their children. But perhaps what’s more evil is the fact that we live in a world where women haven’t been allowed to be self-serving. Should true freedom be widely granted to women, there would be little need for the nefarious deeds committed by the women in these shows. articles.title: Unauthorized ‘Gilmore Girls’ Doc ‘Drink Coffee, Talk Fast’ Sets Release Date as Series Alum Scott Patterson Joins as Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 13, 2026 9:00am PT Unauthorized ‘Gilmore Girls’ Doc ‘Drink Coffee, Talk Fast’ Sets Release Date as Series Alum Scott Patterson Joins as Producer (EXCLUSIVE) By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest ‘Wolfenstein 3’ in Development at Xbox’s MachineGames 17 hours ago ‘Unlike Anything Else’: As ‘GTA 6’ Approaches, the Gaming Industry Braces the World for Its Pop Culture Takeover 20 hours ago More Than Half of Video Game Workers Laid Off Over the Past Two Years Are Still Unemployed, GDC Industry Report Finds 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ink On Paper Studios The “ Gilmore Girls ” documentary “Drink Coffee, Talk Fast” will be releasing on video-on-demand platforms next week with series alum Scott Patterson (who played the beloved Luke Danes) now on board as an executive producer and doc subject. Airing for seven seasons on The WB/CW from 2000-2007 with a one-season revival at Netflix in 2016, “Gilmore Girls” starred Lauren Graham and Alexis Bledel as iconic mother-and-daughter-duo Lorelai and Rory Gilmore. Related Stories ‘The New Stanford Prison Experiment’ Creators Break Down Its Shocking Finale Netflix Names Mattel Executive Roberto Stanichi as VP of Consumer Products and Experiences Per Ink On Paper Studios, the unauthorized documentary about the series will feature “all new, never-before-seen interviews with cast members, behind-the-scenes insights from the crew, stories from writers and directors, and heartfelt testimonials from fans whose lives were changed by the show.” Initially revealed as a Kickstarter project that hit its goal within its first 48 hours in September 2025, “Drink Coffee, Talk Fast” is now available to rent along with exclusive bonus content from the documentary-making process. The doc will be wildly available to stream for a fee on Apple, Google, and other major platforms on Tuesday, Nov. 17. “Drink Coffee, Talk Fast” is not affiliated with “Gilmore Girls” IP holder Warner Bros. Entertainment Inc. or the producers of “Gilmore Girls.” An authorized “Gilmore Girls” documentary is currently in the works at HBO Max with participation from creator Amy Sherman-Palladino alongside her husband, executive producer Daniel Palladino, and star Lauren Graham. Patterson’s participation in the “Gilmore Girls” doc is being announced ahead of the the film’s premiere at The Palace Theater in Los Angeles Friday as part of the Secret Movie Club and Los Angeles International Film Festival (LAIFF). Patterson will also be featured in the doc, alongside a number of new names just added to the cast list, in footage that was shot after the Kickstarter campaign ended. “Drink Coffee, Talk Fast” is directed by documentary filmmakers Meghna Balakumar and Kevin Konrad Hanna (“Clockwork Girl,” “Mike Mignola: Drawing Monsters”). Adam F. Goldberg is an executive producer. Jim Demonakos is a producer. “We couldn’t have been more excited to have Scott join us for this film,” Balakumar said. “He is so deeply connected to the ‘Gilmore Girls’ fandom, and we’re so glad we had the opportunity to capture that.” Along with Patterson (known for playing Lorelai Gilmore’s longtime will-they-won’t-they love Luke Danes), newly announced documentary participants include Lesli Linka Glatter (director), Susanne Daniels (former president of entertainment, The WB), Demi Adejuyigbe (co-host of the “Gilmore Guys” podcast), Rachel Kamerman (production designer), Mark Strasburg (first assistant camera) and Stephen Clancy (steadicam operator and director). These actors join the number of previously announced interviewees, including: Kelly Bishop (Emily Gilmore), Jared Padalecki (Dean Forester), Chad Michael Murray (Tristin Dugray), Keiko Agena (Lane Kim), Sally Struthers (Babette Dell), Liz Torres (Miss Patty), Emily Kuroda (Mrs. Kim), Rose Abdoo (Gypsy, Berta), Kathleen Wilhoite (Liz Danes), Michael Winters (Taylor Doose), Aris Alvarado (Caesar), Matt Jones (Morgan), Nick Holmes (Robert), Grant Lee Phillips (the town troubadour), George Anthony Bell (Professor Bell), Shelly Cole (Madeline Lynn), Vanessa Marano (April Nardini) and Olivia Hack (Tana Schrick) as well as director Jamie Babbit, writer and producer Stan Zimmerman, costumer Valerie Campbell, casting directors Jami Rudofsky and Mara Casey, and “Gilmore Guys” podcast co-host Kevin T Porter. articles.title: took down Outlook email
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Microsoft Outlook Still Down In 365 Outage: Company Sees Sporadic Improvements, Though No Sustained Recovery CJ 4DPlex Pacts With B&B Theatres To Equip Single Missouri Site With 3 Premium Large Format Screens ‘Star Wars: Episode IV – A New Hope’ To Play At Cosm As Disney Teams With Shared Reality Firm View All November 12, 2026 8:53pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images UPDATED with latest company comments: Earlier this evening Microsoft posted an update on the outages to its 365 platform noting “positive results with our efforts to restart affected infrastructure and recover server availability.” The optimism was short lived. About an hour later, the company announced that their efforts were “not taking as expected.” The company subsequently said it was “adjusting traffic protocols, redistributing traffic, and applying strategic traffic blocking measures,” and “observing partial recovery across regions in which we’ve applied these adjustments.” The bad news was, it reported, “these actions aren’t resulting in sustained recovery.” Related Stories News Microsoft Offers Buyouts To 60,000, A Quarter Of Its Workforce News Eyeing More 'Minecrafts' And 'Fallouts', Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games The widespread outages began around 1 p.m. ET, and impacted users in the United States and elsewhere. Watch on Deadline The tech giant issued a string of social media posts throughout the day on Thursday acknowledging that users had been reporting issues with access, throwing a major wrench into business communications across sectors. Enterprise and business customers of Microsoft 365 were experiencing problems connecting to email via the Exchange server as well as accessing other services. The U.S. is one of the main regions affected, but Microsoft says it potentially poses a problem across the world. As the outage dragged into the end of the work day, the tech giant put out a less-than-encouraging status report. “We’re continuing to pursue all available pathways to restore service, as our actions taken thus far have not provided the anticipated relief,” the company wrote. “Our investigation has found that a core process on the affected servers is becoming overwhelmed, which causes the servers to stop responding and contributes to the capacity loss.” Workers are “fully isolating a portion of our service infrastructure, restarting the affected components, and gradually reintroducing traffic to confirm our services remain stable,” the company went on to say. “We’re also analyzing traffic patterns across our entire service infrastructure and evaluating whether isolating traffic within each region may allow affected regions to recover independently.” After the initial issues with email, word surfaced about users unable to connect with Teams, Azure, OneDrive, Copilot and other offerings. The home page of outage detection site DownDetector was filled almost entirely by Microsoft alerts. “We’re investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas,” the company posted at around noon ET on Thursday. “While we’re working to mitigate impact, we’ve confirmed the issue may affect Microsoft 365 service connectivity for users in any region.” Microsoft later clarified, “We’ve determined a portion of infrastructure is experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, which is likely contributing to the connectivity errors.” A status hub designed to provide service updates cited “an unexpected increase in a specific type of service traffic to determine whether it’s contributing to the elevated load. In parallel, we’re evaluating options to redirect traffic to alternate infrastructure to expedite relief.” Media companies were among those across all business sectors whose activities slowed to a crawl due to the tech glitch. Employees at Amazon Prime Video, Skydance and NBCUniversal and other companies confirmed to Deadline they were in the dark. There were no immediate indications of a possible cause, though online speculation touched on factors like digital downloads of Grand Theft Auto VI pre-orders or hackers looking to make a statement. Still other theories sought to connect the outage to the day’s other momentous tech news: the ouster of Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia. Huang was forced to resign after admitting to an affair with a suspected Chinese spy and amid reports of affairs with executives at his own company. The origins of Microsoft 365 date to the early 2010s, when the company was ramping up its efforts to transition its Office programs Word, Excel and PowerPoint to the cloud. After a meteoric rise as a software maker in the 1980s and 1990s, Microsoft weathered some lean years after a federal antitrust lawsuit and a sluggish initial response to the advent of the internet. Under CEO Satya Nadella, Microsoft has successfully pivoted into cloud computing and, more recently, AI en route to a multi-trillion-dollar market valuation. Shares in Microsoft have thus far not been affected by the outage, finishing Thursday’s trading day up a fraction to $523. The company’s stock, along with those of a dozen or more large companies placing heavy bets on AI, will come under increasing scrutiny on Wall Street in light of the Nvidia news. Tom Tapp contributed to this report. ‘Ebenezer’ At $1.5M In Previews; Johnny Depp Pic Seeks $40M WW Opening Jason Voorhees Returns: Steve Miner To Direct 13th Entry Of ‘Friday The 13th’ ‘Virgin River’ Gets Season 9 Renewal; Will Be Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Microsoft Seeing “Improvements” As Outlook Email Comes Back Up Read More About: 37 Comments

articles.title: ‘Project Hail Mary’ Cinematographer Greig Fraser On Bringing 1980s Pop Culture Influences To Ryan Gosling Sci-Fi Hit — ToruńCamerimage
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana ‘Project Hail Mary’ Cinematographer Greig Fraser On Bringing 1980s Pop Culture Influences To Ryan Gosling Sci-Fi Hit — ToruńCamerimage From Local to Global: Anshuman Jha & Sarah-Jane Dias On Advocating Animal Rights In ‘Lakadbaggha 2’ & Uniqueness Of Crafting An Indian Action Franchise Rooted In Local Martial Arts Rising Star Molly McCann On Finding Her Place In Panem For ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ View All November 13, 2026 5:41am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ryan Gosling in 'Project Hail Mary' Amazon MGM Studios/Everett Collection Oscar-winning cinematographer Greig Fraser took time out of shooting Sam Mendes’ The Beatles films to reflect on how he and directors Phil Lord and Christopher Miller crafted the visuals for summer box office hit Project Hail Mary . Fraser spoke to Deadline during the Toruń Camerimage Film Festival and said that working with Lord and Miller had been a long time in the making. “I’ve known Phil and Christopher for a while in passing but we hadn’t worked together yet until this film,” he said. “What I love about them is that there is definitely a thread that runs through their films but genre-wise, they are completely different in everything they do. They are like these savants that just keep flicking between different formats and ratios and stories but there is an underlying theme in their work. What I think is beautiful about their work is that we all grew up on the same films and he same cartoons and we are all influenced by the same series of things.” Related Stories News 'Project Hail Mary' Composer Daniel Pemberton Built "A Language From The Ground Up" Using New Instruments - Sound & Screen Film Festivals Camerimage Opens With Minute Of Silence For Kraków Mass Shooting; Darren Aronofsky Honored & Luca Guadagnino Introduces 'Artificial' Fraser noted that pop culture references from the 1980s featured heavily in the discussions about how to portray the look of the Ryan Gosling starrer and he specifically noted Lord’s mention of Scooby-Doo when they discussed conveying the story’s transitions from space to Earth. Watch on Deadline “It gave me the idea in my head about the Scooby-Doo transition of the wobbly lines when there was a flashback,” he says. “I knew exactly what he was talking about. I also knew that in no way, shape or form would any film that we all contribute to have wobbly lines, and he said the same thing. So, then everything became a translation of how we do what we felt in the 1980s from films like E.T. or cartoons from pop culture. How do we translate that into what we’re creating now as filmmakers.” To achieve this look, Fraser, whose credits also include the first two instalments of Dune and The Batman , said he shot with a mis-timed shutter to create image streaking when transitioning the scenes. Project Hail Mary is an Amazon MGM film, which sees Ryan Gosling play a science teacher who wakes up in a spaceship light years away only to discover he is humanity’s sole hope to save Earth from a sun-dimming parasite. The film, which is based on Andy Weir’s novel of the same name, splits across two alternating timelines – present-day space and flashbacks on Earth. Fraser outlined the reasoning behind making the space scenes feel a “bit cooler” and the Earth scenes “a bit warmer.” “It was a fine balance to strike because you could absolutely go on a trope of space being cold and fluorescent lit and all kind of sci-fi,” he said. “And Earth is this thing that they are fighting for, and this is why he’s up there. So, you needed to be warm with the memories, and you need these things to be lovely memories. “But, at the same time, the Earth is dying because the sun is dying and you don’t want to sit through two and a half to three hours of a film where you want to jump off a building. You really need to come out and enjoy his experience, and he needs to grow from the experience.” The Australian DoP added that the opening scene, where Gosling’s character wakes up in space unaware of where he is, was crucial. “We specifically did not want that to feel like a space film,” he said. “He couldn’t wake up in a laboratory. I wanted him to wake up in a high-end hotel or what was effectively a high-end health retreat, so the audience is kind of discombobulated about where he is and what he is doing. He continues: “There’s a CG shot, which we all designed, where the camera goes past revealing him as this tiny person in this little window [in the spaceship] and this is another pop culture reference where we referenced The Empire Strikes Back as there’s a scene at the end of that film where you’ve got these little figures in the window. We liked that idea that he’s on a journey going past.” ToruńCamerimage takes place November 7-14, 2026. ‘Ebenezer’ At $1.5M In Previews; Johnny Depp Pic Seeks $40M WW Opening Jason Voorhees Returns: Steve Miner To Direct 13th Entry Of ‘Friday The 13th’ ‘Virgin River’ Gets Season 9 Renewal; Will Be Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Microsoft Seeing “Improvements” As Outlook Email Comes Back Up Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Virgin River’ Gets Early Season 9 Renewal, Officially Becomes Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie NFL Quarterback Sam Hartman To Headline ‘The Bachelor’ For Season 30 On ABC ‘Virgin River’ Gets Early Season 9 Renewal, Officially Becomes Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Hulu Series ‘The Spot’ Starring Claire Danes & Ewan McGregor Gets Release Date, First-Look Photos View All November 13, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L to R) Alexandra Breckenridge as Melinda Monroe and Martin Henderson as Jack Sheridan in Episode #701 of 'Virgin River' Courtesy of Netflix Netflix ‘s content leadership may be changing but one thing remains constant — Virgin River getting another early renewal. The long-running romantic drama starring Alexandra Breckenridge and Martin Henderson has been picked up for a ninth season months ahead of its 2027 Season 8 premiere. It will once again consist of 10 episodes, bringing the show’s total to 94 episodes. Patrick Sean Smith returns as showrunner and executive producer. With the renewal, Virgin River officially becomes the longest-running original scripted series on Netflix — and all of streaming — by number of seasons after taking the title with a qualifier last year. It has edged Spanish teen drama Elite , which ran for eight seasons. In number of episodes, 94, Virgin River ties current Netflix record holder, comedy Grace and Frankie, which produced seven seasons and is half-hour with an overall run time significantly shorter than that of hourlong Virgin River . Related Stories News 'The Body' Creators Address Show's "Unexplained Mysteries", Tease Season 2 Hopes Books Everything We Know About Netflix's 'Icebreaker' Adaptation So Far Alongside the renewal, Netflix also revealed that the adaptation of the popular Robyn Carr novels has passed the half-billion views mark this year. Watch on Deadline Virgin River, one of Netflix’s “blue sky”, “comfort” series, has defied the notion that streaming series cannot run for too long. The show has benefited from its sustainable premise, chronicling relationships among characters in a small town, appealing leads in Breckenridge and Henderson and strong supporting cast anchored by veterans Tim Matheson and Annette O’Toole, as well as attractive economics, keeping the budget reasonable by filming in Canada in a handful of primary locations with few stunts or special effects involved. The string of early renewals handed to Virgin River in the last few years has allowed the series to stay on a yearly cadence, dropping a new season every 11-13 months. There is no release date yet for Season 8 but a late spring premiere appears likely. As Deadline reported in March , Season 8 won’t feature two longtime cast members who are not returning, Marco Grazzini, who played Mike, and Lauren Hammersley, who portrayed Charmaine. Joining the cast is Natasha Calis in the heavily recurring role of Dr. Astrid, with an option to become a series regular in Season 9. Virgin River, which wrapped production on Season 8 in August, follows the romantic journey of nurse practitioner Melinda Monroe (Breckenridge), who moved to the remote California town of Virgin River after a personal tragedy, and charismatic local bartender Jack (Henderson), who is haunted by his past. The renewal comes a month after Peter Rice joined Netflix as new Chief Content Officer. It was done by Head of UCAN (US – Canada) Scripted Series Jinny Howe, who has continued in her role after the executive shake-up, now reporting to Rice. A self-professed romance buff, Howe was a fan of Virgin River before taking oversight of the show starting with Season 5 when Smith came in as new showrunner, replacing Sue Tenney. “Mel, Jack, and the whole town of Virgin River have become a place that feels like coming home, for viewers around the world,” Howe said. “Reaching Season 9 as our longest-running original scripted series, with over half a billion views, is a milestone that speaks to how deeply fans continue to love being a part of this community. Patrick Sean Smith and the entire team have done a beautiful job in keeping fans engaged in this world, and we can’t wait to invite fans back for more.” Season 8 will follow Mel and Jack’s journey as new parents as their adopted baby is fighting for his life. Across its first seven seasons, Virgin River has spent 28 weeks in the Global Top 10, and reached the Top 10 in over 80 countries. Smith executive produces with Erin Cardillo, Richard Keith, Jackson Sinder, Mary Page Keller, Thomas Ian Griffith, Norman Buckley, Ian Hay, Tenney, Roma Roth, Christopher E. Perry and Carr. “We’re all so grateful for our partnership with Netflix and incredibly proud to be a part of their legacy,” Smith said. “In a world that can sometimes feel increasingly disconnected, there’s something meaningful about having a place people want to return to. I’m incredibly proud of what we’ve built and continue to grow, and deeply grateful to the cast, crew, writers, and fans who have made Virgin River feel like home the world over.” The renewal comes ahead of Smith’s appearance on the panel “The Netflix Effect: How Book-to-Screen Adaptations Are Capturing the Heartland” at the Texas Book Festival on Nov. 14. “I’m incredibly proud of our show and couldn’t be more thrilled to have the opportunity to continue into Season 9!,” Breckenridge said. “Everyone on our production works so hard to make the world of Virgin River come alive. It’s truly been a gift to be here.” Added Henderson, “It’s staggering to think we are still making Virgin River after all these years and I’m delighted to get to play the role of Jack for the ninth straight season! It means the world to me that fans connect with the work we do in such a profound and passionate way—we wouldn’t be here without them all so, THANK YOU….as long as you guys want it we’ll keep making it to the best of our ability!” ‘Ebenezer’ At $1.5M In Previews; Johnny Depp Pic Seeks $40M WW Opening Jason Voorhees Returns: Steve Miner To Direct 13th Entry Of ‘Friday The 13th’ ‘Virgin River’ Gets Season 9 Renewal; Will Be Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Outlook Email, Other Services “Approaching Normal” After Massive Outage Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Stephanie Fuchs, Arianna Castoldi, Oscar Nominee Rémi Grellety Launch Autlook Collective, European Documentary Hub
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew IDFA Artistic Director Isabel Arrate Fernandez On Festival’s Competition Lineups, “Huge” Interest In Elizabeth Holmes Doc, And AI In Documentaries Cinema Eye Honors Nominations: ‘American Doctor,’ ‘You Can See Everything’ Lead With 7; ‘Time And Water,’ ‘NAZA’ Close Behind [Full List] ‘The Baddest Speechwriter Of All’ Trailer: Ben Proudfoot And Stephen Curry Combine On Portrait Of Extraordinary Adviser To MLK View All November 13, 2026 6:41am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R Stephanie Fuchs, Arianna Castoldi, Rémi Grellety of Autlook Collective Severin Wurnig/Autlook Collective EXCLUSIVE: Three of documentary’s top talents are teaming up to form Autlook Collective , a new company conceived as a European documentary hub with expertise in sales and production. Stephanie Fuchs , CEO of Autlook Filmsales, Arianna Castoldi, former head of documentary at Mediawan Rights, and two-time Oscar-nominated producer Rémi Grellety , president of Warboys Films, are partnering on the forward-looking initiative that comes as many companies in the nonfiction space are scaling back. “The team’s role is to bring the right partners to the table at the right moment,” notes a release, “with a preference for joining projects during development or production, while there is still time to shape the financing plan and prepare the film’s launch.” Production involvement will be considered on a film-by-film basis, separately from sales representation. Related Stories Documentary IDFA Artistic Director Isabel Arrate Fernandez On Festival’s Competition Lineups, “Huge” Interest In Elizabeth Holmes Doc, And AI In Documentaries Documentary IDFA Announces Competition Lineups, Adds ‘Musk’ And Elizabeth Holmes Documentary ‘You Can See Everything’ “In these specific times and challenging ones, I think we should try things a bit differently,” Grellety tells Deadline. “I think there’s value in working together — producer and sales agent — earlier on in the life of a project. So, that means that we will have the ability on… a curated amount of projects, to come in early, try and find production money for the team, whether through French or European production, but also relying on our network of potential partners around the world, including in North America. And then be a part of the production and work with the team to launch the film in the best way possible — festival strategy, sales, awards campaign.” Watch on Deadline Autlook Filmsales is based in Vienna; Autlook Collective will be headquartered in Paris. “It was important for us to be a majority French company and not just a sub office or a new division,” comments Fuchs. “The idea is it’s going to be under the Autlook umbrella, so it will be [an] expansion, but also in order to start co-producing… it makes a lot of sense to do this in [Paris],” where Grellety is based. Castoldi will lead Autlook Collective’s sales activity, working closely with Fuchs and Autlook Filmsales. “The idea is obviously to keep on doing what Autlook is doing, but also be a key partner for both universes,” Castoldi says. “Meaning that if a French documentary producer needs our help for European partners and for partners outside Europe, we can do that. But at the same time, if an American partner or someone else coming from other parts of the world needs some help [getting] into Europe and into France, we can do it as well because we all have that experience. We all have behind us at least 10, 15 years of market experience. We know the people, we have already our network… Putting all our strengths together in a moment where the market is a little bit tough, we believe it’s the solution. So, expertise and know-how all together.” The Autlook Collective trio sees opportunity where others have shrunk to defensive positions. “It is risky to expand in a time where people are scaling down,” Fuchs acknowledges. “But… I strongly believe there has always been an audience for documentaries and it’s not going to go away… I think we’re in a very unique position that we have the strong standing or we have a strong slate and I’d much rather build on that and bank on that and risk the expansion rather than believing in the, let’s say, more negative outlook.” Adds Grellety, “Difficult times makes for daring choices. I think we have to be there. I think we all believe in documentaries… And even considering the state of the world, I think it’s even more important than ever.” Elizabeth Holmes in ‘You Can See Everything’ A24 /Courtesy Everett Collection The timing of the Autlook Collective launch, in fact, may be auspicious. Documentaries have enjoyed a sudden resurgence at the box office, led by the Elizabeth Holmes-themed film You Can See Everything , which has earned $80 million in the U.S. and is just beginning to open internationally, making $1.4 million abroad to date. NAZA , the investigative documentary about Israel’s conduct of the war in Gaza, has made $13.5 million internationally, against $1.3 million in the U.S. Everest: The Other Side , directed by Oscar winners Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi and Jimmy Chin, has collected $1 million internationally and another $2 million domestically in less than two weeks of theatrical release. “When you see documentaries doing well at the box office again, and I feel like there is this new wind coming in, it’s also the perfect time [to launch],” notes Fuchs. “I believe that the audience is there, but maybe was a little bit waiting for something different in terms of stories,” Castoldi observes. “I would say the audience today is very attentive to the political situation all over the world. And the fact that some documentaries like Musk or like NAZA are bringing people to theaters, it’s a proof that there is an interest in the world around [us]; that has always been the core of documentaries.” Matthew Carey Autlook Collective will be a presence at the IDFA Forum, which runs Sunday through Wednesday (November 15-18) in Amsterdam. The new company isn’t ready to announce initial projects, but… “We are in discussions,” Fuchs allows. “I think for us all, it’s very important to not rush it and to not just sign films for the sake of signing them and starting with a big slate. It’s really the creation that’s important. But we have been starting to have conversations and starting to talk to filmmakers and to partners to also put the word out a bit like, ‘Look, that’s what we’re planning.’ Again, having the option to get on board earlier on that we currently have been doing also opens a lot more conversations that can happen.” Fuchs adds, “That’s why also IDFA’s going to be a very important moment for us to have these conversations in person when so many of, at least of the European doc community is going to be there.” Grellety will not only be representing Autlook Collective at IDFA, but the latest Oscar-contending film on which he serves as a producer, Closure , from director Michał Marczak, is also screening in the festival. His Oscar nominations came for producing I Am Not Your Negro and Soundtrack to a Coup d’Etat . The success of those documentaries speaks to a strong curatorial eye, an asset possessed by the three Autlook Collective principals. “We will build on what we know how to do, what we’ve been doing, which is a curated approach,” Grellety says of Autlook Collective. “A curated approach in selecting projects, in being there with the project over time and not just for a short moment of time. It’s this approach that is the core of what we want to do.” ‘Ebenezer’ At $1.5M In Previews; Johnny Depp Pic Seeks $40M WW Opening Jason Voorhees Returns: Steve Miner To Direct 13th Entry Of ‘Friday The 13th’ ‘Virgin River’ Gets Season 9 Renewal; Will Be Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Outlook Email, Other Services “Approaching Normal” After Massive Outage Read More About: Comments

This fandom was never about a single moment, and the Golden World Tour is how we keep it going – bringing that ‘Takedown’ energy to arenas around the world, where fans can sing, dance and help Huntr/x seal the Honmoon.” Watch on Deadline The North American tour dates in June, July and August include stops in Chicago, Atlanta, Los Angeles and Newark, New Jersey, among others. articles.title: Microsoft “Continuing To See Improvements” As Outlook Email, Other Services “Approaching Normal”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Microsoft “Continuing To See Improvements” As Outlook Email, Other Services “Approaching Normal” Microsoft Outlook Still Down In 365 Outage: Company Sees Sporadic Improvements, Though No Sustained Recovery CJ 4DPlex Pacts With B&B Theatres To Equip Single Missouri Site With 3 Premium Large Format Screens View All November 13, 2026 6:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source AFP via Getty Images Microsoft says it is getting to the other side of a massive outage that took down Outlook email , Teams videoconferencing and other services Thursday. “We’re continuing to see improvements in service availability, with email queues significantly reduced and approaching normal levels,” the company posted Friday on an update page . “Some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery as recovery continues.” Related Stories News Microsoft Outlook Still Down In 365 Outage: Company Sees Sporadic Improvements, Though No Sustained Recovery News Microsoft Offers Buyouts To 60,000, A Quarter Of Its Workforce The tech giant also said it has ruled out “malicious activity” as the cause, but it has not identified what set the problems in motion. The company’s 365 platform, which provides enterprise and business customers with an array of services, went down Thursday morning U.S. time and it soon became clear that other global regions were also affected. As of the start of 2026, Microsoft reported 450 million global customers on its 365 platform. Watch on Deadline Many eyebrows were raised by the timing of the mega-glitch shortly after the seismic ouster of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after he admitted to multiple affairs, including with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Ultimately, there did not appear to be any link between the two situations, but they only served to emphasize the degree of control tech companies have over everyday life. Banks, hospitals, government offices and schools, along with an array of corporate customers of Microsoft, saw their operations hobbled. “We’ve implemented additional mitigation measures and are restoring the remaining affected infrastructure while investigating residual service issues,” Microsoft added in the post. “We’re closely monitoring service health and validating recovery across affected connection methods to ensure sustained service stability.” The company pledged to “continue to treat this with urgency until full mitigation, and we will share a full post-incident report with root cause and defense-in-depth actions after mitigation is complete.” ‘Ebenezer’ At $1.5M In Previews; Johnny Depp Pic Seeks $40M WW Opening Jason Voorhees Returns: Steve Miner To Direct 13th Entry Of ‘Friday The 13th’ ‘Virgin River’ Gets Season 9 Renewal; Will Be Netflix’s Longest-Running Scripted Series Outlook Email, Other Services “Approaching Normal” After Massive Outage Read More About: 5 Comments

articles.title: Taylor Swift To Perform At CMA Awards For First Time In 13 Years
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise Rick Cosnett, Richard Kind & Tammy Blanchard Join Alice Eve In Indie ‘The Long Run’ ‘Avatar: Seven Havens’ Sets Book 2 Release Date At Paramount+ ‘School Spirits’ Season 4 Confirms Return Of Milo Manheim & Jennifer Tilly, Ups Maria Dizzia To Series Regular, Adds 4 To Cast View All November 13, 2026 7:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Taylor Swift Getty Images UPDATED: Taylor Swift will perform live at the 60th CMA Awards , returning to the stage for the first time since 2013, the Country Music Association announced Friday morning. A two-time CMA Entertainer of the Year, Swift is nominated this year for Single of the Year with “I Knew It, I Knew You,” marking her 26 th career CMA nomination. “I Knew It, I Knew You” was Swift’s first new song in more than 10 years to be marketed as a country song reach No. 1 on U.S. country radio. Swift first attended the show in 2006, winning her first CMA Award in 2007 (Horizon Award). She became the youngest Entertainer of the Year winner in 2009 and remains to this day the youngest artist ever to receive the honor. Related Stories News 'The View' Headed To Italy In 2027 Amid 30th Anniversary Celebration Casting Karla Souza To Star In 'Grey's Anatomy' Texas Spinoff At her last performance in 2013, Swift received the Pinnacle Award and performed “Red” with Vince Gill and Alison Krauss. Watch on Deadline She joins previously announced performers Ella Langley, who leads this year’s noms with nine, along with Cody Johnson, Miranda Lambert, Tim McGraw, Kacey Musgraves, The Red Clay Strays, Zach Top, Tucker Wetmore, Luke Combs, Vince Gill, Megan Moroney, Mumford & Sons, Chris Stapleton, Lainey Wilson and Stephen Wilson Jr. Additionally, Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Halestorm, Hardy and Marcus King will take part in a tribute to Brooks & Dunn. A salute to Dolly Parton is also planned. Hosted by Lainey Wilson for a third consecutive year, the CMA Awards airs live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday, November 18 (8-11 p.m./ET) on ABC and Disney+ and is available next day on Hulu. PREVIOUS, Nov. 10: The Country Music Association and ABC have revealed the next round of performers for The 60th Annual CMA Awards , adding Luke Combs, Vince Gill, Megan Moroney, Mumford & Sons, Chris Stapleton, Lainey Wilson and Stephen Wilson Jr. to the lineup. Also, Brothers Osborne, Luke Bryan, Halestorm, Hardy and Marcus King will come together to celebrate Brooks & Dunn, this year’s recipients of the CMA Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award. Combs is up for Album, Entertainer, and Male Vocalist of the Year this year, and Moroney returns to the CMA Awards stage earning nominations in the Female Vocalist and Song of the Year categories. Mumford & Sons will make their CMA Awards debut, joined by four-time nominee Chris Stapleton, who is up for Entertainer, Male Vocalist, Musical Event and Music Video of the Year. Stapleton will also team up with Stephen Wilson Jr., a four-time nominee this year in New Artist, Male Vocalist, Song and Music Video of the Year categories. PREVIOUS, Nov. 5: The Country Music Association and ABC have announced the first group of performers for the 60th annual CMA Awards. The initial lineup includes Ella Langley, who leads the 2026 noms with nine, along with reigning male vocalist of the year, Cody Johnson, Miranda Lambert, Tim McGraw, Kacey Musgraves, The Red Clay Strays, Zach Top and Tucker Wetmore. After taking home three CMA Awards last year, Langley leads this year’s nominees with nine, including Entertainer, Album, Female Vocalist, Musical Event and Music Video of the Year, plus two nominations each for Single and Song of the Year. Lambert notched seven nominations this year, including two for Single of the Year and one for Album of the Year as a producer, two for Musical Event of the Year, Song of the Year as a songwriter and her 19th nomination for Female Vocalist of the Year. With 70 career nominations, Lambert holds the record for the most CMA Awards nominations by a female artist. Musgraves landed five nominations this year, including Album, Song, Female Vocalist, Musical Event and Music Video of the Year. Johnson is up for four CMA Awards this year, including Entertainer, Male Vocalist, Single and Music Video of the Year. The night also will feature a tribute to Dolly Parton, honoring the country music icon. Hosted by Lainey Wilson for a third consecutive year, the CMA Awards airs live from Nashville’s Bridgestone Arena on Wednesday, November 18 (8-11 p.m./ET) on ABC and Disney+ and is available next day on Hulu. articles.title: ‘Ebenezer’ Counts $1.5M In Previews On Thursday; Johnny Depp Pic Hopes For $40M WW Opening
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Ebenezer’ Counts $1.5M In Previews On Thursday; Johnny Depp Pic Hopes For $40M WW Opening ‘The Two Popes’ Producer Mark Bauch Launches Film & TV Company One Day’s Walk ‘Ramayana: Rise Of A Legend’ Powers Past $100M+ At Global Box Office View All November 13, 2026 7:37am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Johnny Depp as Ebenezer Scrooge Paramount The first big greenlight of Paramount’s new administration since last year’s Skydance merger, Ti West’s edgy PG-13 Ebenezer , saw $1.5M in previews that began at 2PM. The movie for some time has been primed to be Johnny Depp’s comeback at the box office as far as non-franchises go, Paramount lighting that wick back at San Diego Comic-Con with the 3x Oscar nominee’s surprise method actor appearance which brought fireworks to the confab. Ebenezer heading into the weekend hopes to make at least $20M for the weekend for a No. 1 take, and another $20M from 63 markets including Australia, Brazil, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Spain and the United Kingdom. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office Books 6 New Christmas Movies Coming Out In 2026 From ‘Ebenezer’ To ‘Clashing Through The Snow’ We haven’t had many Christmas-themed family movies post Covid, so comps are hard. Ebenezer ‘s take is under the $3.7M previews of Amazon MGM Studio’s Red One which starred Dwayne Johnson and Chris Evans (that had action elements where as Ebenezer is spooky, so a hard comp there) and it’s under the $2.2M made by Universal/Illumination’s animated The Grinch back in 2018. Watch on Deadline Critics aren’t wild about the net $38M take of Charles Dickens’ A Christmas Carol at 53% Rotten. Exits last night were 4.5 stars and a 63% definite recommend on PostTrak. Note critics are never really wild about Christmas anything, i.e. Warner Bros evergreen The Polar Express (55% Rotten, which was declared a dud when it came out but grossed $329M WW), The Grinch (60% fresh), Universal’s live action Jim Carrey How the Grinch Stole Christmas (50% Rotten), Red One (29% Rotten) and even the fun and raunchy Office Christmas Party (41%). Sony opened Wednesday the Jim Caviezel action movie Ghost Soldier about a former Green Beret who protects his Wyoming neighbors against a ruthless corporation threatening their rural community. It’s booked at 2,558 theaters and opened Wednesday with previews to $2.3M and posted another $800K yesterday for a $3.1M running cume. Those who bought tickets gave it a 90% Rotten Tomatoes audience score and 4 stars on PostTrak while critics are sorry they were taken hostage at 42% Rotten. Nicholas Hoult and Pete Davidson star in ‘How To Rob A Bank’ Megan Schoenbachler/Amazon Amazon MGM Studios’ has the 87North action comedy How to Rob a Bank from the Fall Guy and Bullet Train director David Leitch which robbed $900K in previews that began yesterday at 4PM. The movie, which stars Nicholas Hoult and Zoë Kravitz, moved from its Labor Day weekend frame to here in order to get more people. It’s only expected to post in the single digits over Friday-Sunday. Critics felt that their time was robbed at 33% on Rotten Tomatoes. The pic cost a reported net $40M. One concern by some is that both Ghost Soldier and How to a Rob a Bank are going after the same male audience, though Ghost Soldier is clearly older. In terms of post Covid comps, How to Rob a Bank ‘s preview figure here is on par with Universal’s Renfield which grossed $900K in previews for an $8M opening. Pic’s blurb: Bank robbers are posting their heists on social media, causing police to chase them. Also wide this weekend at 1,206 theaters is Bleecker Street’s release of their Cannes title Victorian Psycho which is expected to do in the single digits. The Maika Monroe and Jason Isaacs movie is 75% fresh on RT. Toho and GKid s ‘ Godzilla Minus Zero ended its first global week with $73.6M we hear, which is comprised of $40.5M first week in U.S./Canada and $18.6M in Japan. We told you yesterday that Sony and Prime Focus’ Ramayana: Part 1 clicked past $100M global, the bulk of that made in India. articles.title: Christian Cousins Dies: Former Child Actor Of ‘Kindergarten Cop’, ‘Knots Landing’ Was 43
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Christian Cousins Dies: Former Child Actor Of ‘Kindergarten Cop’, ‘Knots Landing’ Was 43 KPop Demon Hunters Announces 2027 Global Arena Tour Dates In North America, U.K. & Europe Michael John Roberts Dies: ‘TripTank’, ‘BoJack Horseman’ Animator, Director & Producer Was 48 View All November 13, 2026 8:14am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Christian Cousins in 2017 and in a 1989 'Knots Landing' publicity photo Facebook/Lorimar Television Christian Cousins , the former child actor who, along with his twin brother Joseph, starred in the 1990 film Arnold Schwarzenegger comedy Kindergarten Cop , died last month following a battle with liver disease. He was 43. His death was announced by his half-brother, Jonas Roeser, on Instagram. “It’s hard to share that my brother, Christian Cousins, has passed away,” Roeser wrote on October 22. “Christian and his twin brother, Joseph ‘Joey’ Cousins, are my brothers through my biological father. They grew up in California while I was in Washington and I didn’t get to know them until I was in college. Before that, I grew up watching them on television in Knots Landing and the lead role of Dominic in Kindergarten Cop with Arnold Schwarzenegger. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News Michael John Roberts Dies: ‘TripTank’, ‘BoJack Horseman’ Animator, Director & Producer Was 48 “But those roles are only a small part of how I’ll remember Christian,” Roeser continued. “He was a character, full of passion and energy, with big stories and even bigger dreams. Christian had been very sick with liver disease. It brings me comfort to believe he is now in heaven with his mother, free from the pain he was carrying. Rest easy, Christian. I hope your soul is at rest and that you’ve found peace. You are my brother and you will be missed.” In addition to their Kindergarten Cop role, Christian and twin brother Joseph, who were born March 17, 1983, in Orange County, California, shared the roles of Bobby Gibson Ewing on 88 episodes of CBS’ primetime soap Knots Landing from 1987 to 1993. They also shared roles on Critters 3 (1991) and Eerie, Indiana (1991) and appeared as separate characters on a 1988 episode of Highway to Heaven , a 1989 TV movie called Roxanne: The Prize Pulitzer, Empty Nest (1992) and the film Twin Sitters (1995), their final credit. The young cast of ‘Kindergarten Cop’ with Arnold Schwarzenegger in a 1990 publicity photo Universal/Everett Collection Christian appeared in the 1993 TV movie A Waltons Thanksgiving Reunion as Clay Jones, a son of Judy Norton’s Mary-Ellen Walton character. In a 2020 Kindergarten Cop reunion Zoom hosted by Yahoo Entertainment and featuring the Cousins brothers as well as a surprise appearance by Schwarzenegger, Christian said that, as an adult and having retired from acting, he went into the furniture business as an executive, and also co-owned a CBD business. News of his death was first reported by the New York Post. Cousins is survived by brother Joseph Cousins and half-brother Roeser. Complete survivor information was not immediately available.
