articles.title: Pierce Brosnan & Helen Mirren Talk Toxic ‘MobLand’ Marriage, Murder, Madness & What’s Next
articles.full_text: Helen Mirren is brandishing an enormous, shiny carving knife. With a wicked little smile, she leans over her on-screen husband Pierce Brosnan , the blade hovering close to his throat. As her MobLand character Maeve Harrigan, she’s already (probably) been dropping antifreeze in her beloved hubby Conrad’s tea and, so far in the show, we’ve seen best friends bumped off, the couple’s eldest son chain-sawed to death and, in the Season 2 premiere , a full-on massacre at the dog track. This couple are, shall we say, complicated. Now, Mirren swoops in with her (actually fake) knife and rather un-murderously uses it to cut the (also fake) Sunday roast on the table. She and Brosnan are so in sync, such a perfectly dead-pan double act, that everyone in the room breaks into laughter. After all, it’s something special to be in the presence of acting royalty — Dame Mirren, who, among many epic roles, played Queen Elizabeth II in The Crown , and Pierce Brosnan, the actual former 007 . Related Stories News Dan Hicks Dies: Longtime Voice Of NBC Sports Was 64 Below The Line International Cinematographers Guild Marks 100 Years Of "Protecting Crafts, Livelihoods & Creative Voices" Mirren and Brosnan could have met on set some 46 years ago, only they never crossed paths while filming The Long Good Friday . In fact, they wouldn’t work together directly until The Thursday Murder Club , which premiered just last year, in which Mirren plays a retired MI6 agent and Brosnan a former union leader, solving crimes together in a retirement community. It was on that set that they got chatting about a script they’d both been sent about London gangsters, co-created by Guy Ritchie and Ronan Bennett , written by Jez Butterworth with Bennett and Esther Watson . “Do you like it?” Brosnan and Mirren asked each other. And that was it, they were in. Before the Season 1 shoot, the pair talked about their approach. They’d play it London mobster, with a South London-specific accent. But Ritchie had other ideas. About 20 minutes before the first shot, he told Brosnan, “Go Irish!” And Brosnan, being from Ireland, did just that. Then he called Mirren to break the news. That first season proved a massive hit for Paramount+ — one of its biggest original series debuts ever — with 26 million global viewers and 8.8 million in just the first week. WATCH: THE MOBLAND INTERVIEW WITH PIERCE BROSNAN AND HELEN MIRREN As Mirren and Brosnan sit together now post-shoot, there’s a continuous stream of storytelling and shared jokes between them, and something about the many mutual friends and much shared history between stage and screen brings a familial quality. It’s probably part of the reason we easily believe that Maeve and Conrad are forever bonded, despite, and probably because of their mutual depravity. Since Season 1 we’ve watched Maeve pour metaphorical poison in Conrad’s ear — sometimes he takes it on board, sometimes he doesn’t — while Conrad rules the roost, viciously stamping out anyone with even an imagined whiff of disloyalty. And top of his most-trusted list is Harry Da Souza (Tom Hardy), his ‘head of security’ — a title that seems to include everything from crime scene clean-up to keeping Conrad and Maeve’s psychotic grandson Eddie (Anson Boon) in check. Harry’s wife Jan (Joanne Froggatt) is none too fond of the Harrigans, but she’s stuck with them, because Harry is friends-for-life with Conrad and Maeve’s second son Kevin (Paddy Considine), whom he met in prison years back. As Season 1 rolled into Season 2 , the ante was upped again and again by Conrad’s quick temper and his emerging cognitive decline, alongside Maeve’s increasingly deranged scheming. Horrifying family secrets emerged, and even worse, vile Eddie started dating Harry’s chronically-moody teenage daughter Gina (Teddie Allen). Kevin made a (probably insane) move to take over the family, and Conrad is wondering if Maeve’s poison stash is meant for him or his illegitimate daughter Seraphina (Mandeep Dhillon). While the family holes up at their country estate in the Cotswolds, Harry’s keeping a foot in both camps, but Maeve is out for his blood, no matter what. Oh, and Jan tried to leave the whole mess behind and ended up getting catfished by a killer. But then luckily, she’s quite handy with a weapon herself… MobLand ’s Season 2 finale airs on Paramount + on November 20 th and with the show already renewed for Season 3, Brosnan and Mirren admit they’ve seen scripts for the first few Season 3 episodes. Will they tell us what’s coming? Probably not. But long may the MobLand chaos reign… DEADLINE: I went down a Reddit rabbit hole about this show. People are very, very invested. So, my first question to you both would be, what’s your take on whether these two are pure psychopaths or what drives them? What made them this way? HELEN MIRREN: We’ve talked a little bit about their backstory, haven’t we? Just between the two of us. It’s not something we particularly went into when we first started the project. When we first started, we just started, and just took every day as it came and didn’t really do much- PIERCE BROSNAN: In-depth investigation. We were shooting from the hip. MIRREN: Yes, absolutely. BROSNAN: Guy [Ritchie] gave us five scripts and we both said, “Do you like it?” And we both said yes and we jumped. MIRREN: Yes, we jumped. There was no time to have a really in-depth discussion. We didn’t have any rehearsal time or anything like that. BROSNAN: We still don’t. Pierce Brosnan as Conrad Harrigan and Helen Mirren as Maeve Harrigan In ‘MobLand’, Season 2. Luke Varley/Paramount+ MIRREN: But over time, Pierce and I have been talking a little bit about where we think this relationship started. And obviously, it started in Ireland and it logistically makes sense that it would’ve been during the time of The Troubles, so that also makes sense for their two characters. They’re creatures of their life, if you like. And I guess I don’t think they have psychopathic… Do you think they do? BROSNAN: I certainly don’t have it, no. MIRREN: What an insult. How dare you. BROSNAN: Just a lovely home in the Cotswolds, they’re a delightful family. They’re a little bit twisted here and there. MIRREN [deadpan to BROSNAN]: get rid of her because I’m very offended. [Laughs] DEADLINE: Well, there is the small matter of antifreeze poisoning and getting your son’s head chopped off with a chainsaw, but we’ll just gloss over that. BROSNAN: That’s what makes it compelling. Oh, she’s had it in for Harry ever since the beginning. I think she understands instinctively, the danger of Harry, the power of Harry… She’s not quite sure, if push came to shove, who would have final say. Helen Mirren MIRREN: Yes. And also, you don’t want to investigate these things too much. It’s not a modern psychopathic drama, it’s a Jacobean tragedy, a comedy-tragedy. And you don’t want to psychologically pull these things apart too much. It’s a sort of wonderful, mad ride. It’s like going on Magic Mountain in Disneyland. You pay your money and you take the ride. BROSNAN: Guy set the tone for it. His style of directing is, you go out, you rehearse it and you think, “Oh, that’s OK.” And he says, “OK, let’s shoot. Going in 5… going in 4.” And you shoot it. MIRREN: And bang, you’re in it. BROSNAN: You’re in it. And you might have flubbed a line, or you might have got something misplaced, but he keeps shooting, so you’re moving very fast. MIRREN: It’s a great energy. DEADLINE: Helen, in the past, you’ve said that you are lucky if you get two takes, that’s the pace this moves at. Does your stage experience feed into the way that you operate on this kind of a fast-moving set? MIRREN: I think absolutely. BROSNAN: I would say yes. We’re both from the stage. I mean, Dame Helen certainly has a wealth of stage experience. I was in quite a few good plays in the day. And this is the closest to going back to the theater for me, in the sense that you have broad scenes, rich scenes to play, you shoot them very fast. And you’re surrounded by brilliant actors. MIRREN: Great young actors. BROSNAN: So, it’s an ensemble. MIRREN: Who, with or without our personal background, they are all in it and up for it, aren’t they? I mean, maybe they’re following our guide, I don’t know, but there’s no messing around. BROSNAN: Everyone’s ready to go. Once the trap’s up, you’re in, go out there. And of course, the writing of Jez Butterworth, we always go back to that because his text is so rich and so nuanced. And like Helen says, it’s a Jacobian tragedy-comedy and there’s a wealth of humor in there to be had in the broad strokes. BROSNAN: So, it’s an ensemble. MIRREN: And a weird poetry. There is a poetry in there. BROSNAN: There is a lyrical, nuanced rhythm to his speech. MIRREN: Dark poetry. DEADLINE: I love that you mentioned Magic Mountain before, because I actually had ‘roller coaster’ written in my notes. Brosnan and Mirren in ‘MobLand’ Season 2. Luke Varley/Paramount+ MIRREN: It’s a roller coaster in the dark. DEADLINE: It’s really funny at times. Are there moments where you crack up on set? Because some of the lines you get to say are just such zingers. MIRREN: They are, they are. BROSNAN: You nailed them so brilliantly. MIRREN: So do you, Pierce. You really have a big emotional explosion so brilliantly. BROSNAN: Thank you, thank you. But I do love your tone of phrases as Maeve. DEADLINE: I liked your analogy about “the trap goes up” and everyone’s ready. It’s so pertinent because Season 2, Episode 1 at the dog track, that scene directed by Guy Ritchie is wild. Conrad’s on the back foot. I think the only thing that matters to him is whether Maeve respects him in that moment. Because she gives him a look of pride. BROSNAN: Yes. MIRREN: Yes, absolutely. We improvised. I improvised the line as we were leaving. They never used it because I think he didn’t want us exiting, but I improvised the line as we were walking out hand in hand. I said, “I f**king love you.” It’s like, “At last he’s back. My man, I’ve got my man.” Tom Hardy as Harry Da Souza and Paddy Considine as Kevin Harrigan in ‘MobLand’, season 2. Luke Varley/Paramount+ BROSNAN: Conrad needs Maeve. He needs Maeve and they both need each other. They’re joined at the hip in this kind of cataclysmic life of theirs. And Guy revels in it. I mean, that was a fabulous day. MIRREN: That was a great day, wasn’t it? So fun, it was fantastic. BROSNAN: We came back from lunch on that particular day and Guy said to Helen and I, “Well, I’m just going to stand over there. I want to show you what you’re going to do.” I was like, “OK.” We were standing there with all the lads, all the bad guys. And Guy came in and played Helen, and then he played me and started shooting everybody. He was blocking the scene for us. DEADLINE: How was he at playing you Helen? MIRREN: Well, it was a Bob the Builder version of Maeve. BROSNAN: He’s always there in his braces [suspenders]. Ga-da, ga-da, ga-da [shooting noises] He went all around the room, ga-da, ga-da, ga-da. MIRREN: He loved it. You could tell he was dying to be in it himself. DEADLINE: There was a recent event in London about the show, and there was some talk that somebody is going to challenge Harry in Season 3. Now, why do I think that might be Maeve? Because she just would love to see him dead. MIRREN: Oh, she’s had it in for Harry ever since the beginning. I think she understands instinctively, the danger of Harry, the power of Harry, and the danger of him. She’s not quite sure, if push came to shove, who would have final say, whether it be with Conrad or with the family in general. And I think although he’s unbelievably valuable to the family, sometimes you have to be aware of giving people too much power within your world. Do you know what I mean? Pierce Brosnan as Conrad Harrigan in ‘MobLand’ season 2. Luke Varley/Paramount+ BROSNAN: Oh, yeah. As Conrad, I know very much what you mean. MIRREN: They can take over. Anyway, we’ll see where that goes. We don’t know. It’s a great, fabulous adventure, the whole thing, so we absolutely have no idea where we’re going. BROSNAN: We have the first three episodes of the third season, which is 10 episodes. DEADLINE: Do you often get the script and go, “Will the bullet be between my eyes this time?” MIRREN: “Am I still alive at the end?” All the time. DEADLINE: What happens in Season 2 in Ireland with Eddie and Gina is such a Maeve-coded twisted mess. Do we think Conrad knows what really went on, or is he closing his eyes to it? BROSNAN: It’s six of one and a half a dozen of the other. And because his mental faculty is somewhat diminishing here, and I have no idea where Jez is going to take this road. And I haven’t asked him. I don’t want to know, really. But at the same time, there’s ways of playing it where you as the actor know, and you as Conrad know what’s going on around you. You have to be aware. It’s basically Maeve. As much as I love her, she is lethal. Helen Mirren as Maeve Harrigan in ‘MobLand’ Season 2. Luke Varley/Paramount+ DEADLINE: Could she ever do anything bad enough to break them up? MIRREN: Yes. I think there is a point at which Conrad would cut her off, cut her out. Although she’s done heinous things in and around the family, I don’t know, actually. I don’t know, I don’t really want to talk about that. BROSNAN: It’s best not to know. MIRREN: Yes, play it as it comes. BROSNAN: You really can’t turn the corner until you get there. DEADLINE: My thought when Conrad went to the neurologist and they said, “Your impulse control is depleted,” I thought, maybe it was always like this.” MIRREN: It’s so great to watch Pierce do those scenes. You know it’s coming, because obviously, you’ve read the script and you learned the lines and now we’re in the scene. And I love it when Pierce… It’s like watching this volcano erupt. It’s like Mount Etna erupting and you know it’s coming. I love sitting in that living room and thinking, oh, Pierce is going to erupt. It’s going to be so fantastic. And it always is. He just commands it, it’s fabulous to watch. Joanne Froggatt as Jan Da Souza and Tom Hardy as Harry Da Souza In ‘MobLand’ Season 2 Paramount+ DEADLINE : I listened to a podcast with you Helen where you talked about how sometimes, playing a character, you would go into it imagining they were drunk. Is that a factor with Maeve? MIRREN: Absolutely. And luckily she normally is drunk all the time. BROSNAN: Sauced. It’s a good one. MIRREN: It’s liberating. BROSNAN: Yeah, it is liberating if you feel like you’re tanked up as the character in that particular scene. It gives you a rhythm, and it gives you a kind of safe place to pick your way through the scene, as it were. MIRREN: Yes, it just opens up all kinds of possibilities. When you’re drunk, you don’t care about anything. The second season was tough because the scripts were coming in late and everyone was under the gun… but we get on really well. I mean, Helen and I were cast, and then it was always going to be, “Who’s playing Harry? Who’s it going to be?” When Tom Hardy came onto the stage, we couldn’t be happier. Pierce Brosnan BROSNAN: They’re animals. I mean, Conrad is an animal. He’s this kind of bull of a man who’s not quite in control. MIRREN: A bull or panther? BROSNAN: Panthers are very sleek. MIRREN: Yeah, maybe he’s more bull. But he’s a little more adroit than a bull. Although bulls in the ring are incredibly adroit, actually, when you watch them in a bullfight. They’re incredible. BROSNAN: They’re very nimble. Do you have an image for Maeve? When we were doing The Thursday Murder Club and you and I both said, “Well, let’s do this,” we were sitting there one morning, having a cup of tea. You were on your laptop and you said, “This is what I’m thinking about for Maeve.” And Helen opened up her laptop and there was this photograph of this Australian monster. MIRREN: A blonde lady, yes. BROSNAN: A blonde lady, yeah. With peroxide blonde, white hair. MIRREN: Yes, white hair. Nails black, all in black otherwise. BROSNAN: I remember thinking, “Oh my god, she’s got her character already. What am I going to do? What am I going to do?” Helen Mirren as Maeve Harrigan and Pierce Brosnan as Conrad Harrigan In ‘MobLand’, Season 2. Luke Varley/Paramount+ DEADLINE: I was going to ask you, actually, did either of you look at real-life criminals as some kind of inspiration, or even fictional criminals? BROSNAN: You did. MIRREN: I did, yes. A little bit. But the thing is to… It’s kind of useful, but really what you do is invent there and then on the spot, and allow, as Pierce said, allow the text to guide you, lead you, inspire you. That’s your jumping off of this, really, rather than some sort of theoretical study of the criminal mind. We’re not in that world. It’s not a documentary, docudrama, of any sort of… You’re in the world of imagination, a kind of excessive gothic world. And I think honestly, that’s the great entertainment of it. And it’s undoubtedly entertaining. BROSNAN: Absolutely, utterly, yes. And they’re compelling characters and everyone likes to play. Everyone likes to give performance. It is one of those shows where you can give a performance, play a performance. MIRREN: And how strong all the characters are as well. I love how strong all the women are. All the female characters have real agency, real energy, real complication. None of them are there just as a sort of cipher of any sort. And likewise, all the male characters. The chaps, Paul [Emmett J. Scanlan]’s character. Obviously, Anson’s character. They’re all such individual, interesting characters on their own. None of them are fillers at all. DEADLINE: Paul, he’s such a character, but he could have just been just some minor, lackey person, given a different writer. MIRREN: Yes. And I think he’s going to really appear more and more. BROSNAN: Absolutely. He’s loved, he’s adored. Top man. DEADLINE: When there were mutterings that Tom Hardy wouldn’t come back for Season 3 due to some rumored disagreements, both of you spoke up in support of him on social media. So, it’s obviously a close-knit cast? BROSNAN: Very much so. That was a real storm in a teacup. It really blindsided me when I read the reports. I thought, “What the heck is going on?” Because the second season was tough because the scripts were coming in late and everyone was under the gun. We had a first season which is really tight and wonderful and magnificent and fresh and new. It’s sometimes hard to really just keep it on track, but we get on really well. I mean, Helen and I were cast, and then it was always going to be, “Who’s playing Harry? Who’s it going to be?” When Tom Hardy came onto the stage, we couldn’t be happier. DEADLINE: It’s hard to imagine anyone else in that role. MIRREN: No, no, no. Absolutely not. DEADLINE: As Harry he has this stillness and it’s in great contrast to the chaos around him. Did you know he was going to play it like that? MIRREN: No, no. That is his incredible power. It’s spellbinding. I can’t think of the right way to put it, but backwards and coming forwards. The stillness of Tom, the power of Tom is fantastic. And it’s so great against Maeve, Conrad, Eddie, Seraphina, who are all such big, big, mad characters. DEADLINE: Looking forward, at the end of Season 2 and into Season 3, what’s it going to take to keep these two at top of the power dynamic in the family? Because it is a rocky situation right now. MIRREN: Well, money, I guess. BROSNAN: Money, love prevails. MIRREN: It’s not just money, is it? It’s power. BROSNAN: It’s power, the lust for power. And fear of dying. You don’t want to die. Mortality is circling the wagons here. And they know about death. MIRREN: They’re saying, “Down to death.” Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Patrick Hoerl’s Autentic Buys Gedeon Media Group’s Assets & Launches Studio
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Jeff Goldblum To Narrate Cliburn Piano Competition Doc Series ‘Exit Stage Right’ ‘Line Of Duty’: Arnott, Fleming & Hastings Return To Service In First Look At Season 7 Of BBC’s Record-Setting Cop Drama Gang Dong-won & Kim Go-eun To Lead Netflix Korea Romance-Action Period Drama ‘The Twilight Between Us’ From Kim Won-suk View All November 12, 2026 8:59am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Patrick Hoerl Autentic Patrick Hoerl’s German factual specialist Autentic has acquired the assets of Gedeon Media Group (GMG), and is launching a studios business off the back of the deal. GMG was forced into judicial liquidation earlier this year by a French Commercial Court after running into financial difficulties, with Autentic among those expressing interests in a rescue deal. Autentic has now won out. The Munich-based has now established Gedeon Studios as a French production and distribution subsidiary, with GMG’s 3,000-hour catalog being subsumed into Autentic Distribution and a digital channels division going into Autentic’s channel management unit. Related Stories Executives Tubi CEO Anjali Sud, Roku Media President Charlie Collier Leaving The Fold As Fox Sets Exec Team After Roku Close News Good News Network Sold To Group Including Whalar Co-Founder James Street The asset deal includes Gedeon Programmes, Docland Yard and MC4. Gedeon filed was placed in liquidation in August, with the program units allowed to continue trading while a buyer was sought and sales arm Terranoa shuttered immediately. Watch on Deadline Gedeon Studios will oversee all ongoing GMG productions and project development, including approximately 25 hours of television programming currently in production and two feature-length documentaries. A seven-member team from the existing organization will join the new business. This includes senior producers Laurence Favreau, Valérie Guerin and Coraline Roch and Head of Development Mina Cuche. Carine Nonnenmacher, one of GMG’s senior producers, will lead the new studio, with GMG’s founder and former President, Stéphane Millière, working closely with the new company as Senior Consultant, Programme Development. Gedeon was founded back in 1996 with the creation of Gedeon Programmes, and went on to become one of France’s most well-known factual production companies and the winner of more than 500 international awards for its docs in genres such as science, archaeology, history, culture and heritage. The likes of the BBC, CCTV, National Geographic, PBS, NHK, RADIO Canada, RAI, RTS, RTVE, SBS, SVT and ZDF have all counted themselves as buyers. Autentic has a similar reputation in Germany, well established in factual genre. “With Gedeon Studios in Paris and Autentic in Munich, we will have teams in the two biggest markets in Europe,” said Patrick Hoerl, Managing Director at Autentic. “By combining the expertise of both companies, and using significant synergies in the monetization of content, will make us more resilient in the current, challenging market environment. “Over more than three decades, Stéphane Millière and the Gedeon team have built an extraordinary legacy, establishing the company as one of the most respected names in factual production. We are proud to continue that journey together with the team in France, preserving valuable expertise and creative excellence while laying the foundation for the next phase of growth.” Millière added he was “very pleased that Autentic is taking over the assets of the Gedeon Group through a new company that will continue to build on the work of the outstanding editorial team that has worked alongside me to develop the brand, carry forward ongoing projects and distribute the catalogue established over the past 30 years.” “This alliance between two strong brands and two talented teams further strengthens the potential of Autentic for the years to come. I have the greatest respect for Patrick Hoerl, who has always been a passionate advocate for the documentary genre. I am delighted that he will become President of this new Gedeon.” Jensen Huang Is Out As Nvidia CEO Amid Affair Scandal; Successor Sought Eddie Murphy & Ama Qamata Voicing Animated Fantasy Movie ‘M’Tali’ ‘Focker-In-Law’ Premiere Pics: Grande, De Niro, Feldstein & More Breton Replaced As Federation Studios Prez; Montefiore Ups Stake Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Paramount+ Greenlights Damian Lewis-Starring Premier League Comedy Series ‘Day 1s’ From Matthew Vaughn, Cristiano Ronaldo & Thierry Henry
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max BBC Boss Matt Brittin & Industry Leaders Set To Attend Culture Secretary’s Emergency Meeting Next Week Following Brand & Walliams Scandals Barbara Broccoli Appointed President Of UK’s National Film & Television School Lionel Uzan Succeeding Pascal Breton As President Of Federation Studios; Montefiore Ups Stake View All November 12, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L to R: Cristiano Ronaldo, Damian Lewis, Matthew Vaughn, Thierry Henry Ian Gavan/Getty, Steve Gullick, Ilya S. Savenok/Getty, Courtesy Thierry Henry A sports comedy series combining the unlikely foursome of Damian Lewis , Cristiano Ronaldo , Matthew Vaughn and Thierry Henry has found a home at Paramount+ . In one of its first big greenlights since the Skydance merger, the streamer has made a straight-to-series order for Day 1s , which tells of a young soccer player playing for Brentford FC in the UK’s Premier League. Day 1s is the first TV project from Ronaldo and Kingsman director Vaughn’s UR-Marv Studios and counts another soccer superstar, Henry, amongst its EPs. Producer Darren Dein conceived of the idea, Vaughn has directed the pilot and BAFTA-winner Dan Mazer ( Borat ) is set to showrun. Related Stories News Pierce Brosnan & Helen Mirren Talk Toxic 'MobLand' Marriage, Murder, Madness & What's Next News Sterling K. Brown To Narrate 'The Elite: Army Rangers' Docuseries For Paramount+ While in development, the show was reported to be about a soccer agent but the 10-parter in fact follows a gifted young player who achieves his dream of playing in the Premier League, bringing along his friends who stood by him long before the money, fame and success – his Day 1s. Watch on Deadline The project was the first TV show set at UR-Marv but it’s been a busy week for Ronaldo and Vaughn. We revealed late last week that their irreverent action-comedy Stuntnuts starring Chris Hemsworth and Sam Rockwell would be heading to the American Film Market. Alongside UR-Marv, producers on Day 1s are Dein’s DoubleD Sports and Kris Thykier ’s Archery Pictures . Day 1s is one of the first big bets placed by the new Paramount+ regime since the Skydance merger. Vaughn thanked the likes of Casey Bloys, Sarah Aubrey and Amy Gravitt for taking a chance on Day 1s. “It’s the perfect project for Cristiano and I to start our company with – and to say he is a friend and a partner is a true honour,” he added. “I’m sure the man who has broken every record in football will soon be doing the same in film and TV.” Ronaldo said: “I’ve spent my entire life in football, and I know that some of the most powerful stories happen away from the pitch. Football is about dreams, ambition, loyalty, sacrifice and the people who believe in you from day one. That’s what makes Day 1s special. As a producer, I’m proud to help bring a different side of the game to life, through a story that I believe can connect with audiences far beyond football. To take this first journey in the industry alongside my partner and friend Matthew Vaughn and having a superb former player and a great person like Thierry Henry on board makes this all even more special.” The series will be executive produced by Vaughn, Dein, Ronaldo, Henry and Lewis, along with Doug Ellin, Mazer and Thykier ( Hijack ). Vaughn is repped by WME and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole; Henry is repped by DoubleD Sports; Mazer is repped by CAA, LBI Entertainment and Davis Law Group; Thykier is repped by Del Shaw Moonves Tanaka Finkelstein Lezcano Bobb & Dang; and Lewis is repped by Markham, Froggatt & Irwin and Range Media Partners. articles.title: Lucasfilm Sets ‘Star Wars: A New Hope’ IMAX 70mm Re-Release & New Behind-The-Scenes Doc ‘The Hero Awakens’ For 50th Anniversary Celebrations
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Eddie Murphy & Ama Qamata Voicing Animated Fantasy Movie ‘M’Tali: The Everlasting Spring’ ‘Soul Patrol’: J.M. Harper On Exploring The Complex Legacy Of The First All-Black U.S. Special Ops Team In Vietnam Ryūsuke Hamaguchi’s ‘All Of A Sudden’ To Open AFI Silver’s 2026 European Union Film Showcase — Full Lineup View All November 12, 2026 9:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source From left: Mark Hamill, Carrie Fisher and Harrison Ford in 'Star Wars' aka 'Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope' (1977) Everett Lucasfilm and Disney have restored the original Star Wars (1977) and will release the film in multiple formats, including IMAX 70mm, as part of the franchise’s 50th anniversary celebrations. The re-release is among several events Lucasfilm and Disney announced this afternoon for next year’s anniversary celebrations. Screenings of the original 1977 version of Star Wars will begin on February 19. In addition to the IMAX 70mm screenings, the film will also be presented in Digital IMAX, Digital Cinema, 70mm, 35mm, and 4DX. Related Stories News 'Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope' To Play At Cosm As Disney Teams With Shared Reality Firm News Adam Driver Says No More Kylo Ren: 'Star Wars' "Ship Has Sailed" On May 4th, 2027, Lucasfilm will release a new behind-the-scenes documentary, The Hero Awakens , from filmmaker R.J. Cutler on Disney+. The film is said to detail the making of Star Wars . The company’s synopsis reads: “This film will be a unique treat for fans as it exclusively features archival footage and audio captured during and around the making of the historic film in 1977.” The Hero Awakens is produced by Lucasfilm, Cutler and This Machine, and Kennedy/Marshall. Watch on Deadline 2027 Star Wars events already on the calendar include Shawn Levy’s Star Wars : Starfighter , which will be released on May 28. Season 2 of Ahsoka will premiere January 20, 2027. Star Wars Celebration will take place on April 1-4 in Los Angeles. “It is incredibly special to mark the 50th anniversary by returning the original version of Star Wars to theaters so audiences can experience this part of film history on the big screen,” Lucasfilm Co-President Lynwen Brennan said in a statement. “We look forward to celebrating with our fans all year long—from the releases of ‘Ahsoka’ and ‘ Star Wars: Starfighter’ to exclusive merchandise, new publishing stories, unforgettable experiences and interactive games. articles.title: Sophie Nélisse Gives ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 Update: “I Actually Just Wrapped”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn PGA Create Lab Announces 2026 Fellows Elijah Wood Says “Muscle Memory” Kicked In Playing Frodo On ‘The Hunt For Gollum’ Set ‘VisionQuest’ Teases Surprise ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Character Return In Post-Credits Scene View All November 12, 2026 9:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sophie Nélisse attends Paramount+'s 'Yellowjackets' Season 4 premiere on Nov. 11, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Katie Flores/PMC With two seasons and a movie on deck, Sophie Nélisse has wrapped on her Heated Rivalry movie star character. The actress, who plays Rose Landry on the Crave / HBO Max series, told Deadline that she finished filming her scenes for Season 2 just two days before walking the red carpet for Yellowjackets ‘ final season, premiering Nov. 20 on Paramount+ with Premium Plan. “We have started filming Season 2,” Nélisse noted. “I actually just wrapped the day before yesterday, I wrapped two days ago.” Related Stories News What To Expect For ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2: Everything We Know So Far Trailers ‘Yellowjackets’ Trailer: The Team Adjusts To Civilization With Creepy Alanis Morissette Soundtrack In Final Season The update came after Deadline revealed that, following the show’s Season 2 renewal , series creator Jacob Tierney is filming two seasons and a Christmas movie , back-to-back. Watch on Deadline With the immense success of the show, based on Rachel Reid’s Game Changer novels, Heated Rivalry has received critical acclaim and became HBO Max’s top acquired scripted series ever with more than 10.6 million US viewers in two months. Nélisse feels “really grateful” to be apart of that story, given its impact on LGBTQ audiences. Sophie Nélisse on filming ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 and seeing how much viewers have been impacted by and resonate with the series pic.twitter.com/2Dhb2WcnNP — Deadline (@DEADLINE) November 12, 2026 “I don’t think none of us could have predicted this kind of success, but I couldn’t be happier because it’s one of those projects that people were in it truly for the right reasons,” she explained. “And they poured all their hearts and souls into it because they truly believed in the story, in the craft, in Jacob’s vision. “And there’s just this genuineness on set, and I think that that really transpired on screen. And I think that’s why it’s knowing the success that it’s knowing, because the connections are real between every character. And because it’s a story that I think needed to be told for so long.” Nélisse continued, “Yes, I’m so happy for Hudson [Williams] and Connor [Storrie], but also, it feels really special to be part of a show that resonates so well with people on such a deep level. Seeing testimonies of people coming out or finally being able to talk about a story that they’ve never been able to voice before, it feels like the work that you’re doing actually has a real impact. And I think that’s something that I feel really grateful to be a part of.” Sophie Nélisse as Rose Landry and Hudson Williams as Shane Hollander in ‘Heated Rivalry’ With Rachel Reid’s Game Changer novel The Long Game serving as the basis for Season 2 of Heated Rivalry , production began on the sophomore season of Tierney’s Crave Original series adaptation in Canada in August. Deadline previously reported that Justice Smith, Charlie Gillespie, Daniel Diemer, Shaheen Jafargholi, Emily Hampshire, Edvin Ryding, Robert Naylor, Sabrina Jalees, Priyanka, Brendan Morgan, David Tomlinson, Gerry Dee, Michelle Mylett, Lauren Chan and Nick Stahl have been cast in Season 2 , which is set to premiere in spring 2027. articles.title: ‘Ebenezer’ Review: Johnny Depp Blissfully Goes All Scrooge In Ti West’s New Horror-Flavored Take On Dickens Christmas Classic
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Pete Hammond Pete Hammond Awards Columnist/Chief Film Critic @DeadlinePete More Stories By Pete ‘Ebenezer’ Review: Johnny Depp Blissfully Goes All Scrooge In Ti West’s New Horror-Flavored Take On Dickens Christmas Classic Robert Pattinson To Receive 40th Annual American Cinematheque Award ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Review: Oscar Winner Takashi Yamazaki’s Vision Of Japan’s Most Iconic Monster Is Back Bigger Than Ever Battling An Even Deadlier Foe View All November 12, 2026 9:04am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Johnny Depp in Ebenezer from Paramount Pictures. Paramount Pictures There have been countless iterations on the Charles Dickens yuletide classic, “A Christmas Carol” which was first birthed to the world as a novella in 1843, but has been a favorite of Hollywood for nearly a century. Actors have warmed to the bah humbug of it all in various takes beginning with Reginald Owen in 1938’s A Christmas Carol to perhaps still the best, Alastair Sim in the 1951 version. George C. Scott and Patrick Stewart did well-regarded TV movies. Bill Murray did a contemporary comedic version with Scrooged. Albert Finney turned it all into a big screen musical in 1970. Even Kermit and Miss Piggy jumped on board with The Muppet Christmas Carol, and no less than Mr. Magoo in the evergreen (and personal favorite) Mr. Magoo’s Christmas Carol. In 2017 Christopher Plummer even took a whirl with Scrooge in the clever and wonderful biopic, The Man Who Invented Christmas which was all about Dickens writing the time honored tale. Related Stories News Daisy Ridley, Darren Criss, Travis Fimmel & Judy Greer Join Catherine Zeta-Jones In Tate Taylor's Marriage Counselor Thriller 'Cupid'; Filming Underway -- AFM News Johnny Depp & Ti West Land In A Chilly London For 'Ebenezer' Global Premiere It seems inevitable though that modern day master of all disguises, Johnny Depp would get a turn at bat, and in the latest version, Ebenezer , he has done just that. To say it is a perfect fit for Depp would be an understatement as he finds his own unique way into the role, but in a bit of a twist manages to unearth more humanity in Ebenezer Scrooge than previous versions that saved all that for the inevitable happy ending. Here, insufferable as he can be, this Scrooge allows us to have more empathy for the man as his own past is revealed as the source of his discontent. The other wrinkle with this version is brought by its director, Ti West , previously known as a horrormeister with the trilogy of X, Pearl, and MaXXXine , but it turns out he is a lifelong fan of the Dickens tale and found it ripe for more emphasis on its horror aspects built in with the infamous ghosts so crucial to the story. After all, the original title of the novella was “A Christmas Carol. In Prose. Being A Ghost Story At Christmas”. Paramount’s campaign for the movie also leans into this with the ad line: “If You Think You Know His Story, Think Again”. Fear not though, we do know the story and this is still all very PG13 and not as bloodletting as the filmmaker’s past filmography. West , and his screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern, have too much reverance for what Dickens hath wrought to mess around with the bones of the tale we know all too well. Paramount’s marketing department wants us to believe this is all new but it really isn’t for the most part, just an excuse for Depp to play in the sandbox. Watch on Deadline Ebenezer, with fine period production design by Eve Stewart and darkly lit cinematography from Checco Varese, perfectly sets the tone as we meet Ebenezer Scrooge and his even more greedy business partner Jacob Marley (an ideal Ian McKellen ), just before Marley succumbs to a heart attack. It is Christmas Eve and neither owner was all too swell to loyal but beaten-down employee Bob Cratchit (an effective Rupert Grint ) who is anxious to spend time with his family including wife Clara ( Daisy Ridley ) and young son Tiny Tim (Freddie Lee Grey). There is also a visit from Christmas-loving nephew Fred (Sam Claflin) who can’t understand his uncle’s disdain for the holiday and what it really means. As Scrooge retires for the night, the fireworks begin, first with a view from down under from the late not-so-great Marley with a foreboding warning. Then we have a visit from the Ghost Of Christmas Past (a spirited Andrea Riseborough ) who takes him back (Arthur Conti is the younger Ebenezer) to his roots growing up, to his own family life, and most notably to his one and only true love Belle (Ellie Bamber) in a relationship doomed to failure as his early inclination for money over love seems to take hold. Here we see the human being, flawed but recognizable, taking his first wrong turn. Cue the Ghost Of Christmas Present (a dynamic turn from Severance Emmy winner Tramell Tillman ) who really turns on the gas to show Scrooge a miserable world, including for the Cratchit clan involving death and despair. West finds his deepest dive into the tropes of horror with this sequence, about as dark as any version of A Christmas Carol can get. And then it gets even darker with the Ghost Of Christmas Future (creature actor Robert Strange) who is so imposing he needs to say nothing, just show what will become of Ebenezer – and it is not pretty. It is no spoiler to reveal how it all works out and Depp clearly is having a blast playing it to the hilt. Fortunately the audience will walk out with their Christmas spirit (if not the spirits) intact. I am not sure the world needed yet another dance with Dickens and Scrooge. As mentioned at the top of this review there is plenty to savor from the cinema of Christmases Past that hold up quite nicely to revisit year after year after year, but I have to say it is satisfying to see Depp give it a go. After a very rough patch in his life and career, just like Ebenezer Scrooge, this gifted actor is seeing the light again. Producer is Emma Watts. From co-creators Dan Levy and Rachel Sennott, Big Mistakes is a comedic family saga within a high-stakes crime thriller. It follows Nicky (Levy) and Morgan (Taylor Ortega), two deeply incapable siblings who are in over their heads when a misguided theft for their dying grandmother accidentally pulls them into the world of organized crime. Blackmailed into increasingly dangerous assignments, they clumsily fail upwards, sinking deeper into chaos they’re ill-equipped to handle.
