articles.title: AI Audio Startup ElevenLabs Expands Nvidia Collaboration Amid CEO Jensen Huang’s Affair Scandal
articles.full_text: × Nov 11, 2026 8:00am PT AI Audio Startup ElevenLabs Expands Nvidia Collaboration Amid CEO Jensen Huang’s Affair Scandal By Corbin Bolies Plus Icon Corbin Bolies Latest Nvidia Stock and AI World Rocked by CEO Jensen Huang’s Affair With Alleged Chinese Spy 22 hours ago AI Takes Center Stage at Tech-Forward AFM With Innovation Hub and AFM House Expansion 1 day ago Elvis Music Owners, Eminem Publisher File Sprawling New Lawsuits Against AI Music Generator Suno: ‘The Next Elvis Won’t Pick Up a Guitar’ 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images ElevenLabs is keeping its yearslong Nvidia partnership strong, no matter the national-security chaos enveloping the chipmaker’s CEO . The AI audio startup said on Wednesday during its New York Summit it would expand its partnership with Nvidia to power its suite of voice agents, dubbed ElevenAgents, with the tech provider’s Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, its latest open model that helps power AI agents’ understanding of workflows and human reasoning. Some of the expanded features for the agents unveiled on Wednesday include memory features, routines and helping users architect new agents. Related Stories Invercine, Gema Films and Gaman Cine, Top Producers on Latin America’s Film-TV Scene, Bring to Market New Productions Alex de la Iglesia on His Upcoming Chilean Shoot ‘The Misunderstanding’: ‘Reality Has Become My Parallel World’ The company is also employing Nvidia’s Vera Rubin architecture to provide the compute required for the deployment of its AI agents, capacity the company said would help support large-scale demands from businesses. Some of those demands include powering the voice agents used for Centralna e-Rejestracja, the appointment-making platform within Poland’s national online health system, and the companies said they wanted to make more voice agents available to governments worldwide with Nvidia’s AI architecture. The two are also trying to bring such agents to robots. The expanded collaboration, CEO Mati Staniszewski said in a statement, was necessary as “voice agents become critical infrastructure.” “By combining our audio models and agents, with Nvidia’s LLMs, accelerated computing and security stack, we’re giving enterprises and governments the platform they need to deploy voice agents at massive scale,” Staniszewski said. “Nvidia has been a superb partner to us, and we’re excited to keep building together.” The two companies have been partners since 2022, with ElevenLabs using Nvidia’s GPUs to power its first text-to-speech model and Nvidia using ElevenLabs to create voiceovers for videos at company events. Nvidia last year became an ElevenLabs investor, complete with a splashy produced video posted to Staniszewski’s LinkedIn page. ElevenLabs completed a $300 million employee tender offer in September that valued the company at $22 billion, doubling the $11 billion valuation it reached in February after a funding round. But the expansion comes as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has become enveloped in a national-security scandal over his affair with a Chinese tech executive allegedly recruited by China to spy on Huang and learn more about the company’s AI technology. Huang, who pulled out of ElevenLabs’ summit this week, is currently under investigation by Nvidia’s board of directors and the FBI over the relationship. He will continue leading the company throughout the inquiries. “For decades we adapted to computers — keyboards, screens, menus. Now computers are learning to speak our language,” Huang said in a statement about the ElevenLabs partnership. “With Nvidia Nemotron reasoning inside ElevenAgents and Nvidia accelerated computing powering large-scale deployments, enterprises and governments can run voice agents securely at national scale — and make talking the fastest way to get things done.” ‘Logan’ Star Dafne Keen Says ‘I Was Offered Cocaine’ as an 11-Year-Old in Hollywood and Hugh Jackman ‘Made Sure No One Abused My Hours’ on Set Loading comments...

articles.title: Skydance Succession: As David Ellison Sets His Team, Heads Are Rolling as Hollywood Finds Out Who’s Really in Charge
articles.full_text: Illustration by Will Hooks Of all the things keeping David Ellison up at night, the countdown to 2028 may be the most pressing. At least that’s what many media observers and Hollywood insiders believe. Ellison’s anxiety, they say, isn’t fueled by the forthcoming presidential election or the Olympic Games that will descend on Los Angeles, where Ellison now owns two iconic studio lots. Instead, his agita is arising from the 8 movies he still needs to acquire or produce in 2028 to reach the magic number of 30 — that’s the benchmark Skydance pledged to meet annually in order to close the $111 billion acquisition that made his company a content behemoth. Related Stories Sanfic Mórbido Lab Lineup Ranges From an LGBTQ Alien Monster Comedy to a Mapuche Parable, Extreme Horror and Cold War Sci-Fi ‘The Cry of Serankwa,’ an Indigenous Eco-Thriller and Triple Sanfic Industria Award Winner, Strikes Distribution Deal for Latin America Between Paramount and Warner Bros. Pictures, 22 films have been dated for 2028 so far. A large number of those — like “Gremlins 3,” Baz Luhrmann’s rumored Joan of Arc biopic and an untitled movie from the Duffer brothers — have yet to start production. And, of course, Hollywood is keeping a close watch on how the new regime handles the urgent task of closing deals with Margot Robbie and Greta Gerwig for a “ Barbie ” follow-up. Zohar Lazar Despite Skydance’s other pledge — to streamline costs via cutting-edge technology — feature films remain one of the most expensive gambles in the business (and that’s if audiences respond). The challenge before Ellison and his team is to churn out hits fast — not just to prove their hotly debated merger will be viable in the long run but to generate the cash needed to pay down the combined company’s staggering $80 billion debt. Five weeks in, if Team Ellison is losing sleep about the operational challenges ahead, it’s not letting that on to the media. “People are viewing our $30 billion-plus content spend as an expense, but content is our asset,” Skydance chief financial officer Dennis Cinelli told Variety , speaking ahead of the company’s third-quarter earnings report. “Whether it’s for our theatrical or TV business, both of our streaming platforms, third-party sales, the networks portfolio — we’re investing in content because it has proved tremendously valuable. We’re confident we can drive growth and increase profitability and cash flow.” On Nov. 9, as Skydance unveiled its first quarterly earnings report as a combined company, leadership said a big push will come in early 2027 to offer consumers a bundle of the streaming services now under the Skydance roof: HBO Max and Paramount+. The price will come at a competitive discount designed to allow Skydance to gain market share among subscribers, one source says. Skydance plans to offer a fully integrated service that puts both brands on a single platform — which will make it easier for the company to keep viewers moving around its streaming universe — by 2029. There is much speculation that the company will eventually retire the Paramount+ moniker, given that HBO is the more powerful consumer brand. Meanwhile, Skydance is touting the power of its portfolio: A combined 205-million streaming subscribers in more than 100 global territories, a library of roughly 15,000 films and more than 100,000 hours of TV series. Hollywood’s new colossus has a content library larger than its studio rivals’ by a significant factor, even if its stewards change, as James Gunn and Peter Safran found out the hard way this week. (The DC Studios chiefs made it just five weeks into the Skydance regime before Ellison announced on earnings day that he would replace the pair with producer Jeremy Latcham, an early architect of Marvel Studios.) Superman, Batman and many other characters in the Skydance vault represent a treasure trove of the kind of IP that can yield new adaptations and spinoffs for decades. The chance to buy Warner Bros.’ vault was so attractive that last year even Netflix, the leader in global streaming, was driven to give up its build-not-buy philosophy regarding big acquisitions to chase Warner Bros. and HBO — until Ellison stuck his foot in the door and refused to leave without a deal. Streaming is the engine of the future for Skydance. But in the short term, the company’s fate will be determined by that of its linear cable channels. With the merger, Skydance hasn’t just doubled down on this sector — it has tripled down; Skydance has by far the industry’s collection of linear cable channels. Its TV portfolio is anchored by CBS and spans some 55 cable networks, including CNN, TNT, TBS, Cartoon Network, TCM, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central, BET, Discovery, TLC, Food Network and HGTV. But the traditional business of cable television is deteriorating; subscribers are slowly but surely giving up on linear cable services in favor of streaming platforms. The erosion of once-reliable cable TV profits has bedeviled Hollywood’s majors for more than a decade and has been a catalyst for the latest round of merger mania. As was the case for Paramount and WBD when they were separate companies, the enlarged Skydance remains heavily dependent on linear TV for cash flow and profits — and the cable and satellite biz remains a steadily melting iceberg. In the second quarter of this year, for example, Paramount’s TV business revenue slid 9% to $3.1 billion, but the segment still delivered all of the company’s adjusted $1.1 billion earnings for the quarter. Skydance’s ability to meet its post-merger financial targets hinges on whether the TV business crumbles faster than Ellison and his financial engineers have projected, and whether streaming sees commensurate growth to make up for it. That’s a lot to leave to fate. Here’s the quandary: Skydance must slash costs while investing in content and paying down its immense $80 billion in net debt. The numbers may not add up. “[W]e are concerned more aggressive cost-cutting measures in TV media could leave the segment vulnerable to a faster-than-expected rate of revenue declines,” MoffettNathanson analyst Robert Fishman wrote in an Oct. 23 research note. Industry veterans have watched the creation of Skydance with wonderment. More so than Disney’s acquisition of 21st Century Fox, the union of Paramount and Warner Bros. feels like a milestone transition for the motion picture business that emerged in the 1910s and ’20s around silent films. Both iconic studios were foundational brand names for entertainment back then, and there is great hope among the many industry insiders who have worked across both that those proud logos and studio lots will endure for another century. After finally closing the WBD acquisition, Skydance leadership opened themselves up to a media firing squad on the Paramount lot in early October. Ellison and team addressed burning questions about real estate, cash flow, layoffs and more. Yet inside the company, rank-and-file employees across both operations feel left in the dark. Conversations with staffers in many corners of the Skydance business yielded a feeling of “radio silence,” as one person put it, from the top as pink slips loom and anxiety around greenlights and general spending persists. On balance, another source inside the company deadpanned: “It’s been about a month” since the two entertainment giants combined (Skydance had no comment on the matter). Skydance’s CEO David Ellison, left, and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz, right, pose for a picture on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange on Oct. 8. AP Photo/Yuki Iwamura Who can blame them, as the town places bets on whether Ellison will have the cash to pay back his lenders. Skydance’s interest expenses are expected to be more than $6 billion next year. According to financial projections, the company intends to reduce that debt load from a figure that is seven times larger than its adjusted annual earnings to a number that is three times larger than adjusted net earnings, which is a more typical debt ratio for large companies. If that model doesn’t hold, Ellison will need to find additional sources of capital. Will his father, billionaire Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, whose Ellison Family trust committed $14 billion in equity financing for the WBD takeover, be willing to pump even more money into his son’s gambit to create one of Hollywood’s biggest conglomerates? That remains to be seen. There have also been rumors that David is hunting for more big-money backers to keep Skydance afloat — including Elon Musk. Cinelli told Variety that Skydance is not seeking any additional capital at this time. (Skydance and Musk declined to comment on the tech mogul’s possible involvement.) Skydance’s pledged $30 billion annual spend on new content towers over those of rivals Netflix ($20 billion annually) and Disney ($24 billion in 2026), but investment and prayer alone will not make a meaningful dent in the company’s tremendous liabilities. To that end, bloodletting will come in the form of layoffs (expected by the end of the year and extending into the first quarter of 2027) and ruthless efficiency targets. Insiders at Skydance say cost savings from the company’s acquisition of Paramount Global will blow past an anticipated $2 billion in cuts and approach $3 billion. That’s after only a year in control of the former Shari Redstone empire. Fat-trimming opportunities from the inherited Warner Bros. Discovery books also abound, three sources say. A recent team meeting on the Warner Bros. lot revealed that Skydance will be looking closely at its financial commitments to sporting events like the Olympics. Unexpected (and eyebrow-raising) expenses have been discovered, like trifling luxury costs that amount to “tens of millions” of dollars, per two sources, on hospitality hospitality splurges like dining, travel and gifts. The former WBD regime spent in ways big and small — like stacks of receipts for sandwiches and green juices from the gourmet grocery store Erewhon. There will also be “millions” saved by combining or reducing spends on outside vendors, studio services, redundant marketing budgets and more (one source even suggests press junkets will be revamped. Sorry, journalists: No more sushi at the Four Seasons. And Ellison’s executive table prides itself on its strong, effective characters. Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz, a respected operator and the former CEO of Mattel, has claimed daily operations as his purview. President Andy Gordon and CFO Cinelli will mind people and the purse, respectively. HBO golden child Casey Bloys sits atop the entire streaming operation with JB Perrette. Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein are now at the molten core of the movie business, controlling both Paramount, WB and DC Studios. Former CBS chief George Cheeks now runs all of linear TV and news. And what about David? “There’s a lot of talk about David Ellison. Not since Walt Disney have you had an owner-operator running a major Hollywood company,” says Cinelli. “David is uniquely well-positioned to lead. He’s someone who loves the creative aspect of the business, and wants to spend his time making films and shows with passion. But he also grew up in Silicon Valley. His mentors and most valuable lessons come from that place, and that’s exactly what Skydance needs to succeed in the future.” As any Hollywood executive knows, all the strength in the world cannot account for the exercise in pain that is managing creative budgets. Take the juicy fallout around “Barbie 2” as a case study. As Ellison toiled for almost a year to win WBD, that company was stuck in tense negotiations for a sequel to Warner Bros.’ highest-grossing movie ever: “Barbie.” Director Gerwig and co-screenwriter Noah Baumbach dangled a concept for a sequel in front of now-axed WB film chiefs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy. They would not, however, allow a new movie into development until new deals were struck for themselves, producer-star Robbie and her A-list Ken doll Ryan Gosling that reflected the runaway success of the first film. So the negotiations, led by the creative team’s all-powerful CAA agent Bryan Lourd, broke down. The creatives were demanding equal pay, which one person familiar with the deal pegs at around $25 million each for Gerwig, Robbie and Gosling (Baumbach would share in the writing fee with Gerwig, and he conveniently received a new overall deal at Warners while the “Barbie” negotiations were churning). Team “Barbie” also requested increased pieces of the back end, at which point then-WBD CEO David Zaslav balked — shutting down the talks as the studio’s licensing rights to the famous toy faced a year-end deadline for renewal. Ellison, Keisz and Lourd are keen to make the “Barbie 2” deal happen by the end of the year, two sources say, and Kreiz is obviously close to the property as Mattel’s former chief executive. But for a company with an $80 billion debt tab, how does a decreased profit margin make sense? In the view of former Warner Bros. CEO Barry Meyer, the key thing that the new owners need to remember is to invest in creativity. At the end of the day, it’s all about the movies and shows. “Creating value with the content is very, very important. Distribution is usually a lot more commoditized than content,” says Meyer, who spent 41 years at Warner Bros., capped by a 14-year run as CEO. “Content is creative. Content is unique. Streaming is how you get it there, but the content is where the value is.” Todd Spangler and Jennifer Maas contributed to this report. articles.title: Daniel Dae Kim and 3AD Board North Korean Defector Documentary ‘School for Defectors’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 11, 2026 8:00am PT Daniel Dae Kim and 3AD Board North Korean Defector Documentary ‘School for Defectors’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Daniel Dae Kim and 3AD Board North Korean Defector Documentary ‘School for Defectors’ (EXCLUSIVE) 34 minutes ago ‘Train to Busan’ Director Yeon Sang-ho on AI Thriller ‘Paradise Lost’: ‘Something as Mysterious and Unknowable to Us as a Black Hole’ 55 minutes ago ‘Adolescence’ Writer Jack Thorne Adapts Matt Haig’s ‘The Humans’ for London’s West End With ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Matt Smith 7 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Damien Fry/Changho Lim “Lost” and “Hawaii Five-0” star Daniel Dae Kim and his production company 3AD have joined filmmaker Jeremy Workman’s documentary “ School for Defectors ” as executive producers. The film follows a small South Korean school where every student escaped from North Korea. The film is set at Jangdaehyun School, in an industrial part of Busan. The school has just 20 students, and each of them is a defector from the North. Workman was let into a community that had never been filmed before. His film looks at the young people there in terms of both what they have lived through and the lives ahead of them. Related Stories ‘The Cry of Serankwa,’ an Indigenous Eco-Thriller and Triple Sanfic Industria Award Winner, Strikes Distribution Deal for Latin America Cineplex Boards Sanfic Title ‘La Residencia’ From ‘Algo Azul' Director Mariel García Spooner 3AD joins a producing team that also includes Bearing North , WildBrush Media, SonaFilms and Hooligan Films. “3AD and I are really excited to join ‘School for Defectors’ as executive producers. We believe deeply in the power of documentary filmmaking, and in telling the story of this special high school, Jeremy has poignantly revealed a story full of heart, humor and humanity,” Kim said. “School for Defectors” premiered at the True/False Film Festival in March. Since then it has screened at a dozen more festivals, including Florida, RiverRun, DC/DOX, Calgary, Hamptons, Woodstock, Heartland and Vancouver. It has won six awards so far and is set to screen at Doc NYC. “What we think makes ‘School for Defectors’ so special is that it’s not simply a story about North Korea. It’s a story about youth, hope, and the universal desire to belong,” Workman said. “Daniel Dae Kim has built a remarkable career championing stories and communities that deserve greater visibility, and we’re incredibly honored to have him and 3AD help bring this film to an even wider audience.” Workman, who is repped by UTA, makes portraits of unusual and often obsessive people. His credits include “Secret Mall Apartment” (Netflix), “Lily Topples the World” (Max), “Deciding Vote” (The New Yorker), “The World Before Your Feet” (Prime Video) and “Magical Universe” (AMC+). Across close to 200 reviews, his documentaries hold a combined 95% score on Rotten Tomatoes. Kim earned a Tony nomination for his role in “Yellow Face.” He hosts and executive produces “K-Everything,” a four-part CNN travel series about South Korea’s cultural reach around the world, which premiered May 9. In June, he appeared in Season 2 of “Avatar: The Last Airbender.” Off screen, his testimony before Congress helped get the COVID-19 Hate Crimes Act passed. He has worked with a number of AAPI community groups and served as advisory council co-chair of TAAF. He is repped by CAA, Linden, Gang, Tyre, Ramer, Brown & Passman, and Narrative. Kim set up 3AD in 2014 to make work in every medium and genre built around people who have historically been underrepresented on screen. The company’s credits include ABC hit “The Good Doctor,” Amazon Prime thriller “Butterfly” and IFC documentary “Bad Axe,” which made the Oscar shortlist in 2022. Producer John Cheng runs development at 3AD, which is under a first-look TV pact with 20th Century Studios. articles.title: ‘Rings of Power’ Season 3 Premiere: [SPOILER] Dies in Shocking Murder, Sauron Assembles Ringwraiths and Jamie Campbell Bower Is Galadriel’s Lover Celeborn
articles.full_text: × Nov 11, 2026 8:15am PT ‘Rings of Power’ Season 3 Premiere: [SPOILER] Dies in Shocking Murder, Sauron Assembles Ringwraiths and Jamie Campbell Bower Is Galadriel’s Lover Celeborn By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest ‘Rings of Power’ Season 3 Premiere: [SPOILER] Dies in Shocking Murder, Sauron Assembles Ringwraiths and Jamie Campbell Bower Is Galadriel’s Lover Celeborn 32 minutes ago Donnie Dunagan, Original Voice of Bambi, Dies at 92 2 days ago James Gunn Speaks Out After Stepping Down at DC, Says It Had ‘Highest of Highs’ but ‘Has Been Trying’: ‘I Dislike the At-Times Corporate Nature of the Job’ 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ben Rothstein/Prime SPOILER ALERT: This article contains major spoilers for the four-episode premiere of “ The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power ,” now streaming on Prime Video. After a two-year break, it’s time to return to Middle-earth — and to say goodbye to one major character from “The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power.” Season 3 has dropped its first four episodes on Prime Video, and it’s immediately clear that the show has kicked into high gear. The show jumps ahead five years as Sauron (Charlie Vickers) rises to power, commands a massive orc army and begins assembling the ringwraiths, aka his creepy Nazgûl enforcers. He recruits several men to fight for the honor of being a ringwraith, including one surprise combatant: Theo (Tyroe Muhafidin), who wins. Related Stories ‘The Cry of Serankwa,’ an Indigenous Eco-Thriller and Triple Sanfic Industria Award Winner, Strikes Distribution Deal for Latin America Sanfic Mórbido Lab Lineup Ranges From an LGBTQ Alien Monster Comedy to a Mapuche Parable, Extreme Horror and Cold War Sci-Fi Sauron is in complete control, and the elven, dwarven and human cities are scrambling to hold on and remain free. But the season starts out on a tender note, flashing back to the love story between Galadriel (Morfydd Clark) and her long-lost husband Celeborn (Jamie Campbell Bower). They fell for each other in their youth but have since been separated — for now. In the present, Galadriel and Arondir (Ismael Cruz Córdova) are met by an orc named Marnûkh (Adam Young), who defects from Sauron’s army and promises to lead them to an imprisoned elven blacksmith who could forge them a ring. In Episode 4, the trio makes their way to Gundabad, a mountainous orc prison, where they learn in a twist that the elven blacksmith had died weeks ago. However, they do rescue Celeborn, who’d been locked up for who knows how long. Galadriel, Arondir, Celeborn and Marnûkh fight their way out of Gundabad, but they’re met by a ringwraith who faces off against Arondir. The shadowy knight removes his mask, and it’s revealed that Theo has joined Sauron’s inner circle. Arondir tries to reason with the young man, but Sauron appears and orders Theo to kill the elf. Theo plunges his sword into Arondir, murdering him in a shocking twist. Elsewhere in Middle-earth, things aren’t going much better. The humans are divided, with Numenor’s King Pharazon (Trystan Gravelle) surviving an assassination attempt from a Faithful follower of the blind, deposed Queen Regent Mirel (Cynthia Addai-Robinson). Earien (Ema Horvath), the daughter of Elendil (Lloyd Owen), has also been working as a spy for the Faithfuls, but she’s found out by Pharazon and killed. Over in the dwarven mountains, King Durin IV (Owain Arthur) is dealing with a succession problem. He’s challenged for his father’s crown by his brother Thrain (Eddie Marsan), who wants to work with the ringwraiths to protect the dwarves. They settle the disagreement with a fight, but Durin is thrown off after he learns that his wife Disa (Sophia Nomvete) previously had a fling with Thrain. Durin loses the showdown, and his right to rule the kingdom. Middle-earth’s saving grace may come on the wizard coattails of Gandalf, who finally dons his famous pointed hat after speaking with the mysterious, all-powerful Secret Fire. Red light therapy has moved well beyond the dermatologist’s office. Once largely reserved for luxe celebrity treatments , the technology is now a popular fixture in at-home wellness routines, with everyone from skincare enthusiasts to fitness devotees investing in LED devices designed to support skin health and post-workout recovery. While LED face masks have dominated much of the conversation, red light therapy panels offer a more versatile alternative. Unlike masks, which are generally designed to target the face, panels can be positioned to deliver light to larger areas of the body, from the neck and shoulders to the back and legs. Many combine red light, commonly studied for its potential skin benefits, with near-infrared wavelengths being investigated for muscle and joint recovery. Some are compact enough to fit on a desk, while others require dedicated floor space and cost well over $1,000. Shoppers should pay attention to the number and type of wavelengths, treatment coverage, adjustable settings and whether a stand is included. It’s also worth distinguishing the science behind red light therapy from the marketing. Research suggests that certain wavelengths may improve skin appearance or help with particular types of pain, but evidence varies by condition, and the benefits of any specific consumer device aren’t guaranteed. Below, we’ve rounded up seven red light therapy panels worth considering — from entry-level investments to more elaborate additions to your wellness routine. The clinical-grade panel features 480 LEDs across six wavelengths, spanning 630 nm red light to 1064 nm near-infrared light, allowing users to target everything from surface-level skin concerns to deeper muscle and joint tissue. Unlike smaller panels that require multiple sessions to cover different areas, the 64-inch Blaze delivers head-to-toe coverage in a single setup, with a motorized, 360-degree rotating stand that makes it easy to use while standing or lying down. It also offers preset modes for skin health, muscle recovery, hair growth and more, plus customizable intensity and pulsing settings for a more tailored experience. Overall, it’s one of the most versatile options for anyone serious about incorporating red light therapy into their wellness routine. It also features a built-in timer and foldable stand, making it easy to incorporate into a morning or evening routine. While it lacks the extensive customization of more expensive models, its straightforward design makes it a practical entry point for beginners. articles.title: Kate Berlant and John Early to Host Film Independent Spirit Awards
articles.full_text: × Nov 11, 2026 8:26am PT Kate Berlant and John Early to Host Film Independent Spirit Awards By Clayton Davis Plus Icon Clayton Davis Chief Awards Editor byClaytonDavis Latest Kate Berlant and John Early to Host Film Independent Spirit Awards 30 minutes ago Is ‘I Play Rocky’ Original or Adapted? Stallone’s ‘Rocky’ Origin Story Faces a ‘Barbie’-Style Oscar Dilemma (EXCLUSIVE) 18 hours ago Oscars: Best Original Score — Could One of Hollywood’s Most Overlooked Composers Finally Get His Moment? 22 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sela Shiloni Kate Berlant and John Early , two of comedy’s most gloriously unpredictable performers, will co-host the 2027 Film Independent Spirit Awards . The 42nd annual celebration of the best in independent film and television takes place Saturday, March 6, 2027, at the Hollywood Palladium, eight days before the 99th Academy Awards on March 14. The date marks a later slot on the calendar and a return to Saturday after this past year’s Sunday, Feb. 15 ceremony, which was hosted by “Saturday Night Live” alum Ego Nwodim. Related Stories Benjamín Vicuña, Star of Netflix Hit Series 'Envious,' Joins ‘My Last Stand' by Goya-Winner Matías Bize Cineplex Boards Sanfic Title ‘La Residencia’ From ‘Algo Azul' Director Mariel García Spooner “If there’s one thing we don’t need, it’s another predictable awards show,” says Film Independent President Juan Devis. “Kate and John are two of the funniest, strangest and most brilliantly unpredictable performers working today. They embody everything we love about independent storytelling: originality, fearlessness and a healthy disregard for convention. We’re excited to shake things up, break a few rules and have some fun along the way.” The hosts are ready for the assignment. “We’ve always been obsessed with awards shows, and we’re so honored we get to host the coolest one. Tune in to see if we choke under pressure!” Berlant and Early say in a joint statement. Berlant and Early join a roster of past Spirit Awards hosts that includes Nwodim, Aidy Bryant, Hasan Minhaj, Megan Mullally and Nick Offerman, Aubrey Plaza, Nick Kroll and John Mulaney, Kate McKinnon and Kumail Nanjiani, Fred Armisen and Kristen Bell, Andy Samberg and John Waters. Friends and creative collaborators for more than a decade, Berlant and Early have built a devoted following on a distinctive brand of absurdist comedy that blends sharp social satire, improvisation and performances that rarely go where you expect. Their joint work includes the acclaimed sketch series “555” and the Emmy-nominated Peacock comedy special “Would It Kill You to Laugh?,” which took familiar comedic conventions and twisted them into something entirely their own. Individually, both have carved out celebrated careers across film, television and live comedy. Berlant’s film credits include “Sorry to Bother You,” “Once Upon a Time… in Hollywood” and “Don’t Worry Darling,” and she has appeared in FX’s comedy-drama series “The Bear.” She also earned acclaim for her one-woman show “Kate” and her comedy specials “Cinnamon in the Wind” and “Parmesan.” Early is best known for his breakout performance in the dark comedy series “Search Party,” which ran on TBS before moving to HBO Max, as well as his stand-up special “Now More Than Ever.” He recently made his feature directorial debut with “Maddie’s Secret,” which also features Berlant. This year’s ceremony adds two new categories, best international first feature and the Digital Creator Award, expanding the show’s reach across platforms. Filmmaker Roman Coppola will also bring his artistic vision to the show in the newly created role of creative consultant.The Nominee Brunch, the annual gathering that honors all nominees and features the presentation of the Emerging Filmmaker Awards, returns to The London West Hollywood on Saturday, Jan. 9, 2027. articles.title: From a ‘Hell House’ to ‘The Woods,’ Stephen Cognetti Proves His Versatility as a Scary Movie Maestro
articles.full_text: × Nov 11, 2026 8:30am PT From a ‘Hell House’ to ‘The Woods,’ Stephen Cognetti Proves His Versatility as a Scary Movie Maestro By William Earl Plus Icon William Earl @beautifulbill Latest Variety Announces Program for Inaugural Women of Awards Season High Tea 23 hours ago The Team Unveils New Board as Firm Regroups After Rebrand From Wasserman 1 day ago Danielle Fishel Gets Honest About ‘Girl Meets World’ Pay, Says She Knew She Was Disliked on Set for Setting Boundaries (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy photo Stephen Cognetti ’s newest film is a hard pivot from the franchise that made him a household name in horror. Cognetti, who wrote and directed all five chapters in the found footage “ Hell House LLC ” franchise, just finished filming his latest feature, “ A Body in the Woods .” It stars Emma Roberts as Alice Lincoln, a turn-of-the-century woman who lives in a remote cabin in an area of the woods that might be haunted by a witch. Related Stories Benjamín Vicuña, Star of Netflix Hit Series 'Envious,' Joins ‘My Last Stand' by Goya-Winner Matías Bize Invercine, Gema Films and Gaman Cine, Top Producers on Latin America’s Film-TV Scene, Bring to Market New Productions Manifest Pictures is launching international sales for the film at AFM . Cognetti spoke with Variety about his dark new vision, his influences and the future of “Hell House LLC.” How did you come up with the idea for this new film? I actually wrote this right after the fourth “Hell House” movie. I felt like I was in a very good state of mind, scare-wise. It was the quickest first draft of a script I’ve ever written. I got the idea, and it just flowed. What did Emma’s performance bring to the film? She’s not only a wonderful actress, but she’s just so creatively intelligent. She has all of these good instincts. She just gets things better than anyone I’ve ever worked with on screen. Every discussion with her is on another level because she understood everything. From what we were doing behind the camera to what she was doing on screen, she just has a great understanding. Were there any movies you were inspired by for the look of “A Body in the Woods?” There were two films that really inspired me. The first is not horror at all, but it’s “The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford.” When I was writing this, I was not only always thinking about the visuals; I was also listening to the soundtrack the entire time. “Assassination” was always in my head. Also, Robert Eggers’ “The Witch” is a film that I just adore. I love everything he did with the camera. It is a very deliberate movement, slow movement, and the camera takes its time. We take our time story-wise; we take our time with the scares, the story. I wouldn’t call this a slow burn at all, but I just love the style of a well-paced, slower horror film, rather than something like I’m used to in the found footage world, which is very jumpy and we’re hopping around quickly, getting to scare after scare. Here we’re just building a world and building a character who’s mostly isolated. How are you a different director from when you first began? You’ve got to learn to pivot quickly. It has gotten a lot easier with every subsequent film, just because I’ve learned how to strategize better and how to put together a game plan for every day. When something’s not working, that experience helps a lot. Will there eventually be another “Hell House LLC” movie? There is a future story. The fifth one, for better or for worse, ended on a cliffhanger, and that was always the intention. But making those films is impossible for where I’m at right now, for a lot of behind-the-scenes reasons. But I would always love to tell more of the story. I just don’t know how it would ever be able to happen. It might come in other forms. I’ve always said that there might be a novel, a graphic novel, to not only tell the final chapter, but also flesh out more of the story that we’ve seen. In terms of a movie, there’s nothing on the horizon yet, but I would never say never. ‘Logan’ Star Dafne Keen Says ‘I Was Offered Cocaine’ as an 11-Year-Old in Hollywood and Hugh Jackman ‘Made Sure No One Abused My Hours’ on Set Loading comments...

articles.full_text: × Nov 11, 2026 8:56am PT Alief Boards ‘Borges and Me,’ Closes Major Market Theatrical Sales (EXCLUSIVE) By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest ‘Gordon,’ a Big Netflix Series From Argentina, Unpacked by Pablo Trapero and Star Rodrigo de la Serna 2 days ago Sanfic Prizes: ‘Monguen’ and ‘Narciso’ Win at Pared-Back Ceremony Due to Sudden Demise of ‘A Fantastic Woman’ Director Sebastián Lelio 3 days ago Seville European Film Festival Honors Agnieszka Holland, Thierry Frémaux and Cartoon Saloon 5 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Luis Gnecco and Fionn Whitehead in 'Borges and Me' France and U.K.-based Alief has boarded as a sales agent “Borges and Me,” a big scene adaptation of U.S. writer Jay Parini novelized memoir of a life-changing encounter with Argentine literary great Jorge Luis Borges. Directed by Marc Turtletaub (“Jules”) and produced by his label Big Beach (“Miss Sunshine”), “Borges and Me” stars Fionn Whitehead (“Dunkirk”), Luis Gnecco (“Neruda”) and Alan Cumming (“Avengers Doomsday”). Related Stories Sanfic Mórbido Lab Lineup Ranges From an LGBTQ Alien Monster Comedy to a Mapuche Parable, Extreme Horror and Cold War Sci-Fi Alex de la Iglesia on His Upcoming Chilean Shoot ‘The Misunderstanding’: ‘Reality Has Become My Parallel World’ “Delightfully imbued with poetry, magical realism and melancholy, ‘Borges and Me’ is a charming ride with an outstanding British cast. We are delighted to be representing the film,” said Alief President Brett Walker, announcing the pickup. The Edinburgh Festival world premiere has also closed first major market theatrical deals before the AFM with Icon Distribution (U.K. and Ireland), Rialto Distribution (Australia and New Zealand), German-speaking Europe with MFA Film and Spain, bought by Alfa Pictures across what alien describes as “multiple major markets.” Alief is now in conversations with buyers from Central Europe, MENA, Mexico, Cono Sur countries of Argentina, Chile and Uruguay and Asia, it told Variety on the first day of trading at the American Film Market . Written by Oren Moverman (“The Messenger”), working off an earlier adaptation by “Borges and Me” picks up on Parini (Whitehead) in 1971 as young American graduate student at Scotland’s St. Andrews U. desperate to find his voice as a writer, who is persuaded by mentor Scottish poet and Borges translator Alistair Reid, to chauffeur Borges for a week’s road trip in the Scottish Highlands to meet poet George Mackay Brown (Peter Mullan). Their journey—an improbable road trip in an old Morris Minor—transforms from a reluctant obligation into a profound, life-changing experience, Alief noted. In real-life, Argentina’s Jorge Luis Borges was a towering literary presence. Asked to name the greatest works in Latin America literature, Nobel Prize winner Mario Vargas Llosa answered “Borges, everything.” Yet Borges wrote famously in a poem that “I have committed the worst of all sins: I have not been happy.” The Borges Parini encounters in 1971 is a 72-years legend making up for lost time: eager, though blind, to grasp the moment, feel it to its fullest. As played by Gnecco, that drivers moments of comedy, but as the film builds in emotion in his second half, delivers a life changing lesson for Parini. “ Borges has remained with me every day of my life,” he says in his voiceover narrative. “Oren Moverman pivots between moments of graceful poetry and others of simpler feelgood sentiment. The final balance slightly favors the latter,” Guy Lodge wrote in an upbeat Variety review. Peter Mullan (“My Name Is Joe”), Freya Mavor (“My Policeman,” and Morven Christie (“The Bay) also star. “Borges and Me” is a Big Beach presentation of an Ossian International, Big Beach, Lemming Film, and A Private View production. Alex Polunin, Turtletaub, Michael B. Clark, Tim Foley produce; Stephen Burt, Moverman and Parini executive produce. “It is a thrill to work with Big Beach,” added Alief partner Miguel Govea. “Their gorgeously shot ‘Borges And Me brings to life the book, capturing its essence of time, place, and recollection in a strikingly clear and evocative upbeat road movie that audiences and buyers are connecting with.” Director Marc Turtletaub added: “We are thrilled to be working with Alief for international. Their passion for the film was apparent from the first conversations we had with them. And we love the enthusiasm from the distributors who they have partnered with.” “We fell in love with ‘Borges and Me’ for its warmth, gentle wit and endearing charm. It’s a beautiful story about an unlikely friendship between two very different generations, and how much they come to learn from one another,” said Kelly Roger CEO, Rialto Distribution. “We are very excited to be releasing ‘Borges and Me ‘in the U.K. and Ireland next year and can’t wait to share it with audiences everywhere,” said Spencer Pollard, CEO, Icon Film Distribution, a John Gore Studios company “‘Borges and Me’ is a delightful package -– combining the poetic of Borges with the magic of the Highlands. We trust German arthouse audiences will love it,” added Christian Meinke,foinder of MFA Film Distribution. articles.title: Judge Declines To Dismiss Donald Trump’s Defamation Claim Against BBC
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Judge Declines To Dismiss Donald Trump’s Defamation Claim Against BBC House Blocks Effort To Impeach Secretary Of Defense Pete Hegseth Pete Hegseth Defends Tenure, Lavishes Praise On Trump & Calls Impeachment Threat “Sabotage” In Rare Pentagon Press Conference View All November 10, 2026 6:06pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Donald Trump & the BBC headquarters in London Getty A federal judge on Tuesday declined to dismiss Donald Trump ‘s defamation claim against the BBC over edits made to a documentary about January 6th that aired in advance of the 2024 election. U.S. District Judge Jeffrey Kuntz rejected the BBC’s efforts to toss the case, ruling that Trump had sufficiently pleaded actual malice. In his ruling, Kuntz wrote that the BBC confirmed “it had edited a video to make it appear as though President Trump made a statement he never made. And it acknowledged it chose to release the video in a documentary only a week before the 2024 Presidential Election, at the time it would have the most impact. To make sure it was seen in Florida, BBC even emailed U.S. and Florida based commenters with instructions to on how to view the documentary.” Related Stories News Netflix's 'The Perfect Neighbor' Beats 'Mr Nobody Against Putin' To Top Prize At UK Grierson Documentary Awards Legal Hasan Piker's $72.5M Defamation Suit Over Lynching Quotes Should Be Tossed Out, Scott Jennings Says; Statements Are "Literally True," CNN Contributor Claims He added, “Whether President Trump can prove these claims and establish he sustained damages at summary judgment or trial is left for another day.” Watch on Deadline The judge kept alive Trump’s defamation claim but dismissed his claim of violation of Florida’s Deceptive and Unfair Trade Practices Act. Trump sued the BBC for $10 billion. In the documentary, Trump: A Second Chance? , a clip is shown from his January 6 speech, in which he says, “We’re going to walk down to the Capitol … and I’ll be there with you. And we fight. We fight like hell.” In fact, the remark was an edit of different portions of the speech. Trump claims that the documentary — which was produced by October Films — was streamed on iPlayer by “hundreds of individuals” using a VPN in the U.S., despite it being geoblocked in America. His lawyers have accused the BBC of a “brazen” attempt to interfere in the 2024 U.S. election, which the corporation denies. In the fallout from edited speech, BBC director general Tim Davie and Deborah Turness , who led the news division, stepped down. The BBC apologized, calling it an “error of judgment,” but they did not offer to pay any damages. The judge wrote of the editing, “Trump properly alleges that BBC spliced and edited together a twelve-second segment that resulted in reputational harm based off ‘deceptive and defamatory distortion.'” “On its face, a twelve-second clip seems insignificant, but in the context of the complaint, these twelve seconds are the result of splicing two segments that are separated by nearly fifty-five minutes in the speech from which the segment is sourced.” Among other things, the BBC contended that Trump lacked personal jurisdiction, as the Panorama documentary did not air in Florida, where the case was filed. The judge ruled that Trump had sufficiently claimed jurisdiction. The judge wrote, “Trump has alleged extensive contacts tying BBC to the State of Florida. BBC tries to frame this as an operation entirely disconnected from Florida. That cannot be the case. Trump is a Florida resident, and the Documentary is almost entirely about Trump. Portions were filmed in Florida and BBC identified Florida as an important part of the Documentary. Therefore, ‘it seems disingenuous’ for BBC to argue that they ‘could not have anticipated being haled into court in Florida.'” Kuntz was nominated to the bench by Trump and confirmed by the Senate earlier this year. Trump called the ruling a “huge victory” and called the BBC “a terrible abuser of truth.” He wrote on Truth Social, “We will continue fighting against, and defeating, all of those who try to deceive the American People!” A BBC spokesperson said, “We are surprised by this decision but respect the Court’s authority and note the case will now proceed to the next stage. “We remain confident in our position and will continue to respond through the proper legal process. It would be inappropriate to comment further while proceedings are ongoing.” Sarandos Faces Unrest From Past & Present Execs Over Netflix’s Direction ‘Mike Hammer’ Star, Film & Stage Actor, Dies At 85; Career In Photos Jason Orley Directing New Take On Rom-Com ‘You’ve Got Mail’ For Warner Bros Leah McKendrick Sets ‘Voicemails From Isabelle’ Follow-Up; Maddie Ziegler Stars Read More About: 7 Comments

articles.title: ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Dance Offs On Grammy Night Bring Tough Competition To Quarterfinals
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Dancing With The Stars’ Recap: Dance Offs On Grammy Night Bring Tough Competition To Quarterfinals How Film Producer Scott Budnick & Celebrity Barber VicBlends Teamed For A New Training Program In California Prisons ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 Debuts To Series’ Best Premiere Audience Yet View All November 10, 2026 7:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Dancing With The Stars' SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the Season 35 Dancing with the Stars quarterfinals. It’s hard to believe Dancing with the Stars Season 35 is nearly over, but we’ve officially reached the quarterfinals. There are seven couples remaining, but only five can make it all the way to the finale later this month. One couple is facing elimination on Grammy night, where the contestants will be performing to some of the biggest hits in music from artists including Evanescence, Sisqó, Beyoncé, Janet Jackson and more. Related Stories News Luke Bryan, Megan Moroney & Vince Gill Among Performers Added To CMA Awards News Former 'DWTS' Contestant Danielle Fishel Says Judges Tougher On Female Contestants: "Men Get A Pass" For the second week in a row, the couples are performing a second dance on Tuesday night. This week, they’re going toe-to-toe for the dance off, which pits two couples directly against each other to a live accompaniment. The pairings are as follows: Amber vs. Ezra, Jenna vs. Tatyana and Connor vs. Maura. Watch on Deadline After earning immunity with the highest cumulative score to-date last week, Harry and Jenna will sit out of the dance off. Sheryl Crow, Brandy and Monica, and Maren Morris will join the stage to perform some of their hit songs for the head-to-head competition. Let’s get into it. INDIVIDUAL DANCES Paralympian Ezra Frech with Daniella Karagach . These two were in a flow state last week, and after earning a 10 from Derek for their Disney Night performance, they’re taking on an Argentine tango to “Crazy in Love (Remix)” by Beyoncé for Grammy Night. SCORE: 27 out of 30 Olympian Amber Glenn with Pasha Pashkov . As if she hasn’t already, Amber says she really wants to show off her inner athlete on the ballroom floor this week with a paso doble to to “Bring Me to Life” by Evanescence. SCORE: 28 out of 30 Reality star Maura Higgins with Mark Ballas . After barely escaping elimination last week, Maura is putting all her focus into an Argentine tango to “Thong Song” by Sisqó. She’s working through some pain in her rib, so that’s proving to be a challenge in rehearsals, but she pushes the pain aside and delivers a performance that Carrie Ann calls “a work of art.” SCORE: 27 out of 30 Actress Jenna Dewan with Val Chmerkovskiy . She got a perfect score last week, so Jenna is riding high and ready to take on a jazz routine to “All For You” by Janet Jackson. She previously performed at the Grammys, so she’s also got to stake her claim when walking on the floor Tuesday night. SCORE: Actress Tatyana Ali with Jan Ravnik . This Fresh Prince star has been friends with Will.I.Am for more than two decades, so she much do justice to a tango to “Boom Boom Pow” by Black Eyed Peas. She’s got to nail the sharpness of this choreography in order to wow the judges. SCORE: Comedian and podcaster Connor Wood with Rylee Arnold . Based on the comments from the judges last week, he’s got to take the lead if he wants to impress them tonight with an Argentine tango to “SexyBack” by Justin Timberlake featuring Timbaland. Now, if only he could stay on his axis point, as Carrie Ann points out. SCORE: 27 out of 30 Actor Harry Shum Jr. with Jenna Johnson . Harry says he’s avoiding doing salsa dancing for so long because it reminds him of a hard time in his childhood, so dancing a salsa to “Die with A Smile” by Lady Gaga and Bruno Mars is bringing up a lot of emotions for him. SCORE: 29 out of 30 DANCE OFF Amber Glenn and Pasha Pashkov vs. Ezra Frech and Daniella Karagach competed in a Rumba to “The Boy Is Mine” by Brandy and Monica. WINNER: Amber & Pasha (+2 bonus points) Jenna Dewan and Val Chmerkovskiy vs. Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik faced off in a Cha-Cha to “The Middle” by Zedd, Maren Morris and Grey. WINNER: Jenna and Val (+2 bonus points) Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold vs. Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas . will compete in a Cha-Cha to “All I Wanna Do” by Sheryl Crow. WINNER: Maura and Mark (+2 bonus points) Who goes home? After a night of tough competition, Jenna and Val are sent home. Next week is the semifinals. Rowling “At All,” Insists He’s “Super Clear” About Trans Support View All November 10, 2026 8:43pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paul Bettany in 'VisionQuest' Dennys Ilic/Disney+/Courtesy Everett Collection SPOILERS: This post contains details about the VisionQuest Season 1 finale episode “Forever” A major player appears to be returning to the MCU following the Season 1 finale of VisionQuest . In a post-credits scene from Tuesday’s finale episode “Forever”, a hooded figure that appears to be Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom raises the rubble of Wundagore off Wanda Maximoff/Scarlet Witch ( Elizabeth Olsen ) after she seemingly killed herself under the collapsing mountain in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022). “Scarlet Witch, awaken. Your power will be mine,” says the hooded figure. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News ‘VisionQuest’ Seems Eager To Confront Dangers Of Unregulated AI, But The Team Behind It Says MCU Series Isn’t A Reflection Of Current Events News What To Watch Before ‘VisionQuest’: From ‘Age Of Ultron’ To ‘WandaVision’ The post-credits scene seems to hint at Olsen’s return for Avengers: Doomsday , premiering Dec. 18 in theaters, after Vision (Paul Bettany) was reunited with both their sons, Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica) and Billy (Joe Locke), in the finale, which follows the events of WandaVision (2021) and Agatha All Along (2024). Marvel Studios hinted at the family potentially being fully reunited on social media ahead of Thursday’s finale, sharing a message in binary code that appears to translate to: “We could never truly leave each other, even if we tried.” Wanda previously said that to Tommy and Billy in the finale of WandaVision . Meanwhile, Olsen has said “ I know nothing ” when asked about her character’s potential return to the MCU. “I don’t know what’s going on. It’s safer for me to not know anything because then I can’t make a mistake in a situation like this. I rather know nothing,” she said in March. articles.title: ITV Cutting $40M From Media & Entertainment Budget Due To Weak Advertising Market
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max How The ‘Married At First Sight UK’ Scandal Has Impacted Hit Show Around The World Jonathan Ross Explains Backstory Behind “Tasteless” David Walliams Joke ITV Cutting $40M From Media & Entertainment Budget Due To Weak Advertising Market View All November 11, 2026 12:59am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Love Island's Maya Jama ITV2 With “weaker demand for advertising” in Q4, ITV has identified £30M ($40M) worth of cost savings from its networks division, which will soon be sold to Sky . Total Advertising Revenue is set to drop 5-10% in Q4 and 2-3% for full year 2026, ITV said today in its Q3 trading update. The network is therefore finding savings from its Media & Entertainment biz, which houses the ITV network and streamer ITVX, “to align our costs with advertiser demand.” ITV said £25M will come from content savings and another £5M from “discretionary non-content savings,” with the total content budget for 2026 now expected to be around £1.2B. Related Stories News 'Britain's Got Talent' Producer Urges "Anyone Who Feels They Have Been Subject Of Wrongdoing" To Come Forward Following David Walliams Allegations News ITV News & Guardian Closer To Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations About British Star After Injunction Appeal Deadline Passed ITV boss Carolyn McCall put the sticky ad market down to “continuing broader macroeconomic uncertainty, increased digital advertising on global streaming platforms and the impact of Less Healthy Food regulations, which came into effect on 1 October 2025.” Watch on Deadline ITV revealed a similar saving target last year due to a “softening economy” in the UK. The news comes as Comcast-owned Sky pushes on with its £1.6B acquisition of ITV, although as revealed last week the UK Culture Secretary has now officially tasked two UK regulators with probing the deal. The Love Island network is bullish that it will make it through the probe unscathed. “This is an expected and important milestone in the regulatory review process, and we are pleased that it is moving at pace,” said McCall. “We continue to expect completion in the second half of 2027.” The news was revealed today in ITV’s Q3 results, which showed total revenue of £2.7B, almost flat with the same figure for the first nine months of 2025. Media & Entertainment revenue was also virtually flat at £1.4B, with digital revenue helping offset the advertising declines. Producer-distributor ITV Studios , which is not being sold to Sky, also posted stable revenue of around £1.3B. Within ITV Studios, ITV said revenue, margin and profit are “heavily weighted to Q4,” pointing to a “strong pipeline of deliveries” like Netflix Italy’s SuburraMaxima, Peacock’s Love Island US: Beyond the Villa and the seventh season of Line of Duty for the BBC, alongside “significant high-margin licensing deals” in the global partnerships division. McCall said the sale of ITV network to Sky will “position ITV Studios as a highly attractive, pure play, global content business.” As previously guided, ITV Studios’ EBITA margin will be at the lower end of the 13% to 15% range, reflecting the revenue mix in the year, ITV said. Elsewhere, streaming hours to ITVX shot up by 29% to more than 2 billion minutes viewed. “Despite a more challenging market, we remain on track to deliver good revenue growth in ITV Studios and continued profitable digital revenue growth in Media & Entertainment (M&E) over the full year,” said McCall. “While the outlook for advertising remains muted, we are firmly focused on self help and mitigating actions, while continuing to execute our strategic priorities to drive performance across both businesses.” Sarandos Faces Unrest From Past & Present Execs Over Netflix’s Direction ‘Mike Hammer’ Star, Film & Stage Actor, Dies At 85; Career In Photos Jason Orley Directing New Take On Rom-Com ‘You’ve Got Mail’ For Warner Bros Leah McKendrick Sets ‘Voicemails From Isabelle’ Follow-Up; Maddie Ziegler Stars Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘NAZA’ Becomes One Of The Most Watched Docs On Theatrical Release In 2026
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie ‘NAZA’ Becomes One Of The Most Watched Docs On Theatrical Release In 2026 Tyler Gallant To Star In Caravaggio Art Heist Drama ‘Nativity’ Buyers Dig Beta Cinema’s Norwegian Oscar Entry ‘Growth Of The Soil’ View All November 11, 2026 1:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Filmmaker Yuval Abraham (right) interviews a source in 'NAZA' The Guardian/JW Films Bombshell Gaza documentary NAZA by Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor is on track to become one of the most-watched documentary films on theatrical release of 2026. New figures, collated by producers The Guardian and JW Films, reveal that the film had been seen by a world-wide audience of 1,547,033 across 47 territories by November 6. With $13.5 million in international gross, excluding the U.S. where it has grossed more than $1 million, it ranks among the best-performing documentaries internationally of 2026 to date. Related Stories News Avi Nesher's Israeli Box Office Hit 'Our Loves' Brings Its Characters "To The Brink" But Is Not An "October 7 Movie" News Asian World Film Festival Reveals Asian Vision & Focus On Sections Based on interviews with 24 Israeli intelligence officers and soldiers, the documentary exposes the AI, phone surveillance and points-based systems deployed by the Israeli military in Gaza to identify targets, Hamas-related or otherwise, and then kill them in their homes regardless of whether other family members are likely to die in the strike as well. Watch on Deadline The documentary has performed best in Italy, where it was released by I Wonder on September 29 shortly after its Venice world premiere. The doc has reached 717.517 admissions there to date, with the film still playing in 379 cinemas, making history as the third most-watched documentary of all time in Italian cinemas, behind only Fahrenheit 9/11 and The March of the Penguins . Having started as a self-release through Michael Tuckman’s mTuckman Media in the U.S., Neon signed on as U.S. distributor in late October, aiming to enlarge the film’s footprint by building on the successful initial theatrical launch. To date the doc has clocked 83,673 admissions across the U.S. and Canada since its release on September 30. In the UK and Ireland, Dogwoof released NAZA on October 15 with a special live event screening at the Ritz in London, featuring directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, alongside producer Jim Wilson and exec producer Jonathan Glazer. The Q&A was broadcast live to a further 104 cinemas across the UK and Ireland. The release received strong support from the entire Picturehouse circuit, as well as venues from the three major multiplex chains (Odeon, Cineworld and Vue) alongside several independent cinemas. The live event alone attracted more than 7,000 admissions, with NAZA since climbing to 102.509 to date. In France, during a 48-hour event release due to French rules for films to be streamed online, NAZA attracted an audience of over 82,000 admissions. The film screened in more than 260 theaters nationwide, with nearly 500 screenings over two days. It topped the box office on both days, making it one of the most-watched documentaries in French theaters in 2026. The doc’s German distributor ImmerGuteFilme Germany has reported 83.355 admissions in the territory to date, with its strongest day to date on Sunday, November 1. In Austria , it has drawn 16.521 spectators, with Polyfilm releasing on October 1. In both countries, NAZA is outperforming Abraham and Szor’s Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land and Kaouther Ben Hania’s Oscar-nominated feature The Voice of Hind Rajab at the same stage. There was also a strong turnout in Spain, where Elastica released on October 9 on 105 screens, reaching 61.783 visitors by last Friday. Smaller countries are also reflecting the huge public interest in NAZA . Benelux distributor Cherry Pickers counted 132.323 admissions, a level of interest echoed by the over 50.000 visitors in Switzerland. The release said there are similar stories in other territories such as Australia / New Zealand, Scandinavia, Indonesia or Romania, Thailand, Poland, Mexico and Japan. The theatrical success follows the film’s high-profile premiere in Venice in September where it received a 25-minute ovation and won the Special Jury Prize. It has since won the Audience Award in San Sebastián and the Critics Prize at the Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival. At the New York Critics Circle Awards on November 8, it won Best Political Documentary, having also been nominated for Best Documentary Feature and Best Directors. NAZA is nominated as Best Documentary Feature for the Gotham Film Awards and included in both the DOC NYC shortlist and the shortlist for Best European Documentary at the European Film Awards. articles.title: India’s Yellowstone International Film Festival Announces Documentary And LGBTQIA+ Slates
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Lightdox Acquires Sales Rights To IDFA World Premiere ‘The Big Boom!’, Gabriel Tejedor Film With Explosive Contradictions India’s Yellowstone International Film Festival Announces Documentary And LGBTQIA+ Slates Oscar Winner David Dinerstein Boards ‘Room Of The Absolute’ As EP; Award-Winning Doc Creates Portrait Of Ukrainian Artist Alla Hurenko View All November 11, 2026 1:02am Add us as a Google Preferred Source YIFF EXCLUSIVE: The upcoming Yellowstone International Film Festival in Mumbai, India has announced its documentary lineup, highlighted by the Asian premiere of Oscar contender American Doctor . Director Poh Si Teng’s film examines three U.S. physicians who volunteered their medical expertise to treat Palestinian children severely injured in Israel’s sustained attack on Gaza (it screens Thursday at DOC NYC after being named to that festival’s prestigious shortlist). Joining American Doctor at the Yellowstone festival will be fellow documentary feature Herland , directed by Kallol Mukherjee, also making its Asian premiere. “In a deeply conservative Indian village where women are forbidden from stepping outside without male permission, Bhagyashree and her growing sisterhood rise in defiance, claiming their right to work and confronting generations of patriarchal control,” reads a description. “As their resistance gathers force, the cost of being seen as equal begins to turn dangerous. How much are they willing to risk?” Related Stories News Watermelon Pictures Co-Founders Talk Future Plans & Growing Hollywood Support For Palestinian Stories: "We've Been Seeing A Renaissance With A Lot Of The A-Listers" Documentary Inaugural West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival To Showcase Oscar-Contending Documentaries, 20th Anniversary Screening Of 'Blood Diamond' YIFF Documentary feature The Wolf , directed by Wancheng Gu and Prasad Shetty, “follows Yuan, a 60-year-old queer former village mayor in Shanghai, as she navigates love, family obligations, and shifting economic landscapes while seeking autonomy and reinvention later in life.” Watch on Deadline The Yellowstone International Film Festival runs from November 30 to December 4 in Mumbai, capital of the Indian state of Maharashtra. Among the short documentaries programmed in the festival is Born Secret , directed by Riley Fitchpatrick, in which the filmmaker “returns to his hometown that built the atomic bomb . ” Scroll for the list of doc shorts in the lineup. YIFF YIFF also revealed its slate of LGBTQIA+-themed films. In addition to documentary The Wolf , features include Elephants in the Fog , winner of the Jury Prize in the Un Certain Regard section of the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. The film directed by Abinash Bikram Shah “follows Pirati, matriarch of a Kinnar (Trans) community in a Nepalese village, who dreams of escaping to a normal life. When one of her daughters disappears, she must investigate and choose between love and responsibility.” Tank Time (LGBTQIA Short) – A lonely, nonbinary teen finds courage, friendship, and a glimmer of magic in a stolen fish, a petty neighborhood feud, and an unexpected crush. Filmmaker – Jess Burgess; Country – United States; Runtime -16:39 The Witch of Vihar Lake (LGBTQIA Short) Mitthu, a timid young boy and his teenage sister Ishita live in a village close to Vihar Lake, where stories of a terrifying witch prevail. The village locals don’t dare go close to the forest or the haunted lake. Mystery and magic surround the siblings as they grapple with their parents’ ignorance and anger. We follow a bewitched Ishita and Mitthu in their coming-of-age journey as the threat of the witch looms over their lives. Filmmaker – Joey Kaushik; Country – India; Runtime – 10:47 The Sailor & The Chef – ( LGBTQIA+ Doc Short) Piyush & Sushil met entirely by chance 30 years ago at a theatre in Mumbai, India. Unbeknownst to each other, they were both gay & seeking partners in a time when the internet was nascent, and there was barely any out & proud queer community. Filmmaker- Ashish Sawhny; Country – India; Runtime -20:23 At this year’s festival, YIFF launches the inaugural KSF Queer Grant, in association with the Keshav Suri Foundation (KSF) and Lotus Visual Productions, committing $20,000 USD “towards the production of independent films by emerging LGBTQIA+ filmmakers in India. The initiative will select two filmmakers, each receiving $10,000 USD in production funding, alongside a nine-month program of industry mentorship and end-to-end creative and production support.” The grant has been established with a three-year commitment to ensure the long-term sustainability and impact of the initiative, YIFF notes. “Over the course of these three years, the collaborating organizations aim to support six filmmakers in producing six films, providing emerging queer storytellers with the resources and opportunities to bring their stories to life and share them with the world.” Tushar Tyagi, founder of Yellowstone International Film Festival YIFF Yellowstone International Film Festival founder Tushar Tyagi said, “Talent and compelling stories exist everywhere, but the opportunity to bring them to life is not always accessible to everyone. For many queer filmmakers in India, the challenge is not a lack of imagination or stories to tell, but access to the resources, industry networks and support needed to turn their creative vision into a film. Through this grant, we want to help bridge that gap by giving filmmakers the freedom and means to tell their stories with honesty and authenticity.” Tyagi continued, “Our ambition is to nurture a new generation of queer Indian voices, bring narratives rooted in lived experiences to the screen, and create opportunities for these stories to travel beyond borders. These stories deserve not only to be told, but to be seen, heard and celebrated by audiences around the world.” Keshav Suri, founder of the Keshav Suri Foundation YIFF Keshav Suri, founder of the Keshav Suri Foundation, commented, “Representation in cinema must go beyond having LGBTQIA+ characters on screen. It is equally important that people from the community have the resources and creative freedom to tell their own stories. There is no shortage of talent or compelling stories within the community, but access to funding and industry opportunities remains a challenge. Through this grant, we want to help bridge that gap and give more queer filmmakers the opportunity to bring their stories to life.” Neeraj Churi, founder of Lotus Visual Productions YIFF “For too long, queer filmmakers in India have faced challenges in securing funding and finding the right partners to bring their creative visions to life,” said Neeraj Churi, founder of Lotus Visual Productions and Sundance-winning producer of Cactus Pears . “And yet, some of the most exciting and original voices in Indian cinema are emerging from within the LGBTQIA+ community. We believe these filmmakers should have the opportunity to tell their own stories, on their own terms. The KSF Queer Grant is about creating that opportunity, combining financial support with mentorship and practical filmmaking guidance. Our hope is that this initiative will not only help make two films possible, but also open doors for a new generation of queer storytellers.” In addition to The Sailor & The Chef and Born Secret noted above, these are the short documentaries programmed in the 7 th edition of the Yellowstone International Film Festival: In the Silence After – (Doc Short) A son returns home to care for his mother, filming the last year they will spend together. Filmmaker – Sebastian Delascasas; Country – Colombia, United States; Runtime -16:50 No Matter the Weather – (Doc Short) Renée, 83, broke her ankle. Fortunately, she can rely on her granddaughter Florence, who steps in as her caregiver. While this ordeal brings them closer than ever, it inevitably confronts them with the reality of Renée’s decline. Filmmaker – Florence Lafond; Country – Canada; Runtime -14:30 A Sunflower in Delhi – (Doc Short) In a tiny women’s only beauty parlour, generations of devoted customers, including the filmmaker’s family, reflect on letting their hair go grey. The film meanders between the intimate oasis of the Sunflower Chinese Beauty Parlour and the bustling city landscape outside. articles.title: Web Summit Cancels Day Two As Storm Charles Hits Lisbon
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Web Summit Cancels Day Two As Storm Charles Hits Lisbon ‘The Perfect Lie’ Actor Matthijs Van De Sande Bakhuyzen To Lead AFM-Bound Arctic Thriller ‘The Art Of Survival’ M. John Harrison Wins The 2026 Booker Prize With ‘The End Of Everything’ View All November 11, 2026 1:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Lucy Hyslop, Brooke Stites, Jess Kirkman Tyler Miller/Web Summit, Sportsfile, Getty Images Storm Charles has put paid to day two of Web Summit in Lisbon , Portugal. Organizers said it had shut down for the day on government advice and expects to be back up and running for day three on Thursday, November 12. Web Summit is an enormous event, attracting 70,000 attendees including tech leaders and politicians from around the world, as well as media execs and sports stars. Organizers notified delegates and speakers of the day two cancellation overnight. The Prime Minister of Portugal Luís Montenegro said Tuesday that his office had recommended Web Summit events be suspended given the expected impact of two storms, Bruna and Charles. He added the final decision rested with Web Summit organizers, who quickly decided to heed his advice. Related Stories News SAG-AFTRA Members Ratify TV Animation Contracts, Securing 12.6% Wage Increase For Voice Actors News SAG-AFTRA Votes To Extend Duncan Crabtree-Ireland's Contract With Updated Title Schools and shops have been closed in Lisbon, and local transport and non-essential public services are shutting down. Some flights have been delayed and cancelled. Watch on Deadline “The Government of Portugal has formally advised Web Summit that, due to the risks posed by Storm Charles, including tidal flooding, severe disruption to public transport and the impact of high winds on external structures, Day 2 of Web Summit should not take place,” organizers said. “This follows discussions with the Portuguese Government, the National Emergency and Civil Protection Authority (ANEPC), and the Public Security Police (PSP). Web Summit will of course respect the Government’s direction, and accordingly, Day 2 (Wednesday, November 11th) will not take place.” Organizers said they are working with the authorities and emergency services to monitor conditions but expect to proceed with events on Thursday as the storm passes. The day three lineup on Thursday is slated to include SAG AFTRA boss Duncan Crabtree-Ireland in a session entitled Hollywood’s Identity Crisis, moderated by Deadline.
