articles.title: Comedian Lucy Beaumont Fears Being Blacklisted By TV Industry After Blowing Whistle On David Walliams
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Channel 4 Becomes Latest Network To Delete David Walliams Shows MGM+ Greenlights Gilded Age-Era Series ‘The American Heiress’ Starring Julianna Margulies Netflix Refuses To Remove Russell Brand Stand-Up Special Featuring Crude Sex Joke View All November 11, 2026 1:13am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lucy Beaumont Sky News Comedian Lucy Beaumont has said she has risked her television career by speaking out about David Walliams because the industry doesn’t tolerate troublemakers. In an interview with Sky News (watch below), the Taskmaster star and Hullraisers writer revealed that she was one of the “whistleblowers” on Walliams, who has been accused of using his fame and power to prey on teenage girls. Walliams, known for Little Britain and Doctor Who , strongly denies wrongdoing. Beaumont told The Cathy Newman Show that a young person working on a TV show approached her with concerns that Walliams allegedly hosted teenagers in his dressing room. Beaumont said she contacted one of the young girls. Related Stories News David Walliams Being Cut From New Movie 'Fing!' Following Allegations; Comcast-Owned Sky Exits UK Distribution Of Film News 'Britain's Got Talent' Producer Urges "Anyone Who Feels They Have Been Subject Of Wrongdoing" To Come Forward Following David Walliams Allegations “She was in a really bad way,” Beaumont said. “I was really worried she was going to take her own life because of it. She had put stuff online, and there was evidence that she was in a dressing room. I offered to pay legal fees to try and get her some protection — and I’m not saying necessarily that what she said was true — but I wanted to help her because it was a world that she was really out of her depth with.” Watch on Deadline Beaumont continued: “I believe she had signed an NDA [non-disclosure agreement] to say — and this is the issue with some of these NDAs — the NDA wasn’t just about she couldn’t talk to the media. It was that she couldn’t — I’m nearly crying telling you this — talk to family or friends or a therapist.” She added: “There’s no proper duty of care. There’s no social services that you deal with, and it’s partly because the industry is very well-managed.” Turning to her decision to speak out, Beaumont said she doesn’t think she will work in television again because people “lose work” for challenging high-profile individuals and are painted as a “trouble causer.” She added that people are “very replaceable” in the business and there are “lots of other people who can do your job.” Beaumont joked that she would become a Pilates teacher. ITV News and The Guardian published their investigation into Walliams on Tuesday, detailing how he allegedly used his position on shows like Little Britain and Britain’s Got Talent to meet teenagers and pursue sexual contact with them. One of the teenagers was alleged to be 15 at the time of her interaction with Walliams. Beaumont said she spoke to The Guardian as part of its reporting. “I am not a sexual predator… I have not broken the law,” Walliams told ITV News. “I am devastated that some of the women I met ten to twenty years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.” He continued: “Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with… I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.” Sarandos Faces Unrest From Past & Present Execs Over Netflix’s Direction Matthias Schoenaerts & Diane Kruger Headline Thriller ‘The Writer’; Latest News ‘Saturday Night Live’ Hits 2-Year Viewership High With Host Druski ‘Mike Hammer’ Star, Film & Stage Actor, Dies At 85; Career In Photos Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: Jonathan Ross Explains Backstory Behind “Tasteless” David Walliams Joke
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max James Graham’s BBC Drama ‘Sherwood’ To End After Season 3 Netflix’s ‘The Perfect Neighbor’ Beats ‘Mr Nobody Against Putin’ To Top Prize At UK Grierson Documentary Awards How The ‘Married At First Sight UK’ Scandal Has Impacted Hit Show Around The World View All November 11, 2026 1:39am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jonathan Ross Lia Toby/Getty for the NTA's British TV presenter Jonathan Ross has landed himself in some hot water over the past week for his past association with both David Walliams and Russell Brand . The Guardian and ITV News’ report into allegations against Walliams including from teenagers referenced a joke Ross made at the 2004 British Comedy Awards. “The comedy awards is 15 years old – 15 years old! And like most 15-year-olds, it’s drunk, it’s unpredictable and it’s probably going home with David Walliams,” Ross joked at the time. Ross addressed the joke and the broader allegations this morning, saying in a statement he is “as horrified by the revelations about David Walliams and the crimes of Russell Brand as the rest of the nation.” Related Stories News Comedian Lucy Beaumont Fears Being Blacklisted By TV Industry After Blowing Whistle On David Walliams News David Walliams Being Cut From New Movie 'Fing!' Following Allegations; Comcast-Owned Sky Exits UK Distribution Of Film Ross said the “tasteless joke that I would not dream of making today about anyone” was submitted to him by the Comedy Awards writing team at the time. Watch on Deadline “I believed that the punchline was a reference to the fact he had publicly dated younger women, exaggerated for comic effect,” said Ross. “Had I had any reason to suspect that it might be referring to actual events, I would not only have refused to use it, but I would not have felt comfortable continuing a personal or professional relationship with him. I also like to think that I would have acted upon that knowledge.” Ross’ association with Walliams and Brand has been scrutinized in recent days. Along with the Comedy Awards joke, The Guardian published an image of Ross with Walliams at a charity quiz. In the photo, Ross is sat at a table while Walliams has his arm around an 18-year-old who accused Walliams of “pleading with me to share a bed with him” and “putting his head in my lap and making me stroke his head.” There is no suggestion that Ross was aware of any of the behavior Walliams has been accused of. Ross’ past association with Brand, who was jailed earlier this week for 10-and-a-half years for rape and sexual assault, has also come up in recent days. The pair created scandal in 2008 for prank calling Fawlty Towers actor Andrew Sachs and making lewd comments about his granddaughter, who had previously been in a relationship with Brand. After trying to have the articles blocked via the courts, the Walliams allegations dominated the news agenda yesterday and have called into question a culture that previously allowed men like Walliams and Brand to flourish. Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said “the allegations are the latest in a long line of reported abuses of power in an industry where we have known for so long that the power imbalances are huge.” Walliams has been dropped by his agent and his shows including Little Britain have been removed from BBC iPlayer. He is accused of using his celebrity to prey on women as young as 15, making contact with them through work, including on Britain’s Got Talent , to pursue them for sexual purposes. Deadline has contacted Walliams’ legal representatives for comment. In a statement to ITV News, Walliams denied all allegations against him. When trying to prevent publication of the articles, Walliams’ lawyers revealed that he had made two attempts to take his life because of the allegations. “I am not a sexual predator… I have not broken the law,” Walliams said. “I am devastated that some of the women I met ten to twenty years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.” He continued: “Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with… I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.” Sarandos Faces Unrest From Past & Present Execs Over Netflix’s Direction Matthias Schoenaerts & Diane Kruger Headline Thriller ‘The Writer’; Latest News ‘Saturday Night Live’ Hits 2-Year Viewership High With Host Druski ‘Mike Hammer’ Star, Film & Stage Actor, Dies At 85; Career In Photos Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Lightdox Acquires Sales Rights To IDFA World Premiere ‘The Big Boom!’, Gabriel Tejedor Film With Explosive Contradictions
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Lightdox Acquires Sales Rights To IDFA World Premiere ‘The Big Boom!’, Gabriel Tejedor Film With Explosive Contradictions India’s Yellowstone International Film Festival Announces Documentary And LGBTQIA+ Slates Oscar Winner David Dinerstein Boards ‘Room Of The Absolute’ As EP; Award-Winning Doc Creates Portrait Of Ukrainian Artist Alla Hurenko View All November 11, 2026 2:02am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Big Boom!' Mira Film Basel GmbH EXCLUSIVE: Lightdox has acquired world sales rights to The Big Boom! ahead of its world premiere in the Frontlight section of International Documentary Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ). Swiss filmmaker Gabriel Tejedor directed the feature documentary that explores “the contradictions of a Bulgarian town pulled into Europe’s shifting geopolitical order, where arms production for Ukraine’s front lines collides with enduring ties to Russia, personal convictions, and the everyday need to survive.” The Big Boom! premieres at IDFA on Saturday. Watch the film’s trailer below. Related Stories Documentary Riz Ahmed Boards Elham Ehsas' Short Film 'Forgotten Spaceman' About Afghanistan's First Astronaut Documentary IDFA Announces Competition Lineups, Adds 'Musk' And Elizabeth Holmes Documentary 'You Can See Everything' The documentary contrasts ancient traditions in Kazanlak, Bulgaria’s “Valley of Roses,” with the town’s major industry – the Arsenal weapons factory. That defense contractor, founded in the 19 th century, “provides work for thousands of people manufacturing weapons and ammunition,” according to a synopsis. “Through the lives of four residents, Tejedor examines the place this industry occupies in the town’s economy and identity, and the questions it raises for those whose lives depend on it.” Watch on Deadline Mira Film Basel GmbH “ The Big Boom! brings us face to face with a contradiction at the heart of today’s Europe – a town making the weapons of war while struggling with its own loyalties and beliefs,” commented Lightdox CEO Anna Berthollet. “Gabriel Tejedor finds a way into this reality that feels both clear-eyed and deeply human. As someone of Bulgarian origin myself, I find his sensitive portrayal of Kazanlak and its people particularly meaningful. He reveals the layers of history, identity and geopolitical influence that shape the region without reducing them to a political argument. We’re delighted to bring this timely film to audiences worldwide.” The Big Boom! is the fifth feature directed by Tejedor, the filmmaker and journalist “whose work explores utopias and the relationship between individuals and authority across the former Soviet Union and its satellite states.” Director Gabriel Tejedor Mira Film Basel GmbH “I have never been interested in war or weapons. But the invasion of Ukraine shattered my convictions,” Tejedor said in a statement. “Ever since, one question has haunted me: what does it mean to be a pacifist today? I do not judge the workers at Arsenal, nor the local population. The Big Boom! does not seek to lecture, but to confront the grey zones of a continent trapped in its own paradoxes.” ‘ The Big Boom! ‘ Mira Film Basel GmbH The film is a production of Mira Film Basel GmbH, co-produced by RTS Radio Télévision Suisse, SRG SSR, with the support of Swiss and regional film funds and cultural institutions. Susanna Guggenberger produced The Big Boom! Cinematography is by Thomas Szczepanski; Christine Hoffet edited the film. The score is composed by Petar Dundakov. articles.title: How The ‘Married At First Sight UK’ Scandal Has Impacted Hit Show Around The World
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max James Graham’s BBC Drama ‘Sherwood’ To End After Season 3 Entertainment 360 Acquires Max Stein’s Brigade Netflix’s ‘The Perfect Neighbor’ Beats ‘Mr Nobody Against Putin’ To Top Prize At UK Grierson Documentary Awards View All November 11, 2026 3:37am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: The team behind Married at First Sight ( MAFS ) Australia is “reviewing” Channel 4’s report into the show, which has been axed in the UK following rape allegations. Deadline asked some of the teams behind versions of MAFS around the world whether they will take heed of the report. Australian broadcaster Channel Nine and MAFS producer Endemol Shine Australia told us they are “examining the findings,” while noting “many of the recommendations for improvement are already in place for MAFS Australia .” “We are always reviewing our participant protocols to ensure our participants’ safety and wellbeing,” added a spokeswoman for Endemol Shine Australia. “Production of MAFS Australia continues.” Related Stories News Channel 4 Cancels 'Married At First Sight UK' After Rape Allegations News Matthew Weiner Exits Eddie Murphy Peacock Series 'The Chairman' As Showrunner Channel 4 axed MAFS UK following rape allegations revealed earlier this year by BBC News, which the men accused of wrongdoing deny. Following these allegations being made public, two reviews were commissioned by Channel 4 CEO Priya Dogra, one examining welfare protocols and the other looking into whether changes should be made to protocols to strengthen contributor welfare in the future. While the latter, penned by ex-BBC One boss Lorraine Heggessey, suggested MAFS UK could continue if it took in some changes, Dogra axed the show last week. Watch on Deadline Many of the versions around the world are made by different production outfits than MAFS UK such as MAFS Australia , which is produced by Banijay-owned Endemol Shine Australia while the UK version is overseen by Seven.One Studios -owned CPL. The two versions are “separate productions and separate shows,” according to the Endemol Shine Australia spokeswoman. Deadline understands MAFS Australia protocols already in place that were suggested by Heggessey include cast being allowed to keep in touch with friends and family outside the show, a regular refresh of the show’s psychologists, and keeping casting and welfare teams separate. The Australia team have separate issues they are dealing with. New South Wales Police told BBC News last month that inquiries had taken place “following a report of inappropriate content being shared.” Channel Nine has confirmed that it is “aware of a police investigation.” There were also allegations, published by BBC News, that contestants were not told about their on-screen partners’ previous criminal convictions. Responding in a joint statement, Channel Nine and Endemol Shine Australia said they had “strong protocols in place to ensure participant safety and wellbeing.” In the U.S., MAFS is made by another different company, North Road-owned Kinetic Content. A spokeswoman declined comment on the Channel 4 review and whether MAFS could implement some of the recommendations in the States. We understand the American version is not currently filming and hasn’t been picked up for new seasons at this point. ‘MAFS UK’ still on sale MAFS is one of the world’s most successful formats. It originated in Denmark, where it still airs on local network DR1, produced by Seven.One-owned Snowman Productions. Seven.One told us other versions around the world that it controls remain business as usual, while its distribution arm will continue selling older editions of MAFS UK to global buyers. A Seven.One spokeswoman said: “The external reviews of contributor welfare on Married at First Sight UK confirmed that Channel 4 and production company CPL’s welfare protocols were compliant with the Ofcom Broadcasting Code; the Heggessey review found that they were ‘extensive, extremely thorough and of a high standard from which other productions in the industry have learnt’. Despite the findings of the reviews, Channel 4 has made the independent strategic decision not to continue the show. This decision has no impact on the show in other countries.” In the UK, however, the fallout from the cancelation continues. Its axing came on the day Russell Brand, a former Channel 4 presenter, was found guilty of rape and sexual assault . Several days later, allegations of sexually exploitative behavior towards women and teenagers were published about Little Britain co-creator David Walliams, who denies the allegations and says “I am not a sexual predator… I have not broken the law.” Channel 4 is moving on from MAFS . All past seasons of MAFS UK plus the American, Australian and New Zealand versions have been removed from Channel 4’s VoD platform, while a planned spin-off has been cancelled. Channel 4 boss Dogra was merely a few weeks into the job when the MAFS UK allegations broke. She will likely face questions on the show when she appears in front of a parliamentary committee on Tuesday and has said its “considerable budget” will now be used to “find the next generation of distinctive and disruptive British television.” This will be a key task for new programs chief David Brindley, who starts in a few weeks’ time. articles.title: ‘Days Of Our Lives’ Actor James Reynolds Reveals Parkinson’s Diagnosis; Condition Being Written Into Storyline
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Days Of Our Lives’ Actor James Reynolds Reveals Parkinson’s Diagnosis; Condition Being Written Into Storyline ‘Much Ado About Nothing’ With Tom Hiddleston & Hayley Atwell Sells Out, Tops $2M Gross; ‘Here There Are Blueberries’, ‘Downstate’, ‘Fantasticks’ Fill Seats – Broadway Box Office Richard Schiff Among Cast Added To Broadway’s ‘Awake And Sing!’ Revival View All November 11, 2026 8:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source James Reynolds at 2018 Daytime Emmy Awards Getty James Reynolds , who has played Abe Carver on Days of Our Lives for 45 years, has revealed that he’s been diagnosed with Parkinson’s disease and that his condition will be worked into the storyline of the long-running soap. In an interview with ET (watch it below), Reynolds, 80, concedes that he initially tried to mask his symptoms while on set but that he was increasingly unsuccessful. Asked about the decision to address the diagnosis within the storyline, Reynolds said, “Well, it kind of goes back to when I thought I was hiding it. The writers also wanted to incorporate because it was obvious. It was obvious. And we play life here.” Related Stories News 'Days Of Our Lives' Actor Robert Kelker-Kelly's Cause Of Death Revealed Casting 'Days Of Our Lives' Casts Long-Awaited Dominic Marino Reynolds continued, “And there are many other characters who have gone through real-life issues that then are mirrored on the show, and this is an issue that it is going to be mirrored on the show and there’s nothing any of us can really do about it.” Watch on Deadline The actor, who is the longest-running Black actor in a single series in television history, said he feels his character is particularly well-suited to the storyline. “I feel like the value of Abe as a character [is he] overcomes a lot, has tremendous amount of strength, deals with a lot of things with humor as well as understanding.” Reynolds, who has kept his diagnosis private except for family for a few years, says the symptoms – shaky hands, occasional balance issues, sometimes a shortness of breath – become increasingly difficult to conceal. “I thought I was hiding it but I wasn’t. You play that game with yourself.” The actor said in the last few weeks he realized he might have been showing early symptoms – “horrible dreams” that caused him to thrash and fall out of bed – as long as 15 to 20 years ago, a realization he said he came to after watching actor Alan Alda’s recent interview on C BS Sunday Morning, during which Alda said his earliest Parkinsons symptom was acting out his dreams. (Watch Alda’s interview below.) articles.title: M. John Harrison On Early Adaptation Interest & Why He Almost Added ‘A Film’ To His Booker-Winning Novel’s Title
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart M. John Harrison On Early Adaptation Interest & Why He Almost Added ‘A Film’ To His Booker-Winning Novel’s Title Charlie Sheen’s ‘Mostly Sheenius’ Podcast Lines Up Michael Douglas As First Guest: Rob Lowe, Martin Sheen & Denise Richards Also Set To Appear Web Summit Cancels Day Two As Storm Charles Hits Lisbon View All November 11, 2026 8:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source M. John Harrison Wiktor Szymanowicz/Getty Images With interest in a big-screen adaptation, M. John Harrison has told Deadline he wanted to call his Booker Prize -winning novel ‘ The End of Everything : A Film’, but got cold feet at the last minute. Harrison won the Booker for ‘The End of Everything’, to give his book its final title. It follows a beachcomber living on the English coast after a disaster has struck. He finds a mysterious object in the sea and brings it inland. As well as spurring book sales, there is always sharp interest in adapting Booker titles. ‘The End of Everything’ has distinctive landscapes and characters as well as mysterious shape-shifting alien entities called the iGhetti. Related Stories News M. John Harrison Wins The 2026 Booker Prize With 'The End Of Everything' News Douglas Stuart, Marlon James & Elizabeth Strout Among 13 Authors On The Booker Prize Longlist; Organizers Say 2026 Selection "Rewards Risk" Fresh from winning the prestigious literary award, Harrison told Deadline that he visualized scenes from the book as he wrote them, and noted, as have others, that his novel has a cinematic quality. Watch on Deadline “When I’ve constructed a scene, when I turn it into words, I can see it. And I was, in fact, going to subtitle this novel ‘The End of Everything: A Film’. I lost my nerve at the last minute, but I now really wish I’d done it, because it’s got the structure of a kind of middle-European film, with the right provenance to be very watchable indeed.” The book is published by the Serpent’s Tail imprint, marking its first Booker win. Similarly, it was the first win for 81-year-old Harrison who served as a Booker judge in 2022. “We do have some interest, it hasn’t gone far enough to be able to talk about [in detail], but there is interest in doing something,” the writer told Deadline when asked if an adaptation was in the works. Harrison would rather his book came to screen as a movie than a series. His take is it would be a European-flavored film, with someone of the ilk of late and pioneering Hungarian director Béla Tarr at the helm. “I think for me, personally, if it were to happen, that it would be a film. And it would remind you either of a difficult French film, or a Béla Tarr film,” Harrison said. The author is an avowed movie fan, but whether he would be involved in any adaptation of his lauded book is not clear. “I watch lots of films, I love films,” he said. “But it’s like art, I see a lot of paintings, but I don’t know a great deal about how they’re painted and therefore I wouldn’t feel entirely comfortable being involved in a process like that.” He added that he could envisage how the book might work on screen, and how an adaptation could win his approval. “There are ways that that that book would have to be done to be made into a film that made me excited – that continued my excitement from writing the book – but I have faith that I might find somebody who could do that.” Booker Chief Executive Gaby Wood has also noted the filmic qualities in ‘The End of Everything’ and has said: “Readers will also recognize many tropes from cinema: the disaster movie, the road movie, the couple on the run, the noir heroine with a gun in her bag, the apocalypse.” Harrison pushes against classifications such as science fiction although that is the genre his work, stretching to 13 novels, is placed in. Booker’s Wood noted that he is the first winner “to have emerged from the bona fide SF world.” Sarandos Faces Unrest From Past & Present Execs Over Netflix’s Direction Matthias Schoenaerts & Diane Kruger Headline Thriller ‘The Writer’; Latest News ‘Saturday Night Live’ Hits 2-Year Viewership High With Host Druski ‘Mike Hammer’ Star, Film & Stage Actor, Dies At 85; Career In Photos Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Peacock Phasing In Mobile Updates, With Vertical ‘Voice’ Clips, More Home Screen Sports, Browsing Tweaks & More
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Film Accelerator Open Cities, Run By Ex-Sundance CEO Joana Vicente & Producer Jason Kliot, Reveals First Projects ‘Tangles’ Cast Members Seth Rogen, Julia Louis-Dreyfus & Bryan Cranston On Animated Film’s Rare Back Story AMC Global Media Posts Mixed Q3, Previews ‘The Walking Dead’ AMC+ Bow View All November 11, 2026 8:07am Add us as a Google Preferred Source NBCUniversal ‘s Peacock is ushering in a number of updates to its mobile app, overhauling the browsing experience, putting more sports on the home screen and expanding its vertical video offerings. The updates encompass a wide range of features, from overhauled browsing to a “jump back in” button to an influx of vertical video spanning clips and microdramas. The strategic goal of the updates is to connect with subscribers at key moments throughout the day and increase viewing time, recognizing the role that mobile devices now play in the streaming ecosystem. Just as traditional mobile players like YouTube have been leaning into the living room, legacy media players like NBCU are putting increasing emphasis on their mobile offerings after beginning on their most familiar device, the TV screen. Related Stories News How The 'Married At First Sight UK' Scandal Has Impacted Hit Show Around The World News HBO Max-Paramount+ Bundle Set To Launch In Early 2027, David Ellison Confirms Last month, NBCU parent Comcast said Peacock delivered its second straight quarter of profitability during the third quarter, though its subscriber level stayed flat at 48 million. Watch on Deadline During a press briefing in New York on Tuesday, Matt Strauss, Chairman of NBCUniversal Media Group, said he wasn’t at all discouraged by Peacock’s scale six-plus years after its launch. He pointed to the long-term strategy of the service, which started up at a very different moment for the media business, when ad-free binge releases seemed like the inevitable future. Peacock initially was mostly focused on its free, ad tier, and today still has 80% of its subscribers on its cheaper ad-supported plan. “We arguably didn’t build Peacock to win a streaming war. We built Peacock for growth in the aftermath of a streaming war,” Strauss said. “And that’s where I think we are right now, which is the next phase of growth is going to be around who can win another hour per user per month. And to go and evaluate through that lens, you have to think differently about the user experience. And the phone and mobile has to be a first-class citizen.” Testing is already under way on many of the features, which will go live and be updated continuously through early 2027. Peacock is enhancing its search capabilities with conversational AI, looking to enhance personalization. The updates build on existing features like Your Bravoverse, Clips Feed, and Peacock Performance View. John Jelley, SVP of Product and UX for the NBCUniversal Media Group, emphasized the company’s efforts to tailor its AI approach to the streaming realm. “We combine that in what we call a large action model,” he said during the press briefing. “Rather than predicting the next word as LLMs do, we’re actually predicting the next action.” Vertical video has been on Peacock for nearly two years now, with the service pioneering the format for live sports. NBCU’s long-term rights deal with the NBA, which began in 2025, offered an opportunity to showcase the technology, which will now be expanding to shows like NBC mainstay The Voice . Other sports like college basketball and golf will also get the vertical treatment. Microdramas, which have grown into a multi-billion-dollar category and are seen as a potent on-ramp for streaming viewers, will be an increasing presence on Peacock. At least one new micro title will land on the service each week, the company is promising. These series are generally licensed from third parties but in some cases are commissioned in-house, as in the case of Bravo scripted microdramas like the recently premiered Charmed by a Southern Monster . Spanish-language NBCU subsidiary Telemundo has already been pushing into the microdrama space. “NBCUniversal has an unmatched ability to turn the shows, sports and stories fans love into experiences that extend well beyond the screen,” said Jim Denney, Chief Product Officer, Global Streaming & NBCUniversal Media Group. “Our ambition is for Peacock to be more than a place to watch. With this new mobile experience, we’re evolving Peacock into an entertainment platform that gives fans more ways to discover, participate and strengthen their connection to their favorite stories, teams and franchises, turning viewing into deeper engagement and lasting fandom and loyalty.” Peacock is exploring new setups on its home screen to help viewers quickly “jump back in” to programming they enjoy. Hubs devoted to key franchises will lead not only to episodic fare but also games, microdramas, podcasts, clips and other related material. Watch on Deadline Marina Grasic, Jonathan Avildsen, and Jason Taylor are producing. Gary Lucchesi, Christian Mercuri, and Ruzanna Kegeyan serve as executive producers. New Yorker Avildsen, the son of Oscar-winning filmmaker John G. Avildsen ( Rocky ), has been part of the city’s graffiti culture for forty years. He will create and curate the film’s art and assemble real graffiti writers to contribute. “As a lifelong New Yorker, this is a world for which I’ve always had a fierce passion,” said Cirulnick. “Jonathan Avildsen and Matthias are key to making it authentically— and with Diane, it’s a filmmaker’s dream.” “Graffiti is a global language,” said producer Jason Taylor. “It’s in every city on earth and it’s never had its definitive modern film.” “In Matthias and Diane we have two of the finest actors in cinema today to carry this original film,” said producer Marina Grasic. “The dialogue, the characters, rang so true to me,” said producer and technical advisor Jonathan Avildsen. “I’m excited to help bring this script to life authentically.” Cirulnick is repped by Brillstein Entertainment Partners and Gersh. articles.title: WME Signs Investigative Journalist Mariana Van Zeller
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Paul Wesley Latest To Join Netflix’s ‘Icebreaker’ ‘Chucky’ Creator Don Mancini Signs With Independent Artist Group Lisa Edelstein, Kevin Pollak & Joe Swanberg Among New Additions To SM Goldberger’s ‘Your Heart Is A Hummingbird’ View All November 11, 2026 8:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mariana van Zeller Miguel Angelo EXCLUSIVE: Mariana van Zeller , the Peabody and Emmy Award-winning journalist, filmmaker and co-founder of Muck Media, has signed with WME for representation in all areas. Known for her reporting as a leading authority on the global shadow economy, Van Zeller has led investigations into the opioid crisis, immigration and the explosion of scamming as a global industry. The latter is the subject of her new feature doc Super Scam Me , released Oct. 17 on Hulu, Disney+ and National Geographic. As co-founder of Muck Media, Van Zeller hosted and executive produced their flagship series Trafficked with Mariana van Zeller for National Geographic. The series earned 16 Emmy wins and 88 nominations over five seasons. Other Muck Media titles include the Emmy-nominated Sundance doc Science Fair , Netflix’s Mucho Mucho Amor and The Fall of El Mayo , and HBO Max’s American Pain . Born and raised in Portugal, Van Zeller studied journalism at Columbia University. Her work has been recognized with a Peabody Award, a duPont-Columbia Award, a Television Academy Honor and the Livingston Award for Young Journalists. She also hosts The Hidden Third , a weekly podcast about crime, black markets and the people who live inside them. Watch on Deadline WME will work with Van Zeller to expand her business across documentaries, television, digital audio and video, publishing and beyond. The journalist continues to be managed by Michael Lasker and Nate Dixon at Mosaic. articles.title: Kate Berlant And John Early To Co-Host Film Independent Spirit Awards
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Patrick Hipes Patrick Hipes Executive Managing Editor More Stories By Patrick Austin Film Festival Reveals Audience Award Winners, Sets Dates For 2027 Film & Script Competitions ‘Elsinore’s Andrew Scott To Receive Palm Springs’ Desert Palm Achievement Award, Actor Palm Springs Film Awards Honorees: ‘La Bola Negra’ To Receive International Star Award View All November 11, 2026 8:38am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kate Berlant and John Early Sela Shiloni Comic duo Kate Berlant and John Early have been set to co-host the 42nd annual Film Independent Spirit Awards , which take place March 6, 2027 at the Hollywood Palladium. It will mark the latest team-up for the pair, which have collaborated on numerous projects including the sketch series 555 and the 2022 comedy special Would It Kill You to Laugh? which scored them an Emmy nomination for writing. Most recently, Berlant appeared in Early’s feature directorial debut Maddie’s Secret , in which he also starred. We’re excited to shake things up, break a few rules and have some fun along the way.” Previous Spirit Awards hosts include SNL alum Ego Nwodim last year, Aidy Bryant, Hasan Minhaj, Megan Mullally and Nick Offerman, Aubrey Plaza, Nick Kroll and John Mulaney, Kate McKinnon and Kumail Nanjiani, Fred Armisen and Kristen Bell, Andy Samberg and John Waters. This year’s Spirits will also feature two new categories: Best International First Feature and a Digital Creator Award. articles.title: Justin Long, Banks Pierce & Katy Mixon Greer Starring In Family Pic ‘Slater’s Gold’; Producer-Director Launches Texas Studio — AFM
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Britt Robertson Joins Kellan Lutz In Faith-Based Survival Thriller ‘The Rescue’ — AFM Andy Garcia Joins Tim Roth & Timothy Spall In ‘Murdering Michael Malloy’ — AFM May El-Toukhy’s Venice Golden Lion Winner ‘Woman Unknown’ Gets U.S. Deal During AFM View All November 11, 2026 8:47am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Justin Long, Banks Pierce and Katy Mixon Greer Getty/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE : Justin Long ( Dodgeball ) and Katy Mixon Greer ( American Housewife ) will star with Banks Pierce ( The Pitt ) in family film Slater’s Gold. Also starring are Kate Wilson, Henry Heffernan, Keith Rushing, Brooke Lyons, Harrison C. Thomas, Todd Terry and Glenn Morshower. The film from writer, director and lead producer Micah Lyons ( Bad Men Must Bleed ) recently wrapped production after shooting in Shreveport, Louisiana and will be screening privately for potential buyers and sales agents at this week’s AFM in LA. Related Stories News Matthias Schoenaerts & Diane Kruger Headline 'The Writer', Thriller Set In Underground Graffiti Art World -- AFM News Britt Robertson Joins Kellan Lutz In Faith-Based Survival Thriller 'The Rescue' -- AFM Slater’s Gold “follows 13-year-old Slater (Banks Pierce), as he discovers a mysterious clue linked to lost Civil War gold. Determined to help his impoverished single-mother (Katy Mixon Greer) escape the clutches of her scheming fiancé, Everett (Justin Long), Slater sets out on a dangerous adventure through rural Louisiana swampland with his little brother Noah (Henry Heffernan) and his fearless crush Lindsay (Kate Wilson). Guided by the wisdom of his grandfather (Keith Rushing), Slater must navigate the terrifying town-recluse, unforgiving terrain, a dilapidated salt mine, and find the treasure before it’s too late. But with Everett standing in their way, Slater soon discovers that some things are worth far more than gold.” Watch on Deadline Slater’s Gold , is produced by Breath of Life Productions in association with Bleu Bayou Pictures and Aisle7 Post, with Micah Lyons, Bridget Uhles, J.C. Doler, and Harrison C. Thomas serving as producers. The team also includes Keith Rushing as executive producer and Eric Gibson as line producer. Slater’s Gold creative team includes cinematographer William Hellmuth, casting director Tracy Kilpatrick and music by Erick Schroder. Original story and songs are by Keith Rushing, screenplay is by Micah Lyons. The film marks the launch of Lyons Family Studios, a full-service film and TV studio with three sound stages and an LED Volume headquartered in Longview, Texas. In 2027, Lyons Family Studios and Breath of Life Productions will release Stigmas (in post-production), a romantic thriller starring Amelie Anstett, Robert Knepper, Mia Fugate, Harrison C. Thomas and Leah Kate, and is gearing up to shoot the Latina-driven story of Lost Girl , based on the story of Rebecca Contreras. According to the producers, Lost Girl is financed and currently in the development, packaging and casting phase. Filming is slated for spring 2027 at the Lyons Family Studios. Inspired by his own childhood, writer-director Micah Lyons shared: “I am so proud to be a part of this amazing and heartfelt story. As a child of the 90s, my aim was to make something that felt just like the films I grew up on – equal parts fun, authentic and emotionally rich, highlighting real situations that real kids go through every day across America. As an ode to the classics like Stand By Me and The Sandlot , this is the movie that millennials have been begging Hollywood to make since we were kids!” Justin Long is represented by Independent Artist Group and Yorn Levine. articles.title: Gabriella Yacyk Joins Unicorn As Head Of Comedy
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Paul Wesley Latest To Join Netflix’s ‘Icebreaker’ ‘Chucky’ Creator Don Mancini Signs With Independent Artist Group Lisa Edelstein, Kevin Pollak & Joe Swanberg Among New Additions To SM Goldberger’s ‘Your Heart Is A Hummingbird’ View All November 11, 2026 8:53am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Gabriella Yacyk Matthew Gilbertson EXCLUSIVE: Unicorn , the 360 management firm and content studio, has expanded its executive team with the hiring of Gabriella Yacyk . Yacyk, most recently Senior Director of Development at The Second City, will lead talent management and IP development for Unicorn’s comedy division, reporting directly to co-CEOs Scott Dunn and Chris Gera. “Gabriella is a true comedy industry unicorn, who cut her teeth at some of the most iconic comedy institutions,” Dunn and Gera said. “Welcoming her to our leadership team underscores our desire to identify and foster singular comedic voices, serving as true partners to talent as they work to develop new and exciting content.” Related Stories Late Night TV James Talarico Stuns 'SNL' With Post-Midterms Cameo & "Trump Freezers" Swipe Podcast Comedians Leslie Liao & Jason Cheny Team With All Things Comedy On 'Happy Fun Times' Podcast During her nearly three years at The Second City, the legendary comedy institution that helped launch the careers of everyone from Bill Murray and John Belushi to Tina Fey and Steve Carell, Yacyk spearheaded their expansion into original media for all platforms. She oversaw a slate of scripted and unscripted television, podcasts and digital originals, and launched their first digital comedy ensemble, an initiative focused on developing emerging comedic talent through original short-form content. Watch on Deadline Prior to The Second City, Yacyk held development roles at Comedy Central, where she worked with emerging and established comedians including Bowen Yang, Rachel Sennott, Ayo Edebiri, Benito Skinner, Mary Beth Barone and Stavros Halkias. Her work spanned talent development, original programming and stand-up, including Comedy Central’s Up Next showcase, Comedy Central Stand-Up Presents and hour-long stand-up specials Esther Povitsky: Hot for My Name and Josh Johnson: #(Hashtag) . Based in Gowanus, NY, Unicorn launched in April 2025 under the leadership of creator economy veterans Dunn and Gera. Previously, Dunn co-created popular digital properties Recess Therapy and Bob Does Sports at Doing Things Media, while Gera led digital content strategy at BuzzFeed and Comedy Central. Unicorn’s hiring of Yacyk emphasizes their goal of further expansion into the comedy content realm, both by building long-term infrastructure and support for comedic clients, and developing innovative IP. One recent effort in IP building is the YouTube show Human Trials , hosted by comedian Mark Normand, where comedians perform for hyper-specific live audiences — i.e., 50 bald men, 50 Gen-Z girls or 50 clowns. The show garnered 25 million views in its first week.
