articles.title: Skydance Bosses Throw Shade On Warner Bros Film Slate; Q4 Profit Will Take $200M Hit
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is A Box Office Hero With $32M Live-Action Foreign-Language Opening Record, Best Ever For Gkids – Sunday AM Update ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is King Of The Global Weekend Box Office With $63M, Towers Over ‘Ramayana’s $55M+ WW Opening View All November 9, 2026 3:53pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz Getty/Courtesy There’s a lot for Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz to be proud of in their purchase of Warner Bros . As Ellison said Monday during Skydance’s Q3 earnings call, “We have approximately $40 billion [in film] franchises which I think highly strengthen the overall portfolio,” and that “a new movie will arrive on our service every other week; film is a major driver of acquisition and engagement on our platforms.” Related Stories News Skydance Floats First Earnings Report As Hollywood Mega-Studio: Sizing Up The New Empire News Skydance Film Bosses Dana Goldberg & Josh Greenstein & The Warner Bros To-Do List: Pics That Are Ready, In The Works Or On Fire Despite potential plusses from the merger, Ellison and Kreiz also drew attention to the losses in store from Warner Bros’ 2026 film slate. More specifically, Ellison wasn’t shy in acknowledging that Paramount is in better financial waters going forward than Warner Bros on the feature side. Today’s earnings didn’t include the consolidated Warner Bros figures since the merger closed during Q4, just five weeks ago; still, Paramount brass painted a less-than-rosy picture of what’s around the corner. Watch on Deadline Said Ellison at the call’s onset, “The 2026 Paramount film slate is expected to generate $500 million more in lifetime profits than last year’s. We’ve now taken on another company with mixed results across the business…” He added, “We do have some headwinds particularly in studios where Warner Bros film has underperformed this year and will weigh on Q4 results. We’ll apply the same playbook we did at Paramount: greenlighting more selectively, prioritizing profitable streaming growth over subscriber count, optimizing linear and driving efficiency through the cost structure.” “We’ve proven it works, and we’re confident it will work again,” Ellison said, as the company is still looking at $6 billion synergies from the merger. Kreiz mentioned at the top of the call about the merger, “What I’ve seen, the various parts of the company are in strong shape. The Warner Bros. Discovery team did a good job managing their business and delivered the expected result through the close, with the one area of softness in the movie studio, and we are looking to build on their good work.” Skydance CFO Dennis Cinelli drilled down further on the red ink from Warner Bros, which saw right before the merger closed a major bomb in the Tom Cruise-starring political satire Digger , which cost $160M before global P&A and yielded $50.3M in worldwide box office. Cinelli said, “For the full year, Warner Bros is on track with our underwriting plan, with the exception of the near-term film slate. And Paramount remains on track for our 2026 guidance which is including the high-end of the profitability range at $3.9 billion adjusted EBIDTA.” The CFO added, “While the Paramount film slate continues to perform well, that will be more than offset by the continue underpeofmance of the Warner Bros film slate. Based on this, we expect to have a $200M headwind to adjusted EBIDTA in Q4. That includes films already released quarter to date as well as films that we will release going forward.” The $200M headwind is essentially Digger , more or less. There was a report out there that Warner Bros’ 2026 slate was bound to lose $800M for the full year; we know from sources that is false. Even with the expected blockbuster success of Legendary’s upcoming Dune: Part Three , the WB slate is estimated to lose around $400M, per sources. It hasn’t been a great year at the box office for Warner Bros, with global box office misfires such as Supergirl, The Bride, Digger and no film grossing more than $100M domestic. However, the Burbank lot is slightly ahead of Paramount at the domestic box office year to date, from January 1-November 9: $569M (-70% vs. same frame in 2025) to $537M (+15% vs. ’25). Combined, the two studios count $1.1 billion at the domestic box office YTD, ranking behind Universal ($1.9B), Disney ($1.6B) and Sony ($1.4B). Paramount’s high points have been Scream 7 ($121.9M domestic) and Scary Movie ($108.2M). In a further sign to Wall Street that it is cutting fat, Skydance today announced the departures of prolific filmmakers James Gunn and Peter Safran as DC Studios’ heads . They are being replaced by early-2000s Marvel exec Jeremy Latcham, who departed the Disney-owned studio in 2017 before the explosion of Black Panther, Avengers: Infinity War and Avengers: Endgame. Ellison wasn’t all poo-poo on Warner Bros today. He gave props to New Line’s upcoming 2027 Christmas event title Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum calling the movie, “a compelling theatrical offering.” Co-CEOs Shade WB Pics In First Earnings Report As Mega-Studio; Streamer News Gunn & Safran Out As Chiefs, Marvel Alum Jeremy Latcham In; Gunn Reacts Bell, Menzel, Gad & Groff To Reprise ‘Frozen’ Roles In Nat Geo/Disney Animation Series ‘Yellowstone’s Cole Hauser Preps FBI Action Thriller ‘Pale Horse’ With Eye To Star Read More About: 6 Comments

articles.title: Kris Bowers On Creating A Love Letter To Ghana & Film History With His Score For ‘The Eyes Of Ghana’ – Sound & Screen Film
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Kris Bowers On Creating A Love Letter To Ghana & Film History With His Score For ‘The Eyes Of Ghana’ – Sound & Screen Film Dominic West Joins Irish-Set Drama ‘A Weekend In The Country’ — AFM Tom Rob Smith Writing Fiction Book Based On West Memphis Three Murder Case — Thessaloniki View All November 9, 2026 4:15pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source “We wanted this score to be a love letter to Ghana and to the history of film,” Kris Bowers says of his work on The Eyes of Ghana , the latest feature from Canadian filmmaker Ben Proudfoot. The Oscar-winning musician was speaking at Deadline’s Sound & Screen Film event, where a live orchestra performed parts of Bowers’ score. Related Stories Festivals Oscar-Winning Director Ben Proudfoot Talks Historical Significance Of ‘The Eyes Of Ghana’, Scoring Doc At Abbey Road Studios & Why Project Was A “Full Circle Moment” For Barack Obama Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Tonys, Guilds & More Directed by Proudfoot, with Barack and Michelle Obama and content creator IShowSpeed on board as producers, The Eyes of Ghana spotlights Chris Hesse, the 93-year-old forgotten personal cinematographer of revolutionary African leader Kwame Nkrumah. The Eyes of Ghana details the rise and fall of Nkrumah, a towering figure of African history who served as Ghana’s first President and led decolonial efforts across the continent. Nkrumah was toppled in 1966 by a CIA-orchestrated military coup. As a result, the films made during Nkrumah’s time were ordered to be burned. Hesse is the film’s unsung cinematic hero, along with his protégé, filmmaker and producer Anita Afonu. The documentary unveils a huge archive of surviving celluloid films from Africa’s liberation era in the 20th century, which were long thought to be destroyed but were quietly safeguarded by Hesse for more than 60 years. L-R: Dela Botri and Kris Bowers perform at Sound & Screen Film JC Olivera for Deadline Bowers and Proudfoot previously worked together on the 2023 short The Last Repair Shop , which won the Documentary Short Film Oscar in 2024. The musician said he became involved with The Eyes of Ghana after Proudfoot sent him a sizzle reel of the footage he was working with. “I remember watching it in my car,” Bowers says. “After I finished watching it, I was filled with emotion just because of how much, as a Black man, my own history is lost. And it’s sad that at some point you have to give up. So, the idea that someone like Chris Hesse has preserved this history and a vision of people that look like me that I had never seen from that era made me feel incredibly moved.” The Eyes of Ghana was produced by Breakwater Studios ’ Proudfoot and Nana Adwoa Frimpong, Afonu, Bwayo and Brandon Somerhalder alongside Higher Ground’s Ethan Lewis and Vinnie Malhotra. Barack and Michelle Obama are executive producers. The film was released as a one-night theatrical event across the U.S. and Canada on October 28. It is currently enjoying a sold-out run at DocHouse in London. The film also screened at the Dikan Center in Accra, Ghana. Check out the conversation with Bowers in the video above. articles.title: Lionsgate Film ‘My Jesus’ Adds Cheyenne Jackson & Country Singer Carly Pearce Among 6 Newly Cast
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Judy Reyes To Debut Passion Project ‘Freestyle: A Love Story’ Theater Play In L.A., Starring Justina Machado & James Martinez Manny Montana Joins ‘Tulsa King’ For Season 5 Tim Robbins & Giancarlo Esposito Join Apple TV’s Wyatt Russell-Led Monsterverse Series View All November 9, 2026 4:17pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Abby Glover, Sophia Bunnell, Chloé Flowers, Pilot Bunch, Cheyenne Jackson and Carly Pearce Drue Schnelle, Alexander Finch, Lucie Keen, T.J. Baker, Vince Truspin and EXCLUSIVE: My Jesus film has added 6 new cast members, including Abby Glover, Sophia Bunnell, Chloé Flowers, Pilot Bunch, and Cheyenne Jackson . They join the previously announced cast, led by Aliza Kate Barlow: Gavin Casalegno, Monica Potter, Kay Oyegun, Beau Bridges, and Charles Esten. Country singer Carly Pearce will make a special appearance in the project from Lionsgate and Kingdom Story Company, inspired by the Anne Wilson book My Jesus: From Heartache to Hope . The music-driven, coming-of-age film follows the inspiring story of Anne (Barlow), a regular teenager who is driven by a life-altering moment to post a video of herself singing online, triggering an avalanche of responses and catching the attention of executives across the Christian and country music industries. But finding her voice means Anne must also navigate the impact her gift has on everyone around her, including the changes it brings to her family and friends and the weight of her own expectations. Along the way, she must redefine how she views herself, her place in the world, her relationship with God, and ultimately, her purpose. Related Stories Casting Anne Wilson Song 'My Jesus' Inspires New Film With Aliza Kate Barlow To Lead; Gavin Casalegno, Beau Bridges Among Cast News Aly Muritiba & Luca Castellani Talk Live-Action Short 'America,' A Tragic Love Story Rooted In Immigrant's Quest For Self-Empowerment -- The Backstory Glover will play Liz, Anne’s sister; Bunnell will play Emma, Anne’s friend; Flowers will play Carson, Anne’s friend; Bunch will play Wylie, Anne’s classmate; and Jackson will play Dan, general manager of the Grand Ole Opry. Watch on Deadline In addition to Barlow playing Anne, Casalegno plays her brother Jacob. Potter plays Anne and Jacob’s mother, Lynn, alongside Charles Esten as their father, Kent, and Bridges as their grandfather, Bob. Kay Oyegun will direct the film in her feature directorial debut and has also written the screenplay. Kingdom Story Company’s Joshua Walsh, Brandon Gregory, Andrew Erwin, and Daryl LeFever will produce, with Jim Miller, Matthew West, and Robert Deaton serving as executive producers, alongside Capitol Christian Music Group’s Brad O’Donnell and David Blackman. Meredith Wieck and Maria Ascanio are overseeing for Lionsgate. Gaby Ludlow at Kingdom Story Company and Phil Strina at Lionsgate negotiated the deals. Glover is represented by Take 3 Talent Agency, Rebel Creative Group, and Vainshtein Law. Bunnell is repped by Paradigm Talent Agency and Circle Management + Production. Flowers is repped by Gersh and Luber Roklin. Bunch is represented by CESD, Formation Talent Agency and Thruline Entertainment. Jackson is represented by Buchwald, Entertainment 360, and Lichter, Grossman, Nichols, et al. articles.title: Skydance Games Hit By Layoffs
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Skydance Floats First Earnings Report As Hollywood Mega-Studio: Sizing Up The New Empire SiriusXM Taps Tubi Chief Anjali Sud As New CEO Indie & Alternative Cinema Surges From ‘Stray Kids’ To ‘Heated Rivalry’ – Specialty Box Office View All November 9, 2026 4:40pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Skydance Games has lost a number of staffers over the last few days, making it the latest division to be slimmed down and restructured after the merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. “As part of our ongoing efforts to position Skydance Games for long-term growth and success, we are implementing reorganization and operational shifts across a few areas of our business. We have stepped back and taken some time to consider where we are investing our efforts and have made the difficult decision to scale down some of our projects,” said a Skydance spokesperson. “As a result, there are roles impacted. This is not a reflection of the talent, dedication, or creativity of those affected and we are grateful for their contributions. We are committed to approaching the process with transparency, care and respect for those who are leaving the company.” Related Stories Executives Skydance Bosses Throw Shade On Warner Bros Film Slate; Q4 Profit Will Take $200M Hit News HBO Max-Paramount+ Bundle Set To Launch In Early 2027, David Ellison Confirms It wasn’t immediately clear how many role were impacted or which projects are being scaled back. Watch on Deadline Paramount Games Studio was created last summer by the merger of Skydance and Paramount gaming businesses and that in turn became Skydance Games after the merger with WBD closed Oct. 6. The combined group is headed by president of Skydance games and experiences, Tony Driscoll, who previously worked with Fortnite . Late last month, Skydance launched a voluntary buyout program across the company as it shifted to a five-day-a-week in office policy. Co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz have promised Wall Street at least $6 billion in cost synergies from the merger, which will include layoffs . The duo earlier today presented their first quarterly earnings since the deal closed. There’s been considerable consolidation in the games sector in recent years. Last month, Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to 25% of its workforce, including at the Xbox division. “Most of my game team at Skydance Interactive got laid off today. I’m not impacted by the layoff but I’m definitely processing my emotions today. They are good peeps to work with and I would work with them again in a heartbeat. Please consider them for any open roles you have at your game dev company,” Rebecca Vessal, Senior Gameplay and Game AI Programmer at Skydance Games, wrote on LinkedIn. “Skydance just lost a ton of great talent yesterday, said engineer David Vera, on the platform, recommending several dozen art, design and engineering colleagues. articles.title: 40th Australian International Documentary Conference Announces First Group Of Speakers: Poh Si Teng, Tamara Kotevska, Basil Tsiokos & More
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew 40th Australian International Documentary Conference Announces First Group Of Speakers: Poh Si Teng, Tamara Kotevska, Basil Tsiokos & More XTR Joins Oscar Contender ‘Y Vân: The Lost Sounds of Saigon,’ Award-Winning Documentary About “The Quincy Jones of Saigon” WETA And DC/DOX Partner On New $250,000 Fund To Support Documentary Filmmaking In DC Area View All November 9, 2026 4:43pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source AIDC The Australian International Documentary Conference ( AIDC ) will be welcoming some of the top talents in the documentary field to its upcoming 40 th edition. Among the first speakers to be announced: Poh Si Teng , director of Oscar contender American Doctor and founder of Tiny Boxer Films; Oscar-nominated filmmaker Tamara Kotevska ( The Tale of Silyan , Honeyland ); Basil Tsiokos , senior programmer, Sundance Film Festival; Rachel Antell, co-founder of the Archival Producers Alliance; Mandy Chang, CEO of Documentary Film Council, and Darren Dale, managing director and producer, Blackfella Films. Related Stories Podcast Doc Talk Podcast Goes Live With Director Poh Si Teng And Physicians Of 'American Doctor' Documentary 'American Doctor' Unveils Trailer, Sets Theatrical Release Date; Award-Winning Film Follows U.S. Physicians Who Treated Children Badly Wounded In Gaza AIDC, which describes itself as “the Southern Hemisphere’s premier industry event for documentary and factual storytelling,” will unfold from March 8-11 in Sydney – the first time the conference has been held in the capital of New South Wales in more than 30 years. An online marketplace follows, running from March 23-24. Watch on Deadline AIDC speakers. Clockwise from top left: Darren Dale, Poh Si Teng, Basil Tsiokos, Mandy Chang, Tamara Kotevska, and Rachel Antell. AIDC The conference also announced its theme for 2027: Reframed, which AIDC says “invites us to look at the same realities through different lenses: to ask who gets to frame the truth, and what happens when we challenge the narratives through which accepted points of view have been historically understood. “Through guest speakers and sessions, Reframed will call into question selective reframing through propaganda, misinformation, censorship and distorted realities, and will prompt us to harness alternate ways of seeing an existing truth through a contemporary lens by bringing in new, different and multiple viewpoints.” AIDC notes the 2027 edition of the conference offers the opportunity to “look back in order to look forward, acknowledging that our understanding of the world is never fixed and ever changing. Reframed asks us to reconsider what we think we know: to reveal what has been hidden, challenge what has been accepted, restore voices that have been silenced, and shine a light on what previous frames have left out.” In a statement, AIDC CEO and creative director Natasha Gadd said, “Celebrating our 40th anniversary as we embark on a new era, AIDC 2027 will be an essential gathering place for the documentary and factual sector to showcase not only what our diverse and creative storytelling community continues to create but to also actively reframe what the future could hold through bold thinking, innovative practice and radical solutions to complex sector challenges.” Gadd continued, “Through our 2027 theme, Reframed, AIDC provides a vital forum to explore and interrogate who gets to frame the truth, the forces that shape our understanding of reality, and to consider what becomes visible when we change the frame.” AIDC’s move to Sydney has been made possible by a new Principal Partnership with the government of New South Wales through Screen NSW. “Screen NSW is proud to support the return of AIDC to NSW for its landmark 40 th anniversary edition,” commented Screen NSW executive director Kylie Munnich. “With a packed line-up of compelling speakers and sessions, AIDC is set to bring together the best minds in documentary filmmaking, commissioning and financing from around the world. “We’re excited to see Sydney become a hub for discussion and collaboration, reinforcing NSW’s position as a leading destination for the screen industry. We’re also delighted to present the FACTory International Pitching Forum, which continues to connect talented creators with decision makers and to champion bold new documentary projects.” More than 750 Australian and international delegates attended AIDC’s 2026 edition. The organization announced a group of decision makers attending for the first time in 2027 along with companies new to AIDC’s market. In addition to Basil Tsiokos of the Sundance Film Festival, 2027 participants include Howard Myers-Rifai, Head of Unscripted Originals, Foxtel/Binge (Australia); Denise Barren, Assistant Director, The Whickers (UK); Aleksandra Derewienko, Head of Sales, CAT&Docs (France); Jane Nice, Head of Development, Icon Entertainment (Australia); Cynthia Paribello, Development Coordinator, Original Content, ESPN (USA), and Caden Pearson, Commissioning Editor, NITV (Australia), with more to be confirmed. Returning commissioners and funders from high profile companies in the doc and factual space include Zoe Stinson, Acquisitions and Productions Manager, TVF International (UK); Pamela Martínez, CEO/Managing Director, Limonero Films (Spain); Bo Zhang, Head of International Department – Factual, bilibili (China); Jessie Shih, Director of Program Development, PTS | Taiwan Plus (Taiwan); Choy Lin Mok, Commissioning Editor, TRT World (Turkiye); Kazz Basma, Head of Sales & Acquisitions, Sideways Film (Spain), and Paul Wiegard, Co-Founder and CEO, Madman Entertainment (Australia). These are additional program announcements made by AIDC for its 40 th edition: AIDC MARKETPLACE & INDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT AIDC’s 2027 Marketplace & Industry Development Program will once again provide an expansive range of business and development opportunities specifically for documentary and factual practitioners. Alongside sales, acquisitions, and funding decisions resulting from AIDC marketplace activity, in the past seven years, AIDC’s industry development initiatives have unlocked over $3.6 million in professional and project development opportunities, and awards and prizes. Confirmed AIDC Marketplace attendees include representatives from high-profile broadcasters, streamers, distributors, sales agents and funding bodies like: ABC (Australia), BBC Storyville (UK), bilibili (China), Boardwalk Pictures (USA/Australia), Cargo Film & Releasing (USA), CAT&Docs (France), DMZ Docs (South Korea), DocPlay (Australia), Documentary Australia (Australia), ESPN (USA), Foxtel/Binge (Australia), Icon Entertainment (Australia), In-Docs | Docs By The Sea (Indonesia), Jambika Docs (Spain), Limonero Films (Spain), Madman Entertainment (Australia), NITV (Australia), Paramount ANZ (Australia), PTS | Taiwan Plus (Taiwan), SBS (Australia), Shark Island Foundation (Australia), Sideways Film (Spain), Sundance Film Festival (USA), The Post Lounge Group (Australia), TRT World (Türkiye), TVF International (UK), The Whickers (UK). The 12th edition of AIDC’s market centerpiece, The FACTory International Pitching Forum , presented by Screen NSW, is currentlyaccepting submissions, with projects sought across three strands; theCentral Showcase (for projects in development with internationalpotential); New Talent Showcase (for projects by filmmakers presentingtheir first major work); and Rough Cut Showcase (for projects seekingsales, distribution, and exhibition opportunities). Selected projects willpitch live to decision makers during AIDC 2027, and also compete for seveninternational pitch prizes from festivals and markets, including SheffieldDocFest (UK), Visions du Réel (Switzerland), Doc Edge (New Zealand),Docs by the Sea (Indonesia), DMZ Docs (South Korea), Tokyo Docs(Japan) and Hot Docs (Canada). The final submission deadline is Sunday, 8November. Meetings between industry guests and accredited producers will again take place through Cut to the Chase , AIDC’s curated meetings program for Business Pass and All Access Pass-holders. Now open for submissions, Cut to the Chase matches producers and their projects to the most relevant commissioning editors, acquisitions executives, distributors, sales agents, financiers and funders, with meetings with local and international decision makers participating in person taking place during AIDC and additional international meetings arranged online. Returning for its fourth year is AIDC’s slate-pitching program The Showroom , designed specifically for established Australian production companies with multiple non-fiction projects in development. The Showroom generates business opportunities through extended meetings and exclusive access to high-level buyers representing international broadcasters, streamers and sales agents attending AIDC. Applications open 18 November. The AIDC 2027 Marketplace & Industry Development program will also host a number of partnered initiatives, including the fifth year of the $100,000 Shark Island Foundation Feature Docs Pitch , offering up to four projects a $25,000 development grant and the opportunity to participate in the Shark Island Kangaroo Valley Development Lab; The Post Lounge Group Doc Pitch, with selected projects sharing in up to $35,000 of equity investment through development, production, and post-production support; and the $20,000 DocPlay Indie Booster, providing two independent feature documentaries at any stage, from development to completion, with up to $10,000 per project to boost their theatrical screening campaigns. Pitch meetings for each initiative take place as part of Cut to the Chase. AIDC’s philanthropically-funded program for emerging and diverse storytellers – Leading Lights – will also return for its 10th anniversary edition, featuring a tailored professional development program and the exclusive Leading Lights Pitch co-presented by AFTRS. Applications for Leading Lights are accepted until 6 December, with successful recipients receiving a complimentary AIDC 2027 Sessions Pass. 2027 AIDC AWARDS Set to close AIDC 2027 on Thursday 11 March 2027, entries are currently sought for the prestigious 7th annual AIDC Awards, recognizing outstanding completed works of new Australian documentary and factual content across a refreshed seven categories: Best Feature Documentary, Best Documentary Series, Best Factual Series, Best Documentary/Factual Single, Best Short Documentary, Best Audio Documentary and Best Digital First Documentary. Submissions close Sunday 22 November, with late submissions accepted until Wednesday 25 November (late fee applies). AIDC members will also soon be able to nominate Australian industry professionals for the fourth annual AIDC Southern Light Award, a $5,000 cash prize given by AIDC to an Australian documentary and factual industry luminary for their outstanding contribution to the sector. Opening date to be announced soon. Between AIDC’s combined Marketplace, Industry Development and Awards programs, AIDC 2027 has already unlocked access to over $275,000 in project development funding, professional development and prizes for delegates. Further announcements about AIDC’s Indigenous Creators Program and major new initiatives and pitching opportunities will follow in the coming weeks, with the full session program to be revealed 2 February 2027. articles.title: ‘Being Heumann’ Composer Francesco Le Metre Tapped Into Judy Heumann’s Drive And A ’70s Punk Rock Spirit – Sound & Screen Film
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt ‘Being Heumann’ Composer Francesco Le Metre Tapped Into Judy Heumann’s Drive And A ’70s Punk Rock Spirit – Sound & Screen Film Alaskan Crime Procedural ‘Wild Life’ From Juliet Lashinsky-Revene In Development At NBC Untitled Signs Nnamdi Asomugha & His iAm21 Entertainment Banner View All November 9, 2026 4:45pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source For composer Francesco Le Metre , the brief when first discussing Apple Original Films ‘ disability rights drama Being Heumann with director Siân Heder was to capture the spirit of its subject, activist Judy Heumann, through music. With his score, he says, he was aiming for something “honest and intimate” — not “too big or too cinematic” — that reflected Heumann’s “personality, her drive, her humanity, but also at the same time, the impact that she had on the community.” Related Stories News Siân Heder & The ‘Being Heumann’ Crew On Creating An Inclusive Film & Production Environment – Contenders London Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Tonys, Guilds & More One throughline to the score was the sense of a “call to action” — the “big punk rock,” DIY spirit of the ’70s, which Le Metre captured through drums. “We had to deconstruct the drumming a little bit, so we played very unconventional grooves, and then also the strings,” he explained in conversation at Deadline’s Sound & Screen Film. “We performed the strings with a guitar pick instead of col legno to convey the sense of punk rock and, again, the DIY spirit of the movement.” Strings also helped, Le Metre said, to capture the sense of Heumann as someone with drive and racing thoughts who was moved to act fast. “I worked on a lot of string textures, kind of like these short phrases that were bouncing one to another. And I did the same thing with the melodic writing. When it came to her humanity as well, instead of writing a straight melodic line, I had small motifs interweaving into one another, to represent her thoughts or impulse.” Gaelynn Lea and Francesco Le Metre at Sound & Screen Film JC Olivera for Deadline Being Heumann marks the Sicilian composer’s first collaboration with Heder, the director behind another inclusive disability-themed crowd-pleaser in Apple’s groundbreaking Oscar winner CODA . Ruth Madeley stars as Heumann, who in 1977, led disabled activists in an occupation of San Francisco federal offices, refusing to leave until the government implemented landmark disability-rights protections. Others in the cast include Mark Ruffalo, Dylan O’Brien, Madeline Delp, Rob Delaney, Ray Fisher, Michael Patrick Thornton and Daniel Durant. Heder directed and co-wrote with Rebekah Taussig, adapting Heumann’s memoir. Producers include Heder, Kevin J. Walsh, David Permut, John W. Beach and Kevin Cleary. The film premiered at TIFF in September before being released in select theaters and on Apple TV this month. Watch the conversation with Le Mitre in the video above. articles.title: Johnny Depp & Ti West Land In A Chilly London For ‘Ebenezer’ Global Premiere
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Johnny Depp & Ti West Land In A Chilly London For ‘Ebenezer’ Global Premiere Diane Warren Talks Emotion At Working With Andrea Bocelli On ‘Maserati: The Brothers’ Song: “I Was Sobbing” – Sound & Screen Film Japanese Horror Manga ‘Noah Of The Blood Sea’ Set For Feature Adaptation As Tyrus Pictures Options Rights View All November 9, 2026 5:24pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Johnny Depp attends the "Ebenezer" Global Premiere at Odeon Luxe Leicester Square Eamonn M. McCormack/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures Christmas came early to London’s Leicester Square on Monday as Johnny Depp touched down for a red-carpet global premiere of Ebenezer in the company of director Ti West and cast including Rupert Grint, Sam Claflin, Tramell Tillman, Ellie Bamber and Robert Strong. The red carpet was decked out with Christmas trees and artificial snow while 1950s festive classics blasted out in the backdrop, and if by magic, temperatures dropped, ending an unseasonably balmy autumn. The chilly conditions did not deter fans who crammed into the red-carpet enclosure, most of them there for a glimpse of Depp. He did not disappoint, arriving in a timely fashion to talk to handpicked media and then walk the fan line. Related Stories News Johnny Depp Open To Reprising 'Pirates Of The Caribbean' Role To "Send Them Off On A Better Note" Documentary Joe Perry Bows Out Of Hollywood Vampires Doc Screening As Aerosmith Ramps Up For Hollywood Bowl Gigs Johnny Depp attends the “Ebenezer” Global Premiere at Odeon Luxe Leicester Square Photo by Tristan Fewings/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures Depp’s latest role as Ebenezer Scrooge is being billed as the actor’s comeback, after being left out in cold following his high-profile legal battles with ex-wife Amber Heard. Watch on Deadline Rumors are rife that if Ebenezer performs well, it could help green-light a reboot of the Pirates of the Caribbean franchise with Depp reprising his Captain Jack Sparrow role. Whether this comes to pass remains to be seen but it was plain to see on Monday night that Depp was the main draw, with the public at least appearing to have moved on. Talking to Deadline on the red carpet, West said he and Depp had bonded over a shared love of Charles Dickens’ ‘A Christmas Carol’ as well as admiration for Alastair Sim’s performance as Ebenezer Scrooge in an 1951 adaptation. ´Ebenezer’ director Ti West talks on casting Johnny Depp as Ebenezer Scrooge: “He [Depp] was obsessed with Scrooge since he was a little kid. When he found out about the movie, he was like, ‘Alistair Sims is a huge reason why I’m even an actor.’” pic.twitter.com/A2zFDV8J5r — Deadline (@DEADLINE) November 9, 2026 “I’ve been obsessed with it since I was little kid. I would read it every Christmas, and I was into it because it was a ghost story and then I saw the George C. Scott film when I was really little and Marley really scared me,” he said referring to Clive Donner’s 1984 version. “I’ve had a fascination of it and a version in my head that I was waiting for someone to make that they didn’t make. What’s also cool about it is that it’s one of the rare stories that because it’s so enduring, redoing it, is part of the charm,” he said. West said Depp had approached him about the role when he heard the production was in the works. “He was obsessed with Scrooge since when he was a little kid also which I didn’t know and so when he found about the movie he was like, ‘Alastair Sim is a huge reason why I am even an actor.’ It was a weird cosmic thing where it was meant to be,” said West. Depp confirmed West’s account in a public interview ahead of heading inside the cinema. “I adored it as a child and to this day I know there is no better person to play Ebenezer Scrooge than Alastair Sim… the challenge is to find another angle,” said Depp, praising West for creating a atmosphere on set in which there was space to experiment with the role. Johnny Depp talks childhood obsession with ‘A Christmas Carol’ and Ebenezer Scrooge at the ‘Ebenezer’ premiere in London pic.twitter.com/hnRAOiODqS — Deadline (@DEADLINE) November 9, 2026 Not surprisingly, given West’s horror filmography, there is a gothic horror to feel to the adaptation, giving the work an extra frisson that goes beyond past big screen versions. Ellie Bamber, who plays Ebenezer’s long lost love, that it also remains very much a family film. “It’s still very Christmassy with a hint of fright.” ‘Ebenezer’ star Ellie Bamber discusses Ti West’s gothic horror take on Charles Dickens classic: “It’s still very Christmassy with a hint of fright.” pic.twitter.com/EzT3xoTHKa — Deadline (@DEADLINE) November 9, 2026 Co-CEOs Shade WB Pics In First Earnings Report As Mega-Studio; Streamer News Gunn & Safran Out As Chiefs, Marvel Alum Jeremy Latcham In; Gunn Reacts Bell, Menzel, Gad & Groff To Reprise ‘Frozen’ Roles In Nat Geo/Disney Animation Series ‘Yellowstone’s Cole Hauser Preps FBI Action Thriller ‘Pale Horse’ With Eye To Star Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: ‘Here There Are Blueberries’ Broadway Review: Evil As Banal As A Bowl Of Fruit
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Here There Are Blueberries’ Broadway Review: Evil As Banal As A Bowl Of Fruit ‘Wanted’ Broadway Review: Historical Musical Plays With Gospel Truth Richard Lloyd Dies: Guitarist With Influential Punk Pioneers Television Was 75 View All November 9, 2026 7:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Michelle Beck, Delia Cunningham, Kathleen Chalfant, 'Here There Are Blueberries' Matthew Murphy Here There Are Blueberries , the exceptional Pulitzer finalist docu-drama that opened Off Broadway two years ago to great admiration, finally makes its Broadway debut tonight at the Barrymore Theatre. The play, about a mysterious real-life cache of one-of-a-kind Auschwitz photos submitted to the United States Holocaust Memorial Museum in 2007, remains as intriguing as ever – and with source material as grotesquely mesmerizing as these candid snapshots, how could it not? In fact, the sheer emotional heft of that photo album and everything it suggests dominates Blueberries to an extent that the play itself can seem rather thin at times, not entirely unworthy of the material at hand but not on equal footing either. Revelations about the banality of evil carry a force no matter how familiar we are with the concept, but familiar we are, and Blueberries can feel somewhat naive at times in its presumption that no one in the audience has ever heard of Hannah Arendt. But in the grand scheme of things, and in light of the historical tale being told here, those quibbles with dramaturgy shouldn’t diminish the real achievement that is Here There Are Blueberries . The play is vital and more often than not riveting. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News ‘Other Desert Cities’ Review: Julia Louis-Dreyfus Gets Seriously Funny For Broadway Debut News ‘860’ Broadway Review: Billy Crystal Remembers The Stuff Of Life And Loss Performed by an excellent cast – any production that features the great Kathleen Chalfant is an opportunity not to be missed – Here There Are Blueberries is, at its core, a detective tale. In 2007, a young Holocaust museum archivist named Rebecca Erbelding (Delia Cunningham) receives a letter at her D.C. office from a man who wants to donate a cache of WWII snapshots. Delia Cunningham, Kathleen Chalfant, Michael Cerveris Matthew Murphy The offer isn’t unusual – the museum serves as a repository for such keepsakes – but the nature of his collection most certainly is. The photo collection long in the man’s possession is more than a rarity, it’s absolutely unique: The images are of Nazi officers – including some of the highest ranking and most notorious, from Mengele to Höss – in their living quarters just over the wall from the camp’s atrocities. Some are of an almost surreal vacation lodge a few miles away, where officers, SS guards and female office workers alike would be treated to days of rest and relaxation for jobs well done. One officer is given five days there for his murder of two Jews attempting to escape the camp. Such images had never been observed in photographs before, and their discovery is nothing less than historic, generating headlines across the globe, with much of the public fascination falling on the young German female camp office workers enjoying their vacation lodge days and food-and-drink treats. “Here,” says the caption (in German) of one such photo, “there are blueberries.” The play is structured as an investigation, lead by the young archivist, as the museum staff seeks to uncover the circumstances under which these snapshots were taken, who took them, who is pictured, and, perhaps most intriguingly, how on earth did they survive when all over such evidence was destroyed by the Nazis themselves as the regime fell? One such question – how did the man who possesses the photos discover them? – is easily answered: A retired U.S. Army Lieutenant Colonel (Michael Cerveris) found the album in the abandoned apartment he briefly inhabited while stationed in Frankfort at the end of the war. Why he kept them in his possession, and did so secretly, is unknowable – he died shortly after making the museum donation. Other questions posed by the photos are of a more philosophical nature. Did those seemingly carefree young women at the lodge have any idea that the office work they were doing contributed to the genocide next door? And if so, how could they ? Conrad Ricamora (foreground, right) Matthew Murphy Blueberries , for all its demands on facing harsh truths, plays a bit coy in feigning shock at the answers, as if Judgment At Nuremberg never existed, an excusable but still noticeable manipulation. A bit more difficult to overlook are other red herrings seemingly designed to give the play momentum, such as will the museum board accept the donation of the Nazi photos when its mission is to chronicle the victims, not the victimizers? It’s a stick man argument. Blueberries is on sturdier dramatic ground when new characters – the relatives of the Nazis and camp workers in the photographs – begin arriving mid-show to offer their perspectives. The sister of an office worker sticks with the usual denials, but others are revelatory, not least the grandson of Rudolph Höss, who relates an unnerving tale of his family’s complicity and his own struggles with the violence he fears is an inheritance. The grandson’s tale is riveting, as is Brandon Flynn’s performance, a stand-out in a uniformly excellent cast that, in addition to those mention above, includes Conrad Ricamora, Scott Barrow, Michelle Beck and Montego Glover, all playing a variety of roles. Derek McLane’s stark set design, dominated by the many tall-legged stand-up desks used by the museum archivists to study the photos, is stellar, as are the crucial projections (designed by David Bengali) that allows us to see what the archivists are seeing. The photos projected onto the walls would be transfixing even without the superb lighting design (David Lander) and sound design (Bobby McElver) that further an entirely earned mood of dread and even despair, never more so than during a late scene that finally gives all those unseen victims their moment in this story, and in a manner so wrenching it won’t be spoiled here except to say that another photo album enters the story, and its story of survival is every bit as astonishing as the first. Brandon Flynn Matthew Murphy In the end, Here There Are Blueberries has sailed past its own here-and-there shortcomings to land on a final thought, artfully told and with clarity of conviction: Just imagine how many untold boxes of forgotten family memorabilia and grim relics are waiting to be discovered, with secrets as efficiently hidden as those sealed away in the human heart? Title: Here There Are Blueberries Venue: Broadway’s Barrymore Theatre Conceived and Directed By : Moisés Kaufman Co-Written By: Kaufman and Amanda Gronich Cast: Scott Barrow, Michelle Beck, Michael Cerveris, Kathleen Chalfant, Delia Cunningham, Brandon Flynn, Montego Glover, Conrad Ricamora Running Time: 1 hr 30 min (no intermission). articles.title: Keira Knightley On Fans Quoting ‘Love Actually’ To Her: “It Means Nothing To Me”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Keira Knightley On Fans Quoting ‘Love Actually’ To Her: “It Means Nothing To Me” ‘Paddington: The Musical’ Sets Broadway Cast With Tony Hale, J. Quinton Johnson, Jessie Mueller & More ‘Clueless’ Actor Breckin Meyer Says He’s Reprising Travis Role & Writing For TV Series Reboot View All November 9, 2026 7:29pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Keira Knightley on 'Love Actually' Universal Love Actually has become one of the most quotable and memeable films of all time, but for star Keira Knightley , it’s a distant and vague memory. In a new interview, Knightley opened up about fans approaching her and quoting the film, but it doesn’t mean much to her. “I have not watched Love Actually since the premiere, which was when I was 18,” Knightley said in an interview with Heart . “So, I think I’m the person that knows it the least of anybody.” She continued, “I know that people have a particular look on their face and then they say things to me and I know that means they’re quoting Love Actually, but I don’t really know what it is. It means nothing to me.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories Casting Breaking Baz: Keira Knightley, Stephen Dillane & Luke Thompson To Lead Stage Adaptation Of Oscar Winner 'The Lives Of Others' Into West End News Keira Knightley, Alicia Vikander & Jamie Dornan Set For Dark Comedy 'The Worst' -- EFM Love Actually is a Christmas romantic comedy directed by Richard Curtis and released in 2003, featuring separate love stories. Knightley played Juliet, a married woman who learns her husband’s best friend, Mark (Andrew Lincoln), has feelings for her. Mark professes his love for her with giant cards, while her husband is in the next room. Juliet gives Mark a quick kiss and returns to her husband at home. The scene is one of the most remembered, but for Knightley, it was only a week of filming when she was 17 and didn’t leave a lasting impact. In fact, in a 2024 interview with the Los Angeles Times , Knightley said one of the only lasting impressions she had of the scene was that it was “creepy” and “slightly stalkerish.” Watch Knightley’s interview in the video below. articles.title: Pink Announces Sphere Residency, Becomes First Female Solo Headliner at Venue
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All November 9, 2026 9:41am Add us as a Google Preferred Source P!NK Theo Wargo/Getty Images Pink is set for a nine-date residency at the Sphere in Las Vegas next year, the pop star announced on Monday, becoming the first female solo headliner at the high tech venue since it opened in 2023. “This idea has been bubbling up for years, and I finally get to share it with all of you,” Pink wrote on her social media on Monday. “Let’s celebrate! The highs, the lows, the new, the scary, the never been done before. For the first time, I’m giving a show a home and I hope you’ll visit. It’s my FIRST EVER residency. @spherevegas, 2027. I can’t wait to have you over.” Pink will open her residency on Wednesday, September 29, with subsequent shows on October 1 and 2, October 6, 8 and 9, October 27, 29, and a final show on October 30. Presale will begin on November 18 at 10 a.m. PST, with a general onsite starting at 10 a.m. on November 20th. Pink will become the first female solo act to headline the Sphere and just the second woman overall after the Gwen Stefani-fronted No Doubt played a residency of their own over the summer. She joins a list of stars including John Mayer, Rush, Carín León and Metallica all slated to play the Sphere next year. Her residency will mark Pink’s most notable concerts since she wrapped her Summer Carnival tour back in 2024. She hosted the Tony Awards over the summer and was just nominated for entrance into the Songwriters Hall of Fame. THR

articles.title: Carly Rae Jepsen Set to Host 2027 Juno Awards
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All November 9, 2026 9:58am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The singer has released her ambitious 24-track double album 'Day and Night.' Mikayla LoBasso Canadian pop star Carly Rae Jepsen has been tapped to host the 56th annual Juno Awards next year. The singer-songwriter will also perform along with Angine de Poitrine, the Canadian Academy of Recording Arts and Sciences (CARAS) said Monday. Jepsen, a three-time Juno winner, will host Canadian music’s biggest night for the first time on April 4, 2027, while Our Lady Peace will be inducted into the Canadian Music Hall of Fame, while also performing. Jepsen for the last 15 years has released a host of critically regarded pop songs. Her breakout hit “Call Me Maybe,” initially released in Canada in 2011, blew up across the world in 2012 and earned the singer two Grammy nominations and a spot atop the Billboard Hot 100. Related Stories Movies Think You'd Never Be a Cult Member or Get Manipulated? 'Father's House' Wants You to Think Again. TV 'The Other Elliot Sister' Greenlit at BritBox With Launch of Austen Anthology Franchise (Exclusive) That followed Jepsen placing third on Canadian Idol in 2007. Her second studio album, Kiss , won album of the year and pop album of the year at the 2013 Juno Awards, while also picking up the single of the year trophy. Jepsen has just released her latest project, Day and Night , a 24-track double album. The 2026 Juno Awards, Canada’s version of the Grammys, was hosted by Mae Martin and featured legendary folk singer and songwriter Joni Mitchell making a rare public appearance in Canada to receive a lifetime achievement award. Michael Bublé hosted the 2025 Juno Awards in his hometown of Vancouver. The 56th Annual JUNO Awards will air live on the CBC network and YouTube channel and is produced by Insight Productions. THR

articles.title: ‘Shame and Money’ Director Explains Why His Int’l Oscar Hopeful About Dignity Feels So Physical
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All November 9, 2026 10:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Astrit Kabashi (left) and Flonja Kodheli in 'Shame and Money.' Courtesy of Janis Mazuch After losing their livelihood in a village, a family in Kosovo is forced to move to the capital, Pristina. But the family struggles “in pursuit of a place in a hyper-capitalist society.” This brief description for director Visar Morina’s ( Exile , Babai ) Shame and Money just teases some of the stresses and challenges its characters face amid a high cost of living. The drama had its world premiere at the Sundance Film Festival, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Grand Jury Prize. The award qualifies the film to compete for the best international feature film Oscar under the updated Academy rules. The cast is led by Astrit Kabashi and Flonja Kodheli and also features Kumrije Hoxa, Fiona Gllavica and Alban Ukaj. Related Stories Movies Think You'd Never Be a Cult Member or Get Manipulated? 'Father's House' Wants You to Think Again. TV 'The Other Elliot Sister' Greenlit at BritBox With Launch of Austen Anthology Franchise (Exclusive) Morina co-wrote the script for the vicky bane and Schuldenberg Films production with Doruntina Basha. Janis Mazuch was the cinematographer, while Joëlle Alexis was the editor. The producers are Fabian Altenried, Sophie Ahrens, Kristof Gerega, Pia Hellenthal and Morina. Oscilloscope Laboratories acquired North American distribution rights and is planning to release the movie in early 2027. THR ‘s review called Shame and Money “a tense and crushing view of the global economy through the eyes of a farmer in Kosovo.” The Sundance jury lauded the director for “his powerful and unique portrayal of human dignity in contemporary Kosovo that universally resonates,” calling Morina “a sensitive filmmaker who masterfully draws the audience into the daily struggles of a family [and who has] deep empathy for his characters.” Morina talked to THR about Shame and Money , which is his third film contending for the best international Oscar after Babai and Exile , and how it tells a story that resonates beyond Kosovo – and not only because the film shows a statue of Bill Clinton, which was erected because, as U.S. President, he led the 1999 NATO bombing campaign against what was then Yugoslavia, which forced the security forces of Yugoslav president Slobodan Milošević to withdraw from Kosovo. What was the inspiration for Shame and Money ? I shot my previous film, Exile , in Cologne. Flonja and Astrit, who are now the leads, had a tiny scene together. After the shoot, I took a picture of them, and they were standing next to each other. And when I was looking at it, it somehow reminded me of my parents. I kept going back to this image, and then Corona started, and I was thinking a lot about my parents and also worried about them. They live near Stuttgart. And somehow this image and the fact that I was worried about them got me to a point where I started to think of them less as my parents, and more as two random people being deeply influenced by politics, in their case because of Milošević. They are pawns of politics, which they don’t understand. But they have to deal with the consequences. So, the starting point was to think about how it would be if they left home now and not 30 or more years ago. Did you know the village where the family lives at the start of Shame and Money ? I actually wrote about the village I grew up in. I even wrote the film for the house in which I grew up. But it has not been used for 20 years, and it was in such a different shape. In the end, we decided to film it somewhere else. But there are actually two shots in my village. Did you focus on the universal experience that the local story, which you are telling, is reflecting today amid a cost of living crisis in many countries? I was very much focused on making the story as local as possible. And I truly believe that if I do a good job, there is no way that other people won’t find themselves in those stories and in those things. I wanted to have the actual numbers, such as the price of peppers, rent, salary – the real numbers at the time we were shooting. How do you think about life in Kosovo as being similar or different from other parts of the world? Kosovo has gone through so many very different phases and so many breaks. In Germany [where I live], for example, people are so used to many structures that they don’t even think about them. But in Kosovo, everything is so new, and you see the structures rebuilding themselves. Basically, you see society trying to make sense of all these changes. You feel like you are in a lab watching a society form itself. Tell me a bit about how you arrived at the title Shame and Money … I went to Kosovo for research, exploring the housing and job market, and spoke to people who were looking for both. Alongside the existential hardship driving these people, there was another force present: shame in front of others and shame in front of oneself. “Even your own mother doesn’t love you if you are broke,” said one man who was working as a day laborer. He sounded embarrassed when he said it. In Albanian, this sounds much harsher and more direct, describing someone who has just realized that even a mother’s love has a price. That sounds scary! This was something I thought was horrifying. But at the same time, I think there is a very strong connection between money and depression. I believe it is impossible to sustain a relatively healthy self – whatever that self may be – if you are constantly forced to prove your worth to others and, even worse, to yourself. If you have to demonstrate again and again that you are capable, that you deserve to belong, that you are something, that you can do something. This inevitably leads to exhaustion and depression. I did come away with a sense that the film was very much about humiliation versus… That was actually a very, very important part. In the end, if I break everything down, it’s a question of dignity. And that’s why we also focused on showing cows and other animals with dignity, and the work people are doing with dignity – everything. As a filmmaker, I can connect to this very much. If every day you put yourself on a street or wherever to find work, trying to convince others that you are worth being a part of it and that you are worth being seen, that you should be accepted, you get demoralized. As a visual and overall experience, Shame and Money made me feel quite exhausted, very much like your main characters. Did you do anything special to make the experience so physical and intense? That was basically the point – the physical experience. It was important not to put the characters on display, not to look down on them, [but] to take them seriously, and to put ourselves in their shoes as much as possible. They become poor, and poverty can also be portrayed in a very voyeuristic way. That’s why it was important to take the work they do seriously. So we were very keen on making any work shown be done as you would usually do it. When we didn’t know how to do something, we asked experts. Do you have any examples or so? For example, I learned what it takes to bring a person from a wheelchair to the bed. You have to make sure that the sheet is very straight; otherwise, it will get complicated and difficult for the skin. And you use your legs as a brake so he does not fall. There are all these tiny things. And that exhausts the actors. The effect of this was that it made the actors so focused on how they do things and move that their lines just came out. Their focus was less on how to say things or how to act and more on how to get this thing done. What does qualifying for the international Oscar category mean for the film and you? Oh, I´m excited. Hopefully, more people will see it. I’m also very glad that people praise the acting very much. So, yes, hopefully this will help with getting the film released in more places, and hopefully more people will watch it. THR

articles.title: Julianne Moore, Josh Brolin and Daisy Ridley Lead the Buzziest Titles at AFM
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All November 9, 2026 10:00am Published on November 9, 2026 (L to R): Stars with projects looking for buyers at AFM 2026: Patrick Schwarzenegger, Daisy Ridley, Josh Brolin, Renée Zellweger, LaKeith Stanfield, Julianne Moore Getty The American Film Market’s 47th edition, taking place Nov. 10-15 at the Fairmont Century Plaza, AMC Century City and The Pavilion in Los Angeles, arrives at a moment of near-total disruption for the independent film business. The models that have long underpinned financing, production and distribution are in flux, squeezed by consolidation, changing audience habits and a market in which the traditional routes to getting a film made and seen are no longer a given. But the upheaval is also opening doors. A new generation of online creators-turned-filmmakers — Curry “Obsession” Barker, Kane “Backrooms” Parson and Mark “Iron Lung” Fischbach among them — is proving that audiences can be built outside the traditional system and carried onto screens. “Oddly, every independent success is still seen as a fluke, or gets put in a bucket,” says Jackie Brenneman, the new head of IFTA, which runs AFM. “What’s not being seen is that almost none of these films should have happened, because the structure of the business doesn’t support independent film. That they’ve broken through the way they have is just the tip of the iceberg of demand. Once we build the infrastructure to connect audiences with the stories they want across all different screens, the numbers are going to be much bigger.” That sense of untapped demand is echoed by international sellers, some of whom are returning to the market after time away. Among them is South Korea’s Finecut, back at AFM after several years with the animated feature Long Long Night , from Korean director Kyu Bock Youm, which follows a rhino and a penguin as they journey across the wilderness together. “As one of the last markets of the year, AFM is an important opportunity to introduce titles launched after Cannes to buyers, particularly for North and Latin America,” says Finecut sales manager JD Kim. “Considering the trajectory from Parasite to K-Pop Demon Hunters , I believe global interest in Korean culture and content remains strong.” THR ’s 2026 Hot List of the titles generating buzz at AFM spans star-led packages, international genre plays, animation, prestige dramas and films at various stages of production. The common thread is a search for projects — and business models — that can find their audience in a rapidly changing independent landscape. ‘Almost You’ Image Credit: Lisa O'CONNOR / AFP, Gareth Cattermole, Stephanie Augello Almost You DIRECTOR Matt Lipsey STARS Juno Temple, Joey King, James McAvoy BUZZ AI and grief collide in this high-concept tale about a robotics engineer mourning her younger sister, who feeds years of messages, videos and social media posts into an AI replica of her. The invention brings comfort — at first — before forcing her to confront a thorny question: if you could bring someone back, should you? A trio of Temple, King and McAvoy gives the timely premise some marquee value for buyers. SALES Bankside Films, UTA ‘ A Speck in the Sea ‘ Image Credit: Daniele Venturelli/WireImage, Katie FLORES / AFP A Speck in the Sea DIRECTOR Orlando Von Einsiedel STARS Josh Brolin, Jeremy Renner BUZZ Oscar-winning documentarian Von Einsiedel (The White Helmets) makes his fiction debut with this based-on-a-true survival tale of Johnny Aldridge (Brolin), a Montauk lobster fisherman who falls off his fishing boat in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean in the dead of night, with his best friend Anthony Sosinski (Renner), asleep below deck. ‘Breakwater’ Image Credit: Daniele Venturelli, Mike Marsland/WireImage Breakwater DIRECTOR Luc Walpoth STARS Olga Kurylenko, Alex Pettyfer BUZZ Action thrillers are a go-to at any AFM, which bodes well for this neo-noir project, about a woman trapped in a toxic marriage (Kurylenko) whose plan to blackmail her rich sadistic husband (Pettyfer) goes horribly wrong, landing her and her accomplice in a fight for survival on the high seas. SALES WestEnd Films ‘Control’ Image Credit: Stefania D'Alessandro, Gareth Cattermole Control DIRECTOR Robert Schwentke STARS James McAvoy, Julianne Moore BUZZ One of the higher-profile star-driven actioners on offer at AFM, this feature, from the director of Red, features McAvoy as a man who wakes up one morning with an untraceable device planted in his head and must follow a mysterious voice’s instructions or devastating consequences. SALES Studiocanal ‘Darlington’ Image Credit: Gareth Cattermole, Dia Dipasupil, Manoli Figetakis Darlington DIRECTOR Sascha Gervasi STARS Renée Zellweger, Dominic Sessa, Peter Dinklage BUZZ Zellweger plays a faded television actress invited to reprise her most famous role — only this time in the real world. Her host (Sessa) is a reclusive tech billionaire who has restored an English country estate and lives there as if it were 1923. As she settles into his carefully controlled fantasy, the line between illusion and reality starts to blur. Alexander Payne is on board as executive producer, which should add some cachet to the package. SALES Rocket Science, CAA ‘The Face of Horror’ Image Credit: Paul Archuleta, Aurore Marechal The Face of Horror DIRECTOR Anna Biller STARS Jonah Hauer-King, Kristine Froseth, Leo Suter BUZZ Biller’s gothic horror takes its cue from Yotsuya Kaidan , Japan’s most famous ghost story and a cornerstone of Japanese horror, adapted more than 30 times, including by Takashi Miike as Over Your Dead Body in 2014. Set amid war and plague, the story follows a knight who kills a landowner, marries his daughter and vows to avenge the very crime he committed. When he betrays her, his wife returns from the grave to exact revenge, drawing his squire and her sister into the supernatural reckoning. SALES Embankment Films ‘Falcon’ Image Credit: Courtesy of @DR Falcon DIRECTOR Marco Bellocchio STARS Pierfrancesco Favino, Louis Garrel, Benedetta Cimatti, Barbara Ronchi, Valeria Bruni Tedeschi BUZZ Bellocchio turns his lens on the boardroom with this drama about Sergio Marchionne (Favino) and his bid to rescue Fiat from the brink of collapse. Framed as a financial thriller with a psychological edge, the film tracks Marchionne’s battles with General Motors and Chrysler and his mentorship of heir John Elkann (Garrel), while counting the personal cost of saving an industrial empire. SALES Rai Cinema International Distribution ‘Feed’ Image Credit: Courtesy of Getty Feed DIRECTOR Leslye Headland STAR Rosamund Pike BUZZ This new project, which Pike will also produce, could provide an injection of socially-conscious body horror in the vein of The Substance for indie buyers. Inspired by 2022 Finnish feature Hatching , it stars Pike as a Muminfluencer desperate to make her gymnast daughter an online sensation. But when she turns to a suspicious supplement to help her along, monstrous things begin to happen. SALES The Veterans, CAA Media Finance ‘Found Alive’ Image Credit: XYZ Films Found Alive DIRECTOR Carlota Pereda STARS Chloë Grace Moretz, Rupert Friend BUZZ Genre buyers get a festival-tested option here: the thriller opened the 2026 Sitges Film Festival ahead of its AFM outing. Ten years after escaping a sadistic captor, a young woman agrees to mentor a newly rescued survivor. When the girl’s story points to other missing victims, she is drawn into a deadly game of cat-and-mouse. The English-language debut of Piggy director Pereda is adapted from Carla Norton’s Edge of Normal book series. SALES XYZ Films; CAA Media Finance, XYZ Films ‘Get Rid of It’ Image Credit: Tiffany Rose, Lionel Hahn, Brianna Bryson Get Rid of It DIRECTOR Ry Russo-Young STARS Daisy Ridley, Sosie Bacon, Simon Rex BUZZ A one-night stand leaves Harper with something unexpected growing inside her in this horror thriller, which sends her and her estranged sister on a desperate search for medical help. With the man from the encounter, religious fanatics and, eventually, the FBI all in pursuit, the sisters must confront both the creature and the wounds that drove them apart. The film is scheduled to shoot in February 2027. SALES Upgrade, CAA Media Finance, Range Select ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Image Credit: AGC Marketing Gods Don’t Give Gifts DIRECTOR Zack London STARS Richard Cotton, Sam Dale, Ben Kersley BUZZ Add another name to the roster of online creators making the leap to features: YouTuber Zack London ( Gossip Goblin) makes his debut with this animated sci-fi horror anthology, set in a future where transhumanism has pushed humanity far beyond recognition. Across four stories, ordinary people turn to strange new technologies to satisfy primal urges, exposing a widening rift between body and mind. SALES AGC Studios ‘It’s Alright’ Image Credit: Paras Griffin, Mike Marsland It’s Alright DIRECTOR Scott Stewart STARS Paul Bettany, Asha Banks, Colin Firth, Gugu Mbatha-Raw BUZZ A Brit feel-good comedy with a strong music hook, this feature from Legion and Dark Skies director Stewart sees Bettany playing an aging rock star, with real-life pop singer Banks as his estranged daughter, an aspriring singer-songwriter. With a score produced by Marius de Vries, music producer on La La Land , CODA and Moulin Rouge!, this package should have AFM buyers humming along. SALES Protagonist Pictures, CAA Media Finance ‘I’m With Stupid’ Image Credit: Jenna Berman, Alexandra Carillo-Vaccino, Oriana Layendecker I’m With Stupid DIRECTOR Hannah Pearl Utt STARS Jacob Tremblay, Kate McKinnon, Ego Nwodim, Chabely Ponce BUZZ A teen comedy about two slackers at the opposite ends of their high school’s social spectrum forced to work together to try and graduate. With few mainstream comedies on offer in the market, this could be the one to get buyers to open up. SALES Upgrade, UTA Independent Film Group, After Hours ‘In Her Shadow’ Image Credit: Paras Griffin/Getty Images for ESSENCE In Her Shadow DIRECTOR Rowan Athale STARS Letitia Wright BUZZ This supernatural horror thriller sees Black Panther: Wakanda Forever star Wright playing Annie Cutter, a celebrated author who adopts the daughter of her estranged, recently-deceased sister, a girl her sister kept locked in a basement for five years. But after taking the girl in, Cutter begins to suspect her sister may have had a reason to be afraid of the child. SALES Bankside Films ‘The Journeyman’ Image Credit: John Parra, Francois G. Durand The Journeyman DIRECTOR Ángel Manuel Soto STARS Patrick Schwarzenegger, Leslie Grace BUZZ Blue Beetle director Soto pivots to sports-crime with this story of a down-on-his-luck tennis pro who is drawn into the dark world of match-fixing as he tries to make ends meet for his family. Schwarzenegger and Grace lead the cast. SALES AGC Studios, WME, UTA ‘The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd’ Image Credit: Benoit Soler The Life and Deaths of Wilson Shedd DIRECTOR Tim Blake Nelson STARS Amanda Seyfried, Scoot McNairy BUZZ Based on true events, this drama, which premiered to strong reviews in Toronto , follows an English teacher trapped in an abusive marriage who takes a job at a maximum-security prison in Oklahoma and falls for a charismatic inmate who is also a student in her class. SALES WestEnd Films ‘ Mare Nostrum ‘ Image Credit: Courtesy of HanWay Mare Nostrum DIRECTORS Mariano Cohn and Gastón Duprat STAR Antonio Banderas BUZZ This feature, from the Argentine directors of Official Competition (2021) should have potential beyond the Spanish-language market. Banderas stars as a container ship captain who takes on a boat of African migrants, only to land in a political storm when he tries to dock in Europe. SALES HanWay ‘The Portrait’ Image Credit: Samir Hussein, Michael Loccisano The Portrait DIRECTOR Sarah Colangelo STARS Gillian Anderson, Rebecca Hall BUZZ A pitch for a more adult demographic, this new project from Colangelo, director of The Kindergarten Teacher (2018) is billed as a Hitchcockian thriller about an acclaimed writer (Anderson) who for years has been having an affair with a married man. When he is struck ill and she can’t see him anymore, the writer commissions his artist wife (Hall), to paint her portrait, setting up a showdown between the two women. SALES Rocket Science, WME ‘Safe Space’ Image Credit: Lisa O'CONNOR / AFP, Aurore Marechal Safe Space DIRECTOR Gillian Wallace Horvat STARS Joey King, LaKeith Stanfield BUZZ Dating is hard enough without an alien. In this high-concept sci-fi comedy from I Blame Society director Horvat, an intelligent but insecure scientist escapes a toxic relationship with a co-worker, only to rebound into what may be the most toxic relationship in the galaxy: an affair with a gorgeous alien. SALES Lucky Number, WME, CAA ‘Speed The Plow’ Image Credit: David Livingston/Getty Images Speed the Plow DIRECTOR David Mamet STARS Anthony Mackie, Sharon Stone, Ben Mendelsohn, Emily Alyn Lind BUZZ Hollywood inside baseball from Mamet, who revisits the town’s power games in this black comedy about a newly appointed studio chief offered a guaranteed blockbuster — or an important art-house film championed by his office temp. The choice becomes a test of professional ambition and personal integrity. SALES The Solution Entertainment Group ‘Untitled Armando Iannucci Package’ Image Credit: Jeff Kravitz/FilmMagic Untitled Armando Iannucci Package DIRECTOR Armando Iannucci STARS Taron Egerton, Alicia Vikander, James McAvoy BUZZ The award-winning writer/director of Veep and The Death of Stalin is trying his hand at the conspiracy thriller in this hot project. Plot details are being kept under wraps but the A-list cast, and Iannucci’s pedigree, should bring buyers in. SALES FilmNation Entertainment, UTA Independent Film Group ‘Violet’ Image Credit: Amy Sussman, Kayla Oaddams, Taylor Hill Violet DIRECTOR Patrick Brice STARS Lili Reinhart, Danny Ramirez, Suki Waterhouse, Mark Duplass, Lukas Gage BUZZ A horror thriller with a tech edge, this feature from Creep director Brice follows a widower Sean (Ramirez) trying to move on after the death of his fiancée, Violet (Waterhouse). He finds new love with his childhood friend (Reinhart). But then Sean begins to receive unsettling text messages from someone, or something, claiming to be dead ex. someone, or something, claiming to be his dead ex. SALES FilmNation Entertainment THR

articles.title: ‘Survivor 51’ Castoff Brady Booker on That “Toxicity” Comment, Starving Through Challenges and What It Means to Be a “Brodie”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Terry Terrones Plus Icon Terry Terrones @terryterrones Follow Sign Up View All November 9, 2026 10:39am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Eric Macksoud and Brady Booker on 'Survivor 51.' Robert Voets/CBS ©2026 CBS Broadcasting, Inc. Logo text Professional wrestler Brady brought plenty of energy, intensity and a whole lot of “brodies” to Survivor 51 , but his aggressive gameplay ultimately caught up with him at the merge. After a chaotic Tribal Council saw even his closest allies turn against him in a 9-4 vote on the Nov. 4 episode, the normally outspoken Brady left without saying a word. In his exit interview with The Hollywood Reporter below, Brady explains his unusually quiet departure, responds to Jelly’s harsh criticism of his behavior and reveals just how much the lack of food affected him physically and emotionally. Related Stories General News Trump Reflects on Republicans' Midterm Losses, Reacts to J.D. Vance's Own Analysis in '60 Minutes' Interview TV Chris Pratt Tapped for King of Comedy Award at 2026 Kids' Choice Awards *** Let’s start with your exit. You’re a pretty outgoing guy, so it was surprising to see you leave without saying a word. What was going through your mind at that moment? I figured I was going to get some votes, but when I got to about six, I started to “read the room.” When Jeff [Probst, host] reads that last vote, it’s like a flash bang goes off. Everything just went “Eek!” and my soul left my body. When I do something brodie, I do it 110 percent. I’m balls to the wall. And when the competition ends, when that weight falls off you, you almost go back to being a regular person. I know that’s tough for people to believe. I do always have this energy, but man, it’s a different animal when I’m competing. I’ve done it at a high level with high intensity. I find that chaos fun, which is maybe why I tried to turn the game into a little bit of chaos myself. But me walking out and not saying anything was that quick thought of, “Do I blow up the game?” And that’s not how I would want it to be played. Now it’s my job to be on the jury. AAs I’m walking up there, you realize the surreal moment of what you’re going through. Only so many people have actually got to go through that. I took it all in — took in Jeff’s beautiful face one last time — and then I took my walk. Maggie, Kilby and Kristin all seemed to be firmly in your corner, yet all three voted against you. Did you see any signs they might turn on you, or did those votes completely blindside you? No, because I was worried about Kristin from the jump once Mike blew that all up. She wanted to believe me, but then I guess as it came closer to tribal and people started to hear numbers; she just ended up believing what the numbers were at. Kilby was advocating for me during tribal. But with the drama he had with Eric and him not wanting to write his name down again because I guess that’s the other option, he was looking out for his game. Then Carter and Lewis, both their names were getting thrown out. I guess that wasn’t shown as much, but they were also worried about themselves. So I appreciate them riding or dying for your boy. But no one’s pulling me aside telling me it’s the vote. No one came up to me and said, “It’s you.” And then with Thien An, she was a ride or die. Same thing with her. She never told me. I wish I would’ve prioritized that relationship a little bit more because of Thien An being so smart and being a ride or die. That’s something I may have overlooked. I truly didn’t have a number one. I was bouncing back and forth. At first, I thought it’d be Dev publicly, and then I thought it’d be Kilby because once the cool kids and the nerds split up, I thought I was going nerd side. I knew I couldn’t fit in with the cool kids. This personality, I get it. brodies are either going to love or hate me, but all I’m trying to do is elicit that reaction, so I get it and have fun doing it. I was going to Kilby, but then Kilby puts his foot in his mouth saying that stuff, and they were feeding me that he was a bad guy. I think Dev’s my number one, but in reality, Dev never was working with me because they had that previous alliance on the beach of their five that they prioritized over everything. And then thinking Maggie could be my number one when we find the boat together, but Maggie’s so frantic and we butt heads like a mom and son. Speaking of Maggie, your relationship with her was interesting. You trusted her with your extra vote and you were clearly working together, but you also seemed to be in conflict at times. Was the dynamic between you two, as you said, mother-son. Definitely. And after that first tribal where I got blindsided and I thought she was on my side. After the extra vote, Maggie saw a little bit of spice in me when I was a bulldozer or whatever, and that’s just me. When the stress is up, the intensity is up. I may be at two and they think I’m at a 10. So that’s where me and Maggie’s relationship fell there. I was a little too much brodie for her, and I get it. I love Maggie as a human being. She’s a fun player. It’s sad that she thinks I’m out here leaking everything because Dev actually walked up to me and Carter and was like, “Hey, are we going to tie Mike into this vote?” And that’s when we went over and told Mike. So great gameplay move by Dev; just further proves that Dev never really gave a crap about your brodie. I mean, dude’s great at playing to someone’s emotions. I bought into it. He’s an actor. Good for him. Unfortunately, Mike, we had this issue at Toka 2.0 that I wasn’t really caught up on. I figured we had such a good relationship that he would bring that up to me. I’m a pretty outspoken, say whatever you want, dog. We can talk. And it seems like he’s just not that type of guy. Misread that. I was actually the only person filling him in on 2.0 Beach. He would’ve got no other information. Before Patt got voted out, you would see Mike attached to Patt’s hip. You’d see them joke around, talk around, getting intimate and intricate information. But with me he would have very bland talks, very business, small talk, move on, very bland, boring. So I guess I’m glad that I could give him a little bit of personality, get him all spiced up and fired up at me. But all I was trying to do was keep brodie involved in the game. You and Kilby had mentioned at the start, right after the merge, that Mike was the person you were going to target. If he hadn’t won immunity, do you think the roles would be reversed and he’d be out and you’d still be in the game? Oh, 100 percent. If Mike doesn’t turn on me there, I still may be trying to be like, “Well, are you sure Mike?” Maybe a bigger threat or maybe Eric, because he’s someone’s extra number. And that’s when I probably should have refocused. The Kristin vote was getting thrown out there and it was only out there because everyone’s deathly afraid of her. She’s Moby Dick and we got to all team up to be Captain Ahab. I’ve never seen a more prepared, strategic, even keel player. If I got on the beach with Kristin day one, that’s who I would’ve died on that beach to make my number one. I knew after her making relationships with other people coming to us, she’s awesome. I knew how much I loved her then. Jelly had some pretty harsh words about you, saying you brought “a level of toxicity to this game that no one needs” and were always trying to take control. Did you have any idea she felt that way, and what’s your reaction to hearing that now? No, absolutely not. I mean, she’s bitter for some reason, but she was bitter with me from episode one. She always thought I was a big dumb jock. I’m not surprised. She was so bitter, but I never did anything to her to make her feel that type of way and control her game.
