George Russell, with his self-imposed estrangement from Bertha, a storyline that carries directly over from last season’s finale , seems to be renegotiating his position to both wealth and family when most feel, like Carrie Coon who embodies Bertha, that “George needs to get his act together.” “We’d set up in the previous season that this extremely well-balanced and well-suited marriage was beginning to hit a rather rocky period, which I think is no more than real life. In films, everyone’s happy ever after — but nobody’s happy ever after in life. We wanted to go on with that and explore it, and see the extent to which they could come together again or not,” says Fellowes. The first episode hints that George is clearly not himself. With another business crisis on hand, he’s even barking at their son Larry (Harry Richardson). Investigators may have also found George’s would-be assassin. “It’s a total life reset for George,” is how Morgan Spector explained his character dynamic during the press conference at The Plaza Hotel. “His relationship with Bertha, has, if not collapsed, at least fallen on hard times. He’s been nearly killed and he also failed his daughter [Gladys] catastrophically. “For George,” he continued, “the relationships with Gladys and Bertha — not so much with Larry — are central to his concept of himself as a good human being. He’s really failed in both of these areas, and his capacity to compartmentalize and be business-ruthless, but loving father at home, is all out the window. Now he’s got to figure out how he can think of himself as a decent person and what his principles really are going forward. That’s all at play in this season.” After nearly losing Gladys ( Taissa Farmiga ), and sparring with Lady Sarah (Hattie Morahan), the duke’s sister, over why a mother would choose her child over the male heir if only one could be saved during childbirth, Bertha is at least pleased that Hector (Ben Lamb), the duke, if it came down to it, chose to save his wife over his child, his heir. “Gladys is doing great, and Bertha feels vindicated about that,” he says. Had Gladys been able to choose between herself and the baby, Farmiga, who is not a mother herself, tells THR , that since “there’s such a high mortality rate for infants at that time, it’s expected that something is probably going to go wrong. And I think at that point she would probably choose herself for the first one, at least.” While Bertha has secured Gladys’ future and place in society, Enid, her former lady’s maid who made a play for George, is still on a journey to lock hers down. “Social mobility and so on and so forth are all represented in the wedding of Oscar and Enid where they are marrying for many reasons, but none of them have to do with romantic love. And you know that was a reminder that we’re back in this very worldly group,” says Fellowes. “She just wants power,” Kelly Curran said of Enid. “And society is her runway to achieve that. Just as Oscar doesn’t have to hide his homosexuality from her, she doesn’t have to hide her ambition. “She sort of ascends each season,” Curran explained. “Now, she has the full support of the van Rhijn family name and this partner who’s really her best friend. It’s an incredible trajectory. So not only can she feel that kind of security and support for the first time in her life, but now she can do something with it. She has a vision and she has taste and she plans.” “They are very unified in their vision of a new society,” Blake Ritson chimed in of Enid and Oscar’s pairing. “Even though they come from very different backgrounds, they’re kind of kindred spirits. They like being disruptors, effectively.” Their union also brings hope to Oscar’s mother Agnes van Rhijn, played by the fantastic Christine Baranski . Fresh off the wedding, she’s downright giddy about hosting a dinner for Grover Cleveland, the President of the United States, as vice-president of the New York Historical Society in the home she shares with her sister Ada Forte. After grieving her husband’s death last season, Ada is finding a new sense of confidence which includes saying no to funding Agnes’s presidential dinner. That leaves an opening for Enid. While news of her daughter-in-law’s servant past doesn’t thrill Agnes, Enid’s ability to finance her dinner does. Cynthia Nixon , who plays Ada, loves Agnes’s new attitude. “One of the delightful and hilarious things that we get to see this season is unhinged Agnes,” she shared. “The ambitions of the Gilded Age were worldly ones,” Fellowes reminds us. “This was not a particularly spiritual society. And they weren’t wrestling as we are where everyone’s always trying to look nowadays like the most generous, charitable person on earth. And you ask any film star what they care about and they go ‘well, what I care about is the destruction of the environment.’ Really, what they care about is what their agent has managed to get with the size of their trailer, but they don’t want to say that, and so they create this illusion. “Well, similarly, in The Gilded Age , what everyone wanted to look like was the most successful person on earth. And a lot of the palaces they built, the clothes they wore, the things they did, were all designed to frame and exaggerate their success. I suppose we remind people [of that],” says Fellowes, who also created Downton Abbey . “After all, it is The Gilded Age ; it’s not The Golden Age. And “gilded” means there is an element of falseness that you’re trying to make something look better than it is, and that’s exactly what they were trying to do.” Peggy’s journey is not false, but rarified for any woman, especially for a Black woman of the time. Everything seems to be going Peggy’s way — personally and professionally. As she prepares for her wedding to Dr. William Kirkland (Jordan Donica), her once contentious soon-to-be mother-in-law Mrs. Kirkland (Phylicia Rashad) has become quite agreeable, even helping to plan the wedding, buying the wedding dress, and inviting her and her mother Dorothy Scott (Audra McDonald), whom she sparred with just last season, to join her “ladies club.” Not only has Peggy’s book Friends in These Times been published, publisher Ada and good friend Marian, she later beams to Agnes, is “talking about a lecture tour.” And her fiancé William, she brags when Ada asks, “is right behind me, urging me on at every step.” Peggy just couldn’t be happier. “She’s sort of undeniable in her Renaissance Woman era, which is exciting,” Denée Benton observed of her character this season. Judging by the first episode, Marian doesn’t fare too well this season. Caught off guard by all the fun she had at her cousin Oscar’s naughty after-party for his and Enid’s wedding at the very type of “establishment of ill-repute” she ended her engagement to Larry Russell (Harry Richardson) for attending last season , Marian, or Ms. Brook rather, stumbles greatly. Caught in a storm that results in Larry’s carriage being grounded, Marian finds herself in a hotel with Larry. Although they both have their own rooms, Larry knocks on her door and sweet talks his way in. Intoxicated by the air of freedom, Marian makes the one mistake her aunts Ada and Agnes had warned her against since the first day she showed up on their doorstep. And, once the sun comes up, the weight of losing her sexual purity fully hits her hard. By today’s standards and customs, especially since she and Larry are clearly in love, Marian’s horror may seem overblown. But Louisa Jacobson in later conversation with THR alongside her co-stars Denée Benton, Harry Richardson and Ben Ahlers reaffirms just how serious the situation truly is. “Marian is the person who reminds us of the way that things were then,” she says. “We have to remember what time period we’re living in — this is the 19 th century! Having premarital sex was the biggest cardinal sin.” That decision, she further explains, could absolutely cost Marian everything. “There’s an external obstacle,” Jacobson says “If people were to find out what happened in episode one between the two of them, she would be put out on the streets; she would be destitute; she would lose marriage prospects; her life would be completely ruined. And that is real. “And that is really hard to understand as a 2026 audience with all the freedoms that we have, and bodily autonomy that we hopefully still have,” she continues. “I think it’s more about there’s an external obstacle there, and there’s the internal obstacle of shame that has been baked in and really internalized due to decades and decades of women learning like these sort of Victorian purity and moral ideals that women were held to. So I think it becomes less about Larry and love, and more about how to navigate those waters and those obstacles.” As time stamped as Marian’s situation appears, The Gilded Age ’s appeal lies in its ability to resonate with today’s sensibilities. That Fellowes says has more to do with human nature. “At the basis of any drama series, you have to remember that human beings don’t change much. And so things that were worrying people in 1500 are probably still with us. You know nobody’s got enough money, and did they marry the right person, and why did their children do what they’re told anymore? You can find all of that in Socrates. And you know it’s still with us. I always hesitate to claim a message. You know, Sam Goldman, if you want to send a message, go to Western Union, and I slightly agree with that. But I do think that it’s good for people to realize that what they’re going through is not unique to them, or because they’re unusually cursed, or whatever it is. But in fact, it’s just part of being alive, and I think that in that way you can make a period drama feel modern because so much of what they’re going through is modern,” Fellowes says. Warfield agrees: “Period dramas are both timely and timeless because they deal with the fragility of you know the human experience. Of course, ours happens to be set in the Gilded Age, and we’re living through another Gilded Age, so history rhymes.” And those miss-if-you-blink cameos by David Letterman and Matt Damon don’t hurt either. *** New episodes of The Gilded Age drop every Sunday at 6 p.m. PT/9 p.m. ET on HBO until Dec. 20. THR

articles.title: John Turturro on Choosing Christopher Walken as His ‘Severance’ Love Interest and Auditioning to Play Madonna’s Boyfriend: ‘She Really Kissed Me’
articles.full_text: Nov 9, 2026 9:15am PT John Turturro on Choosing Christopher Walken as His ‘Severance’ Love Interest and Auditioning to Play Madonna’s Boyfriend: ‘She Really Kissed Me’ By Isabelle Farina Plus Icon Isabelle Farina Latest John Turturro on Choosing Christopher Walken as His ‘Severance’ Love Interest and Auditioning to Play Madonna’s Boyfriend: ‘She Really Kissed Me’ 2 hours ago Tate McRae and Doechii Choreographer Robbie Blue Among World Choreography Award Winners 12 hours ago ‘I’ve Had It’ Podcast Hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan Apologize for Laughing at Charlie Kirk Joke: ‘We Regret It’ 23 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source With over 120 acting credits to his name, John Turturro has accrued a long list of what-ifs and missed opportunities, including a role as Madonna’s boyfriend. Turturro joined Variety’s co-editor in chief Ramin Setoodeh to chat in partnership with the Miami Film Festival and receive the Creative Vanguard Award. In this conversation, the seasoned actor recalled his memorable audition with the pop star in her early days for the 1985 comedic “Desperately Seeking Susan.” Related Stories Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE) “I auditioned for Madonna’s boyfriend. I didn’t know who Madonna was,” Turturro said. “She wasn’t that famous, and we had a kissing scene and she really kissed me. I mean, deeply. I was like, ‘I’ve never been kissed like that in an audition.’ I dropped all my sides, all my pages on the floor. I was like, ‘I thought this was an audition. I didn’t know it was this kind of movie.’” Ultimately, he didn’t get the role as her fictional boyfriend — he played the comical club manager Ray instead — but he claimed her interest in him lasted long after their audition, but he preferred they stick to being friends. “Because some people, you feel like maybe they want to absorb you and I didn’t want to be absorbed,” Turturro said. “I do like her; we’ve always gotten along, but because we didn’t get absorbed. I haven’t seen her in a long time because she was married to all these different guys. I’m married to one woman. One wife is enough. That’s my motto.” Turturro’s extensive filmography means he has stories like this with some of the biggest names in Hollywood, including Martin Scorsese, Tom Cruise, Spike Lee, the Coen brothers, Adam Sandler, Zoë Kravitz and Meryl Streep, to name a few. Along with his slew of interesting stories, his vast career has granted him the freedom to choose which roles he agrees to and which he declines. For Turturro, big-budget franchises versus indie films or plays are two kinds of jobs that fulfill different needs: one gives him financial stability, the other gives him the opportunity to grow as an actor. “[Franchises are] my electrical job, and my other kind of job is my plumbing job, so I consider myself a plumber and then I do some electrical work,” Turturro said. He also revealed he was trusted with the decision of who would play his love interest in Apple TV’s hit series “Severance.” He chose longtime friend Christopher Walken. “He’s actually underestimated,” Turturro said of Walken playing his romantic interest on the show. “People don’t realize the different things he can do. He has a vulnerability to him and a delicacy that people sometimes think is strange, but he’s actually a delicate person and that was the reason I did the show.” It was helpful for Turturro to have a comrade on set because COVID-19 made the Season 1 shooting conditions less than ideal. “With masks and shields, and in that office, it was easy to have a nervous breakdown in that place,” Turturro said. “I was like, ‘I got to get out of this place if it was the last thing I had to do.’” While he is keeping his character Irving’s future in “Severance” under wraps, the actor was eager to discuss his latest starring role as Harry in “The Only Living Pickpocket in New York,” especially the film’s “beautiful” script. “It had a radical gentleness, and so many things nowadays are just in your face,” Turturro said. “The news is in your face, sports are in your face, movies are in your face. I felt there was a humanity to the world, and also there’s an element of class in it that people are struggling to live. That’s what makes an interesting character: obstacles.” Turturro’s portrayal of the complex character has begun to generate Oscar buzz for him — a nomination he has yet to receive in his decades-spanning career. But awards are not at the front of his mind when choosing which projects to participate in. “This is a crazy lifestyle,” Turturro said. “Time becomes more precious as I get older. So, I want to know if I’m going to do something, what am I going to do? And is it something I want to do? And I don’t want to repeat myself. I want to add to whatever I created. I’m not interested in doing the same, singing the same song. Sometimes some singers have to always sing that hit song.” Nate Bargatze Returns to Netflix With New Special ‘Good for Nathan’ (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 9:22am PT Pink Announces 2027 Sphere Residency in Las Vegas By Steven J. Horowitz Plus Icon Steven J. Horowitz Senior Music Writer speriod Latest Paul McCartney Becomes a Billionaire, Making Him the World’s Third-Richest Musician 1 hour ago Katseye Postpones Chicago and Minneapolis Shows Due to Megan’s Illness 4 days ago Trent Reznor and Atticus Ross to Score David Fincher’s ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’ 7 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kurt Iswarienko Pink has announced that she will be staging a residency at Las Vegas’ Sphere in 2027, making her the first solo female pop artist to headline the venue. The pop singer is slated to perform a string of dates next fall. Dates for the residency are September 29, October 1, October 2, October 6, October 8, October 9, October 27, October 29 and October 30. In a post on social media, Pink shared that the show has been in the works for quite some time. “Makes me think of celebration. Makes me feel like I’m on top of the world,” she wrote. “This idea has been bubbling up for years. And I finally get to share it with all of you! Let’s celebrate! The highs, the lows, the new, the scary, the never been done before. For the first time, I’m giving a show a home and I hope you’ll visit. It’s my FIRST EVER residency. @spherevegas, 2027. I can’t wait to have you over. 🩷” Related Stories Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE) View this post on Instagram Artist presale registration is currently available on Pink’s website . Presale begins on November 18 at 10 a.m. PT, while Vibee package presale starts November 11 at 10 a.m. PT. General onsale starts November 20 at 10 a.m. PT. To coincide with the Sphere residency, the SlotZilla zipline at Fremont Street Experience will be rebranded as “P!nkzilla” for a limited aerial attraction. It will run from November 11 through November 19. Pink most recently staged her “Summer Carnival” tour across 2023 and 2024, followed by her “Trustfall” tour in 2023 and 2024. She was nominated for the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame earlier this year, joining a spate of artists including Mariah Carey, Lauryn Hill, Oasis, Shakira and Luther Vandross. This past June, she headed to Broadway to host the 79th Tony Awards. More recently, Pink made headlines after facing backlash for reposting a call for Macklemore to be dropped from the Ed Sheeran tour in the wake of his nightly pro-Palestinian songs and statements. She swiftly made her perspective clear, posting a long message about the controversy. “To the ones who are furious with me: you don’t have to agree with me,” she wrote. “You never did. That’s been our unspoken agreement for twenty-five years, and it still stands, and so do I. You don’t have to agree with one thing Israel’s government does to not want the Jewish family two rows down from you to be scared or targeted at a concert. That’s the only thing I’m asking anybody for. To the ones who are frightened this week, Jewish or Muslim or Palestinian or Israeli or just tired of all of it: I see you. And if anybody wants to really know what I think, just ask me. I’m right here. I’ve never been hard to find. And I’ll keep speaking out, in my own words.” Nate Bargatze Returns to Netflix With New Special ‘Good for Nathan’ (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Gordon,’ a Big Netflix Series From Argentina, Unpacked by Pablo Trapero and Star Rodrigo de la Serna
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 9:28am PT ‘Gordon,’ a Big Netflix Series From Argentina, Unpacked by Pablo Trapero and Star Rodrigo de la Serna A car thief turned Argentina Dirty War death squad member, torturer and ‘perverse psychopath,’ Gordon begs the question of how such a monster could have gained so much power in 1970s Argentina. The series answers that question By John Hopewell Plus Icon John Hopewell Chief International Correspondent john_hopewell Latest ‘Gordon,’ a Big Netflix Series From Argentina, Unpacked by Pablo Trapero and Star Rodrigo de la Serna 2 hours ago Sanfic Prizes: ‘Monguen’ and ‘Narciso’ Win at Pared-Back Ceremony Due to Sudden Demise of ‘A Fantastic Woman’ Director Sebastián Lelio 1 day ago Seville European Film Festival Honors Agnieszka Holland, Thierry Frémaux and Cartoon Saloon 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rodrigo de la Serna in 'Gordon' Credit: Marcos Ludevid 2025 A Netflix Nov. 18 bow, Pablo Trapero ’s “Gordon,” led by “Money Heist” star Rodrigo de la Serna , weighs in and is shaping up as Argentina’s series of the year. Set over 1970-76 and shot over seven months with large cinematographic ambition by two of Argentina’s greatest directors, Trapero (“Leonera,” “The Clan”) and Pablo Fendrik (“The Bronze Garden,” “Amongst Men”), “Gordon” lifts the lid on the real-life Ánibal Gordon – an infamous torturer, psychopath and sybarite of violence – and through him Argentina’s biggest horror story, its 1974-83 Dirty War. Related Stories Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE) If periods of terror can have its icons, one of the War’s was Gordon who acts like a “sci-fi portal, opening doors to Argentina’s different universes of the time,” says Trapero. “Gordon,” a seven-part period psychological action thriller, marks the return of Trapero to his native Argentina after eight years. Unlike the famed international series he has co-directed of late, such as “ZeroZeroZero,” here Trapero also co-writes, with Marcos Osorio Vidal, a sign of his artistic investment in “Gordon.” It’s also a return to the near same time period and film noir-melodrama mix of 2016’s “The Clan,” Trapero’s best festival and commercial hit, a portrait of Argentina’s well-to-do Puccio family which kidnapped and murdered associates for money. Winning a best director Venice Silver Lion, “The Clan” went on to gross $20.4 million worldwide, rating as a blockbuster in Argentina. Hypnotic and nightmarish, “Gordon” first captures its protagonist, played memorably by De la Serna, in a car with his wife and infant son crossing Argentina’s huge grassy Pampa plain to a new home.He courteously greets an old man steering a cart and horse they pass, takes in a wounded puppy and later sipping tea from a porcelain teacup with a new neighbor, Dora, the widow of a Vice-Admiral. “You look like you have a military bearing. Were you in service?” Dora asks at the start of a series’ trailer. “No, no, I’m a simple businessman,” Gordon answers, but is obviously flattered. His gentlemanly charm is also, however, a mask. Cut in the trailer to Gordon and a gang checking revolvers for a robbery, then a torched getaway car aflame after a heist and Gordon being rowed across a lake in the spectacular scenery of Patagonia to pull off another job. Settling in at his new home, Gordon, a dandy, soon builds a secret passageway in his new home to escape from his house and spy on his own family, adopting the self-assumed airs of a quietly dashing domestic James Bond. In real life, Gordon joined Argentina’s military intelligence services as a secret agent in 1968, became a leader of pre-Junta dictatorship Triple A death squads, then, from May to November 1976, director of Automotores Orletti, one of the regime’s most heinous subversive detention and torture centers. How such a monster as Gordon, a car thief in his youth, scaled the ladder of power in 1970s’ Argentina is one of the most pertinent questions the Netflix series seeks to explain. “Gordon” is produced by Adrián Suar, a driving force in Argentine film-TV as an actor, producer at Pol-ka Producciones (“Son of the Bride,” “Violetta”) and former Canal 13 programmer. Suar produces “Gordon” with Diego Andraznik his partner at their new production house, Preludio Producciones. Trapero and De la Serna unpacked “Gordon” in the buildup to its Netflix release on Nov. 18, when it is sure to make an impact. Part of the attraction of classic crime shows is that the forces of order trap the criminal and explain their criminality. Part of the fascination of “Gordon’’ is that he becomes part of the forces of order…. Pablo Trapero : The idea of “Gordon” was to begin with fiction with real events providing their context. Gordon carries the story from beginning to end. He’s like a sci-fi portal , opening doors to Argentina’s different universes of the time. So the most difficult and highly attractive challenge was to make viewers want to watch more about a villain who becomes ever more villainous, for the audience to feel ever more emotion and commitment to the series. Rodrigo de la Serna : What’s interesting about Gordon is that he’s the only character who doesn’t have an ideology nor doctrine in a context of a Cold War between the U.S. and Soviet Republic where Peronism positions itself as a third option – neither capitalism to one extreme and Marxism to the other. Camila Peralta in ‘Gordon’ Cr. Marcos Ludevid / Netflix ©2026 MARCOS LUDEVID 2025 So what drove him? De la Serna : Gordon is a mercenary whose only interest was to be able to make money and experience the pleasure of exercising his true psychopathological essence. The national and international context allowed psychopaths of the magnitude of Gordon to reach places of power, make them their own, take off their masks and become the true monsters they are. It was much easier during these years. Trapero : What we suggest is that during these years, and not just in Argentina, the relationship with violence and the value of human life appeared to change. For Gordon and almost the period, violence became a commodity, without the gravity and consequences which violence really has. De la Serna : From 1955, when Argentina’s Navy bombed the Plaza de Maya, killing 400 people, to oust Perón from power, from this foundational act, the country’s rule of law is replaced by the rule of violence. It begins to be politically legitimate to kidnap and kill people and as Pablo says, violence becomes a commodity. People like Gordon can take off their masks and be the monster they have inside. Pablo, you wrote “Gordon” with Marcos Osorio Vidal, based on the novel by Marcelo Larraquy. How did you attempt to structure the series? Trapero : With the screenplay and in direction, we attempted to change genre from one episode to another so that viewers could follow the story via familiar cinema codes. Episode 1 is like a Western, where a stranger arrives and has to carve out his place, Episode 2 like a secret agent investigative thriller. Without giving spoilers, the last episode nears horror, with beats you can find in the genre. This renews the series’ interest, not only because of Gordon’s story but Argentina’s. To what extent could Gordon be seen as a return to the world and the mix of film noir and melodrama of “The Clan”? Trapero : I’m really a fan noir, a great genre, and melodrama, and here there’s a mix of these two so classic genres where viewers see things that are really dramatic but from a narrative point of view this makes viewing easier despite the subject. And it’s interesting you mention “The Clan.” It was a breakout which made me rethink many things. So much so that I began to make series from then on because, paradoxically, “The Clan” was a hit. I was left, however, with the sensation that I wanted to talk a lot more about this world and that the length of a film wasn’t sufficient, what was needed by the story and the characters. And Gordon offered a kind of return? Trapero : With time I understood that “Gordon” was in a way a revenge, allowing me to return to a similar period, tone and universe, with more time for us and for viewers, to contradict our own sentiments, which is what I think is happening when people watch “Gordon.” In one episode, they feel something about an issue and in another the opposite. In one episode, viewers are annoyed, in anther react in a more relaxed fashion. Rodrigo has delivered a magnificente performance in the sense of fascinating an audience – as we’re beginning to see is the case – with a story which asks so much of viewers. Rather like with “The Clan,” the paths sometimes recommended to attract audiences aren’t those of “Gordon.” Could you give an example? Trapero: If something was predictable, we tried going the other way, to see how it worked. In this sense the work of Rodrigo is extraordinary, how he gets viewers to follow Gordon. And the rest of the cast as well. Because it’s a story which depends a lot on an audience identifying with a tale which is foreign to them. There’s not one character in the series from beginning to end with whom you ca feel identified with, how they conceive the world. Perhaps a little bit with one at some time, a little bit with another at another moment, but it’s very difficult. What were the keys to your performance, Rodrigo? De la Serna : An absolute lack of empathy for others, an “anti-conscience,” you could call it. For an actor, it was an immense challenge This is the darkest role that I’ve ever had. It very close to a vampire or a demon, or he really was a demon, the darkest shadow which a people have dreamed. The Argentine people has its luminous side, but also produces this type of monster. I had to focus on Gordon’s psychopathology. He’s a compendium of all the pervasions I could cover and conceive, like a man who loses what is considered humanity: empathy with others, or an effort to work for a common good, which is what other characters are attempting. He’s a psychopath and perverse, enjoying others’ suffering. And your aims as a director, Pablo? Trapero : The large challenge from early on in the screenplay was how to cover a period which is so dark and so little visited: in audio-visual fiction, there are very few references to this period of Gordon’s life covered by the episodes. It was like opening a Pandora’s box, touching a taboo, something you couldn’t talk about out of fear and the complexes it generates. That drove our writing. Using fiction, we also wanted to bring the youngest generations something which might appear fit for history books, so that we don’t forget about what happens with violence. Sometimes in slogans or on social media violence seems abstract, but it’s beside us all the time and our duty as citizens is to care for others. ‘Gordon’ Cr. Marcos Ludevid / Netflix ©2026 MARCOS LUDEVID 2025 Nate Bargatze Returns to Netflix With New Special ‘Good for Nathan’ (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

articles.title: James Gunn Speaks Out After Stepping Down at DC, Says It Had ‘Highest of Highs’ but ‘Has Been Trying’: ‘I Dislike the At-Times Corporate Nature of the Job’
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 9:56am PT James Gunn Speaks Out After Stepping Down at DC, Says It Had ‘Highest of Highs’ but ‘Has Been Trying’: ‘I Dislike the At-Times Corporate Nature of the Job’ By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Donnie Dunagan, Original Voice of Bambi, Dies at 92 59 minutes ago James Gunn Speaks Out After Stepping Down at DC, Says It Had ‘Highest of Highs’ but ‘Has Been Trying’: ‘I Dislike the At-Times Corporate Nature of the Job’ 2 hours ago Box Office: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Stomps to $6.7 Million in Previews 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images James Gunn has spoken out after he and Peter Safran were replaced by Jeremy Latcham as the head of DC Studios . In a surprising move on Monday, Skydance replaced Gunn and Safran with Marvel veteran Latcham as the president and chief creative officer of DC Studios. It ends Gunn and Safran’s four-year run as the heads of DC Studios, where they rebooted the superhero universe with “Superman,” “Supergirl,” “Clayface” and the HBO series “Lanterns.” Related Stories Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE) Gunn, who is a frequent social media user and regularly chatted with fans on X and Threads, posted a lengthy statement after the news of his stepping down. He gave a shoutout to Safran and thanked the DC fans, but he also spoke out about the challenges of the job. “What only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least,” Gunn wrote. “I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that). I’m always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker I would at least get to take short breaks to unwind, and I’ve stolen even that time from both myself and my loved ones over the past four years” View this post on Instagram Read his full statement below. Oh, boy. What a four years. Thanks to all of you who have supported me and Peter in our time as the heads of DC Studios. When I was a kid growing up in Manchester, Missouri, I used to write and draw my own comics with a mix of DC Comics characters and my own characters. Having full access to these characters to do whatever we wanted has been a dream come true. I didn’t know if I wanted this job when it was offered to me, but I just couldn’t pass up the unique opportunity. I’m glad I took the job. There have been so many highs along the way – releasing Superman and Clayface, making Peacemaker, reading the scripts to The People Vs, the entire process of Man of Tomorrow, which thus far has been the best filmmaking experience of my life, and numerous other moments. The highest of the highs have been all the talented and wonderful people I’ve worked with and grown to love: the DC Studios crew, our talented collaborators, our casts and crews, and the boisterous and hilarious fans. And the best part of all has been working with Peter Safran , the smartest and most competent person I know. You’ve been the best partner a person could ask for, and, more so, a truly good friend. But what only the closest people to me have known over the past four years is my time at DC Studios has been trying, to say the least. I dislike the at-times corporate nature of the job (thanks to Peter for taking the brunt of that). I’m always a very hard worker, but as a filmmaker I would at least get to take short breaks to unwind, and I’ve stolen even that time from both myself and my loved ones over the past four years (Jenn, I love you and I’m sorry and you don’t need to feel guilty for being the happiest of all people that I’m no longer doing this job). And the thing my ADHD hyperfocus has had the most difficulty with has been dividing my time between projects I’m incredibly passionate about and the ones I’m not so much and all the things I have to do as a studio head. So, yes, I will miss the people around me, and I will miss being the co-caretaker of these great characters, but I’m also incredibly relieved and excited to get back to pure filmmaking. That’s not to say Peter and I are immediately done with DC or superheroes. We have Man of Tomorrow out this summer. And we’ve just been engaged on another DC project which I’m writing, and we’ll see where it goes after that. And, of course, the characters we set up will live on. Thank you so very, very much for embracing the characters and stories we’ve put on screen. Love and gratitude, James Gunn Nate Bargatze Returns to Netflix With New Special ‘Good for Nathan’ (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Love Is Blind’ Star Rob Feeley Breaks His Silence on Michaella, the Beekeeper and Why He Nearly Skipped the Reunion
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 10:00am PT ‘Love Is Blind’ Star Rob Feeley Breaks His Silence on Michaella, the Beekeeper and Why He Nearly Skipped the Reunion By Clayton Davis Plus Icon Clayton Davis Chief Awards Editor byClaytonDavis Latest Oscar Predictions: Best Casting — ‘Being Heumann’ and ‘La Bola Negra’ Found the Year’s Boldest Discoveries. Will the Academy Reward Them? 21 hours ago Oscar Predictions: Production Design — Could Something as Innovative and Cool as ‘Backrooms’ Find Love? 2 days ago Jesse Eisenberg and Julianne Moore on ‘The Debut,’ Testing AI to ‘Make Sure It’s Bad’ and Hoping ‘Now You See Me 4’ Gets Made 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix Rob Feeley is sitting in his car. He’s taking the Zoom call from the driver’s seat, two days before the “ Love Is Blind ” Season 11 reunion drops on Netflix — and almost two years following the night that turned him from fan favorite into the most talked-about man on the Boston edition of the dating series. He’s screened the reunion, and the first thing he wants to do is get one piece of internet lore straight. Related Stories Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE) “I’m the Walmart Travis Kelce,” he jokes when asked if the Kansas City Chiefs tight end or Taylor Swift ever reached out about the resemblance that launched a thousand memes. “I’m a lot less athletic and I have a lot less money.” It’s the kind of self-deprecating line that made Feeley, a 40-year-old AI infrastructure salesperson, easy to root for in the pods. That’s where he fell for retail executive Michaella Giorgio and got engaged. But we saw something different at the reunion, as he was hunched forward on the couch with his elbows on his knees, waiting for a beating that never fully arrived. Michaella, as it turned out, saved most of her fire for beekeeper Matt Waldrip, whom she had quietly dated after filming. What did arrive this season was a reckoning. At the cast’s first get-together back in Boston, Feeley spiraled, going after Matt, dismissing the “experiment” and daring viewers to cancel him. Before that, a dinner with his five closest friends left Michaella sitting through a barrage of comments from one of them, his friend Jay. After all of it, the engagement didn’t survive. In his exclusive exit interview with Variety , Feeley alluded to a run of losses in the year before filming. Over the course of our conversation, he lays them out plainly: a long-term relationship ended, he lost his job, two of his best friends died and his father was in hospice. “I’m a human being just like all of us,” he says. “One of my worst moments was caught on Netflix.” Feeley also speaks about why he almost skipped the reunion, his 78-year-old mother who nearly flew across the country to sit in the audience and whether he’d ever do a dating show again. You were a fan favorite early in the season, and then you became the most discussed person on the show, all within a single episode. What was it like when you opened your phone after that episode aired? Man, I couldn’t even really watch it. This has been hanging over my head for a year and eight months. It was one of the toughest moments I’ve had, probably as a person. I watched it before it came out because I had to go film the reunion, but when it aired, I still had to perform at work and everything else. All the text messages, all the hate online. I’ve never really been through that. I got the internet chirps early on, when they first called me “mama’s boy” and “AI this.” But I knew this was going to be a different level. It was a hard time, to be completely honest. It still is. A lot of people were taken by the way you spoke about your mother and your father. I lost my dad in the last couple of years, too, so that connected with me. Looking back, was it too soon to put yourself in that kind of vulnerable position? I’m a person who bottles things in, and it wasn’t just my father. It’s not an excuse. I didn’t know they were going to post my exit interview, and I wasn’t trying to excuse my behavior by blaming it on losses. But subconsciously, I probably wasn’t in the right mental space. The sequence was kind of crazy. My long-term relationship broke up. I left the house. At the same time, I lost my job. Then my best friend passed away. Then my other best friend passed away. And then my father was in hospice. I’m trying to keep my head on straight, and I threw my name in the hat for “Love Is Blind.” I’d never watched the show in my life, to be completely frank. I just wanted to find love. I think all of those things poured onto me without me even knowing it. You tell yourself, “I’ll be OK. Keep moving. You’re a man. Keep moving. This is a good opportunity.” But I didn’t know what the whole thing entailed. No phones, sequestered, all of that. With my anxiety, it was a pressure cooker. There were nights in the hotel room by yourself where I’d talk to my dad. At the top of the reunion, you said you weren’t even going to come. How close were you to being a no-show? Out of respect for Michaella, I owed it to her to come and talk. She and I have talked since the show, but I felt like I couldn’t just leave her on an island. Whatever she had to say about how I behaved publicly, she deserved an explanation publicly. That was a big part of it. But who wants to go in front of America and be a punching bag? I was ready for it, though. Be a man in the night, be a man in the morning. Michaella deserved for me to go to the reunion. You mentioned going away for 50 days after everything came out. Was that a program, or did you seclude yourself? It wasn’t a program. I was depressed. You can ask my friends. I was full of anxiety. I didn’t go into my basement and seclude myself for 50 days. I just worked out, stayed away from a lot of things, didn’t go out, didn’t drink at all, ate right. And I sought counseling. A psychiatrist. I was like, “All right, I got to get this shit right.” I might have showed up to one place in those 50 days. I was very on my grind, focused on getting myself right mentally, because that was a very, very tough experience for me. You seemed grateful at the reunion that you’d made that change by going to therapy. I think it’s important for men to see men like you giving it the seal of approval. Are you still working at it? Absolutely. I just met with my psychiatrist last night. The one thing I’d tell people is, it’s not a two-day thing or a three-day thing. You can’t give up after two or three months. You have to continuously go. I’ve suffered from severe anxiety my whole life. When I was very young, my mom put me in counseling and the lady would be like, “Take your temperature and put it this way” and I felt like I could outsmart her. I had very bad separation anxiety with my mom and my little brother. My psychologist told me anxiety is just another word for fear. You fear the unknown. And that was a lot of what happened on “Love Is Blind.” If you’re going to go to therapy, don’t just go three times and knock it. It takes a long time to really get the treatment. I was surprised I didn’t see your mom at the reunion. Funny story. She’s 78. I bought a house this year and put my mom in the “in-law” apartment because her landlord was steamrolling her and raising her rent. So I still joke that I live with my mom. I have no ego. She was supposed to come to L.A. with my brother. I go downstairs to her apartment, and she’s got her clothes laid out on the bed, so cute and stressing out, like a kid going on vacation. She just wanted to support me. And I said, “Ma, if you’re doing this because you think I need you there, I appreciate it, but I can’t put you on a flight across the country to have anxiety.” And I’m happy I didn’t, because that taping was six hours. It would have been overwhelming for her. It wasn’t fair to my mother. God works in mysterious ways. My best friend came in her place with my brother. I think your mom might go down as one of the favorite parents in “Love Is Blind” history. The one thing is authenticity. She’s an authentic person. Let’s go back to “the dinner” with Michaella and your friends. What was it like watching that episode, and what were the conversations with your boys afterward? I wanted to bring five of my close friends because they’re super important to me. People asked why I didn’t bring women. I just wanted her to meet my close nucleus of friends. I didn’t know my one friend [Jay] was going to behave that way. I didn’t know he’d been drinking beforehand. Rewatching it was a complete embarrassment. I was ashamed. My friend is completely embarrassed. There’s no part of him that thinks that’s funny. In the moment, I didn’t know how severe it was. When I rewatched it, I was like, “What the fuck, jeez Louise.” Michaella didn’t deserve to sit there and listen to any of that BS. These are men of integrity. I know these guys are good people. If I could change it, I’d change it 100 out of 100 times. He and I had a serious, serious conversation. I can assure you he feels 10 times worse than I do. He’s still not back to himself. It’s affected us, it’s affected families. It’s not indicative of who we are. The one person I care about in that whole thing who had to listen to that BS is Michaella. I’ve apologized to her, and I continue to. And no excuses for Jay at all. But it might come out later, so I’ll say it. He’s also been battling stage three lung cancer. It was during that time, too. He’s in remission now, but I don’t know where his head was in that moment and it’s not excusable at all. I just know that right now he’s not in a good place. There’s no one more embarrassed than him and me about that scene. And obviously Michaella. It was tough to watch. Michaella said at the reunion that some of it came from your paranoia. You said it was the cameras. Do you feel like she will go down as “the one that got away?” It would have been great to meet in a different environment. I didn’t behave correctly under the pressure of it. I love who Michaella is. She’s an incredible human being. I think the world of her … still do. I told her I’m here for you whenever you need me, and I mean that. I told her, “You deserve better than me. There’s going to be someone who can do everything you want, and I apologize that it couldn’t be me.” Behind the pods, it was incredible. Then it got to the real world, and I thought, “Holy shit, this might happen.” And I folded. She didn’t deserve that. That’s the reality. I need to ask about “Beekeeper,” aka Matt. Michaella came for his throat the entire reunion but was very soft with you. What’s the story there? Post-show, a lot of the guys hung out. I learned that Michaella and Matt were seeing each other, maybe seven or eight months after the show. To be completely honest, it stung a little bit. No pun intended. (Laughs) You’re doing dad jokes now. Cam’s going to lose his brand. It stung naturally. But Michaella is a grown woman who can date whoever she wants, even if it’s someone from the cast. It’s not her duty to go date someone who’s not. My initial reaction was, “I hope they’re happy.” I didn’t know when they broke up. I wasn’t going to DM Michaella or poke Matt. It’s not my business. Then apparently shit went south. I think a lot of us were shocked. I didn’t know the Harry Potter stuff, the chicken cutlets. He was doubling down. He came off complimentary at first, and then I don’t know where it was going. I was just as surprised as you. That was an electric reunion, I’ll tell you that. John and Sarah were the season’s only married couple. What was your reaction to how their story played out in the end? Listen, there’s no room for infidelity in life. You pick your person. I don’t care if it’s on a TV show. You can’t behave that way. The bed you made, you got to lay in it. I try to mind my business as much as I can. Some of us knew about the text messages, the explicit things. The other things in their relationship, I frankly don’t know anything about. But you can’t text an escort or a stripper, whatever it was. He lost Sarah, so he paid the ultimate price. You don’t like to see anybody go through that hurt, and clearly Sarah was hurt. Families were involved, and it was getting ugly. Then John’s dad got involved. I think Maury is a fierce protector of friends and family. He dated Sarah in the pods, and I think he was protective of her. The father is protective of his son. It just unfolded in a crazy way. Everyone’s emotional, reactionary. My brother and my best friend were sitting right next to John’s dad, so they were in the thick of it. We were all kind of shell-shocked. Michaella’s fall at the reunion looked mortifying, but she took it like a champ. Is that just her personality? When we first met, she had these chattering teeth, like the yellow wind-up kind, because she likes to laugh. She’s self-deprecating like me. She takes things in stride. Life’s not that serious. If anything, it makes her relatable. She took a nice fall and she got up like, “Okay, then.” Michaella is very lighthearted, and that’s part of the reason I fell in love in the pods. I read body language. You’re a big presence; you take up space, but on that couch, you looked like you were in a cocoon, bracing for impact. Am I reading that right? First off, the chairs are super uncomfortable. I didn’t want to lean back and look like I was eating potato chips. My posture sucks to begin with. I’m trying not to bump into Blake on my left, trying to put the pillow under me. The easiest thing was to put my elbows on my knees. But yeah, I took it very seriously. I hurt somebody. It wasn’t a joke to me. I wasn’t coming in loose and busting chops. These are people’s lives. It’s Michaella’s life. I didn’t know what to expect. But try sitting where they had me for six hours. Where do you hope you and Michaella end up after this? Friends? I want her to live the best life ever and keep being a shining star. I think this will catapult her to doing great things. I’d like to be friends and be cordial. We gave each other a big hug after the reunion. I don’t know if they caught that. I texted her that night, like, “How did you take things? I know it was intense.” We did have something great. It was just in a really weird environment for me, and I wasn’t mentally prepared to be the person Michaella needed in that moment. Are you dating anyone? And would you do another dating show like “Perfect Match?” I might get kicked off before I even touch foot on the show. [Laughs] I’ve definitely learned a few things. But right now, I am seeing someone. So probably not. It’s not in my cards at the moment. So that’s a no to “Perfect Match” until further notice. Until further notice, that’s a no, my friend. Anything I didn’t ask that you want to say? First and foremost, I want to apologize to Michaella and not just Michaella. Anybody who was offended, anybody whose experience I ruined that night, I want to vehemently apologize. I’m a firm believer in growth. I’m a human being just like all of us, and one of my worst moments was caught on Netflix. I have an enormous friend group of great people in my community. I coach Pop Warner. I’ve worked hard to build my character and be there for people. I don’t want to let one bad moment define the person that I am. I hope some folks can give me grace. I don’t need people to feel bad for me, but I need people to understand that was one blip. I’m not blaming producers. It was my own behavior. I wish I could turn things back, and that’s not indicative of the man that I am. The “Love Is Blind” Season 11 reunion is now streaming on Netflix. This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity. Nate Bargatze Returns to Netflix With New Special ‘Good for Nathan’ (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

articles.title: Donnie Dunagan, Original Voice of Bambi, Dies at 92
articles.full_text: × Nov 9, 2026 10:38am PT Donnie Dunagan, Original Voice of Bambi, Dies at 92 By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Donnie Dunagan, Original Voice of Bambi, Dies at 92 33 minutes ago Box Office: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Stomps to $6.7 Million in Previews 3 days ago Kimmarie Johnson, ‘Beverly Hills, 90210’ Actress and Miss USA Contestant, Dies at 50 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images for Turner Donnie Dunagan , who provided the original voice of Disney’s Bambi , died Wednesday, Nov. 4, of lung cancer, his agents confirmed to Variety . He was 92. “We were proud to represent a Marine, beloved by fans around the world for his roles in ‘Bambi’ and ‘Son of Frankenstein,'” his agents Kris Jones and Nery Lemus of CelebWorx told Variety . “While he asked us (in his words) ‘not to be sad due to the great life I lived,’ it would be amiss not to share the impact that Donnie had on people when they met him. His love for life was shown through his encouragement. He knew how to inspire and inspired us to be the best we could be. He had an infectious smile, a warmth and charisma that never shook the child-like spirit of his acting youth. He rallied other veterans, loved his fans, and above all else, loved his wife. We will always love you Donnie. You were the best of us.” Related Stories Hulu’s ‘The Circle’ Revival Sets SiriusXM’s Tinx as Host (EXCLUSIVE) Dunagan was born August 16, 1934, in San Antonio, Texas, but his family soon moved to Hollywood after a talent agent scouted him when he was three years old. He made his film debut in “Mary Carey’s Chickens” in 1938 and then played Peter von Frankenstein in 1939’s “Son of Frankenstein” (the grandson of the original mad scientist turned monster creator). He also appeared in “The Forgotten Woman” (1939), “Tower of London” (1939), “Vigil in the Night” (1940) and “Meet the Chump” (1941). In 1942, he voiced young Bambi’s in Disney’s beloved animated movie. After “Bambi,” Dunagan enlisted in the U.S. Marines and became the youngest drill sergeants in Corps history. He served three tours in Vietnam and retired as a major in 1977. For his service, he received a Bronze Star and three Purple Hearts. articles.title: Paramount+ Drama Slate: Series Moving To HBO, Sarah Aubrey & Francesca Orsi Sharing Oversight Among…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Druski Leads One Of ‘SNL’s Most Star-Studded Curtain Calls Ever With Emma Stone, Michael B. Jordan, Austin Butler, Plus Chappelle, Rock, Goggins ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: Hit Series Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie – The Dish ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Spinoff Pushed To 2027-28, Moves Production To New Mexico After Failing To Get CA Tax Credit As Betsy Beers Calls For Program Change View All November 3, 2026 5:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Francesca Orsi and Sarah Aubrey Courtesy Almost a month into Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery into Skydance, pieces are still coming together, and there is probably no area with more pieces to sort out than Skydance’s Direct to Consumer. With the content operations of Paramount+ and HBO/ HBO Max combined under Casey Bloys , now Co-Chair and Chief Content Officer, Skydance DTC, the former HBO & HBO Content CEO saw his portfolio more than double overnight. The expansion is passed on to his senior team which he brought over from HBO/HBO Max, led by Francesca Orsi , Amy Gravitt and Sarah Aubrey , with Paramount+’s EVP and Head of Originals Jane Wiseman leaving as part of the restructuring announced October 23 . Watch on Deadline Related Stories Executives Casey Bloys Unveils His Skydance DTC Content Team Featuring All HBO Max Execs: Francesca Orsi, Sarah Aubrey, Amy Gravitt & More News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Organizing the combined slate has been a priority for the new regime as it is reviewing Paramount+’s development and production pipeline. The process is in early stages and sources stress that no decisions have been made, but various ideas are being discussed, including possibly relocating upcoming Paramount+ drama series to HBO, I hear. Logical targets for a move to HBO are legal thriller Discretion , starring Big Little Lies ‘ Nicole Kidman and Elle Fanning, which has frequently been described as HBO-like; 9/11 first responders limited series The Best of Us , which is headlined by Emmy-winning Succession star Jeremy Strong; as well as a couple of projects awaiting official green light. There have been conversations, which I hear have reached the highest levels, but no migrations, with all series earmarked for Paramount+ remaining there for the time being. Talks are continuing. Even if the two streamers’ slates remain status quo — they are bound to merge eventually as Skydance co-CEO David Ellison has revealed plans for HBO Max and Paramount+ to become one platform in the next couple of years — there could be an HBO stamp on some upcoming Paramount+ dramas via potential involvement by Orsi. While Paramount+ has been staying largely out of the original comedy series game, BET+’s The Varnell Hill Show being a rare exception, its original drama slate is extensive, led by the flagship Taylor Sheridan universe. (The streamer also has next-day comedies and drama procedurals coming from CBS.) In the new structure, HBO Max’s Head of Originals Aubrey, now Head of Paramount+, Max Originals and International Programming, added oversight of all Paramount+ programming, with Wiseman’s team reporting to her. As part of the same realignment, Orsi was promoted from EVP to President, HBO Drama Series and Films in an expanded new role that involves her working with Bloys on determining which drama projects are best suited for HBO. I hear that may involve her taking oversight of Paramount+ original dramas that carry HBO DNA, whether they relocate to HBO or not. Aubrey and Orsi are currently reviewing the Paramount+ drama slate together, and I hear there is a possibility for Orsi to work on shows that stay on Paramount+ whenever it makes sense. articles.title: Skydance Distribution Chief Ray Hopkins Sets Leadership Team, Reveals Exits Of Eight Senior…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In Read the full story By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade AI-Focused Management Firm Collage Adds Kelly Miller And Jack Styne As Partners Tubi CEO Anjali Sud, Roku Media President Charlie Collier Leaving The Fold As Fox Sets Exec Team After Roku Close Charter Stock Sinks As Internet Subscriber Losses Worsen; Could A Comcast Merger Be The Next Move? View All November 4, 2026 2:57pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Deadline In the latest in a series of organizational announcements following the closing of the Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery merger into Skydance , the newly combined company has set its top distribution troops. Ray Hopkins , the longtime CBS veteran who is now distribution president of Skydance , sent an internal memo Tuesday outlining the newly minted execs in his organization and also noting several departures. Related Stories News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Executives David Decker Lands Top Content Sales Role At Skydance With Jay Askinasi Overseeing Ads, Ray Hopkins Leading Distribution Distribution deals will be overseen jointly by Sarah Bergman and Mickey Carter, both of whom hold the title of EVP, Distribution. Bergman has been with HBO and WBD for 14 years, while Carter brings more than a decade of Paramount and CBS experience. Their portfolio spans CBS owned-and-operated stations, 55 basic cable networks, two premium networks, plus subscription streamers Paramount+, HBO Max and Discovery+; free streamer Pluto TV; and more than 100 FAST channels. While distribution is a hugely important business area for all players in the media sector, it is particularly crucial for Skydance, which has almost $80 billion in debt following the $110 billion transaction. In order to reduce that leverage, the company will need to wring as much cash as possible from its partners, but it is also constrained by a consent decree established by state attorneys general in the resolution of an antitrust lawsuit. The agreement requires Skydance to negotiate carriage deals for the Paramount and WBD families of assets as though they were still run by separate companies. Watch on Deadline Hopkins said eight execs will be exiting Skydance as part of the new appointments: WBD’s Rivka Golomb, Kelly Kane, Jeff Cross and Rich Palermo, and Paramount vets David Comisar, Kurt Davis, Deena Demasi and Ken Kay. Other executive appointments include the following: Brad Shipley, EVP, Business Development & Strategy . Shipley, who joined CBS 13 years ago, will oversee strategy, new growth partnerships, Pluto TV and FAST distribution, advanced advertising partnerships as well as business planning and analytics and also be distribution lead for Skydance Global Sports Group. Patrick Cavanaugh, EVP & CFO, Distribution Finance . Following nearly 14 years at the YES Network, he has spent the last decade at CBS and Paramount. He will lead economics for all linear and streaming negotiations, manage the linear affiliate revenue life cycle from deal negotiation through cash collection, as well as all budgeting, forecasting and reporting. Rick Baker, EVP, Deputy General Counsel, Distribution, Business & Legal Affairs . Baker, who joined MTV Networks in 2011, will oversee business and legal affairs for Skydance’s distribution across linear and streaming including domestic broadcast, premium and cable networks, P+, HBO Max, Discovery +, Pluto TV and FAST. With the new role, Cross, EVP, Legal, Distribution & Commercial Partnerships, will be leaving the organization but will remain a senior advisor to the distribution group. Joe Bahr, SVP, Partner Operations . With more than 20 years across HBO, WarnerMedia and WBD, Bahr will manage operational issues across partners, serve as the liaison to product and tech teams, and support delivery of linear and VOD offerings to distributors. Andrew Borak, SVP, Marketing . After starting in affiliate marketing at MTV 20 years ago, Borak has been SVP, Distribution Marketing for Paramount for the past six years. He will lead the combined distribution marketing function, market to distributors and with distributors, lead cross-brand distribution initiatives, and prepare marketing strategies for distribution renewals. Bob Aguanno, SVP, CBS Affiliate Relations . The 25-plus-year CBS veteran will manage relationships with roughly 200 CBS affiliate TV stations and work closely with the CBS Network affiliate board. John Bagwell, SVP, Associate General Counsel . Bagwell has served for more than a decade as lead counsel for CBS Network distribution via the CBS affiliated stations and will negotiate contracts with the station groups and the CBS Network affiliate board. The distribution moves were first reported Tuesday by Reuters. ‘Yellowstone’s Cole Hauser Preps FBI Action Thriller ‘Pale Horse’ With Eye To Star ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic 10½-Year Prison Sentence; Survivor Speaks Out, Rips Channel 4 De Niro Targets Elon At ‘Musk’ Documentary Screening On GOP Spending Spree More from this Story Arc Skydance November 3, 2026 Paramount+ Drama Slate: Series Moving To HBO, Sarah Aubrey & Francesca Orsi Sharing Oversight Among Options Explored Post-Merger – The Dish October 30, 2026 Skydance Chief Communications Officer Melissa Zukerman Unveils Leadership Team, Executive Departures View All Story Arc Read More About: 2 Comments

Jama took to social media to share a goodbye message with some of her best bits from the ITV reality series. “What an incredible era and what an unforgettable time I’ve had, it’s been far too much fun to put into words or a video..but as all good things must come to an end, it’s my time to step down as the host of my beloved Love Island,” Jama shared on Instagram. She continued, “Firstly, I want to thank all of the people who rooted so hard for me to host the show in the first place. I wouldn’t change a thing. To the fans of the show, thank you for every supportive message and every single time you’ve tuned in during my time as host, I’m forever grateful to you all. The show really does belong to the people who watch it and embrace it year after year.” Related Stories News 'The Celebrity Traitors' Trailer Offers First Glimpse Of Players Including Bella Ramsey & Maya Jama: "We're In Game Mode Now" News NBCUniversal's Split From Comcast Will "Allow Us To Move Faster," Media Group Chief Matt Strauss Says Jama joined Love Island UK in Season 9 (2023) after host Laura Whitmore stepped down. As host of the dating series, Jama also hosted companion series Love Island Aftersun and spinoffs Love Island Games and Love Island All Stars . Watch on Deadline Following the summer Love Island UK series, there were rumblings that she was eyeing an exit from hosting duties, and in an interview with Deadline , she addressed those rumors. “I never know,” Jama said about returning to host the series. “[The UK press] always do this. Every time I do a series — that’s happened for the last three years — they’ll say, ‘Maya is leaving.’ And I think they just throw it out there just in case. Then people grab onto it, and they’re like, ‘Oh, are you leaving?'” She continued, “But I never decide if I’m doing the next series until the end of one. So it’s fake news that I’m leaving, but I always decide at the end of a series if I’m going to continue the next year. So we’ll find out.” Jama is coming off of starring in BBC One’s The Celebrity Traitors Season 2 , where she was a Traitor and made it to the finale, but was banished in the last roundtable. She also starred in the second season of Netflix’s The Gentlemen . In her goodbye message to Love Island UK , Jama looked back at her hosting duties, saying, “I started hosting the show aged 28 and during the 9 incredible series met the most wonderful humans along the way. I’ve loved every slow-mo walk, fire pit and live show. I’ll forever be grateful for the experience. But I’ve always believed that to truly grow, you have to take a leap every now and then, and now is my time to throw myself into something new.” “While my own Love Island journey has come to an end, I wish the show and the team all the success in the world, I’ll be cheering you lot on from the sidelines forever,” she ended. Well, fasten your seat belts. Cannes just unveiled Hope , a sci-fi alien monster mash from South Korean director Na Hong-Jin that never lets up for a minute of its two-hour, 40-minute running time and out-Hollywoods anything of its kind made by Hollywood. And guess what? Cannes not only put it in the Official Selection, it’s in Competition — a rare film of this kind to get that kind of instant cred from the festival. articles.title: DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News DC Studios Shakeup: James Gunn & Peter Safran Out, Former Marvel Exec Jeremy Latcham In Read the full story By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is A Box Office Hero With $32M Live-Action Foreign-Language Opening Record, Best Ever For Gkids – Sunday AM Update ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Is King Of The Global Weekend Box Office With $63M, Towers Over ‘Ramayana’s $55M+ WW Opening ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Getting Hot With $80M+ Opening Floor, Presales Ahead Of ‘Wicked’ – Box Office Update View All November 9, 2026 9:16am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc James Gunn and Peter-Safran; Jeremy Latcham Getty/John Winters In a seismic executive shuffle unlike anything Bruce Wayne could pull off at Wayne Enterprises, James Gunn and Peter Safran are leaving their posts as Co-CEOs and Chairman of DC Studios , jobs which they’ve held for the past four years. The dynamic duo will continue to produce on various DC projects and returning to their full-time creative work. They’re currently in post on the Superman sequel, Man of Tomorrow which will open in theaters on July 9, 2027. Related Stories News James Gunn Is Writing His Next Movie Following ‘Man of Tomorrow’: “Already In It” Executives Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit Taking over the comic book entertainment label as President and Chief Creative Officer is former Marvel SVP of Production and Development, Jeremy Latcham . He starts the position on Dec. 1 and reports to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs, Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein. Duly note the tweak here in the reporting structure of DC: Initially the DC Bosses reported straight into the CEO (previously Zaslav, post-merger David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz. Now DC like the other Warner film labels reports into Goldberg and Greenstein. Latcham worked with Gunn previously on Guardians of the Galaxy. Latcham shepherded such mega MCU franchises as Iron Man, Guardians of the Galaxy, Spider-Man and The Avengers . He will lead DC’s film, television and animation slate, overseeing the creative pipeline, along with production, talent and strategy. Watch on Deadline The news hits today as DC’s new parent, Skydance, is reporting their third quarter earnings. For some, the dynamic duo’s departure is a bit of a shock as sources told us that they were staying post Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. However, word was out there that Safran’s contract was expiring in the spring. His name was floated for the film boss job at Netflix under newly installed Film Content Chief Peter Rice, however, from what we know, Safran and Rice haven’t sat down. Gunn and Safran were put in charge of DC by former Warner Bros Discovery CEO David Zaslav as he strove to create a motion picture production label strategy on par with Disney’s. The hiring of Gunn in a creative production executive position was arguably an anomaly: Few filmmakers have led studios; Charlie Chaplin being one of the most notable ones. Gunn and Safran took over DC at a time when the label was waning under the Zack Snyder universe. Zaslav wanted a universe that was built out across film, TV and games. The former WBD boss was adamant about making a Superman movie, and former WB Motion Pictures bosses quietly contracted Gunn to start writing his version before he landed the job with Conjuring producer Safran. During their tenure, they saw the airing of the Matt Reeves’ produced 9x Emmy-winning HBO Max series, The Penguin, a spinoff of the filmmaker’s The Batman starring Colin Farrell. That series was well in the works before Gunn and Safran arrived at DC. They also had two seasons of the Emmy-nominated HBO Max series Peacemaker, which was a spinoff of Gunn’s 2021 Suicide Squad movie starring that pic’s anti-hero played by John Cena. Let’s not forget the animated HBO adult series Creature Commandos. Gunn’s Superman rebooted the franchise a fourth time since the Man of Steel hit the big screen in 1978 with a $618.7M global gross. Their HBO Max series, Lanterns, was a viewership success and their lower budget Clayface with a net $44M production cost was No. 1 worldwide for two weeks in a row, that James Watkins-directed pic’s cume now at $109M WW. Upcoming is Reeves’ The Batman II which has Robert Pattinson returning in the title role and Steven Soderbergh finishing in London for a Feb. 18, 2028 release. Also upcoming for DC in 2027 is The People v. Gorilla Grodd , the eight-episode HBO Max series starring Skyler Gisondo as Jimmy Olsen and Jimmy Tatro as Gorilla Grodd has completed filming. Gunn and Safran serve as executive producers. A big miss for Gunn and Safran was the Craig Gillespie directed Supergirl which cost a net $186M and grossed only $126.4M WW. A graphic novel which was True Grit in its story, the Superman spinoff arrived a year after Gun’s Man of Steel movie, and was perceived by fanboys as being too similar to other fantasy movies, i.e. Mad Max and Guardians of the Galaxy. Gunn and Safran had a big plan for DC, announced as “Gods and Monsters” in January 2023 . It will be interesting to see what projects Goldberg, Greenstein and Latcham keep intact. There was early buzz of James Mangold circling a Swamp Thing movie, and Andy Muscietti penning a version of Batman Brave and the Bold . Of the projects Gunn and Safran announced which wound up fizzling after being long in development was the Peacemaker spinoff series Waller starring Viola Davis, Paradise Lost a series set in the Wonder Woman -verse, Booster Gold and an Authority movie about a bunch of DC antiheroes. Gunn said in February 2025 on social that Authority “is a very big movie, if you’re going to do it properly. Some of the story elements perhaps that are in Superman and some of the other films we fast-tracked, step a little on The Authority … [It’s] the one that got messed with through all of the other things that were happening. The script had a harder time coming along.” In fact, Gunn announced recently he was working on a screenplay for a new feature project . What’s the status of that mystery project? It’s been a while since Latcham has been in the superhero space. He left the Kevin Feige led Marvel in 2017 to found Latcham Pictures, which held first-look deals at 20th Century Fox, Hasbro, and Wonder Project. He produced Bad Times at the El Royale and Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves . Recently, he held an overall deal at Hasbro Entertainment, where he was developing a Dungeons & Dragons sequel and an Action Man film. He’s also producing Lionsgate and Sony’s big screen take of anime Naruto which has Spider-Man: Brand New Day ‘s Destin Daniel Cretton directing. David Ellison, Chairman and CEO, and Ynon Kreiz, Co-CEO, of Skydance said in a statement about today’s news, “James and Peter launched a new era for DC Studios and led it through a period of real transformation, resetting the foundation and building a slate we’re incredibly proud of. We’re grateful for their passion, contributions and commitment to this legendary brand. Jeremy has been a longtime creative partner to both, and we have complete confidence that James and Peter will ensure a smooth, collaborative transition and continue this work with care. We look forward to working with Jeremy to build the next generation of DC storytelling and to doubling down on our commitment to fans.” Said Gunn and Safran: “Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision. In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television with Peacemaker , Creature Commandos, Lanterns and Clayface. We’re immensely proud of the team that turned that ambition into something real, including the actors, crews and executives we had the opportunity to collaborate with. We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow .” Gunn also posted the following to IG: View this post on Instagram “Jeremy brings a deep reverence for DC and its passionate fanbase, recognizing that they are the very foundation of this storied, multigenerational brand,” said Goldberg and Greenstein. “Under his leadership, every film and television show will be ushered from start to finish through the prism of the legions of fans who love and champion it. Jeremy’s track record exemplifies the excellence he will bring to building out DC and the many beloved characters within it.” “DC’s pantheon of characters is among the most iconic in American popular culture. I’ve had the privilege to help bring some of the most celebrated superhero stories to life on the big screen, and I’m excited and honored for the opportunity to now lead DC Studios into its next era. The chance to steward the incredible cast of DC characters to the screen in a way that excites lifelong fans while introducing their timeless stories to the next generation is a massive responsibility that I do not take lightly,” said Latcham. “I am grateful to Dana and Josh for putting their trust in me. I can’t wait to work night and day alongside filmmakers, comic book creators, artists and storytellers of every kind, across film, television and animation, to build something ambitious for longtime DC fans and newcomers alike.” ‘Yellowstone’s Cole Hauser Preps FBI Action Thriller ‘Pale Horse’ With Eye To Star ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic 10½-Year Prison Sentence; Survivor Speaks Out, Rips Channel 4 De Niro Targets Elon At ‘Musk’ Documentary Screening On GOP Spending Spree More from this Story Arc Skydance November 4, 2026 Skydance Distribution Chief Ray Hopkins Sets Leadership Team, Reveals Exits Of Eight Senior Executives November 3, 2026 Paramount+ Drama Slate: Series Moving To HBO, Sarah Aubrey & Francesca Orsi Sharing Oversight Among Options Explored Post-Merger – The Dish View All Story Arc Read More About: 43 Comments
