It is one of three Rifki films at the festival. The Falcon Pictures production, which reworks Oriol Paulo’s 2016 hit “Contratiempo” for an Indonesian setting, stars Reza Rahadian, Mawar de Jongh and Arifin Putra. It debuted on HBO Max on Aug. 7. Related Stories Stephen Chow Told Japan to Stop Aping Kung Fu, Says Boss of Film Fund Behind Kore-eda Hirokazu's 'Look Back' Alien Cat Sent to Conquer Earth Goes Soft for Catnip and Canned Tuna in Taiwan Creative Content Fest Animated Series 'Operation Maomao' Rifki tells Variety that the matter has only recently been resolved. He also has two new features at the festival: romantic comedy “Tua Tua Keladi” and thriller “Sandal Jepit No. 10.” Set among the older residents of a small village, “Tua Tua Keladi” follows the chaos that breaks out when a chemical leak into the village water supply stirs up desire. Unspoken feelings, long-held confessions and passion come out overnight. “I was thinking, if they have young energy to live the second life, [it is] the second chance to love,” Rifki says. He wanted the film to challenge a deep-rooted assumption that older people no longer live with energy. For all the awkwardness of its premise, the film keeps away from eroticism, even with its younger characters. In the digital era, Rifki says, people can record their sexual behavior openly – “and sometimes that kind of freaks me out because I have a daughter. I’m concerned if my daughter [is exposed to] wild media.” “So with the young characters, I try to approach them with something pure, not physical,” he says. “Sandal Jepit No. 10” is a confined-space thriller about the brutal police interrogation of Akbar, a grieving father detained on suspicion of murder. “Indonesians have trauma in politics. Life back in the days of Orde Baru – the New Order in the Suharto era – for around 32 years, we could not criticize the government,” Rifki says. “Now we have the Reformation Era, but it might be happening underground. On social media, if you criticize the government, they will shadowban [your comment].” “We are the low class of society with this kind of fear that, if we do something, someone with power will oppress us. So the movie is about how to fight back,” he says. “If you have social media, netizens are here to help you out. People power now is turning [to] a digital era so we can gain that power again. I’m still sure that [there are] many good people,” he adds. Rifki says the film grew out of his concern over abuse of power in Indonesia today. “[When I was] a film student, I really wanted to try how to speak in rom-com, thriller, drama, and other genres. [I’m] an evolving and growing filmmaker still in the making,” he says. The backbone of all his work, he says, is human moral conflict, whatever the genre. He is also keen to try action and horror. His next film, “Before Thirty,” is set for release in January 2027. Rifki calls it a “survival drama” about a 29-year-old man whose life is failing. “In Indonesia, people always ask: what is your achievement before 30? Young people are punished by that value that you have to be successful before the age of 30,” Rifki says. articles.title: ‘The Undertaker’ Director Thiti Srinuan Reveals He Defecated on Camera for Real as an Actor in Thailand’s Taibaan Universe
articles.full_text: × Nov 7, 2026 8:32pm PT ‘The Undertaker’ Director Thiti Srinuan Reveals He Defecated on Camera for Real as an Actor in Thailand’s Taibaan Universe By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘The Undertaker’ Director Thiti Srinuan Reveals He Defecated on Camera for Real as an Actor in Thailand’s Taibaan Universe 11 hours ago AI Could Make Filmmaking Costlier Than the 35mm Era, Korean Pioneers Warn at Taiwan Creative Content Fest 15 hours ago Papua New Guinea’s Most Expensive Film, ‘Mussau: The First Song,’ Wraps Shoot, Unveils First Looks (EXCLUSIVE) 16 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Naman Ramachandran Thiti “Tongte” Srinuan, director of Thai blockbuster “ The Undertaker ,” put up a photo of himself defecating on camera for real during a session at Taiwan Creative Content Fest in Taipei. The scene dates from his days as a supporting actor with Taibaan Studio. “I was a supporting actor, and I played a crazy person,” Srinuan said. “Because he’s crazy, he relieves himself wherever he likes.” Rather than use a prop, the production had him actually do it on set. Related Stories James Bond Shocker: Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult Late Contenders for 007 After Auditioning for Denis Villeneuve CJ Group's Miky Lee Hailed as ‘Godmother of K-Culture’ as She Receives Asian Hall of Fame Lifetime Achievement Medal “Forty or 50 people were sitting there watching me, and I felt like I couldn’t go,” he said. The session was moderated by Mr. Knee, senior public relations manager at Vieshow Cinemas and the Taiwan Film Critics Society’s founding chair. Knee noted that the photo was a surprise to organizers too, who had only seen it that morning. Srinuan said the episode showed him how far the studio went for realism, and that realism is what makes its universe flexible. Because every character feels like a real resident of the same village, any of them can be pulled out to lead a film, whether the studio wants a ghost story or a romance. Srinuan, who wrote and directed “The Undertaker” and its sequel for Taibaan Studio, was the sole panelist at the TCCF forum on how user-generated content is turning into a route to theatrical features. Much of his talk was about money. Before “The Undertaker” grossed more than THB700 million ($20.8 million) in Thailand, much of the Taibaan universe was bankrolled with revenue from online music videos. The 2023 film, the sixth feature in the Taibaan universe, became the highest-grossing Thai film in nine years. The franchise is rooted in the language and culture of Thailand’s northeastern Isan region. Its sequel arrived this year. Srinuan came into the business as an extra and supporting player in Taibaan Studio’s films. The crew was a small group from rural Thailand with little formal training, so he volunteered to write scripts and then to assist on directing, working on five films in those roles. Those films played almost entirely to Isan audiences, he said. A music video he made that went viral across the country convinced him a film from the region could cross over, and when no one else would take on his script, he directed it himself. Budgets have stayed lean. The first Taibaan film raised THB2 million ($59,000), or THB4 million ($119,000) including marketing, and grossed THB35 million ($1 million), in a market where a typical Thai feature costs THB30 million ($891,000) or more. “The Undertaker” was budgeted at THB10 million ($297,000), though Srinuan said only THB8 million ($238,000) was spent. The other THB2 million was there to make it a round number. Raising money for a follow-up proved harder. “If we were still nobodies with no name, they couldn’t invest in us,” Srinuan said. The team turned to building a following online instead. “Believe it or not, after the first film, the second, third and fourth films were funded by what we built online,” he said. “We earned money from music videos. The views kept running and running until we could take that money and make films.” Because a Thai film can take a year to come together, Srinuan said he took on music videos to fill the months between shoots. His videos have now passed 4 billion views combined. Rather than accept flat fees, he asked clients for a share of the view revenue, which meant a video that flopped earned him nothing and pushed him to learn marketing. He has carried the same terms into features, asking to be paid from ticket sales instead of a fixed fee. Music videos also shaped how he writes. He builds features out of segments of four to five minutes, the length of a music video, and lays them end to end until they reach two hours, an approach he said suits audiences raised on short-form and vertical content. “The downside is people comment that the film swings and the emotions don’t connect. You’re laughing, then you’re made to cry, then you’re laughing again,” he said. “But to me, life is like that. You laugh sometimes, you cry sometimes. So I like it this way.” Comments matter more to the studio than likes or shares, Srinuan said. A trailer is expected to reach roughly 20,000 shares and 2 million views with no paid advertising, and when viewers fixate on an unexpected character in the comments, the marketing shifts toward that character. After the first Taibaan film, Srinuan borrowed Marvel’s habit of announcing a slate, declaring a universe before any scripts existed to push himself to keep working. The title of “The Undertaker” came first. Srinuan said he picked the profession because he figured no one sees more ghosts, but early drafts were all ghosts and had little to do with the job. He then drew on his own childhood in the countryside, when he had no money and was paid to be ordained as a novice monk for funerals, watching undertakers at close range. The film turned from horror into drama, though it was still marketed in Thailand as a ghost film because that genre sells. When the first film played in Taiwan two to three years ago, it did not catch on. “I’d like to ask the market now: does Taiwan still want blood-splattered Thai films?” Srinuan said. He suggested Taiwanese viewers had expected gory, frightening Thai horror, while his ghosts are played for laughs. The moderator, who described the film as closer to a comedy, pointed to “Shutter” as the title that first won Taiwanese audiences over to Thai horror. Isan is Thailand’s most populous region, but its local beliefs did not travel to the country’s other three regions, Srinuan said. For “The Undertaker,” he studied Charlie Chaplin and leaned on visual storytelling over dialogue. Traveling overseas with the first film, he found the comedy landed but the local culture often did not, and he called reaching a global audience a challenge he is still working on. Having already handled writing, directing, acting, editing and sound, Srinuan took marketing classes after finishing the first “Undertaker.” The film opened only in Isan, playing to core fans first, and word of mouth pulled it into cinemas across the rest of the country, a strategy he likened to “the forest surrounding the city.” The moderator cited “Backrooms” and “Milk & Serial,” both from directors who came up on YouTube, as signs of the shift. Srinuan said he saw parallels with his own path and argued that ideas count for more than budgets. “If you don’t create work, miracles won’t happen,” he said. He said the success of “The Undertaker” has also drawn a wave of Thai YouTubers into features. “They think, ‘I have 1 million followers on YouTube. I make a film, so all 1 million people who follow me have to watch it, right?’” Srinuan said. “In reality, the first person goes in and says they didn’t like it, and the other 999,999 start deciding whether to watch or not. Then the second person goes in and says it’s not OK, and 900,000 people are gone.” ‘Bad Day’ Trailer: Cameron Diaz Is a Single Mom Who Accidentally Robs a Bank in Netflix Comedy ‘Beef’ Creator Lee Sung Jin Sets Netflix Projects With Ali Wong, Gene Hong Under New Banner Lila Pictures Jason Statham and Guy Ritchie Reunite — Again — for Netflix Revenge Action Movie ‘Dogfight’ Netflix Grapples With Digital-Ad Squeeze Amid Widening Glut of Streaming Commercials Netflix Orders YA Drama ‘Prep’ Based on Curtis Sittenfeld Novel From Nicole Taylor Netflix Names Mattel Executive Roberto Stanichi as VP of Consumer Products and Experiences Loading comments...

articles.title: Former NCT Member Lucas Wong Makes Acting Debut in Taiwanese Folk-Music Drama ‘A Time’ With Jerry Yan, Ning Chang at Taiwan Creative Content Fest
articles.full_text: × Nov 7, 2026 8:47pm PT Former NCT Member Lucas Wong Makes Acting Debut in Taiwanese Folk-Music Drama ‘A Time’ With Jerry Yan, Ning Chang at Taiwan Creative Content Fest By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest Taiwan’s Content Agency and Partners Put $180 Million Into 27 Projects, From an ‘Our Blues’ Remake to an Off-Broadway Musical 6 hours ago Murder-House Impostor Thriller ‘The Stand-In Family’ Wins Mirror Fiction Award at Taiwan Creative Content Fest 13 hours ago IP Companies Spin Books Into Sold-Out Plays, Series and Signature Scents at Taiwan Creative Content Fest 13 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lin Ying-Hsuan Taiwanese director Tsao Jui-yuan unveiled his new drama series “ A Time ,” rooted in Taiwan’s campus folk music movement of the 1970s, at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF). Tsao, known for “Crystal Boys,” “A Touch of Green” and “Seqalu: Formosa 1867,” spent eight years developing the project, which traces four decades of friendship, love and personal transformation. Related Stories Bill Skarsgård Says He ‘Wasn’t Even Thrown Into the Mix’ to Be James Bond: ‘Maybe They Were Like, “We Can’t Do a Swede”’ Laika’s ‘Wildwood’ Sets Limited-Edition 4K SteelBook Release Two generations of actors play five friends at different stages of their lives. Ning Chang, who is an executive producer for the first time, stars alongside “Meteor Garden” star Jerry Yan, Chen Yi-han, Golden Horse best actor winner Wu Kang-ren and Liang Cheng-chun. The younger ensemble features former NCT and WayV member Lucas Wong , Suri Lin, Fandy Fan, Iain Lu and Joseph Huang. “The starting point for this project was my desire to come to terms with my own youth,” Tsao said. “I’ve always believed that campus folk music is one of the most important cultural IPs in contemporary Taiwan. Against that backdrop, I wanted to tell a story about youth, from youthful recklessness to the different stages of life.” Written by Chi Hsi-lin, “A Time” follows the five friends after Si Mao is injured diving into an empty swimming pool. As he lies in a coma for decades, the others deal with love, guilt and personal struggles, eventually reuniting as long-buried secrets from their youth come to light. Tsao likened casting the younger versions of the characters to searching for a needle in a haystack and praised the five newcomers for their performances and commitment. Chang, who was first approached to act in the series before also taking on the role of executive producer, described Tsao as an “actor scanner,” able to detect even the slightest change in a performer’s emotional state. Tsao said he invited Chang because of her resilience and commanding presence, qualities that reminded him of Kwak Sin-ae, the Oscar-winning producer of “Parasite.” “She’s actually someone I look up to very much,” Chang said. Iain Lu, who plays the younger version of Chang’s character, said the director really emphasizes that actors must fully inhabit their characters. “If we lose focus or get distracted, even for a moment, he notices,” Lu said. Wong, the first Hong Kong-born artist to debut with South Korea’s SM Entertainment, makes his acting debut as the younger Si Mao. “Being able to work with such an outstanding cast on my first acting project taught me so much,” Wong said. “I also learned diving, guitar and dancing for the role. This performance has been a very meaningful experience for me.” Joseph Huang, who comes from a musical family and plays the younger Mian Yang, said the dance movements were challenging for all of them, “but we also really enjoyed being able to express ourselves through singing and dancing in addition to acting.” The five younger cast members performed the Taiwanese folk song “Seasonal Rain” at the press conference, recreating a dance sequence from the drama. articles.title: James Talarico Crashes ‘SNL’ Cold Open: ‘I’m the Guy Who’s Been Texting You Every Day Asking for $5’
articles.full_text: × Nov 7, 2026 8:53pm PT James Talarico Crashes ‘SNL’ Cold Open: ‘I’m the Guy Who’s Been Texting You Every Day Asking for $5’ By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Executive Editor franklinavenue Latest James Talarico Crashes ‘SNL’ Cold Open: ‘I’m the Guy Who’s Been Texting You Every Day Asking for $5’ 10 hours ago Paramount Network Orders 13 Original Episodes of Larry the Cable Guy-Hosted Clip Show ‘American Mayhem’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago ‘Wheel of Fortune’ Grows in Syndication and Streaming as Season 44 Introduces New Gameplay (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source NBC Newly elected Texas Sen. James Talarico crashed this week’s “Saturday Night Live” cold open in order to ask the question on everyone’s mind: How many more of these “Donald-Trump-freezes-the-action-to-ramble” cold opens is “SNL” going to do? Responded “ Donald Trump ” (James Austin Johnson): “Infinity!” Talarico popped up near the end of the cold open to cheers from the “SNL” audience. “I’m the guy who’s been texting you every day asking for $5,” he said, introducing himself. (“In this economy, who can blame you?” said Trump.) “But I think, Mr. President, if we can work together, we can make life better for everyday Americans. It’s clear people want something new. They want something different. I’m talking, of course, about SNL’s cold opens. How many of these Trump freezers are they going to do?” Related Stories ‘The Remarried Empress’ Becomes Most-Viewed Local Original Premiere Ever on Disney+ and Hulu Why 'Suits' Japan Swapped Drugs for Cash: NBCUniversal, TBS Format Chiefs on Localizing Hits at Taiwan Creative Content Fest “ Saturday Night Live ” opened its first episode post-midterm election with Sarah Sherman as Chuck Schumer and Kenan Thompson as Hakeem Jeffries celebrating this week’s “blue tsunami” while refusing to admit that with young Democrats energized, perhaps it’s time for them to step aside and pass the torch to the next generation. But then, of course, Donald Trump (James Austin Johnson) freezed the frame and gave his take on the election. “The Democrats never would have won without this horrible economy and terrible war,” he said. “So, in the words of Moana’s big fat friend, ‘You’re welcome.’” Trump then noted that “They’re saying the era of Trump is over” — leading “JD Vance” to pop in: “and the era of Vance has just begun!” Responded Trump: “No, no way… Who the hell was that?” Trump then pointed out that “the other day we lost, and I didn’t even say it was rigged. I accepted the results, which is almost scarier in a way. It’s like, ‘What the hell is he planning?’ I’ll tell you what I’m planning: ballroom. That’s it. That’s all I care about. Look at that beam, big beam over there. Look at that, and marble. The likes of which you’ve never seen. Oh my God! I hate my life. The next two years are going to be awful. I don’t want to work with these people. It’s not that they’re Democrats; it’s that they’re millennials.” “Trump” then went on a long discourse about the millennial fave TV show “New Girl”: “You know that was a show where Jess was the new girl, but really it was about ensemble, right? Schmidt, Winston. You know I said you got to figure out Winston. They didn’t have Winston figured out the first time. When they gave him the cat, that’s when they unlocked a lot of stories for Winston.” Then came Pete Hesgeth (Colin Jost): “You think some election is going to stop me? Do I look like a person who gets less crazy when backed into a corner? I live a YOLO lifestyle. You only lose often, so I’m gonna keep losing for you, sir, unless Congress impeaches me. But you won’t let that happen, right… Now, if you’ll excuse me, I have to go weigh the female soldiers. Peace out, war in.” Talarico’s appearance came just days after he won the Texas senate race with 55.09% of the vote, beating Ken Paxton and flipping the seat Democrat — the first time there’s been a blue senator in Texas since 1988. Talarico’s win was part of the “blue tsunami” that gave the Democrats control of the House and the Senate, as well as a majority of governorships. Saturday’s episode came with a bit of history: Comedian Druski was host , making him the first online content creator to host the sketch show. Druski , whose real name is Drew Desbordes, was joined by musical guest The Strokes. This season’s guest hosts have so far included New York Knicks superstar player Jalen Brunson (Sept. 26), “Verity” actress Dakota Johnson (Oct. 3), comedian Shane Gillis (Oct. 10) and “Obsession” star Inde Navarrette (Oct. 31), while the music guests have included Katseye, Turnstile, Rosalía and Gracie Abrams. The Halloween episode hosted by Navarrette averaged 5.2 million viewers, making it the biggest audience of the season so far. Next up, comedian John Mulaney is set to host the Nov. 14 episode, while Phoebe Bridgers will be the musical guest. articles.full_text: × Nov 7, 2026 9:00pm PT Emma Stone Ambushes Druski’s ‘SNL’ Monologue in Adorable Fashion By Marlow Stern Plus Icon Marlow Stern Chief Correspondent Latest ‘SNL’: Druski Dons Whiteface as Elizabeth Holmes in ‘You Can See Everything’ Parody 10 hours ago Emma Stone Ambushes Druski’s ‘SNL’ Monologue in Adorable Fashion 11 hours ago Bill Maher Rubs Salt in Trump’s Midterms Wound: ‘Donnie, Are You OK?’ 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source SNL When Druski was announced as a future host of “ Saturday Night Live ,” it was its most interesting move in quite some time . The sketch-comedy show had tapped its first exclusively digital creator (who hadn’t experienced crossover success, a la Issa Rae or Quinta Brinson) to serve as its master of ceremonies, marking its first major foray into the creator space. And the 32-year-old social media sensation addressed it all head-on in his monologue. “It is a dream to be hosting ‘Saturday Night Live,’” exclaimed Druski. “Apparently, people are saying I’m the first internet-content-creator-social-media-influencer-only-make-you-laugh-on-your-phone-TikTok-and-YouTube-and-Instagram star to host this show. People say a lot of things about me, honestly. Some people say I look like a lesbian. I don’t know how true that is. Some people say I’m on Ozempic — could be lies, could be truth to that. Could be a little truth . Some people say they only know me as a white woman.” Related Stories Chang Chen Urges Emerging Taiwanese Actors to 'Be Like Water' at Taiwan Creative Content Fest Golden Horse Showcase ‘The Remarried Empress’ Becomes Most-Viewed Local Original Premiere Ever on Disney+ and Hulu Druski then assured the audience that he wouldn’t be “watered down” by “ SNL ,” and may or may not be planning on doing whiteface. “It is an honor to be on the same stage as so many legends before me,” he said. “And I am living proof that you can bet on yourself and make your dreams come true. I just finished filming my first ever movie with Emma Stone , and she is here right now.” Then, out came the two-time Oscar-winning actress Emma Stone, his co-star in the upcoming Universal Pictures comedy “The Catch,” directed by Stone’s husband, Dave McCary, a former segment director and writer for “SNL.” “I’m actually playing her love interest in the new movie we just did,” boasted Druski. “Oh, that… I’m sorry. articles.title: ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Brutally Roasts Elon Musk Over ‘Epic’ Midterms Defeat
articles.full_text: × Nov 7, 2026 9:57pm PT ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Brutally Roasts Elon Musk Over ‘Epic’ Midterms Defeat By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Executive Editor franklinavenue Latest ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Brutally Roasts Elon Musk Over ‘Epic’ Midterms Defeat 10 hours ago James Talarico Crashes ‘SNL’ Cold Open: ‘I’m the Guy Who’s Been Texting You Every Day Asking for $5’ 11 hours ago Paramount Network Orders 13 Original Episodes of Larry the Cable Guy-Hosted Clip Show ‘American Mayhem’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source NBC An unhinged “ Elon Musk ” hit the “Saturday Night Live” Weekend Update desk this week to address the outcome of Tuesday’s midterm elections — and Musk, as played by “ SNL ” featured player Jeremy Culhane , didn’t quite know how to address it. The real Musk, of course, spent nearly $500 million on Republican candidates, especially in his home state of Texas — which then saw most of its statewide races turn Democratic . “Weekend Update” anchor Colin Jost attempted to get “Elon Musk” (Culhane) to address it: “Elon, you’ve been in the news because you wasted half a billion dollars on the midterms.” Related Stories Elvis Music Owners, Eminem Publisher File Sprawling New Lawsuits Against AI Music Generator Suno: ‘The Next Elvis Won’t Pick Up a Guitar’ Sylvester Stallone Says His 20-Year Rivalry With Arnold Schwarzenegger Only Ended When He Ran for Governor and Wasn’t ‘Doing Movies Anymore’ Said “Elon,” attempting to change the subject: “No, I’m in the news because my car did a flip. My car did a flip. Remember? It was like a freaking Hot Wheel. It was like, and then pop, but I was like totally chill. I was like thug life . Imagine.” Jost then asked “Elon” about halting production on Tesla’s Cybertruck, another major piece of news coming out of Texas this week. “Do you have anything to say about that?,” Jost asked. Responded Elon: “Hey, remember when my car did a flip? It was epic . It was like, but everyone was like, ‘Whoa!’ But I was just like, ‘Hold my beer.'” “Elon” continued to ramble: “Then like, you, me, and Che, we’re just like there. We’re just like hanging out, doing like epic vulgar roast of each other. And then these girls are like, ‘Can we hang?’ And we’re like, ‘No, you know, we’re good.’ And then like, imagine my leather jacket becomes like a suit of armor, like, ‘Shing, shing,’ and everybody’s like, ‘Elon, Elon, Elon!’ That would be amazing, man. Amazing. Like, imagine?” Responded Jost: “I cannot believe you are the richest person in the world.” Jost them recapped for Musk: “You moved to Texas because California was run by Democrats. You moved all your companies to Texas because you didn’t want to pay taxes. You even built your own town in Texas. And now Texas is run by Democrats. So now you’re going to have to pay taxes. So how does that make you feel?” Said “Elon”: “Bad.” “I guess that’s what I thought. I mean, I would feel bad too,” Jost said. Responded “Elon”: “Ouchie! Ouchie! That is another epic vulgar roast from Colin Jost, my poorest friend.” So what is an “epic vulgar roast”? “It’s my AI Grok’s most epic hardcore feature,” “Elon” said. “It’s so vulgar and hilariously funny.” Then Elon asked Grok to make a few “epic vulgar roasts” at his own expense, and the roasts, admittedly, were pretty epic: “Elon Musk, you’re the worst thing South Africa has ever done.” “When you’re on TV, it feels like an episode of ‘Hate on the Spectrum.'” “If you have 100 more kids, one of them will talk to you.” Ouchie Wouchie! “Shut it down, Grok, shut it down!” Elon screamed as he left the “Weekend Update” desk. articles.title: Taiwan’s Content Agency and Partners Put $180 Million Into 27 Projects, From an ‘Our Blues’ Remake to an Off-Broadway Musical
articles.full_text: × Nov 8, 2026 1:04am PT Taiwan’s Content Agency and Partners Put $180 Million Into 27 Projects, From an ‘Our Blues’ Remake to an Off-Broadway Musical By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest Taiwan’s Content Agency and Partners Put $180 Million Into 27 Projects, From an ‘Our Blues’ Remake to an Off-Broadway Musical 6 hours ago Murder-House Impostor Thriller ‘The Stand-In Family’ Wins Mirror Fiction Award at Taiwan Creative Content Fest 13 hours ago IP Companies Spin Books Into Sold-Out Plays, Series and Signature Scents at Taiwan Creative Content Fest 13 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lin Ying-Hsuan The Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA) and its partners have invested in 27 projects, backed by NT$5.64 billion ($180 million) in total, including NT$740 million ($23.7 million) from the agency and NT$4.9 billion ($157 million) in private capital, TAICCA chair Sue Wang said at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF). TAICCA brought together its four joint ventures – Chunghwa Digital Cultural and Creative Fund, Enjoy Entertainment Limited Partnership, momomini Kids Content Fund and Joint Journey Creative – to present their slates. The partnerships span nine countries, and Wang said the joint-venture model allows for more professional and precise investment assessments. Related Stories 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Director Takashi Yamazaki Dreamed of Seeing His Hometown Destroyed by King Ghidorah. He Finally Made It Happen. James Bond Shocker: Robert Pattinson and Nicholas Hoult Late Contenders for 007 After Auditioning for Denis Villeneuve Enjoy Entertainment, a partnership between TAICCA and Taiwanese telecom Far EasTone, said it had invested in 15 projects in its first 10 months: eight in film and TV and seven in music and live events. They include horror film “The Rope Curse 4: Kuntilanak,” which took NT$80 million ($2.6 million) at the Taiwanese box office, a franchise record, and VMTheatre Company’s “Don’t Cry, Dancing Girls the Musical,” billed at the event as the first Taiwanese musical to reach Off-Broadway. On the music side, Enjoy developed the ID. Music Festival with Spotify, which brought 14 Taiwanese acts to two stages in the streamer’s first collaboration with a Taiwanese music event. It also highlighted “Her Voice,” a concert featuring five female performers from Taiwan and South Korea, and indie band Shallow Levée’s “Speak in Silence” project, which pairs the band’s 10th-anniversary album with collaborations with Japanese and Korean musicians and a planned tour of about 50 shows across Taiwan and eight other Asian countries. Enjoy is also behind an immersive project marking 25 years of work by Taiwanese picture-book artist Jimmy Liao. Gary Tsai, general manager of Enjoy Entertainment and COO of Far EasTone’s FET Entertainment Service, said the company aims to take Taiwanese original content to international audiences while adapting international IP for local viewers. Through Far EasTone’s streaming service friDay Video, investment and cross-border partnerships, it hopes to help Taiwanese productions expand overseas and create more opportunities for local talent. Launched in December 2025, momomini Kids Content Fund has made six investments: three in animation, two in live-action and one in drama. COO Phoebe Tsai said the fund weighs each project’s potential impact on the industry alongside content production, talent development and commercial viability. It focuses on children’s content, which Phoebe Tsai said had not previously been treated as a distinct investment category in Taiwan. Its projects include “Who’s Our Sub Today?,” a comedy-adventure series for children ages 8 to 12; “Feifei,” a picture-book adaptation in development as an animated children’s sitcom; and “Mogu & Perol,” which pairs a French IP with Taiwanese talent. The 39-episode series includes six or seven episodes featuring the culture of Taiwan’s Hakka people, one of the island’s main ethnic groups. The fund also backed “Mountain Adventure Squad 2,” a children’s outdoor reality show slated to launch in the first quarter of 2027, and “Hello, Mr. President!,” which received an Excellent Screenplay Award from Taiwan’s Ministry of Culture. Joint Journey Creative’s slate includes Taiwanese films “The Damp,” “All Money Back My Home” and “Suffocation,” as well as Season 6 of Japanese series “ Midnight Diner ,” an international production it is participating in. The Chunghwa Digital Cultural and Creative Fund totals NT$1 billion ($32 million). Chunghwa Telecom holds 64%, TAICCA 30% through the National Development Fund, E.Sun Financial Holding 5% and fund manager CDCC Capital 1%. The fund backs film, TV and other programs at the project level. It also takes equity stakes in companies working in content development and production, international distribution and business integration, and new uses for IP across cultural technology, games and music. Its equity investments include DaMou Entertainment, the production company behind “The World Between Us,” and Horiza Creations, which focuses on international IP operations, data-driven business models and crowdfunding. Its project slate includes “Call of Lobster,” an action comedy spanning Taiwan and South Korea that won the Chunghwa Telecom Award at TCCF’s 2024 pitching competition, and “C’est la Vie,” an eight-episode drama executive produced by and starring Esther Liu, with Tu Cheng-che as screenwriter and director. The fund is also an investor in Shallow Levée’s “Speak in Silence.” Enjoy Entertainment’s slate also includes “ Our Blues ,” a Taiwanese remake of the 2022 Korean series, which launches globally on Netflix on Dec. 3. articles.full_text: × Nov 8, 2026 6:00am PT How to Watch Trump’s ’60 Minutes’ Interview Online The president's post-midterms interview with Ross Douthat is set to air on Sunday, Nov. 8. By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest Laika’s ‘Wildwood’ Sets Limited-Edition 4K SteelBook Release 23 hours ago The Best Cell Phone Plans for Streaming: How to Get Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, HBO Max for Free 2 days ago Katherine Ryan Feeling ‘Grief and Relief’ Over Russell Brand Conviction After Reportedly Calling Out His Behavior on Comedy Central 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. President Donald Trump is set to appear on Sunday’s edition of “ 60 Minutes ” for his first in-depth interview since Republicans suffered sweeping losses in Tuesday’s midterm elections. The president is scheduled to sit down with CBS News correspondent Ross Douthat on Friday, with the interview slated to air Nov. 8. According to CNN, CBS News sources confirmed the plans, while the White House’s Friday schedule listed a pre-taped interview for 10:30 a.m. ET. The best way for cable-cutters to stream the interview online is on Paramount+ Premium . Essential subscribers can stream the full episode on demand beginning Monday, Nov. 9. Related Stories '3 Body Problem' Director Derek Tsang Boards DEA True-Crime Series 'Group 41' From Zhang Yimou’s 'Shadow' Producer Jonah Greenberg (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Silenced Nights’ and ‘You Are the Film’ to Bookend Jogja-Netpac Asian Film Festival You can also access CBS live streams on services on DirecTV and Hulu+ Live TV . STREAM ON DIRECTV The appearance comes just days after Democrats seized control of both the House and Senate , dealing a major blow to Trump’s second-term agenda. The election saw Democrats flip seats in traditionally Republican strongholds, with voters expressing growing frustration over the cost of living and the administration’s war with Iran. Douthat, a longtime conservative columnist for The New York Times who joined “60 Minutes” earlier this year, has been a frequent critic of Trump. In a column published earlier this week, he described the midterm results as a failure of the “New Right.” The interview will mark one of Douthat’s highest-profile assignments since joining the newsmagazine as part of its revamped correspondent lineup. The president has a complicated history with “60 Minutes,” having sued CBS and its parent company over the editing of a 2024 interview with his then-presidential opponent Kamala Harris. Paramount ultimately agreed to a $16 million settlement in 2025. Since Skydance’s takeover of Paramount, CBS News has undergone a sweeping leadership overhaul under editor-in-chief Bari Weiss, including the departure of several longtime “60 Minutes” journalists and the appointment of Nick Bilton as executive producer. Trump most recently appeared on the newsmagazine in April, when a contentious exchange with correspondent Norah O’Donnell saw the president call her a “disgrace.” “60 Minutes” airs Sundays at 7 p.m. ET on CBS and streams on Paramount+. Michael Buckner/PMC Halfway into his first time as DGA president, Christopher Nolan is holding the studios’ feet to the fire in protecting copyrighted materials from AI . In a new interview, the 2x Oscar winner explained that it’s “down to the studios” to go after AI recreations of their work, noting that he was “very pleased” his current Academy Award contender The Odyssey contains a legal warning against using the film to train AI data. “AI is too big a catchall term. It’s describing too many things and it’s being used by companies to absolve themselves of responsibility,” he explained on the Hollywood Insiders podcast. “They sort of want to portray it as this Frankenstein’s monster that can get out of control and can change the world without them having any accountability for it. We have to strongly resist that.” Related Stories News Christopher Nolan Says Directors Union Unlikely To Accept 5-Year Deal With AMPTP; DGA President Talks AI, Healthcare, Tax Incentives & More Ahead Of 2026 Bargaining News Christopher Nolan Elected DGA President, Ron Howard Among New Officers Nolan added, “There’s already legislation in place that protects people, protects creators, etc. And the fact that they these companies hide behind fair-use provisions, for example, I think longer term that won’t hold up in court. There have already been some significant judgments against it. We’re very focused at the Guild about holding the studios to account for protecting their copyrights. We can’t do that. With very few exceptions in the Guild, we are not the copyright holders of the films that we’ve worked on. It’s down to the studios to do that. Watch on Deadline “And I was very pleased to see that the boilerplate at the end of The Odyssey , for the first time, it contains a message saying that this film cannot be ingested and used as training data,” he said. Following his election as DGA president last September, after serving on the Guild’s Artificial Intelligence Committee, Nolan told Deadline there are “excellent protections” in place against AI, “ but that’s not enough .” “You have to have a voice in how this tool is used moving forward. Also, we like to try and have a voice in, what’s the legal framework?” explained Nolan. “Because we generally aren’t the copyright holders of our work, but our income, our residuals, depends on the appropriate monetization of those copyrights. So we’re constantly in dialogue with the companies about, are you maximizing the value of the work that we’ve created? Because we do benefit from that enormously.” ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: Hit Series Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie Cameos By James Talarico, Emma Stone; Druski In Whiteface As Elizabeth Holmes ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic LACMA 2026 Art+Film Gala Red Carpet: Andrew Garfield, Anya Taylor-Joy & More Read More About: 4 Comments

articles.title: Taiwan’s Chunghwa Telecom Unveils Investment Slate Headed By ‘Gunshot’ & ‘Call Of Lobster’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Taiwan’s Mirror Fiction Hands Out $50,000 In Awards For Book To Screen Adaptations Taiwan’s Chunghwa Telecom Unveils Investment Slate Headed By ‘Gunshot’ & ‘Call Of Lobster’ Toei CEO Fumio Yoshimura Talks Global Expansion, GenAI Adoption & Entry Into Games View All November 7, 2026 4:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Gunshot PTS Taigi TV, S11 Partners, Third Culture Content Taiwanese telco Chunghwa Telecom announced a slate of film and series investments at Taiwan Creative Content Fest ( TCCF ), including police crime drama Gunshot , starring Kent Tsai, and Call Of Lobster , starring Choi Siwon and Chang Chen. Chunghwa is one of three Taiwanese telcos that are investing in film and TV content through funds launched in partnership with the Taiwanese government. The company’s previous content investments include feature films Arrested Memory , a Japan-Taiwan co-production directed by Sabu, and The Photo From 1977, directed by Frank Cheng and Sheng-Jung Tang. The two films have a combined 12 nominations in the upcoming Golden Horse Awards. Related Stories News Toei CEO Fumio Yoshimura Talks Global Expansion, GenAI Adoption & Entry Into Games News 'Dune' Star Chang Chen Introduces Six Rising Taiwanese Actors In Golden Horse & TCCF Showcase Gunshot , also starring Chan Tzu-Hsuan, Cheng Chih-Wei, Lu Hsiao-Fen and Mark Lee, follows three police officers with conflicting views of justice trying to navigate a system that rewards visibility over virtue. The eight-part series is produced by PTS Taigi TV with S11 Partners and Third Culture Content . Watch on Deadline Other drama series investments from Chunghwa include Yesterday’s Daughter, Tomorrow’s Mother , a family fantasy series created by award-winning producer Phoebe Ma and director Hung Tzu-peng; fantasy adventure series Guides To The World Below , adapted from a popular Taiwanese comic; and C’est La Vie , an urban drama blending cuisine and women’s personal growth, with actress Esther Liu serving as executive producer. On the film front, Chunghwa is investing in Call Of Lobster , a cross-border action comedy loosely based on the true story of a Taiwanese lobster farmer who offered his services to the North Korean government. Chang Chen and Super Junior member Choi Siwon are set to star in the film, directed by Yin Chen-hao and produced by Calendar Studios . Chunghwa boarded the project after it won the Chunghwa Telecom Award at TCCF in 2024. Taiwan’s Ministry of Culture is also backing the film. Among other film investments, Chunghwa also announced its participation in Studio76’s Demon Of The East – Black Condo , part of a horror cinematic universe spanning four Asian countries. Outside of films and series, Chunghwa is also backing reality cooking show Next Z Chef and indie band Shallow Levée’s Speak in Silence Asian tour. At the slate announcement event in TCCF, Taiwan’s Minister of Culture Li Yuan said: “Chunghwa Telecom is like a pyramid. I am grateful that, beyond building a strong foundation through its thriving core business, the company is also willing to invest at the very top of the pyramid, supporting film and television professionals as they continue moving forward and creating even better work.” Chunghwa Telecom Senior Executive Vice President Lin Wen-chiyh said: “Chunghwa Telecom is more than just a platform operator; we are also a driving force behind the long-term development of the content industry. Moving forward, we will continue to connect funding, creative talent, and domestic and international partners, leveraging our group’s resources and industry partnerships to help Taiwanese content reach international markets.” ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: Hit Series Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie Cameos By James Talarico, Emma Stone; Druski In Whiteface As Elizabeth Holmes ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic LACMA 2026 Art+Film Gala Red Carpet: Andrew Garfield, Anya Taylor-Joy & More Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Emmy Rossum On RAINN Ambassadorship, “Continuing The Conversation” About Sexual Violence After ‘Furious’ Role
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Emma Stone Joins Druski For His ‘SNL’ Debut Opening Monologue While Filming ‘The Catch’ Rom-Com Emmy Rossum On RAINN Ambassadorship, “Continuing The Conversation” About Sexual Violence After ‘Furious’ Role Christopher Nolan On DGA “Holding The Studios To Account” In Protecting Copyright From AI, Including Anti-AI Boilerplate In ‘The Odyssey’ View All November 7, 2026 4:22pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emmy Rossum in 'Furious' Sarah Shatz/Hulu/Disney/Courtesy Everett Collection As Emmy Rossum prepares to return for Season 2 of Furious , she’s keeping the show’s themes close to heart. The Golden Globe nominee, who recently joined RAINN ‘s anti-sexual violence organization as an ambassador, explained that she wants to “take the shame out of the conversation” after playing FBI agent Alice Black, who has to track down a survivor of trafficking. “I think it’s so important to continue the conversation, especially now, because sexual violence is a real problem,” she told the Associated Press . “It’s prevalent for so many women, and it will be in the room tonight, statistically. So, it’s something we must take the shame out of the conversation around it, and learn how to talk about it. I feel, growing up, that sexual violence was not something I knew how to talk about, certainly not something I would feel comfortable talking about with my family.” Related Stories News Emmy Rossum & ‘Furious’ Creator Liz Meriwether On Interviewing Real Trafficking Survivors, Updating A 1987 Thriller & Season 2 “Croatian Beach” Dreams Cancellations and Renewals ‘Furious’ Renewed For Season 2 By Hulu Ahead Of Season 1 Finale Rossum added, “So, being able to partner with an organization that is helping survivors with longterm trauma, with immediate trauma, and also just helping educate us how to not just be part of the solution, but part of prevention as well. I’m talking to much younger kids about consent, and I’m seeing that start even for my daughter, who’s 5, being able to say, ‘please don’t touch my hair’ when she doesn’t want that. So, that kind of empowering language for young people, I think is incredibly important. So, educating myself and others is something I’m very passionate about.” Watch on Deadline Rossum previously told Deadline that she spoke with real survivors of sexual violence and trafficking in researching for her Furious role, noting it was “very important for us to really show women in all of their complexity,” citing her complex character Alice. Emmy Rossum wants to use her crime drama "Furious" to "take the shame out of the conversation" around sexual violence. She spoke at the Women in Film Honors. #EmmyRossum #Furious pic.twitter.com/0vc6QCdG5n — The Associated Press (@AP) November 7, 2026 “It’s these kinds of contradictions that don’t immediately make sense and that don’t add up to a perfect victim, in the way that our justice system likes them to be, in order to be quote unquote ‘deserving of justice,’ or in order for their story to make sense,” she said. “Trauma doesn’t make sense. Violence doesn’t make sense. The aftereffects that it leaves in you don’t make sense. And I think it was with bravery that we all marched towards the fires that [creator Liz Meriweather] set.” In Furious , Catherine Grace (Lola Petticrew) is a survivor of sex trafficking who begins killing wealthy men, leading FBI agent Alice Black (Rossum) down a rabbit-hole of sexual abuse that goes straight to the top. articles.title: Camerimage Opens With Minute Of Silence For Kraków Mass Shooting; Darren Aronofsky Honored & Luca Guadagnino Introduces ‘Artificial’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana Camerimage Opens With Minute Of Silence For Kraków Mass Shooting; Darren Aronofsky Honored & Luca Guadagnino Introduces ‘Artificial’ International Disruptors: Studio N Chief Mikyung Kwon On The Value Of Webcomic IP & Taking Risks With Korean Epic ‘The Remarried Empress’ Antonin Baudry & Simon Abkarian Talk French Box Office Hit ‘De Gaulle’: “The National Icon Did Not Exist In 1940” View All November 7, 2026 4:37pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Darren Aronofsky at Camerimage in 2026. Deadline There was a sombre mood at the opening ceremony of this year’s Camerimage Film Festival as organizers kicked off its 34th edition in Toruń, Poland with a minute’s silence for the victims of the mass shooting in Kraków, which happened a few hours before the event began. According to reports, at least six people are now dead, and more than a dozen injured when a gunman, who is suspected to have ties to far-right ideologies, drove into Kraków’s historic Main Market Square and opened fire. Poland’s Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies were also later found at the suspect’s home. It is the country’s deadliest shooting in decades. Related Stories News Andrew Garfield Does Not Recall Waving At Sam Altman On 'Artificial' Set: "Very Confused By That" News Camerimage: Hype Williams & Darren Aronofsky Set For Honorary Awards Local politicians scheduled to speak at the Camerimage opening proceedings acknowledged the severity of the shooting, which has sent shockwaves across the country today, before opening ceremony proceedings began. Watch on Deadline The festival kicked off Saturday night (November 7) at Toruń’s Jordanski Culture Centre. AI was a major theme during the three-hour ceremony with festival director Marek Zydowicz bringing a humanoid robot to the stage which engaged with him as he stressed that the “hopes and threats” of AI would be a major talking point throughout the 7-day event. The ceremony was frequently interspersed with footage of Francis Ford Coppola, Gal Gadot, Christopher Nolan, Maggie Gyllenhaal, Steven Spielberg and Ben Affleck who all weighed in on the subject of AI in the entertainment space. Aronofsky, who has been a big proponent of using generative AI in filmmaking after launching his creative studio Primordial Soup last year, was honored with Camerimage’s honorary Award for Director. The Requiem for a Dream and Black Swan helmer said it was his third time at Camerimage, and he hoped to keep returning to the Polish event. “The reason I come back is because there’s very rarely film festivals that celebrate the collaboration of everyone,” he said. “They’re very focused on not just the flashy names and that’s really incredible because it honors everyone who makes films possible for people like me.” Karolina Gruszka, one of Poland’s most acclaimed film and theatre actresses, was honored with the Marshal of the Kujawy Pomorze Region Film Award this year. The prolific actress also starred in David Lynch’s last film Inland Empire, and she gave a nod to the late director calling him a “master investigator” of stories. Polish cinematographer and longtime Steven Spielberg collaborator Janusz Kamiński received an award from Deadline’s sister publication THR while Camerimage also paid tribute to Andrzej Wajda, the legendary Polish director behind titles such as The Promised Land and Ashes and Diamonds . This year marks a century since Wajda’s birth and a decade since his death, with Poland’s Senate declaring this year ‘The Year of Wajda’ in the country. Humanoid robot at Camerimage 2026. The opening film this evening at Camerimage was Luca Guadagnino ’s OpenAI origin story Artificial , starring Andrew Garfield as Sam Altman and Yura Borisov as key creative Ilya Sutskever. The director was joined on stage with the film’s cinematographer Malik Hassan Sayeed where the pair discussed the creative process of the film, which is set to be released by Neon in the U.S. on December 25 and in the UK on January 22, 2027. “I’ve been interested and kind of curious about the personalities of what they call tech oligarchs or tech bros for a while,” Guadagnino said. “And when I got the script that Simon Rich wrote, the world he was describing was an immediate hook for me because there was a lot in that that could be told about the dynamics of power and narcissism but at the same time it was an unprecedented setup for showing how very few people control societies.” When pressed about whether there were constraints from a legal perspective when making a film featuring real people like Altman and Sutskever, Guadagnino said: “The only constraints we gave ourselves were facts. We wanted it to be factual, and we didn’t want to dramatize anything.” He continued: “I’m very proud because, of course, you don’t make movies for vetting it through legal, but the very interesting thing is that this movie is 100% vetted by the legal business [and] sometimes the reality is more surprising than fantasy.” Camerimage takes place November 7-14, 2026. ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: Hit Series Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie Cameos By James Talarico, Emma Stone; Druski In Whiteface As Elizabeth Holmes ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic LACMA 2026 Art+Film Gala Red Carpet: Andrew Garfield, Anya Taylor-Joy & More Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Taiwan’s Mirror Fiction Hands Out $50,000 In Awards For Book To Screen Adaptations
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Taiwan’s Mirror Fiction Hands Out $50,000 In Awards For Book To Screen Adaptations Taiwan’s Chunghwa Telecom Unveils Investment Slate Headed By ‘Gunshot’ & ‘Call Of Lobster’ Toei CEO Fumio Yoshimura Talks Global Expansion, GenAI Adoption & Entry Into Games View All November 7, 2026 5:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 5th Edition of Mirror Fiction Awards TAICCA Mirror Fiction , a Taiwanese IP development and production outfit, handed out cash prizes worth more than $50,000 to two authors, to help them publish their works and adapt them for screen, in the fifth edition of its biennial awards. The announcement was made at Taiwan Creative Content Fest ( TCCF ), where Mirror Fiction also unveiled its latest line-up of IPs. Iris Kong was presented with the Grand Prize of $30,500 (NTD1M) for The Stand-In Family , a work about a group of people who are not related but are living together as a family so they can secure ownership of a house. Related Stories News Taiwan's Chunghwa Telecom Unveils Investment Slate Headed By 'Gunshot' & 'Call Of Lobster' News Toei CEO Fumio Yoshimura Talks Global Expansion, GenAI Adoption & Entry Into Games An engineer by profession, Kong said she kept the potential for film and TV adaptation in mind during the writing process, while also striving to ensure the narrative remained compelling and thought-provoking for readers. “I look forward to the story being published and, perhaps, reaching an even wider audience on screen,” said Kong. Watch on Deadline Malaysian author Liang Xuan won the $21,000 (NTD700,000) Jury Prize for Endless Rain , set in a predominantly ethnic Chinese town in Ipoh, Malaysia, drawing from the experiences of her mother and grandfather’s generations. The story follows a mysterious woman who appears in town more than 20 years after she was supposedly murdered. Both works will be developed for publication and potential film or television adaptation by Mirror Fiction. Previous winners of the awards include Port Of Lies , which won the Grand Prize at the second edition and became an award-winning TV series. The awards are supported by property developer Sinyi Realty. Speaking at the awards ceremony, Mirror Fiction General Manager Tung Cheng-yu noted that films adapted from books outperform those based on original screenplays at the box office by an average of over 40%. Viewership for TV series adapted from books is nearly 60% higher. Book editor Patrick Chia, representing the jury for the awards, said the quality of this year’s finalists was consistently high and there was a significant increase in science fiction and fantasy entries, in particular stories set in a dystopian near future or dealing with the impact of new technologies. Lu Yiwen, who won the Grand Prize in the fourth edition of the competition, shared her experience of working with Mirror Fiction after winning the award, which in addition to financial support involves mentorship from experienced editors. “Writing has evolved from something I did in my daily life into a serious endeavor – and, ultimately, my career. I’m grateful for this award, which has truly solidified my identity as a creator,” Lu said. Mirror Fiction also unveiled a slate of new novels suitable for adaptation at the event, including Kevin Chen’s 036037 , about two middle-aged individuals finding closure in their relationship after two decades; Tommy Tan’s crime thriller The Midnight Masseur , in which the art of massage becomes a form of intelligence-gathering; and Hsieh Shu-yu’s Diplomatic Brother s, about two brothers – a diplomat and a strategist for an organized crime syndicate – who swap identities. Chen’s novel Ghost Town has been translated into 13 languages, including English. Last year at TCCF, Taiwan Creative Content Agency ( TAICCA ) co-invested with Mirror Fiction to launch a production outfit Mirror Entertainment, which is currently working on a slate of film and TV projects. ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: Hit Series Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie Cameos By James Talarico, Emma Stone; Druski In Whiteface As Elizabeth Holmes ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic LACMA 2026 Art+Film Gala Red Carpet: Andrew Garfield, Anya Taylor-Joy & More Read More About: Comments

articles.title: James Talarico Stuns ‘SNL’ With Post-Midterms Cameo & “Trump Freezers” Swipe
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic James Talarico Stuns ‘SNL’ With Post-Midterms Cameo & “Trump Freezers” Swipe Ken Ziffren Offers Optimistic View On Industry, Even When It Comes To AI & Federal Tax Credit Legislation Nithya Raman Wins L.A. Mayor Race As Karen Bass Concedes View All November 7, 2026 8:52pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source After of a week that saw MAGA’s political fangs knocked out by a big blue sock to jaw in the midterms , Saturday Night Live tonight leaped into the ring and started swinging from the cold open get-go. In fact, they went Texas BBQ hot with newly elected James Talarico showing up. Related Stories Late Night TV Emma Stone Joins Druski For His ‘SNL’ Debut Opening Monologue While Filming ‘The Catch’ Rom-Com News Druski Serves Elizabeth Holmes Whiteface In ‘Dru Can See Everything’ Sketch During ‘SNL’ Debut Taking another Donald Trump “Talafreako” jab on the chin, the Senator-elect mocked his successful campaign’s relentless emails hitting everyone up for a $5 donation. For a Texan who spent a lot of time in Hollywood fundraisers this year in what many thought at first was a long shot in flipping GOP rule in the Lone Star state, Talarico also displayed some pretty good acting chops and fine comic timing. “That’s Senator Talafreako.” pic.twitter.com/QWMTGgGL5S — James Talarico (@jamestalarico) November 8, 2026 Like the midterms themselves, it wasn’t obvious at first just how good this cold open was going to end up. Watch on Deadline “This is the Dream Team right here,” bellowed Sarah Sherman’s Sen. Chuck Shumer at the Capitol Hill Dems’ post-midterms victory party alongside Speaker-designate Hakeem Jeffries (Kenan Thompson) in the opening seconds. “Not to take credit for the win, that was all me,” the SNL ’s very prominent forehead version of soon-to-be Senate Majority Leader declared in what was an almost classic cold open line because of its sheer untruthfulness. Of course, this being SNL and this still being the Trump 2.0 era, it looked like with all the cast members in action (including James Austin Johnson as Donald Trump and Colin Jost as Defense Secretary Pete “Do I look like a person who gets less crazy when backed into a corner?” Hegseth), the show was going to play it safe-ish and true to form. And, as SNL was delayed again on NBC on the West Coast due to college football, things took a turn. Talarico showed up to a cheer from the studio audience, and everything froze, literally and figuratively. “Mr. President, if we can work together, we can make life better for everyday Americans,” the real Talarico said onstage to the fake pols. “it’s clear people want something new. They want something different. I’m talking, of course, about SNL ‘s cold opens. How many of these Trump freezers are they going to do?” To which Johnson’s Trump honestly replied: “Infinity.” Trump breaks down the midterm election results pic.twitter.com/1yy2ug6Aak — Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) November 8, 2026 In case you were unaware, Democrats hit Team Trump hard and historically Tuesday as the nation voted in midterms that were a referendum on Trump’s second term in all but name. Alaska and Mississippi are still undecided, but otherwise the Dems surprisingly flipped seven Senate seats to take a majority of 54 in the upper chamber. In the House of Representatives, in what was less of a shocker but still stunning, Jeffries will become the first Black Speaker in American history with Democrats now holding 254 seats to the GOP’s 162. L-R: New Hampshire Democratic Senator-elect Chris Pappas, Michigan Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, Georgia Democratic Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms and Senator-elect James Talarico Getty Images Those big blue wins in once solid red Texas and South Carolina, plus the nation’s first Muslim Senator being elected in Michigan and the America’s first openly gay man being elected as the junior Senator from New Hampshire, were almost overshadowed by Democrats’ state victories. Shattering 30 years of Republican rule with Talarico taking LBJ’s old seat back for the Dems, the Lone Star state also elected its first Latina governor. New Mexico voted in the first Native American female governor in the nation’s history and Georgia elected America’s first Black female governor. Add to that, California elected its first Latino governor and Florida voted in its first Black governor.

articles.title: Emma Stone Joins Druski For His ‘SNL’ Debut Opening Monologue While Filming ‘The Catch’ Rom-Com
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Emma Stone Joins Druski For His ‘SNL’ Debut Opening Monologue While Filming ‘The Catch’ Rom-Com Emmy Rossum On RAINN Ambassadorship, “Continuing The Conversation” About Sexual Violence After ‘Furious’ Role Christopher Nolan On DGA “Holding The Studios To Account” In Protecting Copyright From AI, Including Anti-AI Boilerplate In ‘The Odyssey’ View All November 7, 2026 8:54pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source As Druksi made his Saturday Night Live debut, he had some moral support from a friend who happens to be in the Five-Timers Club. On this weekend’s episode of the NBC sketch comedy show, the content creator was joined by The Catch co-star Emma Stone during his opening monologue, whom he joked is his romantic interest in the movie. Related Stories Late Night TV James Talarico Stuns ‘SNL’ With Post-Midterm Election Win Cameo & “Trump Freezers” Swipe News Druski Does Elizabeth Holmes Whiteface In ‘Dru Can See Everything’ Sketch During ‘SNL’ Debut “I think you might have misread that in those scenes, because we weren’t love interests in the film,” said Stone. “But now it is starting to make more sense why you kept looking at me like that for all those scenes.” In June, Druski joined the cast of Universal’s baseball rom-com The Catch, also starring Stone, Chris Pine and SNL cast member Ashley Padilla. Watch on Deadline Following his viral sketches, Druski noted during his monologue that some people say they “ only know me as a white woman .” “I know y’all think SNL is about to water me down tonight, but no,” he promised. “They’re not holding me back from saying anything.” But Druski admitted they did give him a few rules, including “no cussing” and “no whiteface,” to which he quipped, “I can’t promise that.” In addition to Druski’s SNL hosting debut — marking the first content creator without a current movie or TV show to host the sketch comedy show — The Strokes served as musical guest for a fifth time. ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: Hit Series Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie Cameos By James Talarico, Emma Stone; Druski In Whiteface As Elizabeth Holmes ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic LACMA 2026 Art+Film Gala Red Carpet: Andrew Garfield, Anya Taylor-Joy & More Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Druski Serves Elizabeth Holmes Whiteface In ‘Dru Can See Everything’ Sketch During ‘SNL’ Debut
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Emma Stone Joins Druski For His ‘SNL’ Debut Opening Monologue While Filming ‘The Catch’ Rom-Com Emmy Rossum On RAINN Ambassadorship, “Continuing The Conversation” About Sexual Violence After ‘Furious’ Role Christopher Nolan On DGA “Holding The Studios To Account” In Protecting Copyright From AI, Including Anti-AI Boilerplate In ‘The Odyssey’ View All November 7, 2026 9:09pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Shortly after joking that he couldn’t promise Saturday Night Live he’d do “ no whiteface ,” Druski channeled Elizabeth Holmes . On Saturday’s episode of the NBC sketch comedy show, the content creator quickly delivered one of the funniest sketches of the season as he played himself in the sketch “Dru Can See Everything,” which imagines Holmes (Jane Wickline) and husband Billy Evans (Ben Marshall) going to Druski to make their documentary before landing on Nathan Fielder. “I just want people to see me as an ordinary person. Can you do that, Druski?” asks Wickline, to which Druski says, “Based on what I’ve seen so far, I’m gonna go ahead and say no. Y’all have got some of the weirdest, freakiest vibe I’ve ever seen.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories Late Night TV Emma Stone Joins Druski For His ‘SNL’ Debut Opening Monologue While Filming ‘The Catch’ Rom-Com Late Night TV James Talarico Stuns ‘SNL’ With Post-Midterm Election Win Cameo & “Trump Freezers” Swipe Reenacting Fielder and Holmes’ much meme-ified, up-close conversation, Druski asks, “You trying to f*ck me?” When it comes time to have an actress portray Holmes, Dru decides not to call [SPOILER] and just play the part himself, donning his signature whiteface to get into the Theranos founder’s head. Druski’s hosting debut kicked off with “Washington in Focus,” a predominantly Black news panel show, featuring Druski, Kenan Thompson, Andrew Dismukes and new cast member Saidah Belo-Osagie, joking about recent white politicians with Black names who won the midterm elections. In “Two Men Attempt to Make a Purchase at a Dominican Phone Store,” Druski gets into some hilarious antics with Marcello Hernandez as two Dominican employees serving Mikey Day and Jeremy Culhane. Druski played a nightmare birthday girl in another sketch going off on her friend Tina (Veronika Slowikowska) for eating fajitas and wearing a black bodycon dress. In a commercial for “My Corner Guy,” Druski plays the titular fitness service, a guy that hangs out on your local street corner and objectifies you according to your progress. Druski shows off his vocal chops in one sketch of Sarah Sherman and Culhane on a date, in which he proposes to her, only to be rejected while Druski continues with his celebration performance, complete with backup singers, dancers, a marching band and a rap verse by Dismukes as Sherman’s estranged father, plus Wickline on bagpipes and Marshall as the ASL interpreter. A wedding sketch featuring Hernandez as the groom and Belo-Osagie as the bride, sees Druski and new cast member Grace Reiter plays incredibly committed wedding photographers who get a little too close for comfort. In “Golden Age of Hip Hop,” Druski plays a member of the ’80s hip-hop group Lenny and the Street-Smart Crew with Johnson, Marshall, Kam Patterson and Tommy Brennan, featuring their single “Gangs Ain’t Good (Free Your Mind)” and a casually homophobic track, along with its apology track. For his goodnights, Druski was joined not only by Stone and James Talarico—who made a cold open appearance after his midterms victory—but also Chris Rock, Dave Chappelle, Walton Goggins, Michael B. Jordan and Austin Butler. articles.title: ‘Our Blues’, ‘Midnight Diner’ & ‘C’Est La Vie’ Among Projects Backed By TAICCA Joint Venture Funds
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz ‘Our Blues’, ‘Midnight Diner’ & ‘C’Est La Vie’ Among Projects Backed By TAICCA Joint Venture Funds Taiwan’s Mirror Fiction Hands Out $50,000 In Awards For Book To Screen Adaptations Taiwan’s Chunghwa Telecom Unveils Investment Slate Headed By ‘Gunshot’ & ‘Call Of Lobster’ View All November 7, 2026 10:59pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source TAICCA Four Joint Ventures showcase Deadline Four content funds, jointly established by Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA) and local companies, presented the projects they’ve been investing in over the past year in a TCCF showcase today. The line-up from the four funds – Chunghwa Digital Cultural and Creative Fund, Momomini Kids Content Fund, Joint Journey Creative and Enjoy Entertainment – include a wide range of films, series, live performances and immersive exhibitions. Opening the presentation, TAICCA chair Sue Wang said: “These ventures are managed by professional fund managers, based on rigorous risk assessment and management. We want to ensure professional governance in planning the portfolios of these funds.” Related Stories News Taiwan's Mirror Fiction Hands Out $50,000 In Awards For Book To Screen Adaptations News Taiwan's Chunghwa Telecom Unveils Investment Slate Headed By 'Gunshot' & 'Call Of Lobster' Enjoy Entertainment – established by TAICCA, Far EasTone Telecommunications (FET) and Far Reach Entertainment – focuses on premium content and international co-productions. Watch on Deadline The fund has so far made 15 investments since launch one year ago, including into Our Blues , a Taiwanese remake of CJ ENM’s Korean series, which will premiere on Netflix on December 3; and two recent hit films: Taiwanese horror film The Rope Curse 4: Kuntilanak and action film 96 Minute s. Gary Tsai, FET’s COO of Entertainment Service and GM of Far Reach Entertainment, said Rope Curse 4 had recently grossed $2.5M (NTD80M) in Taiwan theatres and has also been released in Malaysia, Indonesia, and soon Cambodia. “The film has Taiwanese taste and flavor but is still resonating with audiences across Asia,” Tsai said. Enjoy Entertainment has also invested in the ID Music Festival in Huashan cultural park, live musicals Her Voice and Don’t Cry Dancing Girls and an immersive exhibition created by illustrator Jimmy Liao. TAICCA is also partnered with Momomini, a Taiwanese media brand and YouTube content channel, in the Momomini Kids Content Fund, which specializes in kids content and has made six investments over the past year. In addition to TAICCA support, the fund is backed by the Fubon Cultural & Educational Foundation and DaWin Creative. Phoebe TSAI, COO of Momomini Kids Content Fund, introduced the slate which includes animations such as comedy adventure Who’s Our Sub Today , and Feifei , based on stories by Taiwanese artist and author Bei Lynn; as well as live-action shows such as Mogu & Perol , a collaboration with France’s Zephyr, and reality series Having Fun In The Mountains . The Momomini fund has also backed drama series Hello Mr President , about a kid who travels to Taipei to meet Taiwan’s president. “Very few production houses in Taiwan make drama for kids and teenagers – it’s been many years since any kids drama appeared on TV. So we’re very honored to have the opportunity with the support of TAICCA to invest in this drama,” said Tsai, adding that the show has finished shooting and will be on air from January next year. Founded in 2025, Joint Journey Creative (JJC) is a joint venture fund between SET Group, TAICCA, Chunghwa Telecom and Japan’s The Far Eastern TV Entertainment. Focused on investments in the transmedia and IP development space, the fund aims to connect Taiwanese creators with Asian and global markets. As one of its shareholders is Japanese, the fund has been building bridges between the content industries in Taiwan and Japan. Its investments include joining the production committee for multiple seasons of Japanese drama Midnight Diner, including season six. “We’re able to create relationships and trust between Taiwan and Japan to pave the way for more collaboration with Japanese parties,” said JJC President Joanne Tsai. JJC has also been running talent incubator programs including a romance drama series workshop that introduces Taiwanese talent to drama producers from Korea and Japan. “We’ve identified several quality scripts and here in TCCF we’re talking to our collaborators in Japan and Korea to see how we can bring them to screen,” said Tsai, adding that the fund is also working with partners in the rest of Asia, Europe and the U.S. The fourth fund, Chunghwa Digital Cultural and Creative Fund, was jointly established by TAICCA, Chunghwa Telecom, and E.Sun Bank, again with a mission to help Taiwanese cultural content reach global audiences, with capital of around $30M (NTD1BN). General Manager Lin Kun-feng explained that the fund is making equity investments into Taiwanese production company Damou Entertainment ( The World Between Us ) and IP development and publishing company Horiza Creations. Chunghwa is also investing in a wide range of film and TV projects, including C’est La Vi e, produced by and starring Esther Liu, Call Of Lobster , starring Chang Chen and Choi Siwon, and indie band Shallow Levee’s tour Speak in Silence.
