articles.title: Tom Rob Smith Writing Fiction Book Based On West Memphis Three Murder Case — Thessaloniki
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Magenta TV’s Cypriot-Set Thriller ‘Brothers’ Wasn’t Allowed To Shoot In The Country. The Producers Explain Why: “The Reasons Were Political” How A Mistake In Warner Bros. Contracts Helped Eleven Film & Jack Thorne Land ‘Lord Of The Flies’ TV Rights — Thessaloniki ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’ Trailer: More Plot Details Emerge In Latest Look At Fincher-Tarantino-Pitt Team-Up View All November 8, 2026 6:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jessie Misskelley Jr., Damien Echols, and Jason Baldwin Jamie McCarthy/WireImage. British writer Tom Rob Smith led an enlightening Q&A session on the difference between writing prose fiction and writing for the screen this afternoon at the Thessaloniki Film Festival, where he is one of the headline speakers. During the session, the Emmy winner, best known for the novel Child 44 and the series The Assassination of Gianni Versace: American Crime Story , also shared his next project: A fiction book based on the West Memphis Three murder case. “I can tell you because I’m coming right to the end of it,” Smith said when Deadline asked about his next project in Thessaloniki. Related Stories News Magenta TV's Cypriot-Set Thriller 'Brothers' Wasn't Allowed To Shoot In The Country. The Producers Explain Why: "The Reasons Were Political" News How A Mistake In Warner Bros. Contracts Helped Eleven Film & Jack Thorne Land 'Lord Of The Flies' TV Rights -- Thessaloniki “It’s based on an American crime. A case called the West Memphis Three. It was a killing that took place in 1993. No one was interested in it when it happened. Then HBO made a documentary about it called Paradise Lost . Everyone got involved, including Peter Jackson and Johnny Depp. I’m doing a fictionalized version of that account.” Watch on Deadline Smith added: “It’s not like Versace , which was a kind of mirror of the case. This is more like Child 44, where you’re taking a real case and telling a story about its ideas rather than the real people.” Damien Echols, Jessie Misskelley Jr., and Jason Baldwin, known as the West Memphis Three, were convicted as teenagers of the 1993 murders of three 8-year-old boys in West Memphis, Arkansas. The prosecutors at the time said the murders were committed as part of a satanic ritual. Echols was sentenced to death, while Misskelley Jr. and Baldwin were given life sentences. The trio was freed in 2011 after serving 18 years. New DNA evidence excluded the three men from all of the crime scene evidence found at the scene. Echols, Misskelley Jr., and Baldwin’s received public support from several high-profile figures, including Johnny Depp and Peter Jackson, who funded their legal defence. The men were also the subject of three Paradise Lost HBO documentaries by Joe Berlinger and Bruce Sinofsky. Deadline covered the documentaries and the trio’s release extensively at the time. The story was also captured in Devil’s Knot, a 2013 fiction feature directed by Atom Egoyan and starring Colin Firth and Reese Witherspoon. The Arkansas Supreme Court reopened the murder case and ordered fresh testing of the DNA found at the crime scene in 2024. The case is still ongoing. Thessaloniki runs until November 15. ‘Heated Rivalry’ Hat Trick: Hit Series Filming Season 2, Season 3 And A Movie Cameos By James Talarico, Emma Stone; Druski In Whiteface As Elizabeth Holmes ‘Godzilla’ Stalks $32M U.S. Bow, Best For Live-Action Foreign-Language Pic LACMA 2026 Art+Film Gala Red Carpet: Andrew Garfield, Anya Taylor-Joy & More Read More About: Comments

articles.title: The Other Midterms Flip: Broadcast Networks, Led by NBC, Dominated Election Night Coverage
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All November 6, 2026 3:18pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ryan Nobles (left), Savannah Guthrie, Tom Llamas, Kristen Welker and Hallie Jackson during NBC's 2026 election coverage. NBC News In addition to changing the composition of Congress and a number of statehouses, the midterm elections brought another kind of disruption to the status quo: For the first time in 6 election cycles, more people watched the returns come in on network TV than on cable. Per Nielsen ratings, 31.21 million people watched primetime election coverage on 13 broadcast and cable outlets Tuesday, significantly more than the 25.43 million viewers for the 2022 midterms. Of that audience, 57 percent (17.79 million) watched on broadcast outlets (NBC, ABC, CBS, Univision, Telemundo and PBS), and just 43 percent (13.42 million) on cable channels. That’s exactly the inverse of four years ago, when 57 percent of viewers went to cable for midterm coverage. It’s been 14 years since broadcast networks drew a clear majority of election night viewers (there was a roughly 50-50 split in 2016). That was also the last election a broadcaster led all comers on — and in both 2012 and this year, NBC finished first. The network had 6.74 million viewers in primetime Tuesday, more than doubling its 2022 average. ABC also improved considerably, growing by 57 percent from four years ago to 5.19 million viewers. CBS was off the pace some at 2.76 million, but it also improved by 8 percent from 2022. Univision (1.54 million), Telemundo (1.06 million) and PBS (about 500,000) made up the rest of the broadcast total. CNN and MS NOW also improved their numbers from 2022, but Fox News tumbled by almost 3.5 million viewers (though it still narrowly led its cable counterparts). The big three broadcasters, however, collectively gained more viewers than Fox News lost, so the off night for Fox doesn’t fully explain the shift in balance from cable to broadcast. So what does? For one, cable as a whole has also suffered across-the-board declines in the past four years. Homes with multi-channel providers (cable, satellite or digital services like YouTube TV or Hulu + Live TV) only represent 42.5 percent of TV homes now, down from 52.3 percent four years ago. That represents a loss of more than 10 million households. Some of it might also be ideological: Fox News leans right, and a night when Republicans took bruising losses might have helped drive ratings down there. MS NOW’s gains could similarly be put down to a blue wave helping the left-leaning channel. Tuesday’s viewer leaders, ABC and NBC, work to project big-tent inclusiveness, which seems to have paid off some. Marc Greenstein, executive vp creative production and field operations for NBC News , pointed to reporting initiatives on the NBC Nightly News and Meet the Press that try go beyond the “left-right food fight,” as he put it, and explore substantive issues and points of commonality. NBC also scored a multi-platform win Tuesday, as its dedicated “Kornacki Cam” live stream of analyst Steve Kornacki throughout the night was the most watched live stream of election coverage. NBC News as a whole led election night streams with 4.39 million hours of viewing on its YouTube channels, according to analytics firm Streams Charts (Twitch streamer Hasan Piker was second with 1.75 million hours). The Kornacki Cam was also something of a tech breakthrough for NBC News, Greenstein said. Kornacki was stationed about 15 feet away from the network’s main desk, but both the TV broadcast and the live stream were able to run simultaneously without interfering with one another. NBC used software from a company called Waves that filters audio, allowing for clean sound on both despite their proximity. “I talked to our engineering team maybe a week and a half before the elections, and it just so happened that [ Saturday Night Live ] had just started using it not too long before,” Greenstein said. “We were literally in the midst of rehearsals when we turned this thing on, and we decided to take the risk and put it out there because we thought it was much more important to really integrate Steve into the [TV] broadcast.” The live stream and on-air telecast ended up being mutually reinforcing, Greenstein said, possibly helping draw viewers in. NBC’s decision desk was also among the fastest to call some key races and the first to project Democratic control of the U.S. Senate. That said, Greeenstein didn’t know ahead of Tuesday night that NBC would end up at the top of the ratings. “We like to think we put in really good groundwork and incredible preparation going into the night, so we always hope that the audience will pay us back for that work,” Greenstein told The Hollywood Reporter . “One thing I will say is that I think NBC, maybe more than others, we just do big events well as a network. You look at the Super Bowl, the Olympics, election night — we just have a bigness and a gravitas. I think that matters on these type of nights, and I think that is an advantage we have.” THR

articles.title: Paul Howard, Son of Moe Howard of The Three Stooges, Dies at 91
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All November 6, 2026 3:57pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paul Howard with dad Moe Howard of The Three Stooges in the 1940s. Courtesy C3 Entertainment Paul Howard, the only son of Moe Howard of The Three Stooges and the narrator of a nine-part 2015 docuseries about the legendary American comedy team, has died. He was 91. Howard lived on Upper East Side of Manhattan and died this week, a spokesperson for C3 Entertainment, the owner of The Three Stooges license and brand, announced. He was the last remaining son of the original comedy team that consisted of Moe, his brothers Curly and Shemp and Larry Fine. Since Moe’s death in 1975 at age 77, Paul Howard served as a guardian of his father’s legacy, offering fans a unique, firsthand view of the man behind the iconic bowl-cut hairdo and timeless slapstick comedy. Related Stories TV 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' Producer Matthew Wright's Cause of Death Revealed Movies David Del Valle, Admired Historian of Horror Films, Dies at 77 He connected with generations of the Stooges faithful at conventions and events over the decades, sharing stories, memories and insights into the lives of his dad, his Uncle Shemp and his Uncle Curly. The docuseries Hey Moe, Hey Dad! features rare archival footage, personal family accounts and interviews with members of the Howard, Fine and DeRita families (Curly Joe DeRita was another member of the Stooges act) and fans including Whoopi Goldberg and Leonard Maltin. (The series is available on The Three Stooges+ YouTube channel .) Moe married Helen Schonberger — a cousin of famed escape artist Harry Houdini — in June 1925, and they welcomed their first child, Joan, in April 1927. Paul arrived on July 8, 1935. (Helen died six months after Moe did, and Joan, a writer and actress, died in September 2021 at age 94. Paul lived in Rifton, New York, for more than 40 years before relocating to Manhattan. His survivors include his wife, Joanne; his daughter, Jennifer; his nephew, Jeffrey; and a cousin, Janie Howard Hanky, daughter of Curly (she was born in May 1948). THR

articles.title: AFM Hot Project: Rosamund Pike to Star in Body Horror ‘Feed’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All November 6, 2026 4:45pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rosamund Pike Courtesy of Getty Oscar-nominated Gone Girl actress Rosamund Pike is set to star in and produce Feed , a body horror project from director Leslye Headland ( The Acolyte , Russian Doll ), which The Veterans is pitching to buyers at the American Film Market next week. Pike plays Erin, a desperate mother determined to make her tween gymnast daughter a star influencer. She finds an obscure collagen supplement that appears to help, but as fame and success arrive, her daughter begins a monstrous transformation. Daniella Isaacs ( People Who Knew Me) penned the script to Feed , inspired by Hanna Bergholm’s 2022 Finnish horror Hatching . Related Stories Movies David Del Valle, Admired Historian of Horror Films, Dies at 77 Movies Sebastián Lelio, Chilean Filmmaker Behind 'Disobedience,' 'The Wonder' and the Oscar-Winning 'A Fantastic Woman,' Dies at 52 Pike will produce through her Primitive Streak banner, alongside Shelley Browning for Magnolia Entertainment, Steven Schneider for Spooky Pictures, Ara Keshishian and Petr Jakl for ZQ Entertainment, and Sam Ritzenberg for Agile Films. ZQ Entertainment financed the development of the script. “Long have I wanted to make a film that plays anarchically with our obsession with social media and self-improvement, our desire for fame without notable admirable skill and, let’s put it out there, the monstrosity of modern motherhood,” said Pike in a statement. “ Feed is film that plays in the genre space, and plays into our current fears, as parents, as citizens, of the digital world . It is contemporary and confronting, and I have found my perfect collaborators in Daniella Isaacs and Leslye Headland, both women who know that to be a girl, in a body, is dangerous, febrile, intoxicating and dare we say it monstrous.” With its high-concept themes and body horror core, the project is clearly looking to play in the same space as Coralie Fargeat’s cross-over hit The Substance (2024), which grossed more than $77 million worldwide. The Veterans is handling international sales on Feed and will be pitching it to buyers at AFM next week. CAA Media Finance is handling U.S. rights. THR

articles.title: ‘The Remarried Empress’ Sets Disney+ and Hulu Record With Biggest Local Original Launch Ever
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All November 6, 2026 5:23pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Remarried Empress' Disney+ Logo text Disney has a royal hit on its hands. The Remarried Empress has become the most-viewed local original premiere ever across Disney+ and Hulu globally, setting a new benchmark for the company’s international programming just three days after its debut. The Korean romantic epic, starring Shin Mina, Ju Jihoon, Lee Jongsuk and Lee Seyoung, launched Nov. 3 with four episodes. Disney said Friday the series also delivered the biggest Korean title premiere to date in more than 50 markets, including the U.S., Britain, France, Spain, Germany, Mexico, Chile, Australia, New Zealand and Canada. Related Stories Movies AFM Hot Project: Rosamund Pike to Star in Body Horror 'Feed' Movies Sebastián Lelio, Chilean Filmmaker Behind 'Disobedience,' 'The Wonder' and the Oscar-Winning 'A Fantastic Woman,' Dies at 52 Disney did not disclose viewing figures. The global premiere record is based on views during the show’s first three days of availability. The Remarried Empress has supplanted Disney’s previous Korean breakout, Moving , as the streamer’s biggest local-original premiere. The 2023 superhero drama became Disney+ and Hulu’s most watched Korean original and was a particularly powerful draw in South Korea and across Asia . The early results for The Remarried Empress suggest a more broadly global breakthrough, with its records extending across Europe and the Americas. Set in a fantasy world of rival empires, the series follows Empress Navier (Shin), whose marriage to Emperor Sovieshu (Ju) begins to unravel when he falls for Rashta (Lee Seyoung), a runaway slave. Navier agrees to a divorce on the condition that she be allowed to marry Heinrey (Lee Jongsuk), the crown prince of a neighboring kingdom, setting off a struggle over love, dignity and imperial power. Yeoh Geena and Hyun Choongyeol adapted the series for the screen, with Cho Suwon ( Still 17 , Pinocchio ) directing. The series is an unusually perfect fit for Disney+, pairing the royal grandeur and storybook fantasy associated with the Disney brand with the scandal, romantic reversals, glossy production values, and wildly attractive stars that have made K-drama a global phenomenon. The show’s world is one familiar to Disney princesses, but its heroine’s challenges — infidelity, divorce and the prospect of a strategically advantageous second marriage — give the fantasy an appealingly grown-up melodramatic charge. The launch follows months of anticipation for the series, including sold-out preview screenings at the Busan International Film Festival. Its trailer generated 13 million views across YouTube and social media in its first 48 hours, according to Disney. The Naver webtoon on which the show is based has amassed nearly 3 billion views, making it one of the form’s most popular titles. Disney brought the premiere forward by a day from its originally scheduled Nov. 4 launch, announcing the change at a Seoul press conference earlier this week as a thank-you to fans. Following the four-episode premiere, two new episodes will arrive every Wednesday beginning Nov. 11, with the finale scheduled for Nov. 25. THR

articles.title: Adam Driver Not Participating in ‘Girls’ Revival: “Wish Them the Best of Luck”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All November 6, 2026 5:24pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ilene S. Landress, Zosia Mamet, Lena Dunham, Jennifer Konner, Allison Williams, Adam Driver and Judd Apatow attend HBO's Post 2013 Golden Globe Awards Party. Frederick M. Brown/Getty Images Logo text Adam Driver has confirmed he will not be involved in the upcoming HBO revival of Girls . In October, it was announced that Lena Dunham , Allison Williams, Jemima Kirke, Zosia Mamet and Andrew Rannells are all set to return for the limited five-episode reboot of the series. Left off the confirmed list of castmembers coming back was Driver, who appeared in all six seasons of Girls . When asked by CinemaBlend in an interview published Friday if viewers should expect him to reprise his Girls character, he said, “No, but I wish them the best of luck.” Related Stories Movies Adam Driver Says "the Ship Has Sailed" on Playing Kylo Ren: "No More 'Star Wars'" Movies Adam Driver Confirms 'Heat 2' Villain Role, Shares Michael Mann Update After Accidental Shooting The two-time Oscar nominee portrayed Adam Sackler, the on-and-off boyfriend of Dunham’s Hannah Horvath. Dunham, who created, wrote and starred in the beloved comedy-drama, recounted Driver’s alleged temper on set of the show in her 2026 memoir Famesick , and further alleged that he threw a chair at a wall near her. “At the time, I didn’t have the skill to … it never entered my mind to say, ‘I am your boss, you can’t speak to me this way,’” Dunham said in an April interview with The Guardian about the actor. “And, at that point in my 20s, I still thought that’s what great male geniuses do: eviscerate you. Which is weird, because I was raised by a male genius who would never do that.” Dunham will executive produce the Girls reboot with Judd Apatow (who was an EP on the original) and Ilene S. Landress and Michael P. Cohen of Good Thing Going. Williams, Kirke, Mamet and Rannells are co-EPs. Production begins in 2027. THR

articles.title: ‘Ellen DeGeneres Show’ Producer Matthew Wright’s Cause of Death Revealed
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All November 6, 2026 6:04pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Matthew Wright and Ellen DeGeneres Matthew Wright's Instagram The cause of death for longtime The Ellen DeGeneres Show executive producer Matthew Wright has been revealed. Wright died Oct. 30 in Los Angeles at age 52. According to a death certificate obtained by People , his cause of death was cardiopulmonary arrest, with hypertension listed as the underlying cause. Obstructive sleep apnea and Class II obesity were also listed as contributing conditions. Wright’s family launched a GoFundMe page seeking support. “His husband, father, sister and niece are in New York, desperate to be reunited for a proper goodbye. We’re asking for all of his friends, who Matt loved so fully, to help the family at this time,” reads the fundraiser description. “As many of you know, Matt & Justin were both laid off this summer. And the unexpected costs of getting Matt home, a funeral and a memorial are impossible for the family to bear.” Related Stories Movies Paul Howard, Son of Moe Howard of The Three Stooges, Dies at 91 Movies David Del Valle, Admired Historian of Horror Films, Dies at 77 Earlier this week, Ellen DeGeneres shared an emotional Instagram video remembering Wright. “He was an amazing guy. He was funny. God, he made me laugh. He would surprise me with things that he did all the time. He was smart. He was kind. He was the part of our show that — I mean, everyone loved him. I loved him. And it’s just shocking,” she said. “We’re gonna miss him. He is and always will be the glue to our entire family at The Ellen Show. ” DeGeneres also reflected on Wright’s close friendship with former Ellen DJ Stephen “tWitch” Boss, who died in 2022 , saying she believes the two are now together again, “dancing and laughing.” Andy Lassner, who also worked with Wright on Ellen , shared a tribute to him on Instagram , revealing that he had seen Wright just hours before his death. “We are all in shock. He was a brilliant producer and an even better human being,” Lassner wrote. “My heart breaks for his husband, Justin, his family, and all of us who loved him. I was so lucky to work beside Matt for so many years and to call him my friend. We should have had so much more time with him.” Wright spent 16 years working on The Ellen DeGeneres Show , joining the daytime talk show in 2006 and remaining with it until its conclusion in 2022. During his tenure, he rose through the ranks to become an executive producer. He is also a nine-time Emmy winner. THR

articles.title: James Bond Surprise: Robert Pattinson Screen Tested to Play 007
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit , Aaron Couch November 6, 2026 6:09pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Robert Pattinson Stefanie Keenan Logo text In a surprise few saw coming, Robert Pattinson has emerged as a contender for 007. The actor, 40, is among those who have screen tested for the role of James Bond, multiple sources tell The Hollywood Reporter , joining hopefuls Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor. Conventional wisdom has been that the next man to get the license to kill would not be a globally recognized star like Pattinson, one of the biggest actors of his age cohort, and already the face of DC Studios’ Batman franchise. The screen tests are said to have occurred the weekend of Oct. 24. THR previously reported that four, possibly five actors were in the mix but only three names surfaced at the time. Related Stories Movies Robert Pattinson to Be Honored With American Cinematheque Award Movies Scarlett Johansson Breaks Silence on 'The Batman Part II' Role: "It Was Very Hard to Figure Out" Another name now surfacing as one of the Bond mystery men is Nicholas Hoult, a runnerup to Pattinson for Batman years ago. Pattinson is a favorite of auteurs from Robert Eggers and the Safdie brothers to Christopher Nolan, whose 2020 spy movie Tenet might feel like a Bond audition in hindsight. And more importantly, he worked with Bond director Denis Villeneuve on the upcoming Dune: Part 3 , which bows Dec. 18 and is said to have gone well for the two men. The actor is in the midst of the biggest year of his career, with a key role in Nolan’s The Odyssey and as the co-lead of A24 hit The Drama and anchoring the well-reguarded movie Primetime , also from A24. He’s currently filming The Batman Part II in London, where screen tests have been taking place. Amazon had no comment on the testing. While conventional wisdom goes against a world famous Bond, these are unprecedented times in the franchise. It is the first Bond movie made under the control of Amazon, which bought out the creative rights from the Broccoli family in February 2025. And producing are Spider-Man ‘s Amy Pascal and David Heyman, producer of the Harry Potter movies. A young Pattinson broke out with a tragic role in 2005’s Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire , before gaining global fame a few years later in Twilight . The Bond casting search comes 21 years after Daniel Craig was set as the next James Bond back in October 2005. He retired from the role after five films with 2021’s No Time to Die , his tenure including the franchise’s first and only $1 billion hit, the 2012 feature Skyfall . THR

articles.title: After 2026 Midterms, Bill Maher Asks Trump, “Donnie, Are You OK?”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All November 6, 2026 8:29pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bill Maher and President Donald Trump. Paul Morigi/Getty Images, Tasos Katopodis/Getty Images Logo text Bill Maher reacted to the 2026 midterm results during the Friday episode of Real Time , moreso reacting to President Donald Trump ‘s response to the election. During the host’s monologue, he said he predicted the midterms would be positive for Democrats. “Well, look, I hate to gloat, but sorry, I have to do a little bit because everybody was hedging about this election,” he said, as a montage of clips of him predicting the results was played. One thing Maher said he couldn’t have anticipated? Trump’s response to the results, he said. Related Stories TV The Other Midterms Flip: Broadcast Networks, Led by NBC, Dominated Election Night Coverage News Jimmy Kimmel, Seth Meyers Call Out Trump's "I Wasn't on the Ballot" Excuse for Midterm Losses: "Shut Up" “Here’s something I could not have predicted, which was Trump’s reaction to the election. He said, ‘Congratulations to the Democrats, they did a good job,'” Maher said wide-eyed, looking around at his Real Time audience. “Donnie, are you OK? I know we’ve been feuding. You sound unwell. You’re not even going to fake it was rigged?” He continued, “And let me tell you something, even with the attempted rigging — and they did try to rig it in every different kind of way; mail-in balloting, intimidating the voters, all that shit — democracy, man. Kind of fucking awesome.” During an interview with The New York Times shortly before 10:30 p.m. on Tuesday, the president said he was “absolutely willing” to accept the results. Trump added, “We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out.” However, he also ranted about the midterms, writing on Truth Social that if he was on the ballot, “we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” Maher’s comment about “feuding” with the president was likely a reference to their recent back-and-forth that was heightened after Trump penned a lengthy social media post where he slammed the comedian as a “complete and total loser,” and shared more details about their recent dinner at the White House. Maher responded to the rant during last week’s Oct. 30 episode of Real Time , joking that the president “went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store.” Elsewhere in the episode, the comedian said he thinks the president has been “amazingly humble” amid the results. “I thought by this time, he’d be suing the voters by name, individually, and arresting the poll workers. Instead, even he was like, ‘You know, even I’m sick of me a little bit.’” He joked that Trump saying he has “a lot of friends in the Democratic party” might open the door for him to visit the White House for a third time. “Wow, I might get to go again. Look at that,” he joked. THR

articles.title: ‘Hold Onto Me,’ Cyprus’ First Oscar Hopeful, Stars a Newcomer and a ‘Dogtooth’ Actor in a Very Personal Father-Daughter Drama
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All November 6, 2026 9:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Hold Onto Me' Courtesy of PÖFF It’s summertime in Cyprus. Iris, 11, spends her days with her older best friend, Danae. But then she hears that her grandfather has died. Visiting town for his funeral is Iris’ father, Aris, whom she has never known. That is the starting point for Hold Onto Me , the feature debut of writer-director Myrsini Aristidou. Can Iris and Aris find a way to connect, even though he is a petty criminal and doesn’t want to take responsibility? Iris doesn’t give up and gets involved in his various schemes, despite warnings from her mother and her older brother. What begins as a stubborn attempt to reconnect slowly unfolds into a fragile bond. But then, Aris’ dark past gets them into trouble. Related Stories TV 'The Remarried Empress' Sets Disney+ and Hulu Record With Biggest Local Original Launch Ever Movies AFM Hot Project: Rosamund Pike to Star in Body Horror 'Feed' Hold Onto Me , starring newcomer Maria Petrova and Christos Passalis ( Dogtooth ), premiered at Sundance, where it won the World Cinema Dramatic Audience Award. It then became Cyprus’ first-ever international feature film Oscar submission. Now, the film screens in the Just Film youth and children’s event of the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) in Estonia. Cercamon is handling sales. Lasse Ulvedal Tolbøll was the cinematographer on the Cyprus-Denmark-Greece co-production. The editors were Jenna Mangulad and Aristidou. Aristidou and Monica Nicolaidou produced the film, with Thomas J. Mangan IV and Mark Hollinger as the executive producers and Anders N.U. Berg, Konstantina Stavrianou and Rena Vougioukalou as co-producers. Watch a trailer for the film right here. Aristidou talked to THR about her bittersweet first feature, pairing an unknown as the young girl at the heart of it with the man who played the son in Dogtooth , her desire to make Hold Onto Me feel different and that first-ever Cypriot Oscar submission. The father-daughter theme is one that the filmmaker has also explored in two shorts. “I feel like this is like a triptych,” Aristidou tells THR . “My first short film called Semele in 2015 is also a father and daughter story and was the first time that I began exploring this theme. Then I did my second short film, Aria , which has a father daughter dynamic again, but with an older daughter – she’s a teenager. They were short, and I wanted to go deeper in this subject matter.” Hold Onto Me allowed her to do so in feature form, but she wanted it to be surprising and different from other films about similar familial relationships. “I wanted to use the archetypical relationship of father and daughter within a love story,” she explains. “It’s kind of a love story. It’s about two people who don’t know how to be together. They are sort of strangers in the beginning. They meet, then slowly come together, and they end up accepting each other or even loving each other in their own way. And when you set this up within the framework of a father, daughter and their family, it creates a different energy.” That is driven by societal expectations we have for family members. “When someone is your family, you are expected to love them, or you have more expectations than from just any stranger,” Aristidou highlights. “However, they are strangers. They have never really met or had any shared experiences. So this is the first time they are reconnecting, and I wanted to explore this.” The characters and story of Hold Onto Me keep developing as the movie unfolds, and that is by design. “On a first feature, it’s very easy to get very obsessed with what you want to do, so I was very tough on myself,” Aristidou tells THR . “When it comes to narrative structure and characters, I like to move the story forward in every scene. When I was writing, I was really thinking about that.” ‘Hold Onto Me’ Courtesy of PÖFF One key reason that the filmmaker has returned to father-daughter stories lies in her own life experience. “It’s very personal in many ways,” she shares. “My parents divorced when I was very young, and I was not really growing up with my dad. He wasn’t entirely gone like this character, but he was not that present. And he’s not a criminal but a writer. It was only when I turned 12 or 13 that we started having more of a relationship. And when I was 15, 16, we really bonded. We reached a point where we started talking about everything and we really forgave each other. We reconnected, and there was really an understanding and acceptance.” The film’s setting is also personal. Hold Onto Me was shot in Cyprus, and for the writer-director, it was particularly important to film near the sea. “I grew up near the sea, so there are references that are very personal,” Aristidou tells THR . “My dad used to have a small boat when I was a kid. I also always used to hang out with older kids because I had an older friend who was my best friend. There is a lot of truth in the film.” The chemistry between Iris and Aris in the film is palpable To ensure the right fit, casting took a lot of time. “We were shooting in July. Around April, I decided I was going to work with Christos,” the director recalls. She wanted to see him interact with different kids, most of them in Athens. The actor then went to Cyprus to meet the girl who ended up making the cut. “I saw Christos with Maria, and they felt family in a strange way,” Aristidou tells THR . “They phsically have things in common and look a bit like family. But Maria had zero experience. She had never done anything [in acting]. But I felt that there was something with them.” ‘Hold Onto Me’ Courtesy of PÖFF With the big casting decisions made, she was hoping to rehearse with the two leads, but that didn’t work out. “Christos was shooting something. And then, he got COVID, so he only arrived a day before the shoot,” she recalls. “We only read the script once, and then I just started shooting with both of them. So I just threw Maria into the wild with him. But I think it worked out perfectly because they didn’t know each other really – just like their characters.” The Oscar submission was, of course, special for the writer-director feel, especially since it’s the first for Cyprus. “It’s a big honor,” Aristidou shares. “I suddenly felt very responsible for my whole country. But in many ways, this film and I are carving this path for Cyprus. There was no film from Cyprus in Sundance before, and then we won an audience award. And then the Oscars . I guess it’s a new thing for everyone here and for me. So I’m learning a lot in the process. I know we’re a bit of the underdogs, but I’m trying to enjoy the ride.” So, what’s next for the filmmaker? “I really love this dynamic of strangers coming together and realizing how similar they are or bonding,” Aristidou says. “I don’t think I would do a father-daughter film again. But there’s something about this narrative arc that I really love. Actually, I’m trying to work on a TV show, which is a crime, spy thriller. But, let’s see. I’m working on a couple of things, and I’m reading a lot of scripts because my agents in the U.S. are sending a lot of scripts to read. So I’m also open to directing something I haven’t written.” THR

articles.title: PÖFF Stands With Ukraine: A Look at Films Featured at Tallinn Made Despite, and Because of, the War
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All November 7, 2026 3:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'To Live to Die' Courtesy of PÖFF The Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ) has been standing with Ukraine and showing solidarity since the 2022 full-scale invasion of the country by Russia, featuring Ukrainian films, showcasing works-in-progress and organizing Ukraine-themed panels in its industry strand Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event. “We are obliged to do everything possible to help and support the Ukrainian film industry at this difficult time, but even more so the Ukrainian people,” PÖFF founder and CEO Tiina Lokk said in 2022. This year, for the 30th anniversary edition of the festival, its PÖFF Standing With Ukraine film showcase is back. “Ukraine is fighting not only for Ukraine, but also for Europe and the democratic world,” Lokk tells THR . ”And so we are going to support Ukraine and stand with Ukraine as long as needed. It is important for Ukraine to remain very visible and to keep its culture. And it is very important for every country.” Related Stories Oscars 2027: Int'l Films in Focus 'Hold Onto Me,' Cyprus' First Oscar Hopeful, Stars a Newcomer and a 'Dogtooth' Actor in a Very Personal Father-Daughter Drama TV 'The Remarried Empress' Sets Disney+ and Hulu Record With Biggest Local Original Launch Ever Marge Liiske, head of the Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event, emphasizes that the industry strand of the Estonian festival also continues to put a spotlight on the war. “We have since the 2022 [full-scale invasion by Russia] very supportive of Ukraine and have always reflected that in our program, both for the festival and the industry events,” she tells THR . She and Triin Tramberg , PÖFF’s new artistic director, highlight that they will always put a spotlight on Ukraine and other countries standing up for important democratic values. “Throughout our program, we’re supporting countries that are fighting for their rights and for their democracy,” Tramberg tells THR . “We also have to understand where we are located. Standing With Ukraine is really important for us as a region, and it speaks to our audiences and our communities, including Ukrainians who live here. It is important to have this moment where they see their own cinema.” PÖFF’s Standing With Ukraine strand this year showcases nine features that are diverse and different. And many also screen in other Tallinn strands, as you can see below. Take a closer look at the films right here. Slava: Shooting With Music Director: Jacqui Morris, David Morris Festival section: Special Screenings ‘Slava: Shooting With Music’ Courtesy of PÖFF Silence the guns and let the music play! This world premiere is about the power of music and culture more broadly. “Sviatoslav Vakarchuk is the lead singer of Okean Elzy, Ukraine’s most successful rock band. He is a former politician and activist who has a PhD in theoretical physics,” reads a synopsis of the film. “Slava has been compared to Bruce Springsteen and Paul McCartney, and his songs are an important part of Ukrainian identity, part of the country’s cultural DNA. He is now channeling his talents to liberate his country.” After playing more than 200 concerts for the troops, he decided to take his band on a worldwide tour to bolster the morale of Ukrainian refugees living abroad. And an international coalition of artists, including Coldplay, stepped up to support the band. Highlights the Synopsis: “Another reason for the tour was to leave a lasting legacy in the minds of the rest of the world of Ukrainian culture – a unique culture Russia has been trying to eradicate for centuries.” Vesna Director: Rostislav Kirpicenko Festival section: Baltic Film Competition ‘Vesna’ Courtesy of PÖFF Honoring the dead becomes dangerous in times of war, as this film shows. In a town in southeastern Ukraine that is occupied by Russian forces, burying the dead has actually been forbidden. The church of a young priest has even been turned into a morgue for executed civilians. But the priest begins to quietly resist, secretly returning the bodies to their families at great personal risk. And in the process, he forms an unlikely bond with an 11-year-old boy who becomes a silent witness to his rebellion. The drama adds a focus on the psychological and emotional warfare beyond the physical battles. “Lithuanian-born Ukrainian director Rostislav Kirpicenko uncovers cynicism, blackmail, and the brutal cruelty of the merciless attackers,” the PÖFF website says about the film. What would you do if you were in the shoes of the locals who face horrible choices – fight back, obey and adapt to the brutal new reality, or even betray? Emphasizes the festival website: “The mightiest impact here is heartbreaking authenticity, showing how Ukrainians are surviving the ongoing occupation.” I Rarely Wake up Dreaming Director: Isabelle Stever Section: Standing With Ukraine ‘I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming’ Courtesy of X Filme Creative Pool War surely can affect love. But how does the transition from peace to warfare – yes, Russia’s full-scale invasion! – affect a queer couple in Ukraine, especially when the geopolitical change comes in parallel with a gender transition? I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming made an impact when it world-premiered at Locarno, leading to conversations between viewers and beyond. You can read our chat with the creators right here. But you really have to watch the film to see how the relationship between Olya and Oleh is put to the test when the gender transition allows the couple to get married, but also stirs up all sorts of personal and national identity struggles. To Die to Live Director: Yuliia Hontaruk Festival section: Doc@PÖFF Baltic Competition ‘To Live to Die’ Courtesy of PÖFF Yuliia Hontaruk’s doc introduces us to three men who have experienced huge change over the course of their lives. In 2014, they had no military experience but volunteered to go to the front line. When they returned home after two years, they tried to find an ordinary life rhythm again. But they just can’t seem to succeed. After all, the war has left its mark on their bodies and minds, which affects their family lives. “It is a brutal truth that is not always easy to capture on film,” the PÖFF summary of the film notes. “And then the men have to go back to war. Their previous experience was merely a preparation for what would happen in February 2022, when Russia launched a full-scale invasion. They are back on the front line, now fully aware of what this does to them.” The filmmaker followed the three men for 12 years, leading to a film whose fragmented feel mirrors the fragmented lives and trauma. Wings Director: Ana Rocha de Sousa Section: Standing With Ukraine ‘Wings’ You can take people out of a war zone. But can you ever really take the war trauma out of their lives? Or in other words: Is living in peace the same as enjoying peace of mind? Wings is a drama, shot in Ukraine and Portugal with creatives from both countries, but it was inspired by the real-life story of a Ukrainian family who fled the war and found refuge in Portugal. If you are interested in a deep dive into the lasting impact and trauma of experiencing war and displacement, plus how there may be a path to finding hope, this one is for you. Living On Director: Nerijus Milerius Festival section: Doc@PÖFF Baltic Competition ‘Living On’ Courtesy of PÖFF Art therapy at a veterans’ theater, yoga sessions, hair salons, para-archery and mountain peaks and much more feature in another Ukraine-focused world premiere coming to PÖFF. Standing with Ukraine is exactly what Lithuanian philosopher and director Nerijus Milerius did when he volunteered to drive cars with medical aid to Ukraine’s front lines. Between August 2024 and June 2026, he documented his experiences on 15 dangerous missions and used the filmed material for his fourth feature. “He records daily life under attack and hears dark humor in Kyiv, Kharkiv, Odesa, Kherson and other bombed areas where he needed a fixer even to gain access,” reads a Tallinn festival tease for the film. And it highlights: “Milerius captures Ukrainians’ resilience and spirit.” Slava Director: Denis Sobolev Section: Standing With Ukraine ‘Slava’ No, this one is not about the rock star Slava we met earlier but a woman. And the story is much more complex. The political thriller is based on a real-life story and shows Slava and Yaroslav Stetsko launching an information campaign, via media and protests, in the U.S. and Europe in the 1960s. Their message: the KGB and the USSR are the architects of political murder beyond Soviet borders. That makes a trial in Karlsruhe, West Germany, take on a political dimension. Bohdan Stashynsky, a KGB agent, has confessed to killing Stepan Bandera, a controversial far-right Ukrainian politician. But while the case is being framed as a “routine” crime, the activists want to highlight that Moscow is exporting political violence via assassinations abroad. The Kremlin responds with threats. And the activists’ friends become concerned, urging them to soften the rhetoric. To see how it all plays out, you’ll have to watch Slava . Camouflage Director: Mykyta Gibalenko Section: Standing With Ukraine ‘Camouflage’ A clash of identity and war already played a key role in one of the films we discussed earlier. They are also in focus in this movie, which premiered at Venice, but in a different way. Vitaly, 22, studies German and moves from Ukraine to Germany, leaving behind his mother, a teacher shaped by the Soviet era, and his sister. And once in Munich, Vitaly finally feels free to be himself and live the life he wants to lead. But a year later, Russia invades Ukraine. And, as you may have expected, due to the war, his mother and sister have to flee their home and seek refuge with Vitaly in Munich. That’s where they learn about his new identity… Traces Directors: Alisa Kovalenko, Marysia Nikitiuk Section: Best of Docs ‘Traces’ Last, but certainly not least, PÖFF Standing With Ukraine will screen a Ukrainian awards season contender. Silence isn’t always golden. Just listen to the six Ukrainian women who survived sexual violence and torture during the Russian war against Ukraine and speak out in Traces . Iryna Dovhan, a former captive-turned-activist, documents testimonies of women affected by the trauma of war-related violence. And following her work, the film weaves together a portrait of collective trauma while opening space for hope. The film premiered in the Panorama section of the Berlin International Film Festival, winning the program’s best documentary award , and became Ukraine’s submission for the best international feature film Oscar. THR

Both British actors certainly have the acting pedigree to play the suave spy, taking up the mantle after Daniel Craig’s 15-year run. They also have a keen awareness of what it takes to work in major franchise fare: Pattinson stars as Batman for DC Studios and is an alum of both the “Twilight” and “Harry Potter” franchises; meanwhile, Hoult plays Lex Luthor in DC’s Superman movies and starred in the 2010s “X-Men” prequel trilogy. Getting Bond 26 off the ground has been a top priority for the property’s new stewards, producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman. Since then, nearly every 30-something British actor’s name has been bandied about in the U.K. and U.S. press, with rumored top contenders including Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden. Variety has learned that Harry Styles has had discussions about the part, and Theo James, 41, also hasn’t been ruled out. Pierce Brosnan, the Bond of the ’90s, recently gave his stamp of approval to Turner, while Gary Oldman threw his weight behind Lowden, his “Slow Horses” co-star. (Oldman also claimed that the next James Bond has already been picked, but no official casting announcement has been made.) Amazon declined to comment on the casting rumors. articles.title: Taiwan’s Chunghwa Telecom Unveils 10 Content Investments, From ‘Gunshot’ to ‘Call of Lobster’
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 7:36pm PT Taiwan’s Chunghwa Telecom Unveils 10 Content Investments, From ‘Gunshot’ to ‘Call of Lobster’ By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest AI Filmmaking Platform Core Studio Launches at Taiwan Creative Content Fest With 24 Specialized Agents 7 hours ago Chang Chen Urges Emerging Taiwanese Actors to ‘Be Like Water’ at Taiwan Creative Content Fest Golden Horse Showcase 12 hours ago Taiwan Audience Study Highlights Cross-Platform IP Opportunities as AI Raises New Risks for Content Industry 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chunghwa/TCCF Chunghwa Telecom , Taiwan’s largest telecom operator, announced 10 new investments at its “Chunghwa Telecom Content Slate and Partnership Showcase,” spanning film, TV and music projects as well as stakes in two production companies. The company pitched the slate as a way to back Taiwanese original IP and link local creators with partners abroad. The event was held at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF), which Chunghwa has sponsored for five consecutive years. Taiwan’s Minister of Culture Li Yuan attended, alongside Chunghwa chief business officer and senior executive VP Lin Wen-chiyh, consumer business group president Hu Hsueh-hai and representatives from the presenting teams. Related Stories Sundance Hires Tracy Brady as Marketing, Communications Chief “Chunghwa Telecom is like a pyramid,” Li said. “I am grateful that, beyond building a strong foundation through its thriving core business, the company is also willing to invest at the very top of the pyramid, supporting film and television professionals as they continue moving forward and creating even better work.” The slate includes four scripted series: police crime drama “Gunshot,” made with PTS Taigi TV, the Taiwanese-language channel of public broadcaster PTS, and S11 Partners; family fantasy “Yesterday’s Daughter, Tomorrow’s Mother,” from producer Phoebe Ma and director Hung Tzu-peng; fantasy adventure “Guides to the World Below,” adapted from a popular Taiwanese comic; and “C’est la Vie,” an urban drama about food and women’s personal growth, with actress Esther Liu as executive producer. Chunghwa has also invested in “Next Z Chef,” billed as Taiwan’s first cooking competition show for young people. Film investments include “Demon of the East: Black Condo,” a horror project tied to a cinematic universe that crosses four Asian countries, and “Call of Lobster,” which won the Chunghwa Telecom Award at TCCF’s 2024 pitching sessions and has since been selected for the Culture Ministry’s first international flagship cohort under its Great Voyage Project. The investments also extend to music, including “Speak in Silence,” an Asian tour by Taiwanese indie band Shallow Levée. The tour will run to about 50 shows in Taiwan and eight other countries across Asia. Alongside project financing, Chunghwa and Chunghwa Digital Cultural and Creative have taken equity positions in DaMou Entertainment and Horiza Creations. DaMou has produced series including “The World Between Us II” and “Wave Makers.” Horiza uses community engagement and crowdfunding to gauge what audiences want. “Chunghwa Telecom is more than just a platform operator; we are also a driving force behind the long-term development of the content industry,” Lin said. “Moving forward, we will continue to connect funding, creative talent, and domestic and international partners, leveraging our group’s resources and industry partnerships to help Taiwanese content reach international markets.” Chunghwa-backed films “Arrested Memory” and “The Photo From 1977” received a combined 12 nominations at the 63rd Golden Horse Awards. The company operates mobile and broadband networks as well as the MOD IPTV service and the Hami Video streaming platform, which together have more than 3 million subscribers. While talking about his role in James Gray’s new movie “Paper Tiger,” Driver was asked by Cinema Blend if he will be returning for the revival. “No, but I wish them the best of luck,” he told the outlet. News of the new “Girls” series broke in mid-October , with creator and star Lena Dunham set to return as Hannah Horvath alongside co-stars Allison Williams as Marnie Michaels, Jemima Kirke as Jessa Johansson and Zosia Mamet as Shoshanna Shapiro. Andrew Rannells also returns to the role of Elijah Krantz. Related Stories Liev Schreiber and Stephen Graham Lead Apple TV's Gripping Serial Killer Thriller 'Nocturne': TV Review The series will have a limited five-episode run on HBO with production starting in 2027. Driver’s career took off after his run as Hannah’s boyfriend on “Girls.” In addition to his role as Kylo Ren in three “Star Wars” movies, he starred in “Marriage Story” and “The Meyerowitz Stories” for Noah Baumbach; “The Last Duel” and “House of Gucci” for Ridley Scott; “Ferrari” for Michael Mann and this year’s “Misty Green.” He’s also worked with director Jim Jarmusch on “Paterson,” “The Dead Don’t Die” and “Father Mother Sister Brother.” In her recent memoir “Famesick,” Dunham described her tumultuous relationship with Driver, saying, “He could be short-tempered and verbally aggressive, condescending and physically imposing. He could also be protective, loving even,” Dunham writes. After the last episode of “Girls” wrapped, Dunham says Driver told her, “I hope you know I’ll always love you” before he said goodbye. articles.title: Stephen Chow Told Japan to Stop Aping Kung Fu, Says Boss of Film Fund Behind Kore-eda Hirokazu’s ‘Look Back’
articles.full_text: × Nov 6, 2026 8:41pm PT Stephen Chow Told Japan to Stop Aping Kung Fu, Says Boss of Film Fund Behind Kore-eda Hirokazu’s ‘Look Back’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘3 Body Problem’ Director Derek Tsang Boards DEA True-Crime Series ‘Group 41’ From Zhang Yimou’s ‘Shadow’ Producer Jonah Greenberg (EXCLUSIVE) 6 hours ago Stephen Chow Told Japan to Stop Aping Kung Fu, Says Boss of Film Fund Behind Kore-eda Hirokazu’s ‘Look Back’ 11 hours ago Why ‘Suits’ Japan Swapped Drugs for Cash: NBCUniversal, TBS Format Chiefs on Localizing Hits at Taiwan Creative Content Fest 13 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Naman Ramachandran Hong Kong star-director Stephen Chow once told K2 Pictures founder Kii Muneyuki that Japanese filmmakers should stop imitating kung fu and build action films on their own martial arts instead, Kii said Saturday at Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei. “He said, ‘You have karate, judo, jujitsu and kendo. That is Japanese culture. Only you can turn it into action films, so you should be the ones doing it. Stop aping kung fu,’” recalled Kii, who said he has shared drinks with Chow in Tokyo a few times. He added that he agreed with Chow, pointing to Netflix sumo drama “Sanctuary” as the kind of project that draws on culture unique to Japan. Related Stories Sundance Hires Tracy Brady as Marketing, Communications Chief Kii’s K2P Film Fund I, which backed Kore-eda Hirokazu’s “Look Back,” could also open its doors to new investors. The fund closed its $33 million equity round in February. Kii said more companies approached K2 about investing after the close, and that the round could reopen if existing backers agree. He has not yet decided whether to do so. Some 30 companies have invested so far, led by MUFG Bank, Japan’s biggest lender. Other backers include Bandai, Dentsu, the government-backed Development Bank of Japan and property companies Tokyu Land and Mori Trust. Kii serves as the fund’s general partner. TThe equity is being paired with loans that are being added one after another and will ultimately total $67 million, Kii said, for a planned total of $100 million and a target of 50 films over seven years. Kii shared the stage with director Nagata Koto, whose Fukushima-set noir “The Nuke Crab” K2 unveiled at Cannes in May. Kii said he and Nagata are aiming for a hit in Japan and in Eastern Europe, including Poland and Ukraine, where he believes audiences who lived through the Chernobyl accident might connect with it. The project is in development, with a shoot targeted for next year. The film follows those who profited from the huge sums that flowed from across Japan into the radiation clean-up of the Tohoku region. Nagata, whose “ Baka’s Identity ” competed at Busan last year, described the subject as socially taboo in Japan and the kind of material that productions involving TV networks or major studios would never take on. “When I took it to Kii-san, he immediately said, ‘That sounds interesting, let’s do it,’ and got it started,” Nagata said. Pairing Japan with one other specific market is a strategy K2 calls “Japan plus one.” “What Americans like about Japan, what the French like about Japan, what Taiwanese audiences like about Japan and what Koreans like about Japan are completely different,” Kii said. “The Japan that Japanese people like is different again.” Kii said that while the world knows about the Chernobyl disaster itself, far less is known about how the lives of people in the area changed afterward. Nagata said her goal is to secure international sales early enough that an overseas release can run alongside the Japanese one. She added that shared emotions such as friendship and family can make the unfamiliar feel closer. “I think jealousy and love are the same anywhere in the world, as long as we are human,” she said. K2 Pictures was set up as an alternative to Japan’s production committee system, under which films are made mainly with the local market in mind. Kii, who started out tearing tickets and making popcorn in cinemas before rising to producer at Toei, said the closed nature of that system kept out both foreign and outside investment, which in turn made it hard to share returns with creators. Profits at K2 are calculated title by title, with 70% going to investors and 30% to the creative side. “Producers and the people involved in making the film aren’t putting up money, but the film exists because of their creativity,” Kii said. The company completed six films this year, including “Look Back,” Kore-eda’s live-action adaptation of Fujimoto Tatsuki’s manga, which competed at Venice, and Son Myung-ah’s debut feature “Trophy,” which is due to open in Korea. Kii said the aim is six or seven releases a year, but admitted that a year in, the pace is “pretty tough.” K2 has opened outposts in Taiwan and Korea with the aim of distributing its films directly in both markets. Kii said 99.9% of Japan’s overseas film business consists of licensing deals, which he argued does little to raise the value of Japanese titles abroad. “Japanese people taking Japanese films to that place and promoting them hard there – I think that’s what raises their value,” he said. Greenlighting at K2 rests with its six or seven producers, Kii included, and he said he does not block a project a producer is set on. The only test is whether costs can be balanced against likely revenue. “Nobody can tell whether a film will be a hit,” Kii said. Kii said that applies equally to arthouse and commercial projects. “If it’s only going to bring in JPY50 million ($330,000), make it for JPY20 million ($130,000),” he said later in the session. The same logic applies to first-time directors. Kii said producers can line up pre-sales, streaming rights deals and sponsorships so that a debut cannot lose money, because a big loss makes it hard for a director to get a second film made. “I want to keep launching new directors from K2 Pictures,” Kii said. “And I want them to be grateful for the rest of their lives. Don’t forget us when you make it big.” Kii also wants the law changed. He said a British entertainment lawyer and an American completion bond executive both told him the film business works much like real estate: producers create assets and then turn them into cash. Japan passed an investment trust law around 2000 that lets real estate be securitized, but it does not cover content. Kii said he has been discussing the need for such a law with lawyers and hopes to push for one. The session was moderated by filmmaker Huang Yin-yu Kou of Taiwan’s Moolin Films, who is also the founder of the Cinema at Sea – Okinawa Pan-Pacific International Film Festival. ‘Jimmy’ Review: Cornball James Stewart Biopic Gets the Manner, but Not the Man ‘One Night In Purgatory’ Sets Cast: Alejandro Edda, Nick Stahl, Michelle Mylett and Grace Dove to Star in Supernatural Horror Film (EXCLUSIVE) Adam Driver Won’t Return for ‘Girls’: ‘I Wish Them the Best of Luck’ Tyler Perry Joins Keisha Lance Bottoms’ Georgia Transition Team Despite Director’s Sexual Assault Lawsuits ‘The End of Oak Street’ Sets HBO Max Streaming Release Date Jesse Eisenberg and Julianne Moore on ‘The Debut,’ Testing AI to ‘Make Sure It’s Bad’ and Hoping ‘Now You See Me 4’ Gets Made Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Triplets of Belleville’ Director Sylvain Chomet Fires Back at AI Accusations Over Dior Film Featuring Robert Pattinson’s Voice: ‘Everything Was Drawn by Hand’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 7, 2026 12:12am PT ‘Triplets of Belleville’ Director Sylvain Chomet Fires Back at AI Accusations Over Dior Film Featuring Robert Pattinson’s Voice: ‘Everything Was Drawn by Hand’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest ‘Triplets of Belleville’ Director Sylvain Chomet Fires Back at AI Accusations Over Dior Film Featuring Robert Pattinson’s Voice: ‘Everything Was Drawn by Hand’ (EXCLUSIVE) 7 hours ago ‘You Can See Everything’ Sparks Frenzy in Europe as Screenings Sell Out and Anticipation Soars: ‘People Are Just Desperate to See It’ 22 hours ago Paris Creator Week Aims to Become the Cannes of the Creator Economy as New Study Forecasts $1.2 Trillion Global Market 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Dior French animation filmmaker Sylvain Chomet, the four-time Oscar nominee behind “The Triplets of Belleville” and “The Illusionist,” is pushing back against accusations that generative AI was used to create his animated short for Dior featuring a voice cast led by Robert Pattinson , Rihanna, Josh O’Connor, LaKeith Stanfield, Louis Garrel and Camille Cottin. The whimsical six-minute film, “Christian Dior’s Night in Color,” produced by Aton Soumache (“The Little Prince”), has sparked controversy online, where some viewers have pointed to apparent visual glitches, including a character with six fingers, as evidence of AI-generated animation. Related Stories Liev Schreiber and Stephen Graham Lead Apple TV's Gripping Serial Killer Thriller 'Nocturne': TV Review The controversy flared because Dior positioned “Night in Color” as a celebration of traditional craftsmanship to launch its 2026 holiday season, drawing parallels between Chomet’s hand-drawn animation and the meticulous work of the house’s couture ateliers. But Chomet and Soumache tell Variety that the film was created using traditional 2D animation techniques, with the characters, backgrounds and key poses drawn by artists. While they acknowledge using automated interpolation to generate some of the intermediate frames that make movement fluid, the pair insists that generative AI was never used to create the artwork. “Some people are claiming Sylvain was contacted two weeks ago and that the entire film was made with generative AI, without a single drawing, but the reality is that this film took seven months to make and it was entirely drawn by artists,” says Soumache, adding that film employed roughly 20 people, including six animators, alongside storyboard artists, designers, background artists, compositors and editors. “We used an automated interpolation system for a very small part of the process, but the film itself is traditional 2D animation,” says the French producer. Chomet, whose latest film “A Magnificent Life” world premiered at last year’s Cannes and was distributed theatrically by Sony Pictures Classics, explains that the interpolation tool was only used to help create the in-between frames on “Christian Dior’s Night in Color.” “It’s a way of automating the repetitive, mechanical part of animation, not the creative work,” he says. The filmmaker says the accusations are particularly ironic given how committed he has been to traditional animation despite pressures to branch into CGI after the huge success of “Toy Story.” “Before I made ‘The Triplets of Belleville,’ it was the era of ‘Toy Story.’ I remember Disney declaring that traditional 2D animation was dead and that everything would be CGI, but I decided to continue making hand-drawn films,” Chomet says. “That’s why I find it so strange that people are attacking me today. I’ve remained faithful to drawing throughout my career. At the same time, I’m going to use the tools that technology offers us.” The film draws on several chapters of Dior’s history, including the couturier’s friendship with Marlene Dietrich, his ties to Hollywood and the creation of the iconic Junon gown in 1949. It also takes inspiration from one of the earliest ideas behind Dior creative director Jonathan Anderson’s Cruise 2027 collection: cinema’s transition from black-and-white to Technicolor. The story imagines Dietrich in Los Angeles, preparing to shoot a movie when the director suddenly decides to film in color. An urgent call is placed to Paris requesting a colorful Dior gown for the actress, sending Christian Dior and his team of seamstresses into a race against the clock. Pattinson narrates the film, while Garrel voices Christian Dior and Cottin plays Dietrich. O’Connor voices a talking chair, Rihanna portrays Dior’s lucky star, and Stanfield plays the Hollywood director. Nine d’Urso, Nadia Tereszkiewicz and Greta Lee voice the three bees. Soumache, whose credits include the Cesar-winning “The Little Prince,” has spent much of his career working in CGI before returning to traditional animation with films including Joann Sfar’s “Little Vampire” and more recently “A Magnificent Life,” a biopic of late celebrated French novelist and filmmaker Marcel Pagnol. “Sylvain and I have been championing traditional 2D animation for such a long time, and Dior came to us because they wanted Sylvain’s very distinctive drawing style,” says the producer whose track record also includes the blockbuster French IP “Miraculous Ladybug.” Chomet explains that the production process on the Dior short was rooted in drawing, even if artists now use digital tablets rather than paper. “But we’re still drawing by hand, it’s just done digitally,” he said, adding that he found it frustrating to work on graphic tablets and planned to “go back to pencil and paper because (he loves) having original drawings.” “I design the characters, we create the storyboards, the backgrounds, the colors. The entire creative process is exactly the same as when I started making animated films. What has changed is the technology,” he said. Chomet also addresses the apparent six-fingered hands that have fueled speculation online. “It’s a movement where the hand is spread out like a fan. In that kind of drawing, you might see six or seven fingers because you’re trying to convey movement,” he says. He argues that he’s seen much worse mistakes in traditional animation. “I’ve seen a character turn his head and suddenly his nose changes shape completely over five frames. These things happen.” The short was conceived as part of a broader collaboration with Dior, with Anderson originating the idea and Martin Latham helping develop the screenplay. “I worked particularly closely with Martin. We developed the script together and then presented ideas for the storyboard, the story and the characters. There was a lot of back-and-forth,” Chomet says. The collaboration also extended beyond the screen, with Chomet’s illustrations inspiring Dior’s holiday collections and boutique windows around the world. “Dior needed to see the designs quite early because they were simultaneously developing the Christmas window displays and physical objects,” says Soumache. “Many of Dior’s windows are based directly on Sylvain’s drawings. They created physical versions of the characters and objects from the film.” Chomet describes Disney’s 1961 classic “One Hundred and One Dalmatians” as his “madeleine de Proust,” the film he keeps coming back to. “Whenever I make a film, I ask myself whether it has that poetry, that beauty of drawing,” he says. “We can tell very different stories from the ones Disney was telling at the time, but we can still preserve that beauty. That’s what I’ve always tried to do, using technology to maintain something traditional.” Along with showcasing France’s vibrant animation talent pool, the short film also reflects Anderson’s love for hand-drawn animation. While at Loewe, he collaborated with Japan’s Studio Ghibli on three collections. articles.title: AI Filmmaking Platform Core Studio Launches at Taiwan Creative Content Fest With 24 Specialized Agents
articles.full_text: × Nov 7, 2026 12:19am PT AI Filmmaking Platform Core Studio Launches at Taiwan Creative Content Fest With 24 Specialized Agents By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest Taiwan’s Chunghwa Telecom Unveils 10 Content Investments, From ‘Gunshot’ to ‘Call of Lobster’ 12 hours ago Chang Chen Urges Emerging Taiwanese Actors to ‘Be Like Water’ at Taiwan Creative Content Fest Golden Horse Showcase 12 hours ago Taiwan Audience Study Highlights Cross-Platform IP Opportunities as AI Raises New Risks for Content Industry 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source imCore Corp. Taiwanese technology company imCore Corp. launched Core Studio , an AI filmmaking platform that aims to cover the full production process, from script development and storyboarding to image generation, editing and color grading, at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei on Saturday. Built by a Taiwanese team with roots in animation and visual effects, the platform runs on its own in-house image-generation model and also works with outside generative AI models. It follows standard filmmaking workflows, so creators can handle several stages of production in one place instead of switching between tools. Related Stories Liev Schreiber and Stephen Graham Lead Apple TV's Gripping Serial Killer Thriller 'Nocturne': TV Review Guests at the launch included Erica Wang, CEO of TCCF organizer the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), along with representatives from the Taipei Film Commission and imCore’s strategic partners, filmmakers and AI industry professionals. “Our team understands that professional creators need more than just image-generation tools. They need a comprehensive solution that can genuinely integrate into their production workflows,” said Charles Lee, founder and CEO of imCore Corp. and founder of TWR Entertainment. “Core Studio was developed around the needs of frontline film professionals, transforming years of production expertise into an AI-powered platform that provides more comprehensive creative support for filmmakers.” The platform’s main draw is a set of more than 24 specialized AI agents that act as a virtual production crew, handling story development, asset generation, visual effects, editing and color grading. imCore pitches them as a way to lower the technical hurdles of AI-assisted filmmaking. For pre-production, Core Studio’s Story Atlas tool breaks an imported script into scenes, shots and storyboards. It also sets up character designs, costumes, props and voice profiles so they stay consistent from one sequence to the next. Every AI-generated output comes with a record of the models, prompts, parameters, costs and human review results behind it. Production teams can use it to track creative decisions and keep an eye on budgets. The platform also includes Real Engine, which combines three image-processing tools: Real Video, Real HDR and Real Revive. They sharpen image detail, raise color depth from 8-bit to 16-bit and fix blown-out highlights in AI-generated footage. A cloud workspace with real-time communication, version control and access management lets teams in different countries work on the same project. Creators of four AI-assisted projects presented their work at the launch, among them Jerry Zhou, the creator of “God Being.” “There are many agents on the editing page that can help with sound effects. I can separate the sound effects and dialogue from AI-generated footage and make detailed adjustments,” Zhou said. “This gives me more flexibility and creative space, allowing me to work more comfortably as a creator.” A24’s ‘It Gets Worse’ Updates ‘Girls’ for British Gen Z: TV Review South International Series Festival Prizes: ’Blindspot Berlin,’ ‘The Oligarch and the Art Dealer’ Win Big ‘Sea of Glass’ Brings ‘Country Gothic Noir’ Tradition to Greece With Story of Two Women Finding Solidarity Across Generations Gay Influencer Famed for Dancing in High Heels Faces Middle Age in Nine-Year Taiwan Creative Content Fest Documentary ‘My Silly Flirty Boys’ Big Daddy: How Jordan Firstman Turned ‘Club Kid’ Into a Glorious, Gay, Oscar-Worthy Crowdpleaser Thessaloniki Film Festival Chief Hopes Event Can Help ‘Ease Pain’ in ‘Difficult’ Times: ‘Cinema Matters’ Loading comments...

articles.title: Davika Hoorne Returning for ‘Inherit’ Sequel, Director Banjong Pisanthanakun Confirms (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 7, 2026 12:59am PT Davika Hoorne Returning for ‘Inherit’ Sequel, Director Banjong Pisanthanakun Confirms (EXCLUSIVE) By Jenny S. Li Plus Icon Jenny S. Li Latest Swiss Labor Exploitation Drama ‘Enjoy Your Stay’ Lands in Indonesia, Directors Hope It Speaks for Migrant Workers 15 hours ago Cristian Mungiu’s Cinematographer Tudor Vladimir Panduru Breaks Down Long Takes on ‘Fjord,’ ‘R.M.N.’ at Jakarta World Cinema Masterclass 3 days ago Jakarta World Cinema Plans to Revive First Feature Competition With International Jury 6 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jakarta World Cinema Banjong Pisanthanakun , the Thai director of horror hits “Shutter” and “Pee Mak,” tells Variety his new psychological horror film “ Inherit ” will get a sequel, with star Davika Hoorne set to return. “Inherit,” a Centrepiece selection at the Toronto Film Festival, where it world premiered in September, is closing the Jakarta World Cinema festival. Pisanthanakun and Hoorne first worked together on 2013 horror-comedy “Pee Mak,” Thailand’s biggest local box office hit of all time. Related Stories Liev Schreiber and Stephen Graham Lead Apple TV's Gripping Serial Killer Thriller 'Nocturne': TV Review Hoorne plays Woranart, a youthful-looking grandmother who moves in with her granddaughter’s wealthy family. The family soon discovers she harbors a centuries-old centipede spirit with sinister designs on the youngest in the household, Oui (Baipor Thitiya Jirapornsilp). Hoorne was Pisanthanakun’s first choice for the immortal grandmother. “The character has to be sexy, beautiful, and funny at the same time. I think of her as a fashion icon, too,” Pisanthanakun tells Variety . “The first image that I have was her wearing a bikini and sunbathing beside the pool, which is very modern. She talks like this [era’s] woman, talking to ChatGPT. She’s a very adaptable girl.” On set, Pisanthanakun advised Hoorne to study Catherine Tramell, Sharon Stone’s character in “Basic Instinct,” and Anthony Hopkins’ Hannibal Lecter in “The Silence of the Lambs.” Hoorne also starred in “A Useful Ghost,” the satirical Thai comedy-thriller that took Cannes’ Critics’ Week Grand Prix in 2025. She regards that film and “Inherit” as her return to cinema. “For movie, I carefully choose the project that I want to do,” Hoorne says. “One project takes around one year of working, so I really have to choose the one I’m gonna live with for such a long time to bring up my soul as an actress. So, trust me, watch it, I pick for you guys already.” Pisanthanakun says that 20 years ago, horror was all about the concept – ghosts in photos or on videotapes – with filmmakers competing over where to make the ghost appear. “Actually, after ‘Shutter’ and ‘Alone,’ there came a time when I really got bored of making horror films; even going to the cinema to watch horror films made me fall asleep right away,” the director says. “After films like ‘Hereditary’ and ‘It Follows’ came out, I felt like there were still other new, refreshing ways to make horror films. The modern horror, especially from the Hollywood side, is now very creative. I think it’s the only genre that still has something creative coming up.” His film “The Medium” was produced by Korean director Na Hong-Jin. “When I made this project with him, he shared his opinion on how the international market would react all the time. I just made this film [the way I normally do]. But he’s gonna give his opinion on how the international audience would perceive it,” Pisanthanakun says. “I want the concepts and the story to be as solid as possible, and I want the atmosphere to be everything. It has to be very unique, and everything has to be like authentic,” he adds. On AI, he says: “I think it’s inevitable in the system, but I think people can use it as long as it’s not violating other people’s rights.” “The Thai film industry right now is not so good – that’s the real pressure because I want this movie to bring Thai audiences back to the cinema,” Pisanthanakun says. “Inherit” opens across Thailand Nov. 19. He adds that public funding for Thai film production is neither robust nor consistent, and only goes to horror. Hoorne has moved into producing girls’ love (GL) titles, a genre of romance stories between women that is popular in Thailand. “It’s gonna be better if we have funding from the other help of the government; that help is the independent themes that can go internationally,” Hoorne says. “When I’m producing a movie or series, it is very hard to find the funding, and it is really hard for Thai films to recruit people for different genres. Because you have to draw people into the cinema, drama or comedy, something that looks small, people tend to wait.” Hoorne has also directed a family short film, “Soap Opera,” which recently wrapped, and will focus on TV series in 2027. Pisanthanakun is leading a Thai-Korean horror co-production.
