articles.title: Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario & Christopher Walken Set For True Crime-Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ — AFM
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario & Christopher Walken Set For True Crime-Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ — AFM International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com ‘Honeymooners’; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM View All November 6, 2026 7:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Taylor Kitsch, Alexandra Daddario and Christopher Walken Eric Ray Davidson/Storm Santos/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE : Taylor Kitsch ( Lone Survivor ), Alexandra Daddario ( The White Lotus ) and screen legend Christopher Walken ( The Deer Hunter ) are set to star true crime thriller The Long Island Bank Robber . Based on a true story, Kitsch will star as Stephen Trantel, “a successful Wall Street commodities trader. After being fired from his job, Stephen’s desperate attempts to keep his family afloat lead him down the unimaginable path of becoming one of Long Island’s most prolific bank robbers.” Daddario will star as Jeanne Trantel, Stephen’s “discerning wife who grows increasingly suspicious of her husband and yearns to pave her own path outside of the home.” Oscar winner Walken will play Stephen’s father, a retired police officer ‘with a strong ethical code.” Related Stories News International Buyers From 12 Territories Launch Film Distribution Network Lokia On Eve Of AFM News Jack Whitehall, Nina Dobrev, Greg Kinnear & Andie MacDowell Set For Rom-Com 'Honeymooners'; HanWay & CAA Launch For AFM Matthew Gentile ( American Murderer ) will direct from a screenplay he co-wrote with Bianca Vera, based on the non-fiction book ‘ Til Heist Do Us Part by Jeanne Callahan and Michael Harvey. Production is to begin this month in New Jersey. Watch on Deadline Vaneast Pictures has acquired worldwide sales rights and will launch the project for buyers ahead of next week’s AFM . The film is being produced by Vince Jolivette and Richie Hill of Filmopoly ( The Threesome ), Chris Bellant of Vision Entertainment ( Neighborhood Watch ) and Danielle Gasher of Vaneast Pictures ( Hellhound ). Taylor Kitsch, Andres Budnik, Liam Scholey, Raymond Kimsey, Matt Allen, Dan Reardon, Kyle Fox, Alan B. Bursteen and Dawn Bursteen serve as executive producers. Patricia DiCerto ( Blue Jasmine ) has joined as casting director. Gentile’s feature directorial debut, American Murderer , was a true-crime thriller starring Tom Pelphrey, Ryan Phillippe, Idina Menzel, and Jacki Weaver. The movie won awards at multiple American festivals after launching at Taormina in Italy. “ The Long Island Bank Robber is a true story I learned about in my youth, growing up in New York City as a true-crime obsessive. A propulsive heist film on the surface, the story also tackles complex themes of grief, survival, and marriage. With Taylor, Alexandra, and Christopher as our three leads — I could not have dreamed of a better cast to bring this film to life,” said director and co-writer Matthew Gentile. “This package is a rare find, with that perfect combination of a gripping true-crime script, a talented director, and a star-studded ensemble. We can’t wait to get this one in front of buyers,” said Danielle Gasher, Vaneast Pictures. “We’re thrilled to bring Matthew Gentile’s vision for this film to life with this incredible cast and crew, and to be partnering with Vaneast for the global sales. This is such a compelling and layered story that we can’t wait to share with the world,” stated producer Richie Hill. Kitsch is represented by Untitled Entertainment and CAA. Daddario is represented by CAA, Untitled Entertainment, and Jackoway Austen. Walken is represented by CAA. Matthew Gentile and Bianca Vera are both with Vision Entertainment and Goodman, Genow. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Dobrev Rom-Com; ‘Obsession’ Producer Pic; New Int’l Distributor Network ‘Buena Vista Social Club’ Sets Broadway Closing & West End Date Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Genre Label Vasaria Pictures Forms Pact With Vertical Horror Streamer TerrorBox
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Genre Label Vasaria Pictures Forms Pact With Vertical Horror Streamer TerrorBox Comcast’s Sky Receives Security Threat After RTE Evacuates Staff International Insider: Russell Brand Guilty; AFM Fires Up; Trudie Styler Interview View All November 6, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Dead Signal' TerrorBox EXCLUSIVE: Vasaria Pictures , the genre label set up by Saw writers Patrick Melton and Marcus Dunston and producers Sean Gowrie and Nick Phillips, has teamed with horror-focused vertical streamer TerrorBox . The pair will work together to develop short-form content, often from emerging horror filmmaking talent, and seek to expand that into feature films. As part of the agreement, TerrorBox will release Vasaria’s short film Jezebel as a vertical series on the platform. Inspired by the classic Hammer horror films, Jezebel was directed by Phillips and written by and starring TikTok creator Claire Dellamar. Related Stories Casting 'Christmas At Maple Hollow Inn' Microdrama Hopes To Channel The Spirit Of Festive TV Movies Through Meta's Series Feature News Eric Roberts, Merrick Hanna & Neela Jolene Starring In Vertical Drama 'It's My Party And I'll Die If I Want To' The Jezebel short has amassed more than four million views on the popular horror YouTube channel Alter, and Vasaria is concurrently developing the property as a feature film in the vein of route taken by horror hits Obsession and Backrooms . Watch on Deadline Vasaria and TerrorBox will also collaborate on a vertical adaptation of Fate , a screenplay by Melton and Dunstan, who wrote four instalments of the Saw franchise ( Saw IV , Saw V , Saw VI and Saw 3D ). Vasaria will explore select TerrorBox titles for potential feature film development. Box Entertainment Group , which Ryan Justice set up in 2025 launched TerrorBox earlier this year as a microdrama service dedicated to horror. This was part of Box’s business model to create genre-specific platforms such as AxnBox, which is dedicated to action, adventure and Westerns. Justice, whose filmmaking credits include Followers and The Wild Man , said: “We’re building a platform where horror filmmakers have a dedicated home to create and keep creating. Partnering with the team at Vasaria brings an incredible depth of experience and storytelling talent to TerrorBox. “Vertical storytelling offers an entirely new canvas for horror, challenging filmmakers to rethink how they build suspense, create tension and scare audiences. We’re only beginning to explore what’s possible with this format, and that’s what makes it so exciting.” “We have been exploring the vertical space for some time, and after meeting Ryan, we knew we had found the right partner,” added the Vasaria team in a statement. “This collaboration gives us the opportunity to discover and work with exciting emerging voices in horror while also bringing our own stories to life in an entirely new format. We see tremendous creative potential in vertical storytelling and are thrilled to be building something with Ryan and the TerrorBox team.” TerrorBox has been expanding its lineup recently through independent acquisitions for titles such as Dead Signal , written and directed by Rick Shepherd and Benjamin Steeper, featuring an ensemble of performers from the vertical entertainment space, including Jessica Jacoby, Aaron Oberst, Candace Mizga, Jarred Harper, Vincent Elric, Rick Shepherd and Zachary B. Rist. The streamer has also bought the Nightmarish TV library of vertical horror shorts. Created by Atlanta-based filmmakers Madison Hoover and Jaime Lucero Jr., this comprises bite-sized horror stories designed specifically for vertical viewing, typically running 90 seconds or less. Titles available on the platform include Ouija , Slasher and Augmented . A deal is also in place with Echo Cell Productions, led by David Wing, and the Echo Cell Collective, an international community of horror creatives working to develop, produce and promote original vertical horror content. ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & Maybe Mergers Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Christmas At Maple Hollow Inn’ Microdrama Hopes To Channel The Spirit Of Festive TV Movies Through Meta’s Series Feature
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Genre Label Vasaria Pictures Forms Pact With Vertical Horror Streamer TerrorBox Comcast’s Sky Receives Security Threat After RTE Evacuates Staff International Insider: Russell Brand Guilty; AFM Fires Up; Trudie Styler Interview View All November 6, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Christmas at Maple Hollow Inn' Pixie USA EXCLUSIVE: Jonas Barnes’ Pixie USA is launching Christmas at Maple Hollow Inn as one of the first microdrama to use Meta’s new Series tool. The romantic holiday drama will star Analisa Southworth Wall and Thomas King , and was developed in partnership with the Bob Evans grocery. The aim is to recreate the feel of a festive TV movie as a vertical series. Blake Studwell directs, with Michael Sokol producing. Filmed in Marietta, Georgia, the family-friendly production will comprise 20 episodes with a total running time of 38 minutes and launches on November 14, as one of vertical series Meta is testing this month, we understand. As such, it will be distributed on Facebook and Instagram, along with YouTube and TikTok. Related Stories Legal Google, TikTok And Meta Sue To Block California's Social Media Law That Restricts Addictive Features For Children News Eric Roberts, Merrick Hanna & Neela Jolene Starring In Vertical Drama 'It's My Party And I'll Die If I Want To' Wall’s credits include Picture Perfect Sister-in-Law and Mother Warrior Unleashed . King’s television credits include Tyler Perry’s The Oval and County Rescue . Studwell previously directed vertical romances Baby, Just Say Yes! and Falling for My Mafia Bodyguard . Watch on Deadline Meta is set to begin testing its new tool, titled Series, which will allow select creators to bundle vertical videos for Reels into episodes on Facebook and Instagram. Meta isn’t commenting on specific titles using the Series feature prior to its launch in certain markets on November 16. Per the synopsis, Christmas at Maple Hollow Inn follows “a determined young woman who reunites with her former flame to save her family’s inn during the Christmas season. Their last hope rests on a spectacular holiday meal for a group of hard-to-impress investors – but she cannot cook. With the kitchen in chaos and old feelings resurfacing, the pair must find a way to preserve the inn’s future while navigating an unexpected second chance at love.” Developed around food and holiday themes, the series will feature Bob Evans mashed potatoes and macaroni and cheese meals at the center of the story. It marks the food brand’s first scripted holiday season production. Ciare James, Senior Vice President and Chief Marketing Officer at Bob Evans Farms , said: “This microdrama brings our brand story to life, showing how Bob Evans holiday favorites can make a memorable meal while leaving more time to enjoy the holiday season.” “Christmas movies have an enduring appeal because they bring audiences into a world of romance, hope and possibility,” added Barnes, CEO at Pixie USA. “Vertical content is reaching tens of millions of people where they are, bringing entertainment directly to their phones. Social media is the new TV, and microdramas are helping drive that shift. “It’s an industry growing so rapidly that it’s almost hard to keep up. With Christmas at Maple Hollow Inn , we wanted to capture that festive magic in a story people can enjoy on their phones. Analisa and Thomas bring warmth and chemistry to the romance, and Bob Evans felt like a natural partner for a film about family, hospitality and the moments that bring people together.” This isn’t the first time Barnes has created a microdrama for a brand, having worked with Procter & Gamble om The Golden Pear Affair , which was developed with Native, P&G Studios and Dentsu Entertainment. Barnes previously worked at Neal H. articles.title: Universal Sets International Rollout Of Alex Gibney Documentary ‘Musk’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Ken Ziffren Offers Optimistic View On Industry, Even When It Comes To AI & Federal Tax Credit Legislation ‘The Odyssey’ Venturing Back Into Cinemas After Mid-November In-Home Release Finn Wittrock & Supriya Ganesh Horror Thriller ‘Portrait’ From Robert Schwartzman Heads To AFM View All November 6, 2026 8:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Musk' Courtesy Bleecker Street Universal International has finally set offshore release dates for Alex Gibney’s controversial four-hour documentary Musk with the UK on Jan. 15, Germany on Jan. 21, Spain on Feb. 5, France on Feb. 17 February and Australia on Feb. 25. More release dates abroad will be announced. The pic has already released stateside via Bleecker Street , opening on Oct. 9 and through Wednesday counted $730K. Some media of late was trying to stir up trouble that theaters were pulling Musk due to pressure from Elon Musk, and well, that’s just not true. The pic debuted in its first weekend at 4 theaters, then platformed to 472 in its second weekend, and dropped to 63 in its third. Hello, it’s a four-hour documentary. If the movie isn’t doing business in auditoriums, it gets pulled, not to mention Bleecker Street titles typically have a limited wide run in theaters for less than a month. Musk is ultimately bound for HBO since it’s an HBO documentary where it will be able to be seen by awards voters. Related Stories Trailers 'Tender Loving Care' Trailer: Mike Leigh's Latest Is A Meditation On Love & Growing Old Trailers 'The Liberation' Trailer: Carrie Coon Stars In Guy Nattiv's Complex Cult Thriller Deadline told you first that Uni was taking foreign. News of the documentary ticked off Elon Musk from the onset, prior to Gibney shooting it with the Tesla and SpaceX boss calling the filmmaker “a douche” on X. At one point in time soon after Uni acquired foreign on the documentary, there was buzz that they were getting cold feet. A Uni spokesperson at the time told us that they had no plans to ditch the movie. articles.title: A Reboot Of Classic Series ‘Tenko’ & A ‘Chalet Girl’ TV Adaptation Are In The Works At Two Brothers Pictures
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart More International Deals For ‘Sherlock & Daughter’ Ahead Of UK & Ireland Premiere On HBO Max ‘Queen Silvia’ Team Hopes For Multiple Seasons After Royal Drama’s Cannes Premiere Terry Sanders Wraps Documentary ‘On Rescuing Democracy And The Rule Of Law’ View All November 6, 2026 8:35am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jack and Harry Williams founded Two Brothers Pictures, which is behind the new Tenko and Chalet Girl adaptations Two Brothers Pictures EXCLUSIVE: A new version of classic BBC wartime drama Tenko is in the works from the producers of The Assassin and Fleabag . Prolific British drama label Two Brothers Pictures has mostly focused on original ideas but, having staffed up, is pushing into optioning and adapting existing works. Another IP-led project in the works is a TV series adaptation of the 2011 movie Chalet Girl . Tenko was produced for the BBC in the UK and ABC in Australia running for three seasons between 1981-1984 and yielding a special in 1985. Starting in 1942, it followed a group of UK, Australian and Dutch civilian women held in a fictitious Japanese internment camp near Singapore. It showed how the women survived the harsh conditions, banded together and fought to survive in the prison camp. Related Stories News 'The Walking Dead' Star Lennie James Leading ITV Thriller 'Nightswimming' From Harry & Jack Williams News 'The Assassin' Star Keeley Hawes Joins Season 2 Of George Kay's ITV Thriller 'Gone' Two Brothers approached the show’s creator Lavinia Warner about making a version for modern-day TV. Anna Symon ( Mrs. Wilson ) is writing the new version of the seminal show. Watch on Deadline “We went to Lavinia Warner, who was the original producer and creator,” Sarah Hammond, Chief Creative Officer at Two Brothers told Deadline. “She had a lot of relationships with the women, and the families of the women who were in the war camp, so she didn’t want to hand the reins over to just anyone, but she was really excited to work with us to bring it back.” Two Brothers was founded by Jack and Harry Williams and is part of Banijay Entertainment. Another series in-the-making from the label is Chalet Girl . Tessa Coates ( Ride or Die ) is on board to pen the TV adaptation. The original 2011 rom-com movie starred Felicity Jones and Ed Westwick. The original Chalet Girl movie Paramount/courtesy Everett Collection Hammond said the TV series will be aimed at the red-hot ‘new adult’ market. “We’re looking at different genres that we’ve never explored before, so the new adult space, for example,” Hammond said. “ Chalet Girl was an indie movie of the 2000s, and that’s something that we’re working with the original producers on, for a new adult version. “What the team loved about the original film was the spiky lead character who felt brilliant and funny, and it’s got all the moving parts of a new adult story. It’s got the sex and the love and the exotic locations and it has a brilliant tone and a real voice. It was something that we thought feels like, if we put the Two Brothers lens on it, could be really exciting.” ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & Maybe Mergers Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Charter Stock Sinks As Internet Subscriber Losses Worsen; Could A Comcast Merger Be The Next Move?
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Fox Corp. Closes $22 Billion Acquisition Of Roku Online Media Pioneer Salon To Shutter: “Our Publishing Model Is No Longer Sustainable” Netflix Woos Mattel Veteran Roberto Stanichi To Lead Consumer Products and Experiences View All November 6, 2026 8:40am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Charter Communications Photo Illustration by Igor Golovniov/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images Charter Communications shares fell 5% in early trading Friday after the pay-TV, broadband and wireless provider reported wider internet subscriber losses in the third quarter. During the quarter, in August, Charter closed its $34.5 billion acquisition of rival Cox Communications, expanding its footprint to 45 states. Quarterly results, reported on a pro forma basis to account for the merger, showed continued erosion of internet and pay-TV customers. Wireless remains a comparative bright spot, with 1.8 million sign-ups over the past year giving the company 13.5 million wireless customers as of September 30. Related Stories News Online Media Pioneer Salon To Shutter: "Our Publishing Model Is No Longer Sustainable" News Lionsgate Quarterly Revenue Pops With Growth Across Film & TV Studios, Library The company shed 233,000 internet customers – 156,000 at legacy Charter and 77,000 at legacy Cox – in the quarter. The subscriber total sat at 34.3 million as of the end of the quarter. Wireless and satellite internet providers, including Elon Musk’s Starlink, have put pressure on major broadband players like Charter and fueled speculation about a potential Charter-Comcast tie-up. Comcast is about to split off NBCUniversal from its connectivity business, which faces similar headwinds. Watch on Deadline Along with the quarterly results, CEO Chris Winfrey unveiled plans to cut $2 billion in costs and reaffirmed a projection for $1 billion in merger-related synergies. Investors seemed underwhelmed, with Friday’s downturn in the stock price extending a 43% drop in 2026 to date. Cord-cutting continues to eat away at pay-TV levels, even though Charter’s Spectrum systems have integrated streaming services aggressively enough to stem the downturn more than many operators. Total video customers fell by 77,000 in the quarter, compared with a decline of 121,000 a year ago. The total subscriber base was 13.8 million at the end of the quarter. Total company revenue rose 9% over the year-earlier period, reaching $14.9 billion. Gregory Williams, an analyst for TD Cowen, anticipated the Friday trade in a client note earlier this week. “Investors may not get constructive until they see a resting place on broadband subscriber losses,” he wrote. “The next catalyst could be a Comcast/Charter tie-up, which may need to occur sooner rather than later given the midterm election results as a broader regulatory signal.” ‘Stranger Things’ Live-Action Prequel Gets Greenlight At Netflix Kitsch, Daddario, Walken Set For True-Crime Thriller ‘The Long Island Bank Robber’ Fox Closes $22B Takeover Of Roku, Creating Massive New Streaming Player Senator’s Letters Preview Dems’ Plans To Probe FCC, Big Tech & Maybe Mergers Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Off Campus’ Season 2 Sets April Premiere Date
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Off Campus' season two. Prime Video Logo text Off Campus is skating back to screens this April, Prime Video announced Thursday. The popular college hockey romance series will officially return for season two on April 28, 2027. Shortly after season one premiered in May, Prime Video announced Stephen Kalyn ‘s Dean Di Laurentis and Mika Abdalla ‘s Allie Hayes would lead the next installment , which didn’t come as a big surprise to many viewers as the couple was a fan favorite in season one. Their relationship will serve as the driving force behind the new season. Season one leads, Belmont Cameli and Ella Bright , will continue to star in the series. Related Stories TV Dave Bautista Reveals He Gained 20 Pounds of Muscle for 'God of War' Series Next Big Thing Jaalen Best Wanted to Be a Pro Athlete. Now He's Playing 'The Greatest' Boxer Onscreen The new season will adapt the plot of Elle Kennedy ’s third novel in the Off Campus series, The Score . The book series Off Campus , which begins with The Deal , follows a new-but-connected couple in each book. The show plans to keep that model. Season one dove headfirst into the age-old romantic trope of fake dating with music student Hannah Wells (Bright), who, in true hockey fashion, is often called Wellsy by her love interest, Garrett Graham (Cameli). “I consider [episode six] a pilot episode or a soft launch for season two and what you’re going to expect,” Kalyn previously told The Hollywood Reporter . “I was so grateful to learn from Ella and Belmont and watch those two great phenomenal actors lead season one.” Abdalla had similar sentiments, sharing her excitement for getting to work more closely with her co-star. “I truly love working with Stephen so much,” she previously told THR ahead of the announcement she and Kalyn would lead season two. “I’m excited that I get to do this with him because I trust him so much.” Abdalla, Kalyn, Bright and Cameli are joined by Antonio Cipriano, Jalen Thomas Brooks and India Fowler as series regulars for Off Campus season two. Julia Sarah-Stone, Khobe Clarke, Miles Gutierrez-Riley and Philipa Soo are set to recur. Charlie Evans and Shay Rudolph will guest star. Off Campus has become a hit for Prime Video. The series reached 36 million viewers worldwide over its first 12 days of release, according to figures shared by the Amazon-owned streamer. It comes in as Prime Video’s third largest series debut over that amount of time, behind The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power and Fallout . Creator Louisa Levy serves as co-showrunner and executive producer alongside Gina Fattore. Wyck Godfrey, Marty Bowen and James Seidman executive produce and Annika Patton co-executive produces for Temple Hill. Leanna Billings of Billings Productions and Neal Flaherty also serve as executive producers. Read THR ‘s Off Campus season one show coverage here. THR

articles.title: Sony Pictures Classics Takes Jean-Pierre Jeunet’s ‘Violette’ for U.S.

The French drama, based on Valérie Perrin’s international bestseller Fresh Water for Flowers , the film follows Violette, a cemetery caretaker — played by Once Upon My Mother actress Leïla Bekhti — whose peaceful life is disrupted with the arrival of a mysterious stranger (Melvil Poupaud) who insists on depositing the ashes of his recently departed mother on the gravesite of a complete stranger. His arrival will force Violette to confront hidden truths of her troubled past filled with hidden truths. Matthias Schoenaerts ( Rust and Bone , The Danish Girl ) co-stars. Violette marks SPC’s fourth collaboration with Jeunet, following the releases of Amelie (2001), Micmacs (2009) and The City of Lost Children (1995). “Jean-Pierre Jeunet has a singular gift for weaving together multiple storylines with humor, pathos and that unmistakable touch of whimsy,” SPC said in a statement. “We’re especially delighted that Violette marks our fourth film together. It continues his lyrical tradition while also feeling completely fresh, and theatrical audiences will be enchanted.” SPC did not reveal details of their planned rollout for the film. The was negotiated between Sony Pictures Classics and Studiocanal, who are handling international sales. THR

articles.title: Former UTA and FaZe Clan Execs Launch Creator Management Firm ISO
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 8:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source ISO's Darren Yan and Mike Lee ISO A pair of veteran executives from the creator space are launching new venture meant to help digital creators expand their businesses across content, music, products and live experiences. The management and representation company is called ISO, and is being launched by Mike Lee, the former head of gaming and livestreaming at UTA Creators, who is CEO, and Darren Yan, former chief talent officer at FaZe Clan, who is head of music. ISO is backed by Influence Media Partners, the music and entertainment-focused investment company. The company’s talent roster includes PlaqueBoyMax, Jasontheween, Ironmouse, Lacy, Vanillamace, Kyedae, RDCWorld, with brand clients that include Electronic Arts, Discord, Underdog and Icenova. ISO says it has more than 90 clients, with a heavy focus on livestreamers, gamers, artists, VTubers and lifestyle creators across beauty, food and other verticals. Creators are increasingly leveraging the audiences they have built through their streams and social channels to build businesses elsewhere, and at the same time brands are eager to work with creators on campaigns and original content. Firms like ISO can help connect those dots. “The next household name is already online, building an audience, and ISO was built for that talent,” said Mike Lee, CEO and co-founder of ISO. “Today’s gatekeepers are algorithms, so understanding discovery, engagement and how content travels is essential. Every creator we work with is running a real business, and our job is to give it room to grow through original IP, products, live events, and expansion into China and platforms like TikTok Shop, where most of the industry still isn’t set up to compete.” “At Influence, we look to invest in partners who bring an innovative approach to the business of culture and entertainment,” added Lylette Pizarro, founder & co-managing partner of Influence Media Partners. “Mike, Darren and the team at ISO are reimagining talent representation for a creator economy that has fundamentally transformed how audiences are built, culture is shaped and revenue is generated. ISO’s playbook directly aligns with our values and investment philosophy, and we’re excited to support their growth.” “Talent development used to be the heart of every company in the representation business. ISO is bringing it back with our model built for the new generation where musicians and creators increasingly share the same playbook: build an audience directly, then build a business around it,” said Darren Yan, co-founder and head of music at ISO. “We invest in our clients from the earliest stages across music, media, products, live events, gaming and tech, with our A&R team applying the same lens to artists by building global fandom online before the market catches on.” THR

articles.title: Emmy Rossum Named RAINN Ambassador Amid New Partnership to Deepen Public Understanding of Sexual Violence and Survivorship (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abbey White Plus Icon Abbey White Contributing Writer View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emmy Rossum Lelanie Foster Emmy Rossum has been named an ambassador for RAINN, the country’s largest anti-sexual violence organization, as the actress and nonprofit launch a new partnership focused on deepening the public’s understanding of sexual violence and survivorship. The Furious star will unite her platform as an artist and storyteller with the nonprofit’s expertise in survivor support to explore how storytelling can inform the public around the realities and misconceptions about sexual trauma and healing. The partnership aims to challenge stigma, amplify survivor voices, use storytelling to connect survivors with critical resources and encourage more thoughtful representations of sexual violence across the entertainment industry. Related Stories TV Newport Beach Film Fest: 'Furious' Star Emmy Rossum Will Receive TV Performance Award, Guest on Live Episode of 'Awards Chatter' Pod TV Why Emmy Rossum Says 'Shameless' Nude Scenes Affected Her Dating Life: "All These Preconceived Notions" “Working on Furious alongside psychologists and survivors reminded me that there is no perfect way to be a survivor,” Rossum says. “I’ve been so moved by the conversations the show has started. As we’ve seen too often of late, survivors are everywhere — from the halls of Congress to college campuses to the film industry — and this conversation belongs to all of us. Through my partnership with RAINN, I hope to turn that awareness into action: opening up conversations, breaking down stigma and helping more survivors find pathways to connection, support and healing.” The collaboration extends the connection to these issues that Rossum, among the nation’s more than 78 million survivors of sexual violence, developed while preparing for her critically acclaimed performance in Hulu’s Furious as Alice Black, an FBI agent and abuse survivor. While making the Elizabeth Meriwether-created series, production leaned on a community of consultants, including numerous survivors of sex trafficking, intimate partner violence experts, forensic psychologists, trauma therapists, FBI agents and human trafficking task force members. RAINN also served as a script consultant on the studio side during the show’s early development. “To tell these stories without re-traumatizing viewers, without explicitly showing the trauma, but instead, as Liz so cleverly did, showing the aftermath of the trauma, takes a lot of care,” the actress says. “What I’m most proud of in our show is how we demonstrated that survivors need not be innocent or likable to deserve dignity or justice. I think understanding the nuances of these crimes, understanding the struggles of survivors and how imperfect people still deserve the right to justice is important.” The announcement comes one day before Rossum will appear at Raising the Prevention Generation, an invite-only event for survivors, allies and advocates, co-hosted by WME and RAINN. The intimate brunch and sitdown in L.A. will feature Rossum; RAINN founder and president Scott Berkowitz; Jennifer Simmons Kaleba, RAINN vp, communications; Aspire Titan Academy student mental health therapist Skye Choe; and Dr. Karen Kay Imagawa, medical director of the Audrey Hepburn CARES Center at Children’s Hospital Los Angeles. The discussion will span how the adults in children’s lives can talk about sexual violence, consent and boundaries in a digital world and how everyone can turn current conversations into meaningful action. “One of the most meaningful parts of our work at WME is helping our clients turn what they care deeply about into real impact. Storytelling has an incredible power to change hearts, minds and perspectives, and Emmy’s commitment to using her voice with such care and purpose is a beautiful example of that,” says Jeanell English, head of community and impact at WME. “Together with RAINN’s decades of expertise, this partnership creates an opportunity to spark important conversations, challenge stigma and make a meaningful difference in how survivors are seen, heard and supported.” Friday’s talk will mark the first step in Rossum and RAINN’s newly minted alliance, which sprung out of a connection made during WME’s inaugural Women’s Health Summit, held in Los Angeles on Oct. 15. Rossum and RAINN chief of victim services Megan Cutter’s intimate fireside conversation “Furious? Good. Now What?” explored the ongoing myths and stereotypes that shape how sexual violence is perceived, the ways survivors respond to trauma and why survivor agency matters. “In recent weeks, calls to RAINN’s National Sexual Assault Hotline increased 73 percent,” Cutter says. “The country is having a hard and necessary conversation about sexual violence right now. Too often, what’s missing is an understanding of what survivors actually go through: that trauma responses vary, that there is no single right way to react and that healing looks different for everyone. Emmy and WME were committed to telling these stories with integrity long before this moment, and that’s what makes them the right partners to help carry this conversation forward.” The collaboration is particularly timely, arriving amid a moment flooded with national headlines and public discussions about sexual assault in the film and TV industry, on college campuses like Cornell University and the University of Chicago, as well as the campaign trail, in states like Maine, Ohio and Arizona. “ Cornell isn’t an outlier . It’s a reflection of what happens on campuses and in communities every day. The difference is that people are paying attention right now,” says Berkowitz. “[It] landed hard because it felt so real. The details differ, but for the tens of millions of Americans who’ve experienced sexual violence, this story was personal and for a lot of parents, it was a wake-up call. Nobody wants their kid to be a victim — or a perpetrator.” The partnership also comes nearly a decade after the #MeToo movement changed public discourse around sexual violence and how survivors are treated. In the years since, the movement has faced backlash and shifts in attention and momentum, but alongside the recent news about campus assaults, Rossum explains why addressing sexual assault must go beyond a moment. “#MeToo was an incredibly important watershed moment in culture. But all social movements require sustained action,” says Rossum. “Sunlight remains the best disinfectant. What happened at Cornell needs to be brought into the light . When our leaders foster a culture that threatens the safety of women, it needs to be called out directly and swiftly.” According to the actress and producer, the most impactful way she and her fellow creative community members can do that is by tackling the issues through storytelling. “There is something about taking the shame out of things by putting them on screen for us to see, warts and all. A character can reach us emotionally in a way that a PSA can’t. We aren’t just being told about something. We’re feeling it alongside someone, and that can change how we understand and treat each other,” she tells The Hollywood Reporter . “That’s the power of stories to me: It can take something that feels isolating and create a connection around it.” That’s why stories are at the forefront of her upcoming work with RAINN. “They can make us feel seen and less alone. That connection matters long after the headlines go away,” says Rossum. “No one was asking for Furious or Josephine or I May Destroy You or even Obsession , which sparked important conversations about consent. But audiences turned out because they’re phenomenal stories about something important. We need to keep telling them.” For RAINN, partnering with a storyteller like Rossum means the conversation around sexual assault, trauma and survivorship does not only have to live within a news cycle and “can reach people who’ve never thought of sexual violence as their issue and help keep this conversation going long after the headlines fade,” says Berkowitz. “The stakes of not talking about this are high. When people don’t understand consent, harm happens. When friends don’t know what to look for, they don’t step in. And when survivors don’t recognize what happened to them, or the people they confide in respond with doubt or blame, healing gets much harder,” he continues. “Sexual assault isn’t an abstract statistic. It’s happening to people we know and love and talking about it openly is how we prevent it and how we support survivors.” THR

articles.title: Robert Pattinson to Be Honored With American Cinematheque Award

In 2026 alone, Pattinson has starred in The Drama , The Odyssey , Primetime and the upcoming Dune: Part Three , and the evening will celebrate those as well as his wide-ranging two-decade career. “Rob has built an extraordinary career defined by his unwavering dedication to his craft, fearless creative choices, and remarkable versatility as an actor. From his collaborations with some of cinema’s most visionary filmmakers to his ability to captivate audiences in major studio blockbusters, Rob has continually challenged expectations and demonstrated the power of great storytelling,” American Cinematheque board chair Rick Nicita said in a statement. “Rob is the perfect choice to receive this award and join our esteemed list of artists who not only love cinema but continue to have a deep impact on our industry. We are thrilled that his filming schedule has allowed us the opportunity to recognize his exceptional contributions to film and we look forward to celebrating his continued achievements.” Related Stories Movies Scarlett Johansson Breaks Silence on 'The Batman Part II' Role: "It Was Very Hard to Figure Out" Lifestyle Jon Bernthal Adds Another Notch on Packed 2026 Résumé by Fronting Fear of God Campaign Ryan Gosling was previously set to receive the American Cinematheque Award in a ceremony this month, but the event was rescheduled after Gosling was no longer available to accept it; Pattinson has also been busy this fall, filming The Batman Part II while taking part in the awards race. Related Stories TV Tony Awards to Air on CBS Through 2032 TV Alex Warren to Host Kids' Choice Awards, Airing on CBS for the First Time; Taylor Swift Leads Nominees Pratt next stars in Way of the Warrior Kid, an adaptation of Jocko Willink’s bestselling children’s novel that premieres Nov. 25 on Apple TV, which he also produced. “I’m incredibly honored to receive Nickelodeon’s King of Comedy Award,” Pratt said. “I spent most of my childhood trying to make people laugh to get out of trouble. articles.title: AFM Hot Project: Jacob Tremblay, Kate McKinnon Join ‘I’m With Stupid’ (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jacob Tremblay, Kate McKinnon, Ego Nwodim, Chabely Ponce Jenna Berman, Alexandra Carillo-Vaccino, Oriana Layendecker Ego Nwodim and Chabely Ponce are set to star in I’m With Stupid , a high school comedy directed by Hannah Pearl Utt ( Cora Bora ). Upgrade is handling international sales on the project and will launch it to buyers at the upcoming American Film Market . Written by Carolina Barlow ( The Hawk ) and Peter Kelly ( Big Mouth ), the film follows a pair of directionless high school seniors from opposite ends of the social spectrum who are forced to work together to avoid the humiliation of failing senior year. Related Stories Movies Sony Pictures Classics Takes Jean-Pierre Jeunet's 'Violette' for U.S. Movies Suzanne Farwell's Starry Rom-Com 'Otherwise Engaged' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM (Exclusive) Tremblay ( Room , Wonder , Good Boys ) plays Noah, a senior with an opinion on everything but no motivation. Ponce ( Girl Group ) is Hadley, Noah’s wealthy classmate who discovers she may have interests beyond becoming a trophy wife. McKinnon ( Barbie , Ghostbusters ) will portray Principal Dunlap, the school’s deeply unpopular and increasingly vindictive administrator. Nwodim ( Return to You , Hoppers ) is Ms. Reed, the students’ unconventional English teacher, who becomes an unlikely ally in their fight to graduate. “I’m thrilled to make a movie that’s this funny but has this much heart, with my dream group of collaborators,” Utt said. Mallory Schwartz ( The Morning Show, Cora Bora ) and Jen Goyne Blake ( Joyland ) are producing. Jonathan Kier and Matt Brodlie are executive producing for Upgrade, alongside Christine D’Souza for After Hours, Marc Danon and Kyle Fox for Fox Global Capital and April Shih for Diversity Hire. “There’s a real appetite for smart, unapologetically funny comedies,” said Kier and Brodlie of Upgrade. “Hannah has a terrific ability to find genuine emotion in absurd situations, and with this exceptional ensemble, we believe I’m With Stupid has all the ingredients to become a new generation’s favorite high school comedy.” Production on I’m With Stupid is set for February/March of 2027, with Rich Delia overseeing casting. UTA Film Finance Group and After Hours are co-representing the film for domestic sales. THR

Russell ( The Fighter ), Quentin Tarantino ( Once Upon a Time in Hollywood ) and Chloé Zhao ( Nomadland ). THR

articles.title: Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music
articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 8:09am PT Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music Former UTA and FaZe Clan leaders aim to shape representation for digital-native stars By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Mike Lee and Darren Yan Unveil ISO, a Next-Generation Management Firm Specializing in Creators, Live Streamers, Gaming and Music 38 minutes ago UFC’s Event Sellout Spree Powers TKO Q3 Earnings 19 hours ago Jessica Alba Battled ‘Major Impostor Syndrome’ as She Built The Honest Company Into an Early Star-Led Business Success Story 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tyler Ash Gaming and digital media veterans Mike Lee and Darren Yan have joined together to launch ISO , a talent management firm that specializes in representing the hottest commodities in marketing and media these days: creators and livestreaming personalities. Based in Los Angeles, Lee and Yan have quietly been building ISO’s operations for about a year, with financial backing from Influence Media Partners, an investment banner that also focuses on digital-native content. The launch of the firm draws on Lee and Yan’s breadth of experience working across gaming, sponsorship and branding and artist development. The pair have also built extensive partnership and distribution connections for entertainment and media platforms across Asia including in China. Related Stories Japan IP Market to Return to Cannes in 2027 as Tokyo Partnership Continues Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Lee, who was most recently head of gaming and livestreaming for UTA’s creators division, serves as co-founder and CEO of ISO. Yan, former chief talent officer at esports lifestyle firm FaZe Clan, serves as co-founder and head of music. ISO (which stands for In Search Of) at present has about 24 employees spread between Los Angeles, New York and Atlanta. The roster includes more than 90 livestreamers, gamers, artists, VTubers (aka livestreamers who use animated avatars) and lifestyle creators active in beauty, food and other highly engaged content verticals. Matt Alsberg, an alum of Sony’s PlayStation, Twitch and UTA, has signed on as ISO’s head of talent. “What we’re trying to build is something that is dedicated to the digital creator,” Lee tells Variety. Both founders have experience working at UTA and large-scale firms that are harnessing the heat of the next-generation stars of the attention economy. ISO was born out of Lee and Yan’s belief that talent representation firms have to operate very differently to support digital-native talent than they have for the past century in traditional film, TV and music. ISO’s roster at launch includes about 90 clients, including notable digital stars such as PlaqueBoyMax, Jasontheween, Ironmouse, Lacy, Vanillamace, Kyedae, jessechrisss, Angelo Marasigan, RDCWorld and more. ISO and its clients are alredy doing business with top-tier brands Electronic Arts, Discord, Underdog and Icenova, the ice cream brand known for its out-there shapes and flavors such as fried chicken. “If we really believe the next household name is going to come from the internet, then why aren’t all of our services optimized toward that internet star? We kept thinking, what if we were to actually blow everything up and we didn’t have an office and we weren’t spending millions of dollars on rent and theaters and showcases? Because our clients aren’t asking us for that,” Lee says. “There are no gatekeepers when it comes to digital media. It’s not four networks. It’s not seven channels. The gatekeepers are just the algorithms that feed your timelines. That’s what’s so incredible about working in this space.” Yan adds the pair’s proximity to explosive youth culture across Asia and in China, which has been an elusive market for so many U.S. firms, is a huge benefit to strategizing on where media and Gen Z and Gen Alpha consumption habits are headed. And it’s crucial for effective talent representation of digital dynamos. “For this generation, how they think and how they behave are not things are conditioned like a TV film actor or a sports athlete or even a music artist where they had to follow this specific pathway to success,” Yan tells Variety . “All of our clients are like, ‘Hey, we’re gonna break some eggs the way that we’re going to do it, and if you guys want to ride with us then you’re going to ride with us.’ That’s always been what we’ve always attached ourselves to. What they want when they look for partners or representation is who’s going to be able to move with us and say to our crazy ideas ‘This is possible.’ Because the talent that we work with will say, ‘Well, if it’s not you guys, then we’re going to do it ourselves. We don’t need a label, we don’t need a studio, we don’t need any of that. We have the money, we have the ingenuity, and whether or not you’re going to support us, we’re still going to build it and we’re going to win.’ ” Lee and Yan previously worked together at esports talent and marketing agencies Press X and Everyday Influencers, which were acquired by UTA in 2018. Lee and Yan then joined UTA. Yan exited UTA several years ago and was doing some consulting for Live Nation when he realized the opportunity to take popular live streamers on global tours, including in China. Yan and Lee have long-established relationships with local distribution partners that will go a long way toward helping talent make inroads in the world’s most populous country. Influence Media Partners is based in New York and specializes in developing and acquiring premium music and entertainment IP. Influence is supported by strategic partnerships with funds and accounts managed by private equity giant BlackRock. The interest in the digital native arena by one of the world’s biggest private equity firms is a sign of the times that Lee and Yan intend to capitalize on. ISO staffers gather to mark the company’s formal launch tyler ash “At Influence, we look to invest in partners who bring an innovative approach to the business of culture and entertainment. Mike, Darren and the team at ISO are reimagining talent representation for a creator economy that has fundamentally transformed how audiences are built, culture is shaped and revenue is generated,” said Lylette Pizarro, founder and co-managing partner of Influence Media Partners. “ISO’s playbook directly aligns with our values and investment philosophy, and we’re excited to support their growth.” The ISO founders see enormous opportunity ahead as the creator economy becomes more mainstream as a marketing and branding vehicle for the biggest brands (hence the interest in the arena from BlackRock). “We really have three pillars main pillars of the business: Talent driven by Mike’s team, our brand business and our music practice, which is artist management consulting,” Yan says. “With our digital native talent and with digital native advertising, we’re going to be able to bridge that gap [for marketers] and be able to drive and show more value. We were in the Twitch space 15 years ago. We’ve been fighting for experimental media budgets our entire careers,” Yan says. ISO has been established with what Lee and Yan call a policy of being “radically transparent” with their employees. The pair have developed a system of bonusing employees for success on a year-round basis, rather than doling out bonus coin once a year, with staffers receiving little information as to how the spoils were divided. The ISO founders also vow that in the effort to encourage collaboration and brainstorming among staffers, they have a formula for recognizing those contributions with bonus coin that comes out of the firm’s share of profits, not from the pool that goes to the primary representative. “The way we think about it is, every six months there is a new defecting faction out of some talent agency starting their own management company. And largely it is for very common reasons. The way we looked at it was, how do we prevent that from happening? How do we retain great talent, not just on our roster but our employees,” Lee says. “We don’t want to get to a point where we’re building this business with them, and then four or five years later they’re going to feel exactly how we felt, that we could own our own book of business and go somewhere else and make you know a lot more money that way. For us, we want to create an environment where [employees] feel like they can do that with a group of people that they trust. They’ll have stability but be making multiples of what they could make anywhere else.” (Pictured: ISO founders Darren Yan and Mike Lee) ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Bloodaxe’: Season 2 of Amazon Viking Drama Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand, Lasse Steen to Cast Drunk Shakespeare Theater Producer Sues Amazon, Alleging Prime Video’s ‘Off Campus’ Violated Its Trademarks ‘House of David’ to End With Season 3 at Amazon, Wonder Project ‘Things We Never Got Over’ Amazon Series Adds Six to Cast Loading comments...

Tickets for the Live Nation-produced engagement go on sale here on Nov. 13, preceded by an “artist presale” on Nov. 11. The group is currently still in the midst of a North American tour that will continue through Dec. 17. articles.title: Wunmi Mosaku Boards Doc Short ‘Swim Sistas’ as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 8:30am PT Wunmi Mosaku Boards Doc Short ‘Swim Sistas’ as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Wunmi Mosaku Boards Doc Short ‘Swim Sistas’ as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) 32 minutes ago Rhys Ifans on the ‘Frightening’ Task of Portraying Parkinson’s in ‘Onwards and Sideways’ and Learning to Wear ‘Costume’ of Disease: ‘I Really Did My Homework’ 2 hours ago ‘Rings of Power’ Star Eddie Marsan on Playing a Power-Hungry Dwarf and Why He Once Had 2,000 Pairs of Orlando Bloom’s Elf Ears in His Attic 3 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ashley Randall Wunmi Mosaku , the Oscar-nominated and BAFTA-winning star of Ryan Coogler’s 2025 hit “Sinners,” has come aboard British documentary short “Swim Sistas” as executive producer. The film, celebrating Black women’s relationship with swimming, was directed by Catherine Joy White (“Bridgerton,” “Fifty-Four Days”), with Naomie Harris (“Moonlight”) narrating. After premiering at DOC NYC and winning several awards on the festival circuit, it has now qualified for the 99th Academy Awards. Related Stories Sky News Stands by Journalist Following Heated Exchange With Abdul El-Sayed: 'We're Proud of Our Correspondent, Who Was Doing His Job' Lady Gaga, Jack White, Boy George Lead Songwriters Hall of Fame 2027 Nominees “The story of our relationship with swimming and water has so much depth and history, complexity that is so beautifully captured by ‘Swim Sistas,'” said Mosaku. “This powerful film and its themes speak personally to me, as I know it does many others, and I could not be more excited to join as executive producer. I believe ‘Swim Sistas’ will not only move people, but change how they see the world, and I’m proud to help its message reach a wider audience, and support its next chapter.” Featuring four Black British women, “Swim Sista” follows Alice Dearing, Great Britain’s first Black female Olympic swimmer; professional rugby player and “The Traitors” contestant Jasmine Boatswain; teenage athlete Lexie Sandiford; and Roni Bruno, who learned to swim at the age of 54. Through their stories, the documentary explores what it says are the “barriers, histories and joy that shape Black women’s relationships with water.” Featuring original poetry written by White, the film sees Harris voice Mami Wata, a central poetic figure embodying “ancestral strength and hope for the future.” “Wunmi is a stunning talent. Her work carries such depth and humanity and to have her join forces with ‘Swim Sistas’ brings another dimension to a world that has always been about so much more than swimming,” said White. “We’re honoured to have Wunmi on this journey with us as we continue to elevate Black women’s voices and reshape the story of who water is for.” Added Afua Hirsch and Amandla Crichlow, executive producers and founders of Born in Me Productions: “Wunmi Mosaku is an actor of such skill and grace, who represents the beauty and power of Black women in a way that has truly universal resonance. We could not be more proud to have her as a partner on ‘Swim Sistas.’” The attachment of Mosaku — also a BAFTA TV award winner for “Damilola, Our Loved Boy” — comes as the filmmakers behind “Swim Sistas” develop plans to expand the project into a documentary series exploring Black women’s relationships with water across the U.S., the Caribbean and Africa. Also joining the film’s executive producing team alongside Mosaku is BAFTA-nominated executive producer Ash Horne (“Marion,” “The Second Time Around”). “Growing up, swimming was something I always took for granted. It was simply part of being a kid and I never really questioned that privilege. So, when I learned that 97% of Black adults and around 80% of Black children in England don’t swim regularly, it really struck me,” said Horne. “‘Swim Sistas’ is a beautiful, heartfelt and important documentary that shines a light on this disparity while celebrating community and the joy of swimming. Catherine Joy White has created something genuinely moving, and I’m incredibly proud to support the film and help bring this conversation to a wider audience.” Originally announced in Variety , “Swim Sistas” has since screened at more than 50 festivals worldwide. Its accolades include best documentary at Women X, a BAFTA- and BIFA-qualifying festival, and the jury’s choice award at the Thomas Edison Film Festival, an Oscar-qualifying festival. The film has also enjoyed a 26-cinema theatrical run, screened at the National Gallery of Art in Washington, D.C., and opened special screenings of “The Little Mermaid” and “The Shape of Water.” It was featured at the inaugural United Nations Swimmable Cities Summit in Rotterdam and is being incorporated into the French national curriculum. “Swim Sistas” is produced by Oriane Pick and Anaïs Ferrato of BAFTA-nominated Candid Broads Productions, with executive producers Hirsch (“Enslaved,” “Africa Rising”) and Crichlow (“Honk for Jesus. articles.title: How ‘Frontline’ Turned Into an Oscar-Winning Documentary Juggernaut
articles.full_text: Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT How ‘Frontline’ Turned Into an Oscar-Winning Documentary Juggernaut Under Raney Aronson-Rath, the decades-old PBS doc series has started winning Oscars (“20 Days in Mariupol”) and appealing to younger generations online. By Marlow Stern Plus Icon Marlow Stern Chief Correspondent Latest Judi Dench Tells All About Bond: It Was Daniel Craig’s Idea to ‘Have Me Killed’ 2 days ago Spike Lee Is Praying the Knicks Don’t Visit the Trump White House 3 days ago John Oliver Reviews ‘You Can See Everything’: Elizabeth Holmes and Billy Evans Are ‘Complete Lunatics’ 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source PBS/Frontline This year’s documentary Oscar race will pit a cringe comedy maestro against the most decorated documentary film producer of the past decade. While plenty of ink has been spilled over Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s form-shattering Elizabeth Holmes curio “You Can See Everything,” it would be a mistake to count out Raney Aronson-Rath. Aronson-Rath has been at the helm of “ Frontline ,” PBS ’ acclaimed investigative documentary series, since 2015. Under her watch, the program has won so many Emmys she’s lost count (it stands at 44) and launches around 20 documentaries a year. In 2024, it took home its first documentary Oscar for “20 Days in Mariupol,” a vivid and violent account of AP journalist Mstyslav Chernov and his colleagues’ time in the Ukrainian city as it withstood Russia’s invasion in early 2022. Related Stories 'Married at First Sight' U.K. Canceled by Channel 4 Following Sexual Assault Allegations Awkwafina's ‘Kate Might Die,’ ‘Outside of Cleveland’ With Alex Wolff Among Projects Selected for U.S. in Progress A few days after Chernov and his team escaped Mariupol with their footage, he and Aronson-Rath got to work on the film. “‘ 20 Days in Mariupol ’ was my debut film. [Raney] and the ‘Frontline’ team helped me practically and creatively transition from journalism to cinema, which is quite a challenge,” Chernov says, adding, “For many of us who are working on socially and politically relevant projects but cannot find a home and distributor, Raney is the last hope to get the film made and find its audience.” Oscar night was “a surreal moment” for Aronson-Rath. “People kept asking me, ‘Are you going to do more of these?!” she recalls. The common refrain was that “Frontline” couldn’t do theatrical films, and then one day it hit her: “I realized I was in charge of ‘Frontline,’ and we had the funding and distribution, so why not?” Aronson-Rath launched Frontline Features last November as a dedicated studio that premieres feature and short-form documentaries in festivals and theaters ahead of PBS airings. Its latest release is “One in a Million,” a feature doc from Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes that follows an 11-year-old girl, Israa, over 10 years as she and her family flee war-torn Syria to Turkey before settling in Germany. A powerful examination of war, immigration and the ties that bind, the film won the Audience Award at this year’s Sundance Film Festival and is poised to earn an Oscar nomination. “I was there from the very beginning. They sent me raw footage of Israa when she was 10 years old,” explains Aronson-Rath, a producer on the film. “I had a feeling that Israa’s story was going to be amazing.” On top of Aronson-Rath’s “extraordinary passion and professionalism,” Azzam is grateful that Frontline gave the project the benefit of time: “We were following real people going through major changes in their lives, which required patience, trust and a willingness to embrace uncertainty, and having that long-term commitment was essential,” explains Azzam. “Raney was always there with her unwavering belief in the film and her understanding that this wasn’t simply a story about refugees reaching Europe, but about what happens afterward: growing up in exile, searching for belonging and navigating identity.” Frontline also lent valuable “editorial experience,” Azzam maintains. Aronson-Rath’s team typically assigns investigative reporters to aid projects, conduct deep legal reviews and analyze rushes to make sure they meet their editorial standards. Aronson-Rath caught the journalism bug writing for The China Post, an English-language newspaper for expats in Taipei, after graduating from the University of Wisconsin. While attending the Columbia Journalism School, she caught a screening of Steve James’ 1994 documentary “Hoop Dreams” at Film Forum in downtown Manhattan. “It was a really transcendent moment for me,” she remembers. “I’d found the form that I love.” Years later, Aronson-Rath worked closely with James on “Abacus: Small Enough to Jail,” about a family-owned bank in Manhattan’s Chinatown that was the only financial institution to face criminal charges following the 2008 financial crisis; the doc earned “Frontline” its first Oscar nomination in 2018. “Public television has for decades tried to broaden its appeal to younger audiences, often without success,” says James. “From the day Raney took over, it was clear that she wanted to find more innovative ways to tell powerful true stories.” Frontline has, under Aronson-Rath, proven intensely popular among younger generations. Its YouTube channel has 4.8 million subscribers — eclipsing 1 billion views in July with an astonishing 422 million hours watched. It also has three features lined up for 2027, including Chernov’s next film, which Aronson-Rath will be producing. “One of the others is a film I’ve been working on for 20 years with a filmmaker named Dan Edge,” she shares, “focusing on one character we met two decades ago who came back from Iraq.” She flashes a grin. “I love a longitudinal, epic story.” ‘House of David’ to End With Season 3 at Amazon, Wonder Project ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Bloodaxe’: Season 2 of Amazon Viking Drama Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand, Lasse Steen to Cast ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon ‘Rose Hill’ Amazon Series Adds Siobhan McGroarty, Sophia Reid-Gantzert, West Mulholland Loading comments...
