articles.title: ‘Dune’ Launches Arrakis-Inspired Press-On Nail Collection With Glamnetic
articles.full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. The world of “ Dune ” is getting the beauty treatment. Ahead of the Dec. 18 release of “Dune: Part Three,” Glamnetic has teamed up with Warner Bros. on a limited-edition collection of press-on nails inspired by the sci-fi franchise, marking its first foray into the beauty category. Launching Nov. 5, the limited-edition Glamnetic x Dune collection features nine nail sets drawing on the films’ characters, mythology and distinctive visual world, from the glowing blue eyes of the Fremen to the giant sandworms that roam Arrakis. The partnership marks the franchise’s first beauty collaboration, according to Glamnetic, with prices ranging from $21.99 to $23.99. Related Stories Russell Brand Found Guilty of Rape and Sexual Assault in London Trial; Taken Into Custody ‘Bad Day’ Trailer: Cameron Diaz Is a Single Mom Who Accidentally Robs a Bank in Netflix Comedy Among the designs is “Spice Melange” ($21.99), featuring a translucent burnt-amber finish outlined in fine gold, inspired by the precious substance at the center of Frank Herbert’s fictional universe. “Eyes of Ibad” ($21.99) takes its cues from the Fremen’s signature blue-in-blue eyes, with iridescent cobalt chrome and an aurora-like shimmer. LIMITED-EDITION Dune x Glamnetic Collection shop now “The Maker” ($23.99) pays tribute to the franchise’s colossal sandworms through sculpted gold, amber and ridged chocolate-brown detailing, complete with a cobalt stone accent. “Reverend Mother” ($23.99) features a more elaborate combination of multicolored jewels, gold chrome, smoky mauve and black-and-gold detailing, while “Chip & Shatter” ($23.99) pairs a milky cream base with textured, crackled gold foil. The collection is the latest entertainment-inspired launch from Glamnetic, which has previously released licensed nail sets celebrating “Harry Potter,” including designs inspired by Hogwarts houses, the Marauder’s Map and the Deathly Hallows. The brand has also expanded into sports merchandise through a partnership with Fanatics, offering team-branded manicures featuring official NFL, NBA, MLB and other league logos and colors. The launch comes just over a month before “Dune: Part Three” arrives in theaters Dec. 18, bringing Villeneuve’s blockbuster trilogy to a close. The upcoming Warner Bros. and Legendary film draws from Herbert’s 1969 novel “Dune Messiah” and takes place nearly two decades after Paul Atreides’ rise to power, following the consequences of his reign as emperor and the growing threats to his rule. Timothée Chalamet and Zendaya return as Paul Atreides and Chani, alongside Florence Pugh, Anya Taylor-Joy, Rebecca Ferguson, Javier Bardem and Jason Momoa. Robert Pattinson joins the franchise as Scytale, a central figure in the conspiracy against Paul. Villeneuve directs from a screenplay co-written with Brian K. Vaughan. The franchise has already proved fertile ground for unconventional merchandise partnerships. Ahead of 2024’s “Dune: Part Two,” watchmaker Hamilton collaborated with the filmmakers to create a futuristic wrist device worn in the film, subsequently releasing two limited-edition Ventura watches inspired by the prop. Chalamet also worked with Cartier on a custom necklace for the film’s London premiere, featuring roughly 900 gemstones in desert-inspired shades of amber, orange and blue. The Glamnetic collection offers a considerably more affordable entry point into the world of Arrakis, arriving just in time for the franchise’s theatrical finale and the holiday shopping season. The Glamnetic x Dune collection will be available beginning Nov. 5. Loading comments...

articles.title: Robert Pattinson to Receive 40th American Cinematheque Award
articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT Robert Pattinson to Receive 40th American Cinematheque Award By Angelique Jackson Plus Icon Angelique Jackson angelique814 Latest Pixar Names Jonathan Garson as President; Jim Morris Moves to Emeritus Role 16 hours ago Neve Campbell Confirms Return for ‘Scream 8’ 3 days ago ‘X-Men’: ‘Hunger Games’ Actor Ben Wang Circling Iceman Role in Marvel’s Reboot 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Stefanie Keenan Robert Pattinson will be honored as the 40th recipient of the American Cinematheque Award. Pattinson receives the award in celebration of his own two-decade career, in which he’s established himself as one of the most versatile actors of his generation. The actor will be feted on Feb. 9, 2027, at the Beverly Hilton in Beverly Hills. “Rob has built an extraordinary career defined by his unwavering dedication to his craft, fearless creative choices and remarkable versatility as an actor,” American Cinematheque board chair Rick Nicita stated, announcing Pattinson’s selection. “From his collaborations with some of cinema’s most visionary filmmakers to his ability to captivate audiences in major studio blockbusters, Rob has continually challenged expectations and demonstrated the power of great storytelling.” Related Stories Rhys Ifans on the ‘Frightening’ Task of Portraying Parkinson’s in ‘Onwards and Sideways’ and Learning to Wear ‘Costume’ of Disease: ‘I Really Did My Homework’ Clio Barnard's 'I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning' Bought by Kino Lorber for North America (EXCLUSIVE) In 2026 alone, Pattinson starred opposite Zendaya in the dark romance “The Drama”; played the villainous Atinuous in Christopher Nolan’s epic “The Odyssey” and portrayed “To Catch a Predator” journalist Chris Hansen in “Primetime,” which also marked the debut film from Pattinson’s production company Icki Eneo Arlo. He wraps up the year as a shape-shifting assassin in Denis Villeneuve’s “Dune: Part Three.” Pattinson is currently in production on Matt Reeves’ “The Batman: Part II,” reprising his role as Batman/Bruce Wayne in the sequel to the blockbuster superhero movie. That level of dexterity is par for the course for Pattinson, who has curated a career that spotlights his range as a performer. The actor’s filmography spans his breakout roles in the “Twilight” and “Harry Potter” franchises to more eclectic fare like Robert Eggers’ “The Lighthouse”; “Good Time,” from Josh and Benny Safdie; Bong Joon Ho’s “Mickey 17”; “Die, My Love” with Jennifer Lawrence; and Nolan’s “Tenet.” “Rob is the perfect choice to receive this award and join our esteemed list of artists who not only love cinema but continue to have a deep impact on our industry,” Nicita continued. “We are thrilled that his filming schedule has allowed us the opportunity to recognize his exceptional contributions to film and we look forward to celebrating his continued achievements.” Pattinson joins a distinguished group of honorees including Michael B. Jordan (last year’s recipient and the eventual best actor Oscar winner), Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, Denzel Washington (Pattinson’s co-star in the upcoming film “The Take”), Nicole Kidman and George Clooney, among others. To note, Ryan Gosling was previously selected to receive the 40th American Cinematheque award. But when the “Project Hail Mary” star had a scheduling conflict with the gala (originally set for Nov. 2), the event was postponed to 2027. The annual American Cinematheque gala is a fundraiser for the nonprofit organization, supporting its year-round programming at the Aero Theatre in Santa Monica, the Los Feliz 3 Theatre in Los Feliz and the Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood. ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson ‘Reacher’ Renewed for Season 6 Ahead of Season 5 Premiere ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon Drunk Shakespeare Theater Producer Sues Amazon, Alleging Prime Video’s ‘Off Campus’ Violated Its Trademarks ‘Bloodaxe’: Season 2 of Amazon Viking Drama Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand, Lasse Steen to Cast Loading comments...

articles.title: How Grimes’ Cameo in Theater-Bound AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Came Together (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Nov 5, 2026 9:00am PT How Grimes’ Cameo in Theater-Bound AI Film ‘Gods Don’t Give Gifts’ Came Together (EXCLUSIVE) By Corbin Bolies Plus Icon Corbin Bolies Latest Scarlett Johansson Says ‘The Batman 2’ Role Was ‘Very Hard to Figure Out’: ‘It Gave Me a Lot of Existential Angst’ 19 hours ago Meta to Help Bring ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ to 3D Screens — and Its $1,299 VR Glasses 3 days ago Utopai Studios Names Former Disney AI Leader Hans Ku as Chief Product Officer 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fable Even in the AI era, there’s still no better way to reach a favorite artist than by sliding into their DMs. Zack London, who directed the upcoming AI film “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” under his moniker Gossip Goblin, had long been a fan of Grimes , the moniker of 38-year-old experimental pop artist Claire Boucher. But he didn’t necessarily expect that love to be mutual, not until he noticed she had followed his X account and started engaging with his videos. Related Stories South International Series Festival Prizes: ’Blindspot Berlin,’ ‘The Oligarch and the Art Dealer’ Win Big 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Spins Up Massive Numbers for Sony's Quarterly Earnings Then in March, Boucher replied to clips shared on Gossip Goblin’s X account. London responded , offering her a role in a project of his. Sensing an opportunity, he then sent Grimes a direct message just expressing how much he loved her music. “We started chatting, and it was like, ‘Oh, we know a ton of the same people,’” he tells Variety last month over lunch in Chelsea, coming off several prerelease screenings of the AI film. “She was like, ‘I would love to do something with you.’ And then, it was basically, ‘Well, I wish I knew that earlier, but let’s find a way for you to be in this.’” The fruit of those DMs will bear next month in Boucher’s minuteslong cameo in “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the first AI feature set to debut in theaters. Boucher plays “Zaynith Alda” in one of the early sequences in the post-apocalyptic film, which aims to satirize humanity’s relationship with technology. Alda, a brash, demanding aristocrat who hails from the rich Halvorith family, seeks a “dreamspool” an illicit, induced experience in the world of “NiiroCradle” that lets people experience alternate realities. Boucher’s cameo — and that of YouTuber and Logan Paul pal Mike Majlak, who also makes a brief appearance — injects a dash of celebrity into the bold ambitions of “Gods Don’t Give Gifts,” the R-rated sci-fi film trying to barrel its way past society’s aversion to AI films and into the best animated feature category at the Oscars. Fable, the AI studio behind the film, has leaned in, setting a Times Square marketing campaign featuring Boucher’s appearance. Fable The studio also hosted screenings targeting animation voting bloc members of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences across New York and Los Angeles ahead of its Dec. 4 debut, eager to try and assuage the Academy’s concerns about all things AI and urge them to consider the gory film among the likes of the critically acclaimed “Wildwood” and “Toy Story 5.” (Variety’s “Awards Circuit” does not list “Gods Don’t Give Gifts” among the Academy’s potential contenders.) “You only need to see Grimes’ brilliant performance in the film to understand how much things are about to change for animated movies,” Fable CEO Edward Saatchi said in a bullish statement. “We hope the Academy will recognize that a film that is seminal (the first AI film), wildly technically novel and (most importantly) good deserves a nomination.” Boucher declined an interview request. Her spokesperson, Mitchell Jackson, said in a statement that Boucher “appreciates indie artists using new tools to create independent art—especially in the age of big studio monopolies.” “She was particularly impressed that they had such a large team and were involving and compensating so many artists, voice actors, and musicians,” her spokesperson said. “She believes in supporting the right kind of culture around AI in cinema rather than acquiescing to the current model of having no standards.” The Zaynith Alda character was already written into the film’s nearly two-hour runtime, but Boucher’s appearance forced London and his co-writer Jacob Batchelor to adapt the role around her persona. That meant giving her the chance to help design the character, including a mechanical-looking mask that adorns Alda’s face, and nixing the British accent native to the rest of the film’s world. Once those were set, a multi-continent team of London in Stockholm, his editor and sound engineer in Romania, and Boucher and her producer in LA worked together to record her lines from her home. Is there a recording anywhere of Boucher attempting a British accent? “If there are, they’re on a hard drive somewhere,” London says. Boucher is also one of the highest-profile examples of a celebrity authorizing their likeness for an AI project, following examples such as UFC fighters in Higgsfield’s “Cully Hill Boys” and “The View” co-host Sunny Hostin licensing her image and novels to Fountain 0 to make AI adaptations — featuring her likeness — of her books. It’s a testament to celebrities’ slow embrace of AI in culture, including everything from Ben Affleck’s Netflix-owned InterPositive startup for AI tools to actors like Michael Caine licensing his voice to the AI audio firm ElevenLabs. Others, however, remain fearful that AI could exploit their likenesses without permission or compensation . It helps that Boucher has long championed AI. In 2023, she launched an AI software program called “Elf.Tech,” where fans could use her vocal likeness in their tracks so long as she received 50% of the master recording royalties, and in a 2024 PBS interview called AI an “opportunity” for artists that, with democratized access to professional tools, could see “actual talent, like, really rise to the top.” For this film, London says Boucher authorized her license for free and refused to be paid, a fact her spokesperson confirmed. “She said, ‘You guys are scrappy, just put that money towards the other actors [and] your film,’” London says, calling Boucher part of “a different class of artists that look at the big picture of what are you doing, what is the holistic statement surrounding, and not getting hung up on the process.” Watch a clip of Boucher’s appearance below: ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role ‘Reacher’ Renewed for Season 6 Ahead of Season 5 Premiere ‘Off Campus’ Sets Season 2 Release Date at Amazon Drunk Shakespeare Theater Producer Sues Amazon, Alleging Prime Video’s ‘Off Campus’ Violated Its Trademarks ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson Loading comments...

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed Mocks Trump and Ted Cruz’s Cruel Rhetoric on ‘The View,’ Jokes He Wants ‘Jihadist Leprechaun’ Printed on a Hat
articles.full_text: × Nov 5, 2026 9:14am PT Abdul El-Sayed Mocks Trump and Ted Cruz’s Cruel Rhetoric on ‘The View,’ Jokes He Wants ‘Jihadist Leprechaun’ Printed on a Hat By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest ‘Dune’ Launches Arrakis-Inspired Press-On Nail Collection With Glamnetic 14 minutes ago Katseye’s Megan Skiendiel Fronts Rare Beauty and Warby Parker’s New Eyewear Collaboration 14 minutes ago Tim Burton and Loewe Team Up on Luxe ‘Nightmare Before Christmas’ Collection 3 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Abdul El-Sayed fired back at President Donald Trump and other Republican politicians who attacked his Muslim faith during his Senate campaign during an appearance on “ The View ” Thursday, just two days after his historic victory in Michigan. The 42-year-old Democrat, who defeated Republican Mike Rogers to become the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate , reflected on the Islamophobic rhetoric that dominated the final weeks of his campaign and credited Michigan voters with rejecting the divisive attacks. Rahman and Hans Zimmer's Soundtrack “They weren’t attacking me. They were attacking the idea of an America big enough for me,” El-Sayed told the co-hosts. “I didn’t take a bet on my abilities or anything. I took a bet on the goodness of the people of Michigan.” During the interview, Sunny Hostin ran through some of the most incendiary remarks made about El-Sayed by prominent Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, who suggested there was something “very, very evil” about him, and Sen. Ted Cruz, who called him a “jihadist leprechaun.” “I want a hat!” El-Sayed joked in response to the latter insult. Hostin also brought up Trump’s remarks at an October campaign rally in Michigan, where the president called El-Sayed a “jihadist” and suggested he would “have to go through a metal detector before he’s allowed to go into the Senate.” Trump also invoked the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks while urging voters to reject the Democratic candidate. “If they had something to say about the price of gas or the price of groceries or the fact that people can’t see a doctor, they would’ve said it,” El-Sayed said of the Republican attacks. “But they didn’t have anything to say.” “I kind of knew they were gonna reach for the red meat,” he continued. “But here’s the problem with the red meat: It becomes an addiction. Once you go there and you put that out there, then you’re forced to defend it. So what do they do? They double down. They triple down again.” As for Trump’s metal detector comments, El-Sayed reiterated a challenge he first issued to the president at a campaign rally in Kalamazoo last week. “I’ll do a metal detector test all day because I have nothing to hide,” he said, before addressing the president directly: “Donald, if you’re watching, a lie detector is still on the table.” ‘Carrie’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series Adds Eight, Including Sean Astin, Patricia Clarkson Drunk Shakespeare Theater Producer Sues Amazon, Alleging Prime Video’s ‘Off Campus’ Violated Its Trademarks ‘House of David’ to End With Season 3 at Amazon, Wonder Project ‘Reacher’ Spinoff ‘Neagley’ Renewed for Season 2 at Amazon Elizabeth Banks Officially Set to Play Karen Read in Amazon Series Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Toy Story 5’ Writer-Director Andrew Stanton Wants To Bring Nuance To The Conversation Between Kids & Technology
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Destiny Jackson Destiny Jackson Crafts Editor, Awards @DestinyDreadful More Stories By Destiny ‘Planted!’ Game Dev Ben Cawthorne On Digging Up Chaos In A Competitive Gardening Game ‘Tenzing’s Jennifer Peedom On Bringing The Everest Pioneer’s Story To Life — Deadline Screening Series Taraji P. Henson Encourages Artists To ‘Knock Down’ Walls, Sarah Finn Celebrates Casting Community & More At 2026 Newport Beach Film Festival Honors View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Toy Story 5 Disney/Pixar For the better part of three decades, Woody ( Tom Hanks ), Buzz ( Tim Allen ), and the gang have kept audiences company through the ups and downs of growing up. Now, Toy Story 5 finds the franchise entering a new chapter, with Jessie ( Joan Cusack ) taking center stage and technology changing the way children play. Co-writer and co-director Andrew Stanton helps usher in a new group of characters: Lilypad (Greta Lee), a frog-framed tablet, and Blaze (Mykal-Michelle Harris), a confident young girl who marches to the beat of her own drum. Alongside the familiar faces, the new toys bring fresh possibilities to a story that still has plenty to say about childhood and the evolution of social connection. Below, Stanton talks to Deadline about developing another entry, digging deeper into Jessie’s backstory, and the cherry on top of the cake: Taylor Swift’s new pop-country single, “I Knew It, I Knew You.” Related Stories Executives Pixar Veteran Jim Morris Moving To Emeritus Position As Jonathan Garson Named New President News Disney To Undergo More Layoffs With Divisions Eyeing Up To 20% In Cost Savings DEADLINE: How did you and co-screenwriter Kenna Harris decide which new characters would join the story? And how did that ultimately influence the direction of the film? Watch on Deadline ANDREW STANTON: There are unsaid expectations with every Toy Story movie now that we’ve had several installments. I think audiences, even unconsciously, expect to meet somebody new along the way and add to the cast. We bemoan that because the cast is already so huge. I always say I have so many mouths to feed, and if I gave everybody one line, the movie would be over in one scene. So we not only have to be judicious about who we add, but also about who we let go of and who we push to the background. By the time we’re doing five, you’re thinking there may be more. I don’t get too caught up in worrying about everybody getting their fair share of time. I just let the needs of the story dictate things. Right from the get-go, I knew I wanted it to be about Jessie, and I wanted a device to represent technology coming in. That dictated Lilypad right away. In this world, I don’t buy that TVs and phones can just talk to you. There has to be something, character-wise, built in to bring them to life in the same way Forky was in Toy Story 4 . So making a frog frame around an iPad was something I came up with very early on, when I was writing by myself. Even in the first draft, I was concerned I was late to the party on this issue, given that technology has been around kids and their toys for at least 10 or 15 years. It’s only gotten more advanced and smarter, and social media and all that stuff have come in more recently. I also started thinking about those early technology toys. We all have these devices, even the computers on our desks, and they change every three to five years. They get upgraded to something else. I thought about the short life those devices have. There’s always that drawer in my house with spare batteries, rubber bands, and cords you don’t know what they’re for. When my kids were little in the 2000s, it started having things like fun calculators for kids. You don’t know how long to keep that stuff. I thought, what a horrible existence for the first generation of tech toys to go through, being played with by kids and then discarded. That was pretty early on, too. It was about creating characters to represent that first generation of technology. The story dictated the new cast. I’ve also just never grown up. Body humor still cracks me up. I was amazed to find out there hadn’t been a toilet-training toy of any sort in the history of toys. I thought, “Well, let’s introduce one and see where that goes.” Toy Story 5 Disney/Pixar DEADLINE: Outside of your own experience, what did other research look like? Did you all happen to talk to other children or parents about how they interact with toys and technology? STANTON: Eventually we did. I’m a little superstitious about knowing the world’s rules or people’s opinions too soon because it starts to influence things. I like to be free to roam about the cabin any way I want for a while. I know there are going to be many years of debating this, many more voices coming in, and many more people weighing in, all meaning well. But there’s this rare window of about a year where it’s just mine, and I get to go, “Where does my mind go?” I have strong opinions based on observing children and not seeing toys played with by older kids. It just seemed to me that the window was getting younger and shorter, that little kids were playing with toys for less time. I remember playing with toys, and some of that was because I had younger siblings. I played all the way up until I was 10. That was really what I wanted to explore from an entertainment and narrative standpoint: What is that doing to the characters we’ve come to know and love over these generations when they’re just getting less time with a child? That was enough to play with for a while. But eventually, we did our own research because we have a lot of young parents who work at Pixar . We didn’t have to go outside the walls to find a large group of people sharing their frustrations and concerns about their children being introduced to technology, when they should be, and how every kid was different. It was nice to know that it was messy. Kenna and I didn’t want to make it a black-and-white binary where this was bad, and this was good, because that’s never good drama. It’s always good drama when it’s in the gray, and it’s messy. You can see the reason why you’re introducing it, and it’s not going away. Some kids are different from others. That made for really good exploration. There are upsides, otherwise, people wouldn’t be tempted to use technology. Kids are shy. Kids live in communities where there might not be anybody like them in terms of their interests, disabilities, or abilities, and suddenly they can reach other people they wouldn’t otherwise reach. Andrew Stanton DEADLINE: I think that’s one of the things that really works about the film. It doesn’t feel preachy, and it would have been easy to lean one way or the other, especially when discussing technology and how children interact with it. How did you find that balance? STANTON: It would be so easy if it were a story about technology just being bad because then nobody would do it. Everybody wants their kid to have these experiences. There are upsides, otherwise, people wouldn’t be tempted to use technology. Kids are shy. Kids live in communities where there might not be anybody like them in terms of their interests, disabilities, or abilities, and suddenly they can reach other people they wouldn’t otherwise reach. As a kid, before there was all this technology, all I wanted was to have a can and a string so I could still talk to my best friend way down the street. That impulse is in us as natural human beings and as kids. The idea of having a secret clubhouse where you can say hi to your friend, with all those innocent needs, is understandable. Technology is also so involved in how our world functions. We want our kids to know how to operate in the world. It does some cool stuff, and we all played games. We were part of the gaming culture. As ’80s kids, we all ran to the arcades. TV was always around, and everybody thought it was going to rot our brains. Maybe it did, but we all did it [laughs]. It’s complicated, and that’s what makes it interesting. The thing I cherish about growing up before all this stuff was how much boredom gave me the skills to enjoy being in my own head. That was something nobody could take away from me. I hate the thought of my kids having less access to that, of having less of that full experience. It’s like the difference between the joy of reading and making up the whole thing in your head versus seeing a movie where it’s all been decided for you. Those are gifts in life that you realize the older you get, and you hate the idea that anybody coming into the world might be shortchanged. We realized that it isn’t about technology itself. It’s a choice. It’s a choice to turn off the TV, it’s a choice to turn off the device, and it’s a choice in how you use it. That’s where we realized the universal truth. I didn’t want anybody to look at any of the movies we make, let alone the Toy Story movies, 10 or 20 years from now and feel they were so dated that they couldn’t relate to them anymore. We’ve always tried to be in the grandparent business. What we used to say is that we’re not just trying to get kids to watch our movies. We want you to like them and have them touch you in a universal and human way so much that, even as a grandparent, you go, “I have to make sure my grandkids watch this particular movie. It was one of my favorites.” Toy Story 5 Disney/Pixar DEADLINE: I enjoyed the film’s new visual style, especially the imaginative playtime sketches. Talk about that aesthetic. STANTON: It seems really obvious now that we found it. We just wanted something that felt handcrafted, kid-conjured, and had an improvisational feel. It had to feel like make-believe in your head, or even when you’re vocally pretending with your friend. You’re allowed to pivot mid-sentence, and suddenly they’re all vampires [laughs]. We wanted to figure out how to make it feel like that visually. It’s sort of like theater, where a spotlight can suddenly come on, something new appears, something is removed, and you’re open-minded to the rules changing at any moment. We compared it to trying to invent a new color. Everybody pictured something a little different. But “ephemeral” and “temporal” were the words that kept coming up. So there was the chalky feel, the fact that things faded off, and the sense of a dream, where your focus was wherever things locked in, but everything else could change. Mood, color, and everything could shift. That childlike illustration-book feeling, but theatrical, was ultimately what we found. DEADLINE: Looking back at the previous Toy Story movies and thinking about Andy, we didn’t focus on his friend group too much outside the house. So, it was cool to me that Bonnie has Blaze as a companion for her. When did she come into the picture? STANTON: The friendship direction of Bonnie making a new friend evolved throughout the making of the story. In the early days, we just wanted Jessie to go to her old address, have it be rural and farm-like, and have new owners. That was it. There wasn’t going to be any connection with Bonnie and the girl who lived there. So we had free rein to ask, “Who should be there?” We wanted to make it a bit more mixed and culturally diverse, and make it feel like how the world looks to us, both emotionally and culturally. Also, [there was a desire of the animators] to conquer curly hair really badly. They wanted to do it right because the technology had changed even since Brave . So, Blaze was thought up by Kenna and [conceptualized by the art team], and we loved it. Then the character started telling us something [as we developed the story]. We worked hard to make sure Bonnie felt different, both race-wise and, more importantly, girl-wise. She wasn’t the trope of a little girl. She was a little left of center. She thought in vibrant, random ways, and she was special. But she’s shy and not brave enough socially to expose that. That’s very common for any kid: showing the real you. But Blaze is the one who does that. We thought about having Bonnie find her tribe in a person who can understand how her mind works. We thought, what if Blaze was the shining example of confidence in that kind of thinking and also being a little left of center? She was just one year older, and when you’re that young, one year older is the coolest club to be in, to be hanging out with. We became enamored with her as a character, and she quickly became the model for somebody Bonnie could connect with, admire, and be friends with, if we could just get them to meet. That ultimately turned the whole story around. The universal thing that will make this movie speak to you 10 or 20 years from now, nostalgically, is when you find that kid who doesn’t think exactly like you, but you complement each other just right. As you get older, you realize that’s one of the most valuable things you find in your life, whether you meet them in college, at a young age, or even later. Those are the things you value most. Suddenly, it became a very priceless story. DEADLINE: You mentioned that the film initially started as a Jessie-centric story. Was there ever a version of the script where Jessie was reunited with Emily, or was that always something you knew you wanted to avoid? STANTON: There was. We just knew there was power in closing that wound for her, so we didn’t know how to go about it. I did the most obvious thing in my first draft. We hid the address from the audience. It was only seen by Bullseye on the back of Jessie’s chaps, and we would always have Bullseye nudge her chaps, thinking he just wanted something like a dog. Without getting into the long plot, it became a third-act moment where he finally brought her to what she thought was Bullseye’s home, only to find out he had brought her to the address on the back of her chaps. We revealed it at the last second, and she suddenly got to witness Grandma Emily playing with her granddaughter, the baby. It was very moving, but it took a lot of mountain-moving to get there. We knew the feeling we had captured for Jessie was something to aspire to and find another way to get to, which ultimately resulted in the finished movie. We worked hard to make sure Bonnie felt different, both race-wise and, more importantly, girl-wise. She wasn’t the trope of a little girl. She was a little left of center. She thought in vibrant, random ways, and she was special. Andrew Stanton DEADLINE: I have to say, one of the things I really loved was Buzz’s relationship with Jessie. When you think about the history of Toy Story and how Buzz has always been so tough, brave, and confident, I left the theater thinking he’s a total “wife guy.” He’s completely smitten with Jessie. STANTON: Is that a term, or is that your own term? I’ve never heard that term. DEADLINE: It’s a term on the internet, so I can’t take credit for it. If a guy is really into his wife or girlfriend, you say he’s a wife guy. STANTON: I’m stealing that. But to get to your point. Nobody even questioned his behavior for five seconds. We always knew Buzz had a big heart. DEADLINE: So he’s always been a softie? Was that the idea behind the dynamic? STANTON: At least for Jessie. I think we all know there’s that person who does that to us. I don’t think he’s like that for anyone else, but I do buy Buzz when he kisses Jessie. I loved the role reversal. Jessie just doesn’t seem like the kind who’s going to lift her leg during a kiss, and neither does Buzz, but I do buy Buzz’s foot pop when he kisses Jessie. There was never even a debate that I can remember. We had spent so much time with him, like a best friend, that we thought, “Well, all bets are off on how he’s going to act when Jessie is in the room.” Jessie, I think, has always been the lead in their dancing pair. She’s always known what effect she has on him and has been gracious enough not to rub it in or squander it. She enjoys it. She enjoys playing that flirtatious game. She knows she can get Buzz’s attention and obedience without much effort, and I don’t think she ever abuses it. Toy Story 5 Disney/Pixar DEADLINE: Lastly, when did Taylor Swift come into the picture? Were you involved in those conversations, and did you know where her song would fit into the movie? STANTON: To this day, it’s a pinch-me moment. I can’t believe it happened, and I can’t believe how it happened. We reached out through the proper channels about a year and a half before the movie’s release, not knowing she was deep into her Eras Tour and didn’t have the time. I didn’t even know if word got to her beyond her brother [Austin Swift] at that point. But eventually, Taylor had circled back around to our request, and as her brother tells it, she was excited, saying how much she loved the Toy Story movies. So she saw the movie at a private screening, and we got a FaceTime straight from the theater with her and her brother on the phone, and she said, “I want to do the song.” And we couldn’t believe it. It came together pretty quickly and even involved a FaceTime from Bob Iger, who was standing with Taylor Swift in the studio, telling me the song was great. She had gotten him out of his house and made him drive down to the studio [laughs]. When [“I Knew It, I Knew You”] was placed in the film, and I had heard it, it felt like kismet. It felt like Jessie’s voice. It still blows me away that it happened and that it happened the way it did. articles.title: Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Max Goldbart , Jake Kanter November 5, 2026 6:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand Getty Russell Brand has been found guilty of rape. After two days of deliberations, the jury at London’s Southwark Crown Court delivered a verdict on seven sexual offense charges, finding the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was found not guilty on two other counts of rape and one of attempted indecent assault, which was reduced from indecent assault during the trial. Brand firmly denied all the charges, based on allegations made by six women . The charges and verdicts are detailed below. Related Stories News Russell Brand Trial: Jury Begins Verdict Deliberations News Russell Brand's Defense Argues Channel 4 Film "Poisoned Well Of Justice Deliberately" Judge Mr Justice Bennathan told Brand that he would be given a “custodial sentence of some length,” and he was remanded in custody until sentencing on Monday. A rape conviction can carry a sentence of life in prison in the UK. Watch on Deadline The verdicts were read out to silence in the courtroom after the judge told those present not to react to the jury’s decisions. Deadline has been reporting daily from a live video feed of the courtroom since the trial began around a month ago. It was initially anticipated to take at least six weeks but has taken less than four. Within minutes of the verdicts, BBC News reported that Brand was being investigated over further rape allegations made by two women. The Metropolitan Police said its investigation “remains ongoing.” Outside the Courthouse, the detective superintendent in the case, Andy Furphy, said Brand “used his influence, status and fame to exploit and sexually offend against women.” “As his profile grew, so too did his sense of entitlement.,” he added. “I hope this conviction sends a clear message that no one is above the law, no matter how famous or powerful they may be.” Over the past month, the court has heard from all the accusers, who have a lifelong right to anonymity. Deadline can report, however, that three of the complainants that Brand was found guilty of sexually assaulting worked in the TV and radio industry, including former employees of MTV and Channel 4. All accusers came forward after seeing allegations about Brand in a Channel 4 documentary in 2023 and reading about him in The Times. Brand’s defense argued that this documentary “poisoned the well of justice deliberately” and “fundamentally corrupted” his accusers, while having a “truly devastating effect” on Brand’s life. The prosecution said the exposé was not a “magic force” that caused six separate women to “recast” their memories, but that it had caused them to come forward and tell stories about their encounters with Brand that had “haunted them for years.” The allegations stretched from 1999 to 2009, a period that saw Brand go from being an unknown actor to, in his own words, “staggering fame” after he started dating superstar Katy Perry. Charge 1, Complainant 1: Rape Complainant 1 alleged that she was raped by Russell Brand after meeting him on the fringes of the Labour Party Conference in 1999. C1 invited Brand back to her hotel room and alleged that he pushed her onto the bed and raped her. Brand, who was not famous in 1999, argued that the encounter was consensual. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 2, Complainant 2: Attempted Indecent Assault Complainant 2, a former MTV employee, accused Brand of attempting to pull her into a toilet at the network’s London offices in 2001. During the trial, judge Mr Justice Bennathan reduced the charge from indecent assault to attempted indecent assault because there was “insufficient evidence” to support the original count. Brand’s defense was that he did not recall the incident, but denied that he attempted any non-consensual assault. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 3, Complainant 3: Sexual Assault Complainant 3 alleged that Brand “lunged and squeezed” her breasts within minutes of their first meeting in 2004 while attending the birthday party of a TV producer at London’s Nordic Bar. Brand denied sexually assaulting Complainant 3, who worked at MTV at the time. Verdict : Guilty Charge 4, Complainant 3: Rape Complainant 3 alleged that Brand grabbed her arm and dragged her into the toilets of the Nordic Bar. The woman claimed that Brand climbed onto the toilet seat, exposed himself, forced his penis in her mouth, and ejaculated. In his defense, Brand argued that Complainant 3 willingly accompanied him to the toilet, where they had a “kiss and a cuddle.” He denied orally raping the woman. Verdict : Not guilty Charge 5, Complainant 4: Sexual Assault Complainant 4 alleged that she was sexually assaulted by Brand at a radio station in 2004 or 2005. She claimed that Brand “grabbed” her, pushed her up against a wall, and kissed her “sloppily and aggressively.” Brand denied the incident. Verdict : Guilty Charge 6, Complainant 5: Rape Complainant 5 alleged that she was anally raped by Brand at his London home in 2009 days after meeting him backstage at his stand-up show, where she gave him consensual oral sex. Complainant 5 said they had consensual vaginal sex at his home,efore alleging that Brand turned her on all fours and unexpectedly penetrated her anally, removing his condom. Brand said the anal intercourse was consensual. Verdict : Guilty Charge 7, Complainant 6: Sexual Assault A former Channel 4 employee, Complainant 6 alleged that Brand demanded a massage and put his head into the area of her genitals during a workplace incident in 2009. Brand told the court that he could not recall the incident. articles.title: Final Chapter Of ‘Mass Effect’ Studio BioWare To Be Told In Super Channel Feature Doc From Fennessey Films and Score G Productions
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse JioStar’s Alok Jain On Reality TV Competition, Building Indian Formats & The End Of ‘Koffee With Karan’ ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Propels Sony Pictures To Huge Q2 Profit Boost Bri Lee’s Novel ‘The Work’ Set For TV Adaptation At Dollhouse Pictures View All November 5, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Massive Effect: The Bioware Story' Fennessey Films/Score G Productions EXCLUSIVE: The final days of legendary video games studio BioWare will be told in a doc from Shane Fennessey and Adam Scorgie for Canada ‘s Super Channel . Massive Effect: The BioWare Story will document how the Edmonton, Canada-based games company grew from being founded in 1995 by three medical doctors – Ray Muzyka, Greg Zeschuk and Augustine Yip – to selling 100 million copies of its role-playing games, which include Mass Effect , Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , Dragon Age and Baldur’s Gate . Written and directed by Akash Sherman ( Clara ) and co-produced by Canada’s Fennessey Films and Score G Productions , the film has a unique insight into the story, with filming beginning two years before Electronic Arts announced the closure of BioWare on October 21 last month and continuing to lens throughout. Related Stories News Titan1Studios Adapting Stephen R. Bown's 'The Company: The Rise and Fall Of The Hudson's Bay Empire' As Historical Drama Series News European Production Association CEPI Welcomes Canadian Bodies As First International Members This allowed the filmmakers to capture BioWare’s finale chapter, as the news of the studio’s closure reverberated through the gaming industry. EA decided to shutter studio, which was known for its complex narratives and world building, after recent releases underperformed, and 400 jobs were cut. Watch on Deadline Muzyka, Zeschuk and Yip will feature in the film, along with a plethora of major players from the video game world. These include Douglas Reilly, Vice President of Lucasfilm Games; John Riccitiello, former CEO of Electronic Arts; Casey Hudson, game director of Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic and Mass Effect ; Geoff Keighley, creator of The Game Awards; Victor Lucas, creator of The Electric Playground ; voice actor Jennifer Hale; and longtime BioWare developers Mark Darrah, David Gaider, Drew Karpyshyn, Aaryn Flynn, Mac Walters, Trent Oster, James Ohlen and Caroline Livingstone. “When the production team asked for our blessing to tell the BioWare story, we were honored and deeply moved,” said BioWare co-founders Muzyka and Zeschuk in a statement. “BioWare was never just about the logo or the building. It was about the stories brought to life by the amazing people on our dev teams, and the fans who defended those worlds, championed them and carried them forward. We’re proud this film honors those who made it all possible. The best stories never really end. They live on in our memories and wait for someone to pick them up again.” A website has also been set up for the BioWare community to share photos, videos and how the company touched their lives for the chance to appear in the film. “BioWare’s fans have been part of its journey since the very first game,” said Scorgie. “It’s only right that they help us tell the rest of the story.” “The BioWare founders are my hometown heroes,” added writer and director Sherman. “It’s a privilege and responsibility to share the journey of underdogs who came together to create deeply beloved storytelling. Their golden era kindled a spark in me and in an entire generation. With the studio’s recent closure, the film is now a profound valediction.” Canada’s Super Channel commissioned the doc, which is being planned for a major film festival run and a world premiere next year. Jhod Cardinal of Upstream Flix is handling worldwide sales. The Canada Media Fund supported production. “We are thrilled to bring Massive Effect: The BioWare Story to Canadian audiences,” said Kim Ball, EVP Content & Communications for Super Channel. “As an Edmonton-based company, we’re especially proud to celebrate BioWare’s extraordinary hometown story and the people, creativity and groundbreaking storytelling behind some of the most beloved games of a generation.” Producers Fennessey Films and Score G are behind the likes of Funny Money: The Dane Cook Story , Dolph: Unbreakable , Inmate #1: The Rise of Danny Trejo , Breaking Olympia , Singhs in the Ring and The Great Ones . articles.title: ‘The Bend In The River’ Trailer: In Robb Moss Oscar Contender, Friends Reunite For Possibly Final Journey Down The Colorado
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Russell Brand Found Guilty Of Rape & Sexual Assault Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Meryl Streep On How Fellow Oscar Winner Introduced Her To ‘My Undesirable Friends’ Documentary: “I Was Just Absolutely Entranced’ Magnolia Pictures To Qualify ‘Just Look Up’ For Oscars; Documentary Examines Climate Activist (And Standup Comedian) Michael Greenberg Doc Talk Podcast: Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival’s Ken Jacobson On State Of Nonfiction Filmmaking, Competitive Oscar Race And More View All November 5, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: One of the most acclaimed documentaries of the year – nearly 50 years in the making – arrives on Netflix December 4. The Bend in the River , the Oscar-contending film directed by Robb Moss , marks the culmination of a cinematic project that began in the late 1970s with Riverdogs , which documented a rafting trip that Moss took with his friends down the Colorado River through the Grand Canyon. Those friends were in their 20s at the time, carefree and often clothing-free as they enjoyed life with the vitality and insouciance of youth. Moss documented another rafting trip with those friends in 2003’s The Same River Twice , his chums then in middle age. The new film finds the group rafting again, as river currents and the progress of time draw them closer to old age. Related Stories News Matthew McConaughey In 'The Rivals Of Amziah King'; Green Day-Inspired Road Trip Comedy 'Nimrods' -- Specialty Preview Documentary In 'The Bend In The River,' Friends Head Down The Colorado Again On Cinematic Journey Stretching Back Over 45 Years - Doc Stories Watch the trailer for the film above. Third River Films “The film interweaves moments from the distant past with those of the recent present,” notes a release, “taking viewers back-and-forth through time and inviting personal reflections on the inexorable flow of aging and the unfinished project of living.” In addition to his work as a filmmaker, Moss has taught film at Harvard University for over 30 years. Among his former students: Lance Oppenheim ( You Can See Everything ), two-time Oscar nominee Joshua Oppenheimer, Oscar nominees Yance Ford, RaMell Ross, and multiple Emmy nominee and Sundance Film Festival award winner Lauren Greenfield. Some extraordinary collaborators worked with Moss on The Bend in the River, including producers Lisa Remington (Oscar winner for The Only Girl in the Orchestra ) and Kristin Feeley, director of the Sundance Institute’s Documentary Film and Artist Programs. The film’s executive producers include Oscar winners Frances McDormand and Joel Coen as well as Oscar-winning producers Shane Boris ( Navalny ) and Jeff Reichert ( American Factory ). Moss received the Lifetime Achievement Award at the 2026 Woods Hole Film Festival in Massachusetts. The Bend in the River earned the Artistic Vision Award at the Big Sky Documentary Film Festival in Montana and it won two awards at DOC LA, including Best Documentary and Best Editing, the latter award recognizing the work of Jeff Malmberg. It is set to screen at DOC NYC on November 12 after making that festival’s shortlist of the year’s best feature documentaries (DOC NYC calls it “a masterful meditation on the eternal, the temporal and the inevitable.”). Barry Wasserman stands behind an image of his younger self in ‘The Bend in the River’ Third River Films The Bend in the River screened at the 2025 edition of Doc Stories in San Francisco. At a Q&A there, Moss spoke about his approach to the filmmaking. “It’s not really built out of biography, ‘This happened and that happened,’” Moss said. “People had extraordinary lives, biographically, that aren’t in the film. And it seemed when there were scenes like that that had too much biography, it’s like the film flattened. But the whole thing had to move more… the dynamic of something going downstream. It just had to keep bouncing forward even as it went backwards and forwards. The beginning of the piece had to be very clear what we were up to, that there were going to be multiple timeframes. [But] there’s no saying there’s multiple films, there’s no saying there’s multiple timeframes, there’s no dates, timestamps, there’s no voiceover, there’s no music to cover up cuts.” Watch the trailer for The Bend in the River above. Robert Pattinson is Antinous in ‘The Odyssey’ Universal Pattinson gained industry attention at 19 years of age when he joined the Harry Potter franchise in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and is also known worldwide for The Twilight Saga . For four decades, the prestigious American Cinematheque Award has been designed to recognize extraordinary artists whose talent, vision, and contributions have made a lasting impact on cinema. Their passion and filmography not only exemplify excellence in filmmaking but also reflect the cinematic artistry and breadth of American Cinematheque’s programming, which bridges film history to its future and celebrates the theatrical experience. The award has celebrated an impressive roster of filmmakers and performers, including among others Eddie Murphy, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese, Jodie Foster, Denzel Washington, Nicole Kidman, George Clooney, and last year Michael B. Jordan who received the honor before going on to win the Best Actor Academy Award. The 40th Annual American Cinematheque Award Gala will be executive produced by Rick Nicita of RPMedia, along with Madelyn Hammond and Javier Infante of Hammond Infante Productions. It serves as an annual fundraiser for the non-profit organization, supporting its year-round programming at the Aero Theatre in Santa Monica, Los Feliz 3 Theatre in Los Feliz, and Egyptian Theatre in Hollywood. articles.title: ‘Joy Will Prevail,’ Starring Griffin Dunne as Architect Louis Kahn and Alexis Bledel, Tells the Story of the Director’s Childhood Home (Exclusive PÖFF Trailer)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All November 4, 2026 6:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Joy Will Prevail' Courtesy of PÖFF Louis I. Kahn , just like the buildings he created, is an architectural icon. The Estonian-born American architect, based in Philadelphia, founded his own atelier in 1935. Among his famous, and often monumental and monolithic, buildings are Bangladesh’s Jatiyo Sangsad Bhaban, or National Assembly Building, the Kimbell Art Museum in Fort Worth, Texas and the Salk Institute for Biological Studies in La Jolla, California. Now, the final three years of his life and work get the big-screen treatment in Joy Will Prevail , directed by Max Korman, the grandson of Steve Korman, who, as the biographical drama shows, commissioned a house from the celebrated architect outside Philadelphia. The Korman House became the final residential building designed by Kahn. It was completed shortly before his unexpected death in 1974, and it became the director’s childhood home. Related Stories Movies 'La Bola Negra' Wins Another Prize -- London Film Festival's Audience Award Movies Tinie Tempah, Nathalie Emmanuel, Russell Tovey Set for HollyShorts U.K. Honors (Exclusive) Max Korman’s feature debut tells the story of the creation of Kahn’s final residential commission and his unlikely friendship with Steve Korman, painting a portrait of the architect and his legacy. The film also touches on how Kahn quietly navigated a complex personal life as the father of children with three different women. After its recent world premiere at the Philadelphia Film Festival, Joy Will Prevail , appropriately, gets its international premiere in Estonia, at the 30th edition of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival ( PÖFF ), on Saturday, Nov. 7. Griffin Dunne ( The French Dispatch , After Hours , An American Werewolf in London ) stars as Louis I. Kahn, with Jennifer Beals ( The L Word , NCIS: New York , Flashdance ) and Alexis Bledel ( The Handmaid’s Tale , Gilmore Girls ) adding further star power. Ben Rosenfield portrays Steve Korman, with Molly Ephraim also part of the ensemble cast. Joshua Echevarria was the cinematographer, with editing handled by Sarah Flack. J. Andrew Greenblatt, Max Korman, Derek Dienner and Alex Peace-Power are the producers on Joy Will Prevail , with co-producers Anthony Faure, Christopher Rivera and Grace Wagner. Kahn, born in Kuressaare on the Estonian island of Saaremaa, and the story of his final years return to the country where his life began this weekend. After the Saturday PÖFF premiere in the presence of Dunne and director Korman, the film team will visit Kuressaare for a special Sunday screening of Joy Will Prevail . Their visit to Estonia is organized in cooperation with the Louis Kahn Estonia Foundation. THR can now exclusively premiere a trailer for the film. It provides a first appetizer for the biographical and cinematic journey that is Joy Will Prevail . Watch the teaser with Dunne, Beals, Bledel and more right here. THR

articles.title: Meta Hires Rich Latour to Lead In-House Content Studio (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 6:39am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rich Latour Courtesy of Subject Meta has hired a TV veteran to lead its in-house content studio. The tech giant and owner of Instagram and Facebook has brought on Rich Latour to be VP of content studio, running its social and content teams within the company’s communications and public affairs division. Latour will report to Tucker Bounds, the company’s head of communications and public affairs, and will be responsible for developing and executing Meta’s content strategy. That will include brand storytelling, focused on the Meta brand and the impact it has on communities; executive social, amplifying brand-level messages through the voices of the company’s top execs; product content support, with a particular emphasis on social; and international social content. Latour joins Meta from BlackRock, where he was managing director, global head of content, creative and events, where he led the investment firm’s global content strategy. Before BlackRock he worked at Goldman Sachs as its VP of digital content. He spent nearly two decades at NBC News, much of it as a producer and senior producer at NBC Nightly News , where he received 4 Emmy Awards and 2 Edward R. Murrow Awards. While Meta’s revenues and profits are still focused within products like Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp, Latour joins the as the tech giant is leaning into AI via its Muse agent, and into virtual and augmented reality via its glasses and headsets. While the content studio is outward-facing (it’s about telling Meta’s story), content is poised to become a bigger part of the company’s portfolio. THR

articles.title: Thaddea Graham to Be Honored at the Oscar Wilde Awards (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Thaddea Graham Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images for US-Ireland Alliance Thaddea Graham, the actress from Northern Ireland known for her turns on Sex Education at Netflix and Bad Sisters and Margo’s Got Money Troubles at Apple TV, will be honored at the 21st annual Oscar Wilde Awards . Organized by the US-Ireland Alliance, the event is set for March 11 at the Ebell in Los Angeles in its traditional evening spot three days before the Academy Awards. It celebrates the work of those who are Irish — and some who are not — who contribute to film, television and music. Irish American actor Jack Reynor was announced last month as an honoree. Guests also will be treated to a performance by the Irish synth-pop singer Shobsy. Related Stories Movies 'Joy Will Prevail,' Starring Griffin Dunne as Architect Louis Kahn and Alexis Bledel, Tells the Story of the Director's Childhood Home (Exclusive PÖFF Trailer) Movies 'La Bola Negra' Wins Another Prize -- London Film Festival's Audience Award Graham, 29, will receive the Wilde Card Award, “which is presented to someone we expect you’ll hear a lot more from,” US-Ireland Alliance president Trina Vargo said. Previous honorees include Saoirse Ronan, Barry Keoghan, Sarah Bolger and Bad Sisters actress Eve Hewson. Graham last year appeared alongside Julia Roberts, Ayo Edebiri, Andrew Garfield and Michael Stuhlbarg in Luca Guadagnino’s After the Hunt , and she has reunited with the Italian director on the upcoming hot-button film Artificial , which stars Garfield as OpenAI CEO Sam Altman. She also played the personal assistant of George Clooney’s actor character in Noah Baumbach’s Jay Kelly (2025). Graham was discovered as a baby on the steps of a building in Changsha, China, when she was a few days old. She was adopted at 13 months and brought by her parents to County Down as one of the first Chinese-born children adopted in Northern Ireland. “I always say I would not be here had it not been for the kindness of strangers,” she told The London Times in April. “From the earliest days of someone stopping and seeing I’d been left, picking me up and looking after me, I’ve seen that kindness throughout my life, from my parents, who are wonderful, through school and the support of my teachers. My primary-school teacher introduced a Chinese New Year celebration, which she continues even though I’m not there anymore.” In 2021, Graham portrayed the head of Sherlock Holmes’ band of street urchins on Netflix’s The Irregulars and recurred on the BBC’s Doctor Who . After playing the therapist O in 2023 on the final season of Sex Education , she sparkled as the stubborn detective Una Houlihan on the second season of Bad Sisters in 2024 and as the roommate of Elle Fanning’s character this year on Margo’s Got Money Troubles . After an FYC Emmy event last year for Bad Sisters , Graham told the Times that she “had a lot of people coming up to me from Asian backgrounds saying, ‘It’s amazing seeing you in this show. It’s amazing seeing you as one of the lead characters. We so admire the kind of representation people are taking over there. And also for you to have a different accent — for you not to have the accent people might expect.’” Shobsy last year completed a U.K. and European tour with SO Recordings labelmates MY BABY, then took the stage at SXSW. In July, he performed at an Irish music industry showcase hosted by Ireland’s president, Catherine Connolly, at her Dublin residence, and he recently released the EP The World Will Not Remember alongside a new single, “Perfect.” Shobsy Courtesy US-Ireland Alliance THR

articles.title: Trump Crashes Out After Democrats Flip House and Senate, Slams Fox News and Texas’ Greg Abbott
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 7:33am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Donald Trump Alex Wong/Getty Images After Democrats flipped the U.S. House and Senate on Tuesday night, it’s safe to say President Donald Trump wasn’t too thrilled. Hours after the polls closed and it was revealed that Democrats won some surprising races in the 2026 midterms, including for the Texas, South Carolina and North Carolina Senate, Trump took to Truth Social hours after the polls closed with several posts, slamming Fox News and Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott, who lost re-election to Democrat Gina Hinojosa . “If Greg Abbott, the Governor of Texas, hadn’t become a RINO in the last six months of his Political Life, he wouldn’t have lost,” he wrote in one post. “He went back to his original formula, and it wasn’t pretty!” Related Stories News Elon Musk Responds After His Record $474 Million Bet on Republicans Ends in Blowout Midterms 2026 Hollywood Sat Out the Billionaire-Tax Fight. Its Workers Could Pay the Price. Trump added in another, “Why does FoxNews have Bill de Blasio, the Worst Mayor in the History of New York City, on air, ranting and raving like a Lunatic? He left the City in disgrace, and the damage he caused was incalculable — It has never been the same, and now he’s telling us how to run America. FoxNews bears responsibility for these losses by constantly and consistently putting on the Dumocrat opposition, and worse. GOD BLESS AMERICA!” Along with posting a photo of his signature red caps, with the word “VETO” displayed on it, he also wrote , “I’m going to become a Political Pundit, both good and bad, on the reasons these Candidates won and lost!” Earlier in the evening, as it started to become clear that it was going to be a big night for Democrats, Trump initially claimed that he would have won in a landslide if his name was on the ballot. “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE! Thank you for your attention to this matter,” he wrote on Truth Social. However, Trump wasn’t eligible to be on the 2026 ballot as he’s currently the sitting president of the United States. He also can’t run again in 2028, as the 22nd Amendment of the U.S. Constitution limits any person to being elected to the presidency twice, and Trump was already elected in 2016 and 2024. While Trump appears furious at the midterm results, he also told The New York Times shortly before 10:30 p.m. on Tuesday that he’s “absolutely willing to accept” them. The president added to the Times , “We’ll work with the Democrats, and we’ll, you know, look forward to working with them. We’ll probably work something out.” THR

articles.title: What Abdul El-Sayed’s Wild, Historic Ride to the Senate Means to One Michigander
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Mikey O'Connell Plus Icon Mikey O'Connell Senior Entertainment Editor View All November 4, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dr. Abdul El-Sayed Salwan Georges/Getty Images I’m just a Great Lakes boy, standing in front of his home state, asking for some clarity. And, perhaps, I’m a little closer to getting some. Dr. Abdul El-Sayed , the Michigan native fond of exercising the right to bare (his impressive) arms , has just won my home state’s messy Senate race by six points. This is a boon to Democrats’ legislative goals — and to my own mental health. Because, in an admittedly myopic move, I decided early on that he would be the one candidate to whom I’d pin all of my 2026 hopes. Not just because he’s a litmus test for non-coastal Americans’ appetite for progressive politics. Because I deeply needed to know if my complicated home state was capable of electing a loud, liberal, practicing Muslim to such a high office. Related Stories News Trump Crashes Out After Democrats Flip House and Senate, Slams Fox News and Texas' Greg Abbott News Elon Musk Responds After His Record $474 Million Bet on Republicans Ends in Blowout My doubts were not without merit. I spent my adolescence in deep red Livingston County, in a smallish town with exceptional public schools and a storybook Main Street that now has shops that sport trans pride flags in their widows and hosts an annual and very well-attended Gilmore Girls festival. Last December, mid-Hanukkah, that same Main Street was bombarded with white supremacists carrying signs that read “Happy Holidays, Heil Hitler” while reportedly spicing up their antisemitic campaign by calling passing holiday shoppers the n-word and the f-slur. Mike Rogers, El-Sayed’s MAGA-endorsed opponent, grew up in Livingston County as well. And he represented our town during his years in the Michigan State Senate before going on to represent those same constituents in the House of Representatives. My dad couldn’t stand him. Still can’t. And I vividly recall rolling my eyes under the brim of my marching band hat (it’s called a Shako!), whenever I had to watch Rogers gladhand the town’s Republican majority at football games as he made his leap to national politics. What I wouldn’t learn for another 25 years is that El-Sayed’s grandparents were helping to raise Abdul just a few miles away. Because Livingston County is also home to Jan and Judy Johnson, the newly famous TV stars whose series of campaign spots for their grandson epitomize the kind of Michiganders who I know and come from. OK, that was arguably too much color about one random cluster of towns an hour’s drive west of Detroit. But if this much paradox can exist within this 15-mile radius, how can anything but an election like the one we’ve just had tell me where the majority of people’s heads and hearts are at? Because I didn’t grow up in the only culturally bipolar part of Michigan or any other state. This country is a real trip, and most of us realized that before 2016. I’m back in Michigan a lot, just last week in fact, but I haven’t voted there for almost 20 years. Another thing I have in common with Mike Rogers is that I spend most of my time in another place. California, for me. And watching so much of this race from afar has been a tough hang. El-Sayed regularly had to endure a gun-toting pardoned Jan. 6 insurrectionist crashing his rallies. He had to navigate his proximity to the national sideshow that is Hasan Piker. His campaign was wildly outspent by the Rogers one, which blanketed the airwaves with some exceptionally racist content. And, on the eve of the election, El-Sayed’s primary opponent, Haley Stevens, distracted from the conversation with her left-field endorsement of Rogers that may have ejected her from the Democratic party and possibly a political career. If it isn’t clear by this point, I am aligned with El-Sayed on many issues. I made a few modest donations to his campaign. I’ve been wearing a baseball cap with his name on it most weekends since before the primary. I sent his spoof of the So You Think You Can Leave sketch to everyone I’ve ever met. But, for me, I didn’t really need to know if Michigan was ready to go full liberal. I just wanted some assurance, in this grotesque circus of a race, that the majority of those in the complex and diverse place that I still consider home could recognize what I believe to be a good man in some slightly different packaging. Everybody likes to invoke the whole “As [insert state here] goes, so goes the nation” thing. Wow, humble much? If that was ever even true on an electoral level, I don’t believe it is any longer. But it can be on a personal one. Because as Michigan goes, so goes my optimism for America’s future. And today, I feel a little bit better on that front. This is part of The Hollywood Reporter’s ongoing midterm coverage. You can check out all of our pieces here . THR

articles.title: AFM Hot Project: Daisy Ridley, Sosie Bacon, Simon Rex Join ‘Get Rid of It’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L to R): Simon Rex, Daisy Ridley, Sosie Bacon Matt Licari, Gita Bass, Leon Bennett Daisy Ridley , Sosie Bacon and Simon Rex are set to star in Get Rid of It , a horror project that Ry Russo-Young will direct from a script by Gemma Holdway. Production is scheduled to begin at the start of the first quarter of 2027. Ridley will play Harper, who discovers she is pregnant after a one-night stand with a drifter named Miller, played by Rex. Bacon will play Harper’s sister, Jessie. The sisters set out on a cross-country road trip and find themselves fighting for survival when they learn that what is growing inside Harper may not be human. Related Stories TV Thaddea Graham to Be Honored at the Oscar Wilde Awards (Exclusive) Movies 'Joy Will Prevail,' Starring Griffin Dunne as Architect Louis Kahn and Alexis Bledel, Tells the Story of the Director's Childhood Home (Exclusive PÖFF Trailer) Ridley will next be seen in Ti West’s Ebenezer , opposite Johnny Depp. Her earlier credits include Zak Hilditch’s We Bury the Dead , Joachim Ronning’s Young Woman and the Sea and the role of Rey in the most recent Star Wars trilogy. Bacon currently stars opposite Nicole Kidman and Jamie Lee Curtis in Elizabeth Sarnoff’s series Scarpetta. She recently appeared in the SXSW title Family Movie alongside Kevin Bacon, Kyra Sedgwick and Travis Bacon. Her earlier work includes Parker Finn’s Smile and Brad Ingelsby’s series Mare of Easttown. Rex played Mikey in Sean Baker’s Red Rocket . He has also starred in Nic Pizzolatto’s Easy’s Waltz and Zoë Kravitz’s Blink Twice . “This project’s strength is its compelling point of view and heart beneath the horror,” Russo-Young said. “I’m thrilled to bring it to life with such an extraordinary and gifted group of collaborators.” Russo-Young previously directed the sci-fi teen thriller Before I Fall , starring Zoey Deutch, and the drama The Sun Is Also a Star , with Charles Melton. She has also directed episodes of the Apple TV+ series Shrinking, which stars Harrison Ford and Jason Segel. David Lancaster, whose producing credits include Whiplash , Nightcrawler and Drive , is producing. Upgrade, CAA Media Finance and Range Select are handling sales and will present the project to buyers at the fall market. THR

articles.title: Toni Collette to Lead Apple TV Dramedy ‘Lenni’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 8:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Toni Collette Christian Hogstedt Logo text Apple TV ‘s latest series is going to opposite ends of the Earth for its inspiration and physical location. The streamer has picked up a dramedy called Lenni , with Toni Collette playing the title character. The series is based on a critically acclaimed Norwegian show, Pernille , and has started production in Australia, almost literally the other side of the world. In Lenni , Emmy winner Collette ( United States of Tara, Wayward ) will play a child welfare worker and divorced mother of two kids who “spends her days fighting for other people’s families while her own is in a constant state of hilarious chaos,” the logline reads. “The season follows Lenni through a new case, where the stakes couldn’t be higher as her work and personal life collides.” Related Stories TV 'Monarch: Legacy of Monsters' Eyes Season 3 Shakeup -- If It's Renewed Movies Ted McGinley Tapped to Narrate Volleyball Documentary 'Kings of the Beach' The cast also includes Ciarán Hinds, Dan Wyllie, Josh McKenzie, Celeste Barber, Genevieve Hegney, Arka Das and Wayne Blair. Made Up Stories and Keshet International are producing Lenni . Sarah Scheller ( Strife, The Letdown ) is adapting the Norwegian series, and Dearbhla Walsh ( Margo’s Got Money Troubles, Bad Sisters ) is directing. They executive produce with Bruna Papandrea, Steve Hutensky and Katie Amos of Made Up Stories, Avi Nir and Keren Shahar of Keshet International, and Collette. Also exec producing are Pernille creator Henriette Steenstrup, Bård Fjulsrud and Tanya Badendyck. Collette starred in Mae Martin’s Wayward on Netflix last year. Her other recent series credits include The Power at Prime Video, The Staircase at HBO Max and Pieces of Her at Netflix. She is repped by CAA, United Management, Finley Management and Jackoway Austen. THR

articles.title: NBCUniversal Invests in India Microdrama Producer in $80 Million Fundraising Round
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All November 4, 2026 8:21am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EloElo Group operates microdramas app Story TV. EloElo Group NBCUniversal and Hornbill Capital have led an $80 million Series C fundraising round for Indian microdrama producer EloElo Group, founded by former Flipkart executive Saurabh Pandey. The new capital will allow the Story TV platform operator to produce new vertical dramas for export internationally, including to the U.S. market. The Series C investment, usually done to allow startups to scale operations, follows NBCUniversal’s Peacock streaming platform launching the unscripted vertical series, Campus Confidential: Miami , as part of a wider push into mobile content to reach new audiences. “At NBCUniversal, we see significant opportunity in mobile-first storytelling and emerging formats like micro dramas to engage audiences and meet evolving viewing habits. Under Saurabh’s leadership, EloElo has developed a differentiated, mobile-first approach with a clear focus on content and storytelling, positioning the company for long-term success. We’re excited to bring NBCUniversal’s global capabilities to the partnership as EloElo expands beyond India, including into the U.S. market,” Deepak Arya, executive vp of corporate strategy & development at NBCUniversal, said in a statement. EloElo Group, which launched in Bengaluru, India in 2020, points to an expanding slate of over 5000 micro dramas in six languages, while a Dolphin AI agentic production engine. Across its apps, EloElo Group added it has over 40 million monthly active users. “This Series C deepens our content across languages, with a sharper focus on premium originals, doubles down on Dolphin AI, and takes what we have built to more audiences and more markets,” Pandey, founder and CEO of EloElo Group, said in his own statement. Microdramas, which are typically produced in 60-90 second episodes and strategically written with a hook, a spike and a cliff hanger to get viewers onto the next episode, have caught on in North America and elsewhere internationally after coming out of China during the pandemic era.
