articles.title: Tinto Brass, Director of the X-Rated ‘Caligula,’ Dies at 93
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All November 4, 2026 8:38am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tinto Brass Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images Tinto Brass, the Italian director best known for helming the X-rated Roman Empire epic Caligula , starring Malcolm McDowell, died Wednesday in Rome, his family announced. He was 93. Brass started out in the 1960s with avant-garde films before he pivoted to erotic cinema, with his other features in the genre including Salon Kitty (1976), The Key (1983), Paprika (1991), All Ladies Do It (1992), Frivolous Lola (1998) and Cheeky (2000). McDowell starred in the title role as the sexually deranged emperor in Caligula (1979), written by Gore Vidal and produced by Penthouse magazine founder Bob Guccione. The film, also featuring Helen Mirren, Peter O’Toole , John Gielgud and lots of orgies, was slammed by critics and audiences after its original release. Related Stories Oscars 2027: Int'l Films in Focus 'Ulya' Director Dives Into His Third Latvian Oscar Contender, Which Stars a Rising Actor as a Female Basketball Legend and Became a "Blockbuster" Movies BAFTA Breakthrough Ted Evans Shares What Sign Language Taught Him About Film - and What's Next After 'Retreat' Brass and Vidal clashed during production and would disown the feature — the director was unhappy with the editing (done after he was fired), the screenwriter with how Brass rewrote his script. Caligula , however, gained a cult following over the decades, and a 178-minute “ultimate cut” version received a showcase at Cannes in 2023. Born in Milan on March 26, 1933, and raised in Venice, Giovanni Brass earned a law degree, worked as an archivist at the Cinémathèque Française in Paris and served as an assistant director to Roberto Rossellini and Alberto Cavalcanti. He made his feature directorial debut on Who Works Is Lost , which screened at the 1963 Venice International Film Festival, then helmed Yankee (1966), a Western, and the murder mystery I Am What I Am (1967), starring Jean-Louis Trintignant . (The last one received a 4K restoration and a screening at Venice in September.) In 1970s, he won the Golden Bear at the Berlin International Film Festival for his surrealist comedy The Howl , which he also wrote. Survivors include his second wife, Caterina, whom he married in 2017, and his children, Bonifacio and Beatrice. His first wife was Carla Cipriani; he was married to the daughter of Harry’s Bar founder Giuseppe Cipriani from 1957 until her death in 2006. THR

articles.title: Stocks Rally Higher After Democrats Flip Congress
articles.full_text: × Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Nov 4, 2026 7:01am PT Stocks Rally Higher After Democrats Flip Congress By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Former OnlyFans Star Camilla Araújo Sets ‘Plot Twist’ Podcast Launch in New Expansion Into Long-Form Entertainment 46 minutes ago Stocks Rally Higher After Democrats Flip Congress 2 hours ago Democrats Win House and Senate in Sweeping Rout of GOP 12 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Wall Street cheered the Blue Wave that put Democrats in control of both the Senate and House , with major market indexes and media stocks posting gains Wednesday morning after the midterm elections . The Dow Jones Industrial Average soared over 1,100 points in early trading, up 2.2%, to nearly 53,000, while the Nasdaq Composite index was up 2.4%. Analysts said the Democrats’ sweeping congressional win cleared away political uncertainty — and investors were bullish on the likely gridlock in D.C. keeping policies unchanged. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' “Still more uncertainty looms, but one thing is certain, there will be gridlock and historically this is good for the market,” Jay Woods, chief market strategist at Freedom Capital Markets, told CNBC . Woods said the market uptick also partly stemmed from President Donald Trump’s “initial tone and reaction to the results,” after Trump told the New York Times he would accept the midterm election results . As of Wednesday morning, Democrats held a 54-44 edge in the Senate over Republicans, with two races (in Mississippi and Alaska) yet to be called, according to the AP . In the House, Dems had secured 228 seats — giving the party a clear majority — and the GOP stood at 139, with outcomes in 68 races still undetermined. Media stocks that gained in early trading the morning after the midterms included Netflix (+4%), Comcast (+4%), Disney (+3.8%), Skydance (+2.8%) and Fox Corp. (+2.4%). Big tech stocks — despite analysts warning that Democratic majorities in Congress could create headwinds for AI data center buildouts — also rose: Apple (+6%) Amazon (7.6%), Alphabet (+4.9%) and Meta (+2.4%) all were trending higher. Opposition to massive data center projects became a key issue in the midterms. While some Democratic efforts to curb data center buildouts may be realized, “Our base case is that the data centers are going to be built and delays are already part of life for construction projects,” Jonathan Pingle, chief U.S. economist for UBS, said in a Nov. 4 research note on the elections. “We expect that it may be difficult to come to agreement at the federal level to meaningfully restrain the data center buildout and heavily regulate AI, in particular since the White House has been opposed to doing so.” Not all stocks got a boost. Shares of Elon Musk’s SpaceX were down 1.3% in morning trading and Tesla’s stock was off -2.4%. Musk, the world’s wealthiest individual, spent at least $474 million backing Republican candidates, per CNBC , including $224 million toward the campaign of Texas attorney general Ken Paxton in the contest for the open Senate seat in Texas — which Democrat James Talarico won by a 12-point margin. Voters in Texas also elected Democratic contender Gina Hinojosa governor, who unseated incumbent GOP Gov. Greg Abbott. “Guess my election-interfering space lasers didn’t work this time,” Musk posted on X late Tuesday night, followed by a shrug emoji. Also falling post-election were shares of Trump Media & Technology Group, the operator of Truth Social (Trump’s primary social media platform). TMTG stock was trading down more than 10% in Wednesday morning trading, pushing its market cap under $1.5 billion. The Trump family trust owns 41% of Trump Media, Reuters reported last month. ‘Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Trailer: The Wilderness Survivors Return Home Loading comments...

articles.title: Paris Creator Week Aims to Become the Cannes of the Creator Economy as New Study Forecasts $1.2 Trillion Global Market
articles.full_text: × Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Nov 4, 2026 7:26am PT Paris Creator Week Aims to Become the Cannes of the Creator Economy as New Study Forecasts $1.2 Trillion Global Market A study unveiled today at the event revealed that the global creator economy is on track to reach $217.3 billion in 2026, with France emerging as major hub. By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest Paris Creator Week Aims to Become the Cannes of the Creator Economy as New Study Forecasts $1.2 Trillion Global Market 1 hour ago Dominic West, John Cleese, Portia de Rossi Join Jeff Daniels in Trudie Styler’s Comedy ‘The Reception’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago Cannes Chief Thierry Fremaux Hails French Film Model as CNC Head Gaëtan Bruel Vows to Fight for Its Future at 80th Anniversary 6 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Marc Lesage-Moretti Paris Creator Week is doubling in size this year, drawing 8,000 industry professionals and top executives from YouTube, Twitch, LinkedIn and traditional media giants including Banijay and Mediawan. The gathering kicks off today at the Halle de la Villette where a new study is being unveiled, revealing that the global creator economy is on track to reach $217.3 billion in 2026, marking a 26.2% year-on-year increase. The market, which has nearly tripled in size over the last five years, is projected to reach a staggering $1.22 trillion by 2033. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' France has emerged as a major international hub for the booming creator economy which will reach $10.1 billion locally this year, up 23.7% from 2025. It could more than double to $24.3 billion by 2030, per the study. That makes France the world’s seventh-largest creator economy and the third-largest in Europe, behind the U.K. and Germany. The sector already accounts for 227,000 full-time equivalent jobs in France. Marc Lesage-Moretti, a former Goldman Sachs vice president turned content creator, known online as Jokariz, who co-founded Paris Creator Week in 2024, says the findings underscore a dramatic shift in an industry which took time to be taken seriously. “In the United States, everyone was talking about the creator economy, but when I started using that term in France three years ago, people looked at me as though I was speaking Chinese to them,” Lesage-Moretti tells Variety in a zoom interview a few days before the start of the event. “They would say, ‘Oh, the creator economy? You mean 14-year-old kids making entertainment videos in their bedrooms on YouTube?’” “People hadn’t yet understood how much this industry was becoming professionalized,” he says, citing HugoDécrypte, the popular French digital news outlet, which now employs around 40 people, including journalists and human resources staff. The huge expansion of the Paris Creator Week this year underscores how the general perception has evolved. It’s grown from 4,000 participants last year to an expected 8,000 this year, while its exhibition space has increased fivefold, from 200 to 1,000 square meters. YouTube alone is taking a 100-square-meter stand, Lesage-Moretti points out. The event is also becoming increasingly international, with overseas attendees accounting for 30% of participants. Global platforms including YouTube, Twitch, LinkedIn, Spotify and SoundCloud are sending senior executives, while traditional entertainment groups are joining discussions about the future of content creation, distribution and monetization. “The idea is to create the VivaTech of the creator economy,” says Lesage-Moretti, referring to the major Paris technology conference. Unlike consumer-facing creator conventions, Paris Creator Week is positioning itself as a B2B gathering where creators, media execs, platforms, brands, agencies and investors can explore partnerships and new business models. The event’s growing appeal also reflects a major shift in advertising spending. According to the study, sponsorships and commercial partnerships now account for 49.8% of the global creator economy, followed by advertising on creator content at 22.7% and paid subscriptions at 13.8%. Advertisers are expected to contribute $172.8 billion to the sector in 2026, representing 79.5% of total spending, while creators themselves receive an estimated $92.6 billion, or 42.6% of the overall market. “Commercial partnerships are the main driver of growth,” Lesage says. “Brands that traditionally invested their money in other media or advertising channels are redirecting those budgets toward content creators.” “And we’re not just talking about luxury brands. We’re talking about every kind of brand: banks, major corporations, large businesses. We have major companies that now handle their financial communications through content creators,” Lesage says, adding that the money from these partnerships goes directly from a company to a content creator without the platform taking a single euro.” The industry’s rapid expansion is also fueling a wave of M&A’s. According to the Paris Creator Week study, 70 acquisitions took place globally in the first half of 2026, up 23% from the same period last year. North America accounted for 64.3% of acquisition targets, compared with 27.1% for Europe. Paris Creator Week is dedicating an entire conference track to M&A, looking at how investors value creator-led businesses and manage the “key man risk,” when companies are built around a single personality. Lesage says some businesses closely tied to their founders have managed to attract investment. For instance, the French podcast company Legend which lured a Belgian fund at a valuation of €72 million. “These are businesses that people thought couldn’t be sold because they were too dependent on a single personality, but we’re seeing that’s not necessarily the case,” he says. For Drew Baldwin, head of Prentiss Media, founder of Tubefilter and creator of the Streamy Awards, the next stage of growth will depend on whether creators can evolve from individual personalities into scalable media businesses. “I still think creators on social platforms, including YouTube, are renting audiences. They don’t own the audience,” Baldwin tells Variety . “And the creators who can figure out how to take their audience and own that relationship are the ones who are going to be able to build new businesses around that community.” Baldwin, who is leading a session comparing the European and American creator economies at the Paris confab, argues France is well positioned to see its local creator economy thrive, even if it’s currently lagging behind the U.S. “France has always been, culturally, a champion of independent voices,” he says. “French cinema has an outsized footprint considering the size of the country. You have the Cannes Film Festival. You have an extraordinary amount of production coming out of France.” “Now, the question is: Will they champion the entrepreneurial spirit? And I think the answer, when I look at Paris Creator Week, is yes.” Baldwin says the U.S. has been ahead of the curve because it’s got a “common language and a more unified advertising market that make it easier to scale businesses.” As in the film and television business, Baldwin anticipates some consolidation in the digital space as creators compete for budgets traditionally reserved for media companies. “Like with any maturation in the economy, there will be consolidation. There will be winners, and there will be those that close shop,” he says. The major challenge is to overcome the key man risk, says Baldwin, who points to MrBeast, Dhar Mann and the British creator collective the Sidemen as examples of creators building businesses capable of expanding beyond their original social media audiences. “Those who can scale, like the Sidemen, WatchTime Studios and Dhar Mann, are the ones who are going to be able to do large-scale media deals,” he says. “Instead of just using creator marketing budgets, they can unlock true media budgets, which are really big.” That convergence is starting to happen even in heavily regulated markets like France, where major production groups including Banijay and Mediawan are exploring opportunities in the creator economy alongside streaming platforms and broadcasters such as TF1, Netflix and Canal+. “Creators are increasingly interested in working with distributors and platforms beyond the ones where they originally built their audiences,” says Lesage-Moretti. “If you’re a YouTuber, it makes sense to be present across social media platforms to diversify, but it also makes sense to explore cinema.” Lesage-Moretti cites the landmark experiment of French YouTuber Inoxtag, whose documentary “Kaizen” was released by MK2 French theaters and sold around 300,000 tickets in a single day. It launched on the same day on YouTube where it generated 40 million or 50 million views overall. Baldwin is also using Paris Creator Week to formally launch Creator Kitchen, an initiative aimed at bringing together executives from traditional and new media. The Paris edition will include an intimate dinner at L’Envol, Michelin-starred chef Thibaut Spiwack’s rooftop restaurant at the Philharmonie de Paris, near the event’s venue. Guests include Twitch CEO Dan Clancy; Justine Ryst, managing director of YouTube France and Southern Europe; Gregg Bywalski, managing director of Webedia Creators; Vincent Grynbaum, managing director of Mediawan Thematics; Nielsen CFO Jessica Holscott; and Mathieu Gallet, managing director of Bourdin Media and chairman of the supervisory board of Les Echos. For Baldwin, the growing appetite for an industry-focused gathering like Paris Creators Week illustrates that the industry is becoming a fully fledged part of the entertainment biz. “Why are thousands of people coming to this? It’s not a fan event. This is the business of the creator economy,” he says. Lesage-Moretti, who is still financing the event with co-founder and managing director Pierre Alary, says they’ve received outside interest but want to keep control. “The real question is what advantage an outside investor would bring us? We have a very clear roadmap and strategy for how we’re going to accelerate our international expansion,” he says. “France has always been able to attract people from all over the world to Cannes for the film festival. We think the same thing should happen in the creator economy.” ‘Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Trailer: The Wilderness Survivors Return Home Loading comments...

articles.title: Thomasin McKenzie, Finn Cole and Antony Starr to Lead ‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest,’ Logical and Protagonist Launching at AFM (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: × Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Nov 4, 2026 7:30am PT Thomasin McKenzie, Finn Cole and Antony Starr to Lead ‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest,’ Logical and Protagonist Launching at AFM (EXCLUSIVE) By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Thomasin McKenzie, Finn Cole and Antony Starr to Lead ‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest,’ Logical and Protagonist Launching at AFM (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Quentin Tarantino Thought He Was ‘Letting Down’ Brad Pitt by Not Directing Cliff Booth Sequel: ‘I Felt Bad About That’ 7 hours ago Jason Statham and Guy Ritchie Reunite — Again — for Netflix Revenge Action Movie ‘Dogfight’ 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Credit: Ben Sarikaya, Getty, Getty The legend of Robin Hood is set to be given a new retelling in “The Lie of Sherwood Forest,” launching at the upcoming AFM with Logical Pictures International and Protagonist Pictures handling sales. The film — coming from German production company augenschein and beginning production on Nov. 9 — is being directed by Patrick Vollrath (“7500,” “Subversion”) and will star Thomasin McKenzie (“The Testament of Ann Lee”), Finn Cole (“Peaky Blinders,” “Last Breath”) and Antony Starr (“The Boys,” “The Covenant”). Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' Smylie Bradwell (“Faith,” “Hamnet”), Brian Vernel (“The Odyssey,” “Slow Horses”) and Richard Durden (“Star Wars: Episode IX – The Rise of Skywalker”) are also among the cast. Harris Kauffman wrote the screenplay, based on a story by Joachim Hedén and Patrick Vollrath. According to the description, “The Lie of Sherwood Forest” transforms the “familiar folklore into a “grounded, hard-hitting fight for survival, loyalty and justice, bringing a contemporary edge to one of storytelling’s most enduring figures.” The story sees Robin Hood and his companions deceived by a young woman into undertaking a daring mission to rescue her captured brother, an operation that spirals into a perilous heist. As loyalties fracture and hidden motives emerge, the outlaws must confront the true cost of their choices — and the price of challenging those in power. As per the synopsis: “But what begins as one desperate lie will inadvertently change the course of the legend forever.” “‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest’ is a radical new take of one of the world’s most enduring legends, reinvented as a bold, visceral and relentlessly propulsive film,” said Dave Bishop, CEO of Protagonist Pictures. “Patrick Vollrath will deliver an electrifying cinematic vision to a story that turns mythology on its head, combining gripping set pieces with genuine moral complexity.” Added Andrei Kamarowsky, head of international at Logical Pictures Group: “What immediately drew us to ‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest’ was the ingenuity and novelty of its premise: one young woman’s desperate deception sets Robin Hood and his outlaws on a dangerous journey that will ultimately reshape the myth. It remains true to the spirit of the original folklore while bringing a fresh perspective, real emotional stakes, and unrelenting tension.” The film is produced by augenschein’s Maximilian Leo, Jonas Katzenstein and Daniel Sonnabend, in co-production with ZDF and with funding support by Film- und Medienstiftung NRW, German Federal Film Fund (DFFF), German Federal Film Board (FFA), German Films, European Investment Fund and Creative Europe Media. “Our collaboration with Patrick on 7500 was a defining moment for augenschein, and we’ve been excited to find the right opportunity to work together again.” said Katzenstein. “Having developed the idea with Patrick, we’re thrilled to partner once more on this action thriller.” Added company partner Leo: “The film builds on the edge-of-your-seat tension and visceral, grounded action that defined 7500, taking those elements to an exciting new level within the world of Robin Hood.” Augenschein and Logical Pictures Group will finance, and the group’s sales subsidiary Logical Pictures International LPI will co-rep sales alongside Protagonist Pictures. Protagonist’s Bishop, George Hamilton and James Pugh serve as executive producers, while Frédéric Fiore, Ryan Wickers, and Kamarowsky will be executive producers for Logical Pictures Group. Titled “Lenni,” Collette will lead the cast of the series along with Ciarán Hinds (“Game of Thrones”), Dan Wyllie (“Love My Way”), Josh McKenzie (“La Brea”), Celeste Barber (“The Letdown”), Genevieve Hegney (“Colin From Accounts”), Arka Das (“The Airport Chaplain”) and Wayne Blair (“Total Control”). articles.title: Big Daddy: How Jordan Firstman Turned ‘Club Kid’ Into a Glorious, Gay, Oscar-Worthy Crowdpleaser
articles.full_text: Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Max Montgomery for Variety It’s 3 p.m. at the Sunset Tower Hotel, the purgatory hour between lunch and dinner at one of Hollywood’s favorite places to hammer out deals and gaze at stars. Jordan Firstman decides it’s late enough in the day for his first Aperol spritz, which leads to some reminiscing. It was a decade ago that über-producer Greg Berlanti invited the then-25-year-old Firstman to the Tower Bar to discuss the trajectory of his career. Berlanti, who became the showrunner of “Dawson’s Creek” at age 27, has served as a coach for more than one young queer creator, and Firstman had just sold a series to the cable channel Sundance TV, based on his romantic intergenerational short film “Call Your Father.” He was getting pushback from the network about casting a 50-year-old out gay actor in the lead. Max Montgomery for Variety “He wasn’t an unknown; he was a great working actor,” Firstman recalls, declining to give his name. “The studio was like, ‘We would love to cast a gay actor, but there’s just no one that even touches the level of fame we need to justify you doing the show at this budget.’” Firstman stabs Aperol-soaked ice with his straw, tensing at the memory. “I got to a place where I told them, ‘I’m not doing this if the actor isn’t gay.’ I was a little bit threatening, like, ‘You guys don’t want to look homophobic.’” Sundance TV ended up passing on the show, prompting Berlanti to attempt to rescue it for the nascent HBO Max. It would languish there for years, and then disappear altogether in that company’s revolving door of mergers and executive changes. My, how times have changed. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' Firstman, 35, does not resemble the typical filmmaker whose career launched into the stratosphere out of the Cannes Film Festival. His baggy jeans, chest-hugging polo and Oakley raver sunglasses lend themselves better to the hipster neighborhood of Silver Lake. (Not coincidentally, that’s the setting of Rachel Sennott’s HBO comedy “I Love L.A.,” on which he co-stars as a stylist and BFF to Sennott’s aspiring talent manager, Maia.) Impishness is Firstman’s trademark — he’s all easy crooked smiles and bouncing brown curls. That quality is what’s made his “Internet Gay” persona travel so readily — as evidenced by his more than 1 million followers on Instagram and TikTok. Yet in May, Firstman took the French Riviera by storm with “ Club Kid ” — his feature debut as a writer-director and first turn as a leading man on the big screen — where the project inspired a heated bidding war. Indie giant A24 beat out Focus Features, Searchlight, Netflix and Mubi for a global rights deal worth $17 million, instantly solidifying Firstman as a force to be reckoned with. “Club Kid” tells the story of nightlife promoter Peter (Firstman), who has blinked and lost 10 years of his life to hard partying (ketamine, cocaine and GHB are supporting characters in the film), a circuit of on-demand lovers and a deep indulgence in modern queer life in New York City. Depression and low self-esteem hover over Peter like buzzing drones, swatted away by late nights and early mornings and Uber Eats and laptop porn. That cycle is disrupted when 10-year-old Arlo (newcomer Reggie Absolom) shows up at the door of Peter’s SoHo apartment announcing he is his son. Both father and child are saved and tested in equal parts, as we learn that truly happy endings never come home with us from the club. The magic trick of “Club Kid” is Firstman’s ability to sell a broad, humorous story about the kind of love that fundamentally changes us — all while being firmly rooted in the digital, unapologetically gay culture that formed his artistic sensibilities. Firstman is the creative love child of Judd Apatow and Nicole Holofcener, delivered unto a Gen Z cohort who’ve become obsessed with watching movies in theaters. “It’s been amazing to see the kinds of people that relate to this film, but it really is a movie about growth,” says Firstman. “In Telluride, I watched a 75-year-old conservative man leave the theater in tears. Then we took it to the New York Film Festival, which I was very nervous to do, and showed it to the 35-year-olds who do drugs. I built the story to work on levels, with the top being a layer of warmth that feels like a hug. I explore some of my more transgressive ideas beneath the surface. If you don’t get it, there’s still a story that will make you laugh and feel something.” For those not familiar with Firstman, he’ll seem like an overnight sensation. To others, he’s a veteran comedic force for the chronically online. From the tiny town of Northport on the North Shore of Long Island, Firstman made the pilgrimage to Manhattan that countless hopeful queer people had before him. While building his social following with razor-sharp snark, Firstman worked in writers’ rooms for cult comedy series such as “The Other Two,” “Search Party” and “Big Mouth.” He also wrote a now-legendary sketch for Aubrey Plaza when she hosted the 2020 Independent Spirit Awards, highlighting gay representation among that year’s nominees that might not be obvious to the straight eye; it ended up becoming a tribute to an astonished Laura Dern, who tearfully stood up and cheered. Max Montgomery for Variety Starting out, Firstman didn’t dare dream of ascending the stairs to the Grand Palais or carving a path to the Oscars stage. “It was the era of the TV auteurs,” he says of his early idols. “Phoebe Waller-Bridge, Donald Glover, Lena Dunham: I had a voice and felt confident I could do that. They are storytellers. The directing part has always been scary to me, because I’m not as versed in images. I’m the person at the museum who has to ask why the painting is good. Words are the way I get my point across.” Firstman overcame that fear to shoot “Club Kid” in just 26 days last year. With a production budget just shy of $5 million, Firstman sacrificed his own fees as writer, director and star in exchange for two nonnegotiables: There had to be a pivotal location shoot in London, and the movie had to be shot on pricey film stock — a decision he defends with the weariness of a seasoned auteur. “That was vital; we shot on 35mm. We want prints of this movie made,” he says with a kind of reverence. Not for his own ego, but for his vision of how “Club Kid” needs to exist in the world of cinema. Two-time Oscar nominee and longtime Firstman mentor Richard LaGravenese (“The Fisher King,” “Behind the Candelabra”) isn’t surprised the debut director is calling his own shots. “What makes Jordan special is that, like any good artist, you don’t wait for an invitation,” LaGravenese says. “You create the space for yourself in the culture. He’s done it by sticking to who he is.” When I spoke with Firstman at Cannes after “Club Kid” exploded, he told me that the script began as a frothy experiment meant to evoke the dreamy wish-fulfillment films of the early aughts like “Uptown Girls,” starring Brittany Murphy, and “Big Daddy” from Adam Sandler. “That’s how I was pitching it, and once I started writing, it got a little ‘Kramer vs. Kramer,’” he said. The movie also had to be decidedly, gloriously gay. It’s not lost on Firstman that “Club Kid” sits alongside other 2026 releases that represent some of the most elevated queer stories that mainstream Hollywood has produced in years, with several of them sitting in the awards conversation with Firstman’s film: Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s “La Bola Negra,” Andrew Scott’s tearjerker “Elsinore,” Jane Schoenbrun’s “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” and Lukas Dhont’s fellow Cannes player “Coward.” Queerness is integral to these movies, but not exclusively the point — they are portraits of soldiers propping up unjust wars, artists defying heteronormative conventions to find themselves and, in Firstman’s case, a fading party boy belatedly becoming an adult. Max Montgomery for Variety “I feel like there hasn’t been a defined generation of new filmmakers since the Safdie brothers era began,” Firstman says. “Los Javis and Jane and Lukas and I are all around the same age. Our collective is so queer, and people are responding, and the movies are doing well.” At the Tower Bar, we cave and order french fries to soak up the spritzes. Firstman is recognized by a musclebound music producer dining nearby with a woman of equitable attractiveness. “He’s hot,” Firstman says, “but he’s a really nice guy. And he has a great kid!” If Firstman is indeed part of a new wave of queer storytellers, some might say it took a minute for him to ingratiate himself to that community. Prior to his Cannes breakthrough, his brand was, well, messy. Firstman excels at highlighting the absurdity of celebrity and the pretension of coastal media types. Last year, he criticized the crossover sensation “Heated Rivalry” for what he called a narrow depiction of gay sex (he said that’s “not how gay people fuck,” and that the show eroticized two closeted athletes falling in love under deep cover). The show’s rabid fans descended, and Firstman made it right by deploying his online instincts and recruiting “Heated Rivalry” star Hudson Williams for a TikTok post satirizing the whole blowup. In the clip, Williams lip-synched Nicki Minaj’s 2015 MTV VMAs acceptance speech, in which she aggressively called out host Miley Cyrus for remarks she’d made about the rapper in an interview (“Miley, what’s good?”). Firstman played Cyrus, claiming she’d been taken out of context. This Minaj-Cyrus exchange also appears in “Club Kid,” as Firstman’s character sells drugs to a group of shrill gay guys locked in a bathroom stall. Much of the press tour for “Club Kid” has been a reframing of Firstman’s intentions, especially as it relates to his fellow queer people. “You really can’t try to steer the narrative within the gay community. But I’m speaking to them from my heart, and I feel confident in what I’m showing them. I’m also doing my best to be a good friend, and to protect my cast,” he says. “It’s been amazing seeing messages from people who say they feel seen by the movie — even the judgy-ass bitches in the nightlife community. They were like, ‘ You did that .’” Josh Hutcherson, Firstman’s co-star on “I Love L.A.,” who describes him as his brother, says the filmmaker is “one of the most sensitive people I know. He has an abrasive and controversial mask he wears, and it’s very funny. His humor shakes up the right people. But he’s also got an amazing sensor for humanity.” That “Club Kid” leads with its heart might confound Firstman observers, but the movie’s sentimental value is why A24 made its big bet. Because on the other side of that LBTGQIA+ embrace is the rest of the moviegoing market, and the eight-figure check cut by the boutique studio means “Club Kid” must leg out at the box office through the holiday season and beyond to reach profitability, after opening in limited release this weekend. Firstman is personally involved in the marketing, recruiting famous DJs to spin at premiere parties in Paris, Rome, London and New York, while rolling out merchandise like “Club Kid” cropped T-shirts that resemble one his character wears in the film (“I Love Björk and Bareback,” it reads). Some of his peers have suffered the slings and arrows of failed crossovers. In 2022, Universal Pictures backed comedian Billy Eichner’s noble attempt to program a gay romantic comedy for wide audiences in the Apatow-produced “Bros.” That film grossed only $14 million worldwide on a $22 million budget, not accounting for the significant marketing cash the studio spent. While Firstman’s film is quite different, the projects may invite an inevitable comparison. Max Montgomery for Variety A24 and Firstman are betting on word-of-mouth, which also has its consequences. Conservative rage-baiters could latch on to “Club Kid” for its depiction of a child spun into the chaos of a druggy NYC underbelly. The film’s 100% Fresh Rotten Tomatoes score (based on 65 reviews), however, is a good indicator that audiences are receiving Firstman’s intended message. After all, the kid in “Club Kid” is often the one doing the child-rearing. “The world of this movie isn’t sensationalized: I don’t put a positive or negative lens on the party scene. I just try to show these people for their beauty and their flaws and their creativity,” says Firstman. “I wanted to explore what felt universal. A general millennial malaise, like, what are we doing? The pandemic was six years ago, and we still feel like we’re in our 20s — but we’re not. This has permeated our culture. So many friends of mine wanted to stop partying and didn’t know how.” But for a movie about generational sadness, “Club Kid” is riotously funny, filled with Easter eggs for meme lovers and culture queens. During a dance sequence, Firstman and a friend do choreography to the chant “No arms! No legs! No eyes!,” a reference to a 1998 micro-scandal caused by Claire Danes, who used those words to describe the people she saw in the Philippines while filming the prison drama “Brokedown Palace.” (When a character expresses confusion about the dance, Peter screams, “Google ‘Claire Danes Philippines!’”) One of the film’s best jokes was sacrificed for a leaner run time, Firstman laments. On his second day of daddy duty, Peter takes little Arlo to brunch at the glitterati staple Balthazar. He asks if his son, born and raised in the U.K., likes the spot because it was founded by another Brit (celebrity chef Keith McNally). Peter jokes that “James Corden isn’t even allowed in here anymore,” referencing a nasty 2022 beef between McNally and the late-night host over the latter’s alleged rudeness to the staff. “Who is James Corden?” the boy asks. Peter sighs with jealousy and tells the kid he’s so lucky not to know. Max Montgomery for Variety “If I want a bunch of gays to be screaming the Nicki Minaj speech, the gays will like that. But a straight guy will still get the message — you’re trapped in the bathroom with annoying gays,” Firstman says with a laugh. There’s also the script’s parade of memorable nicknames for drug use, with “Sniffany Haddish” as the moniker for cocaine. Want to mix that with ketamine? Then you’re having “a little Charlie, a little Kirk.” Administering your drugs in the rectum for faster results? That’s a “Benson Boof.” A millennial born on the tail end of his generation, Firstman grew up with the competitive noise of friends posting their best, most successful lives minute by minute on social media. As the sweet orange liquid in our glasses turns to slush, he says he’s grateful that fame and artistic praise didn’t come so fast or easy. Whatever fate the box office and the Oscars hold for “Club Kid” and Firstman, he’s leveled up as both an artist and a man. “Life gives you what it gives you when it does,” he says, imagining a world where that Sundance TV show had actually been made. “I don’t know where I’d be now. My voice and vision are more fully formed because of my experience.” At the last second, I try to tempt Firstman with another round, but he declines. After all, he’s on his way to the first L.A. screening of his film, to be moderated by “Anora” Oscar winner Sean Baker. He bids me farewell when, half in his car, Firstman springs out and runs back to the valet stand. “This is for you,” he says, handing me a lighter emblazoned with the words “Club Kid.” Location: Roleplay Design showroom; Styling: Chloe and Chenelle/A Frame Agency; Grooming: Kristen Shaw/A Frame Agency/St. Meto; Look 1 (Black Suit): Full look: Gucci; Look 2 (Blue Shirt): Full look: Tom Ford; Watch: Tiffany; Look 3 (Black Jacket with White Shirt): Jacket, shirt and tie: Dolce & Gabbana; Look 4 (Black Sweater): Sweater: Prada; Jeans: All Saints Loading comments... articles.title: Former OnlyFans Star Camilla Araújo Sets ‘Plot Twist’ Podcast Launch in New Expansion Into Long-Form Entertainment
articles.full_text: × Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Nov 4, 2026 8:00am PT Former OnlyFans Star Camilla Araújo Sets ‘Plot Twist’ Podcast Launch in New Expansion Into Long-Form Entertainment By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Former OnlyFans Star Camilla Araújo Sets ‘Plot Twist’ Podcast Launch in New Expansion Into Long-Form Entertainment 33 minutes ago Stocks Rally Higher After Democrats Flip Congress 2 hours ago Democrats Win House and Senate in Sweeping Rout of GOP 12 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Camilla Araújo Camilla Araújo, a YouTuber, entrepreneur and former OnlyFans creator, is launching her next endeavor: “Plot Twist,” a new weekly interview podcast series featuring guests from pop culture and beyond. “Plot Twist” episodes will premiere on Araújo’s YouTube channel, which has more than 9.3 million subscribers, and will also be available across major podcast platforms. Short-form clips and highlights will be distributed across her social media channels, reaching her combined audience of more than 27 million followers. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' “I’ve spent the last few years building my career in front of millions of people, and along the way I’ve met so many other incredible creators who are doing the same,” Araújo said in a statement provided to Variety . “The one thing I’ve realized is that there is always so much more to who someone is than what you see online. That’s why I created ‘Plot Twist’: to get in there and have real conversations that go beyond the clickbait and the headlines.” According to Araújo, on her podcast, she will focus on talking about “all the reasons why getting out of the box is the actual key to creative and financial freedom.” “I want to talk about those unseen moments, those hidden fears, and those crazy decisions that led people to really become who they are now,” she said. “Everyone’s life is full of unexpected plot twists, and this is the place where we’re going to talk about them. Let’s fucking go!” Araújo was born in Raleigh, North Carolina, to Brazilian immigrant parents. The 24-year-old first rose to prominence following her appearance in MrBeast’s record-breaking “Squid Game” recreation in 2021. That same year, she joined OnlyFans and won a massive following — writing in a social media post that she earned more than $11.5 million from the site in 2025. In a January 2026 video, Araújo announced that she was leaving OnlyFans to start Becoming Her, a paid online social media mentorship course “exposing the viral content formula I used to make millions from my phone and how you can steal it.” According to Araújo’s reps, her “Plot Twist” podcast is centered on the idea that no one should be defined by a single label. Each episode will feature conversations with celebrities, entrepreneurs and cultural figures about the pivotal moments, unexpected challenges and personal decisions that shaped their careers. Recording for “Plot Twist” is scheduled to start before the end of 2026, with a premiere date TBD. The podcast will be produced by Elan Gale through his unscripted production company, TheYearOfElan, and shot in person at Main Character Studios in Miami. In addition to launching “Plot Twist,” Araújo has additional products and business ventures in development. She also has used her platform to support charitable causes and community-driven fundraising initiatives, including animal welfare efforts. ‘Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Trailer: The Wilderness Survivors Return Home Loading comments...

articles.title: Daisy Ridley, Sosie Bacon and Simon Rex to Star in Road Trip Horror ‘Get Rid of It’ From ‘Whiplash’ and ‘Drive’ Producer
articles.full_text: × Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Nov 4, 2026 8:00am PT Daisy Ridley, Sosie Bacon and Simon Rex to Star in Road Trip Horror ‘Get Rid of It’ From ‘Whiplash’ and ‘Drive’ Producer The film is being launched at the AFM by Upgrade, CAA Media Finance and Range Select By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest Thomasin McKenzie, Finn Cole and Antony Starr to Lead ‘The Lie of Sherwood Forest,’ Logical and Protagonist Launching at AFM (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Quentin Tarantino Thought He Was ‘Letting Down’ Brad Pitt by Not Directing Cliff Booth Sequel: ‘I Felt Bad About That’ 7 hours ago Jason Statham and Guy Ritchie Reunite — Again — for Netflix Revenge Action Movie ‘Dogfight’ 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Credit: Gita Bass, Martin Rusch, Matt Licar Daisy Ridley , Sosie Bacon , and Simon Rex are teaming up for upcoming feature “Get Rid of It,” set to shoot at the start of 2027. The film is being directed by Ry Russo-Young from a script by Gemma Holdway, and is being launched at the American Film Market by Upgrade, CAA Media Finance and Range Select, who are handling sales. “Get Rid of It” follows Harper (Ridley) and her sister, Jessie (Bacon), who embark on a cross-country road trip when Harper discovers she’s pregnant after a one-night-stand with a mysterious drifter named Miller (Rex). The sisters find themselves fighting for survival as they discover the thing growing inside Harper may not be human. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' The project is being produced by independent film veteran David Lancaster , whose credits include “Whiplash,” for which he received a best pictures Oscar nomination, plus “Nightcrawler” and “Drive.” “Propulsive and playful, this project’s strength is its compelling point of view and heart beneath the horror. I’m thrilled to bring it to life with such an extraordinary and gifted group of collaborators,” said Russo-Young. Ridley can be seen in Ti West’s upcoming film “Ebenezer” opposite Johnny Depp and has previously starred in Zak Hilditch’s “We Bury The Dead,” Joachim Ronning’s “Young Woman and the Sea,” and as Rey in the most-recent “Star Wars” trilogy. Bacon is currently starring opposite Nicole Kidman and Jamie Lee Curtis in Elizabeth Sarnoff’s series “Scarpetta” and recently appeared in the SXSW breakout “Family Movie” alongside parents Kevin Bacon and Kyra Sedgwick and brother Travis Bacon. She’s also known for her work in Parker Finn’s horror-hit “Smile,” and Brad Ingelsby’s detective drama “Mare of Easttown.” Rex is known for his acclaimed performance in Sean Baker’s “Red Rocket” and has recently starred in Nic Pizzolatto’s “Easy’s Waltz” and Zoë Kravitz’s “Blink Twice.” Russo-Young’s previous directing credits include the sci-fi teen thriller “Before I Fall” starring Zoey Deutch, coming-of-age drama “The Sun is Also A Star” with Charles Melton, as well as the acclaimed AppleTV+ series “Shrinking” headlined by Harrison Ford and Jason Segel. ‘Yellowjackets’ Season 4 Trailer: The Wilderness Survivors Return Home Loading comments...

articles.title: Music Industry Moves: Jackson Wang Inks With WME; Position Music Signs Arkai to JV With Lindsey Stirling’s Label
articles.full_text: × Breaking News Becerra Wins California Governor; Democrats Take the House and Senate Nov 4, 2026 8:23am PT Music Industry Moves: Jackson Wang Inks With WME; Position Music Signs Arkai to JV With Lindsey Stirling’s Label By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Music Industry Moves: Jackson Wang Inks With WME; Position Music Signs Arkai to JV With Lindsey Stirling’s Label 31 minutes ago Justin Timberlake to Release Four-Part ‘Tell-All’ Docuseries, Featuring Janet Jackson, on Apple (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago Olivia Rodrigo, Katseye and Sienna Spiro to Be Honored at Variety’s 10th Annual Hitmakers Event 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Singer-songwriter Jackson Wang , currently starring in an Apple campaign tied to his new single and music video, “Thank You,” has signed with WME for representation. Wang’s 2019 debut album, “Mirrors,” became the first album by a solo Chinese artist to hit the Billboard Top 200 and over the years he has collaborated with Ciara, Swae Lee, Major Lazer, Gucci Mane, and others, and has headlined Los Angeles’s Kia Forum and Brooklyn’s Barclays Center; in 2022 he was the first Chinese solo artist to perform on the main stage at Coachella. In addition to WME, he continues to be represented by Team Wang Records and Roc Nation. Related Stories 'Ellen DeGeneres Show' EP Matthew Wright Dies at 52 in 'Unfathomable Tragedy'; DeGeneres Shares Tearful Video Calling Him the 'Glue to Our Family' + Position Music has signed Grammy-winning group Arkai to a JV label deal with Lindsey Stirling’s label LindseyStomp , through Position Music A&R, Jake Versluis. Described as “Hans Zimmer meets 2Cellos,” the Juilliard graduates have worked extensively in film and television, including the Emmy Awards, the Grammy Museum, the NBA Finals and others. Stirling says, “Arkai represents everything I hoped this label imprint could stand for: bold artistry, fearless creativity, and a willingness to push beyond the boundaries of genre. Jonathan and Philip are extraordinary musicians, but what excites me most is the heart and imagination they bring to everything they create. I couldn’t imagine better partners than Position Music to help us build a home where visionary artists can take big creative swings and bring their music to the world.” + Empire has announced two senior appointments in its New York office: Leesa Brunson-Boland as Senior Vice President, A&R Operations, and Bina Fronda as Senior Vice President, Marketing. Brunson previously served as Head of A&R Operations at 300 Entertainment following nearly two decades at Def Jam Recordings, where she worked with Rihanna, Jay-Z, Justin Bieber and Teyana Taylor. Fronda joins from Ultra Records where she was VP of Marketing, working closely with their artists such as Steve Aoki, Sofi Tukker and Benny Benassi. + British singer-songwriter Danny Griffiths has signed with Glassnote Records and released of his debut single, “Lightweight Champion,” which has been widely shared in demo form on social media. He is represented by Prolifica Management and Solo Agency Limited. Glassnote founder Daniel Glass says, “When we first heard Danny’s songs and then witnessed the passionate response from the audience each night he performs, we knew he belonged with us. It is always a dream to have so many respected industry people requesting a song that has not been released yet. Such is the case with ;Lightweight Champion,’ which, until now, only belonged to Danny Griffiths’ fans.” + Create Music Group has named Hayley Silvertown Chief Legal and Business Affairs Officer at the company. Based in the company’s Hollywood headquarters, Silvertown will oversee Create’s legal and business affairs functions and partner with the executive team on strategic transactions, investments and partnerships. She comes to Create from Paul Hastings where she was Of Counsel. She previously held roles at such firms as Willkie Farr & Gallagher and Shepard Mullin Richter and Hampton. She also worked in the business affairs departments of ICM and Warner Chappell music publishing. + Nebula17, the Los Angeles-based music and creative company founded by former Avex USA CEO Naoki Osada, has announced a major expansion of its executive team, publishing roster, label operations, and international initiatives. Daniel Hong joins Nebula17 as Chief Operating Officer, working alongside founder and CEO Naoki Osada on company strategy, operations, and growth while leading the company’s international division. He previously served as CEO of YG USA and COO of JYP USA, where he worked closely with globally successful acts including Blackpink, Stray Kids, and Girlset. Martha Blair Reynolds joins as Senior Director of Marketing, following her work at Ricky Reed’s Nice Life Recording Company. René Mark joins as Director of Digital with experience managing campaigns for BTS, Le Sserafim, and Tinashe at Interscope Geffen A&M and Nice Life Recording Company. Natalie Walsh joins as Director of A&R after working with Sabrina Claudio, Nasri, and Adam Messinger. Harukaze Wakabayashi joins as Senior Manager, International, from Warner Music Japan. Zac Cruz joins as A&R / Marketing Manager following roles at Avex and Revels Group, while Oscar Cornejo joins as Head Engineer, with credits including Grammy-winning work with Tyla and projects with Kanye West and Willow Smith. Nebula17 has also added three creators to its U.S. publishing roster: producer, musician, and sound designer Oh Gosh Leotus; Florida-born artist, songwriter, and producer Hydra; and producer Xansei. On the label side, Nebula17 has signed New York-based artist, producer, and musician Hojean. The company has also entered into a global distribution partnership with the Orchard. + Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (HBSE) has announced announced the hiring of Joe Giordano Jr. as Senior Vice President of Entertainment Booking. In this role, Joe will oversee entertainment booking for HBSE’s premier properties, including Prudential Center in Newark and Loew’s Jersey Theatre in Jersey City, and assist with the programming of other HBSE venues. “Joe’s deep experience in the entertainment industry and proven track record of building strong relationships while attracting major touring acts will be a tremendous asset to our team,” said Sean Saadeh, Chief Programming Officer and Head of Entertainment, Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment. “Joe has a rare ability to pair creative vision with instinctive talentspotting, consistently identifying and elevating entertainment experiences that resonate deeply with audiences.” Prior to becoming Oak View Group’s Vice President of Stadium, Arena and Theater Alliances, Giordano spent nearly a decade working for ASM Global (Legends), where he held national responsibilities in booking, and went on to serve as the Assistant General Manager at BOK Center in Tulsa, OK. + Oak View Group has announced a new agreement with Independent Artist Group (IAG) , to work with the agency’s music and comedy touring artists. The deal enables OVG to make touring and music assets from IAG artists available to OVG brand partners for promotional opportunities through the company’s vast network of sponsorship sellers across North America. Operating as an independent contractor, OVG will provide sponsorship and partnership services to IAG artists, identifying cross-promotional prospects and branding deals on behalf of IAG booked tours, the announcement states. “OVG’s sponsorship sales team is nationally recognized for forging groundbreaking, collaborative partnerships with top tier brands, teams and talent, to maximize awareness and impact,” said Dan Griffis, President, Global Partnerships, Oak View Group. “Music is a natural fit for OVG, and we’re excited to combine our sales expertise with the power of IAG’s unmatched roster of artists to create strategic alliances that benefit all partners and brands involved.” “Oak View Group has always been a valued partner of the agency, and we look forward to enhancing our relationship to the benefit of our artists. Building upon OVG’s extensive preexisting brand relationships and expertise to further our artists marketability makes a great deal of sense and we can’t wait to get started,” said Jarred Arfa, EVP and Head of Global Music and Peter Pappalaordo, EVP, Head of Global Touring for IAG. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson , Dominic Patten November 3, 2026 10:03pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source The U.S. Capitol building in Washington, D.C. Photo by Al Drago/Getty Images UPDATED with Talarico, El-Sayed results, 12:05 a.m. PT/3:05 a.m. ET Wednesday: James Talarico , whose upset victory in Texas helped form the Democrats’ new majority in the Senate, gave a victory speech Tuesday night in which he invoked his faith and a message of unity. Across the nation, that unity manifested as a historic blue wave that transformed the political landscape and secured Democratic majorities in the Senate and the House of Representatives. Those transformations came in places like the once deep-red Lone Star state, but also in Georgia, Kansas, Ohio and in Michigan with Abdul El-Sayed ‘s Senate seat win. GOP dynasties were toppled in South Carolina and Maine, Gina Hinojosa denied Greg Abbott a fourth term as Texas governor to become that state’s first Latina leader, and nearby, ex-Interior Secretary Deb Haaland New Mexico’s win means she will be the nation’s first female Native American governor. Related Stories News Hollywood A-Listers Send A Message To Voters On Social Media News Trump Celebrity Supporters: Famous Folks In Favor Of The 47th President “This is a victory the size of Texas,” Talarico told supporters in the midnight ET hour, at a lecturn displaying the sign, “Love Thy Neighbor.” Watch on Deadline “We just showed that a politics of division is no match for a politics of love, and we just sent a message to every billionaire mega donor, every trillionaire megadonor, every corrupt defender of this broken political system in this state, in this country, power belongs to the people,” Talarico said. Clockwise from top left: James Talarico, Ken Paxton, Troy Jackson, Susan Collins , Abdul El-Sayed and Mike Rogers Getty Images He was undoubtedly referencing Elon Musk , who poured hundreds of millions into the midterms , including a major chunk to defeating Talarico.

Mayor Vote Counting Continues In Nailbiter Election View All November 4, 2026 6:50am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: New Hampshire Democratic Senator-elect Chris Pappas, Michigan Democratic Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed, Georgia Democratic Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms and Senator-elect James Talarico Getty Images Democrats won up and down the ballot in the midterms , and votes are still being counted on what could ultimately be a 75-seat House majority and 54 or more seats in the Senate. There also were many firsts, reflecting the party’s diverse coalition that helped them score victories even in deeply red states. Related Stories Politics Midterm Elections: Mike Johnson To Step Down From House Republican Leadership After Democrats’ Blowout Victories Politics Hollywood Celebrates Midterm Results: “The Blue Wave Made Landfall, And Now The Red Wedding Begins,” Says Jimmy Kimmel Among them: The first Black woman governor Keisha Lance Bottoms , the former mayor of Atlanta, won a sizable victory over Republican Rick Jackson. In her victory speech, she recalled visiting the grave of her great-great grandmother, who was born in 1845, 20 years before emancipation. “I know I am standing on shoulders made of steel,” she said. The first openly gay man elected to the U.S. Senate Rep. Chris Pappas (D-NH) won election to the U.S. Senate in New Hampshire by a significant margin defeating Republican John E. Sununu. “Win, lose or draw, I am the luckiest guy because I am married to a man I love,” Pappas said in his victory speech after embracing his husband. Watch on Deadline The first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate Abdul El-Sayed emerged the winner after a race filled with drama — including national attention to primary rival Haley Stevens’ endorsement of Republican Mike Rogers in the race’s final days. In his victory speech, El-Sayed noted that it would be JD Vance who would be swearing him in in January. Vance characterized him as an extremist and Trump called him a jihadist. “Donald, I know you struggled with my name. So after JD swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me senator,” El-Sayed said.

articles.title: Trudie Styler Talks Journey To Directing ‘Up Against It’ & ‘The Reception’ Back-To-Back: “I’m In A Happy Place”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie WTFilms Boards Italian Alps-Set Comedy-Thriller ‘The Dregs’ With Maddie Phillips & Stephen Lang – AFM Tinto Brass Dies: Italian ‘Caligula’ Director Was 93 Pierfrancesco Favino First Look In Marco Bellocchio’s Sergio Marchionne Bio-Pic ‘Falcon’ Unveiled – AFM View All November 4, 2026 7:29am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Trudie Styler on the London Underground with cinematographer Dante Spinotti during the shoot of Up Against It Andrew Cooper Trudie Styler arrives at the London offices of Maven Screen Media , her joint production company with Celine Rattray , bearing gifts: bottles of organic extra virgin olive oil. Featuring Styler and husband Sting ’s names on the label, they are the last of a batch made from the 2025 olive harvest at Villa Il Palagio, their beloved 16th Century estate in Tuscany. She is not here to talk about her long love affair with Italy, however, but rather back-to-back directorial feature film credits Up Against It and The Reception as well as her and Rattray’s commitment to championing female-driven storytelling. Related Stories News Jean-Claude Van Damme Returning To Martial Arts Roots In Yakuza Action Pic 'Katana' For Jeremy Zag & The Veterans -- AFM News Chris Jericho To Star In Creature Horror 'I Am The Teeth', Epic Launches Sales For AFM London-set romantic comedy Up Against It stars Antonio Banderas and Eva Birthistle as warring divorced couple Alvaro and Saffron, who are forced to reconnect when their only daughter Rose is struck down with cancer, an illness she had previously battled as an infant but has no memory of. It received a buzzy world premiere in Toronto. Watch on Deadline The Reception , revolving around a chaotic wedding party and featuring Jeff Daniels, Guy Pearce, Sabrina Impacciatore in the cast , is on the cusp of shooting in Scotland when this interview takes place, with cameras now rolling since late October. The features, being sold by Beta Cinema at the upcoming AFM , mark the latest chapter in a producing and directing career that began in the early 1990s when then actress Styler came to the conclusion that combining motherhood and repertory theatre or being on set was going to be a tall order, especially with Sting on the road touring. “I decided to give acting a pause,” she says, revealing that she called Oscar-winning Chariots of Fire producer David Putnam for advice. “I said, ‘Could we have a meeting, because I want to know something about being a producer, and if I’ve got it in me to be one, and if you think I’ve got it in me to be one’,” she recounts. “He was my great mentor in how to be a producer and getting IP… he described it as putting pans on stoves,” she says. “It wasn’t a bad concept… it was sort of like when there’s a bit of heat around one project, keep the others simmering, but really go all in for the one that is showing some heat.” Her first producer credit was 1993 documentary Boys from Brazil , sparked by Styler seeing Brazilian transvestites working as prostitutes in the Bois de Boulogne in Paris and then wondering about their back stories. She tapped John-Paul Davidson to direct. The pair met during a trip to the Amazon in the early days of the Rainforest Fund which Styler co-founded in 1988 with Sting to protect rainforests and their indigenous people. The resulting work would air as part of the BBC’s now defunct documentary Under the Sun strand. “It got like about 5.5 million people, which I was told was a good number, although it I got castigated by the fourth estate for making something in such poor taste,” says Styler. Davidson would go on to direct and produce the travel shows of Micheal Palin and Stephen Fry, while the fund has since raised more than $45 million for 300 indigenous driven projects across three continents. Her next project Moving The Mountain , was directed by Michael Apted (then fresh off 35 Up ) and took its title and cue from a book by exiled Chinese student leader Li Lu chronicling China’s 1989 pro-democracy protests and their brutal ending with the Tiananmen Square Massacre. He had been introduced to Styler by a friend shortly after his arrival in the U.S. in late 1989 after escaping China where he was wanted by the authorities. “I met him that winter and he’s been in my life ever since,” recounts Styler. “Now he has a big hedge fund company.” She enlisted Apted as a director after bumping into him on a flight on the way to New Orleans to join Sting in the city. “I said, ‘Oh, coincidence!’ And he said, ‘No, I’ve actually come to see your husband about a project’… I said, ‘Ah well, can I talk to you about my project’,” she recounts. Styler remains banned from China to this day due to the film, which played a raft of festivals including the Berlinale and won an IDA award. She would go on to produce a dozen documentary and fiction features under her Xingu Films banner, named after Xingu Park in Brazil, before going on to launch Maven with Rattray in 2011. Styler also earned kudos for her championing of emerging directors, with Xingu Films getting behind Guy Ritchie ’s 1998 breakout first feature Lock Stock and Two Smoking Barrels and follow-up Snatch (2000), as well as Duncan Jones’ Bafta-winning debut Moon (2009), for which she was also Bafta nominated, among others. She recalls being approached by Ritchie’s then rookie producer Matthew Vaughn , who knocked on the door of her home out of the blue. “Matthew had the native wit and charm and the brain to be able to manifest pretty much what he wanted. He said, ‘I want you to meet Guy. He wants to meet you. By the way, you know his father’, and I was like ‘I do?’” She discovered that Guy Ritchie’s father is John Ritchie, the advertising exec known for producing the iconic “Happiness a cigar called Hamlet” ads, who she had convinced to create a campaign for the Rainforest Fund. “When I met Guy, he asked, ‘So what did you think of my script?’ I replied, ‘Even if I thought it was really stupid, I would have done this to help you because your dad helped me’,” recalls Styler, suggesting that what Vaughn and Ritchie lacked in experience they made up for in chutzpah. “It was a seminal moment… those young bloods were going to do it no matter what.” Xingu’s filmography also includes Styler’s feature directorial credit on the 2002 documentary Sweatbox , co-directed with Davidson, going behind the scenes at the Walt Disney studios and the making of the animation The Emperor’s New Groove at Disney, in which Sting was involved as chief songwriter. Styler would break into fiction feature directing in 2018 with Freak Show, an adaptation of James St James’ best-selling novel, starring Bette Midler and Alex Lawther, before returning to documentary in 2023 with Posso Entrare? An Ode To Naples . Up Against It Up Against It Maven Screen Media She continues to tap into her process as a documentary producer and director for her fiction work. For Up Against It , she spent time with NHS oncologists, notably at the Royal Marsden Hospital in London, in preparation for the film, which hinges around the fact that the best shot at survival for Alvaro and Saffron’s daughter Rose is the conception via IVF of a so-called “saviour sibling” with matching T-cells. While the premise sounds dark, the film is not, with Styler bringing a celebration of life; love and moving on, while holding on, to the big screen, reminiscent of Working Title classics such as Love Actually or Four Weddings and a Funeral but more complex. “TIFF was sort of amazing because I wasn’t prepared to have the applause, and people weeping, and also really roaring with laughter… In Up Against it , you do laugh as much as you’re touched and moved… that’s why I love cinema as a shared experience,” she says. Styler directs from a screenplay by Camille Griffen, based on an original story by Chloe King who wrote a first draft after being inspired by a segment on the NBC’s Today Show. Citing her research and discussions with oncologists, Styler says that around four saviour siblings were created in Europe last year but that the practice is being superseded by developments in paediatric oncology and CAR T-cell therapy, which uses a patient’s own white blood cells to fight cancer “I didn’t connect with it through the cancer story as much as that of the couple,” reveals Styler. “The couple split up because of Rose’s cancer. It seemed counterintuitive that you would break up when your child was in desperate need of you both, but then I spoke to oncologists who said that the path to a cure amongst families who have got a long cancer protocol in their lives, often requiring the mum to stay in hospital with the child, can put an enormous strain on the marriage.” Although the story was born out of a U.S. news item, Styler opted to transpose it to the UK where she has a better grasp of the health system. “I don’t know enough about it to get into the weeds of what universal medical care is there, but I do know a lot about the NHS, so I thought I’m just on better ground and safer ground,” she says, With two sisters who worked as nurses, one specialized in intensive care for babies, and the other in women’s health, Styler also has a deep respect for the staff throughout the NHS. “They’re not paid that well. They do many, many more hours a week than many other professions do… I felt that in the movie it was important to really include them,” she says. Styler adds it was also a joy to bring London to life on the big screen, describing the film as a love letter to the city, where she was based in the early years of her career as an actress. “I wanted it to look beautiful and diverse… it’s full of so many nations. And at its best, I think it’s a glorious city,” she says. “Because I don’t live here all the time now, I think I have a great nostalgia for it, and all it gave me when I was 18, 19, and I started to live my life as an actor, and that’s all I’d ever wanted to be.” “Through my kind of rose-tinted eyes, it’s the city that really gave me the love of arts that I have. I remember going to see Ian McKellen and Judi Dench in their Macbeth at the Donmar Warehouse and how brilliant and simple it was,” she continues. “My agent at the time, Elspeth Cochrane, was Ian’s agent. She managed to purloin me a ticket and when I saw that, ‘I was like, oh God, I really want to be at the RSC and do this.” The cast and crew for Up Against It taps into Styler’s network built over her 50-year career and life on the celebrity circuit with Sting. Antonio Banderas, Trudie Styler and Úrsula Corberó on set of Up Against It “I knew Antonio in the 1990s when he was married to Melanie [Griffith]. Then for a long time, our paths did not cross. I was living in New York, and he came to live in England for a bit,” she says of her connection with Banderas. “I’d been thinking who could play Alvaro because he’s not to everybody’s taste with his sexist remarks… somehow Banderas is one of those transcendent actors in that whatever he does, he remains lovable.” She recounts how a month after she sent the screenplay to his agent Manny Nunez, the actor requested a Zoom call in which he said he loved the part but requested one tweak. “He said, ‘I really love the script, but what I cannot be is a barrister called Peter.’ I said, ‘Of course, we will tailor make it to you,” she recalls, with Peter then becoming larger-than-life conductor Alvaro. Further cast include Úrsula Corberó ( Money Heist ) and Arinzé Kene ( The Pass, Lee ), as Alvaro and Saffron’s new partners, who become unwitting peacekeepers in the IVF process overseen by the real-life Human Embryology Authority, as well as Forest Whitaker, as NHS oncologist Doctor Augustus Abara, with Richard E. Grant, Mickey Sumner and Selana Tan also putting in appearances. Eden Hamilton ( The Railway Children Return ) plays Rose. Styler’s connections with Whitaker go back to 2013, when she was a coproducer on Christmas musical A Black Nativity , in which he co-starred alongside Angela Bassett and Jennifer Hudson, with the film shooting on location in New York’s Saint John the Divine cathedral. When Whitaker revealed he was not happy with his hotel, Styler invited him to stay at her New York apartment instead. “He said, ‘I never do that kind of thing.’ I said, ‘Well, the offer’s there.’ Later in the day, he asked, “Are you serious about me coming to stay at your apartment? I’d be really quiet.” I said, ‘Forest, it’s not a small apartment. There’s plenty of room’. My kids had gone to college, or they were working elsewhere… and Sting was on the road. I said, ‘It would be lovely to have your company’. We’ve called each other roomie ever since,” she recounts. After accepting the Up Against It role, Whitaker requested time with an oncologist for a briefing on Rose’s treatment to understand the real-life protocols around treating cancer. Styler’s award-winning crew, featuring editor Walter Fasano ( Call Me By Your Name ), Dante Spinotti ( Heat, L.A. Confidential ) and late multi-Oscar nominated Ghandi and Blue Planet composer George Fenton, is also the fruit of long connections. She has known Spinotti since the 1980s, working with him on films such as Mario Orfini’s Cinecittà-shot 1988 film Fair Game ( Mamba), in which she starred as a woman locked in an apartment with a deadly snake by her deranged computer scientist husband. He previously worked on Freak Show and Posso Entrare? and is also the cinematographer for The Reception . The interview takes place just days after Fenton’s unexpected death at age 76 in early October . Styler is caught off guard by the mention of his name and looks visibly pained by the thought of his passing, with the interview pausing momentarily. Styler, who is still reeling from his death, explains her friendship with Fenton goes back to a 1978 theatrical production of Hamlet at the Belgrade Theatre in Coventry in which she played Ophelia and he oversaw the music. “I was 23… He wrote my songs for Ophelia and through the years we just sort of ran into each other, and then this year I had nine months with him, composing that very beautiful score, seeing so much of him, and it’s like we recaptured those days in 1978, I think it was just before he did Gandhi .” “Spending those nine months with him was a sheer pleasure and also did a lot for my confidence, with him encouraging me and saying, ‘When you played Ophelia, I came to your first night. I thought it was a really stunning performance, and now you’re a director. You go on and direct as much as you want because you’re good.’” Maven & Backing Female Driven Storytelling Producer Piers Tempest, Trudie Styler and Celine Rattray at the TIFF Up Against It premiere Getty Images While revelling in her time behind the camera, Styler remains committed to Screen Media, her joint female focused banner with Rattray. Launched in New York in 2011, with offices in London, the company moved its main base to the UK capital in 2025. When Rattray first approached Styler in New York with the idea of working together, she had been mulling a move back into acting despite the then recent success of Moon. “She said, ‘Well, have a think about it’, and I said, ‘If we do it, it’s going to be something that’s niche and focuses on something missing in the film industry… what’s missing?’ We both look at each other and go, ‘Us?’” “Seventeen years later, here we are, making films that have pushed the needle on women in film above and below the line, and we’re very proud of what we’ve done.” The slate to date has included Andrea Arnold’s American Honey (2016) as well as Sundance prizes winners Novitiate by Maggie Betts and The Kindergarten Teacher by Sara Colangelo, with more recent credits including Scarlett Johansson’s Cannes-selected Eleanor The Great, Gurinder Chadha’s Christmas Karma , and Katie Holmes’ romantic comedy Happy Hours , which debuted in Tribeca in June. Men are not excluded with the company also getting pictures such as Guy Nattiv’s’s Skin (2018) and Mark Meyers’ Human Capital (2019). Styler cites figures collated by the Center for the Study of Women In Television and Film for the top 100 grossing U.S. films of 2025 showing that women accounted for 26% of producers, 20% of editors, 20% of writers and 11% of directors. “Since we’ve been more based in the UK, 90% of our films have been female directed,” she says proudly, highlighting the contrast. Additionally, 80% of Maven’s films since 2020 have had women in the leading role, while 70% were written by women. Styler acknowledges that it remains an uphill battle for women to achieve gender parity in the film and TV industries, says she remains optimistic for the future. “I do feel that the demographics are behind us. When I look at my grandchildren, we’ve got eight. I see that they are incredibly well informed, and they are no pushovers. And I do think it will get keep getting better and that storytelling will be more female driven,” she says. “I have to think like that because the alternative is to give up and retire and swing in a hammock or something, but I don’t have that in me. I’ve got lots of energy, and I love doing what I’m doing. I’m a grandmother, and I’m 72… I feel it’s my time to do what I want, and I’m really not afraid of saying what I think to anybody about this situation.” “Celine and I will continue to push on female-driven stories written by women, with women cinematographers… and wherever we can populate the films with diversity and women we will do it because the industry needs it and the world needs it. We need narratives that are more balanced. Otherwise, we are telling so many male action movies that really don’t have a beating heart.” On her own personal journey as a director, she says it is too early to say what comes next after Up Against It and The Reception , but admits she is in her element right now. “I don’t know now how many more films I’ll direct. Antonio said to me, ‘You seem so peaceful when you’re directing, the set’s so quiet, you never raise your voice.’ It’s because I’m actually in a happy place with myself and I’m so grateful to all these collaborators that are part of this.” Antonio Banderas, Eva Birthistle and Trudie Styler on the set of Up Against It Andrew Cooper Bass & Raman In Dead Heat For Mayor As Counting Continues Elected California Governor In Rout Of Ex-Fox News Host Steve Hilton Jean-Claude Van Damme Returns To Martial Arts Roots In Yakuza Action Pic Sky-ITV: Competition Bodies Get Greenlight To Probe $2.2B Deal Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger & Nico Greetham Join Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell In ‘Survive: The Game’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Holocaust Drama ‘The Night Of Broken Glass’, With Clive Owen, Mélanie Laurent & Alexander Pettyfer, Gets North American Deal Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger & Nico Greetham Join Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell In ‘Survive: The Game’ Indie Film Fund Archetype Media Finance Launches With Nicolas Cage & Lucy Hale Films Among First Projects View All November 4, 2026 7:37am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (l-r) Isabella Pappas, Heidi Berger, Nico Greetham Ruth Crafer/Faye Thomas/Luke Fontana EXCLUSIVE : Isabella Pappas ( Stranger Things: The First Shadow ), Heidi Berger ( Ludwig ) and Nico Greetham ( American Horror Story ) have joined the cast of Scout Taylor-Compton’s Survive: The Game , currently filming in Gipuzkoa, Spain. The trio rounds out the lead ensemble opposite previously announced stars Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander and Rohan Campbell. The film is shooting in Spain’s Basque region. The synopsis reads: “When a group of friends unearth an ancient board game inside a secluded cabin with a violent past, each roll of the dice brings a deadly fate to life, and the only way to survive is to finish the game.” Related Stories News Olivia Holt, Jaimie Alexander & Rohan Campbell Set For Scout Taylor-Compton's Horror Movie 'Survive: The Game'; Filming Underway In Spain News Riccardo Scamarcio, Heidi Berger, Marco Palvetti & Nikesh Patel Join Cast Of Puglia-Shot Wedding Action-Thriller 'White Tide' - AFM Taylor-Compton is directing from a script she wrote with Michael Kennedy. The film is being lensed by Andy Patch, with editing by Bryan Shaw. The film is produced by Randy Wayne and Talia Bella under their Rebellium Films banner, Tom O’Connell and Scout Taylor-Compton of Building Blocks Productions, and Amy Covell of Red Phoenix Productions. Watch on Deadline Executive producers include Leire Apellaniz of Sr. y Sra., Mark Albela, Michael Kennedy and Dauntless Productions. U.S. casting is by Jonathan Clay Harris, CSA, and European casting is by Luci Lenox.
