articles.title: Funko Launches New ‘Harry Potter’ Mystery Collectibles Ahead of HBO Series
articles.full_text: As HBO prepares to bring audiences back to Hogwarts this Christmas, Funko is getting in on the magic with a new collection of “Harry Potter” mystery figures , including a chance to uncover an ultra-rare collectible. The new “Harry Potter” POP! Mystery collection features six characters from the original film series: Harry Potter , Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley, Luna Lovegood and twins Fred and George Weasley. Each four-inch vinyl figure comes in blind-box packaging, meaning buyers won’t know which character they’ve received until they open it. Each box also includes a corresponding collectible POP! card. Related Stories Box Office: ‘Street Fighter’ Scores $13 Million Debut as ‘You Can See Everything’ Opens at No. 2 With $5.5 Million on Friday 'Ghosts: The Possession of Button House' Scares Up U.K., Ireland Box Office Win Funko x Harry Potter Pop! Mystery Box SHOP ONLINE $14.99 Priced at $14.99 each, the figures have equal one-in-six odds of appearing in a standard box. Collectors also have a one-in-72 chance of discovering a special Mystery Chase figure, with an even rarer one-of-one Worldwide Chase potentially hidden in the collection. The release is part of Funko’s recently introduced POP! Mystery line, which taps into the growing popularity of blind-box collectibles. Previous collections have featured characters from “KPop Demon Hunters,” “One Piece” and Warner Bros. horror franchises. Funko has also introduced a buyback program for eligible one-of-one figures, offering collectors $10,000 in exchange for verified rare finds. The latest “Harry Potter” merchandise arrives ahead of HBO’s highly anticipated television adaptation of J.K. Rowling’s bestselling book series, which is scheduled to premiere Dec. 25 on HBO and HBO Max. The new series will introduce a fresh generation of Hogwarts students, led by Dominic McLaughlin as Harry Potter, Arabella Stanton as Hermione Granger and Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley. The cast also includes John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall, Paapa Essiedu as Severus Snape and Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid. The first season will adapt “Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone,” with Francesca Gardiner serving as showrunner and executive producer and Mark Mylod directing multiple episodes. HBO is already developing a second season based on “Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets,” with Kit Harington recently announced as Gilderoy Lockhart. The HBO adaptation marks the franchise’s first major live-action television retelling, more than two decades after Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint first brought the central trio to the big screen. The original eight-film franchise, released between 2001 and 2011, remains one of the highest-grossing film series of all time. Funko’s new “Harry Potter” POP! articles.title: Nicolas Cage Says ‘I’m a Little Bit Homeless’ and ‘Living in Hotels’ After Sinkhole at His House

articles.title: BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’
articles.full_text: × Nov 3, 2026 8:11am PT BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’ By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest BBC Deputy Director-General Says ‘A Lot Has Changed’ After Editing Error That Triggered Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit: We’re in a ‘Much Stronger Place’ 45 minutes ago Olga Kurylenko and Alex Pettyfer to Star in Crime Thriller ‘Breakwater,’ WestEnd Films Boards Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Magical Realist Tale ‘6TM’ and ‘Searching for SmarterChild,’ About One of the Earliest Chatbots, Win Top Industry Awards at Ji.hlava Festival 4 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Speaking about an editing error that triggered a $10 billion defamation lawsuit pursued by President Donald Trump against the BBC , the broadcaster’s deputy director-general Rhodri Talfan-Davies said Tuesday that “a lot has changed since then.” Talfan-Davies said there were two issues about the BBC’s handling of the controversial episode of investigative show “Panorama.” “One was the actual edit itself, and second, and I think probably more profound in the end, was the BBC’s sluggishness in its response,” he told journalists at a Broadcasting Press Guild lunch. Related Stories Korea Box Office: Anime Phenomenon 'Chiikawa' Remains Unstoppable as Yeon Sang-ho Thriller 'Paradise Lost' Debuts 'Ghosts: The Possession of Button House' Scares Up U.K., Ireland Box Office Win He outlined the measures that the BBC had implemented to address these issues, which included his own appointment in June 2026. “A lot has changed since then. There’s been a reform of the editorial standards committee, which has been led by Caroline Thomson. The role of the deputy director-general has been created precisely to grip those types of moments and make sure that we get to quick, timely decisions,” he said. He added that the BBC had “instigated over the last 12 months what we call ‘Final Gate’ processes on our most contentious programs.” Explaining what these “Final Gate” processes were, he said, “It means that before you commit to transmission or broadcasting, all the key players involved in the title, including editorial policy, including compliance execs in each of the key genre, they get in the room and they go line by line through the key risks of the program. So there is a really diligent and thorough assessment of the program before it airs.” He cautioned that he couldn’t guarantee that “there won’t be future issues in an organization that digs deep and delivers big investigations … I mean, I’m not naïve.” However, he added, “I do think the processes and controls put in place in the last 12 months put us in a much stronger place.” Talfan Davies, who is a journalist by training, recalled his reaction when he heard of the editing error. “I thought it was a mistake,” he said. Prompted by Variety to expand on that, he said, “Well, I don’t think there was anything malign in it. Right? I think the edit as it stood in the program created a mistaken impression about what precisely was said in that moment by the President, and we caught that issue. It was a BBC review that identified the issue. The real problem was we then didn’t act quickly to put the issue to bed, to be transparent about what had happened, and to apologize for it.” Questioned about whether there was an issue with the culture among BBC journalists that may have caused the editing mistake, he responded, “No, because I think if you look at the wider program, the whole program, you’ll see the extreme care that has been taken in terms of the balance of perspectives and viewpoints in the program. I just think that one edit was problematic.” Asked if he felt it was more likely that the BBC would be able to win the case in the U.S. than six months ago, he said, “Well, I think the key next moment is the decision by the Florida court on whether it has the jurisdiction to even decide this. I think our case on that is very strong, but I’m not in the business of second guessing judges. But we have put our best foot forward in terms of setting out the arguments about why we don’t think it should be heard in a U.S. court, and we’ll wait to hear what the judge says.” Moving onto other issues, Talfan-Davies was asked about accusations of left-wing bias at the BBC by right-wing politicians like Nigel Farage. Talfan-Davies explained what his response would be if Farage were in the room making that accusation. “I’d say two things. Firstly, it’s not my experience at the BBC. I’ve worked in many newsrooms. The discussion is robust, and the conversation is pretty open-minded in terms of different perspectives,” he said. “What I would say is that whilst I don’t see that evidence of bias, you always have to constantly review how you’re doing. “One of the parts of my role is to make sure, as an executive team, we up the ante in terms of how we robustly review our editorial performance. It’s one thing to look at audience metrics, but you also need to really closely scrutinize and be rigorous about how you’re delivering, if you like, your ‘public mission.’ It’s one of the areas that I’m discussing with [the BBC’s director general Matt Brittin], and we’ll say more in the coming months about how we really up the ante on that.” ‘Elsinore,’ ‘I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning’ and ‘Animol’ Lead British Independent Film Awards Nominations Versant Sees Q3 Profit Drop Despite Upticks in Non-TV Operations Creators Pounce on Midterm Elections, Hoping to Win New Viewers and More Dollars MS NOW Has 2026 Midterm Elections Coverage: Here’s How to Watch Election Night Results Live Online Free BTS, Katseye Drive Hybe to Record Quarterly Revenue and Profit ‘Okinawa Saudade’ Director Matsubayashi Yoju on a 10-Year Journey Tracing Brazilian Dancers’ Island Roots Loading comments...

articles.title: Disney To Undergo More Layoffs With Divisions Eyeing Up To 20% In Cost Savings
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro , Nellie Andreeva November 2, 2026 7:29pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Walt Disney Studios Exterior Gilbert Flores/Getty Images The Walt Disney company is laying the groundwork for more cuts, with thousands poised to be impacted. According to sources, the new round of layoffs will be made across multiple divisions, including TV networks and the motion picture studio, at varying amounts. As is customary in the run-up to staff reductions, managers of the affected teams have been given targets, with some asked to achieve as much as 20% in annual cost savings, we hear. Disney declined to comment on the latest cuts, first reported by Bloomberg, whose exact timing is unclear. Related Stories Executives Utopai Studios Names Former Disney AI Exec Hans Ku Chief Product Officer News 'Star Wars' Voices & Sounds Made Available To Gamers And Creators By Tech Firm Voicemod There have been ongoing layoffs at Disney throughout the year following Josh D’Amaro taking over as CEO from Bob Iger on March 18. In April, 1,000 roles would be eliminated, followed by several hundred in July, with Pixar and National Geographic among the divisions most affected . Watch on Deadline The process accelerated in August when the entertainment conglomerate extended a Voluntary Early Retirement Offer to longtime executives. That process has now been completed, with some sources indicating that more eligible managers opted for the package than anticipated. The VERO was always considered a precursor to layoffs. “This is one of several actions we’re taking to reshape our organization, including involuntary staff reductions that have already begun in some areas and will continue into next year,” Disney EVP and Chief People Officer Sonia Coleman wrote at in memo back in August. Since then, a couple of hundred employees were laid off in late September , largely in areas such as tech and HR, and last week, another 100-200 employees in its Experiences division were pink slipped, the majority of them at Disney’s Imagineering campus in Glendale. “I think like all of our similarly situated competitors, and certainly all of our competitors in the tech industry, there is a need to constantly evaluate how you’re structured,” Dana Walden, President and Chief Creative Officer of The Walt Disney Company , said about the continuous layoffs during Bloomberg’s Screentime conference last month. “Technology set their sights on our business, and we must survive and thrive and grow. That’s what we’re going to do.” D’Amaro has put a focus on cost reductions since ascending to the top Disney job earlier this year. At the most recent Disney earnings call, he spoke about using some of the savings to invest in growth areas. “When our teams work smarter, we can serve more people across our parks and digital platforms and do it more cost-effectively,” he said. “That frees up capital to reinvest aggressively in what drives long-term value: new content and next generation guest experiences, as well as technology infrastructure that keeps Disney at the forefront of entertainment.” Disney’s global head count stood just north of 230,000 as of the end of the most recent fiscal year. articles.title: New Anti-Harassment Laws Lead To Questions From UK Film & TV Industry
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max John Leeson Dies: Actor Who Voiced Iconic Role In ‘Doctor Who’ Was 83 Ex-YMU Global Entertainment Boss Launches London Agency Repping Creators Including Topjaw’s Jesse Burgess Russell Brand’s Defense Argues Channel 4 Film “Poisoned Well Of Justice Deliberately” View All November 3, 2026 1:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty EXCLUSIVE: Big UK production groups and studios have been busily preparing for new anti-harassment laws that will impact the film and TV industry, but questions remain. Last Friday, UK-wide legislation came into force that means employers are now liable for harassment of their staff, cast and crew by third parties. Employers must take “all reasonable steps” to prevent harassment, the law now states, and claims can be made up to six months after an incident takes place. The legislation is part of the UK’s much-discussed Employment Rights Act, one of the ruling Labour Paty’s flagship pieces of reform. Related Stories News International Insider: European TV In Peril; Venice & TIFF Latest; Mercedes Ron Interview News International Revenues Of $2.1B Boost British TV Makers, Census Finds, As Pact Warns BBC Must Avoid "Managed Decline" The adustment has led many big production houses and studios to update their harassment policies in preparation, we are told. “These changes give victims much stronger legal protections,” said the government when the legislation, which applies to all industries, came into force. Watch on Deadline In practice, this change means that if cast or crew are harassed during a production by a third party, be that an agent, someone on location or even someone who has nothing to do with the project, the production company or studio could now be liable for the claim. “This is a significant change,” said Elizabeth Peyton-Jones, who runs The Talent Trust, which takes real-time reaction data from crew working on productions. “As an employer, you can’t now say, ‘I can’t control what other people do.’ You have to take responsibility. And the duty of care reaches beyond the set.” Producers we spoke with were mostly aware that the legislation was coming in and have been preparing, but they still have questions over just how far this duty of care reaches. Peyton-Jones used the example of a wrap party, where people who didn’t work on a project could be invited and incidents could happen. Would the producer then be liable for the actions of that third party? “Wrap parties are an interesting example because they are informal,” she added. “People have been working together for a long time; stress and exhaustion are high. If someone doesn’t speak up until long after production has wrapped, and if nothing was time-stamped and no action was taken, then a production company can’t simply say it didn’t know. It should therefore have a mechanism for people to raise concerns.” Deadline understands at least one large production outfit considers wrap parties, late-night working and staying in hotels as part of its risk assessments. “Where does the buck stop?” Other examples floated to Deadline that require clarity include incidents that take place on the street when crew are doing vox pops, harassment on transport on the way to-and-from a set, or situations where crew have to accompany third parties for filming. The vision behind the legislation, communicated by the government last week, is that “whether a passenger harassing a bus driver, a waiter being intimidated by diners, or a shop worker dealing with abuse from customers, reforms will ensure that unacceptable behaviour is not treated as part of the job.” Max Rumney, the deputy CEO of producer trade body Pact , which represents hundreds of UK indies, said the question of “where does the buck stop?” is confusing his members, and he doesn’t feel he has all the answers from government. “In many ways this is a law for environments that are slightly different to ours,” he explained. Pact’s legal chief sent a note to all members last week, which Deadline has seen, urging them to “update their anti-harassment and bullying policies, if you have not already done so, to ensure that you remain compliant with the law.” We are also told that training body ScreenSkills has updated the anti-bullying and harassment module on its training passport in line with the legislation. This all feels necessary. Just a few weeks ago, a survey from UK arbitration service Acas found that two-fifths of employers across all industries were unaware of these changes in law. Making things more confusing is the fact that the law has technically come into force but detailed guidance will only be available from early 2027. Deadline understands the UK’s Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, and Digital, Culture, Media and Sport have both been prepping the industry, meeting with trade associations, hosting webinars and pushing employers to update their policies. The departments wouldn’t be drawn on specific examples of when an employer would be liable for harassment or not. We spoke with big production groups in the UK who said they have been preparing for the change but wouldn’t come on the record to discuss further. One HR executive at a big player said they had updated contractual terms for future productions in order to account for the new third-parties law. Of course, some indies are much smaller, often one-or-two-person bands, and many don’t have HR departments, which could lead to issues with the new law. Movies are often run by production outfits only created for that particular project before being shut down. If an incident takes place on one such movie but is only reported months afterwards, the responsibility could fall on a company that has just been dissolved. Pact’s Rumney, however, reckons bigger productions will be more problematic. “Small indies make smaller productions and they know how to do these things,” he added. In the UK film and TV industry, harassment remains a huge topic, in part due to high-profile instances of allegations in recent years. The anti-harassment legislation came into force on the day a prosecuting barrister delivered closing arguments at the Russell Brand trial, for which the Forgetting Sarah Marshall star is accused of three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of attempted indecent assault. Brand denies all allegations and says all relationships were consensual. Those we have spoken with rejected the idea that the new law will lead to a flood of harassment complaints, with many barriers that prevent the industry’s majority freelance workforce from making claims still in place. “I think there will still be resistance [to complaining],” said Peyton-Jones. Talent Trust research has previously pointed to a “silence gap” on UK productions. A report recently found 40% did not feel respected or treated with dignity on a production and yet more than three quarters (76%) didn’t feel they could speak up without worrying about unfair repercussions. Many concerned industry folk are hopeful the “silence gap” will begin to close now that the long-expected CIISA anonymous whistleblowing service has launched . The new harassment laws could contribute to a further closing of the gap, but this feels a bit of a way off. On Alan Carr’s Life’s A Beach Podcast , the Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire star was incredulous about a report in The Mail on Sunday claiming he told Celebrity Traitors producers that he was uncomfortable with “macho banter” during filming. “I’ve never had stuff made up about me before,” Acaster told Carr, who won the first season of The Celebrity Traitors on the BBC. “There was something in the papers that said I’d complained cos Rob and Romesh had been teasing me.” Related Stories News 'The Celebrity Traitors' Finale Draws Record Audience To BBC News 'The Celebrity Traitors': BBC Says It's "Categorically Untrue" James Acaster Made Complaint About Co-Stars' "Macho Banter" “I was like: I’ve been friends with those guys for like over 10 years. They were lovely the entire show. I didn’t complain about any of my fellow players. It was so completely fabricated. They contacted my agents and Rob and Romesh’s agents [and] all of them said: ‘That is categorically untrue.’ They [the Mail ] went: ‘Cool, printing it tomorrow.'” Watch on Deadline In a story splashed on the front page of the Mail on Sunday last month, the newspaper quoted a “snitch” on the show as saying: “Rob and Romesh clearly thought they were having a bit of a laugh, but James began to feel quite a lot of it was at his expense, and away from the cameras he started to get annoyed and upset by it. The BBC also issued a forceful denial. A spokesperson said: “Claims of teasing amongst the cast on the show and claims of complaints about teasing are categorically untrue. There were no incidents of this nature and there is no evidence to support these allegations.” Acaster told Alan Carr’s Life’s A Beach Podcast that he admitted being a traitor to fellow contestant Jerry Hall, but the scene did not make the final edit. “I looked her in the eye and said, ‘I think it might be me too, Jerry,’ and she said, ‘You’re very sneaky.’ And I told her I was very sneaky and it might be me,” he said. Related Stories News 'Carrie's Mike Flanagan Reflects On Supernatural YA Drama & Says 'Warhammer 40,000' Series Has "Very Cool And Unexpected On-Ramp" News Amazon Shares Fall On Q3 Earnings Miss As Big Tech Market Rout Continues “Royal love stories are working tremendously well,” Justus Riesenkampff, EVP Nordics & Benelux at Beta Film, told Deadline. “We’ve had a lot of classic period pieces, but people are intrigued in these modern royal stories. Queen Silvia has a lot of elements that will also resonate with the younger audiences. It is an ideal setup and also has the potential for future seasons.” Watch on Deadline Silvia met Carl Gustaf, the Crown Prince of Sweden, when he was a guest at the ill-fated 1972 Munich Olympic Games, where Silvia was working. Season 1 focuses on the early years of their relationship, from the day they met until the eve of their marriage. “At first glance, it’s a classical royal story; a noble person marries a commoner,” said Carsten Kelber, Producer at German label Pyjama Pictures, which produces with Sweden’s Unlimited Stories. “But in this story it is very different and there are a lot of surprises that lie within the main characters and their backgrounds,” He added” “A lot of the usual tropes or patterns are turned upside down in this story. The genre is clear, it’s a romantic drama, but it’s also a very modern view on relationships and female empowerment.” The royal couple remain married and a regal drama that includes many characters still alive has echoes of The Crown as well as Dutch series Máxima , which Beta also distributes. The Queen Silvia producers notified the royal family the series was happening. Miguel Alexandre ( Gran Paradiso ) directs from a screenplay he penned with Lisa Hofer ( Black Island ) and Pauline Wolff ( VAKA ). As with shows that have gone before such as The Crown , the series covers real-life historic milestones, but the conversations and drama that took place behind closed doors is where the writers’ skills come into play. Kelber said: “What happened in the car on the way to the event? What did they talk about, what was his or her take on what was happening? This is the fun thing to think about. It is, of course, fictional freedom. Our director likes to call it ‘poetic truth.’” The setup lends itself very naturally to a big European drama involving producers from Sweden and Germany. “The story takes place both in Germany and Sweden and they move back and forth and there are both Swedish and German characters in it; it’s very seamlessly a [Swedish-German] coproduction,” said Frida Wallman from Unlimited Stories. Given Season 1 takes in four years of a relationship that has lasted over half a century, the hope is for multiple seasons. “I would hope for many,” Kelber said. “Each phase of this marriage is so interesting.” Disney To Undergo More Layoffs With 20% Divisional Cost Savings Eyed Jason Statham & Guy Ritchie Reunite For Netflix Feature ‘Dogfight’ Boost California Tax Incentive To $1 Billion-Plus ASAP, Exiting Governor Says ‘Elsinore’ Leads British Independent Film Awards Nominations Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Bosses At ‘Clangold’ Producer Beetz Brothers Hail Skydance For Backing Casey Bloys: “A Strong Sign The HBO Line Will Continue”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Titan1Studios Adapting Stephen R. Bown’s ‘The Company: The Rise and Fall Of The Hudson’s Bay Empire’ As Historical Drama Series Bosses At ‘Clangold’ Producer Beetz Brothers Hail Skydance For Backing Casey Bloys: “A Strong Sign The HBO Line Will Continue” ‘Carrie’s Mike Flanagan Reflects On Supernatural YA Drama & Says ‘Warhammer 40,000’ Series Has “Very Cool And Unexpected On-Ramp” View All November 3, 2026 2:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Clangold' HBO Max/Eveliene Klink Ever since Paramount and Warner Bros. merged, producers around the world have been wondering what it will mean for their prospects. For Germany ‘s Beetz Brothers , which launches crime doc Clangold on HBO Max globally on November 13, the appointment of Casey Bloys as Skydance’s content chief is a “strong sign” those making high-end, mainstream productions will be well served. Georg Tschurtschenthaler, Chief Creative Officer at the Berlin-based Beetz, addressed the merger in an interview with Deadline, noting that “some information” about the new business was trickling down to international producers. Related Stories News 'The Gilded Age' Season 4 Star Taissa Farmiga Talks Gladys' "Intense" First Episode Executives Skydance TV & DTC Co-Chair JB Perrette Unveils Leadership Team, Executive Departures “There was relief because Casey Bloys remains at the top of the structure, which is a strong sign that the HBO line will continue,” he said. “The launch of [HBO Max drama] Four Blocks Zero was a big thing in Germany. All the newspapers reported on it, and internationally it reached the HBO top 10. That was a very good push. The signs seem positive, although that is simply what we know at this stage.” Watch on Deadline Christian Beetz, co-CEO and co-founder at Beetz, added discussions for program orders remain separate with HBO Max and Paramount+, though Skydance co-CEO David Ellison has said they will eventually merge into one service. “They currently have very different programs,” he said. “I think there is still some time to go.” HBO Max’s upcoming four-part doc Clangold centers on one of the biggest criminal cases in Germany’s history, when a 100kg Canadian gold coin known as ‘Big Maple Leaf’ was stolen from Berlin’s Bode Museum in 2017. The story, directed by Jan Zabeil, follows the investigation into the audacious heist, the legal proceedings and prosecutor Katrin Faust’s cat-and-mouse struggle with perpetrators, but is considered humorous and light-hearted at times as the absurdity of the situation is revealed. Members of the Remmo family, an influential Mhallami-Arab group in Berlin whose image is fueled by rap and film, were ultimately convicted of the robbery and the doc looks closely at them. Beetz restructure For the Leonine Studios-owned Beetz, which is known for docs such as Sundance doc Eternal You , the launch of Clangold comes after it restructured this year under six genre labels. Christian Beetz and Georg Tschurtschenthaler Beetz Brothers Premium content arm Beetz Originals was responsible for Clangold . The others are Elon Musk Unveiled – The Tesla Experiment producer Beetz Investigate; Wacken – Hearts Full of Metal maker Beetz Music; Beetz Sports, which is making a film about World Cup winner turned extreme sports competitor André Schürrle; The First Lady maker Beetz Queer; and Beetz Factual, which made Trump’s America . Tschurtschenthaler and Beetz said this was partly in response to a belief the market is becoming increasingly commercial just as the film festivals that have traditionally underpinned their business model chase artistic movies. “We had an internal debate about how to position ourselves, and we arrived at the phrase, ‘We want to entertain — entertainment that resonates,'” said Beetz, who launched the company with his brother Reinhardt 26 years ago. “In contrast to some other projects, we add complexity and depth because we think there is a big audience that wants to be entertained but also wants to learn something,” added Tschurtschenthaler. “That was the core of Clangold . It is a heist story, so but have reinvented the crime genre a little – it is very funny and the first episode is really entertaining, but a second layer goes deeper into the controversial topics of organized crime, migration and integration.” He added the restructure was also based on expertize within the company. “In this more challenging market you need to be outstanding with every project,” he said, while Beetz added the global streamers’ focus on entertainment meant, “Every click counts and that is where the money is.” Beetz estimated his company has won in excess of 150 awards, but has shifted focus away from the likes of IDFA and Sundance to the International Emmys and other ceremonies that are “closer to the market” in 2026. “This is a substantial change,” added Tschurtschenthaler “In the old days – maybe three to five years ago – having a film in competition at Sundance would automatically trigger sales and bring in a large audience. That is not the case anymore. The digital world works differently, and that has led to a fairly drastic change in our strategy.” 2027 plans Upcoming projects include ZDF doc Countdown to the Midterms , which follows how the race for Congress is shaping up on both sides, with analysis from the likes of Tucker Carlson, Phil Murphy and Karen Attiah. German filmmaker Marcel Mettelsiefen is directing the Beetz Factual show. Vienna , meanwhile, is a Beetz Original that goes inside the story of Taylor Swift’s three canceled concerts in the Austrian capital in August 2024 after intelligence was received about a planned terror attack by a teenager who was radicalized through TikTok. “We have the USP of Taylor Swift and the breaking-news element, but we are telling the inside story and exploring the relevance of a new type of Islamic terrorist — digital terrorists who do not necessarily speak Arabic or appear particularly religious,” said Tschurtschenthaler. “The story ultimately connects to the manosphere. At the end of the day, these are lost kids. Some move toward the right and some move in other directions.” The company’s Elon Musk doc, which looks into the alleged failure of the billionaire’s Tesla company to address concerns over deadly faults with the autopilot function of its self-driving cars, sold widely earlier this year . Kaleidoscope has the rights in the U.S., UK and Ireland, with Mediawan Rights selling it elsewhere. Mediawan, the French group that bought Beetz parent Leonine in 2024, has been looking at how its production assets can work together to fund projects. The company made news last month when it teamed with Reese Witherspoon to buy her Hello Sunshine business from Candle Media, adding it to a lineup also including Brad Pitt’s Plan B Entertainment and Slow Horses producer See-Saw Films. Beetz chuckled at the idea of co-producing with Witherspoon, but said the bigger focus was identifying its own IP that could work internationally as scripted projects. “Then we can bring them together with the right people from the fiction side,” he added. articles.title: France Opens War Crimes Investigation Into Beirut Deaths Of Artist-Filmmaker Ali Cherri’s Parents
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie France Opens War Crimes Investigation Into Beirut Deaths Of Artist-Filmmaker Ali Cherri’s Parents Josh Hartnett, Emma Thompson, Sally Hawkins, Danny Huston, Robert Aramayo & Chloe Pirrie Join Elle Fanning & Julianne Moore In Rebecca Miller’s ‘Moonsong: A Life In Seven Verses’ – AFM ‘Who Is Still Alive’ Trailer: Watermelon Pictures Sets U.S. Theatrical Release For Swiss Oscar Entry View All November 3, 2026 4:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Photo of a young Ali Cherri and his parents retrieved from the rubble of their bombed apartment building Ali Cherri The French War Crimes Unit has opened a judicial investigation into the Israeli army’s bombing of a residential building in Beirut in November 2024 in which seven civilians were killed, including the parents of Franco-Lebanese artist Ali Cherri . Related Stories News Neon Joins Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor’s Explosive Gaza-Israel Doc ‘NAZA’ News International Insider: Votes Cast In Israel & Brazil; Tokyo Drift; Domingo Corral Interview The decision comes six months after Cherri, who is known in the film world for his Cannes Directors’ Fortnight-selected feature The Dam, and the Paris-based International Federation for Human Rights (FIDH) filed an official complaint to the unit about the incident. The case concerns the Israeli military’s bombing of a residential building in Beirut on November 26, 2024, just a few hours before a ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hezbollah was due to come into effect. The strike destroyed three floors of the apartment block with Cherri’s father and mother, Mahmoud Naim Cherri and Nadira Hayek, as well as a domestic worker employed by the couple, Birki Negesa, among the seven civilians who were killed. Watch on Deadline Two investigating judges from the French War Crimes Unit have been appointed to investigate the case. “To our knowledge, this is the very first judicial investigation opened into the crimes committed by the Israeli army in Lebanon since October 2023,” said Clémence Bectarte, lawyer and coordinator of the FIDH Litigation Action Group. “We hope that this investigation will shed full light on the bombing of 26 November 2024, which we qualified as a war crime in our complaint.” Cherri, who divides his time between Paris and Beirut, is one of Lebanon’s best-known contemporary artists, whose work has shown at the Guggenheim, Tate Modern and the Jeu de Paume among many other galleries. As he holds dual French and Lebanese nationality, the judicial investigation will focus only on the bombing of his apartment. The French courts do not have jurisdiction over the events that led to the deaths of the victims, who were not French nationals. “The opening of this judicial investigation marks another important step in our fight against impunity and our struggle for justice for those who were killed. For my family and me, it is essential that this investigation establish responsibility and ensure that those who ordered and carried out this bombing are held accountable for their actions.” said Cherri. Tensions between Israel and militant group Hezbollah ratcheted up in 2023 when the latter intensified attacks along Israel’s northern border in the wake of the October 7 Hamas attacks on the south of the country. Israel launched a military campaign in Lebanon in September 2024, involving aerial bombardments and a ground invasion, which killed more than 4,000 people and displaced another one million inhabitants. The Israeli military has been accused of targeting buildings in Lebanon in a bid to take out Hezbollah militant operatives in full knowledge that civilians would also be caught in the strike. A fragile ceasefire has been in place since November 2024, with the Israeli army still occupying parts of southern Lebanon and sporadic skirmishes. articles.title: Lucky Number Unveils First Image Of Hiam Abbass In Psychological Thriller ‘Daughter Of Eden’ – AFM
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Lucky Number Unveils First Image Of Hiam Abbass In Psychological Thriller ‘Daughter Of Eden’ – AFM France Opens War Crimes Investigation Into Beirut Deaths Of Artist-Filmmaker Ali Cherri’s Parents Josh Hartnett, Emma Thompson, Sally Hawkins, Danny Huston, Robert Aramayo & Chloe Pirrie Join Elle Fanning & Julianne Moore In Rebecca Miller’s ‘Moonsong: A Life In Seven Verses’ – AFM View All November 3, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Daughter of Eden © Flower Market Films Ltd, Newgrange Pictures Limited, British Broadcasting Corporation, The British Film Institute 2026 EXCLUSIVE: Lucky Number has released a first image of Succession star Hiam Abbass in London-set psychological thriller Daughter of Eden , in which she plays a woman suspected of having connections with the Saddam Hussein regime in a past life. The Paris-based sales company is gearing up for an AFM sales launch for the debut feature of Iranian British director Ahmadi, after buzzy shorts including the BIFA nominated Bitter Sea and Leila’s Blues which screened at Cannes Directors’ Fortnight as part of Tunisia Factory. The cast also features Yasmin Al-Khudhairi ( ( A Good Girl’s Guide to Murder ), Amir El-Masry ( Giant ) and Lindsay Duncan ( Birdman ). Related Stories Casting Jeremy Renner & Josh Brolin Set For Orlando von Einsiedel's 'A Speck In The Sea'; 193 Launching Sales At AFM News Josh Hartnett, Emma Thompson, Sally Hawkins, Danny Huston, Robert Aramayo & Chloe Pirrie Join Elle Fanning & Julianne Moore In Rebecca Miller's 'Moonsong: A Life In Seven Verses' - AFM Al-Khudhairi stars as British Iraqi nurse who begins to suspect that one of her patients may be connected to the fate of her parents under Saddam Hussein’s rule in Iraq. Watch on Deadline Driven by a desperate need to uncover the truth about her family’s past, she becomes increasingly entangled in the life of her patient, as her search for answers threatens to consume her and blur the line between justice and revenge. Beyond its psychological thriller premise, Daughter of Eden explores the lasting trauma of political persecution and the legacy of violence across generations. “Daughter of Eden began with a question I kept coming back to: how far might someone go for justice when the past still feels painfully present? I wanted to explore the pain that can stay with a person long after the violence itself has ended,” said Ahmadi. The film is produced by Jack Tarling of Shudder Films ( Kneecap , God’s Own Country ) and Pietro Greppi of Lunapark Pictures ( Flux Gourmet ) in co-production with Jackie Larkin of Newgrange Pictures. It is funded by the BFI (awarding National Lottery funding) and BBC Film, in association with Screen Ireland, Civic Studios and Three Point Capital (TPC), with the BFI and BBC Film having previously developed the project. “We are very excited to be working on Fateme Ahmadi’s debut feature, a compelling psychological thriller that builds an unsettling sense of tension and uncertainty, drawing audiences deeper into its world until the very end,” said Lucky Number. “ Daughter of Eden skilfully revisits the perpetrator–victim relationship by taking a careful and in-depth look at the psychology of its characters, reflecting on the uncomfortable questions and exploring the lasting consequences of trauma and political violence.” Lucky Number will be screening a first promo-reel for the film at the AFM. “We’re excited to partner with Lucky Number to give an exclusive first glimpse of the film to distributors at AFM whilst we make the finishing touches,” said Tarling and Greppi. Lucky Number was launched by Olivier Barbier, Ola Byszuk and Lenny Porte in 2024 with a focus on ambitious French and international auteur films with a global appeal. Remaining true to its founding mission, its 2026 slate has featured Berlinale Perspectives title Where To? By Assaf Machnes; Cannes Un Certain Regard selection Strawberries by Laïla Marrakchi, which is Morocco’s 2027 Oscars entry; Directors’ Fortnight selected Death Has No Master by Jorge Thielen Armand, which is Venezuela’s entry, and Jacqueline Lentzou’s Venice Orizzonti Best Director winner Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra . articles.title: More International Deals For ‘Sherlock & Daughter’ Ahead Of UK & Ireland Premiere On HBO Max
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart More International Deals For ‘Sherlock & Daughter’ Ahead Of UK & Ireland Premiere On HBO Max ‘Queen Silvia’ Team Hopes For Multiple Seasons After Royal Drama’s Cannes Premiere Terry Sanders Wraps Documentary ‘On Rescuing Democracy And The Rule Of Law’ View All November 3, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sherlock & Daughter The CW, HBO Max EXCLUSIVE: Sherlock & Daughter is heading to a raft of new territories. The series is on The CW and HBO Max in the U.S. and is about to premiere on HBO Max in the UK and Ireland on November 5. From Starlings Entertainment in association with The CW, the series stars David Thewlis as iconic detective Sherlock Holmes and Blu Hunt as Amelia Rojas, a young Native American woman determined to prove to the world-famous sleuth that he is her father. Dougray Scott plays Holmes’ infamous nemesis Professor Moriarty. Public broadcasters RTP and CT have acquired it for Portugal and the Czech Republic respectively while other buyers include AB1 in France, Viasat in Poland and Magenta TV in Germany. In Belgium it has landed with SVOD service Streamz and Canal+ has acquired the show for pay TV in Austria and Switzerland. YES has taken it for Israel. Related Stories News Bosses At 'Clangold' Producer Beetz Brothers Hail Skydance For Backing Casey Bloys: "A Strong Sign The HBO Line Will Continue" News 'The Gilded Age' Season 4 Star Taissa Farmiga Talks Gladys' "Intense" First Episode The show performed well on The CW and HBO Max in the U.S. It has already gone to countries around the world including SBS in Australia, NRK in Norway, SVT in Sweden, DR in Denmark, YLE in Finland, RUV in Iceland and Amediateka in the CIS region. Watch on Deadline Sherlock & Daughter was created, written and executive produced by Brendan Foley. The Closer alum James Duff is showrunner, joined by writer Shelly Goldstein and writer/consultant Micah War Dog Wright. It is produced by Starlings UK affiliate Albion Television and its co-producing partner StoryFirst, together with financiers Krempelwood and MBM3. “It’s an honor to bring a show that has become such an international hit home to HBO Max in the UK and Ireland – both the home of its setting and where it was made in Dublin and London by a fantastic cast and crew, led by mighty performances from David Thewlis, Dougray Scott and Blu Hunt,” Foley said. “In these bumpy times, we’re very proud it has appealed so widely across generations worldwide, from new younger followers to veteran fans of the world’s greatest detective.” Ahead of the UK premiere and off the back of the latest distribution deals, Starlings CEO Karine Martin said: “Sherlock Holmes may belong to London but it took a global audience to make this homecoming truly extraordinary. articles.title: UK Theme Park Alton Towers Permanently Closes David Walliams Attraction
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake British Star Loses Bid To Stop ITN & Guardian Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations UK Theme Park Alton Towers Permanently Closes David Walliams Attraction ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Star James Acaster Trashes Report That He Made Complaint About Co-Stars View All November 3, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source David Walliams Merlin Entertainments The World of David Walliams , an attraction at British theme park Alton Towers, is shutting up shop. The Merlin Entertainments-owned park said it would permanently close the Walliams-themed attraction after it opened in 2021, bringing to life characters from his books, such as Gangsta Granny. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office News Oscars: Every Best Picture Winner Back To The Beginning In 1929 A Merlin Entertainments spokesperson told Deadline: “As the 2026 peak season at Alton Towers Resort comes to an end and following our regular review of rides and attractions across the resort, we have taken the decision to permanently close the World of David Walliams.” Merlin Entertainments did not elaborate, but it is understood that the company took a range of operational and guest experience factors into consideration. Walliams’ literary agent at Independent Talent has been approached for comment. Watch on Deadline The closure follows Walliams’ publisher, HarperCollins, dropping the author and halting the publication of his back catalog following misconduct allegations. Walliams strongly denied wrongdoing after accusations about his behavior were published in The Daily Telegraph last year. Separately, Deadline revealed in September that YMU is no longer actively representing the comedian and his profile has been removed from the agency’s website. A source said Walliams “is not currently in a commercial relationship with YMU” following amicable talks in early 2026. Walliams is an established presence on British television and beyond, having created and co-starred in Little Britain with Matt Lucas in the noughties. They have made attempts to revive the BBC comedy and even spoke to Netflix about a new series in 2020. Walliams has appeared in series, including Doctor Who and Agatha Christie adaptation Partners in Crime , and had roles in movies including Murder Mystery and Stardust . He served as a judge on Britain’s Got Talent for a decade alongside Simon Cowell, but left the show under a cloud after comments he made about contestants were leaked to The Guardian in 2022. In one example, he called someone a “c***.” Walliams later apologized for his comments. articles.title: British Star Loses Bid To Stop ITN & Guardian Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake British Star Loses Bid To Stop ITN & Guardian Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations UK Theme Park Alton Towers Permanently Closes David Walliams Attraction ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Star James Acaster Trashes Report That He Made Complaint About Co-Stars View All November 3, 2026 6:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images A well-known British man has lost his bid for an injunction against ITN and The Guardian to prevent the media outlets from publishing allegations of sexual misconduct. In a High Court judgment, the star’s claim for an injunction was denied, but a temporary order preventing the man (known as PPT in court proceedings) from being named remains in place pending an appeal. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office News Oscars: Every Best Picture Winner Back To The Beginning In 1929 The case has generated significant interest in the UK, sparking widespread social media speculation about the identity of the man at the heart of the allegations. “The claimant’s claim for an injunction was dismissed,” said Mr Justice Nicklin in a judgment Tuesday, per BBC and Sky News. Watch on Deadline “The court did not determine whether the allegations, or any of them, were true, and the dismissal of the claim does not amount to approval of any publication the defendants may decide to make.” During a hearing, PPT’s legal team argued that publishing would be “highly likely” to lead to his death by suicide after he had made two previous attempts to take his own life. Gavin Millar, who made the case for ITN and The Guardian , argued that the news organizations had a duty to publish information that was in the public interest. The two outlets are seeking to publish allegations of inappropriate and exploitative sexual activities with girls and young women based on the accounts of more than 30 sources, The Guardian reported. In a written submission to the court, PPT’s lawyers said: “It is important to understand that this drastic effect on the claimant is not from guilt of the wrongdoing alleged (which is denied) but because of shame arising from deep-rooted childhood trauma and the fear of ‘trial by media.'” The court heard that PPT had made two previous attempts to kill himself: In May, when ITN and The Guardian gave him an opportunity to respond to the allegations; and in July, when he absconded from a secure hospital. ITN is the British news group behind ITV News, Channel 4 News, and Skydance’s 5 News. Set against the backdrop of Mississippi-set, coming-of-age tale Miss Christian Babe explores the experience of growing up Muslim in the American South, navigating questions of identity, faith, community and belonging. The movie builds on Fatima’s work exploring underrepresented perspectives and the complexities of Muslim identity, which began with her hit one woman play Dirty Paki Lingerie , with characters from the show then spun into Americanish . Related Stories News The Dazey Phase Boards Best Yet Entertainment Co-Founder Kareem J. Mortimer's 'House On Fire' News Tori Spelling Thriller 'Lost in The Everglades' Filming; A+E 'Alone' Indian Remake; 'Egghead & Twinkie' AFM Launch & Paramount Backs Manchester Hospital Cinema - Global Briefs Fatima who co-wrote Americanish with Iman Zawahry, who directed, also co-starred as Sam Khan, a career focused PR exec living with her equally driven sister Maryam in Queens, where they are joined by newly immigrated cousin Ameera. After a festival run, the film was acquired by Sony International. Watch on Deadline The new film taps into Fatima’s teenage experiences growing up in Mississippi before heading to New York. “I grew up Muslim in small-town Mississippi so obviously that meant church on Sundays and pageants on Saturdays. It was absurd, and it was home. I’d never seen that world on screen, and am thrilled to bring it to life,” said Fatima. The Dazey Phase’s co-head Jake Casey ( Hallowarrior ) and Head of Business and Strategy Danielle Benedict ( Heightened Scrutiny ) are on board as producers alongside Rohi Mirza Pandya ( Hiding Divya ). Mirza Pandya, one of the founders of Box Office Guru Media , brings more than two decades of experience in film marketing, audience strategy and championing culturally resonant stories. “I’m excited to partner with Aizzah and The Dazey Phase on a story that brings a fresh perspective to the screen,” she said. “ Miss Christian Babe has the opportunity to connect with audiences through its distinctive cultural lens and its deeply human themes.” Founded by Syracuse, New York natives Jake and Eva Casey, The Dazey Phase focuses on inclusive and responsible storytelling from a unique perspective, with recent projects including Hallowarrior (Shudder), Heightened Scrutiny (Sundance 2025) and Desire Lines (Sundance 2024). “I’m thrilled to help bring Aizzah’s vision to life. Her storytelling is something that really excites me; it’s vivid, specific, and personal,” said Jake Casey. articles.title: BBC Top Brass “Looking At Options” For Next Phase Of $400 Million Worth Of Savings, Says Deputy DG
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max BBC Top Brass “Looking At Options” For Next Phase Of $400 Million Worth Of Savings, Says Deputy DG New Anti-Harassment Laws Lead To Questions From UK Film & TV Industry John Leeson Dies: Actor Who Voiced Iconic Role In ‘Doctor Who’ Was 83 View All November 3, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Celebrity Traitors' BBC/Studio Lambert The BBC ’s top brass is in the process of “looking at options for the next stage of savings,” according to the Deputy Director General, which will total another £300M ($400M). Rhodri Talfan Davies said it is very unlikely another big savings announcement will come before Christmas but stressed that the “lion’s share” of the cash has to be found before the end of the current BBC charter in 2027/28. He said these conversations are currently taking place at the very upper echelons of the broadcaster. “The executive senior team is now looking at options for the next stage of savings,” Talfan Davies told journalists at a Broadcasting Press Guild lunch. “We haven’t yet shared those with the [wider] team because we’re still working through them. There are lots of ideas on the table, but until the Executive Committee reaches a decision, there’s nothing to announce.” Related Stories News 'Blue Eye Samurai' Sets Season 2 Release Date At Netflix News Jason Statham & Guy Ritchie Reunite For Netflix Feature 'Dogfight' Talfan Davies was interim Director General in April when the BBC announced it was laying off 2,000 people. Since then, his new boss Matt Brittin, the permanent DG, has been busily enacting the £500M savings plan, a tricky task in the funding climate. Around £200M has been found so far. Watch on Deadline Last month, the BBC made the long-awaited announcement that it would be shutting youth-skewing linear network BBC Three along with the BBC Scotland channel and Radio 4 Extra. Our analysis spotlighted how the worst is to come and floated that speculation internally has turned to the future of radio and podcast streamer BBC Sounds. Today, Talfan Davies gave press a window into the corporation’s thinking around Sounds and VoD platform BBC iPlayer, which is in the process of being transformed. “The real question – and I don’t know the answer – is whether iPlayer will be more and more the home for some of our biggest audio brands,” he speculated. “But you’ll still need a strongly creative collection of all your services. Brands come and go, but there will be a home for BBC audio content and its listeners.” The BBC remains unsure over its future funding model as charter negotiations with the government continue and Talfan Davies said the corporation is in the meantime having to “ride two horses in terms of financial outcomes, which is not ideal.” The main funding solution to have emerged so far appears to be the so-called “ Netflix tax,” which would force streaming service subs to pay the £180 annual license fee as it desperately tries to get more audiences to pay the fee. With Netflix in a tight spot having just laid off 1,000 staff itself, Talfan Davies acknowledged that the streamers “might not be supportive” of the proposal but said “in some ways it’s not a million miles” from yesteryear. He was referring to a time when audiences in the UK had to pay the fee even if they only watched other linear TV channels. “There are echoes of that reform in what has been suggested,” said Talfan Davies. Case against Donald Trump “very strong” Donald Trump Photo by Roberto Schmidt/Getty Images On the day of the U.S. midterms, and with Republicans expected to be inflicted with heavy defeats, Talfan Davies addressed the $10B defamation lawsuit the BBC faces from Donald Trump. While saying he is “not in the business of second-guessing judges,” Talfan Davies said the BBC’s case to have the defamation suit thrown out of a Florida court over jurisdiction is “very strong.” “We’ve put our best foot forward in setting out the arguments about why we don’t think it should be heard in the U.S. at all,” he said. “I would like the judge to agree.” The situation emerged when a BBC Panorama show made a botched edit of Trump’s Jan. 6 speech that appeared to show him inciting insurrection. Talfan Davies, who as Deputy DG now oversees the editorial standards and legal teams, said “a lot has changed” internally since the error was made and the “sluggishness” of the BBC’s response was “probably more profound” than the error with the package itself. He stressed the BBC has introduced “‘before final gate’ processes for our most contentious programmes” that sees key people involved “go through a programme line by line.” He caveatted by saying “anyone in my job who says there won’t be future issues in an organization is being naive.” “The BBC does big investigations,” he added. “I’m not naive about that. But I do think the processes and controls we’ve put in place have made us much stronger.” Disney To Undergo More Layoffs With 20% Divisional Cost Savings Eyed Jason Statham & Guy Ritchie Reunite For Netflix Feature ‘Dogfight’ Boost California Tax Incentive To $1 Billion-Plus ASAP, Exiting Governor Says ‘Elsinore’ Leads British Independent Film Awards Nominations Read More About: Comments

The eight-episode half-hour addiction-themed dramedy is now in production in Utah starring Craig Ferguson and Megyn Price. The series will be distributed by Angel. Craig Ferguson stars as Nick McTavers and Megyn Price stars as Liza. In Quitters , “after Liza, an upbeat soccer mom, falls into the cycle of opioid addiction, she lands at Unplugged, an unconventional recovery center run by Nick McTavers, a former heavy-metal legend. To put her life back on track, Liza must learn to rely on an eclectic family of patients and counselors who help her navigate the long road of recovery.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Starring In Addiction Dramedy Series 'Quitters' For Angel News BBC Top Brass "Looking At Options" For Next Phase Of $400 Million Worth Of Savings, Says Deputy DG Lennon will play Brian, Liza’s husband, “caught between love for his family and the limits of what he can endure as her addiction takes hold”. The series is directed by Darrin “Fletch” Fletcher and Chet Thomas and produced through their FletChet Entertainment banner, and was written and created by Dave Parkin. Executive producers include Chet Thomas, Darrin Fletcher, Eric Handler, Chase Vergari, Ibrahim Mohammed, Dave Parkin, Edward Neumeier, Rob Gibbs, HR Brown and Alema Harrington. “This ensemble is everything we hoped for,” said Fletch and Chet. “Every role has been cast with someone who brings real heart and humor to it, on both sides of this story — the recovery center and the families whose lives it touches. articles.title: Russell Brand Trial: Jury Begins Verdict Deliberations
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake British Star Loses Bid To Stop ITN & Guardian Publishing Sexual Misconduct Allegations UK Theme Park Alton Towers Permanently Closes David Walliams Attraction ‘The Celebrity Traitors’ Star James Acaster Trashes Report That He Made Complaint About Co-Stars View All November 3, 2026 8:10am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand Getty Russell Brand ‘s rape trial has concluded and the jury has begun deliberations on a verdict. After more than three weeks of evidence, the jury will now consider whether to convict or acquit Brand of seven charges: three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault, and one count of attempted indecent assault. The latter was reduced from indecent assault during the trial. Brand has pleaded not guilty to all charges. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office News Oscars: Every Best Picture Winner Back To The Beginning In 1929 A verdict will not be returned on Tuesday after Judge Mr Justice Bennathan sent the jury home at 4PM local time. He told jurors to “resist talking about the case” until they are all gathered again on Wednesday morning. The judge spent much of the day summarizing the evidence for the jury, going through each charge in detail. This followed closing arguments from the prosecution and defense. Watch on Deadline In legal directions last week, the judge told the jury that they are not under pressure to reach a swift verdict. “No jury can be criticized for taking too little or too much time in their deliberations, you alone must decide on that,” he told them. Bennathan said the jury must reach unanimous verdicts on each of the charges to convict Brand. He reminded jurors last week that the burden of proof is on the prosecution and that Brand is entitled to the benefit of the doubt. In legal directions to the jury last week, Bennathan also told the jury to disregard the 2023 Channel 4 documentary that carried allegations about Brand when coming to their decision. “Do not think that a few women making anonymous complaints in a TV show adds any support at all to the prosecution,” he said at the time. “The defendant denied the allegations [in the documentary] in robust, detailed terms. They were never tested in any court.” Both the prosecution and defense discussed the documentary at length during their closing arguments. articles.title: Netflix Acquires Joel Coen’s ‘Jack of Spades,’ Planning Big Push for Next Oscar Season
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All November 2, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Joel Coen Stephane Cardinale - Corbis/Corbis via Getty Images Netflix has a full plate for this Oscar season — its contenders include La Bola Negra , 14th , Possible Love , Ray Gunn , Ink , Gentle Monster , The Mosquito Bowl , Avedon and In Waves — but that hasn’t stopped the streamer from making plans for next Oscar season, as well. The streamer has acquired the worldwide distribution rights to Joel Coen ’s next directorial outing, Jack of Spades , which is based on Frances Frederica Montrésor’s 1901 novel The Alien: A Story of Middle Age and is being described as “a sinister gothic mystery filled with intrigue and betrayal set in the atmospheric Scottish Highlands.” The film, which wrapped production earlier this year, will be released in theaters in fall 2027 ahead of its release on the platform. And the company sees it as a major awards prospect. Related Stories TV Druski Signs Deal With Netflix, Sets Church Comedy 'Collect & Praise' Business Netflix Layoffs Hit U.K., With VP, Production Anna Mallett Among 2-3 Percent of Staff Affected The film stars the 36-year-old Olivier Award winner Patsy Ferran , as well as Golden Globe winner Josh O’Connor, Golden Globe winner Damian Lewis and Oscar nominee Lesley Manville . Joel Coen wrote it with his brother Ethan (both won multiple Oscars for 2007’s No Country for Old Men ), as well as Eleanor Catton and Conor McPherson; and produced it with his wife, Frances McDormand (who won an Oscar for producing 2020’s Nomadland , and also was a producer on her husband’s 2021 film The Tragedy of Macbeth ), as well as Indian Paintbrush’s Steven Rales, Blueprint Pictures’ Graham Broadbent and Peter Czernin, and Robert Graf. The film’s crew includes numerous frequent collaborators of Joel Coen, among them cinematographer Bruno Delbonnel (2013’s Inside Llewyn Davis , The Tragedy of Macbeth and 2018’s The Ballad of Buster Scruggs ) and composer Carter Burwell (1984’s Blood Simple , 1987’s Raising Arizona , 1990’s Miller’s Crossing , 1991’s Barton Fink , 1994’s The Hudsucker Proxy , 1996’s Fargo , 1998’s The Big Lebowski , 2000’s O Brother, Where Art Thou? , 2001’s The Man Who Wasn’t There , 2003’s Intolerable Cruelty , 2004’s The Ladykillers , No Country for Old Men , 2008’s Burn After Reading , 2009’s A Serious Man , 2010’s True Grit , 2016’s Hail, Caesar! , The Ballad of Buster Scruggs and The Tragedy of Macbeth ). Jack of Spades marks a reunion between Netflix and Joel Coen following The Ballad of Buster Scruggs , which landed three Oscar noms, including best adapted screenplay for the Coen brothers; and between Netflix and Josh O’Connor following The Crown (2019-2020) and 2025’s Wake Up Dead Man . The Coen brothers are represented by UTA and attorney Pat Murphy. UTA represented the sale. THR

articles.title: Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell Set for Kennedy Center Honors
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All November 2, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell JC Olivera/Getty Images; Phillip Faraone/Getty Images; Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images; Ernesto Ruscio/Getty Images; Larry McCormack/Variety/Getty Images The latest honorees for the revamped Kennedy Center Honors have been unveiled. This year’s honorees are singers Paul Anka and Barbara Mandrell, composer David Foster, actor Andy Garcia and writer David Mamet, it was announced on Monday. The latest Kennedy Center Honors will take place at Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C. The Kennedy Center itself has been at the center of a legal battle as U.S. President Donald Trump slammed a court decision to block his name, twice, from being added to the building’s exterior. The board at the arts institution also chose to shut down the Kennedy Center, with Trump in social media posts suggesting the closure would allow future renovations. Related Stories Music Bryan Adams Releases New Trump Protest Song "Lake Ontario" Music Neil Young Sues Trump for Using "Rockin' in the Free World" at Rally: "The Opposite of Everything Donald J. Trump Stands For" Launched in 1978, the annual Kennedy Center Honors event recognizes individuals who have made lifetime contributions to American culture through the performing arts. “We are recognizing amazing artists whose lifelong work has shaped American culture and inspired generations of audiences. We are proud to honor this year’s class and to continue a tradition that has defined the Center for nearly 50 years,” Trump said in a statement. There’s no word on whether Trump will again host the 2026 Kennedy Center Honors event. The ratings for the 2025 Kennedy Center Honors, hosted by Trump at the Kennedy Center, dropped to a new all-time low. Last year’s honors gala aired on CBS and Paramount+ amid news of Trump’s plans to rename the Kennedy Center to The Donald J. Trump and The John F. Kennedy Memorial Center for the Performing Arts. The push to rename the arts institution has drawn blowback, including by members of the Kennedy family and resulted in numerous artists dropping out of planned performance at the Kennedy Center. THR

articles.title: Golden Globes: ‘Club Kid’ Submitted as Drama (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All November 2, 2026 9:40am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jordan Firstman and Reggie Absolom in 'Club Kid' Courtesy of A24 Club Kid , Jordan Firstman ’s acclaimed film about a club promoter who stays too long at the party, has been submitted by distributor A24 for Golden Globes consideration as a drama, rather than a musical/comedy, The Hollywood Reporter has exclusively learned. This classification means that the film — which Firstman wrote, directed (as his feature directorial debut) and stars in — will compete in the genre-specific Globes categories (picture, actor and actress) against the likes of The Odyssey , La Bola Negra , Dune: Part Three , Elsinore , All of a Sudden , Fjord and Possible Love , rather than Wild Horse Nine , The Invite , The Debut , Artificial , Obsession , Project Hail Mary and Tender Loving Care . Related Stories General News 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards: 'General Hospital' Wins Best Daytime Drama TV The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award A24’s decision, which was made in close consultation with Firstman, may come as a surprise to some given Firstman’s background in comedy and the fact that some have described Club Kid as an elevated variation of Big Daddy , the 1999 Adam Sandler comedy about a man who unexpectedly becomes the guardian of a young child. But Club Kid becomes considerably more dramatic as it progresses, and Firstman — who shines in a decidedly dramatic courtroom scene late in the film — has cited heavier films like 1978’s An Unmarried Woman and 1979’s Kramer vs. Kramer as key inspirations. Club Kid had its world premiere at the Cannes Film Festival in the Un Certain Regard section, after which it received a seven-minute standing ovation and sparked an overnight bidding war among distributors. The film ultimately sold to A24 for $17 million, making it the biggest sale of the fest. It has since played to raves at the Telluride, Toronto, New York and other film fests. And it will begin a platform theatrical release on Friday. THR recently broke the news of two other high-profile Globes categorizations: Obsession as a musical/comedy and Artificial as a musical/comedy . THR

articles.title: Indigenous Documentary ‘Ceremony’ Lands at Netflix
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All November 2, 2026 9:47am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Ceremony' smayaykila-films Netflix has nabbed the Indigenous feature documentary Ceremony after a SXSW world premiere. Director Bianchi Hanuse’s film will land on the streamer in 2027 after winning awards at SXSW, Hot Docs and the Sydney Film Festival. Ceremony centers on British Columbia’s Nuxalk Nation as it looks to restore the local population of ooligan fish, whose arrival every spring sustains the First Nations community and its ritual celebrations. The restoration efforts, including broadcasts from the Nuxalk Radio station, also underline the resilience of the Indigenous community in the face of challenges from climate change and colonialization. “Nuxalkmc [Nuxalk people] asked for this story to be told and that responsibility took 12 years because our truth isn’t an easy one to tell. It’s a story most Canadians have never heard. We made it for us and with Netflix, we’re sharing it beyond our valley,” director Hanuse said in a statement. Related Stories Movies Netflix Acquires Joel Coen's 'Jack of Spades,' Planning Big Push for Next Oscar Season TV Druski Signs Deal With Netflix, Sets Church Comedy 'Collect & Praise' In Canada , Netflix has acquired earlier Indigenous-themed or directed content, including the late Jeff Barnaby’s Rhymes for Ghouls , Stephen S. Campanelli’s Indian Horse and Miranda de Pencier’s The Grizzlies . In 2024, Netflix acquired the documentary Yintah, which follows Indigenous activists with the Wet’suwet’en First Nation looking to protect their lands and was directed by Michael Toledano, Jennifer Wickham and Brenda Mitchell. Netflix also streams the Arctic-set Indigenous comedy North of North , a co-production with the CBC. That ongoing support for Indigenous movies and creators also comes amid calls by local indie producers and other cultural nationalists for Netflix and other U.S. tech giants and foreign players to be subject to the same content expenditure obligations as traditional broadcasters. Ceremony is written by Hanuse and Jessica Mayhew and is produced by Smayaykila Films. THR

articles.title: Like, Subscribe, Graduate: Emerson College Launching Content Creation Major (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All November 2, 2026 9:52am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Henry Winkler speaks at Emerson College's 2026 commencement ceremony in Boston. Photo by Lisa Aileen Dragani/Getty Images Communications students matriculating into Emerson College next year will have an entirely new major to choose from: A bachelor of arts in content creation. The Hollywood Reporter has learned that the Boston-based college will launch the new degree program in the fall of 2027. The new degree underscores the rapidly changing dynamics of media, with creator-led platforms like YouTube, TikTok and Instagram continuing to grow at a rapid clip even as traditional film and TV production and distribution seems to be flat or declining. The new major will pull from the school’s existing infrastructure and expertise in areas like storytelling, production and communications while incorporating creator-focused areas of study like marketing, audience development, branding and business strategy, given the owner-operator nature of the creator world. Students will develop original content while studying the business and ethics of digital platforms, while also learning how to reach and engage audiences. “Emerson has long prepared students for success in emerging creative industries with a focus on hands-on, real world application in our academic disciplines and now this new major builds on our tradition by combining creativity, technology and entrepreneurial skills for the next generation,” said Emerson president Jay Bernhardt. Emerson, which is among THR’s 25 best film schools of 2026, has an envious alumni list that includes former Warner Bros. film co-chief Pamela Abdy, filmmakers Daniel Kwan and Paul Thomas Anderson, writer Norman Lear and actors like Henry Winkler and Jennifer Coolidge. The bachelor of arts in content creation will be housed in Emerson College’s School of Communication, within the department of strategic marketing and business. “Our new content creation major prepares students to be a part of the evolving creator economy , teaching them not only how to produce compelling digital content but also how to build a successful entrepreneurial career,” said Brenna McCormick, chair of the department of strategic marketing and business. “From digital and financial literacy to business and marketing, this major has the essential ingredients to help students turn their creative visions into something bigger.” THR

articles.title: Marc Maron to Be Honored With Inaugural Richard Lewis Award at Comedy Gives Back Gala
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All November 2, 2026 10:47am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Marc Maron attends the AFI Los Angeles premiere of 20th Century Studios' 'Springsteen: Deliver Me From Nowhere' at Hollywood's TCL Chinese Theater on Oct. 22, 2025. (Photo by Jesse Grant/Getty Images for 20th Century Studios) Comedy Gives Back — a nonprofit founded by Jodi Lieberman, Amber J. Lawson and Zoe Friedman to provide a safety net for the comedy community — is finding another way to do so by launching its first ever gala in honor of the late Richard Lewis . The Richard Lewis Humor & Humanity Gala, dubbed “a night of comedy and neurosis,” is set to take place at Hollywood Improv in Los Angeles on Nov. 15. The organization will present an inaugural trophy that night as well, also called the Richard Lewis Humor & Humanity Award, in honor of his legacy and his years-long commitment to uplifting his peers. They’ve settled on the first recipient, Marc Maron , who will be feted at the event, which will be hosted by Jeff Garlin and feature Nick Kroll as a presenter. Related Stories News Jeff Garlin Considered Suicide After Tumultuous 'Goldbergs' Exit General News Publicist Emily Vespa Joins Birch Public Relations “Richard Lewis was one of a kind. He was fearless, painfully honest and could make you laugh about the things most people are afraid to talk about. To receive an award in his name is incredibly meaningful, especially knowing it supports comedians who need help,” said Maron in a statement. Lewis, who passed away at age 76 in February 2024, was an early supporter of Comedy Gives Back and he served as a member of the org’s board. The fundraiser will host comedy and entertainment insiders while raising money for the mission of providing financial assistance, mental health resources and addiction recovery support for comedians in need. “Richard wasn’t just a comedy legend. He was our friend and an early champion of Comedy Gives Back. We couldn’t imagine a more fitting first honoree than Marc Maron. This evening is about celebrating Richard’s incredible legacy while continuing his commitment to taking care of the comedy community,” said co-founders Lieberman, Lawson and Friedman in a joint statement. Maron, a veteran stand-up and actor, launched his podcast WTF With Marc Maron in 2009. After 16 years, he stepped away to focus on other endeavors like his acting career. He stars in Stick and recently appeared in the Bruce Springsteen biopic, Deliver Me From Nowhere. Comedy Gives Back’s Richard Lewis Humor & Humanity Gala is being sponsored by HBO and the Johnny Carson Foundation. More intel can be found here . THR
