articles.title: Sacha Baron Cohen Talks Tarantino, AI & Why Undercover Comedy ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Will Be His Last — Comedy Means Business Podcast
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Newsom’s November Surprise: Boost CA Film & TV Tax Incentives To $1B ASAP, Says Exiting Governor Read the full story By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Stephen McKinley Henderson To Topline Crime Drama ‘Anglers’ From Debut Filmmaker Zoe Simone Sacha Baron Cohen Talks Tarantino, AI & Why Undercover Comedy ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Will Be His Last — Comedy Means Business Podcast Isabela Merced & Patrick Schwarzenegger To Play Lorena And John Bobbitt In Hulu’s ‘Good American Family’ Anthology View All November 2, 2026 10:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source There’s an apocryphal quote attributed to the late, great George Carlin: “It’s the duty of the comedian to find out where the line is drawn and cross it deliberately.” If that’s true, few have crossed it more frequently—or more fearlessly—than Sacha Baron Cohen . Very few, also, have had the global impact in feature comedy that he has had. Over the last three decades, Cohen has permeated global pop culture with a range of original characters. In particular, Ali G , his faux-streetwise cultural appropriator from Staines-upon-Thames, and Borat, his blundering Kazakh journalist, have helped drive cultural conversation, even as the work has provoked backlash in equal measure to laughter. Related Stories News Jack Lowden On James Bond & Gary Oldman's 007 Endorsement: "It's All Very Flattering" News 'The Man With The Bag' Trailer: Arnold Schwarzenegger & Alan Ritchson Star In Amazon MGM's Christmas Heist Caper Inclined until recently to let his characters speak for themselves, Cohen has generally taken the public’s response in stride, committed to the goal of helping to “make a slightly more tolerant society” through satire. A master of disguise, whose disruptive influence on comedy dates back to ’90s London, his M.O. has been to send meticulously crafted, memorably buffoonish characters careening through the real world. The goal? To expose the assumptions, prejudices and absurdities of those interacting with them in the real world — whether on the right or left, in a position of tremendous power or someone off the street. Watch on Deadline The work that goes into these films, and the stakes behind them are immense; repeatedly, across projects, Cohen has put his life on the line for the sake of a joke. Naturally, then, he’s spoken on more than one occasion about retiring from his work in undercover comedy. He makes the claim, once again, while discussing his latest feature, Ali G: Who Iz I? — his first film centered on the character in more than 20 years, and his first as director. If this is indeed Cohen’s last outing with his experimental form of filmmaking, he’s gone out with a bang. He calls Who Iz I? his “most extreme and ambitious” movie to date — his version of The Avengers , as a film in which he inhabit multiple of his characters. Not just his breakout character, Ali G, but also two of his creations for Showtime series Who Is America? : the obnoxious ultra-liberal Dr. Nira Cain-N’Degeocello, who becomes the Dr. Evil to Ali G’s Austin Powers, as well as the Israeli anti-terrorism expert Erran Morad. (Notably, Cohen even consulted with Christopher Markus and Stephen McFeely, the screenwriters behind Avengers: Endgame and myriad other MCU projects, in constructing his narrative.) Released last month, Who Iz I? finds Ali G resurfacing decades after the cancellation of Da Ali G Show when he learns that his girlfriend Julie (Morgana Robinson) is pregnant and he must find a way to support his family. When Nira Cain-N’Degeocello learns of the return of the “white culture appropriator,” he makes it his mission to get him canceled. The film culminates in a sequence shot continuously over eight hours and 12 locations, involving nearly 200 crew members and hundreds of carefully choreographed beats. To achieve it, Cohen brought in specialists in prosthetics, animatronics and explosives, alongside magicians and world-famous psychologists. “The end scene is, according to [VFX supervisor] Rob Legato, the most difficult scene ever shot,” Cohen tells me on today’s episode of Comedy Means Business , “and he worked on Titanic .” On this week’s podcast, Cohen shares the backstory behind his decision to bring Ali G back, before getting into the extreme prep that’s made his films possible. We also discuss his career beginnings, and how his early academic work and lifelong interest in identity have fueled his films from Ali G Indahouse on — works whose intentions can be easily misinterpreted, which have more on their mind than some give them credit for. Explaining how each of his character comedies has been approached with a different genre in mind — Who Iz I? is a fugitive thriller — Cohen talks pressing through fear on set, navigating the online discourse around his work, and the unsettling recent “move towards the acceptance of political violence” that inspired his latest film. Also: his studies under iconic French clowning guru Philippe Gaulier, who passed away this year; his concerns surrounding AI; mastering sword fighting for his new play The Popinjay Cavalier , marking a long-in-the-works collaboration with Quentin Tarantino; and more. Check out the full conversation by clicking above. articles.title: Sandy Frank Dies: Legendary Distributor & ‘Name That Tune’ Producer Was 97
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Newsom’s November Surprise: Boost CA Film & TV Tax Incentives To $1B ASAP, Says Exiting Governor Read the full story By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter Druski Strikes Deal With Netflix Ahead Of ‘Collect & Praise’ Launch HBO’s ‘Big Little Lies’ Kicks Off Production On Season 3, Sort Of Paramount+ Names Damla Dogan As Unscripted Chief View All November 2, 2026 11:21am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sandy Frank Courtesy Sandy Frank , the veteran TV distributor and producer, has died at the age of 97. Frank is best known for producing and distributing game shows such as Name That Tune and The Dating Game as well as bringing Japanese monster movies to the United States. Starting out as a sales executive for Paramount Pictures in the late 1940s, Frank went on to work at NBC before becoming President of Worldwide Sales at Wrather Corporation, which produced and distributed Lassie and Lone Ranger. He subsequently launched Sandy Frank Program Sales, where he sold series including You Asked For It before also moving into production with Sandy Frank Entertainment (SFE). Related Stories News John Leeson Dies: Actor Who Voiced Iconic Role In 'Doctor Who' Was 83 News Marty Erlichman Dies: Barbra Streisand's Longtime Manager Was 97 Series he worked on included Name That Tune, Face The Music, The Parent Game and The Dating Game. Watch on Deadline Sandy Frank Entertainment also produced Battle of the Planets , a U.S. adaptation of the Japanese anime series Science Ninja Team Gatchaman, after discovering the series at Mip TV in Cannes. The series was an after-school hit throughout the 1970s. He was also well known for bringing other Japanese content to the U.S. including the Gamera films with a number of them including Fugitive Alien and Time of the Apes appearing on Mystery Science Theater 3000. Well known as a syndicator and distributor, Frank also funded a children’s orphanage in Cannes and would regularly arrange for Mip attendees, including buyers, to attend the orphanage during the market. “For over 50 years, SFE was synonymous with a take no prisoners style of television sales. Mr. Frank was a bigger-than-life TV executive. To say he was unrelenting and tenacious would be an understatement. The lengths Mr. Frank would go to make a sale were legendary [even] if it meant forcing a plane to land to get to a meeting or being relentlessly persistent until the TV station program buyer finally surrendered and made a deal,” said Frank’s longtime collaborator Bob Cohen. “Sandy Frank was the opposite character of the schlepper salesman Billy Loman in Death of a Salesman . Mr. Frank cut a glamorous style of a TV executive jet-setting around the globe, usually with the arm of a beautiful lady companion. Handsome, lean, fashionable, Mr. Frank left an indelible mark on modern TV production and distribution.” Frank’s proudest moment was acquiring the rights to Anwar Sadat’s autobiography with Sadat , the miniseries, produced in 1983 by Columbia Pictures with Frank becoming the first Jew to address the Egyptian Parliament. The executive also championed the cause of independent TV production by fighting the repeal of the Prime-Time Access Rule (PTAR). The PTAR limited the hours the networks could program, benefiting independent producers. “For those of us who loved him, he was caustic, manic, tough, generous, smart, fearless, sensitive, and a genius. He truly was one-of-a-kind, and his gravestone will read America’s Best TV Syndicator,” added Cohen. articles.title: Trump Lawsuit Against Wall Street Journal Over Epstein Story Dismissed by Judge
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By The Associated Press Plus Icon The Associated Press View All October 31, 2026 5:01pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Donald Trump Courtesy of Getty Saying the president was “grasping at straws,” a federal judge on Saturday threw out Donald Trump ’s $10 billion lawsuit against The Wall Street Journal and media mogul Rupert Murdoch over a story reporting on his ties to Jeffrey Epstein . U.S. District Judge Darrin Gayles in Miami dismissed the suit with prejudice, ruling that the president did not prove the defendants made defamatory statements with actual malice as required by law. The ruling said the lawsuit had attempted to “manufacture” flaws in the Journal ’s investigative reporting. Related Stories TV Bill Maher Responds to Trump's 1,318-Word Social Rant: "He Went Off on Me Like Kelly Clarkson in a Toy Store" Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) When a case is thrown out “with prejudice,” it cannot be refiled again and the dismissal is permanent and incontrovertible. The dismissal is a blow to Trump and his administration, which have both pursued adversarial relationships with news organizations during his second term. In addition to the Journal, he is embroiled in lawsuits involving the BBC, The Associated Press and — most recently — CNN, MS NOW and Politico, which are suing him for restored access after he banished them from the White House in mid-September. Trump has denounced media outlets that write things to which he objects and frequently calls them “fake news” and insults their journalists. Trump called the reporting ‘malicious’ The lawsuit against the Journal was over a story it published last year describing a sexually suggestive letter and drawing that the paper said bore Trump’s name and was included in a 2003 album compiled for Epstein’s 50th birthday. The letter was reportedly collected by disgraced British socialite Ghislaine Maxwell as part of a birthday album for Epstein years before he was first arrested in 2006 and subsequently had a falling-out with Trump. The letter bearing Trump’s name includes text framed by the outline of what appears to be a hand-drawn naked woman and ends with, “Happy Birthday — and may every day be another wonderful secret,” according to the newspaper. Trump denied writing it and called the story “false, malicious, and defamatory.” The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Miami, accused the paper and its reporters of having “knowingly and recklessly” published “numerous false, defamatory, and disparaging statements,” which, it alleged, caused “overwhelming financial and reputational harm” to the president. Epstein died by suicide in a New York jail cell in August 2019 while awaiting trial on federal sex trafficking charges. The lawsuit was dismissed once, then refiled Gayles previously dismissed the suit in April, saying Trump had failed to make the argument that the article was published with the intent to be malicious. But he gave the president a chance to file an amended complaint, which he did in May. In Saturday’s ruling, the judge cited the Supreme Court’s landmark 1964 ruling in New York Times Co. v. Sullivan. That decision made it harder for public figures to win libel lawsuits because it requires proof that a media outlet knowingly published something false or showed a reckless disregard for the truth. “The Amended Complaint falls short of pleading actual malice,” Gayles wrote. “Indeed, the allegations regarding malice are conclusory, vague, sometimes inconsistent with the Article, and often irrelevant to whether Defendants knew or should have known that the statements in the Article were purportedly false.” The judge also noted that the Journal’s story did not ignore or minimize Trump’s denial, “Rather, it informed readers that President Trump decried the Letter as a fake and denied writing it.” Gayles also said several other allegations in the lawsuit did not have merit. THR

articles.title: ‘Green Room’ Director Recalls How Patrick Stewart “Saved” Movie From Being Scrapped
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 31, 2026 5:13pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Patrick Stewart and Macon Blair in 'Green Room.' Scott Green/A24/Courtesy Everett Collection Logo text Green Room director Jeremy Saulnier paid tribute to Patrick Stewart ahead of a Los Angeles screening of the film on Friday, recalling how the sci-fi icon “just swooped down, nosedived into our cruddy ass movie and saved us.” Celebrating the film’s 10th anniversary, Saulnier addressed the crowd and noted Stewart’s death at 86. “Who’s sad as fuck we lost Patrick Stewart yesterday? Me,” he said in a video posted on the Film Updates X account. “I came here to shamelessly promote Slayground , but instead, I’m just gonna celebrate Patrick Stewart. He had no business doing this movie. He every option to do otherwise.” Related Stories Movies Before 'Star Trek,' Patrick Stewart Proved His Sci-Fi Chops in 'Dune' Critic's Appreciation Patrick Stewart's Career Was a Rare and Thrilling Marriage of the Prestigious and the Populist The director remembered how production on Green Room was “at the point of no return, building sets, and under the gun without Darcy,” noting that the lead character of Darcy Banker had not yet been cast. However, that’s when the Star Trek star came in. “We’re fucked, and we were close to shutting down. And Patrick Stewart, out of the blue, sort of expressed interest in the project,” Saulnier said. “And in a whirlwind, about a week later, I was on the phone with him. I left the stage [thinking,] ‘Maybe we’re gonna have to break down the sets and shut the whole movie down.’ Instead, this dude came out of nowhere, from way above our sort of zone, and just swooped down, nosedived into our cruddy ass movie and saved us, and said yes. And the movie was instantly greenlit.” “We moved forward, and I thank him for just taking that leap and making Green Room a thing,” he added. “Patrick Stewart is why I still can make movies. He saved the day. Too good to be true.” The Rebel Ridge director remembered Stewart as a “fucking sweetheart, true gentleman, [who was a] very kind leader to our whole cast.” He also shared a story about how one day, the actor came to him and said he “wanted to add a little something” to a scene. “I was like, ‘What is it, Patrick?’ He’s like, ‘Well, during this one part of the scene, when the camera’s coming through there, I’d like to say, fuck!’ And I was like, ‘And?’ ‘Just fuck.’ I was like. ‘Permission granted, sir,’” Saulnier recounted. “And I just knew that he was completely aligned with the film, its aesthetic, its intentions and with me as a filmmaker, and it was just this lovely, lovely thing.” Stewart died Wednesday at his home in Los Angeles following “a brief and poignant journey with Alzheimer’s disease and Lewy body dementia,” longtime spokesperson Kelly Bush Novak announced. After his death, his former co-stars and Hollywood notables shared an outpouring of tributes . Among those who have paid homage to the X-Men star are Ian McKellen, Kevin Feige, William Shatner, Seth MacFarlane, Hugh Jackman, Minnie Driver, Rebecca Romijn, Halle Berry and James Marsden, among many others. THR

articles.title: Tovah Feldshuh Shuts Down ‘Nobody Wants This’ Cast Tension Rumors Amid Adam Brody “Free Palestine” Support
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 31, 2026 6:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tovah Feldshuh and Adam Brody. Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images, Amy Sussman/Getty Images Logo text Nobody Wants This actress Tovah Feldshuh is shutting down claims that tensions are rising among the cast amid recent comments Adam Brody made saying he is in support of “a free Palestine.” “Tensions are NOT RISING. Profound differences of opinion are. Please do not conflate the two — And none of it will be brought to the set,” she wrote in response to a Threads post made by AzatTV that reads, “Tensions are emerging on the set of the Netflix series Nobody Wants This .” Feldshuh added, “I deeply enjoy filming [ Nobody Wants This ] and hope we are chosen to go on for a fourth season.” Related Stories TV 'Nobody Wants This' Star Condemns Adam Brody's Gaza "Genocide" Comments TV 'Nobody Wants This' Season 3 Explained: Does Joanne Finally Convert to Judaism? What Happens to Morgan and Sasha? In an interview with GQ , Brody said of the war in Gaza, “put me down as thinking it’s a genocide. Put me down as wanting a free Palestine.” He added, “It’s awful that it’s taken so much death and misery, but it does feel like it’s reaching a breaking point that it should have a while ago.” Feldshuh, who plays the mother of Brody’s character Noah on the Netflix show, told The New York Post of the actor’s comments, “To accuse the Jewish people of genocide is wild.” She added, “It’s right out of Hitler’s playbook. You take the victim and you make the victim the perpetrator.” The actress said that it “makes a difference to the [Jewish] community,” when asked by the Post if “accusations of genocide are worse when they come from Jewish people themselves.” “I believe that the perseverance of the existence of the state of Israel is crucial to the well-being of the democratic world and of the free world,” Feldshuh said. “Of course, Israel needs the United States, [but] the United States needs Israel, believe you me.” Feldshuh also told the outlet, “My job, as Bina but also as Tovah, is to love the people on set at my place of work, to be kind.” She added, “With the backdrop of global antisemitism, I am thrilled to be chosen to play a Jewish matriarch. Thrilled and proud, and that will never change.” Erin Foster, creator of Nobody Wants This , has also reacted to Brody’s statement, saying on the Not Skinny But Not Fat podcast that “it’s complicated.” “I think our work environment, our set is very similar to dinner tables around the world where people are having debate and discussion and disagreeing,” Foster said. “While I love Adam, I also disagree with him, and that’s okay.” “I think that as the creator of the show, all I can say is that I want our Jewish fans to know that I see you and I hear you and I understand how you feel,” she continued. “And the show has always been and always will be a love letter to Judaism. That is why I made this show. It’s because of how beautiful of an experience I’ve had becoming Jewish and being a Jewish person, and sitting here right now at this time in the world where there is almost zero positive representation of Jewish people, I think it’s so important to have that.” “That being said, everyone is entitled to a different opinion than me. I can just tell you what I created this show for, what the intention of the show is,” Foster concluded. THR

articles.title: ‘SNL’: Inde Navarrette Digs at Shane Gillis’ Joke About Women Dressing Like “Whores” at the Gym as Tom Hanks Crashes Cold Open
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 31, 2026 8:54pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Inde Navarrette Screenshot Logo text Inde Navarrette made her Saturday Night Live hosting debut on the show’s Halloween episode, and kicked things off with a dig at the most recent host of the late night series. The actress began her monologue by referencing her star-making role in Obsession : “You probably know me from the movie Obsession . People ask me if I’m anything like my character Nikki, and I’m like, no. No, no, don’t do that.” “But the thing is, I’m nothing like my character in Obsession . Like, my boyfriend is here tonight to support me,” she said, as the camera panned over to her boyfriend, Nick Aiello, duck-taped in the audience. “We have such a chill relationship, right?” Related Stories News LAPD Arrests Two for Murder of Christina Downer, Sister to 'SNL' Writer Jimmy Fowlie Movies Santa Barbara Film Fest: Inde Navarrette, Jaafar Jackson Among Eight Tapped for Virtuoso Awards Navarrette went on to discuss how she’ll be next portraying Rogue in Marvel Studios’ X-Men reboot . The character preps requires a lot of working out, she noted. “I can’t believe I’m saying this, but I’m gonna be in a Marvel movie. I know it’s really important for Marvel that you get really fit, so I’ve been working out a lot.” “So every morning, I put on my little whore outfit, and I hit the gym,” she said, in a callback to Shane Gillis’ controversial monologue on the most recent episode of SNL on Oct. 10. During his SNL appearance, he said at the top of the episode, “I haven’t been to the gym in so long, I didn’t know women just dress like whores now. Look, I’m sorry, there’s no other way to describe. Have you seen it? I’ve seen it. You’ve seen the shorts? They’re those neon, like, artificial vape-colored [shorts], and the wrinkles go around the cheeks and all combine at the butthole. And don’t look, you’re not allowed to look!” Continuing with her monologue, Navarrette invited the SNL cast to the stage to show off their Halloween costumes “since none of the cast could go out tonight.” Marcello Hernandez appeared as “a sexy TSA agent,” as Kam Patterson portrayed Elizabeth Holmes. Jeremy Culhane also joined, using his time during Navarrette’s monologue as an audition for Jake Schreier’s upcoming X-Men movie. “I know you were cast as Rogue in the new X-Men movie, and I randomly heard they, like, I guess they haven’t even cast Wolverine yet,” Culhane said, to which Navarrette replied, “Oh, I’m so sorry. I can’t comment on that.” “Well, I can, and I’d love to be in the movie with you,” Culhane, dressed as Wolverine, said. Grace Reiter then joined dressed up as none other than the bird at the center of the viral Kelly Clarkson, Art of Play controversy . “It’s actually a group costume,” Reiter said, as Veronika Slowikowska popped in dressed like American Idol winner. “I want to buy the bird,” she said. “Sell me the damn bird!” “I am not for sale!” Reiter as the bird said. Inde Navarrette's monologue! pic.twitter.com/l4KCxVpyfS — Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) November 1, 2026 Tom Hanks’ classic Halloween character David S. Pumpkins made a surprise appearance in the cold open, opened by Reiter and Culhane as they embarked on a spooky ride. James Austin Johnson’s Trump, of course, crashed the party to discuss the upcoming midterms. “Are you sad you don’t get to see your third David Pumpkins scene? I’ll send you four minutes. He keeps popping up and confusing the people on the ride. ‘But you don’t actually have a lot in common with Mr. Pumpkins.’ We both appeared in 2016. We’re both very loud, very orange, and very frankly annoying,” Johnson’s Trump said. “Good acting, great ass. A great ass on Hanks — something that I’ve enjoyed lately admiring,” he added. “Not that there’s anything wrong with that. Just that I might be gay.” He was joined by Nicki Minaj (“my friend and future press secretary”), portrayed by Saidah Belo-Osagie, who showed her support for the president. “Trump’s out here killing it — and by it, I mean my career,” Belo-Osagie said. “I’m Nicki, the Trumpy. Like, I don’t even know why you Democrats bother at this point. Like, give it up. It’s me,” she added before exiting the stage. “Thank you, Nicki. She’s got quite an ass. If only it were on a man, perhaps then I could admire it,” Johnson’s Trump said. And Slowikowska also appeared as Katie Zacharia, Trump’s brief, former White House Press Secretary, to butcher SNL ’s opening catchphrase, “Live from New York, it’s Saturday Night!” She instead said, “With confidence. Live from New York. And from so many cities,” before she was cut off. history’s most heinous, homicidal haunts pic.twitter.com/udeRgaZLhw — Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) November 1, 2026 Pumpkins wasn’t the only character of SNL ‘s past to pop up, as Bobby Moynihan’s Drunk Uncle appeared during the Weekend Update segment. He was even joined by the Milwaukee Brewers, the 2026 World Series champions. Christian Yelich, Brice Turang and team manager Pat Murphy were on hand to rep for the winning team. Moynihan even joked that Yelich was Pete Davidson. Navarrette rose to acclaim this summer for her starring turn in Curry Barker’s new horror hit. She plays Nikki Freeman, a woman who is cursed after Bear (Michael Johnston) wishes that she’d love him more than anyone else in the world. The low-budget film grossed over $522 million worldwide, breaking a plethora of records along the way: Obsession is Focus Features‘ biggest movie of all time; is the top-grossing festival acquisition (hailing from TIFF); and earned the biggest second-weekend box office spike in modern times outside of the Christmas holiday. She’ll next star in Marvel Studios’ X-Men reboot, Apple Original Films’ sci-fi thriller The Waffle House Index , which she will also executive produce. Saturday night marked Navarrette’s SNL debut, and she was joined by Gracie Abrams as musical guest. Elsewhere on season 52 , Jalen Brunson , Dakota Johnson and Gillis have hosted. After the Obsession actress, Druski will host on Nov. 7; he is the first social media influencer to ever host SNL . The Strokes will be the musical guest. John Mulaney will host the Nov. 14 episode, and he’ll be joined by Phoebe Bridgers. Before Saturday night’s episode, SNL shared a tribute for Patrick Stewart, featuring a clip from his 1994 appearance on the show. THR

articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Crashes Into Tokyo Film Festival With Stars Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe in Tow
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All November 1, 2026 1:57am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Godzilla Minus Zero, Godzilla, 2026. GKIDS/Courtesy Everett Collection The King of Monsters finally stomped his way into Japan ’s largest celebration of cinema on Sunday as Takashi Yamazaki ’s wildly anticipated Godzilla Minus Zero played to a packed pair of screenings at the Tokyo International Film Festival. The sold-out shows easily drew the liveliest crowds of this year’s Tokyo festival — the latest Toho -backed monster epic doesn’t open commercially in Japan until Nov. 3 — with numerous die-hard kaiju fans attending in costume or carrying their own Gojira figurines into the theater. Related Stories Music Macklemore Wraps Up Free Palestine Tour in London: "It Was More Uncomfortable for Me to Stay Silent" Movies 'Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting' Review: Whimsical Chinese Film Explores Myth and History Through a Series of Tasty Treats Godzilla Minus Zero is playing as the “centerpiece film” of the Tokyo festival’s programming this year, and it undoubtedly brought a welcome jolt of energy to the event as it moves through its second half. When the credits rolled on the second screening inside Hulic Hall Tokyo, the crowd erupted into uncharacteristically rapturous applause, with the always respectful but typically subdued Japanese festivalgoers all smiles and excited chatter over favorite monster moments as they poured into the autumn evening in Tokyo’s Ginza district — where much of the carnage on screen takes place. Godzilla Minus Zero is a direct follow-up to Godzilla Minus One (2023), which Yamazaki famously wrote, directed and VFX-supervised. The film was a smash with both critics and mainstream moviegoers, making history as the highest-grossing live-action Japanese film ever in North America ($57.1 million) and later becoming the first film in the multi-decade Godzilla franchise to take home an Oscar, winning the best visual effects award despite competing in the category against Hollywood tentpoles with vastly bigger budgets. The sequel picks up in 1949, two years after the events of Minus One , as Japan struggles to rebuild from the devastation of war and Godzilla’s attack. The Shikishima family’s hard-won peace is threatened by a new calamity, with the film also bringing iconic franchise rival King Ghidorah, the three-headed kaiju, into Yamazaki’s postwar world. Yamazaki’s return to the helm for the follow-up has lifted expectations across the globe — and the critical response so far, along with the enthusiastic reception at home in Tokyo on Sunday, suggests he delivered. Godzilla Minus Zero premiered in September at the New York Film Festival, where The Hollywood Reporter ’s chief critic David Rooney gave it a rave , calling the film a “radioactive blast” and “a crackling kaiju epic every bit as exciting as its predecessor.” The movie currently holds a score of 92 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 52 reviews. Godzilla Minus Zero ’s two leads, Ryunosuke Kamiki and Minami Hamabe, took the stage to introduce the Tokyo festival screenings and share a few words with fans. Kamiki told the audience he was both “excited” and “a little bit scared” because he could “feel people’s anticipation building as the film’s opening is now very close.” Hamabe added that the first film was so “beloved by fans all over the world, that now for the sequel, well, we need it to be even bigger and better.” “I’m just curious to see how people will receive it,” she added. ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ stars Ryunosuke Kamiki, Sae Nagatani and Minami Hamabe. The duo then welcomed to the stage child actress Sae Nagatani, who plays their characters’ adopted daughter, Akiko. “Together, we play the Shikishima family, and that wouldn’t be complete without our Akiko,” Kamiki said as the little girl joined them and said hello to the audience. “Having a family usually makes us stronger, but it can also make us vulnerable,” Kamiki then said, launching into a bit of plot preview. “[Our family] is trying to always think of family first. But when Godzilla appears, we have to try to protect the family and that leads to some very hard decisions.” Added Hamabe: “I’m very happy to to have met you all here today, and I hope you will enjoy the story of what happens to the Shikishima family — and also, the Godzilla experience, of course!” GKIDS opens Godzilla Minus Zero in cinemas across North America on Nov. 6, following Imax early-access screenings on Nov. 3. THR

articles.title: Netflix’s New Releases Coming in November 2026
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All November 1, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clockwise from top left: 'NFL Netflix Gameday,' 'Possible Love,' 'The Hunting Wives,' 'The Altruists,' 'The Mosquito Bowl,' 'Cunk on Cinema,' 'Black Doves,' and 'Allen.' Jevone Moore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images; Netflix New seasons of Netflix hits Black Doves and The Hunting Wives ; an Aussie alien comedy from the makers of Bluey; a Julia Garner-led dramatic retelling of the rise and fall of crypto empire FTX; Lee Chang-dong’s critically acclaimed Oscar frontrunner; Philomena Cunk explaining the power of cinema; and football, both real and imagined, with the NFL and Peter Berg’s latest film are just some of the highlights of the new film and TV projects hitting Netflix in November. Returning for a second season on Nov. 5, is Netflix’s hit series Black Doves . Something of a sexier version of Slow Horses , Black Doves is another spy drama set in London and stars Keira Knightley, Ben Wishaw and the always incredible Sarah Lancashire. The action in season 2 picks up after the event of the first season, with “Helen (Knightley) is still betraying her nation’s secrets to the covert organisation she serves: the Black Doves. But after the misadventures of last Christmas, and with her husband Wallace (Andrew Buchan), preparing to become Prime Minister, she is walking a more treacherous line than ever.” Related Stories Business Japan's Anime Industry Hits a Record High of $28 Billion in 2025 TV Donald Glover Writing, Starring in 'PUBG' Video Game Adaptation in the Works at Netflix Netflix launches arguably its best shot at an Oscar in 2027 on Nov. 6 with Lee Chang-dong’s Possible Love . The long-awaited film from the Korean auteur behind the modern classic Burning , Possible Love debuted at the Venice Film Festival this year where it won the Silver Lion. The film has been praised to the high heavens by critics, and currently boasts a whopping 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes, 95 on Metacritic and 4.2 on Letterboxd. Hmmm, sounds like a must-see. A logline for the film reads: “A story of two married couples — a laid-off worker and his spouse and a documentary filmmaker and her spouse — crossing paths to film a documentary and facing their different lives and hidden desires.” A potential palate cleanser to the highbrow filmmaking of Possible Love is Jeffrey Walker’s Allen that debuts on Nov. 12. An Australian original film, Allen tells the story of a man wistfully longing for the return of the alien he met as a child, and his life turned upside down when he returns. The comedy feature comes from Ludo Studio (yes, the people behind Bluey !) so the Aussie creative team leans into the silly humor. On Nov. 15, Philomena Cunk is back with more musings on how the world works. This time, our intrepid Philomena takes on the topic of the movies, in Cunk on Cinema . In six episodes, Cunk traces the history of the moving image and its impact on society and culture. Along the way, the grills the likes of Michael Bay and Benedict Cumberbatch, so much so they are left flummoxed . Diane Morgan returns of Cunk and the series is written by Black Mirror’s Charlie Brooker. Watch it! You won’t regret it. On Nov. 18, Netflix unveils its big, potentially discourse-shaping, limited series The Altruists . The latest tech-bros-suck project to hit the timeline, the eight-episode gets inside the rise and spectacular falls of the founders of crypto empire FTX. The series synopsis reads: “The story of Sam Bankman-Fried and Caroline Ellison, two hyper-smart, ambitious young idealists who tried to remake the global financial system in the blink of an eye – before they were accused of stealing $8 billion and became Gen Z’s own Bonnie & Clyde.” Emmy-winner Julia Garner plays Caroline and Anthony Boyle plays Sam. The show is created, written and showrun by Oscar-winner Graham Moore. Netflix’s big Hollywood movie release for November is Peter Berg’s The Mosquito Bowl , which debuts on a big day for football on the streamer. Launching on Nov. 25th, the film is based on Buzz Bissinger’s 2022 nonfiction book The Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II about the legendary bowl game. The synopsis reads: “Following the attack on Pearl Harbor, four of America’s top college football stars set their fame aside to enlist in the Marines. As they prepare for the brutal invasion of Okinawa, they’ll play in a legendary game featuring some of the greatest players in history — a game that, for many, will be the last they ever play.” The film stars Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis. The film is something of a Friday Night Lights reunion with the involvement of Berg, Bissinger, producer Brian Grazer and the music provided by Explosions in the Sky. It’s the big one on Nov. 25. NFL Netflix Gameday: Thanksgiving Eve will see the Packers play the Rams at the SoFi Stadium and it will be NFL’s first-ever Thanksgiving Eve matchup. Netflix and the league are taking this one really seriously and are looking to establish it as a key date in the TV calendar, so they’ve pushed the boat out and hired U2 to provide the halftime entertainment. And finally, Nov. 26 will see the return of the ludicrously entertaining series, The Hunting Wives . Malin Akerman’s Margo and Brittany Snow’s Sophie are back and up to no good once more, but at the start of season 2 “Sophie and Margo are on the outs. But soon enough, old secrets and new foes force them back together. As they play their dangerous games, the question arises. Are they the hunters or the hunted?” The show has been a huge hit for Netflix and has already been renewed for a third season. Movies added to Netflix in November include A Sudden Case of Christmas, Air Force One, Barbie in the Nutcracker, The Best Christmas Pageant Ever, Bridesmaids, Cliffhanger, The Croods, The Day After Tomorrow, Fury, Ghosting: The Spirit of Christmas, Insidious: Chapter 2, Smile, Insidious, Insidious: Chapter 3, Looper, The Mummy, No Sleep ‘Til Christmas, Public Enemies, Resident Evil, Resident Evil: Apocalypse, Richard Jewell, Same Time, Next Christmas, Stand by Me, Weekend at Bernie’s, Misty Green, Pressure, The Super Mario Galaxy Movie and Whiplash . articles.title: Heidi Klum Dressed Up as a Severed Human Hand for Her Annual Halloween Party
articles.full_text: × Oct 31, 2026 8:12pm PT Heidi Klum Dressed Up as a Severed Human Hand for Her Annual Halloween Party By Tanya Fedak Plus Icon Tanya Fedak Latest Heidi Klum Dressed Up as a Severed Human Hand for Her Annual Halloween Party 12 hours ago Netflix’s ‘Cliff Booth’ Won’t Play in Regal and Cinemark Imax Theaters 2 days ago Netflix’s ‘Haunted Hotel’ Renewed for Season 3 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images for Heidi Klum Is it really Halloween without Heidi Klum ? The supermodel, who has become known for her over-the-top costumes, has returned for another year of her annual Halloween party, this time opting to dress as a realistic-looking severed human hand. At last year’s party, Klum dressed as the mythological monster Medusa, which featured a headpiece decorated with writhing snakes and a trailing tail, while her husband, Tom Kaulitz, went as an ancient Greek soldier she had turned to stone. It ultimately took a team of 15 artists to create her costume, Klum told Variety at the 2025 event . Related Stories Paul Bettany Says He ‘Blew Out’ 10 Blood Vessels in His Eye While Filming ‘VisionQuest’: ‘I Was Just Wildly Overacting’ Joshua Jackson Teases ‘Sex, Drugs and Rock 'n' Roll’ in New HBO Max Series ‘How to Survive Without Me’: ‘I'm Getting Too Old For This S---’ “There still needs to be people that create moments with real people … to me, it’s like a beautiful art,” she said. When asked about her elaborate look, she shared, “This is only good for the night. Tonight. Everything goes down the drain, so to speak, in the shower.” This year’s celebration marked the 25th year of Klum’s Halloween party. Some of her past looks include notable characters such as E.T., Fiona from “Shrek,” Jessica Rabbit and the werewolf from Michael Jackson’s “Thriller,” as well as creatures like a peacock, worm and butterfly. Earlier this year, Klum hosted the 22nd season of “Project Runway,” where she also served as a judge alongside Nina Garcia and Law Roach. Klum returned to the fashion competition series last year after previously exiting in 2018. Prior to her departure, she hosted the show for 16 seasons since its 2004 debut on Bravo. Alongside Tim Gunn, Klum created a new fashion competition show titled “Making the Cut” for Prime Video in 2020, which ran for three seasons. articles.title: ‘SNL’ Cold Open Crashed by Tom Hanks as David S. Pumpkins, Nicki Minaj and Donald Trump, Who Admits He ‘Might Be Gay’
articles.full_text: × Oct 31, 2026 9:03pm PT ‘SNL’ Cold Open Crashed by Tom Hanks as David S. Pumpkins, Nicki Minaj and Donald Trump, Who Admits He ‘Might Be Gay’ By William Earl Plus Icon William Earl @beautifulbill Latest ‘SNL’ Cold Open Crashed by Tom Hanks as David S. Pumpkins, Nicki Minaj and Donald Trump, Who Admits He ‘Might Be Gay’ 10 hours ago Martin Scorsese Says His ‘Cleopatra’ Movie With Angelina Jolie Was ‘Ruined’ by Seth Rogen and the Sony Hack: ‘It Was Gonna Be Really Wild’ 2 days ago ‘Christmas at the Kringles’ Director on Mixing Holiday Horror, Humor and Heart With a Cast of Comic Ringers 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source NBC Tom Hanks returned to “Saturday Night Live” on Halloween night to revive his lounge-y David S. Pumpkins character in a cold open that skewered President Trump’s increasingly bizarre comments on the stump and his fixation with men’s physiques. The segment also featured Saidah Belo-Osagie as Nicki Minaj in a spoof of the star’s vocal support for Trump and his MAGA movement. The bit cast Minaj as Trump’s next choice for press secretary, on the heels of Katie Zacharia’s spectacularly quick flame-out in the job earlier this month. Related Stories Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden Revenues Climb 11% to $390 Million Thanks to ‘Harry Potter’ Tour, Increased Production (EXCLUSIVE) J.K. Rowling Claims Trans Activism in the 21st Century Is ‘Elitist,’ Pens Essay Defending Her Views: They ‘Haven’t Changed’ Despite ‘Death, Rape and Torture Threats’ The segment opened with Grace Reiter and Jeremy Culhane as a young couple taking a ride at a low-end amusement park Halloween celebration. Kenan Thompson then pops up in a ghoulish Grim Reaper costume to guide the couple through a series of scary scenes. Pumpkins, the character that Hanks first limned for the show in 2016, popped in with a dorky dance routine accompanied by Mikey Day and a special cameo appearance by former “SNL” trouper Bobby Moynihan. Day and Moynihan wore full-body skeleton jumpers with white face paint. As the ride continued, James Austin Johnson turned up as President Trump, who stepped in to interrupt the ride and lament about Republicans being poised for a thumping in the Nov. 3 midterm election. The segment then went into a string of surprisingly risqué jokes about Trump’s unusual obsession with the butts of candidates that he has been endorsing as he’s hosted a string of campaign rallies in recent weeks. “We both appeared in 2016. We’re both very loud, very orange and, frankly, very annoying,” Johnson as Trump said. “Good acting, great ass. A great ass on Hanks — something that I’ve enjoyed lately admiring. Not that there’s anything wrong with that. Just that I might be gay.” Trump then whined that “the midterms are on Tuesday. The polls say we’re doing very badly — aww aww. They’re saying Texas is turning purple, just like my hand.” Johnson then raised his hand to show a gigantic bruise. Johnson as Trump called Texas’ GOP candidate for the U.S. Senate, Ken Paxton, “an ugly son of a bitch” but urged voters to chose him over Democrat James Talarico. Trump acknowledged that Talarico is “much better looking. What a dynamic ass.” As Trump spoke, the other players in the scene were in freeze mode. Thompson’s Grim Reaper character broke from the scene and rushed past Johnson as Trump. Trump called out “thank you for that donation” to which Thompson replied, “Yeah, you wish, bitch.” Belo-Osagie barreled into the segment as Minaj toward the end as Trump hails her devotion to the cause. “Trump’s out here killing it — and by it, I mean my career,” Belo-Osagie as Minaj said. Trump noted that Minaj is well-known for her curvy rear-end: “Perhaps if it was on a man, I could admire it,” Johnson as Trump remarked. In closing, Trump brought out Zacharia who flubbed her attempt to deliver the signature “SNL” opening line, “Live from New York, it’s Saturday night.” The Halloween installment of “SNL” is hosted by “Obsession” star Inde Navarrette , with Gracie Abrams serving as musical guest. articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Stars Relive Hollywood Ovation and Fan Chants for Yamazaki Takashi at Tokyo Festival
articles.full_text: × Oct 31, 2026 10:18pm PT ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Stars Relive Hollywood Ovation and Fan Chants for Yamazaki Takashi at Tokyo Festival By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Stars Relive Hollywood Ovation and Fan Chants for Yamazaki Takashi at Tokyo Festival 10 hours ago Tokyo Asian Future Drama ‘Jani Be Good’ Probes Silence and Motherhood in a Chinese-Indonesian Family, Marking Ariani Darmawan’s Return 16 hours ago ‘Before the Rain’ Director Milcho Manchevski on Tokyo Competition Title ‘Sister Brother Manhole Cover,’ Whistleblowing and the ‘Death of Beauty’ in Cinema 16 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Naman Ramachandran The cast of “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” brought the glow of a Hollywood standing ovation to the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival on Sunday, two days before Yamazaki Takashi’s follow-up to his Oscar-winning “Godzilla Minus One” opens in Japan. Kamiki Ryunosuke, who returns as lead character Shikishima Koichi, and Hamabe Minami, who reprises the role of his wife Noriko, had flown back to Japan only two days earlier from the film’s premiere at Los Angeles’ TCL Chinese Theatre. Related Stories 'The Mosquito Bowl': How a Parrot Proved to Be Peter Berg's Biggest Challenge ‘It: Welcome to Derry’ Surprise Halloween Episode Drops on HBO Max “The energy was simply extraordinary,” Kamiki said. “Feeling that raw enthusiasm firsthand made me realize all over again just how deeply Godzilla is loved around the world. It was an invaluable experience.” Applause in the 900-seat theater reportedly ran on without a break. Hamabe said the cast later met premiere-goers at an after-party, where many approached them with big smiles to share their reactions. Some had dressed in Godzilla-themed outfits or wore Godzilla badges. The red carpet was open to passersby, Kamiki recalled. Some fans held up large posters and asked for autographs, while chants of the director’s first name broke out from the crowd. “It wasn’t just a polite ‘Takashi,’” he said. “It was like: ‘TAKASHI! HEY, TAKASHI!’ It was roaring.” When Yamazaki went over to sign autographs, the crowd erupted again, leaving Kamiki convinced that “Takashi of the world is truly amazing.” The Tokyo event also marked the first stage appearance of child actor Nagatani Sae, who returns as Shikishima Akiko. Kamiki walked her onstage. In “Minus One,” which aired on Japanese TV’s “Friday Roadshow” on Friday, Akiko’s part consisted mostly of crying or single words such as “Where?” This time, the script gave her full dialogue. “We were like, ‘Really? Can she do this?’” Kamiki said. “But when we got on set, she had all her lines memorized perfectly and delivered them flawlessly.” Hamabe said Nagatani had barely left toddlerhood during the first shoot and was easily frightened by the many adults on set. “So reuniting on this film, I was amazed by how much of a wonderful young girl she had grown into,” she said. “She chatted with us so much, taught me various things, and was very dependable in her acting.” Nagatani said she wasn’t nervous during filming. She recalled Kamiki continuing to rub her back even after the cut was called on a scene in which Akiko cries. She then asked her co-stars how she could become a fine actor while still in elementary school. Kamiki told her she already outshone them both, and said that appearing in both “Minus One” and “Minus Zero” at her age was “an amazing achievement in itself.” According to Kamiki, the new film picks up two years after the events of “Minus One.” “I hope viewers can imagine what those two years were like for them, and see how the family stands together against what comes next,” he said. Hamabe put the gap at two to three years. She said the family had settled into everyday life together before Godzilla resurfaces to threaten it. Asked why the franchise has endured, Kamiki echoed the view of the director and fellow cast members that each Godzilla film mirrors the era in which it is made. “But personally, when I reflect on it, take Godzilla’s existence or the theme music: I cannot even remember when I first heard it or realized, ‘Oh, this is Godzilla’s theme song,’” he said. “It has always been alongside us, which is why I personally think it has remained loved for so long.” Hamabe said that from a human standpoint, Godzilla is overwhelming and impossible to defeat. “Yet, when Godzilla appears, humans unite and stand together to face it,” she said. “I think seeing that human resolve is the first thing that moves people’s hearts.” “Minus One,” the 30th Japanese live-action entry in the Godzilla franchise, grossed more than JPY7.65 billion ($50 million) at the local box office. It became the first Asian production to take home the visual effects prize at the 96th Oscars, and went on to collect more than 50 honors at home and abroad. “Minus Zero” is the first Japanese film to be certified as Filmed for Imax. articles.title: Inde Navarrette Wins Halloween With Penis-Destroying Robot ‘SNL’ Sketch ‘The Inventor’s Wife’
articles.full_text: × Nov 1, 2026 1:33am PT Inde Navarrette Wins Halloween With Penis-Destroying Robot ‘SNL’ Sketch ‘The Inventor’s Wife’ By Marlow Stern Plus Icon Marlow Stern Chief Correspondent Latest Inde Navarrette Wins Halloween With Penis-Destroying Robot ‘SNL’ Sketch ‘The Inventor’s Wife’ 6 hours ago Inde Navarrette Takes Swipe at Shane Gillis During ‘SNL’ Monologue 11 hours ago Bill Maher Fact-Checks Kid Rock After He Compares Abdul El-Sayed to 9/11 Hijackers on ‘Real Time’ 1 day ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source NBC After a pretty weak cold open that was crashed by Tom Hanks’ David S. Pumpkins, Donald Trump (who admitted he “might be gay”) and his MAGA minion Nicki Minaj, and an amusing opening monologue where host Inde Navarrette took a swipe at Shane Gillis , the Halloween edition of “ Saturday Night Live ” aired a surprisingly fun sketch called “The Inventor.” The sketch opens with Navarrette delivering a eulogy for her dead husband, an “eccentric” inventor who “spent his final days in his workshop building god knows what,” adding, “My husband loved his inventions and he… liked his wife.” Related Stories J.K. Rowling’s Agent Slams Trans Rights Protest at ‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’ in London: It Put ‘Others at Risk’ Warner Bros. Studios Leavesden Revenues Climb 11% to $390 Million Thanks to ‘Harry Potter’ Tour, Increased Production (EXCLUSIVE) When she returns home from the wake, she sees that her husband’s left behind a gift for his widow in his workshop —a cute, Wall-E-like robot called the PD 44. The two become the best of friends, though she can’t figure out what PD’s “purpose” is. We jump six years into the future, and Navarrette’s lonely widow is finally ready to date. She matches with a nice-looking man named Tom Oakland (played by Ben Marshall) on a dating app, and the two go out on a romantic date. They seem to click, and she takes him back to her apartment for a nightcap to meet PD — when, all of a sudden, PD transforms into a giant, menacing killer robot, rips Tom’s penis off and hurls it into the moon. “PD stands for Penis Destroyer?!” exclaims Navarrette’s widow, before the robot shoots Tom with a laser beam until he explodes, covering her in blood. “He did love me… My husband loved me after all!” says the delighted woman. The sketch was a fine showcase for Navarrette’s crack timing and commitment to the bit, and one of the better “ SNL ” digital shorts in quite some time. articles.title: Valladolid Festival Prizes: Alain Gomis’ ‘Dao’ Wins Golden Spike, ‘La Gradiva’ Takes Silver
articles.full_text: × Nov 1, 2026 5:02am PT Valladolid Festival Prizes: Alain Gomis’ ‘Dao’ Wins Golden Spike, ‘La Gradiva’ Takes Silver Lisandro Alonso earns best director honors, and Alba Rohrwacher and Swann Arlaud receive acting prizes, while Claudia Estrada Tarascó’s 'Salen las lobas' emerged as one of the festival's discoveries By Emiliano de Pablos Plus Icon Emiliano de Pablos Latest South Boost: María Ripoll and Max Lemcke Feature in a Project Lineup Reflecting Andalusia’s Growing TV Ambitions 5 days ago Valladolid Film Festival Draws Global Auteurs, 30 World Premieres and Emerging Spanish Talent 1 week ago Fueled by ‘La Bola Negra,’ Spain’s Indie Distribution Make Robust Gains, to Be Highlighted at Valladolid’s Merci Market 1 week ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Dao' Courtesy of Valladolid International Film Festival French-Senegalese filmmaker Alain Gomis ’ “ Dao ,” an expansive family saga spanning Europe and Africa, was awarded the Golden Spike for best film at Spain’s 71st Valladolid International Film Festival ( Seminci ) while Marine Atlan’s acclaimed debut “ La Gradiva ” received the Silver Spike. Unfolding between a wedding in France and an ancestral memorial ceremony in Guinea-Bissau, Gomis’ three-hour film blurs fiction and documentary, gathering a sprawling cast of professional and non-professional performers to explore family ties, migration and the pull of inherited traditions. The international jury praised the film’s distinctive cinematic form, citing its use of rhythm, duration and movement to create an intimate yet immersive atmosphere. Related Stories Producer Will Packer Stumps to Get Out the Vote and Launch a Private HBCU Fundraising Campaign Bill Maher Fact-Checks Kid Rock After He Compares Abdul El-Sayed to 9/11 Hijackers on ‘Real Time’ “Dao,” which world premiered in competition at Berlin, marks Gomis’ return to fiction features after “Félicité,” winner of the 2017 Berlinale Grand Jury Prize. Reviewing the new film, Variety ’s Guy Lodge called it the director’s “most vibrantly expansive and accessible” work. The Party Film Sales handles international sales while Janus Films holds North American distribution rights. Atlan’s “La Gradiva” premiered at Cannes’ Critics’ Week, where it won its top Grand Prix, before receiving the Melbourne International Film Festival’s Bright Horizons Award in August. At Valladolid, the French-Italian feature also picked up the José Salcedo editing prize for Guillaume Lillo and the Rainbow Spike, recognizing LGBTQ-related cinema. ‘La Gradiva’ Courtesy of Valladolid International Film Festival Set during a French school trip to Naples and Pompeii, the film follows a group of teenagers navigating desire, insecurity and the last moments of adolescence. “Seismically sensitive and deeply moving,” wrote Variety critic Jessica Kiang, who called it “one of the most piercingly accurate and immersive portrayals ever” of that precarious age. MK2 Films represents international sales. Argentine filmmaker Lisandro Alonso, whose credits include “Jauja” and “Eureka,” earned the Ribera del Duero best director award for “Double Freedom,” the well-received sequel to his 2001 debut “Freedom,” sold by Luxbox. Acting honors went to Alba Rohrwacher for Stéphane Brizé’s “A Good Little Soldier,” in which she plays a corporate executive caught in a system of profit at any cost, and Swann Arlaud for Emmanuel Marre’s “A Man of His Time,” about a French engineer drawn into the Vichy regime. Marre’s film also picked up the cinematography award for Olivier Boonjing. Austrian filmmaker Sandra Wollner won the Miguel Delibes screenplay prize for “Everytime,” a drama exploring grief and memory through digital technology. The official competition jury gave a special mention to Tiago Guedes’ “Aquí.” Beyond the main competition, Thai filmmaker Sompot Chidgasornpongse took the Meeting Point prize for “9 Temples to Heaven,” which premiered in Cannes’ Directors’ Fortnight. The contemplative family pilgrimage drama marks the fiction-feature debut of a longtime collaborator of Apichatpong Weerasethakul. Marc Ferrer’s “Cinemanía” received the Fundos Award, while Manon Coubia won the ESCAC directing prize for “Forest High.” Spanish debut “Salen las lobas” emerged as a double audience favorite, taking both the Meeting Point Audience Award and the Seminci Youth Prize. Directed by Claudia Estrada Tarascó, the film follows girls in a juvenile justice facility who bond over music and dreams of a Barcelona trap competition. Produced by Alba Sotorra’s Oceanika, it is sold internationally by MoreThan Films and is set for a Dec. 11 Spanish theatrical release through Silencio Cinema. In the Alchemies section, Ivan Marković’s “Promised Spaces,” a portrait of Cambodia’s rapidly transformed urban landscape, collected the Grand Prize. David Baute’s “Benigno,” about an elderly man preserving a disappearing way of life in the Canary Islands, received a special mention and the environmental Green Spike. Hassen Ferhani’s Algeria-France production “Alea Jacarandas” took the Time of History Grand Prize, with the special award going to Mariano Llinás’ “Life of Jorge Luis Borges.” Isabelle Stever’s “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming” received the FIPRESCI critics’ prize, while Markus Schleinzer’s “Rose” won the main competition Audience Award. Seminci unveiled its winners Saturday morning in Valladolid after organizers canceled the traditional closing gala following a deadly train accident in Toledo province. Held Oct. 23-31, the festival’s 71st edition was led by interim co-directors Mariona Viader and Javier H. Estrada following the death of José Luis Cienfuegos last December. Organizers reported a provisional audience tally of 100,000, more than 120 film discussions and participation by over 90% of the directors represented in its official sections. The festival closed with the Spanish premiere of Gael García Bernal’s “Hombre al agua.” And the Awards: OFFICIAL COMPETITION Golden Spike Alain Gomis, “Dao” Silver Spike Marine Atlan, “La Gradiva” Ribera del Duero Award for Best Director Lisandro Alonso, “Double Freedom” Best Actress Alba Rohrwacher, “A Good Little Soldier” Best Actor Swann Arlaud, “A Man of His Time” Best Cinematography Olivier Boonjing, “A Man of His Time” Miguel Delibes Award for Best Screenplay Sandra Wollner, “Everytime” José Salcedo Award for Best Editing Guillaume Lillo, “La Gradiva” Special Mention Tiago Guedes, “Aquí” MEETING POINT Meeting Point Award Sompot Chidgasornpongse, “9 Temples to Heaven” Fundos Award Marc Ferrer, “Cinemanía” ESCAC Award for Best Director Manon Coubia, “Forest High” ALCHEMIES Grand Prize Ivan Marković, “Promised Spaces” Special Mention David Baute, “Benigno” TIME OF HISTORY Grand Prize Hassen Ferhani, “Alea Jacarandas” Special Award Mariano Llinás, “Life of Jorge Luis Borges” DOC. Spain Award Eloy Enciso Cachafeiro, “Letters from an Inner Exile” Special Mention Beatrice Gibson, “At Night” OTHER FEATURE AWARDS Pilar Miró Prize for Best New Spanish Director Sebastián Uría, “Adiós, ríos” Miniminci Prize Javier Martínez and Christian Garnez, “Momonsters. Película de Navidad” Seminci Youth Prize Claudia Estrada Tarascó, “Salen las lobas” SHORT FILM AWARDS Golden Spike Arnas Balčiūnas, “Class Photo” First Silver Spike Blanca Camell Galí, “First Fire” Second Silver Spike Natalia Marín, “Chronicle of Tiredness” Best European Short Film Wannes Vanspauwen and Pol De Plecker, “Pithead” Best Spanish Short Film Mariona Martínez, “L’enterrament de la sardina” Castilla y León Short Film Award Juan Carlos Mostaza, “Under the Lake” NON-OFFICIAL AWARDS Rainbow Spike Marine Atlan, “La Gradiva” Green Spike David Baute, “Benigno” FIPRESCI Prize Isabelle Stever, “I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming” Audience Award — International Competition Markus Schleinzer, “Rose” Audience Award — Meeting Point Claudia Estrada Tarascó, “Salen las lobas” YOUTH JURY AWARDS International Competition Lance Hammer, “Queen at Sea” Meeting Point Jacqueline Lentzou, “A Day in the Life of Jo: Chapter Phaedra” Best Short Film Francisco Visceral Rivera, “El tamagochi escarlata” Emmitt Smith Talks ‘Dancing with the Stars,’ Taylor Swift’s Impact on the NFL and the State of the Dallas Cowboys Under Dak Prescott: ‘He’s the Best We’ve Got’ Loading comments...

Why wait until Christmas to start unwrapping? Advent calendars make the case for treating yourself all December long, and this year’s lineup goes well beyond the usual bite-sized chocolates. This year, brands are finding increasingly creative ways to cash in on the tradition. Nespresso has teamed up with Swarovski for a sparkly caffeine fix, Lego is bringing holiday cheer to a galaxy far, far away, and Bloomingdale’s is packing more than $1,200 worth of luxury beauty products into a single box. Many of this year’s most coveted calendars are also reusable, with collectible figurines, ornaments and keepsakes designed to outlast the holiday season. The actor, who stars as Severus Snape in the upcoming HBO series adaptation of J.K. Rowling ‘s books, recently responded to criticisms of his joining the cast following the author’s infamous social media campaign of transphobia . “For me, I first came to this story through the books,” he told Time . “So people have got a lot of feelings about this. Obviously, everyone’s got the right to their own opinions about whatever.” Related Stories News J.K. Rowling To Be Subject Of BBC Documentary Examining Her Rise & Gender Identity Views News J.K. Rowling On Why Paapa Essiedu Won’t Be Fired From ‘Harry Potter’ Series For Advocating For Trans Rights Essiedu continued, “I concentrate on the job at hand, which is to give as much humanity, as much depth, dimensions, layers, complexity to a character that has a lot of that. That is my job, and it’s a privilege, and it’s an honor to do it, and I look forward to being able to do it for a long time now.” Watch on Deadline Having been outspoken against transgender rights in recent years, Rowling previously celebrated UK’s Supreme Court last year ruling that prohibits trans women from being legally recognized as women. At the time, more than 400 people signed a letter urging the country’s film and television industry to take action on trans rights , including Essiedu. When it comes to the internet’s reaction of Paapa Essiedu being cast as Severus Snape, he says he’s focus is on bringing humanity and complexity to the character. “I concentrate on the job at hand, which is to give as much humanity, as much depth, dimensions, layers, complexity… pic.twitter.com/KaqK1d2N4T — TIME (@TIME) October 30, 2026 Rowling commented on Essiedu’s pro-trans advocacy after fans speculated if the actor would be axed from the show. “I don’t have the power to sack an actor from the series, and I wouldn’t exercise it if I did. I don’t believe in taking away people’s jobs or livelihoods because they hold legally protected beliefs that differ from mine,” she posted on social media. Meanwhile, Essiedu’s co-stars John Lithgow and Bel Powley have expressed their disagreement with Rowling’s anti-trans views. Premiering on Christmas Day, Harry Potter began filming in the UK last summer. Its cast includes Dominic McLaughlin as the titular boy wizard, Alastair Stout as Ron Weasley, Arabella Stanton as Hermoine Granger, John Lithgow as Albus Dumbledore, Janet McTeer as Minerva McGonagall and Nick Frost as Rubeus Hagrid. On Saturday, the Oscar winner boasted about Klara and the Sun ‘s 78% Rotten Tomatoes audience score (now at 73%), while slamming the “sad lost souls” who gave the movie a negative review, contributing to its 26% critics rating. articles.title: Steep Height? No Sweat: ‘Everest: The Other Side’s Jim Morrison And Jimmy Chin Rappel Down Side Of West Hollywood Building [Video]
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Oscar Contender ‘To Hold A Mountain’ To Open In Theaters In December Ahead Of HBO Debut ‘When A Witness Recants’ To Premiere On HBO Soon, Dawn Porter’s Documentary On Shocking Wrongful Conviction Case Inaugural West Hollywood Human Rights Film Festival To Showcase Oscar-Contending Documentaries, 20th Anniversary Screening Of ‘Blood Diamond’ View All October 31, 2026 5:26pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jim Morrison (left, carrying skis) and Jimmy Chin rappel down a billboard in West Hollywood on Friday, October 30, 2026. Matthew Carey Ski mountaineers Jimmy Chin and Jim Morrison are going to great lengths – and heights – to spread the word about the National Geographic documentary Everest: The Other Side . The pair ascended to the top of a 12-story building on the Sunset strip in West Hollywood, CA Friday evening and successfully rappelled down the side. The vertical journey took them along the face of a massive advertisement for the feature film, which opened at 551 theatrical locations on Friday, including IMAX screens. The film, directed by Chin and Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi , shows how Morrison overcame multiple tragedies to achieve the unthinkable – scaling the north side of Mount Everest and then skiing down it, a feat never before accomplished. Related Stories News Everest Doc And 'Breeder' Anchor Indie Frame With Few New Releases - Specialty Preview News Elizabeth Chai Vasarhelyi & Jimmy Chin Talk 'Everest: The Other Side': "This Is The Most Difficult Film We've Made" - Contenders London “I actually can’t believe how big it is,” Morrison said of the billboard. “It’s huge.” Watch the video of their descent below. Morrison had his skis strapped to his back as he rappelled, but skiing down a right angle, naturally, wasn’t in the plan. “It’s definitely too steep,” he told Deadline. “But it does bring back memories [of Everest] looking down at that part of the line and being on a steep place there with Jimmy this time. It was nice to have him right next to me instead of [filming from] so far away.” Jim Morrison on Mount Everest National Geogrphic Oscar winners Vasarahelyi and Chin’s original intent was to document the quest of Morrison and his life partner, elite ski mountaineer Hilaree Nelson, to summit the dangerous north face of Everest and ski down the formidable Hornbein Couloir. But in September 2022, while on a climbing excursion with Morrison to Manaslu in Nepal, Nelson was killed in an avalanche while skiing down the mountainside. “We were in communication with Jim the whole time” as he grieved, Chin explained during a screening of Everest: The Other Side at the Academy Museum Friday night. “I was with him a lot and we were documenting throughout.” Morrison went through a period of depression after Nelson’s death but rallied and ultimately decided to try to accomplish what he and Nelson had set out to do. For Vasarhelyi, the filmmaking mission became, “How do you honor a story that just got a lot more painful? And also, how do you support Jim through this journey?” Jim Morrison climbs the world’s tallest mountain in ‘Everest: The Other Side’ National Geographic/Jimmy Chin Everest: The Other Side premiered at the Venice Film Festival and then screened at Telluride and Toronto. At Friday night’s Q&A, Morrison shared his reaction to seeing the completed documentary. “The first time I watched it, [producer] Shannon [Dill] and Jimmy came to my hometown and screened it for me and some really close friends of mine. And there was just a tremendous amount of anxiety and I guess stress in the room and tension,” Morrison recalled. “And when it ended, I went up to Jimmy and I put my arms around him and he was crying and I was crying… And he had a real sense of, ‘What [does he] think, what’s about to happen? Does he like it?’ And I just put my arms around him and I said, ‘I lived it, Jimmy. I lived all of it.’” Morrison’s unprecedented ski down the north side of Everest took four hours to complete. At any moment, a wrong move could have been fatal. He spoke to the concentration necessary to accomplish the task. “I’m very focused on putting myself into that space to be sure that I can do it when and if I need to do it,” he said. “I feel very alive when I’m doing that. I feel very connected to the intention of life that I’m living and that I’m living a good life. And for me, it fulfills me. It’s my passion. It’s my drive. It has been since my mom at a very young age pushed me outside and just said, ‘Go outside.’ And I fell in love with nature. And I think there are people that are extraordinarily passionate about their art or their music or going to space — and going to space probably isn’t a really safe endeavor. There’s a whole lot of people that are risking a lot to help that person get to space. But I personally think it’s a good thing for humanity to push the envelope and to strive to do great things and to build great teams to make them happen. And I think it’s valuable and important and I’m really happy that we were able to honor Hilaree in this way by telling the story and achieving the goal and keeping her story alive.” The rappel down the Sunset building, comparatively — that was no sweat. “Rappelling down was a ‘pinch me’ moment,” he said, “but not one I was really afraid of.” Watch the video of Morrison and Chin’s descent below, as well as an interview we did with them immediately afterwards. articles.title: Tom Hanks Returns As David S. Pumpkins For ‘Saturday Night Live’ Opener — Interrupted By Donald Trump’s Fear Of A Midterm Ass-Whipping
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Tom Hanks Returns As David S. Pumpkins For ‘Saturday Night Live’ Opener — Interrupted By Donald Trump’s Fear Of A Midterm Ass-Whipping Judge Again Tosses Out Donald Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit Against The Wall Street Journal Over Its Reporting On Jeffrey Epstein Birthday Letter What To Watch For As Networks Cover Midterm Election Night: More Data, More Coverage & More Competition View All October 31, 2026 8:52pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tom Hanks returned to Saturday Night Live as David S. Pumpkins for a Halloween-themed opener, albeit his skit was suddenly interrupted by Donald Trump (James Austin Johnson) as he implored supporters to try to prevent a potential midterm drubbing. “The midterms are on Tuesday, and the polls say we’re doing very badly,” Johnson’s Trump said. “Ahhh. They are saying Texas is turning purple, just like my hands. And if it goes blue, then just like my hand, I will leave it for dead.” Related Stories Late Night TV Inde Navarrette Kicks Off ‘Saturday Night Live’ Debut With Shane Gillis Quip About Her “Little Whore Outfit” For Getting Into Marvel Shape News What To Watch For As Networks Cover Midterm Election Night: More Data, More Coverage & More Competition The skit spoofed some of Trump’s closing midterm messaging, including his admiration for men’s asses, the suggestion that Nicki Minaj would be his new press secretary, and some of the strange grunting noises he has uttered at rallies. It’s been just over 10 years that Hanks first appeared as Pumpkins, a strange man who shows up in a Halloween attraction wearing a cheap black and orange pumpkin suit and flanked by two men in dancing skeleton outfits. Hanks’ first cameo as the character took place just a couple of weeks before Trump’s first election to the White House. Watch on Deadline Saturday’s opener started with a couple taking an amusement park ride, only to be confused by Pumpkins’ appearance in what was supposed to be a scary attraction. Then, Trump interrupted the skit, noting that Pumpkins “keeps popping up and confusing people on the ride. The end!” Johnson’s Trump went on, “But you know, I actually have a lot in common with Mr. Pumpkins. We both appeared in 2016. We’re both very loud, very orange, and very frankly annoying, but we love Tom Hanks.” Hanks tried to stay in freeze frame as Johnson’s Trump talked. “Look at him back there. Good acting, great ass,” Trump said. “That’s something I’ve been doing lately — admiring men’s asses. Not that there’s anything wrong with that — just that I might be gay.” In reality, Trump has been talking about men’s asses — specifically the behind of Sen. Jon Husted (R-OH), seeking to hold on to his seat against Democrat Sherrod Brown. Johnson’s Trump went on, “They’re calling it gay dementia. Dementia, short for dementia, show me their butts.” The skit also made reference to the U.S. Senate race in Texas, where Trump and Republicans have invested heavily in Ken Paxton’s race against Democrat James Talarico, hoping to keep the U.S. Senate from flipping. But Paxton has had a series of corruption scandals that has made the race a tossup, and even Trump has remarked on the candidate’s lackluster appearance. Johnson’s Trump said, “You gotta vote for that awful Ken Paxton. God, what an ugly son of a bitch! I hate, I hate Ken Paxton, but you got to vote for him because we can’t have this Talafreako, who is frankly much better looking and wow, what a dynamite ass! It’s like a pillowcase full of comforts back there.” The skit also featured an appearance by Saidah Belo-Osagie as Minaj, who has appeared at Trump’s rallies. “She’s got quite an ass. If only it were on a man, perhaps I could admire it,” Johnson’s Trump said. Also making a brief appearance was Veronika Slowikowska as Katie Zacharia, whose recent tenure as press secretary lasted less than a week. The real Zacharia had talked about who she would want to play her on SNL , and mentioned Scarlett Johansson. That was not to be. David S.
