articles.title: Selma Blair Apologizes for Plane Arrest: “Not One Day Have I Intended to Hurt or Frighten Anyone”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 30, 2026 5:26pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Selma Blair at the Fashion Trust U.S 2026 Awards at Nya Studios on April 8 in Los Angeles. Charley Gallay/Getty Images Selma Blair is apologizing for her Oct. 11 plane arrest, where she allegedly assaulted two flight attendants onboard a Delta Los Angeles-New York flight. “Hi. It’s me, and I know I’ve been quiet for a couple of weeks since October 11th, and you deserve to hear from me directly, and I’m sorry that it’s taken this long,” the actress said in an Instagram video Friday. “There is a legal matter going on, and my lawyers have asked me to not say anything about that day, and I’m listening to them. And I take this very seriously.” The Legally Blonde star noted that “what I can tell you though is very simple, and the truest thing I know about myself [is] that not one day ever have I intended to hurt or frighten anyone, a day in my life.” She continued, “And so to the people that I disappointed, that I hurt, that I frightened, alarmed; I am so sorry.” Related Stories General News Selma Blair Speaks Out on Plane Arrest: "Did Not Intend to Harm Anyone" General News Selma Blair Is Accused of Assaulting Four People. Can Her Career Survive Another Scandal? Blair was arrested at John F. Kennedy International Airport on Oct. 11 after an alleged incident on a Delta plane that resulted in two flight attendants being injured and one being sent to the hospital. Blair was also transported to the hospital after the outburst, and she also allegedly repeatedly kicked the police officer who took her to the hospital and a nurse in the chest. She pleaded not guilty to two counts of assault, while separate charges from the FBI are expected to come as the agency investigates all assaults that occur onboard aircrafts. Blair thanked those who have reached out and “sent wishes of love or caring. It has meant everything to me and my son, who is my world, as a scout who is also OK.” “So right now, I’m going to be taking care of my health and my son and thinking of you all with gratitude and love,” she concluded. Blair’s spokesperson previously spoke out , releasing a statement that read, “Selma Blair experienced a medical emergency on the flight. There was no attempt to open the door of the aircraft. Selma did not intend to harm anyone.” Her attorney Shawn Barnes said in a court appearance after the incident that Blair had been working “extensive hours and exhaustive hours” ahead of the flight, and also hit her head on a bankhead. “These factors, coupled with the altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation,” Barnes said in court. In a separate statement, Blair’s rep said, “The suggestion by anyone that Selma does not have multiple sclerosis is outrageous,” she has the neurological condition pseudobulbar affect, “which bears directly on how a medical episode presents to people who do not know her.” “It should be noted Selma has worked on seven film and television projects in 2026 alone, only a couple of which have been announced. She has launched a skin care line, a clothing line, and a line of eye-glass readers, each built around the idea of beauty and utility for people whose bodies do not always cooperate,” the rep continued. “She remains a visible and relentless advocate for disability rights, for the MS community, and this year for the Jewish community in the face of rising antisemitism, including from the stage of the ADL’s State of the Arts event at The Jewish Museum two weeks ago. Selma had never been arrested before Sunday night. There is much more to this story than has been reported, and we ask to consider the entirety of the facts before rushing to judgment, whether in the courtroom or in the court of public opinion.” THR

articles.title: ‘Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting’ Review: Whimsical Chinese Film Explores Myth and History Through a Series of Tasty Treats
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Leslie Felperin Plus Icon Leslie Felperin Contributing Film Critic lesliefelperin Follow Sign Up View All October 30, 2026 5:36pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Fuxi Four Tales of Feasting Uluka Studio Limited Following up his well-received 2021 feature A New Old Play , Sichuan-reared Chinese writer-director Qiu Jiongjiong continues to deploy heightened artifice and quasi-theatrical mannerisms (painted stage sets, rippling cloths representing water, actors in wacky costumes playing astral bodies or dogs, and so on) with his eccentric but addictive latest, Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting . Although Fuxi runs a trim 135 minutes compared to New Old Play ’s three-hour run time, Qiu still manages to cover more than 2,000 years of myth, history and mythic history with a quartet of stories that revolve around special meals and banquets. (The word “fuxi,” intertitles helpfully explain, can either be a noun meaning delicious food or a verb signifying the savoring of such delicacies.) Related Stories Movies Eric Bauza Remembered as a "Once-in-a-Generation" Talent Who Gave Looney Tunes a New Voice Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting The Bottom Line Spicy and addictive, if not easily digestible. Venue: Tokyo Film Festival (Competition) Cast: Lee Kang Sheng, Lee Hong-Chi, Annie Chen, Fan Guang Yao, Wang Talu, Wang Yitong, Xue Xuchun, Wang Hai, Zhou Jiarui Director/screenwriter: Qiu Jiongjiong 2 hours 15 minutes The different segments, each one offering varying mixtures of slapstick comedy and memento mori solemnity, don’t have much to do with one another story-wise. So Qiu pulls it all together with a framing device about a film crew making each segment, the tales linked by the presence of the sun or Sol (Wen Ke) and Luna aka the moon (Xiao Luxi’); both actors rock massive sun- and moon-shaped headpieces. Yes, the whole thing is just as bizarre as it sounds, but Qiu’s relentless visual brio keeps the soufflé aloft while the serious intent adds a complex, umami aftertaste with a hint of the tingly, numbing flavor so distinctive in Sichuan cuisine. Indeed, much of the dialogue here is reportedly in the Sichuan dialect, a nuance that native speakers are likely to appreciate more than the international viewers, who may have caught this at the Tokyo Film Festival, where it premiered in competition. Nevertheless, the performances and the English-language subtitles succeed in getting across the mix of high and low cultures on display here, as each chapter throws together peasants and aristocrats, ordinary folk and fantastic beings, actors and filmmakers in a giddy muddle. The effect is a little reminiscent of commedia dell’arte with all that breaking-of-the-fourth-wall stuff, especially since the mise en scene here is so archly theatrical. The first minutes kick off with a bit of slightly baffling comic business featuring Sol and Luna interacting with the film crew making the movie we’re presumably watching — although the names of the people playing the roles of “prop master” and “costume designer” and so forth don’t match the names of the real people who actually performed those roles for Fuxi listed in the end credits. Anyway, we soon settle into the first chapter, which takes place “long ago,” when our ancestors, simian-sort of hominids, lived in the forest and had long tails which they believed were “sacred fuxi to be offered at life’s most solemn moments.” And by offered we mean eaten, as is the case with the tail of one aged granny played by veteran Taiwanese actor Lee Kang-Sheng, a frequent collaborator with auteur Tsai Ming-liang. As granny lays dying, her tail is cut off, butchered into chunks like oxtail, stewed and served up to the community, a dish that looks pretty tasty if you don’t mind the self cannibalism. Next comes the second chapter, set in a period of early agrarianism, wherein King Wang, Sichuan’s fourth king, has abdicated the throne and turned into a cuckoo but still flies home to enjoy some tasty fuxi prepared for him annually. Something gets lost in translation here, but the visuals are still rather splendid and props are due to Fan Guang Yao in the role of Wang for the solemnity he manages to muster while wearing giant fake wings and a massive wig of white hair. Ultimately, the third and fourth chapters have the most heft dramatically, making the earlier proceedings feel like pleasant forgettable amuses bouche . The third chapter, set in China’s medieval period, features a quartet of fantastical creatures gathering to remember the life of poet and gastronome Su Dongpo (Lee Hong-Chi), a man of many talents but whose honesty frequently got him into trouble with the powers that be, resulting in several periods of exile. Su’s book boy (Wang Yitong) prepares dishes invented or closely associated with his master for a dinner party consisting of a Harvester (Xue Xuchun) who ferries souls to the underworld, water spirit Yaksha (Wang Hai), an older woman called Granny Spring Dream (Zha Xinji), and a fox in human form (Wang Talu). All enjoy the feast as scenes from Su Dongpo’s life are performed. The final tale revolves around servant boy Zhang Sanxing (Zhou Jiarui), who is living in the early 20th century and witnessing the fall of the Qing dynasty, the last to reign before the ascent of Communism. Once again, Harvester, Yaksha and Fox nosh on fuxi with young Zheng, who is transitioning to the land of the dead, the whole spectacle overseen once again by Sol and Luna before a final pullback to reveal the cast and crew celebrating with food and drink at the wrap party. While it all may not make a huge amount of sense on a first viewing, there is an undoubtable sensual pleasure to be had from Qiu’s painterly sets, the goofy costumes, and the food styling itself. Viewers are advised to watch with an open mind and a full stomach. Full credits Venue: Tokyo Film Festival (Competition) Production companies: Uluka Studio Ltd., Hongkong Spark Peak Entertainment Group Ltd, Yu Tang Culture Creation Co. Ltd, Harvest 9 Road Entertainment, Lespros Entertainment, La Fonte, Zilch Inc, Parallax Films, Red Sea Fund Cast: Lee Kang Sheng, Lee Hong-Chi, Annie Chen, Fan Guang Yao, Wang Talu, Wang Yitong, Xue Xuchun, Wang Hai, Zhou Jiarui Director/screenwriter: Qiu Jiongjiong Producers: David Tang, Ding Ningyuan, Zhao Jin Executive producers: Leo Lee, Liu Yujun, Wang Talu, Ko Yao-Tsung Co-executive producers: Takashi Homma, Huang Yue, Yawen Lu, Lenny Han, Zhao Jin, Liu Yuan, Sam Zhang, Jiahao, Li Jing, Zhang Huiting, Zhang Jingyu, Li Li, Sunny Sun Co-producers: Li Yuwen, Frank Yung, Tom Tung, Xu Haochen, Vosuke Kikuchi, Sophie Erbs, Timothee Cliquet, Aubrey Lee, Wang Xiaoxiao, Mo Jinjin, Xue Fei Directors of photography: Robbin Feng Yuchao, Goopi Liu Tailin Production designer: Qiu Jiongjiong Costume designer: Bai Yun Editors: Qiu Jiongjiong, Liu Xinzhu, Xu Chen Sound designer: Wang Ran Music: Diao Lili Sales: Cao Liuying/Parallax Films 2 hours 15 minutes THR

articles.title: The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By THR Staff Plus Icon THR Staff View All October 30, 2026 5:46pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source From left: John Mulaney, Jason Segel, Adam Brody, Seth Rogen, Julio Torres and Ted Danson were photographed May 3 at the Luckman Club at Soho House West Hollywood for THR's Comedy Actor roundtable. Beau Grealy The Hollywood Reporter ‘s Off Script roundtable series has won its first Daytime Emmy Award. The awards -season showcase was recognized at the 2026 Daytime Emmys Friday night, where it won in the arts and popular culture category after receiving its third consecutive nomination . In total, the series has garnered six Daytime Emmy nominations since 2017. Off Script beat out fellow nominees Beyond the Gates: Welcome to the Neighborhood: An Entertainment Tonight Special (CBS Media Ventures), Variety & CNN Actors on Actors (CNN Digital | Variety), Variety Studio: Actors on Actors (PBS) and Working in the Theatre (AmericanTheatreWing.org). Related Stories Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards Movies Santa Barbara Film Fest: Inde Navarrette, Jaafar Jackson Among Eight Tapped for Virtuoso Awards Off Script is the magazine’s iconic roundtable series , which has aired on IFC, streaming on AMC+, over the past three years. The series consists of five episodes of Emmy contenders: drama actress, drama actor, comedy actress, comedy actor and stand-up. Executive producer Elisabeth D. Rabishaw accepted the award for THR . Rabishaw thanked the National Academy of Television Arts and Sciences “for the recognition” and praised the fellow nominees in the category. Among those thanked, Rabishaw singled out former AMC Networks exec Blake Callaway, who she noted greenlit the series, and thanked all of those at AMC Networks who worked on the show. Talent on last year’s roster included Seth Rogen, Parker Posey, Helen Mirren, Keri Russell, Kristen Bell, Michelle Williams, Ted Danson, Walton Goggins, Jamie Foxx, Adam Scott, Seth Meyers, Niecy Nash-Betts, Diego Luna and many others. Moderated by THR ’s Lacey Rose and Mikey O’Connell, the series is known for its sharp, unfiltered roundtable format, delivering honest, insightful and often hilarious conversations about the craft and chaos of working in television. But what truly sets Off Script apart is its unmatched ability to curate a who’s who of Hollywood who rarely, if ever, share the same stage. But the roundtable series is not just limited to Emmys season: for the Oscar season roundtables , categories covered include director, actor, actress, songwriter and producer. THR‘s Scott Feinberg, Beatrice Verhoeven, Ethan Millman, Seija Rankin and Mia Galuppo moderated 2025’s Oscar season roundtable episodes. THR also has expanded its roundtable series to include podcasters and Broadway actors. The nominated season of Off Script With The Hollywood Reporter was executive produced by THR editor-in-chief Maer Roshan; former vp, video production and development Jason Rovou, former co-editor-in-chief Shirley Halperin; and Rabishaw. Postproduction was done by Framework LA. THR has received six Daytime Emmy nominations prior to this, four for the roundtable series. In 2024 and 2025 , THR earned a nom in the same category. In 2024, the publication also earned a nomination for best shortform program with Hollywood Atelier: Rob Pickens , produced by Rovou. Off Script , previously titled Close Up With The Hollywood Reporter , was nominated for three Daytime Emmys in 2021 , 2019 and 2017 . THR also previously won a Los Angeles area Emmy for its roundtable discussion The Hollywood Reporter in Focus: The Wolf of Wall Street , which aired on PBS SoCal. The Daytime Emmy win follows on the heels of THR ’s big showing with the National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards earlier this week, where THR received 96 nominations, more than any other outlet. Earlier this year, THR won a field-leading 20 first-place awards at the Southern California Journalism Awards and received the Webby People’s Voice Award for best entertainment-themed website, in addition to an American Society of Magazine Editors award for best cover. In 2025, THR earned 13 first-place wins at the National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards. THR is a flagship entertainment media brand, offering in-depth reporting, analysis and thought-provoking reviews; unparalleled access, world-class photography and video; and feature exclusives in its award-winning weekly magazine and dynamic website. THR also boasts prestigious live events, industry-leading philanthropic, empowerment and diversity initiatives and hugely successful video series including Off Script . THR

articles.title: LAPD Arrests Two for Murder of Christina Downer, Sister to ‘SNL’ Writer Jimmy Fowlie
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 30, 2026 5:48pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jimmy Fowlie at HBO's premiere screening for 'Sarah Squirm: Live + In the Flesh.' Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images for HBO Two people have been arrested for the murder of Christina Downer, the sister to Saturday Night Live writer Jimmy Fowlie, the Los Angeles Police Department announced Friday. Police arrested Downer’s boyfriend, Delorean Bijon Brandon, and Kaylee Nicole Markowski on Thursday. “On December 18, 2025, Christina Downer was reported missing after her ex-husband requested a welfare check when he had not heard from her for an extended period of time. Downer’s boyfriend, Delorean Brandon, claimed that she had moved out several months earlier, leaving behind all her belongings, including her vehicle and dog,” the LAPD said. Related Stories Movies 'Fair Play' Doc About Olympic Gymnast Jordan Chiles Set for 2027 Release on Hulu, Disney+ (Exclusive) Movies Bill Hader Is the Cat in the Hat -- This Time a "Much Different Version" Than He Played on 'SNL' In their statement, police said, “Robbery- Homicide Division detectives assumed the investigation after Downer’s cellphone was discovered washed ashore on Santa Monica Beach. Through various investigative techniques, detectives identified Delorean Brandon and Kaylee Markowski as the individuals responsible for Downer’s murder, the disposal of her body, and the concealment of their involvement.” On Dec. 22, 2025, Fowlie shared a social media post asking for help finding his missing sister, sharing a multiple of images of Downer. Months later, in April of this year, he announced that “the LAPD has informed our family that Christina is no longer alive, and the case has officially transitioned from a missing person to a homicide investigation.” The SNL writer shared in his April post that he believes his sister’s “phone and social media were compromised” in the weeks before she went missing, and those who took her phone “used it to hide the fact she was gone, to ask for money, and to create a false narrative that she was going ‘off the grid.’” “I am sharing this because I believe that whoever is responsible is hoping to erase her in every way possible,” he wrote. “I want to amplify her story in the only way I know how. And to express that she was a beautiful person who matters in this world, especially to me.” The LAPD’s Robbery-Homicide Division will present the case to the L.A. Country District Attorney’s Office for filing consideration. The investigation is still ongoing. THR

articles.title: Timbaland Files $15 Million Fraud Lawsuit Against Former Managers
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All October 30, 2026 6:23pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Timbaland Leon Bennett/Getty Images for The Recording Academy Timbaland has filed a $15 million lawsuit against his former manager and business manager, accusing the two executives of fraud, breach of fiduciary duty and civil theft, among other claims. In a 65-page suit filed in Los Angeles Superior Court on Friday, Timbaland alleges that the manager, Gary Marella, “stole millions in unauthorized commissions, fees, and reimbursements,” used Timbaland’s funds to pay Marella’s employees, and “falsified financial records and communications to conceal unauthorized payments” from the producer. Related Stories Lifestyle Snoop Dogg's 'Doggyland' Expanding Children's Book Series (Exclusive First Look) Movies David Bowie Returns to Berlin With Immersive Event The former business manager Bruce Seckendorf, Timbaland, whose real name is Timothy Mosley, alleges, “failed to pay Mosley’s mortgage and allowed his home to reach the brink of foreclosure.” The suit claims Seckendorf’s firm “failed to timely pay substantial federal taxes, causing millions in penalties and interest, while continuing to pay themselves, the Marella Defendants, and other professionals millions in commissions, fees, and purported loan repayments.” “Defendants used their entrusted authority to enrich themselves and others, conceal financial misconduct, and deplete Timbaland’s valuable assets,” the suit says. “Plaintiffs seek to recover their losses, compel an accounting, and stop the continuing unauthorized use of Timbaland’s name for Defendants’ benefit.” Per the suit, Timbaland only learned of the alleged misconduct because he got a foreclosure notice at his home last year. After receiving the notice, the suit says, Timbaland called Seckendorf, who the producer says failed to “clearly explain why his office had failed to make the mortgage payments without informing Mosley.” Timbaland subsequently took on independent legal counsel and financial representatives, who had investigated the issue, “uncovering unauthorized payments, concealed credit-card arrangements, falsified communications, undisclosed liabilities, and purported loans Mosley had never knowingly agreed to,” the suit states. “The foreclosure was not caused simply because Plaintiffs had no money,” the complaint says, adding that the “Seckendorf Defendants thus prioritized nearly $900,000 in payments to Defendants and attorneys they engaged in five months, while failing to pay for twelve months of mortgage arrears they caused and concealed from Mosley.” Per the suit, the two defendants were terminated in 2025. Seckendorf and his firm didn’t immediately responded to request for comment. In a comment, Marella said that “I strongly dispute these allegations.” “Unfortunately, Tim is attempting to shift responsibility for his own overspending and financial decisions onto someone else (again) as he did before we managed him,” Marella said. “When I began managing him in 2017, long after producing his biggest hits, he was already broke and in debt, had spent all of his money, and was living in a rental. His financial problems did not begin with me. I came in to help rebuild his business. Over approximately nine years, we generated roughly $75 million in business. Despite that, Tim continued spending beyond his means, ultimately having to sell his home last year due to his actions and move into a rental in Coral Gables. Those were the consequences of his own financial decisions, no one else.” Timbaland first started working directly with Marella and Seckendorf in 2016 while dealing with financial misconduct claims against his previous representation, according to the complaint. Marella is the CEO of Mono Music Group, which along with Timbaland has represented other hitmakers such as Poo Bear and ATL Jacob. Seckendorf is a partner at LL Business Management, which was listed on Billboard’s top business managers list last year and represents the likes of Feid, Pusha T, Clipse and Cirkut among others. Mono Music Group, LL Business Management and the firm Seckendorf Hasson Reilly & Kobay CPA’s are all co-defendants in the suit as well. Marella and Seckendorf had worked with Timbaland during a period of significant business ventures for the producer, including launching his popular Verzuz series with Swizz Beatz during the pandemic and selling his catalog to Hipgnosis Songs Fund back in 2019. Regarding Verzuz in particular, Timbaland alleges that Marella took $500,000 more than he was entitled to on two separate incidents relating to $5 million payments from the venture. On the Hipgnosis sale, Marella took $775,000 more than his allotted 10 percent commission would’ve called for, the suit says. Tim was fully aware of the 15 percent commission I received on the Hipgnosis catalog sale,” Marella said. “We spent more than a year and a half helping organize his business affairs and resolve outstanding issues to make that transaction possible. Calling that compensation unauthorized now does not erase his knowledge of the arrangement at the time. I stand behind it and will substantiate through the legal process. As for Verzuz, he was aware of our management commission. His business manager paid us with Tim’s approval.” Marella also co-founded the beat marketplace Beatclub with Timbaland, though as the suit alleges, Marella “grossly mismanaged” the company and treated Mosley as a piggy bank to repair the problems he created. The suit claims Marella “depleted investor funds, spent company money contrary to how he represented it would be used, incurred obligations Beatclub could not pay, failed to pay employees and creators he hired, and spent money contrary to board restrictions.” Marella called Beatclub, “a startup,” further stating that “the ups and downs are par for the course. We launched the platform in 2019, raised outside investment, and together contributed more than $1 million of our own money. In 2024, we let go of most of the staff and had to rebuild. The company’s financial challenges do not, by themselves, establish misconduct by anyone.” Seckendorf, Timbaland alleges, “knowingly provided substantial assistance through payment authorizations, disbursements, and control over Plaintiffs’ financial accounts, thereby substantially enabling the misconduct and contributing to Plaintiffs’ resulting harm.” Timbaland also brings claims for fraudulent concealment, breach of contract and misappropriation of name, photograph and likeness. “Defendants spent much of their careers benefiting from Timbaland’s career, catalog, reputation, and relationships,” the suit says, “yet left Plaintiffs with depleted assets, undisclosed liabilities, costly litigation, and the burden of reconstructing their own financial affairs.” This story was updated at 8:27 p.m. PST to include comment from Gary Marella on the lawsuit. THR

articles.title: Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff File for Divorce After Three Years of Marriage
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All October 30, 2026 6:37pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff at the MTV Video Music Awards at UBS Arena on Sept. 11, 2024 in Elmont, New York. Mike Coppola/Getty Images for MTV Margaret Qualley and Jack Antonoff are divorcing after three years of marriage, with court records obtained by The Associated Press showing that a divorce filing was made Friday. A source told People magazine that the split is “a mutual decision,” adding, “They share a deep affinity and love for one another, and though their romantic partnership is ending, they will absolutely be lifelong friends.” Qualley’s reps did not immediately respond to The Hollywood Reporter’s request for comment. Related Stories Music Jack Antonoff Blasts Ed Sheeran Over Removing Macklemore From Tour Over Palestine Comments: "Stand The F*** Up" Movies Jack Lowden, Margaret Qualley Top Bookie Odds for Next James Bond and Bond Girl Although the divorce filing is recent, the pair reportedly separated in July. At the time, a rep for Qualley confirmed the breakup to People and pushed back on speculation surrounding their split. “The narratives running in the press about Margaret and Jack are categorically untrue. There are no trust issues. There was no infidelity or anything outside of respect and partnership in this relationship,” the actress’ rep said in a statement. Earlier this week, the Bleachers frontman opened up about performing songs inspired by his former relationship with The Guardian. He said he was initially “worried” about performing the songs about but now views it differently. “It’s actually been really beautiful,” Antonoff said. “Songs which I wrote recently, I obviously was really worried about this specific thing,” he added. “I sat long and hard with it and thought, ‘If I change the setlist …’ and in my gut there was a unanimous jury that said, ‘No, this is the deal. The deal I’ve made with my audience is that I’m going to tell you honestly how I feel and I’m going to risk at any moment having to stand behind it for fucking ever.’” The Substance star and Antonoff began dating in 2021 and married in August 2023. THR

articles.title: Bill Maher Responds to Trump’s 1,318-Word Social Rant: “He Went Off on Me Like Kelly Clarkson in a Toy Store”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 30, 2026 7:38pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bill Maher on 'Real Time.' Screenshot Logo text Bill Maher has responded to President Donald Trump ‘s lengthy social media post where he slammed him as a “complete and total loser,” and shared more details about their recent dinner at the White House. During Friday’s episode of Real Time with Bill Maher , the comedian addressed a few of the statements made in Trump’s post. He began the monologue by discussing the upcoming midterms and how former President Barack Obama caused a “big scandal” for a comment he made at a campaign rally saying that Trump has “got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.” Related Stories Music Canadian Rock Icon Bryan Adams Takes Aim at Trump, Says His Protest Song Gets Standing Ovations in Red States (Exclusive) Music Bryan Adams Releases New Trump Protest Song "Lake Ontario" Maher said, “And the Republicans all said, ‘Leave the Cheesecake Factory out of this!’ Well, I mean, I should know. I just had dinner there. I hear it went well. What have you heard?” The host then asked, “Now, did you see the 1,300-word Tweet he sent out? Longest ever. Kind of a flex.” He joked that “dining at the White House is the opposite of the Cheesecake Factory. After you leave, they review you.” “He went off on me like Kelly Clarkson in a toy store,” Maher added. “I mean, eating with Trump is like dating Taylor Swift. It’s a lot of laughs at the time, but later on, they’re tearing you a new asshole.” Maher was then handed a printed copy of Trump’s Truth Social post, and began to “address a few of the allegations.” Before that, he noted, “Look, I don’t want it to be this way. The whole point of having these dinners was talk, disagree, but listen, which he does in person, but don’t hate each other. And then I go back to my job here and then the heartaches begin.” “It begins, ‘Let’s talk about the complete and total loser Bill Maher.’ You got me there. I’ll own that,” Maher joked, going on to explain “what pisses me off” is that “he doesn’t even notice what I say,” specifically citing a line in Trump’s post where he wrote, “[Maher] doesn’t think it was a good thing to take the Nuclear Weapon away from Iran, which shows you that he is not very smart.” Real Time then played a series of clips showcasing the opposite of Trump’s claim. Maher then moved on to another section: “Page two, he talks about how I call him incessantly. I’ve never called you, you call me. I’d be afraid to call you. You’re the president. I think you’re too busy. Well, plainly not. He’s talking about me, ‘He invited himself to the White House.’ As if you could do that. ‘Sir, Bill Maher is here.’ ‘Well, he’s not invited, but the law.” He also read aloud Trump writing that Maher is a “major POTHEAD.” Maher’s response: “Well, I guess the cat’s out of the bag now. Boy, that explains a lot. I thought I was just happy.” (Later in the Real Time episode, Kid Rock, who was at the dinner, told Maher he was “pretty high” at the White House.) He continued reading Trump’s post, “‘Bill had alcohol in his hand,’ that you gave me, ‘as he walked through the White House,’ and then — I love this — ‘Overall, I thought it was a good meeting.'” “‘I understand he’s doing his thing. I never took it personally,'” Maher recited, dumbfounded. “‘He’s not a nice guy, and what he spouts isn’t what he believes. He has to cater to his base, which is mostly composed of losers,’ that would be you assholes,” the host said to his audience. Trump penned a 1,318-word Truth Social post on Sunday, where he criticized Maher, Real Time and producer Chuck LaBella. He wrote, “Let’s talk about this COMPLETE AND TOTAL LOSER, Bill Maher. He’s got a Low Rated Show on equally Low Rated HBO, which was once, long ago, a Network of Quality and Excitement — But that’s all gone. It’s not ‘HOT’ anymore! Maher’s friend and business associate, Chuck LaBella, was also a friend of mine, worked on The Top Hit Show, The Apprentice, as a ‘gofer’ and, because of the success of that show, Number One and Top Rated on many weeks, with the Finale’ being among the Top Shows of the Year, he was automatically and quickly brought up through the Ranks of NBC, along with everyone else associated with that Historic ‘Happening.'” Trump’s post seemingly was made in response to jokes Maher made during his monologue on the Oct. 23 episode. “It’s just a little odd that Trump keeps gushing about men’s bodies, and how handsome they are, and their jawlines, and their asses, their physiques,” said Maher. “I’m a little hurt. I was there for dinner for four hours last week, and not a peep. Nothing.” Maher said, “Trump has the lowest approval rating of any midterm candidate ever. Only one percent of the Republicans are mentioning him in their ads.” The president also wrote in his post that LaBella asked if he’d ever appear on Real Time , which he said led to their first meeting last year. “In any event, over the last few years, LaBella would call me nonstop to say, ‘Hello,’ be very nice, and tell me how much Bill Maher ‘loves’ and respects me, and would constantly ask of me, even before I was President, for any form of meeting with Maher and, would I do his show?” he wrote. “When I became President, I agreed to meet, after the first one, and the last one, but never agreed to do his show, which he wants me to do, DESPARATELY [sic] — It won’t happen! When I have watched the show, which isn’t often, it always ends with dishonesty, about me at least, but, who cares?” He also later claimed LaBella and Kid Rock, the latter of which appeared on Friday night’s Real Time episode, “called me incessantly about meeting with Bill Maher,” which led to their first dinner in March 2025. “My first response was, ‘Fellas, this guy’s a Goofball,'” Trump wrote. THR

articles.title: 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards: ‘General Hospital’ Wins Best Daytime Drama
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All October 30, 2026 8:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Daytime Emmy nominee Amanda Setton, with Troy Lennon Appel, in 'General Hospital.' Disney/Christine Bartolucci The 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards were presented Friday night, with General Hospital taking home the top prize of best daytime drama. The series, which went into Friday night’s show up for 13 awards, won three other awards and saw its Genie Francis receive the lifetime achievement award. Beyond the Gates also won four awards, with star Tamara Tunie winning best actress in a daytime drama series. Best actor in a daytime drama went to The Bold and the Beautiful ‘s Scott Clifton. Tunie, who won her first Daytime Emmy, paid tribute to the “host of Black actresses who paved the way for me, and I feel them as I stand here tonight, beginning with the legendary Cicely Tyson, the first Black woman to appear on a daytime television show, The Guiding Light .” Related Stories TV The Hollywood Reporter Wins 2026 Daytime Emmy Award Music Tom Morello, Annie Lennox, 'KPop Demon Hunters' Songwriters Honored at 2026 SONA Awards Fellow best actress nominee Heather Tom, from The Bold and the Beautiful , was eyeing a record-setting seventh trophy, which would have made her the most awarded actress in daytime history. The Young and the Restless led this year’s nominees with 18 nominations. Though it only won three awards, two of those came in the supporting performer categories. Roger Howarth was named best supporting actor, and Beth Maitland was named best supporting actress. The Kelly Clarkson Show won five awards, including best daytime talk series, but the singer-host of the now-completed talk show didn’t appear to be at the Daytime Emmys . And Clarkson didn’t win the award for best daytime talk series host. Instead that honor went to fellow former talk show host Sherri Shepherd, whose eponymous talk show was canceled after four seasons. Other notable winners include Tracee Ellis Ross, who won best travel and adventure program for her Solo Traveling show; Keke Palmer, who won for her work executive producing Glam Through the Ages ; and Ina Garten, who won best culinary host for her Be My Guest Food Network series, which was named best culinary instructional series. Midway through the ceremony, NATAS chair Terry O’Reilly offered a timely, political speech, just days ahead of the 2026 midterm elections. Speaking about a congressman who was jailed in 1798 after criticizing the president in print, O’Reilly highlighed the power of the people. “The free press in 1800 was not saved by a court. It was saved by citizens who were engaged and informed,” he said. Turning to the present day, O’Reilly called out “the most sustained effort to control what Americans see and hear in this country that were faced in my lifetime.” He cited specifically journalists being banned from covering the Pentagon and president, the DOJ antitrust investigation into the White House TV press pool and the challenge to the news exemption enjoyed by late night and daytime programs, including The View . “It is not much of a leap, from silencing political speech, to suppressing creative expression,” O’Reilly added. “The characters, the storylines, the points of view that someone in power decides are no longer welcome. Here, in the cradle of Hollywood, this town of all towns, we know where that can lead. We have seen what happens when those in power begin drawing up lists of people and pops and ideas that they are willing to label as un-American. We should never wish to see that again.” Turning to the “consequential” midterms on Tuesday, O’Reilly issued a call to those in the audience: “Let’s stand together to resist those who would seek comfort in a quieter media.” And NATAS additionally inducted a number of individuals into its Gold and Silver Circle Society, recognizing industry leaders who’ve demonstrated enduring contributions to television through their 50 or 25 years in industry. The 2026 Gold Circle inductees are Allen Media Group CEO Byron Allen, performer Patrika Darbo, actor-director-producer Francesca James and host-producer Meredith Vieira. The Silver Circle inductees are Fox TV Stations executive vp, programming and development Stephen Brown and announcer warm-up host Rubin Ervin. The Hollywood Reporter won its first Daytime Emmy , taking home the award for best arts and popular culture program for THR ’s Off Script roundtable series. Fellow PMC brand IndieWire additionally won best editing for a daytime studio program for its craft roundtables, with Trevor Wallace accepting for the brand. The 53rd Daytime Emmy Awards ceremony took place on Friday, Oct. 30 at the Hollywood Palladium. A complete list of the 2026 Daytime Emmy Awards winners follows. articles.title: Macklemore Wraps Up Free Palestine Tour in London: “It Was More Uncomfortable for Me to Stay Silent”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All October 31, 2026 3:13am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Macklemore at the Free Palestine Tour in London on Oct. 30, 2026 Photo credit: Zoe Rain Macklemore brought the final night of his Free Palestine Tour to London on Friday, telling a U.K. audience: “I don’t believe that staying silent is brave.” The sold-out event at the capital’s OVO Arena Wembley boasted a crowd of over 12,500 people, who cheered and screamed as the U.S. rapper spoke. The gigs come weeks after he was removed from Ed Sheeran’s Loop Tour for expressing his pro-Palestine views on stage. Sheeran later said it was a promoter decision to drop Macklemore, and that venues set to host the concerts threatened to pull out if Macklemore was on the bill. Related Stories Movies 'Fuxi: Four Tales of Feasting' Review: Whimsical Chinese Film Explores Myth and History Through a Series of Tasty Treats Business Japan's Anime Industry Hits a Record High of $28 Billion in 2025 In response, Macklemore launched his own benefit concert with acts in the British capital such as Aja Monet, Cure for Paranoia, Dana Saleh, Nemahsis, Lucas Jones, Paloma Faith, Roze, Shadia Mansour and Vic Mensa. Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg was among the guest speakers, along with Hollywood superstars Mark Ruffalo, Susan Sarandon, Javier Bardem, Cynthia Nixon, as well as Melissa Barrera and Julian Casablancas, dialing in remotely. “It was more uncomfortable for me to stay silent than to say something,” said Macklemore about the situation with Sheeran. “And I just want to say, I don’t believe that saying something is brave. I don’t believe that saying something is courageous. I believe that saying something is human. And those children in Gaza are our children. There is no separation.” He continued: “I want to say thank you to every single soul that is in here tonight who decided to step up, leave their couch, be in community, be reminded and feel what that frequency of love feels like.” Macklemore added about the 50 members of the British House of Lords who urged the U.K. government to ban his concert: “Regardless of what the 50 Lords have to say, this is a story of equality for all human beings around this earth.” All proceeds from the concerts in Dublin, Paris and London will go toward organizations supporting Palestinian communities through humanitarian relief, medical care, education, advocacy, policy change and community initiatives, according to the rapper’s team. Popular Irish acts Hozier and Kneecap were included on the lineup in Dublin , as was Boega, Sheeran’s backing band that pulled out of the Loop Tour in solidarity with Macklemore. After widespread backlash, Sheeran was emotional as he addressed the controversy onstage in Philadelphia last month : “I don’t want to disappoint fans, and I’ve never wanted to be an activist musician, but this has put me in the middle of an important and passionate argument about freedom of speech and the most complex political issue on the planet,” he said. “My concerts have always been a safe space for everyone, and that matters hugely to me. […] What happened in Israel and at the Nova Music Festival on October 7th was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain. What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable, and disproportionate.” Sheeran told the crowd: “Honoring my commitment to my fans is also completely essential to who I am, and that is why I’m here tonight on my own and continuing my current tour.” The singer added that he was “deeply worried about the idea that venues pre-approve content for performance. […] This happens in so many places that I perform around the world, but it should never happen in the free world.” According to numbers from the British Red Cross , the death toll in Gaza is over 69,000. Almost 1,200 Israelis were killed in the Oct. 7 attack in 2023. THR

articles.title: Georgia’s ‘Guria’ Wins Best Film at Asia Pacific Screen Awards as Thailand’s Sompot Chidgasornpongse Takes Director Prize
articles.full_text: × Oct 30, 2026 9:25pm PT Georgia’s ‘Guria’ Wins Best Film at Asia Pacific Screen Awards as Thailand’s Sompot Chidgasornpongse Takes Director Prize By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sanjay Gupta, Indian Director of ‘Kaante’ and ‘Zinda,’ Dies at 59 5 hours ago Sourav Ganguly’s ‘Bigg Boss Bangla’ Among Highlights as Indian Media Giant JioStar Revenues Climb 10% 9 hours ago How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made 10 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Asia Pacific Screen Awards Georgian filmmaker Levan Koguashvili’s “Guria” was named best film at the 19th Asia Pacific Screen Awards , handed out Oct. 30 at The Star Gold Coast in Queensland, Australia. Koguashvili shared the prize with fellow producers Olena Yershova and Boris Frumin. The film was made across seven countries: Georgia, Switzerland, Luxembourg, Bulgaria, Türkiye, Norway and Saudi Arabia. Related Stories ‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference Thai director Sompot Chidgasornpongse won best director for “9 Temples to Heaven,” a co-production involving Thailand, Singapore, France, Norway, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia and Qatar. Myanmar’s Aung Phyoe received a special mention in the directing category for “Fruit Gathering.” Afghan director Shahrbanoo Sadat took the Jury Grand Prize for “No Good Men.” This year’s field comprised 36 nominated films from 32 countries and regions. Nepalese actor Pushpa Thing Lama won best performance for “Elephants in the Fog,” and South Korea’s Sim Su-bin was named best new performer for “The World Before.” The screenplay award went to Rakan Mayasi, Wahid Ajmi and Pôl Seif for “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep,” backed by Belgium, Lebanon, Palestine, Qatar and Saudi Arabia. Vietnamese cinematographer Nguyễn Vinh Phúc won for “Hearing.” New Zealand’s Paloma Schneideman took best youth film for “Big Girls Don’t Cry,” produced by Vicky Pope and Thomas Coppell. The animation prize went to “The Violinist,” a co-production between Singapore, Spain and Italy that was co-directed by Singapore’s Ervin Han and Spain’s Raúl García. Itab Azzam and Jack MacInness won best documentary for “One in a Million,” a U.K.-U.S. film that follows the life of a Syrian refugee. Isabelle Kalandar, who both directed and produced “Another Birth,” received the Cultural Diversity Award for the Tajikistan, U.S. and Qatar collaboration. India’s R. Gowtham earned the Young Cinema Award, given with NETPAC, for “Members of the Problematic Family.” Malaysian filmmaker Haziqah Azemi won the Forum Filmmaker Award, run with The Post Lounge Group, for her project “Garek.” The story centers on a woman whose relationship is tested when she faces religious persecution after becoming pregnant outside marriage. Azemi, who took part in the Griffith Film School and APSA Regional Reels program, came back to APSA this year after developing the project with mentoring from APSA Academy member Yulia Evina Bhara. Tracey Vieira, chair of the Asia Pacific Screen Awards, said: “From ‘Guria’ and ‘No Good Men’ to ‘Elephants in the Fog,’ this year’s winners remind us of the extraordinary stories emerging from our region and the importance of creating opportunities for these voices to be recognized internationally.” Veteran Indian producer Bobby Bedi was handed the FIAPF Award for outstanding contribution to film in the Asia Pacific. Luis Alberto Scalella, president of FIAPF, said: “Through landmark films such as ‘Bandit Queen’ and ‘Fire,’ he has championed powerful stories that have challenged audiences and resonated far beyond India.” The ceremony also revealed five projects selected for the 2026 MPA APSA Academy Film Fund, each of which will get a $10,000 grant funded entirely by the Motion Picture Association. They are Payal Kapadia’s “A Memory of Being Here” (India), produced by Thomas Hakim; Davy Chou’s “My Father’s Glory” (France, Cambodia), produced by Charlotte Vincent; Taifeng Liu’s “A Place in the Sun” (China), produced by Janet (Yan Yan) Wu; Nicole Midori Woodford’s “Incarnation” (Singapore, Japan), produced by Anthony Chen; and Zhanana Kurmasheva’s documentary “The Story of My Shirt” (Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, China, Chile), produced by Banu Ramazanova. Three of the five projects are directed by women. Chen returns to the fund after working on “We Are All Strangers,” which received a grant in 2023 and was among this year’s nominees. Urmila Venugopalan, president and managing director, Asia Pacific, at the Motion Picture Association, said the success of films such as “9 Temples to Heaven,” which received MPA APSA Academy Film Fund support in 2021, “shows the importance of supporting filmmakers and their stories from the earliest stages of development.” Every APSA nominee, along with members of the nominations councils and juries, joins the APSA Academy, whose president is Australian screen veteran Jack Thompson. The body now has upward of 1,816 members across 84 countries and areas. The full list of winners: Best Film “Guria,” dir. Levan Koguashvili; prod. articles.title: How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made
articles.full_text: × Oct 30, 2026 9:38pm PT How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sanjay Gupta, Indian Director of ‘Kaante’ and ‘Zinda,’ Dies at 59 5 hours ago Sourav Ganguly’s ‘Bigg Boss Bangla’ Among Highlights as Indian Media Giant JioStar Revenues Climb 10% 9 hours ago How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made 10 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Hidari Inc. Keanu Reeves joined Japanese stop-motion feature “ Hidari ” after watching the project’s pilot film, with his team getting back to the filmmakers about a week after the screening was arranged to set up a Zoom call, director Kawamura Masashi said at the Tokyo International Film Festival , where he also updated the film’s fundraising push. Kawamura, who created, wrote and is directing “Hidari,” appeared with co-director Ogawa Iku at a session reporting on Film Frontier, a talent development program backed by Japan’s Agency for Cultural Affairs and run by festival organizer UniJapan. The program has paid for the team’s travel to markets and industry events. Related Stories ‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference Reeves’ casting as the lead voice was announced at Cannes in May, but Kawamura said the actor had seen the pilot before the festival. “We were heavily influenced by Kurosawa’s films, so when the puppet was being made, I asked for Mifune Toshiro and Keanu Reeves added together, divided by two and then aged,” Kawamura said. From then on, Kawamura kept Reeves at the top of his list for the lead voice. The film’s producers took that seriously, found a way to reach the actor and arranged for him to watch the pilot. “About a week later we heard back, and it was, ‘OK, let’s do a Zoom,’” Kawamura said. “I was thinking, so this is how fast things move these days. Then we got on the call and Keanu was there on the other side.” “Hidari” has also caught the eye of “RRR” director S.S. Rajamouli . Kawamura said he met the Indian filmmaker at Annecy, showed him “Hidari” and ended up in a standing conversation of about 30 minutes about how the film was made. “He said, ‘You’re amazing. How did you make this?’” Kawamura said. Kawamura said an encounter like that, with a director he would rarely cross paths with otherwise, could only happen at a festival. “There’s the surprise inside the theater, and there are the connections after you walk out,” he said. The team shot the proof-of-concept short around three years ago, paying for it themselves with help from crowdfunding, and posted it on YouTube. It has since drawn about 5.3 million views and roughly 120,000 followers, many of them overseas, according to Kawamura. “Wood carving, stop-motion and a period drama – it’s a very austere project,” he said. “If we’d pitched it with just a written proposal, I don’t think anyone would have understood it.” With Film Frontier support, the filmmakers pitched “Hidari” at the Annecy Animation Showcase, part of the Cannes Film Market, carrying one of the hand-carved puppets with them. Kawamura said the puppet drew bigger crowds than its makers, and the Cannes platform put the film in front of live-action and action fans as well as distributors and agents. “Stop-motion is a really small world, and people tend to assume it’s a narrow market,” Kawamura said. “But even though it’s stop-motion, we think of it as an action film.” The budget is large, and the team is still out selling the project, seeking grants and partnerships with overseas distributors, Kawamura said. “In terms of speed, we’re making it the indie way,” he added. “Thanks to being light on our feet, I think the project has managed to make it across thin ice.” Earlier this month in Busan, Dwarf Studios producer Matsumoto Noriko said talks with a U.S. company that had offered to fund the entire budget, in exchange for all the rights, had stalled. Ogawa, who works at stop-motion house Dwarf Studios, attended Annecy this year. He said the technique remains niche in commercial film and TV animation, but festival shorts and student sections are full of it, and studios from Europe, North America and beyond converge on Annecy. “When I took the puppet along, it was hugely popular,” he said. “It was fun.” Film Frontier, now in its third year, is part of the Agency for Cultural Affairs’ Creator Support Fund, which backs creators for around three years, from project development through to overseas rollout. articles.full_text: × Oct 30, 2026 11:20pm PT Sourav Ganguly’s ‘Bigg Boss Bangla’ Among Highlights as Indian Media Giant JioStar Revenues Climb 10% By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sanjay Gupta, Indian Director of ‘Kaante’ and ‘Zinda,’ Dies at 59 5 hours ago Sourav Ganguly’s ‘Bigg Boss Bangla’ Among Highlights as Indian Media Giant JioStar Revenues Climb 10% 8 hours ago How Keanu Reeves Landed in Stop-Motion Samurai Epic ‘Hidari’ – and Why S.S. Rajamouli Wanted to Know How It Was Made 10 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jio Hotstar JioStar , the Indian media giant backed by Reliance Industries, grew revenue from operations 10.1% year-on-year to INR68.1 billion ($710 million) in the July–September quarter despite a weak advertising market. Profit after tax fell 13.2% to INR11.5 billion ($120 million). Former India cricket captain Sourav Ganguly hosted the first-ever “ Bigg Boss Bangla,” which launched this quarter on streaming service JioHotstar . The reality franchise rolled out in six languages, and all editions together pulled in more than 90 million viewers in their first three weeks. That makes “Bigg Boss” the biggest entertainment property on the platform. Related Stories 'Clean Hands' Review: Zach Braff Is a Cop on a Crusade to Save His Addict Daughter in an Uneasy Fact-Based Crime Drama ‘Street Fighter’ Review: Video Game Fighter Film Knocks Itself Unconscious Reliance Industries credited JioStar’s revenue growth to subscriptions and to advertising on digital entertainment. Gross revenue rose 9.8% to INR79.4 billion ($829 million). Margins came under pressure. EBITDA from operations dropped 10.5% to INR13.7 billion ($143 million), and the margin fell to 22.1% from 28.1% a year earlier. A 36.6% drop in investment income pulled total EBITDA down 13.6% to INR15 billion ($157 million). The quarter was also well below April–June, when JioStar booked INR109.5 billion ($1.1 billion) in revenue from operations. JioHotstar averaged about 440 million monthly active users over the three months, up 10% on the prior year. In September, the platform relaunched under the JioHotstar name in the U.K., Canada and Singapore. Reliance said active subscribers in those three territories have grown about 30% since then. The company also introduced “Pay Kisi Aur Se” (“Ask Others to Pay”), which lets users send a subscription payment request to a friend or relative. Reliance said the feature raised payment initiations by 10%. Subscribers on mobile plans now get up to two hours a month of viewing on connected TVs. The average JioHotstar viewer on a connected TV watches three times as much as one on a phone. Watch time for entertainment content grew more than 15%, with Hindi and regional markets performing well. Reliance said titles including “India Ke Top 1%,” “Khatron Ke Khiladi,” “Hustle” Season 5 and “Bhojpuri Bawaal” strengthened JioStar’s position as the country’s top entertainment network. “Resort” became the most-watched title in the streamer’s history, which Reliance cited as evidence that its bet on long-running series is paying off. Rajkumar Hirani’s “Pritam & Pedro” set the platform record for a short-running series. “Heart Beat” Season 3 and new series “Court” both opened strongly, and Hindi drama “Thukra Ke Mera Pyaar” Season 2 improved on its first season. Tadka also grew its catalog, adding nearly 100 titles spanning reality, sports and other categories. In sports, the England–India cricket series gave JioHotstar its biggest audience yet for a bilateral series played abroad. Wimbledon, the U.S. Open and the opening weeks of the 2026–27 Premier League season drew steady audiences and were monetized more effectively, according to the company. JioStar also expanded its commerce integrations, which had been limited to cricket, to all three events. The results came two days after Jio Platforms, Reliance’s separate telecom and digital arm, listed on Indian stock exchanges. Reliance said the INR301.9 billion ($3.15 billion) IPO is the largest in India to date. Mukesh Ambani, Reliance’s chairman and managing director, said the issue was subscribed more than 22 times. articles.title: Ozu Shapes Mishima Yukiko’s Tokyo Competition Title ‘Two Cigarettes, Three Nights’
articles.full_text: × Oct 30, 2026 11:40pm PT Ozu Shapes Mishima Yukiko’s Tokyo Competition Title ‘Two Cigarettes, Three Nights’ By Mark Schilling Plus Icon Mark Schilling Japan Correspondent Latest Pink Film Veteran Zeze Takahisa Champions Original Stories at Tokyo Masterclass 6 hours ago Ozu Shapes Mishima Yukiko’s Tokyo Competition Title ‘Two Cigarettes, Three Nights’ 8 hours ago AI Can Critique Shakespeare but Can’t Write It, Russo Brothers’ AGBO Execs Tell Tokyo Market 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mark Schilling Known for her dark relationship dramas, including the 2017 multiple-award-winner “Dear Etranger,” Mishima Yukiko has taken a different approach with her latest film, “Two Cigarettes, Three Nights,” which is in competition at the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival . Based on a 2014 novel by Chihaya Akane, it stars Matsuoka Mayu as Kanna, a picture book illustrator who has tired of her nice-but-boring live-in boyfriend (Inoue Yuki) while having nothing but a physical connection with her cynical married lover (Nakajima Ayumu). Related Stories ‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference Then a close friend from her college days, Haseo (Narita Ryo), reenters her life after a gap of seven years and once again becomes her confidant. Now a salesman for a drug company and still single, Haseo is something of a womanizer, though he keeps his relationship with Kanna strictly platonic. Shot in Kyoto, Hiroshima and Toyama Prefecture, the film makes screenwriter Sawai Kaori’s talky script feel visually dynamic, while avoiding cliché shots in Kyoto and Hiroshima, two of Japan’s most famous tourist destinations. Instead of posing against temples and cherry blossoms, the two principals stroll along a riverbank or on railroad tracks as they renew their friendship – and flirt with something more. “When deciding on a location, it’s not just about picking a ‘pretty’ spot,” says Mishima in an interview at Tokyo Midtown, the main festival site. “Rather it’s more about choosing a place where the scene comes to life.” “Also, the novel has a lot of scenes set inside a coffee shop, but in the movie (Kanna and Haseo) are walking just about the whole time,” she adds. Years ago, she and a male friend spent more time walking together than sitting inside a shop and talking, she recalls. “We didn’t talk about our worries and troubles – we’d walk until dawn, just chatting about trivial things.” “Trivial” is not the word to describe the film’s dialogue, but it has a bantering tone, as well as an unfiltered honesty. At the same time, Kanna and Haseo don’t face each other right away. “I didn’t want them to do that until a certain point,” says Mishima. “I wanted them to always be looking in the same direction. So when they go into a ramen shop, they are sitting side by side at a counter. The same with buses and trains – they sit next to each other, looking in the same direction.” A big influence in her shotmaking style, Mishima says, is Ozu Yasujiro, who often filmed characters side by side or even making the same motions in unison. “I love how he captures the way people move within the flow of Japanese life, without cutting the shot, creating a sense of wonder,” she says. “He is also brilliant in how he makes a grand narrative emerge from small, personal moments, so I’ve been greatly influenced by that as well. My film starts from that personal perspective, but then it kind of opens up to the world.” The film’s first act hints at sex comedy, and Mishima cast both of her leads – Matsuoka (“Tremble All You Want”) and Narita (“Convenience Story”) – with their comic abilities in mind. But she has crafted something more intimate and complex, with an ending open to interpretation. “I thought that having a good sense for comedy was essential for the long dialogue scenes,” says Mishima. “They require a sense of rhythm and actors with a feel for comedy have it. It makes a huge difference.” The film is no lighthearted laugh fest: Kanna and Haseo are not always likable characters, acting in ways selfish, callous and even cruel. “I think movies should be able to portray all kinds of people and tell all kinds of stories,” says Mishima. “And it’s good to have characters that represent all kinds of people, too.” “I think viewers will probably be able to relate to their emotions,” she adds. “They’ll be able to find a part of themselves – ‘Oh, I’ve felt this way too.’ That’s what makes a good actor. No matter how bad the person they’re portraying is, you end up understanding them or rather you can’t help but feel the way they do. That’s their charm.” Other characters add their perspectives, such as a surly bartender who is close to Haseo and thinks Kanna is hurting him, and Kanna’s jaded college friend who freely admits to cheating on her husband and sympathizes with Kanna’s infidelities. “I wanted to present the story in a multi-layered way,” says Mishima. “The film’s Japanese title is ‘The Male Friend,’ but it gradually drifts away from that theme. It’s more a story about what Kanna comes to see. By spending time with Haseo, she gains a perspective that lets her see not just herself but the world.” Kanna’s art also changes. In sharp contrast to the commercial hack work that pays her bills, she completes a painting that grows out of her three eventful days with Haseo. “What I want to convey is embedded in that final painting,” says Mishima. “Kanna learns something in Hiroshima about herself and the world and puts that message into her painting. I wanted to depict the whole process, right up to the point where viewers come to see her painting and receive that message.” Alexander Ludwig on ‘Unabomber’ Movie, His ‘Hunger Games’ Death Scene and ‘White Lotus’ Season 4: ‘It’s F—ing Wild’ Blackpink and ‘White Lotus’ Star Lisa Documentary ‘Always Lalisa’ Sets Global Release France Riots Put Hollywood Shoots on Alert as Curfews Disrupt Movie Theaters: It ‘Has Now Been Flagged as a Problem Area’ Thailand Bets on Film Tourism to Turn Movie Locations Into Travel Destinations Loading comments...

articles.title: Japan’s New 2027 Anime Award Should Put Creators in the Spotlight, Industry Leaders Say at Tokyo Market
articles.full_text: × Oct 30, 2026 11:51pm PT Japan’s New 2027 Anime Award Should Put Creators in the Spotlight, Industry Leaders Say at Tokyo Market By Kambole Campbell Plus Icon Kambole Campbell Latest Japan’s New 2027 Anime Award Should Put Creators in the Spotlight, Industry Leaders Say at Tokyo Market 8 hours ago Taiwanese Feature ‘Uncle’ Wins Top Prize at Tokyo Gap-Financing Market Awards 1 day ago Aliens, Dinosaurs and a Father’s Death: ‘Kefi’ Director Saito Kisin Brings a Surreal Take on Grief to Tokyo 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kawakami Takashi A new Japanese anime award planned for 2027 should put the people who make anime in the spotlight, industry leaders said at TIFFCOM , the market of the Tokyo International Film Festival . The session was moderated by Fujitsu Ryota, programming advisor for the festival’s animation section. Shimizu Akira, a director of the Association of Japanese Animations (AJA), is president and representative director of A-1 Pictures. He was joined by Studio Chizu president Saito Yuichiro, producer of “The Girl Who Leapt Through Time,” “Summer Wars” and “Wolf Children,” and Saito Masaya, chief manager of Toho’s animation division and planning group leader. Related Stories ‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference The award’s name and outline will be revealed Nov. 2 at the closing event of Tokyo Anime Next, the festival that organized the session. Co-hosted by the AJA and the Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Tokyo Anime Next runs Oct. 30–Nov. 2 in Tokyo’s Ikebukuro district, with several events at TIFFCOM. The 2027 launch date has yet to be confirmed, and the panelists stressed that their views were not the award’s official positions. “Creators should be highlighted – and they should be put in the limelight,” Shimizu said when asked about the timing of the launch. Saito Masaya said Toho had helped work on the concept for the award, and agreed that creators should be highlighted. He added that the award could give fans a more direct connection to the people behind anime’s global popularity. The company wants to “help achieve a wider reach to anime fans and help give them a wider perspective,” he said, bringing them closer to different creative styles and approaches. Saito Yuichiro, a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, said an award is only one part of what the Academy does. “There are many different branches of work beyond the award,” he said. “The Academy Award in the United States is a domestic award, but it now has a global membership. They also provide training, and try to create a sort of succession plan for the industry. This kind of philosophy is the backbone for the award.” Ideally, the panelists said, financial support and training would also be among the building blocks of the new award. Saito Masaya said he hoped the award “can contribute to the changing of the ways audience enjoy anime.” He wants fans “to notice a certain aspect and ask who is behind this,” he added. Shimizu said the need to showcase the value of Japanese animation was “one of the key phrases.” “Japanese anime has a very unique workflow and processes, so who does what and who evaluates what, and who delivers those, and how are they embraced and valued by the audience,” he said. The panel noted that some awards have already picked up on that uniqueness. The Annie Awards have added a best international anime production for TV/media category for their 54th edition. “Japanese anime is a standalone established category,” Shimizu said, “anime is different from Disney, it is different from Pixar.” He said the new award should reflect those differences by spotlighting the creators who work on each part of an anime’s production. “For a layperson, the beauty of the anime can’t be expressed clearly in words,” he said. Saito Yuichiro said the world has two major trends. “The first one is this European Art History, generated from that long history and value system, and the worldwide large-scale trends centered in the United States. The world is composed of these two systems,” he said. He asked whether Asia could build its own equivalent “aesthetics and value system,” and whether an awards body could help bring an Asian voice into a system he sees as dominated by Europe and the U.S. “Borderlessness is very important, what I’d hope is to blur the boundaries between these areas of the world with these awards,” he said. articles.title: Japan’s Film Funds Look Beyond Production Committees to Build New Financing Models
articles.full_text: × Oct 31, 2026 1:15am PT Japan’s Film Funds Look Beyond Production Committees to Build New Financing Models By Lin Ying-Hsuan Plus Icon Lin Ying-Hsuan Latest Annecy Winner ‘The Violinist’ Found Its Italian Co-Producers at Tokyo Market, Director Ervin Han Tells Anime Co-Production Panel 1 day ago Japan’s Anime Market Hits Record $28.2 Billion as Local Sales Surge 1 day ago ‘Godzilla Minus One’ U.S. Success ‘Wasn’t a Strategy; We Just Tried,’ Says Toho CEO at Tokyo Festival 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lin Ying-Hsuan Japan’s production committee system, in which a group of companies jointly finance a film and share its rights, has helped spread risk across the industry. But it can also cap budgets at what the industry itself can raise, make it harder for overseas investors to take part and slow decisions when every rights holder must agree. At a panel at TIFFCOM , the content market of the Tokyo International Film Festival , speakers examined whether film funds can ease those limits while still fitting Japan’s market. Related Stories ‘God of War’s’ Bruno Velazquez, ‘Mandalorian & Grogu’s’ Hal Hickel Detail Cinema-Gaming Crossover at View Conference “Film Funds in Japan: What Works, What Doesn’t, and What Comes Next” featured Kii Muneyuki, CEO and producer of K2 Pictures, which works with filmmakers including Kore-eda Hirokazu , Miike Takashi and Nishikawa Miwa; Ibe Tomonobu, CEO of Questry, a Tokyo startup that uses digital securities to fund anime and other Japanese content; Nakagawa Keita, managing director at MUFG Bank; and Motoyanagi Yusuke, partner at law firm Nishimura & Asahi. Kii presented K2P Film Fund I as one example of a new structure. The fund closed in February at about JPY5 billion ($32 million) and aims to back around 50 films over seven years. It is a blind pool, meaning investors commit money before the films are chosen. Its investors include MUFG, the Development Bank of Japan and other financial institutions and companies, and a greenlight committee oversees project approvals. Kii said five films had been released in theaters in 2026. Kii said a central question for film funds is how to return revenue to creators, including income from streaming and other windows after a film’s theatrical run. He also said it is hard to rely on overseas box office, and that Japanese companies need to build businesses beyond distribution. The panel compared financing structures in the U.S. and South Korea. In the U.S., producers combine presales with completion guarantees to help secure bank loans. A completion guarantee covers delivery of a film on budget and on schedule, rather than its commercial performance. South Korea relies on public-private support, with government-backed guarantees helping projects get bank financing. Nakagawa presented a Japan-specific feasibility study commissioned by the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry. MUFG was selected to carry it out on March 31. Running through February 2027, the study will use real-world data to develop valuation and completion-guarantee models, and test the full process from application and review to contract drafting. The study assesses feasibility and does not guarantee that financing or completion guarantees will become available. The discussion closed with four priorities: regulation, capital, creators and cross-border business. These include clarifying which regulations should be expanded and when, combining debt with subsidies and completion guarantees, and building creator returns into fund structures. Speakers also pointed to language and tax hurdles to cross-border investment, including “permanent establishment” rules that can make international investors liable for Japanese tax.
