articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Searchlight Pictures Marketing EVP Michelle Hooper Leaving Studio Steven Paul’s SP Media Creates Joint Venture With Lionsgate To Expand New Businesses, Closes Film Pact ‘Clayface’ Beams $43M WW Opening, Delivers Paramount-Warner Bros. Second No. 1 Weekend Win Since Merger – Global Box Office View All October 26, 2026 5:31pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Michelle Hooper Searchlight Pictures EXCLUSIVE: We hear that Searchlight Pictures ‘ EVP of Marketing Michelle Hooper , who delivered the specialty label numerous Oscar nominations and wins during her two-decade tenure, is exiting. Hooper led publicity, awards and creative marketing operations, earning the studio 21 Best Picture Oscar nominations — including Best Picture winners Slumdog Millionaire , 12 Years a Slave , Birdman , The Shape of Water and Nomadland ; a total of 183 Oscar nominations; and 49 wins. Related Stories News Disney Hit By Layoffs, A Couple Hundred Workers Cut News Disney+ & Channel 4 Strike Landmark Deal In UK As far as Golden Globes go, her work delivered 32 awards from 133 nominations, including 20 Best Picture noms and eight wins. Hooper, who joined Searchlight in 2006, is respected by her peers for her taste, whip-smart instincts, creativity and ingenuity in marketing, and was internally known as “the closer,” bringing a film’s campaign home in its final stretch. Her campaigns for various Oscar winners often dialed into the cultural zeitgeist, from understanding how Nomadland would resonate in the context of the pandemic, to spotting the cultural relevance of Slumdog Millionaire in the Obama era, and appreciating the historical significance of 12 Years a Slave , which was closely followed by Birdman. This season, Hooper’s awards campaigns include for Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine (93% certified fresh) and Tony Gilroy’s Behemoth! (87% fresh on Rotten Tomatoes). Watch on Deadline Prior to joining Searchlight, Hooper spent four years at Fox Broadcasting where she was VP of Entertainment Publicity. While at Fox, Hooper spearheaded the implementation of national publicity campaigns for multiple series such as launching American Idol , 24 , Arrested Development , Family Guy and The Simpsons . Prior to joining Fox, Hooper was the Director of Entertainment Communications at CBS Entertainment in New York, where she was part of the team that launched and created the publicity campaign for Survivor . After Disney acquired 20th Century Fox in March 2019, Hooper made the jump. I understand that Hooper’s departure is part of the cuts that occurred at the Disney studio earlier this month. Other notable releases during Hooper’s Searchlight administration include James Mangold’s eight-time Oscar-nominated A Complete Unknown, starring Timothée Chalamet as Bob Dylan; Jesse Eisenberg’s A Real Pain , which won an Oscar for Kieran Culkin; Marielle Heller’s Nightbitch starring Amy Adams; Yorgos Lanthimos’ four-time Academy Award winner Poor Things, starring and produced by Emma Stone; Lanthimos’ follow-up Kinds of Kindness , also starring Stone with Jesse Plemons, Hong Chau and Margaret Qualley; and Andrew Haigh’s romantic drama All of Us Strangers starring Andrew Scott, Paul Mescal, Jamie Bell and Claire Foy. She also oversaw the marketing on streaming originals such as Tina Mabry’s The Supremes at Earl’s All-You-Can-Eat starring Uzo Aduba, Aunjanue Ellis-Taylor and Sanaa Lathan; Karrie Crouse and Will Joines’ Hold Your Breath starring Sarah Paulson; and Eva Longoria’s Oscar-nominated Flamin’ Hot , which became the first original film to debut simultaneously on both Hulu and Disney+ and is Searchlight’s most-watched streaming motion picture of all time. Other past successful films during Hooper’s reign include The Favourite, Can You Ever Forgive Me?, Isle of Dogs, Super Troopers 2, Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri, Gifted, Jackie, Brooklyn, Wild, The Grand Budapest Hotel, Beasts of the Southern Wild, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel, The Descendants, The Tree of Life, Black Swan, 127 Hours, Crazy Heart, 500 Days of Summer, The Wrestler, Juno, Once, Little Miss Sunshine and The Last King of Scotland. Hooper shared the Publicist Guild of America’s Maxwell Weinberg Showmanship Award for her work on Survivor . She is a member of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences and BAFTA. articles.title: Milcho Manchevski Talks ‘Sister Brother Manhole Cover’, His Second Feature Of 2026 & Exposing Corruption At Macedonia’s Film Agency — Tokyo
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Bill Kramer Says AMPAS Plans To Expand List Of Festivals That Can Serve As Qualifiers For The International Oscar Category Milcho Manchevski Talks ‘Sister Brother Manhole Cover’, His Second Feature Of 2026 & Exposing Corruption At Macedonia’s Film Agency — Tokyo Janus Films Acquires Alfonso Cuarón’s ‘Y Tu Mamá También’ Ahead Of 25th Anniversary 4K Re-Release View All October 26, 2026 5:48pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tokyo Film Festival. This week, Macedonian filmmaker Milcho Manchevski returns with Sister Brother Manhole Cover , his second feature of the year, which screens in competition at the Tokyo Film Festival. Directed by Manchevski from a screenplay he also wrote, Sister Brother Manhole Cover follows siblings Malina and Viktor, who live on the outskirts of post-Communist Macedonia. They make their living stealing bronze busts and manhole covers, which line their city’s streets. When a routine theft goes wrong and Viktor is badly injured, Malina strikes a desperate deal with a corrupt doctor, forcing them into a dangerous journey through Macedonia’s underworld. Their journey leads to an unexpected refuge: the opulent home of the doctor’s blind mother. Related Stories News Parallax Films Boards Sales On 'Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting' Ahead of Tokyo World Premiere News Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi Pledges Support For Japanese Film At Tokyo Fest Opening Sister Brother Manhole Cover is Manchevski’s ninth feature. The filmmaker debuted his first documentary, Good People , earlier this year at the Sarajevo Film Festival. Watch on Deadline “It’s unusual to have two films come out at the same time, but better two than zero,” Manchevski joked in an interview with Deadline ahead of his trip to Tokyo for Sister Brother, adding that he is enjoying this productive period after spending many years being barred from producing films in his home country. Manchevski, who won the Golden Lion at Venice with his debut feature Before the Rain (1994), was blacklisted and had several projects halted by the Macedonian Film Agency after he reported corruption at the organization. Manchevski’s accusations were later upheld by Macedonia’s Anti-Corruption Commission after an investigation. Below, the veteran filmmaker, who lives between New York and Macedonia, speaks with Deadline about the extensive witch hunt he endured after exposing corruption at the Macedonian Film Agency, finally getting to make Sister Brother Manhole Cover, and why he believes the Tokyo Film Festival is the perfect launchpad for movies. Sister Brother Manhole Cover is a Banana Film production, in co-production with Gala Film (Bulgaria), Sense Production (Serbia), Tirana Film Institute (Albania), Berkeley Media Group (UK), Amarcord Production in association with Augustus Color (Italy) with the support of North Macedonia Film Agency, the Bulgarian National Film Center, Film Center Serbia, the Albanian National Center of Cinematography, and Italy’s Direzione Generale Cinema e Audiovisivo – Ministero della Cultura. The Rome-based Coccinelle Film is handling world sales on the title. DEADLINE: Milcho, where did this idea come from? MILCHO MANCHEVSKI: I wanted to make a film about sisterly and brotherly love—something we rarely see in movies or even in literature. It was also partly inspired by Macedonian folk songs and folk literature, which often include the theme of sisterly love. Sometimes it turns shocking and dark, but it is always fully dedicated. That was the initial embryo. Then I wanted to talk about inequality and wealth inequality. I think that’s the premier issue of today. So many problems in the world go back to this sense of unfairness and inequality. That feeling festers in people. But I didn’t want to turn it into an exclusively dark story. I thought it should be told through defiance and humor, because Victor and Marlena don’t see themselves as victims. They see themselves as people with agency—people who do things. Unfortunately, pretty much the only thing they can do is petty crime. DEADLINE: Yeah, I loved the idea of people stealing the busts. It’s so European. MANCHEVSKI: People actually do it. It’s three euros a kilo for the metal. I did a little research. There was an explosion of new monuments in Macedonia in the early 2010s, because the nationalist government decided to reintroduce us to our past. There was plenty of cash just lying around. And the manhole covers, they cover the underground and the septic part of us that we don’t really want to smell or see. Then our heroes take them off, and you can smell the reek. DEADLINE: I read this film was previously titled Leaving Copacabana? MANCHEVSKI: Yes. The title was Leaving Copacabana . Copacabana was their slum, which we constructed for the film. The little shacks you see are leaning on an ancient aqueduct. We got permission from the government to work there because it’s a national monument. We constructed the shacks for two reasons: first, to have full control; and second, so we wouldn’t go into somebody’s home—somebody’s slum—and disrupt their life. The slum was jokingly called Copacabana, as if they were in Brazil. The tagline was “sister, brother, manhole cover.” But that title somehow took over because it’s more irreverent and catchier, and I think it describes the film better. It’s not so much about leaving one place and going to a richer place; it’s about their relationship and society. DEADLINE: Where did you shoot this film? There are a lot of locations. MANCHEVSKI: Everything was done on location. There was no studio. And even on location, we didn’t want to change too much. The exception was the slum, which we constructed based on actual slums in Skopje. Most are inhabited by Roma, but not exclusively. We built it around the aqueduct because I liked the graphic quality, but also because it incorporated the ancient past into the very prosaic present of the characters and the whole community. Everything else was scouted around Skopje. We looked for actual places that had a certain smell, places where you could feel the underbelly, but also places that could give us a cross-section of society. For example, you have the illegal dump, which we had to sanitize so people could work there. DEADLINE: That was a real dump? MANCHEVSKI: That was a real dump. We took over a corner of it, sanitized the area, and brought in our own paper and cloth—things that didn’t stink too much. We had to ward off dogs. We liked that particular dump because you could see the highway below. Again, there was this contrast: here and there, us and them. That’s necessary when you’re telling a drama. The house was a real house, too. We didn’t do much to it; we brought in the piano and the busts, which we created, of course. I’m taking one of the manhole covers to the red carpet in Tokyo next week. DEADLINE: You’ve become a regular at Tokyo Film Festival. Why do you screen your films here? MANCHEVSKI: It’s an old love story. Before the Rain , my first film, played Tokyo. Going there and spending time there was so nice. I like how people in Japan, and especially at the festival, appreciate films. They take special care with them; they create new posters and trailers. It’s not just a run-of-the-mill place or festival. Then Dust played there, and then Kaymak . Now, I want to go there—it is at the top of my list. DEADLINE: This is your second film of the year. You were in Sarajevo with the doc Good People. I read that this was mostly because for years you were unable to produce anything? MANCHEVSKI: Yes, for a while, I wasn’t able to work because I reported corruption at the film agency in Macedonia. I did it twice, and it was eventually confirmed by the Anti-Corruption Commission and the State Audit Office. As retaliation, they blacklisted me, filed criminal charges against me, launched a smear campaign, and blocked my previous films and films in progress. Eventually I won two court cases against the agency, and the dam broke. This film was initially approved in 2022, and then, at the same time, the tragedy in Kočani happened. I felt I should make a documentary about it. The two films are completely different stylistically. There’s a lot of humor in Sister Brother ; there’s no humor in Good People . It’s somber, with a glimmer of hope at the end. The overlap mostly happened in the edit, where you can shuttle between the two. I know it’s unusual to have two films come out at the same time, but better two than zero. DEADLINE: You’ve worked across the United States and Europe and have been able to make many different kinds of things. Many European and American filmmakers now talk about how difficult it is to make work. How do you feel about the industry today? MANCHEVSKI: I’m always an outsider, and I like it that way. I’ve lived in New York since 1985, but recently I’ve mostly been making films in Europe because of the general attitude toward filmmaking and the arts. Financing is always tough. It’s the curse of filmmaking. I’m jealous of painters and poets: you sit down, do your work, and it’s done. Maybe nobody will see it or like it, but at least it’s finished. With film, you first have to sell it and then make it. Filmmaking involves a lot of money, technology, and egos. Working in Europe has advantages, but distribution is not as muscular as in Hollywood. But nobody tells you how to end the film, whom to cast, or whether you need to reshoot a scene. You want feedback and collaboration, but it’s not a situation where the money dictates what the art will look like. That’s why I prefer Europe to Hollywood. I’ve worked in the United States—I worked on The Wire for HBO, made an independent film, developed films with studios, and even started a studio film. But in the last decade or so, there has been pressure to conform ideologically and make films with messages. I think every film has a message by default. The question is whether it offers more: Is there beauty in the film? Is there something profound? Does it talk about a bigger truth rather than just a message? The pressure—from festivals and film funds—to be message-driven and ideological comes at the expense of everything else. Even when I agree with the message, it’s a pity that so much contemporary cinema turns into two-dimensional pamphlets. articles.title: Neil Young Rocks Trump With $10M Suit Over Using That ‘Free World’ Tune Again
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Jay Z & Apple Make It Official! Hova’s Headlining The Super Bowl Halftime Show Neil Young Rocks Trump With $10M Suit Over Using That ‘Free World’ Tune Again ‘Smear’ Campaign: George Clooney, Betty Gilpin, Adam Scott & Laverne Cox Team To Read Clark Gregg-Penned Political Play As Midterms Fundraiser View All October 26, 2026 6:48pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Neil Young, Donald Trump Getty Images Almost no one expects Donald Trump to keep his word, but unlike most, Neil Young ain’t taking any crap from the former Apprentice host. Having repeatedly told Trump to keep his MAGA mitts off his classic Rockin’ in the Free World song, the 80-year-old Grandfather of Grunge took the poll struggling POTUS back to court today with new $10 million copyright infringement suit. And, as Young always does on the guitar, the two time Rock & Roll Hall of Famer let Trump have it. “ Rockin’ in the Free World is a blistering anthem that contrasts the hollow promises of American political rhetoric with the harsh realities faced by the poor, homeless and forgotten,” the short but sharp complaint says. “The lyrics paint vivid street-level portraits – a mother discarding her baby, addicts lost in despair, garbage piling in the shadows of prosperity – while the repeated chorus delivers a savage irony, celebrating freedom that clearly isn’t shared by all. In short, the Song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for.” Related Stories News CNN And Politico Again Are Barred From Air Force One Politics 'Smear' Campaign: George Clooney, Betty Gilpin, Adam Scott & Laverne Cox Team To Read Clark Gregg-Penned Political Play As Midterms Fundraiser Trump first used the 1991 hit back at the very start of his first serious (semi-serious?) White House run in 2015. Young told him to back off then and told Trump to back off again in 2020 with legal action. As Young’s critiques of Trump got louder and louder in song and from the stage, it seemed the 45th and now 47th President, or at least his attorneys, got it — until October 12. in Youngstown, Ohio. Watch on Deadline The the five-page filing in federal court in Virginia states: “Just prior to Donald J. Trump taking the stage to speak at the Youngstown Rally, the Committee caused Rockin’ in the Free World to be played. On information and belief, the Committee has caused the Song to be played numerous times at other rallies designed to encourage Republican votes in the upcoming mid-term elections.” As today made clear, you don’t mess with old Neil and you don’t break your word to him. “Donald J. Trump (‘Trump’) is now and at the time of all rallies this year was personally aware that a license would be required to play the Song at rallies and that Young has not, and would not, grant the required license,” proclaims the complaint. “In 2020 Young sued another corporation formed by Trump, Donald J. Trump For President, Inc., for copyright infringement of Rockin’ in the Free World along with another song written by Young,” the document by lawyers Scott Simmons and Robert Besser against Trump 47 Committee Inc. adds. “Donald J Trump For President, Inc. asserted no defense and immediately settled shortly after it was served, promising that it would never again use Rockin’ in the Free World without a license and permission from Young.” The White House did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment on the complaint. But, with 80-year old Trump posting fast and furiously for struggling GOP candidates, don’t be surprised if the octogenarian barbs starting flying like Tomahawk missiles soon-ish. On the other hand, the Neil Young, or at least his lawyers couldn’t resist a bit of wit, or at least a legalese laugh at Trump’s expense — and maybe even their own. “Young has suffered damage to his reputation and brand as a result of the implication that he supports Donald J. Trump in any way,” the filing says in a statement that literally no one anywhere would ever think. Keep on rockin’ that in the free world. articles.title: ‘Gilded Age’ Creator Julian Fellowes Calls HBO’s Casey Bloys “Our Protector & Our Defender From Very Early Days” During Season 4 Premiere

I certainly do, and I say that with both pride and happiness.” Related Stories News ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 Red Carpet Photos: Carrie Coon, Morgan Spector, Denée Benton, Cynthia Nixon & More News ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 Release Schedule: When Do New Episodes Come Out? Deadline reported in 2019 that, after NBC ordered the series, the creator’s vision for the period piece proved too ambitious for the constraints of broadcast TV. Universal TV shopped the series, and it landed at HBO in a competitive situation. The series finally premiered in 2022, with Season 4 debuting on Sunday, November 1. During the presentation, Fellowes also gave a shout-out to NBCU’s Pearlena Igbokwe as “one of the first to recognize” the specialness of the series. He also mentioned Bob Greenblatt for not letting it rest and for making the series, and called HBO’s Francesca Orsi “wonderful” for bringing the series home. Watch on Deadline Fellowes said that he had always been interested in the Gilded Age, calling it “a very interesting period of American history,” adding, “I think it was the beginning of modern America, and it was the moment that America decided they didn’t want to copy Europe and have five generations before anyone could be invited for dinner and all that kind of thing.” “Whatever one says about the so-called robber barons, the fact is, within a few years, the century would begin what we would know of as the American century,” he continued. “And in both world wars, the voice of America was the loudest at the peace table, because America had arrived, and it was the big, giant new power of the world.” AMPAS To Expand Festival Qualifier List For International Oscar SAG-AFTRA Faces Reckoning As Few Members Qualify For Streaming Bonus Clooney & Others Set For Read Of Political Play ‘Smear’ As Midterms Fundraiser Keanu Reeves Takes Over From Alan Ritchson As Lead In Netflix Actioner ‘Maelstrom’ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Rolf de Heer & Fellow Tokyo Jury Members Talk Festival ‘A-List’ Ratings, Co-Production & How To Judge Films
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Rolf de Heer & Fellow Tokyo Jury Members Talk Festival ‘A-List’ Ratings, Co-Production & How To Judge Films Parallax Films Boards Sales On ‘Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting’ Ahead of Tokyo World Premiere Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi Pledges Support For Japanese Film At Tokyo Fest Opening View All October 26, 2026 9:40pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Yov Moor, Oh Jungwan, Rolf de Heer, Makiko Watanabe, Alex Lo Deadline Australian filmmaker Rolf de Heer , president of the competition jury at this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival, talked about the significance of ‘A-list’ ratings for film festivals at the jury press conference today. Tokyo has recently had its status as an A-list festival reaffirmed by the Fédération Internationale des Associations des Producteurs de Films (FIAPF), a Brussels-based global organization that rates film festivals. But the practice of rating festivals, and the process and criteria for rating them, has proved controversial over the years. Related Stories News Milcho Manchevski Talks 'Sister Brother Manhole Cover', His Second Feature Of 2026 & Exposing Corruption At Macedonia's Film Agency -- Tokyo News Parallax Films Boards Sales On 'Fuxi: Four Tales Of Feasting' Ahead of Tokyo World Premiere In March this year, FIAPF overhauled its festival accreditation system for the first time since 2007, with a new framework that classifies 17 festivals as “A-list” and expanding the overall number of accredited festivals around the world. Five of these festivals are based in the Asia Pacific region, including Tokyo, Busan, IFFI Goa, Cairo and Shanghai. When asked about the ratings system, De Heer said: “Tokyo has always been considered an A-list festival by most people who attend festivals, so in that sense I don’t think it makes a lot of difference. This sort of categorization seems to be becoming more important in terms of the quality of films that are available to a festival, so in that sense it may help that Tokyo now officially has that rating again, but I don’t think it changes the festival so much.” Watch on Deadline FIAPF’s old system classified festivals in four groups: competitive, specialized, non-competitive and documentary and short film festivals. The 2026 reform collapsed the four categories into one group of 49 accredited festivals across 29 countries on five continents. When pushed on the subject with another question, De Heer said: “It matters a great deal to some people and not at all to others, and that is at it should be.” De Heer is heading the main competition jury at this year’s Tokyo film festival , along with Korean producer Oh Jungwan, New York and Tokyo-based producer Alex C. Lo, French colorist Yov Moor and Japanese actress Makiko Watanabe. The jury also talked about international co-productions, as several films in this year’s line-up of 15 competition titles have been structured this way. Lo agreed with a question from the audience about the growing trend: “I didn’t notice there’s an increasing number of co-productions in the festival line-up, but it’s true that a lot of producers in Europe, US and the rest of the world are increasingly seeking co-production opportunities, mainly due to the link to their local government production support.” When asked about the potential for co-productions between Japan and Australia, De Heer noted that the Australian film industry does not approach co-production in the same way as European producers: “It makes no sense for a Japanese film to shoot in Australia, and it makes no sense for an Australian film to shoot in Japan. Europe is very good at doing co-productions only on a financial basis. Australia is not so good at that. “The sort of co-productions that work out of Australia have a natural story where some things need to be shot in Japan, some things in Australia. Those will always be possible if the scripts come and if they’re right.” The jury also talked about their criteria for judging the 15 films in competition, which includes titles from across Europe and the Asia Pacific region. Oh Jungwan said: “For me as a jury member, I’m looking at whether I’m convinced by the story the director is telling and the way he’s telling it.” She later said she’s also prepared to fight for the films she loves and once had a seven-hour discussion about a film when serving on another jury. Yov Moor said: “When watching each film, I’m looking at what is interesting and sincere in the film, but also really trying to imagine what the next film of this director could be.” Makiko Watanabe added: “I try to see films without any preconceived notions and don’t try to look for answers while watching. As jury, there are other things we need to look at, but mostly I’ll look for what touches me and later digest what I took from the film.” Tokyo International Film Festival opened last night and runs for ten days in the Hibiya-Ginza district of Tokyo. It closes on November 4 with the awards ceremony and a screening of Korean filmmaker Yeon Sang-ho’s Colony. articles.title: Bill Kramer Says AMPAS Plans To Expand List Of Festivals That Can Serve As Qualifiers For The International Oscar Category
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Bill Kramer Says AMPAS Plans To Expand List Of Festivals That Can Serve As Qualifiers For The International Oscar Category Milcho Manchevski Talks ‘Sister Brother Manhole Cover’, His Second Feature Of 2026 & Exposing Corruption At Macedonia’s Film Agency — Tokyo Janus Films Acquires Alfonso Cuarón’s ‘Y Tu Mamá También’ Ahead Of 25th Anniversary 4K Re-Release View All October 26, 2026 10:39pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Bill Kramer AMPS The Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences will expand the list of festivals that can serve as standalone qualifiers for the International Film Oscar category, AMPAS CEO Bill Kramer confirmed this morning during an interview with Deadline at the Tokyo Film Festival. Related Stories News Oscars 2027 International Feature Film Submissions By Country: UK, Argentina, Iran, Rwanda Among Latest To Declare Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Kramer, who has become a frequent fixture on the international festival circuit in recent years, is at Tokyo alongside AMPAS President Lynette Howell Taylor and Chief Membership, Impact and Industry Officer Meredith Shea to take part in a series of public talks titled Academy in Tokyo. The sessions are one of the headline events this year at the Tokyo Film Festival . Kramer will also receive an honorary leadership award. Ahead of the festivities, Kramer sat down with Deadline in Tokyo. “Our plan is to expand the number of festivals,” Kramer told Deadline when asked about the list of festivals that can serve as feeders for the International Oscar category. Currently, under the rules introduced in May, films that win the top award at Berlin, Busan, Cannes, Sundance, Toronto, and Venice can be automatically submitted for the international category alongside films chosen by a country’s official submission committee. Watch on Deadline Kramer continued: “We started with six festivals because we wanted to make sure there were juried awards, which not every festival has.” Kramer added that the new rule is part of the Academy’s plan to globalize its efforts and approach the international category in a “more holistic way.” “A few years ago, the first thing we did was create a rule allowing refugee filmmakers who are no longer in their home country to have their films submitted by a host-country committee,” Kramer said. “That was the first step in creating a broader aperture for who can participate in the category. The next step was to consider how we could select films beyond committee-selected submissions and ensure greater global representation.” Kramer said AMPAS remains in constant conversation with film festivals across the globe. “We want to make sure there is proper global representation in the number of festivals we’re working with for this category,” he said. “It’s all about inviting more films into the conversation.” On the topic of international, Kramer said 25% of the Academy’s membership now resides outside the United States—a natural reflection, he believes, of global shifts in film production and consumption. “I think the lines between U.S. and non-U.S. cinema, first-run and classic films, animation, and documentaries have become much less distinct,” he said. “A lot of this has to do with the pandemic, when people at home watched films they normally wouldn’t have watched—young people especially. It changed the nature of our industry.” Kramer said the Academy’s increasing global makeup is one of the main factors that makes YouTube the most appropriate broadcast home for the Oscars moving forward. It was announced in December 2025 that YouTube won the rights to host the Academy Awards starting in 2029. The Google-owned service outbid other offers, including one from the Oscars’ longtime home ABC, which has been hosting the event since 1976. Disney’s deal runs through 2028. YouTube’s first show will be the 101st Oscars ceremony, and its deal will run through 2033. “The beauty of the YouTube deal is that everyone will see the same show,” he said. “We’ll have control over fan engagement and reach 2.5 billion people around the world at the same time, on the same night, in more than 30 languages. It also gives us more quality control over what our fans see and experience. That’s really important.” YouTube’s deal for the Oscars has been one of the biggest shifts as streaming platforms take on more live events. Netflix has the SAG Awards, now renamed The Actor Awards, and Prime Video will broadcast the Emmys from 2027. But the alliance between big tech and the film world hasn’t been without substantial friction; take Amazon’s mishandling of Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial . When asked whether the Academy has planned for similar scenarios, Kramer concluded: “There’s no censorship allowed at the Academy, at the Oscars, or on our broadcast. We’ve been very clear about that, and Google and YouTube completely understand.” The Tokyo Film Festival runs until November 4. articles.title: Riley Voelkel & Shiva Negar To Voice Adult Animated Comedy Project ‘Above Average’
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Riley Voelkel & Shiva Negar To Voice Adult Animated Comedy Project ‘Above Average’ Hiding In Plain Sight: Top Execs On Unlocking The Value In Legacy IP Disney+ Among Buyers For RTÉ & BBC Drama ‘The Walsh Sisters’ View All October 27, 2026 3:16am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Riley Voelkel & Shiva Negar Tyny, Red Pants Productions, JVH Media EXCLUSIVE: Riley Voelkel and Shiva Negar will lend their voices to adult animated comedy series Above Average . The show, which is in late-stage development, comes from creators Andrew Deutsch and Cailin Walker-Bent at Canadian animation collective Red Pants Productions and Josh Harris at JVH Media in the UK. Above Average is billed as an irreverent look at celebrity culture, corporate power and society’s obsession with being exceptional. It is set in Metrocropolis, the superhero capital of the world, where crime-fighting is big business, saving lives requires a license and public image often matters more than public service. Determined to make a difference, he turns to SALT, three washed-up, middle-aged superheroes operating out of a dilapidated laundromat, and their accountant. articles.title: Brett Morgen’s David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience Set For Berlinale World Premiere
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Vantage Media Takes North American Rights To Pole-Dancing Drama ‘Exotic’ As Trailer Unveiled Brett Morgen’s David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience Set For Berlinale World Premiere Horror ‘The Block’ With Jack Falahee, Saphira Moran & Jackie Earle Haley Wraps; Unveils First Look View All October 27, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source David Bowie “Stage” Blackout The spirit of late pop and rock icon David Bowie is set to return to Berlin , the city he called home in the mid-1970s. The Berlin Film Festival has announced it will world premiere U.S. documentarian Brett Morgen ’s immersive concert experience David Bowie “Stage ” during its 77th edition in the city’s 17,000-capacity Uber Arena venue. Combining previously unseen Bowie concert footage and an immersive sound and light experience, the production is billed as “a new way of experiencing one of the most influential artists of the 20th century”. Related Stories News Berlinale 2027 Retrospective To Explore Visions Of The Future In Nod To Centenary Of Fritz Lang's 'Metropolis' News Quiver Distribution Takes U.S. For Jérémy Comte's Ghana & Canada-Set Drama 'Paradise' The work is designed around recently discovered and restored footage from the 1978 Isolar II World Tour, during which Bowie performed material from his landmark album ‘Heroes.’ Watch on Deadline Morgen first discovered the original camera negatives while working on his Grammy Award-winning, Oscar-nominated bio-doc Moonage Daydream, charting Bowie’s life and career. World premiering in Cannes in 2022, it was the first film to be officially authorized by Bowie’s estate. The new three-screen immersive experience combines large-scale projections and transparent LED screens with an elaborate lighting design by lighting designer Patrick Woodroffe, whose credits include collaborations with The Rolling Stones and Elton John. The production is further enhanced by a specially created sound mix from Academy Award winner Paul Massey ( Bohemian Rhapsody , Michael, Moonage Daydream ), and places audiences at the centre of a live concert experience using state-of-the-art 7.1 surround technology and spatial audio design. The production is a collaboration between Rob Hallett’s Wonderworld, the David Bowie Estate and Morgen. “David Bowie has bestowed upon us an extraordinary treasure, an unprecedented concert experience that has yet to be witnessed,” said live entertainment veteran and former AEG International President Hallet. “Working hand-in-hand with David Bowie’s Estate and Brett Morgen, we are ensuring this experience is 100% faithful to his legacy while making his genius accessible to global fans and a new generation.” Berlinale Director Tricia Tuttle added: “To have this world premiere in Berlin, a city so closely connected to David Bowie, makes the experience especially meaningful,” added Tricia Tuttle, Director of the Berlinale. “The Berlinale is a place where cinema, art, and new forms of storytelling intersect. It’s like a dream come true: Bowie, Brett Morgen, a world-class sound and light team all coming together in the city’s premiere music arena.” Morgen, whose credits also include Kurt Cobain bio-doc Cobain: Montage of Heck and Jane about Jane Goodall, will also be a headline speaker in the talks program of the Berlinale’s European Film Market (EFM). The 77th Berlinale will run from February 10 to 21, 2027, with the David Bowie “Stage ” world premiering on February 14. Yet behind Hogwarts’ enchanted walls lie dark secrets. Harry must find the courage to prove himself against the darkest wizard of all. articles.title: Vantage Media Takes North American Rights To Pole-Dancing Drama ‘Exotic’ As Trailer Unveiled
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Vantage Media Takes North American Rights To Pole-Dancing Drama ‘Exotic’ As Trailer Unveiled Brett Morgen’s David Bowie Immersive Concert Experience Set For Berlinale World Premiere Horror ‘The Block’ With Jack Falahee, Saphira Moran & Jackie Earle Haley Wraps; Unveils First Look View All October 27, 2026 5:40am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: Vantage Media has acquired North American rights to Polish feature Exotic , about a woman’s journey toward self-discovery through pole dancing, ahead of its premiere at the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival . The picture follows a writer whose quest to master pole dancing evolves into something far more profound when the process and community of dancers she encounters help her figure out her true self. It is the first feature of Sonja Orlewicz-Zakrzewska and grew out of her personal fascination with pole dancing. The deal was negotiated by Jessica Russo, COO of Productions and Acquisitions at VMI Worldwide and Vantage Media, and Daniel Vadocky, Head of Sales at Berlin-based Pluto Film, which has also unveiled a first international trailer to coincide with the announcement. Gutek is handling the Polish release. Related Stories News Raven Banner Boards Polish Folklore Horror 'Òpi' Ahead Of U.S. Festival Debut News Poland Selects Paweł Pawlikowski's 'Fatherland' To Compete In International Film Oscar Race “At a time when women’s rights and freedoms are increasingly being challenged in America, Exotic delivers a timely and empowering message about the importance of embracing who we truly are,” said Russo at Vantage/VMI. Watch on Deadline “Through the art of dance, the film celebrates female strength, confidence and self-expression, reminding us that empowerment often begins with the courage to step outside our comfort zones. Exotic is more than a story about pole dancing; it’s a celebration of sisterhood, self-discovery, and the freedom to unapologetically be yourself.” “We are very pleased to have secured a North American distribution deal ahead of the film’s world premiere,” added Vadocky at Pluto Film. “It is a strong sign to its international appeal and audience potential. We have full confidence that Vantage/VMI will successfully distribute the film across all platforms.” Exotic was shot during a recent real-life edition of a pole-dancing Exo Stars Camp featuring real participants and instructors, maintaining the authenticity of this vivid bubble. “As soon as I discovered exotic pole dance, I got so invested that I went straight to Exo Stars Camp,” explains the writer-director. “I was fascinated by the clash of the fragile, intimate universes we carried within us around the camp. It soon became clear that the camp itself was a perfect place to confront fears, leave one’s comfort zone and express oneself more than daily life ever allows. “ The film stars Jaśmina Polak, Magdalena Koleśnik and Monika Frajczyk. Director of Photography is Adam Suzin, with Tomasz Kajetan Naruszewicz as Editor and Tymek Papior as Composer.to here. It received support from the Polish Film Institute’s microbudget scheme aimed at first-time directors. Director, scriptwriter, visual artist and photographer Orlewicz-Zakrzewska holds a master’s degree in photography from the Cinematography Department of the Łódź Film School. Her first short, Cross’n’Carry (2019), screened at festivals including New Horizons, HollyShorts and BEAST Portugal. She also took part in the script training lab Atelier Scenariuszowe and the EAVE Producers Workshop (2021). As a cinematographer, she worked on Enthusiasts , a documentary series for Canal+. Her video art and photography have been shown in numerous exhibitions including the Leica Gallery Warsaw. Exotic will debut in the First Feature Competition of Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival running from November 6 to 22. articles.title: ‘Derek Vs Derek’: British Rewilding Doc About Warring Neighbors Tests Its “Unexpected” Protagonists In All The Right Ways
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max BAFTA Names New Chair Stephen & Simon Cornwell Take On Chairmen Roles At ‘Night Manager’ Producer The Ink Factory As Michele Wolkoff Upped To President Disney+ & Channel 4 Strike Landmark Deal In UK View All October 27, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Derek vs Derek' Joss Barratt Welcome to Global Breakouts , Deadline’s strand in which, each fortnight, we shine a spotlight on the TV shows and films killing it in their local territories. The industry is as globalized as it’s ever been, but breakout hits are appearing in pockets of the world all the time and it can be hard to keep track… So, we’re going to do the hard work for you. We’re in the UK this week spotlighting an environmental documentary about warring neighbors that is gaining big traction. With a U.S. premiere coming shortly, Derek vs Derek has taken years to get to the big screen. Its exec producer Adam Wishart sets out its journey below. Related Stories News The "Algorithm Breaking" 'Hunkkaar' Has Challenged Indian Audiences On The Limits Of Procedural TV - And Their Own Beliefs News International Insider: The Final Edinburgh... Or Is It?; Int'l Oscar Race Begins Name: Derek vs Derek Country: UK Producer: The Slate Works & Damer Films Distributor: CAT&Docs For fans of: Wilding Watch on Deadline Many years in the making, Derek vs Derek started life as a story of rewilding and arrived in cinemas as something quite different, a “universal” tale of warring neighbors who nevertheless never stop learning from each other, says the film’s exec producer, Adam Wishart. The low-budget British documentary is riding on a high and is about to screen in the U.S. for the first time, but its journey to the big screen has been long and winding. The movie follows two neighboring farmers in Devon, enjoyably both called Derek, one of whom, Derek Gow, is a rewilding conservationist, and the other, Derek Banbury, an intensive dairy farmer. Both have a natural distrust of their namesake, but are just about willing to hear them out. Wishart, a BAFTA nominee for the BBC and Apple TV’s fantastic 9/11: Inside the President’s War Room, lives in Devon, a short journey from Gow’s farm. He became aware of Gow and his work some time ago when he was advising on community regeneration. Derek Gow Joss Barratt Wishart was told a director, James Dawson, had been following Gow for some years in order to make a rewilding documentary similar to 2023 hit Wilding . He “tried to get the film commissioned and even used every piece of TV industry capital I had,” but Wishart kept running into brick walls. He felt something was missing. “I was supportive [of Dawson’s vision], but a little sceptical,” says Wishart. “Then he told me that, whenever he stayed with Derek Gow, Derek would point him towards the Banburys and tell him to go and have breakfast with them. Suddenly, it became apparent that there was a lovely film about their relationship and their two different visions.” Wishart knew this was more than a kernel of an idea and Dawson already had plenty footage, but funding was tricky to come by. In the end, money flowed in via a grant from the Redford Center foundation plus crowdfunding. “We’ve made it with a tiny budget, drawing favors from across the industry, with the whole endeavour held together by sticky back plastic and paperclips,” says Wishart, whose production house The Slate Works produced Derek vs Derek alongside Damer Films, with CAT&Docs handling international sales. While “getting documentaries off the ground has always been difficult,” Wishart notes that “it’s harder than ever to do something that doesn’t have an obvious hook – an anniversary, a major event or a famous celebrity.” Testing the protagonist Derek Banbury Joss Barratt The doc sees the Dereks execute their opposing visions while going about their day-to-day lives. Gow is a rewilder who is taking drastic measures like introducing wild boars to his farmland, and he wants to go even further by convincing locals to allow wolves to return to the UK. Banbury is a traditional farmer who is really about making ends meet. Slowly, and at times with great drama, their outlooks move closer towards each other, and Derek vs Derek by no means takes sides. Wishart feels the key to the doc’s success is really in the protagonists’ relationship and their individual characters, which he describes as “brilliant and rather archetypal, but also unexpected.” “There aren’t many documentaries about people like them,” he adds. “We live in such a polarized world that we assume two people with opposing views are going to fall out over every aspect of their lives and never speak again. But it’s perfectly possible to disagree about one aspect of your life and still call your neighbor if your tractor gets stuck.” Speaking a few weeks after the launch of Tom Cruise-starring satirical polemic Digger, Wishart feels docs and features about this subject matter have become overly preachy. “They make one group of people feel that their life choices are wonderful, while alienating another group,” he adds. “I thought [ Derek vs Derek ] was interesting because making a film that sits with only one protagonist can be problematic. It can feel like an ‘NGO film’ or piece of advocacy without much edge. The protagonist isn’t really being tested.” Gow and Banbury are now pals, and Wishart speaks to them frequently, with the pair appearing on Q&A panels around the country to support the movie. Wishart says the movie has made around £120,000 ($160,000) so far. According to the BFI, ticket sales for Derek vs Derek rose 114% week-on-week after launch. The movie has aired at festivals including in Thessaloniki and Zurich and will soon be given its U.S. premiere at New York’s Doc NY. While Wishart is “not betting my mortgage on it,” he says “if the film can find a wider audience” by perhaps picking up U.S. distribution, thereby “beginning conversations about how we relate to the natural world and the food system, then more power to it.” That, he thinks, is the beauty of Derek vs Derek, a “universal” story of grumpy neighbors that could maybe, whisper it, teach audiences a thing or two without them even realizing it. articles.title: Matthew Perry Netflix Docuseries: Five Takeaways From Flimsy Look At ‘Friends’ Star’s Life & Death
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Jay Z & Apple Make It Official! Hova’s Headlining The Super Bowl Halftime Show Neil Young Rocks Trump With $10M Suit Over Using That ‘Free World’ Tune Again ‘Smear’ Campaign: George Clooney, Betty Gilpin, Adam Scott & Laverne Cox Team To Read Clark Gregg-Penned Political Play As Midterms Fundraiser View All October 27, 2026 6:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Roger Castillo, Matthew Perry, & David Pressman in The One About Matthew Perry Netflix SPOILER ALERT: The following article contains details about Netflix ‘s The One About Matthew Perry docuseries. Let’s be honest, Netflix’s just debuted The One About Matthew Perry is mainly for the hardcore Friends fans. Having said that even the devotees of Rachel, Ross, Monica, Joey, Phoebe and Chandler might be disappointed as there’s not much in this Mary Robertson directed three-part docuseries you haven’t heard before. Related Stories News Remembering Matthew Perry: A TV & Film Career In Photos Legal Matthew Perry Death: “Ketamine Queen” Sentenced For ‘Friends’ Star’s 2023 Overdose Over the approximately three-hour running time, The One About draws on tales of drunken nights, funny faces, and the rise, demands, and bends of fame. There’s interviews with old friends, family members (especially Perry’s younger half-sister and licensed therapist Mia Perry Bowick), NBC Entertainment boss Warren Littlefield, The Whole Nine Yards director and one now ex-U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California. Still, in a rush to get not really anywhere at all, the result is pretty much the officially authorized surface level stuff we all used to get in the 1990s from Behind the Music . Unlike VH1’s sometimes under appreciated Behind the Music, The One About Matthew Perry ‘s three-act play of the rise, the fall, and the resurrection never really gains much momentum. The comeback of sorts the third act should promise leaves you feeling at best deceived. The primary fuel here is the people who love the long time addiction-addled Perry, who drowned at the age of 54 in his West L.A. hot tub on October 28, 2023 after taking a ton of ketamine, clearly loved him a lot, and miss him a lot. Yet, The One About ( Friends fans get the nod to the successful sitcom) mainly leans on Perry’s best-selling 2022 Friends, Lovers, and the Big Terrible Thing memoir and its subsequent press tour for its narrative. A decision that, as we know now in hindsight of the book itself, reveals little of the darkness-plagued man behind the Friend, if you know what I mean? Watch on Deadline Still, for better and worse, here are some of the highlights of The One About Matthew Perry : (L-R) Lisa Kudrow , Matt Leblanc , Courteney Cox , David Schwimmer , Jennifer Aniston , Matthew Perry, THERE ARE NO FRIENDS: if you are expecting to hear from Jennifer Aniston, Courteney Cox, Matt LeBlanc, Lisa Kudrow or David Schwimmer in The One About Matthew Perry, you are going to be very upset. While the Friends cast are seen thoughout The One About in behind the scenes footage, clips from the 10-season show, and on press junkets, none of them acquiesced to be interviewed by Robertson. In fact no one from Friends , not the cast, not guest stars, not co-creators Marta Kauffman and David Crane appear in the docuseries. The closest The One About ever gets to the mega-sitcom is one Jeff Strauss, who was a writer/producer on Season 1 of Friends. While Strauss appears to have been close to Perry initially as Friends came together, most of his subsequent observations and remarks about the actor becoming “challenging and problematic” are clearly second-hand at best. MATTHEW PERRY REALLY WANTED TO BE FAMOUS & THEN REALLY HATED BEING FAMOUS: The son of a journeyman actor and an ex-press secretary to a Canadian PM, Perry was also the stepson of a famous Canadian journalist and later Dateline NBC correspondent. From early days as the class clown to hanging around sets with his father figures and trying to catch a break in early 1990s L.A., Perry, as various pre-fame pals attest in docuseries, wanted to be famous. When he got there with Friends , on a level barely anyone achieves nowadays, it was overwhelming. To be precise as one can on such occasions, it seems to, from the docuseries and Perry’s own memoir, brought out crippling insecurities, as much as wealth and notoriety. Problem with The One About , unlike Robertson’s much better last Netflix docuseries Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV, is that it is mostly examined though the lens of the spiraling booze, drug and emotional problems with little sense of context — which feels as hollow as canned studio audience laughter. Also, with that Little Richard attributed quote of “if you don’t want your picture taken, don’t become famous” in mind, the openly ambitious Perry himself is rarely held responsible for his own behavior, actions and addiction. It seems from The One About Matthew Perry that Matthew Perry was a ultimately a perpetual victim who, to quote one of his buddies from the series, “didn’t stand much of a chance” — and that’s just hard to buy. THERE WAS MORE THAN JUST FRIENDS : The stardom and sprawling legacy of Friends, even though it ended nearly 20 years before Perry’s death, seems to have haunted him in both a Hollywood cliche way and a very real disorienting way until the day he died. Spending decades outrunning Chandler Bing, Perry may have never given himself the ability to let go and find success elsewhere, The One About suggests While praised for short and Emmy-nominated stints on The West Wing, Ally McBeal, and The Good Wife , Perry may have floundered on the big screen but his TV leading roles from 2006 – 2013 displayed untapped talents that never got the time or space to thrive. Looking back from the streaming and revival standpoint of 2026, Perry’s leading roles on Aaron Sorkin’s flawed but prophetic Studio 60 on the Sunset Strip , Mr. Sunshine (which Perry co-created) and Go On all deserve much more attention, Robertson postulates in the second episode of The One About . There’s not a lot to argue with the Emmy winner’s POV on that — if only Robertson had done those later shows and roles justice. Getty THE ONE ABOUT DOESN’T HAVE A LOT ABOUT PERRY’S DEATH: I was at court hearings and sentencing hearing on Perry’s death right up until this year. Before that, I was on the story of Perry’s death within an hour or so of his body being discovered in late October 2023 by authorities in his Pacific Palisades home. As more details came out, the sad truth of Perry’s relapses and drug hustle emerged. What also emerged was the fast one the actor played on those around him — pronouncing himself clean and sober when he kept going back to using made his death look inevitable. Like the cast of Friends, you won’t find a lot of that in The One About Mathew Perry – it doesn’t fit the narrative they’ve constructed, true or not. One can debate the truth and consequence of Perry’s life and death for ages, I grant you as someone who saw a lot of it unfold close up. Yet, playing primarily on the slop side of the Netflix street, the docuseries doesn’t give you much more time than to take a breath before the epilogue begins. The One About gives Perry’s death, the investigation and convictions of the scummy doctors, personal assistant and the infamous “Ketamine Queen ” just around 15 minutes at the end of the third and final episode. In a summary, bad people did some bad things. While that is partially true, you never learn anything more nuanced about it than that — which makes the almost three hours up to that point feel like a psych-out of the viewer and the subjects in the docuseries. THIS IS WHY PEOPLE SPEND LESS TIME ON NETFLIX: Love it, hate or just eat it, few nowadays are going to tell you fast food is nutritious. Besides a few funny clips from old Friends episodes and some of Perry’s later work, there is nothing good for you or really even memorable about The One About Matthew Perry once you’ve watched all the episodes. In many ways, the whole series is a juiced up version of Netflix’s recently introduced InstaDocs series and their insta-take on a large event like the OpenAI Hugging Face cyberattack. In another sense, The One About Matthew Perry seems to exist in no small measure to get the streamer’s algorithm to pump you over to more easily digestible programming that you’ll lose interest in fairly quickly. As a passionate fan of Is It Cake? , don’t expect me to regal you with highbrow or die recommendations. Good escapism is a treat to me, and a tasty one at that the better it is cooked. However, at the same time, if you want to know, Ted and Greg, why Netflix subscribers are spending less time on the service, it is air-filled content like The One About Matthew Perry . Content that is truly much ado about nothing. As Perry himself is heard saying in The One About: “Reality is an acquired taste.” AMPAS To Expand Festival Qualifier List For International Oscar SAG-AFTRA Faces Reckoning As Few Members Qualify For Streaming Bonus Clooney & Others Set For Read Of Political Play ‘Smear’ As Midterms Fundraiser Keanu Reeves Takes Over From Alan Ritchson As Lead In Netflix Actioner ‘Maelstrom’ Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Susan Saint James Dies: ‘McMillan & Wife’, ‘Kate & Allie’ Actor Was 80
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Billy Crystal’s ‘860’ Extends Broadway Run To February Sylvester Stallone On Casting Daughter In ‘Tulsa King’: “Of Course It’s Nepotism, You Idiot” Ric Flair Latest Health Update: Ex-Wrestler Wears Eye Patch In Message Reassuring Fans “I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery” View All October 27, 2026 6:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Susan Saint James in 1974 Albert Watson / TV Guide / Everett Collection Susan Saint James , the husky-voiced actress who starred in such popular TV series as McMillan & Wife and Kate & Allie, died Monday, October 26, of pancreatic cancer. She was 80. A rep for Saint James confirmed her death to People. Among her survivors are husband Dick Ebersol, the former President of NBC Sports and executive producer of NBC’s Saturday Night Live. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries Obituaries Walter Koenig Dies: ‘Star Trek’s Original Ensign Chekov Was 90 In a statement, Saint James’ family described her as “generous with her time and energy, which she valued more than money, and instinctively drawn to whoever needed lifting up. She taught her children to pause, be kind and look out for other people.” “She never met a stranger,” the family statement continues. “Every person she met became the most important person in the room at that moment, from a fellow board member to the clerk at the shoe store, who usually walked away knowing her entire life story. Her defining act: weeks after losing her youngest son, Teddy, in the November 28, 2004 plane crash, she delivered his eulogy as a note to each of her other children and her husband, giving them words to heal. Even in the deepest grief of her life, she put everyone else first. Days after the crash she sat with Tim Russert to thank the people who had reached out and to tell them the family was okay.” The statement concluded, “She brought that same fire and positivity to everything that followed, and never lost it. She is survived by her husband, Dick Ebersol, her four children–Sunshine Lucas, Harmony Lucas, Charlie Ebersol and Willie Ebersol–her seven grandchildren; her sister, Mary Mercedes Dewey, as well as her beloved service dog, Lola.” Born Susan Jane Miller on August 14, 1946, in Los Angeles, Saint James was raised in Rockford, Illinois, where she began modeling as a teen. She launched her acting career in a 1966 TV movie called Fame Is the Name of the Game, then booked guest roles in the series Ironside and, when the TV movie became a series titled The Name of the Game , Saint James landed a series regular role. In 1968, she had a co-starring role in Where Angels Go, Trouble Follows , the sequel to the popular comedy The Trouble with Angels. Susan Saint James, Rock Hudson, ‘McMillan & Wife’ (1973) Albert Mackenzie Watson/ TV Guide /ABC/Everett Collection Other TV episodic work from the era included roles in It Takes a Thief and Alias Smith and Jones, but her early signature role arrived in 1971 when she was cast opposite Rock Hudson in the light crime drama series McMillan & Wife , a highly popular program that had Saint James portraying the younger wife and partner in crime-solving. The show lasted for six seasons, with its finale on April 24, 1977, but Saint James had departed early over a contract dispute. Her character was killed off in a plane crash and the “& Wife” part of the title was erased. The show didn’t survive another season; by the end of her run, Saint James had received four Emmy nominations for her performance. Saint James remained a prolific actor following her departure from the successful series, co-starring with Peter Fonda in the film Outlaw Blues (1977), George Hamilton in Love At First Bite (1979), and Jessica Lange and Jane Curtin in How To Beat The High Cost of Living (1980). Jane Curtin, Susan Saint James, ‘Kate & Allie’ (1984) Mario Casilli/TV Guide/CBS/Everett Collection Saint James and Curtin would reunite four years later in what would become high career points for both stars: The CBS sitcom Kate & Allie premiered on March 19, 1984, with the two stars portraying divorced mothers (and childhood friends) with children who decide to share a home in New York’s Greenwich Village. Saint James portrayed Kate, the more free-spirited of the two, with Curtin as the higher-strung conservative Allie. The combination proved a winner (and would be echoed decades later in the Jane Fonda-Lily Tomlin comedy Grace and Frankie ), and the series, created by Sherry Coben, was a hit with critics and audiences, appreciated for its intelligent humor and warm, groundbreaking, chosen-family approach. Saint James was nominated for two Emmys for her performance as Kate, with Curtin nominated for three and winning two. Following Kate & Allie, Saint James largely retired from show business – she’d appear in guest roles periodically – devoting her time to raising a family that included two children from her second marriage, to make-up artist Thomas Lucas, and the three sons she had with third husband, the Saturday Night Live executive producer Dick Ebersol. (She and Ebersol met when she guest-hosted the NBC comedy in 1981). Tragedy struck on November 28, 2004, when a private plane carrying Ebersol and sons Charles and Teddy crashed at the Montrose Regional Airport in Colorado. Dick and Charles Ebersol survived, but 14-year-old Teddy was killed (along with a pilot and flight attendant). After her son’s death, Saint James often devoted her time working with parents who had lost children. Saint James is survived by Ebersol, four children, seven grandchildren, and sister Mary Mercedes Dewey. articles.title: Jack Cressall Writing ‘Camp Justice’ Pilot Based On John Ryan Book ‘America’s Trial: Torture And The 9/11 Case’
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Ted Sarandos Shrugs Off U.S. Troubles To Mark Netflix’s 10 Years In Korea ‘Wentworth: Halfway Home’: Grace Chow & Nadine Garner Among 9 Joining Cast; Watch Trailer International Insider: Turmoil At Netflix; MIA Market Report; Patrick Brammall Interview View All October 27, 2026 8:07am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Naomi Harvey, Jack Cressall and John Ryan; 'America's Trial' (inset) Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: The TV adaptation of John Ryan ‘s non-fiction book America’s Trial: Torture and the 9/11 Case now has a writer. British screenwriter Jack Cressall is writing a pilot for Camp Justice , which will be based on Ryan’s non-fiction book from last year. Naomi Harvey from Golden Possum Productions has developed the book for TV and is attached to produce, with a U.S. co-producer being sought. It was previously with Clockwork Films, as we reported last year when Ryan’s book published. The series will explore the ongoing legal proceedings against the alleged architects of the 9/11 attacks at Guantánamo Bay, and per the synopsis will delve into “the complex legal and political landscape surrounding one of the most consequential cases in modern American history.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Daveigh Chase's Former Manager Vehemently Disputes GoFundMe Claims: "There Are No Medical Bills To Be Paid Or Funeral Expenses" Casting Sosie Bacon Set As Co-Lead Alongside Nikolaj Coster-Waldau In MGM+ Series 'The Black Tapes' Veteran legal affairs journalist Ryan wrote his book after spending a decade reporting from Guantánamo Bay in Cuba, exploring the post-9/11 interrogation program, the consequences of which are still playing out in court more than two decades after the events. The series will look into “justice and accountability and what happens when a nation’s pursuit of both becomes entangled with its own actions.” Ryan said: “Having Guantánamo Bay as my second home for a decade has been the reporting experience of a lifetime. The setting is surreal and the events are the literal definition of stranger than fiction. That’s why I got hooked, despite the costs to my personal life. I’m excited that more people will have a window into what goes on behind closed doors and can experience this bizarre place through Jack’s writing.” Scott Z. Burns’ film The Report , starring Adam Driver, covered similar ground, but was focused on the machinery of the interrogation program. Cressall’s debut short film, My Type , starred Sadie Stanley and Jacob Ward, with Daniel Ruah directing. It premiered at the Santa Barbara International Film Festival this year. He is developing a slate of feature films, including Destemido , a biographical drama about Brazilian big-wave surfer Marcelo Luna, and Dream Car Wash , a coming-of-age drama. For British producer Harvey and her Golden Possum operation, Camp Justice is the latest following an option for the life rights of Cuban baseball player Julio Estrada and development of a series based on John Romero, the godfather of first-person shooter whose titles including Doom , Wolfenstein 3D and Quake . “John’s book offers a rare window into life at Camp Justice,” said Harvey. “In a world where almost everything is captured on camera and shared instantly, one of the most consequential murder trials in modern history is unfolding largely out of public view. “John takes us inside a bizarre, almost surreal ecosystem where grieving families, defence lawyers, prosecutors and accused terrorists coexist on a tropical island where the makeshift court and camp x-ray co-exist with a crazy golf course, tiki bar and gitmo gift shop.” Cressall is managed by Eric Ziech at Untamed Artists LA. articles.title: Anthropic Warns in IPO Filing That Unfavorable Media Coverage of AI Could “Adversely Affect” Its Business
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 26, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dario Amodei Photo by Alex Wong/Getty Images Anthropic, one of the two biggest artificial intelligence labs (alongside OpenAI) filed to go public Monday morning, and alongside platitudes about the wondrous potential of the technology (curing disease that has vexed humanity for centuries!) and the terrifying downside possibilities (“catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”), it warned of the looming threat of the media to its ongoing business. The company, founded by Dario Amodei, is one of the leading frontier labs developing AI tech, but as the company noted in its S-1 filing with the SEC Monday, the public perception of it may pose a serious threat to its ability to continue operating. The filing also noted the risks posed by copyright law, as well as the company’s priorities, including a section that calls out a divergence from OpenAI that may be relevant to Hollywood. But it is the threats of negative media coverage that comes up again and again in the filing, with the risk factors section spelling it out most clearly: “As our business has grown and as interest in us and the AI industry overall has increased, we have attracted, and may continue to attract, significant media coverage, public commentary, and scrutiny from time to time. This coverage and commentary have included, and we expect will continue to include, recurring narratives concerning the potential adverse societal impacts of AI, including that AI may displace or eliminate jobs, may be misused or otherwise cause harm, and may pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity,” the filing states. “Negative media coverage, including public figures making negative or threatening statements about our company, whether accurate or not, could also adversely affect our brand and reputation and may reduce market acceptance of our models, platform, and applications or impair our ability to attract and retain customers,” it adds. “As public awareness of our brand increases, any issues that draw media attention may have an amplified adverse effect on our reputation. If unfavorable media coverage or adverse public perceptions persist or intensify, the demand for our models, platform, and applications could decline and our brand, business, financial condition, and results of operations could be adversely affected.” As for Hollywood, the litigation threat around copyrighted works remains top of mind for the company, which listed all of the lawsuits and threat letters related to books, films, music and other copyright holders, with the company noting that it may require them to acquire a license to the material, which they may or may not be able to secure. The legal landscape around AI and IP remains deeply uncertain. “In each of the actions, we believe we have meritorious defenses and dispute any allegation of wrongdoing,” the company wrote. “Legal proceedings related to these matters can have an adverse effect on us because of defense and settlement costs individually and in the aggregate, diversion of management resources, and other factors.” And then there’s the video element. There are a swarm of startups looking to use the technology to transform entertainment, but Anthropic, unlike SpaceX and OpenAI, has never spent resources on video or image models. The company notes as much in its filing: “Every research project must ultimately advance our mission. This focus also guides what we choose not to pursue,” it says. “For example, we do not currently focus on developing video and image generation models, despite their commercial appeal. That compute instead goes to coding, agentic skills, and safety research—a research decision that has also aided the capital efficiency of our models.” Also unlike OpenAI or SpaceX, Anthropic does not have an advertising business, and while it does spend some on ads (like at the Super Bowl) it is hardly a major player. The company disclosed $147 million in advertising spend in 2025, with marketing and advertising expenses rising by $273 million in the first half of this year “reflecting higher media spend to support product launches.” THR

articles.title: Chris Brown Avoids Prison With Eight-Month Suspended Sentence for London Nightclub Attack
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 26, 2026 7:11am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chris Brown arrives at London court on July 24, 2026. Courtesy of Getty Grammy-winning musician Chris Brown has avoided prison and received an eight-month suspended sentence in a London court after pleading guilty to affray following a confrontation at a London nightclub in 2023, the BBC News website reported on Monday. The incident took place in a nightclub in Mayfair, an upscale area of the British capital. Brown faced sentencing in the Southwark Crown Court along with a co-defendant, his vocal coach Omololu Akinlolu, who also performs under the name of Hoody Baby. Judge Tony Baumgartner told Brown and Akinlolu that their prison sentence was suspended for 12 months, which means they will be imprisoned if they commit another crime in the next year but otherwise stay free in the community. Related Stories Movies 'Ali G: Who Iz I?' Review: Sacha Baron Cohen Reprises Iconic Role, Yielding Equal Parts Belly Laughs and Boredom Movies Sacha Baron Cohen and 300 Ali G Look-Alikes Descend on London Ahead of New Movie 'Who Iz I?' “These sentences are the shortest custodial sentences which in my judgment are commensurate with the seriousness of your respective offenses … Each sentence is one of 12 months or less — by law I am required to suspend each custodial sentence unless you are an excluded offender or I am satisfied that exceptional circumstances relating to the offense or the offender justify an immediate custodial sentence,” Judge Baumgartner said during his sentencing. Brown and Akinlolu initially were set to face a trial over assault and grievous bodily harm charges, but the charges were later dropped. Brown also faced a charge of having an offensive weapon — a tequila bottle, according to reports — though that was dropped, too. He was told by the court judge the famous musician was not entitled to any special treatment, but Brown’s charitable activities and being a father of four were taken into consideration. Judge Baumgartner added Brown’s earlier convictions involving violence were “relevant,” but were now historic. The Grammy-winning artist has spent time in prison before — in Los Angeles — for a probation violation. It came after he pleaded guilty to felony assault of his then-girlfriend, Rihanna . THR

articles.title: Tricia Helfer Stars in Erotic Body Horror ‘Devour’ (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 26, 2026 7:41am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tricia Helfer (Photo by Paul Archuleta/Getty Images) Logo text Former Battlestar Galactica star Tricia Helfer has nabbed the lead role in director Erica Orofino’s erotic body horror pic Devour. Helfer, also known as Charlotte Richards in Lucifer, plays Luisa, a former professional figure skater facing compulsions she cannot control as she becomes dangerously fixated on Karla, her daughter’s friend played by Georgia Bradner (Ghosts, Resident Alien). A forbidden attraction then becomes an obsession and a self-destructive unravelling of Luisa’s life in increasingly terrifying and transgressive ways, according to a synopsis from the producers, Wildling Pictures. Related Stories TV 'Anna Pigeon' Renewed for Second Season on USA Movies Byron Allen's Freestyle Releasing Acquires 'Hello Beautiful' For Theatrical Release (Exclusive) Elizabeth Adams plays Luisa’s daughter, Elia in the horror film also written by Orofino. “I loved how dark and psychological the story was. Erica wasn’t afraid to go there, and that’s what made me want to be part of it,” Helfer said of her role in a statement. Helfer also starred as supermodel living a perfect life with her family until a health scare in Ziad H. Hamzeh’s drama Hello Beautiful feature that adapts cancer survivor Christine Handy’s best-selling novel Walk Besides Me , and has a co-starring role in USA Network ‘s Anna Pigeon series. Erica Orofino added in her own statement: “I wanted to make a film about self-identity, female sexuality and desires that exist outside our dominant norms or moral codes. I curated this cast carefully and I’m grateful this team came together in the way that it did. Tricia was a dream to direct. She will grip your heartstrings and your guts and not let go. Elizabeth and Georgia are going to blow you away.” Matt Code, Alison Almeida and Lucy McNulty are producing Devour, while Todd Brown, Kiersten Hanly, Emily O’Quinn Code, Mike Chapman and Fatima Hayward share the executive producer credits. Blue Finch Films is handling worldwide sales, excluding Canada. Wildling Pictures’ recently brought the thriller Phreaker to Fantastic Fest and earlier releases include the romantic comedy Young Werther starring Alison Pill, Douglas Booth, Iris Apatow and Patrick J. Adams, and the thriller See For Me. THR

articles.title: ‘Bluey’ Soundtrack Gets the Box Set Treatment With New Collectible Vinyl Release
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tim Chan Plus Icon Tim Chan @mrtimchan Follow Sign Up View All October 26, 2026 7:51am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Amazon If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. Fans of the hit animated children’s series Bluey now have a whole new way to experience the show with The Bluey Album Box Set , which brings the music of the show to vinyl for the very first time. The Amazon-exclusive set includes all four of the Bluey soundtrack albums: The Album, Dance Mode!, Rug Island and Up Here . Written and arranged by lead composer Joff Bush, the songs include the Bluey theme song, along with memorable tunes like “Keepy Uppy,” “Sleepytime” and “Cat Squad.” Amazon AMAZON EXCLUSIVE Bluey Album Box Set $109.99 Buy Now On Amazon The box set includes four LPs pressed on colored vinyl, with accompanying full color album sleeves and a pull-out panoramic poster. Everything is stored inside a slipcover box. There are more than 60 songs in total collected in this set. The Album is pressed on a white and blue vinyl disc inspired by the show logo, while Dance Mode! is pressed on pink and orange vinyl, inspired by Bluey’s favorite toy, Chattermax. Rug Island — named after a season two episode where the characters use their imagination to create an island from a rug, throw cushions and colored pens — comes on a green and orange LP. Up Here is pressed on a “blue space”-inspired vinyl. Related Stories BOOK ADVENT CALENDAR Bluey Advent Calendars Are Here for the Holidays, Swapping Bonbons for Books TV 'Stranger Things' and 'The Pitt' Were the Most Streamed Original Series in the First Half of 2026 This is an Amazon-exclusive release, meaning the retailer is the only place to find this Bluey music set online. You can also shop official Bluey merch on Amazon here . All of Bluey’s soundtrack albums have hit the Billboard Kids Album Chart, along with the Billboard Soundtrack Chart. The first release, The Album , debuted at number one on the ARIA Albums Chart in Australia in February 2021, becoming the first children’s album to reach the top of the charts Down Under. The music box set is a great gift idea for Bluey fans and vinyl collectors alike, and comes on the heels of a host of Bluey holiday releases, including an official advent calendar .
