articles.title: Brazil: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Presidential Term Beating Far-Right Challenger Flávio Bolsonaro
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Brazil: Lula Wins Historic Fourth Presidential Term Beating Far-Right Challenger Flávio Bolsonaro RisingJoy Signs International Distribution Pact With NTT DOCOMO Horace Ové’s ‘Pressure’ & Menelik Shabazz’s ‘Burning An Illusion’ Among Titles Screening As Part Of TIFF Cinematheque’s Windrush Season View All October 26, 2026 6:06am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. Andressa Anholete/Getty Images. Brazilian president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva staged a dramatic election comeback Sunday night, beating far-right challenger Flávio Bolsonaro to clinch a historic fourth term in office. Lula took 51.79% of the vote. The win makes the 80-year-old veteran the first Brazilian president since 1988 to win an election after losing the first round of voting. Bolsonaro, who is the son of Brazil ’s convicted former president Jair Bolsonaro, has refused to concede defeat and asked for the results to be annulled. In a rare but not unprecedented turn of events, polls were extended for two hours on Sunday night after both candidates made requests. Lula’s campaign had argued that voters in Salvador, the capital of Bahia, and São Paulo were prevented from reaching polling stations after reports of reduced public transportation. Bolsonaro’s campaign argued that heavy rain in areas in the south of the country had hindered voters. Related Stories Acquisitions Netflix Strikes Deal With Globo For Brazilian Fare Including 'I'm Still Here' & 'India - A Love Story' Festivals BRAVO Film Festival To Pause For 2026 According to data reports in The New York Times, Lula reversed the conservative shift from the first round of voting by earning more than 10 million new votes. The paper reported that Lula gained ground in almost every region of the country, attracting vast new support in major cities like São Paulo. He made gains in working-class suburbs and added 1.3 million votes in the country’s south, which has been a traditional Bolsonaro stronghold. Watch on Deadline In his victory speech on Sunday, Lula noted that he was forced to “overcome interference from the outside” to win a fourth term. The Bolsonaro family are longtime Trump allies. Reuters reported this weekend that officials in Trump’s State Department had pushed for sanctions against Brazil to weaken Lula and return the Bolsonaro family to power. “The election was a defeat for denialism,” Lula said. “It was a defeat for lies.” Lula added: “I highly doubt that Russia, China, or the United States possess an army as victorious as the army of democracy in this country.” ‘Clayface’ Takes No. 1 With $24M, But ‘See Everything’ Draws Nearly $20M Donald Trump Posts 1,300-Word Diatribe Against Bill Maher After Their Dinner Russell Brand’s Former Assistant Alleges “Insane Sexual Appetite” Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Leads Podcast-Based Horror Series ‘Black Tapes’ At MGM+ Read More About: 5 Comments

articles.title: MGM+ Greenlights ‘The Black Tapes’ Horror Series Starring Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Based On Podcast
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie MGM+ Greenlights ‘The Black Tapes’ Horror Series Starring Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Based On Podcast ‘These Summer Storms’ Series Adaptation In Works At Hulu From Melanie Marnich, Erin & Sara Foster Weekly World News Comedy Series From ‘Reno 911!’ Co-Creator Robert Ben Garant Raises $2.5M To Film Full Season Independently In California View All October 26, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nikolaj Coster-Waldau Getty Images MGM+ is expanding its horror lineup with a series order to The Black Tapes , a supernatural investigation drama. Nikolaj Coster-Waldau stars in the eight-episode series based on the 2015 horror podcast of the same name created by Terry Miles and Paul Bae who are writers on the TV adaptation alongside John Rogers ( Leverage ). In The Black Tapes , Dr. Richard Strand (Coster-Waldau), a brilliant psychiatrist with a mysterious past, teams with the obsessed, relentless scientist Alex Regan to debunk paranormal cases of hauntings, possessions, disappearances, and sinister legends – the infamous black tapes. But as Strand and Regan unravel the secrets of these events, they uncover a hidden occult world behind our own and must unravel a centuries-old apocalyptic conspiracy. Related Stories Casting Lucy Fry & Amanda Brugel Join Jensen Ackles In MGM+ Crime Thriller 'Rules Of Prey' News Stephen King's 'The Institute' Unveils Season 2 Trailer: First Look At Alfie Allen As Nolan Reeves Produced by MGM+ Studios, The Black Tapes is executive produced by Miles and Bae as well as Kearie Peak of Peak Pictures and Rogers and Jennifer Court of Kung Fu Monkey Productions, with Rogers serving as showrunner. The series is scheduled to begin production in Vancouver in January 2027 for release on MGM+ in the U.S., UK, Ireland, Germany, Italy, Spain, Belgium, the Netherlands, and Latin America. Watch on Deadline The Black Tapes podcast has amassed over 60 million downloads since its launch 11 years ago. NBC developed a drama series adaptation during the 2018-19 cycle, which was written and executive produced by Bae, Miles and Mathew Arnold. It did not go to pilot. “ The Black Tapes crafts a compelling story around our cultural fascination with the unexplained, while delivering the cinematic, classic storytelling that MGM+ audiences expect,” said Michael Wright, global head of MGM+. “With Nikolaj’s compelling presence and the creative vision of John Rogers, Kearie Peak and our talented production team, we’re excited to make something that is both provocative and hugely entertaining.” The project brings back together Wright, Rogers and Paek. During his tenure as a top TNT programming executive, Wright oversaw several titles from Dean Devlin’s Electric Entertainment that Rogers and Paek were part of: Paek worked on The Librarian movie franchise and the series Leverage , while Rogers was across Leverage and The Librarians TV series offshoot, which he co-created and developed, respectively. “I was an early and passionate fan of The Black Tapes podcast,” says Rogers. “It’s a unique blend of truly unsettling horror and puzzle-box conspiracy mystery. With Paul and Terry not just executive producing, but also in the writer’s room, we have a chance to both bring The Black Tape s to a new generation of genre fans and deepen and expand the mythos in ways that will surprise long-time supernatural horror fans.” The Black Tapes joins MGM+’s current horror slate of From , which is headed to a fifth and final season, and The Institute, whose second season premieres Nov. 8. Best known for his Emmy-nominated role as Jaime Lannister on HBO’s Game of Thrones, Coster-Waldau recently starred in the BBC/Prime Video series King & Conquerer and Apple TV+’s, The Last Thing He Told Me . He next stars opposite Jennifer Lopez in the Netflix film The Last Mrs. Parrish. articles.title: Lowden, Turner or a Dark Horse: One James Bond Casting Test Has Nothing to Do With Acting
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All October 24, 2026 9:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Pierce Brosnan in 1995's 'Goldeneye.' United Artists/courtesy Everett Collection Logo text Final James Bond screen tests have begun, which means there’s a chance that while you’re reading this an actor is auditioning in London for the biggest role of their life, a casting that could make its mark on one of the world’s longest-running film franchises. The oddsmakers — taking a cue from The Hollywood Reporter and others’ reporting — suggest Jack Lowden and Callum Turner are the favorites . Both have their apparent pros and cons. Lowden has a very likable presence on Apple TV’s Slow Horses , where he plays MI5 agent River Cartwright. For years, the role has looked like an audition for Bond. All the things Bond does — drama, action, romance, stunts — are on display, even though Lowden’s character has a rather different low-key vibe than 007. He’s an everyman pick, and that’s a rather refreshing idea that would give Bond writers new notes to explore with the character. Related Stories General News Hannah Einbinder Says Speaking Out for Palestine Is "the Bare Minimum" Movies Jack Lowden, Margaret Qualley Top Bookie Odds for Next James Bond and Bond Girl Turner looks like he might have been grown in a lab to play Bond, which is the best thing about him as a choice, but also a potential detriment if producers want somebody who feels more original. He seems could be perfect for the part — handsome and suave and posh. Between him and Lowden, Turner would also likely win the sex appeal contest. Reportedly in the mix are Jack O’Connell and Josh O’Connor — two actors with such similar names one wonders if sources leaking to the press got the two mixed up and only one of them is actually auditioning. Regardless of who gets the part, there is a lot more to playing Bond than merely fighting and bantering and firing a Walther PPK. There are qualities that many pundits on the sidelines might overlook, but Bond’s producers most assuredly will not: Bond may be a rogue character who plays by his own rules, but the actor cast in the role has to be the ultimate team player. Bond is a massive commitment that requires an actor to adhere to the highest professional standards for more than a decade. The actor may not always be playing Bond, but will forever be a Bond, and therefore must be counted upon to not embarrass the franchise. This means the choice should be somebody who, for instance, isn’t going to sound off divisively about politics, get into messy domestic disputes or start going on public benders. More subtly, it means somebody who’s down to be an agreeable brand ambassador for the part, who will treat fans respectfully and gamely participate in the intense media circus which accompanies every Bond film. They also have to, preferably, not be a jerk behind the scenes — missing on that one could make the typical nine-month production process for a Bond film much more difficult for all involved. These things are true for any lead role in a movie, but they’re far more true for playing Bond due to the iconic importance of the character and expected four-or-five-film commitment. The last thing Team Bond wants is a scandal like the one that befell Marvel after casting Jonathan Majors in a multi-film villain role. That was a mess , and resulted in an announced movie being scrapped. Yet Majors’ part was merely a villain amid an ensemble cast, not a lead who’s on camera in just about every scene. Legendary Bond producer Cubby Broccoli once said casting George Lazenby for 1969’s On Her Majesty’s Secret Service was “biggest mistake in 16 years.” Broccoli said the actor “just couldn’t deal with success. He was so arrogant.” Lazenby made just one Bond film before Sean Connery returned to the role. While Broccoli’s daughter, Barbara, who led the producing team on Bond until just last year, noted to Variety in 2022, “When we cast Bond, it’s a 10-, 12-year commitment … Not everybody wants to do that … It’s not just showing up for a couple of months of filming.” THR

articles.title: Online Comedians Are Making a Mint Mocking Wall Street
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Andrew Zucker Plus Icon Andrew Zucker View All October 24, 2026 10:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Screenshot/YouTube Johnny Hilbrant Partridge never worked an hour on Wall Street, but you’d never guess that by looking at him. Nearly every day, Partridge takes to YouTube to channel his inner finance bro as P.E. Guy, a puffer-vested private equity putz who brags about his million-dollar deals, Aspen manse and private plane. Partridge, who once taught fitness classes in Boston, debuted the character on social media last year, which boosted his following beyond Barry’s and SoulCycle devotees. Today, he has 400,000-plus Instagram followers, up from 7,000 about 18 months ago. Related Stories Influence Peddlers Top Creators' Secret Weapon? Indian Video Editors Music Anthropic Sued for Using Elvis Presley Music to Train AI Models Although Partridge lampoons private equity, his skits resonate beyond buyout boys. “I think a lot of people have that experience of coming in contact with somebody who wants to one-up you and make you feel like they win the conversation because they have an impressive-sounding job,” he says. As certain business figures become as talked about as celebrities, Wall Street yuksters like Partridge are surging on social media. While memes still flood finance bro DMs, creator-helmed videos are gaining momentum on both Wall Street and Main Street. Some riff on Bloomberg headlines, while others simply play on C-suite stereotypes. Other creators skewering corporate life include The Swiss Chris (442,000 Instagram followers), who portrays a highfalutin European banker; Clemente Varas Collado (115,000 Instagram followers), who frequently roasts asset manager BlackRock, and engineer-turned-entertainer Varun Rana (90,000 Instagram followers). It’s not an entirely new trend — Wall Street meme pages have been around for over a decade — but social media algorithms are increasingly favoring shortform video, benefiting creator-actors over anonymous meme lords. It’s led to stalling growth for some picture-heavy accounts, including Trust Fund Terry, which launched about eight years ago on Instagram. Trust Fund Terry has never revealed his identity, though he admits on the phone that he has toiled in consulting and finance. Terry, a pseudonym, said audience building on Instagram has become more difficult thanks to Reels. “I think they’ve really been trying to push the more traditional creators, where they’re telling a story in either short or longform video,” he said. Varun Rana. Courtesy Of Subject The Swiss Chris, who shows his face but remains anonymous, says he first played a character named Goldman Stanley. Chris, who was a banker in Europe, says the industry is one “where the humor practically writes itself.” Josh Kaplan, who runs creator management company Smooth Media, says part of these creators’ success is making their followers feel like they’re alongside Blackstone associates at the watercooler. “I feel like people love being on like the inside of a joke,” says Kaplan, whose company manages Rana. Josh Brown, the CNBC fixture and CEO of Ritholtz Wealth Management, is in numerous texting chains with Wall Streeters who pass around Partridge’s latest videos. He says Partridge’s P.E. Guy character is identifiable to the finance crowd. “When I first started my career in the late ’90s, it was investment bankers who were doing all the IPOs,” he says. “Now in the 2020s, the personification of that level of douchiness is private equity.” These Wall Street jesters are ascending at a moment when there’s immense interest in the machinations of finance firms and rainmakers. Some of the biggest sports storylines now involve the corporate dealings of billionaire owners. Hollywood A-listers are romancing private equity guys. And many consumers are keenly aware of investors behind businesses. P.E. Guy, aka Johnny Hilbrant Partridge (who uses a filter to create his character’s grotesque face.) Pat Greenhouse/The Boston Globe via Getty Images Brown believes Partridge’s and other creators’ outrageous personas stem from the growing number of people with equally outrageous wealth. “It’s a level of satire that television really hasn’t caught up to,” he says. “I think these people are nailing it in a way that maybe 20 years ago The Simpsons would have.” P.E. Guy still attracts the real-life P.E. guys, especially on LinkedIn, where he has over 10 times more followers than on X. “I’ve been able to satirize stuff on LinkedIn in a really fun way, where people don’t always know that it’s a joke because of how absurd things already are on LinkedIn,” he says, “which really tickles me.” This story appeared in the Oct. 21 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

articles.title: Jay-Z’s Victory Lap Continues as He Brings Out Blue Ivy Carter, John Legend, DJ Khaled for SoFi Stadium Opening Night
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All October 24, 2026 10:03am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jay-Z performs at SoFi Stadium on Friday night. Roc Nation “I’ve been away too long,” Jay-Z told a hyped-up SoFi Stadium crowd soon after taking the stage on Friday night. The rap icon was met with cheers as he, at last, brought his yearlong victory tour to Los Angeles. Indeed, it’s been close to a decade since Jay last played a full-fledged solo concert in the city, with Shawn Carter closing out his 4:44 Tour across the street at the Forum in 2017 and playing the Rose Bowl for his joint On the Run Tour with Beyoncé a year later. After a historic three-night run in New York at Yankee Stadium and a few more shows in London and Paris, not to mention an eight-part HBO docuseries directed by Rick Rubin, it’s finally L.A.’s turn, as Jay kicked off the first of two much-anticipated concerts Friday night in celebration of the 30th anniversary of his debut album Reasonable Doubt and 25th anniversary of The Blueprint. Related Stories Music Young Miko Gets Flirty With L.A. During Her Late Checkout Tour Music Feds Sue Ticket Broker Firm Over Alleged $120M Scheme For Beyoncé, Pitbull Tickets The result was a career-spanning tour de force from one of hip-hop’s most seminal figures, and perhaps more Yankee hats and jerseys in the crowd than SoFi Stadium has ever seen. Kicking off just before 9:30 p.m. local time, the show opened with a video of Jay and Beyoncé alone in the seats at Yankee Stadium, with Bey behind him playing with her husband’s hair. Flanked by an impressive backing band and starting the night with “Hovi Baby,” Jay powered through a collection of hits and fan favorites for two hours, from “FuckWithMeYouKnowIGotIt” to “Run This Town,” “Hard Knock Life (Ghetto Anthem),” “Lucifer” and “99 Problems.” “Let me take you back to my home for a second,” Jay told the crowd before launching into “Empire State of Mind” toward the end of the evening. Whereas Jay brought an overwhelming set of surprise superstar guests to his shows in New York, including Eminem, Rihanna, Nas, Usher and wife Beyoncé, L.A.’s opening night was comparably subdued in that department as he performed much more by himself. Still, his daughter Blue Ivy did come out on the keys for “The Story of O.J.” and “Dead Presidents,” while Scarface joined for “This Can’t Be Life” and “Mind Playing Tricks on Me.” DJ Khaled and John Legend helped close it down for the last song for “God Did.” Much of the audience was of course waiting in anticipation Friday night wondering if Jay would address or confirm the reports that he’d chosen himself as headliner for the Super Bowl Halftime show in February. It’d have been a perfect time to make any news on the matter, performing in the very venue hosting the big game, though the world will have to wait, as Jay didn’t so much as reference the news on Friday, keeping it very much about the current show at hand. Perhaps he’s saving some more headline news as he finishes his L.A. stand — and his broader Jay-Z 30 shows — on Saturday night. Night One Setlist: Hovi Baby Izzo (H.O.V.A.) articles.title: Billy Corgan Defends Marilyn Manson Friendship Despite Sexual Assault Claims Against Manson: “I Didn’t Feel That He Was Guilty”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All October 24, 2026 11:44am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Marilyn Manson and Billy Corgan at a SiriusXM event in Chicago in 2015. Timothy Hiatt/Getty Images for SiriusXM Billy Corgan has defended his ongoing friendship with Marilyn Manson despite the latter being accused of sexual assault and abuse by multiple women. “As a Christian person, you have to stand by your friends, but that doesn’t mean you don’t have an opinion, and it doesn’t mean you’re not critical,” Corgan said on the New York Times ‘ Popcast earlier this week. “In his case — and I’m not here to adjudicate it — but the D.A. looked at the case for five years.” The Smashing Pumpkins frontman added: “In some cases, I knew personal things behind the scenes that are not in the public sphere. I personally didn’t feel that he was guilty of the things that he was being charged with, and ultimately the fact that the DA didn’t pursue … [it] was commensurate with the person I knew.” Related Stories Movies Joey King Reveals Conversation With Evan Rachel Wood After Replacing Her in 'Practical Magic 2' TV 'The Shards' Review: Ryan Murphy and Bret Easton Ellis Team Up for FX's Predictably Excess-Soaked Tale of Prep-School Sex, Drugs and Murder Los Angeles County District Attorney Nathan Hochman announced in January 2025 , after investigating for four years, that his office wouldn’t pursue criminal charges against Manson, whose real name is Brian Warner, saying the statute of limitations had run out on the domestic violence claims against him and that prosecutors couldn’t prove charges of sexual assault beyond a reasonable doubt. “We recognize and applaud the courage and resilience of the women who came forward to make reports and share their experiences, and we thank them for their cooperation and patience with the investigation,” Hochman’s office said in a statement at the time. “While we are unable to bring charges in this matter, we recognize that the strong advocacy of the women involved has helped bring greater awareness to the challenges faced by survivors of domestic abuse and sexual assault.” Manson has faced accusations of sexual misconduct from numerous women, including actresses Evan Rachel Wood and Esmé Bianco as well as model Ashley Morgan Smithline and former assistant Ashley Walters. Wood, who was in a relationship with Manson for a number of years, came forward with her claims in 2021. “The name of my abuser is Brian Warner, also known to the world as Marilyn Manson,” she alleged on Instagram at the time. “He started grooming me when I was a teenager and horrifically abused me for years. I was brainwashed and manipulated into submission. I am done living in fear of retaliation, slander or blackmail.” Manson sued Wood for defamation in 2022 but he dropped the lawsuit in 2024 , and the two reached a settlement in which he agreed to cover her legal fees. Manson, who has denied all of the allegations against him, has faced civil lawsuits from Bianco, settling her case in 2023 ; Smithline, whose case was dismissed that year, and she later recanted her claims ; and Walters, whose sexual abuse lawsuit was recently reopened for a second time . “I guess it’s one of those things where I don’t want the world to tell me who my friends are and who I should associate with,” Corgan told Popcast . “That’s politically, socially, and in Brian’s case, we have a relationship that goes back close to 30 years.” Corgan also noted that Manson’s wife Lindsay’s twin sister is married to the Pumpkins’ James Iha, leading him to consider Manson “basically a part of our family.” “There’s a deeper set of relationships there,” he added. Beyond that, Corgan hinted at some insider knowledge of the legal proceedings against Manson that allowed him to make the determinations he did. “Anyone in that situation struggles with the accusations, the seriousness of the accusations. But again, I also knew the inside baseball of the case. I knew certain people who were involved, and so you make those evaluations,” Corgan said. “At the end of the day, I feel I made the right determination, but if things had come out….” he said. “Like people would ask me privately, ‘Well what happens if da da da…’ And I’d say, ‘If he’s guilty or anybody in that situation is guilty, they should go to jail.’ I’m not saying I have any moral supremacy here. I’m saying it’s a case-by-case basis. But I don’t like the idea of… this kind of witch mob thing bothers me.” THR

articles.title: Jeff Garlin Considered Suicide After Tumultuous ‘Goldbergs’ Exit
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All October 24, 2026 2:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Jeff Garlin at the 17th annual Thirst Gala in L.A. this past May. Gonzalo Marroquin/Getty Images for Thirst Project After Jeff Garlin left the ABC comedy The Goldbergs following an HR investigation stemming from multiple complaints about his behavior, he struggled mentally to the point that he considered ending his life. “I had a nervous breakdown, and I was going to commit suicide,” the actor said this week on Ted Danson ‘s Where Everybody Knows Your Name podcast. Garlin contacted his and Danson’s fellow Curb Your Enthusiasm co-star Susie Essman , who got Garlin’s friends to help him get treatment. Related Stories TV Where to Watch 'Grey's Anatomy' Season 23 Online TV Val Chmerkovskiy Returns to 'Dancing With the Stars' After One-Episode Suspension “I reached out to Susie [Essman], and I said, ‘I hate when people don’t reach out, but at noon today I will be dead. I’m letting you know I will be dead.’,” the actor recalled. “And she called [ex-wife] Marla, and she called [girlfriend] Sari and my friend, Brad Morris,” he said. “My girlfriend and my ex-wife called him. He’s one of my best friends. He watched me while they were looking for a place for me to go.” Ultimately Garlin checked into rehab in Cincinnati, Ohio, and underwent dialectical behavior therapy (DBT), which helped him overcome his suicidal thoughts. “I was no longer suicidal,” he said. “They helped get me to a point where I could stand, and then I went out in the world and it took time between therapy and medication for bipolar all that stuff to where I felt kind of whole.” In 2022, Garlin revealed he was bipolar, recently claiming the undiagnosed mental health condition affected his behavior on The Goldbergs . Garlin said he’s “now feeling really good” and is “very content,” adding that he’s sharing his mental health struggles to raise awareness. “The point is … for people who do what we do, we get just as dark as you do,” he said. “We have bad days just like you do. And I, Jeff Garlin, comedian, joyful gentleman, was going to end his life. But I’m grateful that I had friends and family. And then people have been so supportive of me.” Garlin left The Goldbergs in December 2021 after more than eight seasons playing father Murray Goldberg. The mutual decision between Garlin and production company Sony Pictures Television came during production on the ABC series’ ninth season and followed investigations from HR and Vanity Fair , with the latter reporting on an alleged pattern of verbal and physical conduct that made staffers uncomfortable. “My opinion is, I have my process about how I’m funny, in terms of the scene and what I have to do. They feel that it makes for a quote ‘unsafe’ workspace. Now, mind you, my silliness making an unsafe workspace — I don’t understand how that is. And I’m on a comedy show. I am always a kind and thoughtful person,” Garlin told Vanity Fair in December 2021. THR

articles.title: Inde Navarrette Teases Her Rogue Southern Accent for New ‘X-Men’ Film: “Sugar!”

articles.title: Anthropic Sued for Using Elvis Presley Music to Train AI Models
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All October 24, 2026 7:22pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert' Courtesy of EPiC: Elvis Presley in Concert Anthropic has been sued by the owners of Elvis Presley ‘s music for allegedly utilizing his songs to train AI models without permission. As reported by Billboard , the suit was filed Friday and claims the company infringed 274 songs of Presley’s, including “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” “A Little Less Conversation” and “Don’t Be Cruel.” “The Elvis Plaintiffs bring this action to enforce these exclusive rights against the defendant that has built its entire business model based on copyright infringement at a scale never seen before,” wrote lead attorney Richard Busch. “The Elvis Plaintiffs are deeply protective of these iconic songs.” Related Stories Music Chappell Roan Enlists PinkPantheress to Close Out Super Graphic Spectacular Fundraising Shows General News Teen Study: YouTube Rules, AI Doom Increases With Age and Moviegoing Beats Sports on Weekends Authentic Brands Group, which owns the rights to Presley , filed the lawsuit alongside other entities that also own rights to the “Jailhouse Rock” singer, according to Billboard . “‘Claude’ has created infringing output of copyrighted material of virtually every song from every catalog available on the internet, including the Works,” the lawsuit states, per Rolling Stone . “Even after the Defendant supposedly put up ‘guardrails’ after being sued, in one of its latest iterations, Claude continues to infringe: when recently asked to recreate specific songs ‘for a modern audience,’ Claude did so and admitted: ‘These renders keep landing very close to the originals: same structure, same hooks reused with light rewording, and full sets of verses/choruses/bridges. That’s edging past ‘inspired by’ into reproducing the copyrighted song, even when the words are swapped out.’” In August, Round Hill sued Suno and Anthropic , claiming mass copyright infringement. They alleged the AI companies used hundreds of the publisher’s songs to train their AI models without permission. Anthropic was also previously sued by Universal Music Publishing, Abcko, Concord and BMG for similar claims of lyrics being utilized to train Claude, an AI agent. Rolling Stone reports that the suit is seeking $150,000 per infringed song. The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Anthropic for comment, but did not hear back. THR

articles.title: Nathan Fielder Negotiated a ‘Kill Switch’ on ‘You Can See Everything,’ Says Lance Oppenheim: ‘If We Didn’t Find Something, We Could Just Throw It All Away’
articles.full_text: Oct 24, 2026 5:01pm PT Nathan Fielder Negotiated a ‘Kill Switch’ on ‘You Can See Everything,’ Says Lance Oppenheim: ‘If We Didn’t Find Something, We Could Just Throw It All Away’ By Zack Sharf , Payton Turkeltaub Add us as a Google Preferred Source A24 “ You Can See Everything ” might be the buzziest film of the moment, but before the Elizabeth Holmes-focused documentary made it to theaters, co-director Lance Oppenheim has admitted that fellow director Nathan Fielder was so skeptical about being able to weave a unique enough narrative that he negotiated a “kill switch” with A24 before they began filming. In an interview with IndieWire , Oppenheim detailed Fielder’s kill-switch idea and how it helped the project. While Fielder wanted to pursue the documentary with Oppenheim, he worried that “the story had been told so many times already.” (Before the documentary even began production, Holmes’ scandal was already the subject of a popular podcast, best-selling book, an Alex Gibney doc and “The Dropout,” the Hulu scripted series.) Related Stories 'The Gilded Age' Team on Paramount Merger Parallels and Going From Budget Cuts to a Season 3 Breakout: 'You’re Part of a Very Fortunate Minority' MoreThan Films Picks Up ‘Salen las lobas' Ahead of Valladolid World Premiere “Nathan [said to A24], ‘Well, do you think if Lance and I were to go and see if there was something there, would you be comfortable with giving us money and essentially just leaving us alone, and giving us a provision in our deal, whatever the money was, that we could just kill it at any time? If we didn’t find something, we could just throw it all away, we could throw it in the garbage can,’” said Oppenheim. “And they thankfully agreed.” Popular on Variety Oppenheim continued, saying that the “kill switch” negotiation “changed everything,” especially as Fielder remained hesitant about how the doc would come to fruition with just 34 days left before Holmes was set to go to prison. The provision also gave them freedom with the project, he said. “This was the first time where I’ve ever been like, ‘Oh, we actually have room to explore something without any pressure of anyone looking [over us],” said Oppenheim. “ I wish I could have that for every project, because then it really feels like you’re just operating purely out of curiosity. You can essentially fish.” In another interview with Wired Magazine, Fielder also touched on why he wanted such a provision in the contract. “I told A24, ‘I don’t really know what the angle is, but there is something tickling in my brain,’” he said. “She was about to go to prison, so we didn’t know what was gonna happen. I was like, ‘If you guys want, I’m down to go down and start filming and see what emerges. But we need the ability to deliver nothing to you guys if it doesn’t work out.’ And they said ‘Sure.’” He continued: “It really meant I didn’t have to hold back with her or with them. Making a film, or any project, is very stressful. So if we had to pull the plug because it didn’t work out, it would sort of be a relief to me. It’s a very nice zone to operate in. articles.full_text: Oct 24, 2026 6:10pm PT ‘I Play Rocky’ Star Anthony Ippolito on Becoming Sylvester Stallone and Acting With a Dog: ‘He Wasn’t a Huge Fan of Me’ By Marc Malkin Plus Icon Marc Malkin Senior Editor, Culture and Events marcmalkin Latest ‘I Play Rocky’ Star Anthony Ippolito on Becoming Sylvester Stallone and Acting With a Dog: ‘He Wasn’t a Huge Fan of Me’ 12 hours ago Nicholas Galitzine Says Shooting ‘Red, White & Royal Wedding’ Was a ‘Nice Reset’ After World War II Movie ‘The Mosquito Bowl’ 2 days ago ‘Wildwood’ Director Travis Knight on AI: ‘An Amazing Piece of Technology’ but ‘I’m Not Embracing It at All’ 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone/Rocky in "I Play Rocky." Courtesy of Amazon/MGM Anthony Ippolito had to do more than nail Sylvester Stallone’s signature voice to play him in “ I Play Rocky .” He also had to transform his skinny physique to one with bulging muscles. “It had its moments for sure. I was being tested,” Ippolito told me Saturday at the AFI Fest “I Play Rocky” screening in Los Angeles. “It’s like a consistency thing, though. I had a great deal of time, so just an entire lifestyle shift and it was just one of the priorities of every day for a pretty long period.” Related Stories 'Mother Bhumi,' 'Rehana Maryam Noor' and 'The Tourist' Producers Head to Indonesia’s JAFF Market for New Exchange Program Tallinn Baltic Event: New Movie From Darko Lungulov and Ernestas Jankauskas, Plus Titles Directed by Rising Talents Josh Trigg, Marina Palacio and Many More Met and interviewed ‘I Play Rocky’ star Anthony Ippolito for the first time today. We talked about the muscles he put on to transform into Sylvester Stallone and acting opposite a dog playing Butkus. https://t.co/rd2mkN8lBD via @variety #justforvariety pic.twitter.com/yCnvV4IWM9 — Marc Malkin (@marcmalkin) October 25, 2026 As Ippolito previously told Variety ’s Clayton Davis, he spent nearly two years bulking up from about 150 pounds to roughly 180 while training at Gleason’s Gym in Brooklyn. Popular on Variety What did family and friends think? “It happened over time, but a couple of people were like, ‘What’s going on?’” Ippolito recalled. “They didn’t necessarily know I was doing the prep, and they were like, ‘What’s going on here?’ I was like, ‘I’ve been going to the gym, been eating.’” “I Play Rocky,” directed by Peter Farrelly, follows Stallone’s journey to get “Rocky” made in 1976. Now considered one of the greatest films ever made, the odds were way more against Stallone than with him when he first pitched the movie in Hollywood. AnnaSophia Robb plays Stallone’s first wife, Sasha, in “I Play Rocky.” Stephan James portrays Carl Weathers. Rounding out the cast are Kiki Seto, P.J. Byrne, Matt Dillon, Tracy Letts and Jay Duplass. If jitters on the first day of filming weren’t already enough to contend with, Ippolito’s first scenes were with a dog playing Stallone’s pooch Butkus. Stallone famously sold Butkus for $40 when before he found fame because he couldn’t afford to feed him. After selling the “Rocky” script, he bought him back for $15,000. Anthony Ippolito describes his first day filming "I Play Rocky": "Irwin Winkler was actually on set day one. We did a lot of stuff with Butkus that day, and I hadn't met that specific dog until the day prior to shooting, and he didn't happen to take a liking to me until a… pic.twitter.com/7tPKpNnp4M — Variety (@Variety) October 24, 2026 “I hadn’t met that specific dog until like the day prior to shooting,” Ippolito said. “He didn’t happen to take a liking to me until a couple of days in. When you give him enough treats, then he started to warm up. But at that point he was, you know, a 140-, 160-pound dog [and] wasn’t a huge fan of me, so it kind of just added to it. He just did whatever he wanted to do, and that was usually not what we were looking for him to do … In some ways they, they give you the most beautiful stuff. It’s just you gotta be patient.” “I Play Rocky” is in limited release on Nov. 6, followed by going wide on Nov. 20. See more photos from the “I Play Rocky” screening at AFI Fest below. articles.title: SAG-AFTRA Extends Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract and Adds CEO to Title
articles.full_text: Oct 24, 2026 6:20pm PT SAG-AFTRA Extends Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract and Adds CEO to Title By Gene Maddaus Plus Icon Gene Maddaus Senior Media Writer @GeneMaddaus Latest SAG-AFTRA Extends Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract and Adds CEO to Title 12 hours ago Did Karen Bass Expand Film Incentives? Nithya Raman Campaign Flags ‘Whopper’ Claim 2 days ago Agencies and Producers Back U.S. Tax Incentive as ‘First Step’ Toward Hollywood Recovery 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Photo by Rocco Ceselin/SAG-AFTRA The SAG-AFTRA board voted Saturday to extend the contract of Duncan Crabtree-Ireland , the union’s national executive director, for four years and to add CEO to his title. Crabtree-Ireland’s contract was set to expire in 2028, but will now run through June 20, 2032. The financial terms of the agreement were not disclosed. He was paid $1.1 million for the 2026 fiscal year. The extension will carry Crabtree-Ireland through the next round of negotiations with the major studios, with the current deal set to expire in June 2030. In a statement, the union said that the extension will offer “added stability and continuity for the union during a time of unprecedented industry disruption.” Related Stories Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s ‘Jengira’s Magnificent Dream,’ With Tilda Swinton, Boarded by ‘Triangle of Sadness’ Mexican Co-Producer Piano Horror Fans, Rejoice: FilmQuest Breakout 'The Crawling' Is the Gutsy Alien Freakout of Your Dreams Crabtree-Ireland has spent nearly his entire career at SAG-AFTRA, serving as general counsel and chief operating officer before being named national executive director in 2021. He has made artificial intelligence a key focus of the union’s negotiations, reaching a series of agreements that aim to allow performers to capture the upside of AI while protecting them from unauthorized uses of their likenesses. He was also a central figure in the 2023 actors’ strike. Popular on Variety Sean Astin, the president of SAG-AFTRA, praised Crabtree-Ireland in a statement after the vote. “To battle giant global transnational corporations, we need expert leadership with a track record of successful bargaining and significant operational management expertise,” Astin said. “That is Duncan. He is a powerful executive who has led our union at the bargaining table, in the halls of Congress and in boardrooms and conference rooms across the industry and the world. We are thrilled to have guaranteed Duncan’s continued service to the members of SAG-AFTRA.” The extension was approved with 98.34% of the board in favor in a weighted vote. “Leading SAG-AFTRA’s staff is the honor of my career, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to keep doing this work,” Crabtree-Ireland said. “As we continue fighting for human creativity, the coming years will be crucial for charting the path forward. I intend to fight alongside our leadership to make sure our members control their image, likeness, voice, and destiny in the workplace, and that they are compensated fairly in the process. I thank President Astin, the national officers, and the National Board for their trust, and our extraordinary staff team for everything they make possible.” Pictured: Duncan Crabtree-Ireland (left) and SAG-AFTRA President Sean Astin. articles.title: AI Firm Behind India’s ‘Mahabharat’ Series Turns to Indonesian Myth in Cross-Border IP Pact (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 24, 2026 7:30pm PT AI Firm Behind India’s ‘Mahabharat’ Series Turns to Indonesian Myth in Cross-Border IP Pact (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Soccer Drama ‘Forza,’ With AC Milan Great Alessandro Costacurta, Heads to Tokyo Market With EST N8 (EXCLUSIVE) 10 hours ago ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2 10 hours ago AI Firm Behind India’s ‘Mahabharat’ Series Turns to Indonesian Myth in Cross-Border IP Pact (EXCLUSIVE) 11 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Collective Studios The AI technology behind Star Plus and JioHotstar series “ Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh ” is headed to Indonesia . There, its developer Galleri5 and fellow Collective company Collective Studios’ Historyverse plan to create film and series properties drawn from the country’s myths and history. Historyverse, which handles original IP and studio work for Collective Artists Network , is partnering with Galleri5 and Singhasari Special Economic Zone on the venture. Projects will cover mythology, fantasy, history and animation. Indonesian creatives and cultural specialists will work alongside Historyverse’s IP development team, using production tools Galleri5 built in India. Related Stories Ryan Gosling’s Zero-G Stunts on ‘Project Hail Mary’ Broken Down by the Space Epic’s VFX Supervisors How 'Whalefall' Production Designer Ramsey Avery Built the Creature's Stomach Using Mattress Foam and Silicone Bits The first project being discussed is “Echoes of Nusantara,” a working title for an original mythology-adventure. Historyverse will run creative development, production and IP packaging, and will collaborate with local talent to get projects ready for possible financing, production and distribution outside Indonesia. Popular on Variety “The next global entertainment franchises will not all come from Hollywood,” said Vijay Subramaniam, founder and group CEO of Collective Artists Network. “Every market has stories that deserve to travel further, and Indonesia has an extraordinary wealth of them. Our ambition with Collective Studios’ Historyverse is to work with Indonesian creators to develop these stories into films, series and larger entertainment properties for the world. Galleri5 gives us a new way to approach the scale of filmmaking, while the creative vision and the stories themselves remain at the center.” Galleri5’s main product, G5 AI Studio, brings more than 200 AI models together with purpose-built tools for storyboarding, designing characters and worlds, animation, VFX and film-quality video. More than 10,000 ads and videos have been made on the platform. JioStar and Collective Media Network launched “Mahabharat: Ek Dharmayudh,” and Galleri5 built and ran the AI filmmaking technology behind the show. The company is now developing workflows for Historyverse’s theatrical slate, which includes “Chiranjeevi Hanuman – The Eternal” and “Krishna.” Those productions give Galleri5 a base for refining its technology against real-world creative and production demands. “The next generation of global cinema will be built on a very different technology foundation,” said Rahul Regulapati, founder and CEO of Galleri5 and a partner at Collective Artists Network. “At Galleri5, we’re building that foundation with G5 AI Studio, bringing frontier AI models and filmmaking workflows into one platform. We’ve already demonstrated what this technology can do through films and television in India. Now, together with Indonesia’s extraordinary creative talent and Collective’s studio capabilities, we have an opportunity to take locally rooted stories to audiences around the world.” For Indonesian creators, the partnership is a chance to match stories led by local talent, and their own original IP, with tools meant to scale up production. Airlangga Hartarto, Indonesia’s coordinating minister for economic affairs and chairman of the National Council for Special Economic Zones, said the country had no plans to sit on the sidelines of AI development or simply act as a consumer of the technology. “We intend to help shape it. Special Economic Zones allow us to turn that ambition into real productivity, skilled jobs for our young people and new sources of growth on the path to 8 percent,” he said. Singhasari will introduce the venture to Indonesian creators, studios, investors, distributors and creative-economy institutions, and help set up local partnerships and routes to market. KRAT David Santoso KR, CEO of Lokanima and Singhasari Special Economic Zone, said the Kingdom of Singhasari had flourished eight centuries ago on the land the zone now occupies. It was a hub for engineering, the arts, scholarship and government, and its culture was enriched by hundreds of years of contact with India. “Today, with our partners from India, we are bringing that history back to life, this time by mastering the AI transformation. Our aim is to build new competitiveness for Indonesia in the new-technology and digital-content subsectors, with Indonesian talent and IP at its heart,” he said. India’s ambassador to Indonesia, Sandeep Chakravorty, said the Ramayana and the Mahabharata had been part of Indonesian temple culture, wayang (traditional puppet theater) and the popular imagination for over a millennium. “Today, India and Indonesia are writing the next chapter of that shared story with artificial intelligence,” he said. articles.title: ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2
articles.full_text: Oct 24, 2026 8:21pm PT ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2 By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Soccer Drama ‘Forza,’ With AC Milan Great Alessandro Costacurta, Heads to Tokyo Market With EST N8 (EXCLUSIVE) 9 hours ago ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2 10 hours ago AI Firm Behind India’s ‘Mahabharat’ Series Turns to Indonesian Myth in Cross-Border IP Pact (EXCLUSIVE) 11 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix Stars of “ Squid Game ” and “ KPop Demon Hunters ” took the stage in Seoul on Oct. 24 as Netflix celebrated 10 years in Korea with a fan festival, where co-CEO Ted Sarandos previewed upcoming titles including “Tantara” and “All of Us Are Dead” Season 2. “Squid Game” was represented by Lee Jung-jae, Lee Byung-hun and Park Hae-soo, while Ahn Hyo-seop appeared for “KPop Demon Hunters.” Also on stage were Koo Kyo-hwan and Jung Hae-in of “D.P.,” Kim Hyun-joo of “Hellbound,” Yum Hye-ran of “Mask Girl” and Lee Se-dol of “The Devil’s Plan,” among others. Related Stories ‘Industry,’ ‘Doctor Who’ Producer Jane Tranter on Resisting Trends, Centering Women and Telling Stories About ‘People Being Accepted for Who They Choose to Be’ Sofia Coppola on Embracing an 'Embarrassing' Moment in New 'Marie Antoinette' Doc and Showing Strength on Sets Surrounded by Men Dubbed “Netflix Janchi,” the two-day event ran Oct. 24-25 at Sangam Oil Tank Culture Park. Thousands of fans turned out for themed booths, games, merchandise and live music. Popular on Variety “Ten years ago, we dreamed big. But none of us could have imagined that Korean stories would move hearts around the world, and land right at the center of global culture,” Sarandos said. Of the new titles, Lee Chang-dong’s Venice winner “Possible Love,” headlined by Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Cho Yeo-jeong and Jo In-sung, bows Nov. 6. “Tantara,” starring Song Hye-kyo, Gong Yoo and Kim Seol-hyun, follows on Dec. 11. Still undated are “Grand Galaxy Hotel,” with Lee Do-hyun and Shin Si-a; “She, Wolf,” previously known by the working title “Beauty in the Beast,” with Kim Min-ju, Lomon and Moon Sang-min; “All of Us Are Dead” Season 2, with Park Ji-hu, Yoon Chan-young, Cho Yi-hyun and Lomon; and “Solo Leveling,” with Byeon Woo-seok. Netflix launched in Korea on Jan. 6, 2016. Its first international film was Bong Joon Ho’s “Okja.” The first Korean original, the stand-up special “Yoo Byung Jae: Too Much Information,” arrived in March 2018, and “Kingdom” became its first Korean series in January 2019. In July 2021, “Kingdom: Ashin of the North” became the first Korean show to crack the Global Top 10, charting in 58 countries. Netflix has counted upward of 200 Korean titles on its Global Top 10 since it began compiling the chart in June 2021. “Squid Game” Season 1 holds the record for the longest run at 32 straight weeks, nine of them at No. 1. The show’s three seasons are the streamer’s three most-watched non-English series ever, and “Teach You a Lesson” now ranks No. 10 on that list, making it Netflix’s biggest Korean show after “Squid Game.” No other non-English content draws more viewing on Netflix than K-content, and over four in five of its subscribers worldwide have sampled at least one Korean title. “For Netflix, Korea is more than a market. It is where we discovered new possibilities, and where we learned how far a story can travel. And it is one of our most treasured partners for the future we are building together,” Sarandos said. Between 2024 and 2026, first-time directors or writers made more than a third of Netflix’s Korean titles. Park Yoon-seo, an assistant director on “Kingdom” Season 2, made his directing debut this year with YA horror series “If Wishes Could Kill.” “Netflix gave me an opportunity when I was an assistant director on ‘Kingdom: Season 2.’ I’m glad I was able to give new actors that same opportunity,” Park said. He added that he had suggested casting only newcomers to keep the series fresh, and that Netflix signed off because fame wasn’t the priority. Baek Seung-min was a second lighting assistant on “Kingdom” and now heads lighting on “All of Us Are Dead” Season 2. “Working with Netflix Korea at important stages of my career has helped me grow professionally,” he said. From 2016 to 2025, Netflix partnered with more than 80 Korean production companies on shows employing upward of 20,000 actors and crew members, along with 70,000 extras and day workers. Shoots took place in more than 100 cities and towns, with over half outside the Seoul Capital Area in locations such as Busan, Jeonju and Jeju. “When Life Gives You Tangerines” alone drew on nearly 4,000 suppliers and a cast and crew of 600, adding more than KRW90 billion ($60.4 million) to the Korean economy. Netflix’s skills and training programs reached over 6,500 people in Korea between 2021 and 2025. To get those shows to viewers abroad, Netflix now relies on 122 localization partners globally, 119 of them dubbing studios. Colorist Park Jin-young, whose credits include “Possible Love” and “Good News,” said Netflix’s arrival in Korea came just as HDR technology was going commercial. “It felt like going from working with 30 colors of paint for 10 or 20 years to suddenly having 100 colors at my disposal,” he said. Unscripted formats have also exported well. “Physical: 100” became the first unscripted show not in English to lead the Global Top 10, and local versions have followed in Italy and Mexico, with U.S., French and Swedish editions on the way. The streamer also pointed to effects off screen. According to Netflix, 72% of subscribers who watch K-content have said they’d like to travel to Korea. Jeju drew about 2.24 million overseas visitors in 2025, its most in nine years, coinciding with the premiere of “When Life Gives You Tangerines,” while visits to the show’s Gimnyeong Beach location jumped about 96%. Chef Choi Hyun-seok’s restaurant Choi saw sales rise 300% after “Culinary Class Wars” Season 1, and bookings at restaurants of Season 2 contestants climbed 303%. In the U.S., new Korean learners on Duolingo rose 37% in the week “Squid Game” Season 3 launched. Applications for Korea’s TOPIK language exam passed 550,000 in September 2025, three months on from “KPop Demon Hunters,” beating the total for all of 2024. Between April 2025 and March 2026, K-content logged more than 12 billion viewing hours on Netflix, behind only U.S. productions, and rights to the “Hellbound” webtoon have sold to 11 countries since the series launched. Netflix has also opened a Korean-language microsite charting the people, locations and numbers behind its first decade in the country. articles.title: Soccer Drama ‘Forza,’ With AC Milan Great Alessandro Costacurta, Heads to Tokyo Market With EST N8 (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 24, 2026 8:32pm PT Soccer Drama ‘Forza,’ With AC Milan Great Alessandro Costacurta, Heads to Tokyo Market With EST N8 (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Soccer Drama ‘Forza,’ With AC Milan Great Alessandro Costacurta, Heads to Tokyo Market With EST N8 (EXCLUSIVE) 9 hours ago ‘KPop Demon Hunters,’ ‘Squid Game’ Stars Fete Netflix’s Korea Decade as Ted Sarandos Teases ‘Tantara,’ ‘All of Us Are Dead’ Season 2 10 hours ago AI Firm Behind India’s ‘Mahabharat’ Series Turns to Indonesian Myth in Cross-Border IP Pact (EXCLUSIVE) 11 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Riva Studios “ Forza ,” Marco Balsamo’s soccer drama shot between Bali and Milan, has been picked up for international sales by EST N8 , which will take the film to the Tokyo International Film Festival ‘s TIFFCOM market (Oct. 28–30). Before that, it gets its first public screening on Oct. 25 at Jakarta Film Week. Balsamo’s first feature as director centers on Bima, an 11-year-old from Bali who hopes a career as a pro footballer will give his family a better life. A chance bond with a former AC Milan player in the last stretch of his career changes the outlook for both of them. Related Stories 50 Cent Opens Up About Diddy’s Secret Smear Campaign Against Him, Why He Won’t Work With Courtney Kemp Again and Learning His Mom Was Gay: ‘I’m Not Ashamed of That in Any Way’ Ryan Gosling’s Zero-G Stunts on ‘Project Hail Mary’ Broken Down by the Space Epic’s VFX Supervisors Newcomer Ghazi Alhabsyi heads the cast. Balsamo also appears on screen, alongside Tara Sibel Demren, AC Milan icon Alessandro Costacurta and Atiqah Hasiholan, Oka Antara and Tio Pakusadewo, all three winners at the Indonesian Film Festival (FFI). Popular on Variety Balsamo wrote the script and produced with Demren. Riva Studios originated the project, and its producers include Ario Sagantoro of “The Raid” franchise. Adhya Pictures has the film’s Indonesian theatrical release, set for 2027. Interest at home is strong. Both rounds of online tickets for the Jakarta screening, at CGV Grand Indonesia, sold out inside five minutes. “‘Forza’ follows a boy from Bali and a former pro footballer who open new doors for each other, and it bridges Indonesia and Italy the way only football can,” said Sophie Shi, head of studios at EST N8. “It’s a film for audiences around the world, with a story of family and hope that transcends language and culture. Our mission is to take bold Asian stories to audiences worldwide, and a family film told through the world’s most popular sport is built to travel. We’re proud to launch ‘Forza’ to buyers at TIFFCOM.” Shi and Jan Paul Villanueva negotiated the deal for EST N8, with Balsamo and Demren representing Riva Studios. Villanueva, EVP of acquisitions and global distribution, will lead sales with Cathy Ni, head of sales and U.S. distribution, and Shams Pasha, global sales and marketing executive. “We’ve spent years bringing ‘Forza’ to the screen, and Indonesia has been at the heart of it from the beginning,” Balsamo said. “This film is a labor of love and a testament to the perseverance and collaboration behind independent filmmaking. Sharing the film at Jakarta Film Week is especially meaningful. It’s a moment we’ve been looking forward to for a long time.” Demren, who co-founded Riva Studios, said the film was designed for families to watch side by side and discuss afterward. “We hope Bima’s journey reminds audiences how much it matters to have someone believe in you, especially when your dreams feel out of reach,” she said. “Seeing both ticket releases fill so quickly is an encouraging start. We’re looking forward to hearing audiences’ reactions.” Demren and Balsamo set up Riva Studios in 2022 as an independent outfit working in live action, animation and music. In 2024 it bought French animation house TeamTO. “Forza” is its first live-action feature. Also on EST N8’s TIFFCOM lineup are “Tame,” a Thai horror title from B-EST Pictures; Dean Colin Marcial’s crime thriller “Jaguar,” set in Manila; “Master,” Rezwan Shahriar Sumit’s winner of IFFR’s Big Screen Award; “Pilgrims,” a Korean sci-fi animation from Heo Pyoungkang that was selected for Annecy; and “The Invisible Half,” a J-horror from Nishiyama Masaki. The company, which brought together EST Studios and N8, has offices in Los Angeles and Bangkok and has sold and distributed more than 60 titles across over 100 territories. Its catalog includes “Hidden Letters,” which was shortlisted for the Oscars and nominated for an Emmy; “The Monk and the Gun,” Bhutan’s Oscar entry; “A Useful Ghost,” which won the Grand Prize at Cannes Critics’ Week; and “Blood Brothers,” which topped Netflix’s global chart. ‘Hatchet’ Movie: Netflix and Derek Cianfrance to Adapt Gary Paulsen’s Survival Book (EXCLUSIVE) Sex, Love and War: How the Racy Gay Epic ‘La Bola Negra’ Could Win Netflix’s First Best Picture Oscar Netflix Film VP Doug Belgrad Is Out Amid Layoffs CAA’s Roeg Sutherland Says It’s Too Soon to Predict Fallout From Netflix Firings, Thinks Recent Mergers Represent ‘Opportunity’ for Industry Netflix Sets Release Date for Rob Lowe Documentary ‘The Outsider’ ‘Decision to Leave’ Cinematographer Kim Ji-yong on Chasing Natural Light for Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love’: ‘This Is the One Where We Worried, Debated and Planned the Most’ Loading comments...

articles.title: Jay-Z Brings His ‘Jay-Z 30’ Concert Series to a Close in Los Angeles With Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too Short
articles.full_text: Oct 25, 2026 1:42am PT Jay-Z Brings His ‘Jay-Z 30’ Concert Series to a Close in Los Angeles With Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too Short By Steven J. Horowitz Plus Icon Steven J. Horowitz Senior Music Writer speriod Latest Jay-Z Brings His ‘Jay-Z 30’ Concert Series to a Close in Los Angeles With Dr. Dre, Snoop Dogg and Too Short 5 hours ago Slayyyter Cancels Remaining European and U.K. Tour Dates to Recover From Laryngitis 2 days ago Former Eminem Employee Pleads Guilty to Stealing and Selling Unreleased Music 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Roc Nation How does one measure their own legacy: In a series of shows, in the decades since a debut album, in an exhaustive eight-part docuseries breaking down the intricacies of rhymes laid down years ago? That seemed to be the existential question looming over “ Jay-Z 30,” a yearlong celebration that began with a spectacular one-off headlining performance at the Roots Picnic in late May and concluded on Saturday night with the second of two shows at Inglewood, California’s SoFi Stadium. Related Stories Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s ‘Jengira’s Magnificent Dream,’ With Tilda Swinton, Boarded by ‘Triangle of Sadness’ Mexican Co-Producer Piano For Jay, legacy has clearly been weighing on his mind. A new generation of hip-hop artists has emerged, and the decade-long gap since he released an album has opened a space for that generation to question his legacy. So it made sense that he’d revisit his catalog brick by brick, show by show, celebrating a career-long work in progress that crescendoed to a global tour after nearly a decade of artistic dormancy. At SoFi, much like his previous concerts, his performance was a reminder — no, a reinforcement — that nothing at that scale is by accident. And he said as much as the curtain fell on an hour-and-a-half finale of his “Jay-Z 30” series, encouraging those in attendance to believe in what they’ve actually witnessed. Popular on Variety “You gotta be really real with what’s going on in the world,” he said during closer “Encore.” It was a direct rebuttal to the rash of tweets and social media posts claiming that SoFi wasn’t entirely sold out, or that many of the tickets had been given away. “People will tell you that nobody was in here tonight, but you got eyes. You can see. People will tell you that the music wasn’t great, but you got ears. You gotta understand, you gotta question everything. This world with AI and everything, it’s been going on forever. They called it propaganda before. But now, the technology has caught up and people are tricked. A lot of tricknology for us… Make sure you question everything you feel.” Jay-Z brings out Snoop Dogg and Dr. Dre for a medley of classics including “Nuthin’ But a G Thang” at Los Angeles’ SoFi Stadium pic.twitter.com/UGcAN433xi — Variety (@Variety) October 25, 2026 Jay makes that music that you can feel . That’s been the thrill of his shows over the past five months. For those who experienced his rise in real time (and, frankly, many at SoFi probably had, based on their millennial look), Jay has been a pop impresario, a cultural touchstone who helped graft hip-hop culture onto the mainstream. He’s done it through a breathless string of number one albums and hits, and in boardrooms and closed-door meetings. “Jay-Z 30” was an invitation to revisit the path that he took to get there, a way to show that legacy isn’t about the hit that’s next, but rather the ones you landed to get there. To witness it was where the details mattered most. Much like his other performances, the setlist at Jay’s final night at SoFi was somewhat static — “Girls, Girls, Girls,” for instance, once again bled into “’03 Bonnie & Clyde,” while “N—s in Paris” delightfully mashed into “Big Pimpin’.” But the finer details are what make a Jay show such an experience. At each of his shows, he’s found a way to pay homage to the city that’s welcomed him. In Philadelphia, that included guest appearances from Jazmine Sullivan, Bilal and his Roc-A-Fella crew, including Freeway, Beanie Sigel and Peedi Crakk. In New York City, throughout his three-night run at Yankee Stadium , he brought out Alicia Keys for “Empire State of Mind,” as well as Fat Joe and Jadakiss. Naturally, a narrative emerged: Can he really perform a solid headlining set without a supporting cast to sweeten the deal? Perhaps that’s why the guest count at his SoFi shows was so thin compared to others. On Saturday night, he tapped Too Short to perform “Blow the Whistle,” shouting out the Bay Area. Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg came out to do a medley of their own massive hits, including “Nuthin’ But a ‘G’ Thang” and “Still D.R.E.” But it was mainly Jay, every day , in all his resplendence. He traipsed from era to era, hit to hit, his breath control and spark as refined as ever. This was performance at its peak, a marvel to behold of an artist who helped build hip-hop as an institution while adding to the story still being written. Dr. Dre and Snoop Dogg performing “Still D.R.E.” during Jay-Z’s final night at Inglewood’s SoFi Stadium pic.twitter.com/5VayWQblwJ — Variety (@Variety) October 25, 2026 As for what’s next? Rumors have swirled about a new album from collaborators who quickly backpedaled on their statements. The looming question mark of a Super Bowl Halftime Show performance hung in the air at SoFi on Saturday night. But for a string of concerts and a few activations here and there, it felt only right that Jay-Z justify the experience while rapping “Heart of the City (Ain’t No Love)” near the end of the show: “Jigga held you down 30 summers, damn, where’s the love?” Check out the full setlist below: The Watcher 2 Blow the Whistle (Too $hort) Izzo (H.O.V.A.)
