articles.title: Egyptian Cinema Eyes Its Next Act as Industry Veterans Call for Better Scripts, Wider Distribution
articles.full_text: Oct 25, 2026 2:16am PT Egyptian Cinema Eyes Its Next Act as Industry Veterans Call for Better Scripts, Wider Distribution By Essie Assibu Plus Icon Essie Assibu Latest El Gouna Takeaways: ‘Safe Exit’ Wins Top Prize, Arab TV Seeks New Talent and Egyptian Filmmakers Push Boundaries 1 day ago El Gouna’s CineGouna Expands Industry Push: ‘We Want to Give Every Filmmaker a Chance’ 2 days ago British Filmmaker Joanna Hogg on the Fight to Turn Personal Stories Into Fiction: ‘Each Time I’m Learning From Scratch’ 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mohamed Mashish, Hadi El Bagoury, Ziad Srouji (Courtesy of Abdallah Sabry, Mohamed Osama, Ziad Srouji) As the ninth edition of El Gouna Film Festival wrapped in Egypt , the conversation among some of the country’s and region’s leading producers and filmmakers turned to what the industry needs to turn its wealth of talent into films that can find audiences both at home and abroad. Egyptian cinema once dominated film production across the Arab world, but output fell dramatically from its late-20th-century heights. According to figures from the Egyptian Chamber of Cinema Industry, the country produced 112 films in 1988, before output fell to just 16 a decade later. More recently, production has shown signs of recovery, rising from 51 feature films in 2022 to 67 in 2023. Related Stories ‘Industry,’ ‘Doctor Who’ Producer Jane Tranter on Resisting Trends, Centering Women and Telling Stories About ‘People Being Accepted for Who They Choose to Be’ Netflix Joins New Edition of Santiago-Guadalajara Queer Incubator For veteran Syrian producer Mohamed Mashish , who has built a decades-long career in Egypt, capitalizing on that momentum starts with the screenplay. Popular on Variety “We need to have more time for development and scriptwriting,” he tells Variety . “We have all the industry components. But we don’t have scripts. So what can you do? I have a nice camera, a good DP, but we can’t do anything without good scripts.” Mashish has seen firsthand how new platforms can expand the reach of Egyptian storytelling. He produced the 2016 drama “Grand Hotel,” which became the first Egyptian and first Arabic-language series to land on Netflix when the streamer released it internationally as “Secret of the Nile” in 2018. He believes younger filmmakers are also benefiting from greater access to work from around the world. “They’re more open-minded. They’re connected on the internet and everything,” he notes. “Because the platforms are available now, they’re watching more than just our culture. So they are more open and they are ready to move.” But Mashish argues that new perspectives need to be matched with experience. “We have to bring the old generation and the new generation together,” he explains. “The new generation brings a different perspective, but cinema still needs experience, so we need to combine that new talent with the expertise that already exists in the industry.” Egyptian director Hadi El Bagoury , whose 2016 “Hepta: The Last Lecture” became the highest-grossing romantic film in Egyptian cinema, points to streaming as one of the biggest opportunities for homegrown talent. The growth of platforms, he argues, has given filmmakers more places to show their work while exposing audiences to a wider range of filmmaking. “You discover new stories, new directors, new genres,” he says. “You discover a lot more directors, DPs, actors and different styles.” That exposure is also changing what audiences expect from Egyptian cinema. “They want new genres, they want original stories,” El Bagoury says. The shift has particular consequences in the Gulf, a crucial market for Egyptian films. Mashish points to Saudi Arabia’s theatrical expansion as an example of how quickly audiences have evolved. “At the beginning, when the Saudis started to open cinemas, they accepted everything because it was new,” he recalls. “It’s like, ‘I will go to the cinema, I will have popcorn, no matter the kind of movie I will watch.'” “They are more selective than before,” he continues. “They will not accept just anything coming anymore. Because cinemas are now open in Saudi and in the Gulf, they are watching international cinema. So they demand this kind of quality.” For Lebanese producer and distributor Ziad Srouji (“ Palestine 36 ”), whose career spans film and television across the Arab world, reaching audiences beyond the region does not mean making Arab films resemble foreign ones. “Specificity travels; generic does not,” he stresses. “International buyers aren’t looking for Arab films that imitate Western genre cinema, and they’re tired of films made only to explain the region to outsiders. They want stories rooted in a very particular world but driven by a premise anyone can grasp in one sentence.” For Srouji, the challenges often come after the initial idea. “A good idea gets you into the room. It doesn’t get you through production, and it certainly doesn’t get you to an audience.” The bigger obstacles, he believes, are often structural. “Too many films reach the market without a sales agent attached early, without delivery materials ready and without a positioning strategy beyond a festival premiere,” Srouji says. “Sales and distribution need a strategy built from day one, not after the premiere.” El Gouna is among the regional festivals trying to strengthen the path from development onward. CineGouna, its industry arm, launched the Egyptian Voices strand this year, selecting four Egyptian projects in development for tailored training in pitching, packaging and co-production. El Bagoury argues that the industry also needs more ways to reach audiences directly. “We need more Egyptian-owned platforms, more theaters. Theaters that are cheap, accessible to all,” he says. “We need a lot of this so we don’t have to depend on anybody else. We need to show our films in our cinemas and on our platforms.” For Srouji, the ultimate measure of a healthy industry is not simply whether a filmmaker gets a movie made or lands a prestigious festival selection, but whether that success makes the next film possible. “A major festival selection is a launch, not a career,” he says. “Sustainable success is when your second film is easier to finance than your first.” ‘Decision to Leave’ Cinematographer Kim Ji-yong on Chasing Natural Light for Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love’: ‘This Is the One Where We Worried, Debated and Planned the Most’ Netflix Sets Release Date for Rob Lowe Documentary ‘The Outsider’ South Asian Filmmakers to Vie for $150,000 at Tasveer Film Market as Netflix, Aamir Khan Pictures Attend Netflix’s ‘The Blue Road’ Director Han Jun-hee on Why Playing It Safe Is the Real Risk Italian Content Investment Dropped 7.4% in 2025 Largely Due to Uncertainty Over Domestic Tax Credits, Rome MIA Market Report Says ‘Under Siege,’ Netflix’s Second Most Ambitious Colombian Series – a ‘Huge Undertaking Even by Our Standards’ – Bows Nov. 6 Loading comments...

articles.title: Serielizados Prizes: Hagai Levi’s ‘Etty’ and ‘Astonishing’ ‘Killing a Bear’ Win Big as ‘El Observatorio’ Bags the Mind the Gap Pitch Prize
articles.full_text: Oct 25, 2026 3:38am PT Serielizados Prizes: Hagai Levi’s ‘Etty’ and ‘Astonishing’ ‘Killing a Bear’ Win Big as ‘El Observatorio’ Bags the Mind the Gap Pitch Prize By Annika Pham Plus Icon Annika Pham Latest ‘Father’s House,’ Starring David Dencik and Trine-Dyrholm, Picked Up by DR Sales Ahead of Tallinn Competition 4 days ago Tallinn Baltic Event: New Movie From Darko Lungulov and Ernestas Jankauskas, Plus Titles Directed by Rising Talents Josh Trigg, Marina Palacio and Many More 6 days ago Serielizados Program: Steven Moffat, Ferran Adrià and Rodrigo Sorogoyen Bring Star Creator Power to Barcelona 1 week ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Etty Courtesy of Arte France Influential Israeli creator Hagai Levi (“The Affair,” “Scenes From a Marriage”) and prominent Spanish TV-making duo Jorge and Alberto Sánchez-Cabezudo (“La Zona”) won best international and national series at Barcelona’s Serielizados for “Etty” and “Killing a Bear” respectively. The prizes for Serielizados two competitive sections were announced Saturday night at a Serielizados awards ceremony. Popular on Variety Related Stories Netflix, ‘Elite’ Star Ester Expósito and Locarno Winner Mar Coll Adapt ‘La Regenta,’ a ‘Fresh Female Perspective’ on a Big Spanish Classic (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Black Shine, From 'State of Silence' Director Santiago Maza, ’ Delves Into the Aftermath of a 2006 Mining Tragedy That Buried 63 Miners Both series in six-parts reflect the boldness of their respective creators, who broke new ground within traditional genres. In the French-Dutch-German show “ Etty ,” based on Dutch Jewish author Etty Hillesum’s diaries, Levi deliberately opted for a modern spin to the period piece in which we follow the passionate 27-year-old Etty as she embarks on a spiritual and emotional journey in a Nazi-occupied Amsterdam. In the Spanish show “ Killing a Bear ” (“Matar a un oso”) the Sánchez-Cabezudo brothers brought innovation to the crime genre, making a bear the victim, relating the crime from the POV of multiple characters, and expanding the number of prime suspects to a tight community of 262 Anti-Bears chat room in Spain’s idyllic high-Pyrenean Val d’Arán. “With this series, we felt really lucky to have been invited into a world so fully realised, so distinctly Catalan but portrayed with a confidence and a muscularity that left us astonished,” said Finnish producer Roosa Toivonen, also Tallinn TV Beats co-head, who sat on the national competition jury with Canneseries’ Claire-Marine Pietriga and the Berlinale’s Rowan Woods. ‘Kiling a Bear’ Both series also stand out among the best shows that Europe currently has to offer, with the stamp of approval from quality-maker Arte France . Indeed, the European cultural channel was a major backer of Levi’s historical drama – conceived as a feature film in six episodes – which world-premiered out of competition in Venice, was highlighted at Series Mania, and bowed in French cinemas May 6 before launching on Arte.tv on May 16. Shepherded by Les Films du Poisson, “Etty” is sold internationally by Studio TF1 . “Killing a Bear” which had its Catalan premiered at Serielizados fast on the heels of its world premiere at Spain’s Valladolid Film Festival, is the latest prime example of Arte France’s successful collaboration with the largest Spanish pay-TV/SVOD operator Movistar Plus. The Movistar Plus Original, produced by the Sánchez-Cabezudo brothers’ Studio TF1-owned Kubik Films, will bow in Spain Dec. 1. Besides the top win for “Etty,” Arte France also scooped best screenplay at Serielizados’ official International Selection Awards for the French comedy “Camarades” co-created and co-penned by Benjamin Charbit (“Under Control”) and Dominique Baumart (“The Bureau”). Another comedy wooed the international jury: BBC’s hit show “Ann Droid” for which its creator, Bafta-nominated Diane Morgan (“Mandy,” “Cun”), won best performance for her turn as the second-hand robot Linda. On the national competition front, all four selected series won accolades. Next to “Killing a Bear,” the anticipated drama “Segunda Temporada” from the hot creators of Filmin’s “Autodefensa” – writer-director Miguel Ángel Blanca and co-writers Berta Prieto and Víctor Diago – scooped best screenplay. Bringing together a washed-up ghost-writer and a fading trap legend fresh out of jail, the show was developed as part of Serielizados Kick talent lab, before making it as a 7-30-minute drama produced by Barcelona-based Boogaloo Films and Canada. Paris-based Oble handles sales. Beloved Spanish-acting queen Carmen Machi (“Aida,” “La Mesías”), bagged a fresh best actress nod for her performance as tax inspector Sara Santano in the Movistar Plus-100 Balas’ “Celeste” Season 2 which bowed as a world premiere in Barcelona. Last year the show’s creator Diego San José and helmer Elena Trapé scooped two Serielizados wins for “Yakarta,” another example of their inimitable downbeat but sharply observant humor. Elsewhere, the buzzy HBO Max-3Cat co-commissioned dramedy “In Vitro” which offers a witty and heart-warming look at fertility treatments, received a Special Mention. “This [show] really stood out to us for its global appeal and international remake potential,” said the jurors. The series, created by Marc Crehuet with Alejandra Guimerà, was co-penned by Crehuet with Carmen Marfá, Natalia Boadas and Serielizados co-founder Víctor Sala. The latter said the show ,which launched simultaneously Oct. 19 in Spain on HBO Max and 3Cat, garnered an excellent 18.2% share on the Catalan pubcaster. “Many countries could be jealous of the creative courage the Spanish commissioners have shown, as they have helped equally bold producers to greenlight shows of this caliber!” said the jurors of the Spanish competition, who highlighted the central female-characters of different ages in each of the four series. The jurors added: “Serializados is one of these tremendous gems – smaller events where you can see that the content is lovingly hand-picked and curated out of pure passion for the art and craft of series, and the atmosphere is convivial with a lovely team that truly cares about everyone’s experience and hospitality. We, the jury members, had a great time and watching the four nominated shows was a lot of fun, as they are each so brilliant and original in their very unique ways.” Although Serielizados has another few days to run – until Oct. 28 – across various Barcelona venues, co-founder and festival programmer Betu Martínez Molero was pleased with this 13 th edition, led by masterclasses with Levi, Steven Moffat and Sue Vertue, a full day of the Miniput -quality TV festival showcase, and the second edition of the Mind the Gap pitch competition. Mind the Gap The top €5,500 ($6,100) Mind the Gap Award was handed out to the creators of the Spanish show “El Observatorio,” from Laura Roqué, Luis Sorolla and Eloy Zamora. Set in a small village from Sierra Morena, the story turns on a group of astrophysicists investigating mysterious flickering lights, until one of them-Sara starts to believe the light might be her deceased father trying to communicate. “After a great deliberation we’ve decided to award new talent who need to be discovered,” said Arte France’s Alexios Kastrissianakis, co-juror with Mubi’s Ben Driscoll, Movistar Plus’ Laura Escrivá, ZDF Studios’ Susanne Frank and Beta Film’s Peter Lohner. First pitched at the ECAM Forum 2026 where it earned the Serilizados award, the project, in early development, is looking for a producer. The jury also gave two honorable mentions to two female-led series about abuse: the Finnish psychological drama “Dangerous Woman,” produced by Gutsy Pictures for MTV Finland and TV4 Sweden, and the Spanish drama “Callback” created by sisters Joana and Mireia Vilapuig for “This is Not Sweden” producer Funicular Films, with Left Tackle Films. “Callback” was also bestowed the €2,000 ($2,200) Konga Music Agency award. Martínez Molero said: “This year we solidified our position as the leading international TV series festival in Spain and one of the most prominent in Southern Europe, reaching 18.000 attendees across more than 60 activities, including more than 30 national and international premieres.” He added: “We’ve seen a growing interest from both media and audiences for our National and International Competitions, packing our main venues. It’s also been great to see how presenting non-distributed international shows helps put them on the radar of Spanish platforms looking to acquire new series, while also helping local creators connect with key international players in the TV industry.” Following its onsite showcase in Barcelona, Serielizados will bow on line on the streamer Filmin over Nov. 10-22. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Karoline Leavitt Compares Katie Zacharia’s Abrupt Exit As Trump’s Press Secretary To ‘The Apprentice’: “He’s Known For … Moving On From People” FCC’s Sole Democrat Calls On Broadcast Lobby To Push Back On Trump-Backed Chairman’s Regulatory Threats Over Election Coverage Donald Trump Lashes Out At NBC News Reporter As She Presses Him On Why He Supports Ad That Has Been Condemned By Democrats And Republicans View All October 1, 2026 3:02pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Chris Harrison’s The Vow' Fox Nation Fox News Media is rejecting Warner Bros’ claim that the upcoming Fox Nation reality series Chris Harrison ‘s The Vow infringes on its copyright and trademarks to The Bachelor . The new dating series, set to debut in November, is hosted by Harrison, who hosted The Bachelor from 2002-2021. Related Stories News Chris Harrison’s Dating Series ‘The Vow’ Sets Premiere On Fox Nation News Chris Harrison Calls His Exit From ‘The Bachelor’ Franchise “A Very Toxic Situation”: I’m “Grateful That I’m Gone” In a cease-and-desist letter reviewed by Deadline, Ahassim Rashid, VP and intellectual property counsel for Warner Bros Entertainment, owner of The Bachelor , claimed that the teaser for The Vow contained unauthorized uses of the studio’s IP. The attorney cited images of red rose petals “falling in the background with text in the foreground,” and noted that WB had licensed that motif to third parties for separate advertisements and promotion. The attorney also objected to the use of the words “The Bachelor” in the teaser, followed by the image of a man in a tux holding a rose. Also cited was the image of a “mansion in the background meant to evoke the iconic ‘Bachelor Mansion.'” Watch on Deadline Rashid wrote that the teaser “represents a plain attempt to capitalize on and ‘ride on the coattails'” of The Bachelor. In reply, Fox News Media ‘s executive VP and general counsel Katherine Moran Meeks contended that Warner Bros’ attorneys “wrongly assume that Warner Bros. holds any intellectual property rights whatsoever in a falling roses motif or in the words ‘The Bachelor’ when used colloquially to describe a single man.” In the Warner Bros letter, its attorney wrote that they have “no objection” to Fox and Lionsgate “releasing a dating show hosted by Chris Harrison in and of itself.” But Moran Meeks also claimed that Warner Bros was targeting Harrison in “this malicious and vindictive manner.” Fox News Media argued that the use of the falling rose petals are scènes à faire, or “stock elements long associated with the romance genre that have featured in films from American Beauty to Moulin Rouge to Beauty and the Beast . The network also contended that the use of the words “The Bachelor” is protected speech. “Even assuming this fleeting use of ‘The Bachelor’ is also a tongue-in-cheek reference to your show, that kind of ‘word-play, ambiguity, irony and allusion’ receives full protection of the First Amendment and cannot support a claim for trademark infringement,” Moran Meeks wrote. Warner Bros. has yet to comment further. The Hollywood Reporter first reported on the tussle over the new show. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando BravoCon 2027 Sets Dates For Return To Las Vegas ‘Summer House’ Spinoff ‘In The City’ Renewed For Season 2 & ‘Southern Hospitality’ Season 5 Set At Bravo ‘Next Gen NYC’ Renewed For Season 3 As Bravo Expands Franchise To Atlanta With ‘Next Gen ATL’ View All October 24, 2026 8:45am Add us as a Google Preferred Source BravoCon 2027 Bravo Bravo has set the dates for BravoCon 2027 as the fan event returns to Las Vegas from October 22-24, 2027. articles.title: AMC Theatres Wants NYC’s Endangered Kips Bay Multiplex To Remain But Decision “Not Ours To Make”; Scheduled Closing Date Announced
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Sylvester Stallone On Casting Daughter In ‘Tulsa King’: “Of Course It’s Nepotism, You Idiot” Ric Flair Latest Health Update: Ex-Wrestler Wears Eye Patch In Message Reassuring Fans “I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery” AMC Theatres Wants NYC’s Endangered Kips Bay Multiplex To Remain But Decision “Not Ours To Make”; Scheduled Closing Date Announced View All October 24, 2026 9:50am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Adam Aron X AMC Theatres CEO Adam Aron has issued an open letter to New York City residents reiterating the company’s desire to continue operating its longstanding Kips Bay 15 multiplex in the Manhattan neighborhood of that name, but concedes the decision is not AMC’s to make. Neighbors of the Kips Bay-Murray Hill section of Manhattan along Second Avenue near the East River have been vocal about the planned closure of the multiplex that’s been a central commercial hub since 1999 (AMC took over the venue in 2006). The property on which the multiplex sits was privately purchased last year by NYU Langone, one of New York’s major health care systems. Related Stories News AFM Partners With AMC Century City To Expand Theatrical Screenings For Sales Companies, Producers Executives Kyle Davies Exits Bleecker Street For AMC Theatres' New Distribution Label Leawood Films AMC announced in August that the purchase would likely mean the closure of the multiplex by the end of this year, prompting an outcry and protests from residents and other businesses in the area. Watch on Deadline Following “direct engagement” from Manhattan Borough President Brad Hoylman-Sigal, AMC’s Aron issued the open letter concurring with Hoylman-Sigal that the neighborhood needs such amenities as a movie theater, supermarket and housing. Writes Aron, “Since news first broke that our popular AMC Kips Bay 15-screen movie theatre located at 570 Second Avenue in Manhattan will soon be forced against our will to close its doors, I’ve been struck by the extraordinary support that this AMC theatre has received from within the local surrounding community.” Read the entire statement below. “AMC Theatres does not want to go,” Aron writes. “Not one little bit. AMC Theatres wants to stay in Kips Bay….Apparently, NYU Langone Health does not share that view, not ours or not yours. Unfortunately, the decision to retain or end AMC’s tenure in Kips Bay is not ours to make.” According to Aron, the NYU Langone Health facility “wants to expand, seems to be in the process of buying the building in which your (our) theatre now operates, and it wants us gone. In anticipation of such a transfer to NYU Langone, the current building’s owner has terminated our lease.” Aron notes that AMC has “engaged” with NYU Langone to suggest various alternatives that would allow the multiplex to continue operating in some form. “Sadly, any and all variations that we have proposed have fallen on closed minds,” he writes, adding, “We call on NYU Langone Health to open their minds, to think creatively, and come up with a solution that will give the Kips Bay community BOTH of the two things that is wanted most of all: expanded facilities offering the world class medical care that is the hallmark of NYU Langone Health AND a fully functional AMC Theatre on Second Avenue.” The AMC chief warns that time is running out for the venue. “Unless NYU Langone Health lets us delight the Kips Bay community beyond then, to comply with our terminated lease, the lights on AMC Kips Bay 15 will forevermore see their final sunset on January 3, a mere two and a half months from now.” AMC currently operates nine multiplexes in Manhattan. Here is the entire statement from Aron: (One of Two) An Open Letter to the Kips Bay Community About the Future of AMC Kips Bay 15 in New York City “AMC Does Not Want to Go. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Sylvester Stallone On Casting Daughter In ‘Tulsa King’: “Of Course It’s Nepotism, You Idiot” Ric Flair Latest Health Update: Ex-Wrestler Wears Eye Patch In Message Reassuring Fans “I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery” AMC Theatres Wants NYC’s Endangered Kips Bay Multiplex To Remain But Decision “Not Ours To Make”; Scheduled Closing Date Announced View All October 24, 2026 10:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ric Flair at the 44th Annual Sports Emmy Awards 2023 Arturo Holmes/Getty Images UPDATE: Former pro wrestler Ric Flair is reassuring fans that he is focused on “healing and recovery” as he recuperates from a fall in Florida yesterday. In the new update, Flair, wearing an eye patch, thanks concerned fans as well as the Tampa General Hospital staff and doctors “that put up with me until 4:30am.” “I appreciate you all and thank you all and thank you for everything you did for me! I am focused on my healing and recovery right now. I will be okay!” The retired WWE icon was hospitalized yesterday after falling outside a Tampa restaurant. The incident itself came just hours after the 77-year-old former wrestler canceled a Seattle appearance due to a blood clot in his leg. Related Stories News WWE Legend Ric Flair Praises Ted Turner: "He Created So Many Opportunities For So Many Wrestlers" News Hulk Hogan Tributes Come In From Sylvester Stallone, Ric Flair, Sgt. Slaughter, Donald Trump, Jake The Snake And More View this post on Instagram Flair’s daughter Charlotte Flair provided an update on her father’s condition last night, posting on X, “Not my dad telling the doctor he fell bc of warrior dropping him on his head…(ps: he’s going to be ok).” Watch on Deadline The ex-wrestler’s accident was first reported by TMZ, which published photos Friday of Flair on the ground surrounded by medical workers and also being lifted into an ambulance. The outlet reported that Flair was “bleeding extensively” and seemed to have cut his head and his eye in the fall. Earlier yesterday, Flair posted an Instagram message apologizing to fans attending the Washington State Horror Con in Seattle. “Unfortunately, I am dealing with a blood clot in my leg, and my doctors have limited my travel to 3–4 hours. Seattle falls outside that range, and as disappointed as I am, I have to put my health and recovery first. Blood clots are extremely serious and can be life-threatening. We have seen this recently with Jalen Hurts and the complications involving blood clots in his lungs. It is a reminder that this is not something to take lightly, and I must follow medical advice.” Flair continued, noting that he is scheduled to have a procedure on the affected vein, which his doctors say will clear the way for travel. “I look forward to getting healthy and seeing you all down the road.” Flair, full named Richard Morgan Fliehr, is considered one of the most successful WWE pro wrestlers ever, with a career spanning 50 years and at least 16 championships. He retired from active wrestling in 2022. articles.title: Sylvester Stallone On Casting Daughter In ‘Tulsa King’: “Of Course It’s Nepotism, You Idiot”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Ric Flair Latest Health Update: Ex-Wrestler Wears Eye Patch In Message Reassuring Fans “I Am Focused On My Healing And Recovery” AMC Theatres Wants NYC’s Endangered Kips Bay Multiplex To Remain But Decision “Not Ours To Make”; Scheduled Closing Date Announced Anika Rashaun Dies: ‘Real World’, ‘The Challenge’ Alum Was 34 View All October 24, 2026 11:03am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Scarlet Stallone and Sylvester Stallone, 'Tulsa King' Steve Swisher/Paramount+ An interview with Sylvester Stallone from October 16 is going viral thanks to some candid comments the Tulsa King actor made about the casting of his daughter Scarlet Rose Stallone. Stallone has a blunt message to naysayers: “Of course it’s nepotism, you idiot.” The subject came up as Stallone was reflecting on comments he’s heard about the casting. “First they go, ‘Nepotism is terrible,’” he told USA Today . “I said, ‘Oh please, you’re not a good parent if you haven’t performed a little nepotism. Then obviously you don’t care about your kids, because they come first.’” Related Stories News Amazon MGM & Sophia Stallone Developing K. L. Walther's 'The Summer Of Broken Rules' For Film Video Games Scarlet Stallone & Rayll Team To Develop 'Fears To Fathom' Horror Video Game Franchise For Film & TV Stallone added, “‘Of course it’s nepotism, you idiot. That’s why we’re parents. We want the best for our children. So obviously, we let them have every advantage.’” Watch on Deadline The “nepo baby” charge has increased in visibility in recent years, as the offspring of Hollywood celebrities grow in prominence. Ryan Murphy alone has provided a home base for many: Billie Lourd (Carrie Fisher), Emma Roberts (Erik Roberts), Lily Rabe (Jill Clayburgh), Kaia Gerber (Cindy Crawford), Charlie Hall (Julia Louis-Dreyfus), Homer Gere (Richard Gere) and Ella Beatty (Annette Bening and Warren Beatty) have all featured in various Murphy series. Stallone, though, points out that parents can only do so much. “Can they maintain that level of excellence?,” he asks in the USA Today article. “That’s out of our hands. But if you can open the door, we’ll see if they have the ability to go through it. “People will say, ‘She got that job, it’s too easy.’ You’re right. Perhaps it could be. But to maintain that, to be in front of millions of people, you either got it or you don’t.” Quentin Tarantino Surprises At AFI Fest, Shows First 17 Minutes Of ‘Cliff Booth’ Inside BBC Cuts: Service Closures Begin, But Worse Could Be To Come ‘Clayface’ Shaping Up At $23M-$25M; ‘See Everything’ Wide-Eyes $19M Casey Bloys’ New DTC Team Is All HBO Max Execs; Par+’s Jane Wiseman Out Read More About: 27 Comments

articles.title: ‘These Summer Storms’ Series Adaptation In Works At Hulu From Melanie Marnich, Erin & Sara Foster
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘These Summer Storms’ Series Adaptation In Works At Hulu From Melanie Marnich, Erin & Sara Foster Weekly World News Comedy Series From ‘Reno 911!’ Co-Creator Robert Ben Garant Raises $2.5M To Film Full Season Independently In California Casey Bloys Unveils His Skydance DTC Content Team Featuring All HBO Max Execs: Francesca Orsi, Sarah Aubrey, Amy Gravitt & More View All October 24, 2026 2:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Melanie Marnich, Sarah MacLean, Erin Foster, Sara Foster Peter Konerko/Chandra Wicke/David Roemer/David Roemer EXCLUSIVE : With their Netflix comedy series Nobody Wants This launching its third season on Netflix this weekend, Erin and Sara Foster have lined up another series project, These Summer Storms . The drama based on Sarah MacLean’s 2025 novel of the same name is in development at Hulu through 20th Television where the Fosters’ Fatigue Sisters is under an overall deal. Written by Apples Never Fall developer/showrunner Melanie Marnich , These Summer Storms follows Alice Storm who hasn’t been welcome at her family’s magnificent private island off the Rhode Island coast in five years — not since she was cast out and built her life beyond the Storm name, influence, and untold billions. But the shocking death of her larger-than-life father changes everything. Related Stories News 'Nobody Wants This' Creator Erin Foster Responds To Adam Brody's "Free Palestine" Comments: "It's Complicated" Casting Heather Morris & Chord Overstreet In Talks To Return For 'Glee' Reboot Marnich executive produces alongside Erin Foster , Sara Foster and Montana McBirney via Fatigue Sisters, Oly Obst via 3 Arts and MacLean. 20th Television is the studio. Watch on Deadline “I’m absolutely thrilled to be working with the Foster sisters, 20th Television and Hulu to bring These Summer Storms to the screen,” MacLean said. “The team’s vision for the show, combined with Melanie Marnich’s brilliant writing, has made the whole project a dream come true. I cannot wait for the world to witness the delicious chaos of the Storm family in this new, exciting medium.” Marnich recently served as executive producer and showrunner on the Peacock limited series Apples Never Fall starring Annette Bening, which she adapted from Liane Moriarty’s bestselling book. It held the #1 spot on Peacock for two weeks and made Nielsen’s Top 10 weekly rankings for streaming originals. Marnish also executive produced the FX limited series A Murder At the end of the World . She is repped by WME, Rise Management and Jackoway Austen Tyerman. Erin Foster is the creator, writer, and executive producer of Nobody Wants This , starring Kristen Bell and Adam Brody, while Sara serves as an executive producer. The third season of the Emmy-nominated comedy was released Thursday and immediately shot up to #1 on Netflix’s daily US rankings. The Fosters are repped by 3 Arts, WME and Hansen Jacobson. MacLean also wrote Bombshell and Wicked and the Wallflower . Her books have been translated into more than thirty languages. She is repped by Gersh, Root Literary and Hansen Jacobson Teller. articles.title: Jessica Biel Teases How She Plans To “Modernize” ‘7th Heaven’ With Reboot & Create “Safe Space” On Set As EP
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn SAG-AFTRA Votes To Extend Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract With Updated Title ‘SNL UK’ & Cynthia Erivo Give Elphaba-Glinda Shippers A ‘Nigerian Wicked’ Sapphic Parody ‘SNL UK’ Pokes Fun At PM Andy Burnham’s Gogglebox Special In Cold Open With ‘Celebrity Traitors’, ‘Graham Norton Show’ & ‘Great British Bake Off’ Parodies View All October 24, 2026 2:10pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Beverley Mitchell, Jessica Biel, David Gallagher and Catherine Hicks on '7th Heaven' Jerry Wolfe/Spelling Prod./Courtesy Everett Collection Nearly 20 years after we last saw the Camden family, Jessica Biel is bringing a 7th Heaven reboot to a new generation. With a new iteration of the WB/CW show in the works at CBS Studios , which Biel is executive producing through her Iron Ocean banner, the actress who starred as Mary Camden in the original series explained how she wants to “modernize” the Aaron Spelling family drama. “What we want to create, how we want to modernize it, is really the things that are happening for teenagers and families that have teenagers all the way down to the youngest child — technology-based issues, school stuff, bullying stuff, drugs, alcohol,” she said on Collider Ladies Night . “All of those things we want to address in a very real way, which is, I think, what the original kind of gently touched on, but we were very careful about what our audience wanted. We had a lot of limitations. We have less limitations now.” Related Stories News ‘7th Heaven’ Reboot Coming Together At CBS Studios With Jessica Biel Poised To Produce News ‘7th Heaven’ Cast Denounces Stephen Collins Sexual Abuse In Rewatch Podcast Pilot Biel continued, “We still want to keep the DNA of what it was, where you can sit down and watch with your families, but we’re not going to hold back, I think, as much as we did before.” Watch on Deadline When asked why she only plans to return as an EP, as opposed to reprising her role as Mary Camden, Biel explained she’s focused on creating “a safe place for people to be really creative and really vulnerable, because a lot of the stuff that I’m doing now, the content that I’m doing now, it’s emotional stuff. It’s people really putting themselves out there on the chopping block emotionally, and if you don’t have that space protected, I think it’s hard. It’s hard to give those kinds of performances. Barry Watson, Beverley Mitchell, Stephen Collins, Catherine Hicks, David Gallagher, Jessica Biel, Happy the dog and Mackenzie Rosman in ‘7th Heaven’ Darien Davis/ Courtesy Everett Collection “So, I think that’s what I’m constantly trying to do as a producer is just build out that space where everyone feels like they will be taken care of, and it’s safe, you know?” she added. 7th Heaven ran for 11 seasons from 1996 to 2007 on The WB and The CW, following Reverend Eric Camden (Stephen Collins), his wife Annie (Catherine Hicks) and their children Matt (Barry Watson), Mary (Jessica Biel), Lucy (Beverley Mitchell), Simon (David Gallagher) and Ruthie (Mackenzie Rosman). Most of the cast have distanced themselves from Collins, who admitted back in 2014 that he sexually assaulted three underaged girls but was never charged. After the 14-year-old actor, who plays Morgan’s (Olson) son Elliot on the ABC crime procedural, announced this week in a heartfelt statement that his mother Meredith died, his co-stars paid their respects in the comments section. “I’m not quite sure how to write this,” he prefaced in the post . “As I’m sure many of you know, my mama passed away this Saturday. She was everything to me. She taught me school, she taught me empathy, she did everything for our family. She always had the biggest smile and she gave the best hugs. Truly the most selfless person I know.” Related Stories News ‘High Potential’ Gets Post-Super Bowl Slot, Eyes ‘Grey’s Anatomy’-Style 2-Parter On ABC & Disney+ Cancellations and Renewals ‘High Potential’ Renewed For Season 3 As ABC Hunts New Showrunner Following Todd Harthan Exit Lamb continued, “It still doesn’t feel real. Every day I’m going to miss telling her about my day, and talking to her and watching our favorite shows. This isn’t something I ever thought I would have to do. There’s so much she is going to miss in my life, but I’m grateful for the things she was able to experience. I love you, Mama.” Watch on Deadline Olson, who plays an LAPD consultant with an impressively high IQ, was one of several cast members to send their love, sharing memories of Lamb’s mother. View this post on Instagram “Your mama was such a gift, Matthew,” she commented. “She simply overflowed with joy and kindness…and the way she lit up when she looked at you…. that can’t ever be taken away. You are forever her pride and joy. I am here for you forever.” Lamb’s onscreen sister Amirah J, who plays Ava, wrote, “Sending you so much love.” Judy Reyes, who plays Lt. Selena Soto, wrote, “We saw where you got your shine! I’m so so sorry.” “The brightest light always!!!! I’m so so sorry Matthew,” wrote Javicia Leslie, who plays Detective Daphne Forrester, while Detective Lev “Oz” Özdil actor Deniz Akdeniz commented, “Love you mate.” Lamb will reunite with his co-stars in Season 3 of High Potential , which is expected to premiere on ABC in January . articles.title: Chris Harrison Says Warner Bros’ Legal Action Against ‘The Vow’ Feels “Personal”: “You Be The Judge”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn SAG-AFTRA Votes To Extend Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract With Updated Title ‘SNL UK’ & Cynthia Erivo Give Elphaba-Glinda Shippers A ‘Nigerian Wicked’ Sapphic Parody ‘SNL UK’ Pokes Fun At PM Andy Burnham’s Gogglebox Special In Cold Open With ‘Celebrity Traitors’, ‘Graham Norton Show’ & ‘Great British Bake Off’ Parodies View All October 24, 2026 4:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Chris Harrison Michael Buckner/PMC After Warner Bros . hit The Vow with a cease-and-desist earlier this month, Chris Harrison has addressed the legal drama. The former Bachelor Nation host, whose new dating show premieres Nov. 11 on Fox Nation , said it felt “personal” after Warner Bros’ recent letter accusing the reality show of copyright and trademark infringement in a teaser released last month. “I don’t see them going after the 50, 60, 70 other relationship dating shows that have come on in the time that I was there or since I left,” Harrison told USA Today . “There’s been one show that they’ve gone after. Is that a coincidence? You be the judge.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories Legal Warner Bros Fires Off Cease And Desist Over Fox Nation’s ‘The Vow,’ But Network Rejects Claim New Series Infringes On ‘The Bachelor’ News Chris Harrison’s Dating Series ‘The Vow’ Sets Premiere On Fox Nation In the letter, Ahassim Rashid, VP and intellectual property counsel for Warner Bros Entertainment, called out the alleged unauthorized use of the studio’s IP in the teaser, citing images of red rose petals “falling in the background with text in the foreground,” noting that WB had licensed that motif to third parties for separate advertisements and promotion. Rashid also objected to the use of the words “The Bachelor” in the teaser, followed by the image of a man in a tux holding a rose. Also cited was the image of a “mansion in the background meant to evoke the iconic ‘Bachelor Mansion.'” The letter added that the teaser “represents a plain attempt to capitalize on and ‘ride on the coattails'” of The Bachelor . In response, Fox News Media’s executive VP and general counsel Katherine Moran Meeks contended that Warner Bros’ attorneys “wrongly assume that Warner Bros. holds any intellectual property rights whatsoever in a falling roses motif or in the words ‘The Bachelor’ when used colloquially to describe a single man.” Harrison’s upcoming dating show comes after he parted ways with the Bachelor franchise in June 2021, following his support for a contestant amid controversy over a racist photo she previously posted. articles.title: SAG-AFTRA Votes To Extend Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract With Updated Title
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn SAG-AFTRA Votes To Extend Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract With Updated Title ‘SNL UK’ & Cynthia Erivo Give Elphaba-Glinda Shippers A ‘Nigerian Wicked’ Sapphic Parody ‘SNL UK’ Pokes Fun At PM Andy Burnham’s Gogglebox Special In Cold Open With ‘Celebrity Traitors’, ‘Graham Norton Show’ & ‘Great British Bake Off’ Parodies View All October 24, 2026 6:58pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Duncan Crabtree-Ireland attends the 32nd Annual Actor Awards Presented by SAG-AFTRA on March 1, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Earl Gibson III/Deadline SAG-AFTRA has voted to extend National Executive Director Duncan Crabtree-Ireland ‘s contract through June 20, 2032. During Saturday’s meeting, the SAG-AFTRA National Board approved the agreement with a 98.34% vote in favor of extending Crabtree-Ireland’s contract beyond its current June 21, 2028 expiration date, in addition to adding CEO to his title. The updated title “better reflect the breadth of his responsibilities,” which includes his continued role as chief negotiator for the union. Details of the agreement were not disclosed. Related Stories News SAG-AFTRA Board Adopts Resolution Opposing Paramount-WBD Deal But Stops Short Of Joining WGA Lawsuit News SAG-AFTRA Leaders Sean Astin And Duncan Crabtree-Ireland On Their Negotiating Approach, Disney-Open AI Deal, Chance Of Longer Contract Term & More “Leading SAG-AFTRA’s staff is the honor of my career, and I’m grateful for the opportunity to keep doing this work,” said Crabtree-Ireland in a statement. “As we continue fighting for human creativity, the coming years will be crucial for charting the path forward. I intend to fight alongside our leadership to make sure our members control their image, likeness, voice, and destiny in the workplace, and that they are compensated fairly in the process. I thank President Astin, the national officers, and the National Board for their trust, and our extraordinary staff team for everything they make possible.” Watch on Deadline SAG-AFTRA President Sean Astin said, “To battle giant global transnational corporations, we need expert leadership with a track record of successful bargaining and significant operational management expertise. That is Duncan. He is a powerful executive who has led our union at the bargaining table, in the halls of congress and in boardrooms and conference rooms across the industry and the world. We are thrilled to have guaranteed Duncan’s continued service to the members of SAG-AFTRA.” Crabtree-Ireland’s new contract comes at a pivotal moment for the Screen Actors Guild as Hollywood faces uncertain times amid the Paramount Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros, which the union’s leadership has opposed . Back in May, Crabtree-Ireland negotiated SAG-AFTRA’s new deal with the AMPTP, signing a four-year contract with the producers’ trade association. articles.title: ‘Nobody Wants This’ Creator Erin Foster Has “More Story To Tell” With A Season 4, But Isn’t Getting “Too Attached”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn SAG-AFTRA Votes To Extend Duncan Crabtree-Ireland’s Contract With Updated Title ‘SNL UK’ & Cynthia Erivo Give Elphaba-Glinda Shippers A ‘Nigerian Wicked’ Sapphic Parody ‘SNL UK’ Pokes Fun At PM Andy Burnham’s Gogglebox Special In Cold Open With ‘Celebrity Traitors’, ‘Graham Norton Show’ & ‘Great British Bake Off’ Parodies View All October 24, 2026 7:34pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Adam Brody as Noah and Kristen Bell as Joanne in 'Nobody Wants This' Courtesy of Netflix If Netflix wants this, Erin Foster is ready to serve up a fourth season of her Jewish romantic-comedy. Following the release of Nobody Wants This Season 3, the series creator recently confirmed she has “more story to tell” if the streamer gives the show a renewal, but noted she tries not to “get too attached to the outcome” in these situations. “There’s those next steps as people who are not in their 20s, getting married and you’re starting off already kind of behind everyone else,” she told Parade . “I experienced that when I got married, I was 37, and it’s a different experience. So, yeah, I do think that there’s more story to tell.” Related Stories Trailers Kristen Bell & Adam Brody Are Living Under The Same Roof In ‘Nobody Wants This’ Season 3 Trailer News ‘Nobody Wants This’ Creator Erin Foster Responds To Adam Brody’s “Free Palestine” Comments: “It’s Complicated” Foster continued, “But I’m also someone who doesn’t get too attached to the outcome and is sort of fluid about allowing sort of the market to tell us what they want from us. Watch on Deadline In Nobody Wants This , inspired by Foster’s relationship with her music exec husband Simon Tikhman, agnostic podcaster Joanne Williams (Kristen Bell) begins an unexpected romance with Rabbi Noah Roklov (Adam Brody), which shakes both their families as Joanne immerses herself in Noah’s culture and decides to convert to Judaism. Foster’s Season 4 comments come after she responded to Brody’s support of “Free Palestine,” which has sparked controversy among pro-Israel fans of the show. “While I love Adam, I also disagree with him.
