articles.title: Skydance Nordics & Germany Boss Says “We’re Doing Our Best To Manage The Change” After Mega-Merger
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Andy Burnham Becomes First UK Prime Minister To Join ‘Celebrity Gogglebox’ TV Festival Unveils Dates, Venues & Advisory Chair For First-Ever Greater Manchester Edition Canal+ “Making Progress” In Opposing French VAT Hike That It Says Would Force Subs Increases & Cuts View All October 22, 2026 5:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Christina Sulebakk Courtesy of HBO Max “We’re doing our best to manage the change but I’m not naïve.” That was the verdict of Christina Sulebakk , who runs the newly-minted Skydance ‘s operation in the Nordics , Germany and Benelux, over how she is approacing the $110B merger in her territories. Sulebakk, who has been with various iterations of the newly-merged group for 15 years, beginning at HBO Europe, added that “the transformation feels more substantial because the entire media ecosystem is evolving simultaneously.” Speaking at the Munich Media Days conference, Sulebakk was asked about the “elephant in the room” and considered how “some are energized by change and see it as a constant source of opportunity,” while “others naturally worry about what it means for their role, their team, their leaders, their relationships, and the future.” Related Stories Executives Elon Musk & Larry Ellison Will Join Forces To Boost Both Starlink And Skydance, John Malone Predicts Executives Versant Unlikely To Acquire Skydance Cable Networks If They Hit The Market, CEO Mark Lazarus Says Sulebakk is one of the first senior international Skydance executives to speak publicly since the merger closed earlier this month. The majority of Skydance international is being led out of L.A. by JB Perrette, although questions remain over the final shape of the non-U.S. part of David Ellison’s behemoth, including how territories may eventually get divided up. Watch on Deadline “We’re doing our best to manage the change, but I’m not naïve,” said Sulebakk. “I understand that change will have an impact. What may feel even more significant is that the entire industry is changing at the same time. RTL is going through change, ProSieben is going through change, and Netflix is going through change.” She said her approach is about “being present” and communicating. “From a leadership perspective, communication is essential,” she added. “Everything starts with communication: being present, honest, and as transparent as possible. That means sharing as much as you’re allowed to share.” “I’m not here to hold a pen and have a title” Once bedded in, Sulebakk, who took on the German-speaking markets and Benelux territories at the old Warner Bros. Discovery at the start of 2026, stressed that she wants to be an active leader. She pointed to the potential for partnerships with platforms like YouTube and talked up windowing possibilities on the likes of Netflix, Prime Video and Hulu. “I’m not here to hold a pen and have a title,” she added. “I want things to change. I want to look for opportunities in the market.” Skydance Nordics & Germany Boss Spotlights Her Approach Town Hall Takeaways; Are Stock Jitters Valid Or A Market Overreaction? Lede Company The Lede Company has acquired London-based fashion and lifestyle agency Aisle 8 , Aisle 8 founder Lauren Winslade will join as President of Brand for The Lede Company London, bringing her full team of 21 into the firm. Matthew Avento will continue to oversee the Talent and Strategic Communications divisions at the firm’s London office. Founded in 2014 and based in Farringdon, London, Aisle 8’s current roster includes MERIT, Ferrari, Astrid & Miyu, Our Place, Jigsaw, Dr Dennis Gross, Wonderskin, Bicester Village, Jo Loves, and Ruggable, and UK launch work for Away, Vuori, Kulfi, and Le Monde Gourmand. Related Stories Legal Jonathan Majors & Manager Entertainment 360 Part Ways; Actor Facing Domestic Violence Allegations In NYC News Skydance Nordics & Germany Boss Says "We're Doing Our Best To Manage The Change" After Mega-Merger The agency’s services include brand development, media relations, influencer and talent partnerships, social strategy, and strategic counsel across fashion, beauty, and consumer lifestyle sectors. All of these services will be absorbed into Lede’s operations. Watch on Deadline Winslade’s career spans two decades across agency, in-house, and global corporate roles. She began at luxury agency Aurelia PR working on Versace, Salvatore Ferragamo, and Cîroc Vodka, before moving to Ketchum and later Hill & Knowlton, where she led fashion and beauty strategy for clients including Intel and P&G. She was recruited by Harrods in 2012 to head PR & Communications, where she led a 20-person team shaping the store’s omni-channel presence. She launched Aisle 8 in 2014. “We are so excited to add Lauren, a brilliant brand builder, and her incredible Aisle 8 team to The Lede Company London,” Christine Su, Co-CEO of The Lede Company, said in a statement. “With a rare instinct for turning brands into cultural movements, Lauren has built one of London’s most respected communications agencies. The team’s deep relationships across UK media and their expertise in everyday luxury will both help us better serve our clients and further expand our presence internationally.” Winslade added: “When I launched Aisle 8 in 2014, I saw a gap in the market for an agency built on relationships, commercial focus and a digital-first approach to communications. A decade on, joining Lede brings the scale, talent, expertise, and ambition to take that vision even further. More than an acquisition, this is an opportunity to build something bigger for our clients and our people, and I’m thrilled to be starting this next chapter together.” Skydance Nordics & Germany Boss Spotlights Her Approach Town Hall Takeaways; Are Stock Jitters Valid Or A Market Overreaction? articles.title: Space 11 & SK Films Bringing Artemis II To The Big Screen With ‘Return To The Moon: The Story Of Artemis II’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Space 11 & SK Films Bringing Artemis II To The Big Screen With ‘Return To The Moon: The Story Of Artemis II’ Neon Joins Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor’s Explosive Gaza-Israel Doc ‘NAZA’ ‘Dune: Part Three’ Smashes BFI Imax Record With 33,000 Admissions Sold In First 24 Hours View All October 22, 2026 5:58am Add us as a Google Preferred Source NASA's Artemis II Space Launch System rocket carrying the Orion spacecraft lifts off from Launch Complex 39B at Kennedy Space Center. Photo by Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE : Space 11 Corp. and SK Films are behind Return to the Moon: The Story of Artemis II , a new space film with Duncan Copp and Christopher Riley directing. The producers are targeting a PLF rollout for the film, which they say will combine NASA’s real Artemis II mission imagery with the voices of the four astronauts who lived it. Worldwide theatrical release is targeted for summer 2027. The synopsis reads: “Between April 1 and 11, 2026, the crew of the spacecraft Integrity traveled 695,081 miles and reached 252,756 miles from Earth, setting a new record for human spaceflight. The film follows the mission from the launch pad to splashdown in the Pacific.” Related Stories News 'CBS Mornings' To Hold Town Hall With Artemis Mission Astronauts News Artemis II Crew Successfully Splashes Down Off San Diego Coast Space 11 says it is collaborating with NASA under a Space Act Agreement to shoot giant-screen interviews with the Artemis II crew: Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch and Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency. Watch on Deadline The narrative will be interwoven by the four astronauts in their own words and NASA’s high-resolution photography and footage, reformatted for giant screens. A 45 minute version and a shorter format are being planned to go out via SK’s network of giant-screen and specialty theaters, including IMAX theaters, museums, science-centers, and other institutional venues. The film will also be offered to school groups. Duncan Copp and Christopher Riley have both worked with NASA’s astronauts, engineers and scientists, past and present. Copp and Riley produced Ron Howard-presented In the Shadow of the Moon , winner of the World Cinema Documentary Audience Award at Sundance. Riley, a two-time BAFTA nominee, has worked with the Artemis II crew before, on hit immersive experience The Moonwalkers: A Journey with Tom Hanks , which he co-wrote with Hanks. The film is produced by Andrea Iervolino ( Ferrari ), founder of Space 11. Producer Nicola Allieta will also participate in this production. SK, the natural history and science content specialist, most recently released Ocean Dreams , narrated by Shailene Woodley. Andrea Iervolino, Founder of Space 11, stated: “Artemis II belongs to everyone who looked up at the Moon in April. We are honored to tell this story in collaboration with NASA and alongside the four astronauts who took us there. Our responsibility is to make a film that everyone behind this mission, from the teams at NASA and the Canadian Space Agency to the families who waited at home, will watch with pride. With Duncan Copp and Christopher Riley, who know this crew and this history as few filmmakers do, and with SK Films, we will share that journey with audiences around the world.” Bert Ulrich, Executive Vice President of Production at Space 11 and former NASA Film and Television Liaison, added: “In more than two decades at NASA, I learned that nothing moves people like real imagery and the voices of those who were actually there. This film is built on both: NASA’s own photography and footage, and the Artemis II crew recounting the flight themselves. On a giant screen, it is as close as most of us will ever come to flying aboard Integrity. If it inspires young people to reach for a seat on a future mission, it will have done what the best space documentaries have always done.” “NASA’s Artemis II Mission is the perfect subject for giant screen cinema: it invites audiences to experience a historic accomplishment, with the extraordinarily personal perspective of its astronauts, on a scale unparalleled by any other cinematic experience” said Wendy MacKeigan, CEO of SK Films. “We are excited to be working with Space 11 and the brilliant creative team to bring this film to audiences around the world.” Skydance Nordics & Germany Boss Spotlights Her Approach Town Hall Takeaways; Are Stock Jitters Valid Or A Market Overreaction? articles.title: John Anderson Dies: Country Singer Of Hits ‘Wild And Blue’ & ‘Swingin” Was 71
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘860’ Broadway Review: Billy Crystal Remembers The Stuff Of Life And Loss Tom Cruise To Receive 52nd AFI Life Achievement Award Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Billy Crystal, Bradley Whitford Prove Strong Ticket Draws – Broadway Box Office View All October 22, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source John Anderson (2011) Rick Diamond/Getty Images for BMI John Anderson , one of the “New Traditionalist” country singers of the 1970s who broke into the mainstream with chart-topping hits like “Wild and Blue”, “Swingin'” and “Black Sheep”, died Wednesday, October 21, at his home in Smithville, Tennessee. He was 71. His death was announced by family on social media. A cause of death was not disclosed, but The LA Times reports that the singer died in his sleep. The family statement on Anderson’s Instagram page reads, “It is with the heaviest of hearts that we share the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and best friend. To the world, he was a gifted country music singer whose voice and songs touched countless lives. To us, he was so much more. He was the heart of our family, the one who made us laugh, loved us fiercely, and made every ordinary moment feel special. We are completely heartbroken.” Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries Obituaries Freddie Jackson Dies: R&B Hitmaker Behind “Rock Me Tonight”, “You Are My Lady” & Many More Was 70 The statement continues, “His music will live on, but for us, his greatest legacy will always be the love he gave his family and the memories we will carry with us forever.” Born December 13, 1954 in Apopka, Florida, Anderson moved to Nashville after high school, at first performing as a country duo with his sister before finding some success as a solo singer in the back-to-the-roots “New Traditionalist” movement alongside George Strait, Ricky Skaggs and Waylon Jennings, among others. Anderson, even while maintaining the hard-country, keening vocal style of his traditionalist roots, began a move into mainstream country success in the early 1980s with his rocking, uptempo hit “Swingin'” and, with a nod to the more traditionalist style, the fiddle-heavy title song from his 1982 album “Wild & Blue.” The album brought Anderson to the attention of the wider country radio audience, and earned a slew of Country Music Association award nominations, with “Swingin'” named Single of the Year and Anderson winning the Horizon Award for new artists. The ’90s brought continued success, including with the chart-topping singles “Straight Tequila Night” and “Money in the Bank,” and popular albums including Seminole Wind and Solid Ground . He continued recording well into the 2000s, but with more modest results. His final albums Goldmine and Years were released in 2015 and 2020, respectively. Anderson was inducted to the Nashville Songwriters Hall of Fame on October 5, 2014, and the Country Music Hall of Fame in 2024. Following Anderson’s death, country star and former The Voice coach Blake Shelton paid tribute on Instagram, writing, “There is too much for me to say about @johnanderson in just a statement. I am sick and I am stunned. But I am a very lucky man. I got the opportunity to find out that my hero wasn’t just the guy I hoped he’d be. He was so much more than that. John was my friend. I got to see him last Sunday and I don’t even know why but I told him I loved him. That is what fills my heart in this moment. My love and prayers go out to John’s family. This one really hurts.” Anderson is survived by his wife of more than 40 years, Jamie, and daughters Alexa Kate and Brionna Cheri. articles.title: Brian Selznick’s Rome-Set Queer YA Romance ‘Run Away With Me’ Set For Feature Adaptation With Gianni Nunnari Producing
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman , Diana Lodderhose October 22, 2026 7:17am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Brian Selznick, 'Run Away with Me' and Gianni Nunnari Getty Images EXCLUSIVE : Hollywood vet and Italian native Gianni Nunnari , producer on movies including the 300 franchise , Immortals , and From Dusk Til Dawn , is bringing Brian Selznick ’s ( The Invention of Hugo Cabret ) young adult novel Run Away With Me to the screen, with Selznick adapting his own novel. Rome-born Nunnari, an exec producer on The Departed and Se7en , will produce through his Hollywood Gang Productions banner, with executive producer set as Deborah Belford de Furia. Published by Scholastic in 2025, Run Away With Me marked Selznick’s first novel written specifically for a young adult audience. Set in Rome in the 1980s, the queer coming-of-age romance follows Danny, a 16-year-old American spending the summer in Italy, whose life is transformed when he meets Angelo, a mysterious Italian boy. The novel blends more than 100 pages of Selznick’s signature illustrations with prose. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Hollywood Vet Gianni Nunnari & 'Magazine Dreams' Producer Simon Horsman Launch Film & TV Label Euro Gang With Footprints In London, Rome, Madrid & LA; Company Inks Deal With Warner Music Group For Scripted Slate News ESPN Original Series To Depict Formation Of Premier Lacrosse League Selznick is the Caldecott Medal-winning author and illustrator of The Invention of Hugo Cabret , which was adapted by Martin Scorsese into the five-time Academy Award-winning film Hugo . His novel Wonderstruck was adapted into the Todd Haynes-directed feature starring Julianne Moore, with Selznick writing the screenplay. His other works include The Marvels , Kaleidoscope and Big Tree , the latter originating from an idea developed with Steven Spielberg. Nunnari is expected to draw on his longstanding relationships in Hollywood and the European production community to mount the film on location in Rome. He most recently exec-produced Roland Emmerich’s swords and sandals epic Those About To Die in the city. James Canellos and Michael Ritter will also executive produce. The synopsis continues: “What begins as a chance encounter develops into an intense first love as Danny and Angelo explore the Eternal City together, uncovering stories hidden within its streets, monuments and ruins. Their romance is echoed by other love stories spanning the 17th century, 19th century and 1940s, revealing a history of queer love that has endured even when those relationships were forced into secrecy or erased from the historical record. As the boys grow closer, Angelo’s own secrets begin to emerge, forcing Danny to confront the possibility that their relationship, and the seemingly timeless Roman summer surrounding them, cannot last forever.” “ Run Away With Me is a universal story of love in the Eternal City, set in the 1980s, when I was falling in love with love and with Rome itself,” said Nunnari. “For me, bringing Brian’s story to the screen feels very personal.” Selznick added: “I’m thrilled my book is being brought to life by such an extraordinary team. We’re all eager to tell a story that affirms the importance of love, a message that feels more urgent now than ever.” Executive producer de Furia commented: “ Run Away With Me and Hollywood Gang may seem like an unlikely pairing, but they are a perfect combination. I’ve worked with Gianni for years and have seen firsthand his passion for storytelling, history, love, and Rome, while Brian is one of the most extraordinary creative minds working today and someone I’ve been lucky to know for decades. Run Away With Me pulses with the electricity of first love and the discovery that our own love stories belong to a history much larger than ourselves. And, of course, the Eternal City plays a starring role. Don’t we all want to fall in love in Rome?” Selznick is represented by CAA. articles.title: “Horror Is Now Cool” as the Hunt for the Next ‘Obsession’ and ‘Backrooms’ Is on: Rome’s MIA
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 21, 2026 3:21am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Kane Parsons and Curry Barker Alan Chapman/Dave Benett/Getty Images; Amanda Edwards/Getty Images Horror industry leaders came to Rome to praise Curry Barker and Kane Parsons — the YouTubers-turned-directors behind the breakout Obsession and Backrooms horror movies. “The stigma of horror of the past, that it was niche, is past. Horror is now cool, and that’s great,” Andrea Romeo, founder and CEO of Wonder Pictures, which released Backrooms in Italy, told a panel on the genre at the MIA Market in Rome. Peter Kuplowsky, programmer of the Toronto Film Festival’s thrills and spills Midnight Madness showcase, said the Hollywood box office rebound has helped underpin the resurgence in horror films. Related Stories Movies Seth Rogen Watched Curry Barker's Next Movie, Says It's "Even Better" Than 'Obsession' 'Awards Chatter' Podcast 'Obsession' Star Inde Navarrette on Sudden Fame, Cut Scenes, Relationship Takeaways, a Possible Sequel and Going Rogue for Marvel “The U.S. theatricals have bounded back, and there’s been an excitement to watch a movie with a movie again,” he insisted. So the hunt for Gen Z-tinged horror talent will continue. Including in Italy. Romeo after Backrooms wants more box office success: “We started to look for the next Kane Parsons and Oz Perkins. But we also want to find the Italian Kane Parsons. There’s some screenwriters and directors who want to be the next Kane Parsons. But they want to work in English. So we want to understand how to build an Italian background.” At the same time, the Italian Kane Parsons may be a woman. “A young female director will be my dream,” Romeo added. The horror leaders argued non-traditional horror directors like Parsons and Barker had come out of YouTube to offer fresh, new voices and innovation to the fright-night medium for Gen Z movie-goers. Rachael Labes, manager, acquisitions & productions for IFC’s Shudder, said horror films embracing comedy had also opened up new audiences. “There were 10 years where we were getting harsh movies. Now I can go to see a horror film that scares me, but also offers a fun time,” Labes argued. At the multiplex, Barker’s Obsession grossed over $400 million globally on a $750,000 budget and became Focus Features’ highest-grossing release ever. Meanwhile, Parsons’ Backrooms crossed $350 million in box office globally and is A24’s highest-grossing film in a number of countries. Roberto De Feo, an Italian director and screenwriter, says the breakout success of Obsession and Backrooms has allowed Paolo Strippoli’s campy, fun Italian horror thriller The Spiral , which bowed in Venice and is now potentially up for an Oscar. “It’s important to talk about the fact that the audience were used for 30 years to watch movies form the U.S., which was far from the Italian aesthetic. Now they want to see movies that are connected with Italy,” De Feo said. Jonny Bunning, digital marketing manager for UK-based Signature Entertainment, said horror films from new international filmmakers and exotic countries are having success connecting with audiences. “The genre community is interested to hear from a different community to see the different countries’ interpretation of horror and seeing visuals that you’re not familiar with, and that cuts through and piques that interest,” he told the panel. THR

articles.title: ‘La Bola Negra’ Commish Domingo Corral Touts HBO Max TV Deal: “I’ve Found a Home”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 21, 2026 4:12am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'La Bola Negra' Carla Oset/Netflix Former Moviestar Plus+ fiction and entertainment head Domingo Corral intends to continue being Domingo Corral after striking an overall first-look TV deal with HBO Max. “I found a home,” Corral the former director of original content at Movistar Plus+ until he was fired in 2025 told The Hollywood Reporter on Wednesday while attending the MIA Market in Rome. “It’s like a new home, because I feel fortunate to have found a place where they want to do the same things that I want to do, and that’s amazing,” he added. While at the Spanish pay-TV and streaming giant, Corral gave a green light to Cannes breakout films like Oliver Laxe’s Oscar-nominated drama Sirât , Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo’s La Bola Negra, a epic about gay men in war-torn Spain and the Spanish entry for best international feature film at the Oscars, the Javier Bardem drama The Beloved, from director Rodrigo Sorogoyen, and director Alauda Ruiz de Azua’s Sundays. La Bola Negra was acquired by Netflix out of the Cannes Film Festival for an awards season push. The platform’s long release in theaters started on Oct. 16, ahead of streaming on Dec. 2. With success like that, Corral’s sudden exit from Movistar Plus+ led 144 members of the Spanish creative community, including Bardem, Penélope Cruz and Pedro Almodóvar, to sign an open letter in support of the producer, warning of the damage his exit could have on the Spanish industry. Now with his own indie production banner backed by the Warner Bros. Discovery streamer newly-acquired by Paramount Skydance, Corral said of his exclusive TV series collaboration: ‘I’m very happy I can work with HBO, because it’s very important to work with a commissioner that wants to make the same type of shows that I want to make, and that we share the same vision and the same passion for quality TV.” The first TV series from that overall deal is the 1980s-set El Nani, about a petty criminal from the Spanish slums wrongly arrested amid Spain’s transition from fascism to democracy, and to be written and directed by Alberto Rodríguez and Rafael Cobos ( The Anatomy of a Moment ). Expect few series from a “focused” producer, Corral insisted, and TV shows that bring on board the best Spanish creative talent he often worked with while at MovieStar Plus+. At the same time, now for the first time with a global streamer in HBO Max, Corral understands he will need to make series specific to Spain’s political and cultural reality that also potentially resonate worldwide. “I have an amazing opportunity to work for a streamer that is global and that a show I’m making for Spain can be seen all over the world,” he argued. Of course, for that vision to be realized, HBO Max under Paramount Skydance will need to continue being HBO. Corral has no crystal ball, but the early omens are promising after Casey Bloys signed a new multiyear deal to oversee HBO Max and Paramount+ in a new role at Skydance. “That’s really, really positive… It would have been bad news for HBO if that hadn’t happened. Fortunately it has happened. So I’m optimistic,” Corral told THR . THR

articles.title: Netflix Stock and Price Targets Drop as Wall Street Debates If the Streamer Can Flip the Script
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 21, 2026 4:19am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos Andrew Leyden/Getty Images Netflix ‘s highly anticipated third-quarter earnings report is in, but what does it mean? In co-CEO Ted Sarandos’ telling, it’s all about execution. And how is Wall Street reacting to management commentary about the streaming giant’s outlook and largest layoffs in years, including the exit of film head Dan Lin and the replacement of chief content officer Bela Bajaria with Peter Rice? Sarandos discussed content strategy, with co-CEO Greg Peters addressing a 2026 shortfall in advertising revenue. But the key quote from the call may have been Sarandos’ blunt note about staying the course. Related Stories Movies Camel Racing, a Sect and Workplace Democracy: Tallinn Fest Sets Docs Lineup, Special Screenings Movies Great Lakes Creative Producers Lab Unveils Cohort of 15 Film Producers From Seven African Countries “There is no need for a fundamental shift in the strategy,” he said. “We do need better execution in the U.S.” adding: “It’s just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we’d like. So we had some really solid doubles and triples this year, but the other territories count on some of those titles being home runs so that they’ll travel around the world.” In Wednesday pre-market trading, Netflix’s stock was down more than 6 percent at $64.35, signaling a new 52-week low. As of Tuesday’s market close, that low had been at $65.08. So, what can investors take away from the streamer’s updates? Below, The Hollywood Reporter has compiled analysts’ reactions to Netflix’s latest set of results and outlook. Analyst: Mark Mahaney, Evercore ISI Stock rating and price target: outperform, $90, down from $110 Takeaways: “Is A Better Script Coming?” was the key question that the analyst posed in the headline of his report. “For the third quarter in a row, Netflix shares traded off mid-single-digit to high-single-digit percentages in the aftermarket on soft earnings per share results. And this is now the fourth quarter in a row that Netflix guidance has come in lighter on at least one metric. Growth has clearly slowed at Netflix.” Mahaney reduced his financial estimates and pointed out slowed revenue growth, wondering: “What’s Going Wrong And Is There A Fix?” He then put forward some reasons: “We attribute this to some market maturity, consistent competition from large platforms like YouTube, Amazon, Disney, etc. … potentially a structural challenge from short-form content platforms (TikTok, YouTube again), and content mis-execution (i.e. no major global hits since KPop Demon Hunters ).” What to do? “We believe most of these challenges are addressable, and we view Netflix management as highly capable,” the analyst offered. “By bringing in a new chief content officer, Netflix is at least acknowledging and acting on the challenge. We also believe that Netflix, the global hit machine, will likely have a hit in 2027.” And Mahaney shared an upbeat conclusion. “This along with an improvement in content delivery and some key live events (Women’s World Cup) may well drive growth again in U.S. viewing hours, changing the engagement narrative. We also see live events and the expansion of the ad-supported plan to 15 new markets in 2027 as potentially accelerating sub ads growth,” he wrote. All in all, “we believe the Netflix long thesis is still intact. Or at least, we are more confident than the market is that it is intact.” Analyst: Brian Pitz, BMO Capital Markets Stock rating and price target: outperform, $125 Takeaways: “Advertising faces product delays, but [the] long-term vision [is] still intact,” was the analyst’s post-earnings takeaway, with results leading him to “fine-tune” his financial estimates. Despite ad momentum running behind expectations, the analyst continues to see advertising as a key growth opportunity for Netflix. “We remain positive on the long-term monetization opportunity and see the near-term advertising slowdown as buildout pain rather than a structural growth challenge,” he wrote. Content and subscriber momentum are a mixed bag. “Encouragingly, membership growth remains solid, supported by healthy subscriber retention across regions as churn improved year-over-year,” the analyst noted. “We were encouraged that Netflix’s industry-leading churn improved year-over-year globally and in the U.S., better than management expected. However, management acknowledged that U.S. content execution needs improvement, and the incoming chief content officer Peter Rice will focus on it.” Pitz also addressed the role sports could play in the content strategy. “While Netflix is unlikely to buy expensive season-long premium sports rights, it continues to lean into specific live inventory, adding its first NFL Thanksgiving Eve game,” he said. “Live content accounts for only 1 percent of engagement hours despite representing 5 percent of content spend, but it remains an important lever for improving subscriber acquisition and retention and reducing churn.” Analyst: Michael Morris, Guggenheim Stock rating and price target: buy, $78, down from $80 Takeaways: To explain his stock price target reduction, Morris cited “third-quarter results that met guidance but were paired with an outlook modestly short of expectations,” which led him to lower his 2027 revenue estimate to $56.8 billion from $57.1 billion, with his earnings per share forecast down by 9 cents to $3.80. With Netflix cutting its 2026 advertising revenue target to around $2.7 billion from $3.0 billion also made Morris pare back his 2027 ad estimate to $4.0 billion, which he said compares to a $5.2 billion consensus expectation. Of course, the recent content leadership changes and what it means for its programming strategy also featured in his report. “Co-CEO Ted Sarandos described the company’s strategy as ‘unchanged’ while acknowledging ‘we could do better,'” he wrote. “Peter Rice’s mandate as chief content officer is to find more home runs across formats and genres and strengthen talent relationships. Returning franchises including Emily in Paris , The Diplomat and Wednesday , and feature films including Narnia , provide a bridge to a lineup developed under Mr. Rice, and we consider a more impactful slate non-negotiable for renewed investor interest.” He also called content licensing “a silver lining” in content, citing a recent deal with Disney. Concluded Morris: “Netflix is a top platform for licensed product, and in our view more win-win partnerships with underexposed content at attractive terms would be incremental. Bundling with most other major streamers or launching a free service in the U.S. would not sustainably bolster top-line growth.” Analyst: Ralph Schackart, William Blair Stock rating and price target: outperform, no price target Takeaways: The engagement and content debates featured heavily in Schackart’s report. “The company acknowledged the need to accelerate view-hours growth, highlighting India as an example of successful execution, where view hours increased 24 year-over-year and view hours per member grew in the low- to mid-single digits,” he highlighted. The analyst also weighed in on Rice’s content chief appointment. “Management views the transition as an opportunity to improve content execution, particularly in the United States,” he wrote. “Management stressed that the change does not represent a shift in content strategy, but rather an opportunity to take the slate to the next level.” Schackart summarized his takeaways from the results and outlook this way: “Unfortunately, this quarter did not give the bears a reason to pull back on their growth concerns.” What does this mean for investors? “While it may take patience, we believe investors should benefit from accumulating shares on the pullback, recognizing that there is not a near-term catalyst. We believe the company will solve its near-term content concern at some point in 2027.” Analyst: Laurent Yoon, Bernstein Stock rating and price target: outperform, $80, down from $95 Takeaways: Patience was a recurring theme in Yoon’s report, which is entitled “When Success Starts Looking Mature.” “New content boss, new content strategy?” it asked. “Perhaps, but not anytime soon,” it offered. “Despite new leadership with deep experience across TV, film, and streaming, the messaging remains firmly centered on traditional content, live events, and licensing. Any meaningful strategic shift – if there’s one – could take years, not quarters, to show up in the slate or the numbers.” That may also keep weighing on investor sentiment. “Investors will increasingly focus on the durability of ‘double-digit’ growth and the pace of margin expansion as content investment comes back into focus,” the analyst explained. “The risk is not the near-term fundamentals, but perception. A strategy that continues to lean on traditional content, traditional formats, and traditional engagement risks reminding both consumers and investors of the ‘L’ word – legacy. That alone may be enough to keep the stock range-bound near term, even if the underlying business continues to execute well.” Advertising may not be broken, but also made for a disappointment. “Management discussed slower ad product rollouts rather than demand, suggesting a delay rather than disruption, but it still represents a missed opportunity,” the analyst concluded. All in all, he reduced its forecasts for Netflix, which also pushed down the stock price target. “Changes in earnings per share estimates are due to slower-than-expected advertising revenue growth, domestic subscriber growth and margin expansion slightly offset by accelerated buybacks,” Yoon noted. “We also reduced our valuation multiple to 20 times (from 25 times) to reflect slower growth and ongoing negative investor sentiment without a near-term positive catalyst.” Analyst: Rob Fishman, MoffettNathanson Stock rating and price target: buy, $90, down from $100 Takeaways: MoffettNathanson was among the firms cutting their financial forecasts and Netflix stock price target, in this case by $10, following the latest results and management commentary. Fishman wondered about the outlook for revenue growth, especially given the ad revenue updates, and the outlook for content spending following the recent executive changes. “If revenue is slowing, does Netflix need to reaccelerate content spend?” the analyst asked. And he shared that underlying his forecast is 8 percent content spending growth as “management is clearly focused on reining in expenses to invest in high-impact areas, as evidenced by the recent headcount reductions.” His conclusion is that Netflix can continue to improve the monetization of its reach and scale to grow profits in the future. Wrote Fishman: “After the sell-off, we believe Netflix’s downside is limited, and the stock presents an attractive entry point to capture upside in leveraging the company’s global scale to drive incremental growth above the strength of its core business model.” THR

articles.title: Don’t Stop Believin’: ‘Glee’ Revival a Go at Disney+ and Hulu
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All October 21, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The cast of 'Glee' in the season three finale in 2012. Adam Rose/Fox via Everett Collection Logo text Get your slushies ready: Glee is returning. Disney+ and Hulu have ordered a revival of the high school musical, which ran from 2009-15 on Fox. 20th Television, which produced the original series, is also behind the new show. And that is literally all the public information Disney put out Wednesday morning — no producers or cast are mentioned in the press release announcing the series order. Sources say deals for the the creative team are still being finalized, but it’s an extremely safe bet that co-creator Ryan Murphy is involved. Murphy, after all, told The Hollywood Reporter in August that he was “considering” a Glee -vival: “For many, many people now in their 20s, they grew up on that show and it meant something to them,” he said. “The music meant something. So, let’s kick it around and see what we get.” Related Stories TV Disney+ Sets Japanese Horror Anthology Series 'Night Tales Club' With Kiyoshi Kurosawa, Takayuki Yamada TV 'American Horror Story' Scores Season 14 Renewal at FX In late September, Murphy took the idea further , telling Entertainment Tonight that he had finished a script for a new version with co-creators Brad Falchuk and Ian Brennan. Glee ran for six seasons on Fox, becoming a cultural phenomenon almost from the moment its pilot debuted. The series followed the members of the show choir at William McKinley High School in Lima, Ohio, through the ups and downs of high school and beyond. The original cast included Lea Michele, Matthew Morrison, Jane Lynch, Cory Monteith, Chris Colfer, Kevin McHale, Dianna Agron, Amber Riley, Jenna Ushkowitz, Heather Morris, Naya Rivera, Mark Salling, Darren Criss, Harry Shum Jr., Jayma Mays, Dot-Marie Jones and Chord Overstreet. Alex Newell, Jacob Artist, Becca Tobin, Blake Jenner and Melissa Benoist joined the series in later seasons. Glee won six Emmys, including a directing win for Murphy for the pilot episode and best supporting actress in a comedy series for Lynch in 2010. The original series streams on Hulu, and songs from Glee draw about 4 million monthly listeners on Spotify. THR

articles.title: Audiovisual Women Leadership Program Unveils Participants, Sets Tallinn Partnership
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 21, 2026 5:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Audiovisual Women participants Courtesy of Erich Pommer Institut Germany’s Erich Pommer Institut (EPI) has unveiled the participants of its fifth edition of Audiovisual Women, its program designed for female professionals in mid- to senior-level management positions across the European audiovisual sector. The cohort includes 15 media professionals from 11 countries. “The program seeks to strengthen participants’ professional networks, unlock new business opportunities and support the sustainable growth of their careers and companies,” the EPI says. “Audiovisual Women helps female leaders navigate industry challenges, develop innovative business models and harness the opportunities of digital transformation.” The offering is open to female leaders working across the entire value chain of the industry. Participants go through a mix of in-person and online training sessions, one-on-one business coaching, exclusive networking events and a self-study phase. The goal is to strengthen leadership skills and explore key topics, including entrepreneurship, innovation, change management, communication and self-promotion. New this year is a partnership with the Industry@Tallinn & Baltic Event , the industry platform of the Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF). In mid-November, EPI will take the participants to Tallinn to give them the opportunity to expand their networks beyond their home markets and connect with professionals from across Europe. A distinctive feature of the program is its archery-based learning concept, developed by coach Annette Birkholz, which is designed to allow participants to connect, explore, and reflect on systemic patterns. By also involving participants’ hiring managers and encouraging more diverse, gender-balanced recruitment practices, Audiovisual Women further aims to foster “lasting structural change” across the industry. “With Audiovisual Women, we aim to strengthen female leadership and contribute to a more diverse, innovative and equitable audiovisual industry,” says Gabriela Seidel-Hollaender, project manager international training at EPI. “Investing in female leadership is essential to building a more resilient and forward-looking industry.” Audiovisual Women is funded by Creative Europe MEDIA. Partners of the program are FOCAL, Flanders Audiovisual Fund (VAF), PÖFF – Black Nights Film Festival, Industry@ Tallinn & Baltic Event, EAVE – European Audiovisual Entrepreneurs, EWA – European Women’s Audiovisual Network, and Women in Film & Television International (WIFTI). Check out the complete list of Audiovisual Women participants below.
