articles.title: Russell Brand Told Fan To “Clean Up Mess” After Alleged Rape As Accuser Tells Court She “Carried Feeling Of Guilt & Shame” For Years
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Manager Spearheading Entertainment & New Media Biz At Three Six Zero Russell Brand Accuser Says She Reported Comedian To Channel 4 In 2009 After He Allegedly Lay His Head On Her Lap & Demanded Massage Russell Brand Accuser Alleges Witnesses Were Present When He “Grabbed My Face” & “Pushed His Body Against Mine” At Radio Station View All October 21, 2026 5:33am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand arrives at Southwark Crown Court on Wednesday Getty Editor’s note: T his story contains details of alleged sexual offenses that readers may find distressing Russell Brand told one of his fans to “clean up the mess” after allegedly anally raping her at his home in north London, a court has been told. On a busy day at London’s Southwark Crown Court, the jury heard from three of Brand’s six accusers. The court was played a 2024 video recording of a police interview with one woman, whom we are calling Complainant 5 (C5) as she has a lifelong right to anonymity . During the two-hour-long interview, C5 was frequently in tears and distressed as she relived her alleged encounter with Brand. Related Stories News Russell Brand Accuser Says She Reported Comedian To Channel 4 In 2009 After He Allegedly Lay His Head On Her Lap & Demanded Massage Legal Russell Brand Accuser Alleges Witnesses Were Present When He "Grabbed My Face" & "Pushed His Body Against Mine" At Radio Station The Despicable Me star faces three charges of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one of indecent assault based on allegations made by six women . He will set out his defense later in the trial, denies all charges, and has pleaded not guilty. Watch on Deadline C5, who thought Brand was “interesting, articulate and intelligent about things that others would shy away from,” said she met Brand at one of his comedy gigs in 2009 at the Hammersmith Apollo. She was “invited upstairs for drinks,” after which she consensually performed oral sex on him but told him she didn’t want to have penetrative sex. She said he took her number, “thought I’d never hear from him again,” but Brand kept messaging her and soon after she agreed to go to his house in Hampstead, north London. She was driven to his home by a driver, let in by an associate of Brand’s and was told, “Russell’s on the phone to America.” Brand then came downstairs and told her, “This is the best decision you’ve ever made,” she said during the police interview, which was played to the jury to avoid C5 having to retell her story in the courtroom. Deadline has been following the trial live via a closed video stream from the courtroom. C5 alleged that Brand’s demeanor changed when they were kissing on his bed and he suddenly said, “You need to have a shower because your hair smells funny,” which “didn’t sound kind” but made her “feel like I was dirty.” At first, C5 alleged she and Brand had consensual penetrative sex and Brand was using a condom. “I didn’t enjoy the experience because I felt like somebody was just f**king a hole,” she added. “I could have been anyone. It didn’t matter who I was.” After having consensual sex for some time, C5 alleged Brand “turned me onto my front,” and she assumed he wanted to continue vaginal sex. Instead, she said he inserted his fingers into her anus before anally raping her, which she said was extremely painful. C5 alleged Brand said to her, “I want you to feel my cum,” at which point he ejaculated inside her anus and she realized he had removed his condom. After he was finished, she alleged Brand “looked absolutely horrified” and told her, “You need to clean up the mess that you’ve made.” He then left the room and his associate told her that Brand was performing another gig shortly and “whenever you are ready you can leave.” C5 was in tears during the police interview when she said: “I went there knowing I would have sex with him and what I mean is vaginal penetrative sex. I went knowing that would happen. I want to make that clear because I’ve struggled to accept what happened to me because I went there knowingly and willingly.” “He did not act like he’d done anything wrong” That evening, she said she told her flatmate what had happened and was in so much pain she had to “sit on an ice cube tray.” She was later told she had an anal tear and became convinced she had contracted HIV, for which she tested negative. “I wanted to just leave it all behind,” she told police. “I thought maybe he does that all the time. He did not act like he’d done anything wrong.” Since the incident, C5 said she has struggled with alcohol addiction and went to rehab in 2023, during which time she opened up about the incident. Around that time, Channel 4 aired its Russell Brand: In Plain Sight documentary, which was a catalyst for her going to police. “I’ve tried not thinking about it and it hasn’t worked, so whatever happens after this [police interview], I know I’ve sat in a room and said what happened to me,” she explained. “I just don’t want to die knowing that what he did to me I have not said to the right people.” “I carried the feeling of guilt and shame” C5 is the final Brand accuser to give evidence and took to the stand for questioning on Wednesday. All of the accusers came forward after watching the Channel 4 documentary, but none of them know each other, the prosecution has said. Under questioning from Brand’s lawyer Ian Winter, C5, who gave evidence to the court from behind a screen, said she had “carried the burden” and “carried the feeling of guilt and shame” for years after the alleged attack. She was repeatedly pressed by Winter on whether she had in fact consented to anal sex as well as vaginal sex with Brand, but continued to deny that this was the case. “Just because you go somewhere willingly, that does not mean the outcome at the end is [necessarily] consensual,” she said. “I did not make the decision to have anal sex with Mr. Brand. I did not make that decision. We never had a conversation about anal sex.” The summer after the alleged rape took place, the court heard that C5 saw Brand from a distance at an event she was working at during the Edinburgh Festival. She said he texted her and she replied asking why he was messaging her, and Brand responded, “Because you’re dirty and I wanna push you further.” C5 said she then responded by saying, “I think you pushed me far enough, you treated me like an animal,” to which Brand then quickly apologized and the text conversation ended. Pushed by Winter on why she didn’t tell Brand he had raped her, C5 said: “To give you that answer is really difficult.” She was also pressed by Winter on how much she “adored” Brand, with Winter putting forward the idea several times that she was “obsessed” with Brand before she first met him at the Hammersmith Apollo. “You knew he was extremely sexually active with multiple women?,” asked Winter, to which C5 replied: “Correct.” “You knew he had won The Sun newspaper’s ‘Shagger of the Year’ award three years running,” Winter then asked. “I don’t think I was aware of that,” replied C5. The evidence from Brand’s accusers is now over and the court will return tomorrow with witnesses. The court has been told repeatedly that Brand declined to answer questions when interviewed by police. He instead relied on a prepared statement, in which he claimed that he did not recall meeting the women and did not remember their names. He said any sexual contact was consensual. The trial continues. articles.title: Roku Streamer Howdy Buys ‘The Walsh Sisters’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Roku Streamer Howdy Buys ‘The Walsh Sisters’ Russell Brand Told Fan To “Clean Up Mess” After Alleged Rape As Accuser Tells Court She “Carried Feeling Of Guilt & Shame” For Years Amelia Dimoldenberg’s Manager Spearheading Entertainment & New Media Biz At Three Six Zero View All October 21, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The Walsh Sisters Leanne Sullivan EXCLUSIVE: Roku ‘s new streamer Howdy has boosted its offering with the acquisition of exclusive rights to hit BBC -RTÉ adaptation The Walsh Sisters . Starring Derry Girls actor Louisa Harland, the Marian Keyes adaptation follows five Irish sisters through secrets, family feuds and moments of grace. Howdy has landed Season 1 rights from November 5 exclusively in the U.S., with episodes dropping weekly, and will take Season 2 next year around the time The Walsh Sisters launches in the UK and Ireland. The Walsh Sisters , which is based on a hugely popular set of novels, has been a hit for the BBC and RTÉ. Caroline Menton ( Oddity ), Danielle Galligan ( House of Guinness ), Máiréad Tyers ( Extraordinary ), Stefanie Preissner (who also adapted the series), Aidan Quinn and Carrie Crowley also star. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News BBC Scraps TikTok Generation TV News Bulletin 'The Catch Up' Acquisitions The BBC & MHz Choice Board Sweden's Latest 'Wallander' Series The Walsh Sisters joins the likes of Weapons , Django Unchained and The Wicker Man on Howdy. Following its acquisition by Fox, Roku unveiled Howdy last year as a cheaper ad-free streamer for $2.99 per month. “Howdy was built to make great entertainment affordable, and The Walsh Sisters is a perfect example,” said the streamer’s boss Robin Chacko. “It’s a premium drama with real heart and humor that has already resonated with audiences, critics, and fans of the best-selling book series by Marian Keyes.” Cineflix Rights sells the show and struck the deal. Stephanie Coon, the distrib’s VP of Sales in the Americas, added: “After catching the eyes and hearts of audiences around the globe, we’re thrilled that US viewers will have the chance to fall in love with The Walsh Sisters . Their special blend of family drama, trauma, and humor in the face of it all is the kind of emotional honesty audiences crave.” Kefi Chadwick ( Rivals, Death in Paradise ) wrote two episodes of The Walsh Sisters and the series is directed by Ian Fitzgibbon ( Hullraisers, Moone Boy ). The Walsh Sisters was RTÉ’s highest-rated drama in two years, according to the Irish broadcaster. The Howdy deal was brokered by Elias Patlakas on behalf of Roku. articles.title: Snap Enlists Robert Downey Jr. to Push Specs
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Robert Downey Jr. for Specs Snap Inc. Robert Downey Jr. plans to bring a little bit of Iron Man technology to pop culture, linking up with Specs to become its chief customer experience officer. The position is mostly a marketing one, with the Marvel actor working with the Specs team on original content, lens experiences, hardware collaborations and other features. Specs, of course, is the augmented reality glasses concept from Snap Inc. The company was early to the game with the original Snap Spectacles in 2016, which were available in limited quantities. The new version is much more advanced, using technology to overlay images on the real world through a glasses-like form factor, much smaller and lighter than VR headsets. The Downey partnership will launch on TV with a video campaign set to debut during tonight’s New York Knicks vs. Philadelphia 76ers NBA Tip-Off game, with another spot set to launch during game one of the MLB World Series later this week. The first pieces of content are available now on the Specs website and on YouTube. Downey, in a statement, said that the technology reminds him of what Tony Stark himself used in the Marvel movies. “Trying is believing. Having tested practically every wearable tech that’s come to market in the last 20 years, and been largely unimpressed, I was absolutely sold on Specs within 40 seconds,” said Downey Jr. “The applications are endless. Families can share experiences instead of hunching over devices, skills can be honed, big business can streamline development. In short, it delivers on the promise of AR glasses made by a certain techno optimist superhero I portrayed. Life imitates art-imitates life! I’ve never experienced the confident, warm and creatively inviting atmosphere that Evan has cultivated at Specs anywhere else in the tech sector. Wait’ll you see what we create for you to enjoy.” “We’re incredibly excited to welcome Robert Downey Jr. to Specs to help shape the future of augmented reality,” added Evan Spiegel, co-founder and CEO of Snap Inc. “Robert has been imagining what this technology could become for nearly twenty years, and it’s an honor to work with him to bring that vision to life.” THR

articles.title: Christina Applegate Reveals She Was Misdiagnosed and Does Not Have MS: “I Haven’t Gotten Better … I’m Back at Square One”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Jackie Strause Plus Icon Jackie Strause Managing Editor, East Coast jackiedstrause Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 6:04am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Christina Applegate in 2024. Matt Winkelmeyer/Getty Images for Critics Choice Association Christina Applegate returned to her podcast after some time away to reveal that she was misdiagnosed and does not, in fact, have MS. Applegate revealed in a two-part episode of her MeSsY podcast that she co-hosts with Jamie-Lynn Sigler, who has multiple sclerosis (MS), that, in 2021, she was being tested for “everything under the sun,” but not MS right away. She had brain and spinal MRIs, and a spinal tap, which determined that she had RMS, which was, at the time, “on the low scale.” However, Applegate said she was getting progressively worse. The doctor then showed her the lesions on her brain, almost 40, she said, and “that was it. That was my answer to everything that was going on” at the time. Related Stories General News Christina Applegate Breaks Silence Amid Hospitalization Reports to Give Health Update Movies Christina Applegate: Will Ferrell and Adam McKay Gave Me Parts of Their 'Anchorman' Salaries After "Offensive" Studio Offer Applegate revealed her diagnosis in August 2021, at age 49, sharing publicly that she had been diagnosed a few months prior. On her podcast episode released on Tuesday, she said that after her diagnosis, she then leaned on the MS community, which includes her co-host, and started infusions that went on for years, wreaking “havoc” on her body. A “couple of years ago,” however, Applegate said, her doctor wanted to take her off of the infusion and monitor her B cells. When her B cells didn’t change, that’s when they began a study into her diagnosis. Thanks to new technology around brain MRIs, Applegate recently learned she was misdiagnosed. “She came into my room and she said, ‘Congratulations, you don’t have MS. Congratulations.’,” she recalled, fighting back tears. Applegate said everyone else was so happy but, “I’m not happy at all.” “You don’t get misdiagnosed, and then all of a sudden, I’m better,” she added. “I haven’t gotten better, Jamie. If anything, I’ve gotten worse in some ways. So I’m back at square one where I don’t know what’s going on with me, and that’s going to be an online investigation that my doctors are going to get into to find out what has been happening since 2021. Why did this happen? I have every symptom of someone with MS — every single one.” Applegate said there is a high number of misdiagnoses with MS, even after years of infusions like she had. She began crying while saying, “I feel like I let everybody down. I became, you and I, the poster children for MS. I had a reason — I had a fucking reason — as to why my day sucked every day. And now I don’t have a reason, and it’s very unnerving and very confusing for me.” Applegate continued to say she’s currently in a state of shock. “It’s a mind fuck, for sure,” she told Sigler. The investigation into her health is so new, she said, that next week she begins a process that will involve her being her own advocate and finding the right specialists. “I needed some time to process that, but I also needed me time, after the book and some health stuff that was going on,” she said. “I just needed time to find the love in life again.” She said it “hurts to get out of bed; it hurts to stand up. I’m still sleeping all the time. I’ve still got a lot of health issues. But I’m finding ways to make my room joyous and make sure that my doors are open and that I can hear the birds and the fountain outside.” Applegate and Sigler said they will have experts on to respond to the news but that their podcast will also still be an entertaining space for the two of them to discuss the things that bring them joy (like Bravo shows and Andy Cohen). Ultimately, she said she’s not relieved, but Sigler pushed her to be curious. “Your reaction is very human and real, and I think one that anyone would share,” said Sigler, then insisting that Applegate look forward to doing a little dance, “a little shuffle,” over not having MS. “I’ve been talking about that damn jumping for so long!” Applegate said, with a laugh. THR

articles.title: David Ellison, Dina Powell McCormick, Chris Winfrey and Roger Lynch Join Paley Center Board
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 6:17am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The Paley Center for Media in New York Photo by Noam Galai/Getty Images for CBS The Paley Center for Media is adding some boldface names to its board of trustees. The nonprofit says that Skydance CEO David Ellison, Mattel CEO Roger Lynch, Meta president and vice chair Dina Powell McCormick and Charter CEO Chris Winfrey are joining its board, and that Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. is joining its Los Angeles board of governors. The Paley Center operates two facilities, one in New York and the other in L.A., which provide a year-round museum focused on media, entertainment culture, as well as public-facing and invitation-only events like Paleyfest. In fact, the new trustees were announced at the kickoff of the 2026 Paley International Council Summit, which will include sessions with people like Strauss Zelnick, John Malone, David Solomon, Gary Bettman and others. The board is already comprised of media and entertainment heavy hitters that include Lachlan Murdoch, Ynon Kreiz, Eddy Cue, Neal Mohan, Roger Goodell, Tyler Perry and Josh D’Amaro. “We are privileged to welcome this renowned group of exceptional and distinguished leaders to Paley’s Board of Trustees and Los Angeles Board of Governors,” said Maureen J. Reidy, president & CEO of The Paley Center for Media. “Their visionary leadership, innovative insights, and extraordinary expertise will further strengthen Paley’s standing as the media industry’s preeminent nonprofit cultural institution.” “I am honored to join The Paley Center for Media’s Board of Trustees,” added David Ellison. “For decades, Paley has been home to the conversation about how media shapes our culture, preserving the stories that have captivated audiences around the world while championing the creators and innovators who will define what comes next. At Skydance, we believe deeply in the power of media to entertain, inform and bring people together, whether through film, television, streaming or the news. I look forward to working alongside this distinguished group of leaders to support the Paley Center’s vital work and its mission to celebrate and advance the media landscape for future generations.” “The Paley Center has been an enduring force in both preserving media’s history and helping shape its future,” said Roger Lynch. “It is an honor to join the Board of Trustees, and I look forward to contributing to Paley’s important work for years to come.” “Music and media have the power to make us feel seen, open our minds, and connect us like nothing else can,” added Harvey Mason Jr. “That power comes from people with a story to tell and the courage to create. I’m honored to join the Paley Center’s Los Angeles Board of Governors and help champion those voices, celebrate the work that has shaped our lives, and inspire the next generation to leave their own mark.” THR

articles.title: Tilda Swinton to Star Off-Broadway In Solo Show ‘Man to Man’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 6:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Tilda Swinton in 'Man to Man.' Ruediger Glatz Tilda Swinton will make her New York stage debut this winter in Manfred Karge’s Man to Man . The solo show will play the Lucille Lortel Theatre starting Feb. 21, 2027, with an opening night Feb. 28 for a strictly limited eight-week run. Swinton returns to the role after originating the role in 1987. The Academy Award winner is currently performing in the role at London’s Royal Court Theatre, marking her first return to the stage for the first time since the original production. This production will also have limited runs in Scotland at the Traverse Theatre and in Germany with the Berliner Ensemble before coming to New York. Set in 1930s Germany, the play follows a woman who assumes her dead husband’s identity and lives as Ella/Max as the country changes, including through war and dictatorship. The production originated at the Traverse Theatre, which first commissioned the original production in 1987 before it transferred in 1988 to the Royal Court. This revival brings back the original creative team with direction by Stephen Unwin, design by Bunny Christie and translation by Anthoyn Vivis, with revisions by Unwin. Lighting Design is by Ben Ormerod, sound design by Elena Peña and projection design by Matt Powell. Swinton won the Academy Award in 2007 for her role in Michael Clayton . Other film credits include The Curious Case of Benjamin Button, Burn After Reading, Orlando and her frequent collaborations with director Wes Anderson , which include roles in Moonrise Kingdom, The Grand Budapest Hotel , The French Dispatch and Asteroid City . Brian and Dayna Lee, The Royal Court Theatre, Berliner Ensemble, and Madison Wells Live are producing. THR

articles.title: Hannah Berner and Paige DeSorbo’s ‘Giggly Squad’ to Play Madison Square Garden (Exclusive)

Lucio Andreozzi Foto Hannah Berner and Paige DeSorbo’s Giggly Squad is coming to Madison Square Garden. The popular podcast will stop at the Garden for a live recording of the show on Feb. 18, 2027, as part of a broader U.S. and European tour. This will be the first female hosted podcast to perform at Madison Square Garden. Berner and DeSorbo launched the show on Instagram Live in 2020, as the two rose to fame on Bravo’s reality show Summer House . It has since grown into a top 10 comedy podcast. The show, which streams twice weekly, sees the two friends chat about their lives, dating, pop culture, fashion and more. The podcast has previously held live tours across 70 cities, including two shows at Radio City Music Hall, and sparked a New York Times bestselling book, How to Giggle . Giggly Squad was named podcast of the year at the 2026 iHeartPodcast Awards. Giggly Squad recently moved to SiriusXM in a multiyear deal valued at $160 million, according to sources familiar with the matter. As part of the deal, SiriusXM has exclusive global sales for the audio and video episodes of the podcast. New programming from Giggly Squad is expected to roll out in 2027. Previous podcasts to record a show at Madison Square Garden include Kill Tony Live , with Tony Hinchcliffe and Brian Redban, and The Basement Yard , hosted by Joe Santagato and Frank Alvarez. New York Knicks players Jalen Brunson and Josh Hart, and Matt Hillman, hosted a live edition of their Roommates Show from Madison Square Garden’s Infosy’s Theater this past summer. THR

articles.title: Two-Thirds of Microdramas Released in Latest Quarter Outside China Were AI Generated, Says Report
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source An image of My Muse, Holywater’s AI-generated verticals app. Courtesy of Holywater Microdramas released on major platforms are increasingly being generated by AI, according to a new report from Owl & Co. Two-thirds of vertical drama releases outside China in the third quarter of 2026 from 20 top platforms were AI generated, according to the consulting firm’s latest “What We Watched on Vertical” report, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. Compare that with the the percentage of AI-generated stories released in the first quarter of the year (3 percent) and the second quarter (28 percent), and it’s clear that AI storytelling is increasingly dominating the sapce. The development echoes the format’s evolution in China, where microdramas were first popularized and where AI-generated titles have flooded the platforms in recent months. More than 95 percent of titles released in the first three months of 2026 in the country were reportedly made using AI. And it follows U.S. workers in the microdrama industry recently speaking out about the ways that the technology has reshaped the business. In September, workers in the industry told THR that they were observing fewer job opportunities as well as unscrupulous use of the technology on their work. The prevalence of AI in microdramas is reflected in the top-performing titles that Owl & Co. found for the latest quarter on apps that require viewers to pay for their stories. Only one live-action title — ReelShort’s My X-Ray Vision Sees Right Through You — broke the list of the top five highest-performing verticals in terms of minutes watched. And just two live-action titles ( My X-Ray Vision Sees Right Through You and ReelShort’s You’ve Been Replaced, First Love ) made the top 20. Top AI-generated titles, meanwhile, included the number-one best performer, ReelShort’s The Great and Powerful Genie , about a hot genie required by a wish to marry a woman for five years. It was followed by the popular DramaBox fantasy title Deny Me, Dragon King and another DramaBox dragon yarn, Married to the Hidden Dragon King . Overall, Owl & Co. found its tracked apps yielded 63 billion microdrama views in the third quarter and two billion viewing hours. TikTok‘s free PineDrama app was on the ascent, accounting for more than half of all views in the quarter. That’s notable, considering that PineDrama has been live for less than a year. The app is aggressively building its library, adding 15,501 new titles in the quarter, accounting for a more than 300 percent increase compared with the previous quarter. As for paid apps, DramaBox came out on top with 36 percent of views, followed by ReelShort with 29 percent, NetShort with 20 percent and DramaWave with 11 percent. All is not lost for human performance, however. Despite the prevalence of AI dramas in viewers’ feeds at the moment, the Owl & Co. report noted that China is already showing “a pullback towards live action.” The report’s dataset additionally found the number of stories featuring human performers growing alongside the increase of AI titles. And at ReelShort, “we observed live-action titles have a higher chance of remaining in the top 10 percent by views 30 days after release than AI titles,” the report stated. In other words, there is some early evidence that, long term, viewers may express more sustained interest in dramas portrayed by human actors rather than AI-generated performers. THR

articles.title: ‘Yaga’ Review: Carrie-Anne Moss and Hudson Williams in AMC+’s Intriguing but Undercooked Brew of Modern Crime and Ancient Folklore
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Angie Han Plus Icon Angie Han Television Critic ajhan Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Carrie-Anne Moss in ‘Yaga.’ Christopher Lawrence/Crave Perhaps it is only appropriate that Yaga , the new genre-bending thriller from AMC+ and Crave , should feel so devilishly difficult to pin down. After all, it’s only doing what myths have always done, which is transform — to reflect a new context, introduce a fresh perspective, impart an updated moral. And while it takes some time to see what shape this version of the Baba Yaga tale (as in Slavic folklore, not, as is explained by a couple different characters, the movie John Wick ) might take, it’s easy enough to fall under its spell at first. The atmosphere is deliciously chilly, the cast stuffed with actors you’ve loved in other things. But the longer it runs, the thinner its charms grow — leaving behind a show that’s enjoyable enough to binge, but not quite sharp enough to treasure. Related Stories TV 'Yaga' Cast Teases Timely Take on Female Rage, Double Hudson Williams and "A Lot of Chicken Stuff" TV AMC's 'Mayfair Witches: Salem Coven' Gets December Debut as Catherine Zeta-Jones, Carrie-Anne Moss Tease 'Kill Jackie' and 'Yaga' at NYCC Yaga The Bottom Line Plays hard to get. Airdate: Friday, Oct. 23 (AMC+) Cast: Carrie-Anne Moss, Clark Backo, Noah Reid, Hudson Williams, Sheila McCarthy Creator: Kat Sandler Adapted by Kat Sandler from her own play, Yaga opens at a point of uncertainty about whether there even is a mystery to be solved at all, though one presumes we would not all be gathered here if there were not. At some point in the last few days, Henry ( Hudson Williams ), the spoiled 22-year-old scion of a fish processing magnate, has disappeared from his giant mansion perched at the edge of a Canadian island. Well, maybe. Carson ( Clark Backo ), the no-nonsense Whittock PD detective assigned to the case, assumes he’s just out partying; even his dorkier doppelgänger of a roommate, Logan (also Williams), admits Henry’s prone to doing things like jet off to Paris on a last-minute romantic getaway. But there’s reason to suspect his absence has something to do with Katherine ( Carrie-Anne Moss ), a biology professor nicknamed the “Boner Beast” for rumors she sleeps with her students. Henry’s family are concerned enough to have sent in their own smarmy private investigator, Rapp ( Noah Reid ), though not quite concerned enough to cut short their own business trip to Japan. In any case, the kid must be found. As Carson and Rapp’s search for Henry deepens, Yaga cuts a jagged (though, at this point, well-trod by shows like Hulu’s Furious or even Netflix’s East of Eden ) path through themes of wealth, male entitlement, female rage and the purpose of myth. All of it flows toward a reconsideration of the legend of Baba Yaga herself, who bemoans her own malignment in raspy voiceovers that open and close each chapter. “I wonder why you tell stories of the wicked old witch when no one will stay and get to know me,” she complains. “I’m very funny, you know.” And she can be. One of Yaga ’s most potent assets is its tone: equal parts eerie and sexy and mischievous, with occasional flashes of lurid violence. You know a crime drama’s not going to take itself overly seriously when its version of a slick private dick is introduced tripping over his own feet immediately after an onlooker comments on how cool he looks. You know you’re in for something spookier than a run-of-the-mill kidnapping when dead birds, hallucinogenic concoctions and strange ancient symbols quickly become recurring motifs. And you know you’re in for something uneasily horny when our relatable point of entry into this seductive world, Carson, is first shown devouring “fairy smut” (i.e., a romantasy novel) on the job. In Yaga , even an explanation of something as dry as how ears work can sound suspiciously like dirty talk. “A whisper, a moan, a groan,” Katherine purrs, her voice as smooth as the whiskey in her glass. “Your bones listen. Before your brain understands, your bones say yes.” Armed with that unexpectedly playful tone and loaded with enough bizarre clues and creepy discoveries to keep up a brisk pace, Yaga ’s half-hour episodes (seven of eight were sent to critics) practically fly by; it’s the kind of show you can devour in a sitting without even meaning to do so. But it’s also one that starts to feel less substantive as its early promise gives way to uneven execution. While Sandler’s lack of preciousness about her own source material — she’s freely rearranged plot points and added characters, such that even those familiar with the original might be thrown for a few loops — saves Yaga from the airlessness so common to stage adaptations, her handling of the expanded scope isn’t quite so deft. Her cast help make up for some of the script’s thinness. Moss is the icy attention-grabber, turning the very quality Yaga points out should make her invisible — her maturity — into a nigh-irresistible source of sexual power; if there’s a single star turn that makes this whole experience worthwhile, it’s hers. In a more restrained role, Backo also acquits herself quite nicely, mapping out Carson’s interiority through the private, silent reactions she allows herself when she thinks no one’s looking. But while Williams demonstrates admirable range with his dual role as obnoxiously cocky Henry and uncomfortably withdrawn Logan, the characters get less screen time, and thus less depth, than one might hope. And though Reid does his best with the brazenly flirtatious, casually chauvinistic Rapp, Yaga badly overplays its hand with his womanizing. Unless there’s a last-minute reveal that the whole town has been dosed with a love potion, not even Reid’s considerable magnetism can justify the immediacy and intensity with which every single gal Rapp encounters practically throws her underwear at him. The coyness that initially seemed so enticing turns underwhelming as it becomes apparent that Yaga is better at suggesting hidden depths than excavating them, and gesturing at grand ideas than shining new light on them. Even the central question of what’s happened to Henry becomes less urgent the more time we spend in Whittock, among an insular cast of citizens who barely seem to notice the guy is missing, let alone care why. Yaga concocts one entertainingly heady brew, thanks to its beguiling mood and fearless cast. It’s just not, in the end, a fully satisfying one. THR

articles.title: Instagram Lines Up Donatella Versace, A$AP Rocky, Finneas, Chloé Zhao as This Year’s Creator Awards Judges (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 20, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Instagram Instagram is bringing its in-house creator awards program back for a second year: Instagram Rings. Rings will once again see an all-star panel of judges nominate and select winning creators from across the platform, spanning all types of genres and content, with the winners receiving a physical gold ring designed by Emily Adams Bode Aujla (who is also a judge) as well as special digital creative tools that they can use to distinguish their Instagram profiles. The Hollywood Reporter has learned that the 2026 Rings judges panel will include fashion icon Donatella Versace, A$AP Rocky, designer Emily Adams Bode Aujla, Finneas, director Chloé Zhao, professional skier Mikaela Shiffrin, artists OSGEMEOS, head of Instagram Adam Mosseri, dancer and choreographer Charm La’Donna, Instagram head of fashion partnerships Eva Chen, GQ editor-in-chief Will Welch, makeup artist Isamaya Ffrench, chef Vikas Khanna, and creator Jack Edwards. “We really wanted to have this like global mix of people who are moving culture forward in their respective fields and beyond,” Chen tells THR . “It’s people we think that are doing interesting things in the world as well as on Instagram, and who’ve charted their own course.” Chen says that the judges will be both nominating and selecting the winners, “I love watching the conversations where it’s like actors on actors, icons on icons, and that’s kind of the approach we took,” Chen says. “[The winners are] artists who are on their way to becoming iconic in their fields, chosen by like fellow icons, and so it’s not chosen by an algorithm, it is chosen by people in the fields and who are out there in the world who are discovering and inspired by like what their peers are doing on Instagram, and so the thing that we are not centering this around is follower count.” As for what changes the Rings program will in its second year, Chen says that they wanted to complement the physical ring with more of a digital presence, expanding beyonf the gold ring around their profile to include other things. And longer-term, Instagram wants to build an entire community around Rings, seeing as the honorees will be different year after year. Chen notes that the pool of winners will rise from 25 last year to 50 this year. “One of our goals for this program, is year-over-year for you to feel like you are part of this like community of people, and so to me, this program will be a success if a year one winner like strikes up a conversation with a year two winner, and they exchange numbers or they start DMing and they collab on something together,” Chen says. “That sense of connection and community is one of I think the goals for this program. Every year the pool is going to increase, and so hopefully with this year we’re able to start forging those connections and creating that sense of feeling of like you’re part of this group of people who have been recognized.” Instagram will announce this year’s Rings honorees later this month. THR

articles.title: Lin-Manuel Miranda’s ‘Warriors’ Sets Broadway Cast
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 5:30am PT Lin-Manuel Miranda’s ‘Warriors’ Sets Broadway Cast By Rebecca Rubin Plus Icon Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter rebeccaarubin Latest Lin-Manuel Miranda’s ‘Warriors’ Sets Broadway Cast 2 hours ago Box Office: ‘La Bola Negra’ Scores $277,500 From Four Theaters as Netflix Reports Grosses for First Time Ever 2 days ago Box Office: ‘You Can See Everything’ Stuns With $15 Million Debut, ‘Street Fighter’ Leads With $31 Million 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Alyssa Greenberg/WWD Lin-Manuel Miranda has announced the cast for his next Broadway venture, “ Warriors ,” which comes a decade after “Hamilton” became a pop culture sensation. The upcoming production, which opens in the spring, will star Jaci Calderon, Aneesa Folds, Amber Gray, Julia Harriman, Sasha Hutchings, Gizel Jiménez, Jasmine Cephas Jones, Kenita R. Miller, Sasha Allen, Casey Likes, and Donald Webber Jr. — several of whom have either worked on prior iterations of “Warriors” or appeared in Miranda’s other shows, “Hamilton” and “In the Heights. Additional cast members will be announced at a later date. Related Stories '14th,' 'You Can See Everything' and 'Once Upon a Time in Harlem' Lead Critics Choice Documentary Awards Nominations Nathan Fielder and Elizabeth Holmes Are This Year’s Ultimate Deep-Cut Halloween Costume Duo “Warriors” will begin previews at the Lunt-Fontanne Theatre on March 9 ahead of opening night on April 8. Popular on Variety “Warriors” features a book, music and lyrics by co-writers Miranda and Eisa Davis. Based on Sol Yurick’s 1965 novel and Paramount’s 1979 action film, “Warriors” follows a fictional New York gang from the Bronx to their home turf in Coney Island after they’re framed for the murder of a respected gang leader. The movie version of “Warriors” isn’t a musical, but it does feature songs by Barry De Vorzon, Joe Walsh and Arnold McCuller. The stage show originated as a 2024 concept album, executive produced by Nas and produced by musician Mike Elizondo. It featured the voices of Ms. Lauryn Hill, Busta Rhymes, Marc Anthony, Billy Porter, Ghostface Killah, RZA, Colman Domingo, Cam’ron, and Kim Dracula. “We’re having the time of our lives making ‘Warriors.’ It’s a rollercoaster like the Coney Island Cyclone, with all the action of Walter Hill’s classic film,” Miranda and Davis said in a statement. “It’s a New York story to the bone, with music steeped in all the genres that were born and revolutionized here, from hip-hop to salsa to ska and metal and everything in between. It’s an edge-of-your-seat journey from Brooklyn to the Bronx and back again. It’s a dream of a more peaceful city where we all come home alive. This is the sound of something being born.” “Warriors” will be directed by Jenny Koons and co-directed and choreographed by Andy Blankenbuehler, a Tony winner who worked with Miranda on “In the Heights” and “Hamilton.” Producers include Thomas Kail (“Hamilton”), Miranda and his father, Luis A. Miranda, Jr., and Jeffrey Seller. “Warriors” features scenic design by David Korins, costume design by Dede Ayite, lighting design by Natasha Katz, sound design by Jason Crystal, projection design by Hana S. Kim, fight direction by Drew Leary, music supervision by Kurt Crowley, and orchestrations by Kurt Crowley, Mike Elizondo and Scott Wasserman. articles.title: Prince Harry Opens Up About Move Back to England and Wanting to ‘Work It Out’ With King Charles and Prince William: ‘The Most Important Thing Is to Reconcile’
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 5:37am PT Prince Harry Opens Up About Move Back to England and Wanting to ‘Work It Out’ With King Charles and Prince William: ‘The Most Important Thing Is to Reconcile’ By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest LuckyChap International Hires Experienced Searchlight Exec Katie Goodson-Thomas as President of Film 1 hour ago Prince Harry Opens Up About Move Back to England and Wanting to ‘Work It Out’ With King Charles and Prince William: ‘The Most Important Thing Is to Reconcile’ 2 hours ago Emily Watson Joins ‘The Drive,’ Inspired by JFK Assassination, as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images Prince Harry says he wants to make peace with both his father and brother. Speaking in his first major interview since returning to the U.K. with his family earlier in the summer, the Duke of Sussex discussed his complicated and fractured relationship with King Charles and Prince William, claiming that he wanted to fix the much-publicized family rift. “Some people don’t want it to work out. I want it to work out. With everything else that’s going on in the world, the most important thing is to reconcile — that’s the key point,” he told GQ . “Scars stick around forever. But what your perception is, and what your mindset is to those things that have happened, letting go of the past. That’s something that I would encourage everybody to do: If there’s certain things from the past that are still affecting you every day, that’s harder to let go of. But, for me, there’s enough drama in the world and enough drama in people’s lives to continue with issues with family.” Related Stories Oscars: Rwanda Selects 'Ben'Imana' as First-Ever Entry to International Feature Race Amanda Seyfried Rejects Sex Scenes and Turned Down a TV Series Where 'I'd Have to Have Sex All the Time': I Don't Want to Be 'Naked With a Stranger' Harry raised eyebrows in August when it was revealed that he was moving back to the U.K. alongside his wife Meghan Markle and their two children after six years living in California. Unsurprisingly, numerous rumors spread as to why they were ditching life in the U.S. and returning home after their famed “Megxit” in 2020. Popular on Variety Speaking of his return to England and his relationship with the country after several tumultuous years spent dealing with the press (with whom he’s had several legal battles), Harry said his “attitude” had changed. “I think once you’ve been through it, once you’ve been able to talk about it, and raise awareness to it, then people see it for what it is, it makes the environment slightly easier. It’s not going to necessarily stop the behavior, but I think the behavior might — my hope that it will — change,” he said. “What happened back then was then. What’s happened over that over the last six years has been a continuation of that. Some battles that had been fought—and necessarily so. With everything else that’s going on in the world, there’s aspects of the past that I’m sure all of us — me, my family, and some of the British press—that we’d all like to leave behind us and work for the greater good.” Harry, who in the last few years has released a bestselling memoir that detailed his difficult family relationships, and front a Netflix docuseries that did the same, also told GQ that he’s been “really criticized” for telling his story. “I find it fascinating because everybody else is allowed to tell their version of my story, but God forbid I should be able to tell the other side of it.” Charlize Theron on ‘The Odyssey’ Becoming Universal’s Highest-Grossing Movie and Raising Millions to Fight Femicide in Africa With CTAOP Loading comments...

articles.title: LuckyChap International Hires Experienced Searchlight Exec Katie Goodson-Thomas as President of Film
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 6:00am PT LuckyChap International Hires Experienced Searchlight Exec Katie Goodson-Thomas as President of Film At Searchlight, Goodson-Thomas oversaw film including "The Favourite," "Poor Things," "Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri," "The Banshees of Inishirin" and "Wild Horse Nine" By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest LuckyChap International Hires Experienced Searchlight Exec Katie Goodson-Thomas as President of Film 1 hour ago Prince Harry Opens Up About Move Back to England and Wanting to ‘Work It Out’ With King Charles and Prince William: ‘The Most Important Thing Is to Reconcile’ 2 hours ago Emily Watson Joins ‘The Drive,’ Inspired by JFK Assassination, as Exec Producer (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Debbie Zhou LuckyChap International, the London-based joint venture between LuckyChap and Mediawan that was unveiled in late 2025, has given its filmmaking ambitions a shot in the arm with a significant new hire. Katie Goodson-Thomas , a hugely respected and experienced exec who has spent more than a decade at Searchlight Pictures , is set to leave the studio to join the LuckyChap International team in the new role of president of film. Related Stories Laika Submits Original Song From 'Wildwood' for Oscars, 'The Better Part of Bravery,' Performed by The Decemberists (EXCLUSIVE) Oscars: Rwanda Selects 'Ben'Imana' as First-Ever Entry to International Feature Race Working in close partnership with co-managing directors Mona Qureshi and Tanya Qureshi, who joined earlier this year, Goodson-Thomas will spearhead the film slate, with the LuckyChap International leadership trio working in collaboration with LuckyChap partners Margot Robbie, Tom Ackerley, Josey McNamara and Milan Popelka, alongside the broader U.S. team. Popular on Variety At Searchlight, where she was most recently executive vice president, co-head of production and development, Goodson-Thomas played a key role in expanding the studio’s U.K. presence, overseeing numerous award-winning films such as Yorgos Lanthimos’ “The Favourite” and “Poor Things,” Martin McDonagh’s “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri,” “The Banshees of Inisherin” and the upcoming “Wild Horse Nine,” as well as “All of Us Strangers,” “The Roses” and Alice Birch’s forthcoming directorial debut “Sweetsick,” starring Cate Blanchett. “We’re thrilled to welcome Katie to LuckyChap International,” said Mona Qureshi and Tanya Qureshi. “Her career embodies the kind of independent spirit and big-heartedness that inspires us, and her ambition, taste and creative instinct make her a natural fit for what we are building. We can’t wait to have her alongside us as a fellow journeywoman!” Added Goodson-Thomas: “The LuckyChap team has exceptional taste, fearlessness and a creative identity entirely its own, as well as an infectious sense of possibility about what the company can achieve. Searchlight has been such an incredible creative home for me that I always knew it would take somewhere truly special to tempt me away. The opportunity to join that alongside Mona, Tanya and such a brilliant team was simply too exciting to resist. The U.K. and Europe are full of remarkable talent, and I’m hugely ambitious about what we can find, back and get made together.” Goodson-Thomas will officially join LuckyChap International in the new year. “We’re in awe of everything Katie has accomplished throughout her career, and we all feel extraordinarily privileged that she is bringing her undeniable creative talents, vision and depth of experience to LuckyChap International,” said LuckyChap’s US partners Robbie, Ackerley, McNamara and Popelka. “She’s such a kindred spirit culturally, and we’ve long admired her ability to spot exceptional filmmaking talent and champion their projects from the very beginning all the way through. We genuinely couldn’t be more excited to have her join us on this adventure, and to forge a killer slate together that we can all be incredibly proud of!” Added Searchlight president Matthew Greenfield: “Katie has been a wonderful colleague all of these years and LuckyChap International is getting an exceptional and passionate advocate for filmmakers. We couldn’t be happier for her as she takes on this next chapter, and we’re excited to see all that she and the team will accomplish together.” Charlize Theron on ‘The Odyssey’ Becoming Universal’s Highest-Grossing Movie and Raising Millions to Fight Femicide in Africa With CTAOP Loading comments...

articles.title: Hulu’s Mother-Son Mystery ‘Phony’ Mutes Connie Britton’s Charisma Under Visual Effects: TV Review
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 6:15am PT Hulu’s Mother-Son Mystery ‘Phony’ Mutes Connie Britton’s Charisma Under Visual Effects: TV Review By Alison Herman Plus Icon Alison Herman TV Critic aherman2006 Latest For the Love of Television, Please Watch ‘The Lowdown’ Season 2: TV Review 6 days ago Like Its Hero, Marvel’s ‘VisionQuest’ Struggles to Connect Emotionally: TV Review 1 week ago ‘Avatar: Seven Havens’ Takes the Franchise in an Intriguing, Postapocalyptic New Direction: TV Review 2 weeks ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Hulu It’s a shame Hulu shared only half the first season of the streamer’s new comedy-mystery series “ Phony ” with critics in advance, because so much depends on how the show resolves its central source of suspense. The premise is what one character calls a “reverse cuckoo situation,” or at least a potential one: When Sonny (Sam Nivola), a high-school student in the Pacific Northwest, gets into a nasty car crash, he wakes up a week later to a surreal nightmare. His mother, Ellen ( Connie Britton ), has been replaced by someone else, and nobody around him seems to notice. Is he crazy, or is everyone else blind? Related Stories Oscars: Syria Selects Doc 'The Other Side of the Sun' for International Feature Race, Marking First Entry Since Fall of Assad Regime Oscar Predictions: Best Original Screenplay — 'Club Kid' and 'Josephine' Lead a Field of Personal, Timely Stories At first, “Phony” creator Nick Paley, who directed half the season and penned the first couple of episodes, plays into the ambiguity of Sonny’s possible delusion. Obviously, a child who recently suffered a serious head trauma is far from a reliable narrator, and in the premiere, Paley leans into the subjectivity with distorted sound and imagery. When the camera inhabits Sonny’s point of view, as it does almost constantly in the beginning, Ellen does, in fact, look different: thanks to the magic of visual effects, Britton’s eyebrows, nose and other features are all subtly altered, and the changes played up with side-by-side comparisons. Popular on Variety The distortions are especially striking given the actor’s pre-existing place in the pantheon of TV moms. (Britton also serves as an executive producer here.) Ellen is also the principal of Sonny’s high school, and a warm-but-firm educator naturally evokes Tami Taylor, even if Oregon is thousands of miles and metaphorical light-years away from West Texas. Subtly tweaking Britton’s face and voice is effectively uncanny, because viewers have such a deep knowledge of her mannerisms from “Friday Night Lights” and other shows. But for “Phony,” depriving itself of Britton’s full expressive powers cuts both ways. We’re supposed to feel their absence, and do. And yet when it comes to understanding Sonny and Ellen’s relationship, particularly while we don’t understand what actually happened to Ellen and why, the audience is met with just that: an absence. Before the crash, we get a few scenes that establish the status quo of Ellen and Sonny’s relationship. As a single mom and her only child, they’re a tightly knit pair, with Ellen respectful yet wary of Sonny’s growing autonomy. Not that Sonny knows what to do with that independence: He’s an inveterate people-pleaser, insistently upbeat in a way his peers know is “a little full of shit” but unable to stop himself from adapting to suit whoever’s in front of him. Ellen and Sonny’s maybe-final fight goes down when she finds the sex toy he bought in anticipation of sleeping with his girlfriend Chloe (Mahaela Park), because he thinks that’s what he’s supposed to do. Given that so much about Ellen (or is it “Ellen”?) is physically and figuratively obscured, Nivola — Britton’s fellow “The White Lotus” alum, though the two appeared on separate seasons — ends up shouldering the lion’s share of the show. He’s up to the task, giving Sonny a sweetly nervous energy and even some slapstick as he runs around in search of the truth. The tone of “Phony” is lighter and more comedic than one would expect of the horror-adjacent premise, if reflective of Paley’s CV, which includes credits for co-writing “Marcel the Shell with Shoes On” and directing on “Broad City.” Episodes are a zippy half-hour, and unfold in a world where a teen spotting a corpse in the woods is an occasion for a “dead body party” with a massage line. With its evergreen forests and ominous shots of beavers subbing in for owls, “Twin Peaks” is a clear influence, but the predominant vibe is less eerie than benignly kooky. Too insecure to confide in Chloe or his best friend Vogel (Maliq Johnson), Sonny instead finds investigative partners in cousins Mallory (Grace Brennan) and Weldon (Colter Lee), social outcasts — she’s an ex-homeschooler from an evangelical family, he’s just a weirdo — who prove open to his theories. A sympathetic ear is always nice, but the trio doesn’t accomplish much in the season’s first half besides hiring Sharla (Meera Syal), a “private investigator” whose chief qualification is her enthusiastic posts in conspiracy forums. “Phony” nonetheless starts offering hints that Sonny may be onto something. Circumstantial evidence (this Ellen doesn’t return Sonny’s customary triple squeeze) gives way to more objective indicators. Even in scenes outside Sonny’s perspective, Ellen still looks like not-quite-Connie Britton, fielding suspicious phone calls and making covert trips to the bank. “Phony” probably couldn’t draw out the question of whether Sonny is imagining things or not for eight entire episodes, but by the point the screeners stopped, the show is in an awkward lull: too far in to be intriguingly open-ended, not far in enough to judge the journey by its destination. Without knowing not-Ellen’s origins, MO or motivations (or what happened to actual Ellen!), it’s hard to tell what “Phony” is even about, and therefore how well it executes a self-assigned brief. Is the show a coming-of-age story about Sonny learning to listen to his instincts? Is it a family story about how adolescence turns parents and kids into strangers? Is it something much weirder altogether? “Phony” provokes a mild curiosity, rather than a burning urgency, to find out which. Partially handicapping Britton turns out to be a big sacrifice. The first two episodes of “Phony” are now streaming on Hulu, with new episodes airing weekly on Tuesdays. articles.title: BBC Three Among Linear Services Set to Close as Broadcaster Looks for Savings
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 6:20am PT BBC Three Among Linear Services Set to Close as Broadcaster Looks for Savings By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest BBC Three Among Linear Services Set to Close as Broadcaster Looks for Savings 29 minutes ago Merged Banijay, All3Media Entity Sets Top Brass Comprised of Banijay Execs 6 hours ago ‘Slow Horses’ Season 7 Taps ‘The Other Bennet Sister’ Star Varada Sethu, ‘Mank’s’ Tuppence Middleton 24 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Getty Images The BBC has confirmed it will shut down a host of linear broadcast services next year. Among those impacted are BBC Three, BBC Scotland and BBC Radio 4 Extra. The decision was made as the beleaguered corporation seeks to make cuts across the board in a bit to save £500 million by 2028. “We need to make every pound work harder for audiences as we respond to the immediate cost pressures and reinvent the BBC for a changing world,” said BBC director-general Matt Brittin. “We all know that means tough choices.” Related Stories Ava DuVernay’s Doc ‘14th’ to Submit New Original Song by Brittany Howard and Robert Glasper for Oscars Consideration (EXCLUSIVE) Why 'You Can See Everything' Could Make Oscars History as First Doc Nominated for Best Picture “Much of the great content they currently carry will still be found where audiences already enjoy it on iPlayer and Sounds,” he said specifically of the shuttering linear services. “While this follows media speculation, I recognise the confirmation of this news will be hard for audiences and colleagues.” Popular on Variety Content from BBC Scotland, BBC Three and Radio 4 Extra will still be available digitally, via iPlayer, BBC Sounds and YouTube. BBC Scotland will also continue as a standalone channel on iPlayer while some of its content will be available on local broadcasts of BBC One and BBC Two. News director Rachel Jupp will also be making changes within the BBC News division. In response to the news, Directors U.K. CEO Andy Harrower, said: “The removal of BBC Three and BBC Scotland from linear broadcast must not lead to a reduction in the number or range of programmes commissioned for their audiences. For many directors, commissions on BBC Three and BBC Scotland provide essential opportunities for them to develop their craft, take creative risks and progress towards larger productions.” “Directors U.K. is therefore calling on the BBC to guarantee that these changes will not reduce the volume or breadth of commissioning, or opportunities behind the camera. articles.title: Meet Kate DePetro, Fox News’ Social-Media Ambassador to Younger Viewers
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 6:30am PT Meet Kate DePetro, Fox News’ Social-Media Ambassador to Younger Viewers By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Meet Kate DePetro, Fox News’ Social-Media Ambassador to Younger Viewers 34 minutes ago ‘Star Wars’ Comes to 2027 Super Bowl With Animated ‘Alterna-Cast’ for Disney Channel, XD, Disney+ 12 hours ago Christiane Amanpour to Exit CNN in June After 43 Years in TV News 23 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Fox News Media Aficionados of Fox News may not know Kate DePetro as well as they do mainstays like Harris Faulkner, Sean Hannity or Bret Baier. Give them some time. Fox News Media has hired DePetro, a former production assistant, for a new role that may prove to be extremely important to the cable-news mainstay as it seeks broader audiences beyond its traditional TV connections. DePetro will serve as a sort of in-house creator, developing original content and programming aimed at offering a behind-the-scenes look at the goings-on at Fox News Channel , Fox Business Network, Fox Nation, and other properties that are part of the Fox Corp. unit. DePetro will appear primarily on Fox News Now, a social-media platform that launched in June to help forge connections between viewers and Fox News shows and figures. Related Stories ‘You Can See Everything’ Sets Oscar Campaigns for Best Picture, Supporting Actress and More Categories Amanda Seyfried Rejects Sex Scenes and Turned Down a TV Series Where 'I'd Have to Have Sex All the Time': I Don't Want to Be 'Naked With a Stranger' “I’ll have the opportunity to create original content, introduce audiences to familiar faces in a more personal way and share experiences across Fox News Media platforms,” DePetro says in a statement provided via email. “It’s a dream opportunity and I can’t wait to get started.” Popular on Variety Like other TV networks, Fox News Channel is paying more attention to the younger viewers who don’t rely on cable subscriptions for news, information and entertainment. Executives at Fox, for example, have noticed that Fox News has proven a popular option on Fox One, the streaming subscription service that was originally intended as a way to get Fox Sports in front of the digital generation. And Fox News has seen its audience on TikTok, which stood at around 25,000 followers in 2024, rise to 12.2 million as of October of this year. DePetro is “kind of like the ultimate insider,” says David Eccleston, Fox News Media’s senior vice president of brand strategy and consumer experience, during a recent interview. Many of the company’s top personalities have come to interact with her during her five years with the company, he says, and “know who she is and trust what she is about.” Elevating DePetro, who recently worked as an assistant to Dana Perino , the daytime anchor and panelist on “The Five,” spotlights the growing affinity younger viewers have for so-called “creators ” and other figures who find connections on social and digital media platforms. One-fifth of U.S. adults regularly get news on TikTok, according to a Pew Research Center survey from August, 2026 — a statistic that is the same as in 2025 but up from a mere 3% in 2020. Pew also recently found that the share of Americans who say they prefer to get news from television decreased to 28% in 2026 from 34% in 2025, while the share who prefer to get news from social media increased to 19% from 14% in that same time period. Fox News has been paying more attention to creators , podcasters and digital experts. The company’s alliance with the conservative “Ruthless” podcast, for example, continues to expand. On Election Night, “Ruthless” will host a three-hour livestream from a Washington, D.C. bar, airing between 8 p.m. and 11 p.m. eastern on both Fox Nation and Fox News Digital. Brett Cooper, who gained a profile with a YouTube show from The Daily Wire, is now a Fox News contributor who also leads her own digital program via Fox Corp. sibling Red Seat Ventures. Sports-TV powerhouse ESPN has also tapped young, digital savants in a bid to find younger audiences. The Disney sports-media outlet hired Omar Raja, creator of the popular “House of Highlights” account on Instagram in 2020. Since that time, he has even made appearances on ABC’s pre-Oscars red carpet show. Katie Feeney, who developed her own popular sports-focused social-media accounts while in college, joined ESPN in 2025. “There is definitely an opportunity to reach a new audience” for Fox News’ properties, says Eccleston. “We know we can do that on digital and social.” DePetro knows how to get behind the scenes at Fox News because she has worked there. She logged stints as an overnight production assistant for “Fox & Friends,” and later helped supervise the show’s green room, where guests and personalities stay until the time arrives to go on air. As part of her job, she has met athletes, entertainers and world leaders. DePetro met Fox News’ Perino in the green room after reading the anchor’s book, “Everything Will Be Okay.” After a mentoring session, Perino offered her a position as her assistant. Over two years, DePetro helped Perino build a presence on social media. Perino has “been an incredible mentor, advocate and friend who saw something in me before I saw it in myself,” says DePetro. DePetro will juggle other tasks as well. She is also working on “The Vow,” a Fox Nation dating series hosted by Chris Harrison, who once led “The Bachelor” on ABC. She is also the co-founder of Pizza to Pews, an initiative that encourages young people across the country to come to church and make friends. Her new role is aimed at helping Fox News create new bonds as well. l. articles.title: Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 6:30am PT Guillermo del Toro Tears Up as He Says ‘We’re Handing Down a World in Ruins’: ‘It Pains Me Deeply to See Three Generations Fail the Next’ Guillermo del Toro, at the 24th Morelia Film Festival to present the 3D re-Release of his Oscar-winning “Pan’s Labyrinth,” Del Toro reflected on the 20 years that have passed since his anti-fascist fable was first released By Anna Marie de la Fuente Plus Icon Anna Marie de la Fuente @adelafuente1 Latest ‘Leap Year’ Director Michael Rowe’s Cross Border Drama ‘Last Weekend’ Boarded by Mexico’s Paloma Negra 19 hours ago Caos Cine, a New Mexican Distributor, Launches at Morelia Fest With ‘The Huntress,’ Picked Up From Edher Campos and Gabriela Maire’s Zafiro (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Apichatpong Weerasethakul’s ‘Jengira’s Magnificent Dream,’ With Tilda Swinton, Boarded by ‘Triangle of Sadness’ Mexican Co-Producer Piano 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source (l-r) Daniela Michel, Guillermo del Toro, UNAM's Jorge Martínez Micher and Hugo Alejandro Concha. Courtesy of the Morelia Film Festival Mexico’s beloved Guillermo del Toro descended on the 24 th Morelia Film Festival like the rockstar he is, greeted by hordes of shrieking fans that impressed even the most jaded in the crowd. In town to present the much-anticipated 3D Re-Release of “Pan’s Labyrinth,” he was everywhere all at once, holding a masterclass where tickets were as elusive as a seat at Cannes that went on for nearly three hours and a free-wheeling press conference that extended past its time limit. Related Stories Andrew Garfield Could Win an Oscar for 'Artificial' and His Norman Bates-Inspired Turn as Sam Altman Oscars: Pakistan Selects Documentary 'Hanging by a Wire' for International Feature Race (EXCLUSIVE) It was his third time at the fest, 20 years after his multi-Oscar winning “Pan’s Labyrinth’ first played there and years later with his 2018 best picture Academy Award winner “The Shape of Water.” Popular on Variety Before the presser kicked off, Del Toro, an Honorary Doctorate recipient from the National Autonomous University of Mexico (UNAM), received the Filmoteca UNAM Medal, an honor also bestowed on Alfonso Cuarón, in town to support his son Jonas Cuarón’s opening night film, “Campeón Gabacho,” which he produced. Alongside Del Toro were festival director Daniela Michel, “Pan’s Labyrinth” producer Bertha Navarro, his then young lead Ivana Baquero and DP Guillermo Navarro, who took home the cinematography Oscar for his stunning work on the anti-fascist fable. Reflecting on a question posed midway through the press conference about what has stayed the same and what has changed over the 20 years since “Pan’s Labyrinth,” del Toro responded with tears. “The state of our species and society today goes beyond anything we could have imagined back then. But I recognize the same sadness and despair. It pains me deeply to see one, two, or three generations fail the next. We’re handing down a world in ruins, morally, socially and spiritually fractured, with the very fabric that once allowed us to tell fables and parables falling apart.” Asked whether he knew beforehand if “Pan’s Labyrinth” would be well received, Del Toro recounted how his collaborations with both Navarros sustained him through all the challenges they faced. “We embarked on an adventure that was financially horrifying but cinematically beautiful,” he said. “You never know how a film will be received. We only found out when we screened it for the first time at Cannes. We got that famous standing ovation that lasted more than 22 minutes, and from that moment on, everything changed. It changed our lives.” “I think ‘Pan’s Labyrinth’ marked a before and after for me. In terms of creative freedom, possibilities and everything else, I’m where I am today because of that film. But none of it would have been possible without the faith of my immediate family, Bertha and Guillermo.” Said DP Navarro: “Guillermo and I share the belief that cinematic language is storytelling through images that convey emotion and narrative. ‘Pan’s Labyrinth’ is the ultimate expression of that. The camera is constantly searching, discovering and communicating.” “It was also an incredibly difficult shoot. We had a limited budget, had to find unconventional solutions and took risks that could easily have failed. But we gambled and we won. Without a doubt, it’s my best film, and I hold that experience close to my heart. I hope new generations will continue to discover and appreciate it. And now, 20 years later, it returns. Olé!” Producer Navarro, who also backed Del Toro’s career-launching feature debut “Cronos” and his much-lauded “The Devil’s Backbone,” said: “When he gave me the screenplay for ‘Cronos,’ I was absolutely fascinated. Talent shines, and you have to know how to recognize that light. That’s what I saw in Guillermo.” “It’s been an incredible privilege to have made those three great films with Guillermo. I’ve produced many films throughout my life, but those three hold a much deeper significance for me. They changed my life.” Baquero concurred: “’Pan’s Labyrinth’ undoubtedly opened doors for me, both into the genre and in my career. We’ve talked this afternoon about how much the film changed our lives, professionally and personally. For me, acting went from being a hobby – I had worked before ‘Pan’s Labyrinth’ – to becoming my profession. Without that film, I might not be here today. It unquestionably marked a turning point in my career.” Reflecting on its impact on young audiences. Del Toro noted: “There’s an urgency and a fragility and ferocity that coexist in ‘Pan’s Labyrinth.’ And somehow, I think it’s an urgent moment to speak, for the film to speak to a new audience.” Local politics also crept into the conference, with a journalist asking him what he would say to the young people protesting in his hometown of Guadalajara over its current issues of contaminated water, repression and the alleged kidnapping of protesters on Oct. 11. He responded: “This morning at my masterclass, I gave young people the floor to speak about these issues. It’s terrifying that something so fundamental should have to be fought for instead of being resolved through basic humanity and responsible leadership.” “I said it clearly: “Their voices must be heard, and I stand with them 100%. It’s unacceptable that this remains unresolved or that anyone would try to silence them. Speaking out, protesting, and demanding a solution are fundamental rights – anytime, anywhere.” The Morelia Film Festival began on Oct. 16 and wraps Oct. 25. articles.title: Palestinian Filmmaker Rakan Mayasi on His Search for Unconventional Stories and Portraying ‘Communities That Have Not Been on Film Before’
articles.full_text: Oct 20, 2026 6:31am PT Palestinian Filmmaker Rakan Mayasi on His Search for Unconventional Stories and Portraying ‘Communities That Have Not Been on Film Before’ By Jay Weissberg Plus Icon Jay Weissberg Latest Palestinian Filmmaker Rakan Mayasi on His Search for Unconventional Stories and Portraying ‘Communities That Have Not Been on Film Before’ 31 minutes ago ‘Safe Exit’ Director Mohammed Hammad on Staying True to His Vision: ‘I Need to Be Free as a Filmmaker’ 4 days ago ‘Back to Buenos Aires’ Review: Marco Bechis’ Return to the Screen Covers Similar Ground to Earlier Works but is Only Fitfully Effective 1 month ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Atata and Rakan Mayasi Iconoclastic Palestinian filmmaker Rakan Mayasi ’s debut feature “ Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep ” made a splash in this year’s Un Certain Regard in Cannes with its powerful, poetic treatment of a Bedouin community in Lebanon’s Bekaa Valley. This week it plays in a competition slot at the El Gouna Film Festival , where Variety spoke to the director. Inspired by Mayasi’s grandmother, it’s a story of two women who become pawns in a tribal blood feud, played out in a visionary style that owes much to Mayasi’s mentor Abbas Kiarostami, yet has its own rhythm and sensorial, at times almost feverish, point of view. Following its Cannes premiere the film has been warmly received at other festivals, and will be screening at Montpellier’s CineMed followed immediately by the Rome Film Festival, in their Best First Feature section. International sales are being handled by Salaud Morisset . Popular on Variety Related Stories Pedro Pascal in 'Behemoth!': The Oscar-Worthy Role That He (and Latinos) Have Been Waiting For Oscars: Pakistan Selects Documentary 'Hanging by a Wire' for International Feature Race (EXCLUSIVE) The film has several exceptional set pieces: it opens with a car in flames, in the middle there’s a stunningly hallucinatory wedding sequence, and it ends with an evocative longshot that plays with visual space. When you and your cinematographer Pôl Seif were conceiving the film, did you have these already in mind? Some of it was already set and ready in our minds. Some of it, no. For example, for sure the fire, it was there since the beginning. I’m interested in metaphors and how to translate that visually, so with Pôl we had the idea that we zoom in so you feel that the car is getting closer to you and the fire is spreading. We were trying to translate what the metaphor could possibly look like. Whereas the end was rewritten, by the two of us, because it’s a very visual scene. So we blocked it again three days before the shoot ended, and we rewrote it entirely. The wedding scene has been singled out by many critics for its visual beauty and the emotional shift it conveys. In that scene I allowed myself to get out of the narrative, so to speak, to change the rhythm and play with a kind of psychedelic approach. It’s never really stated that this was the actual wedding, and when the one sister, Jawahir, is revealed as a bride, it is very theatrical. The idea was kind of like zooming into her subconscious, into her imagination of a celebration. It allowed me to play around. For example, the whole scene was improvised. I never met any of these dancers before. We made a call for the biggest number of people to join, and we were very lucky because a lot of people came and they were very, very energetic. My job was to just have a microphone and make them more energetic. The scene also allows the community to be seen in a more three-dimensional light. The idea was to juxtapose two emotions and then make the audience feel guilty afterwards. I want to enjoy watching this pleasing, psychedelically shot dance sequence, but then afterwards I will ask myself, what the fuck did I just watch and why did I enjoy that? This was the idea. Is that something that you enjoy in film in general? Do you like that idea of sort of thinking, what the fuck did I just watch? Yes! My next film will be entirely like this. Speaking of things that are unexpected, we’re used to a particular kind of Lebanese cinema that deals primarily with the Civil War and subsequent crises. Yet you’ve chosen something completely different. You’ve gone into the Bekaa Valley and focused on a community that probably hasn’t been seen before in a feature film. I don’t like formulaic films. I don’t like the way we are seen outside, with every film having to talk about the Civil War, or the post-Civil War. I want to go to communities that have not been on film before, mainly because there’s much more depth in plots and characters and life there. This is why I wanted to work with non-professional actors. I could have gotten actors and put them in there in this context, but I prefer not to because this fragile authenticity has to be kept. Also, don’t forget that I’m Palestinian. I lived in Lebanon 20 years, and though I don’t have Lebanese nationality, I also feel Lebanese somehow because I became a filmmaker in Lebanon. But I don’t like the mainstream, so to speak. I like to dig in and see much more into life, basically. Is your next project also set in Lebanon? Half of it happens in Gaza. It was supposed to be my first feature, but it’s a dark comedy, so I had to stop it when the Israeli genocide began in Palestine. Now I’m returning to it a bit slowly; it’s an absurdist, deadpan dark comedy, very different from “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep.” It’s more staged, in a more controlled environment. And it’s about life and death. and the bureaucracy of life, basically. It’s called “The Passport” and I’m in late development/early pre-production. May Odeh, who’s associate producer on “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep,” is producing that film. What’s next for “Yesterday the Eye Didn’t Sleep”? After Cannes, it was selected in 50 festivals, which is fantastic, and it’s doing quite well at the festival circuit. I’m doing a tour of eight festivals in October, including Rome, the Viennale, Valladolid and in Bucharest, Cristian Mungiu’s Cannes Reprise. It will also be in Geneva in early November.
