articles.title: Omar Sy on Taking Creative Control of Netflix’s ‘Lupin’ and Why ‘Black Dumas’ Will Spark Political Debate in France
articles.full_text: Oct 16, 2026 5:22am PT Omar Sy on Taking Creative Control of Netflix’s ‘Lupin’ and Why ‘Black Dumas’ Will Spark Political Debate in France By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest Omar Sy on Taking Creative Control of Netflix’s ‘Lupin’ and Why ‘Black Dumas’ Will Spark Political Debate in France 1 hour ago YouTube’s Virtues, Industry Consolidation, Christie Brinkley and ‘Baywatch’: Trends and Themes From a Busy Mipcom 1 day ago Mediawan’s Pierre-Antoine Capton on Buying Reese Witherspoon’s Hello Sunshine and Doubling Down on Hollywood Amid Consolidation (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Selly Sy/Netflix Netflix ‘s smash hit heist series “ Lupin ” is back bigger and bolder after three years, and its French star Omar Sy , who plays French gentleman thief Assane Diop, has something to do with it. Sy, who served as artistic producer on previous installments, makes his debut as co-showrunner alongside Louis Leterrier for the show’s fourth part, on top of co-producing it through their joint banner Carrousel Studios. Related Stories Trump Says Execution of Fort Hood Shooter by Firing Squad Will Not Be Livestreamed Judge Extends Block on Trump's White House Ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico Speaking in an interview with Variety ahead of the Oct. 23 launch, Sy revealed he made greater creative control a condition of his return on the show. Popular on Variety “There were quite a few moments in previous seasons when I felt frustrated because things I wanted didn’t necessarily end up on screen. So my condition for continuing was that I would have a little more say in the decisions. They gave me that role, and it allowed me to change things,” Sy said during the zoom interview, sitting against a red backdrop of “Lupin” featuring an animated silhouette of Diop and the Eiffel Tower. The new season picks up four years after the events of Part 3, with Assane behind bars before finding himself targeted by a mysterious copycat who pulls off a string of elaborate heists in his name. With a bigger budget from Netflix, Sy and Leterrier leaned further into the show’s superhero-like qualities, expanding its universe beyond the novels of Maurice Leblanc and weaving some futuristic elements. “We’re moving a little further away from Maurice Leblanc…. We brought it more into our own universe,” said Sy. “That’s why we’re going further into the prison setting, introducing new technologies and all these different elements. We’re embracing modernity, whether it’s through the prison itself or all the technology that the copycat uses to trap Assane.” Emmanuel Guimier/Netflix The challenge, Sy says, was to preserve what made “Lupin” a global hit while making the new season feel fresh enough to draw in viewers who have never watched the series. The new role also allowed Sy to bring in rising French actor Théo Christine and explore more emotional side of Assane’s story, Sy, who’s currently shooting Bradley Cooper’s Ocean prequel alongside Margot Robbie, has carved out a career in Hollywood and in European cinema, often serving as a producer on projects exploring social and political issues. He starred in and produced Mathieu Vadepied’s “Father & Soldier,” which shed light on the largely overlooked history of Senegalese soldiers who fought for France during WWI. His upcoming French projects include Ladj Ly’s “Dumas: Diable Noir” (“Black Dumas”), which reunites him with Christine and tells the story of Thomas-Alexandre Dumas, the formerly enslaved man who became France’s first Black general and whose son would go on to become one of the country’s most celebrated writers. Slated for release in October 2027, “Black Dumas” will arrive just months after France’s presidential election, which is shaping up to be one of the country’s most divisive in decades, with the far right leading polls and political tensions running high. “One thing I’m sure of is that ‘Dumas’ is going to generate a lot of debate and discussion,” said Sy, who’s lived in Los Angeles for years but still votes in France. “We need conversations right now. I just hope they can be calm, thoughtful conversations rather than heated ones.” While he had broken through with his first leading role in the French comedy “Intouchables,” it’s his part as Assane Diop in “Lupin” which turned Sy into an international star in 2021. Like “Emily in Paris,” “Lupin” has contributed to boosting tourism in the French capital, and has been hugely successful internationally on Netflix, although the latter has even more merit, being in French. You’re co-showrunner on this season. What made you want to get more involved creatively, and how did that change the way you worked on the series? The truth is, I’ve been involved in the same way from the very beginning. My involvement hasn’t changed. I’ve always been part of all the conversations, from the first to the last. The difference is that before, I was allowed to participate and make suggestions, but I couldn’t make the decisions or necessarily see those ideas through. There were quite a few moments in previous seasons when I felt frustrated because things I wanted didn’t necessarily end up on screen. So my condition for continuing was that I would have a little more say in the decisions. They gave me that role, and it allowed me to change things. For example, bringing in Théo Christine was something we wanted to do, and we went after him. There are decisions like that which might seem quite radical but can take the show somewhere different. That’s what this new role has allowed me to do. But in terms of my involvement, it’s been the same from the start. I just have a little more decision-making power now. Emmanuel Guimier/Netflix I found the father-son relationship with Théo Christine in the first episode incredibly moving. You also worked together with this young actor on Ladj Ly’s “Dumas: Diable Noir,” didn’t you? What’s funny is that actually happened afterward. We approached Théo for “Lupin,” and he said yes. Then, while we were working on the series, he got the role in “Dumas.” The first episode feels more dramatic than previous seasons, especially with the father-son relationship. Was that something you particularly wanted to explore? What’s great about this series is that you have a bit of everything. There’s drama, but there’s also comedy, lighter moments, flamboyant characters and all the action that comes with it. It’s really a place where you can put so many different things. That’s why I always say that “Lupin” is my favorite toy. You can turn it in every direction, you can do all sorts of things in the same universe and with the same character. Were you also interested in exploring the prison setting more extensively this season? Yes, because ultimately we’re dealing with a thief, and prison is part of that world. It’s something we hadn’t really explored before. In the first season, there’s a short sequence where he’s in prison, and we also touch on that world through his father, but we’d never really gone into it in depth. This time, we wanted to explore it further, and we also filmed it a little differently. The prison almost has a futuristic, science-fiction quality. It feels quite stylized. We brought it more into our own universe. That’s really what this season does. We’re fully embracing the world we’ve created. That’s why we’re going further into the prison setting, introducing new technologies and all these different elements. We’re moving a little further away from Maurice Leblanc and bringing more of our own ideas into it. We’re embracing modernity, whether it’s through the prison itself or all the technology that the copycat uses to trap Assane. The production looks bigger and more ambitious. Did you have a significantly larger budget this time? We definitely had more resources. And we have to acknowledge that, because Netflix would be very upset if we said otherwise! They gave us the means to make this season, and it was important to us that you could see and feel that on screen. There’s almost a superhero quality to this season, particularly with the idea of Lupin versus Lupin. It feels a little like a Marvel movie. Yes, but actually, when I say we’re moving away from Maurice Leblanc, that’s one area where we’re not. He did that several times himself. He brought in Sherlock Holmes, and at one point Lupin even faces another Lupin. Maurice Leblanc had already done that. I think it’s Marvel that copied Maurice Leblanc! But seriously, from the very beginning, when we decided to bring Lupin back and make this series, that’s how we imagined the character. Louis [Leterrier] decided to film him using those codes. That’s why his coat is like a cape. We really conceived this character as a superhero. It’s also why you have those shots of him on the rooftops of Paris, with his silhouette against the skyline, almost like a shadow. That superhero dimension has always been part of our vision of the character, and we fully embrace it. I’ve only seen the first episode, but I already suspect that Assane’s best friend might have something to do with what’s going on. Is betrayal one of the central themes of this season? With “Lupin,” there’s always betrayal somewhere. It’s a battle of wits, a game of intelligence, and we need those twists. Very often, betrayal is part of that. One of the things I love about this series is that we established something in the first season that continues to work today: speculation. Everyone is trying to figure out who’s behind everything. It’s like a game of Cluedo, trying to guess who the killer is. I love that. It’s one of my favorite aspects of the series. That whole whodunit element is something we deliberately work on. It’s part of the pleasure of “Lupin,” both for us and for the audience. I feel that quite a few films and series have tried to copy “Lupin” in recent years. I’m not the one saying it! You said it, not me! Has the success of “Lupin” made you want to become more involved in creating other films and series, beyond acting and producing? Yes, absolutely. That’s exactly what we’re working on with Thomas [Benski], Louis [Leterrier] and Carrousel Studios. We’re developing projects that I hope we’ll be able to announce soon. Carrousel really came out of everything we experienced together on “Lupin.” Louis and I discovered each other artistically through this series. At a certain point, we reached another level in our collaboration, and we realized that together we were capable of creating these kinds of projects. Carrousel is really about taking that collaboration further and doing it on a much bigger scale. We’re working on things, and I hope we’ll soon be able to come out with an idea that is still cooking at the moment. What’s also remarkable about this new season of “Lupin” is that someone who has never seen the series could start watching with Part 4 and still get into it. Was making it accessible to new audiences important to you? Thank you, because that’s exactly what we wanted to achieve. That’s also why we took our time. Obviously, we’re continuing a series that has been watched by a lot of people, so there are things we had to preserve. But at the same time, we had to bring something new. Finding that balance was really the challenge, and it’s something we worked on enormously. So hearing you say that is very satisfying, because it’s exactly what we were trying to do. You’ve had a busy year. You starred in “Dumas: Diable Noir,” and you’re also shooting the new “Ocean’s” movie. Have you finished filming that? No, we’re still filming. Can you tell me anything about your character? I can’t! You know how these things work. You can’t really talk about anything until someone tells you exactly what you can say. And since we’re still shooting, I’m keeping quiet. You know what you know, and I can’t tell you anything more. But I can tell you we’re still working on it. We shot over the summer, and we’re now finishing it. It’s great. What’s Bradley Cooper like as a director? Bradley is someone who’s incredibly inspired. He’s very involved, very passionate. He’s completely immersed in what he’s doing. He really enjoys his work and throws himself into it. And because he’s also an actor, he has a way of communicating what he wants that makes it very easy for another actor to understand and deliver. I’d already worked with him as an actor on “Burnt.” Even back then, he was someone who shared a lot with the people around him. Now that he’s also behind the camera, it’s a real pleasure. It’s incredibly inspiring to watch him work. And because I’m also interested in exploring what’s happening behind the camera, particularly as a producer, seeing the way he approaches and invests himself in every aspect of a project is very inspiring for me. You’ve been working in Hollywood for several years now. Are there still things you’re particularly eager to do in the U.S. that you haven’t had the chance to do yet? I don’t really think that way. I don’t approach my career by telling myself that there’s a particular box I still need to tick. That’s not how I function at all. I started in this business with a certain momentum, and I’ve tried to keep moving without making too many plans or calculations. There are encounters, opportunities, things that inspire you. I see it as a movement that continues rather than something that needs to be planned out. Take Carrousel, for example. It started with my meeting Louis, then Thomas, and that led to Carrousel. It’s the same with Bradley. We met on “Burnt,” we got along really well, and today he’s calling me to work with him on this new project. That’s how things happen for me. I don’t sit down and think that I need to do this or that next. It’s not my way of working. The things I do come more from my gut than from my head. What’s interesting about the U.S. industry right now is that alongside all the consolidation, with Paramount and Warner Bros., there are also a lot of independent companies and extraordinary creative talent. That’s what I believe in more. I believe in what’s being created a little on the margins, with lighter, more flexible structures that are more focused on creativity and on bringing something new. Because on the other side, the studios are becoming bigger and bigger. But the more they merge, the more they become fixed and rigid. What’s exciting about creating things is that sense of freedom, that lightness and the ability to adapt. And coming back to Carrousel, that’s exactly what we want to preserve: the ability to move quickly and adapt quickly. You also have Ladj Ly’s “Dumas: Diable Noir” coming out next year, possibly around the time of the French elections. Given the political climate, do you think a film like that could have a particular resonance? What role can cinema play in these debates? One thing I’m sure of is that “Dumas” is going to generate a lot of debate and discussion. For me, that’s also one of the things cinema can do. It’s not its only purpose, obviously, but it can create conversations. When you make a film like “Dumas,” that’s also something you hope to provoke. And given the current political context, I do think a film like this will generate discussion. We need conversations right now. I just hope they can be calm, thoughtful conversations rather than heated ones. You’re still based in Los Angeles, right? Yes, I’m still in the United States. So you’re watching what’s happening in France from a distance? No, I’m not watching from a distance. I’m here, I’m right in the middle of it, and I feel what’s happening. Although you have plenty of problems in the U.S. as well. The thing is, the problems in the United States aren’t my problems. My problems are here. So your heart is still in Paris? Obviously. articles.title: Russell Brand Trial: Second Woman Alleges He Was a ‘Wild-Eyed Maniac’ as He Tried to Pull Her Into Bathroom
articles.full_text: Oct 16, 2026 6:06am PT Russell Brand Trial: Second Woman Alleges He Was a ‘Wild-Eyed Maniac’ as He Tried to Pull Her Into Bathroom By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Russell Brand Trial: Second Woman Alleges He Was a ‘Wild-Eyed Maniac’ as He Tried to Pull Her Into Bathroom 39 minutes ago Jenna Ortega Says She Hopes ‘Klara and the Sun’ Encourages People to ‘Put Down the Computers and Phones’ as Dystopian Film World Premieres in London 15 hours ago Jack O’Connell, Sandra Hüller, Taron Egerton, George MacKay, Rosalind Eleazar, Florian Zeller and More Celebrate London Film Festival at Variety Dinner 21 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source PA Images via Getty Images Russell Brand ‘s criminal trial in London continued on Friday, with his second accuser alleging that Brand was a “wild-eyed maniac” as he tried to pull her into a bathroom. The actor and comedian has been charged with three counts of rape, three counts of sexual assault and one count of indecent assault relating to incidents with six women spanning from 1999 to 2009. He has pleaded not guilty and denied all allegations against him. Related Stories ‘SNL’ Weekend Update Brutally Mocks Trump for Losing Nobel Peace Prize White House's New AI Website Confirms Trump Lost the 2020 Presidential Election Arriving to Southwark Crown Court, Brand wore a grey suit, white shirt and grey skinny tie. His wife, Laura Gallacher, was by his side again after not attending court on Thursday. He told reporters outside the courthouse that the trial has been an “extraordinary and stressful situation,” according to Sky News . Popular on Variety “But it is also an exploration of truth and justice. As I’ve said before, I pray for everybody involved,” he continued. “It’s in a way very, very sad but hopefully it can bring about some conclusions that are beneficial.” On Friday afternoon, the second alleged victim testified in person from behind a blue screen to protect her identity. In the U.K., all complainants in sexual assault cases are granted automatic lifelong anonymity if they so choose. She said she met Brand while working at MTV in 2001 and complimented his T-shirt, which read “I Am Spartacus,” referencing Stanley Kubrick’s 1960 film. It was “jovial and cheerful banter,” she said, according to Sky News. He then asked her where the bathroom was, and she agreed to show him as she was going that direction anyway. Once they got to the bathroom, “his demeanor changed,” she claimed. He allegedly grabbed her arm “hard” and pleaded with her to “come in, come in, come in,” she added. The woman tried to pull herself away, and said at this point Brand had a “wild look in his eye.” Once she broke free, she called him an “idiot” and then he “gave up” and went into the toilet. After the incident, she questioned how Brand “went from jovial and friendly to this wild-eyed maniac,” according to Sky News. She proceeded to tell two colleagues but not her managers as Brand, who hosted several programs for MTV at the time, was a huge “asset” to MTV and she thought she wouldn’t be believed. Following the Channel 4 documentary that investigated Brand in 2023, she reached out to the police. “I decided I thought it was the right thing to come forward,” she said. The woman was then cross-examined by Brand’s defense lawyer, Ian Winter KC, who claimed that Brand was not pulling her into the bathroom to assault her but rather to have a “consensual” sexual encounter. “Why would you try to drag someone into a toilet unless you wanted to assault them?” she replied. “I was there, I know what happened.” When Winter suggested that her memory of the alleged incident could have been altered by the 2023 media circus surrounding Brand, she said “I knew it was wrong,” adding that the documentary and press coverage “did not change my view of the situation.” On Thursday, the court heard from the first alleged victim via her police video interview. She described in detail an alleged rape by Brand that occurred at the Labour Party conference in 1999 after she met Brand at a cabaret show he was performing in. The woman was then cross-examined in person by Winter, again from behind a screen. The first complainant alleged on Thursday that after talking to Brand at the show, she invited him to come back to her hotel room. She said she thought he was gay at first and felt “sexually safe” with him. However, after she went to the bathroom, the complainant alleges that she emerged to find Brand partially undressed. He demanded that she take photos of him topless — which the court then viewed — and then allegedly raped her. “I was frightened. I remember feeling ‘what on earth have I got myself into’ — and then he did rape me,” she alleged. She claimed that she did say no, but struggled to get him off of her as he was “really heavy.” “I did say no,” she said. “I didn’t want his dirty penis inside me. I value my body.” Brand’s trial is expected to last six weeks. ‘The Monster of Florence’ Director Stefano Sollima on ‘Completely Different’ Second Chapter of Netflix’s Hit Serial Killer Series: ‘A Very Complex Story to Tell’ (EXCLUSIVE) Netflix Gearing Up to Lay Off 5% of Workforce: Report Madrid’s Iberseries & Platino Industria Pivots Toward More B2B Activities Where the Hot Button Issues of AI and Microdramas Also Take Center Stage Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later Part 3’ Will ‘Have a Lot of Cillian Murphy in It’ and Backs Jack O’Connell as the Next James Bond Appetite for Agatha Christie Shows No Signs of Slowing 50 Years After Her Death: ‘She Has Such Enduring Appeal’ Netflix Romance ‘Love Untangled’ Director Namkoong Sun on Netflix Freedom and the Funding and Distribution Gap in Korean Indie Film Loading comments...

The mom in ‘Mom’ would be, and should be, Anna Faris.” ‘Mom — which saw Faris play a recovering alcoholic navigating her new life as her mother (Allison Janney), also a recovering alcoholic, moved in with her — ran for eight seasons on CBS from 2013 to 2021. Faris left the show in 2020 to “pursue new opportunities,” but Lorre blamed her departure on “mysterious reasons.” “As the years went by, it became apparent that my initial reluctance to hire Anna was, in fact, correct,” he wrote. “After six years, she left the show for mysterious reasons that were not mysterious to anyone on the show.” Faris wrote on Thursday that she has been sober for a year and a half. “I was on a show about recovery, and then I lived it,” she wrote. “Now I’m healthy, I’m working, and I’m happier than I’ve been in a long time,” Faris added. “If anyone reading this is where I was, I hope that’s useful. articles.title: How Creators Make Money: Digital-Native Leaders on What Drives Audiences and Brands in the Attention Economy
articles.full_text: Oct 16, 2026 6:15am PT How Creators Make Money: Digital-Native Leaders on What Drives Audiences and Brands in the Attention Economy Variety's 'Strictly Business' podcast features conversations with industry leaders about the business of media and entertainment By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest FlyDubai Hijacking Incident Set for Development as an Inspirational Movie by Dori Media Group and India’s Sphereorigin 1 day ago YouTube’s Virtues, Industry Consolidation, Christie Brinkley and ‘Baywatch’: Trends and Themes From a Busy Mipcom 1 day ago From Bob Hope to Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade to ‘Wicked: One Wonderful Night’: How NBC Became America’s Home for TV Specials 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Variety via Getty Images On the latest episode of Variety ’s “ Strictly Business ” podcast, leaders of top digital-native firms discuss the factors that are funneling viewership, fan engagement and brand deals in the creator economy. Aaron Doades, senior VP of product management for Comscore , Zach Miller, president of JesserCo., Jarret Myer, CEO of Uproxx Studios, and Shaun Newsum, CEO of Culture Genesis, gathered in Los Angeles in September for a session held as part of Variety ‘s annual Entertainment and Technology Summit. This session, and much of the day, was devoted to examining how creators and social video platforms are rewiring our world, especially when it comes to marketing and advertising. Related Stories Trump Taps 'Devoted Fan' Katie Zacharia, a Fox News and CNN Commentator, as White House Press Secretary White House Has Spent More Than $440,000 on Pro-Trump TV Ads Paid for by U.S. Government; Administration Defends 'Unapologetically American' Spots and Denies They're Campaign Ads Myer, a digital media veteran, argues that the rise of superpowers in the creator economy (including sports influencers such as Jesser and IShowSpeed) is a movement back toward a monoculture environment. That’s a counterintuitive take given that the disintermediation of media is driving the upheaval across traditional Hollywood (exhibit A: the newly created Skydance colossus). Popular on Variety Listen to the podcast: “The idea that a creator, an event, a movie, a song can have a moment in culture that everyone’s talking about is happening more and more,” Myer says. “The creator economy is bigger than most people assume it is. They think it’s maybe someone who started a channel in their bedroom, but it’s studios, it’s artists, it’s creators that are all happening outside of the traditional Hollywood formation. More and more, these people are creating the monoculture moments that everyone is talking about. Missing out on that is missing out on the point of entertainment and culture.” Newsum, who leads a creator talent management firm, echoed Myer’s sentiment. “These moments of collective mass consciousness. At Culture Genesis, we call them mini-Super Bowls and they’re happening all the time. And you just don’t know about it,” Newsum says. “The creator economy is always on. There’s content being produced all the time.” Comscore’s Doades pointed to data showing that YouTube is becoming a preferred spot for marketers to find “pockets” of younger viewers who are increasingly hard to find on linear channels, outside of sports. “A lot of folks consume content almost exclusively on creator media. Now, when you’re looking at TV versus creator, the incrementality is massive,” Doades said. “We know that in March of 2026, Jesser had a greater unique reach than 14 live NBA games and the incrementality was 99% — meaning 99% of that audience did not tune in to those NBA games.” Miller in his role helps lead the charge for Jesser, the sports influencer who has enormous cachet with young NBA fans and the league itself. Miller has deep roots in traditional media but he sees no turning back for the content marketplace. “If you’re a marketer and you’re trying to reach a younger audience, you’re going to have a really hard time finding them on television. They’re just not watching TV unless they’re watching live sports,” he says. “But on YouTube, you can find these pockets of audience. The question for advertisers becomes, do you want to spend the money on the traditional media channel that has always been the place to spend it and cross your fingers and hope to find younger audiences there? Or do you need to broaden your strategy, swapping some of that spend on TV for digital channels that will allow you to reach that audience. Or at least expand the spend so that you reach your core audience that you’ve been historically reaching on TV.” (Pictured above, l. to r.: JesserCo.’s Zach Miller, Culture Genius’ Shaun Newsum, Uproxx Studios’ Jarret Myer and Comscore’s Aaron Doades) “Strictly Business” is Variety ’s podcast featuring conversations with industry leaders about the business of media and entertainment. articles.title: El Gouna Artistic Director Andrew Mohsen Puts ‘Discovery’ First: ‘We’re Trying to Draw Attention’ to Overlooked Films
articles.full_text: Oct 16, 2026 6:34am PT El Gouna Artistic Director Andrew Mohsen Puts ‘Discovery’ First: ‘We’re Trying to Draw Attention’ to Overlooked Films By Essie Assibu Plus Icon Essie Assibu Latest 5 Fribourg Film Festival Takeaways, From Audience-Driven Programming to Political Cinema 7 months ago Leon Le on Reframing Vietnam Beyond the Western Gaze: ‘Vietnamese Stories Have Been Told Through a Dated, Disrespectful, Ignorant Lens’ 7 months ago Ukrainian Director Zhanna Ozirna Explores Intimacy Under Siege in ‘Honeymoon’ 7 months ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of El Gouna Film Festival For his first edition at the helm of Egypt’s El Gouna Film Festival , artistic director Andrew Mohsen wants to widen the scope of what, and who, audiences discover on the shores of the Red Sea. “Discovery,” Mohsen asserts, sits at the heart of that vision, which builds on the festival’s established place as a showcase for prize winners and standout titles from Cannes, Venice and Berlin, while expanding the emphasis on emerging filmmakers and films that might otherwise escape the spotlight. Related Stories 'SNL' Opens Season With Mamdani Hanging Out With BFF Trump, Natalie Harp Going 'Obsession' Over President Hillary Clinton to Co-Host Podcast on 2026 Midterm Elections With Kara Swisher for Vox Media, Owned by James Murdoch It’s an evolution rather than a break with El Gouna’s past. Succeeding Marianne Khoury, Mohsen, a Cairo International Film Festival vet, who joined the El Gouna programming team in 2023 and later served as head of programming, is looking to deepen the festival’s ties to Arab filmmakers still developing an international profile and to forge stronger connections with filmmakers across Africa, in particular, where the relatively small pool of titles reaching the international festival circuit makes competition for projects particularly intense. Popular on Variety “We are trying to draw attention to the films that didn’t have the same coverage, or the films we feel our audiences need to see,” he tells Variety . Major festivals can screen around a hundred films in a given year, Mohsen notes, yet it is often the prize winners and established directors that remain in the international conversation, while others disappear. A former film critic, Mohsen has attended El Gouna since its 2017 launch. He wants to establish the festival as a go-to meeting point between Arab filmmakers and the international industry and more closely integrate its film selection with CineGouna , its industry and talent-development arm. Internally, that means getting the festival’s various branches working more closely together. Mohsen describes an “open kitchen between us,” with teams exchanging information about filmmakers, projects and guests who could connect with different parts of an increasingly well-established El Gouna network. That effort has become particularly important for Arab cinema . Mohsen says last year El Gouna had just one non-Egyptian Arab film in its narrative competition and one in documentary, its lowest showing for regional cinema since the festival began. Industry-wide competition for films, especially world or regional premieres, is part of the challenge. “We are trying our best to knock on all doors to see how we can expand our connection with the filmmakers,” Mohsen says. Projects backed by other festivals and funds can come with premiere commitments, so El Gouna has responded by investing through its own funding program and approaching filmmakers earlier. Mohsen is also widening the programming scope. Genre cinema has a larger presence this year, a choice he says reflects its growing prominence at major international festivals. Another current emerged across the selection, though not by any explicit design: fear, be it within families, under political regimes, or through anxieties and difficult realities characters themselves struggle to identify. Mohsen points to Miroslav Terzić’s “ Three Weeks After ,” a study of Serbian students confronting the aftermath of a classmate’s death by suicide, as one film in which that unease builds gradually. “You feel you are not really comfortable when you’re watching the film, that there’s something happening, but you cannot put your hand on,” he says. “I find this resonates with what’s happening in the world today.” Another addition is CineGouna Series, led by Egyptian screenwriter Mariam Naoum, an extension of the industry program into an ever more popular medium, both across the region and the wider international entertainment industry. Mohsen sees the move as a natural fit for Egypt, whose television industry has long supplied audiences across the Arab world with on-screen entertainment. “Series, they’re always happening. They’re always selling,” he says. “So we are very strong.” For Mohsen, that strength gives El Gouna an opportunity to invest in a field that remains relatively underrepresented at film festivals in the region. The expansion into series is part of a broader effort to make El Gouna useful to creators beyond simply screening their work. For Mohsen, that means making a case for what the festival can offer filmmakers navigating an increasingly crowded international circuit. “You want exposure, you want connections, you want audiences to react to your film? We can offer all of that.” Asked about the filmmakers he would most like to bring to El Gouna, Mohsen has two names on his wish list: Guillermo del Toro and Park Chan-wook on a festival jury, leading a master class, or simply taking part in the festival. “My two dreams,” he shares. articles.title: Chris Pratt and Pope Leo Explore St. Peter’s Tomb in Trailer for Vatican Documentary ‘Discovering the Origins’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 16, 2026 6:35am PT Chris Pratt and Pope Leo Explore St. Peter’s Tomb in Trailer for Vatican Documentary ‘Discovering the Origins’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Guillermo del Toro Pays Tribute to Late ‘E.T.’ Designer Carlo Rambaldi Ahead of Hollywood Walk of Fame Honor: ‘A Worldwide Maestro of Magic’ (EXCLUSIVE) 23 hours ago Joanna Hogg to Preside Over El Gouna Film Festival Jury 2 days ago Qatar to Bow Domestic Feature Productions at Upcoming Doha Film Festival in ‘Watershed Moment’ 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source A new documentary pairs Pope Leo and Hollywood star Chris Pratt to delve into the history, religious passion and archaeological discoveries surrounding the tomb of St. Peter at the Vatican. Titled “Pétros Ení — Discovering the Origins,” the doc — which launches from the Rome Film Festival on Friday ahead of its international rollout — marks the 400th anniversary, on Nov. 18, of the consecration of St. Peter’s. Variety can reveal its trailer exclusively above. Related Stories Mark Ruffalo Tells Trump 'Hands Off Our F---ing Vote' or 'I'm Gonna Hulk Out': 'You Won't Like Me When I'm Angry' 'SNL U.K.' Mocks Donald Trump and Andy Burnham's First Meeting, Harvey Weinstein, Sam Altman and More in Wild Weekend Update Featuring footage rarely seen by the general public, it “explores how Peter’s burial place became a center of devotion for early Christians and, eventually, the foundation for the first great basilica built under Emperor Constantine,” as the synopsis puts it. The words “Pétros Ení,” in the title, refer to a Greek inscription than means “Peter is here” found near the apostle’s burial grounds. Pratt, who is best known to audiences for starring in the “Guardians of the Galaxy” and “Jurassic World” franchises, guides viewers on a journey beneath the basilica to discover the history and archaeology of one of Christianity’s most important sites. “The journey culminates with the special participation of Pope Leo XIV, who appears in the film’s final scenes to reflect on Peter and the meaning of his tomb beneath the Basilica,” the synopsis says. “It was an incredible honor to collaborate with Pope Leo and the Vatican on this project,” Pratt said in a statement. “The story of St. Peter is foundational to the Christian faith, and I am deeply grateful for the trust and access I was given to bring his legacy to the screen.” Pope Leo in “Pétros Ení — Discovering the Origins.” Courtesy AF Films, Vatican Media “Pétros Ení — Discovering the Origins” is directed by Spanish filmmaker Paula Ortiz and written by Andrea Tornielli. The doc is produced by AF Films, led by Frank Ariza and Manu Vega, together with Vatican Media and La Fabbrica di San Pietro. The high-profile doc is scheduled to start its international theatrical rollout in February 2027 during the opening weeks of Lent, the Christian season of prayer, reflection and preparation for Easter and the central celebration of the Christian calendar, according to the statement. The rollout will bring together regional distribution partners, with Hallow Studios handling U.S. and Canada distribution; Bosco Films releasing the documentary in Spain; and Cinépolis +Que Cine overseeing its theatrical release in Mexico, Brazil and Colombia. articles.title: Indonesian Zombie Franchise ‘Zona Merah: Dead City’ Unveils Teaser, Takes Outbreak Into the City
articles.full_text: Oct 16, 2026 6:41am PT Indonesian Zombie Franchise ‘Zona Merah: Dead City’ Unveils Teaser, Takes Outbreak Into the City By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Boo Junfeng’s ‘Trinity,’ Sidharta Tata’s ‘Slaughterground’ Among JAFF Market 2026 Selections 2 hours ago Singapore Media Festival Launches Creator Summit as Asia TV Forum Adds AI Zone, Microdrama Focus 5 hours ago Busan Takeaways: Record Crowds Meet a Political Storm as Asia’s Producers Close Ranks 6 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Screenplay Films The first teaser for “ Zona Merah : Dead City,” the big-screen adaptation of Indonesian zombie series “Zona Merah,” has landed ahead of the film’s Jan. 14, 2027, release in Indonesian cinemas. Screenplay Films, which unveiled the trailer on Friday, is billing the feature as the largest zombie production Indonesia has ever mounted. The source series, a Vidio original, has racked up more than 34 million views on the streamer. The film follows survivors struggling to outlast an undead threat that grows far beyond anything the show attempted. Related Stories Judge Extends Block on Trump's White House Ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico Todd Haynes, Zhang Ziyi and Daniel Brühl Lead a Star-Studded Lumière Fest Opening With Haynes Teasing ‘De Noche,’ Starring Pedro Pascal “As one of the most ambitious projects we’ve ever undertaken, we want to deliver an extraordinary cinematic experience for everyone, not just fans of the ‘Zona Merah’ series,” said Screenplay Films producer Wicky V. Olindo. Popular on Variety The teaser shows where that ambition has gone. The series stayed mostly in the countryside, among villages and quarantine sites. The film moves the outbreak onto city streets and into malls, with action also staged at an airport. Sidharta Tata returns to direct and shares duties on the feature with co-director Fajar Martha Santosa. “From day one, we knew we had to go all out for ‘Zona Merah: Dead City.’ We filmed across three cities in Indonesia, worked with hundreds of extras, and built incredible set pieces,” Tata said. Several faces from the series are back, including Aghni Haque, Andri Mashadi, Devano, Maria Theodore and Lukman Sardi. Joining the franchise for the first time are Bryan Domani, Shindy Huang, Myesha Lin, Derby Romero and Luna Maya. Maya is also an executive producer on the film. Barunson E&A is handling international sales . articles.title: Anna Faris Was “Hurt” By Chuck Lorre’s Comments About Her ‘Mom’ Exit: “Yikes”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Kylie Minogue, Jonathan Groff & Catherine Tate Join ‘Bad Fairies’ Cast With Cynthia Erivo ‘The Beekeeper 2’ Teaser: Jason Statham Kicks Rogue Govt. Agent Butt To Metallica In First Look At Sequel Anna Faris Was “Hurt” By Chuck Lorre’s Comments About Her ‘Mom’ Exit: “Yikes” View All October 15, 2026 4:38pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Anna Faris responds to Chuck Lorre's comments about her 'Mom' exit. Robert Voets/Warner Bros./Christopher Polk/Deadline Six years after announcing her departure from CBS ‘s Mom , Anna Faris has reacted to Chuck Lorre ‘s comments about her exit. On Thursday, the actress shared a statement explaining that she “never took a day of [the show] for granted” after series co-creator Lorre wrote in his new memoir Sitcom that he “was, in fact, correct” about his initial reluctance to cast her as Christy Plunkett in the sitcom. Related Stories Books Chuck Lorre Q&A On The Care & Feeding Of Sitcom Stars & Why A WGA Strike Doomed Democracy Casting ‘Mom’ Star Anna Faris Exits CBS Comedy Series After Seven Seasons “Yikes. Yes, I read a few things. I really didn’t see that coming. Of course it hurts,” she began in a statement on Instagram . “Chuck gave me a job I loved, and for seven years I never took a day of it for granted. I’m proud of what we made together, and nothing changes how grateful I am for those people and those years.” Faris continued: “I’ve been sober for a year and a half. I was on a show about recovery, and then I lived it. Now I’m healthy, I’m working, and I’m happier than I’ve been in a long time. If anyone reading this is where I was, I hope that’s useful. It gets better. I’m proof.” Watch on Deadline Premiering in 2013, Faris starred in the first seven seasons of Mom as Christy, a recovering alcoholic who struggles to maintain a job, her family and her sobriety as her mom Bonnie (Allison Janney), who’s also in recovery, moves in with her. View this post on Instagram Faris left the show in 2020 to “pursue new opportunities,” leaving Janney as the sole lead for the eighth and final season, which ended in 2021. In an excerpt from Sitcom , Lorre wrote: “I wasn’t sure Anna would be appropriate for this kind of material. Then I thought about how badly I’d bungled my working relationship with Charlie Sheen.” After his experience with Charlie Sheen on Two and a Half Men , Lorre recalled conceding, “Someone’s personal life is none of my business. The mom in Mom would be, and should be, Anna Faris.” Lorre added: “As the years went by, it became apparent that my initial reluctance to hire Anna was, in fact, correct. After six years, she left the show for mysterious reasons that were not mysterious to anyone on the show.” Netflix Shakeup: Bajaria’s Exit Signals Changes To Come As Rice Hire Elicits Praise Steven Soderbergh To Work With Matt Reeves On Final Weeks Of ‘The Batman II’ Shoot Tim Burton And ‘Klara And The Sun’ Author Kazuo Ishiguro’s Secret Project ‘Street Fighter’ $4M Previews, A24 Holmes Doc Draws $2M Read More About: 13 Comments

articles.title: greenlit by Lionsgate
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt ‘Seeker’ Writer-Producer Michael Learner Inks With WME & Untitled Lauren Cohan, Mark O’Brien & Mia Tomlinson Join Prime Video’s ‘Stillwater’ As Series Regulars Talia Ryder, Elizabeth Marvel & Bill Camp Join STX & Aggregate’s True-Crime Thriller ‘PRƎPPY’ View All January 6, 2026 8:12am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Sydney Sweeney in 'The Housemaid Daniel McFadden/Lionsgate Amid big box office success for The Housemaid , its Freida McFadden thriller starring Sydney Sweeney , Amanda Seyfried and Brandon Sklenar, Lionsgate is moving toward a 2026 production start for a sequel, The Housemaid’s Secret , based on the second novel in McFadden’s bestselling trilogy. The project has been in development for the past few months, with Sweeney eyeing to return to star and exec produce, and co-star Michele Morrone also looking to reprise. It’s expected that Paul Feig will return to direct from a script by Rebecca Sonnenshine, who adapted The Housemaid . Producers will include Todd Lieberman of Hidden Pictures, Feig and Laura Fischer of Feig’s Pretty Dangerous Pictures, and Hidden Pictures’ Carly Elter and Alex Young. McFadden will also serve as an executive producer. Related Stories Books Which Freida McFadden Books Are Becoming Movies? ‘The Housemaid’ To ‘The Teacher News ‘Avatar: Fire And Ash’ Burns Trail To $306M U.S.; ‘Housemaid’ Excellent Hold, 2026 Starts +29% Over ’25 – Sunday Box Office Update The film will be overseen by Lionsgate’s Chelsea Kujawa, who also oversaw the first film and brought the project into the studio, alongside Maria Ascanio. Robert Melnik negotiated deals for the studio. Watch on Deadline “It’s clear from both the global box office and from the outpouring on social media that audiences have responded strongly – and audibly – to the totally unique and truly theatrical experience of The Housemaid and want to know what happens next,” said Lionsgate Motion Picture Group Chair Adam Fogelson. “We believed in these stories from the very beginning, and we are beyond excited to bring the next chapter of Millie’s story to life on-screen in collaboration with our outstanding creative partners Todd, Paul, Laura, Carly, Alex, and Sydney. The Housemaid’s Secret is another wildly thrilling book in Freida’s series that has captivated readers worldwide, and we look forward to translating it into a similarly rousing and riotous moviegoing experience.” Said Hidden Pictures’ Lieberman, a producer on both Housemaid films, “We’re thrilled with the reception and incredibly proud of this entire team from Freida McFadden to our partners at Lionsgate, and the outstanding work of Paul and Laura. Most rewarding has been seeing how strongly audiences are connecting with the film.”

articles.title: Netflix’s New Content Chief Peter Rice Will Continue As EP Of LA28 Opening & Closing Ceremonies
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Netflix’s New Content Chief Peter Rice Will Continue As EP Of LA28 Opening & Closing Ceremonies Diddy’s Prison Head Injury Mystery Deepens; Feds Deny Fight With Drug Kingpin Sent Grammy Winner To Hospital FBI Adds Ex-Bellum Entertainment CEO To Most Wanted Fraudsters List; Offering $150K Reward For Info On Fugitive Mary Carole McDonnell View All October 15, 2026 7:08pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Peter Rice Disney EXCLUSIVE: “Netflix is fortunate to have him.” That’s what LA28 boss Casey Wasserman said Thursday night about Peter Rice after the mastermind behind the upcoming Summer Olympics Opening and Closing Ceremonies landed a top gig at the streamer . Related Stories Executives Netflix Names Peter Rice As Chief Content Officer Legal How A Pizza Mogul, The Epstein Files & A $15K MPTF Gala Ticket Has Put A New Wrinkle In An Old Lawsuit Against Casey Wasserman In a dizzying sequence of moves that saw Bela Bajaria ousted as chief content officer at Netflix and former Disney exec Rice parachuted into the job , question remained about Rice’s pivotal role in the 2028 Olympics suddenly being left open. Tonight, Wasserman offered clarification as to what Rice will be doing for the Olympics as well as praised the smooth-operator executive. “Peter has given the LA28 Ceremonies a vision worthy of the moment, and I am deeply grateful for all he’s accomplished. Few people know how to tell a compelling story to the entire world at once, and Peter is one of those rare few. I’m delighted that he’ll stay with us as Executive Producer for the Ceremonies, where his wisdom and counsel will continue to shape what the world sees in 2028. I congratulate him on his new role. Netflix is fortunate to have him.” Watch on Deadline Rice, the onetime chairman of Walt Disney Television and head of 21st Century Fox who exited the company in June 2022 , was tapped to run the L.A. Olympics Opening and Closing Ceremonies in June 2025. Wasserman was in charge of Los Angeles’ failed bid for the 2024 Summer Olympics and kept the job through the city’s awarding of the 2028 Games back in 2017. He has had some brushes with scandal in the years since, but Mayor Karen Bass said early this year she has “full trust” in him. The LA28 board followed with a vote of confidence days later. Erik Pedersen contributed to this report. articles.title: ‘Law & Order’ Season 26, Episode 2 Recap: What Happened To Det. Vincent Riley In Reid Scott’s Final Episode?
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando ‘Law & Order’ Season 26, Episode 2 Recap: What Happened To Det. Vincent Riley In Reid Scott’s Final Episode? Aaron Paul Mourns ‘Breaking Bad’ Co-Star RJ Mitte: “I Am So Sorry You Were Hurting, My Friend” Aaron Sorkin On ‘The West Wing’ Revival: “It Would Be Very, Very Tricky To Do In The Current Environment” View All October 15, 2026 8:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Reid Scott NBC SPOILER ALERT: This post contains details on Law & Order Season 26, Episode 2, which aired on NBC on Thursday, October 15. Earlier this year, Deadline reported that Reid Scott , who plays Senior Detective Vincent Riley, was leaving the NBC procedural. Scott’s exit finally aired in the second episode of Season 26 titled “Into the Mystic.” The episode opens with Riley sitting at his work desk, and something prompts him to look for Ray Biller. When he arrives at Ray’s apartment, the person who answers the door says Ray isn’t there. Riley orders the guy to call Ray to find out where he is. Related Stories News 'Newlyweds': Bruce Helford Tapped As New Showrunner In 'Anything But Love' Reunion With Jamie Lee Curtis, Production Hiatus Extended News 'Friends' Returning To Channel 4 After 15 Years Moments later, Riley calls Nolan Price (Hugh Dancy) and tells him, “Need to talk to you right away. Call me back.” Watch on Deadline Riley then calls Theo Walker (David Ajala) and tells him he’s headed to a bar as “something is cooking.” After heading to the bar, Riley gets a text from Walker saying he’s on his way. As Riley approaches the bar, he notices Ray exiting the establishment. Riley follows Ray, who tells him he needs to talk. However, when he turns around, he shoots Riley twice in the chest and runs off. Walker arrives at the scene and notices a man running away with a gun in hand. However, by the bar, there’s a lot of commotion as Riley bleeds from the gunshot wounds. Walker calls for help, applies pressure, and yells, “Vince, stay with me, come on!” Lieutenant Jessica Brady (Maura Tierney) arrives at the hospital, and Walker fills her in on what happened, leaving her shocked and without words. At the hospital, the doctor tells Walker they couldn’t save Riley, leaving all his colleagues in despair. Robert Calvino, played by James Badge Dale, is introduced to help investigate Riley’s death. Riley’s wife shows up at the police station and tells them that he had been withdrawing “lots of cash” recently. Although Riley’s wife didn’t know what the money was for, she did note that he was a drinker. Jessica Brady and Robert Calvino visit a woman who Riley had been arguing with hours earlier on the day that he died. The pregnant woman tells officers that Riley was giving her cash as he “felt guilty” for killing her husband years before. Brady and Calvino find out Riley was at Ray Biller’s apartment and talk to his friend, who corroborates what Riley was doing there the night he was killed. When they get back to the office, Nolan tells them that Ray Biller’s brother, Wayne, whom he found for murder, was killed in prison. The police find Ray Biller, who was attending his brother’s Wayne funeral, and arrest him as the prime suspect in Riley’s death. Actor Ryan Eggold made an appearance reprising his role as Matt Riley, the troubled brother of Detective Vincent Riley, showing up in court and wanting justice for his brother’s death. The prosecution runs into a problem when Ray Biller’s defense argues that they can’t prove he was the one who killed Riley, as they didn’t recover a weapon. DA Nicholas Baxter (Tony Goldwyn) is determined to put Walker on the stand, but Nolan pushes back as he doesn’t believe Walker actually saw Ray Biller as the man who killed Riley. On the day of the verdict, Ray Biller was found guilty on the charge of first-degree murder. Although it was a victory for the prosecution, doubt remains over whether Walker told the truth, and Nolan remains skeptical about whether they did the right thing. In July, Deadline first reported that Reid Scott was leaving Law & Order , after joining in Season 23. He reportedly decided to exit the NBC procedural due to the strain of the cross-country commute to New York City, where the series is filmed. articles.title: the events in the Season 22 fin…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Cupertino’ Creators Robert & Michelle King On Episode 2’s Shocking AGI Twist & Predicting The Future Again With AI Guardrails Storyline Netflix Shakeup: Peter Rice Is Welcomed Back To Executive Ranks While Bela Bajaria’s Exit Has Layoff-Weary Staff Bracing For More Upheaval ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP Meg Marinis On Season 23 Premiere’s Time Jump, Pregnancy Surprise, James Wolk’s Arrival & Doctor’s Exit; Texas Spinoff Status View All May 7, 2026 8:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Grey's Anatomy' ABC SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about the Season 22 finale of Grey’s Anatomy. Grey’s Anatomy may have not ended its 22nd season with the typical jaw-dropping cliffhanger in order to send off veteran cast members Kim Raver and Kevin McKidd , but the finale did offer some big twists, leaving most characters’ futures uncertain. Related Stories News ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ EP On Teddy & Owen’s Emotional Goodbye, Why Kevin McKidd & Kim Raver Are Leaving And “Painful” Network Budget Constraints News Kevin McKidd & Kim Raver React To ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Exits, Reflect On Long Runs: “It Has Been A True Gift” – See Owen & Teddy Through The Years In a classic Grey’s bait and switch, while the focus early on was on Owen (McKidd) possibly being hurt (or worse) in the bridge collapse, it was Nick (Scott Speedman) who was in fact badly injured. He required a difficult emergency surgery, performed by suspended Bailey (Chandra Wilson) upon Meredith’s (Ellen Pompeo) request. Shaken up by the experience, Meredith proposed to Nick while he was lying in his hospital bed, a throwback to their first meeting when Nick was admitted to Grey Sloan with a failing kidney in Season 14. He said yes, an answer he apparently had had ready since that fateful first encounter. Watch on Deadline In another Grey’s tradition, the finale also included a jaw-dropping WTF moment. Toni (Jen Landon), after some soul-searching over her ex-wife’s appeal to get back together, went to Amelia’s (Caterina Scorsone) apartment to tell her that she had broken it off with her ex and was falling in love with her only to find out that Amelia had hooked up with Cass (Sophia Bush). (Cass had popped in at Grey Sloan earlier in the day to help with the influx of patients from the bridge collapse.) In other developments, Kwan (Harry Shum Jr.) is still fired. He tried to get back on Richard’s (James Pickens Jr.) good graces by helping with injured patients but that didn’t work. New couple Winston and Jules’ secret relationship is no more (secret) after they were intercepted sneaking out of an on-call room by Ben (Jason George), a newly minted plastics fellow. New mom Jo (Camilla Luddington) is facing an existential crisis and may not be a doctor anymore while her supportive husband Link’s (Chris Carmack) dependance on painkillers is becoming worrisome. Bailey, defying her suspension to help save Nick, is considering a career change of her own as she plans to go for a Masters in public health. And the Simone (Alexis Floyd)-Lucas (Nike Terho)-Wes (Trevor Jackson) love triangle, which had been dormant for most of the season, came back in full force after Simone and Lucas slept together and Wes asked her to go steady. Below, Grey’s Anatomy executive producer/showrunner Meg Marinis is breaking down all non-Owen & Teddy developments in the finale and how they would carry over to Season 23, including potential other cast departures and Speedman’s status as his ABC series R.J. Decker is yet to be renewed (but is looking good). For her explanation of McKidd and Kim Raver’s exit and the reasons behind it, r ead Part 1 of Deadline’s interview . ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Scott Speedman as Nick, Ellen Pompeo as Meredith in Season 14. ABC Meredith & Nick: Meet Cute Redo DEADLINE: Meredith and Nick recreated their first encounter for the surprise proposal. How did you settle on that and why did she pop the question? MARINIS : Well, Meredith has always been pretty clear that she didn’t want to get married again after Derek. In truth, she didn’t really want to get married to Derek, they did that in the end because of trying to make sure that they could have the best chances at adopting Zola. And so I think marriage is not something that is ingrained in her, but clearly, when she heard the story of how he wanted to get married in the middle of the season, when his sister came to visit, and how his sister had taken away this happy life from him, I think that got put in the back of her mind that that is something that he’d always wanted, but he’s such a nice guy, he loves her so much that he’s never going to force her to do anything, especially since she had such a painful ending to her first marriage. I think she’s also scared that if she ever got married again, what if she lost him like it happened with Derek? And I think when she realized that you’re going to have that fear no matter what, why not do it? I told Ellen at the beginning of this season, I was like, I want to end with a proposal. And she was like, ‘Agh’. I was like, I do, I do. So it was something that I’ve been planning since the beginning of the season, and it was very seeded with that middle episode between the two of them. I obviously don’t know the fate of R.J. Decker. I haven’t heard anything. And so it was a very small window that we got Scott to come and film in L.A. and so it worked out that, okay, if we can get him in a hospital bed and put him on the table, then we can utilize as much time with Scott that we had. It was kind of a perfect scenario. DEADLINE: You took a leap of fate with the proposal not knowing whether the actor playing the groom-to-be would be available next season. Will it depend on R.J. Decker’ s fate how much we will see of Scott on Grey’s next year? MARINIS : For sure, it will depend on if R.J. Decker goes, and I hope it does for Scott. But he was so game, he flew in on a Friday, we filmed on a Saturday, and we worked it out. He was being part of the Grey’s family. And so we’ll just have to figure out if we can plan in advance with the other show and work it out again. DEADLINE: Are you planning a big wedding? We know Meredith is not keen on the idea but a wedding would bring people back. We haven’t seen many Grey’s alumni for awhile; I feel this season was one of the lightest in terms of cast returns. MARINIS : You know, I don’t, it all really kind of depends on Scott’s schedule and what we decide creatively. I do not think Meredith is a big wedding person, but we’ll just have to see. DEADLINE: And in terms of returns, was it intentional that you had fewer people coming back vs previous seasons? MARINIS : No. When we realized that we needed to exit two characters we wanted to spend the most time on the characters that we have currently. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’: Harry Shum Jr. as Kwan (Blue) Disney/Anne Marie Fox Ben & Kwan: One Rising & One Leaving? DEADLINE: We know about Kim Raver and Kevin McKidd but are other cast members leaving too? For example, Harry Shum Jr. whose character Kwan was fired twice in the last two episodes? MARINIS : His fate is still undecided. Blue is scared out of his mind, so we’ll just have to see when we come back in the fall. He doesn’t have a job at Grey Sloan right now, so we’ll have to see what happens to him. DEADLINE: There was this interesting look on Catherine’s face when Richard kicked Blue out in the finale. It felt like she was persuadable. MARINIS: It’s kind of a different shade on Catherine, it’s nice. DEADLINE: But to reiterate, of the series regulars, no one except Kevin and Kim are leaving, right? MARINIS : We’ll always have to wait to see who shows up in Season 23. DEADLINE: We’ve talked about Ben floating around, trying to find himself since returning to Grey Sloan. He just got this fellowship; has he now settled? MARINIS : I think he’s as settled as Ben Warren can be. But yes, I’m interested in seeing him follow this fellowship and wear those navy scrubs and be looked at someone who has authority now. That was really important to me this season, to bring him out of Bailey’s shadow, to give him a mentor who doesn’t also see him as someone who’s had a bunch of different jobs. She’s just meeting him for the first time as Ben Warren, someone who’s interested in plastics, and so she doesn’t know all the history necessarily. And I think he really is proving himself. I think that was a really powerful story in Episode 17 last week for him, where he saved Maya. He did great work and saved your life and he really deserves those navy scrubs. Bailey & Richard: OGs 4ever DEADLINE: What about Grey’s veterans Chandra Wilson and James Pickens Jr.? Would Bailey’s plan for a degree in public health impact how much she will be on the show next season? And Richard had cancer. Are there any plans for him to scale back? Seems like he’s in every episode. MARINIS : He is in every episode. And those two are our OGs that are the pillars of the show. I do not envision a world where I can scale back on seeing either of them. Just due to the creative, we may be seeing Bailey in a different capacity, though. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Caterina Scorsone as Amelia, Jen Landon as Toni Disney/Anne Marie Fox Toni & Amelia: She Did What?! DEADLINE: You added Jen Landon as plastic surgeon Toni this season. We got this crazy cliffhanger with her and Amelia at the end that opens up two possibilities for Toni next season, her leaving after what happened or her being promoted to series regular. Which on e is it? MARINIS : Well, I love Jen Landon, and we were so lucky to get her and have her, and I think she really enjoyed her time here. Also, her character brings a really great side to Ben Warren, I love their working relationship. She’s this quirky plastic surgeon that we don’t really have a character like her anywhere else, and I would love to have her back. I don’t know if I would use the word promote, because we are in a different time in our industry with the budget, but I would love to have her come back as much as we can. DEADLINE: Speaking of the surprising cliffhanger, where did this seemingly random Amelia and Cass hookup come from? And what does it mean for Amelia and Toni who had just poured her heart out to her? MARINIS : I think Amelia truly felt like Toni was going back to her wife, and I think she was really sad about it. She had an emotional day with Meredith, and this pretty woman asked if she wanted to get coffee after a long day. I know it all happened off screen, but we love the surprise at the end. Obviously, Sophia Bush’s character is married, she’s in an open marriage, so I don’t think Sophia Bush’s character has left her husband or anything. I just think this is more of now Amelia has gotten herself into a little bit of trouble. I think she wants to be with Toni, and I think she was just trying to make herself feel better because she thought she had been rejected. And so, what we have to look for in the future is, can Toni overlook it? Does Amelia need to work her way back or do they have to work together and deny their chemistry while Toni’s repairing her feelings? We’ll just have to wait and see but they’re a great match. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Adelaide Kane as Jules, Anthony Hill as Winston Disney/Anne Marie Fox Winston & Jules: Dangerous Liaison DEADLINE: When we spoke about the power dynamic issue in the Winston and Jules relationship last year, you noted that a lot has changed since Meredith and Derek and that some things that were considered appropriate at the time are not anymore. Yet, you went with the storyline. Why? And what will the repercussions be of them being discovered by Ben? As Winston said when he professed his love to Jules, “I could be fired for everything I’m about to say.” MARINIS : Well, we didn’t see Ben tell Bailey, but you know that that’s going to happen at one point, so I think their little happy bubble will probably be popped, and I think that it’s just going to depend. I mean, Bailey, she’s married to someone who technically was a resident, so we’re just going to have to see how, if it’s hypocritical, for someone to say something. But I think people will have a lot to say about it once they find out that, yes, that was the cliffhanger of, oh no, now everything he was worried about could possibly happen. DEADLINE: But why did you decide to pursue that? And why did Winston do it? There was attraction…. MARINIS : They’re in love, Nellie. He couldn’t deny it. He tried so long. It was two seasons. DEADLINE: Okay, it’s Grey’s , love wins and trumps rules, I guess. MARINIS : But these days we have repercussions, so we’ll have to see what those are. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Chris Carmack as Link Disney/Anne Marie Fox Jo & Link: Breaking Point DEADLINE: Jo is spiraling, she doesn’t even know if she wants to be any doctor anymore, let alone OB or surgeon. Is her internal crisis triggered by postpartum or is she genuinely not sure about her future? MARINIS : I think it’s a little bit in both. I think when you go through something like postpartum, there’s a little bit of I don’t know what my life should look like, what brings me happiness anymore and what brings me down? I think that it’s something that we really were interested in talking about a lot of times, our characters go through really big health scares, and then in two episodes, they moved along just fine. But I think in particular, especially with mothers and difficult deliveries, no one really talks about that, and it’s a disservice. And especially, just talking to so many people about maternal mortality, everyone always thinks, Oh, if the mom and the babies are saved, it’s a happy ending. Well, yes, it’s a happy ending, but you don’t know the emotional burden that people go through after. We heard from this doctor, and I said, this is too powerful a story not to tell and to let women know that it’s okay that you’re feeling like this. And I think, with the career aspect of it, her trigger is her job, because she’s seeing other women go through it. It’s just, can she maintain that or not? is the big question. DEADLINE: And you don’t have an answer right now? MARINIS: Not for you. DEADLINE: And Link, we’d seen from the beginning of the season where this was headed as he seems to be popping more and more painkillers. Is this going to escalate next season? MARINIS : Yes, we’ll definitely deal with the aftermath of this. He also went through such a big health scare at the beginning of this season, and he’s tried to power through the best he can for Jo. He’s someone who really prides himself on his strength and being there for his partner and his kids. And so I don’t think it’s an option for him to be weak and to not take care of them. We’ll have to look at that. When both members of a couple are going through something, it doesn’t necessarily mean that one person has to power through. It’s okay. I think we’re telling a different story about having to turn to medication to numb, I don’t think it’s going to look like the stereotypical abuse of medication that a lot of other shows and movies have done. I think it’s going to be more nuanced. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’ (L-R): Niko Terho as Lucas, Alexis Floyd as Simone Disney/Anne Marie Fox Simone, Lucas & Wes: Three’s Company DEADLINE: Why did you decide to reignite the love triangle between Lucas, Simone and Wes with a big, classic Grey’s finale cliffhanger? MARINIS : Well, I think we put Lucas through it this season with his emotional patient story, Katie. And in that storyline, I think we saw him grow up a lot. I think we saw him grow as a doctor. And I also think Niko Terho had some of his best performances this year. He really went through it with Simone when Katie died. And for Simone, she definitely has feelings to sort out. Wes has been such a casual thing, and he stated that from the very beginning. And also, he’s an intern, she’s a second year, and I think she had always thought that this was just fun, I don’t think she ever thought it was necessarily going to be more than that. And then suddenly, when he’s opening up to her and the finale and saying, Would you want to hang out more?, It’s like, oh, this kind of throws her wrench, because it’s a great looking guy, and he’s clearly a hard working doctor, and you’ve got some pain that she’s seen a little bit about his brother. And then she thought that Lucas was just a one night thing, because that’s what they said, it was mistakes. I think she’s confused. I don’t think she thought both of these options were on the table. ‘Grey’s Anatomy’: Jade Pettyjohn as Dani Disney/Anne Marie Fox New Interns: We Barely Know You DEADLINE: Grey’s introduced a couple of new interns this season but none of them made an impression. Dani had a very memorable first day, but then kind of disappeared. There was a young guy who barely had a couple of lines, two lines. MARINIS : Harrison Meade, yeah. DEADLINE: Any any plans for them to come back? MARINIS : I’d love to see them come back. They really were fun characters to interact with ours. I think just in the last two episodes we had a lot of creative ground to cover with our regulars.
