articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Destiny Jackson Destiny Jackson Crafts Editor, Awards @DestinyDreadful More Stories By Destiny CAPE’s 35th Anniversary Gala Raises $350K As Randall Park, Manny Jacinto, The Women Of ‘The Pitt’ & More Celebrate BTS’ RM Explores Fame, Identity & Curiosity In Debut Art Exhibition ‘Between You And Me’ At SFMOMA Noah Hawley On His Sentimental ‘Amazing Spider-Man #1000’ Comic Book Debut: “He’s The New York Mets Of Superheroes” View All October 15, 2026 6:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards Easterseals Southern California The inaugural Easterseals Disability Arts & Culture Awards ( DARCYS ) celebrated its first competitive class of winners Saturday, marking a new chapter for an awards program formerly known as the Media Access Awards, established in 1979. Co-produced by Easterseals Southern California and Film Independent, the ceremony recognized achievements in authentic disability representation across film, television and media, honoring the performers, filmmakers and storytellers working to reshape narratives in entertainment. Hosted by comedian and cerebral palsy advocate Tina Friml, the ceremony took place at The Barker Hangar in Santa Monica, combining humor with pointed calls for the film and television industry to invest more in recruiting disabled talent. Among the evening’s winners were PBS docuseries Renegades and HBO’s The Pitt , while Facts of Life star Geri Jewell received the inaugural DARCYS Legacy Award and Vincent Rutley took home the Christopher Reeve Emerging Talent Award. Related Stories Casting Casting Society Reveals Artios Awards Non-Film Nominees List: 'The Pitt', 'Heated Rivalry,' 'Pluribus' & More News CAPE's 35th Anniversary Gala Raises $350K As Randall Park, Manny Jacinto, The Women Of 'The Pitt' & More Celebrate Film Independent President Juan Devis, who took over in April this year, replacing acting president Brenda Robinson, who took over the role after the passing of Josh Welsh in January 2025, said that he was happy to continue the organization’s relationship with Easterseals, which has spanned more than a decade. “What we have been fighting for, for 42 years, is access and representation and pushing for the entire ecosystem to understand the value of what we bring,” Devis told Deadline. “Each year I think it becomes more evident that these types of events are just part of who we are.” Watch on Deadline Friml established the afternoon’s tone with an opening monologue that humorously described the gathering as a “truly mass disabling event.” Explaining the DARCYS acronym, she offered her own interpretation of the Y: “Yeah, you’re a good person for watching this.” The comedian also aimed at the healthcare industry, referencing The Pitt , one of the ceremony’s nominees. “The only way to get healthcare [these days] is by going to a fake hospital,” she said, before adding, “I’m still on a payment plan with Doc McStuffins, and that ended six years ago.” Among the biggest laughs of the ceremony came during Friml’s take on an awards-show in memoriam. Instead of honoring industry figures who had died, she eulogized disability tropes onscreen, including “Characters That Would Rather Die Than Be Disabled,” “The Miracle Cure,” “Cripping Up”—the practice of casting non-disabled actors in disabled roles—and “Teary Eyes.” On the first trope, Friml joked, “Sure, your career as a boxer may be over, but have you tried telemarketing?” For “Teary Eyes,” she delivered another punchline: “I don’t want Michael B. Jordan crying because a puppy is dead. I want him crying because a hot woman is still alive.” The humor gave way to a more urgent industry appeal when Amanda Upson, series producer of Renegades , accepted the award for Best Unscripted Series. The five-episode PBS short-film docuseries, hosted by award-winning musician and disability rights advocate Lachi, highlights the lives and cultural contributions of lesser-known historical figures with disabilities. Upson said the project grew into a vision shared by more than 50 disabled filmmakers, emphasizing the value of employing disabled talent both behind and in front of the camera.“We prove that empowering disabled talent behind the camera yields nuanced storytelling that outperforms traditional programming. Please check out their work and hire them,” she said. Upson also called on studios, streamers and foundations to provide more funding for disabled creators, citing approximately $45 million in funding cuts under the current administration and warning of the consequences for disabled artists and their ability to tell their stories. “In the face of near-invisible onscreen representation in this onslaught of systematic erasure, we need allies,” she said. “Studios and foundations, it is your turn to show up and invest mightily in us.” The Pitt won Best Scripted Series and Best Achievement in a Casting Ensemble, with cast members and casting director Cathy Sandrich using their acceptance speeches to highlight the importance of authentic representation. Tal Anderson, who appeared alongside fellow cast members Taylor Dearden, Jessica “Limer” Flores, Christopher Thornton and Diana Elizabeth Jordan, thanked Easterseals, HBO Max and Warner Bros. before recognizing the work of the series’ cast and crew. “Authentic representation is very, very important,” Anderson said. “And The Pitt has done such an amazing, spectacular job when it comes to authentic stories and representation.” Sandrich, accepting on behalf of the casting team, credited creators John Wells, R. Scott Gemmill and Noah Wyle with a commitment to telling stories that reflect the world and communities that have too often been underrepresented on television. “It was an enormous thrill for all of us to cast a disabled actor in a role that had not originally been conceived or written as a character with a disability,” she said. Sandrich also spoke about the importance of audiences seeing themselves reflected on screen, saying that the series’ commitment to authentic casting extended to changing a character’s gender to get the casting right. She praised the performances of Anderson, Thornton and Flores, and noted that the writers had also created roles specifically for disabled actors.“Their talents are undeniable,” Sandrich said. “We feel incredibly lucky to be given such extraordinary material, and we know that our writers, producers, and directors will continue their commitment to reflecting the truth and complexity of our world.” Rutley, recipient of the Christopher Reeve Emerging Talent Award, noted that the ceremony fell on his 41st birthday and offered encouragement to actors still waiting for their breakthrough. “I want to say today is my 41st birthday and I want to give a shout-out to all of the actors whose career didn’t blow up until after 40. I’ll see you on set,” he said. “It’s not a matter of if. It’s a matter of when. Your number will be called. Your name will be called. Today is my day. Tomorrow may be yours. Let’s ride. Love you.” Jewell, meanwhile, reflected on her career and the support of Norman Lear, who cast her in The Facts of Life after seeing her stand-up comedy routine. Jewell recalled meeting Lear in 1980 at the second annual Media Access Awards, where her friend, producer Fern Field, introduced them. “He said, ‘You’re real funny, kid, but you’re way before your time.’ I said, ‘So wait a couple months.’ He waited two months, and then he cast me on The Facts of Life ,” Jewell said. Accepting the Legacy Award at age 70, the comedian reflected on the significance of the recognition and encouraged others to believe in themselves. “I just want to say believe in yourself always, no matter what anybody else believes about you, because anybody who has believed negative confidence or what they think you can’t do, that’s not going to carry you in life. What’s going to kill you is what you believe about yourself, and never underestimate the power of the human spirit. Thank you, and God bless you.” Among those in attendance were Marlee Matlin, Wendi McLendon-Covey, Lisa Whelchel, John Ortiz, Marissa Bode, Cesily Collette Taylor, Scoot McNairy, Abby Elliott, Karen Pittman, Jamie Brewer, Victoria Mack, Daniel Monks, Jessy Yates, Matthew Reeve, Devis and Lynell Davis of Easterseals Southern California. The Inaugural Winners Are: Best Feature Horsegirls Director/Writer: Lauren Meyering Writer/Producer: Mackenzie Breeden Producers: Alix Madigan-Yorkin, Michael Sherman Featured Talent: Lillian Carrier, Matthew Schwab Best Performance in a Feature Anna Sargent, Take Me Home Best Documentary The Haunting of Pennhurst Directors/Producers: Mike Attie, Katarina Poljak, Nathan R. Stenberg Producer: Daniel J. Chalfen Best Scripted Series The Pitt Creator/Executive Producer: R. Scott Gemmill Executive Producers: Simran Baidwan, Michael Hissrich, Erin Jontow, Joe Sachs, John Wells, Noah Wyle Featured Talent: Tal Anderson, Jessica “Limer” Flores, Victoria Mack, Christopher Thornton Best Performance in a Scripted Series Daniel Monks, All Her Fault Best Unscripted Series Renegades Creator: Day Al-Mohamed Series Producer: Amanda Upson Executive Producers: Michael Kantor, Carrie Lozano, Charlotte Mangin Best Achievement in Casting Ensemble The Pitt Creator/Executive Producer: R. Scott Gemmill Casting Directors: Erica Berger, Cathy Sandrich Gelfond Featured Ensemble Cast: Tal Anderson, Jessica “Limer” Flores, Diana Elizabeth Jordan, Victoria Mack, Christopher Thornton Christopher Reeve Emerging Talent Award Vincent Rutley, Actor, Disability Influencer, Author Best Social Creator Cassidy Huff, @CassHuff Zendaya Set For Alex Garland’s Untitled Science Fiction Movie At A24 Key Takeaways Including ‘Baywatch’, YouTube, Skydance & Banijay UK Gov’t “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Sky-ITV Merger Netflix Cuts About 1,000 Jobs; VP Film, Directors & Managers Among Affected Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Rita Coburn & Jeffrey Wright To Bring Their Feature Doc ‘W.E.B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause’ To London
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac London’s Prince Charles Cinema Secures Future With New Long-Term Lease SXSW London Sets 2027 Festival Theme Thessaloniki: Adaptation Of Ioanna Karystiani’s ‘Swell’ Among 2026 Agora Works In Progress Titles View All October 15, 2026 6:55am Add us as a Google Preferred Source After its U.S. broadcast debut and theatrical roadshow tour, W .E.B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause , the new feature documentary by filmmaker Rita Coburn ( Marian Anderson: The Whole World in Her Hands ) on the life and legacy of the legendary writer W.E.B. Du Bois, is heading to the UK. Check out a trailer for the film above. The film will screen on Sunday, October 18, 2026, at the Charlotte Street Hotel in London. The screening will be followed by a conversation with Coburn and actor Jeffrey Wright , who narrates Du Bois’ work in the film. Directed, written, and produced by Coburn, W.E .B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause chronicles the extraordinary life and enduring legacy of Dr. William Edward Burghardt Du Bois, the scholar, historian, sociologist, author, activist, and Pan-Africanist whose work helped shape modern civil rights thought. Related Stories News Jeffrey Wright Taps His College Lacrosse Roots In Promo For PLL Championship Game On ABC News Dustin Hoffman, Juliette Binoche, Jeffrey Wright & Cinematographer Robert Richardson To Be Honored At Karlovy Vary Narrated by Viola Davis, the two-hour documentary explores Du Bois’ writing through dramatic readings by Common, Courtney B. Vance, and Wright. The readings are stitched together with rare archival footage, photographs, and historical documents. “I’m not prouder of any other piece that I’ve been a part of than I am to be a part of this,” Wright said of the film. Born in 1868, just five years after the Emancipation Proclamation, Du Bois lived through Reconstruction, Jim Crow, two World Wars, and the dawn of the modern Civil Rights Movement. The documentary follows his journey from groundbreaking academic achievement (Du Bois was the first African American to earn a Ph.D. from Harvard) to the founding of the NAACP, his international Pan-African work, and his death in Ghana in 1963, on the eve of the March on Washington. The documentary features commentary from leading historians, scholars, and cultural voices, including Raymond Arsenault, Karida Brown, Eric Foner, Henry Louis Gates Jr., Eddie S. Glaude Jr., Nikole Hannah-Jones, David Levering Lewis, and Imani Perry. Coburn’s previous documentaries include Maya Angelou: And Still I Rise and Marian Anderson: The Whole World in Her Hands . W.E .B. Du Bois: Rebel With A Cause screened on PBS in the U.S. in May and has since toured North America. articles.title: Fandango And Plex Team To Integrate Movie Ticket Sales Into Streaming
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Tumble In Technical Adjustment As Inflation, Interest Rate Jitters Roil Markets; Apple Regains $5 Trillion Market Cap Candle In The Wind: 5-Year-Old Media Firm Faces New Questions After Hello Sunshine Exit ‘Elsinore’ And ‘La Bola Negra’ Continue Awards Momentum With Wins At Hamptons Film Festival View All October 15, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source An example of the Fandango movie ticket buying feature on Plex's streaming platform Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Established streaming platform Plex has teamed up with Fandango to allow U.S. users to find showtimes and buy movie tickets as they browse and watch films. Founded in 2011, Plex offers a suite of streaming options from free, ad-supported live and on-demand programming to transactional VOD. Its discovery and community efforts have enabled the company to hold its own in a streaming world dominated by Roku, Amazon and other large-scale players. It operates in more than 180 countries and has more than 42 million monthly active users. Fandango has branched out from its origins under current owner Versant, adding general-entertainment streaming and other offerings, but it remains the leading online movie ticket seller. Related Stories News Discovery+ Raises Prices In One Of Skydance's First Streaming Moves After Merger Close Sports Disney+ To Stream Super Bowl For First Time & Carry Two 'Monday Night Football' Games This Season Especially as moviegoing has rebounded after Covid, a number of streamers have looked to unite the small and big screens in various ways. Roku in 2025 added a “coming soon to theaters” feature to its user experience, but it stopped short of enabling ticket purchases. Watch on Deadline Under the partnership, which lit up this week, Plex users in the U.S. will see a Fandango ticketing option on title pages for movies that are currently playing in theaters. The feature lets them click through to Fandango to find showtimes and buy tickets. The integration also includes direct attribution through measurement firm Kochava, which promises to give studios and advertisers greater visibility into how campaigns and audience engagement translate into ticket sales. As more of streaming has shifted toward advertising over the past few years, with all major streamers except Apple TV making it a major strategic focus, there has also been an increased emphasis on outcomes. In other words, knowing how ads prompt purchase decisions is even more of a brass ring than ever. The Letterboxd-like community aspect of Plex is a key element in the partnership. More than 45 million users create watchlists, the company says, giving it an advantage in terms of content discovery in a marketplace where average viewers struggle to find films and series of interest. “Our vision is to make Plex the place where people can discover what to watch, regardless of where that content lives. Fandango lets us extend that experience to all theatrical releases in the U.S., giving fans an easy way to act once they find a movie they want to see,” Scott Olechowski, co-founder and chief product officer of Plex, said in a statement. “Plex has a unique view into what movie fans are actively considering, from what they’re searching for to what they’re watching across services,” said Jerramy Hainline, EVP of Fandango. “By connecting those discovery signals with Fandango ticketing, we’re making it easier for fans to turn that interest into a trip to the theater, while giving studios and advertisers a more direct, measurable path to ticket sales.” Zendaya Set For Alex Garland’s Untitled Science Fiction Movie At A24 Key Takeaways Including ‘Baywatch’, YouTube, Skydance & Banijay UK Gov’t “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Sky-ITV Merger Netflix Cuts About 1,000 Jobs; VP Film, Directors & Managers Among Affected Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Disney+ And Hulu To Stream Pave Studios True-Crime Podcasts ‘Clues’ And ‘Mother Knows Murder’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Tumble In Technical Adjustment As Inflation, Interest Rate Jitters Roil Markets; Apple Regains $5 Trillion Market Cap Candle In The Wind: 5-Year-Old Media Firm Faces New Questions After Hello Sunshine Exit ‘Elsinore’ And ‘La Bola Negra’ Continue Awards Momentum With Wins At Hamptons Film Festival View All October 15, 2026 7:01am Add us as a Google Preferred Source EXCLUSIVE: Disney+ and Hulu will stream Pave Studios true-crime video podcasts Clues and Mother Knows Murder in exclusive windows before they go into wide release. The two titles, which are part of Pave’s Crime House sub-brand, are the company’s first to be picked up by a major streaming platform. Seeing the growth of YouTube in the living room, Netflix, HBO Max, Peacock and lately Disney+ have been looking to add podcast programming, which is seen as a budget-friendly way to boost view time and engagement. Pave Studios was founded by Max Cutler, who previously founded Parcast and went on to become an executive at Spotify after the streaming giant acquired his company. Related Stories News British True Crime Producer Association Welcomes Non-UK Producers For First Time Including America's Gennie Studios, My Entertainment and Texas Crew Legal FBI Adds Ex-Bellum Entertainment CEO To Most Wanted Fraudsters List; Offering $150K Reward For Info On Fugitive Mary Carole McDonnell Clues , hosted by Kaelyn Moore, will premiere next Tuesday. Mother Knows Murder , hosted by The Rookie: Feds and Claws star Niecy Nash and her daughter, actress Dia Nash, will debut on November 9. Watch on Deadline New episodes of both series will premiere on Disney+ and Hulu one day before they become available on other podcast platforms. Clues , which won a Webby earlier this year, promises to take viewers and listeners “deep into the world of notorious crimes and forensic breakthroughs.” New podcast Mother Knows Murder sees the Nashes breaking down an actual case as they recline in bed. Moore, known as the host of Heart Starts Pounding and the newly premiered Last Trace with Kaelyn Moore said Clues “was developed with a streaming audience in mind from day one. Our goal was to create a show with the production quality and storytelling that would stand naturally alongside other premium content on a streamer like Disney+ and Hulu.” Cutler said the Disney streaming deal is “proof” of the audience-friendly, creator-led approach of Crime House. Disney is “the first of many places we expect these stories to go,” he added. “As streaming platforms increasingly look to add premium content from talented creators, Pave is well-positioned to be a content collaborator to these companies, and we are excited to be working with Disney to bring our shows to their streaming viewers.” Zendaya Set For Alex Garland’s Untitled Science Fiction Movie At A24 Key Takeaways Including ‘Baywatch’, YouTube, Skydance & Banijay UK Gov’t “Minded To Intervene” Over $2.1B Sky-ITV Merger Netflix Cuts About 1,000 Jobs; VP Film, Directors & Managers Among Affected Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Ralph Fiennes Reunites With ‘Conclave’ Producer Tessa Ross & Studiocanal For Story Of Legendary Trainer Henry Cecil & Champion Horse Frankel
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Renny Harlin To Direct Prison Rescue Thriller ‘Evac’ ‘Red Sonja’ Producer Christa Campbell Launches Film & TV Company XTA Media Ron Perlman Lines Up Hemingway Movie & Updates On ‘Sons Of Anarchy’ Spinoff ‘Legends’, That Third ‘Hellboy’ Film & Next Steps For His Asylm Studios View All October 15, 2026 7:02am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ralph Fiennes, Henry Cecil, Frankel Lea Meienberg/Getty EXCLUSIVE : Three-time Oscar nominee Ralph Fiennes is reuniting with Conclave producer Tessa Ross and A Bigger Splash backer Studiocanal on Unbeaten , a biopic of legendary British horse racing trainer Henry Cecil and his most famous charge, Frankel. Fiennes will star as Cecil and serve as executive producer on the film, which is being lined up to shoot next year. The screenplay from Boardwalk Empire WGA nominee Bash Doran, the consulting producer on Beef , will be directed by BAFTA winner Nora Fingscheidt ( System Crasher ) with Tessa Ross producing for House Productions and Rory Aitken producing for Escapade Pictures. 42 will also produce. Pic has been developed with support from BBC Film and Conclave and The Zone Of Interest backer Access Entertainment. Related Stories News Ralph Fiennes, Colin Farrell & Wagner Moura Set For Comedy 'Art' From Director Fernando Meirelles & Screenwriter Christopher Hampton; 193 Launches For Cannes Market News Ralph Fiennes, Viggo Mortensen, Charlotte Rampling, Katherine Langford & More Set For István Szabó's 'Embers'; Filming Underway & First Looks Revealed With Embankment Aboard For Cannes Market Studiocanal is fully financing the film and will release theatrically in their territories of the UK, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, Benelux, Australia and New Zealand. Executive producers include Anna Marsh, Ron Halpern and Joe Naftalin for Studiocanal, as well as Fiennes and Doran. Studiocanal is handling worldwide sales. Watch on Deadline Cecil, knighted by the Queen in 2011, was one of horse racing’s most recognizable and celebrated global figures. A ten-time champion trainer in the UK, the undefeated Frankel was his most famous horse, winning ten Group 1 races. Many consider the horse to be the greatest European thoroughbred ever and a rival to U.S. champ Secretariat. The film will follow the late Cecil’s bittersweet final years as he triumphantly rebuilds his career and life after suffering personal heartbreak, tabloid scandal, health crises and falling out with the industry’s most powerful owner. The relationship with Frankel and rekindling with his third wife Jane McKeown were key to his return to the top of his sport. Tony Rushmer, author of The Triumph of Henry Cecil: The Authorised Biography , is a consultant on the film. Ralph Fiennes commented: “I knew nothing about the legendary Henry Cecil until I read Bash Doran’s screenplay. I was compelled and moved by it and by Henry’s story with the great horse Frankel. Henry was – and still is – a unique figure, complex and competitive in the very specific world of horse racing. I’m delighted to be reunited with Tessa Ross (producer) and to be working alongside Rory Aitken (producer) and Studiocanal. I’m particularly excited to be collaborating with Nora Fingscheidt. Her intensely immersive approach and desire for authenticity is inspiring. I was blown away by her film The Outrun .” The project marks the second collaboration between Berlin Silver Bear winner Fingscheidt and Euro studio Studiocanal following the UK release of BAFTA nominated The Outrun , starring Saoirse Ronan. Fiennes is repped by 42 Management and Production, CAA, and SOWDLLP. Fingscheidt is with Casarotto Ramsay & Associates, Ilene Feldman Management and Homebase. Doran is repped by UTA, Untitled and Schreck Rose. articles.title: Noah Centineo, Andrew Koji’s ‘Street Fighter’: First Reactions
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 12:36am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Noah Centineo, left, and Andrew Koji star in Street Fighter Paramount Pictures Logo text The first reactions to Paramount Pictures ‘ Street Fighter , the latest big screen adaptation of Capcom ‘s iconic video game, are out and, well, if you’re into dumb fun, then the film might be right up your alley. Street Fighter held its premiere in Los Angeles on Monday and Paramount also held a series of screenings this week, and allowed attendees to post brief social media reactions to the movie. The film hits theaters on Oct. 16, and critics’ reviews drop on Oct. 14. The synopsis for the film reads: “Set in 1993, estranged Street Fighters Ryu ( Andrew Koji ) and Ken Masters ( Noah Centineo ) are thrown back into combat when the mysterious Chun-Li ( Callina Liang ) recruits them for the next World Warrior Tournament: a brutal clash of fists, fate, and fury. But behind this battle royale lies a deadly conspiracy that forces them to face off against each other and the demons of their past. And if they don’t, it’s GAME OVER!” Related Stories Movies DC Studios' 'Clayface': First Reactions Movies Austin Abrams' 'Whalefall': First Reactions The full cast includes Joe “ Roman Reigns ” Anoa’i (Akuma), David Dastmalchian (M. Bison), Cody Rhodes (Guile), Eric André (Don Sauvage), Andrew Schulz (Dan Hibiki), Vidyut Jammwal (Dhalsim), Curtis Jackson aka 50 Cent (Balrog), Jason Momoa (Blanka), Don Lee (Gouken), Orville Peck (Vega), Olivier Richters (Zangief), Hirooki Goto (E. Honda), Mel Jarnson (Cammy), Rayna Vallandingham (Juli) and Alexander Volkanovski (Joe). Japanese-born American filmmaker Kitao Sakurai ( Beef , Bad Trip ) directed Street Fighter from a script by Dalan Musson ( Captain America: Brave New World ) and Gary Dauberman ( Annabelle, It, The Nun ). Below is a selection of the first reactions to Street Fighter. This might be a controversial thing to say but STREET FIGHTER (2026) often feels like a better successor to Mortal Kombat (1995) than either recent MK movies. One of the few big-budget projects that actually nails the vibe and energy of anime in live-action. — Andrew J. Salazar (@AndrewJ626) October 13, 2026 #StreetFighter is at its best when it doesn't take itself too seriously. Noah Centineo and Cody Rhodes got the memo, and as such they completely steal the film. Some great needle-drops too. Tbh I didn't really know what was going on though because I was crap at the game. pic.twitter.com/nyOIpuVgEL — Matt Rodgers @LFF (@MainstreamMatt) October 13, 2026 Kitao Sakurai’s #StreetFighter delivers a chaotic mixed bag of action, anime madness, epic characters, combos, and showdowns that don’t always land. However, Sakurai’s brilliance behind the camera has helped craft one of the year’s most visually stunning, fun blockbusters. pic.twitter.com/2Z0qCjFkTr — Phil Roberts (@philthecool) October 13, 2026 #StreetFighter is a winner. It’s a 90s throwback with visual nostalgia but also in its humor and selling of a hot cast. Koji’s Ryu; great. Cody is really funny. Schulz lands a lot, too. Roman’s scary good as Akuma, especially in voiceover. A silly, fun, and fearless good time. pic.twitter.com/I0kAeIqZxy — Brandon Davis (@BrandonDavisBD) October 13, 2026 Street Fighter has some good elements (2D animation is gorgeous & some entertaining fight sequences) but it ultimately falls flat. The cast does what they can with the (not great) dialogue but they look amazing! The jokes rarely land & it feels like half a movie. #StreetFighter pic.twitter.com/JXiLnX1QM7 — Tessa Smith – Mama's Geeky (@MamasGeeky) October 13, 2026 STREET FIGHTER is one sexy looking movie, from the mixed medium elements to its color-saturated palette to its impeccably attractive cast. Sadly, it literally loses the plot one too many times, and its fight scenes begin to feel less like a treat and more like a distraction. pic.twitter.com/qdjb9Ydaes — Bill Bria (@billbria) October 13, 2026 #StreetFighter is like Bloodsport on horse steroids, featuring some delightfully over-the-top, explosive action. It's also funny in a way that both homages the ridiculousness of 80s action movies while poking fun at the toxic machismo those same movies helped inspire. (1/2) pic.twitter.com/mugra84SkP — Chris Killian (@chriskillian) October 13, 2026 To call #StreetFighter a surprise would be a major understatement. It’s a wonderful accomplishment with tons of knockout performances, adapting the gonzo-style of the games in a very exciting way. My one complaint is that I wanted more! Cody Rhodes, your comedic future is bright pic.twitter.com/9qfqN5MBFW — joe 🇱🇧 🎃 (@hackermanjoe) October 13, 2026 #Streetfighter is a Ryu great time at the cinema. With crunching fights, swift quips and charismatic characters, the soul of the game fills every frame making it one of the most fun movies of the year. We hadouken great time. To the fans: "You Win PERFECT"🔥 @ParamountUK pic.twitter.com/YaRPokelu8 — All On The Board (@allontheboard) October 13, 2026 I am a grown ass woman and when I tell you I got legit GOOSEBUMPS from watching #StreetFighter – the way they honour the characters fighting moves and had over 100 Easter eggs as a nod to those who grew up playing it and beyond made me smile. Noah Centineo crushed as Ken! pic.twitter.com/gTRwePWufi — Maude Garrett (@maudegarrett) October 13, 2026 #StreetFighterMovie is KICK-ASS! It PUNCHES its way into one of the BEST FILMS you’ll see this year. Kitao Sakurai hits the perfect combo of style, energy, and fun. Noah Centineo and Andrew Koji land every move, while Callina Liang is a dream Chun-Li. This is the Street Fighter… pic.twitter.com/kAR5HQiuA3 — Anthony Gagliardi @ The Movie Podcast (@AJGaliardi) October 13, 2026 The Street Fighter movie is really fun and I’m going to watch it 8 more times Take that how yall wanna take it but I think all of yall will love how fun the movie is!!!! — Justin Wong (@JWonggg) October 13, 2026 #StreetFighter BRINGS THE GAME TO LIFE! It honours its legacy while delivering spectacular combat, GREAT music & plenty of laughs from start to finish. Callina Liang, Noah Centineo & Andrew Koji are ALL KILLING IT! One of my FAVOURITE movies of the year! 🥊🔥 pic.twitter.com/svRQFnNIv7 — Shahbaz • The Movie Podcast (@shayhbaz) October 13, 2026 STREET FIGHTER is ONE FOR THE FANS. It’s an ADRENALINE-PUMPING spectacle with a striking blend of animation and live-action visuals that keeps fans hooked with every fight. Kitao Sakurai works with a good cast and Callina Liang SHINES as Chun-Li. #StreetFighterMovie pic.twitter.com/AjpATPmal8 — Christopher Gallardo (@chrisagwrites) October 13, 2026 Just got out of the #streetfighter premiere, and I had a blast! The movie really captures the spirit of the games, with tons of fun references for fans. The soundtrack is awesome, and the 2D animation was a real highlight. articles.title: Stephen Chow’s ‘Shaolin Soccer’ Spinoff ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Sets U.S. Release After Dominating China’s Summer Box Office
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All October 14, 2026 4:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Kung Fu Soccer' Encore Films Stephen Chow ’s Kung Fu Soccer is heading to North American and British cinemas after finishing the summer as China’s biggest box office hit. Singapore-based distributor Encore Films said Wednesday that the comedy legend’s long-awaited Shaolin Soccer spinoff will open Oct. 23 in the U.S., Canada, U.K. and Ireland. The rollout will include the original-language version and a newly produced English dub featuring voice performances by Chow, Jimmy O. Yang and MC Jin. The release arrives in the 25th anniversary year of Shaolin Soccer , which became Hong Kong’s highest-grossing local film upon its 2001 release before developing a global cult following. Chow followed it with Kung Fu Hustle (2004), another genre-blending smash that earned more than $100 million worldwide and cemented his reputation as one of Hong Kong’s greatest comedy-action hitmakers. Related Stories Movies Tallinn Black Nights Fest Unveils Baltic Film Competition TV Mikael Marcimain's 'The Cold Song' Marks a Rare Return to Big Swing European TV Drama (Exclusive First Look) Timed at home to tap into this summer’s World Cup fever, Kung Fu Soccer earned approximately $344.4 million (RMB 2.315 billion) during China’s June 1-Aug. 31 summer moviegoing season, becoming the season’s biggest earner. Chow’s return helped lift the country’s summer theatrical revenue to $1.86 billion (RMB 12.498 billion), up 4.45 percent from a year earlier, according to figures from the China Film Administration and Maoyan Research Institute. Written and directed by Chow, Kung Fu Soccer marks his first feature behind the camera since 2019’s The New King of Comedy. Previously announced under the title Shaolin Women’s Soccer , the Hong Kong-China co-production reworks the original film’s martial-arts-meets-scrappy-sports-team premise around an all-female squad of underdogs. ‘Kung Fu Soccer’ Encore Films Zhang Xiaofei, the star of Chinese blockbuster Hi, Mom , plays the captain of the Emei Women’s Football Team, which enters the Supreme Invincible Cup determined to prove its doubters wrong. Dilraba Dilmurat plays the team’s star striker, while Lay Zhang serves as its kung fu mentor, helping the players combine martial arts mastery with soccer skills to overcome formidable opponents and setbacks on and off the field. The ensemble also includes Hong Kong screen icon Carina Lau, Japanese star Takeru Satoh, Sisley Choi, Louis Cheung, Yang and Jin. Encore acquired worldwide distribution rights outside mainland China from Chow’s production banner, The Star Overseas , in June. The October openings in the West follow the film’s earlier theatrical rollout across the Asia -Pacific region. “Following the tremendous response to Kung Fu Soccer across Asia and Oceania, we’re excited to bring the film to cinema audiences in the United States, Canada, United Kingdom and Ireland,” said Encore Films managing director Joyce Lee. “Stephen Chow’s films have always transcended language and cultural boundaries, bringing audiences together through his unique blend of action, comedy and heart,” she added. Encore has also completed a Cantonese dub. “Through a special English-dubbed version that makes the film more accessible to wider audiences, alongside a newly completed Cantonese-dubbed version whose voice cast will be announced soon, we hope to introduce Stephen Chow’s signature style of comedy to new audiences while reconnecting with longtime fans,” Lee said. THR

articles.title: Snoop Dogg’s Daughter Cori Broadus Debuts Character in Animated Series ‘Doggyland’ — Fulfilling a Childhood Dream (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All October 14, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Cori Broadus Mason Sexton Snoop Dogg ‘s daughter Cori Broadus has landed a role in Doggyland , the 3D animated children’s series co-created by her father, fulfilling a childhood dream. This marks the animated debut for Broadus, who plays Maxine, a confident, sassy labradoodle, in the series, which was co-created by Snoop Dogg, Emmy-nominated producer and creator Claude Brooks and Grammy-winning artist and producer October London. Doggyland also marks the beginning of a dream come true for the actress, who has harbored ambitions of becoming part of the world of children’s animation for two decades. As a youngster, she auditioned for the animated series The Backyardigans , but didn’t land the part. Now, she now only is voicing a character but also helped create her. Related Stories Music Tupac Murder Trial: Duane "Keffe D" Davis Sentenced 40 Years to Life in Prison TV Lucian Piane, Former 'RuPaul's Drag Race' Music Producer, Dies at 46 Broadus was hands-on throughout the character development process alongside Brooks, helping shape Maxine’s personality, look and spirit. The 27-year-old describes the character as “an extension of her inner child” — bold, playful, expressive and unapologetically herself. Maxine makes her first appearance in the music video for “You’re Enough,” the title track from Doggyland ’s latest full-length album. “I’m so excited to be part of Doggyland and bring Maxine to life,” Broadus said. “I love that she’s confident, a little sassy, and encourages kids to be themselves. ‘You’re Enough’ is such a special message because I want every kid to know they’re already perfect just being who they are.” Doggyland features a cast of dogs who sing, rap and dance to fun and educational songs that promote social-emotional and cognitive development in young children. Since its inception in 2022, Doggyland has produced a variety of educational songs about affirmations, letters, numbers, colors, animals, good habits and accepting others. The series focuses on delivering positive messages through music and storytelling, making learning an enjoyable experience for young viewers. The show focuses on a group of puppies led by Bow Wizzle (voiced by Snoop Dogg), who serves as the adult mentor to the rest of the cast, including Woofee (voiced by London), a smooth singer who is always cheering on his friends; Yap Yap, a high-spirited character who is known for her positive and cheery personality; Chow Wow, an empathic team player, and Barks-A-Locks, the curious one of the group who is always discovering new adventures. The show, which has been honored with an NAACP Image Award, Telly Award and Mom’s Choice Award, has amassed 1.3 million subscribers to the Doggyland YouTube channel. Said Snoop Dogg (whose real name is Calvin Broadus Jr.): “Looking back at where we are now with Doggyland and everything, it’s wild. When Cori was just an itty-bitty pup, she was always saying how she wanted to be part of a cartoon, and now here we are. Not only is she a cartoon character, but it’s one she helped create herself. What we’ve got here is a beautiful, full-circle moment, and I’m just so proud to be a part of it as her father. Maxine’s got Cori’s confidence, her personality and a little bit of that secret ingredient. I’m talking about sass. What’s even better is that Maxine is coming in hot with that patented Doggyland positive message. She’s here to let the kids know they should love themselves because you’re already enough just the way you are. Life lesson!” From left: October London, Snoop Dogg and Claude Brooks Chris Enriquez Broadus also is a professional DJ, performing under the moniker of Princess Broadus, and an entrepreneur, working in the worlds of beauty, fashion and music, with a growing focus on building brands and experiences that challenge traditional ideas of identity and culture. The message behind Maxine’s debut in “You’re Enough” is said be at the heart of Doggyland’s mission. Maxine encourages young viewers to embrace their individuality and reminds them that there is nothing they need to change about themselves in order to be worthy, lovable or enough. Maxine’s debut follows on the heels of the introduction of Banjo Bucky, voiced by country music singer Jake Tankersley. Watch the “You’re Enough” music video below. THR

articles.title: TikTok Inks Second Major Microdrama Deal, Partners With Made By Us Studios
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:30am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hannah Stocking, who will appear in the TikTok-Made By Us Studios coproduction ‘Player,’ attends the 97th Annual Oscars at Dolby Theatre in 2025. Photo by Monica Schipper/Getty Images TikTok is deepening its commitment to the microdrama format with a new deal aimed at producing vertical stories starring creators. The company has inked an agreement with Made By Us Studios, the production arm of major creator management company Made By All, to co-produce creator-led vertical series for TikTok and its microdrama app PineDrama. It’s the social media company’s second major microdrama deal after it announced a partnership with Issa Rae’s Hoorae Media to co-develop microseries in April. Mady By All, the management company behind Made By Us Studios, represents creators including Dhar Mann (who is already making his own microdramas with Fox and Holywater), One Battle After Another actor Teyana Taylor and YouTuber Adam Waheed. Made By Us Studios is led by former Range Partner Tanya Cohen as well as Made By All founder Leanne Perice and Made By Us president of production Nic Stanich. The deal was announced at MIPCOM, where TikTok unveiled the first two projects in the slate. Player is a romantic revenge thriller starring and co-executive produced by creator Hannah Stocking and additionally produced by Jonas Barnes. The series was written by Arun Blair-Mangat and Chela Reyna and directed by Louiza Zouzias. The Knock is described as a “genre microseries” (no word yet as to the precise genre) starring actor and content creator Adam Rose and actor Zaria Simone ( Pretty Little Liars: Original Sin ). It was created and directed by R.H. Stavis and is executive produced by Spooky Pictures (Watcher) alongside the musician Moby’s Little Walnut Productions. Moby also composed the series’ music. “Micro-series are pioneering a new language of storytelling,” TikTok’s global head of entertainment and micro-series Dawn Yang said in a statement about the deal. “We’re thrilled to partner with Made By Us on a slate that puts creators at the center, alongside established producers and industry talent, to tell stories designed for the feed from the start. This is an exciting step forward in our continued investment in the next generation of premium vertical storytelling on TikTok and PineDrama.” Made By Us Studios co-CEO Tanya Cohen said in a statement that vertical series are “the next evolution” for creators. “The opportunity isn’t to make smaller versions of television — it’s to build an entirely new premium storytelling language around the way audiences actually consume entertainment today,” Cohen added. “TikTok understands that behavior at a global scale, and together we have the opportunity to build franchises with creators who arrive with audience, community and cultural relevance already built in.” TikTok’s deal with Hoorae Media started big earlier in the year with Screen Time , a hit microdrama about a terrible double date. The series, starring Xavier Avila, Jasmine Luv, Eric C. Lynch and Brittney Jefferson, has earned nearly 580 million views globally since it premiered in April. THR

articles.title: Netflix Lays Off Around 1,000 Employees In Largest Cuts Since 2022
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Netflix staff were informed that the company will undergo significant layoffs Wednesday, a source confirms to The Hollywood Reporter , as the streaming giant seeks a reset amid efforts to keep its global business growing. The company is expected to cut about 6 percent of its workforce, or about 1,000 people, making it the largest staff reduction at the company since 2022. Netflix co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters announced the cuts in a memo to staff Wednesday morning. The company’s product, tech, legal and HR teams are said to have been particularly impacted. “Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources,” the co-CEOs wrote in the memo, which was obtained by THR . “Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full- year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high- impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors.” Ted Sarandos lamented at the Bloomberg Screentime summit on Sept. 30 that “overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster.” While the company continues to post robust profits, and remains the biggest player in subscription streaming, its viewing time has stagnated in recent months. With advertising one of the company’s growth areas, it needs to keep boosting that viewership engagement. Netflix has mostly avoided large-scale layoffs in recent years (the last major round of cuts was 2022 ), though the company has made adjustments on specific teams over time. The streaming giant is set to report its Q3 earnings next week, and the company is expected to share more information at that time. You can read the memo from Sarandos and Peters below. Team – We wanted to share that we are making a number of organizational changes and, as a result, we’ll be letting go of roughly 6% of our colleagues, with the greatest impact to our product, tech, legal, and HR teams. Decisions like these are never easy, and we don’t take them lightly. Our top priority today is to support those who are leaving Netflix. The process will vary somewhat by country, but leaders will be connecting with impacted employees soon. If you are leaving, please know that we will support you throughout this transition and make sure you have as much clarity and context as possible. We also want to say thank you. What you’ve built, and the care you brought to Netflix, have made a lasting difference and we will always be grateful. For the rest of the team, we know you have questions, too. Our mission – to entertain the world – is ambitious, and delivering on it requires us to be disciplined about where we prioritize our people and resources. Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full- year forecast. We’ll continue to invest aggressively in high- impact areas to improve our service and further drive growth and innovation. Doing that means making focused choices across the business so we can keep delivering for our members, partners, employees, and investors. We know changes like this are tough, but let’s stay focused. This is one of the most dynamic times in the history of entertainment – and it’s a moment perfectly suited to a company like ours that’s built at the intersection of technology and entertainment. Now it’s on us to step up and meet the moment, together, like we always do. Ted and Greg More to come. THR

articles.title: “Ruthless, Sexual Predator”: Russell Brand Rape Allegations Detailed as Prosecution Opens Case
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 6:56am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Russell Brand arriving at Southwark Crown Court on Oct. 14, 2026. Courtesy of Getty Russell Brand ‘s rape trial is officially underway at London’s Southwark Crown Court, with the prosecution describing the disgraced actor and comedian as a “ruthless” and “calculated” sexual predator. Eight men and four women are serving on the jury, the selection of which took place on Monday and Tuesday this week . On Wednesday, Brand was photographed arriving at the court with his wife, Laura, who was reported to have warmly smiled at him throughout the proceedings in court. Brand, best known for his roles on Big Brother’s Big Mouth and in Forgetting Sarah Marshall , is accused of three counts of rape, three charges of sexual assault and one allegation of indecent assault, with six women alleging crimes dating from 1999 to 2009. He denies all of them, telling a swarm of journalists on Wednesday morning: “I feel blessed. I feel, of course, concerned, but hopeful that this process will lead to good outcomes for everybody — that is my prayer.” (Since the allegations have come to light, Brand has turned to Christianity and been baptized.) Related Stories Movies 'Pop Pop,' 'Kidney' and 'Sounds of the Desert': Tallinn Sets Rebels With a Cause, Critics' Picks Programs Movies Stephen Chow's 'Shaolin Soccer' Spinoff 'Kung Fu Soccer' Sets U.S. Release After Dominating China's Summer Box Office Such was the heavy media presence at Southwark Crown Court that officials were forced to put journalists in an “overflow room” watching through video link, according to BBC News coverage . The BBC described Brand as remaining “very still” throughout Wednesday’s session, rubbing what looked like a pebble. Details of the claims against Brand were revealed by the prosecution, led by lawyer Riel Karmy-Jones. She kicked off by telling the jury that Brand was “ruthless and calculated” in his attacks against the six women, who “have never met each other, and who came forward independently of each other.” “His desire, strong desire for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious,” continued Karmy-Jones in her opening remarks. She called Brand a “sexual predator,” and cited the testimony of a former friend of his, who said Brand bragged to him that he was “a ladies man, a womaniser, and an expert pick-up artist.” According to this ex-acquaintance, Brand said he wanted to “bed 5,000 women” in his lifetime and had set himself “rules” to achieve this. The first complainant, whose claims Brand says are untrue, was said by the prosecution to have been raped by Brand. In her 20s at the time, Karmy-Jones said she was told “exactly what she needed to hear” and that he manipulated the situation to have sex with her “against her will.” This woman reportedly assumed Brand was gay and left the room to use the bathroom, telling him to make a cup of tea. When she emerged from the toilet, the prosecution said, Brand was partially undressed. “She was taken aback, she was shocked and didn’t really know what to do, and in her words, she froze a bit,” said Karmy-Jones. After the alleged rape, the prosecution says Brand was questioned by police. He said if it happened, he didn’t remember the incident. He said he did not remember the complainant’s name but “had never engaged in non-consensual activity.” The first complainant said she was “too scared to say anything” because of his celebrity status. The second complainant’s allegation of indecent assault dates back to 2001, when she was in her 30s and working at MTV. After admiring Brand’s T-shirt, the prosecution said that he offered to give the woman the item of clothing. “Make sure you give it a good wash first,” she says she told him, and offered to show Brand where the toilets were. Here, prosecutors say, he asked her to “come in” and grabbed her forearm. She began struggling and pulling back and described a “desperate, wide-eyed look on his face,” according to the BBC. Brand eventually relented and went into the toilet. A third complainant says she met Brand at a party in Soho, London in 2004. In the middle of a conversation, he lurched forward and grabbed her breasts and squeezed them with both hands, the prosecution told the jury. The woman was “shocked” and Brand had a “big, weird grin” on his face, she said. He grabbed her arm and pulled her toward the toilets. As they drove to another venue later in the evening, the prosecution says Brand pulled out his penis and told the complainant to “suck it.” Karmy-Jones said: “He simply laughed but appeared to accept her refusal.” The fourth complainant relates to an incident in 2004/2005 at Capital Radio, where Brand “grabbed” the woman’s face with both hands and pushed her up against a wall, the prosecution said. “He also grabbed her body, at her breasts, sides and buttocks — aggressively,” according to Karmy-Jones’ counsel. The complainant tried to push him off, but “he was too strong. […] He continued to kiss her on her face, and down her neck and onto her chest area, grabbing her bum and moving his mouth towards her cleavage, and grabbing her breast so hard that it was painful.” She was then able to push him away. A reminder: Brand denies all of these claims. The fifth complainant is reportedly the youngest of the women involved. She is said to have met Brand when he was performing at the Hammersmith Apollo in London in 2009. The incident began with consensual vaginal sex. “She said she did not really enjoy the experience. It felt very awkward and said it could have been anyone,” according to Karmy-Jones. Brand then raped her anally, while the woman asked him to stop, the jury was told. “She spent months and years blaming herself for what had happened, and became extremely anxious and continued to be unwell as a result,” said Karmy-Jones. Prosecutors say after this interaction that the woman received a text from Brand, to which she replied something along the lines of: “Why are you even messaging me?” He is said to have responded: “Because you’re dirty, and I wanna push you further.” The fifth complainant says told him: “I think you pushed me far enough — you treated me like an animal.” His response was immediate — “I’m sorry” — and she did not see or hear from Brand again, the jury heard. The prosecution said Brand was interviewed in relation to this offence, and provided a statement to police. “In that statement he set out that he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity, and that any accounts had been reinvented or imagined after a defamatory documentary and subsequent press reporting,” the counsel informed the court. The sixth complainant accused Brand of sexual assault. She says he demanded a massage when she was working with him in 2009. When she refused, Brand was described as becoming “unhappy” and said he would not complete the task otherwise. He is alleged to have fallen to his knees “and placed his head directly into her groin area.” The woman did complain at the time in 2009 and it “went higher up the ladder,” but she felt it wasn’t taken seriously. Brand denies every single allegation from these six women. Toward the end of Wednesday’s proceedings, the jury was again told that he “provided a prepared statement setting out that he has never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity, and that any accounts had been reinvented or imagined after a defamatory documentary and subsequent press reporting.” The trial could last up to 10 weeks. THR

articles.title: NBC’s ‘Dateline’ Headed to Canada
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 14, 2026 7:08am Add us as a Google Preferred Source From left: Longtime 'Dateline' correspondents Keith Morrison, Josh Mankiewicz and Andrea Canning, and the team’s senior executive producer, Liz Cole, photographed July 26 at PMC Studios in Los Angeles. Photographed by Joelle Grace Taylor NBC’s Dateline , the top-rated true crime series, is getting a Canadian spin-off series north of the border from Nov. 26. Keith Morrison, who got his start in journalism in his native Canada, will be in Toronto on Wednesday to tout the first international expansion of the Dateline franchise as part of a licensing deal with Rogers Studios. Dateline Canada on Citytv and Citytv+ will be hosted by Diana Swain, a former senior investigative correspondent for CBC News and host of The Investigators on the CBC News Network in Canada. She left Canada’s public broadcaster in 2024 after 33 years with the CBC, where Morrison in part perfected his iconic Dateline voice. After starting out in Canadian radio in the 1960s, Morrison joined the CTV Network in 1973 as a correspondent, producer and eventually a news anchor. In the early 1980s, Morrison became a co-host of the CBC Network’s The Journal flagship news and current affairs program. He joined NBC in January 1986 as co-anchor of the 5 p.m. and 11 p.m. news on KNBC-TV in Los Angeles. Dateline Canada will premiere with a two-hour special revisiting the wrongful conviction of Robert Baltovich, who was jailed for the murder of then-girlfriend Elizabeth Bain after her disappearance in 1990. Baltovich spent nine years in prison until 2000, before an eventual acquittal in 2008 after prosecutors dropped all charges. The Dateline Canada t eam, having reviewed police files on the case, claims to have uncovered an unreported police investigation. The long form true crime special will feature Baltovich, a retired Toronto Police officer who worked on the case and experts as it kicks off a Citytv series about sensational Canadian crimes and their victims and suspects. articles.title: Banana Republic Debuts First Scripted Microseries, an Office Comedy Starring Jack Innanen (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Katie Kilkenny Plus Icon Katie Kilkenny Enterprise Reporter, TV & Labor katiekilkenny7 Follow Sign Up View All October 14, 2026 7:09am Add us as a Google Preferred Source In ’The Agency,’ Jack Innanen plays four different employees of a fictional travel agency. Courtesy of Banana Republic Maybelline. Crocs. Marc Jacobs. These are just a few of the brands that have recently turned to the microdramas format to spin a yarn while, naturally, advertising their goods. And now, Banana Republic can be added to that list. The Gap-owned brand debuted the initial episode of its first scripted microdrama on Wednesday, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. The Agency stars Adults and Big Mistakes actor Jack Innanen as four different employees at an old-school, full-service travel agency called Travel & Tours that is rocked when a corporate suit (played by Innanen’s Big Mistakes costar Taylor Ortega) arrives to modernize it. Milo Tucker-Meyer plays the agency’s intern. Soapy, salacious and steamy romance stories might have popularized the microdrama format globally, but the first episode of The Agency positions the series as an office comedy with quick cuts and wink-wink lines and visuals. Innanen‘s characters in the five-episode series include a manager lacking confidence, a cocky cruise specialist, an adventure expert who deeply fears adventure and a Francophile who hasn‘t left American soil since the late ’90s. As one might expect, each of his characters are impeccably dressed in Banana Republic fits. Banana Republic chief marketing officer Meena Anvary said the brand decided to try the format in order to honor its “storytelling heritage.” Banana Republic Travel & Safari Clothing Company, as the company was initially titled, was the 1978 brainchild of a journalist and newspaper illustrator (founders Mel and Patricia Ziegler) whose early catalogs paired travel stories with apparel for sale. “We viewed this as a really interesting opportunity and way for us to hit on the nostalgia of the brand that people know and love and introduce the brand to new audiences via this TikTok series, bringing in some humor and storytelling to it as well,” Anvary said. Anvary was tightlipped about whether the brand will continue to invest in microseries or more entertainment moving forward, saying executives want to see how the audience engages with this first attempt first. But The Agency , at least, is part of a larger trend as Banana Republic’s parent company, Gap, Inc., has recently invested in building up an entertainment infrastructure amid a “fashiontainment” push. Earlier this year the company hired former Paramount exec Pam Kaufman as its chief entertainment officer and fellow Paramount alum Lourdes Arocho as head of licensing . The production company behind The Agency , Banana Republic Productions, dates back to earlier this year when the label collaborated with New York’s Explorers Club on a shortform docuseries about notable figures in science and exploration. “When we look at Gap Inc.‘s fashiontainment platform, it’s been a huge area of focus at the total company,” Anvary said. “For Banana in particular, it’s about us going back to our DNA and heritage and storytelling roots.” Entertainment is particularly valuable for marketing, Anvary added, because it helps keep a brand top of mind for consumers and encourages them to consider it when making purchasing decisions. The Agency , which has been produced especially for the TikTok audience but will be available on multiple social channels, will release episodes (and some behind-the-scenes material) weekly. Watch the series debut below. @bananarepublic Meet Travel & Tours. The last travel agency in New York City, where things have been done a certain way for a very long time. Until now. New faces, big ideas, and a staff that doesn’t exactly see eye to eye. The Agency, Episode 1 is here. ♬ original sound – Banana Republic – THR

articles.title: France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 5:16am PT France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE) Director Melina León was the first female Peruvian filmmaker to screen at Cannes' Directors' Fortnight with her debut feature 'Song Without a Name,' also handled by Luxbox By Anna Marie de la Fuente Plus Icon Anna Marie de la Fuente @adelafuente1 Latest France’s Luxbox, Spain’s Amore Cine Join Melina León’s Ventana Sur Proyecta Title ‘Portrait Huaco’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Maeve Jinkings Set for Women’s Convent-Prison Daring Escape Drama ‘Cabildo 71’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Cannes Festival Winning Producer Quijote Films Launches In-House Scripted Series Division (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Portrait Huaco' Credit: Natalia Grande France’s Luxbox and Spain’s Amore Cine have boarded the Peruvian drama “Portrait Huaco” (“Huaco retrato”) by Melina León, best known for her debut feature “Song Without a Name” (“Canción sin nombre”), which world premiered at the 2019 Cannes Directors’ Fortnight. “ After the incredible journey we shared with ‘Song Without a Name,’ I’m thrilled to continue collaborating with Melina, now as both international sales agent and co-producer,” said Luxbox’s Fiorella Moretti. Related Stories Skydance to Fully Reorganize International; Kevin MacLellan Will Not Lead Key Group 'Cyberpunk 2077' Movie in the Works at Paramount She added: “As a Peruvian, it is especially meaningful to help bring Gabriela Wiener’s bold and contemporary work to the screen through Melina’s singular vision. ‘Portrait Huaco’ explores questions at the heart of today’s conversations in a truly original way, and I have no doubt it will resonate with audiences around the world.” Popular on Variety For Paz Lázaro, who co-founded Amore Cine alongside Edson Sidonie (“Karnawal”) and Juan Pablo Felix (“Mil pedazos”), “Adapting Gabriela Wiener’s ‘Portrait Huaco’ means bringing to the screen a work that bridges Latin America and Spain, weaving colonialism, racism, identity and desire with a voice both ancient and radically contemporary.” “For Amore Cine, alongside our fellow producing partners, this is an opportunity to champion a film with international reach that challenges perspectives and reexamines our shared history.” Based on the autobiographical novel of the Peruvian author, the project participates in the 8th Proyecta Co-Production Forum at Ventana Sur , which takes place in Montevideo, Uruguay this year from Nov. 30 – Dec. 4. Amore Cine and Luxbox join Peru’s Mano de Obra Cine, led by Melissa Cordero, and La Vida Misma Films, which produced “Song Without a Name.” The story follows Gabriela who returns to Lima after her father dies. Back home, she discovers a book by her great-great-grandfather, Austrian explorer Charles Wiener. Her search into the family past becomes a reckoning with the lingering legacies of colonialism, internalized racism and abandonment. “’Portrait Huaco’ combines a distinctly Peruvian perspective with universal themes of identity, memory and colonial heritage. Under the direction of Melina León, the film seeks to preserve its cultural roots and Peruvian creative leadership while embracing an international scope through strategic co-production partnerships,” said Cordero. This is the second time for Mano de Obra to co-produce with Amore Cine. Late coming-of-age drama, “Ofelia,” currently in post,’ is a European-Latin American co-production that includes Amore, Argentina’s Bikini Films, Quijote Films of Chile, Brazil’s África Filmes and CUP Filmes, Spain’s Potenza Producciones and France’s Reality Films. Said Cordero: “I’m interested in producing auteur-driven films with a distinctive cinematic voice and strong cultural identity, as well as genre films that can connect with wider audiences. I’m particularly drawn to stories rooted in Peru and Latin America that explore universal themes, bringing local perspectives to an international audience.” “My near-term strategy is to strengthen Mano de Obra Cine’s position as a production company focused on feature films, building strategic co-production partnerships across Latin America and Europe. I aim to combine public and private financing with international partnerships and distribution opportunities to develop a sustainable slate of films with strong creative identities and international reach.” Director Melina León Fox News Expands Podcasts With All-Female ‘the Girls’ ‘48 Hours’ Expands Use of Video Podcasting With ‘Woman in the Woods’ Erin Andrews and Charissa Thompson Bring Their ‘Calm Down’ Podcast to Colin Cowherd’s The Volume Netflix Doubles Down on Podcasts: Streamer Orders New Shows From Katt Williams and Harlan Coben, Renews Full Slate of Originals Kerry Washington Expands ‘Street You Grew Up On’ Interview Series Into Weekly Ongoing Podcast From Her Simpson Street Production Company and Daylight Nile Rodgers to Host iHeartMedia’s ‘Before the Moment’ Podcast With Sienna Spiro, John Legend and More Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Forensic Files’ to Resume Original Production Amid the Streaming Boom for Vintage True Crime Series
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 5:30am PT ‘Forensic Files’ to Resume Original Production Amid the Streaming Boom for Vintage True Crime Series By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest ‘Forensic Files’ to Resume Original Production Amid the Streaming Boom for Vintage True Crime Series 2 hours ago Gary Cosay, Co-Founder of United Talent Agency, Dies at 92 2 hours ago ITV Studios Revs Up Scripted Dramas and Format Deals Amid Media Arm Sale Process 2 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Courtesy of Radial Entertainment “ Forensic Files ” is headed back to the lab. Radial Entertainment has teamed with Content Partners and ITV Studios to produce new episodes of the series that examines true crime tales from the perspective of scientific evidence and data analysis. The partners plan to deliver 20 fresh episodes that are expected to spark renewed interest and viewership of the “Forensic Files” library of 400 episodes. The series originated in the mid-1990s on Discovery’s TLC channel as “Medical Detectives.” It’s had numerous incarnations since then and is available on YouTube and other ad-supported streaming platforms. With the new batch of episodes, Radial and Content Partners will give the show a big SEO push across multiple digital platforms. Radial is in the midst of executing the same model on the unrelated unscripted series “The FBI Files.” Related Stories Bradley Cooper to Star as Duke in 'G.I. Joe' Reboot From Danny McBride A24 British Shows ‘It Gets Worse,’ ‘Major Players’ and ‘The Ministry of Time’ to Stream on Paramount+ in U.S. “ ‘Forensic Files’ helped define true crime television, and its focus on science and evidence continues to resonate with one of the most loyal audiences in the genre,” said David Buoymaster, Radial Entertainment’s chief investment officer. “Working with Content Partners to create new episodes is a natural next step in our relationship and an opportunity to build on the series’ legacy.” Popular on Variety Content Partners, the Los Angeles-based rights management firm and holding company, has owned “Forensic Files” since 2024. “From the outset, we saw an opportunity to build on the extraordinary history of ‘Forensic Files,’” said Scott Hemming, Content Partners’ executive VP. “Radial shares our commitment to the series, and with ITV America’s production expertise, we’re excited to bring audiences new investigations with the scientific detail and clarity that have made ‘Forensic Files’ a tentpole of unscripted television.” Buoymaster, Cristina Guggino and Katie Carroll are executive producers for Radial Entertainment, with Steve Kram, Hemming and John Mass serving as executive producers for Content Partners. For ITV America, exec producers are Shawn Witt, Jordana Hochman and Sumit David. “’Forensic Files’ stands alongside an elite few true crime franchises that have captivated viewers for decades,” said Witt. “We have enormous respect for what made the original so special and are excited to collaborate with Radial and Content Partners to carry that legacy forward with all-new episodes spotlighting fresh, compelling investigations.” Pablo Torre Sounds Off on the NBA’s Historic Ruling Against the Clippers, Kawhi Leonard and ESPN — and Teases His Next Big Sports Investigation Ethan Hawke Stars in Supernatural Horror Podcast ‘Midnight Radio’: ‘There’s an Intimacy to the Audio-Only Medium’ Kerry Washington Expands ‘Street You Grew Up On’ Interview Series Into Weekly Ongoing Podcast From Her Simpson Street Production Company and Daylight Hillary Clinton to Co-Host Podcast on 2026 Midterm Elections With Kara Swisher for Vox Media, Owned by James Murdoch Fox News Expands Podcasts With All-Female ‘the Girls’ Marvel Launches ‘Countdown to Avengers: Doomsday Official Podcast’ Ahead of Movie’s December Debut Loading comments...

articles.title: DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:00am PT DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest DataFuelX Launches Video Ad Marketplace That Taps 13 Different Publishers 1 hour ago Rachel Nichols Will Lead ‘The Story,’ a Daily Show From Sports Illustrated 2 hours ago Disney Broadens Super Bowl LXI Plans With Pat McAfee, Next-Gen Stats 3 days ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source Cheyne Gateley/VIP As media audiences fall apart, one analytics company hopes to knit some of them back together. DataFuelX , a company led by former TV-sales executives is launching DFX Marketplace, a new way for advertisers to connect to commercial inventory across multiple publishers with a single point of entry. The company, co-founded by Dan Aversano and Michael Strober, two sales veterans who have between them logged stints in senior roles at places like WarnerMedia, TelevisaUnivision, and Nexstar Media, among other companies, launches its offer at a moment when advertisers find themselves hard-pressed to reach large groups of consumers across linear or digital. Related Stories 'Cyberpunk 2077' Movie in the Works at Paramount Bradley Cooper to Star as Duke in 'G.I. Joe' Reboot From Danny McBride “We’re launching a cross-publisher marketplace for linear and CTV, supporting both demographic and audience-based buying. Agencies will have multiple ways to participate –through the platform, APIs or their own AI agents. Our platform will also support direct transaction across linear and digital as well as programmatic execution. This is a very unique model,” says Aversano during a recent email conversation. “Most solutions we have come across are primarily focused on digital-only programmatic transactions.” Popular on Variety The company says DFX Marketplace is supported by 13 premium video publishers representing nearly 40% of linear impressions across more than 50 networks, reaching 70% of U.S. TV households. Aversano declined to name the companies involved, but a Wednesday event unveiling the marketplace is slated to include executives from Fox Corp. and TelevisaUnivison, as well as Sean Cunningham, president and CEO of the VAB, a trade organization that represents most U.S. TV networks to the broader advertising market. The rise of such a marketplace comes as more commercial inventory, particularly that associated with streaming, is purchased in programmatic fashion, or via algorithms and software designed to seek out ad time that is seen by a particular audience niche, such as someone in a particular geographic region, for example, or someone who is likely to be in need of a car or baby products. DataFuelX said its new marketplace will support buying and selling done via agentic AI and will enable AI assistants and customer agents to work across all participating publishers through a single connection. The marketplace is being built to support agentic buying and selling, enabling DFX AI assistants and approved customer agents to work across participating publishers through a single connection while preserving human control over strategy and final decisions. Participants in the new marketplace will be able to keep tabs on planning, activation, optimization and other tasks all under one system. “Premium video remains one of the most powerful ways for advertisers to build reach, but the complexity of differentiating true premium video across an increasingly expanding, but diluted ad inventory infrastructure has limited the growth and its share of overall video ad dollars,” says Cunningham, in a statement. “DFX Marketplace represents an important step toward modernizing that infrastructure for cross-publisher and cross-platform, using intelligence, automation and AI to make premium video easier to access, transact and optimize at scale.” The company says its platform is already used by major publishers and has supported more than $300 million in media transactions. articles.title: ‘Clayface’ First Reactions Praise DC Body Horror as ‘Freakishly Awesome’ and ‘Loaded With Brutal Scenes’
articles.full_text: Oct 14, 2026 6:03am PT ‘Clayface’ First Reactions Praise DC Body Horror as ‘Freakishly Awesome’ and ‘Loaded With Brutal Scenes’ By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest ‘Clayface’ First Reactions Praise DC Body Horror as ‘Freakishly Awesome’ and ‘Loaded With Brutal Scenes’ 49 minutes ago Aaron Sorkin Thinks About Reviving ‘The West Wing’ for a ‘Couple of Seconds Every Day’: ‘I Miss It’ 4 hours ago ‘Tommy & Tuppence’ Stars Josh Dylan and Antonia Thomas on That ‘Intense’ Finale, Why the Detective Duo ‘Keep Missing Each Other’ Romantically and a Potential Season 2 15 hours ago See All Add us as a Google Preferred Source ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection The first reactions are in for DC Comics ‘ body horror thriller “ Clayface ,” with journalists and fans calling it “freakishly awesome” and “everything you want from a villain-led movie.” Directed by “Speak No Evil” filmmaker James Watkins from a screenplay co-written by “The Haunting of Hill House” creator Mike Flanagan , “Clayface” stars Tom Rhys Harries as the DC Universe character and Batman adversary. Clayface is Matt Hagen, an actor whose face is disfigured by a local mob boss. Desperate, he volunteers as a test subject for scientist Dr. Caitlyn Corr (Naomi Ackie), who transforms his body into clay and causes him to lose his sanity. Related Stories 'Ted Lasso' Theme Song Switch: Why Brandi Carlile Took Over for Marcus Mumford in Season 4 Finale — and Is It a Permanent Change? Kelly Clarkson Joins Brandi Carlile's Girls Just Wanna Weekend Festival as Co-Headliner “‘Clayface’ was fantastic,” Collider editor-in-chief Steven Weintraub wrote on X. “An awesome addition to the DCU that doesn’t require any knowledge of DC to enjoy. It’s hard R and loaded with brutal scenes that really surprised me. Audience freaked out a few times during my screening to what was being depicted on screen.” Popular on Variety Film critic Peter Gray added that it “has that comic book flair” but that doesn’t “diminish how BRUTAL it is! Dark, violent, with little levity to offset the nastiness, this is an exciting addition to Gunn’s DCU.” He added that Harries “brings equal boyish charm and quiet menace to the role.” YouTuber Brandon Davis called the film “freakishly awesome” and praised Watkins for getting “creative with Clayface’s abilities.” He added that Harries “is a star” and “kills it.” With a story by Flanagan and screenplay co-written by Flanagan and Hossein Amini, “Clayface” also stars David Dencik, Max Minghella and Eddie Marsan and is produced by “The Batman” director Matt Reeves alongside James Gunn and Peter Safran. It’s set to hit U.S. theaters via Warner Bros . on Oct. 23. See all the first reactions below. Clayface was fantastic.
