articles.title: International Insider: ‘Doctor Who’ Regeneration Underway; MIPCOM Preview; Busan Takeaways
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ASOB Media Offers MIPCOM Buyers ‘A Study On Beauty’ Icelandic Drama ‘Elma’ Set For Siminn Bow As Glassriver Debuts ‘NCU’ At MIPCOM Reelz To Follow The CW’s ‘Police 24/7’; Sky Remains On The Case For Season 3 View All October 9, 2026 8:05am Add us as a Google Preferred Source The 15th Doctor regenerates into Billie Piper on 'Doctor Who' Disney+ Don’t blink, Insiders. Jesse Whittock is here with you in the week Skydance took over Warner Bros. Discovery and Doctor Who began planning for the future. Here we go. Ready? ‘Doctor Who’ Regeneration Underway David Tennant in ‘Doctor Who’ BBC Studios Sonic screwdrivers at the ready: Stories about the Good Doctor with a question mark for a real name always do well on Deadline, and so it proved again with Jake and Max’s top scoop on the latest regeneration of the British sci-fi franchise. After the recent Russell T. Davies seasons were not brilliantly received by fans, Disney exited the show and rights owner BBC Studios (BBCS) put its future out to tender, asking the UK production community for their visions of a reimagined Doctor Who . One eye-catching bid in the “bake-off-style” process saw Line of Duty creator Jed Mercurio and his Hat Trick Mercurio indie throw its hat in the ring. Elsewhere, Line of Duty maker World Productions is down as is Criminal Record ‘s STV Studios, along with a pair of unnamed BBCS-owned labels , proving that while the show has become divisive and a difficult beast to tame, there will always be love for The Doc on British shores. Each producer sees a different future, with STV Studios’ plan being to move production north of the English border into Scotland for the first time in the franchise’s history. The deadline for pitches has now passed and our list isn’t exhaustive – another Scottish bid is rumored, for example. A24 UK, Playground, Mammoth Screen, New Pictures, Big Talk Studios, Expectation and Quay Street have, however, counted themselves out. The new series will premiere on BBC screens during the 2028/29 season, with the winner of the pitch selected in March. For the BBC, the news came in the same week that Director General Matt Brittin urged his staff to channel Elvis, i.e. “a little less conversation, a little more action.” Brittin wants the British public broadcaster to move faster, try more things and hone specialisms quicker. How it does that in a world of declining funding and ultra-competition isn’t clear. As some pretty snarky below-the-line comments on Jake’s scoop revealed, some aren’t convinced. “Be more Elvis, you mean, dead?” read one stinging post. Ouch. With Brittin also telling staff he’s been meeting U.S. streamers, it’s been another intriguing week at the BBC. Related Stories News ASOB Media Offers MIPCOM Buyers 'A Study On Beauty' News Icelandic Drama 'Elma' Set For Siminn Bow As Glassriver Debuts 'NCU' At MIPCOM MIPCOM Preview VALERY HACHE/AFP via Getty Images Croisetting the scene: As you read this, plenty of creatives, sellers and execs will be jumping on planes to Nice Airport for this year’s MIPCOM Cannes , which officially starts Monday. For me, it will be the 4,253,749th MIP in a row. The French event will be seeking to burnish its reputation as international TV’s biggest annual market and conference, and to do that, it needs the best new shows. This week, we dropped our latest Deadline Dozen run downs of the major titles launching at MIPCOM – and you can read about the unscripted 12 here and the scripted batch here . We’ve been ramping up coverage over the last few weeks and will be out in Cannes in force, scribbling up breaking news stories from keynotes and the Croisette, and on stage at several high-profile events and screenings. You’ll be able to read all the coverage by following this MIPCOM link (plenty of scoops there already), but for now, enjoy an interview with Banijay Deputy CEO Jane Turton , another with the bosses at Heated Rivalry streamer Crave and this chat with the producers of buzzy Princess Diana doc Diana Unheard. Watch on Deadline The Deadline Interview: Vikram Malhotra ‘Subedaar’, ‘Maa Behen’ and ‘Daldal’ Vikram Malhotra (inset) Netflix/Prime Video/Abundandia Entertainment For all the talk of AI use, whether the U.S. studios are secretly using it to cut production costs or if Tilly Norwood will ever win an Oscar, there are surprisingly few legacy players who have opened AI-led studios. Vikram Malhotra from India’s Abundantia Entertainment , is one of those few. In our exclusive interview, he explains how staying ahead of the curve means putting his money where his mouth is on “human-first and AI-empowered” creative arm Abundantia AiOn. In 2027, he reveals, this will become a “fully fledged, fully native” standalone AI studio. What does that mean exactly? Click through to find out, along with insights into how Malhotra tempted Anil Kapoor back into an action movie lead and how the market is changing before our eyes. >>> Read the Interview Based In Busan Woohae Cho/Getty Images Korea prospects: Liz Shackleton was in Korea for the Busan International Film Festival (the fantastically-acronymed BIFF) this week, where she heard from the likes of Michelle Yeoh, Maggie Gyllenhaal and Alfonso and Jonas Cuaron, along with Chinese director and Busan jury president Zhang Yimou and fest director Jung Hanseok. Everything Everywhere All at Once star Yeoh, in town for the first time in 15 years to receive an Asian Filmmaker of the Year award, told a press conference about her experiences making Prime Video series Blade Runner 2099 and returning to Asian cinema. The likes of Fan Bingbing and Charlotte Gainsbourg hit the red carpet, along with the stars of The Table: Day and Night , the festival’s opening night screening, who you can see above. All your BIFF needs are here . The Essentials Atwood Films, Sky Films 🌶️ Hot One : Turkish star Hande Erçel has been unveiled as the lead actress in Iranian director and screenwriter Nadar Saeivar’s upcoming Germany-set drama Diaspora . 🌶️ Another : Niamh Algar and French cinema legend Fanny Ardant are leading a thriller series set in an AI-controlled, high-end luxury resort, a rare example of a UK-Greece co-production. 🌶️ Cheeky triple: World War Z and Quantum of Solace director Marc Forster is turning his hand to TV by directing an adaptation of Jamie Scallion’s buzzy upcoming thriller Nines . 🦌 ‘Reindeer’ row reignites: After legal proceedings were dormant for more than a year, Netflix has suffered a blow in its efforts to get Fiona Harvey‘s lawsuit over Baby Reindeer thrown out of court. 💼 New job: David Brindley has been confirmed as the new Director of Programmes at the UK’s Channel 4. 🕴️ Agents: Joe Sugg and Caspar Lee’s agency MVE Management has hired agents from CAA and WME in the U.S., bringing in Carter Broussard, Cara Best and Ben Greenberger. 🛥️ Setting sail: Australian bestseller The Titanic Story of Evelyn is charting a course to TV with newly minted banner The Set Up collaborating with author Lisa Wilkinson for the adaptation. ⛺ Fest latest: Qatar’s Doha Film Festival has unveiled the International Feature Film Competition lineup for its second edition, which is due to take place this November. 🤝 Done deal: Anora maker FilmNation has partnered with nascent British indie High Road Entertainment to develop co-productions. Photo Of The Week Charlie McCaldwell/Getty Images Day In Court – Russell Brand attends a pre-hearing trial at Southwark Crown Court before the case kicks off next week in earnest . The former TV presenter denies charges of rape, sexual assault and indecent assault. articles.title: Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Starring In Addiction Dramedy Series ‘Quitters’ For Angel
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Starring In Addiction Dramedy Series ‘Quitters’ For Angel Faith & Family Outfit Ark Clb Launches With Former eOne Exec Venice Winner ‘A Day In The Life Of Jo: Chapter Phaedra’ Gets North American Deal With 1-2 Special View All October 9, 2026 8:08am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Craig Ferguson & Megyn Price Ian Cunningham/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE : Former late-night host Craig Ferguson ( The Late Late Show with Craig Ferguson ) and The Ranch and Rules Of Engagement star Megyn Price have been set to star in Quitters , a half-hour dramedy series whose eight-episode first season is now in production in Utah. The series will be distributed by Angel , the distributor-producer best known for its faith-leaning content. The synopsis reads: “After Liza (Price), an upbeat soccer mom, falls into the cycle of opioid addiction, she lands at Unplugged, an unconventional recovery center run by Nick McTavers (Ferguson), a former heavy-metal legend. To put her life back on track, Liza must learn to rely on an eclectic family of patients and counselors who help her navigate the long road of recovery.” Related Stories Acquisitions Angel Acquires Michael Keaton-Morgan Freeman Western 'Rode To Ruin', Launches Sales Arm Ahead Of TIFF Market News State Department To Screen 'Young Washington' At U.S. Embassies Producers are Eric Handler, Chase Vergari and Ibrahim Mohammed. It is being directed by Darrin “Fletch” Fletcher and Chet Thomas and produced through their FletChet Entertainment banner, which recently produced the Lionsgate title The Best Christmas Pageant Ever. Quitters was written and created by Dave Parkin. Watch on Deadline Executive producers on the series include Chet Thomas, Darrin Fletcher, Eric Handler, Chase Vergari, Ibrahim Mohammed, series writer and creator Dave Parkin, RoboCop and Starship Troopers writer Edward Neumeier, Rob Gibbs, HR Brown and Alema Harrington. Handler brought the package together and paired it with financing from Script 2 Screen Capital. Handler most recently served as executive producer on the Walton Goggins action-comedy Mister , the Samuel L. Jackson action film The Beast , and Maserati: The Brothers , starring Anthony Hopkins and Al Pacino. Vergari and Mohammed produce and finance through Script 2 Screen Capital, whose credits include By Any Means (Paramount Pictures), starring Mark Wahlberg, and Iconoclast , which premiered at the 2026 Tribeca Film Festival. “This is a world I have wanted to explore for as long as I can remember, and Nick McTavers is a character I understand in my bones. There is real truth in this story, and a lot of heart and humor too, and that is exactly the kind of thing I want to be making,” commented How To Train Your Dragon voice star Ferguson who has previously discussed his own addiction issues in his late 20s. “I’m so grateful for the opportunity to help tell Liza’s story. She’s funny and stubborn and heartbreakingly human, and her struggles through addiction and recovery are shared by so many people. My goal is to shed some light, hope and humor onto this issue, and remove the shame that acts as a barrier to asking for help,” added Megyn Price. “Ten years ago, HR and Alema, who have walked the road of addiction and recovery themselves, brought us this idea. Having Craig and Megyn lead the series now is the culmination of everything we’ve worked toward,” said Darrin Fletcher. Chet Thomas commented: “We want anyone struggling with addiction to know help is out there, and their families to understand what their loved ones are facing. We tell that story honestly but with the humor that so often keeps the people going through it alive.” “Nobody could play Nick McTavers the way Craig Ferguson does, and Megyn is going to break your heart and make you laugh in the same scene. I go back decades with Chet, from our DreamWorks days, and with Craig too, so having them both come together on a show that inspires hope means everything,” said producer Eric Handler. Angel’s slate of original series also includes the post-apocalyptic drama Homestead: The Series , now in its second season. Ferguson is represented by WME, Vault Entertainment, and Gang, Tyre. Price is represented by Independent Artist Group, Leslie Allan-Rice Management, and Myman Greenspan. articles.title: Court TV Parent Law & Crime Ups Rachel Stockman To CEO; Founder Dan Abrams To Remain As Chairman
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Rebound After David Ellison And Top Execs Ring Opening Bell At New York Stock Exchange Joe Rogan Sets Multi-Year Extension With Spotify Eyeing More ‘Minecrafts’ And ‘Fallouts’, Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games View All October 9, 2026 8:17am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rachel Stockman, CEO of Law & Crime and Court TV Courtesy Rachel Stockman , longtime president of Court TV parent Law & Crime, is becoming CEO of the company as founder Dan Abrams steps down from the role. Abrams, chief legal analyst for ABC News, is staying on as chairman of Law & Crime. The company has been owned since 2023 by Jellysmack , a holding company for creator-led media businesses. Court TV, a digitally focused revival of the longtime cable TV mainstay known for gavel-to-gavel trial coverage, was sold by E.W. Scripps to Law & Crime earlier this year. Related Stories Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs Executives Ex-Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz In Line For High-Level Paramount Exec Post Stockman has been at Law & Crime for more than a decade, initially serving as editor-in-chief before a promotion to president. Along the way, she has also executive produced dozens of documentaries and series for Netflix, Paramount+, A&E, Fox Nation and HBO Max/ID. Earlier this fall, she oversaw the launch of “Partners in Crime,” a programming initiative featuring six original series developed with some of true crime’s most-followed creators. Watch on Deadline After spearheading the acquisition of Court TV, Stockman has built Law & Crime into a top true-crime brand. It operates four FAST channels and multiple subscription channels on YouTube, which have collectively generated billions of video views and more than 700 million hours watched across platforms over the past year, according to the company. “Rachel’s ability to direct the business at the highest level while also making so many smart, granular decisions has helped lead us to where we are today,” Abrams said in a statement. “She has truly earned this. I can’t wait to see where she takes us next.” Stockman praised the “extraordinary team” at Law & Crime. “I’m honored to lead this next chapter as we continue to push boundaries, embrace bold ideas and help shape the future of media,” she said. articles.title: Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later: Part III’ Is Currently On The “Back Burner”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later: Part III’ Is Currently On The “Back Burner” TIFF Lightbox Sets Animation Season Guest Curated By Masaaki Yuasa Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc ‘Dependence’ Back Home To London — LFF View All October 9, 2026 8:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ralph Fiennes in '28 Years Later: The Bone Temple' Miya Mizuno/Sony “It’s on the back burner at the moment,” Danny Boyle concluded this afternoon during a Q&A at the London Film Festival when asked about the current status of 28 Years Later: Part III . The veteran British filmmaker continued to say he “hopes” the film will be made if financing can be locked in. Boyle added that the pause in the film series has also been prompted by Alex Garland’s busy schedule. “Alex has been off doing his own film, which is a huge project,” Boyle said. Alex Garland is currently working on A24’s big-screen adaptation of the hit video game Elden Ring. Related Stories News 'NAZA' Producer James Wilson Addresses "Hysterical, Vituperative" Israeli Government Backlash Against Directors News Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc 'Dependence' Back Home To London -- LFF Boyle is at the LFF this year with his latest feature Ink , which screens as one of the festival’s headline galas. Directed by Boyle from a screenplay written by James Graham (Dear England), the film charts the rise of the UK’s notorious tabloid newspaper The Sun in the 1970s under the editorship of Larry Lamb, after he was poached from the Daily Mirror in 1969 by then budding media mogul Rupert Murdoch. Watch on Deadline Boyle told the LFF crowd that he and his producing team felt specific “pressures” while trying to finance Ink. “We found it very difficult to raise the money for this,” Boyle said. “I have no idea why. They didn’t say why they wouldn’t give us the money. We managed to get the money from StudioCanal. They didn’t give us enough money, but they were brave, whereas a lot of people wouldn’t give us the money.” Boyle said his personal theory about why StudioCanal coughed up the money for Ink is because his producer, Tessa Ross, previously worked on the box office hit Conclave with the company. “She’d made them so much money,” Boyle said, adding he was very lucky that “StudioCanal hooked up with Netflix and they bought it for America. They’ve been really good partners because there have been pressures.” Boyle said he will next work on an Antarctica-set film if he can raise the budget. “That’s the next priority,” he said. The LFF runs until October 18. articles.title: Focus Features & Blumhouse-Atomic Monster Snap Up Micro-Budget Horror Film ‘Play House’ From Nicolas Curcio
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Robby Hoffman Sets Second Netflix Special Paramount Teaming With Medieval Times On Family Comedy Movie; Eric Appel Directing From Script By Blaise Hemingway Paul Walter Hauser Set For Crime Drama ‘Garden City’ From John Curran, Magenta Light Studios View All October 9, 2026 8:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nicolas Curcio Gilbert Flores/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster have snapped up Play House , a micro-budget horror film from Nicolas Curcio , in a competitive situation, sources tell Deadline. We’re told this was a seven-figure deal for worldwide rights, excluding Latin America and India. This is a major coup for Curcio’s debut feature, a film made for not much more than $100,000 — roughly 13% of the reported budget of Curry Barker’s low-budget Focus phenomenon Obsession . Related Stories News Top 50 Halloween Movies Photo Gallery: Creepy Classics From ‘Psycho,’ ‘The Shining’ To ‘Obsession’ & ‘Get Out’ News Horror Movies’ Next Wave: What’s Coming In 2026, From Auteur Nightmares To Indie Breakouts Curcio set the project in motion last September after winning the inaugural Fantastic Pitches contest, a micro-budget genre initiative spearheaded by Alamo Drafthouse’s Fantastic Fest and indie studio Chroma, thereby securing funding and distribution. He returned to Fantastic Fest to premiere the film last month. Play House will release in theaters in 2027, with Universal Pictures International handling international distribution. Watch on Deadline Written by Curcio and wife/creative partner Kirby Gladstein, the film follows Elliott (Will Harrison), who while renovating a dilapidated house to win back his ex, discovers VHS tapes of an unaired children’s TV show which begins to seep into his life, threatening his last chance at reconciliation. Pic’s cast also includes Jessica Sula, Jordan Gonzalez, and James Urbaniak. Curcio and Gladstein produced for Skinny Ghost, alongside Ben Gojer, Jack Forbes, and Derek Tramont. Exec producers include Ahbra Perry via Chroma, Daniel Levin via Narrative, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath of Divide/Conquer, and Jason Blum of Blumhouse Atomic-Monster. NPerry repped the film for sales via Narrative Distribution. While Universal art-house label Focus Features has not historically been known as a major horror distributor, outside of recent work with Robert Eggers on titles like Nosferatu and the upcoming Werwulf , they’re now aggressively expanding into the space as supporters of emerging filmmakers, after seeing Obsession break out as their highest-grossing film ever at over $522M worldwide. Divide/Conquer’s Hendricks and Gilreath — EPs on Play House — previously brought that film to Blum, who set it up at Focus, along with his follow-up Anything but Ghosts , dated for May 7, 2027. You can expect much more to come from the collaboration between Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster. Most recently, they announced their partnership on director Josh Giuliano’s Occupant following the buzzy TIFF debut of his first horror film, River . Curcio is a rising filmmaker who recently set up his high-concept thriller spec Sweet Spot , penned with Gladstein, at Paramount Primal, as we first reported. A writer on Sony Pictures Animation’s hit GOAT , he has developed projects for multiple studios, including a live-action Magic School Bus for Universal and an adaptation of Planet of the Nerds for Paramount. His script Barron made the Black List in 2019. Curcio is also known for running a popular screenwriting TikTok account with nearly 200K followers and over 10M likes, and has partnered with studios like Neon, A24 and Paramount to promote films. He is repped by 3 Arts, UTA, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman. articles.title: Netflix’s ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 Casts Peter Ingalls, Mrs. Nelson & More As Production Wraps
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Owen Wilson’s Pryce Cahill Makes Play At U.S. Open In ‘Stick’ Season 2 Trailer All The Songs In ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 So Far ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Finale Recap: The Last Match Of The Season & A Shareholders’ Showdown View All October 9, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clockwise from top left: David Wronko, Elyse Levesque, Erik Althavale, Graham Harvey, Jacinta Forest Lewitski, Lyla Porter-Follows, Martin Roach, Paul Greene, Ryan Northcott and Scott Porter Cameron Radice/Jenna Berman/Kevin McIntyre/Monica Gosselin/Benjamin Laird/Sarah Jane Murray/Time Leyes/Laurent Levy/Kevin Clarke/Malik Daniels The second season of Netflix ’s Little House on the Prairie reimagining has rounded out its ensemble cast with a wrap on production. Ten names have boarded Season 2: David Wronko , Erik Athaval ( American Hostage ), Elyse Levesque ( Ready or Not, Orphan Black ), Graham Harvey ( The Night Agent ), Jacinta Forest Lewitski , Lyla Porter-Follows ( High Potential ), Martin Roach ( Cross ), Paul Greene ( When Calls The Heart, Autumn and the Black Jaguar ), Ryan Northcott ( Anna Pigeon) and Scott Porter ( Ginny & Georgia, Friday Night Lights, Hart of Dixie ). Related Stories Casting Rachelle Lefevre & Charlotte Sullivan Join ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 At Netflix Books Everything We Know About Netflix’s ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 So Far Athavale will portray energetic minister Reverend Alden, who leads Walnut Grove’s Congregational church. Levesque will play Emma Perry, wife of Luther Perry and mother to Maud and Thomas, who secretly calls the shots for her husband’s business. Harvey will play Johnny Johnson, son of Norwegian immigrants and farm boy who has never attended school. Lewitski will play Hannah Walker, Lena Nelson’s farm manager, who is part Dakota and plays first base for the Prairie Clippers. Porter Follows will portray Mrs. Lena Nelson, an outspoken young widow in charge of the farm her husband left behind. Watch on Deadline Roach will portray civil war veteran Simon Hughes, a widower who owns the Blacksmith Shop. Greene will play Luther Perry, husband to Emma Perry and father of Thomas and Maud. Luther is a grain buyer and town baker who poses a threat to the farmers. Northcott will play William Oleson, husband to Margaret Oleson (Charlotte Sullivan) and father to Nellie Oleson (Willa Dunn). And, last but not least, Porter will portray Uncle Peter, older brother to Charles aka “Pa” Ingalls (Luke Bracey) All but Porter’s are recurring guest stars. Uncle Peter is a guest star role in the second season. L-R: Skywalker Hughes as Mary Ingalls, Alice Halsey as Laura Ingalls behind the scenes of episode 207 of ‘Little House on the Prairie’ Eric Zachanowich/Netflix In On the Banks of Plum Creek , Mrs. Nelson is married to a Mr. Nelson, and both are Norwegian neighbors to the Ingalls in their new home in Minnesota. They share a daughter named Anna. Pa also works for Mr. Nelson in Laura Ingalls Wilder’s novel. Mixing hopeful family drama and survival tale suspense, Little House on the Prairie tells the story of one family’s adventure and origin story settling the American West. It is based on Wilder’s semi-autobiographical book series. Rebecca Sonnenshine ( The Boys, Vampire Diaries, Archive 81) serves as showrunner and executive producer. Executive producers include Joy Gorman Wedtels for Joy Coalition, Trip Friendly for Friendly Family Productions, Dana Fox and Pascal Verschooris, who also directs the Season 2 finale episode. More directors include Kat Candler (201), Kyle Patrick Alvarez (202), Julie Anne Robinson (203), Liza Johnson (204), Sarah Boyd (205), Ellen Kuras (206) and Sydney Freeland (207), The adaptation is produced by CBS Studios and Anonymous Content Studio.

articles.title: Netflix Plans Oscar Push for Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love,’ Promoting Jeon Do-yeon for Best Actress (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All October 8, 2026 7:47am 'Possible Love' Courtesy of Netflix Seven award seasons after the Korean film Parasite broke the glass ceiling for non-English-language films at the Oscars by winning best picture, Netflix is angling to get another hugely acclaimed film from Korea the same sort of recognition: Lee Chang-dong ’s Possible Love . The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report that the company is planning a multi-category Oscar push for the film, which is the first in eight years from Korean master Lee, and already has been awarded the Venice Film Festival’s Grand Jury Prize, placed second for the Toronto International Film Festival’s international audience award and is among 2026’s best-reviewed releases, with scores of 100 percent on Rotten Tomatoes and 93 on MetaCritic. Related Stories TV 'The Altruists': Anthony Boyle's Sam Bankman-Fried Caught in Crypto Crisis in Netflix Series Trailer Movies Oscars: Rwanda Picks 'Ben'Imana' as Its First-Ever Best Int'l Feature Submission In addition to an Oscar nom for best international feature (Korea chose the film as its official entry way back in August ), Oscar noms for best picture, best director and best original screenplay (Lee and Oh Jung-mi) are high-priority targets and seem achievable based on the success of non-English-language films in those categories over the decade since the Academy began significantly increasing the number of its members who are based outside of the United States (and are therefore less deterred by subtitles). But Netflix feels that its strongest bet may be the performance of Jeon Do-yeon as Mi-ok, the outspoken half of a working-class couple that is opportunistically befriended by a very wealthy couple, and the company has decided to lobby hard for the 53-year-old to land a best actress Oscar nom. (She previously worked with Lee on 2007’s Secret Sunshine , for which she became the first Korean to win the Cannes Film Festival’s best actress prize, and is now one of Korea’s biggest stars.) Unlike Netflix’s other 2026 ensemble-centric non-English-lanauge film, La Bola Negra , the full cast of which is being promoted in the supporting acting categories, the company has decided to promote the four principal stars of Possible Love in different categories. In addition to Jeon in the best actress race, it will ask voters to consider Sul Kyung-Gu, who plays Mi-ok’s traumatized husband Ho-seok, for best actor; Cho Yeo-jeong, a Parasite alum who plays Ye-ji, a wealthy woman pursuing an interview with Ho-seok for a documentary, for best supporting actress; and Zo In-sung, who plays Ye-ji’s playboy husband Sang-woo, for best supporting actor. The streamer is hoping that the Actor Awards (formerly the SAG Awards), which embraced Parasite with an historic best ensemble nomination (and later an historic best ensemble win), will also recognize Possible Love with a nom in that category. Another key barometer of the film’s prospects may be the increasingly critics-aligned voting body of the Golden Globes, to which Possible Love is being submitted for consideration in the drama categories (as opposed to the musical or comedy categories). Given that two of the highest-profile best actress Oscar contenders — The Debut ’s Julianne Moore and, somewhat surprisingly, Obsession ’s Inde Navarrette — will be competing in the Globes’ musical/comedy actress race, the Globes’ drama actress race looks fairly open, which could bode well for the prospects of Jeon. THR

articles.title: Horror Movies and Politics Are Killing Film Festivals
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Joseph Kahn Plus Icon Joseph Kahn View All October 8, 2026 8:00am Illustrated by Peter Arkle I don’t know why Zack Snyder went to TIFF to premiere his movie. Unless he filmed himself giving Prime Minister Mark Carney a life-saving blood transfusion while chanting “From the river to the sea,” the war thriller The Last Photograph was never going to win that audience over. That audience is the film festival audience, a volatile, reliably left-of-center social media jumble of disgruntled film students, part-time activists/baristas, laid-off drunk sports writers, couples therapy podcasters in denial about the furry husband, all of them believing they are the better Yorgos Lanthimos. Related Stories Guest Column Hollywood Isn't the Snake Pit You Think It Is TV Mr. Belding Was Everyone's Principal Before a filmmaker has a shot at playing the cutthroat politics of the studio system — where one joke in a Hollywood Reporter column can piss off the wrong person — they’ve first got to win that weird-ass room. For decades, film festivals cast themselves as cinema’s refuge from Hollywood’s worst commercial instincts. Now they’re Hollywood’s G League and, increasingly, its most unlikely horror marketplace — where aspiring auteurs compete with movie stars, gore gets dressed up as political commentary and the bloodiest movie on the screen can spark the biggest bidding war. Film school used to be where you learned the craft and got noticed, but nobody’s scouting student films at USC anymore. Today, the Gen Z George Lucas has to take his THX film onto the festival circuit to get discovered — where he’ll find himself competing for attention with the premiere of the latest Mad Max extravaganza. A kid with a camera, a credit card and something to say is suddenly on the same playing field as a $40 million prestige picture starring two Oscar winners pretending to be broke. As more actor-directors arrive at festivals with movies stuffed with famous friends, agents and studio executives sit in their parkas like NBA scouts, clocking which nepo baby can hit ideological free throws in front of a sold-out crowd of programmers and critics. Make every shot, and you get called up to direct Marvel. Miss one, and you’re back to wearing a rubber suit for them. What’s emerged is a schizophrenic marketplace where art and commerce have fused into The Substance . Hiding in the closet, like Demi Moore’s unconscious body, is the quiet Japanese drama about a grandmother dying of cancer. Dancing out front is the festival darling of the moment: whichever horror film has everybody screaming this year. Get Out , Obsession , Megalopolis . Inde Navarrette in the festival favorite Obsession . Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection There is nothing wrong with playing horror or lowbrow genre films at prestigious film festivals. I certainly love them. At the least, it adds a sorely missing sense of humor and whimsy. After all, movies are supposed to be fun. The problem is when the self-importance of festival political activism crosses wires with these horror nerds. As these dopamine chasers inflict their limbic systems on every film, cheering for lizard-brain human suffering, the Olds scramble to give all that bloodlust a higher purpose, laundering it into political statements right there in the Q&A. A horror filmmaker on a festival podium is suddenly facing a town square of Inquisitors, eager to intellectually vivisect the entertainment in search of some morally superior meaning. It’s how body-horror humiliation rituals like The Substance get hyped into Greatest Movie Ever territory on the festival circuit, attracting a combination of prosthetic fetishists, fifth-wave feminists and theater-laugh exhibitionists. Festivals aren’t rewarding leftist politics so much as wrapping gore in political language. By day, it’s a cathedral of art and politics, handing out jury prizes under the ethical guidepost of Javier Bardem. By night, it’s a meat market, serving face-peeling gore to the poors. Under the guise of Everything Is Political, we are indulging the most annoying audience in the world. It’s a crowd that whoops at a decapitation, then posts on Bluesky how the decapitation interrogates colonialism. Of course, there’s a less philosophical explanation for all this: Horror sells. It’s a brutal buyer’s market. There are so many indie films that distributors can buy product for pennies on the dollar. The collapse of international television markets has only given the streamers more power. They budget infinite dollars for their own questionable “original” product, then make ruthless lowball offers for acquisitions. For indie investors, the pathway to getting their money back gets murkier by the day. It’s shortsighted. Sure, the streamers are getting cheap content while filmmakers and investors absorb the risk, but it’s not a sustainable market. The theory seems to be that there will always be another crop of suckers willing to pump money into the ecosystem, so the market will provide. Zack Snyder at TIFF. Frazer Harrison/Getty Images In this environment, festival programmers hold immense power. They are effectively mini-studio heads now, and the agents treat them like it. Everyone pretends the films were chosen purely on merit, but the slate often reads Hollywood with a lanyard and a conscience. It is good business to publicly maintain the separation of church and studio, at least on paper. That prestige is what lets a distributor slap “Official Selection” on the poster and charge real money for a movie it acquired for roughly the equivalent of the price of a midrange Toyota Camry. And the branding works. Check the trades the morning after and see what actually made the headlines. It’s the bidding war for the midnight horror movie: Netflix paying $17 million for It’s What’s Inside at Sundance, Neon matching it a year later for Together , Focus spending a TIFF-record $15 million on Obsession , buyers throwing eight figures at whatever made the Letterboxd crowd scream loudest in the dark. Every one of these sales is a commendable victory for independent filmmaking. But at Sundance, at least, it’s a far cry from the institution Robert Redford set out to build. He dreamed of a temple for Cahiers du Cinéma and woke up to find Fangoria running the gift shop. Demi Moore under a ton of prosthetics in The Substance. Courtesy of MUBI The cinema gods love their irony. Of all the things festivals beg us to take seriously — the climate, toxic masculinity, the corporate fascism Mark Ruffalo wants to smash — the one thing they’ve actually succeeded in elevating is the beheading. The slashing. The eye-gouging. The possessed guy shooting his brains out. Base-level schlock that teenagers once rented on DVD is now the most bankable product in the building. The festivals set out to save cinema from Hollywood’s worst instincts, and they ended up stuffing their bleeding intestines into tuxedos and slapping laurels on them. This story appeared in the Oct. 7 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

articles.title: On the Floor as Skydance Tries to Win Over Wall Street
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 8, 2026 8:05am David Ellison, Ynon Kreiz and Skydance senior leaders ring the bell at the New York Stock Exchange. Alex Weprin On Thursday morning the ornate marble lobby of the New York Stock Exchange in lower Manhattan was turned into a museum of Hollywood history. Visitors checking in to the reception desk were greeted by an Oscar statuette, for best picture, presented to Paramount Pictures for Forrest Gump in 1995. Placed next to the Oscar on the reception area? Worn down Nike sneakers and a trucker hat worn by Tom Hanks in the film as he ran across America. It was a real-world collision of highbrow and lowbrow: Worn down grimy sneakers and a gold statue, welcoming invited guests to capitalism’s unofficial capital. Harry Potter , Forrest Gump and Top Gun: Maverick props at the New York Stock Exchange for Skydance . Alex Weprin/THR The mini-museum inside the NYSE (Harry Potter’s robe and glasses! Maverick’s helmet from Tom Gun ! Props from Game of Throne s, Joker , Barbie , The Amazing Race , Landman , Superman , Star Trek and more) were installed for one day only: Skydance was ringing the opening bell. One floor up from the lobby, on the floor of the exchange, Skydance CEO David Ellison, co-CEO Ynon Kreiz and the entire senior leadership team gathered to ring the opening bell. But first, there was the CNBC hit. CNBC’s David Faber hosted Ellison and Kreiz on the floor of the exchange shortly after 9 a.m. Ellison was taking it all in. “The last time we were here was when we launched the hostile on your show, so to come full-circle today, is really quite remarkable,” he told Faber. From the CNBC, it was up to the balcony, where they rang the opening bell at 9:30 a.m. on the dot, stopping afterward for celebratory photos. They then walked down to the floor, where Citadel trader Peter Giacchi walked them through the “first trade.” It’s all a bit of kabuki theater, of course. Skydance is already trading, and the market had opened a few minutes before, but he guided them through a block trade of Skydance stock, as a gold bell was placed in front of Citadel’s booth for Ellison, Kreiz and other executives to ring by hand, as photographers snapped away. Skydance needs Wall Street to buy in. The banks lined up the financing, but the company needs to grow its share price. The ceremony Thursday morning was mostly for the cameras, but as anyone who has rang an opening bell will tell you, it carries with it weight. Ellison and Kreiz need to find $6 billion in synergies, sooner rather than later (Kreiz reiterated Thursday morning that most of those synergies will not come from staff reductions), and they need to grow a business that still has most of its revenue from declining linear TV assets. The executives said that they believe they have multiple pathways to get there. Growing the content output, reducing costs, rebuilding its technology stack, moving faster. That’s all well and good, but the street remains skeptical. Skydance co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz talk to a Citadel trader on the floor of the NYSE. Alex Weprin That’s why Disney, Comcast and Netflix are flat or down. The execution will be the key, and the window to executive is narrowing. Hollywood is synonymous with show business. The studios and networks and streamers and channels are in the business of showing consumers engaging content. For Ellison, Kreiz and the senior team at Skydance the ceremonial part of the job is over. They’ve been talking about their plans, but the telling part is easy. They are in the show business, and now they need to show that it can work. Wall Street is watching. Skydance at the New York Stock Exchange Alex Weprin THR

articles.title: Andrew Scott Welcomes ‘Heated Rivalry,’ But Feels “Troubled” by Those Who “Don’t Want to See” Painful Queer History
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All October 8, 2026 8:42am Andrew Scott at BFI London Film Festival Courtesy of Getty Hot on the heels of the European premiere of Elsinore , lead actor — and definitive awards frontrunner — Andrew Scott sat down for a career-spanning conversation at London’s BFI Southbank Thursday afternoon. Scott’s tearjerker opened the 70th BFI London Film Festival Wednesday night , as the Irishman was joined by co-stars Olivia Colman, Billie Piper, Johnny Flynn, Luke Thompson and Joe Locke on the red carpet. He was emotional on stage following the feature’s screening and brought out the real-life people who inspired particular Elsinore characters, including Colman’s Professor Margaret Johnson, a pioneer of HIV/AIDS treatment in the late ’80s, as well as the National Theatre’s stage door keeper of 46 years Linda Tolhurst, and Ian Charleson’s sister, Lizzie. Related Stories Movies Oscars: Rwanda Picks 'Ben'Imana' as Its First-Ever Best Int'l Feature Submission Movies Nathan Fielder's Elizabeth Holmes Doc Sets U.K. Release Date Simon Stone’s Elsinore , from Pride ‘s Stephen Beresford, follows the late Ian Charleson’s final weeks before his death from AIDS playing Hamlet at London’s National Theatre in 1989. The gala at this year’s London Film Fest was especially poignant for audiences, with the Royal Festival Hall just a stone’s throw from the NT. Scott covered all bases in Thursday’s Screen Talk session, from playing James Moriarty in the BBC’s contemporary Sherlock revival to solidifying himself as an undeniably magnetic lead presence with his role as the Hot Priest in Phoebe Waller-Bridge’s Fleabag . His recent credits include All of Us Strangers (2023), Blue Moon (2025), Wake Up Dead Man (2025) and Pressure (2026), some of which he also spoke about in depth. One of the session’s most memorable moments was when Scott, who is openly gay, was probed on the discourse that queer joy is dominating cinematic storytelling. He said: “I welcome things like Heartstopper and Heated Rivalry and Red, White, and Royal Blue and all those things that are joyful. I really, really, really do. And I think the fact that there’s lots of different types of gay drama, so to speak, on film [and] television is extraordinary.” He continued about those who lament the return to “sad gays” with a project like Elsinore : “It troubles me a little bit because I think people perhaps don’t want to go back to a time when you’re talking about the AIDS crisis, or you’re talking about [a time] when it was incredibly difficult for gay people. I think that sometimes comes from a place of shame. You go, ‘I don’t want to go back there. I don’t want to see that anymore.’ There’s something a little troubling about that for me, to say: ‘I don’t want to go and see something that was a difficult time.’ Because the shame does not lie with the gay people. The shame lies with the governments who ignored the AIDS crisis and the stigma that was around people and the innate prejudice that was in society. That’s someone else’s shame,” said the actor defiantly as the room applauded. Scott was beaming about Wednesday night’s premiere and described it as a “very, very, very special evening.” It is a surprisingly personal project for Scott, who is also a producer on Elsinore . He famously played Hamlet for 150 shows at London’s Almeida Theatre in 2017, and found the process grueling. “Everybody knows this, but [ Hamlet ] is three hours and 45 minutes long. We do it twice on a Wednesday and twice on a Saturday. I’ve played the part myself,” he said. “It absolutely knocks the stuffing out of you.” He continued about the “Olympian” achievement of Charleson’s: “The idea that he did that when he had no immune system is so genuinely… the physical and psychological toll that must have taken on him. But in another way, it enlivened him, and I could sort of understand that.” Scott said one particular element he found so awful was Charleson’s swollen face from septicaemia, a common problem with AIDS patients. “I think he was concerned that people would be like, ‘Oh my god!’ because he was not recognizable necessarily at some stages, and that’s really heartbreaking and almost humiliating. I can imagine that he thinks this is going to be a humiliating experience to come out and have everybody facing the same direction — at you. The bravery of that, at a time when having that particular disease felt like there was some sort of blame attached to it,” said Scott. Naturally, when discussing the likes of Sherlock , Fleabag and All of Us Strangers , he gushed over his co-creatives Benedict Cumberbatch, Phoebe Waller-Bridge and Paul Mescal. He felt the same working with Colman: “Not just Olivia, but seeing all those people, Phoebe and Paul and Benedict… Actors are the loves of my life in some way,” said Scott. “I love actors… They’re fun and brilliant people. If you are feeling awful when you go on stage, the actors are always there. But Ian Charleson, I know without a doubt that when he told them about [his AIDS diagnosis], the outpouring of support from the theater community, when there wasn’t a lot of support for anybody, was extraordinary. And I’m proud of that. The film sort of addresses that.” He’s still admittedly in disbelief over how huge Sherlock was, and how it changed his career. “I’d been in lots of things before — film, theater, everything, but that was just seen across the world. It was in 230 countries across the world. It was an instantaneous hit with the public, and also the critics seemed to like it. So it certainly change things for sure.” Scott reflected on being torn between pursuing painting or acting as a 17-year-old, and confessed to feeling like his late mother was the most influential creative presence he’s ever had. “Audiences are very discerning, and she was just an example of somebody who loved the theater, loved films, and loved everything about it, but lived a sort of so-called small life. But [she] had a giant effect on somebody who did go into the arts — her son, and my sister is in the arts too — so I guess that local theater groups and art galleries and book clubs and all that stuff matters so much because it’s inspiring and the world might get bigger, but the passion is exactly the same.” Again, the room rewarded the actor’s rallying cry with ardent applause. Understandably, Scott was also asked about his producing aspirations — he loved the experience and plans to do it again — and his “processes” as an actor. He doesn’t consider himself a method actor, but is able to draw on his “sensitivities” and enjoys diving into a character without knowing too much. “What’s so extraordinary about Fleabag and the Priest and the Godmother and all those characters,” he explained, “[is] they don’t even have a name. We don’t know anything about them. We don’t know their backstory. I think sometimes backstory is overpraised, and sometimes I like, depending on the project, to know as much as the audience does.” The B70th FI London Film Festival runs Oct. 7-18. THR

articles.title: Serena Williams Says Her New Barbie Doll Proves a Girl Can ‘Become Anything She Chooses’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tim Chan Plus Icon Tim Chan @mrtimchan Follow Sign Up View All October 8, 2026 8:56am Mattel If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, The Hollywood Reporter may receive an affiliate commission. A GOAT just got a Barbie doll. Twenty-three-time Grand Slam singles champion Serena Williams is the latest athlete to be honored with a doll from Mattel, with the “Barbie Signature Serena Williams Doll” arriving at retailers today. The official Barbie doll is inspired by Williams’ championship victory at the 2005 Australian Open, where she claimed her seventh Grand Slam singles title after returning from knee surgery. Mattel NEW RELEASE Barbie Signature Serena Williams Doll Buy Now AT TARGET $45 Buy Now On Amazon $45 Buy Now AT WALMART $45 The doll pays homage to Williams’ look on the court, with a green and white cutout top with mesh detailing, white skirt and white headband. The doll also sports high socks and white tennis sneakers, along with dangling silver earrings. Her outfit is complete with a tennis ball and a tennis racket from Wilson, Williams’ long time equipment partner. Williams says seeing her Barbie doll for the first time was “so meaningful,” adding that she hopes young girls will see it as an example to go after what they want — and who they want to be. Related Stories General News Sam McDowell, Former All-Star Pitcher Who Inspired 'Cheers' Character, Dies at 84 'Dancing' Diaries Olympian Amber Glenn on Balancing 'Dancing With the Stars' and Ice Skating “Growing up, I didn’t see many girls who looked like me being told there was no limit to who they could become,” Williams says in a release. “I want every girl who plays with this doll to see possibility, not just in me, but in herself. She can dream big, work hard, change direction, break barriers and become anything she chooses.” Timed to International Day of the Girl , Mattel says Williams’ Barbie doll celebrates the athlete’s “influence across sports , business, fashion and culture as she continues to break barriers and inspire the next generation.” “Barbie has always inspired girls to believe they can be anything, from the sports stadium to the fashion runway to the boardroom,” says Nathan Baynard, Vice President and Head of Barbie, Mattel. “Serena Williams embodies that message through her extraordinary achievements as an athlete, entrepreneur and advocate for equality. By honoring her with a Barbie Signature doll, we’re celebrating a barrier-breaking icon whose legacy empowers fans everywhere to dream big and embrace their own potential.” As part of the release, Mattel says its Barbie Dream Gap Project will make a donation to Mrs. Rina’s House of Blessings, on Williams’ suggestion. The organization funds programming focused on education for struggling kids and families in Martin County, Florida, not far from the athlete’s home in Jupiter. After announcing her retirement from tennis in 2022, Williams returned to the courts in June for a much-publicized comeback. The tennis legend received wild card entries to play at Wimbledon in July and at the U.S. Open in September, but has not announced further plans to continue, as of this writing. Walmart ALSO AVAILABLE Venus Williams Fashion Barbie Doll $23.62 Buy Now AT WALMART The Serena Williams Barbie doll comes on the heels of a Venus Williams Barbie that was released last August. Part of the “Barbie Inspiring Women Series,” this doll is inspired by the tennis star’s outfit for the 2007 Wimbledon final, where Williams defeated Marion Bartoli in straight sets to claim her fourth title at the All England Club. Mattel also honored another fierce female this year, with the release of the first-ever Whitney Houston Barbie doll in August. THR

articles.title: Anime Director Masaaki Yuasa Set to Curate Toronto Fest Classic Film Showcase
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 8, 2026 9:00am Lupin III: Castle of Cagliostro Toronto Film Festival The Toronto Film Festival is set to showcase classic films selected by Japanese anime director Masaaki Yuasa that influenced his celebrated animation. Yuasa is known for surreal storytelling and a distinct anime visual style for films like Night is Short, Walk on Girl, Ride Your Wave, his directorial debut Mind Game and Lu Over the Wall, an Annecy award winner. He also directed an episode of Adventure Time and worked on Netflix ’s DEVILMAN Crybaby. In all, 17 features and four shorts selected by Yuasa, including movies by Katsuhiro Otomo, Hayao Miyazaki, Sylvain Chomet and Rene Laloux, will feature as part of the Drawn Universes: Visions in Animation program. The series, to run Nov. 19 to Dec. 29 at TIFF Lightbox, will include conversations with Yuasa and the Japanese director introducing screenings of Richard Williams’ The Thief and the Cobbler: A Moment in Time and Isao Takahata’s Anne of Green Gables: Road to Green Gables. Related Stories Movies Andrew Scott Welcomes 'Heated Rivalry,' But Feels "Troubled" by Those Who "Don't Want to See" Painful Queer History Movies Netflix Plans Oscar Push for Lee Chang-dong's 'Possible Love,' Promoting Jeon Do-yeon for Best Actress (Exclusive) Drawn Universes: Visions in Animation will launch with Paul Grimault’s The King and the Mockingbird on Nov. 19. Akira Toronto Film Festival Yuasa said in a director’s statement released by TIFF: “In curating this series, I wanted to look back at films that sparked my own imagination and influenced both my predecessors and the generations that followed. The diverse lineup includes foundational achievements like Pinocchio and Lupin III: Castle of Cagliostro; visionary masterpieces such as AKIRA, Fantastic Planet and Toy Story 3 ; and contemporary classics including The Girl Who Leapt Through Time and Liz and the Blue Bird. Taken together, these films demonstrate boundless imagination, extraordinary technical skill, and world-building at the highest level, revealing the limitless potential of animated storytelling.” Yuasa in 2013 co-founded Science SARU with Eunyoung Choi, left in 2020 and in 2025 he established ame pippin Inc. The King and the Mockingbird Toronto Film Festival THR

articles.title: Cynthia Erivo to Headline Benefit at Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts in New York City
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All October 8, 2026 9:00am Cynthia Erivo attends the Valentino Antibiblioteca spring/summer 2027 show during Paris Fashion Week on Oct. 4, 2026. (Photo by Arnold Jerocki/Getty Images for Valentino) Cynthia Erivo has a date with Lincoln Center . The Emmy, Tony and Grammy winner has been tapped to headline a benefit concert at the venue’s David Geffen Hall on Nov. 16. The fundraiser supports Lincoln Center’s commitment to arts accessibility through a free and “choose what you pay” programming model. Concert-only tickets go on sale to the general public on Oct. 13. “The arts belong to everyone and everyone should feel that they belong at Lincoln Center,” noted Mariko Silver, who serves as Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts president and CEO. “That belief is at the heart of everything we do. We are profoundly grateful to the supporters who help us open our doors wider, bring extraordinary artists to New York, and ensure that more people can experience the joy, connection and possibility the arts create.” Related Stories Movies 'Prima Facie' Review: Cynthia Erivo Stars as a Lawyer Who Becomes a Rape Victim in This Misfire of an Adaptation TIFF EXCLUSIVE Cynthia Erivo's First Film Since 'Wicked' Required Her to Go Dark, Deep and Fearless: "I'd Feel Sick and Angry" According the institution, the “choose what you pay” model has helped bring in nearly three million people to the Lincoln Center campus through performances, educational events, festivals and open-air experiences since 2022. The model has been adopted by other arts organizations in New York, and it’s even spread to film festivals and other institutions across the country. The gig marks a reunion for Erivo, who last performed at Lincoln Center in the Appel Room, an outing that was recorded for PBS in 2019. She most recently starred in the Wicked films, Poker Face and Drift , among many other projects. She had a fall film festival debut with Prima Facie. Lincoln Center is a performing arts center and civic cultural campus home to 11 resident arts orgs including the Chamber Music Society of Lincoln Center, Film at Lincoln Center, Jazz at Lincoln Center, Juilliard School, Lincoln Center Theater, Lincoln Center for the Performing Arts, Metropolitan Opera, New York City Ballet, New York Philharmonic, New York Public Library for the Performing Arts and School of American Ballet. Programs are made possible in part through public funds provided by the New York City Department of Cultural Affairs and the New York State Council on the Arts. More intel can be found here . THR

articles.title: Karen Read Series Starring and Executive Produced by Elizabeth Banks Ordered at Amazon
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All October 8, 2026 9:00am Elizabeth Banks and Karen Read John Nacion/Variety/Getty Images; John Tlumacki/The Boston Globe/Getty Images True crime fans, this is the best news you’ll (Karen) Read all day. Amazon Prime Video has officially ordered the scripted Karen Read series starring and executive produced by Elizabeth Banks ( Cocaine Bear, Pitch Perfect ). The currently untitled eight-episode (each episode is one hour) drama series inspired by the Law&Crime and Audible Original podcast Karen will be written, showrun and executive produced by Justin Noble ( The Sex Lives Of College Girls , Brooklyn Nine-Nine ). Banks will play Read. The series hails from Warner Bros. Television; Brownstone Productions, David E. Kelley Productions, Audible and Law&Crime will serve as executive producers. In 2025, when Amazon announced it was developing the series, Read had a strong reaction . Related Stories Lifestyle What to Snag (and Skip) During October Prime Day's Final Hours TV Sam Bankman-Fried Docuseries Set at Amazon (Exclusive) “I have nothing to do with that; it’s not authorized by me in any way,” Read said during an interview with WRKO host Howie Carr . Her attorney Alan Jackson said that Read’s story is “Karen Read’s story to tell.” Karen Read wants to tell her story through LBI Entertainment ( Hell or High Water ) — and a book deal. Here’s the short version of Read’s story: “When a Boston police officer is found dead in the snow during a blizzard, all eyes are on his girlfriend, Karen Read. But when she and her legal team claim she’s not only innocent, but that she’s the victim of a conspiracy protecting the real assailants, the story spreads like wildfire, dividing a community in ways they’ve never seen,” the Amazon series’ synopsis reads. “As endless suspicion mounts, in multiple directions, this genre-bending true crime series explores society’s explosive obsession with true crime.” “I grew up in Massachusetts, and like so many people there, we watched this case divide families, friends, and entire towns,” Banks said in a statement. “We have spent years with this material because the questions it raises go far beyond one courtroom: why we choose the stories we believe, and what happens when trust in our institutions breaks down. Justin has written a series that respects and treats with care the complexity of what happened and the public reaction to it. We are grateful to Prime Video, Warner Bros. Television and our partners at David E. Kelley Productions, Wondery and Law&Crime for believing in it from the start.” “This case has more twists and turns than any story I’ve ever consumed, real or fictional,” said Noble. “It makes M. Night Shyamalan look like Nora Ephron. But the reason this story resonates and must be told is because of the profound takeaways it leaves us with: about a deeply imperfect justice system that urgently needs change, about the mistreatment of women by those who weaponize and abuse their power, and about a victim who deserves to be remembered.” In addition to Banks and Noble, the series is executive produced by Max Handelman, Krissy Wall, David E. Kelley, Matthew Tinker, Aaron Hart, Marshall Lewy, Jeni Mulein, Jen Sargent, Rachel Stockman and Dan Abrams. The project came to Audible via its integration with Wondery; Hart shepherded the project. “At its core, this series is about more than a single case — it’s about what happens when truth becomes a matter of perspective and an entire community is forced to confront its own deepest divisions,” said Peter Friedlander, head of global television, Amazon MGM Studios. “With Justin Noble’s sharp, nuanced storytelling, Elizabeth Banks’ captivating presence, and the powerhouse creative team behind this project, we believe this will be a defining series that sparks conversation around the world.” Marshall Lewy, head of Audible content, North America, commented: “The Karen Read case gripped the country because it tapped into questions about truth, loyalty, and who we choose to believe. Karen , the Law&Crime podcast and an Audible Original, set the standard for telling this story and is exactly the kind of IP that translates powerfully to television. We’re thrilled to work with this incredibly talented team.” THR

articles.title: AI-Podcasting Company Rebel Audio Raises Series A Funding at $50 Million Valuation (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All October 8, 2026 9:00am Rebel Audio's Jared Gutstadt; Draft Kings co-founder Matt Kalish Jeremy Cowart/The Portrait Lab; Courtesy of HardScope AI -podcasting platform Rebel Audio is announcing the close of its series A funding round backed by Draft Kings co-founder Matt Kalish, who is now leading a new creator media company. Rebel Audio is targeting a $10 million close, which would value the podcasting company at about $50 million post-money. Kalish’s HardScope, which launched in September with the goal of building out creator-led IP into franchises, led the funding round. Kalish also has a seat on the board of directors. Rebel Audio, which came out of stealth mode in March 2026, employs AI tools to help creators record, edit, publish, translate, distribute and monetize their content. Jared Gutstadt, who previously founded podcasting production company Audio Up, founded the company. Mark Burnett, the TV producer behind The Apprentice, Survivor, The Voice and Shark Tank , is an advisor for the startup, alongside Mike Majlak, the co-host of podcast Impaulsive with Logan Paul, who is also the chief creator in residence. Ben Lurie, Jacob Dezarn, and Jonathan Schulman are also on the board. While the funding round is largely completed, the company still has a 90-day window for additional investment. This follows the company’s oversubscribed seed round of $4.15 million. The latest funding round will be used to expand the company’s AI infrastructure and increase creator acquisition and marketing, as the company grows. “I started my career in dark editing rooms, fighting the tools just to get the work done, and have been building creator tools ever since,” Gutstadt said. “Rebel is the simplest version of that mission: remove the friction, give creators their time back. Matt co-founded DraftKings and scaled it into one of the biggest names in sports entertainment. He knows technology, and he knows performance marketing. That’s the fuel for our network effect.” “Rebel Audio empowers millions of aspiring creators to make great content independently and with almost no friction,” Kalish said. “The next generation of creators will use one-stop-shop AI powered platforms to show you don’t need a big team to create and launch great content. You can get started today, all by yourself on Rebel’s technology. Empowering creators to build ambitious projects and build an audience is core to HardScope’s mission.” THR

articles.title: ‘Inside Out 2’ Director Kelsey Mann Signs with UTA (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit Plus Icon Borys Kit Senior Film Writer View All October 8, 2026 9:12am Kelsey Mann Jesse Grant/Getty Images Logo text Pixar veteran Kelsey Mann, who most recently directed Pixar’s Inside Out 2 , has signed with UTA for representation in all areas. It is the latest animation get for the agency, which in the summer signed longtime Dreamworks and Forgotten Island co-director Januel Mercado. And it continues a trend of animators stepping out of their animation companies to test of the waters of a wider entertainment industry, sometimes beyond straight animation. In September, for example, Minions creator and Despicable Me filmmaker Pierre Coffin signed with WME . Mann’s last movie was Inside Out 2 , one of the biggest critical and commercial successes of 2024. It earned a 98 percent score on Rotten Tomatoes and grossed $1.7 billion worldwide, earning him an Academy Award nomination for best animated feature while setting the record for the highest-grossing directorial debut in film history. A storyboard artist who earned his stripes on Cartoon Network, Warner Bros., and Lucasfilm Animation shows, Mann joined in Pixar in 2009, serving as story supervisor on Monsters University, The Good Dinosaur , which he also co-wrote, and Onward . He also contributed to Pixar’s senior creative team across recent hits including Toy Story 5 , Hoppers , Elemental , and Turning Red . He made his directorial debut with the Monsters University theatrical short Party Central. Mann is now focusing on his next chapter as an independent director and creator. THR

articles.title: Sofia Coppola on Releasing ‘Making Marie Antoinette’ as a Tribute to Late Mother Eleanor, Even Though She Finds Younger Self ‘Embarrassing’: ‘It’s a Gift’ to See ‘Through My Mom’s Eyes’
articles.full_text: Oct 8, 2026 8:38am PT Sofia Coppola on Releasing ‘Making Marie Antoinette’ as a Tribute to Late Mother Eleanor, Even Though She Finds Younger Self ‘Embarrassing’: ‘It’s a Gift’ to See ‘Through My Mom’s Eyes’ By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Sofia Coppola on Releasing ‘Making Marie Antoinette’ as a Tribute to Late Mother Eleanor, Even Though She Finds Younger Self ‘Embarrassing’: ‘It’s a Gift’ to See ‘Through My Mom’s Eyes’ 32 minutes ago Oscars: Rwanda Selects ‘Ben’Imana’ as First-Ever Entry to International Feature Race 2 hours ago ‘Rent,’ Reborn: How Star Gaten Matarazzo, Director Luke Sheppard and a Perfectly Cast West End Ensemble Are Giving the Musical Its Biggest Revival Yet 3 hours ago See All Getty Images for BFI In “Making Marie Antoinette,” Sofia Coppola finds herself in front of the camera. Directed by her late mother, Eleanor Coppola, the documentary offers a behind-the-scenes look at the making of Sofia’s 2006 historical drama “Marie Antoinette.” Eleanor, who died in 2024, filmed over 80 hours of footage during the making of the movie, which starred Kirsten Dunst as the infamous Queen of France. Related Stories ‘Marshals’ Star Luke Grimes Says He Hasn’t Spoken to 'Yellowstone' Co-Star Kevin Costner ‘Since We Stopped Working Together’ During a screen talk at London Film Festival on Thursday, the “Lost in Translation” and “Priscilla” director opened up about the personal project, which she produced. She and her mother first started talking about turning the footage into a film during the COVID-19 pandemic, but it never materialized. “We were all in a bubble together in our childhood home, and she said, ‘Oh, let’s get out that footage,’ and she wanted to revisit it and I’d never seen it before,” Coppola said. “She was excited about like, ‘Let’s make it into something! Do you think it could be a film? Let’s do something with it.'” Popular on Variety At the end of her life four years later, she said, “I want this film to be finished,” Coppola revealed. “And so I felt like, ‘OK, I have to do it.'” “Marie Antoinette” was only Coppola’s third feature, and her biggest production yet, with a large cast and crew. Plus, she was granted unprecedented access to film in the Palace of Versailles, meaning the pressure was on. She told the London crowd that she remembers dismissing her mom filming on set, and feels slightly embarrassed at all the footage of her being stressed out — but also views it as a gift now that her mother is gone. “I would never like to share such a personal thing because I’m in it and it’s embarrassing to see myself as a younger director — I’m not as comfortable being assertive with my words,” Coppola said. “But I just thought, maybe that’s helpful for young filmmakers to see that there is an evolution. And for people who liked the movie, maybe it’s fun to see what it was like on set.” She added, “It’s also a gift to spend this time seeing myself through my mom’s eyes and then seeing her as a mother, watching me, and now I have two almost grown daughters so I can see it as a mother. So it was a really meaningful project for me to work on.” Reflecting on her time filming “Marie Antoinette” now, Coppola told the audience with a laugh: “It still stresses me out.” “Every day we were just falling behind we just didn’t realize how long it took for costume changes,” she added. “But I’m so touched by how many people helped it all come together. The food was incredible to see every day, all the detail that went into it and the whole art department. So it was always exciting to come to set and see what was there, and to be in Versailles. I couldn’t believe it.” The documentary comes with great timing, as “Marie Antoinette” recently celebrated its 20th anniversary. Polarizing after its Cannes premiere due to its highly stylized, coming-of-age point of view on historical events, the movie has now become a beloved cult classic. With “Making Marie Antoinette” and “Marc by Sofia,” about her friend and fashion designer Marc Jacobs, Coppola has spent most of her time on documentaries recently. Though she didn’t reveal much, she told the London crowd that she’s looking forward to making another narrative feature soon. “I’m excited, after working on two documentary projects, to go back to writing and creating an imaginary world and the challenge of how you create that,” she said. “I’m excited about that, but I’m going to go back to writing and try to figure it out.” Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards Loading comments...

articles.title: ‘Elsinore’ Producer Andrea Occhipinti on Bringing Ian Charleson’s Story to the Screen and His Personal Connection to the AIDS Crisis: ‘I Lost a Lot of Friends’
articles.full_text: Oct 8, 2026 8:38am PT ‘Elsinore’ Producer Andrea Occhipinti on Bringing Ian Charleson’s Story to the Screen and His Personal Connection to the AIDS Crisis: ‘I Lost a Lot of Friends’ By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest ‘Elsinore’ Producer Andrea Occhipinti on Bringing Ian Charleson’s Story to the Screen and His Personal Connection to the AIDS Crisis: ‘I Lost a Lot of Friends’ 32 minutes ago ‘The Monster of Florence’ Director Stefano Sollima on ‘Completely Different’ Second Chapter of Netflix’s Hit Serial Killer Series: ‘A Very Complex Story to Tell’ (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Louis Garrel to Play Fiat Heir John Elkann in Marco Bellocchio’s ‘Falcon’; RAI Cinema International Boards for Sales 7 hours ago See All 2026 Getty Images For Italian producer and distributor Andrea Occhipinti , shepherding “ Elsinore ” to the big screen carries a significance that transcends being lead producer of the buzzy movie that last night opened the London Film Festival to a standing ovation, with few dry eyes in the Royal Festival Hall, after making a major splash in Telluride and Toronto. This moving but also very funny film about Scottish “Chariots of Fire” actor Ian Charleson who gave a triumphant final performance as Hamlet at London’s National Theatre in late 1989, shortly before dying of AIDS at the age of 40, germinated from an encounter in Rome between Occhipinti and Charleson in 1987. Related Stories ‘Marshals’ Star Luke Grimes Says He Hasn’t Spoken to 'Yellowstone' Co-Star Kevin Costner ‘Since We Stopped Working Together’ That year Occhipinti, a former actor, co-founded his Lucky Red shingle with American business partner Kermit Smith, “who at the time was HIV positive,” he says. Smith passed away in 2001. “It was a time when AIDS was devastating. I lost a lot of friends,” he says. “That’s why this story is so important to me,” Occhipinti points out. Popular on Variety On the day after “Elsinore’s” triumph in the city where the film is set, Occhipinti spoke to Variety about its long journey. How did Elsinore originate from a production standpoint? I met Ian Charleson in Spain in 1984 on the set of the mini-series “The Sun Also Rises” in which I played a small part as a bullfighter. It was summer and we were a group of actors: Leonard Nimoy, Jane Seymour, Robert Carradine and Ian were the leads. Ian was the finest of the group, the most wicked. Then I saw him again, three years later, in Rome. He was shooting Dario Argento’s “Opera.” He was completely different. He was depressed. And probably at the time, though he didn’t tell me, he was already HIV positive. I remember Ian told me, “my life is a mess.” He was not happy, and he introduced me in Rome to his friend Ethan Silverman. So then Ian dies, and Silverman came to Rome because he was preparing a film with Barry Levinson, and he said to me: “It’s so sad about Ian. Do you know what happened the last months of his life?” And he told me the story. He told me that Ian wanted very badly to play Hamlet, and that when he was called to play Hamlet, he was sick. He had AIDS, but he really wanted to do it, and so on. So I said: “Ethan, there is a film here.” Then what? I had emailed Ethan saying: “I cannot forget that story about Ian wanting to play Hamlet. We should do a film.” That was 2005. Fifteen years later, Ethan came to me and said: “Listen, let’s do this film. I convinced him that we should find an English screenwriter. He accepted. So I went to Cameron McCracken at Pathé UK, with whom I had done many Stephen Frears movies [as a distributor]. He loved the story, and liked the fact that we had thought of Andrew Scott [to play the lead] because Scott looked like Ian, and he’s Irish while Ian was Scottish. They are both theatre actors and movie actors. Andrew had done Hamlet, so he was perfect. McCracken suggested we meet Stephen Beresford as a writer because he wrote “Pride,” in which Andrew had starred. So we did. This film has been a real adventure, because at first it was supposed to be shot in Italy and in London. Then Cameron McCracken decided to retire, so the project reverted to us [Lucky Red]. Two years later, I brought on board Gabrielle Tana with whom I was doing Anton Corbijn’s “A Talent for Murder.” How did you finance “Elsinore” When Gabrielle and Pete Shilaimon joined, with the screenplay and Andrew Scott’s attachment already in place, she suggested Simon Stone as director. I pitched the project to Studiocanal’s CEO Anna Marsh and to Ron Halpern, the company’s EVP of global production, and they were interested and decided to finance the film. At the same time I was already in talks with Studiocanal who, as you know, bought 51% of Lucky Red. What are the next steps? Elsinore will be playing at the Rome Film Festival next week and then lots of other festivals. Focus Features is opening the film in the U.S. on Nov. 20 and we will be doing a lot of screenings for Ampas and Golden Globes voters. Word of mouth is already very good. People are very aware of this film. Most of the releases in other countries will be in January. Besides the significance of the AIDS theme, what are other aspects that make this movie so important for you? As an Italian producer to make such a quintessentially British film, is unbelievable. And to be able to finance it through Studiocanal is really crucial and stands as testimony to the fact that joining forces with them has been a good move in terms of obtaining the financial muscle to make quality indie films, which are a dying breed. Getting this movie made is really about teamwork. The film is also thematically very much about this. It’s about community. It’s about this theatre community protecting Ian’s character, you know, with his difficulty of being sick with AIDS. There is this great line in the film that says, “I’d rather die of Hamlet than AIDS.” That was the spirit. This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity. Andrew Scott attends the “Elsinore” 2026 Opening Gala during the London Film Festival at The Royal Festival Hall. articles.title: ‘NAZA’ Producer James Wilson Says Israeli Government Response to Gaza Doc Has Been ‘Horrible and Scary,’ but Directors are ‘Safe and OK’
articles.full_text: Oct 8, 2026 8:39am PT ‘NAZA’ Producer James Wilson Says Israeli Government Response to Gaza Doc Has Been ‘Horrible and Scary,’ but Directors are ‘Safe and OK’ By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest ‘Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug & Cat Noir’ Getting Live-Action Series Adaptation From ‘Slow Horses’ Banner See-Saw Films and Miraculous Corp (EXCLUSIVE) 41 minutes ago ‘Elsinore’ Star Andrew Scott on Why Movies Should Still Tackle the AIDS Crisis: ‘The Shame Lies With the Governments Who Ignored’ It 1 hour ago London Film Festival Hails the ‘Great Andrew Scott’ as ‘Elsinore’ Opens 70th Edition With Tears, Cheers and ‘The Ethel Merman Disco Album’ 19 hours ago See All Courtesy MK2 Since it premiered in Venice, where it earned a record-breaking near-25-minute stand ovation, “ NAZA ” has emerged one of the most talked-about documentaries of the year. The bombshell film, from Israeli “No Other Land” directors Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, exposes what it asserts is Israel’s deliberate targeting of civilian targets in Gaza, using numerous sources from the Israeli Defense Force. But alongside the overwhelming acclaim for “NAZA” from the festival, praise that has only grown as it now begins it theatrical rollout worldwide, the film also provoked a near instant backlash from within Israel, particularly from members of the Israeli government. Related Stories ‘Marshals’ Star Luke Grimes Says He Hasn’t Spoken to 'Yellowstone' Co-Star Kevin Costner ‘Since We Stopped Working Together’ James Wilson , who produced “Naza,” addressed the doc and the reaction to it at the BFI London Film Festival , describing it as the “hysterical, vituperative, aggressive backlash from members of the Israeli government and Israeli politicians.” Popular on Variety Much of the aggression has been levelled at the directors, including threats from Israel to revoke their citizenship. “To have made a film, a documentary film and be threatened by the political elites of your home country, with charges of treason and defamation… it been very difficult and stressful and horrible and scary for them.” said Wilson, who also references the “rabble rousing” that had incited others to make threats. But the directors, “are safe and they are ok.” Wilson also said that the backlash from within Israel was, in fact, “part of the film,” citing article in the Jewish American magazine Forward. “There’s a meta aspect to that reaction to the film that the film embodies.” But, he noted, the “majority reaction to the film has been, from my point of view, extremely positive, and I’m personally very pleased at that. The critical reaction to the film has been extraordinarily positive.” Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards Loading comments...
