articles.title: WBD’s JB Perrette Makes The Leap To Skydance: Here Is Why Zaslav's Lieutenant Ended Up In Ellison's…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes ESPN & HBO Vet Bomani Jones Teams With Playmaker For Long-Running Podcast ‘The Right Time’ WBD’s JB Perrette Makes The Leap To Skydance: Here Is Why Zaslav’s Lieutenant Ended Up In Ellison’s Executive Suite View All October 5, 2026 4:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc JB Perrette, newly appointed Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV and Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance DTC Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images for Warner Bros. Discovery When Skydance confirmed the company’s executive leadership team Monday, most industry reaction centered on elevated roles for content execs such as Casey Bloys, Channing Dungey and George Cheeks. But another exec in a key new post is JB Perrette , a veteran of streaming since its earliest days and a close associate of Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav . He not only is making the leap to the new company from a top position at WBD — something of a surprise given that execs at the company being acquired generally head for the exits — but his turf also is expanding in some intriguing ways. Related Stories News Post-Merger Skydance Keeping Both HBO Max & Paramount+ Streaming Brands Executives David Zaslav’s Farewell: Warner Bros. Discovery CEO Signs Off In Message To Staff Skydance is due to close the deal Tuesday morning, and Perrette will join Co-CEOs David Ellison , Ynon Kreiz and others at a press conference later that afternoon on the Paramount lot. Watch on Deadline Upon the close of the $110 billion deal, Perrette will be Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance DTC and Co-Chair & Chief Business Officer, Skydance TV. He will have direct global oversight of distribution, advertising sales, content sales, DTC strategy, marketing and business operations. Perrette is poised to benefit handsomely from the merger. An SEC filing in March said he would receive $142 million in various deal-related proceeds, though some portion of that could be deferred given his post in the new company. One source cited the massive payday as a potential motivating factor. “He certainly didn’t need the money,” the person said. “He obviously felt compelled by the opportunity.”

articles.title: Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes ESPN & HBO Vet Bomani Jones Teams With Playmaker For Long-Running Podcast ‘The Right Time’ WBD’s JB Perrette Makes The Leap To Skydance: Here Is Why Zaslav’s Lieutenant Ended Up In Ellison’s Executive Suite View All October 6, 2026 5:59am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc The long-gestating merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery officially closed Tuesday, yielding a new major player in media. Shares in the combined company, Skydance , will start trading later in the day on the New York Stock Exchange. Shares of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery have been discontinued on the Nasdaq. Related Stories News New Skydance Sets Top Executive Structure As Paramount-WBD Merger Set To Close Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” The closing brings to an end a year-long saga over who would control two century-old movie studios along with a pedigreed stable of TV studios, streaming services and networks including HBO and CNN. Now, attention will turn to the difficult economics faced by the new company. It starts off with some $80 billion in debt and an ambitious plan to convert a traditional media company into a tech-oriented operation capable of measuring up to Netflix, Amazon and Disney. Larry Ellison, the billionaire co-founder of Oracle, is a key backer of Skydance. His son, David Ellison , an actor-turned-producer who has made a dramatic entrance to the Hollywood corporate scene at just 43 years old, is running the company as chairman and CEO. Watch on Deadline “Today is a historic day, not just for Skydance but for our entire industry,” David Ellison said in a statement. “From the start, our ambition was to bring these two storied studios together and create a stronger competitor, with the talent, resources, and reach to tell great stories in every genre, on every platform, for audiences everywhere. Now that ambition is a reality. We’re grateful to everyone who made this possible – the employees, creative talent, and production teams of both companies, who worked tirelessly to get us here and inspire audiences around the world every day, as well as the advisors and partners who guided this transaction to completion. Our focus now turns to the future: building a company that empowers creatives, entertains audiences and rewards shareholders. We couldn’t be more excited to get to work.” Gerry Cardinale, a Skydance board member and key financier via his firm, RedBird Capital, called the merger close “a defining moment for the industry. By applying our owner-operator model to Paramount and WBD ’s unmatched portfolio of iconic franchises, premium original programming, and live sports rights, we can protect that legacy while building for a media landscape that’s undergoing transformational change.” The merger was set in motion about a year ago when Paramount, soon after combining with the previous incarnation of Skydance, made an unsolicited offer to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery. The overture was rebuffed multiple times, and it took more than a dozen attempts for the board of WBD to finally warm up to the deal. Along the way, a bid was accepted from Netflix to acquire just the streaming and studio side of the company. Ultimately, that proposal fell by the wayside when Paramount made its sweetened pitch to buy all of WBD. The transaction sailed through regulatory approval, only to hit a major road block in July when the attorneys general of 12 states filed a lawsuit seeking to block the deal on antitrust grounds. The Writers Guild of America filed a similar suit . Thousands of actors, writers, producers and others in the creative community signed a petition opposing the deal. It will likely remain a talking point, especially for high-profile opponents like Mark Ruffalo , who stars in HBO series Task . L-R: California AG Rob Bonta, New York AG Leticia James and David Ellison Getty Images Initially, it appeared that legal and industry objections could have a chance to derail the combination, or at least result in a shrinking of its scale. In the end, though, the AGs agreed to settle the lawsuit with only so-called “behavioral remedies” required under a 5-year consent decree . Skydance agreed to negotiate pay-TV deals for Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery as though they were still separate companies as well as supplying a minimum number of theatrical movie releases, among other concessions. Ties between the Ellisons and President Donald Trump have long been scrutinized over the course of the year-long quest for WBD by Paramount, as well as Skydance’s $8.4 billion purchase of Paramount in 2025. While Skydance has steadfastly denied it has gone out of its way to appease Trump, critics have questioned the motives behind a series of moves by David Ellison and his senior leadership team. The company, which acquired rights to the UFC mixed-martial-arts circuit last year, broadcast a live match from the White House lawn over the summer. It also acquired the Free Press, a right-leaning digital news outlet, and installed its co-founder, Bari Weiss, as editor-in-chief of CBS News despite her lack of TV experience. Paramount, during the lead-up to the deal, hosted Trump during the White House Correspondents Dinner, and Ellison also paid a visit to his compound in Mar-a-Lago. Democratic members of Congress have voiced concerns about the future of CNN, though the consent decree agreed to with the state AGs calls for an editorial oversight board to be installed. articles.title: Amazon Strikes Six-Year Global Deal For Emmys Worth More Than $20M Per Year, Will Make Event Free To View
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Peter White Peter White Executive Editor, Television @peterzwhite More Stories By Peter Conan O’Brien, Bowen Yang & Shane Gillis Podcasts Become Golden Globe Eligible As Shortlist Revealed Amazon Hires Three Netflix Business Affairs Execs As It Moves To Genre-Based Model Alcon Eyes UK Series Adaptations Of ‘Insomnia’, ‘Prisoners’ & ‘P.S. I Love You’ After Launch Of Diego Piasek-Run International Studio Arm View All October 6, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Emmys Frazer Harrison/Getty Images The Emmys officially have a new rights holder. Amazon on Tuesday closed its deal with the Television Academy , as previewed last month , and it’s a significant pact. The partnership gives Prime Video the right to stream the annual TV awards ceremony for the next six years and is thought to be worth north of $120 million in total. The streamer has taken global rights to the event but will make it free to view on its Prime Video service each September. Related Stories News Amazon In Talks To Take Over Emmys TV Deal Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Deadline understands that the deal is worth between $20M-$25M per year, with one source pegging the value at $24M per year. Watch on Deadline The deal succeeds the broadcast wheel, which has seen broadcast networks ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC rotate the rights to air the ceremony each year. That system has been in place for over 30 years, since 1995. Mike Hopkins, head of Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios, told Deadline that it wanted to create a “global event” on Prime Video. “We thought we could increase the viewership, bring in a younger audience, work with the Academy to put a lot more energy, and maybe look at the production itself to try to innovate,” he said. “I feel that we can put the Emmys on a path to global growth and relevance that was probably harder to do when it was spinning from network to network and then distributed in various ways around the world.” The global nature of the deal is interesting, particularly given the fee increase the TV Academy has secured. The broadcast networks have paid between $8M-$10M per year to air in the U.S., but it’s not clear how much revenue the Academy makes from international broadcasters. The event has aired live in a number of international markets including on CTV in Canada, Showcase in Australia, Canal+ in France, TNT across Latin America and Sky Italia, but in many territories it is aired and streamed on smaller services and networks. Television Academy chair Cris Abrego added that he didn’t want to just renew the wheel deal. “I felt strongly from the outset that this was an opportunity to rethink the model,” he said. “Starting every year with a new partner, trying to find a production partner, a brand partner, trying to bring even the simpleness of learnings from the past event into the next year didn’t matter because of the different institutions… that was very challenging. As television and the industry is evolving, the telecast and much like the Academy needed to evolve, and so having a singular home was my goal from the outset.” Former Banijay Americas boss Abrego said that making the show free to view, and not behind a paywall, was a “non-negotiable” for the Academy. “I give Mike credit. From our early conversations, he understood that. It’s not simply just about distributing an award show, they really understood what the Emmys mean to the television community and what we could build around that and we’re really excited about it,” he added. Amazon has put other events in front of the paywall including a number of Amazon Fire concerts and its Black Friday NFL game. Hopkins pointed to the fact that the company has a “very large ad business.” “We have we have a variety of other economic levers we can pull to make it make financial sense for us. We also have nearly all of the streaming services as part of Prime Video in our subscription business, and many of this year’s winners are available to our Prime Video customers via driving to HBO Max or Apple TV. We see it as something that sits as part of our entertainment system with customers where we can celebrate these awards and nominees throughout the year. We can be the home of many of the best shows on television today, not just those that we make ourselves, but our partners are the ones that are always every year going to get the lion’s share of awards,” he said. Amazon itself hasn’t performed particularly well at the Emmys over the last few years; this year, largely thanks to Spider-Noir, which also aired on MGM+, it scored 10 wins; last year, it won five awards at the Creative Arts Emmys and in 2024 it won four.

articles.title: Lucy Hale To Headline ‘Scarlett Holmes’ Limited Series At Roku
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise Lucy Hale To Headline ‘Scarlett Holmes’ Limited Series At Roku Next Generation Collective Launches Initiative To Support The Mental Health Of Young Talent In Hollywood Robert Kelker-Kelly Dies: ‘Days Of Our Lives’, ‘Another World’ Actor Was 62 View All October 6, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Lucy Hale Getty Images Roku has given a green light to Scarlett Holmes , a new Roku Original limited series, with Lucy Hale set to star and executive produce. Said to “put a fresh, romantic spin on the legendary world of Sherlock Holmes,” Scarlett Holmes , produced by Jaggi Entertainment, will debut exclusively on The Roku Channel in 2027. Written by Paris Herbert-Taylor and Katie Wilbert, Scarlett Holmes revolves around the titular character played by Hale, a modern descendant of Sherlock Holmes who has inherited his legendary powers of observation, but instead of solving crimes, she takes on mysteries of love, dating, and relationships. Related Stories News Roku Adds 30 New Bundles To Premium Subscriptions, Offering Combos With HBO Max, AMC+, Fox One & More News Kristin Cavallari To Star As A Reality TV Producer In Romantic Comedy 'Cowboy Hearts' For Roku Each episode’s storyline draws inspiration from a beloved romantic comedy. Joining Scarlett in each episode is her trusty sidekick, “Jane Watson,” (casting TBA) as they help clients navigate mixed signals, secret crushes, romantic dilemmas, and everything in between. But while Scarlett may be an expert at solving everyone else’s romantic problems, her own love life proves far more difficult to decipher. When she falls for “Ollie Moriarity” (casting TBA) — a charming podcast producer secretly planning an exposé on her methods —she’s faced with the toughest case of all: her own. Watch on Deadline “Lucy Hale has the wit, warmth and comedic instincts that make her the perfect creative partner to bring ‘Scarlett Holmes’ to life,” said Brian Tannenbaum, Head of Roku Originals . “This smart, sophisticated series celebrates two genres our streamers love—romance and mystery—through a fresh, playful take on one of the most recognizable legacies in storytelling.” Scarlett Holmes is produced by Jaggi Entertainment with Sophie Tilson and Steve Jaggi serving as executive producers along with Hale. The series is overseen by Morgan Pichinson and Sabrina Lyall on behalf of Roku. Jaggi Entertainment handles international sales. “I am a true diehard fan of romantic comedies, and Scarlett Holme s has that special something that made me fall in love with the genre in the first place,” said Hale . “And I love that it brings mystery into the rom-com world in a way that feels really fresh and fun. It’s charming, sexy, funny, and has a lot of heart. Scarlett is smart, curious, a little complicated, and like so many of us, looking for love. I feel completely thrilled to step into her shoes.” Known for her work in Pretty Little Liars , Lionsgate’s F, Marry Kill , Hulu’s Which Brings Me To You and romantic comedy Puppy Love , Hale most recently wrapped production on thriller Legacy and romantic comedy Princess . She’s also executive producing the mystery drama Dead Letters, which is currently in development at Netflix, and will star in a dual role in the adaptation of the 2017 novel by Caite Dolan-Leach. She’s repped by CAA and Reel Talent Management. “ Scarlett Holmes is the kind of smart, feel-good storytelling audiences crave. Partnering with Roku on such a charming project has been an exciting journey, and we can’t wait for viewers to fall in love with Scarlett and her world,” said Steve Jaggi, CEO Jaggi Entertainment. articles.title: ‘Dirty Dancing’ Musical Heading To Broadway This Winter With Lionsgate Among Producers
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Dirty Dancing’ Musical Heading To Broadway This Winter With Lionsgate Among Producers Ex-‘American Idol’ Contestant Caleb Flynn Sentenced To Life In Prison After Being Found Guilty Of Wife’s Murder ‘Harry Potter And The Cursed Child’ Rebounds With Tom Felton; Christopher Jackson Keeps ‘Hamilton’ On Top – Broadway Box Office View All October 6, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Blake Zelesnikar and Annalese Starzec in 'Dirty Dancing: The Musical' Matthew Murphy Dirty Dancing: The Musical , a new stage production based on the 1987 film, will arrive on Broadway this winter for a limited seven-month engagement, producers announced today. The musical, which will be directed by Lonny Price ( Sunset Boulevard, Sweeney Todd ), who played Neil Kellerman in the original film, and choreographed by Darrell Grand Moultrie ( Fat Ham ), will begin performances at Broadway’s Lena Horne Theatre on Friday, February 12, 2027, with a “gala celebration” on Sunday, March 14. (An official press opening night will be announced at a later date). Related Stories News Breaking Baz: Anthony Mackie Returning To Broadway To Play Macbeth After 16-Year Absence From The Stage Casting Dolly Parton Broadway Musical Sets Its Lead Cast With Katie Rose Clarke As Dolly The engagement runs through Sunday, September 5, 2027. Watch on Deadline The musical features a book by Eleanor Bergstein, who wrote the film screenplay, and songs from the film. The popular movie soundtrack included such songs as “Hungry Eyes,” “(I’ve Had) The Time of My Life,” “Be My Baby,” “Hey! Baby,” and classic ’50s and ’60s pop hits. Producers are The Path Entertainment Group, Lionsgate, LD Entertainment, and Magic Hour Productions. Dirty Dancing is among the screen-to-stage projects currently in the works by Lionsgate, a roster that also includes Now You See Me Live ( arriving on Broadway this fall ), and The Hunger Games: On Stage in London (beginning its second year at a purpose-built theatre in Canary Wharf). Lionsgate is also developing a musical production of the studio’s six-time Academy Award-winning film La La Land from producer Marc Platt, and a stage adaptation of the $400-million hit film The Housemaid . The Broadway production is part of the musical’s ongoing North American tour, which includes pre-Broadway stops this fall in Detroit, West Palm Beach, Boston, Toronto, and other cities. The tour will resume the national run following the Broadway engagement. The cast includes Annalese Starzec as Frances “Baby” Houseman (the role played by Jennifer Grey in the film) and Blake Zelesnikar as Johnny Castle (the Patrick Swayze role). Both will be making their Broadway debuts, as will 21 of the 27 dancers and singers in the production. The official synopsis: “Set during an unforgettable summer in the Catskills in 1963, Dirty Dancing: The Musical follows Frances “Baby” Houseman, whose undeniable connection with charismatic dance instructor Johnny Castle leads to an unexpected discovery of love, passion, and independence. Pulsing with the iconic music from the original film, including such hits as “(I’ve Had) The Time of My Life,” “Hungry Eyes,” “Do You Love Me?” and “She’s Like the Wind,” the musical captures the exhilaration of forbidden romance and the courage it takes to stand by one’s convictions, all told through electrifying dance and a finale that will lift you out of your seat.” The film grossed more than $200 million at the worldwide box office and launched two multiplatinum soundtrack albums and numerous hit singles, earning an Academy Award for Best Original Song and a Grammy Award for Best Pop Performance by a Duo or Group with Vocal “(I’ve Had) The Time of My Life,” performed by Bill Medley and Jennifer Warnes. The movie remains one of Lionsgate’s all-time best-selling library titles, and the studio is currently developing a Dirty Dancing sequel from The Hunger Games producers Nina Jacobson and Brad Simpson and starring Grey in a reprisal of her role of Baby. The stage musical’s creative team includes set design by Brett J. Banakis; costume design by Emily Rebholz; lighting design by Japhy Weideman; sound design by Kai Harada; video design by David Bengali; and hair, wig and make-up design by Robert Pickens. Music supervision and arrangements are by Joseph Joubert, orchestrations by two-time Charlie Rosen, and dance arrangements by Michael Thurber. Co-producers are Magic Hour Productions, Nederlander Presentations and John Gore Organization. Subban To Star In & Produce Canadian Animated Ice Hockey Series ‘Screech Owls’ For CBC, Radio-Canada & TFO Netflix Appoints IMG To Produce FIFA Women’s World Cup 2027 FilmNation Strikes Deal With High Road Over TV Slate View All October 6, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Screech Owls' Shaftesbury/Sphere Animation/CBC/NHL EXCLUSIVE: P.K. Subban is putting on his skates for animated action-adventure series Screech Owls . The NHL All-Star will executive producer and star in the show, which is set to launch in the fall of 2027 in English on CBC and winter 2028 in French on Radio-Canada and TFO (Télévision française de l’Ontario). The co-production is bringing together a number of Canada’s biggest production houses, with Shaftesbury and Sphere Media producing in partnership with the NHL and Boat Rocker. The NHL has exclusive distribution rights in the U.S. and the Nordics, with Boat Rocker taking them elsewhere. Related Stories News Shaftesbury Provides Ailing Canadian Kids' TV Biz With $850,000 Gift Package & Issues "Urgent Call To Action" News 'Committed': First Look At Dustin Milligan & Diona Doherty As Transatlantic Lovers In CBC & BBC Sitcom Based on Roy MacGregor’s book series of the same name and the 2001 live-action series produced by Shaftesbury for YTV and Discovery Kids), Screech Owls follows a team of young hockey players who are swept into a world of hidden clues, high-tech villains and impossible missions. Watch on Deadline John May and Suzanne Bolch, who adapted the live-action series, will return as head writers for the animated show, which is designed as a multiplatform franchise with plans to extend beyond television and books into interactive gaming, consumer products and global licensing. Subban, the defenseman who retired from the NHL in 2022 after 13 seasons with Montreal, Nashville and New Jersey, will play the larger-than-life Screech Owls hockey team coach, who provides guidance for the team as they thwart jewel heists in Vancouver and mind-control plots in Montreal. Cast as the team are Ana Sani, who plays courageous captain Neela; Joshua Odjick, who is charismatic forward Ishkode; Erika Prevost, who plays curious and direct goalie Camille; and returning Screech Owls star Jonathan Malen, who plays brains-and-brawn defenseman Trevor. When duty calls, the team gears up in specially-designed suits that amplify their natural abilities and unlock powerful new skills. Through signature “Power Pulses,” they’re able to outpace pursuers, break through obstacles and turn everyday objects into ingenious crime-fighting tools. PWHL star Sarah Nurse is also making a cameo as herself and the series will feature additional guest stars, who will be announced at a later date. “A major focus of my career has been finding new ways to grow the game and reach young, diverse audiences with positive role models and Screech Owls , a series I grew up reading, does both,” said Subban. “Hockey teaches character, leadership, and teamwork. You don’t need to know what ‘offside’ means to watch Screech Owls – you just have to love globe-trotting kids solving mysteries, working together, and having a blast.” “ Screech Owls is being built as a true multi-platform franchise, reimagining a beloved Canadian story for a whole new generation with adventure, mystery, and heart,” added Christina Jennings, Chairman and President, Shaftesbury. “Partnering with Sphere, CBC/Radio-Canada , Boat Rocker, and the NHL allows us to expand this universe globally, while having P.K. Subban on board adds an incredible layer of authenticity and energy.” Marie McCann, Senior Director, Children’s Content at CBC Kids, added that the “gem of a series is just what kids need right now,” while David Lehanski, NHL Executive Executive Vice President, Innovation & Growth Strategy, said: “The NHL is reimagining how hockey reaches, inspires and entertains youth and families. With Screech Owls we have a unique opportunity to meet kids where they are — through high-energy storytelling, adventure and characters they can connect with – while showcasing hockey’s best attributes in a way kids will love and parents will appreciate.” Shaftesbury and Sphere Animation are producing Screech Owls in association with CBC, SRC and TFO with the participation of the Canada Media Fund, Shaw Rocket Fund, Ontario Creates and the IPF Fund. May and Bolch are head writers and Suren Perera is directing. Executive producers are Subban; and Jennings, Scott Garvie and Jay Bennett from Shaftesbury. Jennifer McCann from Shaftesbury and Marianne Culbert from Sphere Animation are producing. For For CBC, Sally Catto is General Manager, Entertainment; Marie McCann is Senior Director, Children’s Content, CBC Kids; and Swin Chang is Executive in Charge of Development and Production, CBC Kids. For Radio-Canada, Sophie Morasse is General Manager, Entertainment, Sports and TOU.TV; Christiane Asselin is Executive Director, Streaming Services, Youth Programming and Digital Sports; and Nathalie Chamberland is Director, Youth Programming. articles.title: David Ellison, Ynon Kreiz Praise Staff, Lay Out Priorities For New Skydance: “Getting Here Has Been Quite A Journey”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Jill Goldsmith , Dade Hayes October 6, 2026 7:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc L-R: David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz Getty Images Skydance CEO David Ellison , having just closed the historic merger of Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery after fierce opposition, sought to rally the troops Tuesday in a memo to employees. In the lengthy message (read it below), Ellison and Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz thanked staffers for their patience during the year-long process, and outlined top priorities for the new company. Related Stories News Skydancing At Last: $110B Merger Of Paramount And Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Executives David Ellison, Ynon Kreiz Praise Staff, Lay Out Priorities For New Skydance: “Getting Here Has Been Quite A Journey” “Getting here has been quite a journey,” they wrote. “Over the past year and beyond, it has taken hard work, perseverance and commitment with many challenges along the way – but we did it!” Their missive lays out key priorities, including preserving the companies’ legacies, earning trust, creative excellence and becoming “the most technologically capable media company.” Watch on Deadline The Skydance deal alters the media landscape, creating a competitor with the potential to rival Netflix, Disney and Amazon. Yet the transaction also leaves Skydance with an $80 billion mountain of debt, with an already fraught merger process potentially segueing to significant layoffs. Likely layoffs, required in order to pay down debt and deliver $6 billion in projected cost savings, were among the many topics covered in the memo. “Integrating two companies will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce,” Ellison and Kreiz wrote. “We are committed to handling this process thoughtfully and respectfully.” The memo also notes the reasoning behind the Skydance name. It was chosen over some mash-up of Paramount and Warner Bros., the executives explained, because it “doesn’t compete with either legacy. It gives the new company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. – and all our extraordinary brands – to remain in the spotlight.” Here is the full memo (with all-caps in place of select boldface passages in the original): Team, Today we begin an exciting new chapter as Skydance. Getting here has been quite a journey. Over the past year and beyond, it has taken hard work, perseverance and commitment with many challenges along the way – but we did it! To everyone at both companies who helped get us to this moment: thank you. Thank you for your patience, your resilience and, above all, your belief in what we could accomplish together. Bringing Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery together fulfills a vision that began with Skydance’s acquisition of Paramount: to build the next-generation media and entertainment company, powered by creativity and technology. The goal was never simply to add more production capacity, brands or IP. It was to unite the talent, resources and capabilities of these companies into a stronger competitor, one with the scale to take on the biggest players in our industry. Together, we will give these iconic studios the opportunity to win for generations to come. BUILT FOR WHAT’S AHEAD As all of you know, our industry is in a period of profound change. Audiences have more choices than ever, technology is reshaping how stories are created, distributed and experienced, and competition for people’s time and attention has never been greater. We don’t just want to succeed in this environment – we want to win and help shape the future of the industry. We want to lead. And that starts with what we’re building together: a company that tells great stories in every genre, for audiences everywhere, on every platform. A company that can compete in a crowded market and win at global scale, create enduring value for all stakeholders, and strengthen the industry as a whole. As owner-operators, we’re in this for the long term, committed to building Skydance for the future – not simply optimizing for the next quarter or the next year, but creating a company built to endure, evolve and remain relevant. That means being creative-first, audience-focused, tech-forward and globally scaled – building a thriving ecosystem where stories and worlds are imagined, brought to life and experienced by audiences of all ages, everywhere. At the center of it all is a clear purpose: to entertain, inspire and inform the world through extraordinary storytelling. And we’ll be guided every step of the way by shared priorities that shape how we intend to operate, how we make decisions, how we work together and how we show up for our audiences, our partners and one another. OUR TOP PRIORITIES To bring that mission to life, these are the priority areas where we will concentrate our energy: WIN IN STORYTELLING Great stories remain at the heart of everything we do. We will invest in the ideas, creators, franchises and experiences that captivate audiences around the world and create lasting cultural impact. On the big screen, we are committed to making at least 30 movies a year, pairing original stories from today’s most exciting filmmakers with beloved franchises like Harry Potter, Mission: Impossible, The Lord of the Rings, DC, Transformers and Star Trek. On television and streaming, it means storytelling like Game of Thrones, Landman, NCIS, Tracker and SpongeBob SquarePants . In games, it means worlds like Hogwarts Legacy and Mortal Kombat ; and in live sports, it means the NFL on CBS, the UFC, UEFA and March Madness, just to name a few. BECOME THE MOST TECHNOLOGICALLY CAPABLE MEDIA COMPANY Technology is fundamentally reshaping our industry, and we intend to be at the forefront. We will use technology, data and emerging capabilities to improve how we create, distribute and monetize content, from new production tools to personalization and entirely new ways for fans to engage with the stories they love. We will embrace the opportunities AI provides to expand what our creatives can imagine and to make our businesses even more productive. The opportunities ahead are enormous, and we intend to seize them. But one principle will never change: technology must serve the art – never the other way around. LEAD IN A CROWDED MARKET We came together to create another major competitor in the industry. And with our combined scale, assets and global reach, we are positioned to take on some of the largest technology and media companies in the world and to lead in an evolving entertainment landscape. We will use that strength to drive synergies, operate with discipline and invest in the long-term growth of our business. And we will go further than traditional synergies. By embracing the most advanced technologies available and embedding them into how we operate, we will work smarter, move faster and unlock efficiencies the merger alone could not deliver. EARN TRUST EVERY DAY Trust is foundational to everything we do. And we are committed to earning it every day by communicating directly, following through on our commitments and listening closely to those we serve and work alongside. That is essential to our reputation and our long-term success. As we work toward these goals, we must never lose sight of what matters most: our people. We will build a culture where people feel respected, empowered, supported and proud of the work they do. And we will extend that same commitment, with reliability and responsibility, to our creators, audiences, consumers, advertisers and partners. None of what we accomplish happens in a vacuum. It reflects everyone joining forces to unlock the full potential of our assets: an unmatched portfolio of brands, franchises, libraries, IP and creative talent, with decades of history and, in many cases, decades of opportunity still ahead. Together, we can reach audiences across platforms, markets, and generations in ways neither Paramount nor WBD could have achieved alone. With the talent, scale, relationships and resources to build on, we can create something truly distinctive. For audiences, it means more choice and more ways to experience the stories they love. For creators, it means a partner with the scale and capabilities to help their best ideas reach the widest possible audience. For our partners, it means a broader, more powerful platform to build on. And for the broader creative community, it means an enduring commitment to storytelling and the people who make it possible. That is the foundation of Skydance. And it’s why this combination matters so much. HONORING AN EXTRAORDINARY LEGACY The union of these two iconic companies represents an exciting future. But, just as important as what we build together is preserving what has made them iconic in the first place. Paramount and Warner Bros. each have a distinct identity and extraordinary legacy that deserves to stand on its own. In choosing our corporate brand, we never wanted to diminish, alter or overshadow any of the assets that have global recognition and have withstood the test of time. Both studios will continue to operate under their own names, and audiences will still see the Paramount mountain and the Warner Bros. shield before the films and shows they love. Warner Bros. is woven into the history of modern entertainment, from film and television to journalism, sports, unscripted programming and some of the world’s most recognizable characters and franchises. Paramount has an equally extraordinary legacy, with more than a century of storytelling that helped define the American film industry and shape entertainment across every medium. We realized early on that simply combining the two names – WarnerParamount, ParaWarner or ParamountWarner – accomplished none of what we wanted. Every variation somehow made two giants feel smaller, not greater. It asked each to give something up rather than allowing us to create something new. This isn’t a merger of convenience. It’s the beginning of a new era in entertainment, and we wanted a name that looks forward rather than one that simply splices together the past. That brought us to Skydance – a name that obviously has special meaning to David, who chose it for his own studio 20 years ago. It evokes possibility: scale and ambition, creativity and imagination, artistry and innovation. Most importantly, it doesn’t compete with either legacy. It gives the new company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. – and all our extraordinary brands – to remain in the spotlight. Because ultimately, what we are bringing together is much more than brands and libraries. It is the creative spirit, ambition and craftsmanship that have kept these companies culturally relevant for generations. That spirit will continue to be a core part of who we are at Skydance. And who we are will also be defined by what we strive to accomplish – not just for our company, but for the industry at large. That means looking ahead to the forces that are reshaping entertainment and finding ways to harness them to expand what’s possible – for creators, for audiences and for the business itself. FINANCIAL STRENGTH We’re building a diversified company with the financial strength to compete aggressively and the discipline to create sustainable value. That’s not just important to our investors – it’s important to all of us. A financially strong, well-run company gives us the freedom to take creative risks, invest in our people and our technology, and pursue the kind of opportunities that set us apart. In concrete terms, we are together one of the largest media and entertainment companies in the world, with nearly $70 billion in revenue. As we have said publicly, we are also targeting at least $6 billion in synergies, which will make us leaner and more nimble and free up capital to invest in the stories, creators and technology that matter most. Integrating two companies will bring change, including difficult decisions that affect our workforce. We are committed to handling this process thoughtfully and respectfully. THE ROAD AHEAD Today is Day One. We have an incredible collection of assets. Extraordinary creative talent. Global scale. The technology to lead. And most important, we have the people who bring it all to life every day. We have everything we need to win, and that is our goal: to build a next-generation global media and entertainment company that puts audiences first, empowers creators, embraces innovation and creates lasting value for generations to come. But none of this happens without you. Thank you for everything you’ve brought to this moment. We’re proud to write this next chapter with you. Now the real work begins. Let’s go! articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg ‘Dirty Dancing’ Musical Heading To Broadway This Winter With Lionsgate Among Producers Ex-‘American Idol’ Contestant Caleb Flynn Sentenced To Life In Prison After Being Found Guilty Of Wife’s Murder ‘Harry Potter And The Cursed Child’ Rebounds With Tom Felton; Christopher Jackson Keeps ‘Hamilton’ On Top – Broadway Box Office View All October 6, 2026 7:40am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Mark Mortimer in 1997 promo shot for 'Another World' E.J. Carr/NBC /Everett Collection Mark Mortimer , who starred as Nick Hudson on Another World during the 1990s, has died of cancer. He was 59. Mortimer, who lived in the Greater Chicago area, had most recently worked in the building industry as a founder of Inside Out Construction in Batavia, Illinois. His September 23 death was announced by his family . Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries Obituaries Robert Kelker-Kelly Dies: ‘Days Of Our Lives’, ‘Another World’ Actor Was 62 After launching his career as a model, Mortimer made his TV debut in 1996 when he was cast as Nick Hudson on the NBC soap Another World . He was the third actor in the role (following Justin Chambers and Kevin McClatchy) – a long-lost member of Bay City’s central Hudson family – and appeared in 81 episodes through the series’ finale in 1999. Diagnosed with cancer in 2024, Mortimer, born in St. Charles, Illinois, on April 15, 1967, and his wife Christie founded the Integrative Access Foundation, designed to give people facing cancer access to integrative therapies that might otherwise be financially out of reach. “Mark faced the end of his life with the same faith with which he lived it,” his family wrote. “His confidence did not come from believing everything would turn out the way he wanted. It came from knowing where he was going. He believed in Jesus. He believed in the promise of Heaven. And as his earthly life drew to a close, that belief gave him peace. “Mark’s path took him from serving in the United States Army to modeling, acting, and eventually to entrepreneurship,” his family noted. “He was never afraid to reinvent himself or pursue a new idea.” In addition to his wife Christie, he is survived by daughter Hunter and other extended family. articles.title: Paramount Enlists Steven Spielberg In Primary Creative Producer Role For Next ‘Transformers’ Movie, With Michael Bay In Early Talks To Direct
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Justin Kroll Justin Kroll Film Editor @krolljvar More Stories By Justin Paramount Enlists Steven Spielberg In Primary Creative Producer Role For Next ‘Transformers’ Movie, With Michael Bay In Early Talks To Direct Maude Apatow And Mike Faist To Star In ‘The Maid Of Orleans’ Sam Esmail And His Production Company Esmail Corp Sign With WME View All October 6, 2026 7:43am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Optimus Prime in 2007's 'Transformers' Paramount/Everett Collection EXCLUSIVE: Paramount Pictures and Hasbro are getting closer to bringing their Transformers back to the big screen and look to be reuniting with some familiar faces to help bring the franchise back to life. Sources tell Deadline that Paramount has appointed Steven Spielberg to focus on all creative aspects of the next live-action Transformers film alongside longtime producer Lorenzo di Bonaventura. Michael Bay is in early talks to return as director. Spielberg continues as executive producer and will now lead the creative direction for what will be the eighth live-action installment. He held a similar creative role for the first two Transformers films that launched the franchise, which has generated more than $5.4 billion in global box office revenue and turned Hasbro’s toy brand into a worldwide phenomenon. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office News Peter Cullen Dies: Voice Of Optimus Prime In ‘Transformers’ Was 85 Together, Spielberg and di Bonaventura will guide this new chapter to honor the spirit of the early Transformers films. Mark Vahradian, Don Murphy, Tom DeSanto and Hasbro will also produce. Watch on Deadline The film is being developed based on a script by Jason Fuchs. Plot details are under wraps other then the film being set in modern day. As the project is in early development, no cast details yet. Since the first film opened in summer 2007, the franchise has become of the biggest properties on the Paramount lot. Spielberg, Bay and di Bonaventura played major roles in that first films’ success, with Spielberg identifying Bay as his choice to direct the first film. While Bay and di Bonaventura would remain the primary architects at the center of the franchise for the next four installments, Spielberg was less hands on as exec producer. Bay ultimately took a break from the franchise after the 2017 pic Transformers: The Last Night . Since then, the most recent installments, Bumblebee and Transformers: Rise of the Beasts, while not complete misses, did not live up to the standards prior installments had delivered on. So when the Skydance merger was completed , newly minted Paramount Pictures co-chairs Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg made it a priority to breathe new life into the franchise and Spielberg on board for the new film’s development; one of the first meetings Greenstein and Goldberg had as co-chairs was with Spielberg following Skydance’s merger with Paramount in August 2025 to talk about many things including Transformers. That courtship continued over the next year, with Spielberg finally agreeing to this new hands-on role after reading Fuchs’ latest script. The next decision was who would direct, with Bay being the first stop to see if he was up to returning. Bay had been open to the idea over the years and, after reading the script and meeting with Spielberg earlier this week, he was on board. Transformers is one of a handful of properties gaining momentum at Skydance’s Paramount as Deadline also recently reported Brad Pitt is returning to star in a World War Z sequel with Edward Berger directing. Spielberg is repped by CAA. Bay is repped by Range and CAA. Page Six was first to report news about Bay’s return. articles.title: ‘Fjord’, ‘All Of A Sudden’, ‘Minotaur’ & ‘Coward’ Among Titles Set For 30th Edition Of The American French Film Festival In L.A.
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana Juno Films Takes North American Rights To ‘The Extraordinary Miss Flower’ International Disruptors: Reta Guetg On Building Zurich Film Festival’s “Trendy” Identity & Why New Owners Want To Keep It Small, Nimble & Close To Hollywood Percy Hynes White & Jeff Wahlberg Lead Lovers-On-The-Run Thriller ‘Crime Novella’, Roland Emmerich Exec-Producing & First Look Revealed View All October 6, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Fjord' Neon The 30th edition of the American French Film Festival , which runs November 3-8 at the DGA Theater Complex in L.A., has unveiled its 2026 lineup. Highlights this year in the program include French Oscar entry Minotaur , Cristian Mungiu’s Fjord , which is Romania’s official Oscar entry and Lucas Dhont’s Coward , Belgium’s Oscar entry. As previously announced, the festival will open with In Waves , from French-Vietnamese director Phuong Mai Nguyen. The animated feature, which features the voices of Will Sharpe and Stephanie Hsu, is set against the backdrop of California’s surfing world and is adapted from L.A. illustrator AJ Dungo’s eponymous cult 2019 graphic novel. Related Stories Festivals Netflix-Acquired Animation 'In Waves' To Open The American French Film Festival In L.A. News Oscars: France Selects 'Minotaur' For Best International Feature Film Race Further highlights in the lineup this year include All of a Sudden , Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s French-language debut which is Japan’s Academy Award entry this year, and French co-production Strawberries from director Laïla Marrakchi, which is Morocco’s official Academy Award entry. Watch on Deadline Fjord , which won the Palme d’Or in Cannes earlier this year, stars Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve. The French co-production follows two evangelical parents who are suspected of child abuse and become the subject of an investigation. Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Minotaur is a Russian-language political thriller based on the 1969 French film The Unfaithful Wife by Claude Chabrol. The film won the Grand Prix award in Cannes this year. TAFFF is set to close on November 8 with The American Dream , written and directed by Anthony Marciano. The comedy-drama biopic is based on the true story of real life French NBA agents Bouna Ndiaye and Jérémy Medjana, who launched the careers and represented several elite French NBA players including Victor Wembanyama, Rudy Gobert and Nicolas Batum. The festival will also feature the first U.S. screening of Antonin Baudry’s De Gaulle , the U.S. premiere of comedy All About Corinne and the North American premiere of Guillaume Canet’s psychological thriller Karma with Marion Cotillard. Stephane Brizé’s Venice title A Little Good Soldier will also screen at the fest. The lineup this year includes 60 films and series, with 31 fiction features, 11 series, four documentaries and 14 short films, many of which are either North American or U.S. Premiere presentations. 58 will be up for The American French Film Festival Awards. “Since 1997, the Franco-American Cultural Fund, founder of The American French Film Festival, has brought more than 1,200 French films and series into the Hollywood spotlight and given thousands of French artists, from newcomers to well-known directors, to writers, composers, actors and producers, the opportunity to present their work before their American peers in the heart of Hollywood,” said Taylor Hackford, director and former DGA president and FACF board member. “This year there will be another spectacular selection and delegation to celebrate the 30th anniversary event at the Directors Guild of American, making TAFFF the second oldest film festival in the City of Angels.” François Truffart, exec producer and programmer of the festival said: “For 30 years, The American French Film Festival has established itself as a leading and unmissable international platform on the global circuit for promoting French films and series. Supporting filmmakers from their earliest short films to eventual Oscar recognition, creating a platform where both established and emerging talent can present their work, being the first to launch a series competition alongside feature films and consistently championing female filmmakers, are just a few of the many meaningful milestones I cherish with TAFFF.” TAFFF deputy director Anouchka van Riel added: “This year’s selection is a cinema of resistance. Individuals stand up to systems that exist to grind them down: a corporate machine in A Little Good Soldier and Minotaur , a courtroom built by men in Women on Trial , an online mob in Forsaken and an exploitative labor chain in Strawberries . Running alongside that is a quieter thread about care, illness and what we owe one another, from the friendship forged against cancer in All of a Sudden to the love story at the heart of In Waves . Between those who fight and those who care, the lineup returns to one question: At a time when intelligence is becoming artificial, what remains human? These films answer with the things no machine has learned (yet): to refuse and to care.” The 30th edition of The American French Film Festival takes place November 3-8, 2026. articles.title: Jason Alexander, Josh Radnor & More Wrap On Passover Horror-Comedy ‘Doom Scroll’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News $110B Merger Of Paramount & Warner Bros Discovery Officially Closes Read the full story By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Matt Vioral Heads To Brillstein In Transition To Management After Two Decades At Gersh; Jacob Elordi Among Clients Joining Him Comedians Call On Sebastian Maniscalco, SiriusXM To Restore Working-Class Comic Airplay Following Raw Dog Rebrand American High Levels Up: How Jeremy Garelick & Will Phelps Are Scaling Unconventional Comedy Company – Comedy Means Business Podcast View All October 6, 2026 8:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source L-R: Jason Alexander, Josh Radnor, David Mazouz, Inbar Lavi, and Betsy Brandt Manfred Baumann/Sam Jones/Getty/Yotam Shwartz/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Production company K180 Studios has wrapped on its sophomore feature, a Passover home-invasion horror-comedy titled Doom Scroll from director Natalie Bailey . The cast includes Jason Alexander ( Seinfeld ), Josh Radnor ( Hunters ), David Mazouz ( Gotham ), Inbar Lavi ( Imposters ), Betsy Brandt ( Breaking Bad ), and Erin Darke ( Good Girls Revolt ). Shot in the Canary Islands, Doom Scroll watches as a family’s Passover Seder is ambushed by intruders hungry for revenge, viral fame and power. A college student grappling with his identity must then protect his family and reckon with an ancient myth that becomes terrifyingly real. Related Stories News Josh Radnor Says He's Not Close To His 'How I Met Your Mother' Co-Stars "Not Even A Little Bit": "I Have Love For All These People" News 'Seinfeld' Alum Jason Alexander Apologizes To Courtney Stodden For Filming "Inappropriate" Sketch When She Was Underage: "I Truly Regret It" Founded in 2021 by siblings Becky Korman, Lily Korman and Shai Korman, K180 came to Doom Scroll on the heels of The Floaters , a Jewish summer-camp ensemble comedy starring Jackie Tohn, Sarah Podemski, Aya Cash, Seth Green and Steve Guttenberg, which opened in theaters through distributor Brainstorm Media this summer. Watch on Deadline Reuniting three actors from The Floaters — Judah Lewis, Jim Kaplan, and Max Samuels — the company’s second film also stars Rita Shukrun ( Karaoke ), Gilles Geary ( Cupertino ), Gore Abrams ( The Substance ), Delilah Napier ( Floating Carousel ), Rob McLoughlin ( The Walking Dead: Daryl Dixon ) and Carys Douglas (upcoming The Problem with Poets ). Jason Venokur, a veteran of sitcom 3rd Rock from the Sun , adapted the screenplay from a story co-written with Becky Korman, Lily Korman, and Shai Korman. Becky Korman, Lily Korman, Shai Korman and Chris Collins produced the film, with Venokur serving as executive producer. Bailey came to Doom Scroll after premiering her dark comedy Audrey in competition at SXSW in 2024. She earned the Australian Directors’ Guild Award for Best Direction of a Debut Feature for her work there, more recently working on Apple TV’s Down Cemetery Road . Her other television credits include HBO’s Run , Armando Iannucci’s Avenue 5 and the BBC’s The Thick of It . She is repped by Curtis Brown Group, HLA Management, and Independent Artist Group. Alexander is repped by Innovative, Yumkas Entertainment, and Gendler, Kelly & Cunningham; Radnor by Gersh, 3 Arts, and Frankfurt Kurnit Klein & Selz; Mazouz by Paradigm, Untitled, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman; Lavi by Paradigm, Justice & Ponder, and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman; Brandt by TalentWorks, Patty Woo Management, and Del Shaw Moonves; and Darke by IAG and Anonymous Content. Jonathan Olley/Warner Bros./Courtesy Everett Collection Logo text The Batman: Part II is on pause while filmmaker Matt Reeves deals with a personal matter, sources confirmed to The Hollywood Reporter . “Production on The Batman Part II has been temporarily paused while Matt Reeves focuses on a family matter,” said a DC Studios spokesperson in a statement provided to Deadline , which first broke the news. “Matt has the full support of DC Studios and we look forward to continuing the journey soon.” The Batman Part II began filming in London in June after a winding development process that saw its start date pushed multiple times while Reeves and co-writer Mattson Tomlin wrote the script.
