articles.title: a New York Film Festival screening
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Venice Prize-Winner ‘NAZA’ Brings Explosive Gaza Exposé to U.S. Theaters – Specialty Preview NBCU’s Donna Langley On Industry Mergers, Taylor Sheridan, And The Road to 2027 Anonymous Content, Higher Ground Set Feature Adaptation Of James Baldwin Biography View All September 25, 2026 2:57pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clockwise from top left: 'Artificial,' 'You Can See Everything,' 'Godzilla Minus One' and 'A Statement' Neon/A24/Toho International/Sony The New York Film Festival opens Friday night with a lineup featuring great films of 2026 along with heavy-hitting world premieres. Artistic director Dennis Lim insists the global bows are not “the be all, end all,” but if they come he credits the vibrant Big Apple audience. “The New York audience engages with a film in a way that is meaningful to filmmakers and that creates a memorable launch for a film, so I would credit our audience for that,” Lim tells Deadline of this year’s slate, which includes Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes doc You Can See Everything , NAZA by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, and world premieres from Luca Guadagnino’s Sam Altman biopic Artificial to Tony Gilroy’s Behemoth !, Tom McCarthy’s The Statement and the sequel Godzilla Minus Zero by Takashi Yamazaki. Related Stories Festivals James Gray On Opening The New York Film Festival With ‘Paper Tiger’, Surviving The “Cannes Bubble”, Oscar-Season Hopes And Which Filmmakers Inspire Him – The Deadline Interview Festivals Tom McCarthy’s ‘A Statement’, Jonathan Glazer Documentary ‘Joy Of Joys’ To World Premiere At New York Film Festival Jonathan Glazer , Paul Thomas Anderson and Ava DuVernay will also world premiere new documentaries at this year’s NYFF , which runs through October 12. Watch on Deadline “These films came to us and decided to premiere with us with for different reasons. It just so happens we have a certain number of them this year, which shows that we have proven in the last few years that we can be a pretty good place to launch a film,” Lim says. NYFF’s 64 th edition opens tonight at Lincoln Center’s Alice Tully Hall with James Gray’s Paper Tiger . DuVernay’s 14th , a direct follow-up to her acclaimed 2016 documentary 13th (which opened NYFF that year), is the closing-night selection. Asked to tick down the lineup, Lim says Artificial “was in flux for a while with the change in ownership. When the film was at Amazon we did have conversations about it. It was not going to be a 2026 film. That changed when it landed at Neon” to join the indie distributor’s awards slate. Amazon dropped the nearly finished $50 million film after making a massive investment in Altman’s OpenAI, noting the project would be better served elsewhere. Neon acquired global rights in June. Godzilla , conversely, “came pretty early, long before it was finished. There’s a tremendous amount of intricate effects work on the film. We started the conversation early in the spring. They did not do festivals with the previous film, which was a huge success for Gkids and Toho, and they were interested in doing something different with this one. We saw an unfinished version in the summer and though it would be really fun,” Lim tells Deadline. “The Elizabeth Holmes documentary, obviously, had been in the works for a while. I knew of the existence of the film but was sworn to secrecy when they wanted to have maximum impact in Telluride . It was always understood that it would be a surprise there, and we would announce thereafter.” You Can See Everything from A24 world premiered as a secret screening at Telluride, gobsmacking the audience. The Theranos founder allowed the filmmakers into her San Diego home with unfettered access in 2023 during the days before she reported to prison after being found guilty of defrauding investors. Wrote Deadline’s Pete Hammond in his review : “Nothing seems to be off limits as they agree to be miced-up for at least 12 hours a day, wide-angle cameras in place to get all movements, with other cameras getting closeups. Fielder immerses himself in this weird world as someone she comes to trust, much to his astonishment, becoming so close she asks him along on that last drive to prison.” The doc is Fielder’s feature film directorial debut. His 2023 Showtime comedy The Curse was the first and one of the few television series to world premiere in the NYFF’s main lineup, Lim recalls. NAZA , which world premiered in Venice , was a late addition. The investigation into Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza was shot at night on rooftops in Tel Aviv where the filmmakers interviewed Israeli military intelligence officers and soldiers about destruction and loss of life. “Films are not made in vacuum, they are made by people. There has not been another year where I felt the films to be so directly in conversation with the real world, really are tackling contemporary reality head on,” Lim says. “I think whether they are documentaries or fiction, all films emerge from this world that we all live in together, the reality that we share, and they will engage with real world institutions.” This year’s festival has set 119 films — 75 features and 44 shorts – across its Main Slate, Spotlight, Currents and Revivals sections along with a series of talks complementing the lineup. articles.title: James Gunn & Peter Safran To Stay At DC Studios After Paramount-Warner Bros Merger
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy: When They Are Leaving Warner Bros & What’s Next For Them New Line Boss Richard Brener Poised To Jump To Merged Paramount-Warner Bros – The Dish James Gunn & Peter Safran To Stay At DC Studios After Paramount-Warner Bros Merger View All October 2, 2026 9:48am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc L-R: James Gunn and Peter Safran Getty Images James Gunn and Peter Safran , the bosses of Warner Bros-owned label DC Studios , will continue to lead the film, TV and comic book production hub and do what they do best after Paramount closes its acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery. Once upon a time, the Marvel Cinematic Universe was in Paramount’s hands, having a distribution deal with the comic-book label and launching the megaverse with Iron Man, Thor, Captain America and Iron Man 2. Then Marvel took a hike to Disney, which scooped them up for $4 billion in 2009. With DC, Paramount no doubt gains a massive franchise one-up in its library that already includes Star Trek, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, and Mission: Impossible. Related Stories Executives Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit, Setting Up Likely Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy Exit News Paramount-WBD Will Now Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals We hear the duo had a recent meeting with new Skydance co-CEO David Ellison about their future and it went well. Per this morning’s news, all film units, Paramount and Warner Bros, are to report into Paramount Pictures co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein . The future of Warner Bros motion picture chairs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy remains up in the air at the newly relabeled Skydance entertainment conglomerate; that duo is still in need of a chat with Ellison. Watch on Deadline Gunn has been shooting the Superman sequel Man of Tomorrow, set for release on July 9, 2027. The label’s Clayface, about the Batman antagonist, is their first lower-budget genre movie, opens October 23. Warner Bros’ second highest-grossing movie last year was Gunn’s Superman with more than $618 million at the global box office. Also in production at DC is Matt Reeves’ sequel The Batman Part II set for February 18, 2028. This past summer’s Supergirl didn’t go so well, with a global gross of $126.4M. Meanwhile, the DC-HBO Max series Lanterns has been a ratings success. Co-created by Tom King, Damon Lindelof and Chris Mundy, it saw its third episode score a massive 10M global viewers in its first three days — 7M from the U.S. Since Lanterns premiered August 16, the pilot has been seen by more than 20 million viewers worldwide and continues to grow, the company said. The series launched as one of HBO Max’s top titles . Safran and Gunn were appointed to lead DC Studios in October 2022 in a new label strategy orchestrated by WBD CEO David Zaslav to mimic Disney’s production label hub structure of Marvel Studios, Lucasfilm, Pixar, etc., with myriad production heads. It was arguably the first time (unless we count Charlie Chaplin) that a filmmaker, Gunn, did double duty as a studio executive. Safran already had a hot streak at Warners/New Line with the multibillion-dollar The Conjuring franchise and also producing DC franchise titles like Shazam and Aquaman . Safran had produced on Gunn’s 2021 The Suicide Squad movie and its HBO Max spinoff series Peacemaker starring John Cena, which has clocked two seasons. This is all according to sources Friday morning. Paramount and DC couldn’t be reached for comment. articles.title: Skydance Putting All 3 TV Studios Under George Cheeks: Warner Bros. TV, CBS Studios, PTVS – The Dish
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Post-Merger Skydance Keeping Both HBO Max & Paramount+ Streaming Brands Skydance Putting All 3 TV Studios Under George Cheeks: Warner Bros. TV, CBS Studios, PTVS – The Dish Shane Paul McGhie & Dasan Frazier To Headline Issa Rae’s Male Friendship Comedy Pilot At HBO View All October 2, 2026 3:05pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc George Cheeks, Channing Dungey, David Stapf, and Matt Thunell Sundance/Courtesy More elements of the proposed post-WBD merger Skydance ‘s executive structure are coming into focus ahead of the Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery transaction closing on Tuesday. As Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg are poised to oversee Skydance’s movie studios , Warner Bros and Paramount, another senior executive on Paramount CEO David Ellison’s team, Chair of TV Media George Cheeks , would be doing the same with the combined company’s three TV studios, sources said. (This is being done in streaming too, with HBO’s Casey Bloys in line to run the combo of HBO Max and Paramount+.) Related Stories Executives Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit, Setting Up Likely Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy Exit News Paramount-WBD Will Now Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals As part of his current portfolio, Cheeks oversees CBS Studios , something he has done since joining then-ViacomCBS in 2020, with CBS Studios President David Stapf reporting to him. I hear he will now add oversight of Warner Bros Television and Paramount Television Studios, with Channing Dungey, currently Chairman and CEO, Warner Bros Television Group and US Networks, and PTVS President Matt Thunell both staying on and reporting to him. Watch on Deadline It is part of a role expansion for Cheeks post-merger, which is said to also include some sort of oversight of cable brands on the WBD side. (According to the settlement with the 12 state attorneys general, “Paramount and Warner Brothers are required to continue negotiating their cable packages separately.”) In his current post, Cheeks oversees all linear Paramount networks, including CBS (entertainment, sports and news), MTV, Comedy Central, Nickelodeon and BET. The consolidation makes sense. For instance, Thunell, well-liked by Ellison from their tenure together at Skydance, currently reports to Goldberg who, alongside Greenstein, will have their hands full running both movie studios. There had been some speculation that Dungey, given the size and output of Warner Bros TV and her stature as a top TV executive with clout and connections in the industry, may report directly to the CEOs of the combined company as she does now at WBD. Noah Wyle in HBO Max’s ‘The Pitt’ HBOMAX The move would keep the number of direct reports to Ellison (and now co-CEO Ynon Kreiz) across film, TV and streaming on par with what they were at Paramount Skydance, with Bloys (replacing Cindy Holland, who just stepped down ), Goldberg & Greenstein and Cheeks. The combination also would position the three TV studios for future consolidation. It took Disney six years after the acquisition of Fox assets to fully merge the company’s three TV studios — 20th Television, ABC Signature and Touchstone Television — which was done in two stages. CBS Studios has the most clearly defined lane of the three studios as the primary supplier to CBS (as well as home of Star Trek and an opportunistic third-party seller). As things currently sit, there is some overlap between Warner Bros Television and PTVS. They each have been tasked with mining the IP of their sister film studios (which explained Goldberg’s oversight of PTVS) and have been main suppliers to their sibling streamers HBO Max and Paramount+, respectively. Their common playing area is the open streaming market, as both are actively selling outside and have hits on multiple platforms. ‘Abbott Elementary’ Disney / Sami Drasin Over the past couple of years, Warner Bros Television, historically the largest independent TV studio that produced Friends, ER and The Big Bang Theory , has pulled away from developing for broadcast where it still has hit shows in ABC’s Abbott Elementary and CBS’ Big Bang spinoff Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage and Fox’s sophomore drama Memory of a Killer. That is because networks increasingly stay in-house, which helps makes the economics of broadcast work but essentially shuts out third-party suppliers. It is unclear whether that would change now that WBTV would be vertically integrated with a broadcast network, CBS, for the first time, but CBS Studios is pretty dialed in on the CBS brand and its needs, producing the NCIS and Fire Country franchises, Matlock and Ghosts for the network, as well as Little House On the Prairie for Netflix. Recent WBTV highlights include the continuous success of The Pitt , which just repeated as the winner of the Outstanding Drama Series Emmy , the return of Ted Lasso, and the breakout debuts of Rooster and Big Bang spinoff Stuart Fails to Save the Universe , which have been renewed for Season 2. The studio has coming up the buzzy Harry Potter series. Thunell Frankenstein-ed PTVS last fall when he was tasked with integrating together Skydance Television and all cable production units of Paramount, including Showtime/MTV Entertainment Studios, Nickelodeon live-action and Awesomeness, into the new studio. The company, which produces the entire Taylor Sheridan slate for Paramount+, just scored renewals for both its flagship drama Reacher and its spinoff Negaley . Alan Ritchson as Jack Reacher Jasper Savage/Prime Video While he comes from a legal/business background, Cheeks is known for his creative involvement in the brands he oversees. (He is credited with identifying the franchise potential of CBS’ Fire Country , for example.) In addition to being in charge of CBS Studios for the past six years, Cheeks’ TV studio experience includes a stint as Vice Chairman, NBCUniversal Content Studios. articles.title: Montana Locals Protest Daily Wire’s Pro-ICE Production As Filming Disrupts Businesses With Apparent Dramatization Of Renée Good Shooting
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Zach Bryan Dons “Free Palestine” Shirt For Concert At Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium Pedro Pascal Was Surprised Tony Gilroy Made ‘Behemoth!’ “So Intimate And Healing”: “I Thought You Were Gonna Be Mean” ‘Real Time’: Bill Maher Tells New Skydance Bosses “Don’t Believe What Trump Is Tweeting About Me” View All October 2, 2026 3:12pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Daily Wire's 'Pawn Shop' production in Livingston, Montana sparks protests from locals. Rich Polk/Getty Images for Politicon/Courtesy Keegan Nashan Daily Wire ‘s new pro- ICE movie production has attracted local protesters in Livingston, Montana. Filming under the working title Pawn Shop , the latest project from Ben Shapiro’s Daily Wire and Dallas Sonnier’s Bonfire Legend has upset locals — not just because of its alleged use of blank gunshots, pyrotechnics and a staged car wreck without properly notifying residents and businesses, but because its opening scene appears to dramatize ICE’s fatal shooting of Renée Good in Minnesota back in January. Related Stories News ‘Run Hide Fight: Infidels’: Full Trailer For Jonathan Majors’ Controversial Comeback Movie, Daily Wire Release Date Revealed News Trump Celebrity Supporters: Famous Folks In Favor Of The 47th President Livingston local Brooklyn Wilde, who also works in the film industry as a producer and director, tells Deadline that given how much of a “tight knit small town” Livingston is, “This production crew could have done a lot better with notifying everyone.” Watch on Deadline Deadline has reached out to Daily Wire and Bonfire Legend for comment. Daily Wire's new pro-ICE movie production has attracted local protesters in Livingston, Montana. Filming under the working title 'Pawn Shop', the latest project from Ben Shapiro's Daily Wire and Dallas Sonnier's Bonfire Legend has upset locals — not just because of its alleged… pic.twitter.com/LBCQh4rEkh — Deadline (@DEADLINE) October 2, 2026 Meanwhile, the Livingston Food Resource Center (LFRC) released a statement explaining how the production has impacted its clients, who “already face numerous obstacles to meeting their most basic needs.” The group notes that it is the only resource of its kind in the area, serving one in eight Park County residents, and the production has resulted in an “unacceptable” eight-week low in their attendance. “Since filming began across the street from our building, road closures and armed security guards have increased the barriers to accessing food,” they said. “Our clients deserve to feel unequivocally safe accessing this essential resource.” The LFRC claimed they “were not notified of the plans to film” Pawn Shop in front of their pantry and were only informed about the production when calling the city to inquire. “There was no part of the permit process that allowed us to object or advocate for our clients, as the permit had already been issued and filming was due to start that week,” they added. In response, Wilde has joined fellow concerned locals in protesting the production, chanting “Ben Shapiro is a cuck” and shouting details of Good’s fatal shooting at the hands of U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent Jonathan Ross. “It’s just been people who want to get up and say something,” said Wilde. “And we have a legal right to protest on the street as long as we keep it under 65 decibels, and the cops have been called on us about a dozen times. One of our sweetest protesters was ticketed.” With Rust producer Carter Boehm serving on the production team, the latest collaboration between Bonfire Legend’s Sonnier and Daily Wire comes after their last film, Run Hide Fight: Infidels , was picketed by IATSE. Several crew members walked off over labor issues in South Carolina, shortly before Jonathan Majors was involved in an on-set accident that resulted in his co-star JC Kilcoyne needing stitches “all over his hands” after falling through a window. Deadline has confirmed that the Pawn Shop production is not under an IATSE contract either, while it is under a “conditional start” with SAG-AFTRA. Filming takes place on the set of Daily Wire’s ‘Pawn Shop’ in Livingston, Montana. Courtesy of Keegan Nashan A call sheet seen by Deadline lists Danny Trejo, Harvey Keitel and Henry Thomas among the cast. The synopsis for Pawn Shop reads: “When chaos hits the streets of Minneapolis, a young federal agent is left alone after his partner is seriously hurt and must find a way to survive an increasingly dangerous situation. Seeking shelter inside a neighborhood pawn shop, he becomes trapped with a traditional Hispanic father and his progressive college-age son, forcing three very different men to confront fear, conflicting beliefs and a crisis that tests their courage and humanity.” Having recently filmed in the streets of Livingston, the opening scene appears to recreate Good’s fatal shooting through a sensationalized MAGA perspective, in which writer Jake Harlen describes the character Melanie as “a fat blue-hair.” “The first shot takes Melanie in the neck, below her covid mask. The second in the head, above her covid mask,” the script reads. “Blood SPLATTERS on her PASSENGER’s (40s, female, overweight) forehead and matching covid mask.” In a video of the sequence being filmed, protesters can be heard chanting through a megaphone, “Ben Shapiro is a cuck!” With dangerous stunts involving pyrotechnics, Livingston Fire Department confirmed they were on call, but some locals say they were not properly notified of the sequence taking place in their front yards. Deadline has reached out to the Montana Film Office. Livingston Police Chief Wayne Hard says the department has been contacted with complaints “on a daily basis” since production began. Renée Good “To my knowledge, they have the proper permits,” said Hard. “I don’t know whether or not there was an effort made by the film crew to notify neighboring residents and businesses.” With production scheduled in downtown Livingston through Oct. 10, the Livingston City Commission is holding a special meeting on Saturday at 9am to discuss the handling of the production. Directed by Michael Polish, the latest Daily Wire movie comes after Majors’ protested production, Run Hide Fight: Infidels , a sequel to the company’s 2021 feature debut. Meanwhile, Wilde and fellow protesters have discussed “a counter piece that could distract” from the movie, potentially making a documentary “not only about what they’re doing here, but also potentially tying it back into the tragedy that actually happened.” The filming of Pawn Shop comes as Good’s family filed two federal lawsuits on Thursday against the U.S. government, including a wrongful death claim and a complaint against Stephen Miller, Kristi Noem, Tom Homan and Jonathan Ross, as well as other federal agents. Ross shot Good dead on Jan. 7, 2026, as she attempted to drive away from an ICE operation in Minneapolis, amid the Trump administration’s militarization of major U.S. cities. articles.title: Selma Blair Announces ‘Hineni’ Doc About Antisemitism After She Was “Erased” Over Islamophobic Comments
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Zach Bryan Dons “Free Palestine” Shirt For Concert At Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium Pedro Pascal Was Surprised Tony Gilroy Made ‘Behemoth!’ “So Intimate And Healing”: “I Thought You Were Gonna Be Mean” ‘Real Time’: Bill Maher Tells New Skydance Bosses “Don’t Believe What Trump Is Tweeting About Me” View All October 2, 2026 4:11pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Selma Blair attends Variety Power of Women LA on Sept. 23, 2026 in Beverly Hills, California. River Callaway/PMC More than two years later, Selma Blair is taking the fallout over her Islamophobic comments and channeling it into a documentary about antisemitism . On Thursday, the actress announced at the ADL State of the Arts Reception in New York City that she’s making a documentary entitled Hineni ( Here I Am ) to say what she “couldn’t say two years ago” when she first apologized for her comments . “Two years ago I learned what erased feels like, and I’ve decided the opposite of erased is making something. So I’m making a film,” she said in her remarks . “The last time I let cameras in, it was about my body. This time it’s about my people. It’s a documentary about antisemitism, and as confounding and confusing as it seems to be because no one wants to talk about geopolitics but it seems to get intermingled completely, but I wanted to make this made for the people who are not in this room.” Related Stories News Selma Blair Now Claims Ignorance Was Cause Of Her Vitriolic Rant Against Islam & “Terrorist Supporting Goons” Agencies Selma Blair Parts Ways With Rep Team Including CAA And Narrative PR Blair continued, “It’s called Hineni . Here I am. The thing I couldn’t say two years ago, I’m now saying with a camera crew behind me. It goes to Israel, so people can see why that land is not an abstraction to us. And it talks to people who disagree with me, on camera, and keeps the disagreement in the cut, because you don’t change a mind by only talking to people who already agree with you.” Watch on Deadline Acknowledging the “ ignorance and rage ” of her words at the time, in the wake of the Oct. 7, 2023 Hamas attack on Israel, Blair come under fire in February 2024 for writing in a comment regarding Rep. Cori Bush (D-MO) and Rep. Rashida Talib (D-MI), “Thank you so much. Deport all these terrorist supporting goons. Islam has destroyed Muslim countries and then they come here and destroyed minds. They know they are liars. Twisted justifications. May they meet their fate.” During Thursday’s reception, Blair reflected on the moment. “It offended people, and I did apologize right away. No conditions, no fine print. I meant it then and I mean it now, and I’m leaving the comment there, because the comment was not the story,” she said. “Here’s what happened next. I’ll try to tell it fast, because it happened fast,” added Blair. “The brands I worked with were gone within a day. A few partnerships I’d spent years building were shelved. My agency was gone. My lawyer was gone. My publicist was gone. My book agent was gone. My book publicist was gone. My social media manager was gone. My son’s godmother was gone – my best friend. While some friends in the business quietly stood by me, most of them were gone. And of course, my manager, my supposed friend of thirty years, and a Jew, was gone too. I still don’t know what any of them were thinking. No one returned my calls. I know the phone stopped. Not rang less. Just stopped.” Following Blair’s 2024 comments, her representatives at CAA and Narrative PR parted ways with the actress known for roles in Cruel Intentions , Legally Blonde , The Sweetest Thing and more. Blair was previously the subject of the Discovery+ documentary Introducing, Selma Blair , which explored her multiple sclerosis diagnosis and how she adapted to living with the neurological disorder. articles.title: ‘Behemoth!’ Review: Pedro Pascal Hits All The Right Notes In Tony Gilroy’s Lyrical Love Letter To The Music Of The Movies – New York Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Pete Hammond Pete Hammond Awards Columnist/Chief Film Critic @DeadlinePete More Stories By Pete Kevin Feige Accepts Will Rogers Foundation Pioneer Of The Year, Promises Many More Movies To Come ‘Verity’ Review: Dakota Johnson And Anne Hathaway Play Authors In Psychological Thriller, But Are They Really Alter Egos For Colleen Hoover? ‘Digger’ Review: Tom Cruise Explodes In Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s Surprising And Urgent Disaster Movie Satire View All October 2, 2026 5:00pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'Behemoth!' Searchlight It has been 14 years since Tony Gilroy last directed a feature film, 2012’s The Bourne Legacy. Before that was Duplicity and in 2007 his sensational Oscar-nominated Michael Clayton. He has been busy though, notably the critically acclaimed TV series Andor, but it is good to see his rare sophisticated storytelling back on the big screen with the compelling journey of a lifelong cellist whose nomad-like life reaches a crescendo and turning point after years of following the music professionally and personally. Behemoth! , which had its world premiere today at the New York Film Festival , is the rare movie set in the world of Hollywood music soundstages and it undoubtedly is a love letter to this crucial, usually final, aspect of the production process. But its central focus is on the family and romantic ties of one musician, Alex Serian ( Pedro Pascal ), who was born to be in an orchestra — in fact he couldn’t escape it — and that has taken its toll on this man for whom music is the one and only steady beat in his life, if not his heart. Related Stories Documentary ‘You Can See Everything’ Directors On Filming Complex Doc: “If We Can’t Agree On What’s Happening, There’s Something There” – NYFF Festivals NYFF Turns Up The Heat As ‘Godzilla’, ‘Artificial’, ‘NAZA’, ‘You Can See Everything’ Spark Festival Buzz Alex’s grandfather was a session musician for movies who died playing on one in 1959; his absent father, Peter ( Hank Azaria ), also was a composer for cartoons and television, if not a creatively satisfied one; his mother Ginnie ( Jo Beth Williams ) was a successful musician herself; as was his brother Andy ( Will Arnett ), who had a taste of fame in a ’90s rock band. In many ways the devotion to their professional life all took a toll on this family, and in Alex’s case turned him inward — a traveling cello player drifting from city to city, and relationship to relationship, being on the road the only real life he knew, his true potential never completely met. Watch on Deadline Now after 20 years he is returning to Los Angeles, getting day work on a number of movie-scoring sessions but also dealing with family issues including the failing health of his mother, his brother’s quirkiness, and perhaps the biggest lingering question he has still in his life via an encounter with a 15- year-old prodigy, Viviana Glenn (Alexa Swinton), who not only has a huge following on the pop circuit (think Billie Eilish) but who also has now been called in to replace the composer on the movie Behemoth! (a code name for the secret film the are working on). All of this is played out in non-linear fashion as we meet Alex on a session for a movie, but as he plays the notes, Gilroy’s script goes to flashbacks of his earlier life, back and forth between present day and various years, jobs and romantic liaisons. First we get a look at his past romantic entanglements as one woman yells at him complaining about another she discovers he slept with. That one is a funny bit with a determined Carol Spedding ( Olivia Wilde ), with whom Alex had a fling in Chicago, but is now taking things overboard insisting he made a huge mistake breaking it off. This woman is just one boiling bunny removed from a restraining order and Wilde amusingly plays it for all its worth. In another flashback in Dallas we meet fellow musician Nadia Hynes ( Eva Victor ), who is involved sexually with the emotionally reserved Alex while at the same time committed to another very wealthy man, Dennis Glenn (Matthew Lillard). Cutting to six years later she has tragically died and Alex finds himself invited to her funeral, where her very young daughter Viviana demonstrates her unique talents with a piano composition. Alex begins to get a nagging feeling this girl could actually be his daughter from that long-ago relationship. Her musical abilities are just one clue. While at the funeral he runs into an old flame and close friend of Nadia (Margarita Levieva), leading both again to the bedroom. It won’t be the last time he visits this mansion as his quest for the truth leads him back in a totally different guise. Gilroy skillfully weaves all these vignettes in and out, each with its own particular musical theme as again it is music always leading the way through the maze of Alex Serian’s life. To do this no single composer was hired to create the all-important score, but rather nine well-known maestros with distinct talents — Michael Giacchino, James Newton Howard, Michael Abels, Emily Bear, Lukas Frank, Henry Jackman, Nami Melumad, Brandon Roberts and Alan Silvestri — who together make up The Behemoth! Collective, and who serve up a musical score that, to my ears, is hands down the year’s best. The memorable original song written for the fictional Viviana, “Your God Is Sleeping,” could be a major hit. Combined with magnificent sound design, Behemoth! is a feast for the ears. A total of 303 AFM musicians in Los Angeles were used in the musical sequences. And for all the talk of L.A.’s sad production decline as a shooting location, Gilroy has delivered a winning antidote for that as the City Of Angels has never looked so good. Pascal, utterly convincing as this accomplished musician, subtly plays Alex in a low-key style with no showboating or anything that rings false in a portrayal where he simply becomes this wandering soul in search of himself after years of denial. The supporting players (Carmen Cuba was casting director) could not be better. Victor ( Sorry, Baby ) is quite good as Nadia, nailing the complicated feelings of someone married to her music like Alex but confused in love. Kaya Ralls is a complete delight as Bronte, a young fellow musician Alex mentors; Swinton as the 15 year old Viviana is superb; Williams is equally impressive as Alex’s mother in two poignant scenes 10 years apart; Azaria as Alex’s dad is terrific, seen via a brutally honest video letter Alex discovers 25 years after it was recorded; and Wilde and Arnett are in for lighter moments that offer a nice balance to the heavier ones. Erik Griffin also has some good moments as the orchestra manager. In the end though, Behemoth! is not just a revealing character study of a man ultimately looking for his true place in the world, but also a gorgeous and glorious tribute to those who make the music that help make movies like this one so much richer. Producers are Gilroy, Sanne Wohlenberg and John Gilroy (who also did the complex editing for the film). Title: Behemoth! articles.title: Zach Bryan Dons “Free Palestine” Shirt For Concert At Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Zach Bryan Dons “Free Palestine” Shirt For Concert At Robert Kraft’s Gillette Stadium Pedro Pascal Was Surprised Tony Gilroy Made ‘Behemoth!’ “So Intimate And Healing”: “I Thought You Were Gonna Be Mean” ‘Real Time’: Bill Maher Tells New Skydance Bosses “Don’t Believe What Trump Is Tweeting About Me” View All October 2, 2026 8:34pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Zach Bryan performs during the Bud Light Backyard Tour on Feb. 9, 2024 in Las Vegas, Nevada. Christopher Polk/PMC Following Robert Kraft ‘s campaign against Macklemore, Zach Bryan made a statement with his performance at Gillette Stadium . During Friday’s stop at the Kraft-owned venue for his With Heaven on Tour, the Grammy winner stepped onto the stage with a “ Free Palestine ” shirt after Kraft and other venue owners pressured Ed Sheeran to drop Macklemore from his tour over his outspoken support for Palestinians. With another performance scheduled at the Massachusetts venue on Saturday night, it remains to be seen if Kraft will pull the plug. Related Stories Touring Macklemore Announces Free Palestine Tour “Sold Out Immediately,” Lineup Coming Soon News Ed Sheeran’s Controversial Gillette Stadium Concerts Canceled As Boston Braces For Nor’easter The show comes after Ed Sheeran was forced to cancel his Gillette Stadium shows last weekend amid a nor’easter headed for Boston, despite caving to Kraft’s demands. Opting to remain publicly neutral on the issue, Sheeran subsequently released a statement saying it was the “ promoter’s decision ” after Kraft assembled several of the tour venues to give him an ultimatum. articles.title: DOJ Argues CNN & Other Outlets Can Be Banned From White House If Trump Determines They Didn’t Meet “Minimum Requirements Of Professionalism”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Kennedy Center Honors To Move To D.C.’s Capital One Arena Amid Closure Of Arts Complex U.S. Job Growth Slowed To 29,000 In September, With Slight Dip In Movie And Music Employment Fox News Tops September And Q3 Ratings; MS NOW Sees Gains, CNN Shows Uptick In Some Categories View All October 2, 2026 9:36pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Donald Trump Andrew Harnik/Getty Images The Justice Department argued that Donald Trump can legally ban CNN , MS NOW and Politico from the White House because he determined that they didn’t meet the “minimum requirements of professionalism.” Last month, a federal judge granted the three outlets a temporary restraining order that forced the White House to reinstate dozens of their reporters’ hard passes. The outlets are now asking the judge to extend that 14-day order for a longer term via a preliminary injunction, claiming that Trump’s ban is a violation of their First and Fifth amendment rights. U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly, a Trump appointee, has said that he is bound by the precedent set in In a 1977 D.C. Circuit opinion, Sherrill vs. Knight, in which the judges ruled that “the protection afforded newsgathering under the First Amendment guarantee of freedom of the press requires that this access not be denied arbitrarily or for less than compelling reasons.” Related Stories Late Night TV 'Real Time': Bill Maher Tells New Skydance Bosses "Don't Believe What Trump Is Tweeting About Me" News Kennedy Center Honors To Move To D.C.'s Capital One Arena Amid Closure Of Arts Complex In a court filing on Friday , the DOJ claimed that the Sherrill case still would allow for the president to restrict the three outlets from accessing the White House grounds because the White House has a “compelling interest.” Watch on Deadline The DOJ lawyers claimed that the Sherrill decision does not “prevent the President from concluding that bona fide journalists would identify sources instead of relying on anonymous sources, commit to factual accuracy, and provide the White House an opportunity to comment, rather than ‘perform their duties in a way that … interfere[s] with the White House’s daily operations.’ …At a bare minimum, it is a significant violation of decorum to publish classified and sensitive national security information.” The news outlets’ legal team has rejected that assertion, writing in a filing earlier this week that Trump’s “statements also make clear he implemented the ban to coerce more favorable coverage from CNN, MS NOW, and Politico, and to deter other journalists and news organizations from newsgathering and reporting that the President might view as negative. And his administration has continued to retaliate against Plaintiffs even after the temporary restraining order, only underscoring that Defendants’ motive is to punish and chill journalism they dislike.” Even as access to the White House grounds has been reinstated, the White House has continued to restrict CNN from coverage of TV pool assignments, including travel with Trump on Air Force One. The outlets’ lawyers, led by Theodore Boutrous Jr., also noted that Trump and other White House officials “overlooked that the First Amendment protects reporting on matters affecting national security.” Kelly has set a hearing for Thursday on the news outlets’ motion for a preliminary injunction. In granting a TRO, Kelly concluded that the White House failed to provide due process to the news outlets. The DOJ has pointed to letters sent to the outlets as evidence that they were given due process. But those letters were sent on Sept. 22, four days after Trump’s ban was started. The judge also has noted that some of the objectionable stories cited by the DOJ do not have to do with national security. Kelly wrote in his order that “even the justifications provided to Plaintiffs after this case was filed are ambiguous about the true purpose of the revocations: while Defendants’ letters to Plaintiffs mention national security concerns, they purport to identify reporting that ‘threatened national security and/or spread falsehoods’ leaving open the possibility that all the stories fall into the later bucket, rather than the former.” Skydance Putting All 3 TV Studios Under George Cheeks: WBTV, CBS Studios, PTVS ‘Verity’ Solid $32M Start; ‘Digger’ At $10M Lowest Cruise Open In 19 Years What’s Next For De Luca, Abdy; Top Film Jobs To Greenstein, Goldberg Post-Merger Skydance Keeping Paramount+ & HBO Brands Read More About: 2 Comments

articles.title: ‘Concrete Turned to Sand’ Dives Into Oyster Farms, With Otherworldly Imagery From the ‘Backrooms’ DP (Exclusive Clip)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 2, 2026 5:45am 'Concrete Turned to Sand' film still Courtesy of Slag Pile Films If the liminal atmosphere in Backrooms , enhanced by the cinematography of Jeremy Cox, gave you a sense of dread, his camera work on Concrete Turned to Sand will take you into a very different space – oyster farms in British Columbia, Canada. Yes, oyster farms! But again, you better get ready for an immersive sensory cinematic experience that will plunge you into a world full of otherworldly, almost sci-fi-esque, images and all sorts of different emotions and sensations. The film from Vancouver-based directors Jessica Johnson and Ryan Ermacora, will screen, starting on Oct. 11, in the BFI London Film Festival ‘s (LFF) Documentary Competition program, but it is not your regular doc. In fact, notes about the film, which is shot on 35mm, describe it as “a radical refusal of the conventional documentary narrative.” Related Stories Business MIA Market Unveils 2026 Program, Lineup For Digital Era TV Daniel Ezra's Full-Circle Goodbye to 'All American' The movie from Slag Pile Films received its world premiere at the Hot Docs Canadian International Documentary Festival in Toronto and will now celebrate its international premiere in London. Audiences can expect natural richness, such as underwater images of glistening shellfish, to encounter ecological dread. After all, the oysters on the coast of the Discovery Islands that are featured in the film take years to reach maturity, but all around them, the pace of environmental change is accelerating. And through Cox’s lens, nature looks, and almost feels, otherworldly. The film’s soundscape, created with sound artist and musician Scott Gailey, adds another key sensory layer. ‘Concrete Turned to Sand,’ courtesy of Slag Pile Films Don’t expect a multitude of data charts and the like, though. After all, the press notes for the film highlight: “Amid accelerated climate change and lives increasingly hyper-mediated by technology, the film resists the impulse to explain, choosing sensation over exposition.” You can catch a trailer for Concrete Turned to Sand right here, but THR can now also premiere an exclusive clip from the film at the end of this post. Through their work, Johnson and Ermacora explore “the convergence of labor, landscape and the political and economic forces that shape them.” As a result, in Concrete Turned to Sand , oyster farming becomes a lens for the collision of different time scales: the years it takes an oyster to mature, the accelerating pace of environmental change, and the geological time of our planet. And that is by design. After all, the creative team explains: “By placing human labor and science within these vastly different temporalities, the film asks us to reconsider not only how we look at the state of the environment, but how we understand our own brief presence – and effect – within it.” The rich cinematic imagery and sound give new forms to the often complex and invisible realities of climate change. ‘Concrete Turned to Sand,’ courtesy of Slag Pile Films “We worked with scientists to provide insight into ocean acidification and its impacts, while offering perspectives on the geological timescale of our ecological circumstances,” say Johnson and Ermacora. “This project explores methods of representing climate change by experimenting with optical and auditory techniques that play with the distanciation between the viewer and the ecological subject of the film. Concrete Turned to Sand creates an encounter between the beauty and strangeness of our world, engaging us to think beyond our atomization and towards broader ecological understanding and context.” For some scientific insight and to get another glimpse into the world of the film, check out an exclusive clip from Concrete Turned to Sand below. THR

articles.title: It’s Skydance: David Ellison Brands Combined Paramount-Warner Bros. With His Studio’s Title
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 6:11am David Ellison David Becker/Getty Images The entertainment business’ newest conglomerate has a name: Skydance . David Ellison on Friday shared on X that once Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery combine, the new corporate brand will take the name of the studio he founded 20 years ago. But while that will be the corporate name, Paramount and Warner Bros. will serve as sub-brands. “Both have distinct identities, extraordinary legacies and brands that have resonated with audiences for generations,” Ellison wrote. “We wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. — and all our extraordinary brands — to remain in the spotlight.” The name answers one of the bigger unanswered questions about the new company, which will firmly be among the biggest in the business, alongside The Walt Disney Co. and Netflix. In the entertainment business, the truth is that the corporate brand doesn’t always matter. It does for Disney, which is synonymous with a certain type of family-friendly content, and it does for Netflix, which is synonymous with streaming, but the industry past and present has been filled with owners that have names like Comcast, Viacom, News Corp., Versant, Capital Cities, etc. Hardly household names for most consumers. For most public companies, a corporate name is just a corporate name, a “house of brands” to hold the consumer-facing ones, even if they may share the name of a film studio. Ellison founded the Skydance film studio in 2006, and used it as a vehicle to acquire Paramount last year, before pivoting to Warner Bros. Discovery shortly after. He also posted a sizzle video featuring footage from some of the film and TV projects of the combined company, ending with a title card that perhaps tees up just how how is thinking about the individual brands that will live within Skydance. David Ellison’s reveal of Skydance as the holding corporation name. @ellisonskydance/X The card features the Skydance logo in the middle, surrounded by the logos for the Paramount and Warners film studios, CBS, HBO Max, Paramount+, DC Comics, Nickelodeon, and CNN, suggesting the importance of those brands to the larger strategy. Reading between the lines, one gets the sense that the film studios and streaming platforms will retain their own identities, with CBS (sports and broadcast), Nickelodeon (kids and family) and CNN (news) anchoring their own parts of the business. “We have big goals for Skydance, and we intend to pursue them with passion, imagination and a willingness to take smart risks,” Ellison wrote. “At the same time, we will honor what makes Paramount and Warner Bros. special — giving both studios the opportunity to grow, tell more great stories and bring those stories to even broader audiences around the world, powered by the scale and capabilities of Skydance.” The $111 billion mega-merger is slated to close next week, with Ellison joined by former Mattel chief Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO. Other members of the leadership team are still being determined. THR

articles.title: Guillermo del Toro Defends Tom Cruise’s ‘Digger,’ Rips “Petty” Headline
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 6:28am Riz Ahmed in 'Digger.' Courtesy Warner Bros. Pictures Digger has found a big defender in Guillermo del Toro . The Oscar-winning Frankenstein and The Shape of Water director posted a couple of times over the last 24 hours advocating for the beleaguered Alejandro G. Iñárritu film, which has generated polarized ( some scathing ) reviews. The director’s first message on the subject was reacting to a post from the entertainment news site IGN, which had written, “The theater experience won’t change your mind on Digger , and the laughs that are there still will be when it hits HBO Max.” Related Stories Movies Why Is Tom Cruise's 'Digger' Facing Such a Bumpy Box Office Road? Movies Tom Cruise's 'Digger' Was Originally Titled 'Blah, Blah, Blah,' Iñárritu Reveals Del Toro shot back : “Entirely Petty headline. Love it or not. And, yes, I do. The film delivers in scale, ambition and reach at a theatrical screen level. Daring, bold and Cinematically complex. Decidedly a Theatrical experience.” Then, reacting to a post about Ken Russell’s controversial 1971 film, The Devils , del Toro wrote, “I was a kid and I remember this film — released by [Warner Bros.] was [called by critics] ‘excessive, overbearing’ etc and, in my country, Mexico, we were told that the Church explicitly considered it blasphemy. And here we are … I LOVE it more than ever — because it is NOT about possession but what the political narrative does with it. Glad WB takes risks — even now…” Continued the director, now directly referring to Digger : “BTW there is a ‘climate change’ movie in release that Is NOT about climate change but the manipulation of narratives — and yes it is released by WB (possibly the very last movie WB as such will ever release) and has been deemed ‘excessive, overbearing’ so see it in a theatre.” Not too many are expected to see Digger in a theater this weekend, however, with the film eyeing a domestic opening that’s south of $15 million. On the reviews front, the film currently sits at 54 percent positive on Rotten Tomatoes. The audience score is higher at 65 percent (presumably, given all the hubbub in the press, those still going to see the film had at least some idea what they’re going into). Iñárritu and del Toro have been friends for decades and regularly consult with one another on projects. The duo, along with Alfonso Cuarón, have been called Mexican cinema’s “Three Amigos.” In a profile on the trio’s friendship from The Los Angeles Times in 2006, Iñárritu said, “We share, we complain, we fight, we suggest. And then you support.” Del Toro’s next film is The Buried Giant , a stop-motion animated adaptation of Kazuo Ishiguro’s 2015 novel for Netflix. THR

articles.title: Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros.
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Mia Galuppo Plus Icon Mia Galuppo Senior Entertainment Reporter miagaluppo Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 6:57am Pamela Abdy and Michael De Luca attend the 'Digger' London premiere. Stuart C. Wilson/Getty Images Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy are out at Warner Bros, an insider tells The Hollywood Reporter . The news of film chiefs’ imminent exit comes as Paramount Skydance prepares for its landmark $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. The combined David Ellison-owned super studio is now called, simply, Skydance, with the merger expected to be finalized on Oct. 6. Paramount film heads Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein are expected to oversee both movie studios. Abdy and De Luca are said to have told associates they have been in talks for a possible next act at Netflix. De Luca and Abdy‘s tenure heading up Warner Bros. Motion Picture Group began in 2022 and has been marked by highs and lows. The highs have included box office successes like the Minecraft Movie ($960 million, globally) and Ryan Coogler’s Sinners ($370 million, globally), along with critical achievements like last year’s Oscars best picture win for Paul Thomas Anderson‘s One Battle After Another and other wins for Sinners . The misfires have included expensive swings like Maggie Gyllenhaal‘s The Bride! and Tom Cruise starrer Digger , which is tracking to open this weekend to a dismal $8 million to $15 million on a $125 million-plus budget. De Luca and Abdy joined Warner Bros. from MGM, where they oversaw that storied studio’s film slate for two years until its 2022 $8.5 billion acquisition by Amazon Prime Video. At Warners, they inherited a slate from the previous regime, headed by Toby Emmerich, that included Legendary’s Dune franchise and the box office hit Barbie , along with Bong Joon Ho‘s Mickey 17 and Robert De Niro starrer The Alto Knights , the latter of which was personally greenlit by Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav. As for their own auspices, the duo is known for being director-friendly, offering a big studio home (and big studio budgets) to filmmakers like Anderson, Coogler, Alejandro Iñárritu and Emerald Fennell. The auteur-driven titles were buffeted by a series of IP plays and franchise offerings, predominantly hailing from the studio’s New Line division, De Luca’s longtime stomping grounds, like the well-received Final Destination reboot and a Conjuring installment. De Luca and Abdy’s exit comes amid a flurry of other executive announcements at the soon-to-be-combined studio. Earlier this week, Cindy Holland exited her post as Paramount Skydance’s streaming chief, with HBO boss Casey Bloys expected to lead all streaming efforts at the combined studios. Also this week, it was announced that Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz would come on as co-CEO with Ellison. Puck first reported the news of De Luca and Abdy‘s exit. THR

articles.title: SCAD Savannah Film Fest: Keanu Reeves, Seth Rogen, Gemma Chan and Jordan Firstman Among Big Names Set for Honors (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking News Michael De Luca, Pamela Abdy Out at Warner Bros. close By Scott Feinberg Plus Icon Scott Feinberg Executive Editor of Awards ScottFeinberg Follow Sign Up View All October 2, 2026 7:11am Gemma Chan, John Cho, Carrie Coon, Rosalind Eleazar, Jordan Firstman, James Gray, Anthony Ippolito, Billie Piper, Keanu Reeves and Seth Rogen Courtesy of Subject (4); Benjo Arwas; Heather Hazzan; Will Aldersley; Macrae Marran; Simon Emmett; Brian Bowen Smith Later this month, a veritable parade of A-list movie stars and filmmakers — many of whom are in serious contention for Oscars — will head south to attend screenings of their work and collect special honors at the 29th edition of the SCAD Savannah Film Festival , the nation’s largest university-run film festival.
