articles.title: Amy Goodman Documentary ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ Acquired by Music Box in North America, Home Entertainment Release Set for Oct. 20 (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:10am PT Amy Goodman Documentary ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ Acquired by Music Box in North America, Home Entertainment Release Set for Oct. 20 (EXCLUSIVE) By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest AGC Studios Launches AGC Digital, a Division Focused on Nurturing Creator-Led Intellectual Property 1 day ago Thessaloniki’s Agora Crossroads Co-production Forum to Feature 14 Projects From 15 Countries 1 day ago Woody Allen’s New Movie to Star Marton Csokas, Jemima Kirke and More as WestEnd Boards Sales 1 day ago See All Courtesy of Music Box Films Music Box Films has acquired North American rights for documentary “ Steal This Story, Please! ,” and will release the film on all major digital platforms on Oct 20. The film, initially self-distributed by the filmmakers, had a successful theatrical release across the U.S. in the spring, grossing close to $1 million. “Steal This Story, Please!,” which focuses on the work of trailblazing independent journalist Amy Goodman , is directed by Academy Award nominees Carl Deal and Tia Lessin. Popular on Variety Related Stories Alan Cumming Sheds His 'Traitors' Kilt for 'Tip Toe', a Searing Parable of Homophobic Backlash: TV Review Music Box will also release the film on DVD and Blu-ray with the physical media release date to be announced. It will have a live online screening on Oct. 13 at 8 p.m. ET, followed by a live Q&A talkback with Goodman, alongside Lessin and Deal (“Trouble the Water,” “Citizen Koch,” “The Janes”). Premiering at the 2025 Telluride Film Festival, “Steal This Story, Please!” went on to win audience awards at 11 festivals — including Mill Valley, Palm Springs, Santa Barbara and Woodstock. The film, which had theatrical booking support from Michael Tuckman’s mTuckman Media, opened on a single screen in New York at the IFC Center in April, grossed over $30,000 opening weekend and was held over for 12 weeks. Expanding nationally, the documentary screened in more than 50 markets and was one of the best performing non-fiction releases of this year. Music Box has acquired the film for theatrical and home entertainment rights, taking over theatrical bookings moving forward. In a statement, the distributor said that Goodman “has reported some of the most urgent and underreported stories of our time on her daily global newshour Democracy Now!. Drawing on an extraordinary archive, filmmakers Carl Deal and Tia Lessin take us behind the scenes with the warm, wisecracking granddaughter of an Orthodox rabbi — raised in a tradition of asking hard questions — as she navigates a media landscape reshaped by technology, corporate consolidation, and political assaults on the press.” It added, “Urgent, provocative and unexpectedly funny, ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ explores what’s at stake when journalism is threatened, and why the act of bearing witness has never mattered more.” Deal said, “We are thrilled that ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ will be part of the Music Box family of high-quality independent films, and that Amy’s story will get to home audiences far and wide at a moment when free expression is in the crosshairs of the President of the United States.” Lessin added, “Long before attacks on the press became a defining feature of our political life, Amy Goodman understood that democracy depends on independent, uncompromised journalism that doesn’t bow to power. We are excited to join forces with Music Box Films to build on the theatrical success of the film and ensure that it reaches home audiences in the same spirit of editorial freedom and direct engagement that has defined Amy’s work, as well as our own.” “ ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ had the highest-grossing week of any documentary in the history of the Music Box Theatre in Chicago,” said Music Box Films. “We are thrilled to continue our relationship with Amy, Carl and Tia, in expanding the audience reach of this powerful documentary.” “In a marketplace where industry leaders continually harp on about the limited theatrical prospects for documentaries – especially those of a political nature – the unabashed success of ‘Steal This Story, Please!’ proves that audiences are still wanting to be moved and entertained,” said Tuckman. “Grossing close to a million, the release is a testament to Carl and Tia’s belief that theaters are still the best place for documentaries to engage and inspire audiences.” “Steal This Story, Please!” is executive produced by Jane Fonda, Rosario Dawson, Tom Morello, Sheila Nevins, Julie Cohen, Tony Tabatznik, Bill Haney, Jonathan Logan and Steve Silberstein, produced by Deal and Lessin, with producers Karen Ranucci, Diana Cohn and Caren Spruch. The sale of the home entertainment rights was negotiated by Brian Andreotti on behalf of Music Box Films and Ben Schwartz and Joe Tufano at Submarine. articles.title: How Elizabeth Holmes Was Secretly Filmed for ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: 7-Person Crew, 16-Hour Shoots and Cameras Covering the ‘Whole House’
articles.full_text: Oct 2, 2026 8:10am PT How Elizabeth Holmes Was Secretly Filmed for ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: 7-Person Crew, 16-Hour Shoots and Cameras Covering the ‘Whole House’ By Jordan Moreau Plus Icon Jordan Moreau Latest Nathan Fielder Speaks Out on Living With Elizabeth Holmes While Filming ‘You Can See Everything’ Doc: ‘She Seems So Genuine’ but ‘I Know She’s a Liar’ 1 day ago Ex-‘American Idol’ Contestant Caleb Flynn Found Guilty of Murdering Wife 3 days ago Elizabeth Holmes Posts Cryptic Message From Prison Ahead of ‘You Can See Everything’ Release: ‘I Was Silenced for a Long Time’ 4 days ago See All Courtesy of A24 Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim shocked Hollywood and the world when they revealed they’d secretly been filming Elizabeth Holmes ahead of her 11-year prison sentence for their documentary, “ You Can See Everything .” The film had a surprise premiere at the Telluride Film Festival last month and had another early screening at the New York Film Festival on Wednesday, where the co-directors peeled the curtain back on how they pulled off the shoot. Holmes and her partner Billy Evans invited Fielder, Oppenheim and a small camera crew into their San Diego home 34 days before Holmes began her Theranos fraud prison sentence. Fielder, who makes his feature directorial debut with the film, is known for blending bizarre, real subjects with absurd, scripted comedy on his shows “Nathan for You” and “The Rehearsal.” But he had planned to stay behind the camera when he and Oppenheim embarked on “You Can See Everything.” Popular on Variety Related Stories Paranormal Comedy 'Don't F — k With Ghosts' Premieres On Demand, Launches Original YouTube Channel (EXCLUSIVE) Prime 'Big Deal Days' 2026: What to Know About Amazon's October Prime Day Sale “I was like, ‘I’m definitely not going to be in this when we started,’” Fielder said. “I was behind the camera with Lance, and it was strange. [Holmes and Evans] would keep talking to me or asking me questions, and I would answer from off-camera. But then eventually, the operators would start panning over to me because the conversations would be long.” “You became this accidental investigator of everyday moments,” Oppenheim added. “I feel like that also came about too because the way we were shooting it initially was with one camera and anamorphic lenses, and it was extremely cumbersome. It was the wrong approach for this. Every time we would miss a moment or try to change a lens, that would be when they would also be engaging Nathan off-camera. So eventually, probably about a day of getting it fully wrong, we decided essentially to completely change the way both of us work.” Fielder and Oppenheim both brought crew members from their past projects, including cinematographer David Bolen, who worked on Oppenheim’s recent film “Primetime” and his docs “Spermworld” and “Some Kind of Heaven.” “It basically made us work in this completely new way, which oddly and ironically, is as close to the tenets of documentary filming, which is just fly-on-the-wall, vérité filmmaking,” Oppenheim said. “So we had three cameras, two operators, one would be sometimes on Elizabeth or Billy, one would be on Nathan, and we basically pick zones of the house and have these extremely long zoom lenses. Then I would be hidden behind the wide camera. We were trying to do that in an effort to try and take all the pressure away from any moment. We would be shooting like 16 hours a day, so they wouldn’t really know what we were interested in necessarily.” “We didn’t always know either,” Fielder joked. “We started setting up the cameras where we had a wide lens that would cover the whole house, so if something happened, we wouldn’t miss it. The other two 25mm to 250mm lenses could be wide, but then also zoom, so we could basically capture everything.” Fielder revealed that the crew was comprised of just seven people, and only four of them would be inside Holmes’ house at any time. He also shouted out Bolen, who “found a way to make shots look beautiful in the day or the night.” “As long as there was a light, we could make it work,” Fielder said. “If we were live and then something interesting started happening, [Bolen] could pick up the camera and tripod, move to a new spot, re-lock the head in 10 seconds. It looks amazing, and it’s a testament to the team who put this together. It was down to this whole dance we had, and it was just amazing and one of the best experiences I think we’ve had making something because of that exploratory freedom and being able to let our curiosity drive us.” Oppenheim and Bolen collaborated on “Primetime,” starring Robert Pattinson as “To Catch a Predator” host Chris Hansen. The film was shot in a boxy 4:3 aspect ratio to mimic the retro, reality TV look of “To Catch a Predator” from the 2000s. Oppenheim used the same format on “You Can See Everything” to get close-up, reaction shots from Holmes, Evans and Fielder. “One thing we realized with the one camera that’s panning is that the moment you say something to someone, you want to see their face the moment they hear it,” Fielder said. “Especially in a movie like this, where you’re trying to evaluate if someone’s being honest or not, when you have to swing, you’re missing a few seconds.” Oppenheim added, “The aspect ratio of the movie came about because we’re confined largely in one space, and there was so much. Every time we put the camera somewhere, when we originally were in a larger aspect ratio, it felt like you were seeing so many details that were distracting you from the human face. The face is the ultimate landscape. You wanted to be on their faces when something would happen and really study it and linger there, because that could get the closest you could possibly be to being there.” Taylor Swift Announces ‘The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore’ Album With Four New Songs Taylor Swift Praises Phoebe Bridgers’ New Album ‘Lost Weekend,’ Calls It an ‘Absolute Triumph in Every Way’ Dakota Johnson on Being in Taylor Swift’s ‘Patient Zero’ Music Video: ‘We Respect Each Other’s Creative Minds’ Taylor Swift Recalls How ‘I Knew You Were Trouble’ Was Written as a ‘Really Sad Ballad’ in Grammy Museum Conversation Video Todd Rundgren Slams Taylor Swift, Says She ‘Ruined Music’ and Is ‘the Apotheosis of Mediocrity’ Taylor Swift Surprises Emmys in ‘SVU’ Parody but Skips Show to Attend Chiefs Game With Tom Cruise Loading comments...

articles.title: Ynon Kreiz, Newly Minted Co-CEO Of Paramount, To Get Pay Bump After WBD Merger Close, $31.5M…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes , Jill Goldsmith October 1, 2026 2:27pm Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc Ynon Kreiz, who will be co-CEO of the combined Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images Ynon Kreiz , who was tapped Wednesday as Co-CEO of the soon-to-merge Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery, will collect a $31.5 million signing bonus and at least $35.1 million a year in total compensation by 2027. In an SEC filing Thursday, Paramount laid out terms of the former Mattel CEO’s 5-year contract and said its board of directors approved the appointment of Kreiz on Sunday. His exit from Mattel was announced Wednesday morning, with Paramount revealing his new post later in the day. After a lengthy legal challenge by 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America put it in limbo for two months, the $110 billion merger is slated to close on Tuesday. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” News Paramount-WBD Merger Is A Go As Judge Approves Legal Settlement, Last Hurdle To Close Kreiz will receive a signing bonus in the form of restricted stock units [RSUs] worth $31.5 million. Beyond the signing bonus, the filing lays out two sets of figures – one covering the brief pre-merger period and then another reflecting the time after the completion of the deal. The official first day of Kreiz’s employment contract is Monday, October 5, meaning he will have had time to put a few office supplies in desk drawers and visit the commissary before the elevated figures take effect. Kreiz, 61, will be paid an annual base salary of $3.5 million, rising to $5 million the day after the merger closes. His annual bonus targeted at $1.5 million will increase to $4.9 million. He will be eligible for 2.6 million shares of Class B stock along with another stock award of 1.25 million shares. Within 15 days after the merger close, he will be granted RSUs worth up to $5.1 million, prorated based on the part of the first year of employment following the merger close. Starting on October 5, 2027, the first anniversary of the start of the contract, Kreiz will be granted annual equity awards worth $20.1 million. While there are a number of variables, as is always the case with executive compensation, the upshot of the new figures is that Kreiz will be at the high end or above the range of his recent pay at Mattel. In 2023, he took home $18.9 million for running the toymaker, with the tally jumping to $37.8 million in 2024 and then declining to $15.1 million last year. The filing said Kreiz, who led Endemol Group, Maker Studios and Fox Kids Europe before joining David Ellison as Co-CEO, has “extensive leadership experience in the media and entertainment industry.” That background merited his appointment to the company’s board of directors along with the exec position, the board said. articles.title: International Insider: Merger Approved!; RTS London’s AI Buzz; Deadline @ Zurich
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max International Insider: Merger Approved!; RTS London’s AI Buzz; Deadline @ Zurich ‘Celebrity Traitors’ Returns With Biggest Ever Launch Ep Of Nearly 9 Million Viewers BBC Gives First Look At ‘The Last Detectives’ Crime Drama From Matthew Barry, Nicola Shindler View All October 2, 2026 5:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Paramount-Warner Bros. is set to close Getty Images Welcome, welcome Insiders. Max Goldbart here taking you through a week in which one of the biggest entertainment deals of this century was waved through. Read on. And sign up here . Merger Approved! Getty Images C-suite winners and losers: In the end it all happened quite quickly. Several weeks back it appeared that David Ellison might feel the full force of regulators in the UK and Europe, not to mention dozens of U.S. state AGs. Fast-forward to Wednesday and the $110B Paramount -WBD mega-merger was officially waved through and the new company will officially launch on Tuesday (October 6). Thoughts moved at lightning speed to the C-suite winners and losers, and we didn’t have to wait long for the departure of Cindy Holland, who it is heavily presumed will be replaced by HBO boss Casey Bloys as chief of streaming across both behemoths. In her email to staff, Holland hinted at Ellison “optimizing for HBO stability,” clearly a somewhat barbed nod to her successor. HBO was talking up its Spanish originals at Iberseries in Madrid this week and all eyes will now be on how much Bloys looks to expand the joint operation’s streaming strategy outside of the U.S., with internationals boss Sarah Aubrey expected to remain by his side. Nellie Andreeva’s deep dive can be found here . One name that wasn’t expected to pop up this week was Ynon Kreiz, the Israeli-born former Endemol Group boss who exited Mattel, and was then swiftly named co-CEO of Par-Warner, sharing top-dog duties with Ellison. Kreiz brings weighty international experience to the new entity, and was for a couple hours rumored to be taking up a big international job before being named co-chief. The long-serving Gerhard Zeiler still holds the international keys at Warner with Kevin MacLellan in an equivalent post at Par. Thoughts now turn to the outposts of both of these big beasts, where there is surely much rejigging and “optimizing” to come. Related Stories Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be Layoffs Executives David Ellison's "Coziness" With Donald Trump Is "Way Overstated", Per Paramount Backer Gerry Cardinale AI Chatter @ RTS London Watch on Deadline BBC Studios Generating headlines: Just a day before the merger completed, Reemah Sakaan, the boss of Paramount UK network 5, was facing tricky questions across the pond over political interference from her new overlords, but she batted them away with aplomb. This was at the RTS London Convention, where the great and good of the Brit TV industry gathered for a day jam-packed with news lines. With hundreds being laid off across the BBC and Channel 4, a new content chief set to be imminently announced at the latter, and the mergers at Sky-ITV and Banijay-All3Media taking hold, there was plenty to address. In the end, it was AI that once again generated headlines. Prime Video international boss Kelly Day laid down the gauntlet with a full-throated backing of AI first up, as she said the tech is “not a threat to creativity,” but is “creativity unleashed.” Not to be out-headlined, BBC DG Matt Brittin then raised eyebrows when he out-the-blue admitted he’d been sent a fully AI-generated episode of Doctor Who. “Pretty good,” was his verdict, leading BBC commissioners in the crowd to choke on their morning coffee. The reality is that the tech is here to stay and the peeps in charge clearly want to be realistic about its benefits… Creatives may take a little while to join them. Steven Knight, who is vehemently anti-AI, spoke a few hours after Brittin. However, all the crowd really wanted to know from the Peaky Blinders creator was the identity of the next 007, given that Knight is writing the Amazon MGM movie (Amazon was also sponsoring the RTS event). In the end, the crowd waited and waited, before all they got was a firm “no” to the question of whether writing the movie about the most famous spy on earth is giving him sleepless nights. Knight was neither shaken, nor stirred. All our RTS coverage can be found here . The Insider Interview: Academy Boss Bill Kramer @ Zurich Photo courtesy of Violeta Sofia Our Deadline Studio in Zurich was replete with big stars and industry names over the past week (for Martin Moszkowicz, Romain Bessi and more click here ), so it was difficult to boil the Insider Interview down to one. In the end we opted for a fascinating sit-down with Academy chief Bill Kramer, Mattel Studios’ Robbie Brenner and Sony Pictures Classics’ Michael Barker. The trio, unsurprisingly, wanted to chat about Obsession and Backrooms, the year’s big hits that look set to usher in a wave of YouTube creatives to mainstream film. For Kramer, their breakout success speaks to “the importance of fandom,” no matter where it comes from. >>> Watch the Interview Global Breakout Big Band Story, TF1 The French TV industry has its challenges at present, but Cat’s Eyes stands out. TF1’s series is about to launch Season 2 and is based on a cult 1980s Tokyo-set manga. The first season was a ratings hit airing on Hulu in the U.S. We checked out what the growing international buzz is all about. >>> Read The Breakout The Essentials Anthony Avellano for Deadline/Sarah Dunn/Getty/Stefan Kokovic/Getty 🌶️ Hot One : Nicolas Cage, Michael Sheen, Jordi Mollà, Emilio Sakraya and Adrian Topol are starring in C.L.A.Y. , a psychological cyber-thriller from Simon Afram. 🌶️ Another : Cast has been confirmed for Woody Allen’s next movie including Marton Csokas and Jemima Kirke. 🥇 Team unveiled: Banijay set out its new sales team under Cathy Payne, with Rachel Job nabbing a top job and a number of long-serving execs exiting. 📆 Premiere date: Indian rural horror Kaali Keti will be given a theatrical release on October 23. 🚪 Closing down: True Brit Entertainment, UK seller of The Death of Robin Hood, has filed for bankruptcy . 🏆 Awards latest: The European Film Academy has named Beki Probst, Marin Karmitz and Sandra den Hamer as the first recipients of its new Community Award. ⛺ Fest latest: Stewart was at Iberseries in Madrid, where co-pros , YA and the Banijay-All3 merger were in the spotlight. ⏱️ To the Tardis: Multiple BBC Studios labels will likely apply to be the next producer of Doctor Who . 🍿 Box office: KPop Demon Hunters 2 is targeting a “very broad theatrical release,” per Ted Sarandos. 🖼️ First look: At the third season of hit African drama series Shaka iLembe before its MIPCOM debut. articles.title: U.S. Job Growth Slowed To 29,000 In September, With Slight Dip In Movie And Music Employment
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Fox News Tops September And Q3 Ratings; MS NOW Sees Gains, CNN Shows Uptick In Some Categories Warner Bros Fires Off Cease And Desist Over Fox Nation’s ‘The Vow,’ But Network Rejects Claim New Series Infringes On ‘The Bachelor’ Fox Business To Debut ‘Big Money In The Morning’ To Replace Maria Bartiromo’s Show View All October 2, 2026 5:46am Add us as a Google Preferred Source U.S. Department of Labor building in Washington, D.C. Robert Knopes/Education Images/Universal Images Group via Getty Images U.S. job growth slowed in September to 29,000, while unemployment ticked up to 4.2%. Overall, the employment situation was largely unchanged during the month, amid continued concerns over rising prices. Employment in movies and music dipped slightly, shedding about 200 jobs to 328,500. Employment among broadcasting and content providers fell by 3,000, to 328,100. Industry lobbyists have pointed to job losses in movie and TV production as they press for passage of a 20% federal incentive, with hopes that Congress will take up a bill during the lame duck session. Related Stories News Aaron Sorkin Clarifies He "Was Never Asked" To Omit Trump From 'The Social Reckoning' But Film Is "Not A Red-Blue Thing" News Fox News Tops September And Q3 Ratings; MS NOW Sees Gains, CNN Shows Uptick In Some Categories The figures from the Bureau of Labor Statistics are the final monthly release before the midterm elections on Nov. 3. Watch on Deadline The Bureau of Labor Statistics also revised previous months’ figures, as is typical. The figures for July were changed downward by 31,000, showing a loss of 10,000 jobs. August’s job numbers, which were surprisingly robust, were revised down by 29,000 jobs, to 133,000. The biggest gains were in health care, adding 17,000 jobs, while there was a slight growth in construction and manufacturing jobs. The average hourly earnings rose by 5 cents, or 0.1%, to $37.81. Over the past 12 months, average hourly earnings have risen by 3%. Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal, called the report “mediocre.” She wrote on X, “The biggest sore spot = wage growth of 3% in past year. articles.title: ‘Night Of The Living Dead’ Vertical Microdrama Readied For Horror-Focused App Room418
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Prime Video’s ‘Bloodaxe’ Adds Maddy Ambus, Steven Brand & Lasse Steen To Cast Disney+ & Indonesia’s Vidio Launch Subscription Bundle ‘Shaka iLembe’: First Look At Season 3 Of MIPCOM-Bound African Zulu King Drama View All October 2, 2026 6:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Dylen Postnikoff is a co-founder and CEO of Room418; the original 'Night of the Living Dead' Courtesy/Everett Collection EXCLUSIVE: A newly-established microdrama business geared towards horror is adapting genre classic Night of the Living Dead ahead of its full launch. L.A.-based Room418 is positioning itself as a studio and platform that puts “vertical-first originals at the center of a dedicated destination for horror fans, alongside curated programming in vertical, horizontal and mixed formats.” A slate of acquired shows will launch the vertical video app, with original productions following. Related Stories News Vertical Video Economy Worth $150B, Even Without China – Owl & Co Report News Vertical Video Studio LoveHit Launches With Adaptations Of Literary Classics Starring Microdrama Regulars & Eric Roberts Former Blink49 Studios, CBC and Shaftesbury exec Dylen Postnikoff is leading Room418 as co-founder and CEO. Postnikoff, a comms and marketing specialist who helped shape the international profiles of Schitt’s Creek and Anne With an E , has been working at Wild Cards maker Blink49 since June last year . With horror from emerging creators already one of the stories of the year in film and TV through the successes of Curry Barker’s Obsession and Kane Parsons’ Backrooms , Room418 is looking to tap into the zeitgeist. As such, it is planning on working with creatives who’ve found success on Wattpad and digital platforms. Watch on Deadline An invite-only beta version of the Room418 app will launch this fall ahead of a commercial launch, featuring a slate of licensed horror content. Ten original and adapted projects have been optioned and are in development as well. Notably on the development slate is a vertical reimagining of George A. Romero’s 1968 horror classic Night of the Living Dead . The film has been in the public domain since its original release due to an error by its original distributor. The news comes hours after Deadline revealed filming has wrapped on Twilight of the Dead , a horror pic considered the “final chapter” of the late Romero’s zombie saga. Also on the slate is a screen adaptation of Ben Sobieck’s When the Black-Eyed Children Knock , which was popular on Wattpad. Room418 and Slash Management are also co-producing an original project with digital horror creator Monse Gutierrez, whose social handle is @CVNELA. The company is also collaborating with L.A.-based REELi Studios on an original horror series inspired by Filipino folklore, with production planned in the Philippines. “What makes horror so interesting globally is that fear is universal, but the mythology is local,” said Postnikoff. “Every market has its own stories, folklore and voices, and horror audiences are unusually willing to cross borders to discover them. At the same time, mobile has changed where discovery actually happens. We’re building Room418 to connect a global genre audience with a new generation of creators and stories designed for the way people are watching now.” The Room418 team see horror as particularly well-suited to the growing microdrama market, with cliffhangers and fan culture making aligning the genre with vertical video’s quick-hit format. “Vertical changes more than the frame,” said Postnikoff. “It changes the rhythm of the storytelling, how quickly you establish a world, where you build tension and how you earn the next episode. What excites us is what that unlocks. “A microseries can be a complete entertainment experience in its own right, but it can also introduce a filmmaker, prove an audience for an idea and become the first expression of IP that grows into film, television and beyond.” Postnikoff has worked in entertainment and media for more than 15 years, leading on brand and franchise strategy for the likes of Murdoch Mysteries and Kim’s Convenience . She’s hoping to apply her expertize in studio positioning, corp comms and audience growth to Room418’s mission to create a horror-first destination for genre fans. Room418 is working with technology firm KINO Studios on the app’s product and technical infrastructure. Members of KINO’s founding team previously were executive producers on A24’s Undertone , which premiered at the Sundance Film Festival. Should Room418 originals be successful, the company is eyeing expansions into film, television, adaptations and experiences. The invite-only beta of the Room418 app will launch later this fall ahead of the company’s commercial rollout. articles.title: Paramount-WBD Will Now Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs David Ellison’s “Coziness” With Donald Trump Is “Way Overstated”, Per Paramount Backer Gerry Cardinale Starz Goes Dark On Verizon FiOS Amid Carriage Dispute; Verizon Responds View All October 2, 2026 6:27am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc After the expected close of their merger, Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery will together be known as Skydance . CEO David Ellison revealed the new name Friday in a post on X . The $110 billion merger is projected to be finalized on Tuesday after a year-long pursuit by Ellison and a two-month delay caused by antitrust lawsuits by 12 states and the Writers Guild of America. Related Stories News Paramount-WBD Merger Is A Go As Judge Approves Legal Settlement, Last Hurdle To Close Executives Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” “What once was the peak, is now just the beginning,” Ellison wrote. “Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren’t rewriting history – we’re equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling.” The choice of the name, he said, stemmed from several objectives. One is to preserve the history of Paramount and Warner Bros. as individual entities under the Skydance umbrella. “We never wanted a new corporate identity to diminish, alter or overshadow either one. Instead, we wanted a name that would give the combined company an identity of its own while allowing Paramount and Warner Bros. – and all our extraordinary brands – to remain in the spotlight.” Watch on Deadline When Skydance acquired Paramount in August 2025, the company wanted to take advantage of Paramount’s familiar consumer brand while also emphasizing Skydance as the corporate parent. That meant the official name was “Paramount, a Skydance Corporation,” which was later streamlined to “Paramount Skydance Corporation.” Before the two large media companies combined, the new entity also faced the legal obstacle of an antitrust lawsuit by 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America, which labeled it an illegal monopoly. The settlement of the lawsuits, laid out in a 5-year consent decree, requires separation of the Paramount and WBD operations in several business areas. It also tries to guard against one of the major studios being dissolved, as has been the fear of merger opponents. Those precautions meant that a name appearing to favor one merger partner over the other would also be a potential problem. In the absence of any official guidance on the name, colloquial handles like “WarnaMount” or “ParaBros” became commonplace. One stark reality of the new identity is that Discovery Communications, which went public in 2008, two decades after the Discovery Channel lit up as a cable network, will now no longer have its name in lights. What once was the peak, is now just the beginning. Paramount and Warner Bros. shaped over a century of culture. By combining them, we aren't rewriting history — we're equipping these iconic studios with a more powerful engine. Together, we are Skydance: a creative-first home for… pic.twitter.com/uInLRY3IrE — David Ellison (@ellisonskydance) October 2, 2026 Paramount-Warner Bros Will Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals Par-WBD Film Shakeup: Greenstein & Goldberg Poised To Run; De Luca, Abdy Likely Out ‘Verity’ To Seduce $55M+ Global Bow As ‘Digger’ Impacts Theaters ‘Celebrity Traitors’ Returns To BBC With Biggest-Ever Launch Episode More from this Story Arc Paramount WB October 2, 2026 Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit, Setting Up Likely Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy Exit October 1, 2026 Ynon Kreiz, Newly Minted Co-CEO Of Paramount, To Get Pay Bump After WBD Merger Close, $31.5M Signing Bonus View All Story Arc Read More About: 17 Comments

articles.title: Canal+ Calls VAT Hike “A Direct Attack” On Its Operations In France As Guilds Protest Move
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie CANEX Creations CEO Osahon Akpata Talks Mission To Shake Up Film Finance in Africa: “There Is A Huge Opportunity To Create IP That’s An Investable Class” Kelli Garner & Michael Stahl-David To Co-Star In Romantic Road Movie ‘You Always’ Dark Sky Films Takes U.S. Rights To Prize-Winning Emirati Horror ‘The Vile’ View All October 2, 2026 6:29am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Canal+ HQ in Boulogne Billancourt Getty Images Paris-based pay-TV giant Canal+ has hit back at the French government’s plan to double the VAT rate on TV subscriptions from 10% to 20% saying it could leave a potential €200M ($225M) hole in its finances. The planned hike was confirmed in a draft budget plan for 2027 presented by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu on Thursday. The controversial package aimed at reining in France ’s public debt, with the government says is poised to hit a record 121.7% of domestic product (GDP) in 2027, proposes some €43B ($48B) worth of “recovery measures” which include increasing revenue from VAT. Related Stories News David Michel Buys Cottonwood Media Out Of Federation Studios News YouTube Says 'Obsession' & 'Backrooms' Point To Awards Future For Films Born On The Platform In a separate development, the budget plan also includes a proposal to cut to a tax deduction for YouTube , YouTube, TikTok, Facebook and Instagram linked to payments they make to France’s National Cinema Centre (CNC). Watch on Deadline These platforms were integrated in 2016 into France’s virtuous system of obligations, under which all entities distributing content in the territory are required to pay a percentage of their local revenue to the CNC, which is then put back into the local film and TV industry. Up until now, the obligation was based on around 35% of their advertising revenues thanks to 66% “abatement” but this has been halved. The measure is expected to raise around €60M ($60M) Canal+ reaction Canal+ called the decision to double the VAT rate for TV subscriptions “inconsistent” and “ill-advised”, noting that the government had only just last year confirmed that the 10% rate would stay in place. “If adopted, this measure would have a massive negative impact on the Group’s revenue and operating margin, potentially reaching €200 million annually, while the revenue gain for the State would amount to less than a quarter of that figure,” read a statement from the pay-TV giant. “Canal+ would be unable to absorb such a loss in France and would consequently be forced to adjust its operations in mainland France and the Overseas Territories. This would inevitably impact subscription prices, workforce levels, and financial contributions to the film and sports ecosystems—and the creative sector more broadly. The film and rugby communities have already rightly raised alarms regarding the risks this measure poses to the future of their respective industries.” Canal+, which floated on the London Stock Exchange in 2024 as part of a restructuring by Vivendi and has also expanded its footprint in Africa with the acquisition of the MultiChoice Group last year, said the VAT hike in France would lead it to double down on its international activities. “With operations now spanning nearly 70 countries, Canal+ regrets this direct attack on its business in its home market of France; it will draw the necessary conclusions and accelerate its international expansion strategy,” said the pay-TV. Industry reaction Rumors of the proposed VAT regime change for Canal+ had already sparked alarm bells with the French film and TV sectors earlier this week. Canal+ is one of the France’s major backers of local and European films and series. In July, it pledged more than $1 billion (€980 million ) for French and European cinema over five years in a fresh deal with the country’s main producer groups. It followed a previous accord in which Canal+ invested €480 million in French and European films from January 1, 2025 to December 31, 2027. News of the tax hike for Canal+ also follows in the wake of news that the government was also planning a €47M ($53M) cut in public funds for state broadcaster France Télévisions in 2027 . Pre-empting the confirmation of the Canal+ VAT hike, France’s film and TV guilds put out a statement earlier this week. Bannered “Who wants the skin of French film and TV”, it declared that the Canal+ VAT hike combined with the France Télévisions cut flew in the face of promises made by President Emmanuel Macron at his Lumière Summit in September. “That summit…. had the stated aim of placing France at the heart of global creative production,” it read. “France Télévisions and Canal+ are two pillars of French film and audiovisual financing. “Through their investment obligations, pre-buys, and commitments under the media chronology rules, they enable hundreds of projects to get off the ground each year, ranging from debut features and auteur-driven works to genre films and international co-productions. Cutting their resources inevitably reduces their capacity to invest in creative work. Since funding obligations are tied to revenue, every euro taken away from these groups translates into fewer funded projects, fewer shoots, fewer jobs, and less diversity on screen. Targeting both groups in the same budget means striking at the very heart of the French model. articles.title: BRAVO Film Festival To Pause For 2026
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Erik Bright Joins PMK Entertainment As EVP Content & Strategic Communications ‘Clarissa’ Trailer: David Oyelowo, Sophie Okonedo, India Amarteifio & Ayo Edebiri Lead Starry Virginia Woolf Adaptation AGC Studios Launches Digital Division Focused On Creator-Led IP View All October 2, 2026 7:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source BRAVO Film Festival. Organizers behind the BRAVO Film Festival , the popular L.A.-based event focused on Brazilian cinema, have canceled the 2026 edition of the festival. Organizers said the event will not take place due to circumstances beyond their control. They added that preparation for next year’s edition will continue. “Our commitment to Brazilian cinema and to the filmmakers, partners, and audiences who have supported BRAVO has not changed,” Talize Sayegh, the festival’s founder and executive director, said in a statement. “We are grateful for that community and focused on returning next year with a festival worthy of it.” Related Stories News DramaBox Sets Brazilian Vertical Series From Cimarron & Trio Of Colombian Originals In Latin American Push News Prime Video Sets Launch Plans For Marília Mendonça Documentary 'Sentimento Louco' Founded in 2008, the BRAVO Film Festival often serves as a U.S. showcase for the year’s most exciting Brazilian talent. The festival traditionally screens Brazil ’s submission for the Best International Oscar as its opening title. In 2024, that was Walter Salles’ I’m Still Here, and 2025 was The Secret Agent , directed by Kleber Mendonça Filho and starring Wagner Moura. Watch on Deadline The organization has longstanding partnerships with American Cinematheque, the Brazilian Consulate in Los Angeles, Cinema do Brasil and Projeto Paradiso. “This pause gives us time to keep building what BRAVO stands for: a stronger bridge between Brazilian filmmakers and Hollywood,” Thiago Macêdo Correia, the festival’s creative director, said in a statement. “The work continues, and we are excited to return next year with the stories, talent, and energy that define Brazilian cinema.” The festival ran across November in Los Angeles. The 2025 edition opened at the Academy Museum. articles.title: Josh Greenstein & Dana Goldberg Poised To Run Combined Paramount Warner Bros Film Unit,  Setting Up Likely Michael De Luca & Pamela Abdy Exit
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony TIFF Midnight Madness Hit ‘River’ Gets Winter 2027 Date From Blumhouse Atomic Monster ‘Verity’ To Seduce $55M+ Worldwide Opening As Box Office Braces For ‘Digger’ Impact – Global Preview ‘Ebenezer’ Trailer: Johnny Depp Leads Ti West’s Dickens Remake View All October 2, 2026 7:15am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Story Arc L-R: Josh Greenstein, Dana Goldberg, Michael De Luca, and Pam Abdy Skydance/Courtesy The soon to be merged Paramount Warner Bros Motion Picture unit under the freshly labeled Skydance is bound to be run by current Paramount Motion Picture co-chairs, Josh Greenstein and Dana Goldberg , multiple sources say. Related Stories News Paramount-WBD Will Now Be Called Skydance, David Ellison Reveals Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs This comes after a sleepless night for Warner Bros’ Motion Picture Chairs Michael De Luca and Pam Abdy , who we hear, first learned that they weren’t making the jump to the new company from reports last night. It’s our understanding that Paramount co-CEO David Ellison never made a phone call to them about their future and whether or not there’s a job offer in hand. The news comes at a stinging time, as Warner Bros’ faces an epic flop in the $125M-$160M+ priced Tom Cruise starring, Alejandro Iñárritu social satire, Digger, which is poised to open to around $30M WW or less this weekend. De Luca and Abdy have been at Warner Bros since June 2022, when they jumped over from MGM following Amazon’s acquisition of that storied studio. The duo recently re-upped their contracts under WBD CEO David Zaslav through 2030. Key to their future at the new Paramount Warner Bros is whether or not Ellison continued to honor their current terms, which would have Warner Bros marketing and distribution departments report into them. From the sounds of it, those are tough terms for the numbers-crunching Ellison to honor. He’s a loyalist to his 16-year production colleague Goldberg, and longtime amigo Greenstein who have been steering the motion picture unit into financially reasonable shape following the old Paramount. Watch on Deadline Paramount will inherit a combined slate around 71 dated features through 2028, 56% of that generated by De Luca and Abdy’s Warner Bros. There’s still more to be dated by both studios in 2028. Paramount will also gain a film library that includes the $4.37 billion global grossing 2025 slate that De Luca and Abdy built as well as Oscar winners One Battle After Another, Sinners (until the rights of that film revert to its director Ryan Coogler) and Weapons. In addition, the new Paramount is looking at a potential $1 billion-grossing year-end holiday tentpole in Warner Bros/Legendary’s Dune: Part Three. There appears to be some talks as to exactly what De Luca and Abdy’s role will be in the new entity, however, the duo weren’t contracted to report into other motion picture chairs, rather the CEO. Reporting into Greenstein and Goldberg doesn’t sound like a likely scenario for the duo per sources. De Luca and Abdy could be offered a producing contract in the new Skydance. The executive chart for the new Paramount Warner Bros is expected to be announced in a matter of days. Ellison brought in former Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz as co-CEO. “Ellison will focus on the company’s long-term strategy, creative vision and direction, including its talent relationships, strategic partnerships, technology and capital allocation,” Paramount said. “Kreiz will focus on the company’s day-to-day management and integration of the combined businesses.” There was an optimistic buzz on Thursday that De Luca and Abdy would also have gate rights on the Melrose lot, and potentially report into Kreiz, but that’s not the likely scenario. Additionally in the new Paramount Warner Bros as of late, Casey Bloys was tapped as streaming head of the combined Paramount-WBD with Paramount’s current Chair of Direct-to-Consumer, Cindy Holland departing. Mark Thompson was told he’d stay on to oversee CNN going forward. While De Luca and Abdy had a great run at the box office last year, this year has been littered with myriad misfires including The Bride, Supergirl with no movie earning more than $100M stateside. The total domestic box office for Jan. 1-Oct. 1 is $448.4M. However, Paramount, too, hasn’t had a great box office year, their current domestic box office YTD right behind Warners with $429.8M, however, they had two $100M+ domestic titles in Scream 7 and Miramax’s Scary Movie. At the year-to-date North American box office, the newly combined Paramount Warner Bros would count $878.2M ranking behind Universal ($1.8B), Disney ($1.55B) and Sony ($1.28B). Under De Luca and Abdy, Warner Bros tallied 30 noms earlier this year, which tied the studio’s record from 2005. Warners took home 11 of those Oscars (six including Best Picture for One Battle After Another , four for Sinners, and supporting actress Amy Madigan’s win for Weapons ). The two had a reputation for protecting filmmakers’ vision, and were audacious in bankrolling auteur projects like Paul Thomas Anderson’s most expensive movie ever, the $140M One Battle After Another and Coogler’s $90M period vampire musical Sinners. One Battle After Another wound up being Anderson’s highest grossing movie ever at $213M+ at the global box office, though film finance sources questioned its profitability. Sinners was a great success with close to $372M WW. De Luca and Abdy presided over MGM starting in January 2020 until April 2022. There they built a slate which assisted in fueling the studio’s sale to Amazon for $8.45 billion for the 4,000 title library. During their run there, theatrical releases included No Time to Die, House of Gucci, Paul Thomas Anderson’s Licorice Pizza, not to mention they teed up Creed III, which became the highest-grossing in that franchise and the second-highest-grossing in the Rocky franchise. Paramount could not be reached for comment. articles.title: Obscured Releasing Acquires NA Rights To ‘The Drug In Our Pocket’ Ahead Of Hamptons World Premiere
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Obscured Releasing Acquires NA Rights To ‘The Drug In Our Pocket’ Ahead Of Hamptons World Premiere Oscars: Pakistan Picks Mo Naqvi’s Doc Thriller ‘Hanging By A Wire’ As Best International Feature Entry ‘Musk’ Director Alex Gibney On World’s Richest Man: “He’s A Bullsh*tter” View All October 2, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source 'The Drug in Our Pocket' Obscured Releasing EXCLUSIVE: Obscured Releasing has acquired North American distribution rights to The Drug in Our Pocket , a documentary by Anne Sundberg about the pernicious effects on young people of constant smartphone use. The feature produced by Beth Kojima and Anne Sundberg holds its world premiere Saturday at the Hamptons International Film Festival in New York, and heads from there to the Heartland International Film Festival in Indianapolis and the Newport Beach Film Festival in Southern California. The Drug in Our Pocket is expected to get an Oscar-qualifying run this fall, followed by a limited theatrical release in early 2027. Related Stories Acquisitions Obscured Releasing Takes North America To Emily Robinson's SXSW Horror Pic 'Ugly Cry' News Sian Clifford Satirical Comedy 'Lady' Scores U.S. Deal “ The Drug in Our Pocket examines how smartphones, designed to connect us, have radically reshaped childhood, adolescence, and mental health,” notes a release. “Through intimate conversations with young people, parents, and leading experts, the film reveals a generation that is thoughtful, articulate, and increasingly aware of how digital environments shape their attention, emotions, and sense of self.” Watch on Deadline The documentary premieres as dozens of states have banned or restricted the use of cell phones in schools, recognizing the impact of the devices on student mental health. Similarly, several countries including Australia, France, Greece, Malaysia, and Brazil have moved to ban or restrict teen access to social media. From Instagram “With The Drug in Our Pocket , director Anne Sundberg brilliantly weaves psychological expert interviews, behind-the-scenes stories from tech whistleblowers, and deeply personal accounts of teenagers and parents exposing how big tech and our government have failed us,” said RJ Millard and Bill Guentzler of Obscured Releasing. “This is a necessary call to action highlighting the impact of social media and technology which offers us the steps we can take to reclaim our power, and attention.” Sundberg’s credits includes four films co-directed with Ricki Stern: The Trials of Darryl Hunt , Joan Rivers: A Piece of Work , The Devil Came on Horseback , and Reversing Roe . Director Anne Sundberg Courtesy of HamptonsFilm In a statement, Sundberg said, “RJ and Bill are brilliant at connecting films to audiences. They understood that for us, The Drug in Our Pocket isn’t just about documenting young people’s experiences growing up online. They share our vision that this film can start a larger movement asking us all to pay attention to our attention. We are thrilled to be working with them on this release.” The acquisition deal was negotiated by Anne Sundberg and Beth Kojima on behalf of the production and Bill Guentzler and RJ Millard on behalf of Obscured Releasing. The Drug in Our Pocket is directed by Anne Sundberg and produced by Beth Kojima and Anne Sundberg. Kojima, Sundberg, and John Wayland wrote the film. Wayland edited the documentary. Timo Elliston and Brian Jones composed the score. Executive producers include Regina K. Scully, Jenna Bush Hager, Crystal McCrary McGuire, Ashley Graham, Lizzie Tisch, and Jonathan Tisch. Obscured Releasing Obscured Releasing was launched by RJ Millard and Bill Guentzler in 2025 “to build film-first distribution strategies that prioritize collaboration in order to engage audiences through festival play, publicity and promotional campaigns, theatrical runs, and thoughtful VOD release windows.” Among its titles are Blue Film , starring Reed Birney and Kieron Moore; Siobhan McCarthy’s trans high school comedy She’s the He ; Christian Nilsson’s Westhampton , starring Finn Wittrock, RJ Mitte, Jake Weary, Amy Forsyth, and Tovah Feldshuh. Documentary releases include Stop The Insanity: Finding Susan Powter , and Endless Cookie . Amazon MGM Studio’s Colleen Hoover thriller Verity grossed $4.5M in its overall previews, which is right where it should for arguably the author’s second most popular novel-to-the-screen after It Ends With Us . articles.title: Disney’s Worlds Collide Tour Hits All the Right Notes With ‘Descendants,’ ‘Zombies’ and ‘Camp Rock’ Stars
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke , Brianna Nordyke , Brooklyn Nordyke October 1, 2026 7:32am The Worlds Collide cast Courtesy Disney Concerts It’s safe to say there are a lot of tired — but really, really happy — kids in Los Angeles on Monday morning. Crypto.com Arena was filled on Monday night with adults and kids — from toddlers to teens — for a jam-packed, fast-paced, high-energy show courtesy of Disney . Eight cast members from three of the company’s hit movie franchises — Descendants , Zombies and Camp Rock — performed a three-hour show (with a 20-minute intermission) featuring all the big songs from those movies and then some, with the whole thing ending around 10 p.m. This reporter’s own kids didn’t get to bed until close to midnight — but they will tell you it was definitely worth staying up late for. Related Stories Business Disney+ Strikes Streaming Bundle and Content-Sharing Deal With Indonesia's Vidio Business Disney Entertainment TV Comms Chief Naomi Bulochnikov-Paul Departing The cheers were deafening inside the arena for the Worlds Collide tour, which features Malachi Barton ( Zombies 4, Camp Rock 3 ), Liamani Segura ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland , Camp Rock 3 ), Dara Reneé ( Descendants: The Rise of Red ), Mekonnen Knife ( Zombies 4 ), Hudson Stone ( Camp Rock 3 ), Swayam Bhatia ( Zombies 4 ), Kiara Romero ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland ) and Alexandro Byrd ( Descendants: Wicked Wonderland ). Among the set list were such songs as “It’s On,” “One Beat Away,” “Play My Music” and “We Rock” from the Camp Rock movies; “Like the Zombies Do,” “The Place to Be,” “Ain’t No Doubt About It” and “Someday” from the Zombies franchise; and “Perfect Princess,” “Chillin’ Like a Villain,” “Rotten to the Core” and “Ways to Be Wicked” from the Descendants soundtracks. Renée brought the house down with her powerful rendition of “Evil Like Me” from Descendants (sung by Kristin Chenoweth and Dove Cameron in the original), while Barton brought out his guitar for “Tomorrow” from Camp Rock 3, a song he said he’d begged to be allowed to perform. Stone, who also performed with his guitar, noted he’s the youngest on the tour, at 14 years old, but held his own with the rest of them. (The other performers range in age from 17-26.) Even with numerous costume changes, the show moved quickly. Between the different songs, at times various cast members would come out and address the audience directly, giving words of encouragement and inspiration. For example, Romero and Byrd talked about embracing your cultural heritage, while Romero, Segura and Bhatia spoke about the importance of friendship. Each of the actors got their time to address the crowd directly, and on big screens were shown images and videos of all the performers when they were younger. Many of them talked about their earlier ambitions to be professional singers, actors and/or dancers. A few of them, including Reneé, Barton, Segura and Stone, also got their chance in the spotlight to perform original solo songs, including “Never Waste a Heartbreak” (Reneé), “Stay for the Credits” (Barton), “Talk” (Stone) and “All the Things I’ve Learned So Far” (Segura). (In a nice touch, merchandise being sold in the lobby included not only shirts with all of the performers together but also tees featuring each person individually.) Among the younger fanbase, Barton and Segura have emerged as big stars, and the crowd went wild for their duet of Camp Rock ‘s iconic “This Is Me,” originally performed by Demi Lovato and Joe Jonas in the movie. In a surprise moment, Barton, who also stars alongside Bhatia in Disney’s upcoming series Coven Academy, brought out the stars of that show, which debuts Thursday. The show included elaborate choreography and big numbers and set pieces along with quieter moments, including a medley around a faux campfire. Barton and Segura again dueted on a Camp Rock song, “Wouldn’t Change a Thing,” during that portion, which also featured Romero singing “If Only” (from Descendants ), Reneé and Byrd singing “So This is Love” (from Cinderella and Descendants: The Rise of Red ) and the entire group singing the Camp Rock chant. The Worlds Collide cast Courtesy Disney Concerts So what did the younger attendees think about the show? Here are some reviews from two in the target demo: Brianna, age 14: “It was really engaging. They really wanted you to stand up and dance and be part of it, like when they taught us all a dance. The music was really good. I liked how they sang songs from even the [previous] movies that a lot of them weren’t in, like ‘If Only’ and ‘Someday,’ which was my favorite Obviously, those songs are really good. I also liked how they brought out their own stuff, like Hudson Stone sang ‘Talk’ and ‘Stay for the Credits,’ which are both really good singles that they made. “I liked how they showed videos of them when they were younger, so like I feel like it could have like inspired some kids to pursue what they want to do in their life. They also had a lot of messages about positivity. It was really nice because I feel like they were inspiring all the kids. I think it was a good length with an intermission.” Brooklyn, age 11: “What I liked about the Worlds Collide tour is that I loved all their outfits, how they spread positivity to children and just telling you to be yourself, and I loved how they showed younger pictures of [the performers], and I thought that was really fun. I loved how they mixed the songs. They are really good singers and I loved it overall. They were just telling kids to be their self, and I thought that was really positive, and I really liked how they did that. “I also thought the costumes were really good because they had a theme for everything, and they all had matching outfits, and I thought that was really cool. My favorite song, if I had to choose one, it would probably be ‘Wouldn’t Change a Thing’ from Camp Rock, because it’s a really good song. I also liked how they walked through the audience too. I really enjoyed it overall, and it was a really good show.” The Worlds Collide tour hit the Kia Forum in Inglewood on Wednesday and next travels to the Honda Center in Anaheim on Thursday before leaving Southern California for stops around the U.S. and Canada. It’ll go global starting in December with stops in Mexico, Great Britain, Germany, France and more. THR

articles.title: Bennington College, Alma Mater of Brett Easton Ellis and Donna Tartt, Launches Screenwriting MFA
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Mia Galuppo Plus Icon Mia Galuppo Senior Entertainment Reporter miagaluppo Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 8:00am Bennington College Bennington College Bennington College has long been known for graduating literary talent, with notable alumni like Brett Easton Ellis, Donna Tartt and Kiran Desai. Now, the Vermont school is looking to break new screenwriting stars. Bennington is launching an MFA in screenwriting, planning for a two-year low-residency program that will see a small cohort of students participate in four ten-day residencies, two at Bennington in Vermont and two in Los Angeles, as well as eight ten-week online courses. “This is a unique screenwriting MFA, perfectly suited to our times,” said Theodore Braun, the director of the new Bennington program. “It blends the rigor of residential education with the flexibility of low residency, giving writers anywhere access to Bennington’s humanistic tradition of the liberal arts, elite screenwriter mentors, and the immersive professional energy of Los Angeles.” Related Stories Business Disney+ Strikes Streaming Bundle and Content-Sharing Deal With Indonesia's Vidio The Show Formerly Known as 'South Park' 'South America' Takes on the Literal Dicks of Big Tech Billionaires in New Episode Braun notes that the inaugural class will be “just six gifted, driven writers-students who are serious about building a body of work and launching a professional screenwriting career.” As for faculty, Bennington has lined up working writers that include The Holdovers writer David Hemingson and Bridgerton writer-producer Janet Lin, as well as Alexa Alemanni ( The Librarians ), Malia Scotch Marmo ( Hook ) and Aaron Rahsaan Thomas ( S.W.A.T. and Friday Night Lights ). Over the course of the program, students will produce feature scripts, spec television episodes, an original pilot and series bible, among other projects. The program will culminate in a capstone industry showcase in Los Angeles. Bennington has already graduated several well-known screenwriters, including Melissa Rosenberg, responsible for the Twilight adaptations, and Sofia Alvarez, who is behind the To All the Boys I’ve Loved Before films. “I think what Bennington excels at — its whole reason for being — is finding, nurturing, and empowering original voices,” offers Rosenberg. “That and the spirit of collaboration make it a wonderful place to launch this new MFA.” THR

articles.title: ‘Trailer Park Boys’ Actor Michael Smith Has Sexual Assault Charge Dismissed
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All October 1, 2026 8:03am Michael Smith as Bubbles (center) is flanked by fellow cast members John Paul Tremblay and Robb Wells. Netflix Logo text Mike Smith, the Nova Scotia actor best known for playing Bubbles on the Trailer Park Boys comedy , has had a sexual assault charge against him dismissed. A three-day sexual assault trial in Dartmouth, Nova Scotia began Thursday, but Judge Jill Hartlen called a halt to the case after crown prosecutors declined to present any evidence, according to the CBC News website on Thursday. “The court has dismissed the charge against Michael Smith, concluding the legal proceedings that began in October 2025 regarding an allegation dating to December 2017,” Trailer Park Boys Inc., a Nova Scotia-based company that produces the series and in which Smith is one of three directors, said in a statement obtained by The Hollywood Reporter. Related Stories TV Netflix's New Releases Coming in October 2026 TV 'East of Eden' Review: A Terrifying Florence Pugh Towers Over Zoe Kazan's Accomplished Netflix Adaptation of the John Steinbeck Classic The company also has as directors Trailer Park Boys co-stars John Paul Tremblay, who plays Julian, and Robert Wells, who plays Ricky. The company added: “Now that he (Smith) is cleared of this matter, Mike is resuming his responsibilities with Trailer Park Boys Incorporated.” Bubbles, Julian and Ricky and the rest of their Sunnyvale Trailer Park crew featured in the cult Canadian mockumentary about three petty criminals running scams from their Halifax business. The franchise included a TV series that streamed on Netflix and movies. Smith stepped away from Trailer Park Boys Inc. in Oct. 2025 when he was charged with one count of sexual assault stemming from an alleged incident in 2017, and pleaded not guilty. The CBC, Canada’s public broadcaster, on its online news site said an unnamed complainant against Smith in a statement said she was “unwilling to sacrifice my mental health” by testifying during the trail. The Trailer Park Boys was created in 2001 by Barry Dunn, Wells, Tremblay and Mike Clattenburg and originally launched on Canada’s Showcase channel. The series ended its Canadian TV run in 2008. Netflix picked up the Trailer Park Boys property in 2014. THR

articles.title: What Ratings Issues? NBCU Telemundo Chair Touts World Cup Success for Live TV
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All October 1, 2026 8:30am Luis Fernández Courtesy of NBCUniversal Telemundo Enterprises Luis Fernández , chairman of Spanish-language media powerhouse NBCUniversal Telemundo Enterprises and former Telemundo news chief, was one of the high-profile keynote speakers on Thursday afternoon at the sixth edition of Iberseries & Platino Industria in the Spanish capital, Madrid . In his appearance, he spent some time modestly taking a victory lap for Telemundo’s success with the soccer World Cup 2026, as well as touting the power of live and linear TV. Telemundo is part of entertainment company NBCUniversal, which is owned by Comcast but is scheduled to be spun off by the cable and telecom giant next year. “The FIFA football World Cup was the most-watched sports feature in Spanish [in the U.S.]. We never had those ratings,” Fernández told the Madrid event during his appearance entitled “Leadership, relevance and transformation of the Spanish-language audiovisual industry.” He particularly lauded the combined World Cup offerings across both streaming and linear services, emphasizing: “We were able to bring together Telemundo and Peacock, our streaming platform. Five out of the 10 most-watched programs on Peacock were events that happened during the World Cup.” Fernández also told the Iberseries crowd that based on how the World Cup was presented and consumed, his company’s advertising sales team signaled to him that they were expecting better Los Angeles Summer Olympics 2028 ad momentum than previously thought. The exec on Thursday further touted the importance of constant reinvention in the media and entertainment sector. “This industry has to reinvent every year, every month, every day,” he said. “And if you’re not adapting and reinventing yourself, you will be out of the system.” That means rethinking approaches and taking some risks. “If we fight, if we work, are bold and fearless, and also creative, we’ll be able” to succeed, he concluded. Luis Fernández at Iberseries 2026 As one example of the change he has brought to Telemundo, Fernández pointed to his early efforts to move beyond the image as a reality TV-centric broadcaster despite some initial skepticism within the company. “I was thinking of what we could do to improve the channel, to be more competitive, and to be more relevant,” he said. “We have reality TV, but we also have news, we have sports, we have fiction. So we had to get rid of that image that had formed.” How does the Telemundo chair feel about the outlook for linear TV versus streaming? “I think that streaming services are our rivals and our competitors, and I think that linear TV really has a lot of power in live shows,” Fernández offered. “The streaming services eventually will be able to be good at live TV, but right now, live TV is something where we have much more to offer.” Pointing to the World Cup again, he also shared: “I always hate when people say that linear or traditional TV is falling in viewership, ratings.” It will not surprise you that, in this context, Fernández also told Iberseries about his interest in continuing to offer up sports programming, including beyond soccer. “For me, that’s one of the key pillars of our strategy for the upcoming years,” he emphasized. “Sports licensing is one of the things that we’re investing in.” Asked about his view on AI, the exec replied: “It is an opportunity.” Without going into too much detail, he mentioned that the media space has always faced technological changes. Wednesday’s conference day saw creators of series that address far-right politics, the climate crisis and more discuss whether great dramas can change the world. And Mediawan executives shared insights on their strategy and focus, including such hits as F1: The Movie , Slow Horses and Call My Agent! On Tuesday, Amazon MGM Studios executives discussed the success of the Mercedes Ron young adult novel adaptations and Spanish zombie horror film Apocalypse Z , while Parrot Analytics shared data trends and estimates for the subscriber impact of Netflix’s Argentina hit series The Eternaut . And a YouTube top executive predicted at Iberseries that more Obsession – and Backrooms -style film hits from online creators. The sixth edition of the industry gathering wraps up on Friday. THR

articles.title: CNN Chief Mark Thompson May Stay On After Sale — Though Contract Talks Are Early
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 8:50am CNN chief Mark Thompson Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images CNN may have more stability than some had feared under the combined Paramount-Warner Bros. David Ellison has held discussions with CNN CEO Mark Thompson about keeping the veteran executive in charge of the cable news channel, a source familiar with the matter says. The contract talks, however, are said to be very early, and there is no assurance that they can come to terms on a new deal. No change in leadership is expected at deal close, with Thompson’s current contract to lead CNN running into next year. The Wall Street Journal , which first reported the news, said that Thompson wants assurances that he will have autonomy over the global news brand, including on editorial matters. CNN will have an “editorial independence board” once the deal closes , with a group of journalists establishing guiding principles for the news outlet, and resolving any disputes with corporate leadership. If Thompson and Ellison are able to come to terms on a new deal, it would come as a sigh of relief to many CNN talent, who have been fearful of a dramatic overhaul at the channel post-merger, especially given Bari Weiss’ aggressive changes at CBS News. That doesn’t mean CNN won’t undergo changes under the combined company, but it does mean that Thompson will be able to continue executing on the digital reboot that he is in the middle of overseeing. While CNN’s linear ratings have been challenged in recent years, it remains a profit center among the WBD cable channels, filings show. Those profits will be particularly important as the combined company seeks to pay down an estimated $80 billion debt load. That said, one observer says that the merger will almost certainly require some level of consolidation between CBS News and CNN, though the devil may be in the details as things move forward. THR
