articles.title: ‘Rolling Loud: The Movie’ Review: Owen Wilson Plays a Very Bad Dad in a Tone-Deaf Would-Be Comedy
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Frank Scheck Plus Icon Frank Scheck View All October 1, 2026 9:00am 'Rolling Loud: The Movie' Ketchup Entertainment An underage teenager gets snuck into a hip-hop music festival headlined by Travis Scott and soon goes missing, his desperate father frantically attempting to find him before it’s too late. No, it’s not a harrowing drama based on the tragic 2021 real-life events at Scott’s Astroworld concert in Texas, where 10 concertgoers were killed in a fatal crowd crush. Instead, Rolling Loud: The Movie is…a comedy. Discuss among yourselves. Rolling Loud: The Movie The Bottom Line A bad idea, terribly executed. Release date : Friday, October 2 Cast : Owen Wilson, Matt Rife, Christine Ko, Christian Convery, Jolene, Henry Winkler, Travis Scott Director-screenwriter : Jeremy Garelick Rated R, 1 hour 35 minutes To say that this effort written and directed by Jeremy Garelick ( The Wedding Ringer , Murder Mystery 2 ) — who is modestly described in the film’s press notes as “reinventing Hollywood comedy with brain, heart, and guts” — comes across as tone-deaf is an understatement. Even if you ignore the disturbing parallels to past events, this story of a dad attempting to bond with his 13-year-old son by irresponsibly sneaking him into the popular hip-hop music festival of the title while lying to his wife and the festival’s security personnel just feels icky. Did I mention it’s a true story? Related Stories Movies 'Practical Magic 2' Summons $30M to End Spider-Man's Streak at No. 1 Movies 'Practical Magic 2' Whips Up $4.7M in Box Office Previews Yes, the filmmaker apparently did take his 13-year-old to the festival, filled with people walking around in various states of undress and many of them using drugs, against his wife’s wishes. And he did lose contact with his son, unable to reach him because of the lack of cell phone reception. Apparently, rather than feeling chastened, he thought: “What a great idea for a movie!” Of course, it still could have worked if the film actually proved funny. Instead, it’s a witless, moronic, slapstick-filled mediocrity that basically serves as a feature-length commercial for the popular music festival where parts of it were filmed (Live Nation is among the production companies). To that end, the film features not only Scott, playing a recliner-chair-loving version of himself (don’t ask), but also such real-life hip-hop stars as Sexyy Red, Ski Mask the Slump God, and Ty Dolla $ign, none of whom are likely to enlarge their fan base. Wilson plays hapless furniture salesman Hank — he works at “Raymond & Ferguson” — who tells his wife Melanie (Jolene) that he’s taking their son Zion (Christian Convery) to their lake house, but instead brings him to Rolling Loud. There he runs into his co-worker Terry (comedian Matt Rife , managing to make his character as annoying as his stand-up), whom he had just been ordered to fire by their boss ( Henry Winkler , squandering some of that good will from Barry ). Distracted by Terry, Hank doesn’t think much of it when Zion excuses himself to go to the bathroom. But he becomes increasingly anxious when his son fails to reappear, and that’s when the would-be comic complications ensue. They include an episode in which Hank retreats to a quiet room, only to discover that his lying conversation to his wife has been broadcast to a disapproving crowd outside; a physical altercation with security guards when he attempts to report his son missing; and accidentally throwing Linda (Christine Ko), a festival volunteer worker, off of a Ferris wheel, injuring a wheelchair-bound bystander in the process. And, of course, Hank also accidentally takes drugs and begins tripping. And the volunteer strips naked to distract the security guards, revealing a forest-level growth of pubic hair in the process. (The appealing Ko, who provides some genuine amusement in her role, deserved better). It’s all about as laborious as it sounds, with Wilson, utilizing his familiar style of motor-mouthed pathos and desperation, working very hard to infuse comic energy into the strained proceedings. By the time he gets onstage with Scott and then disastrously leaps into the mosh pit, all you’re thinking is that he needs to collaborate with Wes Anderson again, and as soon as possible. As for Scott, if he survived the fallout from Astroworld, he can survive this. Full credits Production: American High, Live Nation Production, Live Nation Studios, Rolling Loud Distributor: Ketchup Entertainment Cast: Owen Wilson, Matt Rife, Christine Ko, Christian Convery, Jolene, Henry Winkler, Travis Scott Director-screenwriter: Jeremy Garelick Producers: Stella Bulochnikov, Jolene, Jeremy Garelick, Will Phelps, Doug Banker Executive producers: Ryan D. Adams, Dan Kaplow, Michael Rapino, Matt Rife, Pasquale Rotella, Christina Shams, Matt Philip Whelan, Matt Zingler Director of photography: Bradford Lipson Production designer: Kathrin Eder Composer: Chanda Dancy Costume designer: Wlaa Elashkar Casting: Findley Davidson, Mary Vernieu Rated R, 1 hour 35 minutes THR

articles.title: Martin Grove, Longtime Columnist for The Hollywood Reporter, Dies at 83
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All October 1, 2026 9:12am Martin Grove Courtesy of Grove Family Martin Grove, who wrote more than 3,300 columns for The Hollywood Reporter over 25 years as one of his era’s most respected and influential film experts, has died. He was 83. Grove died Tuesday at Providence Cedars-Sinai Tarzana Medical Center of cancer-related natural causes, his daughter, Universal Pictures vp media Alyson Grove, told THR . He inspired her to work in the business, she said. Grove’s “Hollywood Report” column, which centered on box office analysis, marketing and distribution, appeared on the pages of THR from July 1985 through January 2000. His “Filmmaker Focus” column, which showcased the art of making movies, then served as an exclusive THR.com feature through December 2010. Related Stories TV Peppino Mazzullo, Voice of Topo Gigio, the Italian Puppet on 'The Ed Sullivan Show,' Dies at 100 Movies John Grover, Film Editor on Six James Bond Movies, Dies at 87 “My dad truly loved his time at THR ,” his daughter said. The amiable Grove also appeared as a movie expert on CNN’s ShowBiz Today from 1989-2001 and as a movie analyst for CNNfn’s The Biz from 1996-2004, and his entertainment business reports could be heard weekday afternoons on the all-news Los Angeles radio station KNX from 1999-2004. In 2001, Grove taped luncheon interviews at Wolfgang Puck’s Spago in Beverly Hills with the likes of Ron Howard, Ridley Scott, Steven Soderbergh, Wolfgang Petersen and Michael Bay for the AMC series Behind the Screen . And from 1990-2008, he produced, wrote and provided the voiceovers for 90-second sponsored movie previews distributed to airlines including American, United, Delta, Northwest and TWA. Born on March 30, 1943, in Perth Amboy, New Jersey, Martin Allan Grove received his bachelor’s degree from Rutgers University, where he majored in art history and journalism and worked for the campus radio station, WRSU. En route to earning his master’s degree in screenwriting from NYU’s School of the Arts by taking night classes, he spent his days at ABC, where he handled radio network publicity and then business publicity for ABC television. As management, he helped keep WABC, New York’s top-rated radio station, on the air during several extended talent and engineering walkouts in 1967 by filling in on the graveyard shift for such popular DJs as Bruce Morrow (Cousin Brucie) and Dan Ingram. “As the strikes went on,” he said, “WABC created new jingles promoting ‘The Strikebound Sound of 77 WABC,’ and I had my own ‘Marty Grove’ jingle to use on the shows I did.” Grove later directed publicity for the advertising firm Foote, Cone & Belding, headed corporate communications and investor relations for 20th Century Fox in New York and Los Angeles and led marketing for Warner Bros. Television in Burbank (at Fox, he did marketing for its Movietone News library of newsreels as well). Before studios routinely announced box office figures, Grove served from 1985-95 as an Entertainment Tonight consultant for a Monday feature that projected grosses, and he appeared frequently on ET as a film expert during this period. Grove interviewed celebrities and filmmakers for THR ’s televised coverage of the 1987 Cannes Film Festival and anchored the paper’s TV coverage of the NATO/ShoWest theater owners conventions in Las Vegas from 1987-91. Starting in 1988, he hosted half-hour talk show episodes about Hollywood and two-minute commentaries about movies for Movietime, the cable network that later became E! Entertainment; produced, wrote and hosted the series For Your Consideration about Oscar and Golden Globes contenders on Time Warner Cable in New York and L.A.; and was a film industry analyst for the Financial News Network. During his career, Grove showed up on the NBC Nightly News , the CBS Evening News , ABC World News Tonight , Today , 20/20 , CNBC’s Power Lunch and Fox News programs was quoted in The New York Times , Wall Street Journal , Time , Washington Post , Sunday Times of London , Rolling Stone and Agence-France Presse . Since 2008, he served as CEO and president of ZAMM.com, for which he wrote, produced and voiced hundreds of movie preview videos as part of a content partnership with Amazon. A member of the WGA West, Grove sold screenplay pitches to Paramount and Columbia that he wrote and developed but that were not produced. He also authored a novel set in the world of network television, 10 pseudonymous mystery novels and a half-dozen pop-culture paperbacks, including an authorized biography of John Travolta, an instant biography of Elvis Presley published within days of his 1977 death and profiles of The Beatles, The Osmonds, Henry Winkler and Paul McCartney. Along the way, he still examined the estimated box office numbers every Sunday and the actuals every Monday. In addition to his daughter, survivors include his wife of 55 years, Marjorie; son Geoffrey; daughter-in-law Hilary; granddaughter Reesa; and grandson Rogan. THR

articles.title: Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 8:30am PT Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE) By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest Pro ‘Fortnite’ Gamer Cody ‘Clix’ Conrod Launches New Holding Company Full Box to Align Owned Businesses, Collabs and Philanthropy (EXCLUSIVE) 20 minutes ago Fugitive Films Co-Founder, Former MTV Scripted Boss Launch Romance-Focused Vertical Content Studio, Rommi (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Author Chloe Gong on ‘Eyes of Kings’ ending, ‘Deadlock’ debut and how she wants ‘These Violent Delights’ adapted for TV or film 5 days ago See All Full Box Professional “Fornite” player and star gamer Cody “ Clix ” Conrod has launched Full Box Inc., a creator-led holding company to encompasses his nine businesses, ventures and community initiatives A nod to the sport itself, the name “Full Box” comes directly from the massive Epic Games-developed online game, where the term describes surrounding an opponent with control, skill and competitive execution. Per Full Box, the name “reflects both the competitive mindset that has defined [Conrod’s] career and the company’s approach to building a complete business ecosystem around a creator.” Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again Joining Conrod at Full Box is Darren Glover, who spent six years building the gaming division at VaynerSports and served as Conrod’s first agent. Glove is set as Full Box CEO while Conrod serves as founder and chief creative officer and continues to compete and stream at the highest level of “ Fortnite .” Popular on Variety Full Box is focusing its holdings around three pillars: Operating Companies, Full Box Ventures and Impact. Built around Conrod’s commitment to giving back to the community he grew up with, Full Box Inc.’s Impact arm houses the Dr3amin Access Fund, a career development initiative providing kids with gaming PCs, hardware and programming designed to create pathways into competitive gaming, content creation and game development. The Fund formalizes Conrod’s longstanding grassroots efforts, which delivered more than $250,000 in gaming equipment through Clixmas, his large-scale holiday event, in 2025. “When we’re talking about new talent in the space, little short story: A gaming computer that I gave away around two years ago to a kid that was on 60 FPS, playing on a console, had no earnings. I gave him a Clixmas computer, and now he’s literally here in Belgium competing for $10 million right next to me, and he made over $150,000,” Conrod told Variety during an interview out of the Fortnite Global Championship last month. “So that one kid, his name is Joshreyli , happened off of me giving away, I think at that time was like 40 computers. So as time gets on, and now that it’s an official thing where people could now give us money in the Dr3amin Access Fund, and we could give that back, how many more kids can we help elevate and give access to, where they could actually become that? So these next five years is really just continuing to build it.” To date, Full Box Inc.’s Operating Companies division is comprised of owned businesses including: ● Clix Gaming, a content and production company spanning live streaming, competitive gaming, brand partnerships, and interactive digital experiences across Fortnite and Roblox. ● Clix Creative: A creator-led game studio building experiences within the competitive Fortnite ecosystem, built around ranked play, personal progression and tournaments. ● Dr3amin Clothing, the apparel and lifestyle brand inspired by Conrod’s personal journey. Full Box Ventures currently supports: ● Reach Clipping: The fastest-growing clipping agency on Content Rewards, helping creators and brands scale short-form distribution through performance-based clipping campaigns. ● Real Sports App: A booming social sports platform combining live scores and play-by-play with community, conversation and gaming at its core. ● Rorra: A next-generation water filtration company focused on making cleaner water more accessible. ● TapCaps: A brand co-founded alongside fellow creator Lacy, blending gaming and mainstream culture through limited-edition blind-box collectibles that double as clickable fidget toys and functional keyboard keycaps. ● XSET: A gaming lifestyle brand and media network where Conrod serves as a competitive player and co-owner. Glover says the overall Full Box business is made up of multiple revenue streams which are all built around, but not beholden to, Conrod’s “Fortnite” presence. “‘Fortnite,’ Roblox, ‘Minecraft,’ and ‘Grand Theft Auto’ are the only games that you can earn within the game itself,” Glover says. “So our business model is vertically integrated, which is very unique in the gaming world, where there are lots of people that make content about video games and they monetize on the media of the content, which is great. That’s a super simple way, but that’s a really bumpy road to create a business around that. ‘Fortnite’ gives you the ability to make money by playing the game. You’re creating content about the game. We have a creator code; that’s people putting in an affiliate link in the store when they buy something. They’re supporting Clix by putting in code Clix, which is a whole different content model and a fun thing that Cody has created are these, ‘Use Code Clix’ commercials.” Glover adds: “So we have an affiliate link model from all the commerce that’s happening inside of the store. We have games and experiences that we’re building with Clix Creative that we monetize specifically based on engagement, very similar to a YouTube model… So we’re making revenue for the business by players playing our maps and experiences. So we we’ve got this like very cool model that we make content about the game and we make content within the game. So for us, it’s not about trying to predict where the game goes.” This includes not only an ongoing collaboration with “Fortnite” maker Epic Games, but also one of its major investors, Disney. “We have a really good relationship with Disney,” Glover says. “I just saw Josh [D’Amaro], the CEO, last Friday, and praised him for his belief in ‘Fortnite.’ So for us, it’s not about trying to predict where they go. It’s just us creating the infrastructure that’s going to support wherever they take it.” Abhishek Chaubey, Navdeep Singh to Present Shivam Shankar’s ‘Bhed, Bakri, Bhoot’ on Anurag Kashyap-Curated YouTube Channel (EXCLUSIVE) John Oliver Embarrasses Trump Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy Over ‘Godawful’ YouTube Reality Show and ‘Real World’ Past In Docuseries ‘Keinaan, Go Back to Somalia,’ Finnish-Somali YouTube Star Turns Racist Comments Into a Personal Statement Director and Producer James Wan on YouTube Filmmakers: ‘You Don’t Even Need to Be in the System Anymore to Get Something Made’ Google’s Sean Downey on the YouTube TIFF Takeover, Oscars Ad Integration and Creators vs. Influencers Netflix, Amazon and YouTube Form D.C. Paramount has agreed to set up a board to keep tabs on the independence of its news properties as part of its recent settlement with a set of state attorneys general who wanted to block its deal. Thompson’s current contract is believed to run out in 2027. Popular on Variety The Wall Street Journal previously reported on the talks between Paramount and the executive. The news could bring some relief to staffers at CNN, who have been worried about the fate of the news division under Paramount. Staffers have wondered about Paramount CEO David Ellison’s commitment to credible newsgathering given recent scrutiny of the executive he installed at CBS News, Bari Weiss. They are also concerned about the direction Paramount may see for CNN’s new streaming service. CNN’s progress with digital audiences has been slowed by a bevy of changes in the company’s corporate direction in recent years. Thompson last week expressed a desire to stay in the role. “I am enthusiastic about staying,” he told employees during a recentl town hall meeting, according to two people with knowledge of his remarks. Even so, he also confided he has no knowledge of how Paramount Skydance wanted to proceed once it completes its acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. “How Paramount wants to run news” is not known to him at present, he said. During his tenure, Thompson has focused on getting CNN content in front of younger viewers and digital audiences. CNN has been testing new formats with its “CNN All Access” subscription service, and has seen up and coming personnel like Abby Phillip and Harry Enten gain some traction. Warner Bros. Discovery projected in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission earlier this year that CNN will generate $600 million in profit in 2026 on $1.8 billion in revenue. articles.title: Grammy Asian Pop Category Will Go Forward, CEO Says: ‘We Understand This Conclusion Will Not Satisfy Everyone’
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 8:59am PT Grammy Asian Pop Category Will Go Forward, CEO Says: ‘We Understand This Conclusion Will Not Satisfy Everyone’ By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Sia Sells 50% of Music Catalog to Pophouse in $180 Million Partnership Deal 2 hours ago Billy Joel Gives Health Update After Brain Surgery: ‘I’m OK — It Sounds a Lot Worse Than It Actually Is’ 1 day ago LCD Soundsystem Announces 2026 NYC Residency — Including 100th Residency Show 1 day ago See All HYBE Grammy chief Harvey Mason Jr. has issued a statement in which he says the Awards’ controversial newest category, Asian Pop, will go forward for the 2027 ceremony. Mason had previously signaled that the Recording Academy was reconsidering the new category in the wake of decidedly split reactions after it was announced in June. BTS in particular objected to the category , implying that it effectively ghetto-izes a genre of music more than highlighting it and saying they will not submit their music for Grammy consideration in 2027. Related Stories Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again “We hope our music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group said in a statement. Popular on Variety However, Mason is unequivocal about the award going forward, at least for 2027, based on conversations with multiple people in the community. “Over the past several weeks the Academy has been conducting listening sessions and have been in dialogue with leaders of the Asian music community,” Mason’s statement reads in full. “The journey has been rewarding and inspiring. Our organization is at its best when we engage deeply with music people and go the extra mile to understand their lived experiences. “In this case, we heard candid feedback from people in our community who don’t support the continuation of this category. We also heard from people who didn’t have accurate information about the category, and having space to clear up misperceptions has been especially valuable. But by far, the loudest feedback we heard was from people who were enthusiastic supporters of the category, fellow music creators expressing their encouragement for keeping it. “We understand this conclusion will not satisfy everyone, and that never feels good. But at the same time, we are confident it’s the right conclusion for the music community overall. As is the case with all our categories, we will continue to diligently engage with the music community and keep striving to honor this music — and all music — in the best possible way. We look forward to celebrating the Asian Pop Music Performance nominees at the 2027 Grammy Awards.” The Academy also noted that it has received a “robust” number of submissions for the category, signaling strong interest in its first year. The introduction of the award revived a familiar issue with the Grammys ’ genre-specific awards. While the intent may be to recognize music in a certain genre or language, many people within that community feel that it actually ends up being exclusionary, with voters relegating music or artists into those genre categories rather than more-mainstream ones; this has been a common complaint with regard to the Latin Grammys. While BTS has been nominated for Grammy Awards five times, in pop and other categories, the group has never won. “Golden,” from the smash film “KPop Demon Hunters” and performed by the fictional group Huntr/x (vocalists EJAE, Audrey Nuna, and Rei Ami), is widely considered the first KPop Grammy win, taking the award for best song written for visual media earlier this year, although it did not win for best song. articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:00am PT Middleburg Film Festival Sets ‘Being Heumann’ as Closing Night Film, Martin McDonagh, Seth Rogen and Rosalind Eleazar Lead Honorees By Clayton Davis Plus Icon Clayton Davis Chief Awards Editor byClaytonDavis Latest Variety’s ‘Pixels and Pencils’ Animation Panel Returns to SCAD Savannah Film Festival With Directors of ‘Wildwood,’ ‘Ray Gunn’ and More 2 days ago Julianne Moore to Receive Icon Award at SCAD Savannah Film Festival With ‘The Debut’ Set as Centerpiece Selection 3 days ago Lance Oppenheim on ‘Primetime,’ ‘You Can See Everything’ and How Chris Hansen’s Reaction ‘Is Exactly What the Film Is About’ 6 days ago See All Apple Original Films “ Being Heumann ,” Oscar winner Siân Heder’s Apple Original Film, will close the 14th Middleburg Film Festival , which runs Oct. 15-18. The festival has also set Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi’s “La Bola Negra” as its Friday Spotlight and Tony Gilroy’s “ Behemoth !” as its Sunday Spotlight. As previously announced , the festival will open with Jesse Eisenberg’s “The Debut.” Martin McDonagh, Brad Bird, Seth Rogen , Rosalind Eleazar, Guitarricadelafuente and casting directors Adam Caldwell and Bernard Telsey will be honored at this year’s festival. Billie Jean King and Bill Pullman are among the special guests. Popular on Variety Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Paige DeSorbo on Leaving 'Summer House' Behind and Speaking Out About a Past Abusive Relationship: 'Domestic Violence' Can 'Truly Happen to Anyone' Over the past decade, Middleburg has become a reliable fall stop for awards hopefuls. Being close to Washington, D.C., helps it draw national press and its small size gives filmmakers time for longer conversations with audiences. This year’s lineup continues that tradition. Caldwell and Telsey will receive the festival’s Special Achievement in Casting Award and join a post-screening Q&A. The recognition arrives as the Academy’s achievement in casting category enters its second year. Representing “La Bola Negra,” Guitarricadelafuente wrote and performs the film’s original song, “La Nieve.” He will receive the International Spotlight Award, participate in a post-screening discussion and join the festival’s Songwriters and Composers Panel. Gilroy will be on hand for a post-screening conversation following Searchlight Pictures’ “Behemoth!” where Pedro Pascal plays a gifted cellist and former child prodigy who returns to Los Angeles after two decades on the road to record film scores and confront his complicated family history. McDonagh will receive the Director Spotlight Award for “Wild Horse Nine,” also from Searchlight. Set just before the 1973 Chilean coup, the film stars John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell as longtime CIA agents sent from Santiago to Easter Island, where they confront their dark pasts and a conspiracy unfolding around them. Bird will receive the Spotlight Animation Award for Netflix’s “Ray Gunn,” a passion project more than 30 years in the making. Bird wrote and directed the sci-fi noir, which is set in Metropia, a city where humans and aliens live side by side. Rogen will receive the MFF Artistic Achievement Award at an “In Conversation with Seth Rogen” event covering several of his films at the festival. He stars in Olivia Wilde’s A24 film “The Invite” alongside Wilde, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton, playing one of two married couples whose relationships are tested by a dinner party that grows more unpredictable as the night goes on. Rogen also produced Leah Nelson’s animated film “Tangles” with Lauren Miller Rogen, Evan Goldberg and others. Based on Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir, it follows a young artist who moves home to care for her mother after an Alzheimer’s diagnosis. Rogen will join Nelson and Miller Rogen for a post-screening conversation. Eleazar will receive the Breakthrough Actor Award for A24’s “Misty Green,” written and directed by Chris Rock. In her first leading film role, she plays Misty, a once-successful actress whose career has stalled. She is fighting to win back her place in Hollywood while dealing with financial trouble, broken relationships and her own self-destructive streak. The annual Songwriters and Composers Panel will feature Ari Balouzian (“Primetime,” “You Can See Everything”), Lesley Barber (“Gail”), Jesse Eisenberg (“The Debut”), Lukas Frank (“Behemoth!”), Guitarricadelafuente (“La Bola Negra”), Daniel Pemberton (“Ink,” “Project Hail Mary”), Christopher Spelman (“Paper Tiger”) and Diane Warren (“Maserati: The Brothers”). “Toy Story 5” production designer Bob Pauley will lead a masterclass on his more than three decades at Pixar. Pauley was part of the original “Toy Story” creative team, designed Buzz Lightyear for the 1995 film and has worked on all five installments. He will also lead a drawing demonstration focused on new characters from “Toy Story 5.” Tennis legend Billie Jean King will attend with Liz Garbus and Elizabeth Wolff’s documentary “Give Me the Ball!” The film uses rare archival footage and candid interviews to examine the victories, struggles and personal sacrifices behind her tennis career and her fight for equality in sports and beyond. King will sit down with festival founder and board chair Sheila Johnson for a one-on-one post-screening conversation on Sunday, Oct. 18. Finally, Pullman will attend with “Everybody Digs Bill Evans,” Grant Gee’s unconventional portrait of the jazz pianist. Set in 1961, the film follows Evans (Anders Danielsen Lie) after the sudden death of his bassist and close collaborator Scott LaFaro, when grief drives him to stop playing and retreat from New York to his family home. MFF advisory board members Albert Berger and Ron Yerxa executive produce. The full Middleburg Film Festival lineup and honorees are below. The full schedule and lineup are available at middleburgfilm.org . Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:00am PT Theaters Re-Invest $2.7 Billion to Bring In Moviegoers With Heated Reclining Seats, Full-Service Bars, Immersive Sound and More By Pat Saperstein Plus Icon Pat Saperstein Deputy Editor @Variety_PatS Latest Beyond Fest Organizers on Improved Ticketing, Fans ‘As Unhinged as We Are’ and Their 7 Titles Not to Miss 2 days ago ‘Lightworkers’ Doc: Tom Morello, Henry Winkler, Lee Grant and More on Why They Fight for Democracy: ‘Comfort Is a Danger Zone’ 6 days ago Hannah Einbinder Speaks Out After Being Arrested at Netanyahu Protest: ‘Let Us Not Mistake the Spectacle for the Story’ 7 days ago See All Courtesy CinemaUnited As the summer box office closes at an all-time high, theaters across North America are aiming to keep audiences engaged by spending $2.7 billion over the past two years on upgrades and innovations. The exhibition chains are investing big in amenities such as premium large formats and expanded food and beverage services, according to Cinema United , which unveiled its Cinema Investment report Thursday. In the past year alone, theaters spent $1.2 billion to create premium entertainment experiences. The eight largest domestic circuits spent $840 million in the past year after pledging $2.2 billion to modernize and upgrade theaters over a three-year period. Related Stories 'People Are Still Terrified of Me': Sharon Stone on Thriving for 46 Years in Hollywood and Why 'My Lane Was Never Going to Be Sex Psychos' Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Dimoldenberg launched “Chicken Shop Date” in 2014 and has since hosted 115 episodes of the series, a deadpan and flirty digital talk show driven by the host’s British comedic sensibilities and filmed in local chicken shops. Netflix’s licensing of “Chicken Shop Date” is part of the streamer’s broader effort to get into business with creators. articles.title: UTA Streamlines Film, TV and Talent Leadership; Matt Rice Rises to President of Filmed Entertainment Unit
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:02am PT UTA Streamlines Film, TV and Talent Leadership; Matt Rice Rises to President of Filmed Entertainment Unit By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Don’t Lie, Don’t Cry and Use Common Sense: Adam Levy, Judge Judy’s Son, Joins the Family Business With ‘Adam’s Law’ 1 week ago How NBCUniversal Television Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms: ‘We Cheer Each Other On’ 1 week ago Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 1 week ago See All Courtesy of UTA UTA has taken a dramatic step to streamline the leadership of its film and TV lit and talent departments to reflect the industry trends of blurring lines between disciplines. As part of the change, agency veteran Matt Rice has been promoted to president of the new UTA Filmed Entertainment unit. In the new structure, UTA’s Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan have been elevated to managing partners of Filmed Entertainment. UTA has named new department heads to lead key segments: Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner will lead Motion Picture Literary; Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman will run TV Literary while talent will be steered by Hanley Baxter and John Sacks alongside longstanding talent chief Mike Jelline. Related Stories 'It's Time for My Voice': Jennifer Hudson on Reviving 'Dreamgirls,' Booking Tom Cruise for Her Talk Show and Writing Original Music Again Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Another new wrinkle is the formation of a Filmed Entertainment board that includes agency stalwarts including Jelline, Berman, Moorhead, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig and Larry Salz. Popular on Variety UTA chief executive David Kramer outlined the reasoning for the changes in a memo sent to agency staffers on Thursday morning “UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next,” Kramer said. “As the business evolves and film and television increasingly converge, this team positions us to lead that evolution, unlock new possibilities for our clients and bring the full power of UTA to everyone we represent.” Rice joined UTA in 2002 after getting his start at the Broder Kurland literary agency. He’s one of the town’s top representatives of writers, directors and showrunners, including such notables as Phil Lord & Chris Miller, Michael Schur, Alec Berg, Bill Hader, Seth Rogen & Evan Goldberg, Will Forte, Justin Halpern & Patrick Schumacker, R. Scott Gemmill, James Gunn, Dan Goor, Chris McKenna & Erik Sommers, Adam Reed, Sebastian Maniscalco and Matt Rife. “This move reflects what sets UTA apart — a bold, collaborative and forward-thinking approach. I’m excited to build upon the work of this exceptional group of leaders and continue to deliver best-in-class representation to our clients,” Rice said. UTA’s shakeup of its longstanding departmental lines reflects the shifting sands for the content business as well as the business of representing boldface name talent. The growth in audience and influence among the largest social media platforms has revved up the creator economy and birthed a new breed of digital media superstar. All of this has challenged the traditional operations of Hollywood’s largest talent and management firms. Here is Kramer’s full memo: UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next. With that in mind, we are announcing a streamlined, future-focused leadership structure for our Filmed Entertainment group which reflects the evolving business of film and television and will enable us to maximize opportunities for clients. By bringing together partners across Motion Picture Literary, Television Literary and Talent, we will continue to deliver unrivaled seamless client representation, sharpen the agency’s competitive edge and increase efficiency and collaboration. I’m thrilled to announce that Matt Rice has been elevated to President of Filmed Entertainment. Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment. To support Matt and drive leadership across the entirety of the Filmed Entertainment group, we have elevated Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to the role of Managing Partner of Filmed Entertainment. This newly established leadership group will be critical to driving growth, connecting opportunities across our business and delivering exceptional results for clients as film and TV increasingly converge. To further capture market momentum and maximize client opportunities we have also established a Filmed Entertainment board. These senior partnerswill leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives. Board members will include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz. All of our Filmed Entertainment Department Heads play an integral part in ensuring our teams operate at the highest level in service of our clients. As we move to this new chapter, we are excited to appoint several new Department Heads across Filmed Entertainment: Amanda Hymson andJordan Lonner (Motion Picture Literary); Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman (TV Literary); Hanley Baxter and John Sacks (Talent, alongside incumbent department head Mike Jelline). These agents have distinguished themselves through exceptional client representation and will be responsible for furthering the growth of their respective businesses. We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success. Please join me in congratulating our new leadership for Filmed Entertainment. We have so much to be proud of and I can’t wait to see this team take us to new heights in the coming year. articles.title: Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:03am PT Jackie Chan, Anil Kapoor Films Among 335 National Winners at Asian Academy Creative Awards By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Sabu’s ‘Arrested Memory’ Leads Golden Horse Awards Nominations, Shu Qi’s ‘Girl’ Close Behind 3 hours ago Ballet Star Tiler Peck to Make London West End Debut in Susan Stroman’s ‘Little Dancer’ (EXCLUSIVE) 8 hours ago Venice Golden Lion Winner Milcho Manchevski’s ‘Sister Brother Manhole Cover’ Heads to Tokyo for World Premiere, Trailer Unveiled (EXCLUSIVE) 9 hours ago See All Golden Network Asia Films fronted by Jackie Chan and Anil Kapoor are among the 335 national winners named by the Asian Academy Creative Awards . “The Shadow’s Edge” won Best Feature Film for Chinese Mainland, and “Subedaar” won it for India. The winners come from 18 nations and territories and span 39 categories. They now move on to the international round. Grand winners will be named at the gala awards final at Singapore’s Capitol Theatre in December. Related Stories Paige DeSorbo on Leaving 'Summer House' Behind and Speaking Out About a Past Abusive Relationship: 'Domestic Violence' Can 'Truly Happen to Anyone' 'People Are Still Terrified of Me': Sharon Stone on Thriving for 46 Years in Hollywood and Why 'My Lane Was Never Going to Be Sex Psychos' Mediacorp led the company count with 23 wins. Prime Video India and Astro Malaysia collected 19 each, and CNN took 15. Popular on Variety Chinese drama series “The Lead” won more categories than any other title, with six. They included Best Actress in a Leading Role for Liu Haocun. Best Drama Series, however, went to the bigger-budget “Legend of the Magnate.” Malaysia’s haul came with a note of loss. Horror feature “Malam Terlarang” (Forbidden Night) won four categories, among them Best Feature Film and Best Actress in a Supporting Role for Sofia Jane. Its Best Direction (Feature Film) win went to Norhanisham bin Muhammad, who died in May. Astro’s family crime drama “Good Boys Go to Heaven” added five Malaysian wins, taking both Best Actor and the drama series prize. In Japan, “Song of the Samurai” also won five categories but lost Best Drama Series to “Alice in Borderland.” Non took Best Actress for “Miss King.” China’s “Swords Into Plowshares” also collected four wins, as did Season 3 of India’s “The Family Man.” Bai Yu was named Best Actor in a Leading Role for Chinese Mainland. Taiwan broadcaster PTS also scored four wins with “Dogman.” The series took Best Drama Series as well as acting honors for Chang Hsiao Chuan and Tarcy Su. GMMTV’s “Enigma Black Stage” picked up four Thai wins. Scripted categories were hotly contested. Gemini Norawit Titicharoenrak was named Best Actor for “Ticket to Heaven,” while Mono’s Manatsanun Phanlerdwongsakul took Best Actress for “Sweet Dreams.” In the Philippines, Vice Ganda, one of the country’s biggest stars, had to get through an extra tie-breaker round before securing Best Actor for his performance in “Call Me Mother.” Nadine Lustre, who stars opposite him in that film, also advances, though her nod is for headlining Viu’s “Love, Siargao.” Animated feature “The Violinist” took Best Feature Film, Best Animation and Best Screenplay for Singapore. Its voice cast includes Tan Kheng Hua and Ayden Sng. Sng was separately named Best Actor in a Leading Role (Singapore) for the series “Double Helix.” Singaporean independent Refinery Media won three categories for lifestyle show “Man of the Hour.” CNN’s 15 wins came in the factual categories. One went to Kristie Lu Stout, a previous winner, for Best Factual Presenter (Thailand). She will go up against another past winner, Singapore’s Wei Du, who was recognized for CNA’s “Walk the Line: ICE Nation.” Awards chair Beverley McGarvey, president and streaming lead at Paramount ANZ, said the awards show every year how deep the region’s pool of talent and original ideas runs. “Our stories are becoming more confident, more distinctive and more influential, not only in their home markets but with audiences all around the world,” she said. McGarvey said that entry numbers were level with last year’s. She added that the size of the national winners field makes it the world’s biggest showcase of Asia-Pacific content. This year’s jurors came from 38 countries. The awards use a two-round system. A jury of senior industry figures from TV networks, streamers, production outfits, distributors, buyers and screen agencies first scores entries at the national level. It scores them again in the international round to choose the grand winners. articles.title: Kevin Feige Hails Theatrical Experience as ‘the Real Movie Magic’ at Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Tribute
articles.full_text: Breaking News MERGER APPROVED: Paramount Tentatively Sets Tuesday to Close Warner Bros. Deal Oct 1, 2026 9:09am PT Kevin Feige Hails Theatrical Experience as ‘the Real Movie Magic’ at Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Tribute By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Don’t Lie, Don’t Cry and Use Common Sense: Adam Levy, Judge Judy’s Son, Joins the Family Business With ‘Adam’s Law’ 1 week ago How NBCUniversal Television Thrives on Collaborative Energy Between Studios and Platforms: ‘We Cheer Each Other On’ 1 week ago Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts 1 week ago See All Ryan Miller / @captureimaging.com He’s a “great guy who’s incredibly humble” who has also produced 38 movies in 17 years that have delivered more than $35 billion at the box office. Twelve of those titles delivered more than $1 billion; three of them generated $2 billion apiece. Not to mention, Kevin Feige is the architect of the most meticulously crafted, interconnected cinematic universe in the history of motion pictures. Disney Entertainment chairman Alan Bergman reeled off those stunning stats (and admirable qualities) as he took part in Wednesday night’s tribute to Feige, president of Marvel Studios and chief creative officer of Marvel, who was honored with this year’s Pioneer of the Year laurel from the Will Rogers Motion Picture Pioneers Foundation . Related Stories Melissa McCarthy on Getting Serious for 'JonBenét Ramsey,' the Psychiatrist on Set and Hollywood's 'Bulls---’ Excuse for Why Comedies Don't Work Anymore Her Road to the Top: How NBCUniversal TV Studio Chief Pearlena Igbokwe Learned to Balance Business and Creative Instincts “Guardians of the Galaxy” star Chris Pratt and writer-director Jon Favreau were on hand at the Beverly Hilton hotel to laud the Marvel leader. Composer Michael Giacchino was there via video because of illness. Others who paid tribute in prerecorded reels include Marvel’s Louis D’Esposito and MCU stars Robert Downey Jr., Chris Evans, Hayley Atwell, Chris Hemsworth, Paul Bettany, Hailee Steinfeld, Pedro Pascal and Vanessa Kirby. Popular on Variety Feige was the star of the night but the conversation in the packed ballroom was dominated by the big news of the day, Paramount Skydance’s surprise news that Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz is leaving the toymaker to join the Melrose plant as co-CEO with David Ellison. “He believes in the movies, and even more than that he believes in the people who make the movies,” Pratt told the crowd at the Beverly Hilton. The event raised $1.9 million for the Will Rogers Pioneers Assistance Fund, which helps those in the film exhibition community who need assistance. Also in the crowd were Disney chief Josh D’Amaro, AMC Theatres leader Adam Aron and Eduardo Acuna of Regal Cinemas, producer Scott Stuber among others. Favreau echoed Pratt’s comments about Feige’s passion for all things related to cinema. “The man loves movies. He listens to movie soundtracks in his car,” the “Iron Man” director told the crowd. “He’s driving down PCH blasting the ‘Ferngully’ soundtrack.” Feige took a bit of gentle ribbing about his love of custom baseball caps and other characteristics that have become his signature. From video, Giacchino introduced a large tiki band that emerged on stage to perform Marvel movie tunes with a Polynesian flair. The executive and producer lived up to his advance billing for humility in his remarks at the end of the night. And he had some thoughtful observations about what it is that makes moviegoing so special. He even name-checked his childhood haunt, the Rialto Theater in Westfield, New Jersey. (“Sitting in the dark, eating Twizzlers. I was hooked,” he recalled.) “Underneath all the technology and the spectacle, the years of work from development to post. It’s still the same thing: a group of people making something with others, and then a group of people sitting in the dark and experiencing it with others. That is the full process of a movie,” Feige said. “The final crucial part of that collaboration is the audience. Movies are an invitation to experience a story together. When a film connects and the crowd is cheering, laughing and crying together, that shared emotion is the final step in the process. That’s the real movie magic, You might even say it’s not a real movie without it,” he said. articles.title: Hearst Renews CBS Weekend Series ‘The Visioneers With Zay Harding’ Through 2028
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Starz Goes Dark On Verizon FiOS Amid Carriage Dispute Ynon Kreiz Anointed Co-CEO Of New Paramount-WBD; David Ellison Says Mega-Studio Is “Transformational Moment For Our Industry” Ex-Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz In Line For High-Level Paramount Exec Post View All October 1, 2026 6:57am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Hearst Media Production Group has renewed CBS weekend educational series The Visioneers with Zay Harding for two more seasons, through 2028. The show was first announced by Hearst in March 2025. Season 3 of the 30-minute eco-adventure original, which is produced by the Hearst production division in partnership with the VoLo Foundation, will premiere on Saturday. Hosted by Harding, an international explorer, the show features scientists, engineers and everyday people who are creating sustainable environmental solutions. Related Stories Executives Hearst Corp. CEO Steven Swartz Expects "Strong Year" For TV Division, Hints At M&A At A+E Global, Local Stations News 'Lucky Dog: Down Under' Expands Pet Franchise In New CBS Weekend Block The series airs weekend mornings as part of the CBS WKND educational/informational programming block. Timeslots vary by market. Watch on Deadline Guests this season include actor Edward Norton; former NFL player and ocean-conservation advocate Kelvin Beachum; NASCAR driver Austin Green; and Luci Baines Johnson, daughter of Lady Bird Johnson. Episodes are set from the Great Barrier Reef to America’s ports, racetracks and wildflower fields. “Alongside our partners at VoLo Foundation, we’re proud to bring audiences two more seasons of The Visioneers,” HMPG President Bryan Curb said in a statement. “The show has struck a real chord with viewers, sharing stories that prove environmental stewardship can take many forms – and that building a more sustainable future can be an engaging, hands-on adventure.” Thais Lopez V., president of VoLo Foundation, said the series “shows that the solutions to our biggest challenges are already in the hands of people with the courage to imagine a better world and the determination to make it real.” HMPG’s slate includes more than 30 original series and hundreds of hours of content annually on broadcast networks, station groups, connected-TV and streaming platforms. Its library spans 85 series and 6,000 episodes, with content across 100 countries. articles.title: ‘Best Pancakes In The County’: IFC Picks Up Domestic Rights To Nicolas Cage, Justin Long & Shelley Hennig Action-Thriller; First Look Revealed
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas ‘Best Pancakes In The County’: IFC Picks Up Domestic Rights To Nicolas Cage, Justin Long & Shelley Hennig Action-Thriller; First Look Revealed Crime Pic ‘American Muscle’ Being Sold By Protagonist Picks Charlotte Kirk & Neil Marshall Thriller ‘Spiral Down’ Adds Costas Mandylor, Michael Pare, Alessandra Williams, More View All October 1, 2026 7:25am Add us as a Google Preferred Source (L-R) Nicolas Cage, Justin Long and Shelley Hennig Getty Images EXCLUSIVE : Independent Film Company has acquired U.S. rights to Best Pancakes In The County , the action-thriller written and directed by Ken Sanzel ( Kill Chain ) and starring Nicolas Cage ( Longleg s), Justin Long ( Weapons ) and Shelley Hennig ( Unfriended ). The deal was negotiated by Mark Ward, Chief Acquisitions Officer for Independent Film Company and Eduard Osipov at Beno Films on behalf of the filmmakers. Pic will be released in theaters and on digital platforms November 20, 2026. The synopsis reads: “Set over the course of one explosive night, Best Pancakes In The County transforms an unassuming small-town diner into the epicenter of a deadly standoff involving rogue federal agents, a fast-talking con man with a dangerous past and a waitress harboring secrets of her own. As loyalties blur and tensions erupt, survival depends on who can outthink — and outgun — everyone else.” Related Stories Trailers 'Madden' Trailer: Boom! Nicolas Cage Transforms In David O. Russell's Biopic Of NFL Icon Reviews 'River' Review: Joshua Giuliano Makes Directorial Debut With Tragic Family Drama Wrapped In Atmospheric Slasher -- Toronto Film Festival Cage stars as “The S.O.B., an eccentric and cunning criminal caught in the escalating confrontation”. Below is a first-look image. The film reunites Sanzel with Cage following their collaboration on the 2019 action thriller Kill Chain . Long plays Cookie and Hennig is Dolly. The ensemble cast also includes Lauren German ( Lucifer ), Ravi Patel ( Animal Control) , Brandon Mychal Smith ( Get On Up ), Kelly Greyson ( Sleeping Dogs ), Jaylen Moore ( Six ), and Michael Sirow ( Sleeping Dogs ). The movie was filmed in Arkansas and is produced by Eduard Osipov, Raja Collins, Eric Brenner, Niko Fomenko, Gary Preisler and R. Wesley Sierk III. Executive producers include John D. Straley, Audra Gricius, Jina Panebianco, Lance Kawas, Ahmed S. Boomrod, Eugene Pruss, and Nadine de Barros. The film is produced by Beno Films and backed by CaliWood Pictures, with Fortitude International handling international sales. “ Best Pancakes In The County is exactly the kind of eccentric and wildly entertaining ride that Nicolas Cage does better than anyone else,” said IFC Entertainment Group’s Chief Acquisition Officer, Mark Ward. “Ken has built a tense, funny and unpredictable thriller around a fantastic ensemble, and we can’t wait for audiences to experience the chaos this November.” “Working with Nic again was an opportunity to create a character who could be funny, dangerous and completely unpredictable from one moment to the next,” said writer-director Sanzel. “And then he took it to wilder and more unexpected places than I could have imagined. We wanted to take this seemingly ordinary diner, fill it with people with dueling and hidden agendas, juxtapose the threat of violence with the urgency of getting breakfast orders right, and keep turning up the pressure until everything explodes. IFC immediately understood the fast, fun tone of the film, and I’m excited to have them bringing it to audiences.” Watch on Deadline Nicolas Cage in Best Pancakes In The County Ted Sarandos On WB Pursuit, Netflix Engagement Growth Challenges & More Becerra & Hilton Tussle Over Blame For Losing Hollywood Jobs In Debate Sound Decision? articles.title: AGC Studios Launches Digital Division Focused On Creator-Led IP
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac AGC Studios Launches Digital Division Focused On Creator-Led IP London Film Festival: Sam Pollard To Lead Official Competition Jury Ascent Creatives International Launches After DDA Talent & Worldwide Production Merger View All October 1, 2026 8:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source AGC Studios AGC Studios is launching AGC Digital , a dedicated division focused on creator-led content. The studio said the division will partner with digital creators to turn their ideas, content, and audiences into entertainment franchises. Jared Jacobs will lead the division as SVP, AGC Digital. He will report to Joel Zimmer, President, AGC. The studio said Jacobs will be responsible for “identifying, developing, financing, and commercializing intellectual property from the digital ecosystem.” Jacobs previously worked with Warner Bros. Unscripted Television on digital strategy, development, creator partnerships, and new IP. He also served as VP of Development at Night Studios, where he helped lead the company’s creator-led entertainment slate and developed projects with some of the world’s biggest digital talent, including MrBeast, Kai Cenat, Ryan Trahan, Sam & Colby, Moriah Elizabeth, and Zach King. articles.title: UTA Sets New Leadership Structure For Filmed Entertainment Division Under President Matt Rice
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Joachim Rønning Sets Horror Film ‘System’ With Spooky Pictures & Image Nation Studios Neon Counters A24’s SCP Foundation Movie With “Open-Source” Project To Release Under Creative Commons License 20th Century Studios Acquires Horror Package ‘Every House Is Haunted’ From Netflix; ‘Don’t Move’s Adam Schindler & Brian Netto Directing View All October 1, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Matt Rice, newly appointed President of UTA's Filmed Entertainment division Sonali Ohrie UTA on Thursday announced a comprehensive reorganization of its Filmed Entertainment Division, elevating Matt Rice to serve as its President. A longtime partner at the agency who most recently served as head of its TV department, Rice is known for his work with top writer, producer, director, talent and comedy clients like Phil Lord & Chris Miller, Mike Schur, Alec Berg, Bill Hader, Seth Rogen & Evan Goldberg, among others. “Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment,” said CEO David Kramer in an internal memo to staff this morning. Related Stories Agencies UTA Signs 'Brian' Filmmaker Will Ropp Agencies UTA Signs 'Club Kid' Star Reggie Absolom In addition to Rice’s role, UTA has announced the promotion of Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to Managing Partners of Filmed Entertainment. Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner are now heads of Motion Picture Literary, with Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman heading up TV Lit, and Hanley Baxter and John Sacks joining the incumbent Mike Jelline to head up the Talent department. Watch on Deadline Additionally, UTA today announced the formation of a Filmed Entertainment board, consisting of senior partners who, per Kramer, “will leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives.” Board members include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz. Kramer emphasized, in his memo to staff, that the reorg is intended to “increase efficiency and collaboration,” thereby maximizing client opportunities and sharpening “the agency’s competitive edge” amidst a rapidly evolving entertainment landscape. Kramer said that “UTA has never been a place that waits for change,” calling the new leadership structure “streamlined” and “future-focused.” He went on to say, “We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success.” Kramer’s assessment echos comments he made about the agency’s “record-breaking year,” “strength” and “momentum” in an Aug. 26 memo, in which he hit back at a Variety article about recent UTA client departures, which alleged internal anxiety, accusing the author of unprofessional bias. ( Variety ‘s parent company, Penske Media Corporation, also owns Deadline .) Read the full memo below: UTA has never been a place that waits for change — we anticipate where the industry is going and build for what comes next. With that in mind, we are announcing a streamlined, future-focused leadership structure for our Filmed Entertainment group which reflects the evolving business of film and television and will enable us to maximize opportunities for clients. By bringing together partners across Motion Picture Literary, Television Literary and Talent, we will continue to deliver unrivaled seamless client representation, sharpen the agency’s competitive edge and increase efficiency and collaboration. I’m thrilled to announce that Matt Rice has been elevated to President of Filmed Entertainment . Matt is a phenomenal agent and partner who has helped spearhead a transformative expansion of UTA’s television division. In his expanded role, he will lead overall strategy and execution across all areas of Filmed Entertainment. To support Matt and drive leadership across the entirety of the Filmed Entertainment group, we have elevated Allan Haldeman, Blair Kohan, Jay Gassner and Julien Thuan to the role of Managing Partner of Filmed Entertainment. This newly established leadership group will be critical to driving growth, connecting opportunities across our business and delivering exceptional results for clients as film and TV increasingly converge. To further capture market momentum and maximize client opportunities we have also established a Filmed Entertainment board. These senior partnerswill leverage their collective expertise, experience and deep industry relationships to aggressively pursue client development and new initiatives. Board members will include Mickey Berman, Jason Burns, Marissa Devins, Dan Erlij, Chris Hart, Jason Heyman, Mike Jelline, Keya Khayatian, Rich Klubeck, Billy Lazarus, Gregory McKnight, Lucinda Moorhead, David Park, Theresa Peters, Shani Rosenzweig, and Larry Salz. All of our Filmed Entertainment Department Heads play an integral part in ensuring our teams operate at the highest level in service of our clients. As we move to this new chapter, we are excited to appoint several new Department Heads across Filmed Entertainment: Amanda Hymson and Jordan Lonner (Motion Picture Literary); Lucinda Moorhead and Mickey Berman (TV Literary); Hanley Baxter and John Sacks (Talent, alongside incumbent department head Mike Jelline ). These agents have distinguished themselves through exceptional client representation and will be responsible for furthering the growth of their respective businesses. We’ve had an extraordinary year, with UTA clients behind some of 2026’s biggest box office hits and most acclaimed television productions, earning top honors at the Academy Awards, Emmys, Golden Globes and Tonys. We are building from a position of immense strength, and this new leadership structure is designed to carry that momentum forward and position us for even greater success . Please join me in congratulating our new leadership for Filmed Entertainment. We have so much to be proud of and I can’t wait to see this team take us to new heights in the coming year.
