articles.title: Amazon to Develop ‘Shadow Work’ Series Based on Adrienne Miller Short Story, Marc Resteghini to Produce (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 28, 2026 10:15am PT Amazon to Develop ‘Shadow Work’ Series Based on Adrienne Miller Short Story, Marc Resteghini to Produce (EXCLUSIVE) By Joe Otterson Plus Icon Joe Otterson TV Reporter joeotterson Latest ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role 16 minutes ago ‘Icebreaker’ Netflix Series Casts Daisy Jelley, Connor Simos in Lead Roles (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Peter Sarsgaard Joins Kenneth Branagh in Paramount+ Series ‘Laird’ 3 days ago See All Getty Images In a competitive situation, Amazon MGM Studios is set to develop a series based on the short story “Shadow Work” by Adrienne Miller, Variety has learned exclusively from sources. Miller will write the pilot for the one-hour series and serve as executive producer. Former Amazon exec Marc Resteghini will executive produce via Jack Tar Pictures, which has an overall deal at Amazon MGM Studios. According to sources, the producers fielded multiple offers before Amazon preemptively acquired it. Related Stories ‘60 Minutes’ Kicks Off Much-Scrutinized 59th Season With Old Ticks and Tricks ‘48 Hours’ Expands Use of Video Podcasting With 'Woman in the Woods' Reps for Amazon declined to comment. Popular on Variety The logline for the show states that it follows Genevieve Pearce, “an elite ghostwriter trusted with the secrets of the rich, famous, and infamous. She embeds in their worlds, excavates secrets, reshapes memories, manufactures redemption, and transforms the powerful into the people they want the world to believe they are. Because in Genevieve’s world, whoever controls the story controls reality. But as she rewrites everyone else’s stories, she’s forced to confront the first story she ever helped rewrite: her own.” Miller is the author of the novel “The Coast of Akron” as well as the memoir “In the Land of Men,” in which she describes her rise through the male-dominated magazine world to become the first female literary editor at Esquire. During her time at Esquire, the publication won the National Magazine Award for fiction. Miller is also a frequent contributor to Vogue. She is repped by Gersh and Yorn Levine. Resteghini is currently an executive producer on the Amazon series “Young Sherlock,” which received a Season 2 renewal in April . His current slate includes an animated series adaptation of the Tui T. Sutherland “Wings of Fire” books, a feature adaptation of the upcoming Lauren Oliver novel “The Girl in the Lake” in partnership with United Artists, and a series inspired by the lyrics and characters of Billy Joel’s songbook from creator David Weil and MGM Television. Prior to launching his own production banner, Resteghini was a senior creative executive at Amazon for nearly a decade. articles.title: Carrie Coon Set to Receive Vancouver’s First Luminary Award (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 28, 2026 10:15am PT Carrie Coon Set to Receive Vancouver’s First Luminary Award (EXCLUSIVE) Other Luminary Award recipients are Markus Schleinzer and Leah Nelson as VIFF unveils a wide-ranging program of talks, panels and masterclasses By Katherine Brodsky Plus Icon Katherine Brodsky Latest Vancouver Film Festival Reveals 2026 Lineup: Jesse Eisenberg, Cristian Mungiu but Also Local Talent, Indigenous and Nonfiction Cinema 4 weeks ago Green Screen: British Columbia Adopts More Sustainability Practices for Production Shoots 2 years ago Telefilm Canada Focuses on Finding Fresh Voices But Faces Financing Roadblocks 3 years ago See All Fabio Lovino/HBO Carrie Coon will be the first recipient of the Vancouver International Film Festival’s new Luminary Award in the acting category, honoring excellence and dedication to the art of moving image. The “White Lotus,” “The Gilded Age,” and “The Leftovers” star is set to take part in a wide-ranging conversation following the Oct. 4 presentation. Coon also stars in “The Liberation,” which screens earlier that day at VIFF, playing a mother trying to escape the weight of her harrowing past, only to find solace in an all-women’s cult. Related Stories ‘60 Minutes’ Notches Ratings Gain Over Last Year, but Cedes Viewers From Season Premiere Major TV Networks Suspend White House Pool Coverage of Trump in Protest of His CNN Ban Beyond Coon’s appearance, VIFF’s Oct. 1-11 program will feature talks, panels and masterclasses bringing filmmakers, craftspeople, producers, programmers and other industry professionals to Vancouver. The festival will also present Luminary Awards to Markus Schleinzer (“Rose”) for directing excellence and Leah Nelson (“Tangles”) for screenwriting. Popular on Variety The festival’s VIFF Talks series kicks off Oct. 3 with editor Matthew Hannam , whose recent credits include Halina Reijn’s “Babygirl” and Noah Baumbach’s “White Noise.” Hannam, who will be discussing his collaborative approach, began his career as an assistant editor in Winnipeg, working with Canadian auteurs like Guy Maddin. Producer Haley Johnson will discuss the making of “Obsession,” the independently produced film made on a shoestring budget that went on to gross over $500 million worldwide. The Oct. 4 conversation will focus on the film’s production and subsequent trajectory, including a studio bidding war following its Toronto premiere. On Oct. 5, production designers Brandon Tonner-Connolly and Matt Hyland will discuss working together to build the surreal, immersive world of Jane Schoenbrun’s “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma.” The VIFF Talks series concludes Oct. 7 with Mark Mothersbaugh , DEVO co-founder and composer behind Wes Anderson’s “Rushmore,” “The Royal Tenenbaums” and “The Life Aquatic with Steve Zissou,” amongst others. He’ll be in conversation with composer and former Fox studio exec Robert Kraft. This year’s masterclass programming has a distinctly international flavor. Guests include Latvian producer, writer and director Matīss Kaža , who co-wrote and produced Gints Zilbalodis’ “Flow,” which won the Academy Award for animated feature last year. Chilean producer Giancarlo Nasi , whose credits include “The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo,” winner of the Grand Prix at Cannes’ Un Certain Regard n 2025, will lead a session on international co-productions. Berlin-based film editor Evelyn Rack — behind the Cannes Jury Prize winner and Germany’s Oscars submission, “Sound of Falling” — will lead “Editing as Discovery: Narrative, Instinct, and the Unpredictable.” And Barcelona-born, Berlin-based audience designer Isona Admetlla will explore audience strategy and creative distribution. The panel lineup, meanwhile, brings together figures from across the festival and distribution ecosystem. “Curating Cinema in a Shifting Landscape” will feature Pamela Biénzobas , a programmer at the Locarno Film Festival, alongside VIFF documentary programmer Ruun Nuur and critic/programmer Saffron Maeve , for a discussion of how film curation is evolving. “From Festival to Marketplace: Meet the Decision Makers” will bring together Michael Robson of Elevation Pictures, Max Collister of Mubi Canada and Richelle Charkot of Game Theory Films to discuss the path from festival exposure to distribution and audiences. The Vancouver-to-international trajectory will be the focus of “From Vancouver to the World: The Making of Tangles,” featuring director Leah Nelson alongside several members of the creative team behind the animated feature. Based on Vancouver artist Sarah Leavitt’s graphic memoir, “Tangles” was selected for Cannes the best first feature Caméra d’Or at Cannes and boasts a voice cast that includes Abbi Jacobson, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Bryan Cranston, and Seth Rogen. Other panels will examine Indigenous filmmaking and narrative sovereignty, deal-making, documentary filmmaking beyond certainty, and the craft of comedy. The festival will also showcase its Composer Filmmaker Accelerator, an initiative connecting emerging composers with filmmakers through mentorship and hands-on collaboration. It is curated by three-time Emmy-nominated composer Miriam Cutler , whose credits include “RBG,” “Love Gilda,” and “Lost in La Mancha.” The 2026 CFA showcase takes place Oct. 8. Among the filmmakers and industry figures also expected at VIFF are Canadian icon Rick Hansen , actor and “School for Defectors” producer Daniel Dae Kim , and Canadian directors Matthew Rankin (“Ladies and Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney”), Marie Clements (“How We Stand,” “Reclaim My Skin”) and Zach Lipovsky (“Freaks Part II”). articles.full_text: Sep 28, 2026 10:30am PT ‘Kid Detective’ Series Adaptation in the Works at Hulu (EXCLUSIVE) Evan Morgan will executive produce, with Rachel Kaplan exec producing via Abescon Entertainment By Joe Otterson Plus Icon Joe Otterson TV Reporter joeotterson Latest Amazon to Develop ‘Shadow Work’ Series Based on Adrienne Miller Short Story, Marc Resteghini to Produce (EXCLUSIVE) 15 minutes ago ‘Stillwater’: Amazon Series Based on Graphic Novel Casts Ben Hardy in Lead Role 30 minutes ago ‘Icebreaker’ Netflix Series Casts Daisy Jelley, Connor Simos in Lead Roles (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago See All ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection Hulu is developing a series version of the 2020 movie “The Kid Detective,” Variety has learned exclusively. Evan Morgan, who wrote and directed the film, is attached as an executive producer on the project. Alex Berger will write and executive produce. Rachel Kaplan of Abescon Entertainment will also executive produce, with Jonathan Bronfman and Will Woods — who produced the film — producing the series as well. Adam Brody, who starred in “The Kid Detective,” is not attached at this time. Related Stories ‘60 Minutes’ Kicks Off Much-Scrutinized 59th Season With Old Ticks and Tricks ‘48 Hours’ Expands Use of Video Podcasting With 'Woman in the Woods' The logline for the series states, “When a missing persons case reopens the childhood murder he never solved, a washed-up former kid detective gets one last shot at proving his best days aren’t behind him.” Popular on Variety Brody starred as the titular kid detective Abe Applebaum in the film, which debuted at TIFF in 2020. The film was well-received by critics upon its release. In his review for Variety , Tomris Laffly wrote “Splendidly summoning film noir-esque vibes, classically ghastly bad guys and femme fatale types out of a whimsical small town full of grotesque mysteries, this bold and often surprisingly humorous film…grapples with themes related to murder and abuse, as well as the existential dread of its central recluse, who fell grossly short of the promising life he thought he was meant to have in his younger days.” Berger most recently worked on “CIA” at CBS as well as shows like “The Perfect Couple” at Netflix and “Quantum Leap” for NBC. His other credits include “Blindspot,” “The Mentalist,” “Franklin & Bash,” and “Glenn Martin DDS.” Kaplan was previously head of scripted TV at Keshet Studios before launching Abescon studios in 2020. Under that banner, she has executive produced shows like “La Brea” at NBC and has projects in active development across a range of streamers and networks. During her time with Keshet, she shephered shows like “The Baker and the Beauty,” “Lincoln Rhyme: The Hunt for the Bone Collector,” And “Wisdom of the Crowd.” Berger is repped by UTA, A.B. Fischer, and Yorn Levine. Morgan is repped by Range and Verve. articles.title: Fox News To Launch ‘The Girls’ Podcast With Network Personalities And Others As Rotating Co-Hosts
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Fox News To Launch ‘The Girls’ Podcast With Network Personalities And Others As Rotating Co-Hosts Harry Smith To Return To NBC News As A Contributor ‘Saturday Night Live’ Opens Season With Riff On Donald Trump’s Need For More Time With Zohran Mamdani: “Please Let Me Stay Here With You” View All September 28, 2026 9:00am Fox News is launching The Girls , a conversation series for its podcast division that will feature a rotating series of co-hosts each week. The first episode will debut on Thursday, with new episodes dropping that day each week. The conversations will delve into pop culture, parenting, relationships, careers, money and politics. The first episode will feature network personalities Rachel Campos-Duffy , Harris Faulkner and Kat Timpf, new contributor Melissa DeRosa and former ESPN host Samantha Ponder. Fox News Podcasts has expanded its portfolio, debuting Hang Out with Sean Hannity earlier this year. This latest podcast is the latest iteration of a panel format that has worked well for the network, including with The Five and Outnumbered. Campos-Duffy co-hosts Fox & Friends Weekend , and joined the network in 2016. Faulkner, with Fox News since 2005, anchors The Faulkner Focus and co-hosts Outnumbered . Timpf is a panelist on Gutfeld! , and joined the network in 2015. DeRosa previously served in the administration of New York Governor Andrew Cuomo. Ponder formerly hosted ESPN’s Sunday Countdown . Watch on Deadline Porter Berry, president of Fox News Digital and New Media, called the show “a natural addition to our growing podcast portfolio.” Megan Albano, executive vice president of morning programming and program development, said in a statement that the podcast would be a “no-holds-barred format that captures the authenticity and perspectives of the many dynamic women” on the network and elsewhere. This story is set to be explored in a new feature-length documentary for Oxygen . The Versant-owned cable network has greenlit The Siders 16: Ohio House of Horrors (w/t) from KT Studios , the company behind Amazon’s Murder 101 and Peacock’s The Idaho Student Murders. The Siders 16: Ohio House of Horrors will explore the case as it unfolds in real time after the children’s parents Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth Siders, and their grandparents, Gary Siders Sr. and Christina Siders, were arrested at the scene. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals Lisa Vanderpump To Host 'Snapped' Spinoff 'Rich Bitch Rampage' For Oxygen As Part Of Versant Slate News Inside Versant's Content Strategy: True-Crime, A.I., Recognizable Drama IP & More Reality Shows With Wrestlers The group were charged were multiple counts of endangering children, while, in August, Gary Siders Jr. and Elizabeth were also charged with allegations of child sexual abuse in a separate case. Watch on Deadline The film will touch on these unexpected new charges and ask: Who ultimately bears responsibility for what happened to these children? The 90-minute doc will premiere later this year on Oxygen True Crime. It follows the success of The Hooters Murders: Deadly Shift, which was Oxygen’s most-watched doc premiere in more than two years. The Siders 16: Ohio House of Horrors is directed by KT Studios founder Stephanie Lydecker, who also exec produces alongside Kevin Brennecke. Alongside the doc, the network will also launch its first-ever companion podcast series. The ten-part audio series will be available on all major podcast platforms as well as Oxygen’s digital platforms. articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Patrick Hipes Patrick Hipes Executive Managing Editor More Stories By Patrick Santa Barbara Film Festival Awards: ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Star John Malkovich To Get Performer Of The Year Honor ‘Madden’ Trailer: Boom! Nicolas Cage Transforms In David O. Russell’s Biopic Of NFL Icon ‘Wild Horse Nine’ Trailer: Martin McDonagh’s Venice Hit Saddles Up For Awards-Season Run View All September 28, 2026 9:00am 'Wildwood' Laika EXCLUSIVE: Laika , the animation studio that has scored six Oscar nominations for its stop-motion films including Coraline, ParaNorman, The Boxtrolls and Kubo and Two Strings since its founding in 2005, will be honored with the Gotham Anniversary Tribute at this year’s Gotham Film Awards . The tribute commemorates Laika’s 20 years of storytelling and the release of Wildwood , its newest film, which hits theaters October 23 via Fathom Entertainment. The pic will have its world premiere at the London Film Festival October 11 and 10 days later serve as the opening-night film at AFI Fest . Related Stories Trailers Laika Unveils Final Trailer For Latest Stop-Motion Fantasy Adventure ‘Wildwood’ Below The Line 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More It marks the first tribute award revealed for the 36th annual Gothams, put on by the Gotham Film & Media Institute, which take place this year November 20 at Cipriani Wall Street in New York City. Watch on Deadline “After 20 years of pushing the boundaries of modern cinema and animation, this moment feels like both a celebration and an evolution for Laika,” said Jeffrey Sharp, executive director of the institute, which earlier this year teamed with the animation studio to launch Laika x Gotham Animation Accelerator for creators working on animated short films. “With Wildwood , Laika’s most ambitious film to date, and the launch of Laika Live Action opening up new creative territory, the studio continues to expand the possibilities of what handcrafted storytelling can be. We can think of no more fitting honoree for this year’s Anniversary Tribute, and we’re thrilled to welcome the Laika team to celebrate with us.” Travis Knight, Laika’s president and CEO, directs Wildwood , which was written by Chris Butler based on Colin Meloy’s novel. It centers on headstrong teenager Prue McKeel (Peyton Elizabeth Lee), who after her baby brother is abducted by a murder of crows launches with her hapless but loyal classmate Curtis Mehlberg (Jacob Tremblay) a rescue mission into the Impassable Wilderness — an enchanted forest hidden just beyond Portland, OR. It voice cast also includes Carey Mulligan, Mahershala Ali, Angela Bassett, Awkwafina, Jake Johnson, Charlie Day, Amandla Stenberg, Jemaine Clement, Maya Erskine, Tantoo Cardinal, Tom Waits and Richard E. Grant. “We’re deeply honored that The Gotham is recognizing Laika at a moment when we’re celebrating two decades of filmmaking and bringing Wildwood to audiences,” said David Burke, Laika’s Chief Marketing & Operations Officer. “Our partnership on the Laika x Gotham Animation Accelerator reflects something we care deeply about: creating meaningful opportunities for bold new voices to push animation forward. We’re grateful to The Gotham for this recognition and for a partnership grounded in a shared belief in original, ambitious storytelling.” More Gotham tributes will be rolled out throughout the fall, with nominations in the 10 competition Gotham Awards categories to be revealed October 27. articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise ‘Minions & Monsters’ Sets Peacock Release Date ‘Icebreaker’ Netflix Series Casts Daisy Jelley & Connor Simos As Stassie & Nate ‘The Last Of Us’ Casts John Goodman, Ian Alexander & Laura Bailey For Season 3 View All September 28, 2026 9:00am 'Minions & Monsters' (2026) Universal Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection Minions & Monsters will begin streaming on Peacock on October 28, following its July 1 theatrical release. Starring Pierre Coffin, Allison Janney, Christoph Waltz, Jesse Eisenberg, Jeff Bridges and Zoey Deutch, the seventh installment in the Despicable Me franchise and third in the Minions prequel series is set in 1920s Hollywood. As Deadline’s Damon Wise noted in his review, the opening credits alone trace the history of the Universal logo back to the silent-era days of The Trans-Atlantic Film Company. Per the synopsis, the Illumination /Universal film tells “the rambunctious, ridiculous and totally true story” of how the Minions — led by Dick — conquered Hollywood, became movie stars, lost everything, unleashed monsters onto the world and then banded together to try and save the planet from the mayhem they had just created. Related Stories News Universal Becomes First Studio To Pass $5 Billion At Year-To-Date Global Box Office News 'Musk': Was Universal Getting Cold Feet Over Releasing Alex Gibney Doc? The latest installment is directed by Oscar nominee Pierre Coffin, who helmed the first three Despicable Me films and the first Minions movie. Coffin also provides the voice of the Minions in the film, which he has done since the characters’ film debut in 2010. articles.title: Shawn Levy Moves To Disney’s 20th Television With Overall Deal After Long Tenure At Netflix
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Shawn Levy Moves To Disney’s 20th Television With Overall Deal After Long Tenure At Netflix ‘Scrubs’ Zach Braff Gives Discouraging Ken Jenkins Return Update, Teases More Dr. Cox, Turk Mental Health Arc In Season 2 ‘Scrubs’ Stars On How Scott Foley & Rachel Bilson’s Arrival Changes J.D. & Elliot’s Relationship & Impacts Turk’s Marriage View All September 28, 2026 9:32am Shawn Levy Guy Aroch With Stranger Things coming to an end, both series’ creators/executive producers The Duffer Brothers and director/executive producer Shawn Levy are moving on by setting up shop elsewhere. Following the Duffer Brothers’ massive film and TV overall deal at Paramount , Levy and his 21 Laps Entertainment have signed a big multi-year overall deal with 20th Television , a part of Disney Television Studios, where he will develop and produce series across Disney Entertainment’s portfolio of platforms and brands. Related Stories News Duffer Brothers Close 4-Year Film, TV & Streaming Megadeal With Paramount, Set Netflix Exit News ‘La Bola Negra’ Trailer: Latest Look At TIFF’s People’s Choice Winner, Spain’s Oscar Entry & Cannes Breakout Over the past few months, 20th TV has been able to attract top talent from multiple rival studios, signing overall deals with Abbott Elementary ‘s Quinta Brunson, who was at Warner Bros. TV, The Five Star Weekend EP Sue Naegle, who was at Universal, and now Levy. Watch on Deadline “Shawn has a rare ability to tell stories that are wildly entertaining and deeply human, something he’s brought to Disney across two decades,” said Dana Walden, Disney’s President and Chief Creative Office. “He moves effortlessly across genres and franchises with a remarkable sense of what captures audiences and inspires passionate fandom. He’s an incredible storyteller and a true creative partner of the highest caliber, and we are thrilled to be building this next chapter together.” Disney and Levy have an ongoing relationship on the feature side, which may have factored into his decision to also move his TV business there. He directed and co-wrote Marvel Studios’ blockbuster Deadpool & Wolverine and is directing Lucasfilm’s upcoming Star Wars: Starfighter, starring Ryan Gosling. He is also re-teaming with Gosling on Marvel Studios’ Ghost Rider movie. Early in his career, Levy directed the Disney Channel series The Famous Jett Jackson and later produced Alexander and the Terrible, Horrible, No Good, Very Bad Day for Walt Disney Pictures. “Years before I directed movies, I started my career directing and producing television episodes for Disney Channel, and I’ve always felt a kindred spirit in Disney and their storytelling ethos,” Levy said. “Having worked with Dana Walden over the years when we were both at Fox, I know her to be a formidable, smart and authentic person, not to mention a force of nature as an executive. Coupled with the amazing Debra OConnell, Disney Television has such an exciting era ahead, and I’m enthusiastic and inspired to produce the next wave of 21 Laps television series with the entire Disney team. I know from experience the passionate creative DNA of this place, and it honestly just feels like home.” Levy also acknowledged the leadership at Netflix where he spent more than a decade. “I will forever cherish the incredible ride 21 Laps has had with Netflix,” he said. “I am deeply grateful to Ted, Bela, Jinny and the many talented Netflix execs with whom we have worked over the years and, of course, look forward to continuing our collaboration on the Stranger Things universe from the Duffer Brothers.” The animated Stranger Things: Tales From ’85 just returned for a second season with at least one other offshoot series waiting for a green light at Netflix. Previously, Levy directed 20th Century Studios’ Free Guy , the multi-film franchise The Night at the Museum and Cheaper by the Dozen. articles.title: White House Defends Using Taxpayer Money To Run Trump Ad — Even Though It’s Nearly The Same As 2024 Campaign Spot
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Fox News To Launch ‘The Girls’ Podcast With Network Personalities And Others As Rotating Co-Hosts Harry Smith Returning To NBC News As A Contributor ‘Saturday Night Live’ Opens Season With Riff On Donald Trump’s Need For More Time With Zohran Mamdani: “Please Let Me Stay Here With You” View All September 28, 2026 9:35am Screenshot of taxpayer-funded Donald Trump ad The Trump White House is defending spending taxpayer dollars to run a series of ads that have drawn criticism on both sides of the aisle as they resemble campaign spots. In fact, an ad featuring Trump that ran over the weekend is nearly the same as one that he posted on social media in 2023, as he was campaigning for a return to the presidency. The ad that ran over the weekend features the message, “Paid for by the U.S. Government.” The spot he posted in 2023 features the Trump campaign logo. In the spot from the weekend and from his campaign, Trump says that “this is the final battle. With you at my side, we will demolish the deep state. We will expel the warmongers from our government. We will drive out the globalists. We will cast out the communists, marxists and fascists. We will throw off the sick political class that hates our country. We will rout the fake news media and we will liberate America from these villains, once and for all.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Fox News To Launch 'The Girls' Podcast With Network Personalities And Others As Rotating Co-Hosts News Harry Smith To Return To NBC News As A Contributor Steven Cheung, White House communications director, posted on X on Sunday, “Don’t let the Fake News get away with their lies about our epic Public Service Announcements that have been running on tv.” But there has been criticism from both parties. Sen. John Kennedy (R-LA) said that “you can’t spend public money to promote yourself.” He added that “I may end up with a sombrero on my head, but I also think that we ought to have a rule that no politician can have a building named after him while he’s alive.” Kennedy’s reference to a sombrero was to Trump pushing out a deepfake video last fall of House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Trump also has sought to put his name on the Kennedy Center, even though Congress designated it as a memorial to the late president. Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY) posted on X, “Don’t worry, using taxpayer dollars to run ominous campaign ads of the President has been done before and is completely legal… in banana republics.” About $319,000 has been spent on the spot, according to the AP, citing estimates from AdImpact. Two other spots began running last week. The White House sent out a release on Friday contending that the spots “are very clearly not campaign ads; President Trump is not on the ballot and there is no call to action. Instead, the announcements are a reminder for Americans to love their country and know why it’s worth defending — at home, at the border, and abroad.” Federal law bars appropriations from being used for “publicity or propaganda” purposes, but there has been some leeway for the use of taxpayer money for public service announcements on specific issues. The White House pointed to spots by the Obama administration to promote the Affordable Care Act and the Biden administration to spread the word about the Covid vaccine. But the latest Trump spot is centered on Trump himself, not a single issue, and largely mirrors the previous campaign ad . Margaret Dylus-Yukins, legal counsel for ethics at the Campaign Legal Center, said in a statement, “Federal law prohibits taxpayer resources from being used for the benefit of a candidate, political party or public official. These ads almost entirely revolve around President Trump, who is not a candidate, but who has told voters to act as if he is on the ballot in November. The latest ad is a complete republication of a 2024 Trump campaign ad, and the earlier ad echoes themes and messages that Republicans are pushing this election; neither has any apparent connection to any federal program or service.” She added, “At a minimum, this is an appalling abuse of taxpayer dollars, particularly when hundreds of millions of private dollars are already flowing into U.S. elections—and Trump has personally helped raise enormous sums from wealthy special interests for a super PAC devoted to advancing his political agenda.” The U.S. Government is up on TV with this spot — It aired nationally on FOX yesterday during Illinois at #7 Ohio State and also during Fox News Sunday this morning pic.twitter.com/8PP9FPzUZk — Medium Buying (@MediumBuying) September 27, 2026 Shawn Levy Moves To Disney’s 20th Television With Overall Deal After Netflix Stint Taylor Swift Debuts New Music Video; Winners List; Red Carpet Photos ‘Endgame’ Reissue Assembles $26M In No. 2 Late-September Frame Ever New Cuts Hit Tech Unit; Analysis Of What’s Going On With Pubcaster’s Funding Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: BBC Tech Teams Hit With Fresh $50M Round Of Cuts, Including 110 Compulsory Layoffs
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Analysis: What The Heck Is Going On With The BBC’s Funding? ‘Harry Potter’ Producer David Barron Backs AI Adaptation Of ‘The Call Of The Wild’ BBC Boss Matt Brittin On Expected Service Closures: “No Program Or Channel Will Exist Forever” View All September 28, 2026 9:48am BBC series 'Strictly Come Dancing' Guy Levy/BBC EXCLUSIVE : The cuts keep coming at the BBC . BBC Media Tech, the division that powers the UK broadcaster’s online services like iPlayer , has today announced a fresh £37 million ($50M) round of savings after delivering £42M of cuts earlier this year. Around 110 staff in the unit will face compulsory redundancy, while 35 vacancies will be closed. The BBC expects to make a further 180 Media Tech layoffs through voluntary redundancy, which includes the 150 Deadline reported on last week . This will not be the last of the cuts, either. Kelly Kowal, the BBC chief operations and portfolio officer, told staff in an email that Media Tech will need to find an additional £23M of savings in early 2027. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News BBC Boss Matt Brittin On Expected Service Closures: "No Program Or Channel Will Exist Forever" News International Insider: Deep BBC Cuts Begin; Ali G Under Fire; San Sebastian Report The BBC Media Tech cuts follow similar savings announcements in BBC Sport and local radio. Deadline also revealed last week that channel closures are imminent , with insiders expecting BBC Three to be moved online for a second time in a decade. BBC Media Tech will contribute £102M of savings to the corporation’s overall target of £500M, which the BBC must deliver because of the growing number of Brits who are refusing to pay for the licence fee. The BBC tech division will embrace AI to reduce costs, according to Kowal. The unit is also expected to focus on fewer products and push more resource into boosting iPlayer. Matt Brittin, the BBC director general, has been candid about the need to improve iPlayer recommendations and user experience. Kowal told employees: “I want to recognise the uncertainty and worry this news will create, particularly those potentially affected by redundancy or worried about their role. There is no easy way to make these choices, but we will be caring, respectful and considered in how we help people work through their options.” Shawn Levy Moves To Disney’s 20th Television With Overall Deal After Netflix Stint Taylor Swift Debuts New Music Video; Winners List; Red Carpet Photos ‘Endgame’ Reissue Assembles $26M In No. 2 Late-September Frame Ever New Cuts Hit Tech Unit; Analysis Of What’s Going On With Pubcaster’s Funding Read More About: 3 Comments

articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt ‘Landman’ Star James Jordan Joins Neon’s ‘They Follow’ Tom Segura Sets Preposterous Stand-Up Tour For 2027 Mind-Reading Comedian Peter Antoniou Sets 2027 Tour View All September 28, 2026 10:12am 'The Crying Boy,' Carter Swan Gilbert Flores/PMC EXCLUSIVE: As Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil prepares to cross $200M at the worldwide box office, the film’s producer Carter Swan has a new project to announce — a film adaptation of the Keenspot comic book series The Crying Boy by Niall O’Rourke & Rob Moran. Published in 2024, The Crying Boy follows a grieving widow trying to rebuild her life in Queens after the violent death of her husband. Things take a turn for the worse when she must save her young son from an even more terrifying fate, when the haunting painting of a crying child that he eerily befriends proves to be the vessel for an ancient demon that has preyed on children for millennia. Related Stories News Kate Micucci Developing Animated Series 'Toy' Based On Keenspot Comic News Zero Gravity Management Signs Keenspot, Comics Creator Behind Hit Jennifer Lopez Pic 'Marry Me' Following a Ringo Award nomination for Best Single Issue or Short Story, The Crying Boy ‘s first issue is currently in its third printing, with a deluxe collection of the series planned for 2027 via Keenspot’s book distribution deal with Simon & Schuster. Rona Mark is scripting the big-screen adaptation. Watch on Deadline The comic’s co-creator O’Rourke said, “Super excited to work with Carter Swan and develop the project. He brings an incredible amount of experience and knowledge to this. We hit it off straight away after he read the script and he was a big fan of the Keenspot comic book series.” A senior producer at PlayStation Productions for nearly eight years — through end of 2025 — Swan worked on Cregger’s Resident Evil during his time there, as well as HBO’s The Last of Us , Uncharted , Gran Turismo , Twisted Metal and Until Dawn . As an executive producer on The Last of Us , he earned Emmy nominations in 2023 and ’25. For a time the world’s largest publisher of webcomics, Keenspot was founded in 2000. The company first broke into film with the Universal rom-com Marry Me — a 2022 adaptation of one of its webcomics starring Jennifer Lopez and Owen Wilson. The company’s first animated adaptation was Grubbs , based on the comics by Max Weaver, whose voice cast included Wil Wheaton, Jerry O’Connell, Jodie Sweetin and more. Presently, Keenspot is also developing the animated adaptations Toy starring Kate Micucci and Kung Fu Legume starring Sherry Cola and Kheng Hua Tan, among other projects. articles.title: Sylvester Stallone Says He Became Bulimic While Filming ‘Rocky’ Movies, Used Steroids
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All September 26, 2026 2:48pm Sylvester Stallone in 'Rocky V.' United Artists/Courtesy Everett Collection Sylvester Stallone is opening up about the extreme lengths he went to achieve his physique for the Rocky franchise. In a Saturday interview with the New York Times promoting his new memoir, The Steps , out Sept. 29, Stallone reflected on how his relationship with his body changed over the course of his career. During the height of the Rocky and Rambo franchises, the actor became known for his exceptionally muscular physique. “It became very intimate, you might say. It was my armor. I looked at Rocky: very smooth, very normal-looking guy. And then I said, I think the character would start to become a bit more vain. And then in Rambo, you’re playing a warrior, so you’d be a little bit more animalistic. You wouldn’t be so smooth,” he said. “I started to think: Design your body like a jaguar, a cat. Not big like Arnold [Schwarzenegger], but more feral and aggressive and very limber and athletic.” Related Stories Business Sylvester Stallone Learned About Trump Hollywood Ambassadorship While Watching TV: "It Won't Work" Movies 'I Play Rocky' Review: Anthony Ippolito Is an Endearing Pre-Stardom Sylvester Stallone in Peter Farrelly's Crowd-Pleasing Making-Of Drama But Stallone said it eventually became an obsession, leading him to develop bulimia while filming Rocky III . “Then it became an obsession. Really bad. It got to the point where I became bulimic. You heard it here first. I got down to 2.6 percent body fat when I was doing Rocky III, and I couldn’t hold anything down. Or I didn’t want to keep it down because I became so obsessed with staying at that point of fitness, literally an obsessive body-worship kind of thing. And nobody does it without additives and drugs, period. I don’t care what they say.” When asked whether he was taking steroids to achieve his physique, Stallone confirmed that he was. “Oh, my God, you have to. But you do it in a sensitive way — six weeks on, six weeks off. People go, ‘Oh, you don’t get that way naturally.’ No, you don’t. But that also took a terrible toll,” he said. Stallone said his relationship with his physique began to shift when he took on a different kind of role in the 1997 film Cop Land . “It wasn’t until I did Cop Land, when I had to play the weakest guy in the room — partially deaf, overweight — that I felt somewhat liberated,” Stallone said. “Then things went sideways and I just fell out of grace with Hollywood. But yeah, I’ve abused my body. I’ve had nine back operations, two shoulder operations, three neck fusions. Everything is held together with baling wire, but I still want to stay in good shape.” Looking back, Stallone said he no longer views his physique as the armor it once was and wishes he had treated his body differently. “If I could do it over again, I would say, ‘Let someone else carry the banner and don’t do your own stunts,'” he said. “I don’t know what it was about hurting myself all the time.” THR

articles.title: Viral Lesbian Bar Article From Boston Globe Is Piquing Hollywood’s Interest
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Aaron Couch Plus Icon Aaron Couch Film Editor View All September 26, 2026 2:54pm The former headquarters of the Boston Globe. Darren McCollester/Getty Images In the early 2000s, The Boston Globe published a series of bombshell articles that exposed the cover-up of abuse within the Catholic Archdiocese of Boston. The series was one of the more consequential pieces of journalism this century, winning a Pulitzer Prize and inspiring Spotlight , the 2015 film that won a best picture Oscar. Now, a very different Boston Globe piece has captured the zeitgeist — and Hollywood’s attention. The article in question is titled “A Western Mass. lesbian bar required KN-95 masks. When it changed the rules, all hell broke loose.” Related Stories Business UTA Signs the Kansas City Chiefs' Foolish Club Studios (Exclusive) Business UTA Boss Sends Companywide Memo Accusing Reporter of Unprofessional Bias The Sept. 22 article by Annalisa Quinn was all over social media feeds this week and quickly became one of the most read stories in Globe history. Now, insiders tell THR that UTA , which represents the Globe , has been fielding inquiries about potential adaptations for the article — both in the scripted space and the documentary sphere. Indeed, the article has several ready-made characters, from a besieged bar owner drowning in debt to former patrons furious that the bar has killed its mask policy — and who go above and beyond to let the owner know what they think. Articles are optioned all the time, of course, but only a select few make it to the screen, such as this weekend’s Robert Pattinson movie Primetime , which was based on a 2007 Esquire article . As sources involved in newspaper packages note, anything that gives your project a competitive edge is needed in this tough media landscape. “Everyone is scared, and nobody wants to make a decision,” notes one observer in this space. A project based on an article like this one? That could at least give a decision-maker the feeling they’ve got a safer bet. As for the Globe , a spokesperson tells THR, “This story has certainly resonated with a wide range of audiences nationally and internationally. It is now one of the most-read stories we’ve published, and has already garnered many thousands of subscriptions.” THR

articles.title: James Gray on Broader Takeaways From Personal Film ‘Paper Tiger’: “What Connects Us Is What Matters”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All September 26, 2026 3:17pm From left: Roman Engel, Miles Teller, James Gray, Scarlett Johansson, Adam Driver and Gavin Goudey ahead of the North American premiere of 'Paper Tiger' at the 2026 NY Film Festival. Michael Loccisano/Getty Images for FLC James Gray ‘s latest film Paper Tiger , like most of his work, draws from his personal and family history to tell a semi-fictionalized story of a Queens family in the 1980s that becomes entangled with the Russian mob, thanks to a moneymaking scheme pitched to patriarch Irwin ( Miles Teller ) by older brother Gary ( Adam Driver ). Coming after semi-autobiographical coming-of-age drama Armageddon Time , the crime thriller, Gray says, is not a sequel and doesn’t hew as closely to his own experience. “This one is much different. I think that one was much more close to the facts of the case,” Gray said after Paper Tiger ‘s North American premiere at the 2026 New York Film Festival of the differences between his latest film and Armageddon Time . “There are many things that my brother, I’m sure, will recognize as from our life, but it’s not a documentary. And I didn’t think it was a sequel. I wanted to make something kind of a little bit … Hitchcockian. … Pulpier is the wrong word, but a little bit more dramatically intense.” Related Stories Movies 'Paper Tiger' Makes Its Case at NYFF Premiere: "A Labor of Love" Movies New York Film Festival Kicks Off With James Gray, Tony Gilroy and Filmmakers Toast in New Lounge In addition to the thrills, Gray told THR before the Paper Tiger premiere that he’s hopeful audiences recognize the power of interpersonal relationships in the domestic drama. “I was trying to make a film in which the personal connection is everything, that love is everything,” Gray said. “Through that of course you want people to feel suspense and intensity and things that we love in a good drama, you hope. But then in the end, dare I use the word catharsis, what connects us is what matters. It’s almost a cautionary tale.” That broader human resonance is also reflected in the guidance Gray gave actor Roman Engel who plays the youngest of Irwin’s two sons, serving as somewhat of a stand-in for the director himself. “He would mostly just try to tell me to be myself on set and don’t try to live someone else’s experience, try to live your own and do the actions you would do while whatever’s happening to you,” Engel told THR of Gray’s direction. The film ends as Gary, Irwin and wife Hester (Scarlett Johansson) are each dealing with their own personal issues and before they learn of each other’s fates, but Gray hopes that that lack of resolution allows the story to continue on beyond the bounds of the film. “I love the idea that the life of the movie goes on past the movie,” he said in a post-screening Q&A at the NY Film Festival Friday night . “I love the open ending. I love the idea that the film exists past the boundaries of the screen and the time. … With all of the characters, I wanted to make sure that there was a completion to their openness in a way, how open their characters were, and that nobody has the whole picture, because that’s like life, and it’s very untraditional actually for movies. Usually, in a movie somebody has the whole story.” Neon is set to release Paper Tiger in select U.S. theaters on Nov. 13, with a wider release on Nov. 20. THR

articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Review: Monster Movie Genius Takashi Yamazaki Returns With a Crackling Kaiju Epic Every Bit as Exciting as Its Predecessor
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By David Rooney Plus Icon David Rooney Chief Film Critic DavidCRooney1 Follow Sign Up View All September 26, 2026 5:30pm 'Godzilla Minus Zero' Courtesy Everett Collection Writer, director and VFX wizard Takashi Yamazaki three years ago reinvigorated Japanese production titan Toho ’s seven-decade kaiju franchise with Godzilla Minus One , which delivered amply on monster mayhem with sophisticated (and Oscar-winning) effects, but perhaps more importantly, grounded the creature feature in affecting humanistic drama. By dividing the film’s attention between mass destruction and the raw pain of post-WWII trauma, reconstruction and societal reintegration — not to mention the atomic allegory — Yamazaki boldly reimagined the property while honoring the roots of the series’ 1954 original. Related Stories Movies James Gray on Broader Takeaways From Personal Film 'Paper Tiger': "What Connects Us Is What Matters" Movies 'Paper Tiger' Makes Its Case at NYFF Premiere: "A Labor of Love" That same meticulously balanced duality is evident in the director’s approach to the scaled-up sequel, Godzilla Minus Zero , an equally thrilling jolt of marauding monster action anchored by tender themes of family, friendship, camaraderie and personal courage. These are characters about whom we come to care deeply, and Yamazaki trusts his audience to know the value of time spent observing human relationships, ennobling the horror with tangible emotional stakes. Following its world premiere at the New York Film Festival , GKIDS will release the film in the U.S. Nov. 6. Godzilla Minus Zero The Bottom Line A radioactive blast. Venue : New York Film Festival (Spotlight Gala) Release date : Friday, Nov. 6 Cast : Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Yuki Yamada, Kuranosuke Saski, Jun Kunimura, Mio Tanaka, Sakura Ando, Masami Nagasawa, Min Tanaka, Hidetaka Yoshioka Director-screenwriter : Takashi Yamazaki Rated R, 2 hours 15 minutes While the 1949 setting might be expected to make the aftermath of war recede into the past, it’s no less acutely felt here, with resonant moments touching on the complicated perceptions of the Japanese people toward America and the outsize impact on the rest of the world of its military industrial complex. World War II may be over, but its vicious cycle of loss, destruction and power-flexing continues. At the risk of angering the spoiler police — a cue to stop reading now if you’d rather go in blind — the new film ushers in another legendary kaiju first seen in 1964. Promotional materials for the most part refer evasively to “a new threat,” but fan anticipation and advance media have pretty much let the badass three-headed dragon out of the bag. Just as Japanese life appears to be returning to some kind of peacetime normalcy, with Godzilla exiled to the ocean depths and believed to have been killed in the previous movie, King Ghidorah comes swooping in with massive wings generating hurricane-force winds, ripping apart an entire town in the opening action. There’s a ton of sci-fi mythology in the Godzilla series concerning the origins of Ghidorah the Explorer, a creature at various times under the control of alien invaders and time-traveling human terrorists, which supposedly arrived on Earth inside a meteorite intent on detroying the planet, much as it had destroyed Venus thousands of years earlier. Yamazaki wisely ignores all that geek lore, instead treating the dragon as simply another killer Monsterverse freak with regenerative powers, inevitably destined to fight a death match with Godzilla for alpha status. Just as Godzilla can charge up his radioactive dorsal plates and shoot nuclear-level heat rays at his targets, Ghidorah has his own neat trick and three gaping fanged mouths with which to deploy it. The creature design is magnificent, with the huge wingspan and writhing tangle of elongated necks and tails cranking up the menace, while the ferociousness of the monster’s faces is enhanced to great effect by growling and roaring that can sound almost like an evil cackle. The mega-dragon spews out electromagnetic energy in the form of gravity beams; some of the most outstanding sequences involve those lightning-like bolts wrapping antigravitational forcefields around buildings, trains and anything else in Ghidorah’s path, sucked up into the air and then smashed to the ground for maximum wreckage. The heart of the previous film was former WWII kamikaze pilot Koichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki) — stunned by the loss of his parents and crushed by guilt over his conduct in the dying days of the war — daring to dream of a life of domestic contentment only to see that dream repeatedly put in jeopardy. More or less given no choice, Koichi welcomed a young woman, Noriko (Minami Hamabe), into his home in the rubble of Tokyo, along with Akiko (adorable Sae Nagatani), the orphaned child she had found alone and terrified. Two years on, this found family are inextricably bound together, with flinty neighbor Sumiko (Sakura Ando, so memorable in Hirokazu Koreeda’s transcendent Shoplifters ), who also lost her family during the war, serving as “Auntie,” to lend a hand with Akiko. Once Ghidorah’s rampage spreads fresh terror, Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka), the former naval weapons engineer now heading up the government’s Disaster Countermeasures Bureau, begins working on defense plans. He signs up his old comrades from the previous film along with a couple of new ones, meteorological forecaster Aoyama (Masami Nagasawa) and Professor Murakami (Min Tanaka), who lost his family in Hiroshima and may have a hidden agenda. Veteran Jun Kunimura (much better served here than in the Takashi Miike dud Bad Lieutenant: Tokyo ) also turns up as a doctor studying the effects of exposure to Godzilla’s cellular tissue on people involved in the attacks of Minus One . This phenomenon impacts Noriko, who miraculously survived the devastating Ginza attack last time around and has shown remarkable resilience, with her wounds healing at an uncanny rate. Yamazaki infuses tenderness into not just the core family but also the extended group, bound by profound fondness as much as by horrific shared experience. With Ghidorah dictating that the fight will now be airborne, Koichi is eager to get back in the pilot’s seat, compelled by a sense of duty to his country but also by lingering survivor’s guilt. Nodo wrestles with his own guilt over the countless deaths caused during the war by weapons he designed; he will not hear of Koichi putting his life at risk again and possibly robbing Akiko of a father. Nodo agrees only to bring the pilot on as an advisor, but Koichi is not easily deterred. The same goes for Noriko, whose medical condition may have the potential to be weaponized. Nodo and his crew set up a command center in Matsumoto City, where Aoyama determines that they can track Ghidorah as the creature responds to the electromagnetic force of a fast-moving storm system. Around this point Godzilla — fully regenerated and pissed as hell — resurfaces offshore. Given that heavy artillery and bombs have failed to slow down Ghidorah for long, Murakami calls Godzilla’s reappearance “divine providence,” insisting that setting the two monsters against each other is their only hope. Via some ingenious plotting, that entails a plan to lure the beasts into proximity, using a system tested by the professor in a cheeky homage to Hitchcock’s The Birds . The resulting clash of the legendary kaiju is a rip-roaring smackdown in a movie that keeps awing the audience with exhilarating action and then continually one-upping itself in the dustups that follow. I’m fairly sure I stopped breathing during a tense scene in which Godzilla bears down on a seaplane attempting a hurried liftoff. While Spider-Man: Brand New Day generated plenty of sparks and Dune 3 and Avengers: Doomsday are still to come, it’s interesting that some of the most pulse-pounding, intense and inventive action sequences on screens this year have been in two East Asian films — Godzilla Minus Zero and Hope . Stand down, Hollywood. As he demonstrated in Minus One , Yamazaki’s command of big-ass destruction spectacle is breathtaking, this time overseeing a significantly larger VFX team that makes the monsters not only mighty physical presences but also part of an immersive environment in which we experience the full force of their earth-shaking power. This is some of the most impressively seamless integration of major-scale CGI in recent memory. But the masterstroke of Yamazaki’s direction is the skill with which he ensures that the human drama remains no less compelling than the monster faceoffs. The film also benefits from initially making Godzilla the underdog in the fight, bringing back the creature’s representation in Japanese culture of nuclear trauma, natural disasters and the pervasively heavy anxiety that gripped the nation in the postwar years. Watching the Minus movies, you realize how much the lack of that cultural specificity limits the American Godzilla entries and how much these latest two Japanese films serve as a reclamation. While the action in those U.S. productions, notably Godzilla vs. Kong , can pack a visceral charge, the human element generally is forgettable and the mythology sketchy. But the characters here are richly developed, especially Koichi and Noriko, played with a mix of determination and vulnerability by Kamiki and Hamabe that fosters genuine emotional investment in them as both individuals and as a makeshift family; and the wonderful Yoshiyoka’s avuncular Noda, who has some of the film’s most affecting moments. As she was in the previous film, Ando’s hard-edged but soft-hearted Sumiko is a droll scene-stealer, and Nagasawa’s Aoyama is a terrific addition — it’s great to see a woman with authority and sharp intuition on the science team, even if she’s not immune to self-doubt. The first Japanese feature shot in IMAX, the movie looks stunning, with so much detail and nimble movement packed into returning DP Kozo Shibasaki’s frames. Period production design by Anri Jojo and Wataru Hirai is understated but evocative. And the score by another repeat collaborator, Naoki Sato, is a marvel, ranging from brooding apprehension, with solemn choral elements, to thunderous symphonic bursts for the big clashes. With the plot door open to another sequel, here’s hoping Yamazaki will keep on making new entries in this hugely entertaining series. And while we’re raiding the Toho kaiju vaults, bring back Mothra! Full credits Venue: New York Film Festival (Spotlight Gala) Release date: Friday, Nov. 6 Production companies: Toho Studios, Robot Communications Distribution: GKIDS Cast: Ryunosuke Kamiki, Minami Hamabe, Yuki Yamada, Kuranosuke Saski, Jun Kunimura, Mio Tanaka, Sakura Ando, Masami Nagasawa, Min Tanaka, Hidetaka Yoshioka, Munetaka Aoki, Eita Okuno, Miou Tanaka, Sae Nagatani Director-screenwriter: Takashi Yamazaki Producers: Minami Ichikawa, Taichi Ueda, Kazuaki Kishida Executive producer: Hisashi Usui Director of photography: Kozo Shibasaki Production designers: Anri Jojo, Wataru Hirai Costume designer: Aiko Mizushima Music: Naoki Sato Editor: Ryuji Miyajima Sound: Hisafumi Takeuchi Visual effects: Takashi Yamazaki Visual effects supervisors: Takayuki Ueki, Elsin Okubo, Kiyoko Shibuya Casting: Toshie Tabata Rated R, 2 hours 15 minutes THR

articles.title: ‘Star Wars’: Jon Watts to Direct Next Movie for Lucasfilm
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit Plus Icon Borys Kit Senior Film Writer View All September 26, 2026 5:37pm Star Wars Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures/Photofest Logo text Even as Lucasfilm is deep in post-production on its next Star Wars movie, Star Wars: Starfighter , the next phase of a potential new Skywalker Saga is coming into focus. Jon Watts , the director behind a trio of Tom Holland Spider-Man movies, is now attached to direct the first installment of the Simon Kinberg -penned trilogy. It is a return to the franchise for Watts, who previously co-created Star Wars series Skeleton Crew in 2024. Kinberg has been working on writing a mystery trilogy since late 2024. The project is intended to act as the next chapter in what is referred to as the Skywalker Saga, the stories featuring the multi-generations of the Luke Skywalker family. The previous movies have been Episodes I through IX . The next one would be Episode X . Rey Skywalker, the Jedi played by Daisy Ridley in last trilogy released from 2015 and 2019, would appear in some capacity in the new trilogy. Related Stories Business Disney Seeking "Director of AI Enablement" After Warning of Layoffs Amid Companywide AI Push Movies Dolly Parton's '9 to 5' Comedy Returning to Theaters to Support Late Icon's Foundation Lucasfilm had no comment. Sources say the project is still in development and has not yet been greenlit by parent company Disney , although it seems to be project the furthest along the development track after Starfighter . Starfighter is being directed by Shawn Levy and stars Ryan Gosling. The movie is expected to hit theatres May 27, 2027, coinciding with the 50th anniversary of Star Wars . Watts is seen as a reliable choice for the franchise, which has occasionally, and would say famously, struggled with directors. After directing the indie thriller Cop Car , Watts was chosen by Marvel to helm the relaunch of the Spider-Man movies. The Tom Holland-starring movies, which included 2017’s Homecoming , 2019’s Far From Home , and 2021’s No Way Home , became progressively bigger productions and bigger hits at the box office. Watts proved he could navigate the complexities of massive big-budget productions. His post- Spider-Man work included the George Clooney-Brad Pitt-starring Wolfs , the high-profile misfire from Apple that upended its theatrical release and curiously announced a sequel that was never going to be made. Watts co-created and co-wrote Skeleton Crew , the well-regarded but unfortunately not greatly seen series that starred Jude Law and brought an Amblin vibe to the Star Wars universe. Watts directed two episodes of the show, which also had a starry assemblage of helmers that included David Lowery, Lee Isaac Chung, Jake Schreier, Bryce Dallas Howard, and the Daniels. Knight Edge Media broke the news of Watts’ involvement. THR

articles.title: Jalen Brunson Brings the New York Knicks to the ‘Saturday Night Live’ Season 52 Premiere
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All September 26, 2026 8:49pm Jalen Brunson hosts the 'SNL' season 52 premiere. Courtesy of SNL. Logo text Saturday Night Live kicked off its 52nd season with NBA Finals MVP Jalen Brunson as its first host, and he had his starting lineup there to support him. Brunson began his monologue by joking that his time winning the 2026 NBA championship this year with the New York Knicks may mirror his hosting stint. “Tonight I’m gonna approach hosting in the same way I approach the Knicks finals game; so the first three quarters of the show are gonna be god awful. The last sketch is gonna be amazing,” he said. “This summer, I helped the Knicks win the NBA championship. By now, you’ve all heard me talk about it, but you haven’t heard me sing about it… And obviously I’m not going to.” Related Stories TV Jalen Brunson and KATSEYE Kick Off 'SNL' Season 52: Where to Watch the Premiere Online TV 'SNL' Promotes Keri Powers to Sole Head of Talent Department, Rebecca Schwartz Upped to Producer He also joked about being back in Madison Square Garden for the NBA season that’s about to start, where Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce got married this summer. “The new season is just a couple of weeks away, and I gotta say, it’s gonna be pretty cool to be back at Madison Square Garden. Looking around like, wow, just a few months ago, this was the exact spot where Taylor and Travis got married,” he said. Brunson The New York Knicks won the NBA championship in June, marking their first win since 1973. Brunson was awarded with the title of NBA Finals MVP after the dynamic season. To support his debut as an SNL host, the Knicks starting five, Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges, were all in attendance. Brunson said he was going to take questions from the audience, to which the camera panned over to make way for his teammates. Towns kicked off a round of questions, asking, “Can you foul out of SNL ?” Brunson responded, “No, I don’t think so.” “I could be here, like, the whole show?” Towns added. Hart candidly asked the SNL host, “Is it true that you took a $113 million pay cut just to resign with the Knicks?” Brunson said, “Yeah, that’s pretty true.” Hart asked an additional follow-up question: “Wow. So is that money, like, still up for grabs?” Jalen Brunson's monologue! pic.twitter.com/FnPKYkGcu7 — Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) September 27, 2026 The first cold open of the new season poked fun at New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and President Donald Trump’s bromance. Ramy Youssef portrayed Mamdani, while James Austin Johnson returned to dish out his impersonation of Trump. Mamdani was told he had a guest, to which he responded, “What reckless lunatic would travel to see me in this kind of weather?” “Your best friend!” Johnson’s Trump said. “I missed my day one. For some reason that no one can figure out, I really, really like you.” Youssef pointed out the El Niño impacting New York City, telling the faux president, “That’s very kind, but wouldn’t you rather be in D.C.? We’re in the middle of El Niño.” “Oh, El Niño, we don’t like big stores, especially when they’re in Spanish,” Trump said. He went on to talk about his “crazy week”: “I kicked out the press and hung out with the president of China, Xi. And yeah, I went brunette. It’s fall!” “There was this crazy AI stuff, too,” he continued. “I just had dinner with Sam Altman, Elon Musk, and Mark Zuckerberg, and it made me think, wow, RFK Jr.’s probably right about those vaccines.” Ashley Padilla also popped up briefly in the cold open as Natalie Harp, executive assistant to President Trump. Towards the end of the cold open, Youssef’s Mamdani kept on insisting that he needed to get back to work. “Please let me stay here with you,” Johnson’s Trump said. “OK, only if you give us $21 billion for a housing project in Queens,” Mamdani said. “Are you out of your mind?” Trump said, to which Mamdani offered, “What if I follow you back on Instagram?” “It’s a done deal,” Johnson’s Trump concluded. Trump pays Mamdani a visit at Gracie Mansion during the nor’easter pic.twitter.com/gsTsGmoWoN — Saturday Night Live (@nbcsnl) September 27, 2026 Jeremy Culhane reprised his Tucker Carlson impersonation during the Weekend Update segment, where he gave his opinions on this summer’s box office hits. Of Obsession , he joked, “The left’s idea of a horror movie; that a woman is forced to love a man. ‘Oh, no, help! I’m being chased by a heterosexual relationship!'” As for Spider-Man: Brand New Day , Culhane’s Carlson said, “Everybody loves Spider-Man: Brand New Gender.” Colin Jost said, “That’s not what it’s called,” as Culhane’s Carlson continued, “Spider-They, Spider-Them, uses whatever bathroom it feels like.” He also brought up Minions & Monsters , asserting that he was “not talking about the children’s film, I’m talking about the Trump cabinet. That’s right, I’ve turned on Trump, I’m so brave.” The New York Knicks star and Katseye were the first host and musical guest pair of the new season, also notably making their SNL debuts. Next week, Dakota Johnson will host with Turnstile as the musical act. Shane Gillis will host on Oct. 10 with musical guest Rosalia, while Obsession star Inde Navarrette makes her SNL hosting debut on the Halloween episode. She’ll be joined by Gracie Abrams. THR

articles.title: Hints of ‘Sex and the City’ and ‘Narcos’: A Look at Literary Works Being Pitched for Screen Adaptations at Iberseries & Platino Industria
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All September 27, 2026 1:00am The 16 titles featured in the inaugural Literary Works Pitch for Audiovisual Adaptation at Iberseries & Platino Industria Courtesy of Iberseries & Platino Industria If you need any proof of the potential for literary works from the Spanish-speaking world to be adapted for the screen, you need to look no further than YA bestseller author Mercedes Ron’s success with Prime Video and Banijay’s Pokeepsie Films production banner with the likes of the Fault trilogy and the recently launched Drawn Together . Literary Works Pitch for Audiovisual Adaptation, a new initiative developed by Iberseries & Platino Industria in collaboration with the Federation of Publishers Guilds of Spain (FGEE) and featured at this year’s sixth edition in Madrid running Sept. 29-Oct. 2, looks to connect publishers and literary agencies with production companies, streamers, studios and TV networks to feed their search for new intellectual properties. Related Stories Movies Mike Leigh's 'Tender Loving Care' Sweeps San Sebastian Awards as 'La Bola Negra,' 'NAZA' Earn Audience Nods Movies Zurich Summit Game Changer Glen Basner and Edward Berger Reminisce on a Wild 'Conclave' Ride Following a call for submissions, organizers selected 14 works from Spain and Mexico and one each from Germany and Argentina. The stories come from different genres, times and settings. Here is a look at the projects being pitched at Madrid: Alguien como tú by Xavier Bosch Agencia Literaria Antonia Kerrigan, Spain The Catalan author’s novel centers on an intense, cross-border affair between a married woman from Barcelona and an art gallery owner from Paris, with the woman’s daughter later trying to piece together details of the clandestine romance. Alka I. La mujer del infinito by Yaiza Nicolás Yaiza Nicolás, Spain The thriller-like adventure spanning three generations of women journeying through time revolves around a substance that prolongs youth and extends the boundaries of life. Así en la tierra como debajo de la tierra by Ana Paula Maia Scenic Rights, Spain A penal colony in a remote spot in Brazil is in its waning days, and its warden unleashes a horror scenario: every full moon, a selection of inmates is released, only to be hunted down with weapons. Cuando te atrevas a sentir by Tamara Molina Agencia Literaria Antonia Kerrigan, Spain Naila feels like a failure and has no clear goal in life. Bruno always succeeds and has a well-paying job that does not make him happy, but fears that quitting would make him a loser. But these two very different people may find comfort in each other. Cuando vi a la muerte prestar su sombrero by Rodrigo Unda Penguin Random House Grupo Editorial, Mexico This fantasy novel follows The Fates, living in the shadows with one job: guiding human souls to the afterlife. But one day, one of them suffers an injury, and she begins to experience human feelings. El sueño de las Mariposas by Cristina Atienza Cristina Atienza, Spain Mystery, history and memory collide by the sea in this novel about sisterhood. A woman’s interest in astrophysics and her defiance land her in confinement, with forced prayers and punishments. Las esposas del régimen by Miguel Ángel San Juan Alt Autores, Spain A modern mystery intersects with a historical look at women resisting General Franco’s patriarchal dictatorship in this novel, which pays tribute to silenced generations and warns against the return of oppressive ideologies. Masacre en el comedor by Ceferino Reato Penguin Random House Grupo Editorial, Mexico The journalist and political scientist investigates the deadliest guerrilla attack in 1970s Argentina, a Montoneros guerrilla group bombing at a Federal Police building during the country’s military dictatorship. Mentira by Care Santos Scenic Rights, Spain Xenia has had a reputation for getting the best grades and dreams of studying medicine. But then her academic performance suffers when she falls in love online. But who is the mysterious person she falls for, and are they real? Mi vida con él by Hilda Gadea Silvina Estévez, Argentina A film based on the memoirs of Hilda Gadea, the economist, intellectual, and activist who was Ernesto “Che” Guevara’s first wife, is already in the works. Nocturnos by Laura Pérez Alt Autores, Spain The writer and artist’s graphic novel uses a series of dreamlike vignettes to explore the mysterious and magical world of the night. You may not be aware yet, but you may well know Pérez’s work – she was nominated for an Emmy Award for her work on the opening title design for Only Murders in the Building . Too Match by Inma Benedito Agencia Literaria Dos Passos, Spain If you are looking for a contemporary story that has been described as a Madrid-style queer Sex and the City with less glamour, this one may be for you! This diary of failed dates is an ode to heartbreak. Una belleza terrible by José Ovejero Galaxia Gutenberg, Spain This biographical novel dives into the life and times of Leon Trotsky confidant Raymond Molinier (1904–1994), a chameleon-like figure who dedicated his life to revolutionary ideals and the workers’ struggle. Una casa llena de gente by Mariana Sández MertinWitt Literary Agency, Germany The debut novel explores family grief and trauma, generational friction, and memory through a narrative puzzle emerging from diaries and testimonies. Una Madre by Alejandro Palomas Scenic Rights, Spain Set on New Year’s Eve in a Barcelona apartment, the story sees Amalia, 65, fulfill her dream of gathering her whole family for a holiday dinner. It is a night of family and laughter, but also, through flashbacks, old secrets and hidden tensions. Vida y muerte del cartel de Medellín by Carlos Lehder Penguin Random House Grupo Editorial, Mexico If you loved Narcos , you may want to take a look at this one! After all, it is the memoir of a co-founder of the Medellín drug cartel in Colombia, detailing the criminal empire’s rise and fall. THR

articles.title: John Turturro on Joining the Oscar Race — and ‘Severance’ Season 3
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All September 27, 2026 3:39am John Turturro at the 22nd Zurich Film Festival Courtesy of Getty Hot on the heels of his Golden Eye award ceremony on Saturday night, John Turturro entertained another crowd at a Zurich Film Festival masterclass on Sunday. The Emmy-winning U.S. star has been recognized for his performance in Noah Segan’s The Only Living Pickpocket in New York , a project that is already garnering awards buzz . In the film, Turturro plays Harry, a seasoned pickpocket whose carefully controlled life is thrown into turmoil when a job goes wrong, setting off a tense chain of events that unfolds over the course of 36 hours. Related Stories TV Hints of 'Sex and the City' and 'Narcos': A Look at Literary Works Being Pitched for Screen Adaptations at Iberseries & Platino Industria Movies Mike Leigh's 'Tender Loving Care' Sweeps San Sebastian Awards as 'La Bola Negra,' 'NAZA' Earn Audience Nods In a career-spanning conversation with Deadline ‘s Melanie Goodfellow — the actor’s shining Golden Eye trophy neatly nestled between them — Turturro discussed growing up in an immigrant household, his decades-long friendship with Spike Lee, and the transition from acting to filmmaking. Turturro, who has steadily become one of the industry’s most formidable actors yet to put “Oscar nominee” on his resume, was asked about joining the best actor race this year with the Sundance success The Only Living Pickpocket in New York . “I never really have gone the whole hog with it,” he responded about the upcoming awards campaign. “But now I’m the lead in the film, so I’m going to support the film because I love the film.” He explained that being pulled into awards conversations is “helpful to help you do the next thing.” Turturro continued: “Is it nice to be acknowledged? Great, but that’s not why you do it. […] Just because a film is really popular doesn’t mean it will have staying power, but it’s nice to be in the conversation. I don’t look upon myself as being a competitive person. I’m competitive with myself,” he added. “I want to get the most out of what I can do, but it’s not sports!” However, he admitted to feeling surprised by the positive critic reaction out of Sundance. “Finally,” he thought, “I’m in something that people will see… My job is I like to try to improve, and I feel like being an actor is one of the few things you can improve in. You may not be able to run as fast as you did when you were younger, but I have a lot of life experience, and as you get older, you accumulate that, and you can distill things in a way that you couldn’t do when you were young, because you didn’t really experience all those things. And now I’ve experienced life, death, loss, being a parent, being married — what it is to really love someone versus falling in love. That’s a huge difference,” he giggled. Turturro regaled attendees with stories about his impressive stage career. He naturally came on to two major TV performances of his in the last decade: HBO’s The Night Of and Apple’s Severance . He coyly confirmed a return for his character, Irving Bailiff, in season three of the Emmy-winning Severance with Adam Scott. “Yeah,” he (eventually) told the room. “As long as they give me interesting things to do, then I’m interested.” He swiftly took the opportunity to gush over friend and colleague Christopher Walken, whose character, Burt Goodman, began a romance with Turturro’s Irving in season one. “‘Who’s going to be my love interest?'” Turturro asked before joining the show. “And they were like, ‘All these younger guys.’ I said, ‘Well no, I’ve worked with Chris Walken,’ and I said, ‘I want Chris, because I love Chris.’ And I don’t have to act that I love him because I love him.” Though Walken “didn’t understand a lot of the show,” Turturro was able to guide him through their authentic, real-life friendship. “I said, ‘Don’t worry about it. You just look at me.’ We have so much fun because I directed him like three times, and we’ve acted, and we’ve worked together a lot. And he’s a wonderful theater actor, and people obviously think he plays only strange [characters] but he can do a lot of different things. He’s also very sensitive, but he has a childlike joy in his work, and when that happens, anything is possible.” Turturro received a round of applause when discussing the HBO crime drama The Night Of , which ran for one season in 2016 and co-starred Riz Ahmed. It would later win five Emmys, and Turturro was nominated for his role as the eczema-stricken defense lawyer John Stone. “ The Night Of is something I’m very proud of,” said Turturro on Sunday. “It was originally a BBC thing, which I actually never watched because I didn’t want to be influenced.” He even confirmed that he actually wanted to do another season of it. “But they couldn’t agree on what the story would be,” revealed the actor. “But I loved doing it. It was one of those great experiences in my life.” Turturro’s career spans four decades, having worked with acclaimed directors such as Spike Lee, the Coen brothers, Martin Scorsese, Robert Redford, Robert De Niro, Nanni Moretti and Pedro Almodóvar. He first gained international recognition through his collaborations with Lee, appearing in Do the Right Thing and Jungle Fever . With Joel and Ethan Coen, he acted in Miller’s Crossing , Barton Fink , O Brother, Where Art Thou? and The Big Lebowksi , in which Turturro created the iconic Jesus Quintana. For his lead performance in Barton Fink , he won best actor at the 1991 Cannes Film Festival, an experience that Turturro reflected on at his Zurich masterclass. He even confessed to feeling like he lands “more normal” roles in Europe than across the Atlantic, and said he has turned down scripts “again and again” that involve his character being violent towards women. At his Zurich Golden Eye ceremony Saturday night, Turturro collected the award and quoted Italian novelist Cesare Pavese. “[He] once said that the only great thing in life is to begin. I still consider myself a beginner in many ways,” said the star. “I’m very fortunate. I wanted to make a living doing something that interested me and to do interesting work — to share that with an audience, [and that] wouldn’t diminish their intelligence at the same time,” he laughed. “I consider this an encouragement to continue.” Turturro joins 2026 Zurich honorees Julianne Moore and Tom Hiddleston . The 22nd edition runs Sept. 24-Oct. 4. THR
