articles.title: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Director Champions Franchise’s First R Rating as Sequel Rocks NYFF at World Premiere: ‘Censoring’ the Action ‘Was Not an Option’
articles.full_text: Sep 26, 2026 6:08pm PT ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Director Champions Franchise’s First R Rating as Sequel Rocks NYFF at World Premiere: ‘Censoring’ the Action ‘Was Not an Option’ By Antonio Ferme , Zack Sharf Getty Images for FLC “ Godzilla Minus Zero” blew the roof off Alice Tully Hall during its rapturous world premiere screening at the New York Film Festival . The long-awaited sequel to 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” earned rave first reactions from the press earlier in the day, and that adoration rolled right into the world premiere. The movie was met with multiple mid-screening applauses as the crowd went wild for all the kaiju mayhem on screen. Ahead of its debut later this year, “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” has been rated R for “violent content/bloody images,” making it the first entry in the 72-year-old franchise to receive an R-rating. Director Takashi Yamazaki , returning to helm the sequel after 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One” became a roaring success, says securing the rating was “essential to the film.” “Logically, as a studio — and even as a director — you want as many people from the general public to be able to see your film,” Yamazaki told Variety at the premiere Saturday afternoon. “So, an R-rating might seem like a barrier to entry, and conversations about, ‘Hey, could we have not gotten this down to PG-13?’ of course are going to happen. In spite of that, though, there were certain scenes that, for me as a director, were so essential to the film. Censoring it or cutting it was just not an option for me.” Related Stories Taiwan Creative Content Fest Adds Spotlight Screenings to Court International Buyers Under MPA guidelines, viewers under 17 cannot attend an R-rated film without a parent or guardian, a restriction that has traditionally made the rating a commercial deterrent for studios releasing big-budget, four-quadrant films. That stigma has faded over the past decade, starting with the blockbuster success of 2016’s “Deadpool” ($782 million). In 2019, “Joker” ($1.07 billion) became the first R-rated film to cross the $1 billion threshold. That record was later broken by 2024’s “Deadpool & Wolverine” ($1.33 billion) — and more recently — 2026’s “The Odyssey” ($1.72 billion), which currently stands as the 17th highest-grossing film of all time worldwide. Popular on Variety “I think the R-rating, at one point, carried almost a negative connotation,” Yamazaki explained. “In more modern films, it actually creates a sort of expectation and excitement of, ‘Okay, well, they’re not censoring anything. The director and the cast’s voice is there, as is.’ So it is very encouraging to see other films who have preceded us that have already found a lot of success with the R-rating at the box office. Hopefully, we can continue that trend with ‘Godzilla Minus Zero.’” Inside the world premiere screening, New York Film Festival director Dennis Lim acknowledged that the Godzilla franchise might not be the first thing people think of playing at a major film festival. And yet, “We thought it was about time to bring a giant monster movie here.” Yamazaki took the stage to thunderous applause from the audience both before and after the screening, where he asked the crowd not to spoil any of the sequel’s many surprises on social media. “You are the first to see this film,” the filmmaker said. “There are a lot of ‘Godzilla’ fans around the world, so let’s work together and do not do any spoilers. No spoilers, please! I am trusting all of you guys.” Yamazaki also had the audience laughing while explaining how he never intended to create a sequel to “Godzilla Minus One.” Executives at Toho immediately started asking him about a follow-up movie once they saw the first cut of “Minus One,” a thought that made Yamazaki instantly nervous. It wasn’t until the movie opened in theaters and started to be celebrated around the world by audiences that the director realized a sequel would be a viable option. “Toho executives are here,” the director said. “With your reactions tonight I hope they don’t offer a third movie.” Sacha Baron Cohen to Star in Quentin Tarantino’s First Stage Play ‘The Popinjay Cavalier’ Squishmallows Movie in the Works at Amazon MGM (EXCLUSIVE) Ali G Movie Backlash Intensifies in the U.K. as Campaigners Try to Get Film Pulled From Cinemas Amazon Moves to Toss ‘Criminal’ Production Assistant’s Harassment Suit ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Trailer: Sacha Baron Cohen Returns as the London Bad Boy in New Amazon MGM Mockumentary Loading comments...

articles.full_text: Sep 26, 2026 8:58pm PT Jalen Brunson’s ‘SNL’ Monologue Sees Knicks Starting 5 Roasting Each Other By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest Tucker Carlson Returns to ‘SNL’ to Review ‘The Odyssey,’ Gender-Neutral ‘Spider-Man’ and Left-Wing ‘Obsession’ 10 hours ago Jalen Brunson’s ‘SNL’ Monologue Sees Knicks Starting 5 Roasting Each Other 11 hours ago Tamera Mowry-Housley Joins ‘Scrubs’ Reboot Season 2 3 days ago See All NBC Jalen Brunson ‘s “ Saturday Night Live ” monologue featured some familiar faces, as the remaining members of the Knicks starting five visited Studio 8H to roast their team captain. But before Karl-Anthony Towns, Josh Hart, Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby appeared on screen, Kenan Thompson took the stage as ESPN pundit Stephen A. Smith. “Let me say this, Jalen Brunson. I am man enough to admit that I was wrong,” Thompson-as-Smith said. “When the New York Knickerbockers signed you and I did not think that you were the answer, nor did I believe that you could deliver the team’s first championship since 1973, when I was only 5 years old.” Related Stories Taiwan Creative Content Fest Adds Spotlight Screenings to Court International Buyers After Brunson interrupted: “How long’s this going to go?” Smith replied: “About another seven minutes.” Brunson booted his “detractor” off the stage and took questions from the audience, which just so happened to include his teammates. Popular on Variety “I have a question. Can you foul out of ‘SNL’?” Towns asked, referencing his dismissal from Game 5 against the Spurs. “I could be here, like, the whole show?” After Bridges and Anunoby gave Brunson a hard time, Hart asked, “Is it true that you took a $113 million pay cut just to resign with the Knicks?” Brunson said, “Yeah, that’s pretty true,” Hart responded, “Wow, so is that money, like, still up for grabs?” The NBA stars ribbed each other a bit more, and then Brunson welcomed his teammates onstage. articles.full_text: Sep 26, 2026 8:59pm PT ‘SNL’ Opens Season With Mamdani Hanging Out With BFF Trump, Natalie Harp Going ‘Obsession’ Over President By William Earl Plus Icon William Earl @beautifulbill Latest ‘SNL’ Opens Season With Mamdani Hanging Out With BFF Trump, Natalie Harp Going ‘Obsession’ Over President 11 hours ago Inside Ryan Murphy’s Universe: How Director Max Winkler Found Creative Meaning in ‘Lizzie Borden,’ ‘Love Story’ and More 2 days ago How ‘Never After Dark’ Dodges Horror Clichés: Shoot Well-Lit Scenes, Challenge Conventional Storytelling and ‘Pull the Rug Out From Under People’ 2 days ago See All Courtesy of NBC Season 52 of “ Saturday Night Live ” kicked off with its usual cold open, and it involved two unlikely political BFFs. Ramy Youssef stopped by to play New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, whose office was visited by James Austin Johnson’s Donald Trump . “For some reason that no one can figure out, I really, really like you,” Trump said to Mamdani. We’re like one of those unlikely animal friendships, like when a tiger gets together with a baby goat. Anyway …” Popular on Variety The pair discussed the storm currently slamming the East Coast, the Knicks’ championship, this week’s U.N. meeting in NYC, Trump’s recent hosting of China President Xi Jinping, as well as his state dinner with Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Mark Zuckerberg. articles.title: Tucker Carlson Returns to ‘SNL’ to Review ‘The Odyssey,’ Gender-Neutral ‘Spider-Man’ and Left-Wing ‘Obsession’
articles.full_text: Sep 26, 2026 9:58pm PT Tucker Carlson Returns to ‘SNL’ to Review ‘The Odyssey,’ Gender-Neutral ‘Spider-Man’ and Left-Wing ‘Obsession’ By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest Tucker Carlson Returns to ‘SNL’ to Review ‘The Odyssey,’ Gender-Neutral ‘Spider-Man’ and Left-Wing ‘Obsession’ 10 hours ago Jalen Brunson’s ‘SNL’ Monologue Sees Knicks Starting 5 Roasting Each Other 11 hours ago Tamera Mowry-Housley Joins ‘Scrubs’ Reboot Season 2 3 days ago See All NBC On the first “Weekend Update” of “ Saturday Night Live ” Season 52, Jeremy Culhane revived his fan-favorite impression of Tucker Carlson to offer his thoughts on some of the summer’s biggest blockbusters. On “The Odyssey,” Carlson mentioned the specialty format of Imax 70mm, saying, “The Hollywood cabal shoots its filth with millimeters — or as I like to call it, the gay inch.” He added, “I like ‘The Odyssey.’ It’s so nice to see Greek people do something other than make women feel uncomfortable.” Related Stories Taiwan Creative Content Fest Adds Spotlight Screenings to Court International Buyers Carlson then turned his attention to the biggest movie of the year, saying, “Everybody loves ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Gender.'” Popular on Variety “That’s not what it’s called,” Colin Jost asserted, but the conservative commentator was already inventing a theme song: “Spider-They, Spider-Them uses whatever bathroom it feels like.” Carlson then congratulated the movie’s stars on getting married, but stopped himself as he said, “I now pronounce you Mr. and Mrs. — huh? She refused to take his last name.” As Jost reminded him that Zendaya “doesn’t have a last name,” Carlson said, “But where did it go? And who took it? And why? Sorry kids, you don’t get two names anymore. You only get one name, like a dog. That’s the rule. That’s the goal now.” When asked about “Obsession,” Carlson said, “The left’s idea of a horror movie — that a woman is forced to love a man. Oh, no, help! I’m being chased by a heterosexual relationship! Is this what we want? I don’t. Do you? You shouldn’t. But you do. Why? Is that allowed? Maybe.” Carlson continued on, equating “Minions and Monsters” to “Trump’s cabinet” and then saying, deadpan, “That’s right. I’ve turned on Trump. I’m so brave.” And, finally, the pundit made a raunchy “Toy Story 5” joke. “You’ve got a friend in me?” Carlson asked. “And his name is Woody?” Culhane debuted his Carlson impression in Season 51 of “SNL” and reprised the character on “Weekend Update.” This marks the third appearance of the character. Watch the segment below. articles.title: Jia Zhangke Readies Zhao Tao Road Movie ‘Mamma Dunhuang,’ Rules Out AI in Production (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 27, 2026 2:19am PT Jia Zhangke Readies Zhao Tao Road Movie ‘Mamma Dunhuang,’ Rules Out AI in Production (EXCLUSIVE) By Jenny S. Li Plus Icon Jenny S. Li Latest AI Robots Dance in the Rain as Pingyao Film Festival Turns 10, Honors Ann Hui 3 days ago Chinese Feature ‘Big Little Things’ Turns a Real-Life Family Rift Into a Coming-Out Drama Now Headed for Venice Horizons (EXCLUSIVE) 4 weeks ago Shanghai Film Festival Takeaways: Debut Directors Rule the Golden Goblet While AI Remakes the Industry Around Them 3 months ago See All Pingyao International Film Festival Jia Zhangke will turn his attention to location scouting and production design for his next film, road movie “Mamma Dunhuang,” once the 10th Pingyao Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon International Film Festival wraps on Sept. 30. As revealed by Variety , the film follows a woman who drives from Dunhuang, in western China near Central Asia, all the way to the sea. It is set to shoot in early winter. Related Stories Taiwan Creative Content Fest Adds Spotlight Screenings to Court International Buyers “I really love western China, and I go to Dunhuang quite often. Dunhuang was a vital transit hub on the ancient Silk Road, keep going west and you can arrive in Rome. Yet, it is so far from the ocean,” Jia tells Variety . “So this whole film is a continental story that starts in Dunhuang and travels from the west to the eastern coastline – she drives until the sea comes into view.” Popular on Variety Zhao Tao, who won the David di Donatello Award for best actress for “Shun Li and the Poet,” will once again lead a Jia film, playing a homebound woman who uses AI to help her on the journey. “I will not use AI in making ‘Mamma Dunhuang,'” Jia says. “It only plays a role in the story.” Jia founded the Pingyao festival, which marks its 10th edition this year. He says that although it’s only been a decade, “the changes in the broader film ecosystem and the media landscape, as well as technological advancements, are drastic. Pingyao has remained nimble. We’ve been able to adapt continuously alongside the shifts in the film industry and surrounding media, capturing new developments for our curation. Looking ahead, I believe cinema will continue to evolve rapidly, so we will maintain this festival’s agility in the future. That very flexibility allows us to respond in real time to the most pressing cinematic and cultural topics on people’s minds today.” Jia wants Pingyao to remain a haven for cinephiles rather than a hall of fame. Where most international festivals program hundreds of films, he intends to keep Pingyao’s lineup lean, built around the year’s newest boutique titles, so the spotlight falls on the selected films and helps them reach the market. This year’s official program has just 51 films. “As a festival, not only must it have great programs, but also a vibe of equality, freedom, and ease, setting a tone where the filmmakers and audiences can merge together,” Jia says. “We put effort into bringing in films with great artistic value, and meanwhile cover as many countries and regions as possible, prioritizing regions less familiar to Chinese audiences, such as northeastern Europe and South America, hoping to introduce a broader spectrum of cinema to the Chinese audience.” Pingyao’s online ticketing system logged more than 70 million visits this year. Jia says part of the problem is Pingyao’s limited capacity, as the ancient city “is protected as a UNESCO World Heritage [Site]. We’ve been working on building one more theater, ideally inside the ancient city walls, with 300–500 seats to enlarge the capacity. But it is very difficult to realize this plan, we are still discussing.” For its fifth edition, the festival partnered with visual artist Xu Bing on “AI-IF,” a project that invited audiences to make films using AI. Jia says the festival’s AI projects have all been exhibitions, and none of this year’s official selections were made with AI. “We’ve been prudent,” Jia says. “But we maintain an open, observant, and inclusive stance toward AI. When it comes to technology advancement, each of us holds a different perspective, but there should be one fundamental attitude: we must understand and discuss it, not shy away from it. Pingyao upholds a spirit of prudent inclusivity.” Earlier this year, Jia created an AI-generated video . Jia also co-founded Unknown Pleasures , a Chinese art-house distributor named after his 2002 film, and says the company is negotiating to acquire two Cannes titles. In June, it announced deals for Russian auteur Andrey Zvyagintsev’s “Minotaur” and French cinematographer Marine Atlan’s debut feature “La Gradiva.” “We hope Unknown Pleasures’ acquired titles all have a great showcase in Pingyao,” Jia says. articles.title: Beyond Frontman Doc ‘Because of You Ka Kui’ to Open U.K.’s Odyssey Film Festival, Lands Local Distribution (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 27, 2026 3:17am PT Beyond Frontman Doc ‘Because of You Ka Kui’ to Open U.K.’s Odyssey Film Festival, Lands Local Distribution (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Beyond Frontman Doc ‘Because of You Ka Kui’ to Open U.K.’s Odyssey Film Festival, Lands Local Distribution (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago ‘Hanuman Ansh’ Indian Sleeper Hit’s International Distribution Strategy Unveiled by ‘K.G.F,’ ‘Kantara’ Outfit Hombale Films (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago Tokyo Film Festival Unveils Mizoguchi Retrospective, Anime Award Symposium and Teens Cinema Workshop Milestone 2 days ago See All Abnormal Studios “ Because of You Ka Kui ,” a documentary on the late Beyond frontman Wong Ka Kui, will open the sixth Odyssey Film Festival in the U.K., with NGO U.K.-China Film Collab also picking up the Hong Kong film for local distribution. Discussions began in March at FilMart in Hong Kong, which U.K.-China Film Collab attended with the U.K. Film Pavilion. The NGO deployed a similar approach last year with Robin Lee’s Hong Kong documentary “Four Trails,” which opened Odyssey and then played more widely in cinemas in 2025. Related Stories Taiwan Creative Content Fest Adds Spotlight Screenings to Court International Buyers The film, from Hong Kong director Rosa Pang, revisits Wong, the singer-songwriter who drove Beyond creatively and whose songs shaped a generation of Cantonese-speaking listeners in Hong Kong and further afield. The producers are Yip Sai Wing, one of Beyond’s founding members, and Leslie Chan, the manager who is credited with finding the group. Popular on Variety The film is built around interviews with people who knew Wong both personally and through work. These sit alongside rare concert recordings, never-before-shown archive material from his early years and footage that has not been released until now. It follows Wong from his first brushes with music through the rise of Beyond and his growth as a songwriter and performer, looking at his approach to music, his character and his ideals. Pang and Leslie Chan described it as a dedication to “a legend, an ordinary person, through memories of those who truly knew him. The film seeks to rediscover the real Wong Ka Kui.” Wong died in an accident in Japan in 1993, at age 31. The band’s songs have kept finding new listeners since. There is also a U.K. link. The film’s interview with Beyond founding member William Tang was shot in London. After an earlier theatrical run in Asia, “Because of You Ka Kui” will have its U.K. premiere as Odyssey’s opening film. The festival will run Sept. 28–Oct. 10 at a number of cinemas as well as online. Each edition is built around a different theme, and this year’s is #Fashion. “Beyond did not simply follow the fashion of their generation, in many ways, they helped create it, like Oasis for the U.K.,” said Hiu Man Chan, Odyssey’s artistic director and founder of U.K.-China Film Collab. “Their music, image, attitude and style became part of the cultural memory of Hong Kong and influenced generations across Asia. Fashion is not only about what an era wears; it is also about how a generation chooses to see and express itself. That makes ‘Because of You Ka Kui’ a very meaningful film to launch this year’s Odyssey.” Hiu Man Chan said the opening pick reflected the festival’s aim to treat fashion as more than clothing and catwalks, and to explore how film, music, visual identity and pop culture feed into one another. Bringing the film to the U.K. was “my true honor,” Hiu Man Chan added. The selection also stretches the fashion theme to cover youth culture and music. Beyond’s sound and look, which mixed international rock influences with a Hong Kong that was changing fast through the 1980s and early 1990s, became bound up with a generation of young fans. Yip has called the documentary a rare chance to find the “ordinary person” behind the bandleader and icon. Malaysian company Abnormal Studios launched “Because of You Ka Kui” internationally at FilMart in March, as the lead title of its new international sales arm. “‘Because of You Ka Kui’ is not about nostalgia. The honesty of Wong Ka Kui as a person – in what he thought, felt and believed – continues to resonate today,” Pang said. Leslie Chan said that after hearing all the interviews, “I really felt that I came to know Ka Kui all over again.” Odyssey’s sixth edition will program older films alongside new ones. The festival’s opening and some of its program have backing from the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in London. articles.title: Martin McDonagh Jokes About His Past – as a Hitman – and Calls ‘Wild Horse Nine’ His Most Political Film: ‘There’s Too Much Artistic Neutrality and Too Much Saying Nothing’
articles.full_text: Sep 27, 2026 4:54am PT Martin McDonagh Jokes About His Past – as a Hitman – and Calls ‘Wild Horse Nine’ His Most Political Film: ‘There’s Too Much Artistic Neutrality and Too Much Saying Nothing’ By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest Naomi Watts Talks Menopause – ‘I Was Crying in the Bathroom, Trying to Scratch Off My Estrogen Patch’ – Recalls Being Told She ‘Freaked People Out’ Early in Her Career: ‘Yeah, No Shit. I Was Desperate, Behind on My Rent and Getting Evicted’ 1 hour ago Martin McDonagh Jokes About His Past – as a Hitman – and Calls ‘Wild Horse Nine’ His Most Political Film: ‘There’s Too Much Artistic Neutrality and Too Much Saying Nothing’ 2 hours ago Finnish Hit ‘100 Litres of Gold’ Gets Another Round With Sequel ‘200 Litres of Gold’ That’s a ‘Little Bit Darker, a Little Bit Funnier and a Little Bit Bigger’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Courtesy of Jonas Wiemann for Zurich Film Festival Martin McDonagh is taking a stand with “Wild Horse Nine.” “This is probably my most political film. That’s why I find it very exciting to be releasing this monster into the world,” he said at the Zurich Film Festival . “I feel like, in the modern day, there’s perhaps a little too much artistic neutrality, or too much saying nothing, not having an opinion or being apathetic. I’m excited to be doing the opposite with this one.” Related Stories Taiwan Creative Content Fest Adds Spotlight Screenings to Court International Buyers In his new black comedy, two CIA agents (played by John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell) travel to Easter Island before the 1973 Chilean coup. However, it feels surprisingly timely. Popular on Variety “So many things in the present day mirror a lot of those types of interventions in the past. You can actually hear lines that I thought were about 1973 being interpreted by a modern audience as being about Venezuela a few months ago or other places around the world,” he noted. “The Russia jokes in the film are about their interventions in Finland 100 years ago, but we connect them to Ukraine now. I love that it has a resonance I wasn’t necessarily aware of in the writing of it.” McDonagh, who received A Tribute to… Award at the fest, looked back on his past during a masterclass. “I left school very young, at 16, and was unemployed for a long time. But with the hopes of being a writer. Part of that was not wanting to have a real job or a boss. That has remained with me until now,” he said. He wrote radio plays, all of which were rejected – “Mostly by the BBC. But I don’t bear a grudge” – and then became an acclaimed playwright. “As a film fan, I put all that into the energy of the plays. Things would happen that you wouldn’t usually see on stage. Like cats exploding [in ‘The Lieutenant of Inishmore’].” Seeing Al Pacino in “American Buffalo” by David Mamet was a pivotal moment. “I can still remember it to this day. He just came on stage and blew the whole theater away. It was this combination of a play, full of energy and swearing, amazing dialogue and this movie star who, well, you’d realize what acting really was when he was on stage.” McDonagh still writes “without the camera in mind,” but he enjoys the freedom of writing scripts. “It’s like when you don’t go to the gym for a long time; that’s where my theater brain is at the moment. But the muscle memory is still there.” The transition to cinema wasn’t exactly easy. “It was the bad rejections that really inspired me. Maybe I thrive not on encouragement, but anger,” he said. Still, his 2004 short “Six Shooter” won the Academy Award for Best Live Action Short Film. “It was probably the scariest situation I’ve been in artistically. But the wonderful thing was having Brendan Gleeson be part of it. He protected me from any interference. I couldn’t have done it without his help and guidance,” he recalled. He reunited with Gleeson on his hit “In Bruges,” also starring Colin Farrell, where two hitmen are forced to hide out after a mission gone wrong. “I used to be a hit man. People don’t know that. They thought it just was plays and then films. It was plays, killing and then films,” joked McDonagh. “I went to Bruges not knowing anything about it. I was supposed to meet a girl on the second night, and she didn’t turn up. It was this combination of thinking it was the most cinematic, undiscovered town I’d ever seen, and being bored as hell and just wanting to get drunk and get out of there.” Once again, he felt shielded by his lead actors. “Colin and Brendan were great partners in protecting me from any interference from the grown-ups. Who aren’t usually grown up; they’re children with a lot of money. It’s the nature of Hollywood,” he said. “I’m going to get in so much trouble. It’s good that it’s not being filmed, right?” McDonagh tackles serious – even shocking – topics in his films, yet somehow they still tend to be funny. But recently, he’s been noticing a change in his work. “I’ve tried to make sure that the films aren’t just about being cool. They’re about something deeper, and I guess more tragic. I’m leaving room for more contemplative scenes where the characters are on their own and it’s not funny. They’re left to think about their lives or dwell on their regrets.” This was the case with Frances McDormand, who played the grieving mother Mildred Hayes in “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri.” And now with John Malkovich in “ Wild Horse Nine .” “When they’re great actors like Frances or John, you see the sadness in their eyes, and you fill in what they’re thinking about. One of the ideas for John’s character was to give him the entire palette of emotions. You know that John can do comedy, he can do rage and he can do contemplative, quiet stuff. But I’m making sure all those things are together in one package,” he noted. “None of my films are sort of what I would call ‘Hollywood movies.’ They’re not simple, feel-good stories. When actors of that magnitude who have maybe done some of those films, and know they’re a little empty get to work on something different, it frees them up to show their brilliance.” McDonagh wouldn’t want to make bigger movies anyway. “Weirdly, I’m really happy with the trajectory or the level of films that I’ve made. I don’t want a bigger budget. I don’t even want more success. I just want to continue making films completely free from any interference from anyone. That’s a perfect position to be in.” Amazon Moves to Toss ‘Criminal’ Production Assistant’s Harassment Suit Sacha Baron Cohen to Star in Quentin Tarantino’s First Stage Play ‘The Popinjay Cavalier’ ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Trailer: Sacha Baron Cohen Returns as the London Bad Boy in New Amazon MGM Mockumentary Ali G Movie Backlash Intensifies in the U.K. as Campaigners Try to Get Film Pulled From Cinemas Squishmallows Movie in the Works at Amazon MGM (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...

articles.title: Naomi Watts Talks Menopause – ‘I Was Crying in the Bathroom, Trying to Scratch Off My Estrogen Patch’ – Recalls Being Told She ‘Freaked People Out’ Early in Her Career: ‘Yeah, No Shit. I Was Desperate, Behind on My Rent and Getting Evicted’
articles.full_text: Sep 27, 2026 6:14am PT Naomi Watts Talks Menopause – ‘I Was Crying in the Bathroom, Trying to Scratch Off My Estrogen Patch’ – Recalls Being Told She ‘Freaked People Out’ Early in Her Career: ‘Yeah, No Shit. I Was Desperate, Behind on My Rent and Getting Evicted’ By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest Naomi Watts Talks Menopause – ‘I Was Crying in the Bathroom, Trying to Scratch Off My Estrogen Patch’ – Recalls Being Told She ‘Freaked People Out’ Early in Her Career: ‘Yeah, No Shit. I Was Desperate, Behind on My Rent and Getting Evicted’ 1 hour ago Finnish Hit ‘100 Litres of Gold’ Gets Another Round With Sequel ‘200 Litres of Gold’ That’s a ‘Little Bit Darker, a Little Bit Funnier and a Little Bit Bigger’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Naima Mohamud Explains Why Finland Needs a Film Like ‘Halima’: ‘It Was a Long Time Coming’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Courtesy of Andreas Rentz for Zurich Film Festival Naomi Watts waited a long time to become a star. “It was a grind. That 10 years before I met David, I became so locked up and I felt worthless. My agent pulled me aside and she said: ‘We need to have a heart to heart. Honey, you are too intense. You are freaking people out.’ I went: ‘Yeah, no shit.’ I was desperate! I was behind on my rent; I was getting evicted. I didn’t know what to bring to this room,” she recalled at Zurich Film Festival . Related Stories Taiwan Creative Content Fest Adds Spotlight Screenings to Court International Buyers “They told me I wasn’t funny last week, so now I am trying to be funny. They told me I wasn’t sexy – I’m trying to be sexy. You reshape yourself and try to read the tone of what is needed. That’s how it went and I couldn’t be myself anymore. I was either an extreme version of myself or a diluted version of myself. It took a genius like David Lynch to see beyond all that weirdness I built up, undo it and get to the real me.” Popular on Variety The resilience she built up from moving a lot as a kid was helpful, however. “You also have to know why you love it. Are you in it for the right reasons? My goal wasn’t just to be famous. I loved disappearing into these characters. I really cared and continued to investigate. I still do. There’s always more to learn.” Watts received the Golden Eye Award at Zurich Film Festival. During the ceremony, she also recalled these difficult first years of trying to become a successful actress, “which had a lot of dry spells.” “And then, mercifully, I met David Lynch in my late 20s and he changed my career.” “Mulholland Drive” is widely considered as her breakout. “That film gave me the most incredible role that affected people. To this day they still watch it. It’s still on these ‘bests’ lists. I’m just very, very proud to be a part of that film.” During the masterclass at the fest, Watts said she was also encouraged by Nicole Kidman. “She said: ‘All it takes is one thing, one thing could change everything. That didn’t make sense to me for a very long time. Until David Lynch, and then it became very real.” Right after “Mulholland Drive,” she starred in horror classic “The Ring.” “I tried to say ‘no.’ There’s no certainty to anything you do, ever,” she said. “My agents were excited about this. I said: ‘Wait. I just got this critical acclaim, so I want to instantly go into a Hollywood blockbuster-y movie?!’ I fought with my agent at the time. I didn’t know it was going to be a massive hit! I woke up the horror genre, in a way. It was a lucky, lucky break.” Watts also earned raves for “21 Grams” – “Extraordinary things can happen when you get tired and irritable from doing things too much,” she said, recalling that intense shoot. “If there’s any theme in my work, it’s grief. It’s why I do what I do: I’m trying to figure out the meaning of my life. Another one is identity. I love the story [that asks]: ‘Who are you?’ That also comes from my moving around as a kid. I was always on the outskirts of the group, trying to find my way in.” Watts’ recent role, in Ben Shirinian’s “The Housewife,” addresses that too. In the film, set in the 1960s, she plays a seemingly perfect housewife – but one who hides a terrible post-war past. “I never played a character like this, even though I look for flawed women and I’m not afraid of unlikeable. But this was extreme,” she said. She said: “I knew what I was stepping into. I knew it was going to be a daunting, haunting understanding. A character like that comes to you at night, in your dreams.” Ending the masterclass, Watts admitted it took her a while to stop focusing on other people’s opinions. “Vulnerability is a superpower. It has taken me a long time to know that, and own that. I wish I’d learn earlier on to be more myself and [care] less about pleasing people. Some people are born with that level of confidence – I was never that person.” “I still have a lot of self-doubt, but I don’t pretend it’s not a real thing. I try to see it as a gift. It’s more effective than just bullshitting your way through it all.” Being open about her hardships, as well as menopause, proved to be liberating, she said. “Menopause became a huge topic of conversation, because I went through it early on in my life and had no clue what was happening with my body. Once I talked about it with my partner, who is now my husband [actor Billy Crudup], and he was supportive, I went: ‘How about I just own the story?’ I’m in on the joke, although it’s not actually a joke. Why do we just suffer, instead of getting some normalcy? Just own it.” She recalled her first conversation about it with Crudup. “I was crying in the bathroom, trying to scratch off my estrogen patch. I told him what was going on, so nervous, and I thought: ‘He’s not gonna want to be with me anymore!’ He said: ‘Hold on. It’s great that you are taking care of yourself. Why are you ashamed?’ It was so sweet… And sexy. I felt safer than I ever felt.” She ended up founding Stripes Beauty, a brand designed for women navigating perimenopause and menopause. “Men have to be curious and compassionate. And our job, ladies, is to share the story.” Ali G Movie Backlash Intensifies in the U.K. as Campaigners Try to Get Film Pulled From Cinemas Amazon Moves to Toss ‘Criminal’ Production Assistant’s Harassment Suit Squishmallows Movie in the Works at Amazon MGM (EXCLUSIVE) Sacha Baron Cohen to Star in Quentin Tarantino’s First Stage Play ‘The Popinjay Cavalier’ ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Trailer: Sacha Baron Cohen Returns as the London Bad Boy in New Amazon MGM Mockumentary Loading comments...

articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac San Sebastián: Mike Leigh’s ‘Tender Loving Care’ Wins Golden Shell & Best Screenplay ‘NAZA’ Trailer: First Look At Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor’s Much-Talked-About Gaza Documentary Oscars: Denmark Selects May El-Toukhy’s Venice Golden Lion Winner ‘Woman Unknown’ For International Race View All September 26, 2026 1:43pm ‘Tender Loving Care' Thin Man Films Mike Leigh ’s latest and potential last feature, Tender Loving Care , has won the San Sebastián Film Festival’s top prize, the Golden Shell, alongside the award for Best Screenplay. Scroll down for the full list of winners. Leigh’s Tender Loving Care also won the Silver Shell for Best Leading Performance for actress Kate O’Flynn, who shared the prize with Asta Kamma August for her role in Growth of the Soil . That film, directed by Hans Petter Moland, also won the Jury Prize for Best Cinematography. The Special Jury Prize was awarded to Border , directed by Ah Biao; the Silver Shell for Best Director went to Amanda Kernell for Brace Your Heart, while Javier Cámara won the Silver Shell for Best Supporting Performance for his work in 5 More Minutes . The City of Donostia/San Sebastián Audience Award went to La bola negra. Related Stories News International Insider: Deep BBC Cuts Begin; Ali G Under Fire; San Sebastian Report News San Sebastián Industry Awards: Juan Sebastián Mesa & Tatiana Huezo Among Big Winners Ira Sachs presided over this year’s jury in San Sebastián. His fellow jurors were director and screenwriter Genki Kawamura, screenwriter Catherine Paillé, actress and producer Alice Braga, actress Patricia López Arnaiz, actor Bill Skarsgård, and producer Mike Goodridge. Watch on Deadline Leigh was not present in Spain to accept his awards. The veteran filmmaker is currently in New York for the U.S. premiere of Tender Loving Care, so he sent a video message to Spain. “What a great honour it is. Thank you for awarding Tender Loving Care , our film, but not least and especially for The Golden Shell. articles.title: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham Nearly Joins Oasis, But There’s Something A Bit Off About The Gallagher Brothers In ‘SNL UK’ Cold Open
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham Nearly Joins Oasis, But There’s Something A Bit Off About The Gallagher Brothers In ‘SNL UK’ Cold Open Netflix Gives First Look At Charlie Brooker’s New Series ‘Blackmere’ As Rory Kinnear Joins Cast ‘Happy Valley’ Star Sarah Lancashire Leading Dark Netflix Series About A Modern-Day Witch Hunt View All September 26, 2026 2:21pm 'SNL UK' Sky/Eva Pentel/Matt Crockett There was something a bit off about Oasis’ sometimes feuding-yet-touring brothers in the Saturday Night Live UK cold open this week. SNL UK kicked off its Season 2 Episode 3 with new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, played by George Fouracres, returning to his beloved home of Manchester following a speech to the UN where he socked it to Russia, according to his good pal Angela Rayner (Celeste Dring). “I’m sick of Russia trying to divide the British people. We can divide ourselves thank you very much,” jokes Burnham. Before long, Oasis’ brothers Noel and Liam Gallagher, played by Jack Shep and new cast member Freddie Meredith, arrive to offer Burnham the opportunity of a lifetime. Their guitarist has pulled out and Burnham, a guitar player himself, can step in. “Ange, cancel the budget I’m going on tour,” he tells Rayner. Related Stories News David Oyelowo & Viola Prettejohn To Star In 'The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo' TV Series For Sky News Princess Di Returns To 'SNL UK' As "Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android" In Cold Open Skewering King Charles, Ed Sheeran & AI But alas, Burnham is asked to input numerous personal details – a gentle poke at critiques of Oasis’ expensive and dynamically priced tickets – and once done Liam and Noel emerge as two Russian spies. Watch on Deadline “Oasis has always been Russian pop. All songs were made in a lab by Kremlin scientists. ‘Wonderwall’ is really ‘Wonderful Wall’ about the Berlin Wall,” says Russian spy Liam. In the end, following an extended joke about his flip-flopping on calling a general election – “I for example could hold a general election and easily smash it, but as I announced yesterday, I want to, but I could” – Burnham orders the “Russian Mancs” to “leave Britain and go back to being Oasis.” The cold open came in the third ep of the second season of Sky ‘s SNL UK. Amelia Dimoldenberg , creator of Chicken Shop Date, which launches its final season next week, follows in the footsteps of Jeff Goldblum and Jamie Demetriou to host this week. All of SNL UK’ s cast members have returned for Season 2, including Hammed Animashaun, Ayoade Bamgboye, Larry Dean, Dring, Fouracres, Ania Magliano, Annabel Marlow, Al Nash, Shep, Emma Sidi and Paddy Young, with Meredith making his debut. SNL UK is produced by Universal Television Alternative Studio’s UK production team and Broadway Video. Lorne Michaels serves as executive producer. James Longman is lead producer. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt How ‘SNL’ Introduced Season 52’s New Cast Members Saidah Belo-Osagie & Grace Reiter Denver Comedy Works Turns 45: How Club Owner Wende Curtis Fought Through Debt, Covid & Cancer To Preserve A Comedy Institution Marko Zaror & Tyrik Johnson Join Amazon MGM Studios Action Film ‘Deadlocked’ View All September 16, 2026 1:00pm Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter Mike Klubeck/Jill Petracek Saturday Night Live has two new featured players for Season 52: Saidah Belo-Osagie and Grace Reiter . We were first to report on this duo being eyed for the show — first at showcases, and then at screen tests. This adds to recent SNL news which included the departure of Chloe Fineman and Martin Herlihy after seven and five seasons, respectively. Herlihy had most recently been working as a writer on the show, after originally writing and performing as part of sketch trio Please Don’t Destroy. Related Stories Late Night TV ‘Saturday Night Live’ Wraps 2026 Showcases For New Cast: Who Scored A Screen Test? — The Dish Late Night TV Jalen Brunson To Host ‘SNL’ Season 52 Premiere; Dakota Johnson, Shane Gillis & Inde Navarrette Also Set For Studio 8H Belo-Osagie’s hiring comes following a season in which SNL had no Black female cast members. Producers had been looking to rectify this, per our sources, since Ego Nwodim’s surprise exit in the fall of 2025. Watch on Deadline Sources said SNL may shoot its new title sequence featuring the new players as soon as tomorrow. Saidah Belo-Osagie is a Queens, NY-based up-and-comer who created the event series Afrobeats Futura and solo show Saidah Gets Closure . She also previously wrote and directed the short film Tinge and is repped by Gersh, 3 Arts Entertainment, and Frankfurt Kurnit Klein & Selz. Generating buzz online for years, Reiter was one of the original members of TikTok-based sketch show Stapleview . Her credits include Netflix’s upcoming American High mockumentary Minimum Wage , on which she also wrote and directed, HBO’s The Chair Company with Tim Robinson, and the online parody “The Hunger Games (but Better).” Originally from Chippewa Falls, WI, she is repped by Gersh, Mosaic, and Sloane, Offer, Weber & Dern. SNL premieres at 11:30 p.m. ET/8:30 p.m. PT on September 26 with host Jalen Brunson of the New York Knicks and musical guest KATSEYE. Other upcoming host-musical guest duos include Dakota Johnson and Turnstile (October 3), Shane Gillis and Rosalía (October 10), and Inde Navarette and Gracie Abrams (October 31). Created and exec produced by Lorne Michaels, the show is produced in association with Broadway Video. articles.title: Sylvester Stallone Thought His Dad Would “Be Proud” To Make ‘Rocky’ Cameo: “It Got Really Nasty”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Saturday Night Live’: Jalen Brunson’s Knicks Teammates Join Him During Opening Monologue ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts Ina Garten Explains Why She’s “Always Said No” To A Biopic: “It’s My Story” View All September 26, 2026 3:10pm Sylvester Stallone and Burgess Meredith in 'Rocky' 1976 Courtesy Everett Collection As Sylvester Stallone made his breakout performance in Rocky , there was one person he couldn’t quite turn into a fan. While discussing his memoir The Steps , releasing Oct. 23, the 3x Oscar nominee recalled things on set getting “really nasty” after giving his real father Frank Stallone Sr. a cameo as the bell ringer in the 1976 boxing drama’s climactic match. “It was like: I just want you to love me for a little bit,” Sly explained to The New York Times . “Like, look what I did! Share it with me. I know you thought I was a fool my whole life, but here we are.” Related Stories Festivals ‘I Play Rocky’s Peter Farrelly Talks Why The Making Of ‘Rocky’ Was The Next Real-Life Story He Wanted To Take A Swing At – Toronto Studio Politics Sylvester Stallone Told Trump Hollywood Ambassadorship Was “Impossible” But Was Appointed Anyway: “It Won’t Work” On the day of filming, Frank Sr. “didn’t ring the bell properly,” as his son “kept fighting and fighting and fighting. Everything’s choreographed. It’s one, two, three, four, bell. Not six, seven, eight, nine, ten. Carl Weathers is like, ‘What’s going on?'” Watch on Deadline Stallone continued, “And of course it ended up in an altercation by the end. It got really nasty. A really bad Italian drama. But for a moment I thought, Jesus, he’d be proud.” Sylvester Stallone in ‘Rocky’ (1976) Everett Collection In the interview, Stallone explained that his father “was very, very cold and tough” until they reconciled upon his death in 2011. “It would be these constant bombastic explosions and then total silence,” recalled Stallone of living alone with his dad. “If he and I were talking and I said, ‘I don’t know if I agree with that,’ he’d start spinning his fork and suck his teeth, and you knew what was coming. The next thing you know, wham! He had very big hands. You learn to duck. I didn’t put a lot of stuff in the book because I didn’t want a pity party, but it was insane.” In the biopic I Play Rocky , premiering Nov. 6 in theaters, Anthony Ippolito plays a young Stallone as he writes the first Rocky movie and fights to star as the titular boxer. articles.title: Robert Eggers Wants To Do ‘Romeo & Juliet’ Because Things Got “So Dark” After ‘Werwulf’, Joking: “So, I’ll Do Something About Two Teenagers Killing Themselves”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Saturday Night Live’: Jalen Brunson’s Knicks Teammates Join Him During Opening Monologue ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts Ina Garten Explains Why She’s “Always Said No” To A Biopic: “It’s My Story” View All September 26, 2026 4:34pm Robert Eggers explains why he wanted to adapt 'Romeo & Juliet' as his next film. 20th Century Fox/courtesy Everett Collection/Gilbert Flores/PMC SPOILER ALERT for anyone who skipped freshman English! Robert Eggers is teasing his take on William Shakespeare’s Romeo & Juliet . During a post-screening Q&A for his latest macabre title Werwulf , premiering Christmas Day, the auteur joked that the famously tragic conclusion of Shakespeare’s 16th century romance would be a welcome “break” from his usual horror work. “I was doing something else,” noted Eggers of plans for his next project in a video from the event. “But what happened was, after Werwulf , I was writing another horror movie, and it got so dark again, and I was like, ‘I need a break. So, I’ll do something about two teenagers killing themselves.'” Related Stories Acquisitions Focus Features Closing In On ‘Romeo And Juliet’ Adaptation From Robert Eggers News ‘Werwulf’ Trailer: Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Willem Dafoe & Lily-Rose Depp Lead The Latest Celluloid Nightmare From Robert Eggers Earlier this week, Deadline reported that Eggers was eyeing a return to Focus Features for his take on Romeo & Juliet , which has sparked some studio competition. Watch on Deadline Details of Eggers’ adaptation are under wraps. His deal is not yet finalized, but we understand he’ll direct and produce this version of the classic play. The deal would reunite him with a studio with whom he’s worked across much of his body of work, including horror titles The Lighthouse (2019), Nosferatu (2024) and Werwulf . Incredible answer from Robert Eggers about why he turned to Romeo & Juliet pic.twitter.com/003vhqRdCN — The King of Burbank @ Beyondfest (@kingofburbank2) September 26, 2026 In Werwulf , a man (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) in 14th century England finds him and his family threatened by a ravenous beast haunting the town. The film also stars Lily-Rose Depp, Willem Dafoe, Ralph Ineson and more. articles.title: Ina Garten Explains Why She’s “Always Said No” To A Biopic: “It’s My Story”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Saturday Night Live’: Jalen Brunson’s Knicks Teammates Join Him During Opening Monologue ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts Ina Garten Explains Why She’s “Always Said No” To A Biopic: “It’s My Story” View All September 26, 2026 6:00pm Chef Ina Garten at her East Hamptons home. Fairchild Archive/PMC After sharing her story in her 2024 memoir Be Ready When The Luck Happens , Ina Garten is reluctant to trust a filmmaker with the adaptation. The Barefoot Contessa celebrity chef recently explained why she’s “never been willing” to make a biopic about her life, despite being “approached” to adapt Be Ready for the big screen. “It’s funny, I don’t make long-term plans. I do what I do as well as I can, and things come along, and I say no to most of them,” she told People . Related Stories News Food Network’s ‘Barefoot Contessa’ Ina Garten Advocates Day Drinking As A Way To Beat Quarantine Blues News Amazon And Oprah Winfrey’s Harpo Entertainment Ink Wide-Reaching Podcast Deal Garten added, “I’ve been approached to do a movie of my memoir, but I know that when a producer or director gets ahold of a story, they want to make it work on film and they’re going to change it. So I’ve never been willing to do that. It’s my story. I get to keep it. And I don’t want people making up things just for dramatic effect. And so I’ve always said no.” Watch on Deadline The 2024 memoir came after Garten ended the nearly 20-year run of her Food Network cooking show Barefoot Contessa , which ran from 2002 to 2021. Since 2022, Garten has hosted her followup Food Network show Be My Guest , inviting friends to her dinner table in her East Hampton, New York home. articles.title: ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Saturday Night Live’: Jalen Brunson’s Knicks Teammates Join Him During Opening Monologue ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts Ina Garten Explains Why She’s “Always Said No” To A Biopic: “It’s My Story” View All September 26, 2026 8:07pm Jon Watts is directing the next 'Star Wars' film in the Skywalker Saga. Courtesy Everett Collection/Gilbert Flores/PMC After eight years and countless entries in the expanding onscreen universe, Star Wars is revisiting the Skywalker family with its next project. Deadline can confirm that Lucasfilm has tapped Skeleton Crew co-creator Jon Watts (director of Spider-Man: Homecoming , Spider-Man: Far From Home and Spider-Man: No Way Home ) to helm the first installment in a new trilogy of the Skywalker Saga, which is being penned by Simon Kinberg ( X-Men: Dark Phoenix , Prime’s Mr. & Mrs. Smith ). Kinberg, who previously co-created the DisneyXD animated series Star Wars Rebels (2014-’18), has been working on the new trilogy since 2018, with Daisy Ridley reportedly eyed to reprise her role as Rey, as it will serve in the next chapter of the Skywalker Saga. Related Stories News Damon Lindelof Details His Scrapped ‘Star Wars’ That Would Have Tackled “Nostalgia” & “Revision” News ‘Star Wars: Starfighter’ & ‘Star Wars’ 50th Anniversary Edition To Be Released In Imax 70MM The project reportedly has not yet received a greenlight from parent company Disney. Watch on Deadline Beginning with Star Wars: Episode IV — A New Hope in 1977 and the sequels Episode V — The Empire Strikes Back (1980) and Episode VI — Return of the Jedi (1983), the Skywalker Saga continued with the prequel trilogy Episode I — The Phantom Menace (1999), Episode II: Attack of the Clones (2002) and Episode III — Revenge of the Sith (2005). Most recently, the franchise left off the Skywalker Saga with the latest trilogy, Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens (2015), Episode VIII — The Last Jedi (2017) and Episode IX — The Rise of Skywalker (2019), which was led by Ridley’s Rey. Since the last chapter in the Skywalker Saga, the Star Wars franchise has expanded with films and streaming series set throughout the onscreen universe, with the next installment Star Wars: Starfighter set for a May 28, 2027 premiere. Lucasfilm had no comment. Knight Edge Media was first to report the news. It was a riff on their latest meeting earlier this week, an unlikely lovefest between the left-wing mayor and the right-wing commander in chief. articles.title: ‘Saturday Night Live’: Jalen Brunson’s Knicks Teammates Join Him During Opening Monologue
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Saturday Night Live’: Jalen Brunson’s Knicks Teammates Join Him During Opening Monologue ‘Star Wars’ Is Continuing Skywalker Saga With ‘Spider-Man’ Director Jon Watts Ina Garten Explains Why She’s “Always Said No” To A Biopic: “It’s My Story” View All September 26, 2026 9:01pm Saturday Night Live kicked off its 52nd season with a victory lap for Knicks fans, as host Jalen Brunson was joined onstage by his teammates. The 2026 MVP swapped some quips with teammates Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges, OG Anunoby and Josh Hart during his opening monologue on Saturday’s episode, which comes after they defeated the San Antonio Spurs in June to bring the Knicks their first NBA championship since 1973. Related Stories Late Night TV ‘Saturday Night Live’ Opens With Riff On Donald Trump’s Need For More Time With Zohran Mamdani: “I Really, Really Like You” Late Night TV ‘SNL’s Weekend Update Mocks Paramount+, ‘Spider-Man’, ‘The Odyssey’ & ‘Obsession’ Calling on the group during his monologue, Brunson confirmed to Towns you can’t “foul out of SNL ,” to which the center, forward excitedly responded, “So I could be here like the whole show? Nice!” Bridges asked if his arms were “pretty long,” as Brunson validated he has a “great wingspan.” Bridges responded, “Yet, I’ll never fly.” Watch on Deadline Anunoby asked, “Remember in Game 4, when you took that shot at the end and missed it? Remember what happened after?” “Yeah, you tipped it in,” said Brunson, as Anunoby replied with a laugh, “Oh yeah, that was awesome.” Meanwhile, Hart asked if it was true that Brunson “took a $113 million pay cut just to re-sign with the Knicks,” which point guard confirmed is true. “Wow. So, is that money still up for grabs?” asked Hart. “I don’t know. But I do have a question for you. Why did you do this to me at the cup ceremony?” asked Brunson, playing a clip of Hart poking him in the butt as the team celebrated their win. Hart exclaimed, “Because it was funny!” Saturday Night Live kicked off its 52nd season this weekend with host Brunson and musical guest Katseye. The season continues on NBC with guest hosts Dakota Johnson, Shane Gillis and Inde Navarrette, along with musical guests Turnstile, Rosalía and Gracie Abrams. articles.title: Film Execs Ponder Federal Film Tax Credit Impact, Timeline & Potential Price Rises — Zurich Summit
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Film Execs Ponder Federal Film Tax Credit Impact, Timeline & Potential Price Rises — Zurich Summit Cinetic Launches Vertical Leap, Investment Vehicle & Producing Pathway For Pro Athletes — Zurich Summit One Year On, Does AI Actress Tilly Norwood Have An Agent? “We Get Loads Of Offers, But No, We Don’t Need It” — Zurich Summit View All September 27, 2026 4:43am Hollywood sign Presley Ann / Getty Images At this weekend’s Zurich Summit a group of film financiers were asked by Deadline for their thoughts on the prospects of a U.S. federal film incentive. Last week, a bipartisan group of lawmakers unveiled the bill for a 20% incentive, which with bonuses could bring the total rebate to 30%. The move has long been called-for by the U.S. industry concerned by the exodus of production overseas. Alex Walton, former Co-Lead & Partner at WME Independent, told the Summit the move was “hugely positive”: “It’s wild to think there hasn’t been an efficient tax credit in America. It has helped many other countries. Spain is booming because of it now; and all over Europe. It’s going to take some time to be realized and for financial institutions to be able to cash flow it. But you’ve got to believe it will happen within the next three-four years, and then that will see all the foreign tax credits compete harder to maintain their positions.” Related Stories News "I Can Promise You, We Had No Idea That 'Obsession' Was Going To Become 'Obsession'", Says Hit Horror Film's Seller -- Zurich Summit Festivals 'Backrooms' Director Kane Parsons Says: "I Don't View It As A Horror Project" - Zurich Summit A start date is not yet set. The proposed text from last week stated that the credit would apply to qualifying film and TV productions beginning in taxable years after December 31, 2026 (effectively targeting projects starting in 2027). But bills can take years to pass. Watch on Deadline Andrea Scarso, Managing Partner at prolific financier IPR.VC, whose credits include Marty Supreme and Materialists , agreed that a U.S. incentive would be “positive” but also cautioned against rising production costs: “It remains to be seen whether the prices and budgets are also going up by the same amount, which is something that happens in some foreign territories when they increase the amount of tax credit or soft money. It’s always a balance. But overall, I think it’s good news.” Sarah Schweitzman, Co-Head CAA Media Finance, noted: “What’s important is that when you look at some of the international markets, you realize that we’re making movies there because of a tax incentive situation and I think if we’re able to federalize a tax incentive program in the U.S. it’s going to create many more jobs and invigorate crews, which is something we absolutely need in the U.S.” A recent Motion Picture Association study claimed that a federal film tax credit could increase U.S. production spending by $125BN and add more than 143,000 jobs by 2035. You can read more about the bill here .
