articles.title: Paramount Moves Ahead With $7.5 Billion Debt Raise, Part Of Package To Finance WBD Acquisition
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill As Letterboxd Draws Interest From The New York Times, A24 And More, One Of Its Bankers Calls It “A Phenomenon” Paramount Moves Ahead With $7.5 Billion Debt Raise, Part Of Package To Finance WBD Acquisition Kunhardts Expand Life Stories Platform With Unseen Footage From Decades Of Documentary Filmmaking View All September 24, 2026 9:20am Story Arc Getty Images Paramount has started syndication for a proposed senior secured term loan of $7.5 billion – a chunk of change it needs to fund the acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery . It began the process after a legal settlement earlier this week paved the way for the merger to close. Related Stories Legal ParaBros Merger Settlement Sign-Off Delayed As Deal Foes Granted Hail Mary Move By Judge Executives Sturm Und Drang At Warner Bros Amid Paramount Merger Has Insiders Wondering If The Brand Survives Paramount intends to raise approximately $44.4 billion of additional secured debt plus previously announced financings and will “utilize the net proceeds of these borrowings, together with cash on hand and the net proceeds of the previously announced equity financing, to finance the purchase price for its previously announced acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery and the repayment of certain existing debt,” the company said today. On Monday, it settled an antitrust suit brought by a group of 12 State Attorneys General led by California’s Rob Bonta. Bankers then started reaching out to investors ahead of the sale of what’s said to be $49 billion in total debt financing. Watch on Deadline The judge in the case must approve the settlement. That includes the $7.5 billion of investment-grade loans, which started moving forward today; about $30 billion of investment-grade bonds; and some $12 billion of second-lien bonds. Debt syndication is a collaborative process led by underwriters where a group of lenders pool resources to fund a large loan for one borrower – in this case Paramount. Bank of America, Citigroup and Apollo underwrote the buyout debt package, one of the biggest ever and with many moving pieces, to fund the takeover. The other half of the merger equation is equity, financing. Larry Ellison had personally committed to backstop over $40 billion in equity financing for the mega-deal, defrayed in large part by a trio of Middle Eastern sovereign wealth funds led by Saudi Arabia that agreed to come on as investors — and will wind up with hefty combined equity stake in the combined company. articles.title: Dealmakers React To Paramount-WBD Settlement: “Tech Has Won”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade As Letterboxd Draws Interest From The New York Times, A24 And More, One Of Its Bankers Calls It “A Phenomenon” Barry Diller Drops $18B Bid To Acquire Full Control Of MGM Resorts As YouTube Remains Streaming’s Alpha Dog, It’s Adding Even More Unlikely New TV Tricks View All September 24, 2026 11:24am Story Arc Getty Images Mergers-and-acquisitions specialists weighed in Thursday on the Paramount -Warner Bros. Discovery merger, which appears just days from closing despite an 11th-hour legal hiccup. The $110 billion deal is on track to close in the coming days after a settlement of two antitrust lawsuits on Monday, though a federal judge delayed a hearing where she was due to review the settlement. Assuming it does finally close, the transaction “is evidence that, really, tech has won,” said David Hernand, a partner at the Simpson Thacher law firm, during a panel at the Financial Times Business of Entertainment Summit. “Tech came in and said, ‘We can build a better mousetrap on the distribution side.’ Distribution – when we’re talking about electronic distribution, whether it’s cable or internet – is moving atoms, and tech companies are really good at that, as it turns out.” Related Stories News Paramount Moves Ahead With $7.5 Billion Debt Raise, Part Of Package To Finance WBD Acquisition Legal ParaBros Merger Settlement Sign-Off Delayed As Deal Foes Granted Hail Mary Move By Judge Forced to go up against Apple, YouTube, Netflix, Amazon and others, Hernand added, “the traditional companies that relied on broadcast and cable as a form of distribution are trying to play catch-up and figure out how they’re going to play in this world.” Watch on Deadline Hernand’s firm is not involved in the Paramount deal, but two other panelists spoke from the perspective of stakeholders in the transaction. Aaron Sobel, a private equity partner at Apollo Global Management, which provided one-third of the financing for the merger, said it will give a traditional player a fighting chance against Big Tech. “I don’t think you can overstate how important getting that deal done was,” he said. “You had two companies that arguably couldn’t have existed without combining, and having someone like [Paramount CEO David Ellison] support the business is huge.” Prior to the merger, he added, “We were at a crossroads in the industry, where if that deal hadn’t gotten done … Netflix was gonna take over the world. Now, you’re seeing the pendulum really swing back to more traditional media, which is kind of ironic. And David is really betting on IP and what’s in that complex. So the fact that he’s the right owner for that and has the capital, obviously, to support that company, I don’t think you can overstate it.” Alex Michael, senior managing director and global head of sports and entertainment for LionTree, which advised Paramount on the merger, called it “a big deal, literally and figuratively… It was a big domino that everyone was waiting for, and I think it’ll be exciting to see where we go from here.” Sobel said the merger will have “so-many knock-on effects” in a positive way, across the theatrical movie business, distribution, production and “global movies and events.” Noting Hernand’s point, he said the deal was “against where the world was going. And I think there’s a lot of really exciting things that will come out of it.” Netflix, whose chief content officer, Bela Bajaria, spoke just prior to the panel, was the next topic. The streaming giant had agreed to acquire the studio and streaming business of WBD last December. After more than a dozen offers, Paramount finally managed to unseat Netflix with a richer offer for all of WBD. Netflix “kind of showed their hand by going after Warner Brothers, and with all due respect, look at their share price performance,” Sobel said. “The world knows what’s happening on engagement. If you don’t have really valuable IP, they’re going to shift to more traditional strategy over the next few years,” particularly with live events and sports. Noting that “what’s old is new again” for all players in media and entertainment, whether traditional or tech, he added, “I think a lot more of these companies are gonna look similar, not different.” Paramount-WBD is far from the last transaction set to reshape the industry. The panel wrapped with a provocative audience question from an NBCUniversal exec who asked the panel what the best path forward for her company would be. Comcast over the summer announced it plans to spin off NBCU, projecting the move will be completed by mid-2027. Hernand said the company should consider breaking up the portfolio “beyond what they’ve announced, meaning potentially separating NBC from Universal. “The more interesting move there would be combining Universal and Sony,” he added, acknowledging, “I know that would create a lot of outrage in Los Angeles.” Sobel noted that Comcast Co-CEO and Chairman Brian Roberts and his family control the company, and so-called “controlled companies” are often limited in terms of M&A. If Roberts is “open to be more flexible on how his vote works and his exposure to the business, it should be broken up,” Sobel said. “I would think Netflix and Comcast down the digital and the media side should probably come together at some point.” ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event More from this Story Arc Paramount WB September 24, 2026 David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi As CEO’s Soon-To-Be Owned CNN Banned From White House Event September 24, 2026 No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Striving to get a settlement
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Disney Legal Chief Warns Of “Hard Choices” & “Much Smaller Organization” Coming As Company Layoffs Loom David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi As CEO’s Soon-To-Be Owned CNN Banned From White House Event No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” View All September 24, 2026 12:12pm Story Arc L-R: Rob Bonta, Leticia James and David Ellison Getty Images Although David Ellison has given a lot of money to Democrats over the years, the Paramount CEO is probably not donating a dime to Sen. Cory Booker ‘s next campaign. The much disparaged state Attorneys General-negotiated settlement in Paramount’s $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery did not receive the court approval Thursday for which Rob Bonta and Ellison had hoped. Related Stories News Cory Booker Slams Paramount-WBD Merger Settlement But Blames Company And DOJ, Not State AGs News Block The Merger Coalition Asks Judge To Give Them Time To Formally Oppose Settlement Of Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Lawsuit Instead, with briefs expected by midnight tonight from opponents of the mega-merger and Paramount moving ahead with a $7.5 billon debt raise, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin told the assembled attorneys in a hearing today that she wanted them to address by September 29 concerns raised against the deal earlier Wednesday by longtime merger foe Booker (D-NJ). Stressing “I’ll get you a ruling in due course” (and probably stressing out Ellison as a $7 million-a-day ticking fee looms beginning October 1), the U.S. District judge also had some questions today – a lot of questions. Watch on Deadline Addressing a screen full of top firm lawyers and state AG officials during the virtual hearing, Martinez-Olguin wanted to know if the settlement and the consent decree actually “addresses the Clayton Act concerns” that were in the July 13 antitrust suit Bonta, New York’s Letitia James, and 10 other blue-state AGs filed against the merger. With the sharp realpolitiks at play from California Gov. Gavin Newsom and others for a settlement, Martinez-Olguin also had concerns that the roller-coaster deal was “not the result of collusion and was more of an arm’s length process.” Her blunt words clearly landed hard with her immediate audience of attorneys (and maybe the more than 640 others on the Zoom). Even before the judge issued her “homework” for the lawyers, the California Senior Assistant AG Paula Blizzard argued for the settlement while at the same time dismissing Paramount’s “threats” and “blackmail” to “pull out of California.” However, claiming the states were still prepared to take the whole matter to trial starting March 2, 2027 if the consent degree wasn’t approved, Blizzard also acknowledged the backlash the settlement has received over the past 72 hours since it was unveiled on Monday morning. “We absolutely recognize that this merger has engendered a large amount of controversy and commentary and feelings and concerns on a whole host of issues,” she said near the end of the nearly one-hour session. “A lot of these are outside antitrust,” Blizzard added. “They reflect the country’s very broad political and philosophical divides, concerns about the state of the news media, people’s relationship to big companies and consolidation and corporate power, and we hear those voices, we listen to those voices, we respect those voices. But at the end of the day, this is an antitrust case, and it is focused on the antitrust law.” Sen. Cory Booker Photo by Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images Booker’s six-page letter to the judge Wednesday asked for her to “subject the proposed consent decree to an independent public-interest review before entering it.” Paramount filed paperwork of its own Wednesday, just before the virtual hearing, essentially telling the Garden State senator to mind his own business. During today’s hearing, Blizzard appeared to address Booker’s concerns without saying his name. Insisted the deal was “presumptively valid,” she told Martinez-Olguin it was the result of a final surge of talks over “tens of hours, in-person video conferences, phone conferences, drafts-all the normal things you would see in a consent decree, except magnified because you had 12 attorneys general on our side.” It should be noted, New Jersey was one of the states in the ParaBros antitrust gang, and their AG Jennifer Davenport agreed to the settlement announced September 21. The iconic gates of Paramount Pictures Mark Davis/Getty Images Aware his bosses were watching, Paramount outside counsel Josh Holiann made a point of disputing the use of the term ” blackmail” when it came to timed leaks the Ellisons were serious about pulling up Melrose lot stakes, jobs and productions to redder jurisdictions (“It was a business decision …Paramount had to make.”). In a less defensive posture, the Latham & Watkins attorney also promised the judge the penalties in the settlement would now “keep our feet to the fire.” Still, With Para and WBD lawyers Holian, Beth Wilkinson, Jeffrey Kessler, Daniel Petrocelli and Marguerite Sullivan on-screen (some clearly working on something else), it was mainly Blizzard who took point trying to sell Martinez-Olguin on the deal — and it sure seemed like a hard sell. “We believe we have five years of remedies that will remove the competitive concerns we see the harms we see and preserve competition,” Blizzard said. With nodded agreement from Paramount attorneys, Blizzard stressed the divestment of some cable channels if necessary and Miramax and other clauses in the settlement is “the best solution” other than blocking “it completely?” Sounding very much like she was arguing for Paramount, Blizzard ventured into some hard Hollywood realities to give the deal context. “Obviously, in this case, Warner Bros originally said it was going to sell its assets,” Blizzard said. “So, if we block this merger, there will probably be another one, perhaps before Your Honor, in a year or so, and is that the best solution for the markets to preserve the competition that the Clayton Act requested.” Kneecapped to some extent by Zoom-wide technical glitches that initially prevented some of the attorneys and state government officials from participating in the virtual hearing, the hearing on the now delayed settlement sign-off was delayed itself by nearly 15 minutes. Now, with that ticking fee clock ticking, ParaBros closure is also once again delayed — at least until Monday at noon. Well played Sen. Booker. ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event More from this Story Arc Paramount WB September 24, 2026 David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi As CEO’s Soon-To-Be Owned CNN Banned From White House Event September 24, 2026 Dealmakers React To Paramount-WBD Settlement: “Tech Has Won” View All Story Arc Read More About: 8 Comments

articles.title: David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi As CEO’s Soon-To-Be Owned CNN Banned From White House, Again
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic ParaBros Foes Urge Court To Reject Settlement In Midnight Filings: “This Merger Lessens Competition” Disney Legal Chief Warns Of “Hard Choices” & “Much Smaller Organization” Coming As Company Layoffs Loom No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” View All September 24, 2026 5:17pm Story Arc Donald Trump and Melania Trump greet China's Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan to the White House Getty Reporters from CNN aren’t allowed access to the White House’s state dinner or guest arrivals Thursday, but the news outlet’s soon-to-be owner will be breaking bread with China’s president Xi Jinping and Donald Trump , along with a gaggle of tech bosses. Striving to get a settlement in Paramount ‘s $111 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery approved by a federal judge, CEO David Ellison is among the invited guests to tonight’s superpower sit-down. A past donor to Democrats, the son of Oracle founder and close Trump ally Larry Ellison has become close to the MAGA administration in his pursuit of Paramount last year and more recently WBD. That closeness to Trump has proved a major concern to opponents of the ParaBros mega-deal, especially when it comes to the Bari Weiss-run CBS News and, down the line, CNN . Related Stories News CNN Says It Was Denied Trump White House Access To Cover Arrivals At State Dinner For Chinese President Xi Jinping Legal No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” From left: Elon Musk , Mark Zuckerberg, Jeff Bezos and Sam Altman Getty Images The tech-leaning Ellison will be among a band of brothers with Elon Musk, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg, Google co-founder Sergey Brin, TikTok’s Jeff Yass, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang and Microsoft’s Satya Nadella at tonight’s White House event. Along with the titans of traditional industry Trump loves to surround himself with like Boeing CEO Kelly Ortberg, JPMorgan’s Jamie Dimon and Dell’s Michael Dell, Apple’s former CEO Tim Cook and Amazon founder and Washington Post owner Jeff Bezos will be partaking of the three-course meal. Watch on Deadline Chinese officials, White House senior staff, Cabinet members, Trump offspring, congressional GOP leaders and several members of the Supreme Court also are in attendance. Equally unsurprisingly, Fox News ‘ Jesse Watters, Laura Ingraham (called an “American television presenter”) and Bret Baier are on the state dinner guest list with their respective spouses. Banned from the White House by Trump last week, CNN, MS Now and Politico took the administration to court , where Judge Timothy Kelly ordered the outlets be re-credentialed — which they were for a while today and then tonight they were not.

articles.title: CNN & MS Now Say They Were Denied White House Access To Cover Trump’s State Dinner For Chinese President Xi Jinping
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted CNN & MS Now Say They Were Denied White House Access To Cover Trump’s State Dinner For Chinese President Xi Jinping Judge Tosses Donald Trump’s Lawsuit Against Des Moines Register And Pollster Ann Selzer Lawmakers Introduce Bill For 20% Federal Film & TV Incentive — Read The Bill View All September 24, 2026 5:27pm U.S. Marines stand guard as they await the arrival of guests for a state dinner where U.S. President Donald Trump hosts Chinese President Xi Jinping in the East Room of the White House. Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images UPDATED with White House response: Shortly after CNN said that it was denied access to cover the arrivals at the White House State Dinner for Chinese President Xi Jinping tonight, MS NOW announced that it, too, had been barred. The news came on the same day a federal judge ordered the White House to restore hard passes to the networks’ journalists and those of and Politico. Related Stories News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Reporters Allowed Back Into White House After Judge’s Order Sidelining Trump Ban News Reporters Committee And Dozens Of Media Outlets File Legal Brief Urging Judge To End Trump’s Ban On CNN, Politico And MS Now The coverage at the North Portico was scheduled to be open to pre-credentialed media, a wider scope of reporters and photographers than the White House press pool. CNN White House correspondent Kristen Holmes said that they were told that their credential to cover the event was only for a camera and audio, not an editorial presence. She had requested that she and her producer attend. Watch on Deadline “Again, no editorial presence, just a camera and audio, which certainly seems like a reaction to President Trump saying that he wanted the CNN coverage of the event,” Holmes said. The White House said on its rapid response account that it was a “pre-credentialed event,” and “contrary to what the fake news wants you the believe, they don’t just get to have free rein into every part of the White House, every event, and every press call.” The exclusion came after U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly ordered that credentials for CNN, Politico and MS NOW be restored, ending Trump’s five-day ban of the outlets from the White House grounds. The outlets returned to the White House around noon. Then, hours later, Trump complained that CNN and MS NOW were not covering the state visit. Trump claimed that the networks “refused to cover one of the Biggest and Most Beautiful Events to take place in many years, the arrival at the White House of the Highly Respected President of China, Xi Jinping, and his beautiful wife, Madam Peng. The event was magnificent — Actually made for Television but, because they’re Fake News, and because they knew how good it would be, they didn’t want credit to be given to ‘TRUMP,’ they refused to be there. That’s why they have such poor Ratings. Tonight’s State Dinner at the White House, for President Xi, will be spectacular!” In fact, network correspondents said that they were not able to get access to the White House on Thursday morning. And after the White House pulled CNN from the TV pool on Monday, the other four networks in the pool declined to replace them in the rotation. That has meant a dearth of video images from the White House, as TV pool coverage has yet to resume. The latest exclusion does not appear to be addressed in Kelly’s order. Rather, it is an issue about access to a particular event on White House grounds. The press office sends out notice to reporters of events that are open to “pre-credentialed media,” accommodating a much wider scope of credentialed reporters than those restricted to the White House pool. Those who want to attend RSVP, and the White House staff then inform reporters and photographers if they have clearance to go. Last year, after Trump barred the Associated Press from pool access to areas like the Oval Office as well as larger “pre-credentialed media” events in locations like the East Room, the news organization sued. In an initial ruling on a preliminary injunction, a federal judge sided with the AP, concluding that the White House could not bar outlets from press events based on viewpoint. The D.C. Circuit, though, concluded that the White House could exclude the AP from smaller spaces, like the Oval Office and Cabinet Room, but distinguished those areas from larger White House locations like the East Room, where the district judge’s order remains in effect. ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event Read More About: 5 Comments

articles.title: Robert Pattinson Thinks Matt Reeves’ ‘The Batman’ Would Be “Tough” To Fit Into James Gunn’s DCU

Warner Bros./Courtesy Everett Collection/Jonathan Olley/Warner Bros./Courtesy Everett Collection With sequels in the Batman and Superman franchises on the horizon, a DC team-up between the Dark Knight and the Man of Steel doesn’t seem to be in the immediate future. Robert Pattinson admitted it “would be kind of tough” to make his version of Bruce Wayne in Matt Reeves ‘ The Batman movies fit into James Gunn ‘s DCU , which he launched with last year’s Superman . “I think it would be kind of tough to have this version of Bruce outside of [Reeves’] world,” he told LADbible . “It’s one of the only characters I guess because of the length of the shoots but also it’s such a specific kind of [style], the tone of it gets inside you.” Related Stories News ‘Superman’ Sequel ‘Man Of Tomorrow’ Wraps Filming: “Truly A Joyful Experience” News Matt Reeves Confirms ‘Batman II’ Filming This Year After Release Date Delay – Golden Globes Red Carpet Pattinson added, “I remember that happened to me the last time I did it, it took a while. You’re just in the dark, the whole time. Both mood-wise and light-wise, I can’t see anything for like months. It does affect you like you feel strange afterwards.” Watch on Deadline Gunn revealed last July that the script for The Batman: Part II was finished , following several delays. Last August, a letter to Warner Bros. Discovery’s shareholders revealed that filming on the sequel would begin filming in the spring . Warner Bros. recently pushed the movie’s release date to Feb. 18, 2028 as Reeves continued to tease the sequel with camera test footage of Pattinson in costume. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ Sets Brooklyn Week With Guests Mamdani, Springsteen, Fellow Late-Night Hosts & More Hannah Einbinder Speaks Out After UN Arrest, Calls For U.S. To “Bring An End” To Israel Attacks On Gaza Robert Pattinson Thinks Matt Reeves’ ‘The Batman’ Would Be “Tough” To Fit Into James Gunn’s DCU View All September 24, 2026 6:23pm Hannah Einbinder JC Olivera/PMC Following her arrest Thursday at a demonstration outside the United Nations General Assembly, Hannah Einbinder doesn’t want her message to get lost in the headlines. The Emmy-winning Hacks star urged the U.S. government to “bring an end” to Israel’s attacks on Gaza after she was detained for protesting Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ‘s arrival at the UN building in New York. “If the pictures of my friends and me getting arrested in protest of Netanyahu’s shameful visit to New York draw attention to anything, let it be to the devastating genocidal war Israel is waging against the people of Palestine and Southern Lebanon — to the settler attacks, the home demolitions, the bombing of people as they sleep; to the crimes that happen every SINGLE day but garner almost no international press coverage,” she began in a statement on her Instagram Story. Related Stories News Hannah Einbinder, Susan Sarandon Among Protesters Detained Outside UN Amid Netanyahu Arrival; Dozens Of Delegates Walk Out During Israeli PM’s Speech News Macklemore Launches Free Palestine Tour; U.S. Dates To Be Announced “The U.S. government has the power to bring an end to all of this killing, pillaging, and land theft, yet instead it chooses to welcome the butcher of Gaza with open arms. The fact that the orchestrator of all this bloodshed is roaming freely in our cities is an indictment of BOTH REPUBLICANS AND DEMOCRATS who enable and protect architects of genocide like Netanyahu,” Einbinder continued. “Let us not mistake the spectacle for the story: genocide is the headline, and it is time for it to end.” Watch on Deadline Einbinder and Susan Sarandon were among as many as 100 anti-war protesters detained while blocking Bibi’s entrance to the UN, where he spoke with global leaders at the UN General Assembly. Also present at the demonstration were Cynthia Nixon, Elliot Page, Chelsea Manning, Glennon Doyle, Sarah Sherman, Mary Beth Barone, Indya Moore and Caleb Hearon, protesting Netanyahu and the ongoing strikes on Gaza in the Israel-Hamas conflict. “Free, free Palestine ! articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Magic Of Returning To ‘Big Bang’ Stage, Going Multi-Cam In Meta Season 1 Finale & Season 2 Plans
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Magic Of Returning To ‘Big Bang’ Stage, Going Multi-Cam In Meta Season 1 Finale & Season 2 Plans ‘The Beast In Me’ Renewed For Season 2 With Claire Danes Reprising Role; Howard Gordon Back With Netflix Overall Deal David Oyelowo & Viola Prettejohn To Star In ‘The Girl With The Dragon Tattoo’ TV Series For Sky View All September 24, 2026 6:25pm Story Arc (L-R): Lauren Lapkus, Kevin Sussman, John Ross Bowie & Brian Posehn in 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' S1 finale HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about the Season 1 finale “Spoiler: Filmed In Front Of a Live Studio Audience” of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . The Big Bang Theory single-camera spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe went full-circle in the Season 1 finale by turning multi-camera and returning to the stage where the original series was filmed. After getting trapped in a comic book in the penultimate episode, the multiverse-hopping quartet of Stuart (Kevin Sussman), Bert (Brian Posehn), Denise (Lauren Lapkus) and Kripke (John Ross Bowie) found themself in a multi-camera sitcom in the finale, complete with a laugh track. Related Stories News How 'All American' Survived Long Enough To End Its 8-Season Run As The Lone YA Series Left At The CW: An Oral History Agencies Ari Emanuel On His New Memoir, Nikki Finke, Talking To Trump, AI's Upside & The Hollywood Exec He Hates The Most And, in the trippiest moment in a season chockfull of meta references, in the finale, Stuart, Denise, Bert and Kripke witnessed a curtain call for a taping of the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe sitcom where they see identical versions of themselves played by the real-life stars of the HBO Max series: Sussman, Posehn, Lapkus and Bowie. Watch on Deadline Still shocked, the four walked out of the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe soundstage, which is revealed to be Stage 25 on the Warner Bros. lot that housed Big Bang. (The stage is currently home to CBS spinoff Georgie & Mandy’s First Marriage, which co-creator Lorre and Prady executive produce.) “So now what?,” Denise asked in the final seconds of the episode. “I don’t know but I’ve got to believe that the answer is out there somewhere,” Stuart said in a X-Files -esque “The truth is out there” manner, prompting Bert to follow up with “In Burbank?” and Kevin to reply, “or Studio City?,” a reference to the city Warner Bros. is based in and the neighboring area. The finale’s back-and-forth shift between single- and multi-camera involved Stuart Fails To Save the Universe building a multi-camera version of Stuart’s comic book like the one used in Big Bang on the Universal lot where the Warner Bros. TV-produced Big Bang spinoff films its interiors and some exteriors. (The final exterior scene was filmed outside of the real Stage 25 on the Warners lot.) The episode paid homage to the mothership series in other ways too, including incorporating Big Bang ‘s signature animated atom transition, complete with the whooshing sound, using its audience warm-up Mark Sweet, who had worked with Lorre since his 1997 ABC comedy Dharma & Greg, and having the characters sit around a coffee table eating takeouts. In an interview with Deadline, the Stuart Fails creators/executive producers Zak Penn , who comes from genre background, and sitcom veterans Chuck Lorre and Bill Prady , break down how they pulled off the single-camera/multi-camera transitions, how it was filming outside Stage 25, the various Big Bang easter eggs and that ending (where exactly is the answer?). They also address the several digs at CBS, broadcast television and multi-camera sitcoms, the black consciousness adversary introduced in the finale and its implied alliance with Kyle (Ryan Cartwright). The trio gives some clues about the recently picked up Season 2, which already is being written, including when it would premiere. How ‘Stuart’ Brought ‘Big Bang’ (& Its Laugh) Back DEADLINE: Where did the idea to have our heroes be in a multi-camera sitcom come about? Did you want to pay homage to Big Bang? PENN : Yeah, that was definitely part of it. These guys [Lorre and Prady] have a lot to say about it, so it was pretty fertile ground. I don’t think we said at the beginning of the season, we must comment on the sitcom, that wasn’t a goal. LORRE : If our characters on their adventure, on their journey, could be trapped into a comic book, they could certainly be trapped into a sitcom. I mean, we’ve gone past any boundaries of rationale, and this is a spectacularly cool thing to do, let’s do it. Can we explain it? We’re gonna try, we’re certainly going to try. DEADLINE: You used both single-camera and multi-camera versions of the comic book set in the episode. For the multi-cam one that you had to build, did you use any pieces of the original Big Bang set? PRADY : We didn’t use the original sets, but you’re right, we had to build. The only way to do this, because a multi-cam set looks different than a single-cam set, is we had to build the set two times. We had our single-cam comic book store that we’ve been using all season with four walls and a ceiling, and on the next stage over at Universal, they built the multi-cam version of that set and the multi-cam version of the stockroom. But they also had to build the interior of a multi-cam soundstage, they had to build audience risers, the sound booth and the lighting booth that sits behind the audience, the camera alley, all of those features of multi-cam stage, they had to build. Our amazing production team actually went over to Georgie and Mandy, which was in production at the time, so that they could copy it and and get it right. And it was also a change for the director of photography. The camera moves in multi-cam are completely different, the cameras go onto dollies, you have dolly moves that don’t exist in single-cam, and all of that had to be duplicated. So it was a pretty, pretty complicated task. DEADLINE: How many scenes did you have to film twice in both formats? There were scenes that switched between single- and multi-cam. PENN: Probably one third, two thirds, maybe more single-cam. Every time you see that, we had to do it twice, we had to shoot it on both stages, but there wasn’t a live studio audience there for that part of it. The live studio audience was only there when we needed to see the live studio audience. LORRE : For the curtain call. PENN : Because it would have been so boring to watch these little snippets of scenes, it just wouldn’t have made sense to anyone. DEADLINE: Bert makes a comment on the show that the laugh is fake. You just said that the live studio audience was not used for the actual taping of the scenes beyond the curtain call, so the spoiler in the episode’s title is not accurate. PRADY : It’s pretty perverse. One of the things that we battled forever on Big Bang Theory was people saying that this was a laugh track when it was a live studio audience. So here, in fact, the laughter that you’re hearing during the scene, the laugh that Kripke is hearing, those are old laughs from a The Big Bang Theory audience eight or nine years ago. Yes, all of those ironies. (L-R): Ryan Cartwright, Brian Posehn, Kevin Sussman, Lauren Lapkus & John Ross Bowie in ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ S1 finale HBO Max Dinging CBS As “Old TV Thing”, Sitcoms As “Void” DEADLINE: Speaking of ironies, the Stuart Fails To Save the Universe sitcom within the series is promoted as “Coming to CBS this fall.” Is this just a line of dialogue, or is there some truth here? Can you license this show to CBS, home of Big Bang and all other spinoffs, for a linear run? LORRE : That’s a question you’d have to ask HBO. I wouldn’t think so. It was just an opportunity to make a cheap joke about the end of network television. DEADLINE: Yes, the punchline to that was Kyle asking “What is CBS?”, and Kripke explaining it as an “old TV thing,” a dig at broadcast and CBS. Did you write that, Chuck? They’re still employing you. LORRE : I want to bite the hand that feeds me, Elvis Costello. DEADLINE: There was another shot, about a meaningless void and sitcoms being the same thing. Is this how you all feel about multi-cam comedies these days? LORRE : Not at all. No, it was a joke, Nellie. It was an opportunity to try and make the audience laugh. PRADY : It’s certainly what Kripke thinks. LORRE : It might be what Kripke thinks of situation comedies, but the history of this genre is just rich with genius, going back to Lucy and Norman Lear and Cheers and Friends and Frasier. It’s ridiculous to try and put down a genre that has done such great work over decades. PRADY : We’re in awe of the genre. LORRE : It’s much harder to do this than it is to shoot a little movie. It’s much harder to make 200 people laugh, even if they’re related to you. DEADLINE: Chuck, any plans to do another multi-cam sitcom? I saw CBS Entertainment President Amy Reisenbach recently, and she said that the door is wide open for you . LORRE : That’s very sweet of her. I love that woman. I’ve been doing this an awful long time, and Amy is just terrific. She’s been a really big supporter of Georgie and Mandy out of the gate, she’s been nothing but helpful and supportive of us trying to put on a show. DEADLINE: But no current plans for you to do a new sitcom? LORRE : No. My current plans are to take a nap right after we’re done talking. (L-R): Lauren Lapkus, Kevin Sussman, Brian Posehn & John Ross Bowie in ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ S1 finale Behind The Curtain Call DEADLINE: The level of meta play in the finale — I don’t know if mushrooms or something else was involved in coming up with the sitcom idea, but the idea to have… LORRE : It’s not drugs, it is called imagination. It’s something that will go away shortly with the advent of AI sitcoms. But, for the time being, it’s making sh*t up is what’s happening. DEADLINE: But the idea to have the characters looking at actors carrying their real names playing the same characters; talk about how this whole thing made sense. PENN : This is a place that we hadn’t gone, and going there seemed kind of scary, like, how are we going to make this work? And then, how are we going to write our way out of it? I think that was the approach the whole season is what something we could do that would be funny, but also, let’s not just do oh, and now they go to a universe where everybody’s a bird or whatever, like trying to come up with something to top what we had done, and this seemed like the place to go. DEADLINE: Did Brian pay extra because everyone got a straightforward intro when Mark Sweet brought out the cast, he’s the only one who got “hilariously funny”? PRADY : So the cast is allowed to bribe us, and we have a whole set. PENN : Yeah, Brian paid us, you’re right. Brian gave us $1,500, and the rest of the cast gave us like 100 bucks, or someone gave us wine. We couldn’t split it. That was Mark Sweet, right? Whatever he chose to say. PRADY : We were writing the kinds of things Mark Sweet said, which, when we sat down to write it, Chuck and I had heard it so many times, we channeled Mark Sweet, who’s playing himself as the audience warm-up guy, without even thinking about it. LORRE : It was really easy. We’ve been listening to Mark since 1996, since Dharma & Greg . Thirty years, he’s been doing the same act. PRADY : He’s got turns of phrase like, “you know him, you love him.” There’s a whole bunch of stuff that we just know. It’s years of listening to Mark and literally writing what we’ve heard him say. (L-R): John Ross Bowie, Lauren Lapkus, Kevin Sussman & Brian Posehn in ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ S1 finale HBO Max The Magic Of Stage 25 DEADLINE: You filmed the final scene outside of WB’s Stage 25, where Big Bang was shot. How was that? LORRE : That was a fun night. DEADLINE: Was it really rainy, or did you make everything wet? PENN : No, that’s a classic wet-town. LORRE : I loved how we ended it. It’s a really delicate thing to bring a season to an end, or a series to an end, which we’ve certainly been through. It’s a real lot of hoping and wishing and praying that you get it right. I thought we brought the 10 episodes to a wonderful — hopefully, a reason to anticipate Season 2 as well as pleasurable to watch. PENN : There was a bit of magic that night, watching the actors walk out through that door and onto the lot. It definitely felt there was something in the air. LORRE : Yeah, something special happened that night. PRADY : What was really strange that night, because we were shot at Stage 25, which was obviously the Big Bang stage, and walking in and using that stage, like using that as a place to stand and as a place to use the restroom and stuff. I found it very surreal, personally, to walk onto stage 25 with all that muscle memory of the years of Big Bang. 12 years there. The Answer, The Adversary & ‘Young Leonard’ DEADLINE: Speaking of the ending, the final line “I’ve got to believe that the answer is out there.” Was that an X-Files reference? LORRE : It does echo a little bit of The X-Files , doesn’t it? “The answer is out there, in Burbank, or maybe Studio City.” Yeah, it is something of a variation on that, I suppose, I hadn’t really thought about it. PRADY : Not on purpose. LORRE : Just a chance to say Burbank, because whenever you get a chance to say Burbank, you should. DEADLINE: So where is the answer? Is it in Burbank, in Studio City or somewhere else? LORRE : The answer is in Episode 1 of Season 2. DEADLINE: The adversary, that whole swirly consciousness thing we saw at the end, do we know what it is? Don’t tell me the answer is going to be in 201. PENN : The answer will be in 201. DEADLINE: Is Ryan’s character working for the adversary? Because the thing said to him “I gave you one job.” Is Kyle a bad guy? PENN : That version of those two characters work for the adversary. PRADY : But not all versions. PENN : But not the other ones you’ve seen that season. And then there’s another group led by, as far as you know, led by Stuart Prime. That’s the Stuart who shows up periodically to give them clues or hints to try to help them on their way. DEADLINE: Would that be a major point in Season 2 , who’s behind this? PENN : Unquestionably, it’s going to be dealt with. We didn’t want to spend the whole season doing a bunch of mythology shows where we break down every single thing about what’s going on. We just wanted to set some stuff up. LORRE : The truth is out there. DEADLINE: The final shot includes banners for Two and a Half Women and Young Leonard . Chuck, were there spoofs of any of your other sitcoms’ titles that you considered and discarded? LORRE : I don’t think so. I think, just the idea that we’re not quite in the universe where we started this series is the implication of those posters. PRADY : It’s not quite our world. LORRE : It’s close. PRADY : But also in this world, Stuart is a multi-cam as opposed to in our world where it’s a single-cam. So we wanted to show that we were two or three degrees off of our universe. DEADLINE: Two and a Half Women and Young Leonard are not bad ideas. Have Warner Bros. TV executive reached out about possibly doing them as shows? LORRE : No, they haven’t come to us with anything like that, nor should they. (L-R): Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus in ‘Stuart Fails To Save the Universe’ S1 finale HBO Max Season 2: Everything We Know DEADLINE: You are in the writers’ room, right? Have you already mapped out Season 2? LORRE : We started working last week on fleshing out Season 2, which hopefully, I think production begins in January or February. Like Season 1, we’re hoping to write all the episodes before we start, giving all the departments a lot of lead time to do the remarkable stuff they did in Season 1, which was truly benefited also by us being allowed to stay in Los Angeles and do this here with the best crews in the world. PRADY : Yeah, it’s worth saying in every episode that we had the most amazing production team: sets, costumes, props, art direction, photography, lighting, sound. Every person on that stage was a gift, and everyone’s coming back. LORRE : Yeah, everybody’s coming back. One of the little miracles that happened was we got a tax break from the state of California, which allowed us to stay here, stay in Los Angeles, which allowed us to have the best crews. DEADLINE: Can you do the show on yearly cadence? There are a lot of special effects but can Season 2 premiere next summer or next fall? When will it be ready? LORRE : We’re hoping certainly by next fall. We’re shooting to also participate in Comic-Con again next year. We did it this year, and it was great, it was a great way to launch the first season. When the show actually will debut on HBO, we don’t know. But hopefully, we’ll at least have an episode or two finished to do Comic Con. PENN : It’s not going to be like two years between seasons. It’s going to come out next year. LORRE : Next year, yeah. DEADLINE: Will Season 2 be similar in structure, the gang going to a new universe each episode or will you revisit some of the more popular worlds from the first season? LORRE : We’ll try and put together 10 great episodes, and that’s the goal, to not run dry. PRADY : You don’t have to follow a strict rule. LORRE : You can return to a universe, there’s no rule against that. We’re not bound to say we couldn’t go back to some place they’ve already been if there was a great reason to do so. PRADY : Right. We don’t sit here and say okay, well we have to do fan service, so more centaurs. But if more centaurs is really funny and has a story that can be told, then there’ll be more centaurs. But we make fun of our own mythology as we’re going, so I think there’s no real rules about what we’re going to do. We just try to do something that’s interesting. DEADLINE: Will you also keep the idea of original Big Bang stars coming back? And I assume that the characters of Leonard, Howard, and Sheldon will stay off limits because if one of them shows up, he will fix the machine, and its show will be over. LORRE : We’re hopeful that we can have some guest starring opportunities again in Season 2, but we haven’t figured that out quite yet. It was a lot of fun working with Mayim [Bialik] and Melissa [Rauch], Kunal [Nayyar], Kaley [Cuoco]. Having them do something that they never did on The Big Bang Theory , giving them an opportunity to stretch a little bit, that’s been built into this from the beginning, and I hope we can keep it going. DEADLINE: Is there any chance of seeing different versions of Jim Parsons’ Sheldon, Johnny Galecki’s Leonard or Simon Helberg’s Howard ? PRADY : Tune in next season. LORRE : There’s always a chance. We’re not going to limit ourselves as to cameos. If it’s possible and it can be done, great. That was a lot of fun for us, and I think it was a lot of fun for the folks who came and played with us for a couple of days. DEADLINE: What’s the verdict on the custom opening credits? Have fans liked it, skipped it, didn’t care? Will you keep that in Season 2? LORRE : I haven’t talked to fans recently but we enjoyed it, we thought it was funny. PRADY : Our families liked it. LORRE : We thought it was adding value to the show to have different credits, different opening titles every week and break some rules with what we’re used to seeing on all television. PRADY : Maybe we’ll mix it up and, if we can come up with something even crazier, maybe we’ll do that. But don’t quote me on that. DEADLINE: Length-wise, will you keep the episodes brisk and short again next season? [Half of the Season 1 episodes, including the finale, were 15-18 min each ] LORRE : As long as they need to be. And I’m keeping my fingers crossed that some of these shorter episodes we can get on Quibi. PRADY : That has been the goal from the beginning. LORRE : Because kids want to watch these shows on their phones while they’re at the supermarket. That was pitched to me. DEADLINE: Quibi was ahead of its time, let’s just say that. LORRE (sarcastically): Sure. Lessons Learned DEADLINE: What did you learn from the first season? Anything that you want to do differently in Season 2? PENN : I learned a lot about sitcoms personally. LORRE : Special effects take a long time. PRADY : Be patient with special effects. LORRE : Be very patient. I had panic attacks all through Season 1 that some of the special effects that we were asking for were not going to work. They all did but it took time. It’s an arduous process to build stuff that doesn’t exist. PENN : That was the part I was comfortable with. LORRE : He is very comfortable with it; Zak said, It’ll be fine, it’ll be fine. Just let them, It’s not finished yet. It was the thing you hear over and over and over again but it was really gratifying when that stuff works. PENN : There wasn’t a lot that didn’t work, honestly. People might like some episodes more than others. LORRE : That’s inevitable. PENN : But normally, in doing a sci-fi show, you would find like, oh, we couldn’t pull this off, but that never happened to us. I mean, everything got pulled off. The crew, we say it over and over again, but they nailed it. There was never an episode where we walked in and said, Okay, the departments couldn’t really make this work. Let’s write around it. Never happened. LORRE : It took quite a bit for us to figure out how to do the falling through the void sequence, but we got there. There was some trial and error because we didn’t know. It’s one thing to write on a laptop, the character Bert and and Kripke are falling through an endless void, it’s easy to write down. It’s much more difficult to make it a reality, and I think ultimately we got there. DEADLINE: Uh-huh. Ask your actors, they told me they were traumatized filming that scene . PRADY : Well, that was another benefit. LORRE : Traumatized is part of show business. PRADY : I do know that the actors, in all their interviews, kept saying there was a lot more running, they found a lot more running than they thought. articles.title: Disney Legal Chief Warns Of “Hard Choices” & “Much Smaller Organization” Coming As Company Layoffs Loom
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic ParaBros Foes Urge Court To Reject Settlement In Midnight Filings: “This Merger Lessens Competition” Disney Legal Chief Warns Of “Hard Choices” & “Much Smaller Organization” Coming As Company Layoffs Loom No ParaBros Decision Today As Judge Delays Settlement Sign-Off; CA AG’s Office Insists Deal “Not The Result Of Collusion” View All September 24, 2026 7:40pm Disney Chief Legal Officer Horacio Gutierrez, WDC logo Disney EXCLUSIVE: An end-of-week memo from Disney ‘s Chief Legal and Global Affairs Officer has given an blunt warning that layoffs are coming amidst a “transformation process” that includes “automating certain workflows by leveraging the latest technologies.” Without actually saying that AI is taking over or that job losses are on the horizon, the memo by Horacio Gutierrez strongly implies that. Sent out at noon on Sept. 18 to the LGA department, which counts less than 1,000 members globally, the missive has taken on a life of its own. It is being circulated among the Disney rank and file, with many fearing that the unsentimental message to LGA staffers applies to them too as they are bracing for rounds of layoffs, expected to begin as early as next week. Unspecified cuts within the LGA department are not connected to the next round of cuts, I hear. Related Stories News Ex-Disney CEO Bob Chapek Blames Bob Iger For Ouster In New Memoir News Disney Hikes Price Of Disney+ And Hulu Streaming Plans The memo has also been shared throughout the entertainment law community in L.A., NYC and DC. Watch on Deadline Noting that the Mouse House’s “legal, government relations, operations, and others, are going through their own reinvention as technology reshapes how work gets done, and the operating models that underpin those professions,” the multi-tasked Gutierrez says he’s “taking a dispassionate look at every aspect of how we do our work, so we can do it in a more efficient and cost-effective manner.” Gutierrez joined Disney from Spotify in late 2021 under Bob Chapek ‘s short-lived reign as CEO. Replacing Disney veteran Alan Braverman in the top in-house legal job, Gutierrez was one of few key Chapek lieutenants to keep his job when Bob Iger returned as CEO in late 2022. “Obviously, this will require hard choices about where and how we deploy our resources and investments, including our staffing investments and how we work will look different in the months and years ahead,” Gutierrez writes in the memo, adding, “LGA will be a much smaller organization than it is today, and some of you will personally be affected by decisions we make in this process. As a result, we’ll have to consider a whole range of new models for different workloads, including automating certain workflows by leveraging the latest technologies, moving to self-service models where appropriate, engaging alternative legal providers and others, and new expanded share services, even outsourcing.” Proving once again that timing is everything in this town, Gutierrez’s memo came on the same day that Disney unveiled Karandeep Anand as the company’s very first Chief Technology Officer. The ex- Character.AI , CEO will report directly to Disney boss Josh D’Amaro. With the most recent rounds of job cuts hitting Disney in April and then July, execs made no secret on the Aug. 5 earnings call that more are to come. To that, Gutierrez’s email also came as the deadline was looming for qualifying longtime Disney executives to take the company’s voluntary early retirement offer, first unveiled in August by EVP and Chief People Officer Sonia Coleman. The process was always expected to be followed by involuntary layoffs. Cutting to the chase in his September 18 memo and invoking the name of D’Amaro, Gutierrez goes on to tell his staff that “when teams work smarter, Disney can serve more fans at lower costs, freeing up capital to reinvest in the content, guest experiences, and technology infrastructure that keep the company out in front. “Josh’s vision is of a Disney that succeeds in a changing market by breaking internal walls and embracing technology to amplify what makes it great, not by clinging to the way things always have been done.” Disney would not comment on Gutierrez’s memo or on a timeline and scope of the upcoming job cuts when contacted Thursday by Deadline. articles.title: Oscars: Denmark Selects May El-Toukhy’s ‘Woman Unknown’ For International Feature Film Race
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac San Sebastián Industry Awards: Juan Sebastián Mesa & Tatiana Huezo Among Big Winners Mikel Gurrea’s ‘Saints’ Lands Distribution Deals Ahead Of San Sebastián Competition Debut — First Look Trailer Jesse Eisenberg Talks Writing ‘The Debut’ Specifically For His “Favorite Actor And Actress” Julianne Moore & Paul Giamatti — San Sebastián View All September 25, 2026 1:59am 'Woman Unknown' TrustNordisk Denmark has selected May el-Toukhy ’s Golden Lion-winning title Woman Unknown as its entry for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards. The post-World War II, Denmark-set psychological drama stars Mathilde Arcel as a young nanny and housemaid, who is about to marry her wealthy older employer, a widower still haunted by the memory of his late wife. Amid the jubilation of the liberation, there is a darker side, as women who fraternized with German soldiers are tracked down and brutally publicly shamed. A painful secret from Marie’s past threatens to catch up with her. Related Stories Festivals May El-Toukhy On Venice Golden Lion Win & Riccardo Scamarcio Remembers Jeremy Thomas -- Winners Press Conference Festivals May El-Toukhy's 'Woman Unknown' Wins Golden Lion For Best Film At Venice Film Festival - Full Winners List With the Academy’s submission changes, Woman Unknown was already eligible in the international category after it won the Golden Lion in Venice. Mathilde Arcel also went home with the Volpi Cup in Venice for her leading performance. Watch on Deadline El-Toukhy directed from a screenplay she co-wrote with Maren Louise Käehne. The picture was produced by Mikael Rieks for Nordisk Film Production A/S in co-production with Nafta Films, Nordisk Film Production Sweden and Film i Väst with support from The Danish Film Institute, Eurimages – Council of Europe, Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, Riga City Council, Nordisk Film & TV Fund, DR, The Swedish Film Institute, SVT, LIAA, Riga Film Fund, TrustNordisk and Zentropa. Nordisk Film Distribution is distributing in Denmark, while TrustNordisk is handling international sales. Trust Nordisk announced fresh sales on the title following Venice. The film has sold to Memento for France, as well as Spain (Karma Films), Poland (Best Film), Portugal (Nitrato Filmes), the former Yugoslavia (MCF Megacom Film) and Bulgaria (Beta Film). Previously announced deals include Italy (Lucky Red), Benelux (September Films), Latin America (California Filmes), Greece (Neo Films), and the Baltics (Estin Film). articles.title: Tales Of Syria’s Disappeared; Lebanese Wartime Adoption & Palestinian Mental Health Set For Cinemed-Aflamuna Project Incubator
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Tales Of Syria’s Disappeared; Lebanese Wartime Adoption & Palestinian Mental Health Set For Cinemed-Aflamuna Project Incubator Netflix-Acquired Animation ‘In Waves’ To Open The American French Film Festival In L.A. CAPA Deputy Director Unveils Sean Connery Doc; Talks Mission To Expand French Company’s International Reach View All September 25, 2026 2:26am Cinemed- Aflamuna pitching session Cinemed France ’s Montpellier Mediterranean Film Festival, also known as Cinemed , and Beirut-based Arab cinema platform Aflamuna have unveiled the selection for their fifth project incubator event, which will take place within the framework of the festival in October. The initiative, bannered the Aflamuna x Cinemed Encounters and supporting Arab filmmakers from across the Middle East and Africa, will showcase seven projects. They include the documentary Disappeared following five Syrian women as they come to terms with the forced disappearance of their sons and husbands under the Bashar Al-Asaad regime, without ever giving up the search for their fate. Related Stories News CAPA Deputy Director Unveils Sean Connery Doc; Talks Mission To Expand French Company's International Reach Festivals The Guardian To Offer 'NAZA' For Free On Website From November After Theatrical Run & Is Exploring Ways To Show Doc In Israel & Palestinian Territories The work taps into a raw subject in Syria where at least 177,000 people remain missing having been forcibly disappeared by the regime from 2011 onwards. Watch on Deadline It is the latest film from Palestinian, Syria-raised director Anas Zawahri, who made waves this year with My Memory Is Full of Ghosts , revisiting the war-ravaged Syrian city of Homs in 2023, prior to the overthrowing of Al-Assad in December 2024. Further projects in the selection include Palestinian Wisam Al Jafari’s The Hearse to the Final House of Happiness , about a mental patient who is granted a brief leave from the institution where he is being cared for to attend a family wedding. It is Al Jafari’s debut feature after award-winning shorts Ambience (2019), By The Sea (2021), Cinema, Mon Amour (2026.) Hanna Attallah is producing under his Route 243 banner after credits including Thank You for Banking with Us by Laila Abbas, which played multiple festivals including the BFI London Film Festival. Cinemed and Aflamuna launched their joint project incubator in 2021, with the support of France’s National Cinema Center (CNC), to support filmmakers in 22 Arab territories in the Middle East and Africa, Under the initiative the participants attend Cinemed’s professional days, running from October 20 to 22 this year, where they French and international professionals and decision-makers for potential partnerships. “After five years, the Aflamuna x Cinemed Encounters, in the continuity of the Aflamuna connection program, are now a well-established part of the Cinemed Meetings, attracting a vast network of producers, French and European institutions interested in discovering new projects from the Arab world,” said Cinemed director Christophe LeParc. “We are proud to present the seven projects selected this year, and to help expanding their reach and visibility in European markets.” Cinemed runs from October 16 to 24. The 2026 Aflamuna x Cinemed Encounters Selection A Tale of a Feather and a Fish ( Egypt ) Dir. Ahmed El Hawarey Prods . Hala Lotfy (Hassala Films), Jeanne Deny (MAD Solutions) Amidst the shadow of a devastating genetic disease, three broken family members struggle to find salvation; they are guided toward healing by the very loved ones they must care for. Accept My Plea For Burial ( Somalia /Djibouti) Dir. Mohammed Sheikh Prod. Kadir Harbi, producer (Aleel Films) In a remote Somali pastoral village, two twelve-year-old boys, Waasuge and Warmooge, spend their days herding goats and playing. Their rivalry turns tragic when Warmooge dies after falling into a dry riverbed during a game. With no clear witness and conflicting testimonies, suspicion grows. As grief turns to accusation, Warmooge’s mother refuses burial without justice, and the village fractures under the weight of uncertainty and pressure to resolve the truth. Disappeared (doc) France-Syria- Lebanon -Iraq Dir. Anas Zawahri Prod. Ahmad Al Haj (Wind Cinéma) Five Syrian women confront the forced disappearance of their sons and husbands. Through their daily lives and an ongoing search for truth, they resist political erasure, preserve memory, and reclaim meaning within their cities in the Syrian marginalized countryside. I Have Other Friends (doc) Egypt Dir. Yomna Khattab Prod. Muhammad Taymour (Chaos Films) Yomna, the director, on the verge of turning forty, takes us on a personal, intimate journey to portray her female best friends. By navigating the difficult postponed conversations with them, Yomna wonders: ‘Who are my friends when I hit forties?’ The Hearse to the Final House of Happiness Palestine Dir. Wisam Al Jafari Prod . Hanna Attallah (Route 243) When a Palestinian mental patient in his fifties is granted a brief leave to attend a family wedding, the event descends into chaotic absurdity as his political obsession, a restless family, and street protests clash. The Space I Carry (doc) Lebanon-France Dir. Élise Pouchelet, Codirector and producer . Josef Khallouf (The FilmMonk) Born in Lebanon in 1975, at the beginning of the Civil War, Elise was abandoned, then adopted, and carried away to France. Fifty years later, she traces the two lineages that run through her, feeling her way through the fragments and silences that have quietly shaped her. It is in the solitude of the mountains, in the company of wild things, that she finally learns to inhabit the space she carries. Twelve Fig Leaves (doc) Lebanon Dir. Joëlle Abou Chabké Prod. Lara Abou Saïfan (Placeless films) When filmmaker-turned-farmer Joëlle discovers the Bawāhīr, an ancestral Lebanese method of weather prediction, she embarks on a year-long journey to test its accuracy while building a permaculture project with her husband in his native Bekaa village. As climate uncertainty and political instability mount, their quest becomes a search for resilience, ancestral wisdom, and survival. ‘Avengers: Endgame: Encore’ & ‘Primetime’ Eye $3M Previews ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’, Meta Finale & Season 2 Judge Grants Suit Settlement Delay; Company Proceeds With $7.5B Debt Raise David Ellison Dines With Trump & Xi; WBD’s CNN, MS Now Denied Access To Event Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Percy Hynes White & Jeff Wahlberg Lead Lovers-On-The-Run Thriller ‘Crime Novella’, Roland Emmerich Exec-Producing & First Look Revealed
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman , Diana Lodderhose September 25, 2026 3:00am L-R: Percy Hynes White, Jeff Wahlberg, Zlatko Burić, Bobby Soto and Ava del Cielo Getty Images/James Reese Photography/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE : Percy Hynes White ( My Old Ass ), Jeff Wahlberg ( Euphoria ), Zlatko Burić ( Triangle of Sadness ), Bobby Soto ( The Tax Collector ) and Ava del Cielo ( House of Cards ) have been cast in writer-director Omar de Soto’s feature directorial debut, Crime Novella , which was shot on 35mm film. Written, directed and produced by de Soto, the romance crime-thriller “tells the story of two lovers on the run to save their relationship, discovering how far they’ll have to go to stay together.” Below is a first look image. Production wrapped this summer with filming taking place on location in Albuquerque, New Mexico, Los Angeles, Las Vegas and Mexico. In addition to de Soto, the movie is produced by Paul Bennett IV of Replica and Marco Shepherd ( Midway ) of Centropolis Entertainment, which financed the feature. Roland Emmerich is executive producer. Jessica Olthof and Helena Martel Seward are co-producers. Related Stories Casting 'Euphoria' Casts Jeff Wahlberg In Recurring Role For Season 3 News How Percy Hynes White's Xavier Thorpe Was Written Off Netflix's 'Wednesday' Producers describe the film as “a modern descendant of Badlands and Wild at Heart with a transgressive spirit”. Omar de Soto, husband of master of disaster Emmerich, said: “I couldn’t have asked for a more fitting cast. Cash and Valentine have always been the heart of this film, and Percy and Jeff understood the world I was trying to build from the beginning. Percy and Jeff are intoxicating onscreen. You simply cannot take your eyes off them. Zlatko, Bobby and Ava each brought their own special sauce and made our whimsical world feel lived in. I’m incredibly proud of this cast and deeply grateful to my producers and crew who believed in the film and helped us make it on our own terms. This is their moment.” Hynes White is best know for his role in Netflix’s hit Wednesday , where he portrayed Xavier Thorpe in season 1. He also starred in the coming-of-age Sundance comedy-drama My Old Ass . Wahlberg most recently appeared in season 3 of HBO’s smash, Euphoria . Burić won Best Actor at the 35th European Film Awards for his role in Ruben Östlund’s satirical black comedy Triangle of Sadness , which won the Palme d’Or at the 75th Cannes Film Festival in 2022. He has previously worked with Emmerich and Centropolis Entertainment on the disaster epic 2012 . Soto had a leading role with Shia LaBeouf in David Ayer’s The Tax Collector . Del Cielo’s notable credits include Netflix’s House of Cards , From Dusk Till Dawn: The Series and Get Shorty , streaming on MGM+. Hynes White is repped by Innovative Artists and Oscars Abrams Zimel & Associates (OAZ), and Sloane, Offer; Wahlberg is repped by Innovative Artists, Leverage Management, Sloane Offer; Burić is repped by Art Management; Soto is repped by Innovative Artists, Anonymous Content and Goodman, Genow; and Del Cielo is repped by Mitchell & Associates Talent. CAA reps Emmerich and Centropolis Entertainment. articles.title: BBC Studios Names Mediawan’s Sally Habbershaw President Of Global Distribution
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse International Insider: Deep BBC Cuts Begin; Ali G Under Fire; San Sebastian Report Noel Hedges Joins Boat Rocker Studios In Global Acquisitions Role BBC Studios Names Mediawan’s Sally Habbershaw President Of Global Distribution View All September 25, 2026 3:54am Sally Habbershaw Monica Schipper/Getty Images for BAFTA BBC Studios has a new global distribution chief in place. Sally Habbershaw is exiting Mediawan after less than a year to become President of Global Distribution at the BBC’s commercial arm. Her London-based role will see her overseeing BBCS’s worldwide content sales business, reporting into Zai Bennett, BBC Studios Global Content CEO and Chief Creative Officer. BBC Studios has been without a sales boss for most of the year, as the U.S.-based Janet Brown exited in January as part of a plan to move distribution closer to the mothership in the UK. Habbershaw takes up her “newly expanded” post on September 29. Related Stories News 'Doctor Who' Re-Gen Is Go! BBC Calls On Producers To Pitch "Brave" New Vision For Sci-Fi Series News BBC Studios LA Promotes Unscripted Chief Ryan O'Dowd To Oversee Scripted As Mark Linsey & Angie Stephenson Exit “Sally is one of the most accomplished and respected executives in the business and her experience across content investment, distribution, platforms and production makes her uniquely positioned to lead our global content distribution operation,” said Bennett. Watch on Deadline “She brings a rare combination of commercial leadership, creative instincts and deep global market expertise, alongside an exceptional track record of building partnerships and delivering growth across some of the industry’s most successful content businesses. I look forward to working with her as we continue to maximise the value and reach of our outstanding content portfolio.” Habbershaw was the subject of news this time last year in the run up to MIPCOM Cannes, when she replaced Valerie Vleeschhouwer at France’s Mediawan. She was named Chief Distribution Officer at the Adolescence producer. Last year, Deadline revealed that Habbershaw was exiting her New York-based role as Americas sales chief at All3Media International to move back to the UK, though she subsequently joined Paris-based Mediawan. Further back in her career, Habbershaw held senior roles at A&E Networks, AMC Networks, Viacom and several Paramount-owned businesses. She is also a BAFTA Board member and Deputy Chair of BAFTA North America. “After twenty years in the US and, more recently, in France, coming home to do this work here matters to me,” said Habbershaw. “The content and the brand speak for themselves. What made the opportunity irresistible is the moment and the people. “Zai has built a leadership team that is ambitious, thinks differently and is set on making a real impact. I’ve spent my career on the other side of the table from the BBC, so I arrive with a clear view of its strengths and of the work ahead.” Habbershaw’s hire is the latest major development this year in an international TV market that has seen Habbershaw’s former company, All3Media, merge with Banijay. articles.title: BBC Boss Matt Brittin On Expected Service Closures: “No Program Or Channel Will Exist Forever”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake BBC Boss Matt Brittin On Expected Service Closures: “No Program Or Channel Will Exist Forever” ‘Have I Got News For You’ Producer Torches BBC Investigation Into Victoria Beckham Joke As “Total Waste” Of Money BBC Rebukes ‘Have I Got News For You’ After Complaints About “Gratuitously Offensive” Victoria Beckham Joke View All September 25, 2026 5:12am BBC boss Matt Brittin on 'Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg' BBC News BBC director-general Matt Brittin has hinted that the broadcaster is preparing to close TV and radio networks as it looks to save money and better serve audiences online. In an interview that will air over the weekend, Brittin told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg that the BBC’s ambition to save £500 million ($662M) “may well mean” that services are shut. The former Google executive said the BBC “wouldn’t guarantee any program or any channel will exist forever. The tight financial situation means that we’re having to look at some of those decisions a bit sooner than we might like.” Related Stories News 'Have I Got News For You' Producer Torches BBC Investigation Into Victoria Beckham Joke As "Total Waste" Of Money News BBC Rebukes 'Have I Got News For You' After Complaints About "Gratuitously Offensive" Victoria Beckham Joke Brittin’s comments follow Deadline reporting on Wednesday that the BBC is expected to announce the closure of TV and radio networks as early as next week. There is speculation about the future of BBC Three, but nothing is confirmed at this stage. Watch on Deadline “We wouldn't guarantee any programme or any channel will exist forever” BBC Director General Matt Brittin has said that the BBC's financial situation "may well mean" that some channels and radio stations will have to close. #BBCLauraK https://t.co/JZziQESjYy pic.twitter.com/m6Iv4cWEsU — BBC Politics (@BBCPolitics) September 25, 2026 Brittin told Sunday with Laura Kuenssberg : “We might have some channels and services where maybe 100,000 people are watching the broadcast service, but 500,000 are getting those programs on iPlayer. When’s the right time to migrate that service fully to being on demand? And part of my job is to safeguard value for money for the licence fee payer.” He added that the BBC had to go “in different ways to reach audiences and we’re locked into yesterday’s model of how people consume content and actually the audience is always already living in tomorrow’s world.” The BBC’s £500M target expands on a previous savings goal worth £1.5 billion. The bigger picture behind the cuts is that 94% of the UK population use the BBC every month, but fewer than 80% pay the £180 annual licence fee. The BBC is attempting to bridge this gap. Up to 2,000 jobs are at risk under the savings strategy, while the BBC is also involved in tense negotiations with unions over employee pay rises .
