articles.title: Paramount-WBD Settlement Sets Up Editorial Independence Board For CNN And CBS News
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Donald Trump Vows To Appeal Ruling In Networks’ White House Ban Lawsuit, Even Though Judge Has Yet To Rule Paramount-WBD Settlement Sets Up Editorial Independence Board For CNN And CBS News Read The Proposed Consent Decree To Settle The Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger View All September 21, 2026 12:40pm Story Arc CNN; CBS News UPDATED: The potential ownership of CBS News and CNN under one corporate owner has generated months of fear, anxiety and loathing at both networks, but the Paramount – Warner Bros. Discovery settlement tries to resolve some of the issues with the establishment of an editorial independence board. Related Stories News WGA Gets No Writer Layoffs At CBS News, $17.5M For Health Fund As Guild Confirms Settlement Of Lawsuit Against Paramount-WBD Merger News Read The Proposed Consent Decree To Settle The Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Per the terms of the consent decree reached with a dozen state attorneys general, the board will establish a set of guiding principles based on each network’s policies for “accuracy, independence, fairness and journalistic integrity.” The board will resolve any disputes between CBS News employees, CNN employees and management regarding any alleged violations of the principles. And it will monitor “adherence to ethical journalism as defined by journalism industry best practices and to editorial independence.” The decree also sets up who can serve on the body, made up of five retired or active journalists who have worked for a minimum of ten years, and who will be appointed by the combined Paramount-WB board. No more than two members may be affiliated with the same political party. Watch on Deadline “No member of any government or governmental entity, including federal, state, and local governments, may approve or have approval rights over members appointed to the Editorial Independence Board,” per the decree. Officers, directors or non-journalist employees of Paramount-WB also are restricted from serving on the board, whose members will have terms of three years. Paramount would have 180 days to establish the board. There is a designation of a monitoring trustee to oversee Paramount-WBD compliance with the entire consent decree, but that person will have “no role or authority” relating to news operations. A “force majeure” provision can be invoked for events including disasters, strikes, labor disruptions and economic recessions, among other things. A separate settlement with the Writers Guild of America includes a provision prohibiting writer layoffs at CBS News broadcast for five years, the guild said. What the AGs’ consent decree does not do is restrict a combination of CBS News and CNN. Nor does it give the board oversight over who runs the respective news entities, something that has been an issue as CEO David Ellison tapped Bari Weiss to lead CBS News after Skydance’s purchase of Paramount last year. That has raised concerns that the network would be steered rightward, or even in a direction more favorable to Donald Trump. Weiss previously worked as an opinion writer for The New York Times and founded The Free Press, the center-right opinion and analysis site that Paramount also purchased. As part of her changes, she ousted the executive producer of 60 Minutes , while some of the correspondents who were fired have alleged politically motivated interference. Weiss has defended her input to the show, saying it is part of the news process. As part of commitments to close its purchase of Paramount last year, Skydance said that it would install an ombudsman to take complaints over CBS News. The person they hired, Kenneth Weinstein, was not a journalist but the former head of the rightward Hudson Institute. Unlike the traditional role of an ombudsman at a news organization, none of the findings are made public. Other actions have triggered further suspicions, including that, like CBS News, changes would be afoot for CNN, including appointing Weiss to oversee that network as well. As he sought administration approval to purchase Warner Bros. Discovery this year, Ellison hosted a dinner for the Trump White House tied to the White House Correspondents’ Dinner, and he appeared at the president’s State of the Union address. Anna Gomez, the sole Democrat on the FCC, said that the “editorial independence protections included in this settlement remain untested, and there is good reason to be skeptical they will hold up once the ink is dry. Whether these commitments actually protect newsrooms inside CBS and CNN from political, financial, or regulatory pressure, or simply provide cover for further editorial interference, remains to be seen.” Seth Stern, chief of advocacy of the Freedom of the Press Foundation, called the consent decree’s oversight board “worthless.” He said in a statement, “It’s unclear how the attorneys general or courts can constitutionally hold Paramount accountable for the board’s actions or inaction without themselves interfering in content. The attorneys general might be fine with censorship when they’re the ones doing it, but what happens when successors with opposing political views inherit enforcement powers?” California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who led the state AG lawsuit, told reporters that the independent board would “ensure independent, objective, fact-based reporting at CBS News and at CNN.” An independent board is unusual, not not unprecedented. A special committee was set up in 2007 to oversee editorial integrity at the Wall Street Journal , as Rupert Murdoch’s News Corp was looking to acquire the news outlet from the Bancroft family trust. The committee, though, does have a say in major newsroom positions, as it has to grant approval for the appointments of an editor-in-chief and editorial page editor. Comcast committed to an ombudsman when it acquired NBC Universal, with concerns over corporate interference in the editorial process. David McCormick, vice president of standards at NBC News, had already been serving as ombudsman in 1993, and expanded his duties to other NBCU news properties. ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Diana’s Brother Over Memoir Which Midnight Madness TIFF Pic Could Become The Next Box Office Obsession? ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $108M WW More from this Story Arc Paramount WB September 21, 2026 Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios September 21, 2026 Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere” View All Story Arc Read More About: Comments

articles.title: The Final Stretch: California AG Rob Bonta On How Settlement On Paramount-WBD Merger Came Together…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva , Katie Campione September 21, 2026 1:25pm Story Arc Paramount, Rob Bontas Getty Images/Courtesy Paramount ‘s settlement with the 12 Democratic state attorneys general appeared to be a Yom Kippur affair, with the final signoff coming after sundown on Sunday. California Attorney General Rob Bonta was cagey when asked about the exact timeline for the agreement following his Monday morning press conference announcing the deal but when he was cheekily asked by a reporter whether he had brushed his teeth yet by the time all was said and done, he responded with, “I can affirmatively say yes.” Related Stories News David Ellison Hopes To Close Paramount-WBD Deal “In Approximately Two Weeks” As He Hails Legal Settlement In Company Memo News WGA Gets No Writer Layoffs At CBS News, $17.5M For Health Fund As Guild Confirms Settlement Of Lawsuit Against Paramount-WBD Merger “You get to a place in some of these negotiations where you get to 90% maybe 95%, maybe even 99%, and then the last part is often the hardest part,” Bonta added. “Something comes up, something unexpected; you make a lot of progress, then it goes slow, there’s a hiccup — and that was not proven wrong here either.” Watch on Deadline

articles.title: Paramount Shares Fall After Antitrust Deal, But Business Minds Marvel At Favorable Terms
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Paramount Shares Fall After Antitrust Deal, But Business Minds Marvel At Favorable Terms David Ellison Hopes To Close Paramount-WBD Deal “In Approximately Two Weeks” As He Hails Legal Settlement In Company Memo Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger View All September 21, 2026 1:38pm Story Arc Paramount's corporate office in New York's Times Square Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images While Warner Bros. Discovery shares soared 11%, as is often the case of a company about to be acquired, while Paramount shares stumbled on news the companies’ merger will take another two weeks to complete. The stocks’ divergent movement came after news Monday morning of a settlement between Paramount and 12 state attorneys general. A parallel lawsuit filed by the Writers Guild of America was also settled. The agreements pave the way for the $111 billion deal to close, but Paramount CEO David Ellison told staffers in a memo that it would take about two weeks for that final step to occur. Related Stories News Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger News David Ellison Hopes To Close Paramount-WBD Deal “In Approximately Two Weeks” As He Hails Legal Settlement In Company Memo While Paramount’s beleaguered stock jumped 10% earlier in the day, it slumped in the last two hours of the day, possibly on the news that more time is required before the transaction can be completed. Paramount is on the hook for a “ticking fee” of about $7 million a day, payable to WBD shareholders, for every day past October 1 that the deal is not closed. Paramount stock settled at $9.91, its lowest closing price in a month. Watch on Deadline Fears of the ticking fee adding up to around $650 million per quarter ahead of a scheduled March 2027 trial date – a not-inconsequential amount for a company worth about $11 billion – shadowed the legal process in recent weeks. The state AGs and the WGA filed suit in July after federal regulators had approved the deal, and gained surprising traction in a series of early court rulings, giving opponents of the merger hope it would be curtailed or even fully blocked.

articles.title: Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere&#8221…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere” The Final Stretch: California AG Rob Bonta On How Settlement On Paramount-WBD Merger Came Together After Stalemate View All September 21, 2026 3:03pm Story Arc Getty Images Paramount is not leaving California — at least not anytime soon — and that includes both the company’s studio lot(s) and headquarters. The settlement of the anti-trust lawsuit filed by 12 state attorneys general calls for the Paramount, which is set to acquire WBD shortly, to keep both the Paramount lot on Melrose and the Warner Bros. lot in Burbank for the next five years. Related Stories News David Ellison Hopes To Close Paramount-WBD Deal “In Approximately Two Weeks” As He Hails Legal Settlement In Company Memo News Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger “We wanted those lots to be protected, they are part of the the broader solution, and I believe that the future of this merged company is in Los Angeles for many years to come for the foreseeable future,” California AG Rob Bonta said during his press conference about the settlement Monday morning. Bonta was asked about the status of the Paramount headquarters, currently located in Los Angeles. Watch on Deadline “I believe that will be the case, that they will have their headquarters in California for the foreseeable future,” he said, adding, “It’s not part of the deal, I believe there will be public statements.” There had been no public statements on the matter, and the fact that Paramount maintaining its headquarters in California was not part of the agreement raised a few eyebrows. Paramount Chairman and CEO David Ellison did not address it in his official reaction to the settlement or in his company memo Monday, the latter of which noted the combined company’s commitment to producing 30+ movies a year and expanding U.S. film production. Hours later, he stepped in to clear the confusion. “Let me be clear: the newly merged company will be headquartered in Los Angeles,” Ellison said in a new statement. “We aren’t going anywhere. Our history is here and this is where our future is being built.” This brings to an end weeks of tension that culminated in an alleged ultimatum that Paramount would move its headquarters to Tennessee, Texas or Georgia if the anti-trust lawsuit filed by the state AGs was not settled by October 1 when a costly ticking fee to WBD was set to kick in. Per the settlement’s consent decree , the bulked up post-merger Paramount “shall not sell or close the Paramount or Warner Bros. Lots and shall use commercially reasonable efforts to operate the Lots in a manner consistent with past practices, including leasing use to third parties and producing films and television shows.” ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Diana’s Brother Over Memoir Which Midnight Madness TIFF Pic Could Become The Next Box Office Obsession? ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $108M WW More from this Story Arc Paramount WB September 21, 2026 Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios September 21, 2026 Paramount Shares Fall After Antitrust Deal, But Business Minds Marvel At Favorable Terms View All Story Arc Read More About: 9 Comments

articles.title: Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Paramount Settlement Protects Pluto TV, Sets BET & Comedy Central As Potential Divesture Targets While Omitting Premium Channels & TV Studios Paramount To Keep Headquarters In Los Angeles Post-Merger: “We Aren’t Going Anywhere” The Final Stretch: California AG Rob Bonta On How Settlement On Paramount-WBD Merger Came Together After Stalemate View All September 21, 2026 5:27pm Story Arc Pluto TV Photo Illustration by Rafael Henrique/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images Here is a concession no one really asked for — the settlement of state attorneys generals’ anti-trust lawsuit over the proposed Paramount -Warner Bros. Discovery merger includes a provision ensuring that Paramount will keep Pluto TV or another free, ad-supported streaming service for the next five years. Related Stories News Read The Proposed Consent Decree To Settle The Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger News Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger While Pluto TV is protected, the settlement spells out which cable brands Paramount will have to divest if it fails to keep carriage negotiations for the Paramount and Warner Bros. basic cable networks at arm’s length. The list includes two Par nets that already had been put on the block twice, BET (and its various sub-channels) and VH1 , as well as Comedy Central , with the company’s flagships MTV and Nickelodeon out of danger. Overall, television feels a little like an afterthought in the settlement, illustrated by California AG Rob Bonta’s opening remarks at his Monday morning press conference. He spent more than six minutes laying out the agreed-upon terms for film production and had only two lines about TV, one about the establishment of “a news editorial independence board to support CBS News’ and CNN’s continued editorial independence” and one that “Paramount and Warner Brothers are required to continue negotiating their cable packages separately.” Watch on Deadline With state AGs’ action focused on protecting jobs, there is nothing in the agreement that would prevent Paramount from combining some of its post-merger TV studios — Warner Bros. Television, Paramount TV Studios and CBS Studios — which will result in layoffs. Or any guardrails limiting the number of positions that will inevitably be cut when Paramount merges Paramount+ with HBO Max as the company had said. Movies and basic cable were the focus of AGs’ legal battle because those were the areas where there were strong anti-trust concerns. (The combined HBO Max-Paramount+ will become a major SVOD player but will not have dominance in the space.) Still, the complete omission of the TV (or film) studios is surprising, as is the lack of mention of Paramount’s pay cable network Showtime , which, like the basic cable nets, negotiates carriage agreements. That would allow Paramount to bundle it together with WBD ‘s market leader HBO in dealings with operators. Emphasizing that, the settlement’s statement about separate affiliation negotiations for Paramount and WBD’s basic cable channels carries the following disclaimer: “For the avoidance of doubt, this paragraph does not apply to other Combined Entity offerings (e.g., premium cable channels, streaming services, or broadcast)” The omissions are especially glaring given the attention Pluto TV got despite it not being considered in real danger and it having no counterpart on the WBD side. The Curious Case Of Pluto TV Over the past year, Paramount’s leadership has been bullish about Pluto TV, vowing to invest in the AVOD platform and grow it, which they have done in the form of a slew of library content acquisitions and making Pluto part of the company’s backend tech stack convergence alongside Paramount+ – a complex, lengthy process which has largely been completed. Long before the Ellisons arrived on the scene, Pluto’s star had started fading as rivals Tubi and Roku became more popular. Pluto, although it had been a pioneer of FAST when it was founded in 2014, fell back in the market-share race. Its co-founder, Tom Ryan, and other core staffers exited the company. Even so, the new regime has expressed optimism about aiding the potential of Pluto, which had been largely neglected for the previous couple of years. “I am a big believer in the FAST space,” Paramount Chairman and CEO David Ellison said on the company’s Q4 2025 earnings call. Pluto TV was talked up to advertisers at the Paramount upfront presentation in May as a key piece of the company’s ad strategy, with upgrades ongoing and more underway. Most recently, Paramount noted that “Paramount+ and Pluto TV remain at the center of how audiences discover and engage with our programming as we build an entertainment platform for the future” in its Q2 2026 letter to investors, with the company’s executives saying on the earnings call that “we do expect that Pluto will return to growth in back half of the year.” With Paramount making a substantial investment in Pluto TV over the past year, there has been no talk of shutting it down. That has now been put on paper for the next five years in the anti-trust settlement. Basic Cable Haves & Have Nots According to the settlement with the 12 state AGs, “Paramount and Warner Brothers are required to continue negotiating their cable packages separately — a negotiate-separately condition, preserving the competition that exists between them today,” Bonta said Monday, adding, “It will mimic them being separate companies, even post-merger.” As to how that separation will be ensured, the statement is a little vague, noting that there will be a “monitor” and a “state committee” that would assess any complaints. If Paramount is caught in a “material violation,” following a six-month cure period where the company can “come into compliance,” they will have to sell one or more of the following linear networks: BET (Black Entertainment Television, including BET, BET Gospel, BET Her, BET Hip-Hop, BET Jams, and BET Soul), VH1, Comedy Central, Smithsonian, Destination America, and Science. After Skydance’s acquisition of Paramount, the company’s new leadership has shared their intention to revitalize legacy cable brands such as MTV, Nickelodeon, Comedy Central and BET. The inclusion of two of the four on the potential divesture list is somewhat surprising but Paramount still has kept crown jewels MTV and Nickelodeon out of reach. Additionally, the company already has Comedy Central’s biggest program, South Park, locked into a Paramount+ streaming deal for the foreseeable future and just folded BET+ into Paramount+. The rest of the channels on the list are small and, amid linear TV’s continuing decline, Paramount likely won’t mind divesting them anyway. articles.title: Oscar Winner Barbara Kopple On ‘Union Town,’ Her Third Towering Film On American Labor – Camden Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Camden Film Festival: ‘Dependence,’ ‘Revolutionaries Never Die,’ ‘Bucks Harbor’ Take Top Awards As Fall Approaches, Camden International Film Festival Spends Time With ‘The Illusion Of An Everlasting Summer’ ‘Once Upon A Time In Harlem’ Wins $200,000 Library Of Congress Lavine/Ken Burns Prize For Film View All September 21, 2026 5:50pm 'Union Town' Courtesy of Camden International Film Festival Fifty years ago, a young director named Barbara Kopple came out with her first film, a documentary she thought would be little seen. “When I started making the film, I thought, ‘Oh, my parents will see it and their friends and maybe a museum will show it,’” she recalls. That film was Harlan County U.S.A. , about a long running strike at a coal mine in southeast Kentucky, and it was immediately hailed as brilliant, earning Kopple an Academy Award. She would earn a second Oscar for her 1991 documentary American Dream , about a strike at a Hormel Foods plant in Minnesota. Related Stories Documentary Camden Film Festival: 'Dependence,' 'Revolutionaries Never Die,' 'Bucks Harbor' Take Top Awards Documentary As Fall Approaches, Camden International Film Festival Spends Time With 'The Illusion Of An Everlasting Summer' Kopple has made many other documentaries in intervening years – on actor Gregory Peck, singer Sharon Jones, and country band the Chicks (formerly the Dixie Chicks), among others. But she returns to the theme for which she is best known – working people in America — in her new documentary Union Town . It just held its U.S. premiere at the Camden International Film Festival in Maine after bowing at the Venice Film Festival earlier in September. Watch on Deadline UPS workers walk a ‘practice picket line’ on July 7, 2023, in New York City, ahead of a possible strike. TIMOTHY A. CLARY/AFP via Getty Images Union Town follows the battle for better wages and working conditions on three fronts in New York City — at UPS, at Amazon, and among “deliveristas” – that is, people who work for apps like DoorDash making food runs for customers. “I think that they [labor organizers] have a big fight on their hands, but I think that they’re road warriors and I feel an awful lot of hope,” Kopple tells Deadline in an interview at the Camden Opera House, where Union Town screened. “Each time they win something, it’s glorious. It’s wonderful. And they get a little closer and a little closer. And what else can you do? You have to keep fighting… Looking at the people that they work with who can hardly make a living or people who die in the plants because there’s no air conditioning [in summer] or no heat in the winter, it’s just a very human thing to do, so you can’t stop.” In the past four decades, union participation in America has dropped by about half. “[But] they’re still there. They’re still there,” Kopple says of unions. “And if you don’t have them, you don’t have anything.” Director Barbara Kopple with Antonio Rosario, a Teamsters union organizer, at the U.S. premiere of ‘Union Town’ at the Camden International Film Festival on Sept. 19, 2026 in Camden, Maine. Matthew Carey She points to Antonio Rosario, a veteran of a 1997 strike at UPS who serves as the Teamsters lead union organizer for Amazon workers in the northeast. At one moment in the film, Rosario is with his young sons at the dinner table and holds a bundle of sticks in his hands to illustrate the importance of worker solidarity. “Tony is trying to show them the difference that if you have a lot of people together, it takes too much to break it,” Kopple explains. “And if you just have one stick, you can break it. And that’s what it is. It’s people who have your back. It’s people who will help you and it gives you a sense of strength that you can change.” Of the three groups seen in the documentary, deliveristas face the worst conditions and pay – they work year-round in every kind of weather, driving their bikes through snow in winter, for instance. Kopple documents the case of Victor Hidalgo, a 24-year-old man who was working for a pharmacy delivery company in 2024 when a New York Fire Department vehicle hit his bicycle, killing him. At a Q&A following the U.S. premiere, Kopple said Hidalgo’s aunt urged her to put him in the documentary. “She said, ‘I don’t want anyone to ever forget Victor,’” Kopple recounted. “’Please come and film the funeral. Please come and let people know that these things really happen.’” A DoorDash delivery person prepares to bike in the snow in New York City. Noam Galai/Getty Images Deliveristas rely on tips as a major source of income, but customers often don’t give them much (one deliverista recalls a person opening his hand to deposit a tip and placing in his palm a piece of candy). What’s worse, the tips they receive through the app may not go to them; in 2025 DoorDash reached a nearly $17 million settlement in New York after being accused of effectively taking workers’ tips. (Per the New York Attorney General’s office, “Customers were misled into believing their tips would directly benefit Dashers. Instead, DoorDash would keep the tips meant for Dashers and take it out of their guaranteed pay. DoorDash would guarantee pay to a delivery worker, and then only actually pay them whatever the tip did not cover.”). “What it does if people get to see this film is maybe they’ll give big tips. Maybe they’ll talk to the people who deliver or at least understand them,” Kopple says. “Ever since UPS got their contract, every time I see a UPS truck, I stop and I talk to the driver and I say, ‘So how’s your contract? How’s work?’ And they’re looking at me like, ‘Who’s this crazy person?’ But it’s wonderful to do it… [It shows] somebody cares. Somebody’s out there who cares about them. They’re not invisible.” Producer Peter Palandjian, Teamsters union organizer Antonio Rosario, director Barbara Kopple, and producer Hannes Hosp attend the ‘Union Town’ photocall at the Venice Film Festival on September 9, 2026. Aurore Marechal/Getty Images Autlook is handling worldwide film sales for Union Town . The 2024 documentary Union , about the successful effort to organize workers at an Amazon facility in Staten Island, NY, struggled to find U.S. distribution (it was clear Prime Video wouldn’t touch it). That film by Stephen Maing and Brett Story is now streaming through Criterion. Kopple says it’s “too soon to tell” about potential distribution of Union Town . “This was the third time the film has ever shown, and I had just finished it maybe two weeks before Venice. So, it’s totally at the beginning. I mean, I hope it gets great distribution and gets shown far and wide.” ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Diana’s Brother Over Memoir Which Midnight Madness TIFF Pic Could Become The Next Box Office Obsession? ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $108M WW Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Post-Merger Paramount May Overdeliver On Settlement Terms With 36-Film 2027 Slate Amid Speculation About Duplication & WB Leadership
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Resident Evil’ $108.3M WW Opening A Record For Franchise & Zach Cregger, ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ Nears $100M WW – Global Box Office Update Post-Merger Paramount May Overdeliver On Settlement Terms With 36-Film 2027 Slate Amid Speculation About Duplication & WB Leadership Paramount-Warner Bros Penalty If Merger Fails To Release 30 Pics A Year: Divest Miramax View All September 21, 2026 7:17pm 'A Minecraft Movie'; 'A Quiet Place Part II'; 'Sonic the Hedgehog 2'; 'Superman' Warner Bros.; Jonny Cournoyer / Paramount Pictures; Paramount Pictures; Warner Bros.; all Courtesy Everett Collection California Attorney General Rob Bonta can rest easy: A merged Paramount Warner Bros. Discovery would already account for 36 movies on the release schedule for 2027. Note, that’s an organic number of theatrical releases which were always set to happen even before the union of the storied studios came together . As for 2028, the combined entity currently accounts for 25 theatrical releases, hence another five titles are needed to meet the state AGs’ agreed-upon settlement term of 30 films in the merger’s first two years of existence. That should be easy, it’s still early, and awards season fare often gets dated later rather than sooner. Related Stories News Paramount Settlement Terms Laid Out By CA AG Rob Bonta, Who Says Deal Is “Not A Blessing” Of WBD Merger News Done! Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit, Set To Seal Deal For Warner Bros. Discovery Beyond 2029, the AGs’ demand from the merged entity is for 32 films annually over three years. It’s on Ellison to make sure this union isn’t a repeat of Disney-Fox. Missing the annual theatrical release quota could cost Paramount — per the pact with the AGs — its 49% investment in Miramax. In addition, per Bonta, “For each film that they fail to make, should they fail to make any, $30M is paid to be split three different ways, but 90% of it goes to workers.” Watch on Deadline Despite all the pom pom waving that the house of Harry Potter and Batman are now one with the house of Transformers, Star Trek and Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, the question becomes, how will Ellison’s Paramount wrangle this beast? If merged today, both studios combined would count $838.3M at the YTD domestic box office (Jan. 1-Sept. 20) for an 11% market share, ranking fourth behind Universal ($1.78 billion), Sony ($1.22B) and Walt Disney ($1.03B) — global annual numbers were not available at the time of this report for Paramount or Warners. However, Universal leads all studios with around $5B WW, followed by Disney with $4B-plus WW. Rumors that both studios would have to operate separately were wrong. We hear that as Ellison eyes his early corporate structure that one or two executives would oversee overall theatrical and film strategy and likely one or two executives would oversee each film brand. Note that this is all fluid and still in the works. In addition, how the new conglomerate plans to deal with the duplication of marketing and distribution groups is in wait and see mode. Per the release breakdown below, there are plenty of weekends where the studios are dating against each other on the same weekend. In most instances, it’s a matter of counterprogramming — e.g. May 21, 2027, when family animated Warners pic Bad Fairies opens against a new James Wan Paranormal Activity film. However, it’s arguably unprecedented for a major studio to shell out on marketing for two big films from two big labels in the same weekend. Note: It hasn’t been uncommon of late for a big studio to face-off against its adult specialty label — e.g. Universal going up against a Focus Features title. The one glaring tentpole-on-top-of-a-tentpole frame is June 30, 2028 where Paramount’s feature take of video game Call of Duty is up against DC’s Dynamic Duo. Also, there’s the situation of some serious summer stacking. July 2027 has James Gunn’s Man of Tomorrow followed by Crawl 2 (granted, it’s a counterprogrammer) followed by Ocean’s Prequel and A Quiet Place III. Timothée Chalamet as Paul Atreides and Zendaya as Chani Warner Bros. On the bright side, before this year is over, the combined entity has a possible billion dollar hit and award contender in Warner Bros/Legendary’s Denis Villeneuve Dune: Part Three, which could create another Barbenheimer effect at the box office in its competition with Disney/Marvel Studio’s Avengers: Doomsday on Dec. 18. While the studios can operate separately, Bonta says when it comes to negotiating and creating a marketplace where there isn’t reduced competition, “We basically ensure the status quo competition with negotiations (remaining) separately. It’s as if the companies never merged. They can’t bundle their basic cable channel assets. They can’t use them together to reduce competition…They have to remain separate and independent in their negotiations, and when they’re working with the cable companies. Same with the theatrical release. “Usually, when you see [a deal that] reduces competition, you see people paying more for less. So you see less output, less quality. And you see higher prices. We address that by making sure that the fees remain flat, for the three years between the merch company and the exhibitors, the theaters. And then the requirement, this incredible, massive requirement for production output, cures for the less part, instead of paying more for less. You have the flat fee requirement with massive increase in production. So that’s how we address the concerns about reduced competition,” explained California’s AG this morning. The multi-billion dollar question as far as box office goes is whether Warner Bros. Motion Picture Chairs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy make the jump to the new entity. De Luca told us earlier this year that no matter which way the merger went (Netflix or Paramount), “We’re hoping to stay the course.” Last year was a banner year for the duo with $4.3 billion WW. This year, there haven’t been as many hits, but the longtime production partners are known for their excellent relationships with filmmakers like their recent Oscar winners Paul Thomas Anderson, Ryan Coolger as well as Alejandro Inarritu and Zach Cregger, to name a few. Rumors have swirled about DeLuca and Abdy heading over to Sony, or Netflix (that latter rumor fueled around town after their longtime comms chief Katie Martin Kelly departed Warners for the streamer). The reality is that the duo have a four-year extension on their contacts until 2030 to run Warners. A world where the pro-theatrical De Luca and Abdy continue to stay at the helm of their ship isn’t out of the question. Ellison said in a memo to Paramount staff today, “We are tentatively planning to close in approximately two weeks.” Get ready… Here’s how the release schedule looks at this point in time for mid-October 2026 through the end of 2028. Those movies with the same release dates are in bold. 2026 Oct. 16 – Street Fighter (Par/Legendary) The Devils (WB Clockwork) Oct. 23 – Clayface (WB) Nov. 6 – The Cat in the Hat (WB) Nov. 13 – Ebenezer (Par) Dec. 18 – Dune: Part 3 (WB/Legendary) Dec. 23 – The Angry Birds Movie (Par) Dec. 25 – Mr. Irrelevant (Par) 2027 Jan. 8 Untitled horror (Par) Jan. 15 – Children of Blood and Bone (Par) Jan. 22 – Animal Friends (WB/Legendary) Jan. 29 The Rescue (Par) Feb. 5 – Remain (WB) Feb. 26 – K-Pop: The Debut (Par) The Revenge of La Llorona (WB) March 12 – WB/New Line Event Film March 19 – Sonic the Hedgehog 4 (Par) March 26 – Godzilla x Kong : Supernova (WB/Legendary) April 9 – Boys for Life (Par) Panic Carefully (WB) May 14 – F.A.S.T. articles.title: ‘Resident Evil’ $108.3M WW Opening A Record For Franchise & Zach Cregger, ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ Nears $100M WW – Global Box Office Update
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Resident Evil’ $108.3M WW Opening A Record For Franchise & Zach Cregger, ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ Nears $100M WW – Global Box Office Update Post-Merger Paramount May Overdeliver On Settlement Terms With 36-Film 2027 Slate Amid Speculation About Duplication & WB Leadership Paramount-Warner Bros Penalty If Merger Fails To Release 30 Pics A Year: Divest Miramax View All September 21, 2026 8:00pm RESIDENT EVIL, Austin Abrams, 2026. © Sony Pictures Releasing / Courtesy Everett Collection UPDATED: TriStar Pictures/Constantin Film/Davis Films’ Resident Evil rang up a massive $108.3M worldwide , not only the best start the franchise has ever seen, but also Zach Cregger ‘s biggest start as filmmaker surpassing the $70M WW reported opening of last year’s Weapons. What was the previous biggest opener in the Resident Evil franchise? We’re told it was 2012’s Resident Evil: Retribution which bowed to $70.6M WW (note that included Russia and Japan in its first suite at the time). The movie finaled at $240M WW. In addition, the opening alone for Resident Evil beats the global final of the original 2002 movie ($102.9M) as well as the last title, the failed reboot Welcome to Raccoon City ($41.9M). Currently, 2016’s Resident Evil: The Final Chapter stands as the highest grossing title in the series with $312M (51% of that coming from China or $159.5M). Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'Resident Evil' Scores $60M U.S. Opening: Best Ever For Zach Cregger & Franchise - Box Office Update News 'Resident Evil's Austin Abrams Recalls "Harrowing" Stunt Shoot For Zach Cregger's Video Game Adaptation: "You Don't Wanna F*ck Up" Also, get this but this zombie shoot-em up paced like Scream 7, in fact even better (that pic opened to a franchise best $63.5M and $97M worldwide. Comps to Scream 7 were iffy on Thursday night, until they became real. For a horror pic this year at the worldwide B.O., it’s the second best after Backrooms ‘ $118M. In terms of pure international debuts for a horror movie YTD, Resident Evil ‘s $48.3M is the best for the genre, higher than Backrooms ‘ $36.6M. Resident Evil is 66% over Weapons , 33% above A Quiet Place: Day One , and 18% ahead of Alien: Romulus on a like-for-like basis at current exchange rates. What’s impressive is that the movie expanded its audience beyond the Milla Jovovich movies. UK at $5.8M was the top territory (in reported, 2010’s 3D charged Afterlife bowed to $2.5M there). Mexico followed at $5.6M (higher than Afterlife ‘s reported $3.2M). Metropolitan had French speaking markets, while Constantin had Germany speaking markets. France did $2.6M (higher than Final Chapter ‘s reported $1M start). Germany counted $2.5M (higher than Final Chapter ‘s reported $1.3M), Other top markets were Australia ($2.6M), Spain ($2.3M), Brazil ($2.0M), Italy ($1.7M), Saudi Arabia ($1.6M), UAE ($1.4M), Indonesia ($1.4M), Malaysia ($1.3M), Taiwan ($1.2M), the Philippines ($1.2M), and India ($1.1M). And there’s 13% of foreign markets left to go, and they’re big territories for the franchise, i.e. Thailand (Sept. 24), Japan (Oct. 9) and China (still to be dated). South Africa is opening on Sept. 23 while Central Asia is Sept. 24. Final Chapter ‘s $159.5M in the Middle Kingdom is looked at as an anomaly: Just a perfect place in time and space for a Resident Evil in regards to the types of U.S. action movies that fared well in China, in addition to the game’s popularity. Japan was the second highest territory for Final Chapter at $36.4M. In addition, A24’s highest grossing movie ever, Backrooms , clicked past the $400M mark at the global box office. THE ODYSSEY, Cyclops, 2026. © Universal Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection Universal’s The Odyssey was second around the globe in its tenth frame with $21.3M WW in 85 territories ($4.95M domestic, $16.4M int’l) for a worldwide running total of $1.72B (Universal’s highest as we told you with $1.11B offshore, $609.8M domestic). Korea added $3.1M in first place for a $91.6M tally, sailing past Avengers: Endgame ‘s lifetime total and becoming the third biggest Hollywood movie of all-time in the territory behind Avatar 1 and 2. China’s sixth frame was $2M and a $107.7M running cume, yes, still Christopher Nolan’s second-highest grossing there behind Interstellar. Japan added $1.8M in Wknd 2, reaching $7.9M cume, performing well above Oppenheimer at the same point, as well as The Dark Knight Rises . The Odyssey clicked past Dune: Part Two ‘s lifetime total earlier this week. Germany grossed $1.2M in its tenth frame for a $64M cume. ‘Practical Magic 2’ Warner Bros./Courtesy Everett Collection Do you believe in magic, in an old studio’s heart? If so, then Warner Bros’ Practical Magic 2 ranked third on the global charts with $19.1M WW ($12.1M domestic, $7M offshore), $76.8M WW ($50M domestic, $26.8M foreign) for the net $75M production. Top five territory totals are UK ($7.5M), Australia ($3.6M), Mexico ($2.4M), Germany ($1.3M) and Spain ($1.2M). The first 1998 movie finaled at $94.4M WW. Fourth is the eighth session of Sony /Marvel’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day with $17.2M WW ($10.8M offshore, $6.4M domestic) and a running global cume of $2.478B ($944.4M all-time running stateside cume, $1.53B offshore). Pic is in play on 17,500 screens in 67 markets. ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Warner Bros. Stand-up and applaud Ketchup Entertainment’s rescue of Warner Bros Animation’s Coyote Vs. Acme as the movie is on the edge, on the edge of cracking $100M WW with $54.7M in U.S./Canada and $44.3M abroad in 46 territories. That adds up to $99M after a global fourth frame of $10.5M ($4.4M domestic, $6.1M abroad) in the No. 5 worldwide spot. Warner Bros wrote off for $30M on the $70M project which Ketchup acquired global on for $50M (and then sold off foreign on). Other notables: Angel Studio’s action movie Runner starring Alan Ritchson and Owen Wilson minted $4.466M from 31 territories worldwide, of that $1.28M was from offshore and $3.1M domestic. Running global is $15.2M (with $11.9M from domestic). China’s Once Upon a Time in the Middle East from Muye Wen continued to lead the box office in China with a $4.3M weekend ahead of local film V and The Odyssey. Guess how much Middle East has made to date there? $323.8M. OBSESSION, from left: Inde Navarrette, Michael Johnston, 2025. © Focus Features /Courtesy Everett Collection Focus Features’ Obsession minted $2M from offshore this weekend with a current global running cume of $516.7M . That was largely driven by Korea’s third weekend was $1.4M, ranking third behind The Odyssey and local remake The Intern for a $5.6M cume, surpassing the lifetimes of It, Annabelle, Insidious, Five Nights at Freddy’s and A Quiet Place: Day One , in addition to having already overtaken a number of tentpole horrors earlier in the run. ‘Forgotten Island’ DreamWorks / © Universal Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection Universal/DreamWorks Animation’s Forgotten Island started its offshore rollout and know that it’s staggered. The Joel Crawford and Januel P. Mercado directed movie doesn’t hit our shores until Sept. 25. For now, it’s made $1.5M from Mexico, Australia and New Zealand. Mexico posted $900K for a No. 3 rank which includes $400K of previews from last weekend and Wednesday’s Independence Day public holiday. Audience reactions and sentiment are positive with crowds attracted to the pic’s beauty and emotion. Australia bowed to $500K, No. 7 in the territory on 285 screens. Business on Saturday and Sunday was impacted by warm and dry weather and football semi-finals for both the AFL (football) and NRL (rugby). Very good audience and critics reactions are teeing the pic up for a solid run during the upcoming school holidays, which began today across 50% of the country. articles.title: ‘Trump TV’ Promo Uses Clips From ‘The Simpsons,’ ‘Seinfeld,’ ‘Friends,’ ‘The Dark Knight’ & Many More
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom ‘Trump TV’ Promo Uses Clips From ‘The Simpsons,’ ‘Seinfeld,’ ‘Friends,’ ‘The Dark Knight’ & Many More Presley Gerber Dies: Model, Son Of Cindy Crawford & Rande Gerber Was 27 Ke Huy Quan Reveals “Life Changing” Gesture From Spielberg & Lucas When He Was A Kid View All September 21, 2026 8:46pm YouTube Donald Trump has defied copyright complaints from Neil Young, Ariana Grande, Beyoncé and everyone in between for unauthorized use of their music. Today, it posted a promo video for Trump TV that made use of footage from Friends, The Simpsons, Family Guy, Home Alone, Modern Family, Breaking Bad, The Dark Knight , The Office, SpongeBob SquarePants, Parks and Recreation, That ’70s Show and more. Related Stories News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Journalists Denied White House Entry; Colleagues Condemn Trump’s Ban News CNN, MS NOW And Politico Sue Donald Trump Over His White House Ban Among the studios and networks whose IP is used in the promo are Warner Bros., Fox, Nickelodeon, Sony Pictures Television, Disney and NBCUniversal. It’s not a terribly unusual move for the president, who routinely posts AI videos that lift scenes from hit films like Top Gun . It is, however, somewhat unique in its breadth. And perhaps that is the point. Trump TV is a promotional effort launched after the president banned Politico, CNN and MS Now from the White House . The administration billed it “The Essentials Station.” Another (grammatically-challenged) administration pitch for the service was, “Not every big moment has made it on your tv, now it can.” The service provides a live feed of official events, seemingly without the razzle dazzle of which the president is so fond. The New York Times dubbed it “essentially a form of state television.” Watch on Deadline IT'S LIVE. 📺🦅 TRUMP TV IS STREAMING NOW. 24/7, updated in real time, with top past moments, announcements, and the latest and greatest from the administration all in one place. Not every big moment has made it on your tv, now it can. 📲 https://t.co/3KwWkBZ69m pic.twitter.com/g4v7n2J04s — The White House (@WhiteHouse) September 21, 2026 The advent of Trump TV comes after the president denied Politico, CNN and MS Now access to the White House over the weekend, prompting outcry from other media and a lawsuit from the trio . CNN had the White House pool assignment for Monday and was scheduled to be the primary network for coverage. The other TV networks declined to replace CNN in protest of the move, and as a result, there was no TV pool on a day when Trump is traveled to New York. The lack of network-level production is apparent. Video posted on the White House YouTube channel this weekend includes a long, very unTrumpy nine-minute recount of a ribbon cutting. It includes long takes of the president shaking hands with attendees before proceeding to make his remarks. Those, however, are drowned out by the engines of Marine One in the background. ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Diana’s Brother Over Memoir Which Midnight Madness TIFF Pic Could Become The Next Box Office Obsession? ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $108M WW Read More About: 5 Comments

articles.title: Muse Entertainment Unveils ‘Doula: A True Crime’ Trailer As Boat Rocker Studios Boards CBC Doc
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Muse Entertainment Unveils ‘Doula: A True Crime’ Trailer As Boat Rocker Studios Boards CBC Doc ‘Stuff The British Stole’ Producer WildBear Entertainment Reshuffles Top Team To “Get Ahead” Of Industry Transformation BBC Drama ‘Ministry Of Time’ Adds Adeel Akhtar, Ciaran Hinds & Eight More To Cast View All September 21, 2026 9:01pm EXCLUSIVE: Here’s a trailer for Doula – A True Crime , a Canadian doc series from The Walrus and the Whistleblower filmmaker Nathalie Bibeau about a bizarre criminal case of a woman who faked pregnancies. The three-parter, which will premiere on Canadian pubcaster CBC on October 7, looks into the story of Kaitlyn Braun, who aged 24, reached out to more than 40 doulas with the same shocking story: that she had been sexually assaulted and was in her third trimester carrying a stillborn child. We can reveal Boat Rocker Studios has acquired the international distribution rights to the Muse Entertainment -produced show and will launch it at MIPCOM Cannes next month. Related Stories Trailers 'Coven Academy' Trailer Reveals A Forbidden Love Triangle & Explosive Powers In Supernatural Witch Series News A+E Global Media Backs Lifetime Korea Series 'Oh! My Guard' Starring K-Pop Performer Jung Yong-hwa & Hong Seung-hee The doc is notable for including the first interview with Braun, who was hit with 53 criminal charges after doulas, who had helped her and provided pro bono services such as hours of phone and video calls and round-the-clock in-person care, began to question her narrative. Watch on Deadline After piecing together the pattern that had formed over nine months between June 2022 and February 2023, many found others like themselves and started a grassroots campaign for to alert authorities through a viral TikTok counter-offensive. In the trailer, we hear from several doulas shaken by their experience. “I can’t tell you I was assaulted, that’s not really what happened and I can’t tell that I was scammed, that doesn’t encompass what she did to me. I have to tell you the whole story so you understand,” says one. “I have no felt fear like that in my entire life,” says another later in the trailer. The one-minute clip ends with a camera making its way up a porch, where it is met by Braun, who smiles as she opens the door and says, “Hello!” The film was made over several years, and attempts to go beyond the sensationalist reporting that followed the story at the time. Braun conversed with Bibeau several times over extensive interviews and phone calls, offering insight into her actions and motivations. “Everyone knew that Kaitlyn Braun had committed crimes. I wanted to understand why,” said Bibeau, writer, director and producer of Doula: A True Crime . “The deeper I went, the less the story yielded to easy conclusions. Kaitlyn’s deception played on empathy, and the harm it caused was real. “But the very thing that made the harm possible was also what I needed to understand her. I’m drawn to the places where human behaviour resists a clean moral frame. And this story lives in one of those places – where empathy doesn’t get in the way of truth, but brings us closer to it.” Jonas Prupas, Managing Director of Unscripted and executive producer at Montreal-based Muse, said the story “could easily be reduced to its more sensationalist elements,” but that Bibeau had made it “into something nuanced, surprising and deeply human.” Mellany Welsh, SVP and Global Head of Distribution & Brands at Boat Rocker Studios, added the doc offered international buyers “a story they won’t find anywhere else.” Muse – known for the likes of Sullivan’s Crossing , The Kennedys and Nose Deep – made the show for CBC and CBC Gem, with the series premiering on October 7 at 8am ET on CBC. Prupas and Courtney Dobbins are exec producers for Muse. For CBC, Sally Catto is General Manager, Entertainment, Jennifer Dettman is Executive Director of Unscripted Content, and Michelle McCree is Senior Director and Commissioning Editor of Documentary. articles.title: Brixton Community Cinema Creator Abiba Coulibaly On Why She Decided To End The Popular London Film Club
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac ‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’ Trailer: Brad Pitt Revisits The Character That Won Him An Oscar In David Fincher’s Latest Movistar Plus Announces 2027 Slate, Including JA Bayona & Fernando León Projects, At San Sebastián Naomi Watts Says She’d Like To Work With Paul Thomas Anderson & Praises The Advancements Older Women Have Made In Hollywood — San Sebastián View All September 22, 2026 1:02am Abiba Coulibaly Next month, the Brixton Community Cinema , the roving cinema project that has quickly become one of the UK’s most admired film communities under the stewardship of independent programmer Abiba Coulibaly , will close. Coulibaly announced the cinema’s farewell season in August on Instagram . “The closure of Brixton Community Cinema is not to give up and abandon either, just to recalibrate,” she wrote in the statement. Coulibaly launched the BCC in 2022 as a pay-what-you-can pop-up cinema club. She programmed a wide variety of titles, but the cinema’s central focus was international repertory and arthouse films. Past screenings featured titles like The First World Festival of Negro Arts by William Greaves, Abdellatif Kechiche’s La Faute à Voltaire , and Sarah Gomez’s One Way or Another . Related Stories News Muse Entertainment Unveils 'Doula: A True Crime' Trailer As Boat Rocker Studios Boards CBC Doc News 'Trump TV' Promo Uses Clips From 'The Simpsons,' 'Seinfeld,' 'Friends,' 'The Dark Knight' & Many More The eclectic programming made the BCC a must-visit film destination for cinephiles in London. In turn, the cinema’s audience grew and so did its reputation. BCC pop-up screenings moved from small non-arts spaces in Brixton to venues like London’s Cinema Museum. Criterion’s Ashley Clark described Coulibaly as “fantastic” during an interview with Deadline earlier this year . So why end things now? Watch on Deadline Speaking with Deadline ahead of her final screening on October 6, Coulibaly explains that the BCC project simply grew at a pace that was impossible for one person to maintain. “The project had grown more than I ever expected,” she explains. Below, Coulibaly speaks with us in depth about how she built Brixton Community Cinema, what she learned about audiences during the BCC’s successful run, and what she has planned next. Films set to screen as part of the BCC’s final season include Margarida Cardoso’s Kuxa Kanema: The Birth of Cinema (2003) and Sanaz Sohrabi’s essay film An Incomplete Calendar (2026). Legendary artist and filmmaker John Akomfrah will also sit for a discussion with Ish filmmaker Imran Perretta. Scroll down to see the full lineup. DEADLINE: Abiba, you’re closing the Brixton Community Cinema. Why? ABIBA COULIBALY: I always knew it wouldn’t last forever. I was actually adamant from the start that it wouldn’t, because I knew the limits of the “pay what you can” model. So I think it was always more of an experiment. But it all came to a head, I’d say, a year to 18 months ago, because the project had grown more than I ever expected. I then felt I needed to do things like register as a CIC, get a business bank account, and start paying for domains. As I tried to scale up, I realized I didn’t have the time or money to handle all the admin and bureaucracy. I actually ended up losing a lot of time and money in the process. It was too much for just one person. DEADLINE: The cinema did really grow. I did a piece with Ashley Clark at Criterion about his great book on Black cinema, and he name-checked you and the cinema. I was surprised he’d heard of it considering he isn’t based in the UK. Did no bigger institutions or funders come along to invest or support your work? COULIBALY: I read that interview and was really surprised and flattered to see my name mentioned. Ashley and I actually grew up on the same road, opposite each other, but he’s a decade or so older. But in terms of people coming along, honestly, no. Firstly, the question of who you work with has been difficult. It has very rarely been possible to align values and access to resources. I never envisaged having to deliberate so much about working with organizations. Sometimes it would be that they aren’t based in Brixton or Lambeth, or maybe I didn’t agree with their political stances. But in terms of one-off project fees, yeah, sure, I’ve been approached; it would be something like £500. But never any big, long-term support. Generally, money and business aren’t my strengths. For this final season, a friend volunteered to raise some money, and they managed to get £2500 from WeTransfer. That has been our only major partnership or collaboration. DEADLINE: I’ve been to your screenings, and they were always very well attended. What did you learn about what audiences want from cinemas in 2026? COULIBALY: I felt my audience was seeking cinema experiences that could address their real-world concerns. They weren’t really seeking an escapist moment, but rather the space to discuss and engage with relevant things happening around them. I started the project in late 2022. The genocide in Palestine began in late 2023, and I tried at times to speak to that through my programming alongside other things going on in various other countries. I always got the impression that those were the events audiences really wanted to attend. But I also had many difficulties with myself as a programmer. I began with a lot of enthusiasm about the power of cinema. Over the years, that has dampened in some ways. That is also why I want to take a step back. I also got the impression from audience members that they’ve had so many weird institutional failings from both cinemas and arts institutions. It’s really got to the point where there are very few large galleries, museums, or cinemas in London that don’t have some kind of problematic scandal or history. I think people are really searching for cultural spaces which don’t feel so compromising, when it feels impossible to boycott and divest from every single cultural institution in London. Abiba Coulibaly at the BCC’s open-air cinema during the 2023 London Festival of Architecture. DEADLINE: Talk to me about this final lineup. You’re focusing on a large geographical area; there are films from Madagascar, Pakistan, and Malaysia. COULIBALY: To end this run, I felt I needed to choose a theme or location. I’ve always tried to steer clear of regionally focused programming. I sometimes find it a lazy way of attracting audiences. I’m also slightly resistant to labels. I actually saw that BFI Future Film created a little zine for its Young Programmers’ Festival, and inside they said, “Go to Brixton Community Cinema if you want to see Black cinema.” They probably thought it was a really nice way to shout me out, and I’m sure they’re sweet people. But that’s so funny because I show films from all over the world. Ultimately, I believe I’m from the best city in the world. When I was growing up, there was so much mixing between all groups of people. With this final season, I was thinking very clearly about the question: How do you reflect a city back at itself? DEADLINE: You’ve actually done a lot of really important work here. Screening films that people otherwise would never see or even hear about. Have you ever thought about consolidating it all in a book or publication about the cinema? COULIBALY: From the very start of Brixton Community Cinema, I focused heavily on printed material. I used to do a lot of program notes and zines designed by some very talented friends behind the publishing studio Em—Dash, who do all of the graphics for the project. I produced those less over time because it was so labor-intensive. But I have this amazing archive of essays, texts, and interviews that I’ve always thought would make a really great anthology that could also speak to the political moment. For instance, the third or fourth screening I ever did was Jafar Panahi’s Offside , during the 2022 World Cup. When the screening came around, the protests in Iran had really taken off. So, I commissioned a Tehran-based film journalist to write about what it would mean to rewatch the film in this moment. There are so many interesting texts like that that are not only great films but also speak to the social and political context of making the Brixton Community Cinema. It’s really just a case of money. All of the material is there; all of the ideas are there. DEADLINE: You’re not going away completely. You programmed parts of the BFI’s Sarah Maldoror season. Where will people be able to find you? COULIBALY: I’m freelance, so who knows. I’m also a programmer for the Open City Documentary Festival. That’s my one regular programming gig. I will also continue to programme independently. articles.title: Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Princess Diana’s Brother Over “Bulls***” Claim In Bombshell Memoir
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Paramount Settles Antitrust Suit: No Move From L.A., Terms Of Deal, David Ellison & WGA Reaction, Shares Down, Read The Document, More Read the full story By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Princess Diana’s Brother Over “Bulls***” Claim In Bombshell Memoir Tom Cruise Earns Applause With Six-Minute Monologue On Why Art Beats AI In Filmmaking: “There Is Nothing Like Human” BBC Removes Blackface Sketches From ‘That Mitchell And Webb Look’ View All September 22, 2026 1:53am Piers Morgan and Charles Spencer Getty Piers Morgan has received an apology from Charles Spencer, brother of the late Princess Diana , over an inaccurate claim in the Earl’s bombshell memoir. Spencer’s book, Swan Song , has dominated the headlines in the UK for days following his explosive allegation that King Charles III said Diana would soon be forgotten in the aftermath of her death. Morgan drew attention to another section of Spencer’s book, in which the Earl claimed that Morgan published “intrusive” images of Diana in a gym while he was editor of The Daily Mirror. “I come across in the despicable manner imaginable,” Morgan said of Spencer’s book. “There’s just one problem — it’s all bulls***. And very easy bulls*** for me to prove it.” Related Stories News Princess Di Returns To 'SNL UK' As "Deeply Intelligent, Autonomous, Neurokinetic Android" In Cold Open Skewering King Charles, Ed Sheeran & AI News Tilly Norwood Malfunctions During Piers Morgan Interview: "Seems I Had A Little Hiccup" Speaking on his YouTube show Piers Morgan Uncensored , the former CNN anchor continued: “The photographs, which he says that I published, were printed by The Sunday Mirror on November 7, 1993. I joined The Daily Mirror in October 1995. In fact, at the time of the gym pictures, I was doing a showbiz column on The Mirro r’s arch rival, The Sun .” Watch on Deadline 'It's all bullsh*t… you'll be hearing from my lawyers.' BREAKING: Piers Morgan plans to take legal action against Earl Spencer over “fabricated inaccuracies” made about him in his bombshell book on Diana. Watch more 👇 📺 https://t.co/ZWOoVI5C3O @piersmorgan pic.twitter.com/3w66CTrwZc — Piers Morgan Uncensored (@PiersUncensored) September 21, 2026 Morgan added that Spencer had printed “fabricated inaccuracies” that strike “at the heart of his credibility.” He said: “If Earl Spencer can be so incredibly defamatorily wrong about such basic facts involving me, well why should we believe anything else that he puts in this book?” In a statement, Spencer acknowledged the error. “As an historian, accuracy is important to Earl Spencer. He therefore wishes to clarify that his assumption was incorrect. Earl Spencer apologises to Mr Morgan for this error,” a representative of the Earl said. Spencer added, however, that he was correct in his recollection of a phone call he had with Morgan, in which he informed the journalist that he could not attend Diana’s funeral. “Earl Spencer’s account of his conversation with Piers Morgan is accurate. Mr Morgan was surly and annoyed when Earl Spencer called personally to tell him that he was not welcome at his sister’s funeral,” the statement continued. On his show, Morgan addressed Spencer directly. “You will be hearing, and your publishers, from my lawyers because I would like the complete lie you have published about me and those photographs to be removed from your book. And I would like a donation to be made to the King’s Trust for the damage that you have caused with your lie.” It is not yet clear if Morgan will accept the apology. In his book, Spencer recalled a conversation he had with King Charles in 1997 over whether Princes William and Harry should walk behind the coffin of Diana ahead of her funeral. Spencer said his reservations were met with a “stream of anger” from Charles. He writes that the then Prince “unleashed down the phone what I have always taken to be his pent-up contempt for Diana, and his horror that the world was so bowled over by her death. ‘Rest assured,’ he hissed, ‘we’ll forget her soon enough.’” In response, Buckingham Palace said last week: “While we do not comment on books as a matter of principle, His Majesty is mindful that the pain of fraternal grief can cloud reason, affect judgment and colour memory in ways others do not recognise, even many years after such a loss.” ‘Gangs Of London’ Producers Suing Vice, Claiming They Are Owed $20M Piers Morgan Wins Apology From Diana’s Brother Over Memoir Which Midnight Madness TIFF Pic Could Become The Next Box Office Obsession? ‘Resident Evil’ Levels Up With Franchise & Cregger Record $108M WW Read More About: Comments
