articles.title: John Wilson Lays Down ‘The History of Concrete’ With ‘The Weight’, ‘Shaun The Sheep’ In Packed Indie Weekend – Specialty Preview
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill AG Bonta Says Paramount’s California Exit Is David Ellison’s Choice: “It Lies At Their Feet” Steven Paul Talks U.S. Production Incentive And “Uplifts” To Sweeten Deal As Draft Legislation Takes Shape James Cameron’s Lightstorm Vision Acquires Creative-Tech Collective Outsyders View All September 18, 2026 4:15pm The Weight and A History Of Concrete and Shaun the Sheep- The Beast of Mossy Bottom Vertical/John Wilson/Ardman It’s a busy specialty weekend with fewer new studio releases. Well-reviewed Depression-era western The Weight starring Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe in wide release joins comedic doc The History of Concrete by John Wilson in an exclusive engagement. GKids opens Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom and Johnny Knoxville stars in R-rated Tiny Fugitives . From TIFF come Angelina Jolie’s drama Without Blood and doc You Had to Be There (full title below), about how a 1972 Toronto production of the musical Godspell changed the comedy world. Related Stories News The 65 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office News 48 Of The Most Anticipated Movies Of 2026 The Weight from Vertical opens in wide release on 1,504 screens. Director Padraic McKinley’s feature film debut stars Ethan Hawke and Russell Crowe. Certified Fresh at 93% on Rotten Tomatoes, it premiered at Sundance, see Deadline review . Opened the Deauville Film Festival this month, with Hawke receiving the Deauville Talent Award celebrating exceptional artists in cinema. Watch on Deadline Referenced as harkening back to classics such as William Friedkin’s Sorcerer and John Huston’s Treasure of the Sierra Madre , The Weight is set in 1933 Oregon as Samuel Murphy (Hawke) is torn from his daughter and sent to a brutal work camp. Warden Clancy (Crowe) tempts him with early release if he smuggles gold through deadly wilderness, but betrayal festers within the crew, and Murphy questions how far he’ll go to see his child again. Preview events this week included an AMC Dolby Cinema Early Access screening program at 200+ theaters and an Alamo Drafthouse simulcast screening across the chain’s markets followed by a live Q&A with Hawke, co-star Julia Jones and McKinley from the Brooklyn location. Magnolia Pictures drops Sundance-premiering The History of Concrete by the host of HBO series How To with John Wilson at the IFC Center in New York. The comedic documentary is loosely structured around and inspired by cement, the world’s most widely used building material and the bedrock of Wilson’s beloved New York City. He bounces from Rome to check out the Pantheon, built in 126 AD (the world’s largest unreinforced concrete dome), to a concrete convention in Vegas, with long digressions into Hallmark moviemaking, tattoo taxidermy and New York’s underground music scene — interspersed with musings on his career path and Zoom meetings with perplexed potential investors in the project. Wilson’s HBO series ran for three seasons from 2020-23. The History of Concrete sits at 100% RT score (off 41 reviews). Based on presales, it’s looking like the best opening for a documentary in IFC’s 21-year history, per Magnolia. The distributor went heavy on the NYC premiere Wednesday with a concrete truck wrapped in the film’s title treatment parked outside the theater, and a 125-pound poster made entirely from concrete in the lobby. Expands to 20 markets including Los Angeles next week. Greenwich Entertainment is out with You Had To Be There: How the Toronto Godspell Ignited the Comedy Revolution, Spread Love & Overalls, and Created a Community That Changed the World (In a Canadian Kind of Way ) by Nick Davis at Film Forum in NYC. Eugene Levy, Martin Short, Jayne Eastwood and others reminisce about the 1972 Toronto production of the musical Godspell , where Short, Levy, Gilda Radner, Victor Garber, Paul Shaffer and other entertainment icons got their start. Premiered at TIFF. See Deadline review. Executive produced by Judd Apatow. Adds L.A. and other markets next week. Without Blood from Brainstorm Media, directed by Angelina Jolie and starring Salma Hayek and Demián Bichir, opens on 350 screens. Jolie also produced and penned the screenplay based on the book by Italian writer Alessandro Baricco. A young woman seeks a reckoning decades after surviving the brutal murder of her family during a wartime conflict. Premiered at TIFF, see Deadline review . Moderate/wide : GKids is releasing StudioCanal and Aardman production Shaun the Sheep: The Beast of Mossy Bottom on 2,173 screens. The film is currently Certified Fresh at 98% on RT. Official synopsis: The residents of Mossy Bottom Farm are looking forward to Halloween – until the clumsy Farmer trashes the Flock’s beloved pumpkin patch. When Shaun turns mad scientist to fix the problem, things rapidly spiral out of control… With The Farmer missing and a wild beast roaming the woods of Mossingham, all the ingredients are in place for a monstrously fun family adventure. Indie distributor Inaugural Entertainment opens the raunchy R-rated comedy Tiny Fugitives , starring Johnny Knoxville, in about 300 theaters. Co-written and directed by Michael Lewen, it follows a reckless, fiercely determined group of 12-year-olds who hatch a chaotic plot to escape reality and spend the rest of their lives at sleepaway camp. Standing between them and permanent freedom is Bob (Knoxville), the camp’s deranged, relentless, 50-year-old lifer counselor. With Aaron Harris (Matlock) , Isa Bernal Steiner, Jai Soundar, Alyssa Gervasi, with Blake Anderson (Workaholics) and Jay Baruchel (How to Train Your Dragon) . Sundance-premiering The Musical by Giselle Bonilla, written by Alexander Heller and starring Will Brill (Tony winner for Stereophonic ), Gillian Jacobs and Rob Lowe (who also produces), is out on 250 screens. Convinced he’s a big fish stuck in a small pond, bitter playwright Doug Leibowitz has been marking time as a theater teacher until he can get to New York. But when he finds his ex has been dating the person he hates most in the world, the school principal, his plans shift to secretly staging the most inappropriate play possible at the middle school. Unapologetic Partners, Blue Harbor Entertainment and Variance Films are partnering on the release. Live-action biblical drama Daniel and the Fiery Furnace from EKKL Entertainment arrives on 1,493 screens this weekend. Written and directed by Matthew and Daniel Kooman, it’s the origin story of the prophet Daniel against the backdrop of exile in Babylon. Limited: Watermelon Pictures opens Traces of Home by Colette Ghunim at the Angelika in NYC. The doc follows the filmmaker on a journey of self-discovery as she sets out to reunite her parents with the ancestral homes they were forced to flee as children in Palestine and Mexico. Filmed over five years and featuring animation and archival footage. Executive produced by Melissa Barrera and John Leguizamo. Winner of the Grand Jury Prize in U.S. Competition at DOC NYC last November and Best Documentary Feature at San Diego Latino Film Festival. Expands to Laemmle Royal and Laemmle Glendale in L.A. next week. As Alex Gibney’s Musk makes headlines, the Oscar-winning documentarian has another film out this weekend — Knife: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie opens in 18 theaters via Abramorama. Featuring the writer and his wife Rachel Eliza Griffiths and inspired by Rushdie’s memoir Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder , it explores his recovery from a 2022 attack at a speaking engagement where was stabbed 15 times. With personal footage that has never been seen by the public, the doc follows the writer on his physical and spiritual recovery. Quiver Distribution debuts Berlin-premiering coming-of-age drama Sunny Dancer on about 20 screens. A group of teenagers finds friendship at a summer camp for cancer survivors. Stars Bella Ramsey, Neil Patrick Harris, James Norton and Jessica Gunning with a score by Este Haim. Fourth Act Film opens SXSW-premiering documentary First They Came for My College , directed and produced by Patrick Bresnan about a right-wing takeover of liberal arts school the New College of Florida orchestrated by Republican Gov. Ron DeSantis. World premiered at True/False and screened at DC/DOX, IFF Boston, SFFILM and the Florida Film Festival, where it won the Feature Documentary Audience Award. Starts at the Hippodrome in Gainesville, FL, and rolls out to about 30 markets, hitting DCTV in New York City on Sept. 25. ‘Resident Evil’ Leveling Up With Franchise-Record $50M-Plus U.S. Opening Trump Bans CNN, MS Now & Others From White House, Says More To Follow Company & State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of Settlement Meetings Brad Pitt Returning For ‘World War Z’ Sequel; Edward Berger Directs For Paramount Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Paramount And State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of October Settlement Meetings
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten , Dade Hayes September 18, 2026 4:44pm Story Arc L-R: Rob Bonta and David Ellison Getty Images They’re talking! Or are they? And what are they actually talking about? Does everyone need to chill out? Paramount and state attorneys general are talking, we are told. However, the discussions that are occurring over coming to a deal in the battle over Paramount’s $111 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery are far from advanced. Related Stories Legal Paramount Sets California Exit Plans Over Antitrust Battle With Blue States & Stymied $111B WBD Merger News Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Clears FCC Foreign Ownership Review In fact, sources tell us, the conversations that are occurring between David Ellison ’s team and California AG Rob Bonta ’s crew are centered on laying out the agenda for their already scheduled mid-October court ordered settlement discussions. “This is part of the process before you get the principals onboard, it’s pretty straightforward,” declares an individual with direct knowledge of the state of affairs. “The end is not nigh.” Earlier this week, a federal judge made it official and ordered Para, WBD and the AGs to appear for a two-day settlement conference October 14-15 in a San Francisco courtroom. Watch on Deadline Core to the discussions will be scenarios like Paramount potentially operating the film and TV studios of Paramount and Warner Bros. separately, at least for a period of time after the close. Bonta has said a “behavioral remedy” like the company agreeing to release at least 30 films a year, will not satisfy the plaintiffs. Along with studio consolidation, cable network concentration is a key part of the states’ complaint, with speculation centering on some way of moving some of the 50-plus cable networks out of the combined portfolio to avoid running afoul of antitrust limits. Eyebrows (and hopes) were raised late Friday about a potential resolution of Paramount’s legally waylaid WBD merger. The Wall Street Journal reported tonight that Paramount is in “advanced talks” with California’s Bonta over a settlement of the antitrust suit being brought by the Golden State AG and 11 other states. Shares in Paramount, which are down 23% in 2026 to date amid mounting uncertainty about the fate of the merger, jumped 5% in after-hours trading. WBD stock, which is also underwater for the year, rose 6% after hours. After Donald Trump’s DOJ and other major jurisdictions approved the mega-merger with no conditions, the dozen attorneys general filed a much-expected antitrust suit against Para and WBD on July 13. The case, set to go to trial on March 2, 2027, has seen an explosion of threats that Paramount would move to a red state , “blackmail” accusations by Bonta and a media war in the court of public opinion. It could also cost Ellison and his Oracle founding father Larry Ellison some sweet cash with a $7 million a day ticking fee set to WBD shareholders to start on October 1. In that context, talk of advanced talks is just another piece of that PR puzzle. “I get why some want this to look bigger than it is, there’s a lot of pressure here,” an insider notes. “This is too big, too much on the line for anyone to rush a deal,” the source added. “Hold your horses. No one wants to waste anyone’s time.” As with initial talks last month, it is mid-level staff that are in communication as the brass stay above the fray, as it is, we hear. Paramount had a blunt “no comment” on whether negotiations with the AGs were going on and what the status of them are at present. Having called out Paramount previously for alleged leaks that scuttled the last set of behind the scenes talks, Rob Bonta’s office today were 100% by the book. “Potential settlement talks are confidential,” a spokesperson for the CA AG told Deadline In the non-answer answer they added: “We cannot confirm or deny whether settlement talks are occurring or their alleged substance.” Interestingly, Bonta’s office did not complain of leaks or bad faith on the part of Paramount like they did last month when planned settlement talks were cancelled on claims the company was playing the press. While there appeared to be reason for optimism (mild as it is at this stage) there are many caveats to consider — and not just because there is a big Paramount+ streamed UFC fight out of L.A. this Yom Kippur weekend. Getty Images The latest word of discussions follows an ill-fated sequence in August. Bonta canceled negotiations hours before they were set to take place, accusing Ellison of “playing games” ahead of those meetings. “Not only did Paramount leak the alleged substance of settlement discussions, but they misrepresented these discussions, demonstrating a lack of good faith,” Bonta said at the time. Even as recently as Thursday of this week, when Bonta made an appearance at the Atlantic Festival in New York, the top cop of California said the fate of the deal “lies at the feet” of Ellison and the Paramount team. A follow up sit-down on MS Now, Democrats’ favorite cabler newser, contained much of the same even as Paramount leaks tried to up the ante on the Melrose lot packing up for Tennessee, Texas or Georgia. Sources tell us Bonta had a “conversation” with fellow ParaBros antitrust plaintiff NY AG Letitia James while out on the East Coast this week. To that, it is not clear if AG Bonta is back on the West Coast tonight. The leverage has been heavily on the side of the AGs since a string of rulings in the case by a federal judge favored the plaintiffs. Even when it came to setting a date for the antitrust trial, the judge landed on early March, which was a lot closer to the AGs’ preference of April than to Paramount’s stated desire for November. Despite momentum in the case, high-profile Democrats in California, including Gov. Gavin Newsom and L.A. Mayor Karen Bass, have publicly pressured Bonta multiple times to settle the case. The ambitious Newsom and reelection-fighting Bass fear damage to the industry, L.A. and the state if the deal remains pending for several months. At the same time, of course, a damning August report delivered to L.A. County from the region’s Department of Economic Opportunity says the $80 billion debt ladened merger will likely cause the loss of thousands of jobs , adding to the pain for a region already facing a downturn in production and other headwinds. The job loss and economic pain could be much greater if Paramount makes good on their threat to leave L.A., says a September 10 report to the County from the Economic Development Corporation. On the flip side, that same leaked EDC report, which Paramount commissioned, also told the powerful Board of Supervisors that ailing Hollywood would be boomtown if ParaBros went though with jobs and productions galore. As well, the ParaBros court calendar is looking pretty full even before those official settlement talks of next month and the spring 2027 trial. A hearing will be held next week in Oakland on Paramount’s request for a $1.88 billion bond from the plaintiffs to cover “extraordinary losses” the company anticipates due to having to pay those pricey ticking fee during litigation. On September 25, the blue state AGs have to respond to a motion from red state Iowa and Montana to take the validity of the antitrust suit to the Supreme Court. ‘Resident Evil’ Leveling Up With Franchise-Record $50M-Plus U.S. Opening Trump Bans CNN, MS Now & Others From White House, Says More To Follow Company & State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of Settlement Meetings Brad Pitt Returning For ‘World War Z’ Sequel; Edward Berger Directs For Paramount More from this Story Arc Paramount WB September 18, 2026 Those Across The Paramount-Warner Bros. articles.title: ‘VisionQuest’ Creator Terry Matalas Says No GenAI Was Used In Making Of Show: “There Hasn’t Really Been A Need”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘VisionQuest’ Creator Terry Matalas Says No GenAI Was Used In Making Of Show: “There Hasn’t Really Been A Need” Cody Fern Recalls Filming ‘House Of Cards’ When The Kevin Spacey “Nuclear Bomb Hit” Maisie Williams Played ‘Practical Magic 2’ Character As “Sapphic Icon” Despite Sequel Omitting Book’s LGBTQ Plot View All September 18, 2026 5:40pm Paul Bettany in 'VisionQuest' Marvel Despite VisionQuest ‘s subject matter as the first solo outing of the title artificial intelligence, the Marvel series kept things strictly human-made. articles.title: Kohner Agency Lays Off Its Talent Agents Due To “Profound & Unprecedented Economic Pressures”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Netflix Cancels ‘Sweet Magnolias’ After 5 Seasons, Orders New Sheryl J. Anderson & JoAnna Garcia Swisher Series ‘Ladies Of The House’ HBO Lands ‘The Spread’ Starring Javier Bardem With Series Order After Big Bidding War; Miami Drama Comes From Bill Dubuque & Fifth Season Hulu Orders ‘Heatwave’ Ibiza-Set Limited Series From ‘Joan’ Creator Anna Symon View All September 18, 2026 6:13pm EXCLUSIVE : The Kohner Agency is downsizing. Its three talent agents have been laid off. The talent department will stay open to service existing contracts and collect commission only. Owner and President Pearl Wexler stresses that the agency, which has been in business for almost 90 years, is not closing. Its literary department is staying put, and Wexler herself will continue to represent acting and literary clients. “It is with a heavy heart that we must announce a restructuring of our talent representation team, necessitated by the profound and unprecedented economic pressures currently facing the broader entertainment industry,” The Kohner Agency said in a statement to Deadline, which you can read in full below. Related Stories News 'VisionQuest' Creator Terry Matalas Says No GenAI Was Used In Making Of Show: "There Hasn't Really Been A Need" Legal Paramount And State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of October Settlement Meetings The post-Covid, post-Peak TV industry consolidation has been particularly hard on smaller, boutique talent agencies, which have found it hard to survive with a marquee, signature client who commands a big, steady paycheck as a star on an established series. Agencies that shut down in the past couple of years include A3 and KMR. That has further limited opportunities for up-and-coming actors to get an agent. Watch on Deadline Founded by Paul Kohner in 1938, The Kohner Agency is the second oldest in Los Angeles behind WMA (now WME) with long traditions in talent representations. Its early clients include Marlene Dietrich, Greta Garbo, Maurice Chevalier, Billy Wilder, Henry Fonda, John Huston, Ingmar Bergman, Lana Turner and Liv Ullmann. Wexler has owned and run the agency for the past 25 years. Here is the statement: For nearly nine decades, The Kohner Agency has stood as a pillar of the entertainment community, founded in the late 1930s as one of the oldest talent agencies in Los Angeles and built on a bedrock of fierce advocacy, boutique dedication, and deep artistic stewardship. Throughout our history, we have navigated changing landscapes by staying true to our core mission: protecting and nurturing the finest talent in film, television, theater, and literature. It is with a heavy heart that we must announce a restructuring of our talent representation team, necessitated by the profound and unprecedented economic pressures currently facing the broader entertainment industry. This decision was agonizing, and we do not take lightly the impact it has on colleagues who have been valued parts of our professional family. We are incredibly grateful for their hard work, dedication, and contributions during their time with the agency, and we sincerely wish them the very best in their future endeavors. Moving forward, the Kohner Agency leadership will be overseeing the transition to ensure continuity for our clients as we steer the agency through these challenging times. ‘Resident Evil’ Leveling Up With Franchise-Record $50M-Plus U.S. Opening Trump Bans CNN, MS Now & Others From White House, Says More To Follow Company & State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of Settlement Meetings Brad Pitt Returning For ‘World War Z’ Sequel; Edward Berger Directs For Paramount Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: ‘Lollipop Chainsaw’: Cult Japanese Video Game Getting The Live Action Feature Treatment
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Stephanie Cole Dies: British Star Of ‘Open All Hours’ & ‘Doc Martin’ Was 84 International Insider: ‘Naza’ Saga In Israel; France Makes Oscar Choice; Right Royal Timing ZDF Boards BBC Drama ‘Shy & Lola’ Featuring ‘Harry Potter’ & ‘Night Manager’ Stars View All September 18, 2026 6:30pm Lollipop Chainsaw Playstation EXCLUSIVE: Cult Japanese video game Lollipop Chainsaw is heading to the big screen. Deadline can reveal that a live action feature version is in the works as the game’s creators look to establish “a new model for building globally recognized entertainment franchises from Asia.” The latest Lollipop Chainsaw video game launches soon alongside an animated series. Set before the events of the original game and envisioned as an R-rated action comedy, the Lollipop Chainsaw film follows protagonist Juliet Starling, a San Romero High School cheerleader born into a legendary family of zombie hunters. When a catastrophic zombie outbreak engulfs her school, Juliet must fight her way through the undead to save her friends, protect her family, and somehow keep her boyfriend Nick close – even if doing so ultimately requires some highly unconventional arrangements. Related Stories News Amazon Puts Luna Video Game Titles On Fire TV As Free Add-On For Prime Members News Xbox Laying Off 3,200 Staffers, CEO Confirms: "Our Business Today Is Not Healthy" Unveiled today at the Tokyo Game Show , the movie comes under license from Dragami Games and is being put together by an international creative and production team comprising Nada Holdings boss Joe Teng ( As One ), former ZDF Studios drama boss Robert Franke and his Orange Chariot indie, Throne Inc MD Takafumi Yuki, Ambitious Entertainment’s Kirk Shaw and Non Stop TV’s Patricio Rabuffetti. Watch on Deadline Released in 2012, Lollipop Chainsaw has over the years become a cult hit that has sold more than 1.5 million copies worldwide. A remastered edition, Lollipop Chainsaw RePOP , came out two years ago. Dragami Games President Shohei Sato said: “We are truly excited to see our vision take another important step with the franchise’s first live-action feature film. We are especially pleased to be working with such an experienced and passionate international team— one that understands what makes Lollipop Chainsaw special while embracing the opportunity to create something new.” Franke added: “We are making a film that feels unmistakably true to the spirit of Lollipop Chainsaw while standing completely on its own. Longtime fans will recognize the attitude, irreverence, and glorious excess they love, while newcomers can simply enjoy an unforgettable action-horror comedy. Our ambition is to create a film that entertains audiences everywhere, whether they’ve played the game or not.” ‘Resident Evil’ Leveling Up With Franchise-Record $50M-Plus U.S. Opening Trump Bans CNN, MS Now & Others From White House, Says More To Follow Company & State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of Settlement Meetings Brad Pitt Returning For ‘World War Z’ Sequel; Edward Berger Directs For Paramount Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Deadline’s L.A. Law Summit: Nina Shaw & Patricia Glaser Honored On Day Of Big Ideas, Big Insights; Watch The Video Presentations
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Paramount And State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of October Settlement Meetings Banned: CNN & MS Now Shut Out Of White House By Trump; POTUS Says “Other Fake News Media Outlets To Follow” Gavin Newsom Moves To Lasso AI With “Kill Switch” Oversight Executive Order: “We’re Not Waiting To Act” View All September 18, 2026 7:17pm Nina Shaw and Patricia Glaser Earl Gibson III/Deadline via Getty Images Deadline’s inaugural L.A. Law Summit honored two powerhouses of the profession with awards Thursday for Patricia Glaser and Nina Shaw “If you’re perceived, and underline the word perceived, as good, the sky’s the limit in Los Angeles,” Glaser told a packed house at Deadline’s L.A. Law Summit on Thursday at the conference with Los Angeles’ legal and creative heavy hitters to examine the big ideas and big topics for Hollywood “It is truly a meritocracy, and we should be really proud of that.” In a similar spirit, Shaw spotlighted the power of character and the work when she told the September 17 conference: “I’m honored to be part of a legal community that strives to make the world better by supporting the arts. While while much of the work that we do is not known outside of these rooms, we know our contributions matter.” Related Stories Agencies CAA Signs 'Kick On' Filmmaker Nick Kozakis Politics Gavin Newsom Moves To Lasso AI With "Kill Switch" Oversight Executive Order: "We're Not Waiting To Act" When it comes to Glaser and Shaw, as generations of clients and projects, those contributions matter a lot. So, among a legion of lawyers from the top firms in town on panels and in the audience, if Deadline’s L.A. Law Summit is going to have the Glaser Weil Fink Howard Jordan & Shapiro founding parter and the Del Shaw Moonves Tanaka Finkelstein Lezcano Bobb & Dang founding partner in the house, then the esteemed lawyers should be honored for their wide reaching contribution to their profession and the industry That’s exactly what went down this week as litigator Glaser received the Visionary Award and Shaw received the Game Changer Award. Introduced respectively by Glaser Weil’s Gali Grant and Black List founder Franklin Leonard (after a note from WBTV boss Channing Dungey, Glaser and Shaw both addressed the other attorneys in the glass walled conference room at Deadline’s West LA HQ, along with the agents, creators and executives there too. Take a look at the Visionary Award presentation for the Glaser Weil founding partner here: Watch the Game Changer Award ceremony for Shaw and her speech to the L.A. Law Summit here: Beginning with a quote from JFK and remembrance of the recently deceased Glaser Weil parter Roger Howard , the fast paced L.A. Law Summit saw discussions on IP, M&A (can you say ParaBros?), the Creator Economy and, of course, AI. Introduced by Deadline Editor-in-Chief Nellie Andreeva, the sessions were moderated by Deadline’s Executive Editor Dominic Patten, Political Editor Ted Johnson and Senior TV and Labor reporter Katie Campione. Earl Gibson III The day kicked off with Power and Nemesis co-creator Courtney Kemp, Blank Rome’s Cheryl S. Chang, Greenberg Glusker’s Chad R. Fitzgerald and Davis Wright Tremaine’s Nicolas Jampol dived into the intricacies of IP in a multi-platform market. Then Stubbs Alderton & Markiles’ Cathleen Green and Davis Wright Tremaine’s Carrie Casselman joined WME Chief Legal Officer Courtney Braun and the always closing Macro CEO Charles D King to talk M&A. After lunch, Range Media Partners ‘ Jack Whigham, Del Shaw’s Ethan Cohan, Greenberg Glusker’s Matt Dysart and Emmy-winning director-producer Anthony Hemingway centered on the true art of the deal and examined what it really means to be a Creator in 21st Century Tinseltown. Deadline’s first L.A. Law Summit ended on a bang with CAA ‘s Chief Compliance Officer and Deputy General Counsel Tammy Brandt, Glaser Weil’s Jesse Levin and Blank Rome’s Craig Weiner taking on the facts, fictions and future of AI for the industry and society. articles.title: Gerrit Graham Dead: ‘Star Trek’ & ‘Phantom of the Paradise’ Actor Was 76
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘VisionQuest’ Creator Terry Matalas Says No GenAI Was Used In Making Of Show: “There Hasn’t Really Been A Need” Cody Fern Recalls Filming ‘House Of Cards’ When The Kevin Spacey “Nuclear Bomb Hit” Maisie Williams Played ‘Practical Magic 2’ Character As “Sapphic Icon” Despite Sequel Omitting Book’s LGBTQ Plot View All September 18, 2026 8:28pm Gerrit Graham in 'Phantom of the Paradise' (1974) 20th Century Fox Film Corp. Gerrit Graham , the actor known for roles in Phantom of the Paradise (1974) and Star Trek , has died. He was 76. The actor died of lung disease and other health complications on Tuesday in Rhinebeck, NY, according to Variety . Born Nov. 27, 1949 in New York City, Graham trained at Columbia University, where he was head of the school’s Columbia Players theater company. He made his onscreen debut in Brian De Palma’s 1968 sophomore feature Greetings . Graham was most known for his performance as glam rocker Beef in De Palma’s 1974 rock musical horror Phantom of the Paradise . He also played separate roles in Star Trek: Deep Space Nine and Star Trek: Voyager . Related Stories Legal Deadline's L.A. Law Summit: Nina Shaw & Patricia Glaser Honored On Day Of Big Ideas, Big Insights; Watch The Video Presentations News 'Lollipop Chainsaw': Cult Japanese Video Game Getting The Live Action Feature Treatment Over the years, Graham had roles in such films as Beware! The Blob (1972), Demon Seed (1977), Used Cars (1980), National Lampoon’s Class Reunion (1982), TerrorVision (1986), Chopping Mall (1986), Police Academy 6: City Under Siege (1989), C.H.U.D. II: Bud the C.H.U.D. (1989), The Little Mermaid (1989), Child’s Play 2 (1990), This Boy’s Life (1993), My Girl 2 (1994) and more. Watch on Deadline On TV, Graham appeared in episodes of Dynasty , Starsky & Hutch , Laverne & Shirley , The A-Team , The Dukes of Hazzard , The Twilight Zone , St. Elsewhere , Miami Vice , Dallas , Tales from the Crypt , The Wonder Years , Seinfeld , Family Matters , Babylon 5 , Law & Order and more. Also a writer, Graham penned two episodes of The Twilight Zone and wrote songs with the Grateful Dead’s Bob Weir. ‘Resident Evil’ Leveling Up With Franchise-Record $50M-Plus U.S. Opening Trump Bans CNN, MS Now & Others From White House, Says More To Follow Company & State AGs Begin Preliminary Talks Ahead Of Settlement Meetings Brad Pitt Returning For ‘World War Z’ Sequel; Edward Berger Directs For Paramount Read More About: 3 Comments

articles.title: Naomi Watts Says She’d Like To Work With Paul Thomas Anderson & Praises The Advancements Older Women Have Made In Hollywood — San Sebastián
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Naomi Watts Says She’d Like To Work With Paul Thomas Anderson & Praises The Advancements Older Women Have Made In Hollywood — San Sebastián San Sebastián Opens With Political Declarations And Tributes To Werner Herzog & Outgoing Festival Director José Luis Rebordinos Fatih Akin On How A Period Of Professional Crisis Inspired His Paranormal Love Story ‘Ghost Song’ — San Sebastian View All September 19, 2026 2:26am Naomi Watts ANDER GILLENEA / AFP via Getty Images. “I started, by Hollywood standards, quite late,” Naomi Watts began this morning when quizzed on whether the treatment of older women in Hollywood has improved during a press conference at the San Sebastián Film Festival. The British-Aussie actor is at the Spanish festival to receive an honorary Donostia Award for career achievement. “I launched with Mulholland Drive , and I was 30 or 31,” Watts continued. “And I was told that I better get my skates on because it all finishes at the age of 40, but here we are today. I’m in my late 50s now.” Watts continued to praise the improvements in the Hollywood industry that have prolonged women’s careers. Related Stories News San Sebastián Opens With Political Declarations And Tributes To Werner Herzog & Outgoing Festival Director José Luis Rebordinos News Fatih Akin On How A Period Of Professional Crisis Inspired His Paranormal Love Story 'Ghost Song' -- San Sebastian “Look at the Emmys just last week, there were a number of women in strong categories over 50, so that’s heartening to see,” she said. “I do think things have changed. Women are consumers of film and TV. Their stories should be reflected. Everybody needs to see their story reflected in storytelling, so that narrative had to be shifted, and I’m grateful to be a small part of that shift.” Watch on Deadline Here in San Sebastian, Watts is also joined by her Housewife cast and director, Ben Shirinian. The film will screen this evening at the festival following Watts’ Donostia Award presentation. Set in 1964, The Housewife follows Hermine (Watts) and her hardworking husband Russel (Luke Evans), who enjoy a seemingly normal life in New York City — until the fateful day Hermine meets The New York Times journalist Joseph Lelyveld (Tye Sheridan). Following a tip from a Holocaust survivor, Joseph is investigating the possibility that Russel might be a Nazi in hiding. As his inquiry deepens — and his exchanges with Hermine become increasingly intimate — Joseph discovers a series of revelations far stranger and more complicated than he could have imagined. Watts described the role as a challenging “mind twister.” “The storyline was compelling. It is based on true events, and so it really drew me in,” she said. Elsewhere during the press conference, Watts was asked whether she had any professional goals or directors that she’d still like to work with. She responded: “Paul Thomas Anderson is someone I’ve wanted to work with for a long time.” Anderson debuts his next feature, a concert filmed at Carnegie Hall with Geese frontman Cameron Winter, next month at the New York Film Festival. A24 will release that film in cinemas.
