articles.title: ‘Charlie’s Angels’ Stars Jaclyn Smith, Kate Jackson and Cheryl Ladd Reunite at 2026 Emmys to Honor Farrah Fawcett: “Shiniest Angel of All”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All September 15, 2026 12:21am Jaclyn Smith, Kate Jackson and Cheryl Ladd speak on stage during the 78th Primetime Emmy Awards held at the Peacock Theater on September 14, 2026. Trae Patton/NBC via Getty Images The stars of Charlie’s Angels reconvened at the 2026 Emmys , where they paid homage to the late Farrah Fawcett . Kate Jackson , Cheryl Ladd and Jaclyn Smith were onsite to celebrate the show’s 50th anniversary , and present the Emmy for best drama series, which ultimately went to The Pitt . “It’s an honor to be here tonight to present the Emmy for drama series and to celebrate the 50th anniversary of Charlie’s Angels ,” Jackson began, before Smith paid tribute to Fawcett. “I would like to acknowledge someone not standing with us tonight, and that’s my friend Farrah Fawcett. As I’ve said many times, charisma doesn’t need a second season,” Smith said, a reference to her starring turn in only the first season of Charlie’s Angels . “As I said many times, she’s here with us in everyone’s collective memory.” Related Stories Critic's Notebook The Michael J. Fox Tribute, Mariska Hargitay Singing, and Other Highs and Lows From an Ungainly, Ill-Flowing Emmys Telecast TV Inside Zendaya's 2026 Emmys: Date Night With Tom Holland, Surprise Dinner Invite and That Pixie Cut Jackson continued of their co-star, “Farrah was the shiniest angel of all, and she was loved by millions of people all over the world, and she still is today. And they’ll never forget her and neither will we, and I’m sure you won’t either.” “And her iconic poster lives in the minds, and the garages, of many a man,” Ladd added before they announced The Pitt as the best drama Emmy winner. Charlie’s Angels debuted on Sept. 22, 1976, created by Ivan Goff and Ben Roberts. Jackson, Smith and Fawcett starred in season one as three investigators who worked for their boss, Charlie. Fawcett departed as the first installment, and Ladd joined the cast. Heading into this year’s Emmys , The Pitt led the nominees with a total of 25 nods, followed by Hacks with 24 (which set a record for a comedy series nominations in a single year) and Widow’s Bay with 19 . The 78th Emmy Awards telecast live from the Peacock Theater at L.A. Live in Los Angeles Monday night on NBC, streaming on Peacock. Mariska Hargitay served as the night’s host, after last week winning two Emmys at the Creative Arts ceremony. See the full 2026 Emmys winners list and all the dazzling red carpet looks here . THR

articles.title: Massih Parsaei’s San Sebastian-Bound Debut ‘Lovers Sleep Alone’ Chronicles a Queer Man in Exile (Exclusive Clip)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All September 15, 2026 2:30am 'Lovers Sleep Alone' San Sebastian Film Festival The Hollywood Reporter can unveil an exclusive clip from Massih Parsaei’s Lovers Sleep Alone , set to premiere at the upcoming San Sebastian Film Festival . The Iranian filmmaker is competing in the New Directors selection with the Berlin-set drama, focused on an isolated lead character played by Pooyesh Frozandeh in the actor’s first feature film role. With a screenplay from Parsaei and Hanna Thomschke, the tender Lovers Sleep Alone premieres on Sept. 25 at the Spanish film festival and follows Iman, who has built his life in Berlin around absence. “From his family, from Iran, from being known,” continues a plot synopsis. “He drifts through the city, chasing closeness and solitude. Day in, night out, he works as a caregiver for an old man and at a truck wash. He fills the silence with invented stories and a man he meets for sex in a park. On his endless paths through the city, the fragments from the lives of other passersby drifts alongside him.” Related Stories Movies Oscars: Bulgaria Picks Cannes Winner 'The Dreamed Adventure' for Best International Feature Race TV 'Murdoch Mysteries' Producer Christina Jennings Raises Alarm on Canadian Sovereignty: "We're a Bit Under Siege" “When his cousin Maneli visits from Tehran,” the synopsis continues, “what Iman left behind quietly finds its way back to him.” The debut filmmaker said about his personal ties to the project: “This film comes out of my own experience of leaving, and of everything that time doesn’t fix, even long after you’ve arrived. Iman is a queer man in exile, on the margins in more than one way. He stands between the images of desire he grew up with and the ones that are only beginning to form, ones he is still learning to trust.” “I know that in-between from my own life, and I’ve rarely seen it on screen. I didn’t want to explain him, or account for how his past shaped the person he is now. Not his suffering, not a story about being saved. I wanted to show his days, and the state underneath them. Iman is the passer-by we don’t pass by, the one we stay with,” Parsaei added. The clip released to THR , which you can watch below, shows a car window looking out onto the gloomy, bustling streets of the German capital as a passerby ponders over whether fear can often feel like an illness. Lovers Sleep Alone is a Film Five GmbH Production, in co-production with the Konrad Wolf Film University of Babelsberg. The project was funded by Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg & Rundfunk Berlin Brandenburg as part of the Leuchtstoff initiative, and supported by the Young Talent Foundation Berlin. Co-starring with Frozandeh is Ava Darvishi, an Iranian actor, theatre maker and playback theatre practitioner based in Ghent, Belgium, as well as Marcel Kohler, a German stage and screen actor based in Berlin. Check out the snippet from Lovers Sleep Alone below. The 2026 San Sebastian International Film Festival runs Sept. 18-26. THR

articles.title: ‘The Test’ Season 4 Among Prime Video’s New Australian Originals
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All September 15, 2026 2:55am 'The Test' Scott Ehler Photography/Amazon MGM Studios Amazon Prime Video has commissioned three new Australian Prime Original docuseries. The streamer has confirmed a fourth season of its popular cricket behind-the-scenes docuseries The Test . The upcoming chapter will follow the Australia mens test cricket team on their packed 2026-27 schedule that includes daunting tours to South Africa, India, the one-off 150th Anniversary Test against England and the 2027 Ashes tour. Season four should be an intriguing watch as the Baggy Greens enter a period of transition, with many legends aging out and attempts to blood younger players proving a struggle thus far, all under the intense scrutiny of a demanding Aussie press and public. Related Stories Movies Massih Parsaei's San Sebastian-Bound Debut 'Lovers Sleep Alone' Chronicles a Queer Man in Exile (Exclusive Clip) Movies Oscars: Bulgaria Picks Cannes Winner 'The Dreamed Adventure' for Best International Feature Race The Test , a co-production between Amazon MGM Studios, Cricket Australia and Whooshka Media, will stream globally but a released date hasn’t been released yet. Prime Video has also commissioned the true crime docuseries, Free Spirits: The Backpacker Poisonings (working title). Per the streamer, the logline for the series reads, “In late 2024, eight young backpackers from around the world including two Australians set off on the adventure of a lifetime through Southeast Asia, chasing freedom, friendship, and self-discovery. They documented everything on their phones: chaotic bus rides, late-night laughs, voice notes home, and joyful selfies. But after a night out in Laos, everything changed. Today, six are dead. Of the two who survived, one was left permanently blind. Told through the backpackers’ own footage, final messages, and intimate testimony from the survivor and the victims’ families, this three-part docuseries reconstructs the events leading up to the tragedy and the search for answers that followed. More than an investigation, it is a powerful coming-of-age story that serves as a cautionary tale about youth, risk, and the pursuit of adventure in an unpredictable world.” Free Spirits comes from Cineflix for Amazon MGM Studios and will also stream globally. ‘Free Spirits: The Backpacker Poisonings’ Cineflix/Amazon MGM Studios Madness of Three is Prime Video’s third original Aussie commission, and another true crime docuseries. The project, which was produced by Blackfella Films for Amazon MGM Studios, takes indepth look at the 2022 Wieambilla shootings, that became a global news story. A logline for the series reads, “[the docuseries covers] the shocking 2022 murders in Wieambilla, Queensland, when three locals, two of them former teachers, left two police officers and an innocent neighbour dead. With unprecedented and exclusive access, the five-part docuseries explores the conspiracy, delusion and online influence that drove Nathaniel, Stacey and Gareth Train to violence and asks how is it possible to go down the rabbit hole and never come back.” ‘Madness of Three’ Blackfella Films/Amazon MGM Studios “We strongly believe that to be successful globally, you need to be successful locally”, said Sarah Christie, head of Australian and New Zealand originals at Amazon MGM Studios, in a statement. “These new commissions reflect our continued dedication to telling compelling Australian stories that matter – from the sporting moments that unite us, to true crime cases that gripped us locally and made headlines internationally. Australia is home to extraordinary creative talent and we are proud to be investing in series that not only resonate with Australian audiences but captivate viewers around the world. These are powerful, authentic stories told with the depth and insight they deserve.” The three original commissions continue Prime Video’s investment in Australia in recent years, and the company says that it has commissions 34 Aussie original sinces 2019, that span the gamut of television production. Although the company has adopted an Australia-first approach in terms of the appeal of its originals, there have been notable breakout global hits, including the Jacob Elordi-starring limited series The Narrow Road to the Deep North and the black comedy series Deadloch . THR

articles.title: Oldenburg Adds Ned Crowley’s ‘Dead Drop’ to Line Up
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All September 15, 2026 3:00am 'Dead Drop' Ned Crowley The Oldenburg Film Festival has made a late edition to its line-up, adding Ned Crowley Dead Drop to its official selection. The film will have its world premiere at Oldenburg, Germany’s leading indie film fest. The high-concept horror thriller, according to the movie’s publicity material, follows a group of eight strangers who „board a freight elevatorn and find themselves trapped in an ever-worsening life-and-death predicament that ultimately reveals they are all linked together in a sinister, supernatural, or even biblical nightmare.” Related Stories TV 'The Test' Season 4 Among Prime Video's New Australian Originals Movies Massih Parsaei's San Sebastian-Bound Debut 'Lovers Sleep Alone' Chronicles a Queer Man in Exile (Exclusive Clip) The low-budget feature is Crowley’s follow up to his supernatural Western Killing Faith (2025) starring Guy Pearce, DeWanda Wise, and Bill Pullman, which has been a major streaming success, reaching number 2 on HBO Max’s worldwide movie charts and hitting number one in several territories, including Argentina and Brazil. Killing Faith got a boost from fan Stephen King, who, shortly after its premiere at Beyond Fest, posted a review on X, calling it “a quasi-supernatural Western that has echoes of Cormac McCarthy.” King ranked it as one of his favorite films of the year. For Dead Drop , Crowley said he decided to shift away from “sweeping landscapes and A-list actors” to “create something equally compelling within the confines of a locked, claustrophobic 15 foot steel box, driven by the performances of relatively unknown actors.” ‘Dead Drop’ Ned Crawley The film features an ensemble cast including Melissa Neal, Daniel Adeosun, Victor Rivera, Christina Tam, Alexandra kate, Roger Ajogbe, John O’Mahony, and Elijah Craft. Dead Drop is Crowley’s third feature as a director after Killing Faith and his 2016 debut Middle Man, a crime comedy starring Jim O’Heir, Andrew J. West, and Josh McDermitt. The 33 rd Oldenburg International Film Festival runs Sept. 16-20. THR

articles.title: Chicago Film Festival Sets International Competition Lineup With New Films From Ryusuke Hamaguchi, Hirokazu Kore-eda and Lee Chang-dong
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By Seth Abramovitch Plus Icon Seth Abramovitch Senior Writer SethAbramovitch Follow Sign Up View All September 15, 2026 6:00am Ryusuke Hamaguchi (L), winner of the International Feature Film award for ‘Drive My Car,’ attends the Governors Ball during the 94th Annual Academy Awards at Dolby Theatre on March 27, 2022, in Hollywood. Emma McIntyre/Getty Images The Chicago International Film Festival has unveiled the international competition selections for its 62nd edition, with new films from Ryusuke Hamaguchi , Hirokazu Kore-eda and Lee Chang-dong among the highest-profile titles in the lineup. Hamaguchi’s All of a Sudden , Kore-eda’s Look Back and Lee’s Possible Love will compete for the Gold Hugo in the International Feature Competition. The 13-film section also includes Radu Jude’s The Diary of a Chambermaid , Clio Barnard’s I See Buildings Fall Like Lightning , Valeska Grisebach’s The Dreamed Adventure and Andrea Pallaoro’s The Echo Chamber , which will have its North American premiere in Chicago. Related Stories Movies Oscars: Japan Picks Ryusuke Hamaguchi's 'All of a Sudden' as Best Int'l Feature Submission Movies Awards Categories Set for Cannes-Winning 'All of a Sudden' Actresses Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto (Exclusive) The festival, which runs Oct. 14-25, said the competitive program includes 25 North American or U. S. premieres across its International Feature, New Directors, Documentary and OutLook sections. Films from Germany, Japan, Spain, the Central African Republic, Brazil, Nigeria and Turkey are represented. Four selections have been submitted by their countries for the best international feature Oscar: All of a Sudden , Sandra Wollner’s Everytime , Ahmed Hassouna’s documentary Citizen Osama and Lee’s Possible Love . The festival’s fourth annual International Contenders Panel, bringing together filmmakers behind national Oscar submissions, will be moderated by The Hollywood Reporter ‘s Seth Abramovitch on Oct. 17. The New Directors Competition includes Arie Esiri and Chuko Esiri’s Clarissa , Ashgan El-Hamus’ Al Baraneya , Rafiki Fariala’s Congo Boy , Gessica Geneus’ Marie Madeleine and The Riverbank from Enock Carvalho and Matheus Farias. Other selections include Anna Foglietta’s A Common Story , Valentina Maurel’s Forever Your Maternal Animal and Bruno Santamaria Razo’s Six Months in a Pink and Blue Building . Documentary contenders include Alessandra Sanguinetti’s The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer , Erik Shirai’s Sumo: Spirit Weighs Nothing and Mila Aung-Thwin’s The Ultra Runner . Citizen Osama , Mariinka , Summer Drift and Tricontinental, Letter to Open in Case Of will make their North American premieres. The festival’s OutLook Competition, devoted to LGBTQ+ stories and perspectives, includes Ira Sachs’ The Man I Love , Kōji Fukada’s Nagi Notes , Corrin Evans’ Corpus , Abinash Bikram Shah’s Elephants in the Fog and Kris Rey’s Trash Mountain . The Riverbank , Six Months in a Pink and Blue Building and Summer Drift will compete in both OutLook and another international section. Recent Chicago winners that went on to Academy Award recognition include Sirat , The Voice of Hind Rajab , The Seed of the Sacred Fig , Close , Drive My Car and The Worst Person in the World , all nominated for best international feature, as well as best documentary nominee Four Daughters . The complete festival lineup will be announced Sept. 17. Jordan Firstman’s Club Kid will open the festival, while Mouse , from filmmakers Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson, has been selected as the centerpiece presentation. Tickets for the remaining programs go on sale Sept. 28, following a Cinema/Chicago members presale beginning Sept. 18. THR

articles.title: Amsterdam Doc Fest IDFA to Celebrate Tatiana Huezo, Put Spotlight on William Greaves
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All September 15, 2026 6:00am Tatiana Huezo Courtesy of Tatiana Huezo Mexican-Salvadoran filmmaker Tatiana Huezo ( Prayers for the Stolen , The Echo ) will be the guest of honor at the 2026 International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam ( IDFA ), which takes place Nov. 12-22. In addition to the Huezo retrospective, the doc fest on Tuesday also unveiled a spotlight on pioneering U.S. filmmaker, producer, editor and actor William Greaves . Plus, the festival said that it would wrap up its multi-year program “Dead Angle” with a focus on the theme Common Ground, following Borders in 2024 and Institutions in 2025. Related Stories Movies Oldenburg Adds Ned Crawley's 'Drop Dead' to Line Up TV 'The Test' Season 4 Among Prime Video's New Australian Originals IDFA said that its 2026 edition will also feature Huezo’s personal top 10 film selection and a talk featuring the filmmaker. Born in El Salvador and raised in Mexico, she “has developed a distinctive body of work that moves between documentary and fiction, exploring how the violent consequences of organized crime and political turmoil shape the intimate lives of local families and communities,” fest organizers said. “Her cinema is rooted in close observation and shaped by a highly attentive visual and sonic language – allowing memories and experience to surface through atmosphere and deeply personal stories.” Huezo first gained international recognition with her feature-length debut The Tiniest Place (2011), a portrait of a remote Salvadoran village whose inhabitants carry the memory of a massacre during the country’s civil war. Her fiction debut, Prayers for the Stolen (2021), is a coming-of-age story about girls growing up in the mountains of Mexico under the threat of human trafficking by local drug cartels. The spotlight on Greaves (1926–2014) is designed to bring “a rediscovered voice in cinema back into view,” IDFA said. Across a formally inventive filmography shaped by sharp observation of social and political life, Greaves explored Black history and culture.” The spotlight program includes Once Upon a Time in Harlem (2026), capturing a 1972 reunion of key Harlem Renaissance figures in Duke Ellington’s apartment, completed posthumously by Greaves’ son and granddaughter David and Liani Greaves. Also featured are Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One (1971), which turns a fiction shoot in Central Park into a self-reflexive study of a film crew in revolt, and a director’s cut of The Fight . About the Dead Angle: Common Ground focus, meanwhile, will be “exploring the many ways people come together – from extraordinary acts of solidarity and collective resistance to the everyday life of communities and quintessential function of public space,” IDFA highlighted. Among confirmed titles exploring solidarity in times of crisis are Everybody to Kenmure Street (2026) by Felipe Bustos Sierra, Shinsuke Ogawa’s The Battle Front for the Liberation of Japan – Summer in Sanrizuka (1968) and Barbara Kopple’s Oscar-winning American Dream (1990). Finally, IDFA DocLab returns this year with the exhibition of what the fest described as “a diverse lineup of interdisciplinary immersive art and anniversary highlights to be revealed in the coming weeks.” THR

articles.title: Alex Gibney’s ‘Musk’ Premieres in North America as Director Calls For People to “Stand Up and Resist”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By Steven Zeitchik Plus Icon Steven Zeitchik Senior Editor, Technology and Politics View All September 15, 2026 6:19am Jessie Deeter, Richard Perello, Katie Drummond, Alex Gibney, Zhang Xin, Nick Shumaker, Erin Edeiken and Dana O'Keefe attend the premiere of 'Musk' at Scotiabank Theatre on September 14, 2026 in Toronto, Ontario. The movie is a grenade tossed into the technocapitalist battlefield. Harold Feng/Getty Images A polite but outraged crowd greeted Alex Gibney ’s epic four-hour Elon Musk documentary at the Toronto Film Festival Monday night, marking the film’s arrival in North America and offering a glimpse into how the investigative grenade might land in theaters when it’s released in October. “I found it very overwhelming. And that’s a compliment,” one of the people in the audience said. That filmgoer would know — she was Katie Drummond, global editorial director of Wired and a key voice in the film, who was seeing it for the first time. “What stands out to me is how all encompassing [Musk’s] reach and power really are,” she said from the stage, standing next to Gibney. As documented in a Hollywood Reporter cover story two weeks ago, Musk is a four-hour dive into the growing economic and social influence of its polarizing title mogul, sweeping through his fiefdoms that range from AI to social media to automobiles to outer space and questioning both the credit given him and the lack of skepticism about the power he has accrued. One standout section focuses on the secrecy-clouded four-month DOGE period in Washington in which Musk and people who worked for him potentially collected intimate data on tens of millions of Americans, possibly even for later political use. Gibney keyed on that aspect at the Toronto premiere. “Shadow president of the United States,” is how he referred to Musk at one point speaking from the stage, and added, “I think we’re recognizing that a few billionaires are trying to take control of the world and it’s up to us to stand up and resist.” The audience applauded lustily after the movie ended, talking excitedly if nervously to each other as the lights came up and then shot hands in the air during a post-screening Q&A to ask about Musk’s power, filmmaking choices and, yes, potential resistance. At least one Musk stan did turn up at the screening, asking Gibney “would you rather live in a world without the accomplishments of Elon Musk” — a line Gibney parried back with “I kind of question the phrase the accomplishments of Elon Musk.” He added, “Tesla was not founded by Elon Musk; he was not the key inventor. SpaceX also was founded by a lot of powerful engineers.” The product of more than three years of shooting and editing (including a fresh round when its title subject ended up in Washington in 2024), Musk marks a career capstone for Gibney, who has taken on everything from Scientology to Enron to the U.S. military in past forays. The documentary arrives in North America after a blowout screening at the Venice Film Festival a week ago, where filmgoers openly thanked Gibney at the screening for the journalistic and democratic service he provided. The TIFF premiere also followed a conversation at TIFF on Sunday in which the director laid out the case for the film and said he got “nothing back” when he reached out to the mogul’s legal team after a threat. Musk is set to hit theaters in just a little a over three weeks. Distributor Bleecker Street moved the film up one week after A24 said it would drop its surprise Nathan Fielder-Lance Oppenheim documentary You Can See Everything on Oct. 16. Musk will now open New York and Los Angeles on Oct. 9 and then play in most major cities on the 16th, which will put the film up against the Elizabeth Holmes movie. A Barbenheimer situation — Molmes? Husk? — is possible, though filmgoers would need seven hours to spare. The movie will then move to a pay VOD window for as many as four months before HBO airs the film in the first quarter of 2027 — providing no monkey wrenches are thrown in by incoming Warner Bros. Discover owner David Ellison. A major awards push is also planned, with Musk a favorite to be nominated for best documentary and original song (a bouncily subversive David Byrne closing-credit number) and even could land a slot in best picture depending on how the narrative-film field shakes out. A doc has never been nommed for Oscar’s top prize, but both the Gibney and Fielder movies stand a better chance than any nonfiction film has in many years. Gibney’s subject, at least, is less excited about such a prospect. In response to the film, Musk’s attorney Alex Spiro last week sent a letter to filmmakers saying “Because you have refused to screen the film, refused to fact-check it with us and refused the witnesses who came to you, we have every reason to expect that it contains further statements about Mr Musk that you know to be false, or whose falsity you have deliberately chosen not to investigate.” The letter also noted, “As you know, we have attempted to contact you multiple times and requested an opportunity to present the facts in the normal fact-checking process that is the hallmark of ethical journalism. You have refused to engage.” Gibney fact-checked certain details with members of Musk’s team but has not offered to show him the movie, in keeping with a long tradition of journalists not making their work available to subjects before it is released. Gibney’s film also surfaces a text Musk sent ex Ashley St. Clair after the 2024 election in which he said he would “unleash the anomaly in the matrix,” noting his “lasers in space,” which St. Clair believes was a reference to Starlink. “You are on notice, before release, that the insinuation is false,” Spiro’s letter said. Musk kept quiet on X during and immediately after the TIFF premiere. In one of several posts on X last week, he posted, without being known to have seen the film, that it’s “a hit piece that misses, and makes the fatal sin of being boring for 4 hours.” But no one in the audience Monday seemed to be bored, shaking their heads at key moments, clapping enthusiastically at the end and making their approval known when Gibney offered in the Q&A that he would “question the phrase the accomplishments of Elon Musk.” After the talk, attendees mobbed Gibney to ask him everything from his reach-outs to Musk to how he chose which companies and eras of the mogul to focus on, the director spending nearly 20 minutes greeting the fans. THR

articles.title: ‘Slow Horses’ Renewed for Season 8 at Apple TV
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By Lisa de los Reyes Plus Icon Lisa de los Reyes Senior Copy Editor View All September 15, 2026 7:00am Gary Oldman and Kristin Scott Thomas in season six of 'Slow Horses' Apple TV Logo text Spies tend to have a short life expectancy, but the Slow Horses look set to outlast the odds. While there are no promises that the whole team will make it, Apple has announced a season eight renewal for its quirky espionage drama, which took home one Emmy — Saul Metzstein’s best directing for a drama series — from nine nominations Monday night. Slow Horses features Gary Oldman as the irascible Jackson Lamb, head of Slough House (where MI5 sticks its agents when they’ve proved not fit for purpose). His co-star Jack Lowden recently made headlines when Oldman suggested he’s a on the shortlist for the next James Bond , though The Hollywood Reporter understands a casting decision for Ian Fleming’s spy has not yet been made. Related Stories TV Apple TV Reigns at Emmys With 'Widow's Bay' and 'Pluribus' Breakthroughs Movies 'Being Heumann' Review: Siân Heder's Drama About the Fight for Disability Rights Strikes Familiar Notes but Gets the Inspirational Uplift Job Done The six-episode eighth season is adapted from Clown Town , the ninth novel in Mick Herron’s Slough House book series. It’ll see Lamb and Diana Taverner ( Kristin Scott Thomas ) face off in their most explosive confrontation yet. When a botched attempt to blackmail the Park puts Taverner on the offensive, it is up to Lamb to unravel one of MI5’s darkest secrets and put an end to it once and for all. Current castmembers also include Saskia Reeves as Catherine Standish, Christopher Cho as tech expert Roddy, Rosalind Eleazar as Louisa, Aimee-Ffion Edwards as Shirley, Tom Brooke as JK Coe and Jonathan Pryce as David Cartwright. Season six also sees the return of Hugo Weaving as Frank Harkness, River’s birth father, and Olivia Cooke as Sid, an agent who was believed dead. Adam Randall, who won an Emmy for directing in season four and returned to helm season six, will take the reins again for season eight. “We don’t kill anyone Mick hasn’t killed,” Randall teased of the upcoming season in an interview with THR . “It’s really exciting. With Clown Town , I knew I was going to do it, and I was reading the book [thinking], ‘Who survives Clown Town ?’” Jay Hunt, creative director, international at Apple TV added Monday: “ Slow Horses continues to charm audiences all around the world and I’m delighted that Jackson Lamb and his gang of lovable misfits will be back for an eighth season. Their acerbic take on the high-octane world of espionage is completely unique.” Asked if the show could continue if it were to outpace Herron’s novels, executive producer Douglas Urbanski previously told THR , “Most TV shows don’t have books, so we can figure this out. … And there’s another thing: Mick Herron hasn’t stopped writing. I can’t speak for Mick, but you never know, more books might be coming.” Season six of Slow Horses premieres Sept. 16 on Apple TV, with one episode set to drop each Wednesday through Oct. 21. This season adapts both the fifth and sixth novels, Joe Country and Slough House . The previously announced season seven will follow the events of Bad Actors ; its release date has not been announced. See-Saw Films produces Slow Horses for Apple TV, with Jamie Laurenson, Hakan Kousetta, Douglas Urbanski, Randall, Iain Canning, Emile Sherman, Gail Mutrux, Billy Bowring, Helen Gregory, Herron and Oldman serving as executive producers. Season eight is adapted for television and executive produced by Ben Vanstone. THR

articles.title: Keri Russell Confronts a “Culture of Consistent Lawlessness” in ‘The Diplomat’ Season 4 Trailer
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Full List All of the Winners at the 2026 Emmys close By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All September 15, 2026 7:01am Keri Russell and Rufus Sewell in 'The Diplomat' season 4. Courtesy of Netflix Logo text Keri Russell ‘s Kate Wyler is working to “repair a marriage … in a major security crisis” in the latest trailer for season four of Netflix ‘s political thriller The Diplomat , set to return on Oct. 15. While the first season four teaser , released last month, focused more on personal matters (specifically the reconciliation of central couple Kate and Hal Wyler ( Rufus Sewell )), the latest preview deals with geopolitical issues. In the trailer, Kate questions Hal, also the U.S. vice president in the fictional world of the show, and president Grace Penn’s ( Allison Janney , who won an Emmy Monday night for her supporting role in the political thriller ), aggressive approach to foreign policy. Related Stories TV Emmy Awards Snubs and Surprises: 'Hacks' Comes Up Short; John Oliver Shut Out; Allison Janney Scores Unexpected 'Diplomat' Win TV Matthew Rhys Says Keri Russell Is "Always Really the Winner" After His Historic 2026 Emmy Wins It was revealed in the closing moments of season three that Hal and Grace had schemed to steal a Russian nuclear weapon, with Kate figuring out what they did. As the trailer kicks off, she’s shown confronting Grace and Hal about what they did. “My concern is that the two of you together are, yeah, dangerous,” she’s heard saying. “Who pumps the brakes when you two are in the room?” Later she’s shown telling Grace that she’s concerned her “tolerance for risk to human life seems higher than it was.” And she wonders if these “over the line” moves are instead part of a “culture of consistent lawlessness, and I’m part of it.” The preview also features more about the two marriages at the center of the show, with Hal telling Kate he “can’t live like this wondering if you’re about to run” and Grace’s husband, Todd ( Bradley Whitford ) observing that his wife is “different” and he needs a “job that takes me away,” even floating the possibility of something in London, which would bring him closer to Russell’s character. Netflix teases the upcoming season as “two marriages threaten to eat each other alive.” “One catastrophic moment shatters the fragile peace Kate Wyler brokered between the U.S. and U.K., as well as the crumbling marriage she’s trying to save,” the synopsis continues. “While she fights to stem the bleeding, President Grace Penn and VP Hal Wyler’s conspiracy to steal Russia’s most powerful weapon hurtles the United States toward war. Kate and Todd, at best an uneasy pair, unite to stop the Grace-Hal alliance from upending the balance of power abroad and at home.” Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter in May , as The Diplomat was filming its fourth season in Italy (they also shot scenes in New York and the U.K.), Janney indicated more risk taking from her character, who was previously revealed to have been behind the carrier ship attack that kicked off the series. “Grace is not afraid to make bold decisions and to suffer the consequences, whatever they are, and she’ll stand behind what decision she makes,” she said. “Not everyone agrees with her.” And showrunner Debora Cahn teased ongoing fallout from the carrier ship incident. “There was always a very long plan for what the carrier meant to the relationship between these two countries,” Cahn explained. “The consequences reverberate through the third season and will continue through the fourth. It’s satisfying for me to be able to make one geopolitical error resonate over a number of seasons. Look at the relationships between countries. We are still dealing with things that happened decades, sometimes centuries ago. Certainly with the U.K., the origin story [of the U.S.] will always be hanging over the way that we interact now.” Cahn also shared that while four seasons is a relatively long run in the streaming era, she’s not yet nearing the end of this tale. “I grew up in broadcast television, where one season was 22, sometimes 25, episodes, so it feels like we’re just getting started,” she said. “It doesn’t feel to me like we’re in season four. It feels like we’re in the juicy middle.” The cast of The Diplomat also includes Ato Essandoh, Ali Ahn, Nana Mensah and Rory Kinnear. Cahn and Russell executive produce with Janice Williams, Alex Graves, Peter Noah and Eli Attie. Season four of the political thriller, consisting of eight one-hour episodes, is set to begin streaming on Netflix on Oct. 15. THR

articles.title: Hawai’i Film Festival to Open With ‘The Navigator,’ Names ‘Drifter’ as Centerpiece (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Sep 15, 2026 6:00am PT Hawai’i Film Festival to Open With ‘The Navigator,’ Names ‘Drifter’ as Centerpiece (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Nakamura Yuri, Japanese-Korean Actor Known for ‘Romantics Anonymous’ and ‘Pacchigi! Love & Peace,’ Dies at 44 22 minutes ago Hawai’i Film Festival to Open With ‘The Navigator,’ Names ‘Drifter’ as Centerpiece (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Kurosawa Kiyoshi’s Cannes Title ‘The Samurai and the Prisoner’ Sells Wide for Charades (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago See All Hawai'i International Film Festival The Hawai’i International Film Festival presented by Halekulani will open its 46th edition, HIFF46, with the world premiere of “The Navigator,” directed by Jordan Manley, at the historic Hawai’i Theatre Center. “The Navigator” is a made in Hawai’i documentary centered on Nainoa Thompson, who nearly half a century ago became the first Native Hawaiian in 600 years to sail from Hawai’i to Tahiti using no modern instruments. The documentary follows him on a 2,400-mile return voyage accompanied by a new generation of trainee wayfinders, drawing on wisdom instilled by master navigator Mau Piailug. The screening also marks HIFF’s first opening night held at the Hawai’i Theatre Center since the COVID-19 pandemic began. Related Stories Taylor Swift Surprises Emmys in 'SVU' Parody but Skips Show to Attend Chiefs Game With Tom Cruise Zendaya Debuts Pixie Cut and Channels '90s Glamour at the Emmys “It is a tremendous honor for HIFF to open our 46th Festival with the world premiere of ‘The Navigator,’ a film that could not be more deeply connected to Hawai’i and to who we are as a festival,” said Jean H. Lee, HIFF executive director. Lee added that Nainoa Thompson’s legacy “represents the reclamation and perpetuation of ancestral knowledge, a living connection across Oceania, and the responsibility to pass that knowledge to the next generation.” Popular on Variety HIFF46’s centerpiece presentation is the Hawai’i premiere of “Drifter,” the feature directorial debut of actor and filmmaker Sung Kang, who also wrote, produced and stars in the film. Set against the drifting subculture, the story centers on a lone racetrack janitor carrying old wounds, who gets one shot at redemption behind the wheel if he can learn to trust those around him. The festival features 84 films in total, including 34 world premieres, six North American Premieres, 12 U.S. premieres and three international premieres, alongside selections from Cannes, Sundance, Berlin and Busan. The program also includes 86 short films; HIFF is the only Academy Award-qualifying film festival in the state of Hawai’i for short films. The festival’s 24 individual premiere titles include world premieres “Beyond the Smiles: Yani Tseng,” “Making the Line,” “Niu Forever,” “Orphan Myth,” “Sukiyaki” and “Protecting Kahoʻolawe: 50 Years of Aloha ʻĀina”; North American premieres “The House on the Moon,” “The Mage,” “Ugly Duckling Ms. Maeng” and “Will You Still Be My Friend?”; U.S. premieres “Big Little Things,” “Chura Vita,” “Fruit Gathering,” “Lomu,” “Los Vampires,” “Satoko Always,” “Sgt. Haane,” “Sukundimi Walks Before Me,” “We Are Born Good” and “You Are the Film”; and international premieres “2 Valid IDs,” “Guided by Horses” and “Shadow Work.” The lineup also brings in festival selections from Cannes, Sundance, Berlin and Busan, including “Josephine,” “Bedford Park,” “Take Me Home,” “All of a Sudden,” “Coward,” “Fatherland,” “La Bola Negra,” “Minotaur,” “The Station,” “9 Temples to Heaven” and “We Are Aliens,” alongside a studio slate featuring Netflix’s “Ink,” “14th” and “Possible Love”; A24’s “Club Kid” and “The Debut”; IFC Films’ “Tangles” and “Mouse”; Searchlight Pictures’ “Behemoth!” and “Wild Horse Nine”; Amazon MGM Studios’ “I Play Rocky”; and Neon’s “Once Upon a Time in Harlem” and “Clarissa.” Alongside its film program, HIFF46 presents the second annual HIFILM industry conference, featuring conversations with filmmaker Destin Daniel Cretton, “Romanticals” creator Jonah Feingold, producer Walter Hamada, Desert Eclipse CEO Jason Chen, actors Holt McCallany, Henry Ian Cusick, Alex Tarrant and Amy Hill, and writer-producer Dana Ledoux Miller, among others. “At its core, HIFF has always been about where we are,” said Anderson Le, HIFF artistic director. Le noted that the festival can present “an awards contender from Cannes or Sundance one night, a world premiere from Hawai’i the next, and then a new filmmaker from Korea, Japan, the Philippines, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Aotearoa or across Oceania – and they all belong in the same conversation.” The festival runs Oct. 21-Nov. 5 on Oahu and continues through Nov. 15 on Maui, Molokai, Lanai and the Big Island of Hawai’i. articles.title: BritBox’s Modern Adaptation of ‘Agatha Christie’s Tommy & Tuppence’ Stumbles Before Finding Steady Ground: TV Review
articles.full_text: Sep 15, 2026 6:15am PT BritBox’s Modern Adaptation of ‘Agatha Christie’s Tommy & Tuppence’ Stumbles Before Finding Steady Ground: TV Review By Aramide Tinubu Plus Icon Aramide Tinubu Latest BritBox’s Modern Adaptation of ‘Agatha Christie’s Tommy & Tuppence’ Stumbles Before Finding Steady Ground: TV Review 31 minutes ago TNT’s Iraq War Drama ‘High Value Target: The Hunt for Saddam’ Is Dull and Deeply Disturbing: TV Review 2 days ago Netflix’s YA Rowing Drama ‘Crew Girl’ Capsizes and Sinks: TV Review 5 days ago See All BritBox Based on Agatha Christie’s well-liked, but perhaps lesser-known, characters, BritBox ’s “Agatha Christie’s Tommy & Tuppence” is the first contemporary English-language adaptation of the detective duo. Set in modern-day London, the series follows Tommy ( Josh Dylan ), a crime novelist doing a favor for an old friend when he encounters his college sweetheart, Tuppence ( Antonia Thomas ). An aspiring actress, Tuppence has returned to the U.K. following a stint in Los Angeles where she was trying to get her big break. Reeling from their unexpected reunion, neither of them expects to be thrust into the middle of a murder investigation. Though the show takes a moment to get its bearings, “Tommy & Tuppence” blossoms, becoming an engaging mystery drama. It doesn’t quite break the mold, but still carries its audience on an adventure-filled journey of murder and mayhem. Related Stories Spotify Now Lets Parents Block Kids’ Music From Polluting Their Recommendations Nepal’s Oscar Contender ‘Elephants in the Fog’ Rallies Flood Relief Efforts at Toronto and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE) The six-episode series opens at an Alice & Wonderland-themed wedding. Tuppence is there to work as part of the serving staff, and Tommy, a friend of the groom, steps in to take photos after the hired photographer is a no-show. When the pair collide, Tommy is eager to catch up. However, Tuppence is skittish about revisiting the past, especially because her life is currently in limbo. The twosome briefly part ways, but are thrust back together after a guest is found dead, and the groom is arrested for the murder. Popular on Variety Shell-shocked after such a harrowing evening, Tommy and Tuppence find themselves reminiscing about old times in Tommy’s flat. Confused by the brutality of the crime and the resulting arrest and inspired by Tommy’s Aunt Ada (Imelda Staunton), a retired private investigator, the duo begin digging into what really happened at the mad-hatter-themed nuptials. Though the series’ opener begins promisingly, the lackluster clues and haphazard narrative weigh it down. It feels especially taxing since the duo’s first investigation spills over into Episode 2. Moreover, when the duo focus on their messy relationships — particularly Tuppence’s familial and romantic life — instead of the mystery, the series becomes frustrating and tiresome. “Tommy & Tuppence” doesn’t really begin to find its footing until the end of Episode 2. Aunt Ada, the show’s narrator and guide for Tuppence and Tommy, shares a nugget of information that alters the show’s direction. Aunt Ada’s reveal will undoubtedly compel audiences to press play on Episode 3, where the pair’s newly formed agency, Blunt’s Brilliant Detectives, officially gets up and running. As they get into their rhythm, the true spark and chemistry between Thomas’ Tuppence and Dylan’s Tommy start to rise to the surface. Moreover, as the duo begins investigating better constructed mysteries, the former couple’s contrasting personalities — an overly cautious Tommy versus a highly impulsive Tuppence — are revealed. In Episode 3, as the sleuths probe the theft of a rare pearl necklace, they happen upon something much more sinister and alarming; it’s a revelation audiences likely won’t see coming. What’s revealed makes up for the series’ clunky opening while showing how layered and textured the best mysteries are. Things get even more complicated when Tommy and Tuppence find themselves on the radar of local police officers, Detective Sergeant Draper (Callie Cooke), who is happy to have some helping hands and Detective Inspector Merriot (Chizzy Akudolu), who isn’t too keen on having the pair muddling in police affairs. The final three episodes of the season make “Tommy & Tuppence” worthwhile. The amateur detectives remain in an excruciating will-they-won’t-they limbo with Tuppence literally fleeing to avoid facing her past in Los Angeles or a possible future with Tommy. Yet the show’s final mystery is a whirlwind, beginning on Halloween in 1989 and stretching into the present day. These concluding episodes reveal the series’ true potential, which would be better served if the obvious feelings between the couple were left to simmer for a couple of seasons instead of being a constant, recurring theme. “Agatha Christie’s Tommy & Tuppence” is solid, but as the former college sweethearts-turned-sleuths dig deep into intricate crimes that go beyond the obvious, it soars. Luckily, by the time the season comes to a close, it appears “Tommy & Tuppence” and its characters have finally begun to find their footing. The first two episodes of “Agatha Christie’s Tommy & Tuppence” debut Sept. 15 on BritBox, with the remaining episodes airing weekly on Tuesdays. ​ BritBox’s Modern Adaptation of ‘Agatha Christie’s Tommy & Tuppence’ Stumbles Before Finding Steady Ground: TV Review Production: Executive Producers | Katie Draper, Phoebe Eclair-Powell, Jon Farrar, Laura Lankaster, Louise Mutter, Stephen Nye, James Prichard, Robert Schildhouse Production/Distribution Partners | BBCS, Lookout Point Crew: Written by Phoebe Eclair-Powell. Based on the characters by Agatha Christie. articles.title: ‘Annie’ Returning to Broadway for 50th Anniversary
articles.full_text: Sep 15, 2026 6:41am PT ‘Annie’ Returning to Broadway for 50th Anniversary By Rebecca Rubin Plus Icon Rebecca Rubin Senior Film and Media Reporter rebeccaarubin Latest Box Office: ‘Practical Magic 2’ Fizzles With $30 Million Debut 2 days ago Venice Film Festival Takeaways: Malkovich Storms the Oscar Race, Political Movies Dominate Buzz and More 4 days ago ‘Hawaii Five-O’ Movie in the Works From ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Director Destin Daniel Cretton 5 days ago See All ©Columbia Pictures/courtesy Everett Co / Everett Collection Little orphan Annie is returning to the Great White Way. A revival of “Annie” will premiere on Broadway in fall 2027, timed to the classic musical’s 50th anniversary. Sam Pinkleton, the Tony-winning director of “Oh, Mary!” and “The Rocky Horror Show,” is leading the new production. Casting and other key creatives will be announced at a later date. “Annie” revolves around a young orphan who gets adopted by a billionaire as a way to rehabilitate his image. First staged on Broadway in 1977 and adapted into several feature films — most notably the 1982 movie starring Carol Burnett, Tim Curry and Bernadette Peters — “Annie” introduced seminal musical theater songs like “Tomorrow” and “It’s the Hard Knock Life.” Related Stories Fifty Fifty's 'After-School Exorcism Club,' The Boyz's 'Wi-Fi Love in the Palace' and NCT's 'Wind Up: The Movie' Score New Asia Sales for Finecut San Sebastian and Busan Title 'In My Father's Room' Sells Wide for Bitters End (EXCLUSIVE) “If you ask any of my closest friends what I love more than anything on the planet, everyone will have the same answer: ‘Annie’,” said Pinkleton. “’Annie’ is everything I love about New York City: gutsy, fearless and funny as hell. It’s a perfectly constructed musical comedy that my collaborators and I will run toward with joy and abandon — with open hearts and total adoration for this legendary show that has made generations fall in love with musicals.” Popular on Variety “Annie” features music by Charles Strouse, lyrics by Martin Charnin and a book by Thomas Meehan. The musical premiered at the Goodspeed Opera House in 1976 before a pre-Broadway engagement at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts in Washington, D.C. The show officially opened on Broadway at the Alvin Theatre (now the Neil Simon Theatre) on April 21, 1977. It was nominated for 11 Tonys and won seven, including best musical, original score, book and actress for Dorothy Loudon as the cruel orphanage matron Miss Hannigan. “Half a century after a fearless redheaded orphan first walked onto a Broadway stage and sang that the sun would come out tomorrow, that promise continues to inspire audiences around the world, and will do so again,” said producers Michael Alden and Hal Luftig, Cathy Dantchik, and Kevin Connor for Halcyon Theatricals. In a statement, the family of Charnin, the original creator, lyricist, and director of “Annie,” described the show as a “timeless message of hope, joy and optimism.” “Fifty years ago, our father, Martin Charnin, had an idea: that a little redheaded girl who refused to give up might have something to say to the world,” Charnin’s family said. “Today, we believe the true measure of a legacy is carrying it forward – so the work continues to inspire new generations. ‘Annie’ was never about yesterday. It was always about tomorrow.” Although “Annie” hasn’t been on Broadway in decades, the family of Meehan noted that the musical is “performed somewhere in the world virtually every moment of every day — from elementary-school auditoriums to regional theaters and major international stages.” “But Broadway will always be home,” said the family of Meehan. “‘Annie is, at its core, a New York story: spirited, tough, funny and full of possibility. This isn’t a revival; it’s a homecoming.” Adds the family of Strouse, “We take enormous pride in the place ‘Annie’s’ music has earned in the hearts of generations. These songs have become so familiar that it is easy to forget how much power they still hold—and how much joy they still inspire. We cannot wait to hear this extraordinary score ringing out on Broadway once again.” Gillian Anderson Says Sony Exited ‘The Salt Path’ Distribution Deal After Authors’ ‘Fabrications’ Exposed: ‘It Felt Like Such a Betrayal’ Sony Aims to Connect Advertisers to PlayStation Users With Launch of ‘Live TV on PS5’ (EXCLUSIVE) How Maggie Gyllenhaal Used Dakota Johnson and Ellen Burstyn to Reimagine Marilyn Monroe at 100 in Venice Short ‘Flesh Impact’ Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% Maggie Gyllenhaal Says She Tried Using AI to Turn Dakota Johnson Into Marilyn Monroe for Short ‘Flesh Impact’ — Then Scrapped It: ‘Fundamentally Did Not Work’ The Best Celebrity Fragrance Campaigns in 2026: Zendaya, Dakota Johnson, Alexander Skarsgård and More Loading comments... articles.title: HBO Max Supports French Animation and Documentary Investment Quotas as Netflix, Disney and Amazon Push Back
articles.full_text: Sep 15, 2026 6:46am PT HBO Max Supports French Animation and Documentary Investment Quotas as Netflix, Disney and Amazon Push Back By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest Kurosawa Kiyoshi’s Cannes Title ‘The Samurai and the Prisoner’ Sells Wide for Charades (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Celine Dion Delivers Tearful Speech on Opening Night of Paris Residency: ‘I Had Promised Myself Not to Cry’ 3 days ago French WWII Blockbuster ‘De Gaulle’ Lands U.S. Distribution With Samuel Goldwyn Films (EXCLUSIVE) 4 days ago See All HBO Max HBO Max has agreed to dedicate part of its mandatory investment in French and European content for documentaries and animation, embracing new French sub-quota rules that rival streamers are challenging in court. The agreement put HBO Max on a different path from Netflix , Prime Video and Disney+ which have each lodged an appeal before the Conseil d’Etat, France’s highest court, contending that the sub-quotas were introduced without sufficient negotiation and impose obligations on streaming services that traditional broadcasters do not face in the same way. Pauline Dauvin, Netflix’s VP of content in France, even described them as detrimental to the editorial freedom in an op-ed published in Le Monde newspaper. Related Stories Tom Cruise Says 'I Have Nothing Against Netflix or TV' and Rumors About Being Intense on Set Are True: 'I Expect a Lot and I’m Upfront About It' Tom Pelphrey Wins Supporting Emmy for 'Task,' Shouts Out 'Very Pregnant' Fiancée Kaley Cuoco: 'Our Family Is the Crown Jewel of My Life' The dispute stems from a change to France’s so-called SMAD decree, the local implementation of an EU directive which has brought global streaming services operating in France to start investing 20% of their local revenue in European and French-language film and television production since 2021. Popular on Variety Then the end of 2025, France went a step further with new rules aimed specifically at ensuring that genres such as animation and documentary also benefit from the streamers’ growing investment. Against that backdrop, HBO Max has opted to reach agreements with the French industry guilds, including SACD, the Society of Dramatic Authors and Composers; SCAM, the Civil Society of Multimedia Authors; USPA, representing audiovisual producers; AnimFrance; and independent producers union SPI, among others. The precise amounts devoted to the different genres will be determined based on the platform’s 2026 and 2027 fiscal years. “These agreements reflect our desire to continue our commitment to French creative works and to develop productions capable of resonating with both French and international audiences,” said Erlinda Tabla, VP of legal and business affairs at WBD France. “We are pleased to have established, together with the professional organizations, SACD, and SCAM, a shared framework that will allow us to continue this dialogue in the years to come and contribute to the global reach of French audiovisual creation,” she continued. The French government and production guilds have defended the sub-quotas as a way of spreading streaming investment more evenly across the audiovisual ecosystem, notably the animation sector which has suffered from slower commissioning and is being threatened by job losses due to the rise of AI. Isabelle Degeorges, CEO of Gaumont Television and president of USPA, said the agreement with HBO Max “opens up new horizons for audiovisual creation.” “It demonstrates the vitality of our industry and our ability to explore new creative frontiers. This is excellent news for our producers, our writers, and our talent, as well as for the renewal of French and European creativity,” she continued. Emmanuel-Alain Raynal, president of SPI and a producer of the animated feature “Chicken for Linda!,” said the agreement “helps recognize the essential role of documentary and animation” and “marks a new step in the integration of streaming platforms into the French creative ecosystem while further expanding the audiences for our works.” How Maggie Gyllenhaal Used Dakota Johnson and Ellen Burstyn to Reimagine Marilyn Monroe at 100 in Venice Short ‘Flesh Impact’ The Best Celebrity Fragrance Campaigns in 2026: Zendaya, Dakota Johnson, Alexander Skarsgård and More Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% Sony Aims to Connect Advertisers to PlayStation Users With Launch of ‘Live TV on PS5’ (EXCLUSIVE) Gillian Anderson Says Sony Exited ‘The Salt Path’ Distribution Deal After Authors’ ‘Fabrications’ Exposed: ‘It Felt Like Such a Betrayal’ Maggie Gyllenhaal Says She Tried Using AI to Turn Dakota Johnson Into Marilyn Monroe for Short ‘Flesh Impact’ — Then Scrapped It: ‘Fundamentally Did Not Work’ Loading comments... articles.title: Nakamura Yuri, Japanese-Korean Actor Known for ‘Romantics Anonymous’ and ‘Pacchigi! Love & Peace,’ Dies at 44
articles.full_text: Sep 15, 2026 6:52am PT Nakamura Yuri, Japanese-Korean Actor Known for ‘Romantics Anonymous’ and ‘Pacchigi! Love & Peace,’ Dies at 44 By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Hawai’i Film Festival to Open With ‘The Navigator,’ Names ‘Drifter’ as Centerpiece (EXCLUSIVE) 53 minutes ago Kurosawa Kiyoshi’s Cannes Title ‘The Samurai and the Prisoner’ Sells Wide for Charades (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Singapore-South Korea Series ‘Collateral Romance’ Set at Mediacorp, Blintn 3 hours ago See All Getty Images Nakamura Yuri , the Japanese-Korean actor known for Netflix series “ Romantics Anonymous ,” died on Sept. 1 from rectal cancer. She was 44. Her agency, Alpha Agency, confirmed the news on Sept. 14. Born Yuri Sei in Neyagawa, Osaka, Nakamura came from a mixed heritage: her father was a third-generation Zainichi Korean and her mother held citizenship in both South Korea and Japan. Related Stories 'Gomorrah' Writer Maddalena Ravagli to Make Directorial Debut With Sicily-Set 'The Place of Eternal Summer' (EXCLUSIVE) Sally Field Becomes Oldest Emmy Winner in Her Category and Shades Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: 'Our Voices Matter' Her path to acting was indirect. In 1996 she passed the singing audition for the popular talent search program “Asayan,” going on to form the music duo YuriMari with friend Mari Izawa. The pair debuted in 1998 and dissolved in 1999, leaving Nakamura to redirect her ambitions toward the screen. Popular on Variety The pivot proved well-founded. She built up a substantial filmography through the 2000s and 2010s, appearing in festival-circuit titles alongside mainstream fare. Her most celebrated early role came in “Pacchigi! Love & Peace” (2007), the sequel to Izutsu Kazuyuki’s acclaimed breakthrough film, in which she played Kyonja, an aspiring actor navigating life as a Zainichi Korean in Japan. The performance won her the Zenkoku Eiren Award for best actress and the Newcomer Award at the 3rd Osaka Cinema Festival. Later credits continued to demonstrate range. She appeared in Kore-eda Hirokazu’s “After the Storm” (2016), the disaster drama “Fukushima 50” (2020), and Ishikawa Kei’s science-fiction film “Arc” (2021). The Netflix drama “Beyond Goodbye” (2024) and the streaming series “Romantics Anonymous” (2025) – a Japanese remake of the French film “Les Émotifs Anonymes” produced with a Korean production team – marked her final screen appearances, with Nakamura playing Irene in the latter. In between, she took on stage work, including the production “1945” in October 2008, directed by Robert Allan Ackerman. Much of that work was carried out against a backdrop of serious illness that Nakamura chose to keep hidden. In a statement released on Sept. 14, Alpha Agency disclosed that she had been diagnosed with cancer 13 years ago. She and the company president agreed at the time: “We should not tell people at work the name of the disease, as it would cause them unnecessary worry.” She went into remission and continued working, with regular medical check-ups throughout. In January 2025, cancer was found again. Surgery was performed successfully, but metastasis was discovered after the operation. With a full cure no longer achievable, Nakamura shifted her focus to managing the disease and, as the agency put it, aiming “to live a longer, more vibrant life.” Her doctor encouraged her to keep working, and she did. In August 2026, she suffered another bowel obstruction and was told she had only a short time to live. According to Alpha Agency, she faced the news with composure, “maintaining a beautiful and gentle smile throughout her final moments with her family and loved ones.” The agency noted that while Nakamura’s 30s and 40s were “often marked by battles with illness,” they were equally filled with “wonderful encounters, happiness, and fulfilling moments.” Maggie Gyllenhaal Says She Tried Using AI to Turn Dakota Johnson Into Marilyn Monroe for Short ‘Flesh Impact’ — Then Scrapped It: ‘Fundamentally Did Not Work’ How Maggie Gyllenhaal Used Dakota Johnson and Ellen Burstyn to Reimagine Marilyn Monroe at 100 in Venice Short ‘Flesh Impact’ The Best Celebrity Fragrance Campaigns in 2026: Zendaya, Dakota Johnson, Alexander Skarsgård and More Sony Aims to Connect Advertisers to PlayStation Users With Launch of ‘Live TV on PS5’ (EXCLUSIVE) Gillian Anderson Says Sony Exited ‘The Salt Path’ Distribution Deal After Authors’ ‘Fabrications’ Exposed: ‘It Felt Like Such a Betrayal’ Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% Loading comments... articles.full_text: Sep 15, 2026 7:00am PT Oscilloscope Lands North American Rights to ‘Game,’ Rave Thriller From John Minton and Portishead’s Geoff Barrow Starring Jason Williamson of Sleaford Mods (EXCLUSIVE) By Ellise Shafer Plus Icon Ellise Shafer Latest Jeff Goldblum Performs a Jazz Number to Open ‘SNL U.K.’ Season 2: ‘Hoping You’ll Like Me More Than Nando’s or Marmite’ 3 days ago Maggie Gyllenhaal’s Venice Jury Didn’t Award ‘Woman Unknown’ the Golden Lion Just Because It Was Directed by a Woman: It ‘Was Like a Laser Beam’ 3 days ago Venice Film Festival Winners: May El-Toukhy’s ‘Woman Unknown’ Scores Golden Lion, John Malkovich Gets Best Actor and More 3 days ago See All Courtesy Oscilloscope Oscilloscope Laboratories has landed North American rights to “Game,” a rave thriller marking the feature debut of visual artist John Minton and hailing from Portishead founder Geoff Barrow’s Invada Films banner. A theatrical release is being planned for winter 2027. The film stars Jason Williamson of Sleaford Mods and Marc Bessant in their first leading roles. Rob Williams penned the screenplay from a story by Barrow and Bessant, which was developed with Minton and Williams. Related Stories Seven Variety Cover Stars Win 2026 Emmys Taylor Swift Surprises Emmys in 'SVU' Parody but Skips Show to Attend Chiefs Game With Tom Cruise “Set against the backdrop of the 1993 British rave scene, this gripping thriller follows aging raver David (Bessant), who crashes his car deep in the woods after stealing a stash of money and drugs,” the film’s synopsis reads. “Trapped, injured and helpless, he is discovered by a mysterious poacher (Williamson) — but instead of rescuing him, the poacher has other ideas in store.” Popular on Variety Minton and Barrow have previously collaborated on music videos and live visuals for Portishead, with Minton’s other credits including Simple Minds, Oasis’ Live ’25 tour, Noel Gallagher, the Pretenders and music videos for Beth Gibbons, Sleaford Mods and Gazelle Twin. “’Game’ started as an ambition between friends and colleagues, pooling our skills and experience to challenge ourselves to make a feature,” Minton said in a statement. “My career has revolved around visuals for music and live performance, with directing and editing as the foundation of that work. Interpreting world-renowned artists, their personalities and the essence of their music visually has been my thing. Making ‘Game’ felt like a natural evolution of that process into long-form narrative.” He added, “I made the first music videos for Invada Records over 20 years ago, so to now direct Invada Films’ first feature is a full-circle moment for me. If we’d known at the beginning of the process that ‘Game’ would eventually be acquired by Oscilloscope for North America, we would’ve been elated. To see it find a home with such a kindred spirit is bloody exciting.” Deborah Rawlings serves as producer alongside Barrow, who has previously worked in film and TV as a composer for “Civil War,” “Ex Machina,” “Black Mirror” and more. His Invada Records label has released the scores for “Stranger Things,” “Drive” and “Red Dead Redemption.” Williams currently has projects in development with the Imaginarium Corestar, Anton Entertainment and Rebellion Studios. His comic series “Unfollow” is being produced by Margot Robbie’s Lucky Chap for HBO. Oscilloscope Laboratories was founded by Adam Yauch of the Beastie Boys in 2008. Its releases include Lynne Ramsay’s “We Need to Talk About Kevin,” Kelly Reichardt’s “Meek’s Cutoff,” Ciro Guerra’s “Embrace of the Serpent” and more. articles.title: Is the Press Less Free Under Donald Trump? 72% of Democrats Say Yes — but Only 15% of Republicans Agree
articles.full_text: Sep 15, 2026 7:00am PT Is the Press Less Free Under Donald Trump? 72% of Democrats Say Yes — but Only 15% of Republicans Agree By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Spotify Now Lets Parents Block Kids’ Music From Polluting Their Recommendations 1 hour ago Sydney Sweeney Loses More Than 200,000 Instagram Followers Amid Growing Backlash Over Her Nude Sports-Betting Ad 19 hours ago Netflix, Amazon and YouTube Form D.C. Lobbying Group Amid Backlash Over Cost of Sports on Streaming 21 hours ago See All Getty Images President Donald Trump has been antagonistic toward mainstream news organizations during both of his terms. But Americans’ feelings about whether the press is “less free” under the current Trump administration sharply differ along partisan lines. According to a new study released Tuesday by the Pew Research Center , 44% of all U.S. adults say the press has become less free during the second Trump administration, compared with 12% who say it has become more free. About a quarter (26%) say there has been no change, and 17% aren’t sure. Related Stories Finland’s Gutsy Pictures Pacts With MTV, Germany’s Zeitsprung, Sweden’s Götafilm on Zaida Bergroth’s ‘Dangerous Woman’ (EXCLUSIVE) Tom Pelphrey Wins Supporting Emmy for 'Task,' Shouts Out 'Very Pregnant' Fiancée Kaley Cuoco: 'Our Family Is the Crown Jewel of My Life' There’s a huge gulf between Americans based on their party affiliation: 72% of Democrats say the press has become less free since Trump’s return to office, compared with 15% of Republicans, according to the report. Popular on Variety Among those who say the press has become less free under Trump, the solid majority (92%) say that’s a bad thing for the country. Since Trump returned to the White House in January 2025, he has sued several news outlets including the New York Times , the BBC and the Wall Street Journal , while his administration has taken actions that critics view as restrictions on press freedom. Those include the Pentagon imposing new restrictions on media access and its firing of the editor and publisher of Stars and Stripes, a historically independent publication; the White House limiting access to AP staffers after the wire service continued to refer to the Gulf of Mexico despite Trump’s decree it be called the “Gulf of America”; the Justice Department’s subpoenas of New York Times reporters who wrote about the president’s new Air Force One in an attempt to identify their anonymous sources; and the Trump-led effort to defund PBS and NPR , which a federal judge ruled earlier this year violated the First Amendment. And last month, ABC sued the FCC and Trump-appointed chairman Brendan Carr, alleging the commission was waging an “extraordinary assault” on its First Amendment rights through the implicit threat of revoking its local TV broadcast licenses. The FCC insists its order requiring ABC apply for early license renewals was initiated from the agency’s investigation into alleged DEI employment practices at Disney and ABC. Trump routinely tries to discredit and intimidate news outlets by attacking individual journalists and labeling coverage he doesn’t like as “fake news.” In a rambling speech at July’s White House Correspondents’ Association Dinner , he continued the pattern. “This evening it’s really all about the fake news media and your handling of prizes — writing and producing and performing made-up stories like the Academy Awards,” Trump said. Overall, Pew’s study found, most Americans (73%) say press freedom is “extremely” or “very” important to the well-being of society, a level that has been consistent in each of the past three years. Only 8% say it is “a little important” or “not at all important.” However, while Americans largely support press freedom in principle, half or more also say the government should be able to restrict news reporting in certain cases, particularly when it endangers national security or contains inaccurate information. When forced to choose between accuracy and press freedom, Americans are slightly more likely to choose the side of accuracy: 53% say it is more important to prevent inaccurate reporting, even if it limits freedom of the press. That’s compared with 45% who say it is more important for the press to be free to report the news, even if some reporting is inaccurate. About 60% of those surveyed say the U.S. government should be able to require a news organization to take down a news story if it poses a risk to national security, and about half (51%) say the same for stories containing false information. While the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution only addresses government actions to curtail press freedoms, Americans respond similarly when asked if a social media company should be able to take down a user’s post under the same circumstances. According to Pew’s study, many people support tech companies being able to remove someone’s social media post if it poses a risk to national security (67%) or contains false information (53%), but not if it is politically slanted (11%) or critical of the government (15%). The data is based on Pew’s survey of 3,507 U.S. adults from March 23-29, 2026, and 3,488 U.S. adults from June 22-28, 2026. The organization said the surveys are representative of the full U.S. adult population. articles.title: Netflix NFL Opener In Australia Draws 18.5M Viewers, Extending League’s Muted Start To Season
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘The Pitt’ Take Top Series Emmys As Matthew Rhys & Jean Smart Make History: Full Winners List Read the full story By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Chuck Norris, ‘Buffy The Vampire Slayer’s Nicholas Brendon Among Those Skipped By Emmys In Memoriam Emotional Tributes To Catherine O’Hara And Rob Reiner Bookend Emmys In Memoriam Segment Reba McEntire & Sally Field Honor Dolly Parton At Emmys: “If There Are Truly Angels On Earth, We Have Just Lost One” View All September 15, 2026 5:36am A pass play during the San Francisco 49ers-Los Angeles Rams NFL game in Melbourne, Australia. Morgan Hancock/Getty Images Netflix drew an average audience of 18.5 million for its live coverage of the first NFL game played in Australia , according to Nielsen . The viewership of the San Francisco 49ers-L.A. Rams game played in Melbourne equaled that of a game streamed last year from Brazil by YouTube. While retaining audience counts for plenty in today’s media environment, for a juggernaut like the NFL it extends what has been a subdued start to the regular season. The league’s opening-night game last Wednesday on NBC and Peacock fell 11% from last year, averaging 25.1 million viewers. The NFL has been leaning into its activities outside the U.S. in recent years, with global expansion one of the notable media themes heading into 2026. Related Stories News Sally Field Reflects On Filming 'Remarkably Bright Creatures' In Canada: "Let's Keep Our Neighbors Close" -- Emmys Backstage News Emmy Analysis & Scorecards: Apple Breaks Records & Leads Honors With Huge Night For 'Widow's Bay' Globally, the Rams-49ers game pulled in 21.7 million viewers across Netflix’s full scope of 200-plus countries and territories, the NFL said. The non-U.S. audience of 3.2 million for the Australia game marked an improvement over the 1.2 million overseas viewers tuning into the YouTube game. Watch on Deadline Last year, the streaming game was played on a Friday, compared with Thursday this year. The timing of the season kickoff on Wednesday this year, a quirk of the schedule that comes up every now and then, may have contributed to the ratings dip compared with the usual Thursday night kickoff. Matchups also played a role in the ratings drop, with the perennially popular Dallas Cowboys taking on the Philadelphia Eagles on NBC a year ago, compared with this year’s Seattle Seahawks-New England Patriots contest. Although this year was a Super Bowl rematch, last February’s lopsided but workmanlike win by Seattle in the Super Bowl is not fondly recalled by even casual football fans. Ratings for Sunday’s main kickoff to the usual full slate of NFL games, including a marquee prime time matchup between the Cowboys and the New York Giants, have not yet been released. Also to be determined is the tune in for the debut of Monday Night Football, a Taylor Swift-inflected blowout win for the Kansas City Chiefs over the Denver Broncos. More than 340 social impressions and 14.5 million engagements across Netflix and NFL social channels were registered by the 49ers-Rams game, the NFL said. The league noted that it ranks among the most-streamed Thursday NFL games in prime time. Amazon took over exclusive carriage of Thursday night games in 2022. A younger audience also tuned in for the Netflix game, the NFL noted. It averaged 4 million viewers between the ages of 18 and 34, marking the highest level in that demo for a streamed game outside of Christmas. Netflix started airing a Christmas Day doubleheader in 2024, making the broadcasts a centerpiece of the company’s push into advertising, which is now in its fifth year. She was 44. Nakamura’s representatives at Alpha Agency announced her death. “We express our deepest gratitude for the kindness shown to her during her lifetime and respectfully announce her passing,” the statement said, per a Google translation. Nakamura played psychologist Irene in Romantics Anonymous , a Japanese original series about a talented chocolatier (Han Hyo-joo) who takes a job at a small chocolate store despite extreme shyness. It rose to number one on Netflix’s Japanese series chart. Watch on Deadline Nakamura’s other credits include Love Letter From Heaven (2007), Like Father, Like Son (2013), and The 8-Year Engagement (2017). Illness forced her to withdraw from NHK drama Dangerous , according to Japan Daily. Alpha Agency said Nakamura was first diagnosed with cancer in 2013, but did not disclose details about her illness. The cancer went into remission, but was discovered again in January 2025 and the disease had metastasised. She was told in August that she had only a short time to live, per the Alpha Agency statement. “She remained calm, maintaining a beautiful and gentle smile throughout her final moments with her family and loved ones,” Alpha Agency added. “While her 30s and 40s were often marked by battles with illness, she also experienced many wonderful encounters, happiness, and fulfilling moments.
