You can get your Rolls-Royce and your Porsche and your Land Rover, and then you stare at them in your garage and think, ‘Why have I got three cars?’ Once that thought hits you, you get sensible. But if it never hits you, then you carry on being an idiot.” I told Ridley this was a climber’s mentality. Ridley said, “I think of a climb in terms of a beginning, middle, and end. There’s a parallel there with life. You tend not to think about the end. I’m 88 now, and I tend not to ever think about what happens next. I really don’t dwell on it, and I just consider my good fortune about being healthy in full mind and body. That’s an incredible stroke of luck. So I just carry on with that, see how long it’ll take me. At the same time, though, it’s a bit like a climb: The nearer you get to the top is really when you got to watch that you don’t get careless. Alex Honnold visualizes every move on El Cap before he ever leaves the ground. Ridley does the same thing on paper. On a final note, I once asked Ridley what he knows now that he wished he’d known as a younger man. His reply stuck with me: “Nothing. I did OK. Just never forget the steps you took. It’s called experience. Little by little, you’re making decisions intuitively. Everything I do now is intuitive — even controlling my anger on my way into a meeting that’s going to be stupid. I once kicked a wall in a trailer. My foot went through the wall and I fell on the carpet. I lay there, incredibly embarrassed. I’ll never do that again.” From Rules to Live By: How Extraordinary Lives Define What Really Matters by Jimmy Chin Copyright © 2026 by the author and reprinted by permission of Celadon Books. THR

articles.title: SkyShowtime May Be Sold or Shut Down, Board Warns In Memo Shared With Staff (Exclusive)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All September 14, 2026 7:15am SkyShowtime CEO Monty Sarhan Photo by Pablo Cuadra/Getty Images for SkyShowtime Comcast and Paramount Skydance are launching a “review of strategic options” for their European joint venture streaming service SkyShowtime , The Hollywood Reporter has learned. While no decisions have been made as of yet, shutting down the business is one of the options on the table. The board of the JV informed SkyShowtime CEO Monty Sarhan of the strategic review Monday in a letter, which was viewed by THR . Sarhan subsequently shared it with staff at the company. “SkyShowtime operates in one of the most competitive markets in our industry. Despite the excellent work of the team and the strength of what you and the team have built, the landscape continues to evolve rapidly, and remains highly challenging,” the board’s letter stated. “Against that backdrop, SkyShowtime’s shareholders are commencing a review of strategic options for the business, which includes the possibility of a wind down. No decisions have been made, and all options remain under consideration.” SkyShowtime combines content from NBCUniversal and Sky Studios as well as Paramount, effectively offering a service with the combined programming might of Peacock and Paramount+ in the U.S. The service was first announced five years ago, and serves more than 20 different countries in Europe. In his note, Sarhan noted that SkyShowtime currently has “several million subscribers and stand in scale alongside the most established players in the market.” However, with a rapidly changing media environment (when the JV was formed, David Ellison had not yet acquired Paramount, and he is currently seeking to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery), and with media giants reexamining their streaming strategies, the experiment may well be nearing its end. In his note to SkyShowtime employees, Sarhan wrote that: “I know this news creates uncertainty and, as we work through what comes next, my priority and that of the leadership team, is to be there and support all of you. Together, we have created a community and culture with empathy, opportunity, and innovation at its heart. Whatever comes next, we will all continue to be there for one another.” SkyShowtime’s board, in its letter, noted that the companies are taking their time to figure out what the best path forward will ultimately be. “We know the most important question this raises is what it means for the SkyShowtime team. This update is the beginning of a dialogue, not the end of one,” the board wrote. “The service continues to operate as normal for customers and partners, and every role continues unchanged today. At this time, we ask that the team remain focused on bringing our audiences the quality of service and programming you have all expertly delivered over the years, and maintaining momentum of the operating business into 2027. “Where any proposal could affect employees, we will follow the information and consultation processes required in each of our markets,” it continued. “Final decisions will be made after those conversations have taken place.” THR

articles.title: ‘The Last Photograph’ Review: Zack Snyder Tries Indie Filmmaking on for Size, With Painfully Ponderous Results
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Michael Rechtshaffen Plus Icon Michael Rechtshaffen View All September 14, 2026 7:22am 'The Last Photograph' Toronto Film Festival After an extended sojourn working in the DC Extended Universe, successful filmmaker Zack Snyder casts off those studio shackles and goes full-on indie with The Last Photograph , a highly personal, long-in-gestation, self-styled Western that trades lavish studio sets for the wide-open spaces of Colombian location shoots. But while the change of pace undoubtedly felt liberating, the end result comes across as a leaden misfire. Overstuffed with pretentious symbolism and flatly delivered, vapid dialogue that constantly overstates the obvious, the ultraviolent film — about a rogue government agent who enlists the help of a heroin-addicted shutterbug to take revenge on the murder of his brother and sister-in-law and rescue their abducted kids — is certain to be regarded as a major disappointment by Snyder’s rabid fan base. Related Stories Movies Six Years After Starring Father Died Soon After TIFF Short Premiere, 'Strong Son' Director Returns With Grief Drama Movies 'Seventeen' Director Justin Ducharme Talks Portraying Struggling Sex Workers as BFFs in Gritty Vancouver The Last Photograph The Bottom Line Small canvas, big misfire. Venue: Toronto International Film Festival (Special Events) Cast: Stuart Martin, Fra Fee, Constanza Andrade, Marlon Moreno, Quique Mendoza, Gustavo Angarita, Ed Hughes, Pedro Calvo-Anca, Mia Calvo, Jackie Kay, Jose Restropo Director: Zack Snyder Screenwriter: Kurt Johnstadt 2 hours, 15 minutes Positioned as a premium centerpiece for TIFF’s inaugural market, where it is hoping to secure a distribution deal, the 135-minute slog was given Special Event status, meaning there will be no repeat screenings beyond its world premiere on Sunday evening. Many of those who exited the theater shared the same expression of disbelief over what they had just experienced. We don’t know it when we’re first introduced to him, but Ethan Black (Stuart Martin), who would appear to be a loner sheep herder, is actually an ex-DEA agent who thought he had left his more violent ways behind him. That is until his young niece and nephew are kidnapped at a birthday party following the fatal shooting of his diplomat brother and the latter’s wife (Constanza Andrade). Regarded as something of a God-like presence by the locals, Black turns avenging angel as he teams up with Joe Wallace (Fra Fee), a junkie war photographer — when he’s not shooting conflict, he shooting heroin — who snapped a photo of the children’s mother at the moment she was shot in cold blood. Wallace is instrumental in Black identifying and tracking down her killer and hopefully bringing home those missing kids. And so, the two men with very different life philosophies proceed to journey ever deeper into the South American heart of darkness, with a little bit of The Searchers thrown in for good measure. A whole lot of very intense blood-spilling ensues, but to be honest, it often comes as a welcome distraction from screenwriter Kurt Johnstadt’s monotonous dialogue and clunky expository character motivations that are needlessly underscored by redundant flashbacks. Who would’ve thought, for example, that Wallace was constantly hiding behind the lens of his trusty camera as a way to numb himself to the horrors of the world? And when he tells Black, “I’m not good at being noble,” was that a deliberate nod to the Humphrey Bogart line in Casablanca ? And, if so, why? Saddled with characters that play more like memes than fully inhabited human beings, both Martin and Fee , let’s just say, have made a better impression elsewhere. Mexican actress Andrade, whose character happens to be the love of Black’s life, fares somewhat better, but still isn’t quite let off the hook by the film’s overall tendency to portray its female characters in the same misogynistically objectified light. The xenophobic portrayal of the area’s indigenous population is a whole other, uncomfortable issue. To be fair, Snyder, who’s also credited as the film’s cinematographer, captures no shortage of admittedly stirring images throughout, especially those involving flickering light and brooding shadows. The constant intrusion of yellow butterfly imagery, on the other hand, begins to border on the overindulgent long before one final, eyeball-rolling appearance. In the absence of the filmmaker’s trademark super-sized canvas, the usual techniques can’t help but feel forcefully out of scale here. Still, one might justifiably argue that Snyder at least deserves credit for going out on a limb — even if it can’t help but snap under the weight of all that affectation. Full credits Venue: Toronto International Film Festival (Special Events) Production companies: Stone Quarry, Hollywood Gang Cast: Stuart Martin, Fra Fee, Constanza Andrade, Marlon Moreno, Quique Mendoza, Director: Zack Snyder Screenwriter: Kurt Johnstadt Producers: Zack Snyder, Deborah Snyder, Gianni Nunnari, Wesley Coller Executive producers: Alessandro Salem, Kurt Johnstadt, William Doyle, Juan Pablo Solano, Simon Beltran Director of photography: Zack Snyder Production designer: Diego Garcia Costume designers: Stephanie Porter, Johanna Buendia-Para Music: Hans Zimmer, Omer Benyamin, Steven Doar Editor: Melissa Remenarich-Aperlo Sales: CAA 2 hours, 15 minutes THR

articles.title: Gerbil: Inside Hollywood’s Most Unkillable Rumor
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close Richard Gere’s early image in films like 1980’s American Gigolo, and his reluctance to be interviewed about anything personal, left people wondering about his sexuality. Courtesy Everett Collection When the White House was looking for a way to attack Richard Gere this summer, they went low. Very low — even for this administration. Gere, the politically active 77-year-old actor and philanthropist, had criticized President Trump’s “ignorance” for cuts to the U.S. Agency for International Development. At an event promoting an educational partnership on migration, Gere remarked, “He has idiots around him.” Steven Cheung, the White House communications director, fired back in a July 21 post on X, “Not going to listen to a guy who may have put a gerbil up his ass.” Related Stories Opinion Maybe Paramount-Warner SHOULD Leave L.A. Lifestyle Could the Galliano Met Gala Fiasco Mark the End of Anna Wintour's Reign? And there it was. Again! That those in Trump’s orbit would traffic in the tawdry is hardly news. But the choice of this particular angle of attack reveals the almost supernatural staying power of a rumor, or urban legend, that started roughly four decades ago. I was not surprised to see the White House post. Nothing about the gerbil rumor, not its longevity nor its continued impact, surprises me. You see, I have been investigating everything about it for six years. The Hollywood Reporter is releasing the first two episodes of my podcast series, Gerbil , on Sept. 17, and installments will be released weekly on Thursdays after that. The gerbil legend may be the most essential rumor in Hollywood history because it perfectly reveals how the products of the entertainment industry, deliberately and, more importantly, accidentally, express fears, yearnings, nightmares and dreams that worm themselves eternally into our brains. Or, as Stanford communications professor Fred Turner told me, “This is Richard Gere, an American icon. And so in some sense, the gerbil is not just up Richard Gere’s ass, it’s up America’s ass.” Comedian Sam Kinison, among the first to refer to the story in his act. John Atashian/Getty Images The basic version of the rumor — and it is a rumor, not something for which proof has been publicly produced — is that sometime in the 1980s, Richard Gere showed up at the emergency room of Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles with a gerbil lodged in his rectum that he had inserted for sexual pleasure. Somehow this unsubstantiated story became internationally known with almost no major media explicitly reporting it, and before the modern version of the internet. Barely a decade after the word “meme” was coined to refer to things or ideas that can be imitated and culturally transmitted, and before the concept of memes going “viral” had become known outside academia, the gerbil rumor caught on and caught fire. The first stand-up comedian to ever mention Gere and a gerbil in his act appears to be the late Sam Kinison, who was already noticing how widely it had spread in May 1990. At a Las Vegas show, Kinison’s bit went, “I hope it’s a rumor. I was in Miami last night, the fucking crowd there went nuts. Everybody in the country knows supposedly because … I don’t want to get in trouble, but supposedly — supposedly — I guess he was in the hospital. … How good could this fucking feel?” Calling it a rumor is a kind of shorthand because the gerbil thing is far more than simple gossip about, say, who is dating whom. Jan Harold Brunvand, author of numerous books cataloging urban legends, considered the gerbil rumor “modern folklore.” Brunvand noted that Nobel Prize novelist Gabriel García Márquez was fascinated with trying to discover the origins of what he called “lost stories,” often untraceable tales that keep evolving new details such as one about the man who supposedly discovered a large diamond in the stomach of a fish he caught. Or was it a person who found a gold ring in their order of fried chicken? Or a Bible story about a fish with a coin in its mouth? When exactly the gerbil story started is one of the mysteries I aimed to solve. It also has many variants — although none in the Old Testament. (But maybe in Freud!) Some versions mention the use of a cardboard paper towel roll to guide the gerbil inside. Others insist duct tape or condoms were tools. Still others say the ER visit happened at St. Vincent’s in New York or Hollywood Presbyterian. The gerbil is freed and runs around the ER. The gerbil dies and somewhere are X-rays showing it. It’s not Gere, it’s some other celebrity. A reply from the NSA to the author’s Freedom of Information Act request seeking information on the gerbil hearsay. Courtesy To save you a trip, your AI machine will tell you the Gere gerbil rumor isn’t true. But this is part of what drew me to the story. The machines only know what they can search: digitized magazine articles, Reddit threads and fact-checking sites. I decided to figure out what, if anything, might be true about it and why this particular rumor never seems to die. As an investigator, it was my duty to explore the possibility that he did what people said he did. But even if Gere did not do the deed, what might be learned from the undeniable existence of the urban legend? I used old-school journalism. I interviewed doctors, film directors, actors, talent agents, nurses, would-be witnesses, reporters and many others who were there when the story started. I traced everything that had been written, much of it nondigital, dating back to the story’s murky origins. I studied emergency room records, police reports, criminal case files and filed Freedom of Information Act requests. No one had done this thorough a job to trace the legend’s origins and find out what is true and what is demonstrably false about it — and, more importantly, why the damn thing has outlasted nearly every other gossip item in the history of Hollywood. It has been said that we are living in a “post-truth era,” where people decide what is real based not on facts but on how they feel about an idea. Into this factual breach rush memes that reflect ideas of how the world works, ideas that exhibit what Stephen Colbert called “truthiness” rather than truth. As I was starting the project, I would say the word “gerbil” to anyone I met and record their reactions. One person free-associated revealingly that the idea that celebrities are engaged in weird sexual stuff just feels true. “There’s a sinister underbelly to what really goes on in Hollywood,” they said. Not only does the weirdness make sense to outsiders who assume celebrities are not just like us, the details are so odd, it seems no one could ever make this stuff up, so it must be true. “Conspiracy theories are renowned for making a kind of sense that appeals far more than the truth,” says Susan Blackmore, author of the influential 1999 book The Meme Machine. You don’t have to be over 40 to know the rumor is still everywhere. When the gossip merchant known as Deuxmoi appeared on the Taste of Taylor podcast in November 2024, host Taylor Strecker gushed, “Like the first-ever celebrity conspiracy theory is that [Gere] used to shave gerbils, inject them with cocaine, put Vaseline on them and stick them up his butt. And use them as little vibrators …” The anonymous representative of Deuxmoi replied, “I’ve had people message me and be like, ‘My mom’s friend is a nurse, and he really did come in’ … I think people started to believe it for real. … I don’t believe it, but if I have enough glasses of wine, I might, like, start to believe it.” Young, old or whatever, you could also have heard recent tell of the gerbil legend in one form or another on the podcasts of Joe Rogan, Tig Notaro and Mae Martin, Dax Shepard, and Conan O’Brien; on Family Guy , South Park , Curb Your Enthusiasm and Family Feud ; on TikTok posts that garner hundreds of thousands of views, on Lady Bunny’s Instagram feed, and on Tom Green’s recent stand-up special. I could go on. Lemmiwinks the Gerbil, a character inspired by the Gere rumor, on South Park. Courtesy Why has it lasted? When exactly did it start? Why did it start? Perhaps most importantly as a service both to a country weary of lies and to the widely beloved Richard Gere, is there any chance it’s true, and if it’s not true, is there any way to stop it? I took on this project not to dredge something prurient up, but because it actually struck me as important. Mike Rothschild, who has written books about QAnon and antisemitic conspiracy theories, says that he is sometimes criticized for platforming these things. But he believes that the only way to fight them is by reporting whatever truth can be found. If you believe that truth matters, and that a journalist’s job is to fight lies wherever they arise, you have to ask questions of these theories, rather than being baited into easy criticisms that don’t work to stop conspiracy theories. “So much of it is just the weirdness and the salaciousness and the pointing and laughing,” Rothschild says, “rather than really trying to develop a deeper understanding of the psychological forces behind these movements. Because psychological forces don’t get clicks. Pointing and laughing at weirdos waiting for JFK Jr. to come back gets clicks.” Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles, the setting of most renditions of the tenacious gerbil rumor. Myung J. Chun/Los Angeles Times/Getty Images This is the essence of the gerbil investigation. What psychological forces gave rise to all this in its moment and why does the gerbil persist? To paraphrase the great poem: What rough beast, its hour come round, slouched toward Cedars-Sinai to be born? There is little doubt that the gerbil rumor was a form of homophobia. Gere’s early image in films like American Gigolo and plays like Bent , and his reluctance to be interviewed about anything personal, left people wondering about his sexuality. And the death of Rock Hudson from AIDS in 1985 left the public skeptical about which stars in Hollywood were telling the truth about their preferences. This is part of how Hollywood helped make the gerbil legend, shaping stars to deliver fantasies but telling lies along the way. (There’s more. I’m not spoiling the whole series for the sake of this little article!) In a time now when memes like the Coldplay couple or some celebrity’s too-thin thighs run across your screen only to be overwhelmed by the next hourly outrage or craze, the gerbil rumor comes from a slower time and thus can be slowly examined, its rise teased apart, its makers and its impacts exposed, its truths revealed. The rumor was never harmless. In a pioneering early 1990s academic study of the rumor, ethnographer Norine Dresser reported on an 11-year-old girl telling her that she heard the Gere rumor on the playground and believed it to be true. Rock Hudson, then 29, and his new bride, Phyllis Gates, 25, in 1955. The death of the actor from AIDS in 1985 left the public skeptical about which stars in Hollywood were telling the truth about their preferences. Bettmann/Getty Images Dresser noted that, “Through the acceptance of this legend as truth, the children are internalizing a stigma that will be difficult to destroy. As they grow older and learn more about homosexuality, it will remain linked with lurid bestial behavior. As a result, when these children go through their own sexual awareness and ambivalence, these ideas will remain forever connected, and their own self-images and development may conceivably be damaged.” The 11-year-old in 1993 is 44 now. There is no way Gere could have had any idea the rumor would go as far and last as long as it has. As the years have gone on and his hair has whitened, Gere has become nearly as famous for his charity and his spirituality as his acting. As I’ve dug deeper, I’ve come to believe he might be convinced to see that the gerbil rumor, which has bedeviled him for so long — and my reporting shows it has bothered him — could become a tool for enlightenment. Too grand? After six years on this story, I can tell you the gerbil legend has become my teacher, and I think it can help all of us. My initial request to speak to Gere was denied. “Due to his schedule at this time, Mr. Gere will be unable to participate,” emailed a representative for Gere. The most cogent comments he ever made about the rumor were in a 1991 television interview with Barbara Walters. She asked, “Do you have any idea why anyone would want to hurt you, or embarrass you, or try to smear you?” After some back-and-forth, Gere said, “Does any of this bother me personally? No. People have their own motivations for doing crazy things, you know, and it has nothing to do with me. You know, if I’m a cow and someone says I’m a zebra, it doesn’t make me a zebra.” I expect that as the episodes roll out and Gere and his people have a chance to hear what I’m up to — an attempt, finally, to bring the full truth to bear on the rumor — I will get a call from them. As Tom Hanks did by coming on the podcast Dead Eyes to unravel an old mystery about him, I expect Gere will see this project as something that is of service. Perhaps if, instead of pretending that it has not hurt him, he speaks movingly about the fact that it has, that this is not a victimless little joke, something else new and true will be brought to the story. You’ll have to listen to find out if that’s how it turns out. This story appeared in the Sept. 9 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

articles.title: Macklemore Dropped From Ed Sheeran Tour After Pro-Palestine Comments During Performances
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All September 14, 2026 8:34am Macklemore performing May 2024 in Melbourne, Australia. Morgan Hancock/Getty Images Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran ‘s Loop Tour as the rapper drew major headlines for his pro-Palestine speeches during his opening performances on the trek, with Sheeran’s promoter stating Monday that venues set to host the tour threatened to pull out if Macklemore was on the bill. “As the concert promoter for Ed Sheeran’s U.S. Loop Tour, we have been notified by venues on the upcoming U.S. tour dates that they will not allow a concert to take place with Macklemore on the lineup, which would result in the cancellation of the tour and impact hundreds of thousands of fans,” Messina Touring Group, Sheeran’s longtime concert promoter, said in a statement provided to The Hollywood Reporter . “After discussions with stakeholders, Macklemore will not be performing on the remaining support dates.” Related Stories Music Pink Issues Statement Following Backlash for Critiquing Macklemore's Pro-Palestine Comments: "Standing Up for My Own People" Music Macklemore Responds to Backlash Over "Free Palestine" Plea: "Wanting All Humans to Be Treated Equal Should Never Be Controversial" Reps for Sheeran and Macklemore didn’t immediately respond to request for comment. The news was first reported by Rolling Stone. The move comes over a week after Macklemore, who’s long supported the Free Palestine cause, garnered significant backlash from pro-Israel groups after giving pro-Palestine speeches during performances at MetLife Stadium on Sept. 4 and 5. “A big part of the reason why I wanted to do this tour in the first place is so I could stand up in stadiums like this and say two words that are very near and dear to my heart: Free Palestine,” he told the crowd during his first performance. “I said, ‘Free Palestine!’ I want those words to be loud and clear, so that people all the way in Gaza to the occupied West Bank know that we have not forgotten about them.” The Israeli-American Council launched a petition calling to remove him from the tour. The rapper doubled down, telling addressing Jewish members of the crowd during his next show to clarify that “criticism of Israel, criticism of apartheid, being against genocide in no way is a criticism of you. My message is for peace; love for all human beings to be treated with dignity, respect, and equality.” He also shared a post on social media last Monday writing that “wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial.” In its statement, Messina Touring Group didn’t specify which venues objected to Macklemore’s spot on the bill, or if it was all of them. He was slated to perform at all of Sheeran’s upcoming North American stadium dates except for the Miami shows on Oct. 29 and 30. Per Rolling Stone, the venues that objected included Philadelphia’s Lincoln Financial Field, Foxbourough’s Gillette Stadium, Atlanta’s Mercedes-Benz Stadium, Indianapolis’s Lucas Oil Stadium, Charlotte’s Bank of America Stadium, Arlington’s AT&T Stadium and Tampa’s Raymond James Stadium. Messina’s statement didn’t specify why the venues pushed back on Macklemore’s performance, though as Rolling Stone noted, a removal from the publicly owned and operated venues (which include all but Gillette Stadium and Bank of America Stadium) due to his previous statements could raise issues a of first amendment rights. Aside from the groups, others who’d voiced out against Macklemore’s actions included Pink, who reposted a call to remove Macklemore from the tour, drawing significant backlash of her own. Days later, she posted a lengthy statement clarifying her views, stating that she was “standing up for my own people, and I thought I knew going in how lonely that would be. And it’s lonelier than that.” THR

articles.title: Netflix and Sega Set ‘Crazy Taxi’ Game-to-Film Adaptation
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content The Sports Issue: Uniting the Biggest Names in Hollywood With the Athletes They Admire Most close By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All September 14, 2026 8:45am 'Sonic' Courtesy of Fortyseven Communications Netflix is expanding its video game adaptation slate with Sega . The streaming giant is at work on a feature film treatment for Crazy Taxi t o be written by Dan Gregor and Doug Mand, the duo behind the 2025 reboot of The Naked Gun. Neal H. Moritz and Toby Ascher of Original Film and Toru Nakahara, head producer at Sega, are producing the adaptation of the Crazy Taxi game that since a 1999 arcade launch has put players behind the wheel of a fearless cabbie racing the clock through chaotic city streets. Netflix and Sega are also adapting the Sonic game as a new animated series in development with Carlos Stevens and Nakahara, and the Stranger Than Heaven game from RGG Studio and set in early 20th-century Japan to become a live action film, with Nakahara again producing for the video game maker. The Sonic action game franchise began in the 1990s and has sustained strong sales. Related Stories Business Netflix, YouTube and Amazon Launch a Streaming Public Policy Group Movies Netflix to Stream Lee Chang-dong's Films Globally as 'Possible Love' Awards Campaign Heats Up The new multi-title collaboration will look to live-action comedy, kids’ animation and live-action crime adaptations to reflect the range of Sega’s library and expand Netflix’s track record in turning game worlds into scripted and unscripted, live-action and animated films and series. “Great games already have what every adaptation is chasing — characters people love, worlds they know by heart, and fandoms that show up. With Crazy Taxi, Sonic, and Stranger Than Heaven , we get to work across three completely different eras of Sega’s catalog, celebrating everything fans love, while introducing them to new audiences,” Brandon Riegg, vp of nonfiction and transmedia at Netflix, said in a statement. For Sega, the aim is bringing the fan base for its popular games to a new streaming platform, with an eye to franchises. “We’ve watched Netflix take on stories across every kind of format and treat each one with real craft, and seeing that same dedication applied to Sonic, Crazy Taxi and Stranger Than Heaven is something we at Sega are incredibly proud to be a part of,” Shuji Utsumi, president and COO of Sega, said in another statement. Netflix’s earlier video game adaptations include a live action series based on Assassin’s Creed, a live action movie based on the Gears of War game and animated series adaptations for Minecraft, Magic: The Gathering and the Clash of Clans games. THR

articles.title: How to Watch the 2026 Emmys Live Online
articles.full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. TV’s biggest night is here. The 78th annual Emmy Awards take place Monday, Sept. 14, bringing together the casts and creators behind the year’s biggest shows — from “The Pitt” and “Hacks” to “Pluribus,” “Widow’s Bay” and “Beef.” The ceremony airs live coast-to-coast from the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles beginning at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on NBC, with Peacock serving as the official streaming home of the Emmys . Related Stories Jimmy Kimmel in Talks to Renew Late-Night Show at ABC FCC Asks Court to Throw Out ABC's Lawsuit Alleging TV License Review Violates First Amendment, as Agency Repeats Claim the Action Is Unrelated to Jimmy Kimmel or 'The View' STREAM THE EMMYS ON PEACOCK The easiest way for cord-cutters to watch the Emmys online is with Peacock , which will livestream the complete ceremony alongside its NBC broadcast. Peacock Premium currently costs $12.99 per month, while Premium Plus runs $19.99 per month. Both plans include access to the live Emmys telecast; Premium Plus removes ads from much of Peacock’s on-demand library, though commercials can still appear during live events. Viewers can also watch NBC online through live-TV streaming services that carry their local NBC station. Options include Hulu + Live TV, DirecTV , Fubo and Sling TV. Hulu + Live TV. Hulu + Live TV offers a three-day free trial for eligible new subscribers. Availability of local NBC stations can vary by market. STREAM ON SLING Variety and CNN are also joining forces for live coverage from the Emmys red carpet. “CNN & Variety Red Carpet Live: TV’s Biggest Night” begins at 5 p.m. ET and will stream on CNN.com/Watch and the CNN app for CNN streaming subscribers, giving viewers three hours of arrivals, interviews and fashion coverage before the main ceremony. CNN correspondent Elizabeth Wagmeister and Variety co-president and co-editor-in-chief Ramin Setoodeh will host the special live from the carpet, with Melissa Rivers joining throughout the evening to weigh in on the night’s fashion and biggest arrivals. The appearance marks Rivers’ first return to an awards-show red carpet in nearly 20 years, following the years she spent covering Hollywood alongside her mother, Joan Rivers. “Law & Order: SVU” star Mariska Hargitay will host this year’s ceremony, becoming the first woman to solo-host the Emmys since Jane Lynch in 2011. Hargitay is already an Emmy winner herself for playing Olivia Benson on the long-running NBC procedural and enters Monday’s ceremony fresh off Creative Arts Emmy wins for her documentary “My Mom Jayne.” “The Pitt” enters Monday night as the most-nominated show of the year with 25 nods, as the HBO Max medical drama looks to repeat its success from last year. Noah Wyle is again among the acting contenders, while Katherine LaNasa and Taylor Dearden are among the show’s heavily nominated ensemble. On the comedy side, “Hacks” earned 24 nominations for its fifth and final season, setting a new record for the most nominations received by a comedy series in a single year. Jean Smart is once again up for lead comedy actress, while Megan Stalter scored her first Emmy nomination for the show. But “Hacks” has some serious competition. Apple TV’s “Widow’s Bay” picked up 19 nominations, while “Pluribus” scored 18, including a lead drama actress nomination for Rhea Seehorn. Netflix’s second season of “Beef” follows with 16 nominations. There could also be some career milestones. Harrison Ford is in contention for his first Emmy win for “Shrinking,” while Smart has a chance to continue her dominant awards run with “Hacks.” The ceremony will also include television-history tribute s marking the 30th anniversary of “Buffy the Vampire Slayer” and the 50th anniversary of “Charlie’s Angels.” The 78th Emmy Awards air Monday, Sept. 14 at 8 p.m. ET/5 p.m. PT on NBC and stream live on Peacock. PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario (Anthropic!), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ – and we will continue to do so!” Trump wrote in a post on his Truth Social account Monday. Related Stories Jeff Corwin to Return to Television With Wildlife Conservation Series ‘Jeff Corwin’s Southern Wild' Jimmy Kimmel in Talks to Renew Late-Night Show at ABC Trump continued: “We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies! There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so. Conspiracy Theorists, Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers, BEWARE! Thank you for your attention to this matter! President DONALD J. articles.full_text: Sep 14, 2026 8:28am PT SkyShowtime Could Be Shut Down, Warns Board of Comcast-Paramount Joint Venture By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest ‘Emily in Paris’ Star Lucien Laviscount Joins Daisy Ridley in ‘The Good Samaritan’ as Action-Thriller Secures Key Deals (EXCLUSIVE) 59 minutes ago Tessa Thompson and Michael Shannon Join Mads Mikkelsen in Death Row Drama ‘Last Meals’ From Ramin Bahrani (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Sydney Sweeney’s Naked Sports Betting Ad Ignites Backlash From Olympic Athletes: ‘Stop Sexualizing Women in Sport’ 3 hours ago See All Getty Images for SkyShowtime SkyShowtime , the European streaming service co-owned by Comcast and Paramount Skydance, could be shuttered. This was the warning in a letter from the board of the joint venture to SkyShowtime CEO Monty Sarhan, which said a “review of strategic options for the business” had begun. Sarhan subsequently shared the letter — which has been seen by Variety — with staff at the company. Related Stories Jimmy Kimmel in Talks to Renew Late-Night Show at ABC FCC Asks Court to Throw Out ABC's Lawsuit Alleging TV License Review Violates First Amendment, as Agency Repeats Claim the Action Is Unrelated to Jimmy Kimmel or 'The View' “SkyShowtime operates in one of the most competitive markets in our industry. Despite the excellent work of the team and the strength of what you and the team have built, the landscape continues to evolve rapidly, and remains highly challenging,” the letter stated. “Against that backdrop, SkyShowtime’s shareholders are commencing a review of strategic options for the business, which includes the possibility of a wind down. No decisions have been made, and all options remain under consideration.” SkyShowtime was launched in late 2022 and gradually rolled out across more than 20 European territories, combining content from Peacock, Paramount+ and Sky. But the impending Paramount-WBD deal has led to uncertainty at the company, with reports in the media of plans to quietly fold the service into Paramount+. Popular on Variety I know this news creates uncertainty and, as we work through what comes next, my priority and that of the leadership team, is to be there and support all of you,” Sarhan said in his message to SkyShowtime employees. “Together, we have created a community and culture with empathy, opportunity, and innovation at its heart. Whatever comes next, we will all continue to be there for one another.” The letter from the SkyShowtime board underlined that, with much still undecided, the service continued to operate as normal. “We know the most important question this raises is what it means for the SkyShowtime team. This update is the beginning of a dialogue, not the end of one,” it said. “The service continues to operate as normal for customers and partners, and every role continues unchanged today. articles.title: Stagecoach 2027 Lineup: Garth Brooks, Riley Green, Zach Top to Headline
articles.full_text: Sep 14, 2026 8:30am PT Stagecoach 2027 Lineup: Garth Brooks, Riley Green, Zach Top to Headline By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Stagecoach 2027 Lineup: Garth Brooks, Riley Green, Zach Top to Headline 10 minutes ago Lil Durk Acquitted in Murder-for-Hire Trial 3 days ago Jay-Z Brings Justin Timberlake Onstage in Paris 4 days ago See All The annual Stagecoach festival will return to the Empire Polo Club in Indio, Calif. next April, and as usual it has a powerful set of headliners: Garth Brooks , Riley Green and Zach Top, with a reunited Florida Georgia Line set for a special late-night set at the festival, marking the duo’s first officially announced performance since teasing a reunion earlier this year. Other artists on the bill include Hardy, Willie Nelson & Family, Kelly Clarkson, Brothers Osborne, Shaboozey, Dasha, Stella Lefty, Stephen Wilson Jr, Journey, Pitbull, Carín León, Matchbox Twenty, Cameron Whitcomb and more. The festival continues Stagecoach’s tradition of male-dominated lineups, with just Clarkson among the top-billed performers. Lainey Wilson was one of last year’s headliners, since the festival’s 2007 debut, Miranda Lambert has headlined three times, Carrie Underwood twice and Shania Twain once. Related Stories Jimmy Kimmel in Talks to Renew Late-Night Show at ABC FCC Asks Court to Throw Out ABC's Lawsuit Alleging TV License Review Violates First Amendment, as Agency Repeats Claim the Action Is Unrelated to Jimmy Kimmel or 'The View' The festival takes place April 23-25, 2027. Tickets go on-sale starting Friday, September 18 at 11am PT, with payment plans offered at only $49 down. Popular on Variety Of the headliners, Riley Green’s new album “That’s Just Me” is set for release on September 18; Zach Top recently earned two more nominations at the 60th Annual CMA Awards and is currently in the midst of an extensive headline tour; and Garth Brooks, who’s currently on the road with his acclaimed “Blame It All On My Roots” arena tour. Of his upcoming performance, Green says, “Let’s do this again. We’re excited to make it back out to the desert after a wild ride last year. We’ll probably stay all weekend and catch the other sets so come join us.” Top recalls, “When we played Stagecoach in 2024, it was one of the very first festivals where we really drew a crowd for our set. We packed out the Palomino stage and I remember feeling like we were really doing something. Now to be back in 2027 as a headliner is just something truly special.” “Stagecoach is a guaranteed good time,” Brooks adds, “I was shocked by how personal everything there is…from the people working the venue to the people singing along. A MUST if you’re a Country music fan!” Additionally, Late Night on Mustang Stage, presented by Boot Barn, returns with Sean Paul, Florida Georgia Line and Flo Rida, shifting into full-throttle mode after dark with big singalongs and familiar hits that keep the party going after the main stages wrap. “The last time we played Stagecoach was back in 2018, and a whole lot of life has happened since then,” Florida Georgia Line says. “There’s something really special about getting to come back to the desert together, step on that stage again, and share these songs and memories with the fans who have been with us through it all. We couldn’t think of a better place to do it.” Two of Stagecoach’s attractions, Diplo’s HonkyTonk, now in its fifth year, and Guy Fieri’s Stagecoach Smokehouse, return for 2027. Amazon Music is returning as Stagecoach’s exclusive livestream destination for the fifth year in a row. Fans will be able to stream live performances from artists on Amazon Music, Prime Video, Twitch, Amazon Live, and the Amazon Music app on Fire TV. Fans can also listen to the Official Stagecoach Playlist streaming now exclusively on Amazon Music here. articles.title: ‘Crazy Taxi’ Comedy Movie Coming From Netflix and Sega, New ‘Sonic’ TV Series and ‘Stranger Than Heaven’ Film in the Works
articles.full_text: Sep 14, 2026 8:45am PT ‘Crazy Taxi’ Comedy Movie Coming From Netflix and Sega, New ‘Sonic’ TV Series and ‘Stranger Than Heaven’ Film in the Works By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest Trump Says He’s the Only AI ‘Guardrail’ Needed and Mocks Anthropic CEO’s Call for AI Slowdown: ‘Pretending to Be a Perfect Little Angel’ 27 minutes ago FCC Chairman Slams James Talarico as Running a ‘Hoax’ With Jimmy Kimmel Interview, Which ABC Punted to YouTube, to Get ‘Clicks and Donations’ 1 day ago Gary Oldman Predicts HBO’s ‘Harry Potter’ Series Will Be ‘More Satisfying’ for Fans Than the Movies 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Sega Netflix has hit the start button on multiple adaptations of Sega hit gaming franchises. The first project under the companies’ new multititle deal is a feature-film adaptation of “ Crazy Taxi ,” Sega’s long-running racing game. The movie will be written by Dan Gregor and Doug Mand — the writing duo behind the 2025 reboot of “The Naked Gun” — with Original Film’s Neal H. Moritz and Toby Ascher and Sega’s Toru Nakahara, the producers behind the Sonic franchises, on board to produce. Related Stories FCC Asks Court to Throw Out ABC's Lawsuit Alleging TV License Review Violates First Amendment, as Agency Repeats Claim the Action Is Unrelated to Jimmy Kimmel or 'The View' Jimmy Kimmel in Talks to Renew Late-Night Show at ABC Netflix and Sega also announced two other adaptations in development: a new animated “ Sonic the Hedgehog ” kids’ series and a movie based on action-adventure game “Stranger Than Heaven.” Popular on Variety “Great games already have what every adaptation is chasing — characters people love, worlds they know by heart, and fandoms that show up,” said Brandon Riegg, VP of nonfiction and transmedia at Netflix, in a statement. “With ‘Crazy Taxi,’ ‘Sonic’ and ‘Stranger Than Heaven,’ we get to work across three completely different eras of Sega’s catalog, celebrating everything fans love, while introducing them to new audiences.” Toru Nakahara, head producer at Sega, commented: “Expect something cute yet cool for ‘Sonic,’ hilariously crazy for ‘Crazy Taxi’ and a badass action drama for ‘Stranger Than Heaven,’ because we’ve got some amazing creative ideas lined up and we are just getting started. The whole team is absolutely thrilled!” In “Crazy Taxi,” which made its arcade debut in 1999, players sit in the driver’s seat as a “fearless cabbie racing the clock through chaotic city streets — flying off ramps, dodging traffic and chasing tips with punk-rock energy that became the series’ signature,” per Sega. The latest title in the franchise, “Crazy Taxi: World Tour,” is scheduled for release in 2027. “We couldn’t be more excited to continue our longstanding relationship with Sega and bring ‘Crazy Taxi’ to life with our partners at Netflix,” Original Film’s Moritz and Ascher said in a statement. “This film is for anyone who’s spent hours behind the wheel of a yellow cab on their Dreamcast, with the music cranked up, smashing through everything in sight just to make the next fare.” Meanwhile, a new animated “Sonic” series is currently in development with Carlos Stevens and Toru Nakahara. The show will present Sonic and his friends as heroes for an upper pre-school audience, touted as a “high-voltage, comedic, yet emotionally grounded series built for kids who want to feel a little edge, a little attitude, and a lot of ‘that’s my crew’ wish fulfillment,” per Sega. Three seasons of Netflix’s “Sonic Prime” 3D animated series are currently available to stream only on Netflix. “Stranger Than Heaven” hails from RGG Studio, developer of the bestselling “Like a Dragon: Yakuza” series, with over 30 million copies sold. The game, set to be released in January 2027, is set in early 20th century Japan, following a foreigner who claws his way from destitute stranger to feared yakuza to entertainment tycoon. Toru Nakahara is set as producer on the film. “We’ve watched Netflix take on stories across every kind of format and treat each one with real craft, and seeing that same dedication applied to ‘Sonic,’ ‘Crazy Taxi’ and ‘Stranger Than Heaven’ is something we at Sega are incredibly proud to be a part of,” said Shuji Utsumi, president and COO of Sega. “The fandoms of these games deserve storytelling that honors what makes each title special, and we know Netflix shares that commitment. This is just the start of what these titles can become.” The new Sega titles will join Netflix’s growing slate of video game adaptations. Those include a live-action “Assassin’s Creed” series; a live-action “Gears of War” film; animated series adaptations based on “Minecraft,” “Magic: The Gathering” and “Clash of Clans”; the “Overcooked” competition series; second seasons of “Cyberpunk: Edgerunners” and “Splinter Cell: Deathwatch”; and the third and final season of “Devil May Cry.” Chris Rock Says Scott Rudin’s ‘Hard Coaching’ Made Him a Better Filmmaker: Some Creatives Don’t ‘Respond to a Hug’ Sara Bareilles on ‘Good Grief’ and Finding Joy in the Tough Stuff: ‘Grief Is the Mothership of This Record, but It Carries Release, Hope, Optimism and Connection’ Lisa Uncensored: On ‘Always Lalisa,’ Blackpink, Leaked Videos and Bond Girl Dreams Javier Bardem to Be Honored by Rome Film Festival With Lifetime Achievement Award ‘Mr. Irrelevant: The John Tuggle Story’ Trailer: ‘Superman’ Star David Corenswet Plays NFL Player Diagnosed With Cancer in Real-Life Story ‘Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother’ Review: A Blistering Spiritual Actioner Finally Gives Mahershala Ali a Leading Role Worth His While Loading comments... articles.title: Jon Cohen Named President Of Lipovsky & Stein’s Wonderlab Banner
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Jon Cohen Named President Of Lipovsky & Stein’s Wonderlab Banner Comedian Mojo Brookzz Bringing Debut Special ‘I Know You Lying’ To Netflix In October ‘The Family Stone’ Sequel Set At Searchlight With Claire Danes, Rachel McAdams, Sarah Jessica Parker & Many More Returning View All September 14, 2026 7:00am John Cohen, Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein Courtesy/Getty Jon Cohen has joined Wonderlab , the newly launched production company of Final Destination: Bloodlines helmers Zach Lipovsky and Adam Stein , as President. Cohen comes over from J.J. Abrams’ Bad Robot, where he most recently served as Head of Film. “We are so incredibly excited to launch Wonderlab with Jon,” Lipovsky and Stein said. “During his time at Bad Robot, Jon had a discerning eye for discovering some of the brightest genre filmmakers and writers and empowering them to make smart, original movies that connect with audiences. From our first conversations, Jon blew us away with his intelligence and deep creative insights about how to craft great stories. He shares our love of making unique and elevated films that are also incredibly fun and entertaining, and his collaborative nature is a perfect fit for the iterative way we plan to develop new movies at Wonderlab.” Related Stories News Zach Lipovsky And Adam B. Stein Ink First-Look Deal At Sony, Set 'Metal Gear Solid' Movie News 'Final Destination Bloodlines' Duo Zach Lipovsky & Adam B. Stein To Direct Animated 'Venom' Movie For Sony During his tenure at Bad Robot, Cohen produced a wide-ranging slate of features, including 10 Cloverfield Lane as co-producer, The Cloverfield Paradox and Overlord as executive producer. He was also a producer on Lou for Netflix, The End of Oak Street for Warner Bros., and the upcoming J.T. Mollner/Brie Larson film Skeletons , which Sony is set to release in 2027. Watch on Deadline Originally from Highland Park, Illinois, Cohen held executive positions at The Donners Company and Davis Entertainment before joining Bad Robot. “I couldn’t be more thrilled to be joining forces with Zach and Adam, and to be on the ground floor of what they’re creating with Wonderlab,” said Cohen. “I’ve admired the guys’ filmmaking for a while, and their FINAL DESTINATION: BLOODLINES was the sort of clever, impeccably made and wildly entertaining genre movie that so many aspire to create but very few can. As I’ve gotten to know them better, I’ve only grown more impressed with their ambition, work ethic, taste, story sense and talent, and how it’s all fused to an incredibly collaborative process and mindset that makes everyone who works with them long to work with them again. Cohen continued, “I’m very grateful to them for this opportunity, and to Sony Pictures for the faith they’ve placed in Wonderlab, and I look forward to making thrilling, surprising and emotionally resonant genre movies with this group for years to come.” Under a first-look deal with Sony Pictures that has the company developing projects across all of their film labels, Wonderlab projects announced so far include an animated Venom movie for Sony Pictures Animation; video game adaptation Metal Gear Solid ; and The Earthling , based on the Jonathan Marty short story, with the latter two projects being developed for Columbia Pictures. Founders Lipovsky and Stein broke out as the directors of New Line’s Final Destination: Bloodlines , which is now the highest-grossing film in its franchise at around $317 million worldwide. The films above are just the tip of the iceberg when it comes to their slate, which also includes a sequel to their 2018 sci-fi thriller Freaks , Warner Bros./Amblin’s Gremlins 3 , Universal/Amblin’s Long Lost , Paramount’s The Traveler , and more. “Wonderlab’s mission is to make movies using an iterative process that surrounds our creators with candid feedback from test audiences and other filmmakers,” Stein and Lipovsky stated. “It’s a process we’ve built over many years to make sure a film is the best it can be. We’re grateful to Tom, Sanford, and Peter at Sony for helping us scale this process across a slate of awesome films in the pipeline.” ‘Prima Facie’, ‘Wilson Shedd’, ‘Evil Genius’ Reviewed; Deadline Studio Vids Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Producer Remembered By Industry ‘Adolescence’ Scribe Says Writers Using AI To “Cheat” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Brews Up $46M WW & $30M In U.S. Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Gustavo Dudamel Takes New York Philharmonic Baton With Help From Lizzo, Liev Schreiber & More After Helping ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ To Strong Opening, Legion M Expands Film Fund On 25th Anniversary Of 9/11, NY1 Anchor Pat Kiernan On “Putting Yourself Back In That Moment” View All September 14, 2026 7:49am William Franklyn-Miller in 'Young Washington' Angel Studios Angel Studios says its membership program has surpassed 3 million paying members, doubling its level of a year ago. The company, which went public last year, is known for releasing what it calls “values-based” films and TV series. It has promoted to Wall Street the unique role played by the Angel Guild membership plan, which not only provides a recurring revenue source but also creates essentially a giant-scale focus group. Projects are fostered by Guild members, who then weigh in at various stages of a project’s life cycle, reading scripts and viewing test screenings. Related Stories News Gossip Goblin AI Feature 'Gods Don't Give Gifts' Poised To Make Next Leap From YouTube To Big Screen News Is Neon Lining Up UK Distribution? - The Dish Angel burst onto the scene in 2023 when it released Sound of Freedom , an unheralded action movie about child trafficking that became a left-field blockbuster, grossing more than $250 million worldwide. Neal Harmon , the company’s co-founder and CEO, told Deadline in June the Guild had reached 2.4 million members. At the time of that interview, Angel’s historical actioner Young Washington was having its world premiere at the Tribeca Festival. The film wound up grossing $47 million, spawning a sequel. Watch on Deadline Angel’s theatrical slate continues with Runner , an action thriller starring Owen Wilson and Alan Ritchson, with upcoming theatrical releases also including Angel and the Badman , Drummer Boy , Hershey and Zero A.D. On the series front, the company plans new seasons of The Wingfeather Saga, Homestead and Testament . While Angel shares are well below their price at the IPO in September 2025, they have risen more than 20% over the past week, to about $5.50. In a statement, Harmon called the 3 million member mark “an important early milestone” for the Provo, UT-based company. “Growth like this tells us audiences want something different,” he added. “They want great entertainment, they want a voice in what gets made, and they want Angel’s tech and marketing engine to spread the stories they choose to audiences everywhere.” ‘Prima Facie’, ‘Wilson Shedd’, ‘Evil Genius’ Reviewed; Deadline Studio Vids Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Producer Remembered By Industry ‘Adolescence’ Scribe Says Writers Using AI To “Cheat” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Brews Up $46M WW & $30M In U.S. Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Donald Trump Says There Already Are Enough Guardrails Around AI
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted ‘60 Minutes’ Debuts New Season With A Pentagon Exclusive And Hidden-Camera Exposé Amid Plenty Of Scrutiny Of The Show Itself FCC Chairman Brendan Carr Accuses James Talarico Of Running A “Hoax” With Jimmy Kimmel Sit-Down; YouTube Interview Nears 7 Million Views Anthropic CEO Calls For Slowing Down AI Development, Warns Of “Swarm” Taking Over Internet In 6-12 Months View All September 14, 2026 7:54am Donald Trump Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images Amid the increasing alarm over AI ‘s supercharged capabilities, Donald Trump rejected calls for new regulation, saying that there already are guardrails in place. In a Truth Social post on Monday, Trump wrote, “The only control or ‘guardrails’ that AI needs is a STRONG AND SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT, and the U.S.A. has that, in spades! The Trump Administration has stopped AI ‘people’ from doing bad, or potentially bad, ‘things,’ like Dario ( Anthropic !), who is now pretending to be a ‘perfect little angel’ – and we will continue to do so! We already have tremendous CRIMINAL and REGULATORY power over these companies! There is a SICK conspiracy going on against AI and Data Centers, and the only one that is happy about it is China. WHOEVER WINS AI, WINS! We are leading China, and all others, and will continue to do so. Conspiracy Theorists, Treasonists, Traitors, and Leakers, BEWARE!” Related Stories News '60 Minutes' Debuts New Season With A Pentagon Exclusive And Hidden-Camera Exposé Amid Plenty Of Scrutiny Of The Show Itself News FCC Chairman Brendan Carr Accuses James Talarico Of Running A "Hoax" With Jimmy Kimmel Sit-Down; YouTube Interview Nears 7 Million Views On Saturday, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei posted an essay in which he called for slowing down AI development, warning that a “swarm” of AI agents could be capable of taking over the internet in 6-12 months. Watch on Deadline He wrote, “Given the accelerating rate of AI capability development, it’s my worry that in 6–12 months such a swarm could be capable of taking over the entire internet with a persistent botnet (potentially causing hundreds of billions of dollars in damage), and that the scale of damage would continue to increase from there if AI becomes more powerful without the necessary guardrails.” Amodei called on AI companies to commit to third-party evaluators “to verify adherence to safety practices and commitments, report incidents, and help assess the alignment of not just completed AI models but training pipelines and processes.” Sam Altman, the CEO of OpenAI, and Elon Musk, founder of SpaceXAI, signalled agreement with Amodei. Amodei also called on governments to coordinate on safety standards. Trump, though, has warned of a slowdown in AI development ceding the technological arms race to China. articles.title: ‘Lupin’ Part 4 Trailer: Is The Titular Character Up To His Old Tricks Or Is There Really A New Lupin?
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Heated Rivalry’ Distributor Sphere Abacus Buys Digital Outfit Rocket Rights Gersh Signs Victoria Garrick Browne Kevin Macdonald On Capturing Pep Guardiola For Prime Video’s ‘A Beautiful Obsession’: “Like Having Robert De Niro Play A Football Coach” View All September 14, 2026 8:00am “We have a new Lupin .” These shocking words are uttered at the start of the trailer for Netflix ‘s highly anticipated Lupin Part 4, which launches October 23. With the titular character stuck in a glass box, another appears to be on the loose, and the police are keen to find them. Throughout the trailer, we see Assane up to his own tricks, donning different disguises and sewing confusion along the way. Lupin Part 4 begins four years after the end of the previous part. Assane wants to serve out his sentence and keep the promise he made to his son to go and meet their family in Senegal. But his plans are turned upside down by a mysterious announcement signed by Lupin, that multiple museums are to be hit with simultaneous heists. Related Stories News Netflix To Stream Lee Chang-Dong's Previous Works Following 'Possible Love' Silver Lion Win In Venice News Comedian Mojo Brookzz Bringing Debut Special 'I Know You Lying' To Netflix In October Omar Sy will of course return to reprise his iconic role, which has turned Lupin into one of Netflix’s top non-English language shows of all time, and one of its biggest even if you include English language fare. Watch on Deadline Sy is joined by Ludivine Sagnier, Antoine Gouy, Soufiane Guerrab, Shirine Boutella, Théo Christine and Laïka Blanc-Francard in Part 4. George Kay is creator in collaboration with François Uzan and with the participation of Marie Roussin, Florent Meyer, and Tigran Rosine. Edouard Salier, Everardo Gout and Hugo Gélin are directing Part 4, which comes from Gaumont with the participation of Carrousel Studios . Writers are Mathilde Arnaud, Jean-Yves Arnaud, Rosine and Meyer. articles.title: Moveria Film Acquires ‘No Money No Honey,’ Documentary Set For Imminent Premiere At Camden International Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Midnight Madness! A Caped Canadian Prime Minister Stars In ‘Ladies And Gentlemen, Brian Mulroney’ – Toronto Film Festival ‘NAZA’ Review: Israeli Military Accused Of Depraved Indifference To Palestinian Life, Using AI To Kill In Gaza – Venice Film Festival ‘Black Sunflowers’ First Look: Ukraine’s Youth Live Life On The Edge In Propulsive Doc From EP Sean Penn – Toronto Film Festival View All September 14, 2026 8:00am 'No Money No Honey' Mimbre Films/Moveria Film EXCLUSIVE: Moveria Film has acquired international sales rights to No Money No Honey ahead of the documentary’s world premiere at the Camden International Film Festival in Maine. Moveria describes the film directed by Nicole Costa as “a vibrant story of friendship, migration, joy, and resilience” centering on Máxima Mauricio (she/he), “an Argentine non-binary sex worker in New York.” Daniela Camino of Mimbre Films produces along with Costa. No Money No Honey revisits personal VHS tapes recorded by Mauricio between 1991 and 2004, according to a synopsis. “Interweaving this vibrant archival material with post-pandemic 4K footage, the film opens a fluid portal into Máxima’s memory—confronting a childhood marked by abuse and neglect while longing for her golden days across Buenos Aires, Miami, and New York.” Related Stories Documentary Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival Documentary 22nd Camden Film Festival To Showcase New Work By Documentary's Leading Lights: Gibney, Kopple, Oppenheimer, Chin, Vasarhelyi, Poitras & More Lucas Besnard and Yasmin Porangaba negotiated the sales rights deal on behalf of Moveria Film, with producer Daniela Camino representing Mimbre Films. Watch on Deadline Moveria Films “What really drew us to No Money No Honey was the intimacy of Máxima’s story and the way the film brings us directly into her world,” said Lucas Besnard of Paris-based Moveria Film. “I was struck by the contrast between the VHS footage of her past—with all the energy, glamour, friends, and parties—and her life in New York in 2020. Having lived in New York myself, I connected with this side of the city. Máxima is incredibly endearing, and through her story, you get a sense of a queer community and a reality that deserves to be seen and better understood. That’s what made us want to bring the film into Moveria’s catalogue.” Ceskary Avitia of Moveria Film added, “Coming from Mexico, I know how much prejudice surrounds sex work and trans identity. What drew me to this film is that it doesn’t try to convince you of anything; it just asks you to listen to Máxima’s own voice and to the VHS tapes she filmed of her life. Through her archive, someone’s story opens up into an entire community—her friends, their world, and their shared history of trauma and resilience. Nicole Costa gives voice to a community rarely heard on screen, and everyone deserves the chance to tell their own story.” Mimbre Films In a statement, producer Daniela Camino of Mimbre Films commented, “Working with Moveria has been a turning point for No Money No Honey ’s international debut. Their experience and personalized approach are just what a film like ours needed. We are truly confident we will reach audiences around the globe.” No Money No Honey is programmed in Cinematic Vision Award competition at CIFF, the prestigious all-documentary festival that runs Sept. 17-20 in mid-coast Maine. The acquisition expands Moveria’s slate of “bold, auteur-driven international cinema,” according to a release. Founded in 2025, Moveria is an independent production, international distribution, and cultural mediation company “born from a collaboration between tech developers Arnaud Schoenher and Tristan de Oliveira and arts and culture professionals Ceskary Avitia and Isotta Tassoni… Moveria Film merges custom digital tools—including modeling, automation, and optimization—with traditional film production and distribution frameworks, bringing a novel approach to cinema grounded in dialogue across diverse fields to foster new creative experiences, fresh perspectives, and bold narratives about the world around us.” No Money No Honey , running time 80 minutes, is directed by Nicole Costa and written by Costa, Daniela Camino, and Melisa Miranda. Daniela Camino and Costa produced the film. The cast includes Máxima Mauricio Rodas, Sebastian Quiencke a.k.a. La Baronesa Ditra, Antonia Martinez, Nellie Benittez, Mila Miller, Darius M. Curry, Nirvana Garcia, and Iván Monalisa Ojeda. ‘Prima Facie’, ‘Wilson Shedd’, ‘Evil Genius’ Reviewed; Deadline Studio Vids Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Producer Remembered By Industry ‘Adolescence’ Scribe Says Writers Using AI To “Cheat” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Brews Up $46M WW & $30M In U.S. Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Pluto Film Boards ‘Ida’ Star Agata Trzebuchowska’s Horror Feature ‘Sick’ Ahead Of Fantastic Fest Premiere + First Teaser
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Well Go USA Entertainment Acquires ‘The Optimist’ For Digital Release On November 17 Canada’s Precious Metal Productions & Black Fawn Distribution Strike Genre Slate Deal – TIFF Beta Cinema Posts Fresh Deals For Trudie Styler’s ‘Up Against It’ Ahead Of TIFF Debut View All September 14, 2026 8:09am Sick Maciej Edelman EXCLUSIVE: Pluto Film has boarded sales for Agata Trzebuchowska’s horror feature Sick ahead of its world premiere at Fantastic Fest in Austin in September, which will be followed by its European debut at the Sitges Film Festival . The unsettling film about the horrors of growing up is the feature directorial debut of Polish director, screenwriter and actress Agata Trzebuchowska, who is best known internationally for her lead performance in Paweł Pawlikowski’s 2015 Oscar winner Ida . Patryk Sielecki and Adrianna Rędzia at Warsaw-based Lumisenta lead produce, while the cast features stars Konrad Kąkol, Katarzyna Łubik, Monika Niemczyk, Julian Świeżewski, and Eliza Rycembel. Related Stories News Firebook Entertainment Signals Move Into Production As First Movie 'Every Heavy Thing' Heads To Sitges News 'Disforia' Trailer: Spanish Horror-Thriller World Premieres At Austin's Fantastic Fest Set against the backdrop of the summer holidays, Sick revolves around sixteen-year-old Maks (Kąkol) and his older sister Emma (Łubik) who are sent to the Polish countryside to care for their ailing grandmother. Watch on Deadline Trapped together in the heavy, stifling isolation of the summer heat, the siblings’ bond begins to shift into something unsettling and difficult to define. As tensions rise and boundaries begin to blur, their grandmother’s frail presence takes on an increasingly disturbing quality, turning a once-idyllic summer into a haunting passage into adulthood. “We are very happy that Sick has found its home at Pluto Film. From our first conversations, we felt that they understood both the film’s provocative nature and the tenderness hidden beneath its genre elements,” said Lumisenta’s Patryk Sielecki. “The world premiere at Fantastic Fest and the European premiere at Sitges are an exciting beginning for the film, bringing it to audiences open to bold and unconventional stories. At the same time, we believe Sick can resonate beyond the genre circuit, as it is ultimately a deeply emotional story about adolescence, desire and dependence, centered on a relationship that crosses every possible boundary.” Pluto Film MD Daniela Cölle praised Trzebuchowska’s bold reinvention of the classic coming-of-age summer tale. “Agata Trzebuchowska has created an atmospheric and unsettling horror film that transforms the oppressive calmness of a summer into a powerful psychological landscape. Rather than coming-of-age story, Sick is the horror of growing up, exploring the fear, confusion, and loss of certainty that accompany the passage into adulthood.” Trzebuchowska shot to fame for her performance in Ida , as a young woman on the verge of taking her vows as a nun, after being scouted in a café by director Małgorzata Szumowska who knew her friend Pawlikowski was struggling to find the right person for the role. Trzebuchowska has eschewed mainstream fame since to forge her own path as a screenwriter and director. Sick follows short films including the Sundance-selected Heat and Vacancy , which also travelled the festival circuit stopping off at Go Short and Flickers’ Rhode Island International Film Festival. She also continues to act and was recently seen in Pete Ohs’ Erupcja alongside Charli XCX, Lena Góra and Will Madden. Sick will premiere in the New Wave sidebar of the Fantastic Fest running from September 17 to 24, 2026. articles.title: Amanda Brocato Promoted To President Of Rosenfield Media Group
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Jon Cohen Named President Of Lipovsky & Stein’s Wonderlab Banner Comedian Mojo Brookzz Bringing Debut Special ‘I Know You Lying’ To Netflix In October ‘The Family Stone’ Sequel Set At Searchlight With Claire Danes, Rachel McAdams, Sarah Jessica Parker & Many More Returning View All September 14, 2026 8:30am Amanda Brocato Rosenfield Media Group Amanda Brocato has been promoted to President at Rosenfield Media Group . Brocato will now take on a larger role within RMG’s business development and overall strategic direction, while continuing her work in client relations. She maintains her role alongside CEO Zach Rosenfield in corporate communications, as well as overseeing the company’s national footprint of live events, including the likes of the Super Bowl and World Cup. With RMG since its October 2020 formation, Brocato previously served as EVP, Corporate Communications and Live Events. While based in Austin, Texas, she manages a team in both RMG’s Los Angeles and New York offices. Accounts she oversees include the entertainment portfolio for Authentic Brands Group (Authentic) including Shaquille O’Neal, Dunkman, Authentic Studios, Muhammad Ali, Marilyn Monroe and Sports Illustrated . Related Stories Agencies Rosenfield Media Group Ups Sean Grabin To VP Of Literary Division News Melissa Sun Named SVP, Purpose At Rosenfield Media Group Brocato’s work at RMG has included co-developing their AI roadmap alongside Rosenfield with the company’s Director of AI to ensure corporate clients are getting the most out of AI tools as part of their PR and marketing strategies. CEO Zach Rosenfield told us, “Amanda’s promotion is long overdue. When we opened RMG, our only goal was to find a way to bring in Amanda to work for us. We knew how vital she would be to steering the vision of the company and she has exceeded expectations. Because of her PR mind and leadership, RMG’s expansion has been possible.” Watch on Deadline Brocato first met Rosenfield when the two worked together at Howard Bragman’s firm, Fifteen Minutes. Prior to joining RMG, she was a partner at a hospitality-based PR firm in Austin, working with clients including W Hotels, The Line and the James Beard Foundation. She said, “I’m incredibly proud of how far our agency and its reach has grown over the past six years to thrive across entertainment, sports, business and live events. On the foundation of fantastic company culture, I look forward to playing a role in how our business evolves with the times to ensure our clients and partners get the comprehensive representation they deserve no matter the lane they choose to operate in.” Stan Rosenfield and Katie Feldman continue to run the day-to-day within the talent business at RMG, which last year welcomed Sean Grabin as VP, Lit and Authors. ‘Prima Facie’, ‘Wilson Shedd’, ‘Evil Genius’ Reviewed; Deadline Studio Vids Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Producer Remembered By Industry ‘Adolescence’ Scribe Says Writers Using AI To “Cheat” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Brews Up $46M WW & $30M In U.S. Read More About: Comments

Sean McKittrick and Raymond Mansfield produce for QC Entertainment, with Edward H. Hamm Jr., Jameson Parker and Gabrielle Union serving as executive producers.
