articles.title: Paramount & Comcast Streamer SkyShowtime Could Be Shut Down, Board Says
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max ‘Lupin’ Part 4 Trailer: Is The Titular Character Up To His Old Tricks Or Is There Really A New Lupin? ‘Sunday In The Park With George’ Revival Delayed After Ariana Grande & Jonathan Bailey Exit ‘Heated Rivalry’ Distributor Sphere Abacus Buys Digital Outfit Rocket Rights View All September 14, 2026 8:39am 'Landman': available on SkyShowtime in some European territories Emerson Miller/Paramount+ The future of Paramount and Comcast ‘s international streamer SkyShowtime is in serious doubt amid the Paramount-Warner mega-merger. A note from the SkyShowtime board to CEO Monty Sarhan informed him that it has kicked off a strategic review, “which includes the possibility of a wind-down.” “No decisions have been made, and all options remain under consideration,” added the note, which Deadline has obtained. SkyShowtime was launched as a JV streaming service four years back between Paramount and Comcast as a way of entering European territories that didn’t have access to their own streamers Paramount+ or Peacock. It combines shows from those two streamers plus Sky Studios and local originals, and has steadily grown its subscriber base across 22 European markets over the years. Related Stories Executives L.A. County Projects Huge Job Losses If Paramount Exits California; Company Slams Antitrust Action By AGs & WGA In Official Rebuke Legal They're Talking! Paramount & AGs Settlement Talks Set For Next Month; Bonta Downplays Significance As "Standard Course" The board’s note to Sarhan said the update is “the beginning of a dialogue, not the end of one” and “where any proposal could affect employees, we will follow the information and consultation processes required in each of our markets.” Watch on Deadline “We recognise this is difficult news and that it creates uncertainty,” it added. “We are grateful to you and to everyone at SkyShowtime for all that has been achieved.” Sarhan relayed the note to staff, adding: “I know this news creates uncertainty and, as we work through what comes next, my priority and that of the leadership team, is to be there and support all of you.” The news comes amid the Paramount-Warner mega-merger, which we have already reported could create complications for SkyShowtime. In May, industry sources told us Paramount’s proposed ownership of Warner Bros. Discovery’s HBO Max would likely put the David Ellison-run company in breach of its JV agreement for SkyShowtime. A person familiar with the matter, however, told Deadline the review revealed today is “entirely unrelated” and is a “joint review by both shareholders.” THR was first with today’s news. ‘Prima Facie’, ‘Wilson Shedd’, ‘Evil Genius’ Reviewed; Deadline Studio Vids Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Producer Remembered By Industry ‘Adolescence’ Scribe Says Writers Using AI To “Cheat” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Brews Up $46M WW & $30M In U.S. Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Netflix and Sega Set ‘Crazy Taxi’ Film; ‘Sonic’ & ‘Stranger Than Heaven’ Adaptations Also Part Of New Slate Partnership
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Jon Cohen Named President Of Lipovsky & Stein’s Wonderlab Banner Comedian Mojo Brookzz Bringing Debut Special ‘I Know You Lying’ To Netflix In October ‘The Family Stone’ Sequel Set At Searchlight With Claire Danes, Rachel McAdams, Sarah Jessica Parker & Many More Returning View All September 14, 2026 8:45am 'Crazy Taxi' scribes Dan Gregor & Doug Mand Gregory Wallace/Sela Shiloni Netflix has set a new slate of projects with video game company Sega , including film adaptations of their titles Crazy Taxi and Stranger Than Heaven , and a new Sonic children’s series. Dan Gregor & Doug Mand , the screenwriting duo behind 2025’s reboot of The Naked Gun , are penning Crazy Taxi . First released in arcades in 1999, the game puts players behind the wheel of a fearless cabbie racing the clock through chaotic city streets — flying off ramps, dodging traffic, and chasing tips with punk-rock energy. The next installment in the series, Crazy Taxi: World Tour , releases next year. Producers on the film include the Sonic franchise’s Neal H. Moritz & Toby Ascher (for Original Film) and Toru Nakahara. Related Stories News 'Lupin' Part 4 Trailer: Is The Titular Character Up To His Old Tricks Or Is There Really A New Lupin? News Netflix To Stream Lee Chang-Dong's Previous Works Following 'Possible Love' Silver Lion Win In Venice Netflix’s animated Sonic series, in development with Carlos Stevens and Nakahara, is targeting “an upper pre-school audience,” per the streamer — “a high-voltage, comedic, yet emotionally grounded series built for kids who want to feel a little edge, a little attitude, and a lot of ‘that’s my crew’ wish fulfillment.” Watch on Deadline From RGG Studio — developer of the Like a Dragon / Yakuza series — Stranger Than Heaven takes place in early 20th-century Japan, following a foreigner who claws his way from destitute stranger to feared yakuza to entertainment tycoon. Nakahara is producing the live-action feature take. Netflix and Sega come to their new partnership after working together on the animated series Sonic Prime , which ran for three seasons. Sega’s Head Producer Nakahara said, “Expect something cute yet cool for Sonic , hilariously crazy for Crazy Taxi , and a badass action drama for STRANGER THAN HEAVEN , because we’ve got some amazing creative ideas lined up and we are just getting started. The whole team is absolutely thrilled!” Netflix’s Brandon Riegg, VP of Nonfiction and Transmedia, said: “Great games already have what every adaptation is chasing — characters people love, worlds they know by heart, and fandoms that show up. With Crazy Taxi , Sonic and Stranger Than Heaven , we get to work across three completely different eras of Sega’s catalog, celebrating everything fans love, while introducing them to new audiences.” Sega’s President and COO, Shuji Utsumi, stated: “We’ve watched Netflix take on stories across every kind of format and treat each one with real craft, and seeing that same dedication applied to Sonic , Crazy Taxi and Stranger Than Heaven is something we at Sega are incredibly proud to be a part of. The fandoms of these games deserve storytelling that honors what makes each title special, and we know Netflix shares that commitment. This is just the start of what these titles can become.” Sega’s trio of games joins a growing slate of video game adaptations at Netflix that includes a live-action Assassin’s Creed series; live-action Gears of War film; animated series adaptations based on Minecraft , Magic: The Gathering and Clash of Clans ; competition series Overcooked ; second seasons of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners and Splinter Cell: Deathwatch ; and the third and final season of Devil May Cry . ‘Prima Facie’, ‘Wilson Shedd’, ‘Evil Genius’ Reviewed; Deadline Studio Vids Jeremy Thomas Tributes: Producer Remembered By Industry ‘Adolescence’ Scribe Says Writers Using AI To “Cheat” ‘Practical Magic 2’ Brews Up $46M WW & $30M In U.S. Read More About: Comments
